It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its verified public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Squares
providers.description: Squares is a marketplace platform for discovering and booking curated, personally-vetted workspaces around the world — lofts, photo studios, rooftops, and villas suited to remote workers, creatives, and digital nomads. Spaces are scouted across 13+ cities including Almaty, Da Nang, and Austin, and hosts can list their own spaces on the platform. Squares is a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer marketplace website but no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Stere
providers.description: Stere is a New York-based insurance infrastructure company (founded 2021) that lets insurers, MGAs, and distribution partners build and launch digital insurance products - rating, quoting, binding, policy issuance, claims, and premium payments - in weeks rather than years. Its core offering is a "Stere API-as-a-Service" underwriting API (insurers can bring their own API or have Stere build one) plus a separate Stere Unified API and Stere Distribution layer that let brokers, wholesalers, fintechs, and embedded partners reach multiple carriers/products through a single connection (API, SDK, and webhooks). Stere Claims handles FNOL and claims workflow (portions of claims assessment and resolution are marketed as in-development/coming soon), and Stere Pay / Stere Pay Later provides a buy-now-pay-later gateway for insurance premiums. There is no self-serve public developer portal, published API reference, OpenAPI/Swagger document, or sandbox signup on stere.io; the marketing site references a "Stere Docs," "API Changelog," and "API Status" area under /developer/, but those paths return 404 publicly and integration is provisioned per customer after a sales-led partner/insurer onboarding engagement. The APIs below are honestly modeled from Stere's own product marketing pages, not from a published API reference.

providers.name: TeamViewer
providers.description: TeamViewer is a global provider of remote connectivity, remote access, and remote support software used by IT teams, MSPs, and enterprises to manage devices, deliver IT support, and connect operational technology across desktops, mobile devices, and IoT endpoints. The TeamViewer Web API is a RESTful API that uses OAuth 2.0 bearer token authentication and JSON to programmatically manage users, devices, groups, sessions, session reports, and meetings within a TeamViewer company account.

providers.name: Tembo Health
providers.description: Tembo Health is a telemedicine practice (founded 2018) that partners with skilled nursing facilities and senior living communities to deliver 24/7 virtual specialty and urgent care to elderly residents. Its board-certified clinicians provide treat-in-place emergency medicine, psychiatry, cardiology, and dementia care, reducing avoidable ER transfers by roughly 75 percent, and the company works with senior-care operators and EHR platforms such as PointClickCare. Tembo Health is a healthcare services provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Twingate
providers.description: Twingate is a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) platform that replaces legacy VPNs with software-defined perimeters, providing identity-based, least-privilege access to private resources without exposing them to the public internet. The Twingate Admin API is a GraphQL API authenticated via API key (X-API-KEY header) that enables programmatic management of remote networks, connectors, resources, users, groups, service accounts, devices, policies, and DNS filtering profiles.

providers.name: Ubiquity6
providers.description: Ubiquity6 was a San Francisco augmented-reality startup ("Capture & Edit Reality") backed by Benchmark, First Round, and Index Ventures. It built Display.land, a multiplayer 3D/AR/VR capture and creation platform, acquired Wavy AR, and was acquired by Discord in June 2021, after which its products were discontinued. Ubiquity6 never published a public API or developer program; its GitHub organization survives as a set of open-source computer vision and React Native forks, and a few internal packages remain on npm under the @ubiquity6 scope.

providers.name: Ulu Ventures
providers.description: Ulu Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital firm based in Palo Alto, California, founded by Miriam Rivera and Clint Korver. The firm applies decision analysis to venture investing and backs diverse founder teams, having funded 200+ companies producing 10 unicorns and 3 public companies over 14+ years, growing from $3.5M in initial capital to a $138M second institutional fund. Ulu Ventures publishes no public API surface; this profile captures the firm's identity, web properties, and probed security posture.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Valley National Bank
providers.description: Valley National Bank is a nationally chartered commercial bank (OCC-regulated) and the principal banking subsidiary of Valley National Bancorp (NASDAQ: VLY), a regional financial holding company founded in 1927 with roughly $64 billion in assets and more than 200 offices serving consumers, families, and businesses across New Jersey, New York, Florida, Alabama, California, and Illinois. Its business spans consumer banking, commercial banking, and treasury services. As of this profile Valley National Bank operates no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable API specifications; consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached only through third-party open-finance aggregators (Finicity by Mastercard is documented, alongside general Plaid/Tink connectivity) rather than a directly exposed FDX-conformant or first-party API.

providers.name: Vespucci
providers.description: Vespucci (Vespucci Analytics) is a product-analytics platform that helps teams understand why their users engage with a product. Rather than replacing existing analytics, it connects to the event data companies already collect in Amplitude or Segment (via Reverse ETL) and applies statistical and AI models to automatically surface the drivers of activation, retention, churn, and engagement. It provides 24/7 monitoring with automated alerts when behavioral patterns shift, user segmentation, and story-style dashboards, and can push identified segments to activation tools such as OneSignal, MailChimp, and Brevo. Founded in 2021 and based in Brussels, Belgium, Vespucci is backed by Seedcamp.

providers.name: Vircle
providers.description: Vircle is a Malaysian family fintech platform, operated by Debit Circles Sdn Bhd, offering a parent app paired with a prepaid card for children so families can give pocket money, assign chores, and teach kids to earn, save, and spend responsibly. It issues a Visa Prepaid Card (Vircle Club) usable at Visa merchants worldwide and a School Card for cafeteria and campus e-store purchases, with real-time spend alerts and parental controls. Card issuance is provided in partnership with Fass Payment Solutions (Fasspay). Vircle is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As a consumer mobile app it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Waymark
providers.description: Waymark is a healthcare technology and services company that scales value-based, community-based care for people enrolled in Medicaid. In partnership with health plans and primary care providers, Waymark trains and employs local care teams — community health workers, care coordinators, licensed therapists, and pharmacists — and equips them with predictive technology that identifies high-risk patients and coordinates interventions addressing the social determinants of health such as housing, food security, transportation, medication management, and behavioral health. The model is designed to reduce avoidable hospitalizations and emergency room visits, and Waymark operates community-based care across Ohio, Virginia, and Washington. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), NEA, Lux Capital, and CVS Health Ventures. Waymark publishes no public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its public web presence.

providers.name: Wevat
providers.description: Wevat is a Seedcamp-backed fintech and travel-tech company operating a mobile app that digitizes VAT (Value Added Tax) refunds for international travellers shopping in France. Instead of paper tax-free forms, shoppers photograph their invoices in the Wevat app, which consolidates purchases across stores into a single digital tax-refund form, validates it at the departure point, and pays out the refund (up to around 13% of spend) in the traveller's chosen currency via credit card, bank transfer, Alipay, or WeChat Pay. Wevat is a consumer mobile-app product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its public web and business identity.

providers.name: Whill
providers.description: WHILL, Inc. designs and manufactures enhanced personal mobility solutions — electric power chairs and mobility scooters, including the Model C2, Model F, the Modo Breeze ultralight foldable wheelchair, and the Model R three- and four-wheel scooters — and operates an autonomous personal mobility service that has completed over 700,000 rides worldwide across airports and other venues. WHILL was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this writing it is a consumer hardware and mobility-service company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a company record and will be enriched if WHILL launches a developer program.

providers.name: Xperi
providers.description: Xperi Inc. (NYSE: XPER) is an entertainment technology company whose licensed technologies power audio, video, and media discovery experiences across connected cars, consumer electronics, pay-TV, and streaming media platforms. Its brands include DTS immersive audio, HD Radio digital broadcast radio, IMAX Enhanced certification, and the TiVo video platform. Xperi ships its technologies to automakers, device makers, and video providers through commercial licensing and integration programs rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal or API documentation was found, though its TiVo engineering organization maintains an open-source presence on GitHub.

providers.name: Yonder
providers.description: Yonder is a UK-based financial technology company offering rewards credit and debit cards — a "financial membership" that earns points on everyday spending, redeemable across 300+ dining, travel, shopping, entertainment and wellness partners. Cards run on the Mastercard network with no foreign-exchange fees, and Yonder is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) with FSCS-protected accounts held via partner banks. Yonder ships a consumer mobile app and a help centre but does not expose a public developer API or portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (backers include Northzone, Seedcamp and Techstars).

providers.name: Amera
providers.description: Amera (Amera Health Solutions) is a Seattle-based, Y Combinator (Fall 2025) healthcare technology company that automates claims processing workflows for health insurance payers, third-party administrators (TPAs), and self-insured employers. Its normalization engine ingests messy claim inputs from any source — EDI, PDFs, paper, fax, and proprietary/non-standard formats — and turns them into adjudication-ready, structured data that plugs into existing claims cores via API, EDI, or SFTP. The platform automates validation, reconciliation, stop-loss reporting, and real-time visibility and analytics, reducing plan administration costs and cutting carrier submission times from weeks to minutes while keeping full audit trails and HIPAA compliance. Founded in 2025 by Louise Tanski and Deep Kapur (both formerly of Rupa Health), Amera already works with payers and plan administrators representing roughly 100,000 members. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Amera does not yet publish a public developer portal or API specification.

providers.name: Azos
providers.description: Azos is a Brazilian insurtech (founded 2021) that sells fully digital life insurance directly to consumers and through a broker (corretor) channel. Its products include life insurance, serious-illness coverage, accidental-disability coverage, and funeral assistance, all contracted online in minutes with no medical exam, transparent pricing from around R$5/month, and coverage up to R$1 million. The company positions itself as "seguro de vida sem burocracia" (life insurance without bureaucracy) and is backed by Prosus Ventures. Azos runs a consumer app and a broker portal but publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Ballet
providers.description: Ballet is a consumer cryptocurrency cold-storage company founded by Bobby Lee that makes physical, non-electronic wallet cards based on the BIP38 open-source standard, letting people store Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and 1,000+ coins and NFTs safe from electronic hacking and preventable user error. The physical REAL Series card holds the keys; a companion mobile app, Ballet Crypto, lets holders check balances and market value and add assets. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Ballet is a hardware/consumer product rather than a developer platform, so it publishes no public API — this profile captures its identity, security posture, and open-source footprint.

providers.name: Beacon Biosignals
providers.description: Beacon Biosignals develops AI-powered neurotechnology for brain health, applying machine learning to EEG (electroencephalography) data at scale. Its platform serves two markets: precision neuroscience for drug development, where it collects and analyzes EEG across the clinical trial lifecycle (2M+ hours of EEG analyzed across 40+ trials), and home sleep testing diagnostics through the SleepView Monitor and SleepView Direct products (500K+ home sleep tests completed). Beacon is also a prolific open-source contributor in the Julia ecosystem, publishing signal-data and modeling libraries such as Onda.jl, Legolas.jl, EDF.jl, Effects.jl, and Lighthouse.jl. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a life-sciences / neurotech provider; Beacon does not publish a public developer API, so this profile centers on its open-source software surface and company identity.

providers.name: Berkshire Grey
providers.description: Berkshire Grey is a Bedford, Massachusetts-based AI and robotics company that builds integrated pick-and-place, parcel sortation, trailer-unloading, and shuttle-sortation systems for eCommerce fulfillment, retail replenishment, and parcel logistics operations. Its product portfolio is organized around four flagship robotic systems — Core robotic picking system, Dispatch parcel sorter, Scoop trailer unloader, and Stride shuttle sorter — supported by the BG Flex mobile robotic platform and a centralized operating environment that orchestrates fleets of industrial-grade mobile robots for induct, transport, sort, sequence, and fulfill workflows including buy-online-pickup-in-store, curbside, and store replenishment. The company holds 700+ awarded patents (300+ pending) and has deployed solutions with Global-100 retailers and logistics service providers including Walmart, Target, and FedEx, with FedEx expanding from small-parcel sortation into broader AI robotic package-handling capabilities. Berkshire Grey originally went public via SPAC merger with Revolution Acceleration Acquisition Corp in 2021, then entered into a definitive merger agreement with SoftBank Group in 2023 (approximately $375M / $1.40 per share) and is now operated as a private SoftBank portfolio company. Integration with warehouse-management systems is delivered through a proprietary RESTful API surfaced via professional services and a 24/7 remote monitoring and predictive-maintenance support model; the API, BG-OS platform, and any associated SDKs are not publicly documented, and Berkshire Grey does not operate a public developer portal, downloadable SDK, or open-source release for its robotic operating environment.

providers.name: BharatPe
providers.description: BharatPe is a New Delhi-based fintech company founded in 2018 by Ashneer Grover and Shashvat Nakrani that provides digital payments and financial services to Indian small and medium businesses. Its merchant stack centers on a single interoperable UPI QR for payment acceptance across all UPI apps, augmented by BharatPe Speaker for voice transaction confirmations, BharatSwipe POS card machines for offline acceptance, BharatPe One (all-in-one POS), bill payments, and a co-branded credit card. On the financing side, BharatPe originates business loans for merchants through partner NBFCs, runs the InvestBharatPe / 12% Club investment platform, operates the PostPe buy-now-pay-later product, and is a co-promoter of Unity Small Finance Bank. The company reports more than ten million merchant partners across 450+ Indian cities and turned profitable in FY24 with roughly INR 1,700 crore in revenue. BharatPe is owned by Resilient Innovations Private Limited; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, sandbox, or OpenAPI surface — its merchant and consumer products are delivered through native Android/iOS apps and an enterprise sales channel for partners.

providers.name: Bosch
providers.description: Bosch is a German multinational engineering and technology company producing automotive components, industrial technology, consumer goods, and energy and building technology. Bosch operates the Bosch IoT Suite, an open IoT platform offering device management, software rollouts, edge services, and IoT data analytics, along with open source contributions to Eclipse Foundation IoT projects.

providers.name: Buildah
providers.description: Buildah is an open-source, Linux-based command-line tool for building OCI-compliant container images without requiring a full container runtime or daemon. It allows building images from scratch or using Dockerfiles, with fine-grained control over image layers. Buildah supports rootless builds in unprivileged environments and integrates seamlessly with Podman and Skopeo as part of the containers organization. It is commonly used in Kubernetes-based CI/CD pipelines to avoid Docker-in-Docker complexity.

providers.name: Cargolux
providers.description: Cargolux Airlines International S.A. is Europe's largest all-cargo airline, headquartered at Luxembourg Findel Airport in Luxembourg and operating a global Boeing 747 freighter network under IATA designator CV and air waybill prefix 172 (with Cargolux Italia on prefix 356). In the logistics chain Cargolux is the main-leg air carrier: it sells capacity to freight forwarders and general sales agents rather than to shippers, hands cargo to terminal and ground handling operators such as its Luxcargo Handling subsidiary, and files customs and security data on behalf of the contracted forwarder. Its API posture is honestly a customer-contract one. Cargolux publishes no developer portal and no machine-readable contract of any kind — developer.cargolux.com, developers.cargolux.com and docs.cargolux.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/ all return 404 on www.cargolux.com. The only public self-service surfaces are HTML: a track-and-trace widget and a flight scheduler on the marketing site, plus a login-walled Customer Portal at my.cargolux.com. A real quote-and- booking API exists, but it is a bilateral, commercially negotiated forwarder interface — piloted with Kuehne+Nagel in 2021 and extended to DB Schenker — with no published reference, and it is complemented by indirect distribution through the cargo.one, CargoAi and WebCargo by Freightos marketplaces. Underneath, Cargolux runs IBS Software's iCargo SaaS cargo management system and holds a large minority stake in Luxembourg's CHAMP Cargosystems, whose developer.champ.aero portal is the developer surface Cargolux's ecosystem actually reads — CHAMP's, not Cargolux's. IATA e-AWB "Single Process" is documented; no IATA ONE Record or Cargo-XML publication was found.

providers.name: Cartrawler
providers.description: CarTrawler is a leading B2B technology provider of car rental, ground transport and insurtech solutions to the global travel industry. Through its Connect Platform it links airlines, online travel agencies and travel companies to a worldwide marketplace of car rental suppliers, private transfers and ride-hailing partners, displaying millions of cars daily and processing billions of queries. CarTrawler serves 70+ airlines and 250+ travel companies worldwide (including American Airlines, Ryanair, easyJet, Qantas, Southwest, eDreamsODIGEO and Uber), differentiating through proprietary technology, real-time machine-learning pricing and personalized retailing. Integration is delivered through partner and supplier programs rather than a public self-service developer portal; this profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Coverfox
providers.description: Coverfox is one of India's largest online insurance distribution platforms, offering retail insurance products including car, bike, health, and life insurance alongside embedded insurance solutions for lenders, NBFCs, and fintechs. The company partners with 37+ IRDAI-approved insurers to compare, purchase, and manage policies online, and has reached roughly 10 million households across India. Coverfox was backed by Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer program or API at this time.

providers.name: CoverHound
providers.description: CoverHound is an InsurTech marketplace, now part of Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO), that lets consumers and small businesses compare and buy insurance online from A-rated carriers across all 50 states. Its platform covers personal lines — auto, homeowners, and renters — alongside business insurance including general liability, workers' compensation, professional liability, commercial auto, cyber, and directors & officers coverage. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Carpinteria, California, CoverHound provides digital quote comparison, agent-assisted purchasing, and an insurance learning center. It operates as a consumer/SMB web marketplace and publishes no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Custodian
providers.description: Custodian (getcustodian.com) is a Mexico City-based consumer mobile application and insurtech service that centralizes vehicle documentation and automotive administrative tasks. The app helps drivers organize and store important paperwork, track expiration dates for registration, insurance policies, and health certificates, receive renewal notifications, and get assistance with auto-insurance renewals and claims management. A premium annual subscription (450 MXN) adds full document-handling and verification services (including Mexico City vehicle verification). Custodian is a consumer app distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Dejbox (Refectory)
providers.description: Dejbox is a French corporate-catering company founded in Lille in 2015 by Adrien Verhack and Vincent Dupied, acquired by the Carrefour Group in January 2020 and since rebranded as Refectory (refectory.fr). It delivers prepared, seasonal meals to employees of companies located in the peripheral zones of major French cities via a digital canteen (click-and-collect precommande before 10:30) and connected self-service fridges, controlling 100% of its value chain through its own Manufactures and a national network of 23 logistics hubs. Originally surfaced as a Partech portfolio company, it operates in Bordeaux, Grenoble, Lille, Lyon, Nantes, Paris and other French cities. Its consumer platform runs on a public OAuth2/OIDC identity server (customers.refectory.fr) and an API gateway (gateway.refectory.fr).

providers.name: Diana Health
providers.description: Diana Health (heydianahealth.com) is a women's healthcare provider offering personalized in-person and virtual care across the reproductive and primary health lifespan: maternity and prenatal care, labor and delivery, postpartum, gynecology, well-woman visits, menopause management, family planning and contraception, mental health, and wellness coaching, plus treatment for conditions such as endometriosis, PCOS, UTIs, and STIs. The company operates collaborative care-team clinics across Tennessee, Florida, and Texas, accepts most major insurance plans including Medicaid, and emphasizes longer appointments and whole-person (mental, physical, social) care. Diana Health is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. It publishes a consumer marketing and appointment-booking website but no public developer API; this profile is enriched with identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Dokku
providers.description: Dokku is an open-source Docker-powered self-hosted Platform-as-a-Service that helps you build and manage the lifecycle of applications from initial push to scaling out. Often described as "the smallest PaaS implementation you've ever seen" and a self-hosted mini-Heroku, Dokku turns a single Linux host (or a multi-host scheduler such as K3s or Nomad) into a git-push deployment target that builds applications from Heroku-compatible buildpacks, Cloud Native Buildpacks, Nixpacks, Railpack, Dockerfiles, or pre-built Docker images. Dokku is MIT licensed, written primarily in Bash, and maintained by the Dokku organization on GitHub since 2013. It ships an extensive plugin ecosystem covering data stores (Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, Redis, MongoDB, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, Meilisearch, Typesense), TLS via Let's Encrypt, HTTP basic auth, maintenance mode, redirects, schedulers for Docker, K3s and Nomad, multiple HTTP proxies (Nginx, HAProxy, Caddy, Traefik, OpenResty), CI integrations, and an official GitHub Action. Dokku's primary interface is the `dokku` CLI invoked over SSH; there is no first-party public HTTP REST API in core (the historical `dokku-api` Ruby wrapper is archived and unmaintained).

providers.name: Edme Insurance Brokers
providers.description: Edme Insurance Brokers Ltd (formerly Aditya Birla Insurance Brokers, ABIBL) is an India-based composite insurance broker offering corporate, retail, and reinsurance solutions across 30+ industries including aviation, marine, energy, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, technology, and the BFSI and FMCG sectors. The company provides tailored risk management, employee benefits, and claims advisory services, backed by digital customer portals for policy and claims management and employee benefits. Edme is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Edme publishes no public developer program or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Envelop Risk
providers.description: Envelop Risk is a technology-led reinsurance underwriting and analytics firm specializing in cyber and other complex, emerging risks. The company combines actuarial science, machine learning, and cyber threat intelligence to model, price, and underwrite cyber (re)insurance for insurers, MGAs, and capital-market partners. Its platforms include CyberTooth (cyber risk modeling and augmented underwriting), Cyber Threat Intelligence, Envelop Capital Markets, and Envelop Risk Solutions (product development, analytics, modeling support). Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Envelop Risk surpassed a $1bn gross-written-premium milestone. This API Evangelist profile was created as a portfolio-company lead; the company does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Fannie Mae
providers.description: Fannie Mae, officially known as the Federal National Mortgage Association, is a government-sponsored enterprise that plays a critical role in the American housing market. Established in 1938, Fannie Mae operates as a secondary mortgage lender, purchasing mortgages from banks and other financial institutions. By buying these loans, Fannie Mae helps to provide liquidity to the mortgage market, enabling banks to lend more money to homebuyers. Fannie Mae operates a developer portal that hosts API integrations for mortgage industry partners; access typically requires authenticated business relationships.

providers.name: Fetch Robotics
providers.description: Fetch Robotics is a provider of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for the manufacturing, distribution, and fulfillment industries, enabling customers to optimize warehouse and material-handling workflows through robotic automation. Its Fetch and Freight robots are programmed through a ROS (Robot Operating System) interface — standard ROS topics, services, and actions conforming to ROS Enhancement Proposals (REPs) — rather than an HTTP/REST API, and the first-party client, driver, and simulation libraries are published as open source in the fetchrobotics GitHub organization. Fetch Robotics was acquired by Zebra Technologies in August 2021 for approximately $290M; fetchrobotics.com now redirects to Zebra and the autonomous-mobile-robot product line is being wound down (2025-2026), though the open-source ROS packages remain available.

providers.name: Fintary
providers.description: Fintary is an AI-powered commission management and revenue operations platform for insurance distribution — serving brokerages, carriers, and wealth firms. It automates compensation calculation and reporting across complex hierarchies, splits, overrides, and bonuses; reconciles carrier statement data; monitors chargebacks; surfaces real-time revenue and profitability analytics; and provides a white-label producer portal for 24/7 commission visibility. Fintary integrates with agency and distribution systems such as Applied Epic, Agency Integrator, SmartOffice, OneHQ, and BenefitPoint, and states it supports API connections to accounting, document management, and custom databases. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Fintary does not currently publish a public developer portal or API specification.

providers.name: Flex Pharma, Inc.
providers.description: Flex Pharma, Inc. entered the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio lead of bessemer-venture-partners. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 found no API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable surface of any kind. The flex-pharma.com domain now resolves (via Cloudflare) to a consumer online-pharmacy storefront retailing generic and brand erectile-dysfunction medication (tadalafil, sildenafil), whose About page invokes Rockefeller University professor Dr. Rod MacKinnon — a founder associated with the original Flex Pharma biotech — while publishing no corporate entity name, address, or registration details. Treat the present site as unverified and distinct from the original venture-backed company. Only Terms, Privacy, and a Contact page were verified as live; every /.well-known/ path soft-404s to the homepage.

providers.name: Frontlinewildfire
providers.description: Frontline Wildfire Defense is a wildfire protection company that designs, manufactures, and installs exterior sprinkler defense systems for homes, businesses, wineries, summer camps, and new-home communities. The system combines roof- and ground-mounted sprinklers, a pump, and water/foam concentrate with a mobile app (iOS and Android) that lets property owners remotely activate the system, monitor nearby wildfires on a live fire map, and receive evacuation alerts. The company also publishes wildfire risk maps, home-hardening and defensible-space guidance, and works through a network of partner installers. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This is a consumer/hardware company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: getriff
providers.description: Riff (getriff.co) is a voice and video workspace for remote and hybrid teams, backed by Balderton Capital. Its Mac and Windows desktop apps aim to reduce Slack overload and Zoom fatigue with a minimal video header, one-click availability-based chat, multi-screen sharing with drawing tools, advanced echo cancellation, and focus-time scheduling that updates status automatically, plus Google Calendar and Slack integrations. Riff ships as a consumer/team desktop product and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI; this API Evangelist profile captures its identity, legal, and domain-security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital.

providers.name: Go Rise
providers.description: Rise (gorise.co) is a Dubai-based fintech platform that gives migrant workers control over their finances across both their home and host countries. Through a mobile app for iOS and Android, Rise offers bank accounts, insurance, savings and investment options, "Pay Later" installment services, and remittance and money-transfer capabilities. The company partners with regulated financial institutions including United Arab Bank and insurance providers such as AXA Gulf, and is headquartered in DMCC, Jumeirah Lakes Towers, Dubai, UAE. Rise is a portfolio company of 500 Global and has raised funding led by MEVP. This is a consumer financial-services product with no public developer/API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Grapes
providers.description: Grape (Grape Protocol / GrapeDAO, built by Grape-Labs) is Solana-based decentralized infrastructure that gives online communities and DAOs a set of mainnet-ready primitives for identity, reputation, verification, access control, rewards, and governance. Its products include OG (Vine) Reputation Spaces for season-based on-chain reputation, Grape Verification for identity attestation, the Grape Access Protocol (GPASS) for token/credential-gated access, a GSPL DAO directory, a multi-chain Grape Wallet, and a suite of Discord automation bots. Grape ships no REST/OpenAPI surface; developers integrate through first-party TypeScript SDKs (npm) that wrap its Solana programs directly. Backed by Multicoin Capital, it was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gravity
providers.description: Gravity (Gravity Technologies) builds and deploys ultra-fast DC electric-vehicle charging infrastructure for dense urban environments. Its Distributed Energy Access Points (DEAPs) deliver up to five-minute charges from compact, modular hardware that requires minimal real estate and no dedicated utility upgrade, letting operators place high-power charging in garages, curbside, and fleet depots. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDKs at this time, so this profile captures company identity and the domain security surface rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Gyde
providers.description: Gyde is an AI-native health insurance brokerage, founded in 2025 and headquartered in Austin, Texas with an office in New York City. Gyde partners with established insurance agencies through acquisition, embedding AI-powered tools and operational support so brokers can guide clients through insurance, health, and wealth decisions at greater scale. Its products include Gia, an AI assistant that handles client outreach, scheduling, and questions over SMS and voice around the clock, and GydeOS, a broker operating system providing client summaries, conversation transcripts, campaign management, and an AI co-pilot. Gyde launched publicly in January 2026 with $60M in financing led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile tracks its identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hi Marley
providers.description: Hi Marley is an intelligent conversational platform built for the property and casualty (P&C) insurance industry, delivering carrier-to-policyholder communication over SMS. The platform connects carriers, policyholders, and service providers through a single messaging fabric to streamline claims — including Conversational FNOL (First Notice of Loss) intake, Total Loss Assist for auto claims, and Workflow Assist for property claims — layered with AI coaching, sentiment analysis, and data insights. Trusted by 130+ carriers, including four of the top ten U.S. insurers across auto, property, and workers compensation lines. Hi Marley is backed by Emergence Capital and True Ventures. No public developer platform, API documentation, or self-service onboarding was found; the product is delivered as a closed SaaS to insurance carriers.

providers.name: HODL Media
providers.description: HODL Media (hodl.mobi) is the maker of HODL Real-Time Cryptocurrency, a consumer mobile application for iOS and Android that tracks cryptocurrency and stock market prices in real time. The app aggregates pricing from 180+ global exchanges, offers customizable charting with technical indicators, price alerts and bracket management, portfolio tracking with exchange and wallet synchronization (Coinbase Pro, Binance, Ethereum wallets), aggregated news and social feeds, and stock market data from NYSE and NASDAQ. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile HODL Media publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic documentation; this repo is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead.

providers.name: HugeMed
providers.description: HugeMed (Shenzhen HugeMed Medical Technical Development Co., Ltd.) is a high-tech medical-device manufacturer founded in 2014 and headquartered in Shenzhen, China, specializing in airway management and endoscopic visualization equipment. Its product portfolio spans video laryngoscopes (blade, flexible, and stylet types for emergency, anesthesia, ICU, and educational use), single-use endoscopes for gynecology, ENT, gastroenterology, pulmonology, and urology, reusable ENT and urology endoscopes, and medical image processors. The company operates production facilities exceeding 60,000 square meters, employs roughly 600 people, and serves more than 10,000 medical institutions across 100+ countries. HugeMed is a hardware-first medical-device maker and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical integration surface; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and enriched with company identity and infrastructure probes.

providers.name: Improbable
providers.description: Improbable (Improbable Worlds Ltd) is a London-based technology company and venture builder. Founded in 2012, it originally built SpatialOS, a distributed simulation and networking platform for large-scale real-time multiplayer games, and later Morpheus / M² (MSquared), a network of interoperable metaverse worlds. Today Improbable operates primarily as a venture builder and capital allocator, partnering with founders to launch and scale companies across AI, Web3 and the metaverse. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its historical developer surface centered on the SpatialOS Platform SDK, Worker SDK and the `spatial` CLI (distributed via NuGet), plus the improbable-eng and spatialos GitHub organizations; the standalone documentation, status and IMS subdomains have since been retired as the company pivoted away from a standalone developer platform.

providers.name: ironSource
providers.description: ironSource is a Tel Aviv-based mobile game growth platform, acquired by Unity Technologies in a $4.4B all-stock deal that closed in November 2022 and is now operated as part of Unity's Grow Solutions group. The company builds an end-to-end suite for mobile game developers spanning ad monetization, user acquisition, and ad operations. Its flagship product LevelPlay is a unified in-app bidding and ad mediation platform that brokers Rewarded Video, Interstitial, and Banner ad demand across the ironSource Ads network, AdMob, AppLovin, Meta Audience Network, Pangle, Mintegral, Unity Ads, Vungle, and dozens of other ad sources. ironSource Ads is its self-serve ad network and user-acquisition platform offering CPI, CPE, ROAS-optimized, and SKAdNetwork-aware campaign management. Adjacent products include Aura (an on-device content marketplace for carriers and OEMs that originated from the 2021 Bigabid/Soomla portfolio and earlier hardware OEM deals), Tapjoy Offerwall (acquired 2022) for rewarded engagement, and Ad Quality for ad-content monitoring. Developer access is via a REST surface hosted at platform.ironsrc.com — including the Monetization Reporting API (v5/v4), ironSource Ads Reporting API, Application API (v6), Campaign API suite (Campaigns, Audiences, Country Groups, Bidding, Assets, Creatives), SKAN Reporting API, and Cost API — authenticated with Bearer tokens issued from the platform dashboard. Real client integration is delivered via native SDKs (iOS, Android, Unity, Flutter, React Native, Adobe AIR, Xamarin) plus the LevelPlay mediation adapter ecosystem published on github.com/ironsource-mobile. As of 2026 the developers.is.com knowledge center 301-redirects to docs.unity.com, consolidating ironSource documentation inside Unity Grow alongside Unity Ads. No public OpenAPI, Postman collection, or JSON Schema bundle is published by ironSource for the REST surface; documentation is human-readable HTML on docs.unity.com/en-us/grow.

providers.name: Jetty
providers.description: Jetty is a financial-services company built for the real estate industry, making renting more accessible and affordable for renters while helping property managers reduce risk and bad debt. Following its merger with Rhino, Jetty operates across more than 6 million rental units in the United States and offers three core products: Jetty Deposit, a security-deposit replacement that swaps large cash deposits for a low monthly or one-time payment; Jetty Protect, integrated renters insurance and liability coverage; and Jetty Credit, a rent-reporting and credit-building service that helps renters establish credit history while lowering delinquencies for property managers. Jetty is backed by Ribbit Capital. No public developer/API surface is currently published; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: MedeAnalytics (JLL Partners)
providers.description: MedeAnalytics is a healthcare data and analytics company serving health insurance payers and risk-bearing provider organizations, positioning itself as a healthcare performance improvement company that turns claims, clinical, and operational data into actionable insight and measurable financial and quality results. Its platform spans Health Fabric, an AI-powered healthcare data fabric; AI Studio for ready-to-use and custom predictive models; Managed Action for workflow automation; and Integrated Analytics modules with embedded ROI tracking. Solution areas include MLR optimization, HEDIS/Stars quality performance, utilization and network management, value-based care, revenue cycle, population health, and social determinants of health (SDOH). The company was surfaced from a VC portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Menlo Security
providers.description: Menlo Security provides a cloud-delivered Browser Security Platform that protects enterprises and their AI agents at the browser session layer, where most modern attacks and data loss occur. Its core capabilities include pre-render threat prevention using multimodal visual and DOM analysis, patented Positive Selection file security that reconstructs documents to strip malware and macros, AI Adaptive DLP for real-time detection and masking of PII/PHI and financial data, invisible browser isolation for high-risk activity, and Menlo Secure Application Access for identity-based zero-trust access to SaaS, legacy, and private applications for both human users and autonomous agents. The platform integrates with existing SASE/SSE, EDR/EPP, and SOC tooling through a single unified control plane. Menlo Security is privately held and backed by investors including General Catalyst. The company operates primarily as an enterprise security vendor and does not publish a public developer API program; administrative and reporting APIs are available to customers through the authenticated admin console.

providers.name: Noteworthy AI
providers.description: Noteworthy AI is a Techstars-backed company delivering AI-powered grid inspection for electric utilities. Its Noteworthy Inspect product mounts smart cameras on utility fleet vehicles and applies computer-vision and machine-learning analytics to automatically identify pole defects, inventory grid components, and assess distribution-infrastructure conditions during routine operations, without dedicated inspection crews. Use cases span asset inventory and inspection, lighting audits, storm-damage assessment, vegetation management, and joint-use equipment tracking, helping utilities cut inspection operating costs while improving grid reliability and safety. Customers include FirstEnergy, NextEra Energy, Exelon, Xcel Energy, Alabama Power, and Georgia Power; technology partners include NVIDIA, Dell Technologies, Esri, and EPRI. Noteworthy AI is SOC 2 Type II compliant. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Novig
providers.description: Novig is a peer-to-peer sports prediction and trading platform marketed as "America's #1 Sports Trading App," operating as a betting exchange rather than a traditional sportsbook. Users can set their own odds or accept existing lines across two modes: free-to-play with Novig Coins and real-money trading with Novig Cash. The consumer product is delivered as iOS and Android apps and is available in 35+ U.S. states. Backed by Forerunner Ventures, Multicoin Capital, and Pantera Capital. As of this enrichment pass Novig exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: Nuevo Método
providers.description: Nuevo Método (NUME) is an international digital-health and corporate-wellness platform, headquartered in Mexico City and operating across 17 countries in Latin America and Europe. It helps insurers and enterprises deliver personalized wellbeing benefits to employees, customers, and their families across three pillars: mental health (psychology sessions, mindfulness, meditation, sleep tracking), physical health (24/7 virtual medical consultations, fertility guidance, menstrual-cycle tracking, health workshops), and lifestyle (personal-finance courses, financial advisory, and inspirational talks). The company runs a fully remote workforce and reports measurable client outcomes such as improved sleep, productivity, and employee retention. Founded and led by Dr. Ingrid Briggiler (CEO). No public API or developer portal is currently published; this profile captures the company's identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Oasis
providers.description: Oasis Security is a Non-Human Identity (NHI) management and security platform for hybrid and multi-cloud environments. Its Agentic Access Management (AAM) offering discovers, inventories, governs, and secures service accounts, service principals, managed identities, API keys, secrets, and AI agent credentials across AWS, Azure, GCP, Okta, HashiCorp, Snowflake, GitHub, Salesforce, and AI services such as OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock. The platform provides automated discovery and risk assessment, ownership and context mapping, posture management, threat detection and anomaly monitoring, policy-driven governance and remediation, time-bound provisioning, and secure secret rotation. Founded in New York and backed by Sequoia Capital, Accel, Cyberstarts, and Maple Venture Capital, Oasis extends zero-trust and PAM practices to the fast-growing population of non-human and agentic identities.

providers.name: Omnius
providers.description: omni:us (operated by Qidenus Group GmbH, Berlin) is an insurance technology company building agentic AI for claims processing. Its platform automates end-to-end claims handling — from first notice of loss to settlement — across property, casualty, and marine lines, combining document intake, machine reading of structured and unstructured text, images and handwriting, and decision support trained on millions of annotated claims and insurance documents. Products include No-Touch Claim Automation, an Agentic Co-Pilot for complex claim decisions, Leakage Reduction, and a custom Insurance AI Modeller. omni:us was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company markets an enterprise B2B product sold direct to carriers; it publishes a public marketing site, blog, and legal terms, but exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Ooda Health
providers.description: OODA Health is a healthcare technology company modernizing the business of healthcare by automating administration and payments between payers, providers, and patients. Its flagship platform, OODAPay, coordinates billing across all parties to give patients a single consolidated bill while reducing provider administrative burden and bad debt; OODA Optic extends its analytics and administrative tooling. OODA Health worked with payers and health systems including Anthem, CommonSpirit Health, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts and Arizona, Blue Shield of California, and Hill Physicians Medical Group, and was acquired by Cedar. The company was backed by Threshold Ventures. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface has been identified.

providers.name: OpenX
providers.description: OpenX is an independent supply-side platform (SSP) and programmatic ad exchange headquartered in Pasadena, California, founded in 2008. OpenX connects publishers and app developers to advertiser demand through a real-time marketplace that runs OpenRTB-based auctions across display, video, CTV, native, and mobile inventory. Its product suite is organized around the OpenX Exchange (the core marketplace), OpenXSelect (curation, deal creation, and supply-path targeting), OpenXBuild (a software toolkit for assembling custom supply-side workflows and real-time bidstream integrations), and OpenXControl (publisher yield management and demand routing). OpenX exposes several developer-facing APIs documented at docs.openx.com — an OpenRTB API for DSP bidding integrations, a Platform API for account, inventory, demand, targeting, and deal management, a Reporting API for analytics and performance metrics, an OpenXSelect GraphQL API for managing audiences/deals/inventory lists, and an OpenXBuild Real-Time Bidstream API — but the references are gated behind OAuth and OpenX does not publish a public OpenAPI specification or Postman collection. The company is a major contributor to the Prebid.org header-bidding ecosystem (Prebid.js and Prebid Server) and maintains a large GitHub organization with OAuth-based API client libraries in Python, PHP, Java, Perl, and Ruby for the legacy OX3 API. OpenX's business model is transaction-fee based — it takes a share of each ad impression cleared through its exchange — and access to the developer APIs requires an active OpenX account and BD/account-management onboarding rather than self-service signup.

providers.name: Packhelp
providers.description: Packhelp is a European custom and wholesale packaging platform that lets businesses design, order, and warehouse branded packaging — boxes, mailers, bags, tubes, and accessories — through online design tools and a curated catalog of EU-based producers. Packhelp also markets "the first-ever API for packaging," a sales-gated set of web services that let 3PL, fulfillment, marketplace, logistics, and food-delivery platforms embed packaging quoting, ordering, and a drag-and-drop packaging editor directly into their own applications and whitelabel storefronts.

providers.name: Policybazaar
providers.description: Policybazaar is India's largest online insurance aggregator and digital marketplace, operated by PB Fintech Ltd. It lets consumers compare, buy and manage insurance across health, term life, motor, travel, investment and corporate lines from a wide panel of insurers, providing quotes, policy issuance, renewals, claims assistance and advisory. Surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Policybazaar publishes a consumer-facing web and mobile marketplace but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface (no developer/API subdomain, no /.well-known documents, no llms.txt).

providers.name: Prodigy Education
providers.description: Prodigy Education is a Canadian K-8 game-based learning company best known for Prodigy Math and Prodigy English — fantasy RPG-style products in which students battle and quest by answering curriculum-aligned questions. The product is free for teachers and is monetized through optional parent memberships. Prodigy is consumer- and classroom-facing with no public developer API or partner program. Its integration surface is school rostering and SSO: Clever (SSO + Secure Sync district rostering), ClassLink (SSO, with OneRoster district rostering rolling out), and Google (SSO + Google Classroom assignment creation).

providers.name: RADNET
providers.description: RadNet, Inc. (NASDAQ: RDNT) is the largest provider of freestanding, fixed-site outpatient diagnostic imaging services in the United States, operating roughly 440 imaging centers offering MRI, CT, PET/CT, ultrasound, mammography, and other modalities. Beyond its clinical network, RadNet runs a health-technology business spanning eRAD (web-based, cloud imaging workflow, PACS and RIS solutions) and DeepHealth, its AI and digital-health division whose cloud-native "DeepHealth OS" unifies enterprise imaging (Diagnostic Suite, Operations Suite, TechLive) with AI-powered population-health screening for breast, lung, prostate, neuro, and thyroid imaging. RadNet was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. RadNet does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its technology is delivered as enterprise imaging platforms and AI products through eRAD and DeepHealth.

providers.name: RealNetworks
providers.description: RealNetworks is a Seattle-based technology company that pairs AI-powered computer-vision and secure-communication products with its long-running consumer media brands. Its portfolio includes SAFR (facial recognition for security and retail loss prevention), Kontxt (AI messaging and voice security for CPaaS platforms, Telcos, and MNOs), GameHouse (cross-device casual gaming), and RealPlayer (media playback). Product APIs for SAFR and Kontxt are delivered through authenticated partner portals rather than an open developer portal; the historical Real Developer Program (developer.real.com) is no longer live, and no public OpenAPI specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Reliance Health
providers.description: Reliance Health (formerly RelianceHMO) is a healthtech company making quality healthcare accessible and affordable across emerging markets, with operations centered in Nigeria and expanding across Africa and the Middle East. It offers employer-sponsored and individual health plans covering preventative, emergency, and chronic care, telemedicine and doctor consultations through its mobile app, and a network of 3,800+ healthcare partners (hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, and diagnostic centers). Reliance Health combines insurance, its own clinics, and technology to deliver an end-to-end care experience for businesses and their employees. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; the reliancehmo.com application backend (api.reliancehmo.com) is an internal web-app origin, not a documented public API.

providers.name: Reposit
providers.description: Reposit is a UK-based PropTech and fintech company offering a deposit alternative for the residential rental market. Instead of paying a traditional cash deposit, tenants pay a one-time, non-refundable fee (typically one week's rent) for insurance-backed cover, while landlords and letting agents receive protection worth up to eight weeks' rent. The FCA-authorised product is underwritten by a leading insurer and serves letting agents, build-to-rent (BTR) operators, landlords and tenants, with integrations into common property management tools. This profile was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Reposit publishes no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Roost
providers.description: Roost is a Sunnyvale, California home-telematics company that helps property and casualty insurance carriers modernize homeowners and commercial insurance with smart, in-home sensors and monitoring. Its Protection360 commercial loss-prevention service and Security360 white-label home-security bundle detect water leaks, extreme temperatures, and smoke-alarm events, delivering real-time alerts and risk data to insurers, property owners, and third parties. Roost partners with dozens of top P&C carriers, but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; integrations are arranged directly with its engineering team.

providers.name: Shriram Finance
providers.description: Shriram Finance Limited is one of India's largest retail non-banking financial companies (NBFC), with roughly Rs 3.02 lakh crore in assets under management and 3,225 branches nationwide. It offers commercial-vehicle, two-wheeler, used-car, personal, business and gold loans, fixed deposits and fixed investment plans, general and life insurance distribution, Bharat BillPay (BBPS) bill payments, and UPI through its Shriram One app. The company runs consumer web and mobile products but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; a partner portal and a lending-service-provider program serve authorized business partners only.

providers.name: Stride Health
providers.description: Stride Health is a benefits platform that helps independent, gig, and part-time workers access portable benefits that stay with the individual regardless of where or how they work. Stride connects people to affordable health, dental, vision, and life insurance, and provides tax tools, mileage/expense tracking, and savings features for the self-employed. The company reports 4.6 million independent workers served, $8+ billion saved on insurance and taxes, and 130+ partner companies. Stride operates a private B2B partner integration (embedded in partner apps such as gig-work platforms) but publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Stylight
providers.description: Stylight is an online fashion and home-decor shopping aggregator that curates and compares products from more than 100 retailers, letting shoppers browse women's and men's apparel, footwear, accessories, beauty and home furnishings across many brands in one place and then complete the purchase on the partner retailer's own store. The platform operates localized sites across the US, UK, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy, Spain, Belgium, the Netherlands and Canada, runs an editorial style magazine, and monetizes through affiliate partnerships with the retailers it links to. HV Capital was an early backer. Stylight publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, legal and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Superscript
providers.description: Superscript is a UK- and Netherlands-based business insurance provider offering flexible, subscription-based cover for small and growing businesses, sole traders, landlords, and larger enterprises. Its product range spans public and employers' liability, professional indemnity, cyber insurance, landlord insurance, and industry-specific policies, sold direct and through a broker channel. Superscript was surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface; this profile captures its public web identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: SXD
providers.description: SXD is a New York-based design-technology company founded in 2022 that uses patented artificial intelligence to generate zero-waste apparel patterns for the fashion industry. Its SXD AI platform transforms a sketch or design concept into production-ready patterns that eliminate fabric waste before the first cut, and the company reports up to 69% material savings across more than 35 brand and manufacturing partners. SXD has been recognized with the Global Change Award and a top prize at the SXSW Pitch competition, and is backed by Initialized Capital. SXD does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: TikTok Shop API
providers.description: TikTok Shop is TikTok's integrated e-commerce platform that lets sellers, creators, and partners list products, manage inventory and fulfillment, and sell directly within TikTok's live streams, short videos, and shop tabs. The TikTok Shop Open API (open-api.tiktokglobalshop.com) is a RESTful API that uses OAuth 2.0 authentication and enables developers to programmatically manage products, orders, fulfillment, returns, finance, promotions, and seller authorization across TikTok Shop's global marketplaces.

providers.name: truBrain
providers.description: truBrain is a Santa Monica, California nootropics and functional-beverage brand that makes "natural superfuels for performance" — drinkable nootropic shots (2,000mg of natural nootropics per 1oz bottle for focus and motivation), drinkable ketones (Ketone XL, 11g of pure ketones per shot for athletic energy and recovery), plus gummies, functional-mushroom blends, capsules, NAD+, hydration, and sleep supplements, packaged in recycled paper bottles. Founded by a team of neuroscientists and backed by 500 Global, the company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront and has run a Regulation A+ public equity offering. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. truBrain is a consumer packaged-goods company: it publishes no first-party developer API, documentation, or SDKs. The only machine-readable surface at its domain is Shopify's Customer Accounts OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 discovery metadata.

providers.name: Wellxai
providers.description: Wellx (Wellxai) is a Dubai-based health insurtech company that transforms health insurance from reactive to proactive through AI-driven behavior change. Its consumer mobile app pairs behavioral science and gamification with wearable integrations (Fitbit, Apple Watch, Whoop) so members earn xCoins rewards by hitting health goals, step and sleep challenges, and wellness programs, then redeem them with marketplace partners. Wellx also sells to corporates and SMEs and partners with brokers and insurers, positioning healthier behavior as the driver of better-value health insurance. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company exposes consumer iOS/Android apps backed by a private API but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Wisk Aero
providers.description: Wisk Aero is an autonomous, all-electric eVTOL air taxi developer and a wholly-owned subsidiary of The Boeing Company. Wisk is developing its Generation 6 aircraft, a four-passenger self-flying eVTOL designed to operate under human supervisor oversight from a multi-vehicle supervision center, pursuing certification under three FAA programs: Type Certification, Production Certification, and Operation Certification. Wisk evolved from earlier Kitty Hawk programs and has logged over 1,750 autonomous test flights across five aircraft generations since 2010. Announced launch communities include Houston, Texas and Brisbane, Australia (in support of the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games). In March 2026 Wisk was selected by the White House to help lead the safe U.S. introduction of autonomous air taxi flight. Wisk is hardware- and operations-focused, with no public consumer or developer APIs.

providers.name: Zapia
providers.description: Zapia is a personal AI assistant built for Latin America by BrainLogic AI (a Uruguay/Silicon Valley startup), delivered inside WhatsApp and as native Android and iOS apps plus a Flutter web app at app.zapia.com. It engages consumers in hyper-localized, natural-language conversations to compare prices, reply to and transcribe WhatsApp messages and voice notes, organize calendars (with Google Calendar sync), make reservations, and discover nearby businesses using BrainLogic's database of millions of Latin American business WhatsApp numbers. Zapia runs on Claude via Google Cloud Vertex AI and has surpassed 5.5 million users across the region, backed by seed funding led by Prosus Ventures. It is a consumer (B2C) product: as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal — this profile captures its public identity and consumer-facing surfaces.

providers.name: Abercrombie and Fitch
providers.description: Abercrombie & Fitch is a global specialty retailer of casual apparel, accessories, and personal care products operating multiple lifestyle brands including Abercrombie, Hollister, and Gilly Hicks. The company operates through a direct-to-consumer model with both e-commerce and physical retail stores across global markets.

providers.name: Adimab
providers.description: Adimab is a private biotechnology company founded in 2007, headquartered in Lebanon, New Hampshire, with a west coast office in Mountain View, California. It operates a proprietary yeast-based antibody discovery and engineering platform that combines fully human synthetic and immune libraries to generate specific, stable and developable IgGs, heavy-chain antibodies (HCAbs), multispecifics, T-cell engagers and T-cell receptors. Adimab deliberately runs no internal therapeutic pipeline, instead partnering with biopharma companies through funded discovery programs, platform transfer and non-exclusive program deals. The company reports more than 140 industry partnerships since 2009, 675+ therapeutic programs initiated, 90+ clinical programs and 6 commercial products. Adimab publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; its capabilities are delivered as laboratory discovery services and licensed platform transfer under partnership agreements.

providers.name: Arctic Health
providers.description: Arctic Health provides AI-native provider credentialing and payer enrollment for healthcare organizations, handling the workflow end to end — from CAQH management and primary source verification to payer applications, contracting, and ongoing follow-up. The company collects and validates organization and provider data to each state and payer's requirements, submits on the organization's behalf across hundreds of payer portals, and monitors status and compliance on an ongoing basis. It serves medical practices, telehealth groups, RCM companies, and CVOs across all 50 states plus DC, offering both standard and white-label ("For Scale") solutions with AI-powered document extraction and error detection. Arctic Health is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company based in New York City, also backed by Menlo Ventures and Fortitude Ventures.

providers.name: Argus Software
providers.description: Argus Software (ARGUS) is a commercial real estate software provider whose products are the industry standard for cash-flow modeling, valuation, asset and investment management, and development-project appraisal for owners, investors, lenders, and advisors. Founded in Houston, Texas and acquired by Altus Group in 2011, the ARGUS product line is now delivered through Altus Group as the ARGUS Intelligence platform and includes ARGUS Enterprise, ARGUS EstateMaster, ARGUS Developer, ARGUS Taliance, ARGUS ValueInsight, ARGUS Voyanta, and Forbury. ARGUS software is used across the global commercial real estate industry to underwrite acquisitions, perform discounted cash-flow analysis, run portfolio and fund analytics, and standardize valuations. As of this enrichment pass ARGUS exposes no public developer portal, OpenAPI description, or self-service API program; its cloud platform is accessed through the Altus Platform / ARGUS Cloud portal.

providers.name: Ball Corporation
providers.description: Ball Corporation is a global supplier of sustainable aluminum packaging for beverage, food, personal care, and household products, as well as aerospace and other technologies and services for commercial and government customers. Ball operates more than 80 manufacturing plants worldwide and is a leader in aluminum can sustainability and recycling.

providers.name: Clinikk
providers.description: Clinikk (Clinikk Health Hub) is a Bangalore, India-based primary healthcare provider offering membership-based access to unlimited doctor consultations, free prescribed medicines and lab tests, 24/7 teleconsultation, and optional group health insurance in partnership with IndusInd General Insurance. Clinikk operates in-person Health Hubs across Bangalore alongside a consumer mobile app, and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Gesund
providers.description: Gesund.ai is a governance and validation platform for regulated clinical AI, providing infrastructure to build, validate, deploy, monitor, and update medical AI models across regulatory jurisdictions and stakeholders. Its offerings include an AI CRO (contract research organization) delivering independent validation studies for medical AI models, an AI Factory to accelerate in-house model R&D cycles, and a free Validation Hub for testing models against real-world clinical data. Backed by 500 Global and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company focuses on inspection-ready evidence and FDA/QMSR-aligned regulatory compliance for clinical AI teams. The platform is delivered through a hosted web application and currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Homeward Health
providers.description: Homeward Health is a value-based healthcare provider founded in 2022 by former Livongo executives (CEO Dr. Jennifer Schneider) and incubated as the first investment in General Catalyst's Creation fund. Homeward is rearchitecting rural healthcare for the roughly 60 million Americans living in rural communities, taking on full financial risk for the total cost of care of Medicare Advantage members. Its hybrid care model combines telehealth visits over cellular networks, in-home remote patient monitoring, and in-person care delivered through mobile care units, in partnership with regional health plans (e.g. Priority Health), local providers, and community organizations. Homeward is a care-delivery and health-plan-partnership company rather than a developer platform; it publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK.

providers.name: Indio Technologies
providers.description: Indio Technologies is a cloud-based insurance application and submissions platform for commercial insurance agencies and brokers, acquired by and now part of Applied Systems. Indio replaces manual PDF forms and spreadsheets with a library of 10,000+ digitally enhanced "smart" insurance forms and ACORD applications, a submission workspace that packages digital applications, schedule workbooks, document-upload requests and e-signature requests, plus secure document sharing. Indio does not publish a self-service public developer API. Programmatic access is partner/carrier-gated and delivered through Applied Systems - the Applied Epic bi-directional integration and SDK, the IVANS data exchange API (used to move submission and proposal data between agencies, brokers and carriers), and the Applied DevCenter partner developer program. The API surfaces below are modeled from Indio's documented product concepts (submissions, forms/applications, clients, documents and e-signatures); they are logical groupings, not publicly documented endpoints (endpointsModeled).

providers.name: Jupiter Money
providers.description: Jupiter Money is a Bengaluru-based Indian digital banking app (neobank) operated by Amica Financial Technologies Private Limited. Founded in 2019 by Jitendra Gupta, Jupiter delivers a consumer "money app" experience that bundles savings and salary accounts, UPI payments, co-branded credit cards, personal loans, mutual funds, digital gold, fixed and recurring deposits, insurance, and a Jewels rewards program into a single mobile application. Jupiter is itself not a bank — it operates as a fintech marketplace and Loan Service Provider on top of regulated partners. Federal Bank is the primary banking partner for savings, salary, and deposit products, with CSB Bank powering the Edge+ and Edge RuPay credit cards and Federal Bank the Edge Federal VISA card. Lending is provided through partners including Amica Finance Private Limited and Kisetsu Saison Finance, with mutual funds through AIAPL and digital gold through MMTC-PAMP. The product is consumer facing and distributed via the Android and iOS apps; Jupiter does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal. All integrations with banks, NBFCs, NPCI/UPI rails, card networks, and depositories are private business-to-business arrangements rather than an open API program.

providers.name: KWI
providers.description: KWI is a retail technology company founded in 1985 and headquartered in Melville, New York, that delivers a cloud-based, unified commerce platform for specialty and department retailers. The platform combines an iOS mobile point-of-sale, merchandising and inventory optimization, order management with buy-anywhere / fulfill-from-anywhere fulfillment, CRM, clienteling and loyalty, the Snapshot real-time sales analytics application, and AI product image search, all operated as a SaaS managed service with helpdesk, hardware, and payments support. KWI describes an API layer in its platform architecture used to export data to third-party systems and channels --- CRMs, ERPs, SRPs, and supply chains --- alongside packaged connectors such as Shopify Connect and a Klaviyo connector. As of this profile KWI publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, or SDKs; integration is delivered through its professional-services organization under customer contract.

providers.name: Latus Bio
providers.description: Latus Bio is a clinical-stage gene therapy company engineering novel adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids to deliver genetic medicines to precise cell types in the central nervous system and peripheral tissues. The company screens tens of millions of novel capsid variants to build a proprietary database of tissue-targeting "delivery zip codes," pairing engineered capsids with optimized routes of administration so therapeutics reach the intended tissue at a fraction of conventional doses and with minimal off-tissue biodistribution. Its lead programs are LTS-201 for Huntington's disease (AAV.DB-3 capsid) and LTS-101 for CLN2 disease, spanning CNS and ocular delivery (AAV.Ep+ capsid). Latus Bio operates offices and laboratories in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania and in Boston's Seaport district, and is backed by DCVC Bio, 8VC, BioAdvance, Samsung Venture Investment, and KDB. Latus Bio is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company; it publishes no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs
providers.description: Marcus by Goldman Sachs is the U.S. consumer banking brand of The Goldman Sachs Group, launched in 2016 to offer no-fee high-yield Online Savings Accounts and Certificates of Deposit (CDs) directly to retail customers online. Deposits are held at Goldman Sachs Bank USA, a New York State-chartered bank and member of the Federal Reserve System, insured by the FDIC. After Goldman's broad retreat from consumer lending, Marcus no longer originates personal loans and now centers on digital deposit products. Marcus operates NO public first-party consumer developer API and runs no self-serve developer portal for its retail banking products; the Goldman Sachs Developer platform (developer.gs.com) serves institutional Transaction Banking and Marquee offerings, not Marcus consumer banking. Consumer-permissioned account data (balances, transactions, account/holder info) is reachable only through third-party open-finance aggregators such as Plaid, Flinks, and MX, not a documented Marcus API. As a bank chartered in the U.S., Goldman Sachs Bank USA is subject to the emerging CFPB Section 1033 personal financial data rights framework, but no first-party FDX-conformant Marcus developer interface is publicly documented as of this record.

providers.name: Morpheus Space
providers.description: Morpheus Space is an in-space mobility company building electric propulsion systems and mission-design software for the New Space economy. Founded in 2018 out of the Technical University of Dresden, its second-generation GO-2 system uses FEEP (Field Emission Electric Propulsion) technology to deliver continuous, chemical-free thrust for satellite constellation deployment, station keeping, collision avoidance, repositioning, and deorbiting.
