Its flagship product, EASO, is described as the world's first fully autonomous robot for hospital medication logistics: it streamlines supply distribution, restocks medication dispensing cabinets, and retrieves medications from pharmacy storage to reduce errors and free clinical staff to focus on patient care. The technology combines vision-language-action (VLA) models with geometric planning, and Emancro is piloting EASO with leading U.S. hospitals. The company is backed by Amplify Partners. Emancro is a physical-robotics and healthcare-AI company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Entyre Care
providers.description: Entyre Care is a US home health care provider that helps people who care for a friend or family member at home get paid for the care they already provide. Through state Medicaid structured / self-directed family caregiving programs, Entyre Care guides caregivers through eligibility and enrollment, handles the paperwork, and delivers financial compensation alongside professional caregiving guidance and emotional support. The company operates in Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Hampshire, Ohio, Virginia, and Wisconsin, offering tools such as a compensation calculator, a step-by-step guide to getting paid, and localized care teams. Entyre Care is a consumer-facing healthcare services business and does not currently publish a public developer program or API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and enriched with the company's real identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Enveda
providers.description: Enveda is a Boulder, Colorado based drug discovery company that combines artificial intelligence with the chemistry of nature to accelerate the development of new medicines. Its platform mines the vast chemical diversity of plants and other natural sources, using machine learning to decode complex natural compounds, identify their chemical structures and biological activity, and surface novel drug candidates faster than traditional approaches. Enveda was surfaced as a portfolio company of True Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a private biotechnology and drug discovery firm it publishes a corporate and scientific web presence rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, security posture, and web properties.

providers.name: Erasca
providers.description: Erasca is a clinical-stage precision oncology company (NASDAQ: ERAS) headquartered in San Diego, California, whose name is its mission: to erase cancer. The company is singularly focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing therapies for RAS- and MAPK pathway-driven cancers. RAS is the most frequently mutated oncogene and the MAPK pathway one of the most frequently altered signaling pathways in cancer, together accounting for roughly five million newly diagnosed patients globally each year. Erasca pursues three complementary therapeutic strategies intended to comprehensively shut down the RAS/MAPK pathway by targeting multiple nodes and cooperative mechanisms in parallel. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio-linked lead; as a therapeutics company Erasca publishes a corporate and investor web presence rather than a developer API surface, so this record captures verified company identity, legal, and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Ergatta
providers.description: Ergatta is a connected-fitness company that makes game-based home rowing machines, pairing WaterRower-derived water-resistance hardware handcrafted in Rhode Island with a gamified software platform of interactive challenges (Endeavor, Meteor, Wavelength), live and on-demand races, scenic rows, coached classes, and custom workouts. Ergatta sells the Luxe and Lite rowers plus upgrade kits for existing WaterRower and Concept2 machines, delivered through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront with a membership subscription. Ergatta does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web surface and identity for network discovery.

providers.name: Escient Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Escient Pharmaceuticals is a San Diego, California clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class, oral small-molecule therapeutics targeting Mas-related G protein-coupled receptors (MRGPRs) along the neurosensory-inflammatory axis. Its lead programs are EP262, an MRGPRX2 antagonist for mast-cell-mediated diseases such as chronic spontaneous and inducible urticaria and atopic dermatitis, and EP547, an MRGPRX4 antagonist for cholestatic and uremic pruritus. The company was backed by New Enterprise Associates (NEA) and was acquired by Incyte Corporation on May 30, 2024. Escient operates a corporate marketing website only and publishes no public API, developer program, or machine-readable API specification; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Expert Intelligence
providers.description: Expert Intelligence is an AI company building analytical automation for pharmaceutical drug-development laboratories. Its platform turns raw instrument data into signed, regulatory-grade results and surfaces lab-wide trends across instruments, methods, and sites. Two integrated products anchor the offering: EI Flow automates batch analysis by converting instrument output into SOP-aware, signed, explainable results that reach LIMS systems in minutes so analysts review only exceptions, and EI Signal unifies historical data across instruments, methods, and sites to surface drift and anomalies before release. The company promotes exception-based review for higher accuracy, a Limited Sample Model (LSM) approach that needs only 30-50 expert examples, and instrument-agnostic deployment across cloud, on-premises, or hybrid environments. Backed by Sierra Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio and enriched from the company's public website; no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Fabric
providers.description: Fabric is a healthcare care-enablement platform (formerly Zipnosis, rebranded to Fabric in 2024) that streamlines access to virtual and in-person care. Its AI-powered system automates patient intake, symptom gathering, triage, and routing while integrating with existing EMR systems, serving health systems, hospitals, health plans, employers, and brokers. The platform spans synchronous and asynchronous virtual care delivery, an AI navigation and symptom-checking assistant, an intelligent provider directory and scheduling layer, a 50-state virtual clinical network (Evo), and patient engagement and care-management pathways. Fabric was assembled through the acquisitions of Zipnosis, GYANT, MeMD, TeamHealth Virtual Care, and UCM Digital Health. As of this profile Fabric does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; integration is EMR-based and arranged via sales.

providers.name: Feel Therapeutics
providers.description: Feel Therapeutics, an IQVIA business, is a Digital Precision Medicine company on a mission to reinvent how mental health is diagnosed, managed and cared for by bringing objective data, continuous passive measurement and novel digital biomarkers into mental healthcare. Rather than relying on episodic, subjective self-reported questionnaires, Feel develops digital biomarkers from wearable and passive sensor data to enable continuous, objective monitoring. Its solutions span the Feel Digital Precision Medicine Platform (DPMP), Feel DTx precision digital therapeutics, drug-plus / beyond-the-pill programs, and a wearable monitoring device. The company partners with pharma and biotech to advance clinical development, real-world evidence (RWE), and commercialization strategies, and has run 20+ research studies with 3000+ participants.

providers.name: FiberSense
providers.description: FiberSense is a distributed fiber optic sensing (DFOS / distributed acoustic sensing) company that turns existing and purpose-built fiber optic cables into dense arrays of vibration and acoustic sensors for real-time detection, localization and classification of objects and events across critical infrastructure. Its AI/ML algorithms filter noise and false alarms in dense urban, marine and underground environments, delivered as a subscription-based sensing platform rather than a public developer API. Product lines include DigitalAsset (critical infrastructure asset protection), DigitalCity (urban infrastructure and utility monitoring), DigitalMarine (subsea and marine cable route monitoring) and DigitalLeak (pipeline leak detection). Backed by Prosus Ventures; customer support runs through an Atlassian service desk portal.

providers.name: FloatMe
providers.description: FloatMe is a US fintech app offering interest-free cash advances ("Floats") to help members bridge income gaps between paychecks — new eligible members can request up to $50 and existing members up to $100, with no credit check and no reporting to credit bureaus. Beyond advances, FloatMe provides spending tracking and insights, low-balance alerts to help avoid overdraft fees, income and cash-flow forecasting, and an exclusive marketplace of deals on everyday essentials. The service runs on a $4.99/month membership, with optional instant-transfer fees. FloatMe operates a consumer mobile app and website; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Forta (fka Montera)
providers.description: Forta Health (formerly Montera, Inc.) is a San Francisco based digital health company making Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapy accessible to families of children with autism spectrum disorder. Forta connects families with board-certified behavior analysts (BCBAs) and registered behavior technicians (RBTs) for evidence-based care delivered virtually across 43 states and in-home in select cities, with active parent involvement, no waitlists, and Medicaid and insurance accepted. Backed by Insight Partners, the company raised a $55M Series A. It operates a consumer-facing healthcare service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Freenome
providers.description: Freenome is an early cancer detection company founded in 2014 that develops blood-based screening tests to catch cancer in its earliest, most treatable stages. It combines multiomics laboratory science with artificial intelligence and machine learning to read multiple biological signals from a single blood draw, an approach it calls Personalized Cancer Detection. Its SimpleScreen portfolio includes tests for colorectal and lung cancer, validated through clinical research programs such as the PREEMPT CRC study. Freenome is a clinical diagnostics and life-sciences company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead (backed by a16z, CRV, DCVC, and GV) and enriched with the public identity, legal, and domain-security signals available from its website.

providers.name: Frontage Laboratories
providers.description: Frontage Laboratories is a global contract research organization (CRO) providing integrated, science-driven drug discovery and development services across the pharmaceutical and biotechnology lifecycle. Its services span drug discovery (chemistry, biology, ADME/toxicology screening, pharmacology), drug development (DMPK, preclinical safety and toxicology, clinical trial support), laboratory testing (bioanalysis, genomics, central lab, biomarkers), CMC (product development, formulation, analytical services, manufacturing), and agrochemical support. Frontage operates roughly 28 sites across North America, Asia-Pacific, and Europe with about 2,200 employees. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Frontage publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or programmatic integration surface, so this profile captures company identity and web properties only.

providers.name: Fy
providers.description: Fy! (iamfy.co) is an online marketplace for wall art and home decor, curating canvas prints, framed prints, gallery wall sets, and handmade UK-manufactured frames from a community of independent artists. The storefront runs on Shopify and offers an AI-powered "Advisor" tool for personalized wall-design recommendations, an art-for-business program, and an artists hub for creators. Fy was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no first-party developer API; the only machine-readable surface reachable on the domain is the Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth discovery served by the platform.

providers.name: Guide Labs
providers.description: Guide Labs is a product-focused AI research company building a new class of inherently interpretable AI systems and foundation models that humans and domain experts can reliably understand, steer, and debug. Its flagship platform, Clarity, is presented as the first inherently interpretable AI platform and surfaces the internal concepts driving a model's decisions, while its Steerling-8B is presented as the first inherently interpretable large language model. The team has published more than two dozen interpretability papers at top machine-learning venues and ships research artifacts such as PRISM training-data prototypes, the FineWeb Concept Atlas, and Atlas for orienting LLM pre-training data. Access to Clarity is available through platform.guidelabs.ai. The company is backed by Initialized Capital.

providers.name: Habitto
providers.description: Habitto is a Tokyo-based fintech company building a mobile financial wellness app for the Japanese market under the banner お金の新習慣 ("new money habits"). The app pairs a high-yield savings account and a cashback debit card with access to human financial advisors who help users save, grow, and protect their money. Habitto is backed by the fintech-focused venture investors Anthemis and QED Investors. This API Evangelist profile has been enriched with company identity, website link properties, and a domain-security probe; Habitto is a consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Halo Health
providers.description: Halo Mental Health (Halo Health) operates same-day mental health urgent care clinics, offering immediate psychiatric assessments, medication management, crisis intervention, individual and group therapy, and teletherapy for adults and children ages eight and older. Founded by Paul Manley with medical director Dr. Vahid Osman, the Joint Commission-accredited provider runs clinics in Central Las Vegas and Summerlin, accepts commercial insurance and Medicaid, and is building the largest network of urgent cares dedicated to same-day mental health services. Backed by 8vc. Halo Health publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its identity, web presence, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Happiest Baby
providers.description: Happiest Baby is a consumer sleep-technology company founded by pediatrician Dr. Harvey Karp, best known for the SNOO Smart Sleeper - an FDA-authorized responsive bassinet that uses sensor-driven motion and white noise to soothe infants and improve sleep. The company also sells the Sleepea swaddle and sleep sacks, runs a companion mobile app with parenting guidance, and operates a healthcare/hospital program. Its connected SNOO hardware communicates in real time over PubNub; Happiest Baby publishes no official public developer API, and the only programmatic access is via community-built wrappers around the undocumented mobile-app API. Backed by GV and Obvious Ventures.

providers.name: Happy Money
providers.description: Happy Money is a consumer finance company offering fully digital unsecured personal loans, best known for The Payoff Loan, aimed at helping members consolidate and pay off high-interest credit card debt. Loans are funded through a network of community-focused credit unions, banks, and asset managers rather than by Happy Money itself. The company has served over 350,000 customers and facilitated more than $7 billion in personal loans, and operates the industry's first end-to-end API for unsecured lending, offered to lending partners through a gated partner portal rather than as a public self-serve developer product. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a portfolio-company lead (Anthemis) and enriched from Happy Money's public web presence; its lending API surface is partner-gated and not publicly documented.

providers.name: Healint
providers.description: Healint is a Singapore-headquartered digital health company best known for Migraine Buddy, the world's largest migraine and headache tracking and research platform, used by more than three million people to log attacks, symptoms, triggers, medications, and treatment outcomes. The company applies machine learning, mobile sensor technologies, and analytics to help people manage migraine and other neurological conditions, and to generate real-world evidence for clinicians, researchers, and pharmaceutical partners. Healint and Migraine Buddy are now part of Aptar Digital Health, whose regulated companion apps, patient-support software, and drug-delivery platforms operate across more than 120 countries on HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. Healint does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Heltia
providers.description: Heltia is a Turkish digital mental-health and employee-wellbeing platform (an Employee Assistance Platform, EAP) that connects individuals and corporate employees with licensed psychologists and dietitians for online therapy, counseling and nutrition support. Its consumer app offers video sessions with experts, self-assessment tests (anxiety, depression, OCD, motivation) and an expert-reviewed blog, while its corporate products — Esenlik (wellbeing), Sağlık Yönetimi (health management) and brokerage — give employers measurable workforce mental-health programs. Backed by Northzone. Heltia does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK or documentation surface.

providers.name: Hidden Level
providers.description: Hidden Level is a U.S.-based defense and aerospace technology company that turns radio-frequency (RF) activity into trusted airspace intelligence. Its passive RF sensing platform detects and tracks unmanned aerial systems (drones) and other activity across air, ground, sea, and space domains without requiring emitters or heavy on-site infrastructure. Hidden Level packages this as hardware sensor platforms, software platforms, and data platforms serving defense and military, critical infrastructure protection, homeland security, and public safety customers. The company hosts its platform on AWS with least-privilege access, MFA, and TLS 1.3 API communications, aligns corporate controls to NIST SP 800-171, and emphasizes U.S. design and manufacturing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hidden Level's public web and security surface; the company does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs.

providers.name: IBM Db2
providers.description: IBM Db2 is a family of data management products from IBM that includes relational and hybrid database servers running on cloud, distributed, and z/OS platforms, supporting transactional, analytical, and AI workloads. Db2 exposes RESTful services that let applications create, discover, execute, and manage user-defined services natively against the database, and IBM Db2 as a Service on IBM Cloud provides a managed REST API for administering and querying cloud-hosted Db2 databases. Authentication is performed via HTTP basic auth, client certificates, or IBM Cloud IAM Bearer tokens depending on the deployment.

providers.name: Impelpharma
providers.description: Impel Pharmaceuticals is a commercial-stage pharmaceutical company developing first-in-class intranasal drug treatments for central nervous system (CNS) disorders with high unmet medical needs. Its proprietary Precision Olfactory Delivery (POD) technology targets the vascular-rich upper nasal cavity to achieve more rapid and consistent bioavailability than conventional delivery. Its lead product, Trudhesa (dihydroergotamine mesylate) nasal spray, is approved for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults. Impel was backed by Norwest Venture Partners (co-led its 2018 Series D) and later filed for bankruptcy in December 2023. This is a patient- and science-facing pharma company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Imperative Care
providers.description: Imperative Care is a U.S. medical technology company founded in 2015 by Fred Khosravi, neurosurgeon L. Nelson Hopkins, M.D., and Amar Sawhney, Ph.D., that develops connected interventional devices to elevate care for people affected by devastating vascular diseases such as ischemic stroke, venous thromboembolism, and acute limb ischemia. Its portfolio spans the Zoom Stroke System (including Zoom intracranial access and aspiration catheters and Continuous Dual Aspiration / CDAT technology) for fast, effective clot removal, the Symphony Thrombectomy System for venous thromboembolism, and the Prodigy Thrombectomy System for acute limb ischemia, with the Telos robotic-assisted platform in development in partnership with Proximie. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Imperative Care publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical developer portal; this profile captures its public web, security, and corporate surface.

providers.name: Iodine Software (Waystar)
providers.description: Iodine Software is a healthcare AI company whose AwareCDI suite applies clinical machine learning to the mid-revenue cycle, surfacing clinical documentation integrity (CDI) gaps, prioritizing high-impact cases, and automating physician queries so hospitals and health systems capture the complete patient story for more accurate coding, quality metrics, and revenue capture. Its Concurrent, Retrospective, and Interact modules integrate directly into existing EHR and coding workflows rather than exposing a public developer API. Founded in Austin, Texas, Iodine was acquired by revenue-cycle technology company Waystar in October 2025, and its products, blog, newsroom, and legal pages now live under waystar.com and its AltitudeAI platform. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Bain Capital Ventures portfolio company in the healthcare sector.

providers.name: Iterative Health (fka Iterative Scopes)
providers.description: Iterative Health (formerly Iterative Scopes) is a healthcare and life-sciences company that operates an AI-enabled clinical research network, connecting pharmaceutical sponsors and contract research organizations (CROs) with community-based medical sites across gastroenterology (GI), hepatology, obesity, and cardiology. Its SKOUT product applies artificial intelligence to streamline site operations and patient enrollment, and the company runs a global site network embedded in community care practices through partnerships with GI Alliance, One GI, and US Heart & Vascular. Backed by Insight Partners, the company closed a $77M Series C in April 2026. Iterative Health does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Journey Medidtation
providers.description: Journey (Journey Meditation) is a workplace mental health platform that delivers preventive Employee Assistance Program (EAP) services to enterprise organizations. Rather than the reactive model of traditional EAPs, Journey uses AI-powered risk detection (Journey Signal) to identify emerging mental health issues before they escalate and connects employees to clinicians across 190+ countries in 100+ languages. Its offerings include Journey Proactive EAP, the Journey LIVE guided-meditation and wellbeing experience, and a Mental Health Certification training program. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer or API surface has been found; this profile is maintained as a company lead and refreshed by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Jow
providers.description: Jow is a consumer meal-planning and grocery-shopping application that turns personalized menu selection into an automated shopping list. From a catalog of thousands of recipes tailored to household size, dietary preferences and goals (keto, vegetarian, high-protein, gluten-free, kid-friendly, low-calorie), Jow builds a weekly menu and generates the matching grocery order, which users check out through integrated grocery-retail partnerships at optimized prices. Founded in France and available as iOS and Android mobile apps, Jow serves millions of active users. It is a portfolio company of Northzone. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and its probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Kailera Therapeutics
providers.description: Kailera Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the next generation of obesity and cardiometabolic care through a diversified pipeline of GLP-1 based therapies. Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, its lead candidate ribupatide (KAI-9531) is a once-weekly injectable GLP-1/GIP receptor dual agonist in a global Phase 3 program, alongside oral small-molecule GLP-1 candidates and tri-agonist programs licensed in part from Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals. Kailera has raised a $400M Series A and a $600M Series B led by Bain Capital, and priced its IPO in April 2026 (NASDAQ: KLRA). This is a corporate/portfolio company profile in the API Evangelist network; Kailera publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: KeyCare
providers.description: KeyCare is a telehealth platform that connects health systems to a national network of independent, virtual-first care providers through deep Epic EHR integration. Built on Epic using CareEverywhere, MyChart, Telehealth Anywhere, and Book Anywhere workflows, KeyCare lets member health systems extend their own Epic instance to on-demand urgent care (24/7/365 across all 50 states), behavioral health, neurology, primary care, and expanding specialties such as rheumatology, cardiology, and maternal care. The company serves health systems including Allina Health, Memorial Healthcare, Ochsner Health, WellSpan, and Confluence Health. KeyCare is backed by 8VC. This profile has no public API or developer surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Keychain
providers.description: Keychain is an AI-powered operating system and network for the consumer packaged goods (CPG) industry, connecting brands and retailers with the contract manufacturers, co-packers, and suppliers that make their products. The platform lets CPG brands discover and match with vetted manufacturing partners, manage sourcing and production relationships, and streamline the supplier-discovery workflow that has traditionally been manual and relationship-driven. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Keychain was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile surfaced from the a16z venture portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Keychain publishes a marketing and product web presence at keychain.com but does not expose a public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API discovery surface (no developer/API subdomain, no /.well-known catalog, no llms.txt).

providers.name: Kirilys Therapeutics
providers.description: Kirilys Therapeutics is a multi-asset precision oncology company developing targeted therapeutic treatments for cancer patients. Led by co-founder and CEO BT Slingsby, MD, PhD, MPH, the company is building a pipeline of precision medicines and is backed by Catalys Pacific, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and UBE. Kirilys was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage biotech, Kirilys publishes a corporate marketing website (company, news, and contact pages) but exposes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or machine discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Kovzy Co.
providers.description: Kovzy is a restaurant technology company with offices in Tbilisi, Georgia and Yerevan, Armenia, selling an all-in-one SaaS platform for restaurants and cafes. The product is built from three modules that share one back office - a website builder that gives a restaurant its own online ordering site with no commission on direct sales, a QR digital menu customers browse and order from by scanning a code at the table, and a point-of-sale system that consolidates orders arriving from delivery aggregators (Wolt, Glovo), the QR menu, and the restaurant's own website into a single queue, with kitchen management and recipe and cost tracking on top. Pricing is per module and quoted monthly in Georgian lari, and onboarding is self-service through a hosted signup that provisions a restaurant subdomain. Kovzy was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation as of this profile, so this entry describes the company and its partner surface rather than an API.

providers.name: La Vie
providers.description: La Vie Foods is a Paris-based plant-based food company that makes vegan alternatives to pork products, including bacon, smoked lardons, ham, salami sticks, croquettes and meatballs, sold across French and UK retail and foodservice. Its stated mission is to move people from animal to vegetable fat without compromising on taste, citing 88% less CO2, 82% less water and 74% less land use than conventional pork. Its products are stocked by retailers including Tesco, Sainsbury's, Waitrose, Whole Foods Market and Planet Organic, and used by restaurant partners such as Burger King. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of partech. La Vie Foods operates as a consumer packaged-goods brand rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, CLI, packages or programmatic API surface, and exposes no /.well-known/ discovery documents. This profile therefore captures the company's real public web, legal, press and domain-security surface rather than developer artifacts.

providers.name: Layer Health
providers.description: Layer Health is a healthcare AI company building a clinical intelligence platform that reads longitudinal medical records at scale to automate labor-intensive clinical workflows for health systems. Its products span clinical registry abstraction automation (cardiovascular, surgical, and oncology registries), clinical pathways that surface guideline-aligned care opportunities and eligible patients, site-of-care optimization, and automated quality measurement of custom clinical variables. The company positions clinician-validated AI as an embedded workflow layer rather than a standalone tool, citing 50%+ time savings on registry abstraction, and works with health systems including Johns Hopkins Medicine, Intermountain Health, MultiCare, and White Plains Hospital. Backed by GV. As of this enrichment pass Layer Health publishes a marketing and company site only and exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Livspace
providers.description: Livspace is India's largest home interior design and renovation company, founded in 2014 and headquartered in Bangalore. It runs an end-to-end, technology-driven interiors platform: free design consultation, in-browser 3D visualisation, factory-made modular products (kitchens, wardrobes, storage), and managed on-site installation, backed by a lifetime warranty on modular products. Livspace serves 125+ cities across India through 100+ Experience Centres and a network of interior designers, covering full-home interiors, modular kitchens, false ceilings, flooring, painting and related fit-out services. It is a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company. This profile currently exposes no public developer API or SDK surface; enrichment captured its public security, well-known, and llms.txt surfaces.

providers.name: Lotus Health AI
providers.description: Lotus Health AI (branded Lotus AI, at lotus.ai) is an AI-powered consumer healthcare platform delivered through an iOS app that pairs artificial intelligence trained on medical evidence with licensed physicians to provide personalized medical care. The service offers AI-guided care plans built from a member's health data, prescriptions sent to any pharmacy in the United States, lab ordering across 6,000+ test sites nationwide, centralized medical-record management, and 24/7 availability. The company is a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins in the healthcare sector. As of this profile the company exposes a consumer mobile product and physician tooling (Cortex) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Luna
providers.description: Luna is an in-home physical therapy company that dispatches licensed physical therapists to patients' homes for 1:1 treatment sessions covered by insurance, including Medicare and major commercial plans. The company supports orthopedic, sports medicine, neurologic, post-surgical, and geriatric rehabilitation across a nationwide network of thousands of therapists, reaching roughly 85K patients and more than 1.2M in-home PT visits in 2024. Luna was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a consumer healthcare service with no public developer or API program at this time.

providers.name: Manatee
providers.description: Manatee is a digital mental health company delivering family-centered virtual therapy for children, teens, and their parents. It pairs licensed therapists with dedicated care navigators to provide evidence-based treatment (CBT, DBT, and family-systems therapy) for kids ages 5-18 and counseling for caregivers, coordinated through a family app and covered by most major insurance plans across multiple U.S. states. Backed by Techstars, Manatee operates as a consumer telehealth service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Marathon Health
providers.description: Marathon Health is a healthcare services company delivering advanced primary care and occupational health to employers, labor unions, health plans, and brokers/consultants. It operates onsite, nearsite, and network health centers plus virtual primary care, spanning preventive care, mental health, musculoskeletal treatment, lifestyle and medication management, value-driven referrals, and population health management to improve employee health outcomes while lowering total healthcare cost. Backed by NEA. As of this enrichment pass Marathon Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or event/webhook surface.

providers.name: Medefer
providers.description: Medefer is a UK digital-first managed clinical services company that connects patients directly with consultant specialists remotely and safely, working in partnership with the NHS. Its virtual, consultant-led model triages and manages patient referrals through remote review, coordinating in-person tests and treatment through a trusted local and national partner network only when they are needed. Backed by Seedcamp, Medefer brings hospital-level specialist expertise into patients' homes and communities, reducing waiting times for NHS and self-pay patients across a range of specialties. Medefer operates a patient/clinician application and a private internal application backend (api.medefer.com) rather than a public developer API program.

providers.name: MediBuddy (fka DocsApp)
providers.description: MediBuddy (formerly DocsApp) is India's largest digital healthcare platform, operated by Phasorz Technologies Private Limited and founded in 2013 by Satish Kannan and Enbasekar Dinadayalane. Launched as DocsApp in 2015 for online doctor consultations, it merged with and rebranded to MediBuddy in June 2020. The consumer platform delivers teleconsultations (chat, video, voice) across 20+ specialties, at-home lab-test bookings, online medicine delivery covering 95%+ of Indian pin codes, and health checks. It is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Quadria Capital and Rebright Partners. No public developer / API program was found; product access is via the consumer web and mobile apps.

providers.name: Medical Informatics
providers.description: Medical Informatics Corp. (MIC) is a Houston, Texas healthcare technology company behind the FDA-cleared Sickbay platform for virtual and remote patient monitoring. Founded in 2010 by Emma Fauss and Craig Rusin, Sickbay archives, aggregates, and transforms otherwise unrecorded high-resolution physiological waveform data across disparate, vendor-neutral biomedical devices to enable anytime, anywhere remote monitoring, TeleICUs, alarm management, workflow automation, and patient-centered predictive analytics and AI across the continuum of care. The company is backed by DCVC, Intel Capital, Catalio Capital, and the Texas Medical Center. Sickbay is a clinical SaaS platform with no public developer API surface; integration is delivered through the vendor as HL7/device connectivity.

providers.name: Mercanis
providers.description: Mercanis is an AI-powered procurement platform that automates the end-to-end source-to-contract lifecycle for enterprise procurement teams. It combines structured intake, connected sourcing (RFx and supplier comparison), supplier relationship management, contract lifecycle management, and risk, compliance and spend analytics, coordinated by a large fleet of autonomous AI agents. Mercanis serves sectors including energy and utilities, pharma and chemicals, automotive, consumer goods, manufacturing, and construction, and integrates with ERP systems such as SAP and NetSuite alongside procurement networks like Unite. The company is headquartered in Germany with SOC-certified, GDPR-compliant infrastructure. No public developer API, documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface has been identified as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Mirvie
providers.description: Mirvie is a clinical-stage women's health company founded in 2018 and based in South San Francisco, California, pioneering the early prediction of pregnancy complications. Its proprietary RNA platform uses a simple maternal blood test and machine learning to read tens of thousands of molecular messages from mother, baby, and placenta, revealing the underlying biology of each pregnancy months before symptoms appear. Mirvie's first product, the Encompass preeclampsia test, pairs a novel blood test that predicts personalized preeclampsia risk with a preventive care plan and received FDA Breakthrough Device designation. The company is backed by General Catalyst, GV, Mayfield, Khosla Ventures, Foresite Capital, and Decheng Capital. Mirvie operates consumer and clinical web properties (mirvie.com and encompasstest.com) but publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Modern Age
providers.description: Modern Age is a longevity-focused health and wellness clinic based on New York City's Upper East Side. It provides proactive aging interventions including comprehensive Aging Wellness Assessments (blood work, bone-density scans, cognitive testing, and clinician consultation), IV drip therapies, vitamin injections, hormone therapy, medically supervised weight loss, and aesthetic skin and hair treatments. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), the company blends clinical diagnostics with wellness services to help members understand and proactively slow the aging process. Modern Age is a consumer health clinic and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Mural Health
providers.description: Mural Health is a clinical research technology company whose Mural Link platform manages the clinical trial participant experience end to end. Founded by the team that created ClinCard, Mural Health provides integrated participant payments across 10+ global methods (Venmo, PayPal, Zelle, Revolut, bank transfer, virtual and physical prepaid debit cards, and check via mail), in-app travel and rideshare coordination (Uber, Lyft), participant messaging and calendar syncing, and real-time satisfaction analytics for research sites and sponsors. The company works with leading pharmaceutical sponsors, CROs, and site networks to reduce trial dropout and administrative burden across studies in 75+ countries, and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Mural Health does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; system integrations are delivered through partnerships (e.g., ClinOne, Clinical Ink).

providers.name: Netsmart Technologies
providers.description: Netsmart Technologies is a healthcare software and services company serving community-based care providers across human services, post-acute care, home care and hospice, public sector, and physical rehabilitation. Its CareFabric platform unifies electronic health records (EHR) such as CareRecord, myAvatar, and myUnity with workforce management, revenue cycle, analytics, and interoperability tooling. Netsmart is a founding member of the Carequality interoperability collaborative and became the first EHR built for human services and post-acute care to be designated a Qualified Health Information Network (QHIN) under TEFCA, exchanging clinical data via FHIR-based standards. The company publishes no public developer portal or API documentation; integration is delivered through its CareConnect interoperability services, the Netsmart Marketplace partner program, and direct engagement rather than a self-service public API.

providers.name: Niricson Software
providers.description: Niricson Software Inc. is an infrastructure technology company making concrete infrastructure safer through AI-powered digital condition assessment. Its patented AUTOSPEX platform uses machine learning and multi-sensor data fusion (visual, thermal, and acoustic) to automatically detect, quantify, and track defects such as cracks, spalling, delamination, and alkali-aggregate reaction in dams, spillways, bridges, and airfields. Data is collected with its DRONIC architecture and NCX acoustic drone payload, which simulates the traditional concrete hammer-sounding test to identify subsurface delamination up to eight inches deep. Asset owners and civil engineers access results through the login-gated, web-based AUTOSPEX platform to interact with defect maps and compare surveys over time. Niricson operates across the USA, Canada, Australia, and India, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: nlyte
providers.description: nlyte is an enterprise Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) software provider, now part of Carrier, that helps organizations discover, model, and manage physical and virtual data-center assets, capacity, power, cooling, connectivity, and operational workflows across facilities. Nlyte products expose REST APIs (including the NgageAPI / Ngauge web service) plus a portfolio of pre-built bi-directional connectors for CMDB, ITSM, service desk, virtualization, and building-management systems. The API is delivered to customers through the Nlyte customer portal rather than a public developer program, so there is no open developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or self-serve sign-up.

providers.name: Noah Medical
providers.description: Noah Medical is a surgical robotics company building the Galaxy System, a robotic-assisted bronchoscopy platform for interventional pulmonology. The system combines advanced imaging, precision targeting, single-use scope technology, and an adaptive workflow to deliver "tool-in-lesion" confidence for diagnosing lung nodules, improving diagnostic yield and workflow efficiency for physicians. Noah Medical is a medical-device manufacturer focused on clinical hardware and does not currently expose a public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company backed by Hongshan (HongShan Capital / formerly Sequoia China).

providers.name: Nutrisystem (Wellina by Nutrisystem)
providers.description: Nutrisystem is a direct-to-consumer subscription meal delivery service for weight loss, founded in 1972 by Harold Katz and headquartered in Fort Washington, Pennsylvania. The company pioneered prepackaged weight-loss meal subscriptions, transitioned from physical retail to a direct-to-consumer Internet and telephone model in 1999, and added mobile delivery beginning in 2010. Nutrisystem is now operated under the marketing umbrella "Wellina by Nutrisystem" — a multi-brand health and wellness marketplace covering Nutrisystem, Jenny Craig, High Protein, Menopause Support, Low Carb (GLP-1 friendly), and the Club Advantage à la carte membership. The legal operating entity is Nutrisystem, LLC, a subsidiary of Wellful, Inc. (the parent organization formed after Kainos Capital acquired Nutrisystem from Tivity Health in October 2020). Tivity Health no longer owns the brand. Wellful's portfolio also includes South Beach Diet (acquired by Nutrisystem in December 2015 for $15 million) and the Jenny Craig intellectual property (acquired by Wellful in fall 2023 after Jenny Craig's Chapter 7 bankruptcy and relaunched as an e-commerce meal-delivery brand). LinkedIn classifies the company under Wellness and Fitness Services with 501–1,000 employees. Stephen Mikulak was named President in 2021. Nutrisystem publishes no public developer APIs, OpenAPI specs, SDKs, or developer portal. Its only digital surface beyond the e-commerce sites is the consumer-facing Nutrisystem mobile app (iOS / Android) for food logging, weight tracking, journaling, and meal-plan adjustments — and the equivalent Jenny Craig app — neither of which advertise integrations with Apple Health, Google Fit, Fitbit, or any third-party platform. The github.com/nutrisystem GitHub organization exists but contains a single inactive CSS repository last updated in March 2015. The technology footprint is a closed consumer subscription stack with no public developer touchpoints.

providers.name: OpenLoop Health
providers.description: OpenLoop Health is a Des Moines, Iowa-based white-label telehealth infrastructure company that powers virtual care for digital health companies, health plans, diagnostic labs, retailers and pharmacies, and hospitals and health systems. Its platform bundles a nationwide clinician network (covering all 50 states and more than 500,000 patient visits per month), provider staffing, licensing and credentialing, payer coverage and revenue cycle management, diagnostic imaging, regulatory and legal support, and practice management, with AI-powered clinical operations across synchronous and asynchronous care. OpenLoop delivers its capabilities through EHR integrations and protocol-specific API integrations offered to partners via sales; as of this profile there is no publicly published API specification, SDK, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: OriGene Technologies
providers.description: OriGene Technologies, Inc. is a life sciences company that develops and supplies validated research reagents and laboratory services for genomics and proteomics research. Its catalog spans cDNA clones, expression vectors, lentivirus and viral gene-delivery systems, RNAi and CRISPR tools, primary antibodies, recombinant proteins, ELISA and assay kits, and human tissue samples, alongside custom cloning, antibody and protein development, and lentivirus production services. The company operates in the United States and, through OriGene Technologies GmbH, in Europe. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass OriGene publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Ossium Health
providers.description: Ossium Health is a bioengineering company developing off-the-shelf cell therapies manufactured from stem cells recovered from deceased organ and tissue donors. The company operates a proprietary bone marrow and tissue recovery, banking, and manufacturing platform, and is advancing a clinical pipeline of allogeneic cellular therapies targeting hematologic diseases, organ transplant tolerance, and orthopedic conditions. Ossium Health is a private, venture-backed life sciences company; it does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record and was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst.

providers.name: Oula Health
providers.description: Oula Health (Oula) is a modern maternity and women's health provider operating collaborative-care clinics in New York and Connecticut. Oula pairs OBGYNs with certified nurse midwives to deliver comprehensive support before, during, and after pregnancy — including preconception planning, prenatal and postpartum care, gynecology, and miscarriage care — and partners with health systems, employers, and payers to extend that model. It is a patient-facing healthcare provider and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Outcomes4Me
providers.description: Outcomes4Me is a digital health company providing a personalized cancer care navigation platform for patients. The consumer app delivers personalized treatment plans, symptom and medication management, and community support grounded in NCCN Guidelines, serving over 300,000 patients across 100+ cancer communities. Alongside the patient app, Outcomes4Me runs a For Life Sciences business that offers real-world outcomes data, precision content and marketing, and clinical-trial recruitment and patient-reported-outcomes support to pharmaceutical and diagnostics partners. Backed by Sierra Ventures. No public developer/API surface is published at this time; this profile has been enriched with the company identity and domain-security posture that are publicly available.

providers.name: Oxford Science Enterprises
providers.description: Oxford Science Enterprises (OSE) is an independent investment company and venture builder that transforms cutting-edge research from the University of Oxford into commercial companies tackling global challenges across deep tech, life sciences, and health tech. Operating on a "find, fund, build" model, OSE provides patient capital and hands-on company-building to Oxford science founders, backing 50+ flagship companies with a net asset value of around £1.3bn alongside 300+ co-investors. Notable outcomes include Oxford Ionics (acquired by IonQ) and Dark Blue Therapeutics. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; OSE is an investor and venture builder and does not publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Piazza
providers.description: Piazza is an online question-and-answer platform for higher education that connects students, teaching assistants, and professors in a single wiki-style collaborative space for each class. Instructors run a Piazza for their course where students ask and answer questions, post anonymously, use a LaTeX and code editor for technical content, and receive instructor-endorsed answers. Piazza integrates with every major learning management system (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, Sakai, Desire2Learn, and others) via the LTI standard for single-click class creation, roster-based automatic enrollment, and automatic single sign-on. It is used across thousands of universities in more than 90 countries and is FERPA-compliant. Piazza does not publish an official public developer API; LMS connectivity is delivered through LTI, and only community projects wrap its internal endpoints.

providers.name: PlanSwift
providers.description: PlanSwift is Windows desktop takeoff and estimating software for construction estimators - turning digital plans (PDF/image/CAD) into measurable, countable, exportable material takeoffs and estimates across trades like roofing, concrete, earthwork, flooring, and electrical. PlanSwift is owned by ConstructConnect. IMPORTANT - PlanSwift does NOT publish a public web/REST API. Its developer surface is a desktop extensibility SDK embedded in the Windows application - OLE Automation (COM), an internal scripting engine, and a plugin/starter-pack model - exposed through a password-gated "Under-The-Hood" (U-T-H) tab enabled by contacting ConstructConnect (takeoff@constructconnect.com). The public SDK examples on GitHub target PlanSwift9 and are written in Pascal (2008) and Visual Basic (2010). There is no documented HTTPS base URL, no API keys/OAuth token surface, and no web endpoints to model - this entry is an honest stub reflecting a desktop-plugin/COM SDK, not a web API.

providers.name: PlushCare
providers.description: PlushCare is a telehealth and virtual primary care platform that connects patients with board-certified physicians for online doctor visits, available 24/7 across all 50 US states. Services include online prescriptions and refills, urgent care video visits, mental health care and therapy, weight-loss management including GLP-1 medications, chronic disease management, pediatric and preventive care, and sexual health. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in San Francisco, PlushCare accepts most major insurance and offers self-pay memberships. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GGV Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners. As a consumer telehealth service, PlushCare publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public web and domain-security surface.

providers.name: POMS
providers.description: POMS Corporation develops POMSnet Aquila, a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) purpose-built for pharmaceutical, biotech, cell and gene therapy, and medical device manufacturers. The platform delivers FDA-compliant electronic batch records (EBR), production execution, review-by-exception, and plant-floor integration with ERP and equipment systems, deployed on-premise or in the cloud. POMS also offers the POMSnet Falcon EBR analytics dashboards. Founded around its first MES implementation in 1988 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington, POMS sells enterprise software to regulated life-sciences manufacturers rather than publishing a public developer API. Surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead, this profile is enriched from the company's public web presence; no public API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found.

providers.name: Pretzel Therapeutics
providers.description: Pretzel Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class medicines that target mitochondrial biology and cellular energy regulation. Its pipeline spans neurological, muscular atrophy, metabolic, and rare disease indications, applying novel mitochondrial modulation approaches to conditions driven by dysfunctional cellular energy production. Backed by GV, the company operates as a therapeutics developer and publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company record and life-sciences lead.

providers.name: Profluent
providers.description: Profluent is a Berkeley, California AI biology company building frontier protein language models and using them to design functional proteins for therapeutics, gene editing, agriculture, and industrial enzymes. Founded by Ali Madani — previously architect of the ProGen large language model for proteins at Salesforce AI Research — Profluent pairs in-house foundation models with a wet lab to author novel proteins from scratch and validate them experimentally. The company's research has been published in Nature Biotechnology and Nature, and it is best known for OpenCRISPR-1, which it describes as the world's first AI-designed gene editor, released freely for research and commercial use. Profluent also publishes the ProGen3 family of protein generation models, ProseLM for structure-conditioned protein design, the E1 family of protein encoder models, Protein2PAM for CRISPR-Cas PAM specificity prediction, and the CRISPR-Cas Atlas dataset. Commercial partnerships include a multi-target collaboration with Eli Lilly worth up to $2.25 billion, and deals with Ensoma, Corteva, Integrated DNA Technologies, and the Rett Syndrome Research Trust. Profluent is backed by Spark Capital, Insight Partners, Air Street Capital, Altimeter, and Bezos Expeditions. The company does not publish a hosted developer REST API or commercial SDK; its surface area for external builders is the Profluent-AI GitHub organization (model weights and inference code), the Protein2PAM web tool, and partnership engagements.

providers.name: Protege
providers.description: Protege (Protege Health Inc.) is a two-sided data platform that connects AI model builders with high-quality, real-world proprietary datasets for pre-training, post-training, fine-tuning, and evaluation. It curates data from hundreds of sources across healthcare, video, audio and speech, motion capture, architecture/engineering/construction, manufacturing, energy, finance, and agriculture, handling licensing and rights protection while fairly compensating data rights holders. Protege also operates DataLab, a research team focused on data-for-AI challenges. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, CRV, Bloomberg Beta, Footwork, Flex Capital, SV Angel, Liquid, and Shaper Capital. As of this enrichment pass Protege publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and web properties.

providers.name: Provenmetal
providers.description: ProvenMetal is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building fast-turn, American-made printed circuit board (PCB) assembly. The company lets customers upload a Gerber file, automatically infers the board specification, and returns instant quoting for a 7-day standard turnaround with no expedite fees. ProvenMetal automates the traditional manufacturing bottlenecks — part procurement, design for manufacturability (DFM) review, and assembly — and performs 100% X-ray inspection of every board (AI-assisted, cited at 99.8% confidence) before shipment, including the inspection data with each order. It is a domestic B2B PCB manufacturing service aimed at reshoring electronics production, operated out of San Francisco. As of this profile ProvenMetal exposes a customer ordering portal at order.provenmetal.com but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: PsyOptions
providers.description: PsyOptions is a decentralized options protocol built on Solana by Mithraic Labs, providing on-chain American-style options contracts originally designed for use with the Serum/OpenBook DEX. Rather than a hosted REST API, it exposes its functionality through open-source on-chain Anchor/BPF programs and first-party TypeScript client libraries (the @mithraic-labs npm scope: psy-american, psyoptions, market-meta, psy-token-registry, psy-metrics) plus a Rust crate. The project has since been sunset: its documentation and marketing sites are shut down, though the GitHub repositories and published packages remain available for reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. Sector: crypto / DeFi.

providers.name: Qualifi
providers.description: Qualifi is a recruiting and hiring platform that streamlines candidate screening through asynchronous, voice-based phone interviews, automated scheduling, and live video interviews. Recruiters send candidates a pre-recorded phone screen, review responses on their own schedule, and move qualified applicants forward faster, reducing time-to-hire while keeping the candidate experience high. Qualifi offers 50+ applicant tracking system (ATS) integrations, a "Qualifi Copilot" that surfaces the tool directly inside your ATS, and Google/Microsoft calendar sync. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and is SOC 2 Type II certified.

providers.name: REEV
providers.description: REEV is a medical-technology company developing AI-powered wearable robotics for mobility recovery and neurological gait rehabilitation. Its REEV SENSE platform uses smart shoe- and leg-mounted sensors to analyze gait and visualize biomarkers in a mobile app, and its DREEVEN motorized knee-ankle-foot orthosis (KAFO) delivers robotic walking assistance personalized from REEV SENSE gait data. REEV serves outpatient clinics and rehabilitation centers treating stroke, multiple sclerosis, and paraplegia, and is backed by Techstars, NVIDIA Inception, and Bpifrance.

providers.name: Reindeer AI
providers.description: Reindeer AI is an enterprise agentic AI platform that automates back-office business operations across finance, banking, insurance, supply chain, procurement, legal compliance, and global business services. Founded in 2024 with offices in New York and Tel Aviv, Reindeer deploys custom AI agents that learn from operational workflows using its Fast Track Training approach (functional models in roughly two weeks from a small number of samples), with human-in-the-loop escalation, continuous learning, and Model Reality Grounding safeguards against hallucination. It ships 200+ pre-trained skills and 200+ out-of-the-box integrations into systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Workday, ServiceNow, and Salesforce, is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Bedrock, DeepSeek, GLM), and emphasizes customer data ownership and enterprise security (ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type 2, GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA). Reindeer is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, TEAM8, and Vesey Ventures. Reindeer does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal; the product is delivered as an enterprise engagement, so this profile captures company identity and security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Remedee Labs
providers.description: Remedee Labs is a French medical device company founded in 2016 in Grenoble that develops millimeter-wave neuromodulation solutions for chronic pain management. Its flagship product is the Remedee wrist bracelet, which stimulates nerve endings to trigger endorphin release, paired with the myRemedee companion app and human coaching. The company markets two subscription solutions, FibroRem for fibromyalgia and NoviRem for osteoarthritis pain. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network; the product is consumer-facing and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Rippl Care *
providers.description: Rippl (Rippl Care) is a specialty healthcare company delivering value-based, virtual-first behavioral health and dementia care for older adults and their caregivers. Its clinical model spans medication assessments, personalized care plans, counseling, community-resource navigation, and safety guidance, partnering with health systems, providers, and payors. Rippl runs its patient portal on athenahealth and is backed by GV (Google Ventures); it has no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Route 92 Medical
providers.description: Route 92 Medical (r92m) is a neurovascular medical device company committed to improving outcomes for stroke and neurovascular patients through revolutionary procedural change. Its portfolio includes the FreeClimb System of access and aspiration catheters (models 54, 70, and 88), the HiPoint Reperfusion System built on the Monopoint Approach (under investigation in the SUMMIT MAX clinical trial), and the Ascent product line. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Route 92 Medical publishes a corporate marketing and clinical-evidence website but exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Rubicon Project
providers.description: Rubicon Project is a Los Angeles-based advertising technology company, founded in 2007, that built and operated one of the largest real-time bidding advertising exchanges, connecting digital publishers (the sell side) with advertisers and demand-side platforms. In 2020 Rubicon Project merged with Telaria and rebranded as Magnite, now positioned as the world's largest independent sell-side (SSP) advertising company, spanning connected TV (CTV), online video, display, and audio across its DV+, SpringServe, and ClearLine platforms. This profile tracks the company as it exists today under the Magnite brand. Rubicon Project / Magnite publishes no public self-serve developer API or documentation portal — platform access is enterprise and partner-gated through the Magnite Help Center.

providers.name: Saffron Finance
providers.description: Saffron Finance is a decentralized peer-to-peer interest-rate risk adjustment protocol built on Ethereum. Underlying DeFi yield is transformed by a smart-contract vault system according to each user's indicated risk preference, splitting deposits into senior (fixed-income, risk-averse) and junior (variable, risk-seeking) tranches across Uniswap V3 fixed-income vaults. The protocol is governed by the Saffron DAO and its SFI token, and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital in the crypto-web3 sector. Saffron is an on-chain protocol rather than a hosted web-API provider: its developer surface is Solidity smart contracts, published documentation, audits, and whitepapers rather than a REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Scarlet
providers.description: Scarlet is Europe's only Notified Body specialised in software and AI-based medical devices. Operating at scarlet.cc, Scarlet certifies Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and AI as a Medical Device (AIaMD) under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR), streamlining conformity assessment, CE marking, and certificate transfers for manufacturers who ship iteratively and release frequently. Backed by Creandum, Scarlet was built to bring modern, fast-moving regulatory certification to AI and software medical-technology companies. Scarlet is a regulatory and certification services provider; it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Science 37 *
providers.description: Science 37 operates a decentralized, direct-to-patient clinical research platform — the first and only FDA-inspected direct-to-patient site — that delivers clinical trials to participants wherever they are. Its Metasite and Agile Clinical Trial operating model combine patient recruitment, research-grade nursing, telemedicine, eConsent, ePRO, wearable/device integration, and EHR data capture into a single end-to-end SaaS platform used by sponsors and CROs. Backed by GV and Lux Capital, the company has supported 200+ trials across many therapeutic areas. No public developer portal or API surface was found during enrichment (developer./api.science37.com do not resolve); this profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Segway-Ninebot
providers.description: Segway-Ninebot is a global personal-transportation and robotics company, formed when Ninebot acquired Segway in 2015. It designs and manufactures electric kickscooters (the world's top-selling e-kickscooter brand, 13M+ units sold across 100+ countries), self-balancing personal transporters, e-bikes, and — through its Robotics division — RMP mobile-robot chassis and delivery/service robots (Nova Carter, NVIDIA Isaac-powered developer kits). Backed by HongShan. Its public developer surface is limited to Segway Robotics' open-source ROS / NVIDIA Isaac integration packages on GitHub; no first-party REST or OpenAPI product API is currently published.

providers.name: Sidewinder Therapeutics
providers.description: Sidewinder Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Diego, developing a new generation of precision bispecific antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for the treatment of solid tumors. Its engineered biologics bind two complexed targets simultaneously to increase tumor specificity, driving internalization of the antibody-receptor complex and its cytotoxic payload, with the goal of expanding the therapeutic window for hard-to-treat cancers such as colorectal, lung, and head-and-neck squamous cell carcinomas. The company raised an oversubscribed $137M Series B in 2026 (co-led by Frazier Life Sciences and Novartis Venture Fund, with DCVC Bio, OrbiMed, and others) and is advancing its bispecific ADC programs toward clinical development. Sidewinder is a biopharma research company and publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Sirum
providers.description: SIRUM (Supporting Initiatives to Redistribute Unused Medicine) is a nonprofit and the country's largest redistributor of surplus prescription medication. It connects unused, in-date medicine from manufacturers, wholesalers, pharmacies, and nursing homes with patients who cannot afford their prescriptions, operating under drug-donation laws across the United States. SIRUM runs a logistics and matching platform that routes donated medication to community partners and individuals in need, aiming to close the gap for the tens of millions of Americans who skip prescribed medication because of cost. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Snout
providers.description: Snout provides affordable veterinary wellness subscription plans that help pet owners access preventive and routine care without financial stress, while enabling veterinary clinics to increase visit frequency and revenue. Clinics offer monthly membership plans covering unlimited exams and preventative care tailored to each pet's life stage (puppy, adult, senior), and receive upfront payment at the time of service. Snout supports partner practices with dedicated Clinic Success Managers, custom marketing, and staff training, serving 2,500+ providers nationwide. Backed by 500 Global. No public API, developer portal, or developer documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SPT Labtech
providers.description: SPT Labtech is a life-sciences laboratory-automation company headquartered near Cambridge, UK, that designs and manufactures instruments and consumables to accelerate drug discovery and life-science research. Its portfolio spans liquid handling (firefly, mosquito, dragonfly, apricot), sample preparation (chameleon for cryo-EM and Quantifoil supports), and sample management and storage (comPOUND, comPACT, arktic, lab2lab, and BioMicroLab). With 400+ employees across seven global locations and 30+ products, SPT Labtech serves pharmaceutical, biotech, and academic laboratories. It is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; SPT Labtech is a hardware and instrumentation vendor and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Stablecore
providers.description: Stablecore provides digital-asset banking infrastructure that lets banks and credit unions offer stablecoins, tokenized deposits, digital-asset accounts and exchange, and digital-asset-based lending inside their existing core, digital-banking and compliance stacks. The platform targets cross-border payments, treasury management, digital-asset investing, crypto on/off-ramps and stablecoin sponsor banking, with a multi-provider design intended to avoid vendor lock-in and built-in compliance tooling. Stablecore is SOC 2 compliant and an ABA Partner Network member; investors include Coinbase Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners and Bank of Utah. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and product site plus a blog, but no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Strive Health
providers.description: Strive Health is a Denver-based value-based kidney care company that partners with health systems, nephrologists, and payors to deliver comprehensive care for patients across the kidney disease spectrum, from chronic kidney disease (CKD) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) through dialysis and transplant. Its model combines Population Health care teams, Strive Care Partners (nephrologist-led services), Kidney Heroes nurse-practitioner care teams, and the CareMultiplier machine-learning platform for personalized, predictive treatment planning. Strive reports outcomes including higher optimal dialysis starts, reduced hospitalizations and readmissions, and increased home dialysis adoption. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of NEA and Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Strive Health publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: StuffThatWorks
providers.description: StuffThatWorks is a community-driven health research platform where patients with chronic conditions share their real-world experiences to figure out, together, which treatments work best. Members complete structured surveys about their diagnoses, symptoms, and treatment outcomes, and the platform applies collective-intelligence and machine-learning models to turn thousands of patient reports into comparative, condition-by-condition treatment rankings across hundreds of chronic illnesses such as fibromyalgia, IBS, migraine, PCOS, and endometriosis. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, StuffThatWorks is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. The consumer product is delivered as a web and mobile (PWA / Capacitor) application; probing the public domain surfaced no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time — only the SPA's private backend under /api/.

providers.name: Sukino
providers.description: Sukino Healthcare is a Bangalore, India-based continuum-of-care provider specializing in post-hospitalization recovery, rehabilitation, and transitional care for seniors and patients with chronic and neurological conditions. Founded by Rajinish Menon, it operates in-patient continuum care centers alongside home healthcare services, covering neuro, stroke, and knee-replacement rehabilitation, transitional care, and palliative care. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, Sukino is a healthcare services operator and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification at this time; this profile captures its identity and web presence for network discovery.

providers.name: Sweatcoin
providers.description: Sweatcoin is a health-and-fitness app that converts a user's physical steps and movement into a digital currency ("sweatcoins") that can be redeemed for gadgets, subscriptions, travel vouchers, charity donations, and cryptocurrency. Its proprietary movement-validation algorithms count outdoor steps while, the company states, not selling location data. Sweatcoin reports being a top-3 health & fitness app worldwide with tens of millions of users across 180+ countries, and partners with brands and organizations (NHS, Apple, Amazon and 600+ others) through sponsored challenges, clubs, boosts and an affiliate marketplace. The team also launched the Sweat Economy ($SWEAT), a NEAR-Protocol "movement economy" token, and the Sweat Wallet app, turning tracked movement into on-chain digital value. Sweatcoin exposes no public REST/OpenAPI developer surface; integration is via partner and marketplace programs and the SWEAT on-chain token.

providers.name: Tangelo
providers.description: Tangelo is a Latin American fintech company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of QED Investors (a fintech-focused venture firm). Tangelo runs an API-first developer program: it publishes API documentation through a Stoplight-hosted developer portal at docs.tangelolatam.com (workspace "Tangelo Latam Docs") and operates a branded Atlassian status page at status.tangelolatam.com. Its marketing site runs on Webflow. This profile was enriched by live probing of Tangelo's public surfaces; the underlying OpenAPI definition is served behind the Stoplight single-page app and was not machine-extractable in this pass, so spec-derived artifacts (packages, scopes, errors, authentication) remain open for a follow-up once the specification URL is captured.

providers.name: Tenaya Therapeutics *
providers.description: Tenaya Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, focused on discovering, designing, developing, and delivering potentially curative gene therapies and precision medicines that address the underlying drivers of heart disease. Its clinical pipeline includes TN-201, an AAV-based gene therapy for MYBPC3-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), and TN-401 for PKP2-associated arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), both in early clinical development. Publicly traded on Nasdaq as TNYA and backed by investors including GV, the company operates as a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer platform or API surface.

providers.name: The Mind Company
providers.description: The Mind Company is a consumer mental-fitness company that builds a multi-app platform for cognitive and emotional wellbeing. Its apps include Elevate (cognitive training across memory, vocabulary, math, and more), Balance (personalized meditation for sleep, stress, and focus), and Spark (puzzle-based learning). The company is a portfolio company of Felicis and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a direct-to-consumer mobile app business, The Mind Company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed security posture.

providers.name: Tigermed
providers.description: Tigermed (Hangzhou Tigermed Consulting Co., Ltd.) is a leading global contract research organization (CRO) providing integrated drug and medical device development services across the full clinical lifecycle. Its capabilities span preclinical development (medicinal chemistry, compound screening, toxicology, and bioanalytical services), clinical development (medical writing, clinical monitoring, regulatory affairs, and data management), and integrated services including central laboratories, pharmacovigilance, medical imaging, quality assurance, and real-world and post-marketing studies. The company reports 11,000+ global employees, 180+ offices and locations, and 4,000+ customers, supporting the development of 170+ innovative drugs.
