Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as of this enrichment pass Fuse Energy publishes only a consumer-facing web and mobile app and no public developer API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: Genesis Healthcare
providers.description: Genesis Healthcare is a Kennett Square, Pennsylvania based provider of skilled nursing, transitional care, rehabilitation, and assisted/senior living services, operating roughly 175 to 200 centers across 17 to 18 US states with about 27,000 employees serving more than 15,000 residents. Once one of the largest skilled nursing facility operators in the United States, Genesis Healthcare, Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on July 9, 2025 in the US Bankruptcy Court, citing pandemic aftereffects, inadequate Medicaid reimbursement, legacy liabilities from prior expansion, and roughly USD 8 million per month in litigation defense costs against more than 200 pending malpractice and wrongful death claims. At filing the company reported approximately USD 708 million in secured debt, more than USD 1.5 billion in unsecured debt, and at least USD 259 million owed to malpractice plaintiffs. After the bankruptcy court rejected an insider stalking horse bid from ReGen Healthcare / Pinta Capital Partners in December 2025, a roughly USD 1 billion sale to a NewGen Health backed buyer operating as "101 West State Street" was approved in January 2026, with the restructuring still in progress as of this profile. No public developer APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, GitHub organization, or developer portal have been identified for Genesis Healthcare; the company is a healthcare operator, not an API provider, and its public web presence is limited to a corporate brochure site, careers portal, and compliance hotline.

providers.name: GoGuardian
providers.description: GoGuardian is a K-12 education technology company whose suite - Admin (DNS and device content filtering for CIPA compliance), Teacher (classroom management and student engagement), and Beacon (student safety and self-harm / suicide risk detection) - is administered through web dashboards rather than a broadly published public API. GoGuardian's integration model is primarily roster ingestion - it syncs organizations, students, teachers, guardians, and classes from district Student Information Systems via the IMS Global / 1EdTech OneRoster 1.1 REST API (using a Consumer ID / Secret and a OneRoster URL), Clever, ClassLink, and Google Classroom, and it consumes Google Workspace admin APIs on the district's behalf. A developer / partner documentation portal exists at based.goguardian.com ("GoGuardian Based Docs"), but GoGuardian's own outbound developer API surface is partner-gated and not openly published. The API entries below are honestly modeled logical surfaces, not a confirmed public REST catalog.

providers.name: GoodFirms
providers.description: GoodFirms is a B2B research, ratings, and reviews platform that helps service seekers find the best IT services providers, software, and freelancers across various business categories.

providers.name: Hesi
providers.description: Hesi (合思, operated by Beijing Hosi Information Technology Co., Ltd.) is an AI-driven spend and expense management SaaS platform founded in 2014 and backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its cloud platform covers intelligent expense control and reimbursement ("no expense reports needed"), corporate business-travel booking, AI-powered audit and approval, electronic accounting archives, accounts payable/receivable, and business-intelligence analytics. Hesi serves 7,000+ paid enterprises — including large corporations and Fortune 500 firms across China — and runs a PaaS platform with integrations to roughly 1,400 banks. The company operates R&D centers in Beijing, Hangzhou, and Nanchang with 22 direct service offices nationwide.

providers.name: Hippo
providers.description: Hippo is a US homeowners insurance carrier headquartered in Palo Alto, California, operating as the insurance subsidiary of Hippo Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HIPO). Founded in 2015, Hippo modernizes home insurance with instant online quotes — typically under sixty seconds — and a smart home oriented approach that pairs policies with proactive home maintenance guidance through the Hippo Home mobile app, DIY checklists, home health scoring, and partnerships with smart device makers. The company writes homeowners, condo, landlord, flood, auto, and pet policies and operates as both a direct-to-consumer brand and an MGA distributing through a network of 70+ carrier partners, including Bamboo, Stillwater, Nationwide, American Integrity, Liberty Mutual, and Progressive. Hippo's underwriting capacity is anchored by its wholly-owned admitted carrier, Spinnaker Insurance Company, acquired in 2020. Hippo serves 500K+ homeowners across the United States, with concentrated presence in Texas, California, Arizona, Colorado, Missouri, Ohio, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Virginia. There is no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hippo or Spinnaker; the GitHub organization hippoinsurance exists but has no public repositories, and the api.hippo.com hostname is not exposed to the public internet. Integrations with smart home device partners, agents, and MGA carriers are handled through private partner channels rather than an open developer program.

providers.name: Intellitech
providers.description: Intellitech Corporation is a semiconductor test and design-for-test company based in Rochester, New Hampshire, specializing in IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG) boundary-scan technology. Its products include the Eclipse boundary-scan test development environment, the Scan Executive production test platform, and concurrent JTAG hardware testers such as the PT100 and JAF Pro, used for printed circuit board (PCB) testing, in-system FLASH programming, and FPGA configuration. Intellitech is an early Battery Ventures ("Battery Ventures I") portfolio company in the semiconductor sector. The company publishes product, legal, and customer-account pages on its website but does not expose a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or MCP surface.

providers.name: Kaavio
providers.description: Kaavio is an AI-powered product content platform for B2B distributors and manufacturers. It sources product data from supplier submissions, PDFs, spec sheets, internal systems (PIM, DAM, ERP) and the web, validates it with conflict detection and confidence scoring, generates market-ready content (structured attributes, SEO descriptions, FAQs, comparisons, substitutes), and deploys it to destination systems such as PIMs, e-commerce platforms, and channels. The platform handles catalogs ranging from 20,000 to more than a million SKUs and claims a 90% reduction in the time and effort to get market-ready SKU content online. Founded by Derek Gregg and Sam Bobb, based in San Francisco, and backed by Baukunst, Techstars, and Looking Glass Capital ($2.9M pre-seed).

providers.name: Latitud
providers.description: Latitud is an early-stage venture capital firm and founder platform that writes first checks for Latin American founders, positioning itself as a bridge between the LatAm startup ecosystem and Silicon Valley. Its flagship program is the Latitud Fellowship, an eight-week remote program for pre-founders, dealmakers and technical builders that ends with a week-long roadshow in San Francisco, and which invests a $62,500 ideation check on a SAFE for a 2.5 percent stake in a cohort of eight fellows. Latitud also runs a portfolio support practice, a mentor network drawn from companies such as Mercado Libre, Vercel, Auth0 and Cornershop, and a Spanish- and Portuguese-language media surface including a podcast and community channels. Latitud publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable specifications; its public surface is a three-page marketing site (home, fellowship, portfolio) plus an application form, so this profile is an identity and web-properties record rather than an API profile.

providers.name: Laureate Education
providers.description: Laureate Education, Inc. is a for-profit higher-education network founded in 1989 as Sylvan Learning Systems and renamed Laureate Education in May 2004. At its 2017 IPO peak the company operated more than 200 campuses across 28 countries serving over one million students; it became only the third B Corporation to go public when it listed on NASDAQ (ticker: LAUR) on 1 February 2017. Between 2018 and 2021 Laureate executed one of the largest sector-wide divestiture programs in the history of higher education, exiting Brazil (sold to Ânima Holding for ~$765M), the United States (Walden University sold to Adtalem for $1.48B), Australia / New Zealand (sold to Strategic Education), Chile (Universidad Andrés Bello transferred to Fundación Educación y Cultura in September 2020), Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, Malaysia, China, Italy, Cyprus and the United Kingdom — returning $1.29B to shareholders in October 2021. After the divestiture cycle Laureate continued as a pure-play Mexico / Peru operator with five remaining institutions and approximately 460,000 students. In May 2024 the company was acquired by an investor group led by the International Finance Corporation (IFC, a member of the World Bank Group) and Sterling Capital, taking Laureate Education private and delisting it from NASDAQ. The company is headquartered at 1000 Brickell Avenue, Suite 715, Miami, FL. Laureate does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, webhook surface, or status page. There is no Laureate Education GitHub organization. This profile therefore captures the corporate surface — institutions, divestiture history, leadership, investor status, news — rather than a programmable interface. The five remaining campus-network institutions each publish their own consumer-facing websites (UVM, UNITEC in Mexico; UPC, UPN, Cibertec in Peru) but none expose machine-readable APIs documented from the parent.

providers.name: Magicpin
providers.description: Magicpin (operated by Samast Technologies Private Limited) is India's hyperlocal savings and discovery platform, connecting consumers with deals, cashback, and vouchers across restaurants, food delivery, fashion, grocery, beauty, fitness, and electronics merchants in cities throughout India. The company operates a consumer savings app alongside a merchant/brands portal and corporate voucher solutions. As of this enrichment pass Magicpin publishes a consumer web and mobile experience plus partner and brand onboarding portals, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Marble Health
providers.description: Marble Health is a virtual mental-health company providing personalized therapy for K-12 students, delivered through partnerships with schools and school districts and directly to families. Licensed therapists meet with students over video, typically within a few days and with no waitlists, and the service accepts most insurance plans including Medicaid. The platform at app.marblehealth.com handles referrals and intake for school counselors and parents, and Marble Health also runs parent workshops and professional-development training for educators. The company is backed by Costanoa Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Marble Health exposes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface (no .well-known documents and no llms.txt); it is a consumer/patient-facing healthtech service rather than an API provider.

providers.name: MasteryConnect
providers.description: MasteryConnect is a K-12 formative assessment and standards-mastery platform, now part of Instructure. It helps teachers and districts build standards-aligned assessments (from prebuilt items or custom content), deliver common and benchmark assessments, auto-score results, and turn the data into intuitive mastery reports that guide interventions. It integrates tightly with the Canvas LMS through single sign-on and real-time data synchronization. MasteryConnect was originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; it was acquired by Instructure in 2019 and does not publish a standalone public developer API — integration is delivered through the Canvas LMS platform and its REST API.

providers.name: Mirado
providers.description: Mirado is a modern rewards platform that connects marketers and publishers with consumers through a network of more than 100 million cardholders. It delivers targeted, card-linked offers through publisher audiences and gives marketers full transparency into attributed, incremental sales using first-party card and bank data. Marketers reach new audiences and drive revenue at lower advertising cost, while publishers monetize their audiences through rewarding customer experiences. Mirado is an early-stage company backed by Version One Ventures. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and onboarding presence at mirado.ai (marketers, publishers, about, blog, get-started) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Quantum Machines
providers.description: Quantum Machines is a Tel Aviv, Israel-based quantum control company that builds the Quantum Orchestration Platform (QOP) — a unified hardware and software stack for controlling quantum processors at the pulse level. Its hardware portfolio centers on the OPX+ and OPX1000 controllers, which are built around a custom Pulse Processing Unit (PPU) architecture that executes classical control and real-time feedback alongside arbitrary waveform generation, with sub-microsecond classical-quantum round trips and 160 ns active reset latency. The platform is programmed in QUA, the company's domain-specific pulse-level language, exposed to developers through the qm-qua Python SDK and an extensive open-source ecosystem under the qua-platform GitHub organization (QUAlibrate, QUAM, qua-libs, py-qua-tools, qua-dashboards). Quantum Machines also ships peripheral hardware including the Octave up/down converter (to 18 GHz), QDAC-II ultra-low-noise DACs, QSwitch, QBox, and the QCage/QBoard/QFilter cryogenic line. The platform is qubit-modality agnostic, supporting superconducting, semiconductor spin, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and color-center systems, and is used by university labs (MIT, Caltech, Harvard, Princeton, Weizmann) and quantum startups (Alice & Bob, Diraq, EeroQ). Quantum Machines has partnered with NVIDIA on the DGX Quantum hybrid quantum-classical compute platform and acquired the Delft-based QHarbor Bioscience team as a European R&D hub. Quantum Machines does not currently publish a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or self-service developer signup; the QOP control surface is reached exclusively via the qm-qua Python SDK against an OPX/OPX1000 controller (hardware or qm-saas cloud simulator).

providers.name: Rational
providers.description: Rational (rational.to) is a Y Combinator (S26) company building AI employees, or "AI coworkers," for accounting and finance teams. Its AI agents onboard themselves to a firm, build a company "brain," and perform recurring accounting work — accounts payable, AR collections, bookkeeping, bank reconciliation, document collection, expense review, and month-end close — while keeping postings, payment release, and policy-sensitive decisions behind explicit human approval gates with an inspectable review history. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco by Jibril Moinuddin and Christ Xu, Rational targets accounting firms and finance teams facing a structural capacity and labor shortage. As an early-stage company it currently exposes a marketing and agent-discovery surface (llms.txt, ai-discovery.json, RFC 9116 security.txt) rather than a public developer API; this profile captures that surface and will be enriched as a developer platform ships.

providers.name: Relay.app
providers.description: Relay.app was a workflow automation platform (an AI-assisted alternative to Zapier and Make) that let teams build and run automated, multi-step workflows connecting external SaaS applications, with human-in-the-loop approval steps and AI actions embedded in the automation flow. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of 2026 the product has been discontinued: free users lost access on 2026-08-15 and paying customers on 2026-09-14, with the site now serving a shutdown notice and a data-export path only. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook reference are published for the platform.

providers.name: Rivian Automotive
providers.description: Rivian Automotive is an American electric vehicle manufacturer that designs and builds adventure-oriented electric trucks, SUVs, and commercial delivery vans, along with the charging infrastructure and connected-vehicle software that supports them. While Rivian does not publish a public developer API portal, an unofficial GraphQL API powers the Rivian mobile app and has been reverse-engineered by community projects for vehicle telemetry and control.

providers.name: Sales Patriot
providers.description: SalesPatriot deploys artificial intelligence into enterprise supply chain operations, embedding engineers onsite to build custom AI solutions that integrate fragmented business systems (ERP, CRM, email, spreadsheets, and supplier portals) and automate routine workflows. The platform aggregates data from scattered sources into a unified, searchable system, automates tasks such as quoting, sourcing, and data entry, and visualizes real-time operational metrics for executives. It serves defense contracting and procurement, complex multi-source procurement operations, and high-volume distribution. SalesPatriot is a portfolio company of CRV. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network and enriched by the pipeline; the company publishes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC)
providers.description: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) is a leading American technology integrator providing full life cycle services and solutions in the technical, engineering, and enterprise information technology markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC serves the U.S. federal government with approximately $7.4 billion in annual revenues. The company delivers IT modernization, cloud computing, digital transformation, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and data analytics solutions primarily for defense, intelligence, and civilian government customers. SAIC's open source presence is at github.com/saic-oss with DevSecOps tools including Anvil (CI/CD container) and terraform modules for Kubernetes sandboxes.

providers.name: Sixfold
providers.description: Sixfold is a New York City-headquartered AI company building purpose-built artificial intelligence for insurance underwriting across Property & Casualty and Life & Health lines. Founded by Alex Schmelkin (CEO, previously co-founder of Unqork), Jane Tran (COO), and Brian Moseley (CTO, previously Head of Developer Experience at American Express), Sixfold processes unstructured submissions, automates risk research, produces appetite fit scores, generates cited case narratives, and applies underwriting guidelines consistently across submissions. The platform classifies risk using industry standards (SIC, NAICS, ISO), supports 40+ P&C and Life & Health business lines, and deploys either standalone or via a flexible API into existing underwriting workbench, CRM, and policy administration systems. Customers include Zurich North America, Guardian, Generali GC&C, Skyward Specialty, AXIS, and Mosaic Insurance, collectively representing roughly $265B in gross written premium. The company raised a $30M Series B in January 2026 and operates from offices in New York City and Lloyd's of London. Sixfold is the named provider behind these capabilities and is distinct from Cytora, a separate UK-based insurance AI provider. The platform is sold as enterprise SaaS to insurance carriers; there is no public self-serve developer portal, public API reference, SDKs, or open-source release — API integration is delivered under enterprise engagement.

providers.name: Subset
providers.description: Subset is an AI-powered spreadsheet editor built for finance professionals, letting them generate P&L statements from PDFs, build DCF and returns models, and process CIMs and teasers through natural-language instructions inside a familiar spreadsheet interface. Built in NYC and SF by former Wall Street professionals, Subset targets investment and financial-modeling workflows. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Subset ships a consumer/prosumer web application and help documentation but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Sylvera
providers.description: Sylvera is a London-headquartered carbon data and climate intelligence platform — often described as the "Moody's for the voluntary carbon market" — providing independent ratings, market data, and geospatial analytics that help corporate buyers, investors, project developers, governments, and standards bodies make informed decisions across carbon and commodities markets. Founded in 2020 by Allister Furey and Samuel Gill, Sylvera combines remote sensing, machine learning over satellite imagery and LiDAR-derived biomass data, and on-the-ground project assessment to produce letter-graded ratings (e.g., AA, A, B) for carbon credit projects across nature-based (REDD+, ARR, IFM), engineered removals, renewable energy, and cookstove methodologies. The platform's product surface spans Ratings, Market Intelligence (supply, demand, and pricing signals), an Article 6 & CORSIA Hub for compliance risk, a Market Gateway to roughly 400 million tonnes of project inventory, Earth Analytics and a Biomass Atlas for geospatial MRV, and Commodity Insights covering CORSIA, LCFS, CFR, and FuelEU Maritime mechanism eligibility and carbon intensity assessments. Sylvera distributes its data through a web platform, downloadable reports, and a gated Carbon Credit Analytics API (base URL https://api.sylvera.com/v1, JSON API style, API-key auth) used to syndicate ratings and pricing into ESG and sustainability reporting tools such as Workiva, Persefoni, and Watershed. Commercial packaging runs Freemium, Essentials, and Enterprise tiers, with Accelerated Ratings, Market Forecasts, and Geospatial add-ons all sold via contact-sales; there is no public OpenAPI specification, no published SDK, and no Sylvera GitHub organization — the API and full ratings catalog are available only to authenticated enterprise customers.

providers.name: Tepali
providers.description: Tepali is an AI-native operating system for medical spas and aesthetic and wellness practices. It replaces fragmented point solutions with a single system of record, combining marketing intelligence, online scheduling, team management, patient CRM, clinical charting, and inventory. AI agents handle front-desk phone calls around the clock, generate real-time patient documentation such as SOAP notes, treatment summaries, and consent forms, and convert inbound leads into booked appointments. Founded in 2026 and backed by Y Combinator (W26), the company is headquartered in New York City. Tepali currently ships a hosted web application at app.tepali.com and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Tierra Biosciences
providers.description: Tierra Biosciences is a San Leandro, California synthetic biology company using AI-guided, cell-free protein production to synthesize custom proteins on demand for pharmaceutical, industrial, and agricultural research. Its customer-facing Tierra Protein Platform is a web-based eCommerce ordering portal where researchers enter protein sequences and get custom proteins synthesized, validated, and shipped. The company (rebranding toward Revr Bio) is backed by prosus-ventures and Material Impact. No public developer API, SDK, or programmatic-access surface is currently published; this profile was enriched and confirmed as a web-platform-only provider.

providers.name: Use Cases
providers.description: A curated collection of practical API use cases across industries and technical domains. Use cases describe specific scenarios where APIs solve real-world problems, improve workflows, and enable integrations. This repository indexes use case patterns across industries including fintech, healthcare, retail, logistics, and enterprise software, helping API producers and consumers understand how APIs deliver value.

providers.name: Whisperr, Inc.
providers.description: Whisperr, Inc. builds an autonomous customer-retention platform that detects churn risk and acts on it automatically, without a lifecycle marketing team operating campaigns. Whisperr combines behavioral intelligence, autonomous decisioning, and AI-generated content to spot at-risk customers and deliver interventions in under ten seconds, going live in under thirty minutes. It serves SaaS, DTC and subscription-commerce, and mobile-game businesses, and publishes churn calculators plus a voice retention agent (Whisperr Recall). Whisperr is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; it is a product/marketing web application.

providers.name: WPX Energy
providers.description: WPX Energy was an independent oil and gas exploration and production company focused on the Permian and Williston basins. In 2021, WPX Energy completed a merger with Devon Energy Corporation to form one of the largest independent oil and gas producers in the United States. As a result of the merger, WPX Energy no longer operates as a standalone company and does not maintain a public developer API. WPX Energy data is available through financial data providers such as Intrinio and through Devon Energy's current platforms.

providers.name: Yo Fio
providers.description: YoFio is a Mexican fintech founded in 2019 that provides working-capital credit to micro and small businesses, particularly neighborhood corner stores (tienditas). Through a mobile app and web platform it offers revolving credit lines of 7,000 to 200,000 Mexican pesos with up to 14 days of interest-free financing so merchants can restock inventory and pay suppliers. YoFio uses AI-powered machine-vision technology to assess creditworthiness from photos and videos of a store and its inventory, cutting the evaluation process to roughly 15 minutes. It is backed by 500 Global and Oikocredit, and serves thousands of businesses across the Valley of Mexico, Puebla, and Guadalajara. YoFio publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: 1047 Games
providers.description: 1047 Games is an independent video game studio best known for the arena shooter Splitgate and its follow-up title EMPULSE, a free-to-play movement shooter. Backed by Insight Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners, the studio ships games across PC (Steam), PlayStation, and Xbox. As a consumer game publisher it exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, legal, and community surfaces for the API Evangelist network. Added originally as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with live domain-security and identity probes.

providers.name: 51job
providers.description: 51job (前程无忧) is one of China's largest online recruitment and human resource services platforms, operated by 51job, Inc. Founded in 1998 and headquartered in Shanghai, the company connects job seekers and employers through its flagship 51job.com website and mobile apps, alongside enterprise hiring services (ehire.51job.com), campus recruitment, HR outsourcing, training, and assessment offerings. Formerly listed on NASDAQ under the ticker JOBS, 51job was taken private in 2022 by an investor consortium that included DCM, Ocean Link, and company management. 51job does not publish a public developer API or open platform; partner and applicant-tracking integrations (for example via SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting Posting) are arranged through its sales and support teams under contract. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and enriched from 51job's public web properties.

providers.name: Agility Robotics
providers.description: Agility Robotics is a Salem, Oregon humanoid robotics company building industrial bipedal robots for warehouse and factory automation. Founded in 2015 as a spin-out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Laboratory, its flagship product is Digit — described as the first humanoid robot in commercial production deployment — and Arc, the cloud-based automation platform that operates Digit fleets, provides real-time visibility, manages task assignments, and connects Digit to existing warehouse automation including AMRs, WMS, and WES systems. Digit has commercial deployments and pilots with Amazon, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre, with an expanded NVIDIA partnership for foundation-model and simulation tooling. Agility operates RoboFab, a humanoid robot factory in Salem, OR with capacity to produce 10,000 robots annually. Digit has surpassed 100,000 totes moved in commercial deployment at a single Georgia facility. Agility Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Digit or Arc; integration is performed by Agility's solutions team and partners through a gated low-level JSON-over-WebSocket API and pysdk delivered with the robot. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (JFrog, Bazel, Fluent Bit, Kubernetes Cluster API) plus an archived documentation repo for the earlier Cassie research platform.

providers.name: Air Protein
providers.description: Air Protein is a Bay Area food-technology company producing a nutrient-dense, meat-alternative protein made from elements found in the air. Its carbon-conversion fermentation process — derived from NASA closed-loop life-support research — combines carbon dioxide, oxygen, nitrogen, water and renewable energy with hydrogenotrophic microbes to grow a protein flour, which it then transforms into whole-food "air meat" products. Founded by CEO Dr. Lisa Dyson, the company aims to decouple protein production from land and animal agriculture. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV; it publishes a marketing site but no developer API surface.

providers.name: Aivar
providers.description: Aivar Innovations is an enterprise AI consulting and development firm that helps regulated and large organizations move agentic AI systems from pilot to scaled production. Alongside strategic AI consulting, custom AI development, managed AI/ML operations, data services, and cloud transformation, Aivar ships three accelerators: Convogent AI (autonomous voice and conversational agents in 16+ languages with sub-500ms latency), Velogent AI (governed agentic process automation for regulated industries), and Kubogent AI (enterprise AI infrastructure on Kubernetes). The company operates a professional-services model and does not currently publish a public, self-service API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Alta Resource Technologies
providers.description: Alta Resource Technologies is a Colorado-based deep-tech company reinventing how critical minerals are sourced. It uses advanced biochemistry — customizable, engineered proteins licensed from Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and co-developed with researchers at Pennsylvania State University — to selectively separate high-purity rare earth elements and other strategic metals from low-grade ores, mining tailings, and electronic-waste streams such as end-of-life hard disk drives. The protein-based platform binds target elements out of complex, low-concentration solutions with high selectivity while dramatically reducing the environmental footprint of conventional mining and refining, strengthening U.S. and allied critical-mineral supply chains. Alta emerged from stealth in January 2025 and expanded its Series Seed to $10M, backed by DCVC, Voyager Ventures, In-Q-Tel, and Orion Industrial Ventures. As a materials-science and biochemistry company, Alta does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this API Evangelist profile carries its identity and website properties only.

providers.name: American Operator
providers.description: American Operator acquires small businesses from retiring owners and pairs them with vetted operators through an operate-to-own model, where operators begin with a 10% stake on day one and follow a defined path to majority ownership. The company runs an "Exit Confidently" program that gives retiring owners all-cash closes, and supports its operators with hands-on guidance, industry advisors, and a governance structure. Backed by 8vc, American Operator publishes a marketing and applicant website but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface as of this profile.

providers.name: AmpMe
providers.description: AmpMe is a mobile application that synchronizes music playback across multiple smartphones to create a collective, portable sound system. Users connect friends' phones together so their device speakers play the same track in sync, amplifying the audio for parties and gatherings. The app supports streaming sources such as Spotify, YouTube, SoundCloud, and Deezer, and runs natively on iOS and Android. AmpMe was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it is a consumer mobile product that does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Answers.com
providers.description: Answers.com is a consumer question-and-answer and reference website where visitors ask questions and get instant answers across trivia, science, history, and everyday topics, increasingly blended with AI-personality chat, flashcard makers, study guides, and a math solver. It operates as a content and reference destination rather than a developer platform, and the enrichment pipeline found no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile is retained as a company record in the API Evangelist network; the only machine-verifiable artifact is a live domain-security probe of the answers.com host.

providers.name: Anto Biosciences
providers.description: Anto Biosciences is a frontier biology AI lab making the gut microbiome computable for the first time. It builds foundation models for microbial communities and quality-aware, goal-directed sparsification algorithms that filter noise from microbiome data to predict how the gut microbiome affects drug efficacy, toxicity, and safety across diverse populations (by geography, age, and diet). Applications include population-specific drug response prediction, identifying failure mechanisms at the microbial metabolic-pathway level, and molecule optimization for broader effectiveness. Backed by Y Combinator, the company is early stage and research-focused; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or a GitHub organization. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and enriched with verified identity links only (no API artifacts, none published).

providers.name: ApniBus
providers.description: ApniBus is an India-based online bus ticket booking platform that lets travelers search routes, compare operators, select seats, and pay for tickets across government and private bus services. It positions itself as a leading Indian bus-booking marketplace and an official RSRTC (Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation) booking partner, aggregating over one lakh bus services across thousands of routes. The consumer experience spans a website and Android/iOS apps, with UPI, cards, net banking, and wallet payments, instant e-ticket / m-ticket confirmation, live bus tracking, and easy cancellation. ApniBus was surfaced as a portfolio company of Version One Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer or API program at this time.

providers.name: Aptos Orbital
providers.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Ara
providers.description: Ara is a digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising network that finances, installs, and operates rich-media displays across mobility, municipal, parking, and retail settings. It describes itself as the largest U.S. owner-operator of rideshare and taxi car-top digital billboards, running a long-term partnership with Uber alongside in-car, storefront, and parking/municipal kiosk screens. Ara owns the hardware and content-management operations under a subscription model so partners avoid cap-ex and operational overhead. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio/enrichment lead.

providers.name: Aspect Biosystems
providers.description: Aspect Biosystems is a Vancouver, British Columbia biotechnology company developing Bioprinted Tissue Therapeutics — implantable, allogeneic living tissues designed to replace, repair, or supplement biological function in the body. Spun out of an interdisciplinary medicine-and-engineering collaboration at the University of British Columbia in 2013, the company operates a self-described full-stack tissue therapeutic platform that integrates proprietary AI-powered microfluidic bioprinting, computational tissue design tools, therapeutic and hypoimmune-engineered cells, and advanced biomaterials. Its clinical pipeline targets metabolic and endocrine disease, led by pancreatic tissue programs for type 1 diabetes and programs in rare endocrine disorders and liver disease. Aspect has raised more than US$350M, including a US$115M Series B, and holds partnerships with Novo Nordisk (announced 2023, valued at over US$2.6B in milestones) and the governments of Canada and British Columbia. It is a private, pre-commercial therapeutics developer: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Bachatt
providers.description: Bachatt is a daily savings and investments mobile app operated by Trusave Fintech Private Limited, designed for India's underserved and self-employed population. As an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor, Bachatt lets users save from as little as INR 100/day and invest in liquid mutual funds (Insta Fund) with instant withdrawal, curated mutual fund baskets (Bachatt Wealth), gold and silver mutual funds, fixed deposits, and access instant personal and business loans (Insta Loans) up to INR 5 lakhs. The company partners with major AMCs including SBI, ICICI Prudential, Axis, and HDFC and delivers everything through a single UPI-powered mobile application on Android and iOS. Bachatt is backed by Accel. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Bachatt is a consumer fintech app and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Behance
providers.description: Behance is Adobe's online creative networking and portfolio platform where designers, illustrators, photographers, and other creatives showcase, discover, and follow creative work through project-based portfolios. Founded in 2005 by Matias Corea and Scott Belsky, it was acquired by Adobe in 2012 for roughly $150 million and is now tightly integrated with Adobe Creative Cloud and Adobe Portfolio. Behance passed 24 million members by 2020. Adobe has since retired the former public Behance REST API, so the platform no longer exposes a documented public developer program; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record.

providers.name: Benson Hill *
providers.description: Benson Hill (now operating as Confluence Genetics at confluence.ag) is a seed-innovation company that develops high-protein, energy-dense soybean varieties using AI-driven plant science and advanced crop genetics. Its soy solutions serve three markets — animal feed, human food, and renewable fuel — pairing proven genetics with technology and environmental responsibility. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; the company has since rebranded from Benson Hill to Confluence Genetics and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Blank Street
providers.description: Blank Street is a consumer coffee and beverage retailer that began in 2020 as a single 5x10 coffee cart in Brooklyn and has grown into a global brand operating roughly 90+ locations across the United States and the United Kingdom, serving seasonal specialty drinks such as matcha and espresso beverages. The company emphasizes convenience through mobile ordering and a loyalty rewards program via its consumer app, alongside merchandise and gifting. It is backed by General Catalyst and Tiger Global and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Blank Street publishes a consumer web and mobile experience (rewards, ordering, shop, locations, help center) but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or specification surface at this time; this profile captures its public web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Blind
providers.description: Blind (teamblind.com) is an anonymous professional community platform where verified employees discuss compensation, interview experiences, layoffs, company culture, and career decisions while preserving their anonymity through work-email verification. The platform organizes conversation into company channels, industry topics, and location-based feeds, and runs on a freemium model with a For Business offering. It operates primarily as a consumer mobile and web app; no public developer API, developer portal, or well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment (all /.well-known/* probes returned 404). Sector: consumer / professional social network. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures.

providers.name: Blue Wire
providers.description: Blue Wire is a podcast network and monetization platform built for independent sports content creators, positioning itself as "The Monetization Engine for Sports Creators." The company provides sales, marketing, distribution, and operational support so creators can focus on producing content while Blue Wire handles ad sales and sponsorship coordination across a network of 200+ shows and 500+ creators reaching hundreds of millions of listeners. Backed by 500 Global. Blue Wire operates as a media and advertising business and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bonobos
providers.description: Bonobos is a US menswear brand and direct-to-consumer e-commerce retailer, founded in 2007 and known for pioneering online-first apparel sales alongside its physical "Guideshop" fitting-room locations. It sells men's clothing including pants, chinos, dress shirts, suits, and casualwear through bonobos.com. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel, Felicis and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it is a consumer-sector retail company. Bonobos publishes a public retail website but does not operate a public developer API program; this profile captures its real published surface (identity, legal, support, and domain-security posture).

providers.name: Breezy
providers.description: Breezy is a Los Angeles-based proptech startup building what it calls the first independent AI operating system for residential real estate. Founded in 2024 by top-producing agent James Harris alongside Afterpay co-founders Nick Molnar and Anthony Eisen, the mobile-first app consolidates an agent's workflow — comparable market analysis (comps), AI meeting notes, deal-pipeline management, client insights and an AI assistant — into a single workspace, and adds an "UnderBuilt Radar" that uses zoning, geospatial and setback data to flag properties with unrealized development potential across 1,200+ cities. Breezy raised a $10M pre-seed led by Ribbit Capital with participation from Fifth Wall, DST Global Partners, Liquid 2 Ventures, O.G. Venture Partners, Fidji Simo and David Marcus. The company exposes no public developer API today; this profile tracks it as a Fifth Wall portfolio lead.

providers.name: Bright View Technologies
providers.description: BrightView Technologies, Inc. is a Durham, North Carolina optical film company specializing in computational optics and the design and manufacture of Micro Lens Array (MLA) solutions that shape, diffuse, and manage light. Founded in 2002 on intellectual property licensed from Duke University, the company engineers precision optical films and micro-optical structures used in automotive displays, head-up displays, and LiDAR; consumer and mini/micro-LED displays (gain enhancement and LED-hiding films); LED and architectural lighting (beam shaping and diffusion); and augmented- and virtual-reality beam-shaping optics. BrightView is a hardware and materials manufacturer serving OEMs and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead of Battery Ventures and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Burnbot
providers.description: Burnbot is a wildfire mitigation and fuels management company that builds autonomous, remotely-operated machines and delivers field services to reduce hazardous vegetation and conduct controlled, precision fuel-reduction burns. Its equipment operates in steep, remote, and hazardous terrain around the clock in most weather conditions, cutting fuel loads without disturbing healthy vegetation or compacting soil, and is used across fire hazard mitigation, systematic fuels management, and timber operations. Burnbot works with utilities, transportation agencies, land managers, and tribal governments including PG&E, Caltrans, the U.S. Forest Service, and CAL FIRE. Burnbot was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a hardware and field-services company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Bustle
providers.description: Bustle is the flagship lifestyle and culture publication of Bustle Digital Group (BDG), a New York-based digital media company that moves culture forward through premium editorial content, social storytelling, and live experiences. BDG operates a portfolio of eight brands - Bustle, NYLON, Scary Mommy, W Magazine, Inverse, The Zoe Report, Romper, and Elite Daily - spanning lifestyle, fashion, parenting, entertainment, and luxury. The company produces award-winning branded content and campaigns through its BDG Studios and BDGx experiential arm. Bustle is a consumer media publisher rather than an API provider; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead, and no public developer API or specification has been identified on its properties.

providers.name: Camp
providers.description: CAMP is a family experience company operating immersive, rotating themed retail-and-play venues ("The Family Experience Store") across eleven U.S. markets — Atlanta, Boston, Charlotte, Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, Miami, Minneapolis, New York City, Philadelphia, and Washington D.C. It blends hands-on crafts, counselor-led immersive activities, character meet-and-greets, birthday parties, and a curated toy retail store both in-store and through its online shop. CAMP is a venture-backed consumer brand (investors include Bullpen Capital) and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Carter's
providers.description: Carter's, Inc. is the largest branded marketer of young children's apparel in the United States, operating the Carter's, OshKosh B'gosh, and Skip Hop brands. Its customer-facing digital surface includes carters.com and carters.com/cart e-commerce, mobile apps, a rewards program, and vendor / supply-chain integrations, but no public developer API or partner program is currently published.

providers.name: Cider
providers.description: Cider is a global direct-to-consumer digital-first fashion brand geared toward Gen Z shoppers, founded in 2020 and operating primarily at shopcider.com and through its mobile apps. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), DST Global, and Greenoaks Capital, Cider reached unicorn valuation as a fast-fashion challenger to SHEIN, using a data- and community-driven, on-demand manufacturing model to offer trend-forward women's clothing and accessories worldwide. Cider is a consumer retailer; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Cinemark Holdings
providers.description: Cinemark Holdings is one of the largest motion picture exhibitors in the world, operating theatres across the United States and Latin America under the Cinemark, Century, Tinseltown, Rave, and CineArts brands. Cinemark does not currently publish a general-purpose public developer portal; ticketing, showtime, and loyalty integrations are typically delivered through partner agreements and third-party aggregators (Movio, Atom Tickets, Fandango).

providers.name: Cintas
providers.description: Cintas Corporation is a Fortune 500 provider of uniform rental, facility services, first aid and safety products, and fire protection services. Cintas does not currently publish a public developer portal; B2B integrations (ordering, EDI, route management, billing) are delivered to enterprise customers through the myCintas portal, the Cintas Partner Connect program, and account-managed EDI relationships.

providers.name: Cohere Technologies
providers.description: Cohere Technologies is a San Jose, California wireless communications software company developing spectral-efficiency technology for mobile networks. Its Universal Spectrum Multiplier (USM) software delivers a 2x spectrum multiplier for 4G, 5G, and Multi-G networks across FDD and TDD bands, and its Pulsone technology applies the Zak-OTFS (Orthogonal Time Frequency Space) waveform to Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) and Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN). The company sells to mobile network operators and Open RAN ecosystems and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, NEA, Telstra Ventures, Intel Capital, Koch Investments Group, VMware, and Juniper Networks. Cohere Technologies is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Collabra
providers.description: Collabra (Collabra Pty Ltd, ABN 35 672 933 818) is an Australian enterprise AI automation company whose platform combines robotic process automation with large language models to run back-office operations — contract review, revenue assurance, financial operations, vendor management, data processing, and compliance monitoring. Its product suite is CollabraCore (isolated, segmented data-protection workspaces), CollabraGuard (an AI-safety layer that constrains LLM output to prevent hallucinations and errors while logging every action), and CollabraFlow (a rapid build-test-deploy environment for automation workflows). The public tagline is "AI you can trust to run your operations". As of this profile Collabra is a demo-led SaaS with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Collectiv Food
providers.description: Collectiv Food is a next-generation B2B food wholesaler serving professional kitchens across the UK and France. Launched in London in 2022, it combines collective buying power, consolidated deliveries, and direct sourcing through a shortened, patented supply-chain model to supply restaurants, hotels, and caterers with meat, fish, plant-based proteins, dairy, produce, dry and frozen goods, and prepared items. The company emphasizes traceability, responsible sourcing, and sustainability, and is B-Corp certified with an EcoVadis Gold rating. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public API or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Collision (now Web Summit Vancouver)
providers.description: Collision was the major annual North American technology conference organized by Web Summit, held in Toronto from 2019 through 2024 and widely dubbed the "Olympics of Tech." Beginning in 2025, the event was relocated to the Vancouver Convention Centre and rebranded as Web Summit Vancouver, aligning with the global Web Summit family (Lisbon, Rio, Doha, Qatar). Web Summit Vancouver is contracted through at least 2027 and was held May 27-30, 2025; Web Summit Vancouver 2026 is scheduled for May 11-14, 2026. The Collision brand is retired but this profile is preserved for historical reference. Collision/Web Summit does not publish a public developer REST API; the conference operates speaker, partner, attendee, and press portals.

providers.name: Comento
providers.description: Comento is a South Korean career development and mentoring platform based in Seoul that connects job seekers with working professionals. The service offers a Q&A community and timeline for career discussions, free unlimited mentoring questions answered by industry practitioners, resume and cover letter (자기소개서) review, an AI resume analyzer, interview preparation, and job-focused educational programs including bootcamps (직무부트캠프) and classes for the Korean job market. It also runs corporate training and university affiliation partnerships. Comento operates as a consumer-facing web platform and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched with the domain and identity signals that are publicly observable.

providers.name: Continual
providers.description: Continual was an operational-AI / MLOps platform for the modern data stack, founded by Tristan Zajonc (previously Sense, acquired by Cloudera) and Tyler Kohn (co-founder of RichRelevance). It let data and analytics teams declaratively build, deploy, and continuously maintain production predictive models directly inside cloud data warehouses — Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery — using SQL and dbt as the primary interface rather than bespoke ML pipelines. The company raised a seed round led by Amplify Partners and a $14.5M Series A in 2022. The product is now dormant: continual.ai is a parked single-page shell, the documentation host redirects to the homepage, and the last release of the first-party Python CLI + SDK on PyPI was in March 2023. This profile captures the verifiable public artifacts that remain — the PyPI package, the GitHub organization, and a live domain-security posture.

providers.name: Cosmart
providers.description: Cosmart is an Indonesian membership-only B2B e-commerce and procurement platform, founded in 2021 by Alvin Kumarga and Robert Tan, where members (individuals and SMEs) purchase their recurring daily and business needs in larger quantities at competitive prices. The platform lists over 100,000 products across categories including office supplies, electronics, household items, automotive parts, industrial equipment, furniture, and services, with nationwide delivery, flexible payment terms, and dedicated relationship managers for corporate clients. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Lightspeed India Partners. Cosmart does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Coveti
providers.description: Coveti is a curated luxury fashion marketplace that connects consumers with independent designers and exclusive heritage boutiques across Milan and Paris through what it calls "Agentic Commerce" - AI-powered personal styling. Its Fashion Agent builds looks for specific occasions, while The Blind Network sources from 500+ boutiques, offering global shipping to 190+ countries, duty handling, custom 3D shoe design, and private client concierge services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Crema
providers.description: Crema.co is an online specialty-coffee subscription platform and curated marketplace that connects coffee drinkers with independent roasters. Customers take a preference quiz, pick a delivery cadence ranging from every few days to monthly, and receive freshly roasted beans by mail from a rotating selection of more than a thousand coffees sourced from dozens of small-batch roasters. Crema also runs a workplace coffee program for offices. This is a consumer e-commerce brand with no public developer API or developer platform; the repository is retained in the network for completeness and provenance.

providers.name: Crossfit
providers.description: CrossFit is a fitness brand and training methodology built around constantly varied, high-intensity functional movements that combine strength, conditioning, gymnastics, and weightlifting. The organization operates a global network of independently owned affiliate gyms, delivers a coaching certification and education program (the Level 1 through Level 4 courses and specialty seminars), and produces the annual CrossFit Games competition season. CrossFit was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer and affiliate web presence (gym finder, courses, store, Games results) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition.

providers.name: Daleela
providers.description: Daleela, by MotherBeing, is an AI-powered women's health application for the MENA region that combines medically-verified guidance with clinical services. The app offers a privacy-first AI health assistant whose answers are reviewed and approved by women's-health specialists, period and cycle tracking that monitors menstrual cycles and hormonal phases with personalized lifestyle recommendations, on-demand doctor consultations connecting users with specialists in gynecology, dermatology, nutrition, and sexual health within 24 hours, and expert-led educational programs covering hormones, fertility, and fitness. Daleela is distributed as a consumer mobile application on iOS (App Store) and Android (Google Play). It is a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as a consumer mobile product it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Dazzle AI
providers.description: Dazzle AI is an early-stage, pre-launch artificial intelligence company backed by Forerunner Ventures, with the stated mission of closing the gap between what people want and what they can do with AI. As of mid-2026 the product is invite-only: the public site collects waitlist sign-ups and publishes About, Jobs, Press, Support, Terms of Service, and Privacy Policy pages, but exposes no developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Demander Justice
providers.description: Demander Justice (demanderjustice.com) is a French legal-technology company that lets everyday people (justiciables) resolve disputes and take a matter to court without hiring a lawyer. Through simplified, guided online procedures it helps users send formal notices (mise en demeure), file injonctions de payer, and bring cases before the relevant French courts across consumer, housing, telecom, travel, banking, neighbor, and small-claims disputes. The service combines legal information fiches with a step-by-step document-generation and court-filing workflow. Backed by Partech; profiled in the API Evangelist network under the Consumer sector. No public developer/API surface was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: DeporPrivé
providers.description: DeporPrivé is a Mexico-based sports e-commerce platform operating as a members-oriented "Sport Experience & Outlet" that runs flash sales and private, time-limited shopping events across more than 300 athletic brands including Adidas, Nike, and Salomon, with discounts reaching up to 70%. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Mexico, the company curates footwear, apparel, and accessories for running, cycling, swimming, football, and general fitness, and has grown into one of the largest sport-specific online retailers in the country, fulfilling around 1,000 packages per day across multiple sales channels. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer program, API, or documentation surface has been identified for this consumer retail brand.

providers.name: Digital Currency Group
providers.description: Digital Currency Group (DCG) is a cryptocurrency and blockchain holding and venture company founded in 2015 by Barry Silbert and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut. DCG builds, incubates, and invests in companies across the digital asset ecosystem, including subsidiaries such as Grayscale Investments and Foundry. It operates as an investor and parent company rather than a direct API provider; this network profile tracks DCG's public web presence and corporate surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures. Sector: fintech / digital assets.

providers.name: Divvy Homes
providers.description: Divvy Homes is a San Francisco-based proptech company operating a rent-to-own home ownership program. A customer chooses a home on the open market, Divvy purchases it, and the customer moves in as a renter while a portion of each monthly payment builds toward a future down payment, giving aspiring buyers who are not yet mortgage-ready a path toward eventual ownership. The consumer web experience integrates third-party services such as Plaid for bank connectivity and Stripe for payments, but Divvy exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface of its own. This profile was surfaced from venture-portfolio data (a16z, Threshold Ventures) and enriched from Divvy's public consumer website only.

providers.name: Doma
providers.description: Doma is a technology company transforming the mortgage closing process with an AI-first platform for title insurance, title and closing services, and title alternatives. Doma's technology aims to dramatically reduce the cost, time, and complexity of one of life's most confusing and expensive experiences—the mortgage process—serving lenders, mortgage brokers, real estate technology platforms, and homeowners. Doma is backed by Bloomberg Beta, Fifth Wall, and Uncork Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Dooly
providers.description: Dooly was a connected workspace for revenue teams that improved Salesforce CRM hygiene by syncing meeting notes, pipeline updates, and next steps back into Salesforce automatically. It layered a fast note-taking surface, deal vitals, real-time playbooks, and one-click CRM updates on top of Salesforce so account executives could keep their pipeline clean without manual data entry. Backed by Battery Ventures, Dooly was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. The Dooly platform was shut down on June 30, 2025; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and this profile captures the remaining public surface (website, privacy policy, terms) for the record.

providers.name: Doomersion
providers.description: Doomersion (doomlingo.ai) is a consumer mobile language-learning app that teaches languages by "doomscrolling" — a vertical, TikTok-style feed of short-form videos in the learner's target language, matched to their level, with clickable explainer subtitles that let you tap any word for an instant translation and grammar note. Founded by Mostafa Afr and backed by Y Combinator, the app ships on iOS and Android. Doomersion exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this record is an API Evangelist network company profile capturing its public web and identity footprint.

providers.name: Echo Labs
providers.description: Echo Labs is a San Francisco-based company building AI-powered media accessibility for higher education. Its platform audits, captions, and audio describes entire institutional video libraries within 24 hours, producing ADA / Title II and WCAG 2.1 AA compliant closed captions and audio descriptions at claimed accuracy above 99 percent and roughly $0.75 per minute — a fraction of legacy vendor pricing. Echo integrates with major learning management systems (7+ LMS platforms) so universities and colleges can bring existing course video into compliance at institutional scale. The company is SOC 2 certified, completed a pre-seed round, and is a Techstars portfolio company. This API Evangelist profile tracks Echo Labs as a company in the network; the provider does not publish a public API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Emerson Electric
providers.description: Emerson Electric is a Fortune 500 global automation leader with more than 135 years of innovation history. Its portfolio spans automation systems, discrete automation, final control, measurement instrumentation, and test and measurement, marketed through brands such as Fisher, Rosemount, DeltaV, Micro Motion, ASCO, Bettis, PACSystems, Flexim, and NI. Emerson serves industries including power, oil and gas, chemical, life sciences, food and beverage, automotive, data centers, mining, and marine. This repository captures the public APIs, developer resources, and machine-readable artifacts associated with Emerson Electric.

providers.name: Endless West
providers.description: Endless West is a Detroit-based molecular spirits manufacturer that applies food and molecular science to create alcoholic beverages without traditional distilling or aging. The company operates a TTB-approved production facility offering bulk base spirits and ready-to-bottle liquids, turnkey and private-label packaged brands, pre-made concentrates, and contract co-packing and bottling services for other brands and entrepreneurs. Its proprietary Glyph Molecular Spirit showcases a sustainability approach that reduces water usage and CO2 footprint versus conventional distillation. Endless West is a consumer-products and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface; this profile was surfaced as a Partech portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: enechain
providers.description: enechain operates the largest energy exchange in Japan, offering trading opportunities for wholesale electricity and environmental values across an over-the-counter marketplace that connects energy market participants. Headquartered in Tokyo, the company builds energy markets that help buyers and sellers discover prices, manage risk, and trade power and environmental-value products, under the mission "Building Energy Markets, Coloring Our Society." enechain was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures; it publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: EnerGaia
providers.description: EnerGaia is a spirulina producer, incorporated in Thailand in April 2009 and now headquartered in Singapore, that grows nutrient-dense microalgae in proprietary closed bioreactors rather than open ponds to deliver clean, consistent spirulina for food and beverage manufacturers. The company originated from research into using microalgae to capture industrial CO2 from power-plant flue gas and has since focused on making spirulina a mainstream, sustainable food ingredient. Its product line includes Fresh Spirulina Paste, Fresh-Frozen Spirulina, and Freeze-Dried Spirulina Powder, used in beverages, egg substitutes, noodles, meat replacements, pastas, and snacks. EnerGaia is a portfolio company of 500 Global. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Essence Ventures
providers.description: Essence Ventures is an independent, African American-owned media, technology, and commerce company focused on content, community, and commerce for Black women and their communities. Founded by Richelieu Dennis, it acquired Essence Communications (Essence magazine and the Essence Festival of Culture) in 2018, and its portfolio of lifestyle brands has included Afropunk, BeautyCon, and Essence Studios, reaching audiences across print, digital, video, social, and live events. Essence Ventures does not operate a public developer program or API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead awaiting further enrichment.

providers.name: Eventup
providers.description: EventUp is a global online marketplace and directory for event venues, operated by Tripleseat. It lists over 15,000 restaurants, hotels, breweries, rooftop bars, museums, libraries, and other unique spaces that people can browse and request quotes from for parties, weddings, corporate events, and meetings. Event planners and consumers search venues by city, capacity, event type, and amenities and submit free quote requests directly to venue owners, while venue owners list and market their spaces to receive booking inquiries. A companion product, EventUp Planner, adds marketing, planning, and analytics tooling. EventUp is a consumer-facing web marketplace and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or agent/MCP surface. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with the discoverability, identity, and domain-security signals that are publicly observable.

providers.name: EZR
providers.description: EZR (上海驿氪 / Shanghai Yike Information Technology) is a Shanghai-based retail marketing technology company founded in 2015 that builds SCRM and new-retail CRM software for multi-store and chain brands. Its platform combines a Marketing Cloud and in-store CRM to deliver omnichannel member management, WeChat mini-program malls, guide (导购) distribution and full-staff sales tools, live-streaming commerce, points malls, and campaign automation. EZR serves 800+ brands across fashion, beauty, home goods, food, and pharmacy, and is backed by Tencent, JD.com, DCM, and Lenovo Star. The company advertises an open platform of 100+ APIs covering products, users, transactions, and marketing, though it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or API reference.

providers.name: FANUC
providers.description: FANUC Corporation is a Japanese multinational headquartered in Oshino, Yamanashi at the base of Mount Fuji, and is one of the world's largest suppliers of factory automation, industrial robots, and CNC (computer numerical control) systems. Founded in 1972 after spinning out of Fujitsu's numerical control division (originated 1955) under Seiuemon Inaba, FANUC pioneered commercial NC and CNC technology and by the early 1980s held roughly half of the global CNC market. The company operates three primary business segments: FA (CNC systems, servo motors, lasers, and PMC controls for machine tools), Robot (industrial arms from the LR Mate and M-series through the heavy-payload M-2000iA, plus the CRX collaborative robot family), and ROBOMACHINE (ROBODRILL machining centers, ROBOCUT wire EDM, and ROBOSHOT all-electric injection molding machines). FANUC's primary developer surface is FOCAS (FANUC Open CNC API Specification), a licensed C/C++ library (fwlib32.dll) used by machine builders and MES/OEE vendors to read CNC state over Ethernet, plus KAREL and Teach Pendant (TP) programming on the robot controllers and a published ROS 2 driver for the CRX collaborative arms. FANUC does not operate a public REST developer portal or publish OpenAPI specifications; integrations are partner-driven through MTConnect adapters, OPC UA servers, FIELD system edge apps, and the FANUC America customer/training portals.

providers.name: favorited
providers.description: Favorited is a mobile-first live streaming platform that helps content creators run interactive, real-time shows with their audiences. The app centers on participatory formats — games, giveaways, and community interactions — so that viewers feel like they are playing together with a creator rather than passively watching a broadcast, alongside monetization tools for creators. Favorited ships as consumer iOS and Android apps and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment and monitoring.

providers.name: Felmo
providers.description: felmo (felmo GmbH) is a mobile veterinary practice (mobile Tierarztpraxis) headquartered in Berlin, Germany that brings licensed veterinarians directly to pet owners' homes for dogs and cats. Founded in 2019 by CEO Philip Trockels, felmo operates across Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Düsseldorf and 25+ additional German cities, and has treated 300,000+ animals with 8,000+ home visits per month via 140+ mobile vets. Services include preventive care and consultations, examinations and diagnostics, laboratory and imaging, surgical procedures (including a fully-equipped mobile operating vehicle / OP-Wagen), dental medicine and holistic pet care, billed per the German veterinary fee schedule (GOT). Customers book appointments, access medical records and lab results, receive reminders, and message support through the felmo iOS and Android app. felmo is backed by HV Capital and additional venture investors. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public identity and web properties.

providers.name: Finda
providers.description: Finda (핀다) is a South Korean fintech company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Seoul that operates a licensed online loan-comparison and financial-product marketplace. Through its mobile app and website, Finda lets consumers compare loan products from 76+ financial institutions and 400+ products in about a minute, refinance existing loans ("갈아타기"), aggregate accounts and cards for asset management, run financial calculators (interest, DSR, year-end tax, mortgage eligibility), and monitor and manage their credit. Registered as a loan-brokerage/loan-collection corporation under Korea's Financial Services Act, Finda earns commissions from partner financial institutions rather than charging consumers. It reports 3.47M+ cumulative members and 256T+ won in managed loan assets, and is backed by 500 Global. Finda is a consumer B2C platform and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Flashfood
providers.description: Flashfood is a Toronto-based mobile marketplace that connects shoppers with heavily discounted groceries nearing their best-by date at partner grocery stores across the United States and Canada. Through its iOS and Android apps, shoppers browse deals of up to 50% off on fresh produce, meat, dairy, and packaged goods, pay in-app, and pick the items up at a dedicated Flashfood Zone in-store. By routing surplus food away from landfills and onto dinner tables, the company reduces grocery-retail food waste while helping families save on their grocery bills. Flashfood is a consumer-facing app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface.

providers.name: Futureplay
providers.description: Futureplay is a Helsinki, Finland-based mobile game studio founded in 2015 that develops free-to-play games for a global audience, having released six titles for more than 120 million players including Merge Gardens, Battlelands Royale, and Idle Farming Empire. Backed by Creandum and now part of Plarium, the studio operates in the consumer gaming sector. Futureplay publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal; player-facing support runs through a Zendesk help center, and legal terms are hosted on the Plarium company site.

providers.name: Gatsby
providers.description: Gatsby is an open-source, React-based framework for building fast, secure, content-driven websites and applications using GraphQL data sourcing, static site generation (SSG), server-side rendering (SSR), and deferred static generation (DSG). Gatsby is now stewarded by Netlify, which acquired the company in 2023 and sunset the hosted Gatsby Cloud build and preview service, migrating customers to Netlify's unified platform. Gatsby itself is a build-time framework and does not expose a public hosted REST API; integrations are performed locally through its GraphQL data layer and plugin ecosystem.

providers.name: Gloset
providers.description: Gloset is a Mexican peer-to-peer marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned and new fashion — formal dresses, casual wear, handbags, accessories, footwear, jewelry, watches, sportswear, menswear, and swimwear. The platform offers a seller authentication program, curated collections and trending edits, buyer protection with returns and refunds, and integrated payments and shipping, operating primarily in Mexico. Gloset is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, API reference, or technical documentation surface — it is a consumer marketplace web/app product.

providers.name: Golden Child
providers.description: Golden Child is a direct-to-consumer pet wellness brand offering fresh, human-grade, vet-formulated dog food delivered on a subscription basis.
