Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Realm
providers.description: Realm is a consumer home-technology company that gives homeowners data-driven insights about their property's value and its renovation potential. The Realm platform combines public property records, permits, zoning, comparable sales, and neighborhood data into personalized recommendations that show which home improvement projects will add the most value, what they are likely to cost, and how they affect a home's estimated worth over time. Marketed at realmhome.com as "Home Renovation Planning & Home Value Insights," the product is delivered as a consumer-facing web and mobile experience rather than a developer platform. Realm was backed by venture investors including DCVC and GGV Capital and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Reflection AI
providers.description: Reflection AI is an artificial intelligence research lab building frontier open intelligence — open models that let anyone control their own intelligence and help shape the future of AI. Founded by former Google DeepMind researchers and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company frames its work as a path to superintelligence, sharing research and perspectives through its blog rather than a public developer product. As of this profile Reflection AI publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or MCP server; this entry captures the company's verified identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network and will be re-enriched if a developer surface appears.

providers.name: Reflection AI
providers.description: Reflection AI is a frontier artificial intelligence lab building "open intelligence" — releasing open model weights, publishing research, and open-sourcing an "Open Core AI Stack" of deployable containers and recipes so developers can customize and run their own agents. Its product surface spans Open Models (built for customization and long-term control), the Open Core AI Stack, and an "AI Factory" — the physical and operational infrastructure that runs the open-core stack at production scale. The company positions open systems as the path to faster innovation and broader participation in AI, and has publicized collaborations around sovereign AI and AI-factory deployments. As of this profiling pass Reflection AI publishes no public developer API, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification — it is a model/infrastructure company rather than an API provider. This profile was surfaced as a venture-capital portfolio company and enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline; no API surface was found to catalog.

providers.name: Resultid
providers.description: Resultid is an enterprise Operational Intelligence platform that connects what customers say, what teams do, and what operational data shows across every product, location, and service to surface hidden revenue opportunities. It ingests data from hundreds of sources - surveys, calls, CRM systems, reviews, and service records - and applies AI to identify the behavioral patterns that separate high-performing locations from underperformers, bridging the gap between well-measured technical operations and largely invisible human operations. The platform serves automotive, airlines, hospitality, financial services, and retail enterprises. Resultid is a Techstars-backed company; this API Evangelist profile was enriched from its public web presence, which today exposes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs - the product is delivered through an authenticated application.

providers.name: Riiico
providers.description: RIIICO is a Duesseldorf-based industrial software company building 3D-AI tools that digitalize the factory shop floor. Its platform turns reality scans (point clouds) of existing plants into CAD-ready, pre-classified 3D models, cutting 3D modeling time by up to 80% and accelerating factory retrofit, robot programming, and simulation. RIIICO integrates with NVIDIA Omniverse (OpenUSD) and Siemens Xcelerator, and counts Siemens, Volvo, and Schaeffler among its customers. It won the Siemens Inventors of the Year Award 2024 and is backed by Earlybird, PiLabs, and seed + speed. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Rita's Italian Ice
providers.description: Rita's Italian Ice is a Philadelphia-area founded franchise chain of frozen treat shops known for Italian Ice, Frozen Custard, Gelati, and Misto, operating approximately 550-590 locations across the United States under the tagline "Ice Custard Happiness." The brand is privately held under MTY Food Group (acquired 2021). Rita's maintains a consumer-facing loyalty mobile app and a franchise development site, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, webhooks, status page, or developer portal at this time. The loyalty program runs on the third-party Punchh customer engagement platform, and the mobile app was developed with Relevant Mobile; the only network-facing endpoint (api.ritasice.com) is a private backend for the consumer app and returns HTTP 403 to unauthenticated requests.

providers.name: Roboto Games
providers.description: Roboto Games is an independent video game development studio building Stormforge, an open-world survival crafting game where players craft, build, fight, and harness epic storms to survive in a magical fantasy world. The studio was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a consumer game studio, Roboto Games publishes a marketing website, a careers page, and a studio blog, but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface — its player-facing experience is delivered through native game clients (Steam) and community channels (Discord, YouTube, Twitch) rather than an HTTP API. This profile captures the studio's public identity and web properties; no API artifacts are produced because none are published.

providers.name: Rovio Entertainment
providers.description: Rovio Entertainment is a Finnish mobile game company founded in 2003 and headquartered in Espoo, best known for the Angry Birds franchise and a portfolio of casual and puzzle titles played by hundreds of millions of players worldwide. It operates game studios across Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Canada, Spain, and Turkey, and became part of Sega Sammy Holdings in 2023. Rovio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Atomico and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Rovio publishes a corporate/marketing website but no public developer portal, API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Schedex
providers.description: Schedex is a workforce management platform built for food and beverage businesses, consolidating staff scheduling, shift management, attendance tracking, and payroll into a single mobile-first application. It offers mobile clock in/out with location technology, schedule optimization across multiple locations, real-time labor-cost tracking and reporting, automated wage and payroll calculation, leave requests and shift exchange, and a multilingual branded app, with the goal of reducing labor costs by up to 15 percent. Schedex was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Scope
providers.description: Scope (Scope Inspection Ltd, London) is an AI-native inspection platform for the Testing, Inspection, and Certification (TIC) industry and heavy-asset operators. It captures field data through voice, video, and forms (offline-capable), extracts structured data from P&IDs, ASME forms, and inspection drawings, surfaces historical inspection context, and automates report generation in Word, Excel, and PDF. The product pushes results into enterprise CMMS/EAM systems via webhooks and prebuilt connectors, but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface at this time. Backed by Index Ventures and Y Combinator; raised a ~$18-20M round led by Index Ventures in 2026.

providers.name: Scoutzie
providers.description: Scoutzie is a Y Combinator-founded company (2012) led by Kirill Zubovsky. It launched as a curated marketplace connecting startups with top mobile designers and developers, operating from 2012 to 2020, and has since transformed into an AI-powered MVP (minimum viable product) development agency that builds and ships startup products in roughly two weeks. Today Scoutzie sells product-development services, an MVP Agent, founder training, and SEO consulting rather than a public developer API. It was surfaced through the a16z portfolio graph and enriched here as an API Evangelist network company profile.

providers.name: Secondmeasure
providers.description: Bloomberg Second Measure is an alternative-data analytics provider that turns billions of anonymized U.S. consumer transaction records into daily company- and sector-level performance signals for investors and corporate strategy teams. It tracks thousands of public and private companies with 8+ years of transaction history, offering configurable lag options (2-day, 3-day, 7-day) from card swipe. Following its acquisition by Bloomberg, its analytics and transaction-level data feeds are delivered primarily through the Bloomberg Terminal (ALTD <GO> and ECAN <GO>) and enterprise data feeds rather than a public self-serve developer API. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public API surface was found on the provider's site as of this pass.

providers.name: Sensei
providers.description: Sensei is an autonomous retail technology company that uses computer vision and artificial intelligence to enable checkout-free, "frictionless" shopping with no scanning and no queues, while giving retailers real-time inventory visibility and operational insights. It ships in four formats — Store (full-store), Pod (24/7 autonomous unit), Cabinet (plug-and-play), and Lane (human-assisted express checkout) — serving supermarkets, workplaces, mobility hubs, education, hospitality, leisure, and health/wellness venues. Founded in Portugal (HQ Castelo Branco, with Lisbon, São Paulo, and Milan offices), Sensei is a Techstars-backed company that works with retailers such as Continente, Conad, NOS, Muffato, and Galp and technical partners including Mastercard and HP. Sensei is a hardware and computer-vision provider and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation; engagement is demo-based ("book a demo") rather than developer self-serve.

providers.name: Sequen AI
providers.description: Sequen AI operates a Behavior Design Engine — an AI-powered ranking and real-time, in-session personalization platform for consumer applications. Its proprietary Large Event Models (LEMs) generalize user behavior from sparse event data (clicks, scrolls, hovers, purchases) to dynamically rank and re-rank product discovery, search, recommendations, and advertising with sub-20ms latency. Products include Sequen IQ (LEM-based ranking on purpose-built Sequen Ranking Clusters), Sequen Ranktune (model building and experimentation), and Sequen Rumi (analytics and behavioral-insight dashboard). The platform integrates via API with existing stacks. Sequen AI is backed by Threshold Ventures. No public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition are published at this time.

providers.name: Shibuya
providers.description: Shibuya is a platform for curated short films and the independent creators behind them, describing itself as a home where fans help greenlight the future of film and audiences discover original storytelling. Operated by NotShibuya, Inc. and backed by a16z, Shibuya began as a web3 storytelling experiment and has grown into a community-driven curation platform for short-form film, winning a 2025 Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Innovation in Emerging Media Programming. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Shibuya publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its real public web properties.

providers.name: Shiplyst
providers.description: Shiplyst is an India-based ocean freight procurement marketplace and supply-chain technology platform that lets exporters and importers search and compare container shipping rates from 50+ ocean carriers in real time, generate instant quotes, book containers with transparent pricing, and track cargo from pickup to delivery. The platform automates Bill of Lading and invoice generation and offers real-time tracking with exception alerts across its web and mobile apps. Shiplyst is backed by 500 Global. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Shoobs
providers.description: Shoobs is a UK-based online events discovery and ticketing platform focused on urban culture — Afrobeats, R&B, hip-hop, dancehall, comedy, theatre, festivals, brunches and club nights across London and other British cities. Founded as a Y Combinator-backed startup, Shoobs helps fans find and book tickets to events that match their taste, and lets promoters list and sell tickets for urban and Black-British cultural events. The platform pairs an events listing and discovery site with an integrated editorial blog covering artists, concerts and nightlife. Shoobs is a consumer web product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Simplywise
providers.description: SimplyWise is an AI-powered admin-automation platform for contractors, tradespeople, and small business owners. Its consumer mobile and web apps bundle a receipt scanner and expense organizer, an automatic mileage tracker for tax deductions, an AI-powered job/cost estimator, and an AI receptionist that answers inbound calls and messages. The company reports serving more than 1.2 million business owners. SimplyWise is a fintech-adjacent SMB productivity product backed by QED Investors; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, webhooks, or developer portal — the apps are consumer-facing only.

providers.name: Slingshot
providers.description: Slingshot is a self-custody, multi-chain DeFi application and wallet founded in 2020 and headquartered in San Francisco, letting retail users search, send, receive, and swap tens of thousands of cryptocurrencies at aggregated best prices with 0% swap fees. It is available on Web, iOS, and Android with bridging support across Ethereum Mainnet, Arbitrum, Arbitrum Nova, Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, and Canto. Backed by Electric Capital, Slingshot combined centralized-exchange ease with the openness of decentralized exchanges. NOTE: Slingshot announced it is sunsetting, advising users to export their private keys before February 28, 2026; its GitHub organization was archived in January 2026. This profile documents a consumer DeFi product that exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Solda.ai
providers.description: Solda.ai is an AI sales-agent platform that provides fully automated, autonomous sales departments powered by AI agents. Its voice- and text-based AI sales representatives execute the full sales cycle end to end, handling outbound cold outreach, inbound calls, follow-ups, callbacks, conversion optimization via A/B testing, and use cases such as credit-card and loan upselling, card activation, debt collection, and B2B lead qualification. The company markets primarily to banking and fintech customers and states compliance with SOC 2, HIPAA, and the EU AI Act. Solda.ai is a venture-backed company (Accel portfolio) headquartered in Middletown, Delaware. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a marketing site, blog, and legal pages, but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Springcoin
providers.description: Springcoin (operating as Spring Labs) is an AI-native compliance and customer-experience platform for financial services. It builds autonomous AI agents for contact centers, quality assurance, complaint handling, and dispute resolution, alongside SummerGRC, a governance, risk, and compliance product with entity intelligence and an agent builder. The platform integrates with 50+ contact-center and CRM systems and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or open documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Stack
providers.description: Stack is a spatial web browser that organizes the web as cards on a canvas rather than rows of tabs, built for keyboard-first, distraction-free browsing. Features include Fly Mode for fast navigation, multiple user profiles, customizable visual themes called realms, Chrome extension support, and privacy-focused browsing without ads or trackers, with multiplayer collaboration planned. Stack is a consumer desktop application and does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, or SDK. Backed by 500 Global and community-funded via WeFunder.

providers.name: StreetMetrics
providers.description: StreetMetrics is an out-of-home (OOH) advertising measurement, planning, and attribution platform that gives operators, agencies, and brands data-driven tools to plan campaigns, track delivery in near real-time across 1.6M+ OOH units, and measure business outcomes from outdoor advertising. Its SmartSearch planning intelligence surfaces unit-level performance and audience insights, daily-refreshed impression measurement tracks delivery, and attribution connects OOH exposure to website visits, app opens, and in-store lift. No public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation are published; access is delivered through the product platform (Intelligence, Measurement, Attribution, StreetCity) and verified partner operators.

providers.name: StudyEdge
providers.description: StudyEdge (Study Edge) is an education technology company that operates an online learning platform for students, delivering video courses, tutoring, and scheduled study sessions through a consumer web experience. The site organizes learning by school and subject with a Courses & Schedule catalog, a Help Center, and paid membership access, and is hosted on the Thinkific course platform with OpenID Connect sign-in for end users. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, StudyEdge is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal detected during enrichment.

providers.name: Sundae
providers.description: Sundae is a residential real estate marketplace that buys homes directly from homeowners for cash and resells them to a vetted network of property investors. Sellers get a competitive as-is cash offer with no repairs, showings, or fees, flexible closings in as little as 10 days, and an optional cash advance before closing; investors access off-market and distressed properties through the Sundae Marketplace. Backed by QED Investors, Sundae operates a consumer-facing website, an investor marketplace, and an agent referral program. It is a proptech/fintech company and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Suplari
providers.description: Suplari is an enterprise procurement intelligence platform that goes beyond spend analytics, using AI to clean, classify, and unify fragmented spend data across ERP, P2P, and spreadsheet sources. It delivers spend analytics, value orchestration, savings tracking, contract intelligence, and ESG intelligence, alongside procurement-specific AI agents (Suplari Worker, Assistant, and AI Studio) that integrate with SAP, Oracle, Workday, Coupa, Databricks, Snowflake, and Microsoft. Suplari was acquired by Microsoft in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: SVAcademy
providers.description: SV Academy is a tech-sales training and talent-placement organization that runs an intensive Sales Development Representative (SDR) program and places pre-trained, job-ready graduates with employers at no placement fee. It has trained more than 6,000 graduates across the U.S. and Canada and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. SV Academy serves two audiences — job seekers who complete the SDR training program with no prior experience or degree required, and employers who hire and onboard vetted, pre-trained SDR talent. The organization publishes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from SV Academy's public web presence.

providers.name: Sweater
providers.description: Sweater (سويتر) is a Saudi Arabian on-demand mobile car-care company that brings waterless vehicle washing, interior cleaning, detailing, and fragrance services to customers wherever their car is parked. Its app-based platform uses smart scheduling to dispatch field teams by location and uses roughly 7 liters of water per wash versus about 120 liters for traditional methods. The company reports 2M+ washes, 750K+ users, 500+ corporate partnerships, and operations across 8 Saudi cities (Riyadh, Dammam, Khobar, Jeddah, Jubail, Medina, Al-Hassa, and Mecca). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer/B2B services business with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Swiggy
providers.description: Swiggy is an Indian hyperlocal on-demand commerce and food-delivery platform founded in 2014 and headquartered in Bengaluru. Through a single consumer app it connects users with restaurant and merchant partners for food delivery, Swiggy Instamart (quick grocery and essentials commerce), Swiggy Genie (pick-up and drop errands), Swiggy Dineout (restaurant reservations and dining), and the Swiggy One membership program, operating across hundreds of cities in India with a large network of restaurant and delivery partners. Swiggy is a publicly listed company backed by Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners, Norwest Venture Partners and SoftBank Vision Fund. It exposes a login-gated merchant partner portal but does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Tarefa
providers.description: Tarefa (tarefa.co) is an online study companion — "tu compañero de estudio" — for Spanish-speaking university and high-school students, offering structured learning paths, solved exercises ("ejercicios resueltos"), video tutorials, and practice materials across mathematics (calculus, differential equations, probability and statistics, numerical methods), physics (electromagnetism, Newtonian mechanics, energy), and chemistry (inorganic, organic, gas laws, atomic structure, electrochemistry). It is a subscription-based B2C EdTech platform backed by 500 Global. Tarefa exposes no public developer API or documentation at this time; this profile captures its public web surface and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Taxscouts
providers.description: TaxScouts is a UK online tax-return and Self Assessment service that pairs individuals, sole traders, landlords and investors with accredited accountants to prepare, review and file their taxes with HMRC for a flat fee. Founded in London, TaxScouts was acquired by Taxfix and its taxscouts.com domain now redirects to taxfix.com/en-uk. The service is a consumer-facing web and mobile product with pricing tiers for one-off filing, optimisation with HMRC audit protection, and year-round accountant support. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation; this record captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Team8
providers.description: Team8 is an Israel-based venture group that both creates and invests in companies, operating as a company-building foundry alongside a traditional venture-capital fund. Founded in 2014 by veterans of Israel's elite military technology units, the firm builds and backs startups across four domains — Cybersecurity, Software Infrastructure, Fintech, and Digital Health — and believes the greatest successes emerge at their intersections. Team8 pairs founders with capital, deep operating expertise, a community of enterprise CISOs and executives, and a hands-on venture-creation methodology it calls "success by design." It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures Team8's corporate, portfolio, and insights web presence, surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: The Clorox Company
providers.description: The Clorox Company is a multinational consumer-goods manufacturer best known for its bleach, cleaning, and disinfecting brands as well as a broader portfolio that includes Pine-Sol, Liquid-Plumr, Glad, Kingsford, Brita, Burts Bees, and Hidden Valley. Clorox does not publish a public developer-facing REST API; integration with the company is handled through partner, supply-chain, and retail-EDI relationships rather than through a documented internet-accessible API. This profile records the company's web presence, careers/IR resources, and brand directory for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tilt
providers.description: Tilt is a consumer fintech mobile app for building and rebuilding credit. It offers cash advances of up to $400, a line of credit with potential limit increases, and three credit cards (Essentials, Motion, and Engage), evaluating applicants from real-time bank-linked financial data rather than credit history alone. The app adds credit-score monitoring with personalized tips, customizable budgeting and spend tracking, AI-assisted automatic savings, and on-time-payment rewards, for an $8/month subscription after a 14-day trial. Tilt is a consumer application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Tiyaro
providers.description: Tiyaro is an enterprise AI company whose product, DeepQuery, replicates complete business processes as AI agents that can be described in plain English. Rather than rules engines or brittle integration workflows, DeepQuery uses LLMs combined with enterprise-specific product and customer data to identify a solution strategy and execute it across multiple steps using built-in tools. Its flagship application targets customer support and IT service desks - an "IT SuperAgent" trained on hundreds of third-party product procedures that recommends and executes resolution steps for incoming tickets - alongside revenue-operations and sales/marketing automation use cases. The company was founded by a team that previously built an edge software stack for hosting AI applications, and is backed by General Catalyst. Tiyaro goes to market as an enterprise product engaged through a book-a-demo motion rather than a self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Trayd
providers.description: Trayd is a construction payroll, HR, and compliance platform built for commercial trade contractors and subcontractors. It automates certified and prevailing-wage payroll, union and multi-state compliance reporting, field and labor tracking, crew scheduling and dispatch, HR onboarding and benefits, and offers same-day pay, moving tens of millions of payroll dollars each week. Founded in 2022 (Y Combinator S23) and backed by Bloomberg Beta, Trayd operates a private SaaS and mobile application with no public developer API, documentation, or integration surface published at this time.

providers.name: turntable
providers.description: turntable (Turntable Labs) is a consumer social-music company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and union-square-ventures. The original Turntable.fm social listening service shut down in 2013 and its domain no longer resolves. The lineage lives on at Turntable Labs, which operates two consumer music products - Hangout (a social music-streaming and group-chat app at hangout.fm / hang.fm) and Turntable (a create-share-and-vibe GenAI music experience). No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation are published for any of these products - this is a consumer application, not an API provider. Enrichment probes (DNS, HTTP, site fetch) confirmed no developer surface as of 2026-07-21.

providers.name: Vartega
providers.description: Vartega is a Denver, Colorado-based advanced materials company that produces recycled carbon fiber (rCF) from post-industrial scrap as a sustainable, lower-cost drop-in alternative to virgin carbon fiber. Its product line includes EasyFeed Bundles for thermoplastic compounding, chopped carbon fiber in multiple lengths and sizings, and carbon fiber reinforced polypropylene and nylon pellets. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Vestris
providers.description: Vestris is an AI-powered platform that automates the real estate pre-closing process for mortgage title and closing operations. It uses browser agents to log into county tax portals, extract property records, parse purchase contracts, run tax calculations, generate title abstracts, and produce title commitments and closing documents. Positioned as "the AI processing unit for mortgage title and closing," Vestris aims to replace manual title searchers and accelerate property deal closing. The company is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup based in San Francisco. As of this profile it operates a product application (waitlist / demo access) with no publicly documented developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Vetic
providers.description: Vetic is a pet healthcare company in India operating a chain of full-service veterinary clinics and hospitals across 11 cities, paired with a consumer mobile app. Founded by Gaurav Ajmera (ex-COO OYO), Vetic offers in-clinic vet consultations, vaccinations, in-house diagnostics (blood work, X-ray, imaging, endoscopy), surgery, physiotherapy, 24/7 emergency and intensive care, grooming, an in-house pharmacy, pet supplies, pet insurance, video vet consultations, digital medical records, and 2-hour pet food delivery. It is a consumer (B2C) business with no public developer API surface at this time; this profile captures its public web and app footprint.

providers.name: ViralGains
providers.description: ViralGains is an advertising technology platform that collects consumer feedback directly within digital ad units as zero-party data, then combines that real-time, consented consumer input with its VoiceAlike AI to build higher-quality audiences and deliver more relevant, privacy-respecting advertising for brands and agencies. The platform spans zero-party data collection, brand lift measurement, and a dedicated health and pharma offering (VG Health). ViralGains was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and product website but no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Virtusa
providers.description: Virtusa Corporation is a global provider of digital engineering, IT consulting, and outsourcing services headquartered in Southborough, Massachusetts. Founded in 1996, the company helps enterprises across banking and financial services, insurance, healthcare, communications, media, and manufacturing modernize their technology through cloud, data, AI, and application engineering. Formerly publicly traded on NASDAQ (VRTU), Virtusa was acquired by Baring Private Equity Asia in 2021 and employs tens of thousands of engineers worldwide. Virtusa operates as a professional-services and delivery organization; it does not publish a public developer portal or external API program, so this API Evangelist profile captures its corporate and domain-security footprint rather than a consumable API surface.

providers.name: VulcanForms
providers.description: VulcanForms operates integrated digital metal manufacturing factories in the United States, combining in-house designed industrial-scale laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) additive machines, precision machining, automation, inspection, and proprietary AI-enabled software into a single end-to-end production workflow. The company produces mission-critical metal components at production scale for the aerospace, defense, medical, compute, consumer, and industrial sectors, compressing the supply chain into one secure, vertically integrated system. Headquartered in Devens, Massachusetts, VulcanForms is backed by Eclipse, 1789 Capital, D1 Capital and others. This profile currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: WePlayed
providers.description: WePlayed builds AI-powered short-form video for college athletics, automatically turning full game and event footage into shareable highlight clips that athletic departments, sponsors, and fans use to engage audiences and power sponsorship deals. A Techstars Sports Accelerator company that raised a $2 million seed round, WePlayed partners with SIDEARM Sports to distribute highlights across collegiate athletics websites. As of this profile WePlayed does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Whisper Aero
providers.description: Whisper Aero is a Crossville, Tennessee based aerospace company developing ultra-quiet electric ducted-fan propulsion that converts electricity into thrust with roughly 20 percent more efficiency and 20 dB less noise than conventional systems, scaling from 5 to 500 pounds of thrust and 40 to 400 knots for aviation, defense, and commercial applications. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Lux Capital, and Menlo Ventures. The company is a hardware manufacturer and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Wildlife Studios
providers.description: Wildlife Studios is one of the world's largest mobile game developers and publishers, founded in Brazil in 2011. It builds and operates free-to-play games played globally, with more than 4.7 billion downloads across a portfolio of over 60 titles including Zooba, Sniper 3D, Tennis Clash, War Machines, and Sky Warriors, and runs a publishing division for third-party studios. Wildlife is a consumer gaming company: its public surface is player-facing games and corporate/careers content, not a developer platform. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Wynn Resorts
providers.description: Wynn Resorts is a developer, owner, and operator of integrated luxury resorts and casinos, with properties in Las Vegas, Boston Harbor, and Macau. The company does not currently publish a public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Zyg
providers.description: ZyG is an agentic operating system for eCommerce scale that helps product inventors and direct-to-consumer (DTC) brands validate, scale, and finance their growth. Instead of stitching together fragmented tools and agencies, ZyG offers a unified, AI-agent-powered platform that turns great products into successful brands. The company pairs a data-driven ZyG Score with a pay-as-you-grow consumption model and cohort-based financing, positioning itself as a risk-reduction partner across the brand-building journey. ZyG is backed by Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Alamar Biosciences
providers.description: Alamar Biosciences is a precision proteomics company advancing early disease detection through its NULISA platform and ARGO HT System. NULISA (NUcleic acid Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay) combines a sequential immunocomplex capture-and-release mechanism with next-generation sequencing readout to deliver attomolar sensitivity and high-plex multiplexing for protein biomarker discovery, validation, and translational research. The fully automated ARGO HT System processes up to 288 samples per batch with under 30 minutes of hands-on time, supporting large-cohort studies across neurology, immunology, and oncology. Alamar was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a life-sciences instrument and assay provider rather than a public-API company, so this profile captures identity, published web surface, and domain-security posture. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface was found.

providers.name: Aliro Quantum
providers.description: Aliro Quantum (branded "Aliro, The Quantum Networking Company") is a Boston-based, Harvard spin-out building full-stack software for entanglement-based quantum networks. Its platform unifies three core products: the Aliro Simulator for physically accurate, optical-level modeling and validation of heterogeneous quantum networks before any hardware is deployed; AlirOS, a vendor-agnostic control-plane operating system that runs on quantum end-nodes and quantum repeaters across multiple hardware modalities; and the Aliro Orchestrator, a centralized single-pane-of-glass management system that configures, monitors, and operates quantum nodes and services through the full network lifecycle. These are packaged commercially as AliroNet — described by Aliro as the world's first end-to-end entanglement-based quantum network solution — delivered in three modes (Emulate, Pilot, and Deployment) and also available as AliroNet Quickstart, a bundled hardware-plus-software starter package that pairs third-party photon sources, detectors, memories, repeaters, and routers with Aliro's orchestration, control, and data operations software. The company markets Quantum-Powered Security as its anchor use case (Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later mitigation for telcos, utilities, financial services, and defense), alongside quantum-computing interconnects (clustered and blind quantum compute for cloud providers), networked quantum sensors for positioning/navigation/timing, and quantum position verification. Customers and design partners disclosed publicly include EPB of Chattanooga, Boeing, Cisco, the US Air Force, Brookhaven National Laboratory, Stony Brook University, and Noblis. Aliro is backed by deep-tech investors including Cisco Investments and Accenture Ventures, reports more than 50 third-party quantum networking devices already integrated with its stack, and operates with hardware-agnostic positioning across photonic, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and diamond-defect node technologies. There is no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or open-source repository — the AlirOS APIs referenced in Aliro's product materials are vendor-facing integration interfaces consumed under commercial engagement, and Aliro's GitHub organization carries no public repositories.

providers.name: Axoni
providers.description: Axoni is a New York-based financial data infrastructure company that provides real-time, automated replication of data between institutions, reducing reconciliations, data pipeline management cost, and operational risk across capital markets. Its platform lets banks, asset managers, and market infrastructure providers rapidly deploy critical financial networks and share post-trade data in real time. Axoni is used by leading institutions including JPMorgan, Deutsche Bank, BlackRock, and Citigroup, and has been recognized by Risk.net, the A-Team Group, and Forbes Fintech 50. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and is backed by a16z and DCVC. Axoni does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs; its documentation surface is access-gated to customers.

providers.name: Barinthus Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Barinthus Biotherapeutics plc (Nasdaq: BRNS) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel immunotherapies designed to guide and reprogram T cells to overcome autoimmunity, inflammatory disease, chronic viral infection, and cancer. Its lead SNAP-TI and SNAP-CI antigen-specific platforms and ChAdOx/MVA immunotherapeutic candidates power a five-program pipeline including VTP-1000 (celiac disease), VTP-300 (chronic hepatitis B), VTP-200 (high-risk HPV), VTP-850 (recurrent prostate cancer), and VTP-1100 (HPV-related cancer). The company was formed in 2021 through the merger of Oxford University spinout Vaccitech plc and NIH/Johns Hopkins spinout Avidea Technologies, and is headquartered in Germantown, Maryland with research facilities in the UK. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network. As a therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or agent surface.

providers.name: Bayesian Health
providers.description: Bayesian Health is a real-time clinical intelligence company whose adaptive AI platform monitors hospitalized patients continuously inside the electronic health record, surfacing only the patients who need attention and giving clinicians evidence-based guidance to act. Its flagship Targeted Real-Time Early Warning System (TREWS) reads full patient charts — labs, vitals, and clinical notes — to detect sepsis and other deterioration hours earlier while cutting alert volume, and in May 2026 became the first-ever FDA-cleared continuous AI sepsis monitor. Founded by Johns Hopkins professor Suchi Saria, the company deploys through direct EHR partnerships with Epic and Cerner rather than a public developer API, and is backed by a16z.

providers.name: Burlington Stores
providers.description: Burlington Stores is an American national off-price department store retailer offering brand-name clothing, footwear, accessories, home decor, and more at everyday low prices. Explore a wide selection of high-quality, brand-name clothing, home decor, and more at unbeatable prices at Burlington.

providers.name: ClearMotion
providers.description: ClearMotion is an automotive motion-technology company founded out of MIT in 2012 by Zack Anderson and Shakeel Avadhany, headquartered at its US innovation lab in Billerica, Massachusetts, with a UK engineering hub at MIRA Technology Park in Nuneaton, a Shanghai office, and a production plant in Changshu, China. Its CM1 fully active suspension system pairs the ActiValve digital hydraulic actuator with software that counteracts road disturbances in milliseconds, and its RoadMotion service is a crowdsourced, cloud-based road-surface intelligence layer that fuses data from vehicle sensors into a high-definition surface map accurate to better than 20mm, feeding proactive suspension, chassis and ADAS decisions. The company absorbed the Bose Ride and Project Sound active-suspension programs, is led by CEO Christian Steinmann, and ships with NIO (ET9, ES9) alongside collaborations with Porsche, BWI Group and Sona Comstar. Marketing material describes RoadMotion as an "end-to-end cloud API solution", but ClearMotion publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDKs or /.well-known discovery surface — the API is an OEM/B2B integration rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: CloudMinds
providers.description: CloudMinds (Dataa Robotics / 达闼科技) is a cloud-robotics company founded in 2015 with dual headquarters in Beijing, China and Irvine, California, backed by SoftBank and Foxconn. It builds cloud-connected smart machines and the HARIX ("Human Augmented Robot Intelligence with eXtreme reality") cloud AI robot brain, operating cloud robots over its Mobile-intranet Cloud Services (MCS) and Virtual Backbone Network (VBN). Its developer offering is the HARIX Robot Development Kit (RDK) — an app behavior blueprint editor, motion/dance editor, scene-map tools, and a robot simulation/training platform — distributed through the HARIX RDK portal, the HarixRDK GitHub organization, and the official "harix" Python SDK on PyPI. CloudMinds does not publish a public REST API; it exposes flexible APIs and middleware to integrate robots with legacy systems. Added to the U.S. BIS Entity List in May 2020.

providers.name: clounix
providers.description: Clounix (云合智网, Yunhe Zhiwang) is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Shanghai, with additional offices in Hangzhou, Nanjing, Beijing, and Chengdu. It designs high-end networking and communication silicon — high-performance programmable Ethernet switch chips, DPUs (Data Processing Units), and SmartNIC intelligent network cards — along with cloud-native infrastructure hardware and customized software for data centers and 5G networks. Its switch platforms run the open-source SONiC network operating system, and the company maintains a public GitHub organization with SONiC/SAI networking software. Clounix is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It currently publishes no public developer-facing API, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Cognito Therapeutics
providers.description: Cognito Therapeutics is a clinical-stage neurotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2016 out of MIT research by Ed Boyden and Li-Huei Tsai into the link between gamma-frequency neural oscillations and Alzheimer's disease progression. Its lead investigational product, Spectris, is a non-invasive at-home neuromodulation device that delivers synchronized 40Hz light and sound stimulation through a headset and glasses for one hour daily, evoking gamma activity to slow cognitive and functional decline in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. Spectris AD received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation in 2021, and the company closed an oversubscribed $105M Series C in March 2026 led by Morningside Ventures. Cognito Therapeutics is a medical device and therapeutics company: it publishes a corporate and clinical-information website and no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Dexory
providers.description: Dexory is a UK-based warehouse intelligence and robotics company whose DexoryView platform pairs fleets of autonomous mobile scanning robots with physical AI to deliver real-time "ground truth" visibility across warehouses and distribution centers. The robots autonomously scan more than 10,000 pallet locations per hour and up to 18 meters of racking height, building a live digital twin that feeds AI-driven analytics for inventory accuracy, space and slotting optimization, damage/compliance detection, and operational performance. DexoryView is organized into modules (Integrity for stock accuracy and automated cycle counts, Optimise for space and productivity analytics, and Adapt for real-time operational response) and connects into existing warehouse and ERP systems such as SAP EWM, Manhattan, Blue Yonder, and Körber through pre-built connectors. Dexory serves 3PL logistics, manufacturing, food & beverage, retail, pharma, and air cargo operators. Added to the API Evangelist network from Atomico's portfolio and enriched via the pipeline; Dexory does not currently publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Elligo Health Research
providers.description: Elligo Health Research is a healthcare-enabling clinical research organization (CRO) that embeds clinical trials directly into real-world healthcare settings. Through its proprietary IntElligo Research Stack and System of Accelerated Research (SOAR) model, Elligo connects sponsors and CROs to known, diverse patient populations across 115+ hospitals and health systems, 200+ healthcare-based sites, and 100+ research-based sites. Services span site networks, patient access and recruitment, decentralized and hybrid trial solutions, site support and staffing, and concierge patient retention and travel logistics. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Elligo is tracked as a portfolio-lead in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Ember
providers.description: Ember.js is a productive, battle-tested JavaScript framework for building modern web applications. It includes Ember CLI for scaffolding and builds, a best-in-class router with async data loading, the Ember Data layer, a three-level testing framework, the Glimmer rendering engine, and a six-week release cycle that emphasizes stability and easy upgrades through automated codemods.

providers.name: Firestorm
providers.description: Firestorm (Firestorm Labs, Inc.) is a San Diego based defense technology company founded in 2022 that builds expeditionary manufacturing systems and modular unmanned aerial systems. Its xCELL containerized production unit uses HP Multi Jet Fusion additive manufacturing to 3D print industrial-grade PA-12 nylon composite airframes and spare parts at the tactical edge, feeding modular UAS platforms including the Tempest fixed-wing family and the Squall FPV drone. The company holds a five-year, $100M U.S. Air Force IDIQ and closed an $82M Series B in April 2026 led by Washington Harbour Partners. Firestorm ships hardware, not software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Healx
providers.description: Healx is a Cambridge, UK clinical-stage biotechnology company that uses artificial intelligence to discover and develop new treatments for rare diseases. Its Healnet platform pairs generative AI with drug-discovery and rare-disease expertise to build a biomedical knowledge graph from public and proprietary sources - biomedical literature, disease and biochemical datasets, clinical trials and patents - and to identify novel uses for known compounds. Founded by David Brown and Tim Guilliams, Healx advances its own therapeutic pipeline (including its NF1 lead candidate HLX-1502) and partners with pharma companies such as Sanofi. Healx does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hinge Health
providers.description: Hinge Health is a San Francisco-based digital musculoskeletal (MSK) care company founded in 2014 by Daniel Perez and Gabriel Mecklenburg, delivering virtual physical therapy, pelvic health, and chronic pain care to enterprise health plans, employers, and their members. The platform combines on-demand exercise therapy with a multidisciplinary care team — physical therapists, health coaches, board-certified physicians, and orthopedic specialists — augmented by 3D motion tracking, computer vision, and an in-house AI Care Assistant. Hinge Health develops Enso, an FDA-cleared, drug-free wearable that delivers proprietary electrical stimulation waveforms for pain relief, and operates HingeConnect, an EMR/claims interoperability layer that ingests records from more than one million external providers across 120,000+ care sites to coordinate care, surface surgical and opioid risk, and feed real-time clinical context into the digital clinic. The company also runs HingeSelect, a national provider network for in-person MSK care, and contracts with all five major US national health plans plus employers including Boeing, Salesforce, and US Foods. Hinge Health raised more than $1 billion from Insight Partners, Tiger Global, Coatue, and Atomico before completing its IPO on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker HNGE on May 22, 2025, pricing at $32/share and opening at $39.25 for an initial market capitalization above $3 billion. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hinge Health, Enso, or HingeConnect — the platform is sold as a managed clinical service to health plans and employers, and the HingeConnect interoperability surface is operated internally rather than exposed to third-party developers.

providers.name: Let's Do This
providers.description: Let's Do This is an endurance-events marketplace where participants discover and register for mass-participation sport — marathons, road races, trail runs, triathlons, obstacle races and cycling events — across the United Kingdom and the United States. The platform covers event discovery, entry purchase and entry management, team entries, memberships, referral credits and discount codes, and it works with event organisers and charity partners who list and sell places through it. Backed by EQT Ventures. As of July 2026 Let's Do This publishes no public API program: there is no developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDK or webhook surface. A live but undocumented GraphQL endpoint backs the consumer marketplace with introspection disabled.

providers.name: Lily Camera
providers.description: The domain lily.camera currently serves "Lily Camera", a consumer-facing marketplace that connects clients with certified drone pilots for aerial photography and videography across real estate, events, agriculture, construction, and media production. It is a client-rendered single-page application: every requested path returns the same HTML shell, and the routes defined in its JavaScript bundle cover browsing pilots and drones, comparisons, bookings, messaging, a pilot dashboard, and a drone raffle. There is no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, no SDKs, and no /.well-known discovery surface. The site is built on Lovable (GPT Engineer), monetized with Google AdSense, and backed by a hosted Supabase project. No API artifacts could be harvested because the provider publishes none.

providers.name: Limbo
providers.description: Limbo is a direct-to-consumer digital weight-loss and metabolic-health program operated by Vitals in View, Inc., with subsidiaries in the UK (company no. 15047668) and Ireland (company no. 725671). Members wear a body-worn "energy sensor" that reads metabolic signals, and a companion app turns those readings into personalized, nudge-based guidance intended to change eating habits without calorie counting. The company is Seedcamp-backed, raised a seed round in September 2022, and is mid-rebrand from Limbo (limborevolution.com) to Viv (viv.co), with the marketing site now served from content.viv.co. Limbo publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and probed security posture only.

providers.name: LYST
providers.description: Lyst is a global fashion aggregation and shopping platform that consolidates products from more than 27,000 brands and retailers, connecting roughly 160 million annual shoppers with clothing, shoes, bags, accessories and jewelry across a single personalized, AI-driven catalog. Rather than a public developer API, Lyst exposes a partner surface: brands and retailers integrate via product-feed synchronization and a Stripe-powered "Lyst Shop" checkout, with API access granted privately during a two-week partner onboarding. Backed by Accel and Balderton Capital, Lyst also runs an engineering organization (making.lyst.com, github.com/lyst) best known for the open-source LightFM recommendation library.

providers.name: MDClone
providers.description: MDClone is a healthcare data company whose ADAMS platform gives health systems, life-sciences organizations, and researchers self-service access to explore, analyze, and share clinical data. Its signature capability is a synthetic-data engine that generates non-reversible, artificially created datasets which preserve the statistical characteristics and correlations of real patient data without carrying any protected health information (PHI), removing re-identification risk. The platform lets users organize source data, generate synthetic versions on demand, run analytics, and apply generative AI to accelerate research and improve patient outcomes. MDClone is enterprise/customer-gated: access, support, and any programmatic data-export API are provisioned to licensed customers rather than published as a public developer program.

providers.name: Osly
providers.description: Osly is an AI workflow automation platform (a product of Alore AI) that lets startups and prosumers build N8N-based AI workflows from natural language, with no coding required. Users describe automations in plain English to generate email sequences, lead categorization and personalized outreach, spin up internal dashboard UIs, and connect 50+ apps including HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Drive, Notion, LinkedIn and Shopify. Osly was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a marketing site and a hosted application, but no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Pharmaron
providers.description: Pharmaron is a life-science contract research, development, and manufacturing organization (CRO/CDMO) providing R&D services across the full drug-discovery and development pipeline for the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industry. Its services span laboratory research, chemistry, biology, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics, safety assessment, chemistry-manufacturing-and-controls (CMC), and clinical development for small molecules, biologics, and cell and gene therapies. Pharmaron operates globally with facilities in China, the US, and the UK and is publicly listed. It is a B2B partner to drug developers and does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Scalable Capital
providers.description: Scalable Capital is a Munich-based digital investment platform and licensed bank operating across Germany, Austria, Italy, France, Spain and the Netherlands. It offers a self-directed neobroker for trading stocks, ETFs, bonds, funds, crypto and derivatives, automated Wealth (robo-advisory) portfolio management, ETF and stock savings plans, an interest-bearing overnight cash account, and credit services. Backed by Balderton Capital and HV Capital, Scalable Capital serves retail investors through consumer web and mobile applications; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched via public-surface probes.

providers.name: Swordhealth
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital musculoskeletal (MSK) care provider that combines AI with licensed clinicians to deliver individualized physical therapy, chronic and post-surgical pain treatment, and pelvic and movement health programs to members from home. It sells primarily to employers and health plans, and in 2025 launched Sword360, a physical-health data platform. As of this enrichment pass Sword Health publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal; its public technical surface is a trust center (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR), a GitHub organization, and its member/clinician applications. Backed by Bond Capital and Khosla Ventures. Sector: healthtech.

providers.name: The Campbell's Company
providers.description: The Campbell's Company (formerly Campbell Soup Company) is an American manufacturer and marketer of branded convenience food products including soups, simple meals, beverages, and snacks. Major brands include Campbell's, Rao's, V8, Pace, Pepperidge Farm, Snyder's of Hanover, Lance, Cape Cod, Kettle Brand, Goldfish, and Prego. The company operates consumer-facing digital properties, an investor relations portal, a careers platform, and supplier resources, but does not publish general-purpose public APIs.

providers.name: Vedana Therapeutics
providers.description: Vedana Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation medicines for migraine prevention. Founded by biotech investor Anurag Agarwal and antibody-development veteran Leon Garcia, the company emerged from stealth in June 2026 with a $46 million Series A co-led by Westlake BioPartners and Canaan Partners, with participation from Dawn Biopharma and Alexandria Venture Investments. Vedana is building a portfolio of long-acting, subcutaneously dosed monoclonal antibodies that go beyond CGRP by targeting PACAP (pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating peptide) and other CGRP-independent pathways, aiming to deliver complete and lasting relief for the majority of migraine patients who remain suboptimally controlled on current standard of care. Its preclinical pipeline includes VDN-0100 (anti-PACAP antibody, first-in-human planned 2027), VDN-0200 (PACAP x CGRP bispecific), and two undisclosed programs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Vedana is a therapeutics company and publishes no public API or developer surface; this record captures its corporate identity for discovery.

providers.name: VeriSIM Life
providers.description: VeriSIM Life is an AI-driven drug discovery and development company that applies mechanistic artificial intelligence and quantitative simulation to reduce the cost, time, and failure rate of translating drug candidates into clinical trials. Its BIOiSIM platform is a biosimulation decision engine that can screen large libraries of drug-like compounds and run simulation scenarios across species and dosing regimens, while AtlasGEN designs novel molecules and evaluates them for safety and efficacy. The company operates PulmoSIM Therapeutics as a subsidiary. VeriSIM Life exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; the platform is accessed through partnerships and demos. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Vesta
providers.description: Vesta is an AI-native mortgage Loan Origination System (LOS) — a modern, open system-of-record platform that orchestrates the loan manufacturing process through configurable software workflows and AI agents that run real loans end to end. Founded in 2020 by former Blend employees Mike Yu and Devon Yang and headquartered in San Francisco, Vesta gives mortgage lenders a cloud, API-and-integration-friendly LOS to replace legacy origination systems, connecting to the broader mortgage technology ecosystem. The company raised an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)-led Series A. Vesta sells to lenders through a demo/partner-signup enterprise motion and does not currently expose a public self-serve developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Aerodyne
providers.description: Aerodyne Group is a Malaysia-headquartered DT3 (drone technology, data technology, and digital transformation) enterprise solutions provider, founded in 2014. Through its Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) model and the AI-powered, cloud-based vertikaliti asset-management platform, Aerodyne turns aerial and sensor data into deep analytics and actionable insights for infrastructure, power line, wind turbine, solar, and agricultural (Agrimor) asset inspection and management. Operating across 45 countries with a global network of AeroRangers, it was ranked the world's number-one drone service provider by Drone Industry Insights in 2021 and 2022. Aerodyne is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer portal, API, or machine-readable specification has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Ampleforth
providers.description: Ampleforth is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol behind AMPL, a price-stable but supply-elastic cryptocurrency that targets the CPI-adjusted 2019 US dollar by algorithmically adjusting token supply (rebasing) across all holders rather than moving price. The ecosystem spans the AMPL rebasing token, Wrapped AMPL (WAMPL), the FORTH governance token and DAO, and the SPOT inflation-resistant store-of-value protocol built on tranched AMPL collateral. Ampleforth is open-source (smart contracts under the fragmentsorg GitHub organization, working name uFragments), audited, and deployed on Ethereum with cross-chain support. Surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and enriched in the API Evangelist network from its public docs, GitHub org, blog, and community channels; it publishes protocol documentation and an llms.txt but no REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Arcus Biosciences
providers.description: Arcus Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing differentiated cancer immunotherapies, headquartered in Hayward, California. Its pipeline pairs multiple novel molecules across intra-tumoral immune pathways, including the HIF-2a inhibitor casdatifan, the CD73 inhibitor quemliclustat, the anti-TIGIT antibody domvanalimab, the anti-PD-1 antibody zimberelimab, and the CD39 inhibitor AB598. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company profile. Arcus publishes an agent-facing surface (llms.txt, an AI content map, and an Organization schema) but no public developer API.

providers.name: Armory.io
providers.description: Armory.io was an enterprise continuous delivery and continuous deployment company built around the open-source Spinnaker project. Its products included Armory Continuous Deployment Self-Hosted and Managed (an enterprise Spinnaker distribution), Armory Continuous Deployment-as-a-Service (CDaaS) with a declarative GitOps deployment experience, and the Armory Scale Agent for Spinnaker and Kubernetes. Armory was backed by Insight Partners and was later acquired by Harness; the armory.io website now 301-redirects to harness.io and the CDaaS cloud service, developer portal, and status page are decommissioned, while the documentation site (docs.armory.io) and the Apache-2.0 GitHub organization (github.com/armory) remain live.

providers.name: Aseon Labs
providers.description: Aseon Labs builds robotic pitstops for self-driving cars — distributed robotic micro-depots (the "Aseon Pod") that automate charging, interior and exterior cleaning, and inspection for autonomous vehicle fleets directly within their operating zones, so vehicles reset locally instead of returning to centralized facilities. The company says the approach can cut reset costs by up to 50%, reduce downtime by ~65%, and add $50,000+ in annual revenue per vehicle. Founded in 2026 and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026 batch), the Redwood City, CA startup is a physical-infrastructure and robotics company; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Basel III
providers.description: Basel III is a comprehensive global regulatory framework developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) in response to the 2007-2008 financial crisis. It strengthens bank capital requirements by requiring higher quality and quantity of capital (CET1, Tier 1, Total Capital), introduces new liquidity standards (LCR and NSFR), adds a leverage ratio backstop, and includes countercyclical capital buffers and G-SIB surcharges. Basel III implementation in the EU/UK is delivered via CRD IV/V and CRR regulations. The final Basel III package (sometimes called Basel IV) addresses output floor and credit risk model constraints introduced in 2017.

providers.name: beva
providers.description: beva (贝瓦网), operated by ProKids Technology Corp / 芝兰玉树（北京）科技股份有限公司, is a Chinese IP-and-technology driven family education and entertainment company. Its flagship original IP is the little beaver "Beva" (贝瓦) and the "Beva Children's Songs" (贝瓦儿歌) brand, spanning children's music, animation, literature and interactive entertainment, distributed across web, mobile, OTT, IPTV and television channels. Through its ProKids Copyright Content Open Platform (open.beva.com) beva offers online-application and offline content-access APIs that let third-party mobile apps and smart hardware — story machines, smart speakers and kids' robots such as MiTu, Rokid and the Doraemon story machine — embed licensed children's audio and video content. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Blur
providers.description: Blur is a New York-based NFT marketplace and aggregator built for professional traders on Ethereum, founded by the pseudonymous "Pacman" (Tieshun Roquerre) in October 2022 and backed by Paradigm and Standard Crypto. The flagship product, blur.io, offers zero marketplace fees, multi-marketplace sweeping, bulk listing/bidding, real-time mempool reveal sniping, and a portfolio-grade analytics surface that aggregates liquidity from OpenSea, X2Y2, LooksRare, and other Seaport-compatible venues. Blur also operates Blend, a peer-to-peer perpetual NFT lending protocol designed by Paradigm researchers that powers ETH-against-NFT borrowing and Buy-Now-Pay-Later flows without oracles or fixed expiries — Blend has captured the dominant share of NFT lending volume on Ethereum. The BLUR token, distributed via multi-season airdrop campaigns, governs the Blur DAO through the Blur Foundation. The same team launched Blast, an Ethereum L2 with native yield, which now hosts its own NFT activity. Blur does not publish an official public developer API or SDK; on-chain integration happens via the deployed marketplace and Blend smart contracts (Seaport-compatible), and marketplace data is reached through third-party indexers such as Bitquery, SimpleHash, and Alchemy rather than a Blur-operated REST or GraphQL endpoint.

providers.name: BoxxApps Open Data
providers.description: BoxxApps Open Data is a organization open-data portal running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 719 datasets.

providers.name: Cablevision Systems
providers.description: Cablevision Systems was a U.S. cable television company that provided telecommunications and television services (Optimum TV, Optimum Online, Optimum Voice) in the New York metropolitan area. It was acquired by Altice in 2016 and now operates as part of Altice USA under the Optimum consumer brand.

providers.name: Cali Open Data
providers.description: Cali Open Data is a municipal government open-data portal for Colombia running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 663 datasets.

providers.name: Candid Therapeutics
providers.description: Candid Therapeutics is a San Diego, California clinical-stage biotechnology company developing T-cell engager (TCE) antibody therapies for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Launched publicly in September 2024 with a $370 million Series A financing and assembled by acquiring Vignette Bio and TRC 2004, Candid in-licenses differentiated bispecific TCE assets and advances them through US clinical development. Its approach redirects T-cells to selectively deplete autoreactive B-cells, aiming for deeper and more durable depletion than conventional antibody therapy without the manufacturing burden of cell therapy. Its lead investigational asset, cizutamig, is a BCMA x CD3 bispecific antibody. UCB completed its acquisition of Candid Therapeutics on 17 June 2026 for up to $2.2 billion ($2.0 billion upfront plus up to $200 million in milestones), and the company now operates as part of UCB. Candid Therapeutics publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: card.io
providers.description: card.io was a mobile SDK company that provided fast, easy credit-card scanning inside iOS and Android apps using the device camera, letting users capture card details by holding a card up to the lens instead of typing them. Founded around 2011 and backed by Uncork Capital (then SoftTech VC), card.io was acquired by PayPal in 2012. Its scanning SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native were open-sourced in December 2014 under the card-io GitHub organization, and the product was ultimately discontinued. The company operated no public REST or web API; its product surface was a set of client-side mobile SDKs, all of which are now archived. This profile is maintained for network completeness and historical/portfolio context.

Derq surfaces safety and traffic intelligence — crashes, near misses, violations, conflicts, counts, and ATSPMs — through its dashboard and via APIs to third-party systems. It reports 800+ partner farmers, 900+ hectares of projects, and 320+ MW of secured grid capacity. It is a portfolio company of HV Capital and is in the API Evangelist network as a climate-energy company profile; it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.description: Link Cell Therapies is a South San Francisco clinical-stage cell therapy company founded by Stanford investigators Robbie Majzner and Crystal Mackall in partnership with Samsara BioCapital, working on the development of safe and effective CAR T agents for patients with solid tumors. The company's logic-gate technology produces AND-gate CAR T cells that require co-expression of two cancer targets before driving cell cytotoxicity, giving greater tumor specificity than existing logic-gate approaches and aiming to avoid off-tumor toxicity. Alongside additional platforms under development, Link is advancing therapeutic programs across solid tumors and certain hematologic cancers, including a dual-targeting AND-gated CAR program (LNK001) directed at clear cell renal cell carcinoma, and in January 2026 entered a strategic collaboration with Johnson & Johnson to develop logic-gate LINK CAR T therapies. providers.name: Olive AI
providers.description: Olive AI was a Columbus, Ohio healthcare automation company founded in 2012 by Sean Lane (originally as CrossChx, rebranded to Olive in 2017). The company built robotic process automation (RPA), AI, and workflow tooling aimed at the healthcare revenue cycle — including a "digital workforce" marketed as "Olive" that automated repetitive administrative tasks in hospitals and health systems. Olive's portfolio centered on clearinghouse and patient access automation, prior authorization automation, claims status checks, eligibility verification, and process mining for revenue-cycle optimization. At its peak Olive raised more than $900M and reached a $4B valuation, but a series of strategic missteps, layoffs, and cash burn forced an orderly wind-down. In late 2023 Olive sold its clearinghouse and patient access business to Waystar, and in early 2024 sold its prior authorization business to Humata Health, then ceased operations. The Olive AI brand is no longer active and there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; surviving capabilities live on inside Waystar and Humata Health.

providers.name: OnPlan
providers.description: OnPlan (onplan.co) publishes guidance and content on project controls, budgeting, and forecasting for organizations managing projects and capital programs. It is presented as an informational and educational resource rather than a self-service SaaS platform: at the time of enrichment the public surface consists of a homepage, a blog of dated articles, a contact page, a privacy policy, and a sitemap, with no developer portal, public API, documentation, pricing, sign-up/login, or terms-of-service pages exposed. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched from the live site; no machine-readable API artifacts were found to harvest.

providers.name: PartyDAO
providers.description: PartyDAO is the decentralized autonomous organization behind Party Protocol, an open, GPL-3.0 protocol for on-chain group coordination that aims to make Ethereum "multiplayer." Party Protocol lets groups form a Party (a shared Ethereum account with members, an inventory, and governance), collectively crowdfund to acquire assets, govern shared holdings, and distribute value to members — all through audited Solidity smart contracts rather than a hosted HTTP API. PartyDAO also ships Party (party.app), a consumer application built on the protocol. The developer surface is entirely on-chain: smart contracts, deployed contract addresses, and technical documentation for integrating via web3 libraries and direct contract calls. There is no REST/HTTP API, hosted SDK, or OAuth surface; integration happens by calling the deployed contracts.

providers.name: Rabobank
providers.description: Rabobank is a Dutch multinational banking and financial services company organized as a cooperative with a strong focus on the food and agriculture sector. It serves retail, business, corporate, and wholesale customers in the Netherlands and operates a global Food & Agribusiness practice through Rabobank Wholesale & Rural and the Rabobank Group internationally. Rabobank publishes a developer portal at docs.developer.rabobank.com (legacy URL developer.rabobank.nl redirects there) exposing PSD2-mandated open banking APIs (Account Information, Payment Initiation, Funds Confirmation) as well as Premium / Beyond-PSD2 commercial APIs for corporate cash management and notifications, with sandbox endpoints for development and a regulated production tier under PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication. Underlying schemes are aligned with the Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 XS2A Framework.

providers.name: Rainmaker Live
providers.description: Rainmaker Live is a platform for live streaming, virtual events, and audience engagement. providers.name: Ralph Lauren
providers.description: Ralph Lauren is a global leader in the design, marketing, and distribution of premium lifestyle products across apparel, footwear, accessories, home, fragrances, and hospitality. providers.name: Raspire
providers.description: Raspire (RASPIRE) provides runtime security for mobile applications, positioning itself as the first line of defense for Android and iOS apps against AI-powered fraud attacks, API abuse, and runtime threats. Developers upload compiled apps (APK/IPA) and Raspire automatically hardens them with anti-fraud protection, app integrity verification, reverse-engineering prevention, and API protection, without requiring changes to application source code. The platform gives security teams real-time visibility into threats and blocks attacks in real time, and can integrate with existing SIEM systems and application monitoring platforms as part of a CI/CD pipeline. Raspire is a Y Combinator company. As surfaced to the API Evangelist network it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Rebel Girls
providers.description: Rebel Girls is a global media and publishing brand that celebrates inspiring stories about girls and women, empowering young audiences through books, a podcast, a YouTube channel, apparel and accessories, activities, and the Rebel Girls Sport program. providers.name: Sentient
providers.description: Sentient (Sentient Labs / Sentient Foundation) is an open-source AI research lab and crypto protocol building Open, Monetizable, and Loyal (OML) artificial general intelligence. Its work spans agent frameworks (ROMA recursive meta-agent, Open Deep Search, EvoSkill agent-skill synthesis), the OML 1.0 model-fingerprinting system for verifiable model ownership and monetization, and the GRID protocol with Sentient Chat as a universal interface for discovering, composing, and coordinating AI artifacts.
