providers.name: SilverStream
providers.description: Silverstream AI builds infrastructure for autonomous AI agents, focused on making web-browsing and enterprise-workflow agents reliable enough for real-world, production use. Its work includes Silverstream Bench (a platform for storing, reviewing, and sharing Claude Code sessions), the open Pasta-1T dataset of web trajectories for training browser agents, and benchmark results such as 94% accuracy (2-sigma reliability) on ServiceNow tasks. The company emerged from stealth in March 2025 with a $1.2M pre-seed round. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site and product pages but no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or OpenAPI surface, so most API-facing enrichment is not applicable.

Its platform serves broker-dealers, registered investment advisors (RIAs), and enterprise wealth management organizations with digital client and advisor onboarding, automated account opening, data management and aggregation, and advisor productivity tooling built natively on the Salesforce Financial Services Cloud ecosystem. Skience is backed by Insight Partners and operates as a private SaaS provider; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, but it does maintain a SafeBase-hosted trust center documenting SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 2 + HITRUST attestations and a responsible disclosure program.

providers.name: Sturdy
providers.description: Sturdy is a decentralized liquid money market protocol for on-chain lending and borrowing. Sturdy V2 uses a two-tier architecture: a base layer of risk-isolated lending pairs, where each siloed market consists of a single lending asset and a single collateral asset, and an aggregation layer on top that lets lenders choose acceptable collateral types while avoiding liquidity fragmentation. The protocol is oracle-agnostic (using RedStone, API3, and eOracle feeds depending on the market), is governed by the $STRDY token and the Sturdy DAO, and has been audited by Zellic, ChainSecurity, Spearbit, Certik, Code4rena, and Quantstamp. Sturdy is an on-chain smart-contract protocol rather than a hosted REST API: its developer surface is the published smart contracts, oracle integrations, and the Sturdy Subnet, with no first-party web API, SDK, or OpenAPI. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital.

providers.name: ThreatTrack Security
providers.description: ThreatTrack Security was a cybersecurity vendor focused on advanced malware analysis and threat intelligence, known for its ThreatAnalyzer dynamic malware sandbox, the ThreatIQ real-time threat intelligence feeds, and the VIPRE endpoint antivirus product line. The company traces to Sunbelt Software (founded 1994), which GFI Software acquired in 2010; GFI spun the security unit out in 2013 to form ThreatTrack Security. ThreatTrack was acquired by Ziff Davis / J2 Global in early 2018 and the brand was folded into VIPRE Security Group, so ThreatTrack no longer operates as an independent company. Its historical developer surface was an OEM/on-premise integration API for ThreatAnalyzer (JSON/XML output) and ThreatIQ intelligence feeds rather than a public, self-service developer platform. providers.name: Torus
providers.description: Torus is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-powered engineering intelligence platform for capital projects. Torus runs as a managed cloud or a sovereign in-VPC deployment and publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Tower International
providers.description: Tower International was a global manufacturer of engineered structural metal components and assemblies for the automotive industry, primarily serving original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). The company supplied body-structure stampings, frame and chassis structures, and complex welded assemblies for cars, crossovers, pickups, and SUVs. Tower International was acquired by Autokiniton Global Group in 2019 and merged with L&W Group to form the second largest Body-in-White and vehicle frame supplier in North America. As a private manufacturing company with no public developer API offering, Tower International does not expose public REST or web APIs.

providers.name: Treet
providers.description: Treet is a branded recommerce (resale) platform that lets e-commerce brands run their own secondhand marketplaces. Founded in 2021 by marketplace veterans Jake Disraeli and Sonia Yang (formerly of Indiegogo and Airbnb), Treet powers resale for 250+ global brands through four stackable programs: Peer-to-Peer (customers buy and sell from each other for cash or brand credit), Trade-In, Off-Price liquidation of excess inventory, and Returns rerouting. Treet integrates into a brand's existing commerce stack — Shopify, Adobe Commerce, BigCommerce, WooCommerce and Salesforce Commerce, plus logistics (ShipHero, ShipBob), marketing/loyalty (Klaviyo, Yotpo, LoyaltyLion) and returns (Loop, Happy Returns) partners via its "Infinite Integrations" platform. Treet is an API consumer rather than an API producer: it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks of its own, and delivers to brands as a managed SaaS and Shopify app. Backed by Two Sigma Ventures and Techstars.

As a Fortune 500 company, Vulcan serves the construction industry with materials critical for roads, bridges, buildings, and infrastructure. providers.description: Betterfly is a Latin American insurtech and employee-benefits platform that combines voluntary insurance coverage with daily health engagement and rewards. providers.name: Cambridge Terahertz
providers.description: Cambridge Terahertz (thzcorp.com) is an MIT-spinout physical security company building compact, AI-powered terahertz imaging sensors that detect concealed weapons -- guns, knives, explosives, and 3D-printed weapons -- as people walk naturally through entrances, without pat-downs or metal detectors. The 2-pound sensors mount like security cameras, serve hospitals, enterprises, and government facilities, and integrate with existing VMS and security systems over standard REST APIs, though the company publishes no public developer portal or API documentation. Backed by Felicis with a $12M seed round and an NSF SBIR Phase II grant.

providers.name: Convergent Dental
providers.description: Convergent Dental, Inc. is a privately held dental equipment and technology manufacturer headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, best known for Solea, a 9.3 micron CO2 all-tissue dental laser cleared by the FDA for hard tissue, soft tissue and osseous indications. The Solea platform is marketed for anesthesia-free, blood-free and suture-free restorative, soft tissue, pediatric, implant and cosmetic procedures, and has been extended with Solea Perioguide for minimally invasive periodontal therapy, Solea Sleep and Solea Protect. The company sells and services through its own commercial organization and a distribution partnership with Patterson Dental, and supports clinicians with training and education, clinical studies, case studies and the annual Solea Summit. Convergent Dental publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable API contract or agent surface as of this profiling pass.

providers.name: Craftview
providers.description: Craftview Software GmbH is a Frankfurt-headquartered European software group that builds ERP and project-management software for the skilled trades. Formed as a buy-and-build platform, Craftview operates a portfolio of long-established regional ERP brands — C'FLUIDE, ES2000, EXTRABAT, GILDE, KS21, MOSER, OSD, PLENION, RITA BOSSE and WINWORKER — serving green industries, construction-related trades, technical services and specialized crafts across Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands and France. The group reports 25,000+ active customers, 330+ employees and 11 locations across 41 key European regions. Craftview publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API definitions; its software is sold and delivered per brand as on-premise and cloud ERP for trade businesses.

providers.name: Fed10
providers.description: Fed10 is a legislative-intelligence and government-affairs platform staffed by AI agents. It continuously monitors legislation across U.S. state legislatures and Congress, flags regulatory threats and opportunities relevant to a company's business, and delivers actionable policy insights — the analysis a $500/hour policy consultant produces in days, returned in seconds. Founded in 2026 by three former lobbyists and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026), Fed10 packages bill tracking, amendment analysis, compliance-gap assessment, and continuous legislative monitoring into an agentic workflow for public-affairs and compliance teams.

providers.name: Firehawk Aerospace
providers.description: Firehawk Aerospace, Inc. is a Dallas, Texas defense-technology manufacturer founded in 2019 by Ronald Jones, Will Edwards and Steve Edwards that replaces conventional rocket-propulsion production with additive manufacturing. Its proprietary 3D-printed solid rocket fuel, branded 3D-Ultra, is used to build hybrid rocket engines and solid rocket motors whose fuel-grain geometry is printed rather than cast, cutting production timelines from years to weeks while removing the handling hazards of traditional energetics. The company works under U.S. Army Applications Laboratory SBIR Phase III and U.S. Air Force Test Center contracts, has flight-tested an additively manufactured GMLRS-class analog, and is expanding manufacturing capacity in Lawton, Oklahoma and Crawford, Mississippi. Firehawk now operates publicly as Firehawk Defense (firehawkdefense.com); the firehawkaerospace.com domain 301-redirects there. It is a hardware and energetics manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Flagstar
providers.description: Flagstar Bank, N.A. is the OCC-chartered national bank subsidiary of Flagstar Financial, Inc. (NYSE: FLG), the Hicksville, New York holding company formerly known as New York Community Bancorp (NYCB). It is one of the largest regional (super-regional) banks in the United States, formed when NYCB acquired Flagstar Bancorp in December 2022, converted Flagstar Bank, FSB into a national bank (Flagstar Bank, N.A.), and subsequently acquired certain assets and liabilities of Signature Bridge Bank from the FDIC in March 2023; the holding company rebranded to Flagstar Financial in October 2024. Flagstar operates in retail and commercial banking, mortgage origination and servicing, and warehouse lending. On the API front, Flagstar runs a first-party developer portal at developer.flagstar.com (a Broadcom/Layer7 "LivePortal" API Developer Portal), but as of this review it publishes no public, self-serve API products, API documentation, or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger to anonymous visitors — all products are sign-in gated behind partner/consumer-team access. Flagstar has no publicly documented FDX (Financial Data Exchange) participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture; consumer-permissioned data sharing appears to be available only through third-party aggregators (e.g. Plaid, Tink, TrueLayer) rather than a first-party public API.

providers.name: Flowserve
providers.description: Flowserve moves, controls and protects the flow of materials in the world's most critical industries through pumps, seals, valves, and flow control systems. No public developer APIs have been identified; the company offers digital services such as RedRaven IIoT monitoring through customer engagements rather than an open developer portal.

providers.name: Handl Health
providers.description: Handl Health is a healthcare price-transparency AI platform that turns the negotiated rates, gross charges, and cash prices unlocked by the Hospital Price Transparency and Transparency in Coverage rules into clean, usable pricing intelligence. Using proprietary AI models, Handl cleans and organizes publicly available machine-readable pricing files at scale and supplements them with claims, Medicare rates, and provider-directory data to build a holistic, validated dataset. Its products — Iris, AI-driven network analytics for benefits consultants to evaluate and compare carrier networks, and Arke, real-time cost tools that help plan members find high-value care — serve benefits consultants, carriers, third-party administrators, and employers designing alternative health plans. Handl is a Techstars- and StartUp Health-backed company. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public developer API or portal was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: HSBC
providers.description: One of the world's largest banking and financial services organizations headquartered in London. Serves over 40 million customers globally with a strong presence in Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Operates a public Developer Portal (develop.hsbc.com) exposing Open Banking, payments, accounts, and global payments solutions APIs for partners and third-party providers.

providers.name: Inari
providers.description: Inari Agriculture, Inc. — "The SEEDesign company" — is a Cambridge, Massachusetts agricultural biotechnology company founded by Flagship Pioneering in 2016, with additional sites in West Lafayette, Indiana and Ghent, Belgium. Its SEEDesign platform combines genomics, artificial intelligence and predictive design with a multiplex gene-editing toolbox to accelerate crop improvement in soybean, corn and wheat, targeting 10-20% yield gains alongside roughly 40% reductions in nitrogen and water use. Inari runs a partner-first, business-to-business model, licensing designed seed to independent seed companies and breeders rather than selling to farmers directly. Inari publishes an llms.txt at inari.com/llms.txt but operates no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract; its data platform (Databricks-based) is internal. Not to be confused with the unrelated medical-device company Inari Medical.

providers.name: Inhabit
providers.description: Inhabit is a global PropTech software company operating a portfolio of specialized platforms for the residential and vacation rental property management markets, including ResMan, Streamline, LiveRez, Anyone Home, ResidentIQ, ePremium, Rental Guardian, Lynnbrook Group payments, Western Reporting screening, and Bluetent marketing. Its integrated tools span property management, resident and guest CRM and contact center, payments processing, renters and property insurance, tenant screening and income verification, utility billing, and marketing websites, serving multifamily, single-family, student, affordable, HOA and condo, and short-term vacation rental operators worldwide. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Jet2
providers.description: Jet2 plc (London Stock Exchange: JET2, formerly Dart Group plc) is a British leisure travel group headquartered at Low Fare Finder House, Leeds Bradford Airport, Yeadon, Leeds, West Yorkshire — an address confirmed verbatim in the Extended Validation TLS certificate served by www.jet2.com, issued to "JET2.COM LIMITED", company serial number 02739537, jurisdiction GB. Its home market is the United Kingdom. The group combines two businesses that are unusual in this sector for being deliberately fused: Jet2.com (IATA code LS, ICAO code EXS), the UK's third-largest airline, and Jet2holidays, the UK's largest ATOL holder and leading provider of ATOL-protected package holidays to the Mediterranean, the Canary Islands and European city destinations. For the year ended 31 March 2026 the group reported revenue of £7,482.1 million, operating profit of £439.6 million and a record 20.83 million passengers, flying from 14 UK airport bases including newly added London Luton and London Gatwick, with more than 63% of flown passengers buying an end-to-end package holiday and 155 Airbus A321neo aircraft on order. Jet2holidays sells through its own website and through more than 2,500 independent UK travel agent partners, and carries ABTA number Y1256. Where Jet2 sits in the distribution chain is the point of this record. Like easyJet and Ryanair, Jet2.com was built with no Global Distribution System dependency at all: it never filed fares into the GDS rail that Amadeus, Sabre and Travelport have intermediated for forty years, and it therefore never needed IATA's New Distribution Capability as a remedy. Travelport supports Jet2 in Smartpoint only as a "Direct Payment Carrier" — its low-cost-carrier workaround — point-to-point only, no connecting flights, and with no post-booking change or cancellation possible through the GDS at all ("Requests for changes must be made directly through Jet2"). In June 2025 Jet2.com signed a distribution agreement with airline technology company Kyte, whose Kyte Direct Connect (KDC) JSON/REST API "standardises airline NDC and LCC proprietary content", opening Jet2 seats and ancillaries to travel management companies and corporate booking tools for the first time, with the same content reaching agency desktops through AirGateway. Separately, Jet2holidays operates an agency API that lets independent agents sell Jet2 packages on their own bookable websites for commission. Its API posture, stated honestly, is that Jet2 runs real production distribution APIs and publishes nothing about them. There is no developer portal — developer.jet2.com, developers.jet2.com, docs.jet2.com, apis.jet2.com, ndc.jet2.com, partner.jet2.com and trade.jet2.com all fail to resolve — no API reference, no OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI or GraphQL contract, no security.txt, no .well-known catalogue and no official GitHub organisation. api.jet2.com resolves and answers HTTP 200 with nothing but the stock Microsoft IIS 10.0 default page, 404 on every spec path probed. Access is by commercial agreement only, negotiated bilaterally or through Kyte, whose own FAQ states that "Access to airline products is controlled by each airline." This record is an honest stub: apis[] is intentionally empty because no Jet2 API is publicly documented, and listing an undocumented hostname as an API would be fabrication. The evidence, including every URL probed with its HTTP status, is in review.yml. A second enrichment pass on 28 July 2026 found the one genuinely public first-party developer surface Jet2 has, and it is not an API: the Jet2 Design System, published as two npm packages under the @jet2 scope (design tokens for seven brand themes, and a React component library containing a single Button), sourced from Jet2's private Azure DevOps organisation at jet2tfs.visualstudio.com/Jet2Digital and documented at design.jet2.com behind a Supernova login. Both packages were last published in April 2024. The same pass confirmed no /.well-known/ document on any host that answers, no security.txt, no vulnerability disclosure programme, no trust centre, no public Postman collection and no SDK in any package registry. Jet2's engineering voice, such as it is, comes from Jet2 Travel Technologies (J2TT), its in-house development centre in Pune, India, which runs a public blog with an RSS feed.

providers.name: Kos
providers.description: Kos (Kosai, Inc.) builds what it calls the world's first virtual finance employee: an AI agent given its own workstation, org identity, software licenses, RBAC and audit logs, which completes finance and back-office workflows for capital- and inventory-heavy operators across datacenters, defense, energy, long-lead equipment, space and contracting. Kos reviews pay applications and vendor invoices line-by-line against GMP contracts, catching missing backup, overbills and calculation errors; generates, routes and closes out purchase orders inside a customer's ERP; and is taught new workflows over screenshare like a new hire. It is reached over email, Slack, Teams, phone and Zoom rather than through a UI, app or public API. Founded by Tanuj and Mani, who met as graduate researchers at Stanford under Sachin Katti; backed by 8VC, XYZ Ventures, MVP Ventures and Launch, with advisors including former Equinix CFO Keith Taylor. Headquartered in San Francisco, California.

providers.name: Lilac Solutions
providers.description: Lilac Solutions is an Oakland, California climate-technology company founded in 2016 that develops direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology built on proprietary ion exchange media. Its ion exchange beads and modular brine processing systems pull battery-grade lithium from high-grade, low-grade and complex brines without evaporation ponds, cutting water use and shrinking the land footprint and time-to-production of conventional lithium operations. Lilac operates mini-pilot, field-pilot and commercial deployments across the Great Salt Lake in Utah, Nevada, Argentina, Chile, Germany and Indonesia, and manufactures its ion exchange media on a dedicated production line in Nevada. The company is venture-backed with roughly $350M raised, employs about 200 people, and sells industrial hardware and process technology to lithium producers — it publishes no public developer platform, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Lyten
providers.description: Lyten is a San Jose, California advanced-materials company founded in 2015 that invented and commercializes Lyten 3D Graphene, a tunable three-dimensional carbon supermaterial produced by converting methane into nanostructured carbon while co-producing hydrogen. Lyten applies that materials platform across four product lines: lithium-sulfur battery cells and battery systems that contain no cobalt, nickel or manganese and target roughly 40% weight savings versus lithium-ion; 3D graphene reinforced 3D printer filament; concrete admixture and structural adhesives; and chemical/environmental sensors, including the Lyten Atmos continuous methane-intelligence platform that pairs solar-powered LTE field sensors with cloud analytics and dashboards for landfill and oil-and-gas emissions monitoring. The company has raised over $600 million from investors including Stellantis, FedEx and Honeywell, operates a 145,000 sq ft pilot manufacturing facility in the Alviso district of North San Jose, acquired Cuberg's San Leandro battery assets in 2024, and in 2025 acquired Northvolt battery manufacturing assets in Poland and Sweden, establishing a European headquarters in Gdansk, Poland. Lyten is a private company; its shares trade on secondary markets such as Forge Global. It publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal.

providers.name: Photocert
providers.description: Photocert is a London-based visual AI company (a Techstars portfolio company) that authenticates photos and videos at the point of capture to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse across insurance and enterprise visual-inspection workflows. Its platform detects AI-generated images and deepfakes at scale, certifies media with claimed 99.99% accuracy, and automates motor, content, and property (water-leak) insurance claims. Photocert markets REST APIs and SDKs plus a white-label claim/onboarding platform and a camera API component for image certification, though no public developer documentation, OpenAPI, or self-service portal is published — integration is arranged via sales/demo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from the Techstars portfolio and enriched with the honest public surface.

providers.name: Reliance, Inc.
providers.description: Reliance, Inc. (NYSE: RS) is the largest metals service center operator in North America, distributing approximately 100,000 metal products across aluminum, brass, alloy, copper, carbon steel, stainless steel, titanium, and specialty metals to over 125,000 customers including fabricators and manufacturers. Operating under more than 75 distinct brands across 300+ locations in the US, Canada, and internationally, Reliance provides value-added processing services including cutting, shearing, sawing, leveling, stamping, and just-in-time delivery for aerospace, automotive, construction, defense, energy, electronics, and semiconductor end markets.

providers.name: Rookout
providers.description: Rookout is a live application debugging platform founded in 2017 in Tel Aviv, Israel that lets developers set non-breaking breakpoints in running production, staging, and development applications to capture full-stack debug data — variables, stack traces, logs, and metrics — without redeploying, restarting, or stopping services. Rookout pioneered the "live debugger" category for cloud-native and Kubernetes-hosted applications and shipped language agents/SDKs for Python, Java/JVM, Node.js, .NET, Go, and Ruby that attach to running processes and stream snapshots back to the Rookout web IDE or developer's IDE. Dynatrace announced its acquisition of Rookout on July 31, 2023 and closed the deal in Q2 of Dynatrace's fiscal year ending September 30, 2023. The standalone Rookout product has since been folded into the Dynatrace platform as the Dynatrace Live Debugger (and Live Logger), and the rookout.com and docs.rookout.com domains now redirect to dynatrace.com. There is no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, webhook catalog, or CLI for Rookout — the developer surface consists entirely of language agents, deployment integration examples, IDE extensions, and the Explorook desktop helper that exposes local source folders to the Rookout web debugger. The Rookout GitHub organization remains public and continues to maintain those agents, tutorials, and integration samples under Apache-2.0.

providers.name: Skycatch
providers.description: Skycatch built spatial data capture, processing, and analytics for mining and construction sites, turning drone and aerial imagery into high-precision 3D data, volumetrics, and AI-driven site insights. Its products included Spatial Sight, Spatial DataHub (datahub.skycatch.com), and EdgeServer for on-site edge processing. Skycatch was acquired by Caterpillar Inc. on July 7, 2026 (following Caterpillar's RPMGlobal acquisition) to expand its mining technology capabilities. A developer platform exists at docs.skycatch.com but is password-gated, and no public API specification is available. Originally surfaced as a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company.

providers.name: The Human Utility
providers.description: The Human Utility (formerly the Detroit Water Project) is a Y Combinator-backed not-for-profit organization founded in 2014 by Tiffani Ashley Bell whose mission is to preserve human dignity by increasing water affordability for families across the United States. It matches families who are behind on their water bills with donors who want to help, paying utility companies directly on their behalf through crowdfunded donations, community-building, and policy action. Operating in Detroit, Baltimore, and dozens of other cities, it has helped thousands of households avoid water shutoffs. The Human Utility runs a public-facing web application for donors and recipients rather than a developer-facing API product; its source code lives in the humanutility GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched with identity and link details; no public API surface was found.

providers.name: United Solar
providers.description: United Solar (United Solar Polysilicon FZC SPC) is a clean-technology company producing ultra-high-purity polysilicon for the photovoltaic industry from one of the world's most advanced manufacturing facilities in Oman's Sohar Free Zone, with an annual capacity of 100,000 metric tons supporting roughly 40 GW of solar module production. Backed by IDG Capital and the IFC, the company completed a $1.6 billion capital raise in 2026 and is the largest polysilicon producer of its kind outside China. United Solar is an industrial manufacturer and does not publish a developer portal or public APIs.

providers.name: Workplaced Technologies Ltd
providers.description: Workplaced (Workplaced Technologies Ltd) is a workplace-strategy and hybrid-work SaaS platform that helps companies create workplaces that work. Its products cover workplace experience surveys (Dynamics), office occupancy measurement beyond sensor data (Occupancy), space taxonomy and office planning (Taxonomy), desk and meeting-room booking (Booking), and hybrid work policy modelling (Balance), alongside a pricing calculator, free planning tools, research reports, and a partner program. Workplaced is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public developer program - the api.workplaced.com backend is fully authentication-gated with no public documentation or specification.

providers.name: AdStage.io
providers.description: AdStage was a cross-network advertising management, reporting, and automation platform (a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company, founded 2013) that let marketers pull normalized advertising data from Google Ads, Microsoft/Bing Ads, Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, Pinterest, Amazon, Google Analytics and more through a single unified interface. Its AdStage Data API (v1 and v2, HAL+JSON over HTTP with bearer-token / OAuth 2 auth) exposed user, organization, and advertising-entity data plus customizable cross-network reports. AdStage was acquired by TapClicks in April 2020 and folded into TapClicks' Marketing Intelligence platform; the standalone AdStage Data API (platform.adstage.io) is now defunct, though the AdStage GitHub organization and its API Blueprint documentation remain public. The adstage.io domain now serves unrelated PPC/advertising content under new ownership.

providers.name: Alere
providers.description: Alere Inc. was a global manufacturer of rapid point-of-care diagnostic tests, founded in 1991 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. The company operated three business units focused on cardiometabolic, infectious disease, and toxicology testing. Alere's product portfolio included the Alere i platform for rapid molecular diagnostics, the Alere CD4 analyser for HIV management, and the RALS point-of-care data management system for laboratory connectivity. Alere Informatics offered web-based solutions including RALS-Freedom, AegisPOC, and RALS-Web3 for point-of-care device management and data integration with laboratory information systems. Abbott Laboratories acquired Alere on October 3, 2017 for $5.3 billion, and the company now operates as Abbott Rapid Diagnostics.

providers.name: Asylon
providers.description: Asylon Robotics is an American-made robotic security company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Norristown, Pennsylvania, that automates physical perimeter security with autonomous drones, ground robots, software, and AI. Its flagship products include the Guardian automated security drone (the most widely used automated security drone system, with tens of thousands of patrol and alarm-response missions completed), the DroneDog quadruped ground robot built on Boston Dynamics Spot with the Asylon DogHouse charging enclosure and PupPack cellular PTZ payload, and DroneIQ, the Robotic Security Operations Center (RSOC) and software platform that coordinates robotic assets, fixed surveillance, and human operators. DroneIQ exposes an open-architecture integration layer for third-party alarms and sensors (radar, smart fences, Bosch alarm panels, gun-detection computer vision, Genetec), but the company publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; API and integration access is arranged directly with Asylon. Asylon raised a $26M Series B in July 2025 led by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Brine (Tanx)
providers.description: Brine — now rebranded as tanX — is a cross-chain, self-custodial orderbook decentralized exchange (DEX) built on StarkWare's StarkEx Layer-2 scaling engine. It combines the trustless, non-custodial security of a DEX with the speed and low fees of a centralized exchange: gasless trading, rapid off-chain order execution with on-chain settlement, cross-chain deposits and withdrawals, and simple APIs for programmatic trading. The company is backed by Pantera Capital and is repositioning around "a secure and compliant future for crypto." This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Pantera Capital's portfolio and enriched by the pipeline; as of this pass the public REST API host is no longer reachable and the developer surface is limited to the GitBook documentation.

providers.name: Campbell Soup
providers.description: Campbell Soup Company (now rebranded as The Campbell's Company) is a manufacturer and marketer of high-quality branded convenience food products, including soups, simple meals, beverages, snacks, and packaged fresh foods under brands such as Campbell's, Swanson, Pace, Prego, V8, Pepperidge Farm, Goldfish, and Snyder's of Hanover. Historically Campbell's ran a public Campbell's Kitchen Developer API exposing recipes, products, UPC lookup, and nutrition data for web and mobile integrations, though current availability of the public developer portal varies and typically requires partner access.

providers.name: CashDirector
providers.description: CashDirector is a fintech platform delivering AI-powered financial management for small businesses through a white-label, B2B2C partner model. It embeds banking and accounting automation directly into financial institutions' online banking platforms so banks can offer their SME clients a "beyond banking" daily digital business assistant. The platform automates invoicing, expense tracking, cash flow forecasting and receivables management, using AI and OCR to process financial documents automatically. It supports multibanking with minimal IT involvement and reports over 250,000 users across partnerships with six major European banks, positioning itself as Europe's first online accounting system with full banking integration. CashDirector is a Techstars portfolio company; it publishes no public developer portal or open API surface — integration is delivered privately to bank partners.

providers.name: COSCO Shipping
providers.description: A Chinese state-owned multinational shipping and logistics conglomerate and the world's largest container shipping fleet by capacity. Operates container shipping, port terminals, bulk cargo services, and digital supply chain platforms (Syncon Hub, My Reefer, Hi-Dolphin) across global trade routes.

providers.name: DraftKings
providers.description: DraftKings is a digital sports entertainment and gaming company that operates a leading daily fantasy sports platform, an online sportsbook, and an iGaming casino across regulated jurisdictions in North America. The company also runs DraftKings Marketplace for digital collectibles and offers business-to-business gaming technology. No publicly documented developer API or developer portal is currently exposed at draftkings.com; integrations are typically handled through licensed partner agreements rather than self-serve developer access.

providers.name: Element Science
providers.description: Element Science is a San Francisco-based medical device and digital health company focused on high-risk cardiovascular patients. Its flagship product is the Jewel Patch-Wearable Cardioverter Defibrillator (P-WCD) — a low-profile, water-resistant wearable that continuously monitors for and treats life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias in patients at temporary elevated risk of sudden cardiac arrest. The Jewel received FDA Premarket Approval in 2025 and CE Mark / UKCA marking in January 2024. Element Science is a portfolio company of GV. Added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no public developer API or machine-readable specification has been identified for this provider at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Empirico
providers.description: Empirico is a biotechnology company that powers therapeutic discovery with human genetics and small interfering RNA (siRNA) medicines. Combining internal capabilities in human genetics and siRNA chemistry with partner expertise, the company identifies naturally occurring genetic variations associated with health benefits and develops precision oligonucleotide therapeutics for common diseases with significant unmet medical need. In October 2024 Empirico entered a licensing agreement with GSK worth up to $745 million for a clinical-stage oligonucleotide targeting respiratory disease (COPD). Empirico is backed by DCVC. It is a pharmaceutical R&D company and does not operate a public technology or API platform.

providers.name: Endogastric Solutions
providers.description: EndoGastric Solutions is a medical device company focused on treating gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Its flagship offering is the TIF (Transoral Incisionless Fundoplication) 2.0 procedure, performed with the EsophyX Z+ device and SerosaFuse non-resorbable polypropylene fasteners to endoscopically reconstruct the natural antireflux barrier at the esophagogastric junction, plus the combined cTIF procedure that pairs hiatal hernia repair with TIF. The company sells devices and clinician training rather than software, and it has since been acquired by Merit Medical — the endogastricsolutions.com domain now redirects to merit.com/solutions/tif-2-0/. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and carries no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Everstring
providers.description: EverString was a B2B predictive marketing and sales intelligence platform that used data science, machine learning, and a proprietary business data cloud to help go-to-market teams identify their best-fit accounts. Its capabilities included predictive lead and account scoring, account-based marketing segmentation, firmographic enrichment, similar-company discovery, ML-generated keywords, and industry classification, exposed to developers through an Enrichment API on developer.everstring.com secured with access-token authentication. Founded in 2012 and backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, EverString was acquired by ZoomInfo in November 2019 and its data and predictive capabilities were folded into the ZoomInfo platform; the everstring.com website now redirects to ZoomInfo Operations and the standalone developer portal has been largely decommissioned. This profile documents the historical API surface and current public footprint.

providers.name: GE Aerospace
providers.description: A leading manufacturer of jet engines and aviation systems for commercial and military aircraft. Spun off from General Electric to focus exclusively on aerospace propulsion and services, GE Aerospace also offers software-as-a-service tooling, engine health monitoring (Collaborative Insight), TRUEngine certification, and OnPoint maintenance and support services.

providers.name: Kenbi
providers.description: Kenbi is a German healthcare organization focused on nursing education and workforce development, operating through two divisions. Kenbi Academy delivers continuing professional development for care workers with 100+ ZFU-certified courses recognized by all German health insurers and available nationwide, spanning nursing service management, quality assurance, wound care, and instructor training. Kenbi Campus runs vocational nursing programs in Berlin and Hamburg, including a three-year registered nurse generalist program and an 18-month nursing assistant curriculum. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: OSIsoft
providers.description: OSIsoft was the enterprise software company behind the PI System, the operational data infrastructure used across manufacturing, energy, utilities, oil and gas, and other industrial sectors to collect, historize, contextualize, and visualize high-volume real-time sensor and control-system time-series data. Its developer surface centered on the PI Web API (a RESTful interface to the PI Data Archive and Asset Framework), AF SDK, and the PI Square developer community. OSIsoft was acquired by AVEVA in 2021; all osisoft.com and docs.osisoft.com properties now redirect to AVEVA, where the product ships as the AVEVA PI System. This profile is maintained as a historical/acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network, with developer resources pointing at the live AVEVA successor pages.

providers.name: Pinnacle Financial
providers.description: Pinnacle Financial Partners, Inc. (NASDAQ: PNFP) is a Nashville, Tennessee based regional bank holding company whose principal subsidiary, Pinnacle Bank, is a Tennessee state-chartered, FDIC-insured commercial bank (FDIC Cert #35583) originally founded in 2000 as Pinnacle National Bank and renamed in 2012. Pinnacle operates across the Southeast — Tennessee, the Carolinas, Virginia, Georgia and Alabama — serving consumer, small-business, commercial and wealth clients. On the open-finance side Pinnacle runs NO public first-party developer API portal; its consumer digital and mobile banking is delivered on a third-party core/digital platform (Apiture), and consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is made available to fintechs only through data aggregators (Plaid and Finicity/Mastercard) rather than through a documented bank-operated API. No direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture was found; open-finance participation is aggregator-mediated.

providers.name: Pomelo Health
providers.description: Pomelo Health (formerly Chronometriq, founded 2012, headquartered in Montreal with offices in Boston and Toronto) is a Canadian patient-engagement software company operating within the TELUS Health ecosystem. Its cloud platform helps medical clinics reduce no-shows and modernize the front-desk experience with online booking/e-booking, automated SMS/voice/email appointment reminders, digital intake eForms, telemedicine, secure two-way messaging, patient broadcasts, and a patient portal. Pomelo ships as an EMR add-on that syncs with TELUS Health EMRs — Accuro, Medesync, and TELUS CHR — rather than as an open integration platform. As of this review Pomelo Health publishes NO public developer portal, NO documented REST/OpenAPI, and NO public HL7 FHIR CapabilityStatement or SMART-on-FHIR surface; third-party connectivity is achieved through the underlying EMR partner APIs, so this profile is an honest identity stub for a company with a gated, partner-only integration model. Home market: Canada.

providers.name: Qognify
providers.description: Qognify is an enterprise physical-security software provider whose portfolio spans video management systems (Ocularis, Qognify VMS formerly Cayuga, and NiceVision), physical security information management / PSIM (Situator), and video analytics used to protect critical infrastructure, transportation, utilities, and enterprise campuses worldwide. The business was formed in 2015 when Battery Ventures acquired NICE Systems' physical security unit, and was acquired by Hexagon AB in 2023, becoming part of Hexagon's safety and security operations. The brand and products are transitioning to Octave Security, with next-generation offerings delivered under the Coda line (formerly HxGN dC3). Qognify sells through channel partners and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integrations are handled via partner and professional-services channels and the Hexagon support organization.

providers.name: Radionetics Oncology
providers.description: Radionetics Oncology is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing precision radiopharmaceutical treatments for cancer. The company designs small-molecule radioligands that target G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) to selectively deliver targeted radiation therapy to solid tumors, including breast and lung cancer, combining GPCR biology expertise with medicinal chemistry. Radionetics entered a strategic agreement with Eli Lilly in 2024. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer, API, or technical-integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Stampli
providers.description: Stampli is an AI-driven accounts payable and procure-to-pay automation platform (invoice capture, coding, approvals, vendor management, payments, and corporate cards) that stays aligned to a company's ERP as the system of record. Stampli does NOT publish a public, self-serve developer API or developer portal. What Stampli markets as its "API" is a set of pre-built, in-house cloud-to-cloud ERP integrations (plus on-premises "Bridge" connectors and file-based sync) that Stampli operates on the customer's behalf to sync master data - invoices, vendors, purchase orders, GL accounts, locations/entities, and approvals - between Stampli and 70+ ERPs such as NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics, SAP, Oracle, and Acumatica. Access is gated behind a sales/onboarding relationship; there is no documented public REST/GraphQL/WebSocket surface, no self-service authentication, no OpenAPI reference, and no published developer documentation as of this catalog entry. Integrations are configured by Stampli during onboarding rather than by third-party developers against an open API.

providers.name: Universal Health Services
providers.description: Universal Health Services (UHS) is one of the nation's largest hospital management companies, operating acute care hospitals, behavioral health facilities, and ambulatory care access points across the United States and the United Kingdom. UHS manages approximately 400 facilities across 37 states, Washington DC, and the United Kingdom, providing acute care, behavioral health, and outpatient services. As a healthcare provider, UHS operates under CMS interoperability mandates using HL7 FHIR standards for patient data access.

providers.name: Vendease
providers.description: Vendease is a Nigerian B2B food procurement platform (founded 2020, Y Combinator W21, backed by Partech Africa and TLcom) that helps restaurants, hotels, and other food businesses buy fresh and processed food supplies, offering Buy Now, Pay Later financing, supplier consolidation, cold-chain logistics, and 24-hour delivery in Lagos. Vendease publishes no public developer API or SDKs; its procurement, payments, inventory, and tenant management service APIs are internal-only, though its engineering handover documentation is publicly available on GitHub.

providers.name: Verse
providers.description: Verse (verse.inc) is a private company backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, surfaced into the API Evangelist network from Bessemer's portfolio. Its public marketing site is served entirely behind a Cloudflare bot challenge, so the product and sector could not be independently characterized from the site itself during enrichment. What is verifiable: Verse operates a live, authenticated backend API at api.verse.inc built on the Connect RPC protocol (a gRPC-compatible framework — the host advertises the Connect-Protocol-Version header and OPTIONS/GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE methods), fronted by Google infrastructure, and it publishes an RFC 9116 security.txt naming a security contact. No public OpenAPI, developer docs, SDKs, or MCP server were discoverable. Sector remains undetermined pending further research.

providers.name: Via Global Health
providers.description: Via Global Health (VIA Global Health) is a medical equipment and pharmaceutical supplier serving distributors, healthcare providers, and NGOs across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. The company sources quality diagnostic equipment, surgical instruments, maternal and reproductive health devices, infection control and sterilization equipment, cold chain and laboratory supplies, and pharmaceutical-grade consumables from vetted manufacturers, and handles logistics, compliance, and last-mile delivery for low-resource health settings. Buyers request USD-priced quotes on any product page and receive a response within 24 hours, guided by an AI assistant named Amara. It is a quote-and-fulfillment marketplace with no publicly documented developer API surface; a private, robots-disallowed /api/* backs the storefront only. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Wintermute
providers.description: Wintermute is a leading global algorithmic trading firm and cryptocurrency market maker providing institutional-grade liquidity across centralized exchanges, decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols, and over-the-counter (OTC) markets. Its offerings span OTC spot trading for hundreds of tokens, options with bespoke structures, forwards, CFDs, programmatic "API liquidity", and a DeFi trading and liquidity-provisioning arm, plus Wintermute Ventures, an early-stage investment vehicle. Access to Wintermute's trading services is institutional and onboarding-gated through the node.wintermute.com portal (authenticated via an Auth0-backed OIDC / OAuth2 identity provider); there is no public self-serve developer API or open OpenAPI at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Zenflow
providers.description: Zenflow is a San Francisco-based medical device company founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) that develops the Zenflow Spring, a small permanent implant delivered in a minimally invasive in-office procedure to relieve urinary obstruction caused by benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). The company positions the Spring as a long-lasting alternative to daily BPH medications and to more invasive surgical procedures, avoiding their side effects and recovery burden. Zenflow is a medical-device / hardware company and does not publish a public API, developer platform, SDKs, MCP server, or webhooks; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: 21 Market
providers.description: 21 Market is the API Evangelist network profile for 주식회사 21세기전파상 (21st Century Electronics Shop Co., Ltd.), a South Korean consumer-electronics resale company that operates the Repercent (리퍼센트) service at repercent.com. Repercent buys used smartphones and mobile devices — iPhone, Galaxy, tablets, and laptops — from individual sellers, providing instant online price quotes, fast payment, and a simple pickup/logistics flow for secondhand device trade-in. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company and was surfaced into the network as a venture portfolio lead. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface; this profile captures verified company identity, its live web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: 6 Waves
providers.description: 6waves is a global mobile game publisher founded in 2008 and headquartered in Hong Kong, with offices in China, Japan, and the United States. The company partners with independent game developers around the world to publish, localize, and operate social and mobile games, offering culturalization, product guidance, live operations, marketing, platform relationships, customer service and community management, technical support, quality assurance, and VIP management. 6waves is recognized as a pioneer of top-grossing mobile game publishing, particularly in the Japanese market, and is a portfolio company of Insight Partners.

providers.name: Alliance DAO
providers.description: Alliance (Alliance DAO) is a leading crypto, fintech, and AI startup accelerator. Its cohort-based program pairs two weeks of in-person onboarding in New York City with eight weeks of remote acceleration, offering mentorship, lectures, weekly check-ins, and a Demo Day pitch event. Alliance invests $500,000 per startup and runs three cohorts per year. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital, Alliance publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: AlmostApps
providers.description: AlmostApps is a Sacramento, California sports-gaming studio founded in 2022 that builds free-to-play mobile entertainment experiences for sports fans, blending casual gameplay with real-life sports scores and stats. Its flagship product, Tailgate, is a free-to-play mobile sports entertainment app designed to enhance the game-day experience for casual sports enthusiasts. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Parade Ventures. AlmostApps is a consumer application company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation; only a marketing site with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy is publicly available. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Alterego
providers.description: Alterego is a Boston-based startup, spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 2025, building a near-telepathic silent-speech interface: a minimal, non-invasive wearable that detects the faint neuromuscular signals produced when a person internally verbalizes words, letting them interact with AI and computers without typing, tapping, or speaking aloud. Its "Silent Sense" technology responds only to intentional internal speech, keeping private thoughts private while enabling hands-free, screen-free messaging, queries, and information access. The company is pre-launch, backed by investors including Canaan, Granite Ventures, Mayfield, Rembrandt Venture Partners, and Cisco Investments. As of this profile Alterego publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Ambition
providers.description: Ambition (theambitionapp.com) is a consumer mobile application that helps teenagers get ready for real life. The app delivers short daily life-skills courses and 30-day simulated virtual internships across careers such as entrepreneurship, sales, game design, nursing, and wealth management, where US middle- and high-school students pick a path, build technical and life skills in about fifteen minutes a day, and can earn gift-card rewards for completing an internship. Ambition ships as native iOS and Android apps ("Ambition - Shape Your Future" / "Learn and Earn"); it is a business-to-consumer product with no public developer API, SDK, or documented integration surface as of this profile. This entry was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with the real, publicly verifiable identity, legal, and domain-security surface of the product.

providers.name: ARIVE
providers.description: ARIVE (getarive.com) was an urban quick-commerce platform founded in Paris during the COVID-19 pandemic that delivered fashion, beauty, and lifestyle products to customers within hours. Operating across Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, and Paris, it connected more than 500 brands and 200 local stores directly to young, convenience-focused urban shoppers. Backed by Balderton Capital, LaFamiglia, and Triple Point Capital with roughly €31.7M raised, the company ceased operations in mid-2023 following a sale of the business. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or other technical surface was ever published; this profile is retained for network and portfolio-graph completeness.

providers.name: Armstrong Robotics
providers.description: Armstrong Robotics is building general-purpose robots for commercial kitchens, beginning with autonomous dishwashing systems that load, run, and unload dishware without human intervention. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company is an early-stage robotics startup focused on kitchen labor automation. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced lead awaiting a public API surface, and this profile carries only the identity and domain-security signals that could be verified from its public website.

providers.name: Arro
providers.description: Arro is a consumer fintech company that helps people build or rebuild credit without traditional barriers. Its flagship product is the Arro Card, a Mastercard with no deposit and no hard credit check that starts at up to $300 and grows to $2,500, issued by Community Federal Savings Bank (member FDIC). The Arro app pairs the card with financial-education lessons, credit tracking, personalized guidance, and Artie, an AI money coach. Arro is a mobile-first consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Astranis
providers.description: Astranis designs, manufactures, and operates small, dedicated geostationary communications satellites known as MicroGEO. Each spacecraft uses radiation-hardened digital payload technology to deliver dedicated broadband capacity to specific countries, telecom operators, enterprise users, and the U.S. government. Astranis is a satellite operator and manufacturer rather than an API provider; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Atomic AI
providers.description: Atomic AI is a biotechnology company fusing machine learning with structural biology to unlock RNA drug discovery. Founded in 2017 by Raphael Townshend and based in San Francisco, the company builds ATOM-1, an AI foundation model that predicts the three-dimensional structure of RNA to enable the discovery and optimization of RNA-targeted small molecules and RNA-based medicines for previously undruggable targets, including certain cancers and neurodegenerative diseases. Atomic AI pairs its proprietary 3D RNA structure engine with large-scale in-house wet-lab assays. It is backed by Playground Global, 8VC, Greylock, and others. Atomic AI operates as a proprietary R&D drug-discovery platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity and web-surface signals for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AutoLotto
providers.description: AutoLotto, Inc. operates Lottery.com, a mobile platform that lets users in participating US states play official draw lottery games such as Powerball and Mega Millions from their phones, track tickets, view winning numbers, jackpot sizes and draw times, and collect winnings to a linked bank account. Beyond the consumer app, AutoLotto runs a business data-licensing offering that syndicates results and draw data for hundreds of lottery games worldwide to partner digital properties. AutoLotto is venture-backed (500 Global, Pantera Capital) and its parent trades publicly. As of this enrichment pass Lottery.com exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; data access is arranged through a manual "license our data" inquiry form rather than a programmatic surface.

providers.name: B2X
providers.description: B2X is a Munich-founded hardware lifecycle orchestration company that manages the complete service journey of electronic devices for global brands and operators — from warehousing, staging and onsite deployment through customer support, maintenance and repair, returns management, refurbishment and recycling. Its proprietary B2XONE platform combines ONE Connect (self-service customer portals with track & trace and appointment booking), ONE Service (operations management for repair, warehouse, inventory and logistics) and ONE Analytics (real-time KPIs and predictive insights), delivered through a network of 155+ certified service partners across 25+ countries. B2X serves mobile and consumer electronics, retail automation, B2B/enterprise and mission-critical segments. As of this profile, B2X does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Baller League
providers.description: Baller League is a small-sided (six-a-side) football entertainment league and media format founded in Germany that bills itself as "a new era of football, created for the streets by the streets." Teams are captained by professional footballers, influencers, and streamers, with matches played under a fast-paced ruleset and distributed primarily through live streaming and social video (Twitch, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram) rather than traditional broadcast. The organization has expanded from Germany into the United Kingdom and United States and is running its fourth season. It is a consumer sports-media and entertainment brand; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer program. Backed by EQT Ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: Beacon Power Services
providers.description: Beacon Power Services (BPS) is an African energy-technology company building software that helps electricity utilities and energy consumers manage the power grid more efficiently. Its platform spans three products: CAIMS, a customer and asset information management system for utility network, survey, installation, and new-service-connection management; Adora, a grid network management solution for commercial operations, network management, and field operations that helps utilities optimize operations and increase profitability; and Xepp, a consumer mobile app for energy consumption monitoring, instant electricity top-up, solar integration, and flexible payments. BPS serves utilities and distribution companies across Africa (clients include ECG and AEDC) and is backed by Partech. This profile currently has no public API or developer surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Beaubble
providers.description: Beaubble is a community-driven beauty commerce platform that lets creators launch their own customized, premium beauty brands and products by engaging their audiences. The company runs a direct-to-consumer storefront at beaubble.com featuring creator-led lines from talent such as Teni Panosian, Elsa Hosk, Shanina Shaik, Abbie Herbert, Rudi Berry, and Avrey Ovard, selling items like lip stains, freckle pens, and curated bundles. Backed by 500 Global, Beaubble is a consumer e-commerce brand with no public developer API surface; this profile was created by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline and captures the company's public web presence and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Beyond Aero
providers.description: Beyond Aero is a French aerospace company building the world's first electric business aircraft powered by hydrogen propulsion. Its flagship aircraft, "One", is designed to fly more than 800 nautical miles with zero in-flight carbon emissions, targeting the light business-jet market. The company pairs rapid prototyping and iterative aircraft design with in-house engineering tools such as HADES (Hydrogen Aircraft Data Exploration Software). Backed by Initialized Capital, Beyond Aero is a frontier-tech hardware startup rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface at this time. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched with company identity and web/domain-security signals.

providers.name: BigScreen
providers.description: Bigscreen is a social virtual-reality company founded in 2014 by Darshan Shankar. Its flagship Bigscreen app lets people watch movies, mirror their Windows PC desktop, play games, and hang out with friends inside shared virtual rooms across major VR platforms. In 2023 the company shipped the Bigscreen Beyond, an ultra-compact, custom-fit OLED PC-VR headset, followed by the Beyond 2 line. Bigscreen is a consumer VR hardware and software company backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors; it does not currently operate a public developer program or REST API. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: BIT ODD
providers.description: BIT ODD is a Helsinki-based mobile game studio founded in 2019 by former Supercell creative leads Lasse Louhento, Taneli Oksama, and Jani Lintunen. The studio hand-crafts casual mobile games driven by feeling and a sense of wonder rather than aggressive monetization, explicitly rejecting ad-spam and dark-pattern design. Backed by Index Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Makers Fund across a EUR 5M seed and a EUR 17M round, BIT ODD is a consumer entertainment company with no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead and carries only the artifacts that can be honestly probed from its public web presence (domain security, legal pages).

providers.name: Blavity
providers.description: Blavity Inc. is a Black-owned digital media and technology company founded in 2014 by Morgan DeBaun, operating a portfolio of premium content brands and events for Black millennials and Gen Z around culture, technology, travel, and lifestyle. Its properties include Blavity.com (news and culture), AfroTech (the largest Black tech conference and media brand), Travel Noire (travel), Shadow and Act (film and entertainment), and 21Ninety (women's lifestyle). Blavity Inc. monetizes through advertising, branded content, events, and its Blavity Media Group agency. It is a privately held company backed by investors including 500 Global and GV, and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications. This profile tracks Blavity as a company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Burt
providers.description: Burt builds AI teammates (AI coworkers) for logistics, aimed at freight brokers and forwarders. Its agents automate the repetitive, manual work of daily freight operations — track and trace, quoting, scheduling, carrier booking, document processing, proof-of-delivery chasing, and invoice and data entry — so human operators can focus on customer relationships and growing the business. Burt gives full visibility into every AI action with human oversight and approval workflows, rolls out autonomy gradually, and learns from operator corrections and exceptions to build institutional knowledge over time. Burt is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Burt does not currently publish a public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Business Insider
providers.description: Business Insider is a global business and financial news media company founded in 2007 and headquartered in New York City, operating as part of Axel Springer. It publishes fast-paced coverage of markets, technology, finance, the economy, retail, media, and careers across its flagship Business Insider brand and verticals such as Markets Insider. The organization was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm IVP. It operates consumer news properties and content syndication feeds rather than a public developer API program, so this profile tracks its public web presence and domain security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Bykea
providers.description: Bykea is a Karachi-based Pakistani mobility and logistics super-app that offers app-hailed motorbike rides, on-demand parcel and food delivery, cash pickup and drop-off, and digital payments across major Pakistani cities. It connects a large network of motorbike captains with riders and merchants, positioning itself as a low-cost transport, last-mile logistics, and financial services platform for the mass market. Backed by Prosus Ventures (Naspers), Bykea was added to the API Evangelist network as a mobility-sector portfolio lead; this profile has been enriched with the provider's public security surface (a live RFC 9116 security.txt and a HackerOne bug bounty program) and domain-security posture. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or partner API documentation is exposed - the primary web surface sits behind Cloudflare bot protection.

providers.name: C. R. Bard
providers.description: C. R. Bard, Inc. was an American multinational developer, manufacturer, and marketer of medical technologies in the fields of vascular, urology, oncology, and surgical specialties. Bard was founded in 1907 by Charles Russell Bard and was acquired by Becton, Dickinson and Company (BD) in December 2017 for approximately $24 billion. Bard's product lines now operate as part of BD's Interventional segment under the BD Bard brand. No public API or developer portal is published; integrations with hospital and provider systems are arranged through BD enterprise channels.

providers.name: Calificadas
providers.description: Calificadas is a Mexico-based, AI-powered human development company that combines artificial intelligence, strategic consulting, and training to help organizations and teams adapt to rapid change. Its tagline is "human infrastructure for the era of artificial intelligence." Its flagship product, CUALY (cualy.tech), is an AI-native platform for developing human capabilities through diagnosis, personalization, and continuous AI-driven feedback across communication, leadership, and collaboration, using voice and video analysis and AI coaches, plus organizational dashboards and iOS/Android apps. The company also delivers organizational consulting, leadership training, and adaptive training programs, and counts Coca-Cola FEMSA, ManpowerGroup, and Alsea among its clients. Backed by 500 Global, Calificadas was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation; artifacts below reflect its public web and domain-security surface only.

providers.name: Carezone
providers.description: CareZone is a consumer digital-health company (Care Zone Inc., backed by Obvious Ventures) offering a medication-management and family health-organization platform. Its mobile app lets people scan pill bottles to track medications, set reminders, log health readings such as blood glucose and blood pressure, and organize care information for themselves and loved ones, with a free medication delivery service and Medicare savings consultations. CareFlow, CareZone's pharmacy platform, automates traditional pharmacy workflows behind an ecommerce experience. The app reports over 5 million installs. CareZone operates as a consumer product and does not publish a public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Casey's General Stores
providers.description: Casey's General Stores is one of the largest convenience store chains in the United States, operating more than 2,900 stores selling fuel, made-from-scratch pizza, prepared food, and other convenience items primarily in small midwestern communities. Casey's is a publicly traded Fortune 500 company (NASDAQ: CASY) and offers a mobile app for pizza ordering, delivery, and its Casey's Rewards loyalty program. No public developer APIs have been documented; partner and supplier integrations are managed privately.

providers.name: Chai Shots
providers.description: Chai Shots is a Hyderabad-based microdrama OTT streaming platform for vertical, short-form fiction where every episode runs under two minutes. Built by the Chai Bisket team (co-founders Sharath Chandra and Anurag Reddy), it is positioned as India's first regional short-series OTT, launching in Telugu and other regional Indian languages for Gen Z and tier II/III audiences. The platform offers pay-per-episode and unlimited subscription access, a creator-first "Clap" tipping feature, and an AI-native production workflow. It raised a $5M seed round co-led by InfoEdge Ventures and General Catalyst. Chai Shots is a consumer content app with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile carries the company's identity and published web properties.

providers.name: ChemTech AI
providers.description: ChemTech AI is an industrial software company, founded in 2018 and headquartered in New York, that builds autonomous AI control systems for chemical production plants. Its software continuously optimizes manufacturing by autonomously adjusting DCS setpoints to push plants to their maximum safe capacity, sustaining peak production while reducing emissions and losses. The platform is applied across chemical processes including ammonia, nitric acid, phosphoric acid, sulfuric acid, methanol, ethanol, and polyethylene, serving the chemicals, food, cosmetics, and oil and gas sectors. ChemTech AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal are currently published.

providers.name: Chico's FAS
providers.description: Chico's FAS, Inc. is an American women's specialty retailer headquartered in Fort Myers, Florida, operating and franchising stores and websites under the Chico's, White House Black Market, and Soma brands. The company is a leading omni-channel specialty retailer of private branded sophisticated, casual-to-dressy clothing, intimates, sleepwear, and related accessories, with more than 1,400 retail and outlet stores in the United States and a substantial e-commerce footprint. Chico's FAS is part of the KnitWell Group portfolio. Chico's FAS does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; partner integrations are coordinated through corporate channels and the loyalty/credit card partnership with Synchrony and Mastercard.

providers.name: Church and Dwight
providers.description: Church & Dwight Co., Inc. is a Fortune 500 American consumer packaged goods (CPG) company headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey, that manufactures and markets a portfolio of household, personal care, health and wellness, beauty, and specialty products. Best known as the parent company of the Arm & Hammer baking soda brand (the company's flagship since 1846), Church & Dwight operates through three reporting segments: Consumer Domestic, Consumer International, and Specialty Products Division. The company's brand portfolio includes Arm & Hammer, Trojan, OxiClean, Vitafusion, L'il Critters, Therabreath, Hero (Mighty Patch), Batiste, Waterpik, OraJel, Nair, Spinbrush, First Response, RepHresh, Zicam, Flawless, Toppik, Viviscal, Kaboom, Orange Glo, XTRA laundry detergent, and Arrid antiperspirant. Church & Dwight does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; partner integrations are managed through internal portals, and consumer experiences focus on brand websites, e-commerce direct-to-consumer storefronts, and the Innovation Portal for external R&D partnerships.

providers.name: Clicker
providers.description: Clicker is a consumer-facing streaming guide and discovery platform that helps people find where to watch popular and new movies and TV shows across streaming providers, aggregating title availability from services such as Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, Max, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+, Paramount+, Peacock, Starz, BET+, Philo, and FuboTV into a single searchable catalog. The product is a web application (Next.js) organized around TV Shows and Movies browse and search experiences. Clicker is backed by Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Clicker publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; its only backend surface is a private, robots disallowed internal application API.

providers.name: Closing Theory Studios
providers.description: Closing Theory Studios, Inc. is an independent mobile game studio founded in 2023 and based in Austin, Texas, on a mission to bring the real world into games. Its debut title, Househunt (the officially licensed ZillowGoneWild game), lets the 70 million-plus people who browse Zillow for fun buy, guess prices on, renovate, flip, and manage real houses in a casual mobile experience aimed at "non-gamers." The studio was co-founded by Ankith Harathi and Nitin Rajinikanth and raised a $2.3M round led by a16z GAMES SPEEDRUN, with participation from Powerhouse Capital and angel Seth Sivak (founder of Proletariat, acquired by Blizzard). Closing Theory Studios ships consumer mobile games on iOS and Android and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Cooper Standard Holdings
providers.description: Cooper Standard Holdings is a global automotive supplier headquartered in Northville, Michigan, that designs, engineers, manufactures, and sells sealing systems, fuel and brake delivery systems, and fluid transfer systems for global automotive original equipment manufacturers including Ford, General Motors, Stellantis, and Volkswagen. The company operates in approximately 20 countries with around 32,000 employees and is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CPS. Cooper Standard does not publish a public developer program or REST APIs. Its digital presence centers on corporate, investor, supplier, and careers websites.

providers.name: couple
providers.description: couple (couple.me) is an AI companion chat platform operated by Fab AI LTD and backed by Slow Ventures. The consumer-facing product lets users create and customize an AI girlfriend, boyfriend, or anime character, then hold personalized text conversations and request AI-generated images from that companion. It offers a free tier with an optional premium subscription. It is a consumer app with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass; this profile captures the company identity and the domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Cowboy Space
providers.description: Cowboy Space Corporation builds space-based infrastructure for artificial-intelligence computing. Its flagship program, Stampede, is a constellation of solar-powered GPU data centers in Low Earth Orbit that integrate the rocket's upper stage with the satellite to form a megawatt-class data center with active thermal management and integrated compute. The company positions orbital compute as an alternative to terrestrial data centers, whose grid-connection lead times in major US markets can run five to seven years or more, arguing that Earth's energy grid cannot keep pace with AI demand. Cowboy Space is an early-stage aerospace and AI-infrastructure startup backed by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital; it currently publishes a corporate and careers presence with no public developer API.

providers.name: Cowboy Space Corporation
providers.description: Cowboy Space Corporation is a space infrastructure company building orbital data centers to address Earth's power constraints on artificial intelligence. Its Stampede satellite constellation places megawatt-class, GPU-equipped data centers in Low Earth Orbit powered by abundant solar energy, integrating the compute payload directly into the rocket's upper stage to maximize capacity and sidestep the multi-year terrestrial grid-connection delays that constrain traditional data centers. The company is an early-stage, venture-backed lead (backed by IVP); it currently publishes a corporate marketing site and careers portal but no developer portal, public API, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Create
providers.description: CREATE Medicines is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company developing in vivo CAR (chimeric antigen receptor) cell therapies using mRNA lipid-nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) delivery. Its platform reprograms immune cells, including T cells, NK cells, and myeloid cells, directly inside the body rather than extracting and engineering them ex vivo, with clinical and preclinical programs spanning oncology, autoimmune disease, and fibrosis. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub.
