Radia frames WindRunner as a deliberately low-novelty airframe assembled from existing certified technologies to shorten the certification path, targeting entry into service in the early 2030s across three markets: energy (delivering the very large blades that make low-wind onshore sites economic), defense (outsized-volume strategic airlift), and commercial supply-chain logistics. It has assembled an industrial ecosystem of more than twenty suppliers and technology partners including Aernnova, Leonardo, AFuzion, Atitech, Latecoere, Stirling Dynamics, Collier Aerospace and Maximus Air, and has raised roughly USD 128 million from investors including ConocoPhillips, Lauder Partners, LS Power Development and HCVC. Radia is an aircraft manufacturer and logistics operator rather than a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is the Strapi headless-CMS backend at radia.com/strapi that renders its own marketing site, whose content API is permission-locked and undocumented.

providers.name: Realta Fusion
providers.description: Realta Fusion is a fusion-energy company developing compact, scalable, modular magnetic-mirror fusion systems branded CoSMo fusion to deliver zero-carbon heat and electricity for industrial energy needs. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company designs prefabricated fusion modules that can be assembled to meet a variety of industrial power and process-heat requirements, targeting decarbonization of the roughly 37 billion metric tons of annual CO2 emissions from energy production. Realta Fusion is a hardware and energy-systems company and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks it in the API Evangelist network as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Rebag
providers.description: Rebag is an online marketplace for buying, selling, and trading pre-owned luxury goods — designer handbags, watches, fine jewelry, shoes, apparel, and accessories from houses such as Chanel, Hermes, Louis Vuitton, Prada, Goyard, and Gucci. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in New York City, Rebag authenticates every item in-house and is known for Clair (Comprehensive Luxury Appraisal Index for Resale), an AI-driven pricing engine that gives sellers instant, guaranteed buyback quotes. Rebag operates a mobile app, physical retail stores, and consignment/trade-in programs, and is backed by investors including General Catalyst. This profile tracks Rebag's public web presence; no public developer API has been identified.

providers.name: Reno
providers.description: Reno (Reno Home) is a Dubai, UAE based one-stop home renovation platform that connects homeowners and businesses with professional interior designers and vetted contractors, managing renovation projects end-to-end from design and contracting through quality inspections and completion. Its Reno mobile app lets clients track project progress, budgets, timelines and change requests in real time, and it offers a "Renovate Now, Pay Later" financing model with 3, 6 or 12 month installment plans. Reno is backed by 500 Global (500 Sanabil), Hub71 and other regional investors. It is a consumer-facing service and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: SALARY HERO PTE. LTD
providers.description: Salary Hero is a Singapore-headquartered financial wellness and earned wage access (EWA) platform offered to employees through their employers. Its products include Salary on Demand (accessing earned wages before payday), budgeting and spending-tracking tools, savings accounts (a partnership with Dime offering 3% interest), and financial-literacy education covering debt management and investing. The service is delivered via iOS and Android apps and is provisioned by employers, integrating with existing payroll and HR systems. Salary Hero is a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Savion Aerospace
providers.description: Savion Aerospace (FlySavion) is an aerospace company developing sustainable, zero-emissions aviation technology. Its flagship SavionJet is an autonomous blended-wing-body (ABWB) aircraft with a standup cabin and satellite-based piloting via proprietary autonomous flight software, and the company offers Zero-Emissions Flight Credits (ZFCs) as a subscription for organizations seeking carbon-free air travel beyond offsetting. Savion demonstrated a cryogenic LNG-fueled flight in 2019 and is a 500 Global (500 Startups) and Alchemist Accelerator portfolio company. The company operates as an aviation hardware and services business and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Seismic Therapeutic
providers.description: Seismic Therapeutic is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing transformative biologic medicines for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. The company pairs structural biology with machine learning through its proprietary IMPACT platform to design multi-functional antibodies and Immunoglobulin Sculpting (IgSc) enzymes across cell-mediated, allergic, and antibody-mediated immune diseases. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As a therapeutics R&D company it publishes no public developer or API surface at seismictx.com; this profile captures its corporate identity only.

providers.name: Serviceware SE
providers.description: Serviceware SE is a German enterprise software, consulting, and managed-services company with more than 25 years in business, roughly 420 employees, and over EUR 100 million in annual revenue. Its platform spans Enterprise Service Management (ESM) for IT, HR, and customer service, IT Financial Management (ITFM) for cost tracking and technology business management, Corporate Performance Management (CPM) for budgeting, planning, and reporting, AI-powered Knowledge Management, and Field Service Management. Serviceware positions its platform as AI-native, with no-code workflows, data integration, governance, and self-service capabilities. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Shift EV
providers.description: Shift EV is an electric-mobility company that retrofits existing commercial vehicles to electric power through an "electrofitting" service, converting fleet vehicles to EV drivetrains in under an hour with zero upfront cost. The company designs and installs plug-and-play EV drivetrains, lithium-ion battery packs, on-site charging infrastructure, and fleet-management software for FMCG, e-commerce, service, and OEM fleets. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Shift EV was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Simr
providers.description: Simr (a registered trademark of The UberCloud, Inc., based in Los Altos, California) is a Simulation Operations Automation (SimOps) platform that streamlines complex engineering simulations across the product-development lifecycle. It provides self-service, automated infrastructure for running CFD, FEA, multi-physics, and system-level simulations with major solvers such as ANSYS, Abaqus, and COMSOL, deploying directly into customer-owned cloud environments on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, or on-premises. Simr targets enterprise manufacturers, reducing operational overhead for engineering teams while keeping data control and compliance security-first. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Earlybird and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Simr publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Spacee
providers.description: Spacee Inc. (株式会社スペイシー) is a Tokyo-based space-sharing and rental marketplace operator in Japan. Its consumer platforms let people discover and book temporary spaces by the hour: Yoyappin, a booking marketplace for meeting rooms, conference rooms, studios, kitchens and event venues across the Tokyo metropolitan area; THE POINT, a premium coworking and creative "third place" for remote workers; and Office Connect, a nationwide search service for shared offices, rental offices, coworking spaces and virtual offices. Spacee also expands via partnerships (e.g. JR West Japan) and acquisitions (GYYM pay-per-use fitness). It operates as a consumer web and mobile marketplace and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Spider Capital
providers.description: Spider Capital is a seed-stage venture capital firm investing in applied-AI enterprise cloud software that modernizes complex industrial sectors. The firm backs founders across construction, financial services, energy, government, healthcare, insurance, mining, manufacturing, supply chain, and transportation, citing 100+ enterprise cloud investments, a 70%+ seed-to-Series-A graduation rate, and portfolio companies including Mechanical Orchard, Imubit, CoLab, Percepto, Codoxo, Klir, Elara Spatial, and Logiwa. Surfaced as a portfolio company of foundry-group; it publishes no public API or developer surface (venture-capital firm), so this profile carries firm identity rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Stoke Space
providers.description: Stoke Space Technologies is an American space launch company based in Kent, Washington, founded in 2020 by a team of former Blue Origin and SpaceX engineers, led by co-founders Andy Lapsa and Tom Feldman (both ex-Blue Origin). The company is developing Nova, a medium-lift, 100% fully reusable rocket aimed at dramatically lowering the cost of access to orbit, along with its Zenith full-flow staged-combustion first-stage engine, the Andromeda second-stage engine, and a reusable metallic reentry heat shield. Stoke operates a 168,000 sq ft assembly facility and headquarters in Kent and a rocket test site near Moses Lake, Washington. Backed by Spark Capital and others, the company extended its Series D financing to $860 million in 2026. Stoke Space is a physical aerospace/hardware manufacturer and launch provider; it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: StoneEagle F&I
providers.description: StoneEagle F&I is an automotive Finance & Insurance (F&I) technology company that has spent more than 35 years building the software backbone of dealership F&I operations. Its product suite spans Variable Ops (StoneEagleMENU, an electronic F&I menu-selling and product-presentation system, and StoneEagleMETRICS, real-time DMS-sourced sales and F&I reporting), Fixed Ops (PENCILWRENCH and StoneEagleMETRICS SERVICE for the service drive), and industry benchmarking (StoneEagleDATA, transaction-level insight across more than half of U.S. franchised dealers). StoneEagle connects to dealerships through certified DMS integrations and partners such as Dealertrack and F&I Express, but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal — integration is delivered as private, certified dealer and partner connections. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Supponor
providers.description: Supponor is a virtual advertising technology company for live sports broadcasting, now part of TGI Sport. Its software digitally replaces and inserts in-venue brand placements with real-time overlays, letting broadcasters serve region-targeted advertising across multiple feeds, languages, surfaces, and camera angles. Core products include AIR, an AI-driven virtual advertising platform for live broadcast; HUB, a pre-event suite for fixtures, inventory, playlists, creative and approvals; and Data Room, a post-event analytics platform for reporting, video storage, and performance metrics. Supponor works across any sport and surface with remotely deployable, all-weather technology, and is used by organizations including FC Bayern, the NHL, The FA, Serie A, and La Liga. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Northzone; it publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Syntetica
providers.description: Syntetica is a French cleantech company using green chemistry to close the loop on synthetic textiles, starting with nylon. Its proprietary chemical process depolymerises nylon-blend fabrics, separating and purifying Nylon 6 and Nylon 6,6 from elastane, cotton, and other fibres in a single process to produce virgin-quality, low-carbon recycled polymers that drop in as replacements for fossil-derived nylon across textile, automotive, and high-performance applications. Backed by EQT Ventures, Bpifrance, SWEN Capital Partners, lululemon, and MAS Holdings, the company raised a $30M Series A in July 2026 to build its first commercial demonstration facility in France. Syntetica is a materials-science and manufacturing company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Tala
providers.description: Tala is an AI-native digital financial services company providing instant credit, digital wallets, money transfers, and cash-out services to underserved consumers in informal economies. Built on a proprietary, patent-pending credit-decisioning model trained on billions of dollars of lending data, Tala has delivered more than $7B in credit access to over 13 million customers across Kenya, Mexico, the Philippines, India, Vietnam, Guatemala, Panama, and the Dominican Republic. The company also offers Embedded Credit infrastructure for partners. Tala reaches customers primarily through consumer mobile apps; no public developer API or documentation portal is currently published.

providers.name: Tavern Research
providers.description: Tavern Research is a political opinion research and communications firm that integrates polling, message testing, and original ad production for Democratic campaigns and advocacy organizations. It pairs rapid survey research (marketed as "insights in 48 hours"), AI-powered content creation, and large-scale creative experimentation to learn which messages move voters, then produces and optimizes ads through placement. Surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the firm runs a marketing website on Squarespace and publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Techmate
providers.description: Techmate is an on-demand IT field-services network that provides on-site, boots-on-the-ground ("Smart Hands") technical support across 450+ cities. It matches businesses and overstretched IT teams with certified local technicians for desktop and hardware support, network setup, audio/visual work, IT project management, and staff augmentation, with dashboards to track requests, spend, and work history across distributed offices. Techmate is a services marketplace rather than a developer/API platform; it publishes a public website and blog but no developer portal, API, or documentation surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Text'nPayMe
providers.description: Text'nPayMe is an award-winning B2B fintech company, established in Armenia and incorporated in the USA in 2022, that builds embedded payment solutions for banks, fintechs, telecoms, and online shops. Its two core products are a Payment Keyboard SDK, which embeds send-money transactions directly inside 150+ messaging, social, and gaming apps via a payment keyboard for iOS, Android, and a Chrome extension, and a Payment Gateway Hub for transaction routing, reconciliation, and reporting. The company markets an "Apex Security Layer" with proprietary encryption and risk management, supports cross-border payments, and joined the 500 Global accelerator after winning the Entrepreneurship World Cup 2022 National Finals. The SDK is delivered to enterprise customers through direct integration engagements rather than a public self-serve developer portal, so no public API specification, developer documentation, or client packages are currently published.

providers.name: ThatGameCompany
providers.description: ThatGameCompany is an American independent video game studio founded in 2006 by Jenova Chen and Kellee Santiago, known for emotionally driven, art-forward titles including Flow, Flower, Journey, and the free-to-play social adventure Sky: Children of the Light. The studio focuses on creating timeless interactive entertainment that inspires human connection across all ages. It publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a technology / gaming entity and records domain-security posture from live probes.

providers.name: TheNoor
providers.description: TheNoor is a Shariah-inspired and guided company behind "TheNoor" — an Islamic lifestyle mobile application for Muslims, available on iOS and Android. The app bundles daily religious and lifestyle utilities such as prayer times, Qibla direction, Quran, Islamic calendar, and related community and content features into a single consumer product. TheNoor is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes only a consumer website and a private mobile backend at api.thenoor.co; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: TMRW Sports
providers.description: TMRW Sports is a sports, media, and entertainment company founded by professional golfers Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, with Mike McCarley as Founder and CEO, focused on building modern, tech-forward approaches to live sports. Its ventures include TGL, a primetime team golf league played in partnership with the PGA TOUR; WTGL, a professional women's golf league; and a professional flag football league launching in partnership with the NFL. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners, TMRW Sports operates consumer sports and entertainment properties and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Topgolf Callaway Brands
providers.description: Topgolf Callaway Brands is a global golf and entertainment company that designs, manufactures, and sells golf clubs, balls, apparel, and accessories under the Callaway, Odyssey, OGIO, TravisMathew, and Jack Wolfskin brands, and operates Topgolf entertainment venues and the Toptracer ball-tracking technology. Topgolf Callaway Brands does not publish a single public developer API portal, though Toptracer ball-tracking technology is licensed to driving ranges through a separate commercial program.

providers.name: TruckLabs
providers.description: TruckLabs built TruckWings, an automated tractor-mounted aerodynamic device that closes the gap between the tractor and trailer to reduce aerodynamic drag, cutting fuel consumption by a proven 3-6% and eliminating roughly 7-10 metric tons of CO2 per truck each year with an 18-24 month payback. The device deploys automatically at highway speed and retracts below it, reduces buffeting and trailer sway in crosswinds, and installs on both new builds and retrofits in about two hours. TruckLabs was acquired by ConMet, and trucklabs.com now redirects to the ConMet TruckWings product line. As a hardware fuel-efficiency company, TruckLabs exposes no public developer API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture. Backed by Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Ultima Genomics
providers.description: Ultima Genomics is a genomics technology company that develops high-throughput, cost-effective DNA sequencing platforms and solutions, led by its UG200 Series sequencer aimed at population-scale genomics. Its platform spans germline sequencing, oncology, single-cell analysis, proteomics, and epigenomics, paired with library-preparation workflows and bioinformatics tooling. The company does not operate a hosted developer REST API or SDK; its programmatic surface is open-source bioinformatics tools and WDL pipelines published on GitHub, including workflows compatible with AWS HealthOmics. Added to the API Evangelist network via the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio.

providers.name: Valinor
providers.description: Valinor Enterprises is a defense and government technology operational holding company — a "company of companies" that builds and buys mission-critical technologies to fill the gaps others ignore. It centralizes go-to-market, compliance, security, and operations while decentralizing engineering across lean Product Companies including Condor (attritable aerial systems), Dispatch (drone charging infrastructure, selected by DIU for the CADDS program), Harbor (expeditionary medical systems for the Marine Corps), Reflex (smart optics with onboard vision models), and Streamline (AI-enabled data collection with structured ontology write-back). Backed by General Catalyst; raised a $54M Series A led by Friends & Family Capital. Valinor publishes no public API or developer portal; its developer footprint is a GitHub organization and the @valinor-enterprises npm scope.

providers.name: Veritasfin
providers.description: Veritas Finance Limited is a non-banking finance company (NBFC) in India focused on retail and micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) lending to underserved and self-employed customers. Its lending products include MSME and business loans, loan against property, home loans, mortgage and working-capital finance, and used commercial vehicle loans, supported by an EMI calculator, branch network, online payment portals and an investor-relations and corporate-governance section. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. Public probing of veritasfin.in finds a corporate financial-services website with no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface at this time.

providers.name: Verkor
providers.description: Verkor is a French cleantech manufacturer founded in 2020 to fast-track low-carbon lithium-ion battery production in Europe. Operating a "digital by design" industrial model, Verkor produces high-performance battery cells and modules for electric mobility and stationary energy storage, scaling through its Dunkerque Gigafactory toward 16 GWh of annual cell capacity to serve the European market. Verkor is a physical-products/industrial company and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and public web surface within the API Evangelist network. Backed by EQT Ventures.

providers.name: Vermeer
providers.description: Vermeer is an American-Ukrainian defense-technology startup (founded 2018 by Brian Streem; headquartered in New York with forward operations in Kyiv) building vision-based autonomy for unmanned aerial platforms. Its Visual Positioning System (VPS) uses electro-optical and infrared cameras plus onboard AI (NVIDIA) to match imagery to 2D/3D maps and deliver precise navigation in GPS-denied, jammed, or spoofed environments. Products include Air (absolute positioning without GPS), Celestial (star-based navigation), and Terminal Guidance (precision targeting). The technology has been fielded by the Armed Forces of Ukraine and is aimed at defense customers including Lockheed Martin, General Atomics, Northrop Grumman, and the U.S. Air Force and Army. Vermeer exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time; this profile is a company/marketing surface with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Vitesse
providers.description: Vitesse is a universal physical-AI platform for industrial machines, founded by the team behind Tesla's "Model 3 automation hell" fix alongside leaders from SpaceX, Siemens, and Safran. It connects any machine - Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, and legacy PLCs - through 135 native OT connectors, generates control logic from a natural-language description of a process (up to 15x faster than traditional PLC programming), and runs the full stack at the edge on purpose-built industrial controllers with no cloud required. The platform layers hardware, live data dashboards and SCADA views, interoperability, physical AI, and zero-trust OT/IT cybersecurity (NIS2 and NIST aligned) into one stack, with real-time browser-based monitoring across 800,000+ machine hours. Vitesse exposes a marketing website and a login-gated product application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Westar Energy
providers.description: Westar Energy was the largest electric utility in Kansas, providing electric service to homes, businesses, and industries throughout Kansas before merging with Great Plains Energy in 2018 to form Evergy, Inc. As Evergy, the company continues to serve approximately 1.6 million customers in Kansas and Missouri with a focus on grid modernization, smart metering (AMI) through its Gridstream Connect IoT platform, and clean energy transformation including wind power and demand response programs.

providers.name: Wise Systems
providers.description: Wise Systems provides autonomous routing and last-mile delivery optimization software powered by machine learning. Its platform helps fleet operators plan strategy, optimize and dynamically re-route deliveries, dispatch in real time, track driver performance, and improve last-mile efficiency across industries including auto parts, beverage, building materials, container management, field service, food service, healthcare, linen services, parcel/courier, and retail. Wise Systems exposes an internal "Engine API" during customer implementations to connect data inputs and outputs, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs. Backed by Techstars and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

providers.name: Above
providers.description: Above (Above Security) is an AI-native insider risk management platform that detects and investigates risky human and AI-agent activity across SaaS, identity, and endpoints. Rather than flagging statistical anomalies, Above focuses on intent-based insider risk — understanding what a person or AI agent was actually trying to do — and assembles investigation-ready narratives from behavioral signal without invasive screen or keystroke content capture. Its platform pairs real-time user guidance with AI investigative agents to catch data exfiltration, credential leaks, shadow and personal AI use, custom GPT risk, and pre-departure flight-risk data theft. Above is the inaugural sponsor of the Forscie Insider Threat Matrix and publishes the Insider Risk Index. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network from that portfolio.

providers.name: AID:Tech
providers.description: AID:Tech is a Dublin-based payments and digital-identity infrastructure company that bridges Web2 and Web3, delivering self-sovereign decentralized identity (DID), KYC/AML verification, digital wallets with virtual cards, and secure payouts for benefits distribution, disaster relief, and financial inclusion. Its products include Kare (benefits and disaster-relief distribution) and Klimify, and its engineering is rooted in blockchain and distributed-ledger technology (Hyperledger Fabric, Openchain, and the bryk/algo DID methods). AID:Tech does not publish a first-party public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; its public technical surface is its GitHub organization (DID-method reference implementations, a Circle API SDK, and Kubernetes/Hyperledger tooling) and its Medium engineering blog.

providers.name: American Endovascular
providers.description: American Endovascular & Amputation Prevention is a vascular medical practice operating outpatient centers across New York City (Brooklyn, Harlem, and Queens) that specializes in minimally invasive, same-day endovascular treatment of peripheral artery disease (PAD) and related circulatory conditions. Services include atherectomy, angioplasty, stent placement, amputation prevention, diagnostic imaging (angiogram, ultrasound, CTA, MRA), neuropathy neurostimulation, dialysis access management, and venous insufficiency care. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a public website, blog, and privacy policy but exposes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Andustry
providers.description: Andustry is an AI-native industrial equipment broker that streamlines sourcing and procurement for manufacturers. The platform combines AI-powered supplier discovery with manual qualification and commercial negotiation to source industrial machines (CNC mills, lathes, press brakes, laser cutters, robotic cells), machined/forged/cast parts, and robotics and electronics across Europe, China, India, and the United States. Clients hand off a sourcing need and Andustry returns a verified supplier shortlist within 24-48 hours, delivering an average of roughly 30% cost savings and 2x faster sourcing timelines on a commission-only basis with no subscription. Founded in 2026 (Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch) by Het Dave and Johann Stuerken and operated as Andustry GmbH.

providers.name: Assemble Labs
providers.description: Assemble Labs is an AI-powered hardware testing platform that autonomously designs and runs experiments on embedded systems, letting engineers validate firmware against specifications using real lab instruments without manual setup. It converts engineering requirements into executable test cases, drives physical devices through real instrument control (oscilloscopes, power profilers, logic analyzers from Saleae, Tektronix, Keysight, Rohde & Schwarz, Fluke, Yokogawa, National Instruments and Joulescope), performs root-cause analysis, proposes firmware fixes, and verifies them on actual hardware. Test results and reports are committed to Git for traceability. The product runs on-premises and air-gapped with zero data egress, and integrates with VS Code, Cursor, and Claude. Assemble Labs is an early-stage company (pre-seed, $1.3M led by Menlo Ventures) and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: AssistIQ Technologies
providers.description: AssistIQ Technologies builds AI-powered computer vision for the healthcare supply chain, automatically capturing the implants, supplies, and tissues used during surgical cases in real time so hospitals can bill with confidence. Its platform pairs three products - Capture (computer-vision recognition of implants and supplies at point of use), Charge Capture (automated charge data submission and review), and Insights (analytics on supply variation and utilization) - and integrates with major EHR and ERP systems including recognition in the Epic Showroom and a GE HealthCare partnership. AssistIQ reports up to an 80% increase in billable product revenue, a 48% reduction in expiry-related costs, and 15+ minutes saved per case. The platform is HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II compliant. The company is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: Augmenta
providers.description: Augmenta is a Toronto-based generative AI company building the Augmenta Construction Platform (ACP), a Spatial AI system that automates building design — starting with electrical raceway routing and expanding into mechanical and plumbing (MEP). ACP ingests Revit models, accepts conduit run schedules, fly/no-fly zones, and project specifications, then generates clash-free, constructable 3D conduit routes in the cloud and exports them back into Revit as system conduit ready for detailing and prefabrication. The platform combines computational geometry, advanced optimization, and machine learning to handle data-center, hospital, and school-scale electrical builds, and is marketed to VDC teams and electrical contractors as a way to cut BIM time by roughly two-thirds. Augmenta was founded by veterans of generative design for advanced manufacturing, won EC&M 2026 Product of the Year, was named to the 2026 Global Cleantech 100, and signed a five-year strategic partnership with E-J Electric Installation Co. The product is delivered as a SOC2-certified Revit add-in with a cloud back-end; there is no public REST API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: AutoFi
providers.description: AutoFi ("The Sales Momentum Company") is an AI-powered automotive commerce platform that connects online and in-store car-buying experiences for dealerships, OEMs, lenders, and online marketplaces. Its products span digital retailing (online financing exploration and personalized deal paths with real payments and options), showroom solutions (in-store deal-structuring tools that preserve dealership profitability and buyer transparency), and Smartlink lead management (funneling customer responses into dealership workflows). AutoFi was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of enrichment it exposes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile captures its public web and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Berry Genomics
providers.description: Berry Genomics (Beijing Berry and Kang Biotechnology Co., Ltd., 贝瑞基因) is a Chinese genomics and genetic-testing company operating across reproductive health screening, hereditary disease detection, tumor and cancer diagnostics, laboratory solutions, sequencing equipment and reagents, and genomic big-data services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company publishes a corporate marketing site (news, investor relations, careers, and a legal statement) but does not currently expose a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Big Health
providers.description: Big Health is a digital mental health company that develops evidence-based digital therapeutics for common mental health conditions. Its products include SleepioRx and DaylightRx, FDA-cleared prescription digital therapeutics for insomnia and generalized anxiety disorder, alongside the consumer apps Sleepio, Daylight, and Spark Direct. Big Health sells to health systems and providers, health plans, and employers rather than through a public developer program; it currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK. Backed by Index Ventures and SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: BioAge Labs
providers.description: BioAge Labs (Nasdaq ticker BIOA) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Emeryville, California, developing therapies that target the biology of human aging to treat metabolic diseases such as obesity and its related conditions. Its proprietary discovery platform mines longitudinal human multi-omics data to identify aging-related molecular pathways, which feed a therapeutic pipeline that includes BGE-102, an oral NLRP3 inhibitor aimed at chronic inflammation and cardiovascular risk, and an APJ (apelin receptor) agonist developed as an exercise mimetic for obesity. The company is backed by a16z and Redpoint Ventures and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile. BioAge Labs publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time; this profile captures its corporate and web-property identity plus a domain-security probe of its primary web host.

providers.name: BoardEffect
providers.description: BoardEffect is a board management (board portal) platform for meetings, agendas, board books, document libraries, committees, workrooms, surveys, and voting, purpose-built for mission-driven organizations such as nonprofits, healthcare systems, higher education institutions, foundations, and credit unions. BoardEffect is owned by Diligent and is delivered as part of the Diligent One Platform. It does not publish a self-serve public developer API - integrations are handled through a customer-facing Integration Panel (SSO plus documented web services) provisioned per tenant, and the separate Diligent Developer Portal (developer.diligent.com) exposes APIs for the Diligent One GRC platform rather than for BoardEffect's board-management data. Pricing is contact-sales only (annual subscription, tiered by users).

providers.name: Braveheart Bio
providers.description: Braveheart Bio is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and related cardiac conditions. Its lead candidate, BHB-1893, is a selective cardiac myosin inhibitor (licensed as HRS-1893 from Hengrui Pharma) designed to reduce excessive heart-muscle contraction and improve cardiac performance in patients with obstructive and non-obstructive HCM. The San Francisco-based company launched in November 2025 with a $185M Series A led by a16z alongside Forbion, OrbiMed, Enavate Sciences, and Frazier Life Sciences, and filed for a Nasdaq IPO in July 2026. Braveheart Bio is a corporate/scientific organization and does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: C++
providers.description: C++ is a general-purpose, statically typed, compiled programming language created by Bjarne Stroustrup as an extension of C. C++ supports object- oriented, generic, and functional programming and is widely used in systems programming, game engines, embedded systems, scientific computing, finance, and high-performance services. The language is standardized by ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG21 with current revisions including C++20 and C++23. C++ does not expose a network/HTTP API; this index captures the language home, standards process, reference documentation, and ecosystem resources.

providers.name: Campbell's
providers.description: Campbell's (Campbell Soup Company, now The Campbell's Company) is the consumer brand trusted for generations to provide authentic, flavourful, and readily available soups, meals, and recipes. Alongside its consumer website, Campbell's has historically operated a Campbell's Kitchen Developer API that let developers embed Campbell's, Swanson, Pace, Prego, and Pepperidge Farm recipes, products, and nutrition data into their own web and mobile experiences.

providers.name: CANbridge Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: CANbridge Pharmaceuticals (CANbridge Life Sciences Ltd.) is a global, China-based biopharmaceutical company founded in 2012 that focuses on the research, development, and commercialization of transformative therapies for rare diseases and rare oncology. The company in-licenses and develops differentiated drug candidates from around the world for the Chinese and global markets, with a portfolio of approved products and a gene-therapy and enzyme-replacement pipeline. Headquartered in Beijing with offices in Shanghai, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Suzhou, and Burlington, Massachusetts (USA), CANbridge is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming; CANbridge publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Carrick Therapeutics
providers.description: Carrick Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, developing novel oncology therapies aimed at improving outcomes for patients with aggressive and treatment-resistant cancers. Its pipeline centers on transcriptional CDK inhibition, led by samuraciclib (a CDK7 inhibitor in Phase 2) and CT7439 (a CDK12/13 inhibitor in Phase 1), pursued as combination therapies across advanced hormone-receptor-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer, prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, and additional indications. The company is backed by GV (Google Ventures) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company profile; it publishes no developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: ChangeTip
providers.description: ChangeTip was a Bitcoin micropayments and social-tipping service built by ChangeCoin, Inc. (San Francisco), founded in 2013. It let people send small bitcoin tips across Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, Twitch, Facebook, Slack, email, and text by replying with an amount, settling the micropayment behind the scenes to a hosted wallet. ChangeTip published an open API and first-party client libraries (Python and JavaScript) so the community could build tipping integrations and pair external wallets. The company raised roughly $3.5M and was backed by 500 Startups, Pantera Capital, and Gil Penchina. ChangeCoin was acquired by Airbnb in 2016 and the tipping service was discontinued in November 2016; the site now serves only a shutdown notice with balance withdrawal. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cofactor Genomics
providers.description: Cofactor Genomics is a precision-medicine biotechnology company that applies RNA-sequencing and machine learning to build predictive immuno-oncology diagnostics. Its flagship OncoPrism assay is designed to predict which cancer patients will respond to immunotherapy, and the company runs the multi-center PREDAPT clinical trial across more than 24 healthcare systems spanning 11 solid-tumor cancers. Cofactor Genomics is a diagnostics and life-sciences company rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record surfaced from venture-capital portfolios (DCVC, Menlo Ventures, Y Combinator) and enriched with identity and domain-security metadata.

providers.name: Compose
providers.description: Compose (Compose, Inc., compose.io) was a database-as-a-service (DBaaS) provider that offered production-ready, auto-scaling, hosted deployments of open-source databases — MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch, RabbitMQ, RethinkDB, ScyllaDB, etcd, MySQL, and Disque — each provisioned with high availability, automated backups, and a REST API for programmatic management. Founded in 2010 as MongoHQ and rebranded to Compose in 2014, the company was backed by DCVC (Data Collective) and was acquired by IBM in 2015, after which the offering was folded into IBM Cloud as "IBM Compose" / IBM Cloud Databases. The standalone Compose service and its developer surface (compose.com, compose.io, apidocs.compose.com) have since been deprecated and taken offline. This profile documents the surviving, verifiable first-party artifacts — the archived GitHub organization at github.com/compose, the official Go SDK (gocomposeapi) wrapping the Compose REST API, and the official command-line tools (bach, cocli).

providers.name: Convoke
providers.description: Convoke is building an AI-native operating system for the biopharmaceutical industry. Founded in 2024 and based in South San Francisco, the platform unifies fragmented internal knowledge, workflows, and external data into a continuously updating workspace, codifies the decision logic behind high-stakes choices, and generates critical deliverables such as competitive intelligence briefs, portfolio strategy analyses, market research, and scientific manuscripts across the drug development lifecycle. Convoke serves biopharma teams working in business development, competitive intelligence, portfolio strategy, market research, and medical affairs. The company raised an $8.6M seed round co-led by Kleiner Perkins and Dimension. As of this profile, Convoke publishes a public marketing and company site but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Dealogic
providers.description: Dealogic is a global provider of content and software for the capital markets, including deal-management, analytics, league-table, and compliance solutions used by investment banks, sales/trading desks, and investment managers. Dealogic delivers data and connectivity primarily through its Cortex platform, Dealogic Connect, and Analytics products rather than a self-service public developer API; integrations are contracted with customers and accessed under license rather than from a public developer portal.

providers.name: Deep Genomics
providers.description: Deep Genomics is an AI-driven genetic medicines platform company based in Toronto, Canada. It uses biological foundation models (its BioFM Platform) and lab-integrated AI workflows to discover and develop RNA-based genetic medicines, combining AI model development, high-throughput screening technologies, and information systems to accelerate drug discovery and advance new treatments. Founded by deep learning researcher Brendan Frey, the company is backed by investors including Bloomberg Beta and SoftBank Vision Fund. It surfaces no public developer API, portal, or documentation at this time; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Delphia Therapeutics
providers.description: Delphia Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts oncology biotechnology company pioneering "activation lethality," a precision-medicine approach that targets cancer cells' vulnerability to oncogene overactivation by selectively over-activating cancer-linked signaling until tumor cells can no longer survive. Founded by oncology drug developers Kevin Marks, Bill Sellers, and Mike Dillon, the company launched with a $67 million Series A financing led by GV, with participation from Nextech Invest, Polaris Innovation Fund, and Alexandria Venture Investments. Delphia is a preclinical-stage drug developer and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Diverge Health
providers.description: Diverge Health is a value-based care company that partners with primary care practices to improve outcomes for underserved and Medicaid patient populations. It embeds community-based care teams, health coaches, and behavioral health clinicians into medical practices to address medical, social, and behavioral needs, supported by data aggregation and technology. The company backs providers with chronic disease management (diabetes, COPD, hypertension, heart failure), collaborative behavioral health, and social-needs support across multiple states. Backed by GV, Diverge Health operates as a services and enablement organization rather than a public API provider; it currently publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable interface. This profile tracks its public web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DNN Software
providers.description: DNN Software is the company behind DNN Platform (formerly DotNetNuke), a leading open-source web content management system (CMS) and web application framework built on Microsoft ASP.NET and C#. Originally created by Shaun Walker in 2002, DNN provides a modular platform for building websites, intranets, and web applications, extended through custom modules, providers, and skins. For developers, DNN ships a first-party set of .NET libraries on NuGet (DotNetNuke.Core, DotNetNuke.WebApi, DotNetNuke.Web, and related packages) plus a DotNetNuke Web API (ASP.NET Web API) services framework for building authenticated REST endpoints inside a DNN site. The open-source DNN Platform is developed in the open on GitHub under an MIT license, with community documentation, forums, and Discord maintained by the DNN Community.

providers.name: Efference AI
providers.description: Efference AI is a robotics perception and compute company building the hardware-plus-software foundation for data-driven robotics at scale. Founded in 2025 by Gianluca Bencomo and based in San Francisco (Y Combinator Fall 2025), Efference treats machine vision as a software problem, pairing affordable stereo-camera hardware with learned 3D-perception foundation models ("cheap hardware + great algorithms"). Its M1 device targets distributed, robotics-grade data collection at scale, while the H1 stereo system is built for real-time cloud inference with foundation models. The company serves autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots, and drones, and publishes hardware-interfacing documentation and firmware through its GitHub organization. As of this profile Efference exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or authenticated service surface.

providers.name: Fitmint
providers.description: Fitmint is a mobile move-to-earn fitness application from Rabbit Technologies Inc that gamifies everyday walking. Users set daily step goals, level up, open mystery boxes, and earn an in-app currency called $GRIT that can be redeemed for Amazon and other gift cards. The app layers social features such as leaderboards, challenges, and streaks on top of activity tracking to help people build a lifelong habit of walking. Fitmint is a consumer mobile app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider profile and was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst.

providers.name: Formation Bio
providers.description: Formation Bio is an AI-native pharmaceutical company building the pharma company of the future. Rather than applying AI to drug discovery, it focuses on drug development — acquiring and in-licensing clinical-stage drug candidates from pharma companies, universities, and biotech firms, then running them through clinical development far more efficiently than industry standards using its proprietary AI-native platform, data, and fine-tuned models. Led by CEO Benjamine Liu and CTO Linhao Zhang, the company raised a $372M Series D in 2024 led by a16z with participation from Sanofi, Sequoia, Thrive, Emerson Collective, and others, and partners with Sanofi and OpenAI on custom models for the drug development lifecycle. Formation Bio does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Gen.G
providers.description: Gen.G is a global esports and gaming lifestyle organization founded in 2017, with headquarters in Seoul, South Korea and Los Angeles, California. Gen.G fields competitive teams across major titles including League of Legends (LCK), VALORANT, and other publisher-run leagues, and operates gaming lifestyle, content, and merchandise businesses. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Gen.G publishes no first-party developer API; its public digital surface is the geng.gg storefront, which runs on Shopify and exposes Shopify's Customer Account OpenID Connect authentication for shoppers.

providers.name: Genial Care
providers.description: Genial Care is a Brazilian healthtech network providing multidisciplinary, evidence-based care for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and atypical development up to roughly eight years of age. Founded in 2020 in Sao Paulo, it operates a network of clinics ("Casas Geniais") across Greater Sao Paulo delivering ABA (applied behavior analysis), speech-language therapy, and occupational therapy, alongside family assessments, in-person and online consultations, educational content, and a professional training academy. Care is coordinated through a proprietary mobile app that supports continuous monitoring and family engagement. The company partners with major Brazilian health plans (operadoras), which account for the majority of its revenue, and is backed by General Catalyst. Genial Care operates as a consumer/clinical care provider and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Granza Bio
providers.description: Granza Bio is an early-stage biotechnology company reprogramming immunity for target-specific medicines. Founded in 2024 by Dr. Ashwin Nandakumar, Dr. Ashwin Jainarayanan, and Prof. Michael Dustin, the company builds on the discovery of "attack particles" — killing entities released by cytotoxic immune cells, characterized in Prof. Dustin's laboratory at the University of Oxford. Granza Bio is developing an engineered delivery-shell platform that directs therapeutic cargo to specific tissues, with the goal of advancing treatments for cancers, autoimmune disorders, and infections. The company raised $7.14M in seed funding co-led by Refactor Capital and Felicis, with participation from Pioneer Fund and Y Combinator. It is a research-stage life-sciences company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: ImmuneBridge
providers.description: ImmuneBridge is a San Francisco biotech company building a first-in-class integrated screening and manufacturing platform for allogeneic cell therapies. The company screens and expands stem cells from multiple sources (umbilical cord blood, mobilized blood, bone marrow), uses high-throughput automated assays with machine-learning models to predict donor and process performance early, and scales production with IBR403, a small molecule enabling up to 100,000-fold expansion of hematopoietic stem cells. The stated goal is to manufacture tens of thousands of affordable, high-quality immune cell doses (HSCs, NK cells, T cells, and more) from a single cord blood unit. ImmuneBridge is backed by Insight Partners, NFX Bio, M Ventures, and other institutional investors. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Inceptive
providers.description: Inceptive is an AI biotechnology company founded in 2021 by transformer co-author Jakob Uszkoreit and Stanford biochemist Rhiju Das, building foundation models of life to rationally design sequence-based medicines such as mRNA, siRNA, ASOs, and peptides. The company pairs large-scale deep learning with high-throughput in-house wet-lab experiments in a tight design-build-test loop, then licenses successful molecules to pharmaceutical partners. Inceptive is headquartered in Palo Alto with offices in Berlin and Zurich, is backed by a16z Bio + Health, Obvious Ventures, NVentures (NVIDIA), and S32, and has announced strategic collaborations including a multi-year agreement with Alnylam Pharmaceuticals. Inceptive is a research-partner biotech and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Ionic Security
providers.description: Ionic Security was an Atlanta, Georgia data-protection and dynamic-authorization company whose Machina platform let developers add data access, control, and protection to any application with a small amount of code. Machina provided an API-driven service layer for just-in-time enforcement of data-access policies — evaluating user, device, service, environment, and data attributes to allow or deny each request — backed by client SDKs for Java, C, C++, C#, Objective-C, Python, and JavaScript, a Machina CLI, and cloud-storage integrations for AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Storage. Ionic was venture-backed (GV, Kleiner Perkins, Ten Eleven Ventures) and was acquired by Twilio in April 2021 for roughly $30.2 million to accelerate Twilio's data-security capabilities. The company's developer domains (ionic.com, dev.ionic.com, api.ionic.com) are no longer live, but the first-party SDKs and CLI remain published on Maven Central, PyPI, and the IonicDev GitHub organization.

providers.name: Karpatia Benefits
providers.description: Karpatia Benefits is an all-in-one corporate employee-benefits management platform used by 100+ companies to administer insurance, sports and education allowances, and mental-health support for distributed teams. It combines a benefits marketplace of 40+ partner vendors offering corporate discounts, reimbursement processing, and HR analytics dashboards, and says it removes roughly 95% of the administrative work of running a benefits program. The company primarily serves Ukrainian companies with multi-country localization. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer API is published at this time.

providers.name: Mandolin
providers.description: Mandolin (operating as Coral Automation, Inc.) is a San Francisco-based AI automation platform for specialty pharmaceutical workflows, serving infusion centers and specialty pharmacies. Its AI agents handle the complete back-office lifecycle — patient intake, benefits verification, prior authorization, claims, and revenue cycle management — by navigating existing systems, reading faxes, and reasoning over data rather than through developer integrations. The company explicitly markets a no-API, no-integration approach ("Every step, fully automated"), citing outcomes such as 24x faster document processing and eliminated prescription backlogs. Backed by Greylock and SV Angel.

providers.name: Menten AI
providers.description: Menten AI is a biotechnology company pioneering generative AI for peptide drug design. Its MAUD 1.0 platform designs peptide macrocycles de novo for complex, previously undruggable targets by combining generative AI with physics-based models and quantum simulations, reporting nanomolar potency, oral bioavailability, cell permeability, and a greater-than-90% hit rate. The company operates through enterprise partnerships with pharmaceutical organizations rather than a public developer platform, and at the time of this profile publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: MSC Industrial Direct
providers.description: MSC Industrial Direct is one of the largest industrial product distributors in North America, providing metalworking, maintenance, repair, and operations products and services to manufacturers.

providers.name: Nava Therapeutics
providers.description: Nava Therapeutics is a life-sciences company developing lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology for delivering RNA therapeutics precisely to specific organs and cells, aiming to extend genetic medicines to previously untreatable diseases. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network, Nava operates in the therapeutics / RNA-delivery sector and, as a private clinical-stage biotech, publishes a corporate marketing site (pipeline, team, newsroom) but no public developer, API, or integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Niyo Solutions
providers.description: Niyo Solutions (brand: Niyo, goniyo.com) is a Bengaluru, India based consumer fintech founded in 2015 by Vinay Bagri and Virender Bisht, focused on international travel banking and savings for Indian retail customers. Niyo is not a chartered bank; it operates as a neo-banking front end layered on partner RBI-licensed banks — DCB Bank (current flagship for the Niyo zero-forex savings + debit card), SBM Bank India (previous "Niyo Global" forex card, now wound down for new customers and operating a secured credit card variant), Equitas Small Finance Bank (salary / "Niyo Bharat" account) and IDFC FIRST Bank (earlier Niyo Global issuer) — plus card network rails (Visa, RuPay). Niyo's flagship surface is the "zero forex markup" Niyo Global / DCB Niyo Global / SBM Niyo Global Visa debit and prepaid travel cards accepted in 180+ countries, paired with a digital savings account delivered through partner banks. The company has expanded beyond cards into a full travel-banking stack including currency exchange and forex cash delivery, outbound remittance (Send Money Abroad), international flights, hotels and curated experiences, Niyo Express airport services, an international travel eSIM, travel visa assistance, travel insurance, a premium subscription tier, a student program (Niyo Scholarship, NISAP) and a DCB Niyo Secured Credit Card backed by a fixed deposit. Niyo serves over one million international travellers and has raised capital from investors including Accel, Lightrock, Beams Fintech Fund, Tencent, Horizons Ventures, Prime Venture Partners and JS Capital. There is no public REST developer API, partner banking-as-a-service surface, SDK, MCP server, or GitHub organisation — Niyo is delivered exclusively as a B2C iOS and Android mobile application with a marketing and tools website at goniyo.com.

providers.name: Noora Health
providers.description: Noora Health is a healthcare nonprofit that turns the time patients and their families spend in hospitals into an opportunity to learn high-impact health skills. Working through public and private health systems across South Asia, its Care Companion Program trains family caregivers at the bedside so they can care for their loved ones after discharge, reducing preventable complications and readmissions. Founded in 2014 and a Y Combinator-backed organization, Noora Health operates in India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, and Nepal and has trained tens of millions of caregivers and patients. It is a mission-driven organization rather than an API provider, and no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Octant
providers.description: Octant is a precision medicine company developing next-generation small molecule therapeutics by merging biology, chemistry, and computation to engineer drugs that target complex cellular mechanisms. Its programs span protein misfolding and mistrafficking diseases, oncology, metabolism, and immunology, with lead candidate OCT-980 — a first-in-disease oral small molecule designed to correct protein misfolding for rhodopsin gene mutations in autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa. Octant is a portfolio company of 8vc. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Open Souls
providers.description: Open Souls is an open-source framework and philosophy for building "AI souls" — agentic, embodied digital beings with personality, drive, and ego, built on top of large language models. The Soul Engine framework (distributed as the soul-engine npm package and CLI) models agency, memory, emotion, and goal-setting through WorkingMemory, cognitiveSteps, and MentalProcesses abstractions, describing itself as "NextJS + Vercel for the minds of digital beings." The project is now legacy: the opensouls.org site is parked and the hosted Soul Engine cloud service is no longer operating, but the open-source framework and npm packages remain published under the opensouls GitHub organization. Open Souls was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Openbay
providers.description: Openbay is an award-winning online automotive service platform and marketplace that connects vehicle owners with local repair shops and service providers, offering upfront estimates, online booking, messaging, and payment. Its consumer marketplace lets drivers compare and book automotive repair and maintenance, while Openbay+ embeds that commerce into partner and OEM channels and Openbay Otis provides a SaaS platform for repair shops. Backed by a16z and GV, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; this pass found no publicly accessible self-serve developer API surface (the marketing site and consumer app are Cloudflare-protected and expose no real /.well-known documents or llms.txt).

providers.name: Pairio
providers.description: Pairio is an AI-powered maintenance assistant for manufacturing and industrial teams, built by Pairio GmbH in Munich, Germany and backed by Y Combinator. Technicians capture voice, photos, and video on the shop floor, and Pairio troubleshoots machine breakdowns, searches technical documentation and maintenance history, identifies spare parts, generates structured maintenance reports, and creates work instructions. It preserves expert knowledge across shifts, sites, and teams to reduce mean time to repair (MTTR) and unplanned downtime, integrating with common ERP, CMMS, EAM, and document-management systems such as SAP, IFS, IBM Maximo, Oracle EAM, Hexagon, SharePoint, and Outlook. Pairio is a consumer-facing mobile/web application and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: payflows
providers.description: Payflows is an AI-native financial operations platform that unifies procurement, treasury, and accounting into one agentic workspace for finance teams. Its product suites span Apollo (procurement from purchase request to receipt), Vera (vendor and contract management), Athena (accounting and AP automation from AP to tax reporting), and Metis (treasury from payment to bank reconciliation), with spend analytics, cashflow forecasting, global payments, and risk management. Payflows integrates with major ERP, banking, payment, and expense systems. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PHP
providers.description: PHP is a widely-used server-side scripting language especially suited for web development and embedded in HTML. It powers a large portion of the web including platforms like WordPress and Drupal, and provides extensive database support, framework options, and a mature ecosystem. PHP itself is a language and runtime, not a hosted API service.

providers.name: Positive Development
providers.description: Positive Development is a developmental therapy provider specializing in autism care for children, delivering a family-centered, play-based, home-based model that coaches parents rather than relying on intensive clinic hours. Services span emotional regulation, communication development, social engagement, daily living skills, and 1:1 parent coaching, with insurance-based access across multiple US locations. Surfaced as an obvious-ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the enrichment pass found no public developer, API, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: Project Admission
providers.description: Project Admission is a ticketing technology company serving the live event industry — professional sports teams, leagues, artists, theaters, and venues. It layers on top of existing ticketing systems such as SeatGeek, Ticketmaster, and AXS to expand opportunities around the ticket and capture more value before, during, and after an event. Its platform provides branded storefronts, multi-channel inventory management, bulk ticket distribution, split season-ticket ingestion, and fan-engagement tools including influencer and group-sales programs. Project Admission does not publicly expose a developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its verified public web and security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Quantive (fka Gtmhub)
providers.description: Quantive (formerly Gtmhub) is a strategy-execution and OKR (Objectives and Key Results) SaaS platform, historically backed by Insight Partners. The company and its "Quantive Results" product have since been acquired and folded into WorkBoard — quantive.com now redirects to workboard.com and the developer portal (developer.quantive.com) has been decommissioned. The public REST API and OpenAPI reference are no longer reachable, but first-party developer tooling remains published on public registries: the @gtmhub/sdk extensibility SDK on npm (for building marketplace plugins and insights) and the gtmhub-cli command-line client (distributed via Homebrew, Chocolatey, and GitHub releases). This profile captures the surviving developer surface.

providers.name: Ramre
providers.description: Ramre (RamRe) is the brand associated with Ram Reinsurance, now operating as American Overseas Group Limited (AOG) — a Bermuda-based insurance holding company that is tax resident in the United Kingdom. Through its U.S. subsidiaries the group writes non-standard automobile insurance and provides related management services, and it operates as a reinsurer through a subsidiary based in Barbados. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass found no public developer program, API, documentation, or SDK surface: this is a financial-services holding company whose public web presence (ramre.com now redirects to aoreltd.com) is corporate and investor-relations oriented, with no machine-readable API artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: Relation Rx
providers.description: Relation Therapeutics (Relation Rx) is a London- and Boston-based end-to-end biotechnology company developing transformational medicines with technology at its core. The company combines single-cell multi-omics analysis of patient tissue, functional genomics and disease-relevant assays, and machine learning to decode disease biology, identify and validate therapeutic targets, and advance its own pipeline of drug candidates. Relation is a DCVC portfolio company and has announced research collaborations with partners including Novartis. It operates as a therapeutics developer rather than a software or API provider, and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Roomstorm
providers.description: Roomstorm is a real-time B2B hotel room marketplace, best known for building the airline industry's first fully automated platform for providing hotel accommodations to distressed passengers during flight disruptions. Founded by Maksim Izmaylov and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2014), the San Francisco company connects airlines, hotels, and travelers so that irregular-operations (IROPS) rebooking, room sourcing, invoicing, and voucher issuance happen programmatically instead of through manual phone calls. Its backend exposes a JSON REST API (documented in API Blueprint) covering authentication, bookings, hotels, rooms, vacancies, organizations, vouchers, and airport search.

providers.name: Roon
providers.description: Roon is a digital health platform (operating as CareSpace Health Inc.) that helps people navigate serious and critical health conditions by connecting them with trusted answers from leading medical experts. Rather than relying on "Dr. Google" or legacy content sites, Roon publishes thousands of short, doctor-created video answers covering conditions such as ALS, glioblastoma (GBM), dementia, PCOS, fertility, and women's health, organized so patients and caregivers can quickly find vetted guidance for their journey. Founded in 2021 by Vikram Bhaskaran, Arun Ranganathan, and Dr. Rohan Ramakrishna, Roon delivers its experience primarily through consumer iOS apps and its website, and raised a $15M Series A co-led by Forerunner Ventures and FirstMark. Roon is a consumer-facing health information product and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD.
providers.description: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD. (Scenario X) is a financial-technology company building an AI- and quantum-computing-powered platform for financial risk analysis, stress testing, and regulatory reporting. The integrated platform is organized into four modules — Scenario (adverse market-condition design), PPNR (Pre-Provision Net Revenue projection), Risk (market, counterparty, credit, and operational risk), and Console (financial-data aggregation) — plus a quantum-computing offering for predictive financial modeling. It serves banks, insurers, family offices, independent wealth managers, and commodity traders. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer surface has been found to date.

providers.name: SceneRay
providers.description: SceneRay Medical Technology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. is a Chinese medical-device and brain-computer-interface company founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Suzhou Industrial Park. It designs and manufactures implantable neuromodulation systems, focusing on Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) devices and "brain-machine control chip" technology used to treat Parkinson's disease, movement disorders, epilepsy, and treatment-resistant psychiatric conditions. Its product line spans implantable pulse generators, programmable external controllers, and clinician programming systems. SceneRay reports over 100 international patents and 700+ total patent applications, with devices used across 18+ countries. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming. As a medical hardware manufacturer, SceneRay publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or other machine-readable technical surface at the time of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: SevOne (Turbonomic)
providers.description: SevOne and Turbonomic are enterprise IT operations products now part of IBM's AIOps portfolio. IBM SevOne Network Performance Management (NPM) delivers real-time, multi-vendor network monitoring, flow analytics, and capacity planning across hybrid and enterprise networks. IBM Turbonomic is an application resource management (ARM) platform that continuously analyzes application demand and automates resourcing, scaling, and placement decisions across on-premises, cloud, and Kubernetes environments to assure performance while reducing cost. Both products expose REST APIs, but those APIs are hosted on the customer's own appliance / deployment rather than on a public developer portal, so there is no public base URL or published OpenAPI to catalog: the Turbonomic REST API is served from the appliance (for example the /vmturbo/rest path with its bundled Swagger UI), and SevOne exposes the SevOne NMS API and SevOne Data Insight API from the deployed instance. Product and API reference documentation is published by IBM.

providers.name: Simile
providers.description: Simile is a simulation platform for human behavior. Its AI-driven simulations show how and why customers, employees, or populations respond to change, so enterprise teams can find their audience, reach niche populations, de-risk decisions, segment sentiment at scale, and test concepts before a real-world launch. Simile is building a foundation model that predicts human behavior and a product that deploys it at scale. It raised a $100M Series A led by Index Ventures and is backed by Bain Capital Ventures; named customers include CVS Health, Wealthfront, Suntory, Garnett Station Partners, and Banco Itau.

providers.name: Soma
providers.description: Soma (Soma Insurance Services) is a commercial insurance brokerage that positions itself as the fastest brokerage for complex businesses, placing customized commercial-lines coverage across industries including retail, trucking, hospitality, healthcare, finance, technology, manufacturing, and construction. Coverage lines include general liability, commercial auto, cyber liability, professional liability, and builder's risk. Backed by Accel and Cowboy Ventures in the insurance-tech sector. As of this enrichment pass Soma publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public web presence and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Spext Labs, Spext
providers.description: Spext (Spext Labs) is an AI-powered audio and video editing platform that lets users edit recordings by trimming an auto-generated transcript rather than a waveform — a text-first "recording management system" for podcasts, interviews and other spoken-word media. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from a Framer-hosted marketing site (spext.co) and a web application (app.spext.co). As of this enrichment pass Spext exposes no public developer surface — no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery endpoints were found; the profile is retained as a network company record.

providers.name: SpyBiotech
providers.description: SpyBiotech is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation vaccines against infectious diseases and cancer using its proprietary SpyTag/SpyCatcher "protein superglue" platform. The technology snaps target antigens onto virus-like particles (VLPs) to produce highly immunogenic vaccines with greater ease and speed. An Oxford University spinout backed by GV, its pipeline includes candidates such as SpyVLP01 targeting human cytomegalovirus (hCMV). This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; SpyBiotech publishes a corporate marketing website but no public developer or product API surface.

providers.name: Stamplay
providers.description: Stamplay was a backend-as-a-service and API-integration platform — billed as "Lego for developers" — founded in 2012 (Turin, Italy; later San Francisco) and backed by 500 Global. It let developers assemble application backends by visually wiring together third-party APIs, authentication providers, hosted data objects, webhooks, and static site hosting on stamplayapp.com, driven by a JavaScript SDK, a Node.js SDK, and the `stamplay` CLI. The product has been discontinued: the company was acquired (widely reported as Apple, 2019), the stamplay.com domain is now held via MarkMonitor and returns no HTTP response, every source repository in the GitHub organization is archived, and the npm SDK/CLI packages were last published in 2016. This API Evangelist profile preserves the historical developer footprint (SDKs and CLI) rather than a live API surface.

providers.name: Suborbital
providers.description: Suborbital was a developer-tools company building a WebAssembly-based extensibility platform: the Suborbital Extension Engine (SE2, formerly Suborbital Compute), a hosted service for running sandboxed third-party plugins; E2 Core / Reactr, a function scheduler for Go and WebAssembly; Sat, a tiny fast Wasm edge-compute server; Grav, an embedded decentralized message bus; and the subo CLI for building Wasm plugins and scaffolding projects. Suborbital was acquired by F5 in 2023 and the hosted product was subsequently wound down; the suborbital.dev domain has since been repurposed as an unrelated content blog. The first-party open-source client libraries (npm @suborbital/*, the se2-go Go client, and the subo CLI) and the 32-repo GitHub organization remain publicly available.

providers.name: Tamadé
providers.description: Tamadé is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public surface at flowly.world is Flowly, a virtual telehealth clinic offering an evidence-based program for chronic pain and anxiety recovery, delivered through licensed therapists, a mobile relaxation-training app, and VR wellness tools. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a consumer healthcare product with no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or developer documentation.
