Protect AI also stewards a portfolio of widely used open-source AI security projects on GitHub including LLM Guard (input/output scanner toolkit for prompt injection, PII, toxicity, secrets, and data leakage detection), ModelScan (model serialization attack scanner), Rebuff (prompt injection detector, archived May 2025), NB Defense (Jupyter notebook security), AI Exploits (real-world AI/ML vulnerability demonstrations), and Vulnhuntr (LLM-driven autonomous vulnerability discovery), plus the huntr bug bounty platform for AI/ML with over 17,000 security researchers. Protect AI was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in 2025 and is being integrated into the Prisma AIRS AI security platform. No public, programmatic developer API or OpenAPI specification is published for Guardian, Recon, or Layer at the time of this profile — integration is performed via product CLIs, SDKs, eBPF agents, and platform connectors documented behind Palo Alto Networks customer accounts.

providers.name: Quantstamp
providers.description: Quantstamp is a blockchain security firm founded in 2017 that provides expert Web3 security assessments, including smart contract audits, infrastructure and Layer 2 audits, zero-knowledge circuit reviews, and economic exploit analysis. The company has conducted over 1,300 audits across more than 60 blockchain ecosystems and helped secure billions of dollars in digital assets. Quantstamp publishes public audit reports through its certificate portal, maintains open-source Web3 security tooling on GitHub (L2 block explorer standards, ERC-4337 checkers, halo2 zero-knowledge libraries), and runs a research blog. Quantstamp is a services and consulting provider rather than an API-first platform, and does not currently publish a first-party developer API or OpenAPI specification. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: Range Resources
providers.description: Range Resources is an independent natural gas, natural gas liquids, and oil company engaged in the exploration, development, and acquisition of natural gas and oil properties primarily in the Appalachian region. Range does not publish a public developer API; this index tracks the company's public-facing digital properties for reference.

providers.name: Rani Therapeutics
providers.description: Rani Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing the RaniPill, an ingestible robotic capsule engineered to deliver biologic drugs orally in place of subcutaneous or intravenous injections. The platform aims to preserve injection-comparable bioavailability while removing the pain and adherence barriers of needle-based therapies across chronic and metabolic disease areas. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network; the company is a publicly traded life-sciences firm and does not currently publish a developer API, developer portal, or programmatic data surface.

providers.name: Ratify
providers.description: Ratify is a CNCF Sandbox open-source verification framework for container images and other supply chain artifacts in Kubernetes environments. It enables policy-driven artifact ratification by coordinating any number of pluggable verifiers (signatures, SBOMs, scan results, attestations) against a given policy, integrating with Kubernetes admission webhooks via the Gatekeeper policy engine. Ratify is developed by the ratify-project GitHub organization (originally a Microsoft open-source project), written in Go, and distributed as a CLI tool, Go library, and Kubernetes admission webhook server. It supports OCI-compliant artifact stores including Azure Container Registry, Amazon ECR, and Docker Hub. Ratify exposes an internal HTTP verification API (v2alpha1) consumed by its webhook server but does not publish a public-facing REST API or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: React Foundation
providers.description: The React Foundation is a Linux Foundation project announced in February 2026 that supports React, React Native, and supporting components after Meta contributed the React project to the Linux Foundation. It ensures the continued open governance, neutral stewardship, and long-term development of the React ecosystem used by millions of front-end and mobile developers worldwide. The Foundation does not currently expose a public, programmatic REST API; engagement with the project happens primarily through GitHub repositories and documentation channels.

providers.name: Result
providers.description: Result is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) all-in-one business operating system that lets internet entrepreneurs start and run companies end-to-end. The platform unifies app development with built-in payments, AI-powered marketing and content creation, automated customer support, financial analytics, branding and design tools, market research, SEO optimization, legal incorporation, and investor fundraising into a single surface, tied together by a "Company Brain" that retains business context from day one. Founded by Aaryan Kushwah (CEO) and Savio Martin (CTO), the product is in private beta with a public waitlist and does not yet publish a developer/API surface.

providers.name: Revolution Medicines
providers.description: Revolution Medicines is a clinical-stage precision oncology company headquartered in Redwood City, California, developing targeted therapies for RAS-addicted cancers. Its pipeline centers on RAS(ON) inhibitors — including daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), and elironrasib (RMC-6291) — designed to directly target the active, GTP-bound (ON) state of oncogenic RAS proteins across mutations such as KRAS G12X. The company pairs structure-based drug discovery with clinical development to pursue treatments for pancreatic, lung, colorectal, and other RAS-driven tumors. Revolution Medicines is a publicly traded corporate entity (Nasdaq: RVMD) and does not currently expose a public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rhyme (fka PriorAuthNow)
providers.description: Rhyme (formerly PriorAuthNow) is a healthcare technology company that eliminates prior authorization burden by automating the exchange between payers and providers. Its platform delivers touchless prior authorization, gold carding (removing auth requirements entirely through payer-provider collaboration), and a shared dashboard for tracking efficiency. Rhyme processes over four million prior authorizations annually and connects 83 of the largest US health systems with 300+ payers. The company is backed by Insight Partners and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; it publishes no public developer or API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Seed Club
providers.description: Seed Club is a web3 accelerator and community focused on consumer crypto, helping founders build "a dramatically more interesting internet" where the value created by online communities is captured by people rather than platforms. It runs a cohort-based accelerator (currently SC07: Consumer Crypto), a ventures/investment arm, and a portfolio program, alongside a broader community of builders, creators, and token communities. Seed Club operates as a community-owned organization and publishes a public Community Handbook, a blog, and open-source dApp code (Farcaster frames, crowdfunding smart contracts). It is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. Seed Club is a program and community brand rather than an API provider — it exposes no public developer platform, REST/GraphQL API, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Sensome
providers.description: Sensome is a clinical-stage medical technology company developing tissue-sensing microchip technology and proprietary integration processes that embed real-time bio-impedance sensing into minimally invasive medical devices. Its lead product, the Clotild Smart Guidewire System (manufactured with Asahi Intecc), is the first tissue-sensing neurovascular guidewire, providing physicians real-time blood clot characterization to guide Acute Ischemic Stroke treatment; additional indications include lung cancer biopsy guidance. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech, Sensome is a medical-device hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer platform at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Sinclair, Inc.
providers.description: Sinclair, Inc. (Nasdaq: SBGI), formerly Sinclair Broadcast Group, is a diversified media company and one of the largest U.S. local television broadcasters. The company operates 177-185+ TV stations across roughly 79-86 markets affiliated with all major broadcast networks (Fox, NBC, CBS, ABC, MyNetworkTV, The CW), owns Tennis Channel, holds a stake in YES Network, and runs digital multicast networks Comet, Charge!, Roar, and The Nest. Sinclair Ventures houses the company's non-broadcast operations, including ad/martech units (AMP, Drive Auto, Free State, Digital Remedy/Compulse) and broadcast technology subsidiaries (Dielectric, ONE Media Technologies, Bitpath, CAST.ERA, Broadspan Wireless). In 2019 Sinclair acquired the Fox Sports regional sports networks for ~$9.6 billion through a Diamond Sports Group joint venture; Diamond was rebranded Bally Sports in 2021, filed Chapter 11 in March 2023, exited bankruptcy in January 2025 as Main Street Sports Group, rebranded again as FanDuel Sports Network, and is winding down operations in mid-2026. Sinclair publishes no public developer APIs.

providers.name: SlideRule
providers.description: SlideRule is a no-code risk decisioning platform that lets risk and operations teams build, test, and deploy automated decision logic for fraud, credit, compliance, and trust-and-safety use cases without writing code. Its rules engine combines SQL and API data connectors, real-time analytics, A/B testing, backtesting, shadow mode, and case-management automation, and exposes a single API to trigger decision workflows. SlideRule has announced it is joining Block, Inc.; its standalone developer documentation surface (docs.sliderule.io) is no longer publicly reachable, so no live API specification could be harvested during enrichment.

providers.name: Story Health
providers.description: Story Health was a virtual specialty care company founded in 2020 by Tom Stanis (a Google Verily co-founder), Nikhil Roy, and cardiologist Dr. Ashul Govil. Its platform went beyond video visits to give specialty clinicians digital tools for continuous, protocol-driven care at scale, focusing initially on cardiology with care-plan optimization, therapy titration, and evidence-based adjustments between visits. The company raised roughly $27M (a $4M seed in 2020 and a $22.6M Series A in 2022) from investors including General Catalyst and Define Ventures, and was acquired by Innovaccer in September 2025. It operates a marketing web presence but publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Surf AI
providers.description: Surf AI is an agentic security-operations platform that helps CISOs and modern security teams operationalize their entire program with specialized AI agents. It connects across identity, cloud, SaaS, and data systems to continuously monitor assets, surface exposures, trace issues to their owners, and drive automated remediation so teams can shrink the attack surface before it is exploited. The company integrates with 60+ security, identity, cloud, SIEM, and business tools, and is backed by Accel, Cyberstarts, and Boldstart Ventures. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from public sources; Surf AI markets an enterprise platform and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Theta EdgeCloud
providers.description: Theta EdgeCloud is a distributed, hybrid AI and video cloud built on the Theta Network blockchain, offering on-demand GPU compute for AI model training, fine-tuning, inference, video transcoding, and live streaming. EdgeCloud aggregates GPU capacity from data-center hyperscaler partners and a global community of Edge Nodes (consumer and enterprise GPUs) into a single dispatchable compute layer addressable via REST, JSON-RPC, and SDK clients. Core services include EdgeCloud AI Services (on-demand model inference APIs for LLMs, image, audio, and multimodal models such as Llama, Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and Whisper; agentic RAG chatbots; GPU-backed Jupyter notebooks; dedicated GPU pod deployments; and AI training with GPU clusters), EdgeCloud Video Services (the Theta Video API for upload, transcoding, livestream ingestion, DRM, NFT-gated playback, and webhooks), EdgeStore (decentralized object storage), and the EdgeCloud Client (an installable node that earns TFUEL for contributing GPU and bandwidth). Developers authenticate with x-api-key tokens issued from the EdgeCloud dashboard, manage deployments programmatically through api.thetaedgecloud.com and the Node.js SDK @thetalabs/theta-edgecloud, and access on-demand model endpoints (also distributed through RapidAPI). The Theta blockchain layer is EVM-compatible with an Ethereum RPC adaptor, supports TNT-20 tokens and NFTs, and underwrites EdgeCloud's payment, rewards, and staking economy through the THETA governance token and TFUEL gas token. Theta operates as Theta Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California.

providers.name: Topos Bio
providers.description: Topos Bio is an AI-native drug discovery company building all-atom foundation models for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) — dynamic, flexible proteins implicated in diseases such as Alzheimer's and prostate cancer. Its Topos-1 foundation model generates physically realistic conformational ensembles for flexible proteins, aiming to make previously undruggable targets therapeutically viable. The company is backed by Threshold Ventures. No public API or developer platform is currently published.

providers.name: TradeKing
providers.description: TradeKing was a US online brokerage offering commission-based self-directed trading of stocks and options, backed by Battery Ventures. It pioneered one of the first public brokerage APIs, letting developers manage accounts, place equity and options orders, stream real-time market quotes, and manage watchlists over OAuth 1.0. TradeKing was acquired by Ally Financial in 2016 and rebranded as Ally Invest; its API surface lives on as the Ally Invest API (profiled separately as ally-invest in this network). tradeking.com now redirects to ally.com/invest and the historical API hosts no longer resolve. This profile is maintained as a historical record.

providers.name: Truveris
providers.description: Truveris is an independent pharmacy benefits consulting and analytics firm, founded in 2009 and headquartered in New York, that helps employers, benefits consultants, and brokers optimize their pharmacy programs and reduce drug spend. The company turns complex pharmacy claims and contract data into clear, actionable insight through products including the Truveris Marketplace for PBM plan procurement, truGuard for ongoing contract and pricing oversight, pharmacy audits, and PBM contract analytics. Truveris serves hundreds of clients with data-driven cost containment strategies. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties. Backed by Canaan Partners.

providers.name: Ventus Therapeutics
providers.description: Ventus Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Waltham, Massachusetts, with research operations in Montreal, Canada. Ventus uses its proprietary, machine-learning-enabled computational chemistry and structural biology platform, ReSOLVE, together with deep protein-science expertise, to design differentiated small-molecule therapeutics targeting the innate immune system (including cGAS and NLRP3 inhibitors) for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, neurological disorders, and cancer. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment confirmed Ventus operates a corporate/investor website only and publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Vesta Healthcare
providers.description: Vesta Healthcare is a clinical and technology services organization for high-need, frail seniors receiving home-based care. It connects caregiver insights to the broader care team, delivering 24/7 telehealth support, remote patient monitoring, and chronic care management. Vesta partners with home care agencies, health plans, and providers to run value-based population health programs that emphasize clinical quality and personalized engagement, with services covered through Medicare, Medicare Supplemental, and many Medicare Advantage plans. The company (formerly HT Health) is backed by Lux Capital. No public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Vial
providers.description: Vial is a next-generation biotech company advancing first and best-in-class biologics to treat unmet need in Immunology and Inflammation. The company pairs AI-driven drug discovery with automated, technology-enabled clinical trials, working across target discovery (identifying high-value therapeutic targets), molecule design (generating and optimizing molecular candidates), and experimental validation (high-throughput approaches to accelerate development). Its lead pipeline program is an IL-13 x TSLP bi-specific antibody in Phase 1. Vial was originally built as a tech-enabled contract research organization (CRO) focused on reimagining clinical trials, and was backed by General Catalyst. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Vial publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Vitara
providers.description: Vitara (Vitara Biomedical) is a Philadelphia-based medical technology company developing EXTEND, an investigational neonatal support platform that surrounds extremely premature newborns in a fluid-filled, fetal-physiology-modeled environment for their first 28 days, delaying the stress of early air exposure so vital organs can continue to develop. The company aims to improve survival and reduce long-term complications for infants born as early as 22 weeks gestation. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company; Vitara publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and its technology has not received U.S. FDA market clearance.

providers.name: Zudo
providers.description: Zudo builds AI-powered agents purpose-built for the warranty industry, automating customer service and back-office operations for home warranty, auto warranty, and OEM third-party administrators. Its agents (Adam for customer service, Emma for operations) handle claim follow-ups, initiations, and authorizations around the clock to improve warranty customer experience and operating margins. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; the public site is marketing-only with no developer/API surface published at enrichment time.

providers.name: Alpha Natural Resources
providers.description: Alpha Natural Resources is a producer of metallurgical and thermal coal in the United States, mining and processing coal for steelmaking and electric power generation. The company does not offer public developer APIs, but participates in commodity trading data exchanges and supply chain integration with steel producers and utilities.

providers.name: Aon
providers.description: Aon plc is a London-headquartered global professional services firm delivering integrated risk and human capital advisory through two reporting pillars — Risk Capital (broking, reinsurance, risk analytics) and Human Capital (health, wealth, talent, rewards). The firm operates in over 120 countries, lists on the NYSE under the ticker AON, and grew its US middle-market footprint with the April 2024 acquisition of NFP for roughly $13B. Aon publishes named analytics platforms (Risk Analyzer suite, ReMetrica, CyQu, Spectrum, Impact Forecasting catastrophe models, Radford McLagan Compensation Database, SkillsGraph, Gauge, Revenue GPS) but those tools are delivered through gated client portals — no developer portal, OpenAPI catalog, SDK org, or public API reference is published on aon.com.

providers.name: Auto1
providers.description: AUTO1 Group is Europe's leading digital automotive platform for buying, selling, and financing used cars, headquartered in Berlin, Germany. It operates the B2B wholesale marketplace AUTO1.com (used by 60,000+ professional car dealers across 30+ European countries), the consumer retail brand Autohero, and the consumer purchasing service wirkaufendeinauto.de (with localized variants across Europe). The group combines inspection, logistics, documentation, and digital financing into an end-to-end remarketing and retail platform. AUTO1 Group publishes open-source engineering work through its auto1-oss GitHub organization, but does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or published API documentation; this profile therefore captures verified company identity and domain-security posture only. Surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: dopl technologies
providers.description: Dopl Technologies is a Seattle-based data and AI company (founded 2022, Techstars-backed) democratizing access to diagnostic exams and interventional procedures through telerobotic ultrasound. Its Dopl Traverse platform and SonoFlex app let a remote sonographer operate an ultrasound probe over a network from significant distances, extending specialist-level imaging into rural and workforce-constrained regions. Field testing in rural Washington hospitals has reduced patient wait times by over 90 percent. The company cites 50M+ missed ultrasound exams annually and $19.5B in lost revenue from unequal imaging access, and expects FDA clearance in 2027 before expanding into minimally invasive procedures. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation; this record is a network stub maintained for discovery and future enrichment.

providers.name: Dwight Capital
providers.description: Dwight Capital LLC is a leading commercial real estate finance company in the United States, with a loan servicing portfolio exceeding $15 billion across all affiliates. The firm originates Balance-Sheet Bridge and New Construction Loans, FHA/HUD Insured Loans, C-PACE Financing, Mezzanine Financing, and Preferred Equity for multifamily, healthcare, and mixed-use commercial real estate. Headquartered in New York City with an additional office in Sunny Isles Beach, Florida, Dwight is consistently ranked among the top FHA/HUD multifamily lenders in the country and operates as a privately held business specializing in bridge-to-HUD execution for commercial real estate sponsors.

providers.name: e-CROSS
providers.description: e-CROSS is a cross-border e-commerce platform that lets international brands sell into Latin America. Acting as a Merchant of Record, it handles payment processing, currency exchange, logistics and fulfillment intelligence, customs and legal compliance, and storefront localization so merchants can expand into the region with a simple integration into their existing e-commerce stack. e-CROSS is a 500 Global portfolio company. Its public site runs on Wix and exposes a hosted, unauthenticated Model Context Protocol (MCP) server plus an llms.txt for agentic AI access to public site content; e-CROSS does not currently publish a first-party developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK.

The canonical APIs.json index for U.S. EPA APIs and data services is maintained in the environmental-protection-agency repository, which catalogs EPA's Envirofacts Data Service, Air Quality System (AQS), UV Index, and ECHO Compliance and Enforcement APIs. Refer to the canonical record for current API listings, properties, and metadata.

providers.name: Headway
providers.description: Headway is a New York-based mental health technology company building the largest insurance-credentialed network of therapists, psychiatrists, and prescribers in the United States. Founded in 2019 by Andrew Adams, Jake Sussman, Dan Ross, and Kevin Chan, Headway operates a two-sided platform that helps independent mental health providers get credentialed with major commercial payers, Medicare Advantage, and select Medicaid managed care plans, while helping patients find affordable in-network therapy. The platform handles insurance credentialing (claimed to be as fast as 30 days with top payers), benefit verification, claims submission and adjudication, appeals, clawback protection, biweekly guaranteed provider payments, scheduling, telehealth, EHR-style clinical notes, and compliance tooling. Headway is free to join for providers and earns revenue through commissions paid by insurance carriers. Its payer network spans 100+ plans across all 50 states and DC, including Aetna, Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Optum, Oscar, Oxford, Evernorth, and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts, supporting more than 70,000 licensed providers delivering care in 57+ languages across 20+ clinical specialties. Headway has raised over $325M from Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive, Accel, GV, Spark Capital, Forerunner Ventures, and Health Care Service Corporation, with a valuation around $2.3B. Headway does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or partner integration program — its platform is offered exclusively as a managed SaaS to providers, group practices, and health plans. The headway.co GitHub organization exists but only contains forks of third-party open-source libraries (Starlette, Pydantic, Flower, etc.) used internally by Headway's engineering teams. Note that the unrelated headwayapp.co company (a product changelog widget) does publish a public REST API and should not be confused with this provider.

providers.name: Libra Robotics
providers.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

providers.name: Liveprofile
providers.description: LiveProfile is a cross-platform mobile messaging and chat product ("Stay connected with people and things that matter. Chat securely and express yourself freely."). It was originally backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-derived company profile. As of this enrichment pass, liveprofile.com is an invite-only relaunch teaser ("The New LiveProfile") running a waitlist, with apps advertised for Android, iPhone & iPad, and Mac/PC. The company maintains a public GitHub organization and a BetterUptime status page, but publishes no public API surface, developer documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time — so this profile carries identity and operational signals only, awaiting a real developer/API surface.

providers.name: Open mHealth
providers.description: Open mHealth is a nonprofit, community-driven initiative that develops open standards and open-source software for making patient-generated health data interoperable across mobile apps, wearables, clinical systems, and electronic health records. Its core contribution is a library of clinically validated JSON Schema data point schemas — covering physical activity, sleep, heart rate, blood pressure, body weight, blood glucose, and other vital signs — with the sleep, physical-activity, and metadata schemas now superseded by IEEE 1752.1, the IEEE standard for Mobile Health Data co-shepherded by the Open mHealth community. Around the schemas Open mHealth ships a stack of Apache-2.0 reference implementations: Shimmer (a Java/Spring server that pulls health data from Fitbit, Google Fit, iHealth, Misfit, RunKeeper, and Withings APIs and normalizes it into Open mHealth or IEEE 1752.1 data points), omh-dsu-ri (a Data Storage Unit reference implementation exposing an OAuth 2.0-secured Data Point REST API on top of MongoDB and PostgreSQL), Granola (an Objective-C library that serializes Apple HealthKit samples into Open mHealth JSON), a web visualizations library built on D3 and Plottable.js, the OMH-on-FHIR mapping that aligns Open mHealth data points to HL7 FHIR resources, and a sample-data-generator. Open mHealth operates as the steward of the standard, the schema and unit registry at registry.openmhealth.org, and a developer community of thousands of developers and health organizations including Cornell Tech, Kaiser Permanente, Stanford School of Medicine, UC Davis, and UCSF. The project has no commercial API, no paid tier, and no hosted SaaS — all artifacts are open source under Apache 2.0 and the standard itself is openly published.

providers.name: Praan
providers.description: Praan (Praan Climate Technologies) is a deep-tech climate startup working to democratize access to clean, healthy air and to rebuild the atmosphere by capturing air pollution and greenhouse gases with novel filterless technology. Its products include HIVE, an air-purification device for homes and commercial spaces paired with a companion mobile application, and MK II, an air-purification system for industrial environments. Praan is backed by Prosus Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched through the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Praan publishes a consumer hardware and mobile-app surface but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: The Farmer's Dog
providers.description: The Farmer's Dog is a direct-to-consumer pet health company that delivers fresh, human-grade dog food on a personalized subscription. Customers complete an online profile of their dog (breed, age, weight, activity, health goals) and the company formulates and ships pre-portioned meal plans on a recurring cadence. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in New York City, it is backed by Forerunner Ventures among others and has delivered over one billion meals nationwide. The business runs on a JavaScript/TypeScript stack with an internal "Core API" that powers ordering, subscription management, and its veterinarian program, but the company does not publish a public developer platform, API documentation, or client SDKs. This profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture; there is no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Weshine
providers.description: Weshine (闪萌, Shanmeng), operated by Beijing Shanqu Information Technology Co., Ltd (北京闪趣信息技术有限公司), is a Chinese GIF and animated-sticker (表情) search engine. It offers a business-to-business "Expression API" (表情API) with three documented interfaces — a hot/trending interface (热门接口) that returns trending GIFs by category refreshed hourly, a real-time search interface (搜索接口) supporting gif/webp/mp4 and multi-dimensional ranking, and a "magic image" interface (神配图接口) that semantically matches a phrase to a background GIF and composites a caption onto it. The platform reports 800M+ users covered, 300M+ daily searches, and 200M+ animated images sent per day, powering social apps, input methods (including its own KK Keyboard), and browsers. API access is via business partnership; no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK is published.

providers.name: American Equity Investment Life Holding
providers.description: American Equity Investment Life Holding Company is a leading provider of guaranteed income solutions, specializing in the design, development, and sale of fixed indexed and fixed-rate annuity products distributed through independent agents and broker-dealers. The company offers products including IncomeShield, AssetShield, EstateShield, and GuaranteeShield annuities, providing retirees with lifetime income, principal protection, tax-deferred growth, and legacy planning options.

providers.name: Anki
providers.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: CarbonChain
providers.description: CarbonChain is a London- and New York-based carbon accounting platform founded in 2019 that is purpose-built for the highest-emitting, hardest-to- track commodity supply chains — metals and mining, energy, manufacturing, and agriculture. Its AI-assisted platform builds asset- and transaction- level emissions pictures using activity-based emission factors, and packages those calculations into modules for supply-chain emissions, corporate carbon footprints (Scope 1, 2, 3), product carbon footprints, scenario analysis, and regulatory compliance. The flagship CarbonChain Comply release ships a Carbon Reporting Hub aligned with EU CSRD, UK SECR, US SEC, and CDP, along with EU/UK CBAM declaration validation, automated CBAM XML generation, and a Supplier Engagement Module for collecting and validating supplier emissions data. CarbonChain Connect links producers and importers through shared installation-level CBAM infrastructure. The company is a CDP Accredited Provider (2024), is ISO 27001 certified, and is backed by Y Combinator, Union Square Ventures, Voyager VC, and Aera VC, with $10M Series A funding (2023). CarbonChain serves manufacturers, commodity traders, banks, and procurement teams, and offers system-to-system API integration for delivering activity data in and pulling gold-standard emissions calculations out — but it does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source client library. API access is offered as part of customer integration projects rather than as a self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: Cincinnati Financial
providers.description: Cincinnati Financial Corporation (NASDAQ: CINF) is a property and casualty insurer headquartered in Fairfield, Ohio, that markets a full suite of business, home, auto, and life insurance products plus investment services exclusively through a network of independent insurance agencies. Cincinnati Financial does not currently operate a public developer portal or expose customer-facing APIs; agency, claims, and policyholder access is delivered through web portals (cinfin.com, onlineservice.cinfin.com, and the Cincinnati Insurance Mobile App), with technical integrations for appointed agencies handled directly by Cincinnati Insurance IT support.

providers.name: Clearstep
providers.description: Clearstep is a digital health company whose clinical AI agents automate patient triage, scheduling, and care navigation for hospitals and health systems. Built on gold-standard, nurse-developed clinical protocols and integrated with Epic and other electronic health record systems, Clearstep's conversational Symptom Checker and Clinical Triage products help patients understand their symptoms and get routed to the right level of care, while reducing call-center and emergency-department burden for provider organizations. The company sells to leading health systems nationwide and is a Techstars-backed portfolio company.

providers.name: DNOW
providers.description: DNOW Inc. (NYSE: DNOW), formerly NOW Inc. and operating as DistributionNOW, is a Houston-headquartered Fortune 1000 distributor of pipe, valves, fittings (PVF), pumps and packaged, engineered process and production equipment serving the upstream, midstream, downstream energy, and industrial sectors. Spun off from National Oilwell Varco in 2014 and built on a heritage that spans more than 160 years, DNOW combines a global network of distribution branches and engineering facilities with the DigitalNOW platform — shop.dnow.com B2B eCommerce, cXML/OCI ERP punchout integrations, the eSpec product configurator, the AccessNOW automated inventory control system, and a library of customer-facing mobile applications. DNOW does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, or a self-serve API program; customer integrations are delivered through configured cXML/OCI punchout sessions tied to enterprise ERP systems. In June 2025 DNOW announced a definitive merger agreement to acquire MRC Global in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $1.5 billion.

providers.name: Docplanner
providers.description: Docplanner Group is a healthcare technology company that connects patients with doctors and equips medical practices with SaaS tools to manage online bookings, calendars, patient communication, reminders, payments, and online reputation. It operates a patient-facing marketplace plus a practice-management platform across 13 countries under brands including Doctoralia (Spain, Mexico, Brazil, Portugal, and Latin America), ZnanyLekarz (Poland), MioDottore (Italy), Doktor Takvimi (Turkey), Jameda (Germany), and the TuoTempo practice-management/booking platform. The group serves over 300,000 active doctors and handles roughly 25 million appointment bookings each month. Docplanner is backed by Point Nine among other investors.

providers.name: Epsagon
providers.description: Epsagon was an observability and application performance monitoring (APM) company, founded in 2017, that provided automated distributed tracing for serverless and containerized applications — AWS Lambda, Node.js, Python, Go, .NET, Ruby, and Java — correlating traces, metrics, and logs to help teams identify and fix problems fast without manual instrumentation. Epsagon was acquired by Cisco in 2021 and folded into Cisco's observability portfolio, after which the product was sunset. The epsagon.com developer surface (docs, dashboard, and API subdomains) no longer resolves. Its surviving public footprint is the github.com/epsagon organization and the first-party instrumentation SDKs still hosted on npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Go modules, NuGet, and Maven Central. This profile captures that remaining, verifiable footprint.

providers.name: Estately
providers.description: Estately is a Seattle-based, MLS-based residential real estate search platform for browsing homes for sale, recently sold homes, home values, and neighborhood information, and for connecting buyers and sellers with agents. Estately does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its notable developer-facing surface is the open-source `rets` Ruby library it maintains for fetching data from RETS (Real Estate Transaction Standard) servers, distributed on RubyGems with a bundled command-line client. This profile was surfaced from VC-portfolio signals (500 Global, Uncork Capital) and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Green Thumb Industries
providers.description: A leading U.S. cannabis consumer packaged goods company operating a nationwide portfolio of retail dispensaries under the RISE brand and a collection of cannabis brands. Operates manufacturing facilities and retail locations across multiple states.

providers.name: Haladir
providers.description: Haladir is a Y Combinator-backed startup building a decisional AI platform for logistics operations. Describing itself as "the decisional AI layer for logistics," Haladir unifies fragmented operational data from existing warehouse management (WMS), transportation management (TMS), and order management (OMS) systems into a single operational graph, then applies constraint-optimization solvers and machine-learning models to automate supply chain decisions across routing, picking, labor allocation, and inventory. Its approach treats large language models as formalization tools that translate messy operational rules into precise constraints for traditional solvers, rather than as decision-makers. Target customers include third-party logistics providers (3PLs), contract logistics providers, distributors, and shippers managing global supply chains. The company has raised $4.3M in seed funding led by BoxGroup and Susa Ventures. This profile currently exposes no public API or developer documentation; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: HUM Industries
providers.description: HUM Industries is a consumer hardware company building a wearable AI assistant designed to enhance social presence. The device records conversations locally, maintains a rolling buffer of recent audio, and surfaces contextual information such as names, personal details, and commitments back to the wearer through subtle audio cues. The company frames the product as giving people "the freedom to forget" by offloading memory to the device so they can stay present in the moment. At the time of profiling the product is pre-launch, offered through a preorder waitlist, with no public API, developer portal, or third-party integration surface. Backed by a16z; added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: LaunchKit
providers.description: LaunchKit was a set of web-based tools for mobile app developers, built by Cluster Labs, Inc. in San Francisco and backed by GV. Its products included Screenshot Builder for App Store screenshots, Review Monitor for App Store review alerts, a Sales Reporter, hosted App Websites, and Super Users and Cloud Config delivered through the LaunchKit iOS SDK. LaunchKit joined Google in 2016 and the codebase was released as open source under Apache 2.0. There is no live hosted LaunchKit API, developer portal, or documentation today; the surviving surface is a self-hostable Django/JavaScript codebase on GitHub plus an unmaintained Objective-C SDK on CocoaPods. The original launchkit.io domain is no longer company-controlled and now serves an unrelated content site.

providers.name: MasterBrand
providers.description: MasterBrand, Inc. is the largest manufacturer of residential cabinets in North America, producing kitchen, bath, and home organization cabinetry across a portfolio of brands sold through dealers, retailers, and builders. The company designs, manufactures, and distributes a wide array of cabinetry products under brands such as Aristokraft, Diamond, Mid-Continent, Schrock, and others. MasterBrand does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: Material Depot
providers.description: Material Depot is India's design-first interior-materials marketplace and experience-centre network, headquartered in Bengaluru and founded in 2022. It helps homeowners, architects, interior designers, builders and contractors discover, compare, visualize and purchase interior-design materials — tiles, laminates, wall panels, plywood, wallpapers, flooring, sanitaryware and countertops — spanning 300,000+ products across 1,000+ brands and 100+ categories. The company blends online discovery with physical experience centres in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, offering sample ordering, store-visit booking, free design consultations, video-call shopping, mix-and-match visualization, bulk/trade quotations and pan-India delivery. Backed by Accel, Material Depot operates a consumer/B2B web marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Medigram
providers.description: Medigram, Inc. is a healthcare AI governance company founded by Sherri Douville that builds Darwin, a governed decision platform for high-stakes clinical and performance AI. Darwin implements the sociotechnical data-governance architecture defined in IEEE UL 2933 (the six-dimension TIPPSS framework: Trust, Identity, Privacy, Protection, Safety, Security) and ANSI/HSI 2800:2025, scoring AI systems against a five-level maturity model and crosswalking them to ten governance frameworks (IEEE UL 2933, ANSI/HSI 2800:2025, ISO 42001, OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, NIST AI RMF, FDA, EU AI Act, and the HSCC guides). Applications include medtech AI governance, health-system IT review, and professional-sports player-health governance. Historically Medigram provided a secure, cloud-based mobile communication platform for healthcare professionals. Medigram is a portfolio company surfaced from the a16z network; it publishes marketing and standards content but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Polyup
providers.description: Let'sMOD (formerly Polyup) is a Sunnyvale, California company founded in 2015 that builds a consumer platform where users aged 8 and up can play, modify, remix, and share short 3D microgames and AI-powered interactive memes. Originally a computational-thinking and math learning tool under the Polyup brand, the product has evolved into a generative-AI-driven microgame and viral-content community at letsmod.com. Let'sMOD is a 500 Global portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal today; its public GitHub organization contains only internal CLI tooling and configuration. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched via live domain-security probing.

providers.name: Poultry sync
providers.description: PoultrySync is an AI-powered data management platform for the poultry value chain, helping producers increase productivity and reduce errors across broilers, breeders, hatchery, layers, slaughterhouse, feedmill, grandparents, lab, and quality management. The platform automates data collection, provides real-time dashboards, detects anomalies, forecasts production, and supports compliance reporting and audits, integrating with existing ERP systems in days. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation is published as of this profile.

providers.name: PREDIK Data-Driven
providers.description: PREDIK Data-Driven is a big-data analytics and location-intelligence research firm (founded 2008, Coral Gables, Florida) that builds enriched geospatial datasets for site selection, demand forecasting, and web/reference intelligence. Its products cover Point-of-Interest (POI) data, aggregated foot-traffic and human mobility data derived from anonymized mobile devices, company and commercial-area intelligence, and socio-demographic enrichment - divided into geohash-7 (150x150m) cells with 100-200+ variables and coverage of up to 96 countries. PREDIK is a data-delivery / contact-sales provider - datasets are licensed and delivered as managed feeds via REST API, SOAP API, Feed API, or S3 bucket in JSON, CSV, and SQL formats. There is no public self-serve developer API portal or published API reference; access is arranged directly with PREDIK or through the Datarade marketplace. Endpoints are not publicly documented and are therefore not modeled here.

providers.name: Raspire Inc.
providers.description: Raspire Inc. (RASPIRE) is a mobile application security company offering AI-powered, no-code runtime application self-protection for Android and iOS apps. Its SHIELD / XTD platform applies configuration-driven defenses that protect every release from code tampering, reverse engineering, hooking/injection, MITM interception, rooted or jailbroken devices, and runtime abuse without touching source code. The product delivers real-time threat detection, autonomous auto-mitigation, live security event feeds, and compliance-aligned reporting mapped to leading frameworks (OWASP MASVS, PCI DSS, GDPR, HIPAA). RASPIRE was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it is a SaaS security product with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Rizm
providers.description: RIZM is a holistic energy optimization platform for industrial enterprises, operated by Kerith GmbH of Münster, Germany. It integrates data from production, energy procurement, and infrastructure into a digital twin, then optimizes energy system design and day-to-day operational decisions — from long-term infrastructure investment and power purchase agreements to short-term asset dispatch and production scheduling — helping manufacturers cut energy costs and emissions at the same time. Named customers include BMW Group, Bosch, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, and BSH. The product is delivered as a login-gated web application (app.rizm.de) with authenticated documentation; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published at this time. Backed by Point Nine, this profile was surfaced from the venture portfolio graph.

providers.name: Setpointmedical
providers.description: SetPoint Medical is a bioelectronic medicine company developing an FDA-approved implantable neuroimmune modulation platform. The SetPoint System is a small, wireless, implantable device that stimulates the vagus nerve to reduce inflammation, delivering an automatic one-minute daily therapy for up to ten years to treat adults with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis who have not responded well to biologics. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It is a medical-device company with no public API or developer surface; this profile captures its identity and the security/disclosure posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Shelby Williams Industries
providers.description: Shelby Williams Industries is the premier designer, manufacturer, and distributor of seating products in the hospitality and food service industries. With over 70 years of experience, the company produces an extensive line of chairs, barstools, banquet seating, sofas, and tables made from wood, metal, rattan, and fully upholstered materials. Headquartered with US manufacturing in Newport, Tennessee, Shelby Williams serves hotels, restaurants, country clubs, senior living facilities, and banquet venues worldwide. As a contract furniture manufacturer focused on custom B2B orders, Shelby Williams does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Shepherd
providers.description: Shepherd is a technology-driven commercial insurance provider offering coverage for the builders and operators shaping the physical world. It underwrites Primary Casualty, Excess Casualty, and Builder's Risk lines for the construction and renewable-energy sectors, using data and an in-house AI underwriting engine (Nova) to deliver faster indications and modernized risk assessment. Shepherd sells through insurance brokers rather than exposing a public developer platform; it has issued 1,500+ policies across $400B+ in insured volume. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Costanoa Ventures and enriched by the pipeline; no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification was found.

providers.name: Skyfri
providers.description: Skyfri is a cleantech software and hardware company headquartered in Oslo, Norway that builds an operating platform for owners and operators of solar and battery energy assets. Founded in 2021, Skyfri combines an edge-native monitoring and control device (the SSI hardware, which speaks Modbus and SCADA over isolated RS-485 ports to inverters, meters, and sensors) with a cloud platform that automates operations, maintenance, and asset performance management. The software delivers real-time data processing, operational management, weather forecasting, dynamic benchmarking, plant insights, and fault detection to monitor generation and address underperformance and equipment failure across a global portfolio of solar and battery assets. The company has offices in Denver, London, Oslo, Singapore, and Bangalore and is backed by Speedinvest. Skyfri exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; its platform is delivered as a customer application at app.skyfri.com.

providers.name: Thirty Madison
providers.description: Thirty Madison is a US direct-to-consumer telehealth and digital-health company founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York City. It operates a family of condition-focused virtual care brands, including Keeps (hair loss), Cove (migraine), Facet (dermatology), and Nurx (sexual and reproductive health), pairing online medical consultations with mail-order pharmacy fulfillment; the company merged with Nurx in 2022. Thirty Madison publishes no public developer API program, so this profile captures its public security-disclosure and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Tracelytics
providers.description: Tracelytics was a Boston/Providence application-tracing (APM) startup, backed by investors including Google Ventures, that built full-stack distributed tracing for web applications. AppNeta acquired Tracelytics in 2012 and the product became AppNeta TraceView; SolarWinds acquired TraceView in 2016, and AppNeta itself was acquired by Broadcom in 2021. The company no longer operates independently — the tracelytics.com domain no longer resolves and its TraceView Data API (api.tracelytics.com) is defunct — but its verified GitHub organization and first-party TraceView instrumentation packages remain published on RubyGems and npm.

providers.name: Uninstall
providers.description: Uninstall.io was a mobile "uninstall intelligence" platform built by Songline Analytics (Bengaluru/Singapore, founded 2015) whose iOS and Android SDKs tracked app uninstalls, surfaced uninstall reasons, and drove re-install campaigns for customers like Snapdeal, Axis Bank, Zalora, and BankBazaar. Backed by 500 Startups India, Rajan Anandan, and Hive Data, it was acquired by Singapore healthtech company Mobile Health in July 2018. The uninstall.io domain is now parked for sale and no public API surface remains; the GitHub organization and first-party mobile SDKs survive as the public footprint.

providers.name: Unleashed Games
providers.description: Unleashed Games is an independent game studio founded by industry veterans (World of Warcraft, Medal of Honor, Monopoly Go!) and backed by a16z Speedrun, building socially-driven cooperative games. Its flagship title Haven is a cross-platform co-op RPG for families and friends spanning PC, Mac, console, and mobile, with procedurally generated maps, village building, and collaborative combat. The studio publishes no public developer platform or API surface today.

providers.name: Unreal Estate
providers.description: Unreal Estate (formerly USRealty.com) is a tech-enabled flat-fee real estate marketplace and brokerage that lets home sellers list on their local MLS without paying a traditional listing commission, with flat-fee plans ranging from $0 to $449 upfront plus 0.5% at closing, available nationwide except South Dakota. The company also offers buyer services, rental listings with cash rebates, and AI-powered market intelligence, and was acquired by Abode in November 2024. Unreal Estate publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Uxin
providers.description: Uxin (优信) is a Chinese used-car e-commerce company backed by DCM Ventures. It operates the xin.com consumer used-car retail marketplace and the Youxinpai (优信拍) B2B online used-car auction and trading platform that connects dealers with buyers, including vehicle listings, auctions, logistics, and post-sale services. Uxin publishes no public developer portal or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: VANCL
providers.description: VANCL (凡客诚品) is a Chinese direct-to-consumer online apparel brand founded in October 2007 that sells its own-brand men's wear, women's wear, shoes, children's clothing, and home goods through vancl.com and official storefronts on Tmall, JD.com, Douyin, and Youzan. Once China's leading independent B2C fashion retailer, VANCL publishes no public API or developer platform today — its legacy open-platform hosts (open.vancl.com, api.vancl.com) no longer respond. Surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Varada
providers.description: Varada was a Tel Aviv-based data lake analytics accelerator that used proprietary, patented adaptive indexing to dramatically speed up Trino/Presto queries directly on data lake storage. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Varada was acquired by Starburst Data on June 23, 2022, and its indexing technology and engineering team were folded into Starburst's query engine. The company published developer tooling (the vtm cluster-management CLI, a Presto/Trino workload analyzer, and a PowerBI Presto connector) on GitHub but no public API; the varada.io domain is now parked and its GitHub organization has been dormant since the acquisition.

providers.name: Vsim
providers.description: Vsim (Vsim Technology Ltd) is a Manchester, UK physics-simulation startup founded in 2022 by ex-NVIDIA simulation engineers Michelle Lu (CEO) and Kier Storey (CTO). The company builds a next-generation physics simulation platform and an end-to-end reinforcement-learning training framework for robotics, reporting up to 100x training performance speed-ups over existing solutions, with applications across robotics, AI, visual effects, aerodynamics, gaming, and e-commerce. Vsim raised a $21.5M seed round led by EQT Ventures (total ~$24M). It does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Zeal
providers.description: Zeal is a self-custodial onchain crypto wallet built for everyday life, pairing a non-custodial multi-chain wallet with real-world spending through a Gnosis Pay Visa debit card. Users hold USD and EUR stablecoins, earn yield via DeFi protocols such as Sky and Aave, and spend in 150+ countries with cashback, all while retaining full control of their own keys. Security features include Safety Checks, a Privacy Shield, biometric authentication, real-time transaction alerts and card freeze. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Zeal publishes a consumer product and help documentation but no public API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or developer platform.

providers.name: 10x Science
providers.description: 10x Science is an AI-native software company building the first AI-native protein characterization platform for the life sciences, starting with drug development. A Y Combinator W26 company founded out of Nobel laureate Carolyn Bertozzi's laboratory at Stanford University, it automates peptide mapping for protein therapeutics, delivering explainable molecular insights in minutes where legacy tools and manual workflows take months. The company raised a $4.8M seed round led by Initialized Capital and is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; it does not yet publish a public developer API.

providers.name: 83 Sciences
providers.description: 83 Sciences is an AI-native materials-discovery company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) that helps research labs unlock value from unpublished and discarded experimental data. Roughly 90% of experimental data never reaches publication; 83 Sciences works on-site with researchers to capture and structure that hidden data into a queryable database, then applies AI-powered analysis and generative models to learn from a lab's full experimental history — including failed experiments — to surface novel materials, co-authored manuscripts, and patents. Founded by researchers from MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and Columbia and based in San Francisco. The company currently ships no public API or developer surface; this profile tracks its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ADstruc
providers.description: ADstruc is a technology platform for the out-of-home (OOH) advertising industry, founded in 2010 in New York City by John Laramie and Sam Herbert. It provides workflow-automation software, including its Drive product, that lets brands and agencies plan, buy, and manage traditional and digital out-of-home media campaigns, and gives OOH operators cloud-based tools to manage and promote their inventory and interact with clients in real time. ADstruc was acquired by Vistar Media in April 2024 and now operates as part of its programmatic out-of-home advertising stack. No public developer API or documentation surface has been identified for ADstruc at this time.

providers.name: Altru
providers.description: Altru (Altru Labs, Inc.) was a mobile-first, employee-generated video storytelling platform for recruitment marketing and talent acquisition, enabling organizations to capture, edit, brand, approve, and distribute authentic employee video content across career sites, social media, and email/text campaigns, with video transcription in 14+ languages. Founded in 2017 and based in Brooklyn, New York, and backed by Techstars, Altru served brands including Target, PwC, Intuit, L'Oreal, and Box before being acquired by iCIMS on December 14, 2020 and folded into the iCIMS Talent Cloud. Altru no longer operates as an independent provider — altrulabs.com now redirects to icims.com and there is no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Alyne
providers.description: Alyne is a cloud-native governance, risk and compliance (GRC) platform, founded in Munich in 2015 and acquired by Mitratech in 2021, where it is now offered as Mitratech's Alyne. The platform pairs a large curated library of controls and regulatory content with AI-assisted risk assessments, control mapping, maturity scoring and reporting, helping enterprises and FinTechs manage cyber, operational and third-party risk. Alyne is delivered as SaaS through app.alyne.com and is positioned to integrate with common IT, compliance and data systems. As of this profile Alyne exposes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; this record captures its public identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: Ample
providers.description: Ample Foods is a nutrition company that makes single-serving meal-replacement shakes sold direct-to-consumer at amplemeal.com. Its lineup includes Ample Original, a low-carb meal shake with roughly 25g protein and 4g net carbs per 400-calorie serving, and Ample Recover, a higher-carb performance shake with about 31g protein and 33g carbs per 400-calorie serving, sold in ready-to-drink bottles and bulk canisters. Ample is a consumer packaged-goods brand running on a Shopify storefront; enrichment probing found no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, developer portal, or API reference. This profile is a portfolio lead backed by 500 Global and is retained as a company record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Anoria
providers.description: Anoria is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) human-interaction company building a wearable bracelet for the EQ era that measures and tracks emotional states in real time. The device uses the company's proprietary SOMI (state-of-mind inference) model to correlate roughly 150 audio and biometric signals into a "Flow Score" that reflects a user's energy, mood, and focus, then explains why the user feels that way and what they can do about it. Anoria targets founders and creatives who treat their mental state as a performance asset, with the goal of making emotional intelligence trainable. As of mid-2026 the company is an early-stage prototype running an early-access waitlist; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation yet, so this API Evangelist profile captures verified company identity only.

providers.name: ArcSight
providers.description: ArcSight is an enterprise security information and event management (SIEM) platform, now part of OpenText Cybersecurity (formerly Micro Focus, and HP before that). The ArcSight family centers on Enterprise Security Manager (ESM) for real-time correlation and threat detection, alongside Logger for log management and compliance, SmartConnectors for data collection and normalization, Intelligence for behavioral analytics, and Recon for search and investigation. ArcSight was an early Kleiner Perkins portfolio company. It exposes REST and web-services APIs (ESM client services, Logger Web Services, and SCIM user provisioning) primarily to on-premises and SaaS customer deployments rather than as a public developer platform.

providers.name: Artiphon
providers.description: Artiphon is a Nashville-based music technology company that designs smart, portable musical instruments for everyday creativity. Its products, including the Instrument 1, Orba, Orba 2, Orba 3, and Chorda, combine strumming, tapping, sliding, and looping into palm-sized MIDI controllers and synthesizers, paired with companion apps that let anyone make beats, loop sounds, and explore music anywhere. Artiphon sells direct and through retailers such as Guitar Center and Sweetwater. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-hardware company reference.

providers.name: Atrium
providers.description: Atrium is a sales-effectiveness and sales-performance business intelligence platform for revenue teams. It continuously monitors sales KPIs to surface anomalies in rep and team performance, detects which behaviors and activities are driving (or dragging) output, and delivers AI-powered coaching recommendations to managers and reps. The product connects directly to Salesforce, HubSpot, data warehouses, and communication tools rather than exposing a public developer API. Founded in San Francisco by Jason Heidema (CEO) and Peter Kazanjy and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Bullpen Capital, and Electric Capital, Atrium was acquired by Fullcast in 2025 and is now offered as Fullcast Performance; atriumhq.com redirects to fullcast.com and only the customer application login at app.atriumhq.com remains on the Atrium domain.

providers.name: Auxos
providers.description: Auxos is an AI-powered customer research platform that builds 1:1 AI clones of a company's real customers to simulate how they respond to business decisions before those decisions ship. The company recruits and interviews real people matching a client's ideal customer profile, then models each participant as an always-on AI avatar grounded in that interview data. Teams use the resulting synthetic audience to test surveys, messaging, ad creative, pricing, and product flows and retrieve population-scale quantitative results plus qualitative commentary in minutes rather than the weeks traditional market research takes. Auxos is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company founded by Ashton Daniel, Jerry Wu, and Kerry Lu, targeting marketing, product, and research teams. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist; as of enrichment Auxos publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Baletu
providers.description: Baletu (巴乐兔) is a landlord-direct online residential rental platform operated by Shanghai Wanjian Information Technology Co., Ltd. Founded in 2012 and based in Shanghai, it lets tenants rent apartments directly from landlords with monthly-payment ("月付") options, reducing agency fees. The platform spans first-tier Chinese cities including Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen plus more than ten second-tier cities, listing over one million properties. Baletu is a consumer proptech company backed by DCM Ventures, Tiantu Capital, Nan Fung Group, and ZWC Partners, having raised roughly $140M through a 2018 Series C. It ships consumer iOS/Android apps and a partner portal; it does not publish a public developer API program (api.baletu.com serves its own apps).

providers.name: bannerman
providers.description: Bannerman is a San Francisco-based technology company that operates a security guard marketplace, connecting businesses with screened, licensed, insured, and certified security professionals. Founded in 2014 (Y Combinator S14) and backed by Slow Ventures, FundersClub, and Y Combinator, Bannerman brings software and technology to the traditionally manual physical-security-services industry. Its web dashboard lets clients book, schedule, and manage on-site security officers, run real-time GPS patrol tracking and incident reporting, handle communications, and manage billing from a single security-officer-management platform. Clients have included Lyft, WeWork, BMW, Juul, and YSL, with service across San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York, and Chicago. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts are published at this time.

providers.name: BlueTarp Financial
providers.description: BlueTarp Financial is a B2B trade-credit and accounts-receivable financing company, founded in Portland, Maine, that lets suppliers, distributors, and building-materials dealers extend revolving or net-terms credit to their business customers while BlueTarp pays the supplier upfront and assumes the credit risk and collections. Its SmartView portal manages the purchase-to-payment lifecycle: credit decisioning, invoicing, billing, and receivables. BlueTarp was acquired and is now operated as Capital One Trade Credit; its independent site (bluetarp.com) redirects to capitalone.com/trade-credit/bluetarp. BlueTarp publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: CAMP4 Therapeutics
providers.description: CAMP4 Therapeutics is a clinical-stage RNA-medicines biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, pioneering a new class of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapeutics designed to increase targeted gene expression. Built on the company's RAP Platform (Regulatory RNA Activating Platform), which combines epigenomics, computational biology, and machine learning to map the regulatory RNA and signaling circuits controlling gene expression, CAMP4 develops first-in-class medicines for diseases caused by insufficient protein expression, with an initial focus on central nervous system and metabolic disorders such as urea cycle disorders and SYNGAP1. Founded by CEO Josh Mandel-Brehm with scientific co-founders Rick Young (Whitehead Institute/MIT) and Len Zon (Boston Children's Hospital/Harvard), CAMP4 is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). This is a corporate/therapeutics company profile in the API Evangelist network; CAMP4 publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Cardinal
providers.description: Cardinal (trycardinal.ai) is an AI platform for precision outbound sales, built for fast-growing go-to-market teams that want outbound to function like a real engine rather than a collection of disconnected tools and experiments. The company is a Y Combinator-backed startup; its public presence today is a marketing site (product, company, and customers pages plus archived engineering posts) with a waitlist for access. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface has been published yet, so this profile captures verified company identity while the developer program is still forming.

providers.name: Causal
providers.description: Causal (causal.app) is a financial planning and business modeling platform for building spreadsheet-style models, forecasts, dashboards, and scenario analysis, aimed at finance teams and startups doing FP&A and extended planning and analysis (xP&A). Causal was acquired by Lucanet and its capabilities are now delivered as part of the Lucanet CFO Solution Platform; the marketing site redirects to Lucanet while existing customers sign in at my.causal.app. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or docs surface is currently published. Backed by Accel and Kindred Ventures.

providers.name: Ciridae
providers.description: Ciridae is building an AI-native operating system for services businesses — the industrial, construction, and field-service companies that make up the real economy. Its platform replaces fragmented ERPs and spreadsheets with a unified system that automates core business operations across project management, financials, CRM, accounts payable and receivable, and reporting, while keeping humans in the loop to oversee AI decisions. Modules span AI-generated field workforce scheduling, vendor onboarding and compliance, automated payment workflows, and customer order expediting, typically deployed in a two-to-four-week implementation with embedded engineers. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, Ciridae is backed by Accel. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Community Gaming
providers.description: Community Gaming is a web3 esports and gaming platform where players earn cryptocurrency rewards by competing in tournaments and completing quests. Players link a Sequence wallet, collect keys from quests and matches to open loot boxes and giveaway tickets, and enter prize draws paid out in USDC. The platform also serves tournament organizers with hosting tools, sponsorships, and grants. Backed by Multicoin Capital, it publishes a public knowledge center for players and organizers but does not currently document a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: ConvenientPower
providers.description: ConvenientPower (Chengdu ConvenientPower Semiconductor, 成都市易冲半导体有限公司) is an analog and mixed-signal integrated-circuit design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, with offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Xi'an, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Silicon Valley. The company designs high-performance power-management ICs spanning the full link from 220V mains to battery: wireless-charging transmitters and receivers (Qi, up to 100W), USB Power Delivery and UFCS protocol controllers, AC/DC flyback and synchronous rectifier controllers, GaN-integrated solutions, battery-charging management, LDOs and DC/DC converters, and automotive-grade power ICs (wireless charging, LED lighting, eFuse protection, switches). Its parts ship into consumer electronics, accessories, and automotive markets, with more than 330 million units shipped and 160+ patents; automotive ICs are AEC-Q100 qualified. As a hardware semiconductor vendor, ConvenientPower exposes developer resources as chip SDK toolkits, reference designs, and design software rather than a public web API. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Coterra Energy
providers.description: Coterra Energy is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Coterra Energy API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: CrossAmerica Partners
providers.description: CrossAmerica Partners is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The CrossAmerica Partners API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Deep Interactions
providers.description: Deep Interactions is a collaborative, humans-in-the-loop AI builder for product teams, launched out of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch. The platform helps teams move from business goals through design and development to a deployed AI product, turning messy ideas, data, and tools into working software in a single afternoon while maintaining code organization and product coherence. It positions itself as the context layer that lets a whole team build in sync — integrating with existing tools such as Slack, Figma, GitHub, Vercel, and Supabase — rather than producing disconnected solo prototypes. The company is currently at a waitlist-only stage and does not yet publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Diametric Capital
providers.description: Diametric Capital is an equity long/short, multi-manager investment fund firm headquartered in Boston and New York. The firm builds customizable funds that isolate what it calls "True Alpha" — returns uncorrelated to the broader market — by removing beta and factor risk exposure to deliver performance with below-average volatility. Alongside its funds it offers aligned fee structures, capital partnerships, and business development support to entrepreneurs and emerging managers. Diametric Capital is a private financial firm and does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDK surface; it operates a secure client data room for investors and partners.

providers.name: Diamond
providers.description: Diamond (diamond.io) is an early-stage, managed serverless data backend for teams, positioned as "your project, but with AI." The product promises a world-class serverless database where teams bring their own data sources, AI-assisted setup so no schema configuration is required, team collaboration with role management, and single sign-on via Google, Microsoft, and LDAP. As of this profile the public surface is a pre-launch landing page with a "create your workspace" signup form and a sign-in page; no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, pricing, changelog, or status page are published yet. Diamond Inc. is a portfolio company of Partech. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and enriched from the provider's public web surface.

providers.name: Doc Doc
providers.description: Doc Doc (DOCDOC, Inc.) is a Latin American telemedicine platform offering online medical consultations by chat and video across more than 20 specialties, including pediatrics, gynecology, nutrition, psychology, cardiology, dermatology, orthopedics, and general practice. It serves individual patients, healthcare professionals, and companies running employee wellbeing programs, and delivers its consumer product through the app at app.doc-doc.com. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; enrichment found only the marketing site and the patient app.

providers.name: Doxel
providers.description: Doxel is a Menlo Park, California construction technology company providing AI-powered observability and progress tracking for large capital projects. Founded in 2015 by CEO Saurabh Ladha, the company combines 360-degree reality capture (via Insta360 X5 hardware partnership) with computer vision models that compare site video against BIM models to automatically quantify work-in-place by trade, system, and stage.
