The platform layers a "rules of credit" engine on top of those quantities to drive earned-value, schedule, and budget analytics — including 3D Progress View, Production Rates, Schedule (a visual Gantt replacement), Utilities Underground Tracking from drone imagery, and Portfolio-level dashboards. Doxel uses advanced language models to map schedule line items to physical progress and supports Procore-style construction management workflows, with deployments across data centers, healthcare, semiconductor fabs, and EV battery factories. Doxel has raised approximately $57M from Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, and others, and counts 18 of the top 30 U.S. general contractors, 14 of the top 20 data center developers, and 3 of 4 hyperscalers as customers. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or GitHub organization — the platform is delivered as a managed SaaS application at app.doxel.ai with hardware-assisted capture and enterprise integrations arranged via direct engagement.

providers.name: Emailio
providers.description: Emailio is a Y Combinator (Winter 2014) and Thiel Fellowship-backed startup building "email built for wellness" — a consumer email client for iPhone, iPad, and Mac that centers user wellbeing and mental health rather than traditional inbox-productivity metrics. Its pre-launch landing page describes inbox management, email batching, mood tracking, one-click unsubscribe, and Smart Rule Suggestions, with early access gated behind a waitlist. Founded by Martin Stoyanov and Teo Teodosiev with a roughly five-person team, Emailio sits at the intersection of the productivity and health & wellness categories. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; as of this pass it exposes a consumer product only — no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs could be found.

providers.name: EnerVenue
providers.description: EnerVenue is a Fremont, California-based energy infrastructure company building long-duration stationary energy storage using a metal-hydrogen (nickel-hydrogen) battery chemistry derived from NASA-heritage technology that has powered the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station since the 1980s. Co-founded by Stanford materials scientist Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue refined the orbital nickel-hydrogen cell into a grid-scale "Energy Storage Vessel" (ESV) targeting a 30-year, 30,000+ cycle service life with 100% usable depth of discharge, ~90% round-trip efficiency, an operating range of -20 C to +60 C, no thermal runaway risk, and no active thermal management. The ESV's aqueous metal cell (AMC) uses a nickel hydroxide cathode, a nickel-alloy anode, an alkaline electrolyte, and hermetically sealed hydrogen gas storage built from steel, nickel, fiberglass, resin, and water — no lithium, cobalt, or rare earths. EnerVenue is scaling manufacturing through a one-million- square-foot gigafactory in Shelby County, Kentucky (1 GWh phase one, scaling toward 20 GWh per year with ~$1B of follow-on investment) plus a high-volume line in Changzhou, China (250 MWh by Q3 2026, 1 GWh in 2027). Customer commitments exceed 7 GWh and include Pine Gate Renewables (2.4 GWh, multi-year), Green Energy Renewable Solutions (Nicon Industries), Sonnell Power Solutions, and VedantaESS. The company closed a $300M Series B in 2026 to fund the gigafactory build-out. EnerVenue sells hardware, EPC-integrated storage systems, and long-duration service warranties — it does not publish a developer API, SDK, public OpenAPI specification, or open-source repository.

providers.name: Enterprise Integration Patterns
providers.description: Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIP) is a catalog of architectural design patterns for integrating enterprise applications. The patterns describe messaging-based integration scenarios and provide a common vocabulary for architects and developers to design and implement integration solutions. The canonical reference is the book by Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf, organized into six pattern categories: Messaging Channels, Message Construction, Message Routing, Message Transformation, Messaging Endpoints, and System Management.

providers.name: Eversight
providers.description: Eversight is an AI-powered pricing and promotions software company serving consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands and retailers. Its SaaS platform runs continuous, controlled experiments testing untried everyday prices and promotional offers with real shoppers, then applies advanced analytics and AI-powered experimentation to surface revenue-optimizing price and offer recommendations. The product is delivered as two suites — a Retail Pricing Suite that integrates with physical and digital store networks, and an Offer Innovation Suite for CPG trade-promotion teams that deploys standalone or on top of existing TPM systems. Eversight was founded in 2013, acquired by Instacart in 2022, and targets revenue-management, trade-marketing, sales, pricing, and merchant teams. It is a portfolio company of Emergence Capital. No public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal is published — the platform is an enterprise SaaS engagement.

providers.name: Examedi
providers.description: Examedi is a Latin American healthtech company providing at-home medical and laboratory testing. Patients book online and a healthcare professional visits their home to collect samples (blood, urine, PCR and more), with results delivered digitally through the company's app and website. Examedi operates in Chile (examedi.cl) and Mexico (examedi.mx) and runs a live authenticated application backend at api.examedi.com. The company is backed by General Catalyst. No public developer program, API documentation, or OpenAPI definition is published at this time; this profile records the company's identity and discovered surfaces for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Factory Works
providers.description: Factory Works (Factory Berlin) is a Berlin-based venture-building and company-builder firm that partners with entrepreneurs, visual artists, and musicians to turn early ideas into scalable businesses. Positioning itself as a "neo company builder," Factory builds and scales ventures in exchange for equity while handling strategy, product, brand, marketing, legal, accounting, and operations, and it runs a physical Berlin venue with event, restaurant, and studio infrastructure alongside a mentor and investor network. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Factory publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Fifth Door
providers.description: Fifth Door is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) AI-native gaming startup founded by Amir Ghazvinian and Daniel Kan that lets anyone create, share, and play games simply by describing what they imagine, with no coding required. Its generative-AI platform turns natural-language prompts into playable, customizable games, aiming to collapse the time, cost, and technical complexity of traditional game development for players, creators, and studios. Backed by Felicis, the company runs a consumer web app and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: Flowneuroscience
providers.description: Flow Neuroscience is a Malmo, Sweden medtech company founded in 2016 by clinical psychologist Daniel Mansson and neuroscientist Erik Rehn. It develops a medically approved, at-home transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) headset paired with a behavioral-therapy smartphone app to treat major depressive disorder without medication. Its Flow FL-100 device is CE-marked in the EU and UK and received FDA approval (PMA P230024) as the first at-home tDCS treatment for depression, with a US launch planned for September 2026. Flow is backed by Khosla Ventures and other global investors. This is a consumer and clinical medical-device company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Formally
providers.description: Formally is an AI-native platform for legal collaboration that begins with US immigration. It combines intelligent technology, behavioral science, and secure, portable client data to connect immigration attorneys and law firms, individual visa applicants, and employers sponsoring global hires in a single connected product. Attorneys manage cases at scale, individuals track applications and reduce anxiety while retaining ownership of their own data, and employers coordinate visa sponsorship. As of this enrichment pass Formally does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, developer portal, or documentation surface, so this profile captures company identity and published web properties only.

providers.name: Foxintelligence
providers.description: Foxintelligence was a French e-commerce measurement and consumer-insights company that aggregated anonymized online purchase data from email receipts across millions of e-shoppers to give brands and retailers competitive intelligence on where, when, and how much consumers buy online. It was acquired by NielsenIQ and operates today as the "NIQ Digital Purchases" product; the original www.foxintelligence.io domain now 301-redirects to nielseniq.com. The surviving first-party surface is the customer web application at app.foxintelligence.io (login only). No public API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation is published; this profile is maintained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hex Security
providers.description: Hex Security is a Y Combinator (W26) security startup building autonomous AI agents that perform continuous penetration testing against web applications, APIs, and infrastructure. Instead of point-in-time annual pentests, Hex's agents probe systems around the clock — chaining exploits together, validating each finding with a working proof-of-concept, and delivering triaged, reproducible results with no false positives. The product surfaces high-severity issues such as SQL injection, broken access control / IDOR, authentication bypass, and unauthenticated remote code execution. Founded by Ahmad Khan, Huzaifa Ahmad, and Prama Yudhistira. As of this profile Hex Security is pre-public-API: it operates a marketing site (hex.co) and a product application (app.hex.co) but does not yet publish a developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or public API surface.

providers.name: Involve.AI
providers.description: Involve.AI is an AI-driven customer intelligence platform for customer success and revenue teams. It unifies data from CRM, support, product-usage, and billing systems to calculate customer health scores and power an Early Warning System that predicts churn and surfaces renewal and upsell opportunities, with a 9Factor model scoring qualitative and quantitative signals. Founded as a Techstars-backed startup, Involve.AI was absorbed into Jeeva.ai — the involve.ai domain now redirects to jeeva.ai, while the original customer knowledge base remains live at city.involve.ai. Involve.AI integrated with source systems rather than exposing a public developer REST API, so this profile documents company identity rather than an API surface.

providers.name: JD Logistics
providers.description: JD Logistics (Hong Kong listed as 2618.HK) is a technology-driven supply chain and logistics service provider spun out of JD.com and backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. It operates one of China's largest integrated logistics networks, offering express and freight delivery, integrated warehouse-and-fulfillment, cold-chain and pharmaceutical logistics, cross-border shipping, oversized-item handling, and smart supply-chain technology. Through its JD Logistics Open Platform (open.jdl.com) it exposes enterprise integration services for order fulfillment, warehousing, waybill/shipment creation, tracking, and reconciliation to merchants and partners. This profile tracks the company's public developer and open-platform surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: KDDI
providers.description: KDDI Corporation is a Japanese multinational telecommunications operator headquartered in Tokyo, providing mobile, fixed-line, broadband, and enterprise ICT services. KDDI markets its consumer mobile services under the au brand, alongside UQ mobile and povo, and serves enterprise customers globally through KDDI Global and KDDI America. The company operates the KDDI Open API for Developers portal exposing inquiry-gated product APIs including the au PAY Mini App platform, an XR/MEC low-latency application API, a PPM consent management API, and an au mobile Identification Support Service for KYC/identity verification. KDDI also runs the au OPEN DEVICE DEVELOPER SITE for cellular module device certification, and a KDDI Cloud Platform Service knowledge site with developer API references for cloud infrastructure. In 2025 KDDI became an equity partner in Aduna, the GSMA/Ericsson-backed network API venture aggregating CAMARA-aligned carrier APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location) across global operators. Public OpenAPI specifications are not openly published; API access is provided through contact/inquiry workflows after partner onboarding.

providers.name: Lexoo
providers.description: Lexoo is a commercial legal services provider that operates as an outsourced in-house legal team for businesses, concentrating on commercial contract review and negotiation. The company handles routine contract work at fixed rates per agreement with a stated maximum two-day turnaround, so internal legal and sales teams are freed for more strategic work. Alongside contract review, Lexoo runs multi-country projects that engage local counsel across more than 70 countries for work such as terms and conditions localisation and regulatory research, and it builds playbooks and training materials that let client teams handle standard agreements independently. The practice is led by Nathalie Lambert and serves scale-ups and start-ups, with published client references including Trustpilot, Nielsen, ComplyAdvantage, Xeneta, Chattermill and Jokr. Lexoo is not an API-first company: it publishes no developer portal, documentation or SDKs, and its only machine-readable surfaces are the standard WordPress REST API and RSS feed exposed by its marketing site.

providers.name: Manufactured
providers.description: Manufactured is a supply-chain and production platform for hardware and consumer-product brands, backed by Bullpen Capital. Its web application (app.manufactured.com) helps teams run overseas production end to end — issuing sourcing requests to vendors, managing supplier and vendor profiles, negotiating order estimates and contracts under master procurement agreements, tracking production timelines and calendars, and financing purchase orders through production and repayment terms. The product also embeds an AI assistant built on LangChain. At the time of enrichment the public marketing site and the api/docs/developer subdomains were unreachable, and the GraphQL, Lambda and bot backends are private and authentication-gated (introspection blocked), so no public API specification, developer portal, or documentation could be harvested. This profile captures the real, observable surface only.

providers.name: Maquoketa Research
providers.description: Maquoketa Research is a defense-technology startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building autonomous terminal-guidance systems for one-way attack drones. Its platform-agnostic guidance modules add custom computer-vision object tracking to low-cost FPV drone hardware, raising strike success rates from under 25% to roughly 80% while maintaining target lock through GPS jamming and signal loss. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the five-person team ships hardware modules (product lines include GCS, Magpie, Odin, and TGS) that integrate with existing drone flight controllers rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from the company's public website; it currently exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Marker Learning
providers.description: Marker Learning is a special-education technology company that provides AI-powered report-writing tools for school districts and evaluation teams. Its platform ingests referral and assessment documents and automatically drafts comprehensive psychological and educational evaluation reports, citing its sources for transparency, supporting multiple assessment and rating scales, and running built-in compliance checks. The company emphasizes FERPA and NIST CSF compliance. Marker Learning was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Metalogix
providers.description: Metalogix was an independent software vendor providing migration, management, and security solutions for Microsoft SharePoint and Office 365, best known for its Content Matrix SharePoint-to-SharePoint migration tool. Quest Software acquired Metalogix in June 2018, and the metalogix.com domain now redirects to Quest, where the products live on as the Metalogix Content Matrix line. The tooling is delivered as a desktop console with PowerShell cmdlets that drive the supported SharePoint APIs; it does not publish an independent public REST API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or client SDK. This profile is retained for network/portfolio lineage.

providers.name: Mixt
providers.description: MIXT is a chef-driven fast-casual salad and grain-bowl restaurant chain operating across the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles. Founded on sourcing fresh, local, seasonal, and organic ingredients, MIXT prepares its greens, grains, grilled meats, dressings, and drinks in-house and offers customizable salads (80+ ingredients), warm grain bowls, sandwiches, catering, and a rewards loyalty program. MIXT is a Certified B Corporation (since 2018), reflecting a commitment to sustainable sourcing and environmental responsibility. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. MIXT is a consumer restaurant brand and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDKs; online ordering is offered through a hosted ordering surface at order.mixt.com.

providers.name: MobileIron
providers.description: MobileIron was a pioneer in mobile device management (MDM) and enterprise mobility management (EMM), later unified endpoint management (UEM), securing mobile devices, applications, and content for enterprises with capabilities such as Zero Sign-On, Mobile Threat Defense, and secure connectivity. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Ivanti on December 1, 2020, and its platform capabilities are now delivered inside the Ivanti product suite. The mobileiron.com domain now redirects to Ivanti, and MobileIron no longer operates an independent developer or public API program.

providers.name: Mogul
providers.description: Mogul is a modern executive advisory, training, and executive search firm serving 600+ leading companies, with particular focus on leadership development and AI transformation across retail, consumer goods, healthcare, media, and nonprofit sectors. Its services span executive advisory (fractional AI and HR leadership, AI adoption and change management, AI agent buildout), executive training (signature programs from "AI Readiness for Enterprise" through "Organizational Leadership," delivered on-demand or live), and executive search (C-suite, board, and professional placements with succession planning). Mogul reports having educated 1MM+ leaders and counts Amazon, Google, Disney, Microsoft, and Nike among its clients. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Mogul publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation; it operates as a B2B services and training business.

providers.name: MouseCat
providers.description: MouseCat is an agentic AI infrastructure company for risk operations, founded in 2026 and a graduate of the Y Combinator Winter 2026 batch. The platform runs human-quality fraud investigations to help risk teams automatically detect, investigate, and mitigate emerging fraud, scale investigations, build better models, and make faster decisions. MouseCat deploys entirely within customer-owned cloud environments, integrating with the data, vendors, and APIs a risk team already relies on so companies retain complete control of sensitive data. The company was founded by Nicholas Aldridge (CEO) and Joseph McAllister (CTO) and is backed by Y Combinator, Imagination Capital, and SurgePoint Capital. As of this profile MouseCat is an early-stage startup with a public marketing site and a private application; it publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or MCP server yet.

providers.name: NOTHS
providers.description: NOTHS (Not On The High Street, notonthehighstreet.com) is a UK online marketplace that curates and sells unique gifts, jewellery, homeware and personalised products made or sourced by thousands of small UK creative businesses. Founded in 2006 and backed by Index Ventures, the platform connects independent sellers ("partners") with consumers through a curated storefront, seller onboarding, and an affiliate programme. It exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface; its api.notonthehighstreet.com host is a private backend serving the company's own web and mobile storefront. This profile is a VC-portfolio lead enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline via live domain/security probing.

providers.name: Novus (SEI Investments)
providers.description: SEI Novus (Novus) is the portfolio intelligence and analytics platform of SEI Investments, serving institutional investors — asset owners, pension funds, endowments, foundations, and family offices — with manager monitoring, exposure and performance analytics, risk assessment, and reporting across public and private market portfolios. It is an enterprise, client-login product accessed at alpha.novus.com; it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface. Originally an independent portfolio-analytics company (novus.com), it was acquired by SEI Investments.

providers.name: Odessa Technologies
providers.description: Odessa is a Philadelphia-headquartered lease and loan management software company founded in 1998 that powers asset finance for banks, captive finance companies, and independent lenders. The Odessa Platform manages roughly $200B in assets across equipment finance and auto finance, covering the full asset lifecycle from origination through servicing and remarketing on a modern, API-first, Microsoft Azure-hosted SaaS stack with low-code developer tools, packaged integrations, and an Odessa AI layer for agentic asset-finance workflows. The platform's APIs and developer tooling are delivered to licensed customers (no public developer portal, no OpenAPI, no public SDK or GitHub org); profiling here captures the surface visible from the marketing site, integrations catalog, and engineering blog.

providers.name: OSlash
providers.description: OSlash is a productivity tool that lets teams create short, memorable shortcuts — typed as "o/" followed by a keyword — to instantly find and open their documents, dashboards, and internal tools across 100+ connected apps such as Salesforce, Notion, Jira, GitHub, Figma, Asana, HubSpot, and Linear. Delivered as a Chrome extension with enterprise features like SSO and bank-level encryption, OSlash was backed by Accel. As of this profile the public product is marked "Coming Soon" and the company publishes no developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or documentation surface — this remains an enrichment lead with no scored API artifacts beyond a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Oyo Rooms
providers.description: OYO Rooms (Oravel Stays / OYO Hotels & Homes) is a hospitality technology company headquartered in Gurugram, India that operates a global chain of franchised and leased budget hotels, homes, and living spaces. Founded by Ritesh Agarwal in 2013, OYO standardizes and distributes independent hotel inventory through its consumer booking apps and website, and provides property owners with a partner management platform for listings, pricing, and operations. OYO is a consumer travel and accommodation brand; as of this enrichment pass it does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Palus Finance
providers.description: Palus Finance is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) financial-advisory startup that acts as a startup's outsourced financial advisor and Registered Investment Advisor (RIA) with a fiduciary duty to its clients. Palus automatically manages a company's reserve cash and treasury, sweeping idle balances into NVCA-compliant bond portfolios built from U.S. government securities and T-Bills to optimize yield (targeting roughly a SOFR + 1% spread) while preserving safety and liquidity. It connects to a company's existing bank accounts (via Plaid) rather than requiring an account switch, sizes allocations against runway and burn rate, and can be set up in under ten minutes with no minimums or lockups. Palus is a managed, human-plus-software advisory product delivered through its web application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Pass It Down
providers.description: Pass It Down is a Chattanooga, Tennessee digital storytelling company that helps museums, libraries, universities, sports organizations, brands, and nonprofits build interactive online exhibits, digital collections, timelines, and cloud-based touchscreen kiosks. Its stated mission is that every organization should be able to build Smithsonian-quality exhibits in minutes for a fraction of the cost. Related properties include Iconic Moments (a cultural-heritage NFT marketplace) and a sports-storytelling offering. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Pass It Down publishes a marketing/product website but no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, packages, or other machine-readable surface.

providers.name: PatientPing
providers.description: PatientPing is a real-time care-coordination network that delivers e-notifications ("Pings") and ADT-based admission, discharge, and transfer alerts across hospitals, post-acute facilities, health plans, pharmacies, and community providers. Its Route solution helps hospitals meet the CMS Interoperability and Patient Access Rule e-notifications Condition of Participation. PatientPing was acquired by Appriss Health in 2021 and rebranded as Bamboo Health; patientping.com now redirects to bamboohealth.com. No public developer portal or API documentation is published — clinical integration is handled privately via HL7/ADT data feeds embedded in provider workflow.

providers.name: PCI Compliance
providers.description: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) is a set of security standards designed to ensure that all companies that accept, process, store or transmit credit card information maintain a secure environment. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture. The PCI Security Standards Council does not currently publish a public REST API.

providers.name: Penn Mutual
providers.description: The Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company is a mutual life insurer founded in 1847 and headquartered in Horsham, Pennsylvania, making it one of the oldest mutual life insurance companies in the United States. Owned by its policyholders, Penn Mutual offers life insurance and annuity products distributed primarily through career and independent financial professionals, and operates through a family of companies including Vantis Life Insurance Company, Hornor Townsend & Kent (HTK) broker-dealer, and the Penn Insurance and Annuity Company (PIA). Penn Mutual divested its long-held wealth management subsidiary, Janney Montgomery Scott, to KKR in 2024.

providers.name: Pilleve
providers.description: Pilleve is a medication-compliance and controlled-substance monitoring company in the digital health space. Its Amethyst System pairs a smart pill-dispensing device that releases one pill at a time and detects tampering with a patient mobile app and a clinician portal for real-time monitoring, adherence tracking, diversion prevention, compliance documentation, and medication disposal. Pilleve serves hospital systems, pain clinics, and pharmacies, and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass Pilleve publishes a marketing website and a clinician login but exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Please Assist Me
providers.description: Please Assist Me (PAM) is an apartment-amenity and home-management service that partners with residential buildings to handle cleaning, errands, groceries, laundry, dry-cleaning, package handling, and custom special requests for residents. Dedicated per-building teams deliver the service, backed by a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) and a web app for booking and account management, a 24-hour satisfaction guarantee, and body-camera transparency. Backed by Techstars. The company operates a consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Powerus
providers.description: PowerUs is Germany's largest job platform for skilled trades and crafts, connecting tradespeople (electricians, plumbers, roofers, metalworkers, mechanics and more) with employers across construction, electrical and mechanical industries. The platform offers automated job matching based on location, salary and working conditions, one-click applications without cover letters, direct employer-to-worker discovery, and native iOS and Android apps. PowerUs reports 250,000+ registered skilled workers and 6,000+ open positions. It is a consumer/employer marketplace product and does not currently expose a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI-described API surface; its api.powerus.de and docs.powerus.de hosts are private/internal (docs gated behind Cloudflare Access). Backed by General Catalyst and HV Capital.

providers.name: Property Capsule
providers.description: Property Capsule (PropertyCapsule) is a retail and commercial real estate marketing automation and prospecting platform for landlords and brokers. It centralizes property, tenant, and availability data in one place and automatically publishes it as flyers, tourbooks, interactive site plans, aerials, demographics, and competition maps across web and iPad leasing apps. Founded around 2014, the company was acquired by VTS in October 2019 and its capabilities were folded into the VTS Market product. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures.

providers.name: QueueDr
providers.description: QueueDr is a healthcare scheduling automation product that automatically fills unexpected appointment cancellations, rebooks no-shows, and balances provider schedules to reduce lost revenue for medical practices and health systems. Originally a 500 Global-backed startup, QueueDr was acquired by Phreesia and is now offered as the Phreesia Appointment Accelerator within Phreesia's patient intake and engagement platform. The queuedr.com domain now redirects to Phreesia; existing customers continue to sign in at the app.queuedr.com dashboard. No independent public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface is published for QueueDr as a standalone product.

providers.name: Quickshipper
providers.description: QuickShipper is a last-mile delivery and fleet management SaaS platform that helps businesses manage order fulfillment and deliveries. It provides route optimization, order batching, automated or manual dispatching, a courier mobile app, real-time tracking, branded customer notifications, and business analytics. Companies can operate their own fleet or connect with third-party courier providers, and can sync orders automatically through API integration and WooCommerce/WordPress plugins. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Raid Base
providers.description: Raid Base Inc. is a Los Angeles-based game development studio, founded in 2020, building an open-world, sandbox PvPvE game in an original IP where players and crews build reputations through farming, trading, building, fighting, and politics. The team draws from Riot Games, Valve, Blizzard, Microsoft, and Bungie, and the studio has raised roughly $34.4M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), BITKRAFT Ventures, Patron, F4 Fund, and Dreamhaven. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Resolyst
providers.description: Resolyst is a specialty-care platform that positions itself as the intelligence layer for AI-enabled specialty care, extending the reach of the world's leading clinicians with continuous, research-first expertise. Rather than episodic consultations, Resolyst provides ongoing multidisciplinary medical oversight for patients with chronic conditions through specialist nurses, pharmacists, dieticians, physiotherapists and psychologists, connecting patients with local and international experts, embedding clinical research into care pathways, and convening condition-specific international expert panels for second opinions and clinical pathway oversight. Backed by Seedcamp, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Resti Inc.
providers.description: Resti Inc. (resti.cloud) is a cloud-based restaurant management platform used by restaurant chains, primarily across Kazakhstan and Central Asia. It automates HR and payroll (salary calculation from actual hours worked), operational checklists and standards with photo verification, review and reputation management aggregating 2GIS and Yandex Maps, a mobile learning management system (LMS) for staff onboarding and training, and AI-assisted invoice processing and reconciliation. Resti integrates with restaurant POS and back-office systems including iiko, r_keeper, Paloma 365, Poster, and 1C Retail, and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this pass it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, or developer documentation; the customer login portal is at my.resti.cloud.

providers.name: reTravel.io
providers.description: reTravel.io is a travel retention marketing platform that uses data science and machine learning to help travel companies, TMCs, and corporates retain customers, increase attachment rates, and grow revenue from their existing clients. Founded in 2020 by Revital Kristal and Nir Gurevich in Tel Aviv, the platform extracts booking information via predefined plugins and contextually engages travelers across multiple channels with personalized, policy-compliant products. It operates on a performance-based commercial model tied to the uplift it generates and is backed by Techstars. reTravel.io exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Savahq
providers.description: Sava (Savahq) is an early-stage Y Combinator company building what it calls the intelligence layer for enduring legacies and the future of trusts, operating at the intersection of financial and legal technology for trust administration and estate management. As of this profile the public presence is a pre-product landing page at savahq.com that collects email signups, and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface. This record tracks Sava within the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead surfaced from the Y Combinator portfolio, to be re-enriched once a developer or API surface is published.

providers.name: Service Max
providers.description: ServiceMax is a cloud-based field service management (FSM) platform that helps asset-centric and equipment-dependent businesses improve technician productivity, streamline service operations, and maximize equipment uptime. Its product suite spans work order management, scheduling and dispatch, mobile field-technician apps, installed-base and asset management, entitlements and contracts, inventory and parts, and service analytics. Founded in 2007 and an early Mayfield portfolio company, ServiceMax was acquired by GE Digital in 2016, sold to Silver Lake in 2018, and acquired by PTC in early 2023, where it is now offered as PTC ServiceMax. This profile tracks the company within the API Evangelist network; its developer and API surface is folded into PTC.

providers.name: Skipthedishes
providers.description: SkipTheDishes is a Canadian online food-delivery marketplace headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, founded in 2012 and acquired by Just Eat (now Just Eat Takeaway.com) in 2016, under which it operates as the group's Canadian brand. It connects diners with local restaurants and a network of independent couriers for on-demand food delivery and pickup across Canadian cities via its consumer website and mobile apps, and runs a restaurant partner onboarding program and a courier (Skip Network) program. As of this enrichment pass SkipTheDishes publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. The primary domain is served behind Cloudflare bot protection and the partner/partners subdomains are static marketing/onboarding pages, so no OpenAPI, webhook, or SDK surface is available to harvest.

providers.name: SpotPay
providers.description: SpotPay is a global neobank that operates as a stablecoin-based global bank account, letting users hold, send, receive, and spend money anywhere in the world from a single identity-verified digital wallet without a traditional bank account. The service settles payments on blockchain rails using stablecoins and pairs the wallet with the SpotPay Calypso debit card plus Apple Pay and Google Pay support, and lets merchants accept QR-code payments with instant settlement. Founded by Zsika Phillip (CEO, ex-Google) and Thomas Cesare-Herriau (CTO, ex-Brex), SpotPay is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company operating across 40+ countries and registered as a Money Services Business with FinCEN in the United States. As of this enrichment pass SpotPay is a consumer mobile-app product with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; api.spotpay.ai serves only the app's private backend.

providers.name: Stone Ridge
providers.description: Stone Ridge (Stone Ridge Asset Management) is an alternative asset manager founded in 2012 that manages approximately $35 billion across "True Alternatives" — investment strategies designed to be uncorrelated with traditional stocks and bonds — including reinsurance, energy, alternative lending, single-family rentals, opportunistic credit, art, LifeX longevity income, and bitcoin. It is the parent of the digital-asset firm NYDIG and is backed by Ribbit Capital. Stone Ridge serves institutional investors, wealth professionals, and insurance companies and operates a private, authenticated investor/client portal (connect.stoneridgeam.com) rather than a public developer API. As of this enrichment pass no public API, SDK, OpenAPI, or developer documentation surface was found for the firm.

providers.name: Syntropy
providers.description: Syntropy is an autonomous, agentic coding application built for complex, long-horizon software engineering tasks. A developer describes a feature in natural language and Syntropy plans, writes, and tests the implementation, returning a production-ready pull request without the developer having to manage a terminal or an IDE agent session by hand. The product emphasizes large-context handling for heavy, real-world codebases ("no context ceiling, no truncation"), supports custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations so it can pull in a team's own tools, and joins Slack to post updates as tasks complete. Syntropy is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in San Francisco, founded by Saahil Sundaresan and Andrew Kuik. As of this profile it ships as a hosted end-user coding product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Tongdun
providers.description: Tongdun (同盾科技 / Tongdun Technology) is a Hangzhou-based intelligent risk-control and anti-fraud analytics company whose public product presence now operates under the 小盾未来 (Xiaodun Future) brand at xiaodun.com. It uses AI and intelligent-analysis techniques to predict and score fraud and credit risk across consumer lending, banking, insurance, and e-commerce, delivering decisioning, anti-fraud, and risk-management capabilities to financial institutions, small-loan and consumer-finance lenders, auto finance, and internet businesses. Its risk-control services are consumed as enterprise interfaces (风控接口) provisioned behind account registration and sales onboarding; there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK registry surface exposed at this time. This record was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and enriched from the company's live public web presence.

providers.name: Tradeway
providers.description: Tradeway is an AI-powered field assistant for residential trade contractors working in electrical, plumbing, and HVAC. Technicians use it to plan jobs step by step with the right materials and code requirements, to identify parts from a photo with nearby supplier pricing and sourcing, and to get hands-free answers to technical questions on the job site. For business owners it centralizes crew history and field activity into a single view, reducing callbacks and rework through built-in code checks and standardized, repeatable processes so new hires can bill like veterans. Tradeway is backed by Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: TripScout
providers.description: TripScout is a travel media and deals company that curates flight and hotel recommendations for consumers and operates a portfolio of large travel-focused social brands (including the @hotel property at athotel.com). Its core product scans millions of flights weekly and emails subscribers a small set of vetted deals, each paired with featured, splurge, and budget hotel options plus destination context such as weather, festivals, and local activities. TripScout runs a free tier (one deal per week) and a premium subscription. It is a consumer-facing, email- and social-first business and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs. Backed by 500 Global; added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Valar Atomics
providers.description: Valar Atomics is a nuclear energy company developing high-temperature gas reactors (HTGR) with TRISO fuel, graphite moderators, and helium coolant, deployed as grid-independent gigasites of many small reactors that power heavy industry - hydrogen production via the sulfur-iodine cycle, AI data center power, industrial process heat, and clean synthetic hydrocarbon fuels via Fischer-Tropsch synthesis with captured CO2. Its Ward 250 test reactor is a partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy, the San Rafael Energy Research Center, and the State of Utah. Founded by Isaiah Taylor and backed by Initialized Capital, the company publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Z-Trip
providers.description: Z-Trip (在途商旅) is a Shanghai-based enterprise travel and expense management SaaS platform (a corporate travel management company, or TMC) serving medium and large Chinese enterprises. It unifies booking of flights, hotels, trains, car rentals, visas, insurance, and MICE events with automated expense reporting, budget and policy controls, monthly invoicing, and up to 45 days of advance funding. The platform integrates with corporate OA, ERP, cost-control, and HR systems and offers single sign-on, aggregating supplier inventory from 200+ airlines and millions of hotels for 1,700+ enterprise clients. Surfaced from the dcm-ventures portfolio; no public first-party API/developer platform is published, though third-party integration connectors and SSO exist.

providers.name: Zapp
providers.description: Zapp is a London-based premium quick-commerce (q-commerce) business that delivers daily essentials such as snacks, drinks, groceries, household items and pharmacy needs across central London in minutes, 24/7. Founded in 2020 by Navid Hadzaad and Joe Falter, the company operates a network of micro-fulfilment "dark stores" and a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) rather than a public developer platform. Zapp is a venture-backed company whose investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this profile, Zapp exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; it is a business-to-consumer delivery brand surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Zefr
providers.description: Zefr is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of felicis, ivp, uncork-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: adtech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Abogen
providers.description: Abogen Biosciences (Suzhou Abogen Biosciences Co., Ltd. / 苏州艾博生物科技有限公司) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in January 2019 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, dedicated to developing transformative medicines through messenger RNA (mRNA) innovation. The company has built full-scale in-house capabilities spanning the entire mRNA drug development cycle - protein engineering, mRNA sequence design and synthesis, proprietary lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery, formulation, and commercial-scale manufacturing. Its product pipeline covers infectious disease prevention and cancer immunotherapy, and it has advanced an EUA mRNA product along with additional clinical-stage candidates. Abogen is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. Abogen is a pharmaceutical / biotechnology company and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile captures its corporate identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Acalvio
providers.description: Acalvio Technologies is a cybersecurity company specializing in cyber deception technology for preemptive defense. Its platform detects, disrupts, and defeats advanced threats, ransomware, and identity-based attacks by deploying autonomous, AI-driven deception across enterprise, cloud, and government environments. Acalvio integrates with existing security infrastructure such as CrowdStrike Falcon Identity Protection, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, and other SIEM/SOAR solutions, and partners with AWS, Microsoft, and Google Cloud. Acalvio does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its public web and security posture.

providers.name: Ajeer
providers.description: Ajeer (iajeer.com) is a Saudi Arabian on-demand services platform for home and facility maintenance and operations (خدمات الصيانة والتشغيل). Through its mobile application customers request residential maintenance, general labor, installation, plumbing, electrical, and air-conditioning services, connecting them with vetted service providers. Ajeer is a portfolio company of 500 Global, surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a company profile. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public web surface and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Alpine Bio
providers.description: Alpine Bio is a molecular-farming biotechnology company (formerly Nobell Foods and Alpine Roads), founded in 2016 and based in South San Francisco, California. It produces next-generation protein ingredients and bioactives from plants using advanced purification and molecular farming, having expressed more than 15 complex proteins including the world's first plant-derived casein, fractionated soy protein isolates, and activated iron-loaded lactoferrin. The company sells high-purity, clean-label ingredients to food and beverage formulators for applications such as protein shakes, bars, coffee creamers, iron supplements, yogurt, and clear protein sodas, and markets animal-free dairy products under the Nobell Foods brand. It is a portfolio company of a16z surfaced in the API Evangelist network; Alpine Bio publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Angie’s List
providers.description: Angie’s List is a consumer marketplace for finding, reviewing, and hiring local home-service professionals — plumbers, electricians, roofers, landscapers, house cleaners, and hundreds of other trades. Founded in 1995 by Angie Hicks and William Oesterle, it pioneered member-submitted, verified reviews and letter-grade ratings of service providers across U.S. metro markets. In 2017 Angie’s List merged with HomeAdvisor to form ANGI Homeservices (now Angi Inc., NASDAQ: ANGI, part of IAC), and in 2021 the consumer brand and website were rebranded from angieslist.com to angi.com. Angi is a consumer/pro home-services platform and does not currently publish a public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web and security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

providers.name: ApnaMart
providers.description: ApnaMart (Apna Mart) is a Bengaluru-based Indian retail and quick-commerce company founded in 2022 by Chetan Kumar Garg and Abhishek Singh. It operates a network of franchise-model neighborhood grocery and FMCG stores combined with a 15-minute delivery app, serving customers across roughly 14 cities including tier-2 and tier-3 markets such as Ranchi, Hazaribagh, and Bilaspur. Backed by Accel, Peak XV, and Fundamentum, the company blends brick-and-mortar retail with on-demand delivery of daily essentials. ApnaMart is a consumer retail business and does not publish a public developer platform or API surface; this profile in the API Evangelist network captures its identity, domain-security posture, and published web properties.

providers.name: Atlas
providers.description: Atlas is an AI implementation partner built for independent accounting firms, deploying supervised, firm-specific AI "junior accountants" that automate repetitive, data-intensive workflows such as client onboarding, follow-ups, bookkeeping, compliance, and financial reporting while keeping human accountants in control of every decision and client relationship. Founded by Arpit Maheshwari (CEO) and Jagmal Singh (CTO) and co-led by Accel and Stellaris with Felicis participation, Atlas raised a $6M seed round in 2026 to scale its network of partner firms across North America. Atlas is currently a services-led AI company and publishes no public API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Bassetts Ice Cream
providers.description: Bassetts Ice Cream is a Philadelphia ice cream brand founded in 1861 and self-described as "America's oldest ice cream brand." The company is family-owned across six generations of the Bassett / Strange family, retails out of a single counter at Reading Terminal Market in Center City Philadelphia, and operates a wholesale frozen-dessert distribution business serving restaurants, hotels, country clubs, dipping parlors, supermarkets, and caterers within a 40-mile radius of Philadelphia (with distributor partners in the New York metro and Florida). Bassetts also exports to China (since 2008), South Korea (2017), and Taiwan (2020), and ships pints nationwide via Goldbelly. The corporate office is at 1211 Chestnut Street, Suite 410, Philadelphia, PA. The bassettsicecream.com website is hosted on Wix and exposes no public API, no developer portal, and no machine-readable product catalog.

providers.name: Best Food Trucks
providers.description: Best Food Trucks (BFT) operates a food truck booking, scheduling, and mobile ordering platform that connects food truck vendors with property managers, office buildings, event organizers, and hungry customers. The platform lets locations schedule rotating food trucks, lets customers browse menus and place mobile orders ahead of time, and gives trucks a point-of-sale and payments surface for on-site service. Backed by Techstars, the company was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched into the API Evangelist network. This profile currently carries only public infrastructure and security artifacts; no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface was discoverable during enrichment.

providers.name: Big O Notation
providers.description: Big O Notation is a mathematical notation used in computer science to describe the performance or complexity of algorithms, providing a way to classify algorithms by how their runtime or space requirements grow as input size grows. It is foundational to algorithm design, API performance benchmarking, and software engineering education.

providers.name: Bilibili
providers.description: Bilibili (bilibili.com) is a leading Chinese online video-sharing and content community platform centered on anime, comics, and games (ACG), alongside a broad range of user-generated and professionally produced video, live streaming, and community content. Through its open platform (openhome.bilibili.com) Bilibili offers third-party developers authorized account login, open APIs, and content, data, and industry-solution capabilities, with a developer onboarding path for service providers and third-party integrators. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming; sector: media-entertainment.

providers.name: Binary Format
providers.description: Binary format refers to data encoding and serialization methods that use binary rather than text representations, including formats like Protocol Buffers, MessagePack, Avro, Thrift, CBOR, and others used in APIs and data storage systems for efficiency. Binary formats offer significant advantages over text-based formats in terms of size, parsing speed, and type safety.

providers.name: Birdstop
providers.description: Birdstop is an American autonomous-drone and remote-sensing company that lets organizations monitor and inspect field assets at scale without personnel onsite. Its Fealty system is an all-weather, always-on drone that launches in under three seconds, flies for up to 45 minutes, cruises at 45 mph, and patrols 24/7 across public safety, utilities, transportation, construction, and data-center sites. Birdstop pairs networked UAVs and ground stations with computer vision and a patented optical/acoustic detect-and-avoid system to enable safe beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight under some of the FAA's most advanced approvals, delivering Observation-on-Demand intel over the internet. The company is FAA-authorized, SOC 2 certified, and NDAA compliant, and builds its drones in Detroit. Backed by Techstars, Birdstop currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Blue River Technology
providers.description: Blue River Technology is an agricultural robotics and machine-learning company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and a wholly owned subsidiary of John Deere (Deere & Company), which acquired it in 2017. Founded in 2011 by Jorge Heraud and Lee Redden out of Stanford University, the company builds intelligent machinery that combines computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and full-stack software to make farming more precise and sustainable. Its flagship product, See & Spray, uses onboard cameras and deep-learning models to distinguish crops from weeds in real time and target herbicide only where it is needed, dramatically reducing chemical use. Blue River operates as John Deere's autonomy and computer-vision engineering hub, applying the same perception and edge-AI stack across agriculture, construction, and mining equipment. The company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its technology ships embedded in John Deere machinery and is surfaced to growers through John Deere Operations Center rather than a standalone developer program.

providers.name: Brimstone
providers.description: Brimstone is a materials technology company decarbonizing heavy industry through a single-rock co-production process it calls the Rock Refinery. From ordinary calcium silicate rock it extracts multiple high-value materials at once - carbon-negative Portland cement and supplementary cementitious materials, alumina and aluminum, magnesium, titanium, iron/steel feedstock and critical minerals - aiming to use 100% of the feed rock and eliminate tailings while cutting process emissions. The company uses commercially available equipment for a low-cost, market-ready approach, and has secured commitments including Amazon as a buyer of low-carbon cement from its first commercial plant. Brimstone is a private heavy-industry / climate-tech company backed by DCVC and Fifth Wall; it operates no public developer API.

providers.name: Bsquare
providers.description: Bsquare is an IoT and edge-software company known for Windows IoT device licensing, OS consulting (Windows, Linux, Android), device management, and its DataV IoT analytics and SquareOne data platform. Bsquare was acquired by Kontron; the bsquare.com domain now 301-redirects to www.kontron-americas.com, and the Bsquare brand operates as part of Kontron's connected-device software portfolio serving healthcare, avionics, energy, manufacturing, logistics, transportation, and hospitality. No independent public developer API or documentation surface is currently published; this profile carries the honest enrichment of the domain's live security and DNS posture.

providers.name: Buena
providers.description: Buena (Buena GmbH) is a Berlin-based modern property management company serving real estate owners across Germany, managing over 70,000 units. It provides WEG (condominium / Wohnungseigentümergemeinschaft) management, rental property management (Mietverwaltung), and property-management succession (Nachfolge) for owners seeking an alternative to conventional, reactive administrators. Buena positions itself as a technology-forward, proactive Hausverwaltung. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of EQT Ventures and GV and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Buena publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation — this profile captures verified company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Buildots
providers.description: Buildots is an AI-powered construction intelligence platform headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, with offices in London and the United States. The company combines 360-degree hardhat-mounted cameras with computer vision and machine learning models that automatically capture, locate, and classify on-site construction progress against the project BIM model and schedule, producing trade-level performance data, deviation and delay detection, and portfolio-wide analytics for general contractors, project teams, executives, and owners. Buildots reports that projects using the platform together with a performance-driven operating approach have reduced delays by up to 50%. The product family includes Buildots (the AI construction intelligence platform), Genda (workforce intelligence), and a fully managed Capture Services operation that handles routine site capture for customers. Verticals served include data centers, commercial, multifamily, healthcare, industrial, education, and airports. Notable customers shown on the website include Intel, Mortenson, JE Dunn, Turner, Wates, and STO. Buildots was founded in 2018 and is led by CEO and co-founder Roy Danon with co-founders Aviv Leibovici (CPO) and Yakir Sudry (CCO). Investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Future Energy Ventures, Viola Ventures, TLV Partners, OG Ventures, and Tencent. Buildots does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integrations with construction software (e.g., Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud) are arranged directly through the company.

providers.name: Cambium
providers.description: Cambium is an advanced materials company (Cambium Biomaterials, El Segundo, California, founded 2019) that molecularly re-engineers polymers from first principles, pairing AI-driven molecular design with chemistry, materials science, biology, and agile domestic manufacturing to develop and scale next-generation materials roughly 10x faster than traditional methods. Product lines span thermal protection systems, high-temperature structural polymers, and laser/directed-energy protection, serving aerospace, space, defense, motorsport, automotive, marine, and industrial customers. Its SHD Advanced Composites business runs rapid-response prepreg manufacturing across the US, UK, and EU. Backed by 8VC. Cambium publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures corporate identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: Center for Parent Information and Resources
providers.description: The Center for Parent Information and Resources (CPIR) is a federally funded central hub of information and products for the national network of Parent Training and Information Centers (PTIs) and Community Parent Resource Centers (CPRCs). CPIR supports families and youth, with a focus on children and youth with disabilities, delivering resources via the Parent Center Hub website, the Buzz from the Hub newsletter, and an events calendar. No public developer API has been identified; content and updates are delivered through website browsing, newsletter subscription, and an embedded Google Calendar.

providers.name: Cliffs Natural Resources
providers.description: Cliffs Natural Resources is the legacy corporate name for what is now Cleveland-Cliffs Inc., a major mining and natural resources company that produces iron ore pellets primarily for steelmaking customers in North America. The company was renamed Cleveland-Cliffs in 2017 and the canonical profile lives at the cleveland-cliffs repo. Cliffs Natural Resources / Cleveland-Cliffs does not publish a public developer portal or general-purpose REST API surface.

providers.name: Cofia
providers.description: Cofia is an AI automation platform that learns how a team actually works and automatically builds custom workflow automations without manual setup. By monitoring system events and recognizing repetitive patterns, Cofia proposes and assembles custom agents for tasks like prospect list building, outreach and follow-ups, recruiting pipeline management, and data report creation. The company markets itself as "AI automations that implement themselves." Cofia is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in New York City, founded by Moses Wayne (formerly Engineering Director at Duolingo) and Paola Martinez (formerly Senior Product Manager at Brilliant.org). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with what the company publishes publicly. As of this pass Cofia exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
providers.description: Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) is a commercial fusion energy company headquartered in Devens, Massachusetts and spun out of the MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center in 2018. CFS is developing tokamak-based fusion systems built around high-temperature superconducting (HTS) REBCO magnet technology that enables substantially smaller, faster, and lower-cost fusion machines than prior generations. The company's technology pipeline starts with SPARC, a net-energy demonstration tokamak under construction at the Devens campus, and continues with ARC, the planned first commercial fusion power plant, sited in Chesterfield County, Virginia in partnership with Dominion Energy and targeted to deliver approximately 400 MW of electricity to the grid in the early 2030s. CFS is backed by a deep investor base including Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Eni, Equinor, Google, Temasek, Tiger Global, Khosla Ventures, Bill Gates, Soros Fund Management, Lowercase Capital, John Doerr, and TIME Ventures. CFS does not publish a public developer API or SDK; engagement is via partnerships, careers, and investor channels.

providers.name: Cornerstone Building Brands
providers.description: Cornerstone Building Brands is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cornerstone Building Brands API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Crete Professionals Alliance
providers.description: Crete Professionals Alliance (rebranded in 2025 as "Current", current.co) is a growth platform for independent accounting firms, backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. The alliance provides member firms with technology, talent, capital, and strategy to compete at enterprise scale, spanning 48 partner firms across 39 states and 3 countries with more than 2,000 employees. Service lines include accounting, advisory, audit and attest, client accounting services, and tax. This is a professional services / accounting company, not a developer-facing API provider: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDKs, or technical documentation. The record is maintained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph coverage of Bessemer holdings.

providers.name: dehaze
providers.description: dehaze is a Munich-area (Fürstenfeldbruck, Germany) healthtech company, part of the Techstars Berlin cohort, building proprietary causal AI infrastructure that detects chronic and autoimmune disease earlier by identifying overlooked diagnoses, health risks, and inappropriate treatments. Its platform unifies and harmonizes diverse health data (lab results, medical imaging, genomics, clinical notes) into doctor-validated patient journeys, risk-profiles individuals against millions of health journeys and medical guidelines, and runs targeted AI follow-ups to improve treatment adherence for patients, payers, and providers. dehaze has analyzed over 250,000 patient lives across 300 million health events and 200+ AI algorithms, and raised €3.2M in 2026. dehaze publishes no first-party developer API; it exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint and an llms.txt for agentic AI access to public site content.

providers.name: DFDL
providers.description: Data Format Description Language (DFDL) is an open standard for describing data formats used in binary and text files and data streams. DFDL is used to describe the format of existing data so that it can be parsed or unparsed (generated) using a DFDL processor, enabling integration with legacy and modern data systems. DFDL was developed by the Open Grid Forum (OGF) and is also published as ISO/IEC 23415:2004. Apache Daffodil is the reference open-source implementation, with the latest release being version 4.1.0.

providers.name: Distance
providers.description: Distance (Distance Technologies) is a Helsinki-based frontier-tech company pioneering glasses-free extended reality (XR) built on computational optics and lightfield technology. Its systems turn transparent surfaces — vehicle windshields, aircraft canopies, and head-mounted visors — into intelligent heads-up displays without screens, overlays, or wearable glasses. Products include the Acuity visual-intelligence platform and Acuity OS for defense, the Field Operator HUD (FOH) head-mounted system in field trials across NATO countries, and panoramic lightfield HUDs for automotive ADAS and navigation. Distance is backed by GV (Google Ventures) and partners with defense, aerospace, and automotive organizations including Kia, Supacat, Galvion, Patria, and General Dynamics. The company publishes no public API or developer program; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DOT Regulations
providers.description: Department of Transportation regulations governing the safe transportation of hazardous materials and other commercial transport activities in the United States. These regulations help organizations meet regulatory requirements and demonstrate accountability to stakeholders.

providers.name: ElasticRun
providers.description: ElasticRun (legally NTEx Transportation Services Pvt Ltd) is a Pune, India based B2B e-commerce and rural logistics platform founded in 2016 by Sandeep Deshmukh, Saurabh Nigam and Shitiz Bansal. It operates an aggregated, variable-capacity transportation network that stitches together idle logistics capacity to connect FMCG brands and manufacturers to the mom-and-pop kirana stores of rural and semi-urban India. The platform blends mobile technology with local entrepreneurs to run an assisted-commerce model spanning 125,000+ kiranas and 80,000+ villages across 26 states, offering last-mile delivery, B2B distribution and supply-chain services. ElasticRun is backed by Prosus Ventures and SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile is a network stub: no public developer API, documentation or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Elsewhere
providers.description: Elsewhere (Elsewhere Communities Inc.) is a San Francisco based video game studio founded in 2024 by Paul Sawaya, previously co-founder and CTO of Human Interest. The studio was part of cohort 001 of a16z SPEEDRUN, the Andreessen Horowitz accelerator for games and interactive media. Elsewhere describes itself as "a new kind of video game studio emboldened by the desire to rethink the industry", treating artificial intelligence as a normal technology and building games that use generative AI in a humanistic direction rather than a dystopian one. The studio previously worked on a multiplayer roguelike — games "that feel like an adventure you go on with your friends, and the adventure is never the same twice" — and is currently building something new. Elsewhere is a consumer game studio with no public developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no API, no developer portal, no SDKs, and no machine-readable discovery documents.

providers.name: EVERSTEEL
providers.description: EVERSTEEL is a University of Tokyo-originated startup building AI image-recognition systems that automate the inspection and grading of steel (iron) scrap for steelmakers. Its flagship product, Tetsu-Navi Inspection AI (鉄ナビ検収AI), uses high-resolution cameras and computer-vision models to grade incoming scrap, detect impurities and hazardous materials, and standardize what was previously a manual, expert-dependent process — advancing steel recycling and reducing CO2 emissions from steel production. The company works with major Japanese steel producers including JFE Steel and Kyoei Steel, and is backed by DCM Ventures, Mitsui & Co., Coreline, and the University of Tokyo.

providers.name: First Day Entertainment
providers.description: First Day Entertainment Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California game studio building AI-powered games, founded by Stephen Gou (formerly a founding engineer at Cohere) and Mike Mei, and funded by the a16z SPEEDRUN accelerator (batch 002) and MiraclePlus. The studio ships two titles - Heroes of Magic & Cards, a poker deckbuilding roguelike distributed on Steam, and Mana Land, a single-player RPG in which players adventure alongside conversational AI companions, published on itch.io. First Day Entertainment is a consumer games company; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Flexion
providers.description: Flexion Robotics builds the autonomy stack for humanoid robots — from command to control, from manipulation to locomotion, across any hardware and task. Founded by former NVIDIA and ETH Zurich reinforcement-learning researchers (Nikita Rudin, David Höller, Julian Nubert), the Zurich- and San Francisco-based company uses large-scale simulation and reinforcement learning to train generalizable robot policies that transfer to real-world hardware. Its Flexion Reflect model line targets long-horizon autonomous humanoid work. The company raised $50M and is backed by Prosus Ventures. Flexion does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Formo
providers.description: Formo (Formo Foods GmbH) is a Berlin-based food-technology company producing animal-free dairy through precision fermentation and microbial fermentation of koji (Aspergillus oryzae). Instead of cows, Formo engineers microorganisms to make milk proteins such as casein, which it turns into real cheese and cream cheese products now sold across Germany and Austria. Founded by Raffael Wohlgensinger and backed by EQT Ventures, the company has received a US FDA "no questions" GRAS letter for its fermentation-derived casein. Formo is a consumer food producer and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Gardens
providers.description: Gardens (Gardens Interactive) is a distributed, remote-first video game studio founded in 2021 by veterans of Journey, What Remains of Edith Finch, Sky: Children of the Light, Blaseball, Dustforce, Guild Wars 2, and Firewatch. The studio builds lush, living worlds that bring players together to cultivate lasting friendships, and is developing an upcoming shared fantasy adventure — an ever-evolving online multiplayer sandbox set in a shapeshifting, unpredictable wilderness filled with mystery and magic, designed around meaningful moments shared between strangers. Co-founded by Chris Bell, Lexie Dostal, and Stephen Bell and based primarily out of Portland and Los Angeles, Gardens raised a $31.3M Series A co-led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. As a game studio, Gardens publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GitOps
providers.description: A operational framework that takes DevOps best practices used for application development such as version control, collaboration, compliance, and CI/CD, and applies them to infrastructure automation. GitOps uses Git as a single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications.

providers.name: Grassroots Unwired
providers.description: Grassroots Unwired is a mobile-first platform for face-to-face (F2F) outreach, advocacy, and fundraising, purpose-built for political campaigns, nonprofits, labor unions, and community organizations. Its offline-capable mobile apps let field teams run GPS-enabled door-to-door canvassing, capture in-person and peer-to-peer donations, send SMS and digital content from the field, and manage event check-in, registration, and merchandise operations for 4EventDay. The platform keeps collecting data, donations, and check-ins even when Wi-Fi and cell coverage are spotty, then syncs in real time with major CRM, donor, and payment systems (EveryAction, NGP VAN, Blackbaud Luminate, NeonCRM, Stripe, and others).

providers.name: GuildFi
providers.description: GuildFi was a Web3 gaming platform and guild that aggregated blockchain games, quests, achievements, and rewards into a single account layer, letting players discover games and earn across the play-to-earn ecosystem (native token GF). It was backed by Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Animoca Brands, and other crypto investors. In 2024 GuildFi rebranded and consolidated into Zentry (zentry.com), a self-described "Human-Agentic OS" spanning gaming (Radiant), a data layer (zData), an agent layer (zAI), and the ZENT token. The original guildfi.com domain is now defunct (expired TLS certificate, 404s) and GuildFi/Zentry publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or agent surface as of this enrichment pass. This record is a portfolio-lead stub retained for lineage; see x-successor for the live entity.

providers.name: Habitus Associates Co., Ltd.
providers.description: Habitus Associates Co., Ltd. is the company behind Artue (artue.io), an AI-powered online marketplace for original artworks by Korean and international artists. Artue lets collectors discover, purchase, and resell paintings, photography, sculptures, and prints, with natural-language search that finds works by mood, color, style, room type, or budget. The platform is explicitly agent-native: it publishes an llms.txt and ships a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT can search its collection directly. Backed by 500 Global and surfaced into the API Evangelist network from that portfolio.

providers.name: Habyt
providers.description: Habyt is a flexible-living and co-living accommodation provider offering furnished studios, apartments, and private rooms for stays ranging from a single night to several months. Positioned as "a new category of living for people in motion," the company blends hotel-style service and amenities with residential flexibility, targeting mobile professionals, relocators, and long-term travelers. Habyt operates properties across Europe (Berlin, Madrid, Vienna, with Lisbon and Milan announced) and Asia (multiple locations in Singapore), and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital. Habyt is a consumer real-estate and hospitality operator rather than an API-first technology provider; as of this enrichment pass no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Hertha Metals
providers.description: Hertha Metals is a hard-technology steel production company based in Conroe, Texas, working to decarbonize and modernize primary steelmaking after centuries of coke-based blast-furnace iron and steel production. Founded by Laureen Meroueh, the company has developed proprietary pyrometallurgical HERS and Flex-HERS technology that produces steel from flexible feedstocks in a single reactor, and has raised roughly $17M toward a commercial steel plant. Hertha Metals is an industrial / climate-tech manufacturer with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company profile.

providers.name: High Alpha Capital
providers.description: High Alpha is an Indianapolis-based venture firm that creates and funds B2B SaaS and enterprise software companies, partnering with founders through both a venture studio that co-creates companies from scratch and a capital arm that invests in early-stage enterprise software startups. Its focus spans healthcare, sales enablement, supply chain, agtech, and other B2B verticals, and its portfolio and alumni include companies such as Salesloft, Attentive, Lessonly, Stitch, Tenon, and Liminal. High Alpha also publishes the widely referenced SaaS Benchmarks Report.
