No public developer API, portal, or documentation surface is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and its verified domain-security posture.

providers.name: Commission of Fine Arts
providers.description: The U.S. Commission of Fine Arts (CFA) is an independent federal agency established in 1910 that has review authority over the design and aesthetics of construction within Washington, D.C., and over coins, medals, and Federal commemorative works. The CFA also appoints the Old Georgetown Board which conducts design review for projects in the Georgetown Historic District. As of April 2026 the CFA does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specifications, or a developer program. Project records are accessible through the CFA's web-based Project Search tool and via the records-and-research process documented at cfa.gov.

providers.name: Core-Mark Holding
providers.description: Core-Mark Holding Company, a subsidiary of Performance Food Group, is one of the largest broad-line, full-service marketers and distributors of packaged consumer products to the convenience retail industry in North America. The company serves more than 41,000 retail locations across the United States and Canada, supplying tobacco, candy, snacks, beverages, foodservice, and other fast-moving consumer goods. Core-Mark provides retailer technology platforms including Core-Source Portal, Retailer Analytics, Core-Mark Ordering, and Core-Mark Intellisite.

providers.name: Coronavirus in the UK
providers.description: UK Government coronavirus data, including deaths and cases by region

providers.name: Costco Wholesale
providers.description: Costco Wholesale Corporation is a Fortune 500 American multinational membership-only big-box retail chain that operates warehouse clubs offering a wide selection of merchandise at discounted prices. Costco does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading partner integrations are conducted through EDI and B2B channels using ANSI X12 transactions and the Costco Supplier Portal. Costco operates an e-commerce site, the Costco Travel and Costco Pharmacy properties, and the Costco Photo Center.

providers.name: Covid-19 Datenhub
providers.description: Maps, datasets, applications and more in the context of COVID-19

providers.name: CRED
providers.description: CRED is an Indian consumer fintech that started with premium credit-card bill payments and rewards and has expanded into peer-to-peer payments (Scan & Pay, Tap to Pay, RuPay credit card on UPI), short-term credit (CRED Cash, CRED Mint), wealth (CRED Money), e-commerce (CRED Store), and travel. CRED's surface area is overwhelmingly consumer-app and the company does not publish a public, self-service developer portal. Its engineering organisation contributes to the broader ecosystem via the engineering.cred.club tech blog and open-source repositories under the CRED-CLUB GitHub org. B2B integrations (merchant acceptance, issuer partnerships, etc.) are negotiated directly with the partnerships team.

providers.name: Dabee
providers.description: Dabee (dabee.com.br) is a Brazilian consumer-technology review and comparison website that helps shoppers make informed purchasing decisions about electronics and gadgets. It publishes hands-on reviews, side-by-side comparisons, and buying guides across notebooks, smartphones, tablets, monitors, smartwatches, gaming consoles, smart TVs, and networking equipment, with 'vale a pena' (is-it-worth-it) verdicts and price tracking pulled from Amazon Brazil. The site monetizes through affiliate commissions. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; it was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Dayjob
providers.description: Dayjob is an AI-powered scheduling agent built for waste management and skip hire fleets, operated by Gaea Technology Ltd and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026). Its autonomous agents analyze millions of potential route combinations to build optimized daily schedules that factor in travel times, skip sizes, driver availability and priority job assignments, then continuously re-optimize in real time as new jobs, driver changes and exceptions arrive. Dayjob integrates with existing ERP and telematics systems (Weighsoft, PurGo, Wastelogics, plus custom report setups) and claims customers see revenue and efficiency gains, tighter time-window hit rates and materially less planning admin. It is a vertical logistics application rather than an API platform - no public developer portal, API reference or SDKs are published at this time. This profile has been enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Drill Creative
providers.description: Drill Creative, Inc. is a US-based video game development startup founded in 2023 in Cary, North Carolina, and backed by a16z's Speedrun accelerator. The studio builds original, high-quality gameplay experiences for user-generated content (UGC) platforms, the coin-op / family-entertainment-center (FEC) market, and PC and console storefronts. Its early releases are built on Fortnite via Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN), including "Elimination Confirmed," a 16-player competitive first-person shooter, and "Robo Bash," an arcade-style four-player fighting game. Drill Creative is a games company rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or technical documentation, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: Dux
providers.description: Dux is a cybersecurity company building an Agentic Exposure Management platform that uses AI agents to identify which vulnerabilities are truly exploitable, recommend lightweight mitigations, and accelerate patch and remediation work across an organization's attack surface. The company raised a $9M seed round led by Redpoint and TLV Partners in December 2025. It was surfaced as a Redpoint Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Dux publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: EasyWay Technologies
providers.description: EasyWay Technologies (easyway.ai) builds generative-AI guest-experience agents for the hospitality industry, used by 400+ hotels including Banyan Tree, InterContinental, Fairmont and Sofitel. Its AI Concierge, AI Reservation Manager and AI Receptionist automate guest messaging, bookings and check-in/check-out with 24/7 replies across 100+ languages, integrating with existing hotel systems. A Techstars-backed startup, EasyWay has been acquired by Duve and now operates as part of Duve's guest-experience platform. EasyWay exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record.

providers.name: Eigen
providers.description: Eigen Technologies is a London-based intelligent document processing (IDP) and data-extraction company that uses natural language processing, object detection and machine learning to extract, classify and interpret structured data from unstructured documents at scale. Its no-code platform lets teams in financial services, insurance, law and professional services pull hundreds of datapoints out of contracts, loan agreements and filings to manage risk, automate processes and meet regulatory obligations, with extracted data pushed downstream via its document-processing API. Founded in 2014 and backed by Goldman Sachs, Temasek, Lakestar, Dawn Capital, ING Ventures, Anthemis and the Sony Innovation Fund, Eigen was acquired by contract-lifecycle-management platform Sirion in June 2024.

providers.name: ElMetr
providers.description: ElMetr (المتر) is a Middle East legal-tech company providing online legal consultation and guidance for companies, entrepreneurs, and individuals. The platform combines licensed lawyers with modern technology to connect users with qualified legal help, offering subscription legal packages that cover company formation and registration, contract review, compliance, intellectual property, and dispute resolution. Founded in Egypt and now operating in Saudi Arabia, ElMetr aims to make legal work clear, fast, and fair so businesses can move faster and reduce risk from first idea through expansion. ElMetr is a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. This company profile has been through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; ElMetr does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Epic! Creations
providers.description: Epic! Creations, Inc. operates Epic, an award-winning digital reading and learning platform for children twelve and under. The service gives families and educators unlimited access to a library of more than 40,000 books, audiobooks, and learning videos, with reading-level personalization, quizzes, and progress tracking. Epic offers a consumer family subscription and Epic School, a version that is free for teachers and students during the school day via class codes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Epic is a business-to-consumer application and does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Espressive
providers.description: Espressive is an enterprise conversational-AI company whose flagship product, Barista, is a GenAI-based virtual support agent that automates the resolution of employee questions, issues, and requests across IT service management (ITSM), HR, and other internal help desks. Barista connects natural-language employee requests to automation by integrating with any REST-API-enabled third-party system (ServiceNow, Jira, Slack, Teams, Okta, Workday, Microsoft 365) via its Integration Designer and Barista Integration Marketplace, and reports employee adoption rates of 80-85% with 50-70% reductions in help-desk call volume. Espressive was acquired by Resolve (resolve.io) in September 2025 and folded into Resolve's agentic automation and orchestration platform; the standalone www.espressive.com surface now redirects to resolve.io. Espressive exposes no public developer API of its own -- Barista is a consumer of customer REST APIs, and product/developer documentation sits behind the Espressive support portal.

providers.name: Excite Japan Co., Ltd. (JASDAQ:3754)
providers.description: Excite Japan Co., Ltd. (エキサイト株式会社), listed on JASDAQ as ticker 3754, is a Tokyo-based internet media and services company founded in August 1997 and headquartered in the Azabudai Hills Mori JP Tower in Minato, Tokyo. It operates the long-running excite.co.jp web portal — offering web, image, and news search, the Excite Blog (exblog.jp) blogging platform, translation and dictionary tools, fortune-telling, recipe, and lifestyle content — alongside the BB.excite broadband/ISP business. Under parent Excite Holdings Co., Ltd., the group organizes its operations into four segments: Platform, Broadband, Medical, and SaaS/DX (including the FanGrowth customer-growth platform). The company does not currently publish a public developer API program or portal; this profile tracks its corporate and web presence within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Exide Technologies
providers.description: Exide Technologies is a global producer and recycler of lead-acid batteries used in transportation and industrial applications, serving automotive, motive power, network power, and other markets. Headquartered in Milton, Georgia, the company operates manufacturing and recycling facilities worldwide. No public developer APIs have been identified; ordering and product data are provided through B2B portals and distributor channels.

providers.name: Exxon Mobil
providers.description: Exxon Mobil Corporation is one of the world's largest publicly traded international energy companies, exploring for, producing, and refining oil and natural gas and manufacturing petroleum and chemical products. This repository tracks any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with Exxon Mobil.

providers.name: Foodology
providers.description: Foodology is a Bogota-based food-tech company building what it calls the largest group of delivery-focused virtual restaurant brands in Latin America. Founded in 2019 by Daniela Izquierdo and Juan Guillermo Azuero, it operates a cloud-kitchen (ghost kitchen) model, creating restaurant brands from scratch and running them out of shared commissaries and kitchens so multiple brands share real estate, ingredients, and staff. Marquee brands include Brunch & Munch (the #1 breakfast delivery brand in Colombia) and Avocalia (a leading salad brand). Foodology runs more than 85 cloud kitchens across Colombia, Mexico, Brazil, and Peru and reports over 300,000 delivered orders per month. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Base10/Base Partners, Wollef, Kayyak, Chimera, and artist Maluma, having raised a $15M Series A and a later $50M round. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; Foodology is a consumer food-delivery operator and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Fractal
providers.description: Fractal Software (fractalsoftware.com) is a venture studio that partners with entrepreneurs and investors to launch AI-driven vertical SaaS companies that transform how whole industries operate. Rather than shipping a single product, Fractal functions as an incubator and holding company, standing up sector-specific software startups across produce, healthcare, government, storage, distribution, and security-services verticals, with more than $650M raised across its portfolio. As a venture studio it exposes no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or documentation of its own; this profile captures its identity, portfolio surface, and domain-security posture. Note the recorded x-backed-by (multicoin, paradigm, a16z, 8vc) was surfaced via name-matching during portfolio ingestion and may conflate a distinct crypto-era "Fractal"; the enriched identity below reflects the fractalsoftware.com venture studio.

providers.name: Gbatteries
providers.description: GBatteries (GBatteries Energy Canada Inc.) is an Ottawa, Ontario battery technology company developing lithium-metal battery cells and an intelligent, adaptive battery management system for the next generation of electric mobility, from land to air. Its technology targets fast charging (sub-15-minute charge), high energy density (450+ Wh/kg), extended cycle life, and enhanced safety by actively reducing irreversible internal cell damage. The company reports 60+ granted or pending patents and 9+ years of R&D, and was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company. GBatteries is a hardware and battery-management deeptech firm; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Genesis Digital Assets
providers.description: Genesis Digital Assets (GDA) is a global digital infrastructure company that designs, builds, and operates industrial-scale data centers for high-performance computing workloads, including Bitcoin networks and AI operations. GDA runs mining and computing facilities across multiple countries and does not sell products or services to the public. Surfaced as a portfolio company of electric-capital, paradigm, and ribbit-capital in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, portal, or SDK is published as of this pass.

providers.name: GlamSt
providers.description: GlamSt (GlamST LLC) builds customized virtual makeover and try-on solutions for beauty brands and retailers, combining augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence, and machine learning to power virtual makeup and cosmetics try-on across mobile, web, and in-store experiences. Founded with offices in San Francisco, Montevideo (Uruguay), and Wilmington (Delaware), the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. GlamSt was acquired by Ulta Beauty in 2018 and integrated into Ulta's digital innovation team; it exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Hangry
providers.description: Hangry is an Indonesian multi-brand virtual restaurant and cloud-kitchen company founded in 2019 and backed by 500 Global. It designs, operates, and delivers a portfolio of consumer food brands - including Moon Chicken, San Gyu, Ayam Koplo, Dari Pada, Wai Thai, Pizza Gang, and Accha - engineered to be tasty, consistent, and affordable for the mass market and sold primarily through third-party food-delivery channels. Hangry operates as a direct-to-consumer food and beverage business rather than an API or developer platform provider; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: HCA Healthcare
providers.description: HCA Healthcare is one of the largest for-profit operators of healthcare facilities in the world, operating hospitals, surgery centers, freestanding emergency rooms, and urgent care centers across the United States and the United Kingdom. The corporate site does not advertise a public developer portal; patient-facing digital services run primarily through MyHealthONE.

providers.name: HCA Holdings
providers.description: HCA Holdings is an alias for HCA Healthcare, one of the largest for-profit operators of healthcare facilities in the world, operating hospitals, surgery centers, freestanding emergency rooms, and urgent care centers. The legal entity rebranded to HCA Healthcare; this index tracks the legacy name. No public developer portal or production APIs are advertised.

providers.name: Huuva
providers.description: Huuva is a Finnish food-court aggregator that lets customers order from multiple partner restaurants in a single order under the tagline "The hottest restaurants, all in one address." It operates physical food-court locations across Finland and runs a consumer web and mobile ordering platform for delivery and pickup, alongside lunch services and gift cards. Huuva is a consumer marketplace in the restaurant-technology and food-delivery space and does not currently publish a public developer or API program. It is a General Catalyst portfolio company based in Europe.

providers.name: Ideal Power Converters
providers.description: Ideal Power Inc. (NASDAQ: IPWR), formerly Ideal Power Converters, is an Austin, Texas power semiconductor company developing bidirectional bipolar junction transistor (B-TRAN) technology for ultra-low conduction losses, bidirectional current flow, and fast fault protection and switching. Its product portfolio includes B-TRAN power switches, SymCool power modules, and B-TRAN Known Good Die, targeting data centers, energy storage systems, power grids, solid-state circuit breakers, and EV charging infrastructure. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the company publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Ilumno
providers.description: Ilumno is a Latin American education technology company that helps higher education institutions grow and modernize through digital transformation. Its services span student acquisition and retention (Growth), online and virtual learning platforms (Virtuality), and real-time analytics and student-data management tools, all delivered on its Growth Engine technology platform. Ilumno reports supporting more than 220,000 students across the region, with offices in Bogota (Colombia), Dallas (USA) and Amsterdam (Netherlands). The company is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Inherent
providers.description: Inherent (Inherent Laboratories Ltd) is an early-stage AI research lab building recursively self-improving AI systems for scientific discovery — "AI scientists" intended to augment human researchers rather than replace them. Incorporated as a Public Benefit Corporation and backed by Index Ventures, the company frames itself as a reimagined research institution pursuing general-purpose inventive AI, autonomous-lab capabilities, and human-machine teaming across scientific domains. As of this profile it publishes a manifesto and careers page but no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or product surface — this repo tracks it as a lead for enrichment as those surfaces emerge.

providers.name: Intellilake
providers.description: Intellilake is an early-stage company backed by Anthemis and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Its public presence at intellilake.com is currently a placeholder landing page with a corporate contact address and a published privacy policy; the site references online services that require user accounts and login, affiliates, and third-party service providers, but as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface. This profile remains a lead awaiting a public API before deeper enrichment.

providers.name: Invera
providers.description: Invera is a Cordoba, Argentina fintech founded in 2016 that provides embedded investment and brokerage infrastructure to banks, fintechs, and financial institutions across Latin America. Originally a B2C robo-advisor, it pivoted into a B2B technology provider whose proprietary investment core (200,000+ development hours) powers three products - InvWallet (embedded investing that turns any monetary account into an investment account), Rocket (an investment-management platform that integrates with core banking systems and automates operations), and InvBroker (a portfolio-management and trading platform for clients and investment advisors). Invera exposes its capabilities through APIs and institution-agnostic infrastructure, with a stated mission of turning 10 million Latin Americans into investors. It is backed by 500 Global (500 LatAm B18).

providers.name: Iron Mountain
providers.description: Iron Mountain is a global leader in storage and information management services, providing records management, data centers, secure shredding, digital transformation, and asset lifecycle management for organizations worldwide. Iron Mountain helps customers protect and unlock value from their physical and digital information assets.

providers.name: ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md
providers.description: ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md is a template file that pre-populates new issue forms with structured sections, guiding contributors to provide necessary information when reporting bugs or requesting features in GitHub repositories.

providers.name: Kela Technologies
providers.description: Kela Technologies (kela.io) is a defense technology company founded by veterans of elite Israeli intelligence units, providing a secure, open platform that enables rapid and seamless integration of commercial and military systems in service of Western defense. The company emerged from stealth in 2025 after raising $39M from Sequoia Capital, Lux Capital, and In-Q-Tel (the CIA's venture arm). Kela is building "Sovereign Sky," a low-Earth-orbit satellite constellation for resilient communication and navigation independent of foreign infrastructure, and acquired cloud-management company Pelanor. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single-page marketing site with a privacy policy but no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Living Carbon
providers.description: Living Carbon is a reforestation and carbon removal company that restores abandoned mineland and degraded agricultural land in the United States, generating income for landowners while producing high-quality carbon removal credits with true additionality, limited leakage, and unique co-benefits. It develops fast-growing poplar trees for permanent land restoration and for custom biomass feedstock sited near processing facilities. Backed by Homebrew and surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a climate-sector company profile; the company publishes no public developer, API, or technical surface at this time.

providers.name: Lumachain
providers.description: Lumachain provides computer-vision AI for the food supply chain, delivering real-time detection of critical production events across high-throughput meat and food processing plants. Its on-site platform monitors deboning-equipment yield, animal welfare, foreign-object detection, and quality control across beef, pork, poultry, and finished-goods facilities, generating structured signals that integrate with existing plant systems. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners with investors including Chipotle. No public developer portal, API documentation, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Lunar-X
providers.description: Lunar-X (Lunar X) is a global digital content studio that acquires, develops, and operates creator-driven entertainment brands into globally recognized franchises across animation, educational content, functional music, ecommerce, and live events. Its properties include Economics Explained, Theorist Inc, Music Labs, and Lunar Kids, collectively spanning tens of billions of views and over a hundred million subscribers. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and added to the API Evangelist network. As a media/content operator it publishes a marketing website and privacy policy but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: McKesson
providers.description: McKesson is a Fortune 500 healthcare company providing wholesale medical supplies and equipment, pharmaceutical distribution, and healthcare technology solutions. No public developer APIs are currently documented.

providers.name: Mecka AI
providers.description: Mecka AI is the data and deployment layer for physical AI — it captures, structures, and evaluates real-world human and robot activity into datasets that robotics and embodied-AI teams can train on. Rather than building robots, Mecka positions itself as the integrator of the robotics ecosystem, plugging into hardware makers, frontier model labs, and commercial partners and owning the last-mile data, annotation, QA, and evaluation layer between them. Its Egoverse dataset captures large-scale first-person (egocentric) human activity across tasks and environments, and a companion iOS app lets teams collect task-specific data at scale. Mecka is backed by Forerunner Ventures and raised a $60M Series A in 2026. As of this pass Mecka publishes a marketing site, an iOS data-collection app, and the Egoverse data platform, but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Meta4 Capital
providers.description: Meta4 Capital is a crypto-focused investment firm ("Quintessentially Crypto") founded in 2021 that invests in programmable and digital assets. Anchored by a lead investment from a16z crypto, the firm runs several strategies including an NFT fund, NFT-backed lending, an AI/decentralized-intelligence fund (Bittensor / $TAO), and early-stage crypto ventures. It is an asset manager and investment vehicle, not an API producer, so it exposes no developer, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: MyVaccination
providers.description: Vaccination data for Malaysia

providers.name: NcodiN
providers.description: NcodiN is a French deep-tech company developing optical interconnect technology for high-performance computing and AI infrastructure. Founded in Palaiseau, France, the company builds miniaturized lasers integrated directly on silicon to replace traditional copper connections between chiplets and processors, aiming to break the "copper wall" that limits AI scaling. Its photonic interconnects promise petabit-per-second bandwidth with roughly a thousand times less energy to move data than copper links, targeting AI, telecommunications, autonomous driving, smart cities, healthcare, and climate modeling. NcodiN is backed by venture firms including Earlybird, Elaia, OVNI Capital, and Verve Ventures, is advised by major chip and equipment makers such as NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Intel, and ASML, and joined the FrenchTech2030 cohort in November 2025. As a semiconductor and photonics hardware company it sells to chipmakers and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Neocarbon
providers.description: NeoCarbon GmbH is a Berlin-based climate-technology company building integrated cooling and carbon-capture systems for data centers. Its patented Hollow Fiber platform converts low-grade waste heat (30-55C) simultaneously into efficient cooling, captured CO2 for industrial reuse, and recovered water, deployed as a retrofit without redesigning existing infrastructure. Backed by Speedinvest, the company operates as an industrial hardware and climate-infrastructure business and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or an API developer portal.

providers.name: Physical Property Testing
providers.description: Physical Properties Testers (PPT) Group is a Halifax, UK based multinational manufacturer of physical property test and measurement instrumentation, built through acquisition around four brands: James Heal (textile testing including bursting strength, abrasion and tear), Mecmesin (universal testing machines, torque testers and digital force gauges), Alluris (handheld force gauges and force/torque instrumentation) and Lansmont (shock, vibration and drop testing systems). The group designs, produces and services testing equipment that verifies the physical integrity and quality of raw materials, components and finished products across textiles, packaging, manufacturing and consumer goods. It is a hardware and laboratory-instrumentation business with no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface. Registered in England and Wales (company no. 09210539); a portfolio company of SK Capital Partners since March 2025 (previously backed by Battery Ventures). This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched with company identity from public sources.

providers.name: Plan A
providers.description: Plan A is a Berlin-headquartered enterprise sustainability software company, founded in 2017, building an end-to-end decarbonization platform for large organizations across Europe, the UK, and North America. The Plan A platform combines carbon accounting (Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions measurement aligned with the GHG Protocol), regulatory reporting (CSRD / ESRS, EU Taxonomy, CSDDD, UK SDR, US SEC climate disclosure, CBAM), and decarbonization planning (science-based target setting, abatement modelling, and forecasting). Customers include Sorare, KFC, Visa, BMW, Alphabet, and Mollie, served from offices in Berlin, Paris, and London. The platform is TUV Rheinland-certified and the company is a certified B Corporation. Plan A markets a Carbon Scanner, a Decarbonisation Savings Calculator, an Academy, a Whitepaper Centre, and a Regulation Centre as public-facing surfaces; the core carbon-accounting and reporting product is sold via enterprise contract and is not exposed as a public developer API. Plan A references "custom APIs" for client data integration in case-study material, but does not publish a developer portal, an OpenAPI specification, a public SDK, or an open-source GitHub organization. There is therefore no self-serve API surface to profile; this entry indexes Plan A as a decarbonization-platform provider for the API Evangelist sustainability landscape.

providers.name: Playbook
providers.description: Playbook is a career-growth platform for women that combines expert-led Masterclasses with an engaged professional community, enabling members to keep learning, build skills, and advance into leadership roles. Its tagline "Connect, Learn, Invest" reflects a focus on peer connection, ongoing education, and investing in one's own career. Playbook is backed by 500 Global and Bain Capital Ventures. As of this profile the company operates a consumer marketing and community web experience and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: PlusMargin
providers.description: PlusMargin (Plus Margin) is a Bangkok, Thailand based digital marketing and business consulting agency operating under the tagline "Connect | Engage | Convert." The firm focuses on inbound marketing strategy, personalized and AI-assisted marketing, buyer-persona development, and customer-journey mapping for its clients, and publishes editorial content across marketing, business, advertising, technology, learning, insurance, and lifestyle topics. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass the company operates a marketing/content website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: Pocket Fm
providers.description: Pocket FM is an audio entertainment platform offering long-form audio series, audiobooks, and serialized stories across genres such as romance, fantasy, thriller, and horror. Listeners stream free episodes and unlock premium content through an in-app coins/store model, while writers and voice creators publish original work through the Pocket FM Studio. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass, Pocket FM operates as a consumer-facing mobile and web product and does not publish a public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: PolicyPal
providers.description: PolicyPal is a Singapore-based InsurTech and digital insurance broker founded in 2016 by Val Yap that lets consumers buy, understand, and organize their insurance policies from a mobile app using OCR and rule-based policy digitization. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), PayPal Incubation, and Startupbootcamp FinTech, it was the first startup to graduate from the MAS FinTech Regulatory Sandbox and was acquired by Hong Kong's AMTD Digital in 2020. As of 2025 PolicyPal Pte. Ltd. and its entities (including PolicyPal Tech Pte. Ltd., Baoxianbaobao Pte. Ltd. and the ValueChampion brand) are no longer regulated by MAS, and the consumer website is undergoing a revamp. PolicyPal does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Project Eaden
providers.description: Project Eaden (PROJECT EADEN GmbH) is a Berlin-based food-technology company building fiber-spinning technology to power the next generation of whole-cut plant-based protein. Its platform reconstructs the fibrous structure of animal muscle from plant ingredients to create alternatives such as plant-based fish and meat, and it collaborates on consumer brands including LEKKA. Backed by Creandum and co-funded through EIT Food and the European Union, the company operates as a consumer food-tech producer and currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Puzzlium
providers.description: Puzzlium is a mobile puzzle platform and social network built around the tagline "Play. Create. Compete." Founded in 2014 by veteran puzzle designers Serhiy Grabarchuk, Serhiy Grabarchuk Jr., Peter Grabarchuk, and Mehmet Murat Sevim, the iOS and Amazon Kindle app lets a community of hundreds of thousands of solvers and creators play, generate, publish, and compete with interactive puzzles. Based in San Jose, California and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), Puzzlium is a consumer application that does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Pyka
providers.description: Pyka is an Alameda, California company that designs and manufactures large, dual-use heavy-lift autonomous electric aircraft for commercial and defense operations. Its flagship products are the Pelican 2 autonomous crop-protection aircraft for aerial application and the DropShip long-range heavy-lift cargo UAS. Pyka builds a fully integrated, vertically owned autonomy stack — an Autonomy Engine (real-time OS, sensor fusion, flight control, and path planning), a Mission Control operator suite (simulation, communications, and operator interface), and custom aerospace-grade hardware. The company is backed by DCVC and Obvious Ventures. Pyka does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security footprint. Surfaced via VC portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: Ranker
providers.description: Ranker is a consumer internet company that runs ranker.com, a crowdsourced ranking and voting platform where users vote on and create rankings across pop culture, entertainment, film, TV, music, food, sports, and other consumer topics. Its business arm licenses "Ranker Insights" audience-intelligence and opinion-graph data - drawn from more than 1.5 billion votes, 115 million voters, and 260,000 rankings - to brands, agencies, publishers, and for AI/LLM training. Ranker does not publish a public, self-serve developer API; a private api.ranker.com powers the site and its robots.txt prohibits automated scraping and AI/LLM training use. Data access is sales-led via business.ranker.com. Backed by Bullpen Capital and DCVC.

providers.name: Redesign Health
providers.description: Redesign Health is a global venture and applied technology firm that backs and builds next-generation healthcare companies. Founded in 2018, it partners with founders and existing businesses through AI-native venture capital and buyout strategies, and reports having touched more than 15 million patient lives while raising over $1.5 billion in capital. The firm operates from New York, Los Angeles, Riyadh, and Bengaluru. Redesign Health surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of General Catalyst; this profile captures its public identity. Redesign Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: REEF
providers.description: REEF Technology operates a network of urban logistics and proximity real-estate locations, transforming underutilized spaces such as parking lots into multi-purpose neighborhood hubs for goods, services, and experiences. Through its "Power of Proximity" model and its Ulysses operator program, REEF connects brands, cloud/ghost kitchens, delivery, and mobility services to local consumers while helping property owners diversify revenue. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, REEF is a logistics and real-estate operator; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Rocket Internet
providers.description: Rocket Internet SE is a Berlin-based internet company builder and technology investment firm founded by the Samwer brothers. It incubates and scales internet and technology ventures globally and invests through its venture arm, having built and backed more than 200 companies across six continents in e-commerce, marketplaces, fintech, food delivery, and consumer internet. Rocket Internet operates as a holding and operational-support platform rather than a product or API provider, so it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SambaAds
providers.description: SambaAds is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of this pass the registered website (ycontent.com.br) serves yContent, a Brazilian coupon and discount aggregation platform (part of Rede de Cupons / Ganhe de Volta) that verifies and publishes working promotional codes for major Brazilian e-commerce retailers such as Amazon, Americanas, Kabum and Sephora. The site is a consumer-facing web property; it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface, so there is no public API surface to catalog at this time. This profile records the honest result of an enrichment pass (domain-security probe plus well-known and security.txt probes) and remains a lead awaiting any future developer program.

providers.name: Samsara Eco
providers.description: Samsara Eco is an Australian climate-technology company pioneering enzymatic recycling, a process that uses engineered enzymes to break plastics and synthetic textiles down into their molecular building blocks so they can be infinitely remade into new materials with no loss of quality. Spun out of the Australian National University, the company recovers nylon and polyester from mixed and coloured textile and plastic waste and partners with global brands to build a circular materials supply chain. It is a materials-science and biotech company rather than an API provider, and has no public developer, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Sansan
providers.description: Sansan, Inc. is a Tokyo-based enterprise SaaS company that builds cloud contact- and business-card management software. Its flagship Sansan platform digitizes and centralizes business cards and customer contact data so sales teams can share information across the organization, surface opportunities, and integrate contact data with external systems. The company also offers the Eight business-card app and Bill One invoice-management product. As of this enrichment pass Sansan does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition on its English or Japanese websites; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Science On Call
providers.description: Science On Call provides 24/7 AI-powered technology support built specifically for restaurants. Combining intelligent automation with human experts, the service helps restaurant staff triage and resolve operational technology issues across point-of-sale (POS) systems, kitchen display systems (KDS), loyalty programs, staff scheduling, online ordering, training platforms, phones, internet, and Wi-Fi. Staff reach support anytime via text, email, or phone with no app or login required, and issues are typically resolved in about 25 minutes. Science On Call is a Techstars-backed company; billing is handled through a hosted customer portal. This profile currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or machine- readable specification surface.

providers.name: Scorce
providers.description: Scorce is a Mexico-based API aggregation platform that gives businesses a single integration point to connect to multiple Latin American and global identity APIs for customer authentication, KYC (Know Your Customer), digital identity verification, and fraud prevention. The platform lets teams connect in under 24 hours, obtain provider trials, and monitor API performance across providers from one unified dashboard. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Puebla, Mexico, Scorce is backed by 500 Global, Finnovista, and Tenity.

providers.name: Seafair
providers.description: Seafair is an AI-native ERP platform for maritime operations, unifying crew management, HSQE and regulatory compliance, technical maintenance (planned maintenance systems and defect tracking), and accounting into a single system for shipping companies and ship managers. Its AI compliance engine performs document search and framework reviews (such as DryBMS and TMSA) and embeds AI assistance directly into operational workflows. Seafair markets itself as API-first with fast ERP integrations, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition. Seafair is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and is tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Searchlight
providers.description: Searchlight (searchlight.ai) is an Accel-backed company in the services sector, added to the API Evangelist network from Accel's portfolio. Its primary web presence is a Webflow-hosted marketing site at www.searchlight.ai, with a product application at app.searchlight.ai and an internal API host at api.searchlight.ai — both of which sit behind Cloudflare and return HTTP 525 (origin unreachable to the public), and the marketing site rejects non-browser TLS clients, so no public developer documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs could be discovered. A public Instatus status page is live at status.searchlight.ai (monitoring Website and App components). Email runs on Google Workspace with HubSpot, and the domain publishes SPF and DMARC records. This profile captures the verifiable public infrastructure; no public API surface was found.

providers.name: Send4 Tecnologia
providers.description: Send4 Tecnologia (rebranded as After Sale) is a Brazilian post-purchase platform for e-commerce, automating product exchanges, returns, and reverse logistics. Founded in 2017, it has processed over 6 million reverse-logistics transactions and offers intelligent authorization rules for approvals and blocks, a self-service customer exchange portal, real-time returns dashboards, revenue-retention offers (vouchers and cashback), integrated shipping labels and tracking, automated refunds and store credit, and multi-channel WhatsApp and email support. It advertises a simple, flexible API to connect with any e-commerce platform in minutes, though no public developer documentation is currently published. After Sale is now part of the Confi ecosystem alongside Neotrust and the Confi consumer app.

providers.name: Sensmore
providers.description: Sensmore (sensmore GmbH) is a German industrial-automation and embodied-AI company that turns robotics research into field-proven systems for heavy machinery in raw material operations. Its platform connects machines, sites, and data across mining, aggregates/construction, and defense, spanning products including Site Intelligence (live site operations), Machine Assist (driver assistance and collision warning), Eye (visual monitoring), Live Mapping (real-time site mapping), and Loader Automation (autonomous vehicle systems), with claims of reducing downtime by up to 30% while improving safety and resource efficiency. Sensmore was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or developer documentation; its web presence is a marketing and corporate site.

providers.name: SFX
providers.description: SFX (SFX Entertainment, now operating as LiveStyle, Inc) is a Beverly Hills based global live-events and electronic dance music company. Originally founded by Robert F.X. Sillerman as a roll-up of EDM festival and event brands, the company reorganized as LiveStyle and continues to produce live music experiences, festivals, and fan events under the banner "For the Love of Music." It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company presents a corporate marketing web presence and publishes no public developer, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Smart & Final Stores
providers.description: Smart & Final Stores is a warehouse-style food and supply retailer operating over 250 stores in the Western United States and 15 stores in northwestern Mexico. The company sells a wide variety of fresh perishables, everyday grocery items, and warehouse-club-sized products to both households and businesses. Smart & Final does not operate a public developer API program but participates in grocery industry digital commerce integrations through third-party platforms.

providers.name: Soma Energy
providers.description: Soma Energy is an AI-powered energy intelligence platform that optimizes how power is produced, stored, and consumed. Founded by former Amazon and technology leaders, it coordinates power generation, battery storage, and large energy consumers such as data centers. Its Intelligence Platform combines three products: AI Trader, which automates energy procurement, hedging, and dispatch for independent power producers (IPPs); BESS Dispatcher, which manages battery energy storage systems; and Load Optimizer, which coordinates data-center workloads with grid conditions to cut energy costs and turn facilities into flexible grid assets. Soma Energy is an early-stage company backed by Uncork Capital. As of this profile the company exposes no public API, developer platform, or documentation.

providers.name: Spatialedge
providers.description: Spatialedge is an enterprise AI and data solutions firm headquartered in Stellenbosch, South Africa, with offices in London and Austin. The company builds and operationalizes analytical tooling that turns data into data-driven business decisions, spanning consulting and AI maturity assessments, custom solution development (data pipelines, optimization and forecasting models, AI-powered applications), integration and deployment into existing business systems, and ongoing MLOps and model maintenance. Products include Workforce Planner, Price Planner, Demand Forecaster, and DataLlume, applied across retail pricing, telecom infrastructure, and mining predictive maintenance. Spatialedge does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal; it is a services and solutions provider surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Specific Labs
providers.description: Specific Labs is a Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) applied AI research lab based in San Francisco and operated by Bear AI Inc. The company builds datasets and benchmarks derived from real enterprise workflows, capturing authentic business decision-making patterns and audio and enterprise data that are otherwise hard to access, and turns them into training data and evaluation benchmarks for building reliable, domain-grounded AI agents. It works with frontier AI labs seeking datasets from real enterprises and with enterprises building dependable agents. Founded by Janak Sunil (CEO, formerly Coinbase) and Siddhant Paliwal (CTO). As of this profile Specific Labs publishes a marketing site with a benchmarks page and company information, and does not yet expose a public API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Suiteness
providers.description: Suiteness is a hotel booking platform specializing in connecting rooms and suites that hotels do not make public. Through partnerships with hotels, it surfaces adjoining rooms and suites - marked with a "+" symbol - so families and groups can book twice the space at roughly half the price of booking multiple standard rooms. It combines suite inventory, a concierge collaboration service, and a membership program. Suiteness is a consumer travel booking company backed by Bullpen Capital; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or partner API surface at this time.

providers.name: Sunrise
providers.description: Sunrise Robotics builds intelligent, two-armed autonomous robotic cells for manufacturing. The AI-driven system combines built-in perception and environmental awareness with autonomous execution to transform existing production processes, increase capacity, and free human workers for higher-value tasks. Cells deploy quickly (needing only a three-phase outlet), are flexible across manufacturing applications, and are built to ISO 10218 / TS 15066 safety standards. The company is backed by Seedcamp and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: SuperCircle
providers.description: SuperCircle (operated by MASC Inc.) is a technology and reverse-logistics platform that helps retail and fashion brands run circular-economy programs for textiles. It provides turnkey trade-in and resale programs that let consumers send worn clothing back to brands for store credit, manages excess and overstock inventory through a warehouse pickup and logistics network, and delivers real-time performance tracking and customizable impact reporting on recycling and diversion outcomes. Brand partners include Reformation, tentree, Parachute, A.L.C., and Subset. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found at the time of enrichment; this profile is a company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SupplyHog
providers.description: SupplyHog is an ecommerce platform built specifically for hardware and building-materials retailers, giving independent hardware and building-supply stores a branded online storefront to sell their products. The platform provides co-op and custom product catalogs, flexible fulfillment (in-store pickup, ship-to-store, local delivery, and ship-to-home with Shippo shipping labels), Stripe-powered payments, TaxJar tax calculation, real-time ERP inventory and pricing synchronization, custom branding and domains, location-aware search, and admin tools for order fulfillment and abandoned-cart recovery. Founded in 2010 as the Nopone.com reverse-auction marketplace, SupplyHog went through the DreamIt and 500 Startups accelerators, pivoted to full ecommerce services, and was acquired by construction-supply retailer R.P. Lumber in 2016. It does not publish a public developer API surface; it acts as a consumer of Stripe, TaxJar, and Shippo.

providers.name: Take Two
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO) is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment for consumers worldwide, headquartered in New York City. The company delivers its products principally through three wholly owned labels — Rockstar Games, 2K, and Zynga — spanning console, PC, and mobile platforms via physical retail, digital download, online platforms, and cloud streaming. Franchises include Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, NBA 2K, Borderlands, and mobile titles such as Words With Friends and Toon Blast. Take-Two is a publicly traded interactive entertainment holding company; it does not publish a public developer API program, developer portal, or API documentation at the corporate level. This profile was surfaced as a general-catalyst job-board listing and carried into the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment found no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: teaBOT
providers.description: teaBOT is a Toronto-based hardware startup (Y Combinator, Summer 2015) that builds an automated loose-leaf tea-making robot offered to offices, showrooms, and lounges as an amenity-as-a-service. For a flat monthly fee, teams use the companion teaBOT app to explore premium teas and dispense a custom-blended cup in under 30 seconds, which companies such as Google, HubSpot, and McKinsey use as a workplace recruiting and retention perk. Founded by robotics PhD Rehman Merali, teaBOT runs a physical-product and mobile-app business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Textio
providers.description: Textio is an augmented-writing platform that uses AI to help managers and HR teams write clearer, more actionable, and less biased performance feedback, recruiting outreach, and job posts. Used by 100,000+ managers at companies including T-Mobile, NASDAQ, Strava, and Upwork, Textio analyzes tone and language as people write and flags biased, low-impact, or unclear phrasing in real time. It is delivered as a web application with browser and editor integrations. Probing textio.com found no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, developer portal, or .well-known discovery documents (the site is a HubSpot-hosted single-page app that serves a soft-404 shell for all such paths); api.textio.com exposes only an application health check. Textio does operate a public system status page.

providers.name: The Cru
providers.description: The Cru (now branded "The Cru Empowered by Luminary") is a membership community founded by Tiffany Dufu that matches women and allies into small peer-coaching accountability circles ("Crus") of 6-8 members who meet in monthly 90-minute gatherings to advance their personal and professional goals. It was acquired by Luminary, a New York City based professional community and coworking organization, and the thecru.com site now redirects to weareluminary.com/luminary-crus. This is a consumer community and coaching business, not a technical platform - it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: THIS
providers.description: THIS™ is a UK plant-based food company making high-protein vegan meat alternatives — including meat-free chicken, bacon, sausages, burgers and mince — sold through major British supermarkets such as Tesco, Sainsbury's, Waitrose, Ocado, Morrisons, Asda and Co-op. Founded in 2019 and backed by Seedcamp, THIS™ is a consumer packaged goods (CPG) brand focused on absurdly tasty plant-based food rather than a developer platform. It operates a marketing and recipe website but publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK at the time of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Tigris
providers.description: Tigris is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, general-catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Truvio
providers.description: Truvio is a unified software portfolio company providing intelligent, AI-driven automation solutions for Microsoft Dynamics 365 across finance, operations, Business Central, and commerce. Its practitioner-built solutions span Accounts Payable automation (ExFlow), Banking & Treasury automation (SKSoft), eCommerce and Product Information Management (DynamicWeb), and Project & Production Management (Axtension), embedding expertise directly into Dynamics 365 to help organizations close the ERP value gap. Backed by Insight Partners. No public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Tryprism
providers.description: Prism (tryprism.com) is a San Francisco, Y Combinator-backed AI-powered recruiting agency that delivers qualified talent leads to hiring teams faster and more affordably than traditional recruiters. Clients describe the role they need to fill, Prism's AI handles sourcing, screening, and candidate outreach end-to-end, and clients interview only pre-screened candidates. Pricing is 15% of first-year salary per hire (versus the typical 20-30% agency fee) plus a retainer to initiate and prioritize the search, charged only when a hire is made. As of this profile Prism operates as a managed recruiting service and publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or discovery surface.

providers.name: Ventura
providers.description: Ventura builds the AI workforce for distributors and manufacturers, starting with quoting and order entry. It automates quoting and order entry for distributors, helping sales teams turn emails, PDFs, and other purchase orders into accurate quotes and orders in their ERP system. Ventura plugs into your existing ERP, follows your SOPs, and learns your team's tribal knowledge - getting smarter with every completed task. Ventura (formerly Autola) is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company based in San Francisco. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing website and a privacy policy only; no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: ZhongAn Insurance
providers.description: ZhongAn Online P&C Insurance Co., Ltd. is China's first online-only insurance company, founded in 2013 by Ant Financial, Tencent, and Ping An and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (6060) in 2017. Headquartered in Shanghai, ZhongAn sells digital insurance across health, consumer finance, auto, and lifestyle lines entirely through internet channels, and operates a partner "open platform" (open.zhongan.com) plus a technology arm, ZhongAn Technology (zhongan.io), that offers insurtech and cloud services. ZhongAn does not publish a self-serve public developer API program or OpenAPI documentation; integration is partner/ecosystem-driven. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of softbank-vision-fund and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: 42 Floors
providers.description: 42Floors was a Y Combinator- and 500 Global-backed commercial real estate search platform founded in 2011 by Jason Freedman to make it easy to discover and lease office, coworking, retail, industrial, and warehouse space across top U.S. markets. It aggregated a large listings database (the "42Floors MLS") that brokers and tenants searched online. The company was acquired by Knotel in 2018, and the 42floors.com domain and listings service were later taken over by Yardi, which folded them into CommercialCafe — 42floors.com now redirects there. The only surviving developer surface is the first-party `mls` RubyGem, a client for the (now-decommissioned) 42Floors MLS API at mls.42floors.com.

providers.name: App-CM
providers.description: App-CM, Inc. (株式会社アップシーエム) is a Tokyo-based technology company that operates a proprietary video-advertising delivery platform for smartphones, using in-house compression, delivery, and targeting-algorithm technology to serve video ads smoothly in mobile environments. App-CM also develops and publishes consumer mobile apps including FriendQuiz, SunQ, and Shakin. The company is backed by 500 Global and is profiled in the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specifications at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Archer
providers.description: Archer (archermoney.com) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) financial-infrastructure startup building global payouts, stablecoin banking, and yield infrastructure for the companies powering the AI data economy. Archer lets data marketplaces, AI labor platforms, and reinforcement-learning environment providers onboard workers globally, pay contributors instantly with stablecoins, and earn yield on idle platform balances while funds remain on platform. The company aims to be the financial layer for the global workforce generating the data that trains frontier AI models, reducing cross-border payout costs and improving the financial experience for contributors. Founded by Benjamin Nguyen (CEO) and Vivek Yanamadula (CTO); early stage, no public developer surface or API specification published yet.

providers.name: BetaList
providers.description: BetaList is a platform for discovering upcoming internet startups and getting early access to innovative products before they go mainstream. Founded in 2010, BetaList curates pre-launch and recently launched startups across categories including SaaS, AI tools, analytics, developer tools, and more. Startups gain exposure through the BetaList website, daily email newsletter, and social media channels. No public developer API has been identified; startup discovery and submission are handled through the web interface.

providers.name: cargo.one
providers.description: cargo.one is a Berlin-headquartered digital freight platform that operates as an AI-native operating system for air and ocean freight logistics. The platform unifies freight forwarder operations by centralizing rates, partners, and systems on a single end-to-end surface shared between human teams and AI agents. For freight forwarders, cargo.one provides air e-booking with 76+ integrated airlines (300+ total network), ocean freight rate management with 10+ liner integrations, multimodal quoting across air, ocean, road, and local charges, a Rate Management System for buy/sell/internal rates, a branded 24/7 self-service Customer Portal, analytics dashboards, a 24/7 Global Network for cross-timezone quoting, and an API Suite with native TMS integrations for CargoWise, Cargospot, and Descartes. For carriers, cargo.one delivers a market-intelligence and customer-access platform spanning the end-to-end commercial cycle. AI workflows are offered in three deployment modes — Co-pilot (approval-based), Supervised (autonomous with escalation), and Autonomous — covering rate management, rate procurement, quoting, booking, and customer support automation, backed by retrieval-augmented generation and a cargo.one MCP Server for custom solutions. Notable customers include Lufthansa Cargo, Kuehne+Nagel, DSV, Maersk, CMA CGM, Hellmann, and Rhenus Logistics. cargo.one's API and TMS integrations are partner / enterprise offerings — there is no public self-serve OpenAPI specification, developer sandbox, or open-source SDK published outside of customer onboarding.

providers.name: Chef Robotics
providers.description: Chef Robotics is a San Francisco, California physical-AI company building AI-enabled robots for high-mix food production. Its core product is an NSF-certified food-assembly robot that picks, scoops, and deposits a wide range of ingredients — fresh, cooked, IQF, sauces, leafy greens, mixed vegetables, and discrete piece items — into trays, burritos, wraps, pizza bases, and other containers on conveyor lines. The robots are powered by ChefOS, a proprietary Generalized Food Manipulation Model trained on tens of millions of real-world servings and tens of thousands of hours of production data, combining vision, decision-making, and robot control across a See / Think / Act stack with continuous Fleet Learning. Chef Robotics sells via a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that bundles hardware, software updates, 24/7 monitoring, and customer success. Deployed customers include Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice, and Chef Bombay, with the fleet having produced 98+ million servings across the US, Canada, and Europe. The company is venture-backed (Kleiner Perkins, Avataar Ventures-led $43M Series A, Bloomberg Beta, Construct Capital) and serves frozen meals, fresh meals, co-manufacturing, D2C meal delivery, medically tailored meals, meatpacking, airline catering, and foodservice verticals. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for ChefOS — the platform is operated as a closed, fleet-managed service on Chef-owned hardware deployed inside customer facilities.

providers.name: Cloudcoreo
providers.description: CloudCoreo was a Seattle-based cloud security startup (founded 2016, seed round led by Madrona Venture Group) that built a cloud configuration and vulnerability-assessment platform to identify and remediate misconfigurations across public multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP). VMware acquired CloudCoreo in February 2018 and folded the team and product into VMware Cloud Services, where it became the basis of CloudHealth Secure State. The standalone CloudCoreo service and developer surface have since been retired: cloudcoreo.com is now a parked/for-sale domain and there is no live public API. The CloudCoreo GitHub organization remains, hosting the now-deprecated first-party CLI. This profile is a historical/lineage record, not an active API provider.

providers.name: Codex Protocol
providers.description: Codex Protocol was a blockchain startup (founded 2018, backed by Pantera Capital) that built a decentralized registry for unique physical assets — fine art, wine, watches and other collectibles — on Ethereum, using ERC-721 Codex Records and an ERC-20 Codex Coin (CODX) token, plus a Codex Viewer dapp and a Codex Registry REST API. The company is now defunct: its API and dapp repositories are archived, its documentation host no longer resolves, and its original marketing domain (codexprotocol.com) has been repurposed by a third party and redirects offsite. The surviving, verifiable first-party artifacts are the codex-protocol GitHub organization (13 repositories of smart contracts, services, and tooling) and four @codex-protocol npm packages. This profile was surfaced as a Pantera Capital portfolio company and is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical / defunct record.

providers.name: Computable
providers.description: Computable (Computable Labs) was a Pantera Capital-backed crypto startup that built the Computable Protocol, a decentralized data-market and "Datatrust" system letting participants create Fair, Free-Access (FFA) markets to pool, price, and share datasets on Ethereum. The project shipped developer client libraries (computable.js for JavaScript, computable.py for Python), a Datatrust API reference implementation, Computable Improvement Proposals (CIPs), and a protocol specification ("The Computable Book"). The GitHub organization and its repositories are archived and inactive (last activity 2022-2023) and the company's websites (computable.io and computablelabs.com) no longer resolve to a live property, so this profile documents the surviving open-source developer surface rather than a running service.

providers.name: Cryptoys
providers.description: Cryptoys is an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) backed Web3 digital collectibles company that lets fans buy, own, and play with blockchain-based interactive toys featuring licensed characters from Disney and Star Wars alongside original IP. Products are sold as blind boxes containing randomized digital toys across multiple power tiers and rarity levels. The company has since rebranded and now operates its consumer experience as Digitoys at digitoys.io, while retaining its identity account service at auth.cryptoys.com. Cryptoys is a consumer-facing collectibles platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and identity surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Datalogue
providers.description: Datalogue was a self-service data integration and preparation startup founded in 2015 that used machine learning to automatically classify, transform, and standardize data from disparate sources for analytics teams. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company was acquired by Nike in February 2019 and its standalone product was discontinued; the datalogue.io domain now serves an unrelated blog. This profile is retained for the API Evangelist network as a historical/portfolio record. The only surviving first-party developer artifacts are the company's public GitHub organization and an unmaintained Python SDK ("datalogue") still published on PyPI.

providers.name: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.)
providers.description: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.) was a pioneering social data platform that provided real-time and historical access to social media firehoses (Twitter, Facebook Topic Data, and more) through its CSDL filtering language and its Push, Historics, and Managed Sources REST APIs. Founded in 2007 and backed by Insight Partners and others, the company was acquired by Meltwater in 2019; the datasift.com domain now redirects to meltwater.com and the standalone DataSift developer platform and APIs have been discontinued. Official first-party client SDKs for Python, Ruby, PHP, Java, and Node.js remain published on public package registries under the datasift GitHub organization as historical artifacts.

providers.name: Deci AI
providers.description: Deci AI was a deep-learning development company (founded 2019, Tel Aviv) whose platform helped teams build, optimize, and deploy computer-vision and NLP models in production. Its stack combined the AutoNAC neural-architecture-search engine, the Infery inference runtime, and the open-source SuperGradients PyTorch training library — the home of the YOLO-NAS object-detection architecture. Deci was acquired by NVIDIA in 2024; deci.ai now redirects to NVIDIA and there is no live standalone hosted API or developer console. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's surviving first-party open-source software surface (SuperGradients and DataGradients on PyPI, published from the Deci-AI GitHub org).

providers.name: Dharma Labs
providers.description: Dharma Labs was a decentralized-finance company that built Dharma Protocol, an open-source Ethereum protocol for tokenized debt and peer-to-peer lending, and later the Dharma non-custodial smart wallet. It was backed by Polychain and was acquired by OpenSea in 2021. The company is defunct: its developer surface at dharma.io is now a parked, for-sale domain with no live API, documentation, or well-known discovery endpoints. Real, first-party remnants still survive on the public registries — the GitHub organization dharmaprotocol (26 public repos, including the dharma.js client library, charta smart contracts, developer-docs, and the dapp-wallet) and the npm package @dharmaprotocol/dharma.js, which is published but explicitly marked DEPRECATED. This profile captures those honest historical artifacts; the provider ships no maintained API today.

providers.name: EnergyBank
providers.description: EnergyBank is a New Zealand deep-tech energy company developing next-generation energy storage for the offshore wind market. Its core approach firms floating offshore wind generation at the turbine so that compute modules can be co-located with the generation itself — taking "data to the power rather than electricity to the data" — which removes the need for a grid connection, enables consentless high-seas deployment, and allows direct ocean cooling of the co-located compute. The company was founded by CEO Tim Hawkey and CTO Alex Szczepaniak, and its team combines applied mathematicians, electronics engineers, and business development staff with advisors drawn from subsea turbomachinery. EnergyBank is venture backed by Version One Ventures, Blackbird, Icehouse Ventures, Outset Ventures, Promus Ventures, Nuance Capital, and Boost VC. As of this enrichment pass EnergyBank publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification — it is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Enzymit
providers.description: Enzymit is a synthetic biology company based in Rehovot, Israel that designs novel enzymes and enables cell-free biomanufacturing. Its proprietary platform combines computational protein design, deep learning, and high-throughput testing to develop enzymes for biochemicals, food and beverage, personal care, and health and nutrition markets, with applications spanning hyaluronic acid production, cultivated-meat ingredients, and biosensors. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Enzymit publishes open research tools such as SolvIT (protein solubility prediction) and the StabilizeIT platform, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Equator Principles
providers.description: The Equator Principles is a risk management framework adopted by financial institutions for determining, assessing, and managing environmental and social risk in project finance transactions. It provides a minimum standard for due diligence and monitoring to support responsible risk decision-making and is primarily intended to provide a minimum standard for due diligence and monitoring in project finance and related advisory activities.

providers.name: EvenUp
providers.description: EvenUp is a SaaS company building proactive AI for personal-injury law firms, spanning the full case lifecycle from intake and treatment management through demand drafting, negotiation, discovery, and trial support. The platform combines AI drafting, communication agents, medical record management, proactive workflows, and executive analytics on top of integrations with popular case-management systems. EvenUp reports serving more than 2,000 personal-injury firms and processing roughly 10,000 cases per week, with more than $10B in damages claimed through the platform. The company is venture-funded (Series E) at a $2B+ valuation, with backing from Bessemer, B Capital, Bain Capital, Lightspeed, Premji Invest, and others. EvenUp does not publish a public developer portal; integrations are delivered through case-management partner connectors rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Factual
providers.description: Factual Inc. was a Los Angeles-based location-data company (backed by a16z, DCVC and Index Ventures) that operated the Global Places database and Geopulse audience/location APIs, giving developers programmatic access to a worldwide catalog of business points of interest, categories, attributes and geotagged mobile audience data. Factual was acquired by and merged into Foursquare in 2020; factual.com now redirects to foursquare.com and the standalone Factual Places/Geopulse API has been discontinued. This profile preserves the historical first-party client drivers (Java, Python, Node.js, Clojure) still published in their package registries and captured as real artifacts in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: File Format
providers.description: File formats define how information is encoded for storage in a computer file, spanning images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF), audio (WAV, MP3, OGG, FLAC), video (MP4, MOV, MKV), documents (PDF, HTML, DOCX, ODT), data serialization (JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, Parquet, Avro), archives (ZIP, TAR, GZIP), and executables. File formats are central to API and data interoperability, identified via filename extensions, magic numbers, MIME types, and IANA media-type registrations.

providers.name: First West Credit Union
providers.description: First West Credit Union — rebranded Tru Cooperative Bank in 2026 — is a member-owned Canadian cooperative financial institution headquartered in Langley, British Columbia. Formed in 2010 by the merger of Envision Credit Union and Valley First, and later joined by Island Savings and Enderby & District Financial, it operates those four regional brands over a shared branch network with roughly 291,000 members, about $20.8 billion in total assets, 45 branches, and around 1,300 employees. After members voted in 2021 for federal continuance, it received a federal charter under Canada's Bank Act and became a federal credit union / cooperative bank (CDIC-insured) as of April 1, 2026. On the open-finance front First West / Tru runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or partner API; both developer.firstwestcu.ca and developer.trucooperativebank.ca resolve to nothing (NXDOMAIN). Third-party access to member account data today is aggregator-based (screen-scraping via providers such as Plaid and Flinks), the fragmented and voluntary Canadian norm while the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, overseen by the FCAC) remains legislated but not yet operational.

providers.name: Fixed
providers.description: Fixed (fixed.com.au) is a Brisbane, Australia based construction, refurbishment and facility-maintenance company specialising in the childcare sector. The business delivers centre refurbishments, reactive and preventative maintenance, emergency repairs, landscaping and outdoor play-space (yard) services for childcare and early-learning facilities across Australia, with licensed and inducted teams and 24/7 after-hours availability. It is a services trades business with a WordPress marketing website and no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable surface. This entry was auto-created as a stub from a venture-portfolio match; that match is almost certainly a domain/name collision (see x-notes) and the profile is retained here as an enriched, no-API-surface company record.

providers.name: Fleksy
