providers.description: Fleksy (Thingthing Ltd) was a keyboard technology company that built a mobile Keyboard SDK — a white-label, privacy-focused typing engine that iOS and Android developers could embed in their own apps. The SDK provided autocorrect, next-word prediction, swipe/gesture typing, customizable themes, and a plugin system, and the Fleksy keyboard once held Guinness World Records for the fastest typing. Fleksy distributed a native mobile SDK rather than a public web/REST API, so it exposes no OpenAPI, GraphQL, or hosted developer portal. Backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest, the company's public web presence (fleksy.com, docs.fleksy.com, fleksy.dev) no longer resolves and the business appears defunct; this profile captures the surviving public artifact — the first-party FleksySDK CocoaPods pod for iOS.

providers.name: Floobits
providers.description: Floobits was a real-time collaborative code editing service — "remote collaboration tools for dev teams, work together, apart." It shipped editor plugins for Sublime Text, Vim, Neovim, Emacs, Atom, and the IntelliJ family of IDEs, plus flootty, a shared-terminal tool for pair terminal sessions. Plugins connected editors to shared Floobits workspaces where multiple developers edited the same files and terminals in real time over a synchronizing backend (built on a diff-match-patch model). Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of 2026-07-19 the hosted service at floobits.com no longer resolves in DNS and the GitHub org has had no activity since December 2022; the open-source editor plugins and the flootty PyPI package remain the durable public surface.

providers.name: Generalist AI
providers.description: Generalist AI, Inc. is a frontier AI research and product-driven company building general intelligence for the physical world — training robots that work autonomously across factories, warehouses, laboratories, restaurants, farms, homes, and beyond. Its flagship model, GEN-1, is a general-purpose embodied foundation model trained from scratch that reaches mastery of simple physical tasks, going beyond world models and vision-language-action (VLA) approaches. Backed by Spark Capital, the company publishes its research through a blog and open-sources vision and robotics tooling on GitHub. Generalist AI exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Getaround
providers.description: Getaround is a peer-to-peer car-sharing marketplace and connected-car technology company founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, with significant European operations across France, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Norway, and the United Kingdom. The platform pairs private and professional vehicle owners with renters who book cars by the hour or day, unlocking and starting vehicles from a mobile app rather than meeting the owner to exchange keys. The keyless experience is enabled by Getaround Connect, a proprietary in-car telematics device that the company designs and installs in shared vehicles to handle remote lock/unlock, ignition, GPS tracking, mileage reporting, fuel level monitoring, and trip event recording. Getaround acquired Drivy in 2019 to consolidate the European car-sharing market and acquired the HyreCar rideshare-driver rental marketplace in 2022. The company went public on the NYSE via a SPAC merger in December 2022 at a valuation of roughly $1.2 billion, was delisted from the NYSE in July 2024 and transferred to OTC Pink under the ticker GETR after its market capitalization collapsed to roughly $24 million. On February 11, 2025, Getaround announced it was ceasing all United States operations — including HyreCar — while preserving its European business, which continues to operate in major EU cities under the same Getaround Connect platform. Getaround has never published a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; partner integrations with insurers, fleet operators, and automotive OEMs have historically been delivered through private, contract-bound APIs rather than a self-service developer surface. The company's GitHub organization hosts primarily forks of generic open-source libraries (Braintree SDKs, iOS testing frameworks, logging libraries) rather than first-party API artifacts.

providers.name: GoTo
providers.description: GoTo (PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, IDX: GOTO) is the largest technology group in Indonesia, formed in May 2021 through the merger of the on-demand and ride-hailing pioneer Gojek and the e-commerce marketplace Tokopedia. GoTo operates a super-app ecosystem spanning on-demand services (ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery, logistics), e-commerce, and financial technology through GoTo Financial (including GoPay, one of Indonesia's leading digital wallets). The group serves Indonesia's population of more than 270 million, connecting tens of millions of consumers with millions of merchants and driver-partners, and is estimated to contribute roughly 2 percent of Indonesia's GDP. GoTo is backed by a roster of blue-chip investors including SoftBank Vision Fund, Alibaba, Google, Tencent, Temasek, and Sequoia Capital India. This company profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline. Note that GoTo Group's developer surfaces are published per product (Gojek/GoBiz, Tokopedia, GoTo Financial/Midtrans) rather than at a single group-level developer portal; this record profiles the parent holding company.

providers.name: Guardian Life Insurance
providers.description: Guardian Life Insurance is one of the largest mutual life insurance companies in the United States, providing life insurance, disability income insurance, dental insurance, and other employee benefits. This is an alias entry; primary record lives at guardian-life.

providers.name: Heyzap
providers.description: Heyzap was a mobile-game advertising, discovery, and monetization company. It began as a social game-discovery network and pivoted into a mobile ad mediation platform, offering iOS, Android, Unity, Cordova, and Adobe AIR/ANE SDKs that let game developers serve and mediate ads across networks such as AdMob, AppLovin, Vungle, Chartboost, AdColony, and Facebook Audience Network. Heyzap was acquired by Fyber (RNTS Media) in 2016 and its brand was later folded into Digital Turbine. Heyzap never published a public REST API; its developer surface was the mobile ad-mediation SDKs distributed via GitHub (github.com/Heyzap) and package registries. The heyzap.com domain is now parked/for-sale and the developer documentation site no longer resolves; this profile preserves the historical, first-party SDK artifacts that remain publicly available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Hopper
providers.description: Hopper Inc. is a Montreal-based online travel agency and B2B travel fintech company, founded in 2007 by Frederic Lalonde, Joost Ouwerkerk, and Dakota Smith. Its consumer mobile app pairs flight, hotel, car, and homes booking with proprietary price prediction, and monetizes a family of "for any reason" fintech ancillaries — Price Freeze, Cancel For Any Reason (CFAR), Change For Any Reason, and Disruption Guarantee. Through Hopper Technology Solutions (HTS), the company licenses those same ancillaries, agentic AI customer servicing (HTS Assist), white-label travel commerce (HTS Stays, HTS Cars, HTS Packages), and loyalty portals to airlines, banks, and travel providers including Capital One, Air Canada, Wizz Air, Porter, Avelo, and RBC. Hopper has raised more than $740 million from investors including Goldman Sachs, Brookfield, Citigroup, and Caisse de Depot et Placement du Quebec, and its shares trade on secondary marketplaces such as Forge Global and EquityZen ahead of a possible public listing.

providers.name: HTTP/2
providers.description: HTTP/2 is the second major version of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol, defined by the IETF in RFC 7540 and standardized in 2015. It optimizes use of network resources and reduces perceived latency by introducing a binary framing layer over a single TCP connection, with full request and response multiplexing across independent bidirectional streams. HTTP/2 uses HPACK header compression to eliminate redundant header data, credit-based flow control via WINDOW_UPDATE frames, stream prioritization through dependencies and weights, and server push via PUSH_PROMISE frames to proactively deliver anticipated resources. Core frame types include DATA, HEADERS, PRIORITY, RST_STREAM, SETTINGS, PUSH_PROMISE, PING, and GOAWAY, with the protocol preserving the existing HTTP semantics of methods, status codes, and headers while transforming how they are transported on the wire.

providers.name: Image API
providers.description: Image API was a digital business automation company specializing in the digitization, optimization, and management of business processes, forms, and content. The company has rebranded as Docufree and provides enterprise services including document scanning and imaging, digital mailroom automation, business process automation (RPA/AI), electronic signature, cloud document management, and outbound print and mail. Despite the legacy brand name "Image API", the company does not publish a public developer API or API portal. This repository tracks APIs, SDKs, and developer resources should they become available.

providers.name: Immunio
providers.description: IMMUNIO was a Montreal-based application security company (founded 2013) that built a real-time RASP (Runtime Application Self-Protection) platform to detect and block attacks against web applications and APIs without requiring code changes. Its product shipped as language-native agents for Ruby on Rails, Python (Django/Pyramid/Flask), Node.js/Express, Java, PHP, Scala and .NET, covering the OWASP Top 10 including Cross-Site Scripting and SQL Injection. The company raised roughly $8M from Bloomberg Beta, WhiteStar Capital, Real Ventures, Hoxton Ventures and BDC, and was acquired by Trend Micro in November 2017, where the technology was folded into Trend Micro's hybrid cloud and container security for the DevOps lifecycle. The immun.io and docs.immun.io properties have since been retired; the durable public surface today is the first-party agent libraries on RubyGems, PyPI and npm and the IMMUNIO GitHub organization.

providers.name: Impira
providers.description: Impira was a document-AI / intelligent-document-processing company that let business users turn unstructured content — documents, invoices, images, PDFs and webpages — into structured, queryable data by building and training extraction models without code. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Impira was acquired by Figma in early 2023 and its standalone product domains (impira.com, impira.io) no longer serve. Its GitHub organization (github.com/impira) survives, along with two first-party open-source Python libraries still published on PyPI: the official Impira Python SDK and DocQuery, an MIT-licensed document question-answering library. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record; there is no live API, developer portal, or hosted documentation surface remaining.

providers.name: Interana
providers.description: Interana was an event-based behavioral analytics platform for interactively querying large-scale event data (clickstream, product usage, and time-series data) at full resolution. Founded around 2013 in Redwood City, California by former Facebook engineers, it was used at scale by companies including Microsoft Bing. The company's team and technology were acquired by Twitter in March 2020; the standalone product was spun out and continued as Scuba Analytics (scuba.io), and the interana.com domain now redirects to its successor lineage. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical / defunct company record — there is no live public API surface, developer portal, or hosted documentation remaining. The only surviving first-party developer surface is the open-source Interana GitHub organization.

providers.name: iRobot
providers.description: iRobot Corporation is a Bedford, Massachusetts consumer robotics company best known for the Roomba robot vacuum and the Braava and Braava jet robot mop product lines. Founded in 1990 by MIT roboticists, iRobot pioneered the home cleaning robot category and has sold tens of millions of units worldwide. Its current portfolio includes the Roomba Max, Roomba Plus, and Roomba 100/200 series vacuums and combo (vacuum + mop) models, along with AutoWash and AutoEmpty docks, the iRobot Home App for scheduling and mapping, and a cleaning accessories and trade-in program. The proposed acquisition by Amazon was abandoned in January 2024 after regulatory pushback from the European Commission, after which iRobot underwent a major restructuring and layoffs. iRobot's revenue model is direct robot and accessory sales plus recurring consumables; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification, and its homesupport documentation explicitly notes that Wi-Fi connected Roombas do not have an open API. A community of unofficial reverse-engineered libraries (dorita980, rest980, pyirobot) exists but is not endorsed by iRobot.

providers.name: iZotope
providers.description: iZotope is a Cambridge, Massachusetts audio software company founded in 2001 that builds professional plugins for music production, audio repair, mixing, and mastering, with deep investments in AI-assisted and machine-learning-driven audio processing. Its flagship products include RX (audio restoration and dialogue repair widely used in film, TV, and podcast post-production), Ozone (mastering suite with Master Assistant), Neutron (mixing suite with Mix Assistant and Track Assistant), Nectar (vocal processing with Vocal Assistant), Tonal Balance Control (cross-session referencing), and the Music Production Suite bundle. iZotope's assistive technologies analyze incoming audio and propose starting-point chains, EQ curves, dynamics settings, and spectral repairs — historically among the first widely adopted AI features in the professional audio plugin market. iZotope was acquired by Native Instruments in 2024 and now sits inside Soundwide, the Francisco Partners- backed group that also includes Native Instruments, Plugin Alliance, Brainworx, iZotope, and others. Distribution is via desktop plugin formats (VST3, AudioUnit, AAX) for DAWs such as Pro Tools, Logic, Ableton Live, Cubase, Studio One, and Reaper; there is no public REST/HTTP developer API or SaaS developer platform. iZotope does license its DSP and ML-based audio algorithms to OEM partners as embedded SDKs (historically delivered to partners like Sony, Adobe, and Microsoft) and ships a small set of public GitHub repositories that are primarily internal C++/Lua tooling, embedded Linux Yocto layers for iZotope hardware, and accompanying code for academic audio research papers rather than a developer API surface.

providers.name: Light & Wonder
providers.description: Light & Wonder is a leading cross-platform global games company that develops and distributes gaming content across land-based casinos, mobile platforms, and online channels. The company's portfolio includes titles such as Dancing Drums Prosperity, Rainbow Riches, and Gold Fish, and includes subsidiaries SciPlay (mobile social gaming) and Grover Gaming. Light & Wonder operates customer-facing support portals for both gaming and iGaming partners.

providers.name: Microverse
providers.description: Microverse is an online education platform that trains people worldwide to become remote software developers, founded by Ariel Camus with the stated mission of connecting one million people to remote jobs by 2030. Its model pairs students across time zones for peer collaboration that mirrors distributed engineering teams, and it historically charged tuition only after graduates secured a job. Microverse also runs Leap, an English-practice platform for developers. It is a private, distributed company backed by investors including Y Combinator, Hack.VC, and General Catalyst. Microverse does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web presence and security posture.

providers.name: Multi-Tier Architecture
providers.description: A software architecture pattern that separates an application into logical layers or tiers, typically presentation, business logic, and data access layers, to improve modularity, scalability, and maintainability.

providers.name: Nova
providers.description: Nova (Nova Intelligence) is an agentic AI platform for SAP teams, used in production across documentation, functional design, development, and production issue resolution. Its capabilities include code intelligence and system visibility, fit-to-standard analysis mapping custom code to SAP standard, development acceleration for ABAP Cloud and BTP CAP, S/4HANA and Clean Core transformation support, and security vulnerability identification, with claims of a 3x productivity boost at 50% lower cost. Nova is an enterprise, demo-led product with no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time; it is backed by Accel and Battery Ventures. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which probed the company's public surface and found a domain-security posture and a Vanta trust center but no developer or API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: OMG Network
providers.description: OMG Network (formerly OmiseGO) is a Layer-2 plasma scaling solution for Ethereum, providing faster, cheaper value transfer and settlement on top of the Ethereum root chain via a Watcher / child-chain architecture. Surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The project has largely wound down: the omg.network site currently resolves to a redirect loop and the first-party @omisego/omg-js SDK last published in 2022. Sector: crypto.

providers.name: Opsani
providers.description: Opsani was an enterprise software company based in Redwood City, California that delivered an ML-driven cloud platform for Continuous Optimization as a Service (COaaS), automatically and continuously tuning cloud-native (Kubernetes) application configurations for the best balance of performance, availability, and cost. Opsani was acquired by Cisco in January 2022 and folded into the Cisco AppDynamics full-stack observability portfolio (subsequently part of Splunk). The company no longer operates an independent API surface — opsani.com now redirects to Splunk and docs.opsani.com no longer resolves. The one surviving public first-party artifact is the open-source Servo (servox) optimization agent, still published on PyPI and hosted at github.com/opsani.

providers.name: Peer Robotics
providers.description: Peer Robotics builds collaborative autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for manufacturing and warehouse material movement, designed to learn directly from humans to lower the cost and complexity of traditional automation. Its lineup includes the Peer 3000 collaborative mobile robot and the RM250 and RM500 AMRs (250kg and 500kg payloads) that handle pallets, trolleys, bin delivery, and machine tending through an intuitive human-robot dashboard interface. Backed by Techstars, the company operates a hardware and robotics product line rather than a public developer API surface; no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or GitHub repositories were found during enrichment probing.

providers.name: Peptone
providers.description: Peptone is a computational drug-discovery biotech building a Product Engine that targets intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs). It couples experimental measurement of disordered proteins in solution with enhanced-sampling simulation and generative machine-learning models to resolve transient, druggable pockets and design small-molecule drug candidates against them. Peptone describes its stack as an end-to-end Protein Engineering Operating System (PeOS); its open-source research tooling (protein-disorder prediction, ensemble generators, protein language models) is published on GitHub. Peptone is a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Photon Crystal Energy
providers.description: Photon Crystal Energy Technology Ltd. (广东光晶能源科技有限公司) is a China-based perovskite photovoltaic module manufacturer, founded May 2022 and headquartered in Foshan, Guangdong. The company commercializes full wet-process, full-printed perovskite PV modules for building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV), photovoltaic curtain walls, rooftop distributed solar, carports and architectural solar applications. Product families include standard, semi-transparent, textured, architectural color and solar tile modules, and the firm operates a 100 MW full-printed perovskite pilot line with IEC 61215 / IEC 61730 certification milestones. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing/corporate website but no public API, SDK, or developer surface.

providers.name: Placenote
providers.description: Placenote (Vertical AI Inc.) was a San Francisco company that built a cloud-hosted persistent augmented-reality toolkit — a "Persistent AR" SDK that let developers save, reload, and share ARKit/Unity spatial maps so digital content stays anchored to a physical location across sessions and devices. It shipped native client SDKs for iOS (Swift, via the PlacenoteSDK CocoaPod) and Unity, plus multiplayer AR samples such as PlaceInvaders and web mesh-viewing examples. The product was consumed as mobile SDKs backed by a cloud mapping/localization service rather than a public REST API, so no OpenAPI or web API surface was published. The company is now defunct: placenote.com no longer resolves to a live product (the domain is parked) and the docs/cloud service are offline. The Placenote GitHub organization and the published SDKs remain the only live, first-party developer surface, which is what this profile captures.

providers.name: Polestar
providers.description: Polestar is a Swedish premium electric performance car brand, originally spun out of Volvo Cars' Polestar Performance racing arm and now jointly owned by Volvo Cars and Zhejiang Geely Holding Group. Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden and publicly listed on Nasdaq (ticker PSNY) since 2022, Polestar designs and sells a lineup of battery-electric vehicles — Polestar 1 (discontinued hybrid GT), Polestar 2 (fastback), Polestar 3 (SUV manufactured in South Carolina and Chengdu), Polestar 4 (SUV coupe), and the upcoming Polestar 5 GT. The vehicles run a Google Automotive Services–based infotainment platform with Google built-in (Maps, Assistant, Play Store), and support NACS-compatible DC fast charging in North America. Polestar emphasizes sustainability through the Polestar 0 project (climate-neutral car by 2030) and partnerships with Circulor for battery traceability. Polestar does not currently publish or document a public developer API, SDK, OEM connected-car API, or partner integration programme; all known third-party Polestar integrations (Home Assistant, community Python clients) rely on reverse-engineering the unauthenticated customer app endpoints and are explicitly unsupported by Polestar.

providers.name: Sanderson Farms
providers.description: Sanderson Farms was the third-largest poultry producer in the United States, producing over 13 million chickens per week before being acquired by a joint venture of Cargill and Continental Grain in 2022 to form Wayne-Sanderson Farms. Headquartered in Laurel, Mississippi, the company operated processing facilities across the southeastern United States and was a Fortune 1000 company. As a large-scale agricultural and food production enterprise, Sanderson Farms does not offer public developer APIs. The company focused on poultry processing, supply chain management, and food safety operations.

providers.name: Shopkeep
providers.description: ShopKeep was a cloud-based iPad point-of-sale (POS) platform for independent retailers, restaurants, and quick-serve businesses, offering register, inventory, employee management, payments, and analytics. Founded in 2008 and backed by Canaan Partners, ShopKeep was acquired by Lightspeed Commerce in 2020 and its product and brand have since been folded into the Lightspeed Retail (S-Series) line. The marketing domain shopkeep.com now redirects to lightspeedhq.com/shopkeep, and support has migrated to shopkeep-support.lightspeedhq.com. ShopKeep never shipped a publicly documented developer API — a private "API beta" existed circa 2015 and the app backend at api.shopkeep.com remains live as a session-authenticated, undocumented internal service. No public OpenAPI, SDKs, developer portal, or API reference are published, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: SigOpt
providers.description: SigOpt was a machine learning experimentation and optimization platform whose API applied ensemble Bayesian and black-box optimization to tune model hyperparameters, run design-of-experiments, and track experiment metadata at scale. Developers integrated its REST API and first-party clients (Python, Java, R, scikit-learn, Spark, MATLAB) to drive automated hyperparameter search from their training loops. SigOpt was acquired by Intel in 2020 and its hosted API and platform were subsequently discontinued; sigopt.com now redirects to an Intel corporate redirector and the api./app./docs.sigopt.com hosts no longer resolve. The GitHub organization (github.com/sigopt) and the published client libraries remain public as historical, first-party artifacts, including an open-sourced server and optimization engine (sigopt-server, sigoptlite, libsigopt).

providers.name: Source.dev
providers.description: Source.dev builds AI-native software tooling that helps device manufacturers develop, build, and update the operating systems that run intelligent devices such as smartphones and electric vehicles. Its platform virtualizes source access (SourceFS) to cut Android checkout-and-build times from hours to minutes, replays build steps across languages and systems for faster CI, and uses LLM-driven merging (Harmony AI / Continuous Merges) to automatically resolve conflicts when applying security patches and OS upgrades to large, long-lived codebases like AOSP. The company is a sales/demo-led platform for device makers and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or self-serve documentation surface.

providers.name: Streamroot
providers.description: Streamroot was a Paris-founded video-delivery company (backed by Partech and Techstars) that built a peer-to-peer / multi-CDN "Mesh Delivery" and DNA SDK to offload live and on-demand video traffic onto a hybrid CDN+WebRTC peer mesh, reducing bandwidth cost and improving scale for broadcasters and OTT platforms. The developer surface was a client-side (browser and native player) delivery SDK distributed as video-player plugins (video.js, Clappr, hls.js, AVPlayer) rather than a server-side REST API. Streamroot was acquired by CenturyLink — now Lumen Technologies — in 2019 and folded into Lumen's CDN / Mesh Delivery product line. The standalone streamroot.io website and developer docs are offline; the surviving public assets are the (now Lumen-operated) GitHub organization and a set of official but deprecated npm player-plugin packages.

providers.name: Team Wildfire
providers.description: Team Wildfire develops jet engine-enabled fire suppression technology built to prevent catastrophic wildfire losses. Its mobile units, the "Hurricane" and "Storm Cell", apply fire retardant at scale to deny ground to advancing wildfires. The company offers fireground services, evacuation route hardening, asset protection, prescribed fire containment, and military base protection. Team Wildfire is a physical hardware and services company backed by Techstars; it publishes a marketing and services website but no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals available for a non-API company.

providers.name: Trinkerr
providers.description: Trinkerr is a Bengaluru, India algorithmic and social trading platform founded in 2021 by Manvendra Singh and Gaurav Agarwal, backed by Accel and India Quotient. Its mobile app (com.trinkerr.app) automates trades with ready-made algos crafted by industry experts for stock market enthusiasts. As of 2026-07-21 the company website trinkerr.com resolves to a GoDaddy parked page, no api/docs/developer subdomains resolve, and no developer portal, API documentation, or public API surface could be found, though the Google Play listing, LinkedIn, and YouTube channel remain live. Trinkerr does not currently publish a public API.

providers.name: Unigrid
providers.description: UNIGRID Inc. is a San Diego-based sodium-ion battery company founded in 2021 out of UC San Diego Ph.D. research by Dr. Darren H. S. Tan and Dr. Erik A. Wu. Its sodium chromium oxide (NCO) chemistry and alloy anode technology deliver fire-safe, fully passive batteries rated for 30,000+ cycles and -40C to 60C operation, sold as 12V starter batteries (Na+ Fleet), BMS-less rack modules (Na+ Module), residential energy storage (Na+ Casa), and DC rack systems for commercial, industrial, and data center use (Na+ Cleo). Cells are UN38.3 and UL 9540A certified. Backed by Transition VC, Ritz Venture Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Foothill Ventures via an oversubscribed $12M Series A (2024); shipped its first sodium-ion residential batteries in July 2026. UNIGRID publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Upollo
providers.description: Upollo is a startup founded by Cayden Meyer and backed by Index Ventures that helped subscription businesses find and convert repeat trialers, account sharers, and other high-intent users, with its detection surface reachable through integrations such as a Segment browser destination action and Pipedream API components. As of July 2026 its primary domain upollo.ai no longer resolves, its GitHub organization has no public repositories, and the only first-party package remaining in public registries is a 2022 Android SDK on Maven Central, so no live API surface is currently published to capture.

providers.name: Valor Water Analytics
providers.description: Valor Water Analytics was a San Francisco-based water analytics company that built financial data and dashboard tools for water utilities, including leak and revenue-loss detection. A Y Combinator, Imagine H2O, and 500 Global portfolio company, it was acquired by Xylem Inc. (completed February 2, 2018) and folded into Xylem's digital portfolio, now represented by the Xylem Vue platform. valorwater.com redirects to Xylem Vue, and no independent API surface remains published.

providers.name: Vayu Robotics
providers.description: Vayu Robotics is a Palo Alto, California robotics company building AI foundation models and sensing for autonomous mobile robots. Its stack spans Vayu Drive, an end-to-end learned, sim-first foundation model for mobility; Vayu Sense, a plenoptic sensor with embodied AI for high-resolution depth perception; a Vayu Sense Development Kit bundled with NVIDIA Orin; and Vayu One, a low-cost autonomous delivery robot for last- and middle-mile delivery. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company was acquired by Serve Robotics in September 2025. Enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Vela (FKA SR Labs)
providers.description: Vela Trading Technologies (formerly SR Labs) was a New York-based provider of low-latency market data feed handlers, execution gateways, and multi-asset trading platforms (SuperFeed, Metro, DMA Platform) for capital markets, surfaced here as an Insight Partners portfolio company. Vela merged into Exegy in May 2021 and no longer operates independently - tradevela.com is offline (HTTPS refused at probe time) while its DNS now points at Exegy mail infrastructure. Vela published no self-serve public HTTP API; SuperFeed was delivered via the open-source OpenMAMA API (C++/C#/Java) with an OpenMAMA Developer Program, and its 2017 OptionsCity acquisition exposed the now-decommissioned City Trader REST API, for which a first-party Python client survives on the legacy GitHub org. See the exegy profile for the successor company's current surface.

providers.name: Voxel Energy
providers.description: Voxel Energy is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company building energy-independent, off-grid data centers powered by on-site solar generation and second-life EV batteries over a DC microgrid architecture. Founded in 2025 by ex-Tesla engineers Casey Spencer, Max Pfeiffer, and Evan Schmidt, the San Francisco company delivers modular, prefabricated data center power systems that bypass multi-year utility interconnection queues, taking facilities from site selection to commissioning in months. Voxel Energy is an infrastructure hardware company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Yassir
providers.description: Yassir is an Algerian-founded super app providing on-demand and financial services across the Maghreb, sub-Saharan Africa, Canada, and France. Founded in 2017 by Noureddine Tayebi and headquartered in Palo Alto, California with operations centered in Algiers, the company bundles ride-hailing (Yassir Ride), food delivery (Yassir Food), grocery delivery (Yassir Market), and digital financial services (Yassir Cash) into a single consumer mobile app, alongside a Yassir B2B suite covering corporate mobility, meal benefits, procurement, parcel delivery, and digital gift cards. Yassir reports more than six million users, 130,000+ driver and merchant partners, and 4,500 employees operating across cities in Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, South Africa, Senegal, Canada, and France. The company has raised roughly $193M to date, including a $150M Series B led by BOND with participation from Y Combinator and DN Capital, and a global sponsorship partnership with Paris Saint-Germain. Yassir is a consumer and merchant-facing super app: it operates iOS and Android apps and a business portal (go-business.yassir.com) but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source project. Driver, courier, restaurant, and store onboarding flow through partner sign-up forms rather than a developer program, and the yassir-tech GitHub organization currently has no public repositories.

providers.name: Yield Protocol
providers.description: Yield Protocol was a decentralized Ethereum protocol that brought fixed-rate, fixed-term borrowing and lending to DeFi via collateralized debt vaults and its YieldSpace automated market maker for fyTokens (fixed-yield tokens). Backed by Paradigm, the protocol reached a v2 implementation before winding down, and the yieldprotocol.com site now displays a closure notice. There is no REST/HTTP API surface; Yield Protocol is consumed on-chain through its Solidity smart contracts, with first-party developer libraries (vaults, interfaces, YieldSpace AMM, utility contracts) published to npm under the official @yield-protocol scope and source code maintained across the github.com/yieldprotocol organization. This profile was surfaced as a Paradigm portfolio company and enriched from public package and repository evidence.

providers.name: Zenaton
providers.description: Zenaton was a workflow-as-code SaaS that let developers orchestrate background jobs, asynchronous tasks, and long-running business processes directly in application code (Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go) rather than wiring queues and cron by hand. Founded in France and backed by Accel and Point Nine, it processed 10M+ workflow executions monthly across 100+ companies. The product is now DISCONTINUED: the API and app hosts (api.zenaton.com / app.zenaton.com) no longer resolve, the client SDK repositories are archived (last active ~2020), and the zenaton.com domain redirects to co-founder Gilles Barbier's personal site. This profile is retained as verified history — the archived first-party SDKs remain published on npm, PyPI, Packagist, RubyGems, and pkg.go.dev.

providers.name: ZenGo
providers.description: ZenGo (also styled Zengo) is a consumer, non-custodial keyless cryptocurrency wallet that replaces the traditional seed phrase with MPC (multi-party computation) threshold signatures, splitting the signing key into two independent secret shares so there is no single point of failure or seed phrase to lose. Through its iOS and Android mobile apps and browser extension, users can buy, sell, trade and store Bitcoin, Ethereum and other crypto assets, connect to Web3 dApps and NFTs, and access features such as prediction markets. Founded circa 2018 (formerly KZen Networks) and backed by Insight Partners, the company also publishes open-source MPC and threshold-signature cryptography research through its ZenGo-X GitHub organization. As a consumer wallet product, ZenGo does not currently expose a public developer or product API.

providers.name: Zet
providers.description: Zet is a Bengaluru, India fintech that helps unserved and underserved Indians enter the formal credit system. Its core product is a fixed-deposit-backed (FD-backed) secured credit card starting at very low deposits, requiring no income proof or prior credit history, alongside credit-score monitoring and improvement tools, UPI payments, cashback rewards, a ZET Plus subscription tier, and a ZET Fixit credit-report error-resolution service. Backed by General Catalyst and Sequoia Capital, Zet operates as a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) and, as of this enrichment pass, exposes no public developer platform, API, OpenAPI, or documented developer surface.

providers.name: 21Vianet
providers.description: 21Vianet (VNET Group, Inc.) is the largest carrier-neutral internet and data center services provider in China, operating more than 50 data centers across over 20 cities with tens of thousands of cabinets and multi-terabit network port capacity. The company delivers hosting, managed hosting, interconnectivity, cloud, and hybrid IT infrastructure services to enterprise customers, and is the exclusive operator of Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform in mainland China through its Blue Cloud subsidiary. 21Vianet trades on Nasdaq under the ticker VNET. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; 21Vianet does not publish a public first-party developer API program, so most API artifacts are legitimately not applicable.

providers.name: 51Talk Koala (koalareading.com)
providers.description: koalareading.com serves 51Talk考拉外教官网, the marketing landing page for 51Talk's "Koala" online English foreign-teacher tutoring product aimed at Chinese K-12 learners. The site is a single-page property (hero banner plus footer) operated by 大生在线（深圳）文化传媒科技有限公司 of Shenzhen under ICP filing 粤ICP备2023085692号, with lizhen01@51talk.com published as the technical support contact. The profile entered the API Evangelist network as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio lead under the name "koalareading" (考拉阅读 / Koala Reading, a Chinese K-12 reading-comprehension edtech); the domain as observed on 2026-07-19 serves the 51Talk Koala product instead, and the relationship between the two is not asserted here. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, CLI, or machine-readable discovery surface, so this profile carries only probed evidence.

providers.name: Adelphic Mobile *
providers.description: Adelphic is an enterprise demand-side platform (DSP) for programmatic advertising, originally founded as a mobile-first programmatic buying platform and acquired by Viant Technology in 2017. The Adelphic DSP lets marketers plan, buy, and measure omnichannel campaigns across Connected TV, linear TV, mobile, desktop, streaming audio, and digital out-of-home from a single self-service interface, using Viant's people-based Household ID identity resolution to activate first- and third-party data and measure outcomes. It is offered as an enterprise SaaS platform with a hosted UI, online knowledge base, and certification/Programmatic University training rather than a public developer API; the adelphic.com domain now operates as a legacy redirect surface pointing to Viant's product pages. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile surfaced from GV.

providers.name: AgZen
providers.description: AgZen is an MIT spinout building RealCoverage, a sensor- and AI-based system that measures and controls how many droplets of crop-protection product land on every leaf during agricultural spraying. A boom-mounted computer-vision sensor analyzes spray coverage and droplet quality in real time and displays actionable data on an in-cab tablet, automatically optimizing foliar sprays on any sprayer as the operator drives. Growers use RealCoverage to cut chemical and water use by up to 50% while maintaining or improving efficacy and yield, with a typical payback in under a year. RealCoverage retrofits onto any generation of sprayer and won Crop Protection Solution of the Year in 2025. AgZen is headquartered at Greentown Labs in Somerville, Massachusetts and is backed by DCVC Bio, Material Impact, Astanor Ventures, and Syngenta Group Ventures.

providers.name: Alchemize
providers.description: Alchemize is an AI-enabled customs brokerage that automates import compliance workflows for importers. The Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company pairs licensed customs expertise with artificial intelligence to answer regulatory and tariff questions in minutes rather than days, reduce manual data-entry errors before shipments reach the port, and give importers a single view of every shipment, status, and communication via API, EDI, or web portal. Founded by Robert Hou (previously Confido, YC) and Samuel Fu (previously Netflix), Alchemize targets inefficiency in the $30B+ customs brokerage industry with an AI-native compliance and trade-operations platform.

providers.name: Amber Bio
providers.description: Amber Bio is a San Francisco-based biotechnology company founded in 2021 that is pioneering RNA-based gene editing. Its multi-kilobase RNA writing platform is designed to correct thousands of diverse mutations across a patient population with a single product, rather than requiring an independent therapy for each separate mutation. The company positions the approach as safe (minimal off-target effects), reversible, and capable of edits far larger than conventional base or prime editing, targeting previously undruggable genetic disease populations. Amber Bio launched publicly in August 2023 with an oversubscribed $26M seed round co-led by Playground Global and Andreessen Horowitz Bio + Health. It is a pre-clinical therapeutics company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: American Eagle Outfitters
providers.description: American Eagle Outfitters (AEO) is a global specialty retailer operating the American Eagle and Aerie brands, offering on-trend clothing, accessories, and personal care products at affordable prices. The company operates over 1,000 stores across the Americas and online, with a unified commerce strategy spanning e-commerce, mobile, and in-store experiences.

providers.name: American Electric Power
providers.description: American Electric Power (AEP) is one of the largest electric utilities in the United States, delivering electricity to more than 5.6 million customers across 11 states through its regulated utility subsidiaries including AEP Ohio, AEP Texas, Appalachian Power, Indiana Michigan Power, Kentucky Power, Public Service Company of Oklahoma, and Southwestern Electric Power Company. AEP operates the nation's largest electricity transmission network spanning over 40,000 miles and maintains approximately 31,000 megawatts of generating capacity.

providers.name: AMP Fund
providers.description: AMP (AMP PBC) is a public benefit corporation founded in 2025 by Anjney Midha, a former Andreessen Horowitz general partner, to build an independent "AI grid" — a pooled compute utility for frontier AI research teams. Rather than operating as a cloud provider or a conventional venture firm, AMP acts as an independent system operator: data center operators and labs contribute underutilized GPU capacity to a shared network, and member research teams draw base-load and burst compute from that pool at rates intended to sit below the volatile spot market. AMP pairs capital with compute, having raised roughly $1.3 billion for its first fund, and its PBC charter is structured so leadership can supply compute at cost without shareholder challenge. It has also committed a Public Wealth Fund of up to $500 million through 2030 toward education, workforce readiness, healthcare access, and economic resilience in communities affected by the AI transition. AMP publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Anadarko Petroleum
providers.description: Anadarko Petroleum Corporation was one of the world's largest independent oil and natural gas exploration and production companies, with operations across the United States, the deepwater Gulf of Mexico, and international locations including Mozambique and Ghana. Anadarko was acquired by Occidental Petroleum in August 2019 in a $55 billion transaction. The company was known for its operations in the Wattenberg Gas Field in Colorado, the Delaware Basin in Texas, and major deepwater projects. Anadarko did not offer public developer APIs; its technology integrations were primarily through enterprise systems for partners and joint venture operators.

providers.name: API Setu
providers.description: An Indian Government platform that provides a lot of APIS for KYC, business, education & employment

providers.name: Archive.org
providers.description: The Internet Archive

providers.name: Avicenna Biosciences
providers.description: Avicenna Biosciences, Inc. is a Durham, North Carolina drug development company using machine learning-enhanced medicinal chemistry to accelerate the lead-to-candidate optimization process for small molecule drug development. Founded in 2020 and led by president and CEO Chris Meldrum, the company applies computational screening of candidate molecules for drug-like properties to the "last mile" of small molecule discovery, targeting neurodegenerative disease programs including Rho kinase inhibitors for Parkinson's disease and ALS. Avicenna raised a seed round led by DCVC Bio and has signed research collaborations with partners such as Molecure S.A. The company publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable interface as of this enrichment pass; it is catalogued here as an AI-for-drug-discovery company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: AVO
providers.description: Avo (avonow.com) was a New York City-based "building commerce" and workplace-amenity platform, founded 2017-2018 out of Y Combinator (S18) and backed by Insight Partners and Kleiner Perkins with roughly $84M raised. It offered white-labeled same-day delivery of groceries, household goods, alcohol and personal-care items into residential and office buildings with no order minimums or delivery fees, plus on-site and virtual event programming and corporate gifting and recognition services, serving apartment communities, corporations, hospitals and universities across New York, New Jersey, Chicago and Houston. Avo published no API, SDK or developer portal, and as of a 2026-07-20 probe its domain resolves to a parked lander with no operational hosts; Y Combinator lists the company as inactive.

providers.name: Baan
providers.description: Baan (Baan Company N.V., originally The Baan Corporation) was a Dutch enterprise resource planning software vendor founded in 1978 in Barneveld, Netherlands by Jan Baan and later joined by his brother Paul Baan. Baan built one of the first genuinely component-based ERP suites, known for its Dynamic Enterprise Modeler (DEM), its Baan Tools 4GL development environment, and deep manufacturing and project-industry functionality. At its late-1990s peak Baan served roughly 3,000 customers and posted close to $700 million in revenue, making it one of the leading global ERP providers alongside SAP, Oracle and PeopleSoft. Following accounting controversy and a collapse in its share price, Baan was acquired by the British engineering group Invensys in 2000, sold on to SSA Global Technologies in 2003, and absorbed into Infor Global Solutions when Infor acquired SSA in 2006. Baan no longer exists as an operating company or an independent brand: the product line lives on as Infor LN, and the baan.com and baan.nl domains now permanently redirect to the Infor LN product page. Consequently this profile carries no first-party API surface of its own — any modern programmatic access to the Baan lineage is delivered through Infor LN REST APIs and the Infor ION API gateway on Infor's developer platform. Baan Company is listed by Battery Ventures as an exited investment.

providers.name: Berry Health
providers.description: Berry Health is a consumer digital-health company founded in 2023 by British-Ghanaian physician Dr. Fredua Akosa, headquartered in Accra, Ghana, that delivers online medical consultations, prescriptions and nationwide medication delivery for stigmatized and underserved conditions — sexual health, mental health and therapy, dermatology and skincare, and hair loss. Patients consult licensed doctors and clinical psychologists remotely, receive a personalized treatment regimen, and have medication delivered discreetly to their door. The company is licensed by Ghana's Health Facility Regulatory Agency and the Data Protection Commission. In June 2023 it raised a $1.6M pre-seed round co-led by Lightspeed Venture Partners — Lightspeed's first investment in Africa — and General Catalyst, with angels including Reddit COO Jen Wong, Thirty Madison co-founders Demetri Karagas and Steven Gutentag, and former US Surgeon General Regina Benjamin. Berry Health is a direct-to-consumer telehealth service; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK, and its consumer web properties (ourberry.com, app.ourberry.com, ourberry.io) are offline or parked.

providers.name: BerryKitchen
providers.description: BerryKitchen (Berry Kitchen) was an Indonesian online catering and prepared-meal company founded in Jakarta in 2012 by Cynthia Tenggara. It took online orders for lunch boxes and bento meals aimed at office workers across Jabodetabek, and ran the full chain itself - supplier sourcing, cooking, packaging and last-mile delivery - rather than acting as a marketplace. It was backed by East Ventures and 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and was acquired by Yummy Corp in 2019, with the team folded into Yummy Corp's Yummybox unit and the founder subsequently exiting. BerryKitchen never published a public API, developer portal or SDKs, and its domain is no longer operated by the company, so this profile is catalogued for historical and VC portfolio-graph purposes only.

providers.name: Bluebook
providers.description: Bluebook is a Stockholm, Sweden based software company building AI agents for accounting firms, accountants, and CFOs. The platform automates accounting workflows — reconciliations, accruals, accounts payable and receivable, month-end close, reporting, and accounting research — with the stated goal of a "zero-day close", and integrates with the general ledgers firms already run on, notably QuickBooks and NetSuite. The product surface is organized around Background Agents, Checklists (tasks, delegation, human-in-the-loop approvals, month-end close), and an Assistant covering FP&A, flux analysis, and accounting research. Founded in 2024 by Philip Andersson (CEO), Jonathan Andersson (COO), and Filip Stål (CTO), Bluebook went through Y Combinator (Winter 2025) and raised a $3M pre-seed led by EQT Ventures with participation from Y Combinator and angel investors from Affirm, OpenAI, and ElevenLabs. Bluebook is a product company, not an API provider: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: Callisto Media
providers.description: Callisto Media Inc. was a data-driven nonfiction book publisher founded in 2011 by chief executive Benjamin Wayne, operating from 1955 Broadway in Oakland, California (earlier Emeryville) and 220 West 19th Street in New York. It built a publishing model around demand signals rather than editorial instinct — mining point-of-sale data, search volume and category gaps to decide which instructional titles to commission, then matching each topic to a subject-matter author. Its primary imprint was Rockridge Press, best known for diet-, appliance- and condition-specific cookbooks and health titles, alongside the Callisto Kids line of pre-K through grade 12 workbooks, STEM, history and biography titles; the company said it had reached more than 50 million customers and ranked among the top fifteen US publishers by unit sales. It raised venture funding from 137 Ventures in 2017, then contracted sharply — cutting 35 percent of staff in July 2022 and a further 200 roles that October — and on 9 May 2023 its publishing assets were acquired by the independent publisher Sourcebooks in a deal funded by Penguin Random House, with Simon & Schuster Distribution Services continuing to distribute the titles. The brand now trades as Callisto Publishing, a Sourcebooks imprint: callistomedia.com 301-redirects to callistopublishing.com, which 301-redirects again to sourcebooks.com/callisto (chain verified 2026-08-02). Callisto Media is a consumer publishing business, not a software vendor, and has no public API surface. Probes on 2026-08-02 against callistomedia.com, www.callistopublishing.com and www.sourcebooks.com returned no machine-readable contract: /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/ai-plugin.json all 404, /.well-known/agent-card.json and /.well-known/agent.json both 404 (no A2A agent card), and every other probed path answered with the Sourcebooks single-page Magento storefront shell rather than a document. There is no developer portal, no GitHub organization (callistomedia, callisto-media and rockridgepress all 404 on the GitHub API), no published SDK on npm or PyPI, and no llms.txt.

providers.name: Carnival Corporation
providers.description: Carnival Corporation & plc is the world's largest cruise company operating eight cruise line brands (Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, Cunard, P&O Cruises, Costa Cruises, AIDA Cruises), plus the White Pass and Yukon Route. Carnival operates the OceanMedallion wearable IoT technology and mobile experience platform, the Carnival HUB app, the Princess MedallionClass app, and a portfolio of guest-facing digital experiences across its fleet of over 90 ships.

providers.name: Chiral Quest
providers.description: Chiral Quest (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. (凯瑞斯德生化（苏州）有限公司) is a Chinese pharmaceutical CDMO specializing in chiral chemistry. The company operates asymmetric catalytic hydrogenation, enzyme-catalyzed biosynthesis, flow chemistry, and process innovation technology platforms, using proprietary catalysts to develop and manufacture chiral drug molecules, key raw materials, regulatory starting materials (RSMs), and advanced GMP intermediates for global pharmaceutical companies. Founded around its asymmetric hydrogenation catalyst technology, Chiral Quest merged with Jiangxi Longlai in 2012 and with Suzhou Pengxu in 2020; the group employs more than 800 people including a research team of roughly 150. Suzhou is the parent company and R&D center, Jiangxi Longlai is the manufacturing base, and the company maintains offices in the United Kingdom and the United States. Chiral Quest is a brochure-site company with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable data surface.

providers.description: Toronto (CA) City Open Data

providers.name: Cosmic Robotics
providers.description: Cosmic Robotics, Inc. designs and operates autonomous construction equipment that takes on the hardest, most dangerous jobs on a construction site, coordinated as a fleet by a single software layer. Its first market is utility-scale solar energy, with expansion planned into data center construction. The flagship Cosmic-1A is a purpose-built robotic platform for solar panel installation, and Constellation is the coordination and control layer that plans, dispatches, and monitors the robot fleet across a jobsite. Founded in 2023 and based in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco, the company is backed by Y Combinator. Cosmic Robotics is currently a hardware and fleet-software company with no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and any agent-facing surfaces (such as its published llms.txt) as the API Evangelist network enrichment pipeline monitors it for a future API.

providers.name: Dognosis
providers.description: Dognosis is a Bengaluru, India deeptech company building olfaction AI that pairs trained detection dogs with machine learning to find disease from a single breath sample. Its product, BreathEasy, is a non-invasive breath test that produces a VOC-based cancer risk score for clinicians; a Phase 2 study published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology reported over 90% accuracy across seven cancer types, including at early and treatable stages. Dognosis is a portfolio company of Prosus Ventures. No public developer API is published today; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's digital, discovery, and security surface (an llms.txt is served; no /.well-known discovery documents are published).

providers.name: doubleAI
providers.description: doubleAI (legal entity AAI Technologies Ltd.) is an Israeli AI research company building Artificial Expert Intelligence (AEI) — AI systems that focus their full training capacity on a single technical domain to match and surpass leading human experts, rather than pursuing broad general intelligence. Its flagship system, WarpSpeed, is an AI GPU performance engineer that optimizes NVIDIA kernels, beating hand-tuned expert baselines on the majority of tested kernels. Founded in late 2023 by Prof. Amnon Shashua and Prof. Shai Shalev-Shwartz and based in Ramat Gan, Israel, the company has raised roughly $221M from Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Michael Dell, Bessemer Venture Partners, Pitango First, and Greenfield Partners at a valuation exceeding $1B. doubleAI publishes research and open-source code but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Eliyan
providers.description: Eliyan Corporation is a fabless semiconductor company in Santa Clara, California that develops chiplet and chip-to-chip interconnect physical-layer (PHY) IP for multi-die and AI infrastructure systems. Its NuLink die-to-die and die-to-memory PHY, NuLink-X chip-to-chip PHY, NuLink-XD 224G PAM4 SerDes for electro-optical modules, and NuGear chiplets let designers build multi-die architectures on standard organic substrates as well as advanced packaging, using simultaneous bidirectional signaling and support for UCIe, Bunch of Wires (BoW) and its own UMI interface. Eliyan licenses silicon IP and sells chiplets to semiconductor and hyperscale customers rather than operating a public web API; the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Endgame
providers.description: Endgame was an endpoint security company building endpoint protection, threat hunting, and adversary detection technology, and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. It no longer operates as an independent company: Endgame was acquired by Elastic N.V. and its technology was folded into Elastic Security. As of a live probe on 2026-07-20 the endgame.com domain is retained as a redirect only — the site root and every /.well-known/ discovery path answer HTTP 301 to https://www.elastic.co/security/endpoint-security. Endgame publishes no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI description, SDKs, CLI, webhook or event surface, changelog, status page, or MCP server of its own. This profile is retained as a verified-defunct record pointing at the successor product at Elastic; teams evaluating the technology should integrate against Elastic Security.

providers.name: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
providers.description: The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) is responsible for enforcing federal laws that make it illegal to discriminate against a job applicant or an employee because of the person's race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related conditions, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age (40 or older), disability or genetic information. EEOC publishes EEO-1, EEO-3, EEO-4, and EEO-5 workforce demographic data through the EEOC Explore data querying tool and downloadable bulk data files, but does not currently publish a public REST API for programmatic data access.

providers.name: French Address Search
providers.description: Address search via the French Government

providers.name: Gallatin AI
providers.description: Gallatin AI builds AI-powered software for defense logistics, giving military planners and logisticians decision advantage across the tactical, operational, and strategic levels of the supply chain. Its products include Navigator, an AI decision-support "S4" that aggregates and analyzes brigade-level logistics reports in real time to streamline resupply planning; Burrow, a DoD-compliant third-party logistics (3PL) solution managing vendor qualification, transportation, inventory, storage, and fulfillment for domestic and international operations; and Phalanx, an automated asset and in-transit visibility system combining traditional reporting with hardware sensors and computer vision. Founded by veterans of Scale AI, Palantir, Amazon Prime Air, and the DoD, the company emerged from stealth in 2025 and is backed by 8VC, Silent Ventures, Timeless, Moonshots Capital, and Banter Capital.
