providers.description: UK official public record API

providers.name: HAMI
providers.description: HAMI (Heterogeneous AI Computing Virtualization Middleware) is an open-source project that enables GPU virtualization and sharing for Kubernetes workloads, allowing multiple AI containers to share GPU resources efficiently.

providers.name: High Performance Software Foundation
providers.description: The High Performance Software Foundation (HPSF) is a Linux Foundation project supporting open source software for high-performance computing and scientific computing. It hosts projects including Apptainer, Spack, Kokkos, and E4S for building and deploying scientific applications at scale.

providers.name: iPrice
providers.description: iPrice Group is a Southeast Asian e-commerce aggregator and price-comparison platform headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It aggregates billions of live product offers and thousands of coupons from more than a thousand retail partners, letting shoppers compare prices, discover deals, and make more informed purchases across seven markets: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Hong Kong. Backed by 500 Global as part of the Asia Venture Group portfolio, iPrice serves tens of millions of monthly visitors and is known for its large SEA e-commerce dataset. As of this profile, iPrice does not publish a public consumer or partner API, developer portal, or OpenAPI; this record is a company profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kitchen United
providers.description: Kitchen United was a Pasadena, California ghost-kitchen operator that built and ran shared commissary kitchens — branded "Kitchen United Mix" — where multiple restaurant brands cooked out of one facility for delivery and pickup, including a chain of in-store food halls operated with Kroger. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others, the company wound down its physical footprint: in late 2023 it announced it would sell or close all remaining units and pivot to licensing its ordering software, and on 2024-03-14 sbe/C3 founder Sam Nazarian acquired its intellectual property and ghost-kitchen assets into a new holding company, Everybody Eats, alongside C3 and Nextbite. Kitchen United never published a public developer API, SDK, CLI or developer portal, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or package-registry artifact exists for it. The kitchenunited.com domain still resolves but now serves a residual WordPress shell whose only remaining page is unrelated SEO spam, so it should not be treated as a live developer surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Kiwilogic
providers.description: Kiwilogic.com AG was a German conversational-AI pioneer founded in 1999 in Hamburg, with a secondary office in London. It built the Lingubot platform, one of the earliest commercial natural-language dialogue engines for the web, which let online businesses deploy interactive virtual characters that acted as store greeter, customer-support agent, product specialist and entertainer across web sites and mobile messaging channels. The company was backed by Earlybird Venture Capital (approximately $5.2M reported) and won a best-German-startup award in 2000. The Lingubot business was acquired in the mid-2000s and folded into Artificial Solutions, whose Teneo conversational-AI and voice-AI platform is the commercial successor; the kiwilogic.com domain now issues a blanket redirect to teneo.ai. Kiwilogic operates no independent developer portal, documentation, or API surface today, and this profile is maintained as a historical company record within the API Evangelist network rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Klima
providers.description: Klima was a Berlin-based consumer climate-action company operated by Climate Labs GmbH, founded in 2019 by Markus Gilles, Jonas Brandau and Andreas Pursian-Ehrlich. Its mobile app let individuals calculate a personal carbon footprint from a lifestyle questionnaire, then offset those emissions through a subscription funding Gold Standard and Verified Carbon Standard projects, with in-app education and reduction tips layered on top. The company raised roughly USD 16.7M across a 2020 seed round and a EUR 10M 2022 Series A, backed by HV Capital, Keen Venture Partners, Headline, 468 Capital and Adjacent. Klima was acquired by Wren on April 30, 2025; klima.com is now a single-page wind-down notice and the company exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable artifacts.

providers.name: Krosslinker
providers.description: Krosslinker (KrossLinker) is a Singapore-based deep-tech advanced-materials company that designs and manufactures silica aerogels — among the most insulating solids known — using a proprietary, water-based and scalable chemistry and manufacturing platform the company calls Aspire. Its product line spans Cryar super-insulating aerogel composite board, QuintAero ultra-light silica aerogel powder, KrossShield SR Pro aerogel-powered cooling paint, and a flexible aerogel blanket in development, serving cold-chain pharma and food packaging, building and construction passive cooling, and industrial insulation. Krosslinker operates from CleanTech III in Singapore and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a physical-materials manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web, product, and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Krunch
providers.description: Krunch is an on-demand product studio that delivers product management, engineering, and marketing as a service, using AI and code to compress the build cycle for its clients. The team was accepted into the 500 Startup Accelerator program in Silicon Valley and markets prior engagements with Alibaba, Google, Camunda, New Relic, Polkadot, and Bowtie. Krunch operates as a services agency rather than an API provider - as of this enrichment pass it publishes a single-page marketing site with a Calendly booking link and no public developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind.

providers.name: Lab0
providers.description: Lab0 (lab0.ai) is a San Francisco company in the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch building an "AI forward-deployed engineer" for B2B SaaS: agentic systems that automate enterprise software implementation and post-sales delivery. The platform runs discovery, solution design, configuration, custom integration build, testing and go-live in parallel, with the stated goal of compressing 3-12 month deployment cycles down to weeks. Its connector agents profile a customer instance (tables, fields, auth model, processes) to produce a connector spec, then generate the integration, auth, field mappings, callbacks and write-back workflows as staged changes a human team reviews, with every write previewed as a controlled dry-run before it touches the customer instance. Named target systems are ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, Workday and Adobe AEM, plus custom APIs. As of this profile Lab0 is pre-launch as a developer platform: it publishes a marketing site and an llms.txt, but no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or self-serve sign-up. It is sold as a managed engagement via founder contact and demo booking.

providers.name: Lattice Engines
providers.description: Lattice Engines was a predictive marketing and AI-driven B2B customer data platform that applied machine learning to first-party CRM and marketing automation data combined with external firmographic, technographic, and intent signals in order to score accounts and leads, prioritize sales outreach, and power account-based marketing programs. The company was acquired by Dun & Bradstreet in 2019 and the product was rebranded D&B Lattice before being folded into the Dun & Bradstreet Rev.Up ABX go-to-market platform. Lattice Engines no longer operates as an independent brand and publishes no developer surface of its own: as of the 2026-07-19 enrichment probe, www.lattice-engines.com returns HTTP 301 to dnb.com, the apex domain returns HTTP 403, api.lattice-engines.com returns HTTP 404, and developer./docs. subdomains do not resolve. This profile is retained as a historical record; the live successor surface is documented in the api-evangelist dun-and-bradstreet repository.

providers.name: Leaders In Tech
providers.description: Leaders In Tech (LIT) is a leadership accelerator for startup founders and technology executives, founded in 2015 and part of the Y Combinator Summer 2015 batch. Based in San Francisco, it runs cohort-based fellowship programs grounded in experiential, feedback-rich learning: the Founder Fellows Program (10 months, Series A to pre-IPO), the Grove Fellows Program (6 months, pre-seed and seed founders), the Executive Fellows Program (6 months, senior leaders), plus corporate workshops and retreats. Its primary teaching methodology is T-groups — small-group experiential learning built on shared observation, collective accountability and repeated practice — a model brought from the Stanford Graduate School of Business by co-founder Dr. Carole Robin. Leaders In Tech reports more than 350 alumni founders running companies valued at over $75B. It is a leadership-development organization, not a software or API provider: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Lemnos Labs
providers.description: Lemnos Labs, Inc. is an early-stage deeptech venture capital firm that invests at the earliest phases of hardware company formation, helping founders better understand their customer, anticipate problems, and leverage their assets. Lemnos contributes engineering, manufacturing, marketing, and financial capital alongside the check, and deliberately keeps a minimal public presence — its site is a single page that lists only the active portfolio. That portfolio spans robotics and autonomy (Built Robotics, Fort Robotics, Path Robotics, Scythe Robotics, Simbe Robotics, Petra), agricultural technology (FarmWise, Ceres Imaging), autonomous cargo aviation (Elroy Air), space data and precise positioning (Spire, Swift Navigation), simulation (Duality), video analytics (Lumeo), and physical security (Rhombus). Lemnos itself publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital entity whose value to the network is its portfolio graph — several of its companies are meaningful API providers in their own right.

providers.name: LetGo
providers.description: letgo is a mobile-first classifieds and secondhand marketplace where individuals list, browse, and negotiate on used goods — vehicles, electronics, furniture, and household items — with chat-based buyer/seller messaging and location-based discovery. Launched in 2015 and backed by Naspers/OLX, letgo grew into one of the largest peer-to-peer resale apps in the United States before combining its US operation with OfferUp in 2020. The letgo brand and letgo.com continue to operate as a regional classifieds marketplace; the live site currently serves a Turkish-language catalog (category browsing, search, and an otoplus vehicles section per its robots.txt). letgo publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs. The application-internal API under /api/ is explicitly disallowed in robots.txt, and the entire site sits behind an Akamai bot-mitigation challenge, so no developer surface could be verified.

providers.name: Level Headed Games
providers.description: Level Headed Games (Level Headed, LLC) is an independent video game studio building an original online cooperative multiplayer game. The studio describes itself as passionate about making immersive experiences that let players express themselves and have fun with their friends, and is building "fun, surprising, and heavily social video game worlds." Development is community-involved, with an open call for co-op players to join an Alpha playtest community and an email announcement list. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes only a single-page marketing site with no announced title, no public developer surface, and no API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: liangyihui
providers.description: liangyihui is a company operating the web property at liangyihui.net, surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, no API reference or documentation, no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL definition, no first-party SDK packages on any public registry, and no working /.well-known/ discovery surface. The public site is served from Chinese CDN infrastructure (Tengine / kunlunpi) behind a bot shield that answers every path with the same obfuscated JavaScript challenge, so the property soft-404s and cannot be crawled or inspected. A live API host does exist at api.liangyihui.net: it answers its root with a Tomcat-served "Welcome to LYH!" page and returns genuine HTTP 404s for probe paths, indicating a real but private first-party backend for the company's own clients rather than a documented public API. This profile records verified DNS, TLS and endpoint posture only; no API artifacts have been fabricated.

providers.name: Liberate Bio
providers.description: Liberate Bio is a genetic medicine company developing in vivo cell therapies that reach cell populations beyond the liver, the long-standing limit of lipid nanoparticle delivery. Its RAPTOR discovery platform is a scalable in vivo screening system that identifies LNP delivery vehicles which work with existing biology to carry genetic payloads into immune cells in blood, bone marrow, and the spleen. Liberate Bio applies that delivery capability to in vivo CAR-M (chimeric antigen receptor macrophage) programs, reprogramming monocytes and macrophages to eliminate disease-driving cells without ex vivo manipulation, with programs in hematologic oncology and in autoimmune disease via depletion of pathogenic B-cell populations. Founded by Nessan Bermingham, Theresa M. Reineke, and Michael Mitchell, and led by CEO Shawn Davis and CSO Walter Strapps, the company raised $31M from Khosla Ventures in October 2025. It is pre-clinical and publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Light Chaser Animation Studios
providers.description: Light Chaser Animation Studios (追光动画) is a Chinese computer-animation film studio founded in March 2013 by Gary Wang (王微), founder and former CEO of the video platform Tudou, and headquartered in Beijing. The studio produces original CG animated feature films for the Chinese domestic market, drawing on Chinese mythology, literature and history. Its released titles include Little Door Gods (小门神), Tea Pets (阿唐奇遇), Cats and Peachtopia (猫与桃花源), White Snake (白蛇：缘起), New Gods: Nezha Reborn (新神榜：哪吒重生), White Snake 2: Green Snake (白蛇2：青蛇劫起), New Gods: Yang Jian (新神榜：杨戬) and Chang An (长安三万里). Light Chaser is a film-production company rather than a technology vendor: its public web presence is a bilingual WordPress marketing and recruiting site at zhuiguang.com, and as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind.

providers.name: LocalGov.jp
providers.description: Japan grants and subsidies (central J-Grants + 1,916 municipalities)

providers.name: Monell Chemical Senses Center
providers.description: The Monell Chemical Senses Center is "the world's only independent, non-profit scientific institute dedicated to interdisciplinary basic research on the senses of taste and smell." Founded in 1968 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Monell conducts chemosensory research organized around three strategic themes: Healthy Senses and Happy Lives, Senses for a Thriving Planet, and Nourishing Our Future. The center runs postdoctoral training, the Dr. Charis Eng Monell Science Apprenticeship Program, the Monell Science Entrepreneurship Program, an Academic Partnership Program, and the Monell Insiders corporate partnership program. Monell does not publish a public developer API surface; its "product" is knowledge disseminated through scholarly publications and conferences.

providers.name: Myhero
providers.description: TradeHero (operated by My Manisku Pte Ltd, Singapore) is a gamified virtual stock-trading and social-investing mobile app. Users start with 100,000 virtual dollars to practice trading risk-free across 28 stock exchanges and 10 currency pairs, follow and copy validated top traders, learn through a short-tutorial investing academy, and compete on cash-prize leaderboards backed by real-time market data. Founded by former Wall Street trading-platform and Electronic Arts mobile-gaming veterans, and backed by venture firms including 500 Global, KPCB China, and IPV Capital. The public surface is a consumer mobile app and marketing site; no developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published.

providers.name: Nobel Prize
providers.description: Open data about nobel prizes and events

providers.name: Node.js
providers.description: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that enables server-side execution of JavaScript. It uses an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model that makes it efficient for building scalable network applications, APIs, and real-time services. Node.js itself is a runtime and standard library, not an API service, so no OpenAPI specification is published.

providers.name: Parrot
providers.description: Parrot (useparrot.com) is a Y Combinator-backed startup (Spring 2026 batch) building an agentic, all-in-one management platform for collision and auto repair shops. Its AI agents automate estimate auditing, parts procurement (voice agents that compare supplier quotes), insurance claim follow-ups, invoice reconciliation, tax filing, payments and invoicing, inventory management, team coordination, and inbound call handling, and it integrates with CCC ONE, Audatex, and Mitchell 1. Parrot does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: PeakMetrics
providers.description: News articles and public datasets

providers.name: Premier Laboratory Services
providers.description: Premier Laboratory Services is a locally-owned clinical diagnostics laboratory based in Scott, Louisiana, providing testing services to healthcare facilities and providers. Its menu includes LCMS-MS drug testing, PCR testing (respiratory, UTI, STD, women's health, and wound), and blood/clinical chemistry testing, with more than 200 tests available and an advertised 24-hour average turnaround. The company emphasizes local representatives and personalized service, and offers a patient results portal. It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation.

providers.name: Raytheon
providers.description: Raytheon is an American aerospace and defense manufacturer operating as a business of RTX Corporation, the world's largest aerospace and defense company. Raytheon designs, develops, and produces advanced defense systems including precision weapons, air and missile defense systems, sensors, radar, electronic warfare, command-and-control solutions, and cyber capabilities for the U.S. military and allied governments worldwide. Key products include the Patriot missile defense system, StormBreaker smart weapons, RAIVEN electro-optical/infrared sensor suites, and advanced electronic attack systems. Raytheon also develops world-class logistics software through the EAGLE team supporting production management, technical manual development, and product support data. No public developer API or machine-readable specification is available at this time; Raytheon's software solutions are deployed within government program contracts.

providers.name: Represent by Open North
providers.description: Find Canadian Government Representatives

providers.name: Seneca Systems
providers.description: Seneca Systems is a govtech company whose stated mission is "building better government" through software that helps public-sector organizations serve constituents and modernize internal operations. Its flagship product is Romulus, a constituent-relationship and case-management platform aimed at local and state government. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: Sticky
providers.description: Sticky was a San Francisco-based biometric SaaS company (founded 2009, offices in New York and Stockholm) whose cloud platform ran large-scale market research studies using webcam eye tracking and emotion analytics — measuring what real people saw, missed, and felt when engaging with websites, ads, email, and video. A Northzone portfolio company, Sticky was acquired by Tobii on 2017-05-17 and integrated into Tobii Pro, continuing as "Sticky by Tobii". The sticky.ai website is no longer online and Sticky publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Tokaido Health
providers.description: Tokaido Health is an AI-native medication steerage platform anchored in behavioral economics that helps employers and health plans cut pharmacy costs. It identifies same-or-better medications that cost less - via site-of-care steerage, biosimilar substitution, formulary optimization, and polypharmacy reconciliation - and pairs recommendations with incentives that get members to switch, layering on top of the existing PBM and benefits stack. Founded in 2025 in San Mateo, CA; raised $25M in May 2026 led by Norwest Venture Partners. No public API surface is published.

providers.name: Tout
providers.description: Tout (ToutApp) was a sales engagement platform offering email tracking, templates, and analytics for sales teams, and a 500 Global portfolio company. ToutApp was acquired by Marketo in 2017 and became Marketo Sales Connect; toutapp.com now 301-redirects to the Marketo Sales Connect product page on business.adobe.com following Adobe's acquisition of Marketo. Tout no longer operates a standalone developer or API surface.

providers.name: ToutApp
providers.description: ToutApp was a sales-engagement platform founded in 2011 by Tawheed Kader that gave sales teams email templates, email tracking, campaigns, and analytics for outbound selling, backed by Andreessen Horowitz. Marketo acquired ToutApp in May 2017 and folded the product into Marketo Sales Connect (later part of Adobe after Adobe acquired Marketo in 2018). The company is defunct as a standalone business - toutapp.com now redirects to Adobe's Marketo Sales Connect page - and no independent ToutApp API or developer surface remains publicly available.

providers.name: Transphorm
providers.description: Transphorm was a GaN (gallium nitride) power-semiconductor company based in Goleta, California, known for its GaN-on-Si cascode FET technology used in power supplies, fast chargers, motor drives, solar inverters, and EV charging. It was acquired by Renesas Electronics in June 2024, and transphormusa.com now redirects to the Renesas GaN power-discretes product line. Transphorm publishes no public web API surface.

providers.name: Travelguru
providers.description: Travelguru was an Indian online hotel-booking brand that grew into one of India's larger hotel-distribution platforms before Yatra.com acquired a 100% stake in July 2012. The brand has since been folded into Yatra: travelguru.com and the Travel Partner Web hotel extranet now redirect to yatra.com, the former Desiya B2B distribution host is offline, and Travelguru publishes no standalone developer portal or public API surface today. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Trooly (Airbnb)
providers.description: Trooly, Inc. was a machine-learning trust and safety startup that scored the trustworthiness of individuals using publicly available data and digital footprints, offering its Instant Trust screening service to businesses for trust and safety management, risk assessment, and customer relationship use cases. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Trooly was acquired by Airbnb and ceased operations on June 19, 2017, shutting down its external APIs; its technology was absorbed into Airbnb's trust and safety systems and Trooly, Inc. remains an Airbnb subsidiary. trooly.com is now a parked domain and no living API surface exists.

providers.name: TTAGG
providers.description: TTAGG was a social media analytics startup founded in October 2011 in Fayetteville, Arkansas, and backed by 500 Global. It rebranded as DataRank in 2013, providing brand managers with tools to monitor and rank conversations about their brands and competitors across social media, blogs, forums, and e-commerce sites. DataRank was acquired by Simply Measured in 2015, which was in turn acquired by Sprout Social in 2017. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API; datarank.com redirects to sproutsocial.com and ttagg.com is parked.

providers.name: Tulipshare
providers.description: Tulipshare is a London-based impact investor and shareholder advocacy group that uses activist investing to push for ethical and sustainable change at the world's largest companies. It leverages shareholder proposals, direct board and ESG-team engagement, and other shareholder rights on behalf of foundations, asset managers, universities, and pension funds. Backed by Speedinvest. Its consumer website (tulipshare.com) went offline in 2026 and the company publishes no public API surface.

providers.name: Twinn Health
providers.description: Twinn Health builds preventive whole-body MRI infrastructure for early disease detection, pairing AI-structured imaging reports and longitudinal health data pipelines with imaging providers and wellness clinics in the UK, Saudi Arabia, and the wider Middle East. Founded at Imperial College London, validated with UK-based NHS clinicians, and backed by 500 Global and Wa'ed Ventures, it also offers expert MRI report interpretation for individuals. Twinn Health publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Twolabs
providers.description: Twolabs is a San Francisco robotics startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building Tobi, a modular humanoid robot platform for builders to collect data, train skills, and deploy autonomous robots. The two-founder company vertically integrates hardware and AI in-house, streamlining robot training into a Record, Upload, Train, Deploy workflow, and is initially focused on caregiving applications in senior-care facilities such as feeding, dressing, medication reminders, mobility support, and companionship. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; it does not yet publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: UberSense
providers.description: UberSense was a Boston, Massachusetts sports-technology startup whose mobile app provided slow-motion video capture and analysis for coaching athletes, from recreational to Olympic and professional levels. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), UberSense was acquired by Hudl in September 2014 and its technology folded into Hudl's sports video analysis products. The ubersense.com website is now defunct (a decommissioned Heroku app) and the company publishes no public API surface.

providers.name: UK Companies House
providers.description: UK Companies House Data from the UK government

providers.name: Umbala
providers.description: Umbala (Umbala Labs, formerly Umbala Technologies / UmbalaTv) is a Vietnamese consumer video and camera technology startup backed by 500 Global. It built the UmbalaTv short-video and livestream mobile app and later the Umbala Network blockchain platform, including StreamX decentralized live video streaming and the CameraX camera AI/AR engine. The company currently maintains a minimal site at umbala.io and publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its historical umbala.tv domain now redirects to unrelated third-party content.

providers.name: Umoja Labs
providers.description: Umoja Labs is the company behind Umoja Protocol, a decentralized finance product described as a next-gen yield vault token (YVT) protocol for earning yield on blue-chip cryptocurrencies, with automated hedging strategies and the $UMJA token. A 500 Global portfolio company. As of July 2026 the umoja.xyz website and app are offline and the Medium blog has been dormant since April 2025; no public API, developer documentation, or first-party SDKs were found.

providers.name: United Dwelling
providers.description: United Dwelling was a Los Angeles-based real estate development company founded in 2018 by venture capitalist Steven Dietz to address the affordable housing shortage by converting underused garages and backyards into accessory dwelling units (ADUs). The company offered studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom zero-net-carbon units ranging from 328 to 647 square feet and handled permitting, construction, financing, and property management end to end. It raised a $10 million Series B in May 2020 led by Alpha Edison with participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners. The business appears to have wound down - its website has lapsed (Squarespace account expired) and its Los Angeles location is marked closed as of mid-2026 - and it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Unmannd
providers.description: Unmannd (Unmannd Autonomy Pvt Ltd) is an India-based defense technology company backed by Accel and Speciale Invest, engineering autonomous drones under the banner of aerial dominance. Its TITAN 30 is an autonomous defense-logistics drone with a 30 kg max payload, 60 km/h cruise speed, 20,000 ft operational ceiling, and 30 km max range; its FURY counter-UAS interceptor was announced as launching in Q1 2026. Unmannd is a hardware/defense company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Upcode Academy
providers.description: UpCode Academy was a Singapore-based coding school offering short bootcamps and part-time courses (SQL, Python, Web Development with Ruby on Rails, Data Science, Computer Vision, IoT) taught by industry practitioners. Operated by 40 Tasks, a 500 Global portfolio company whose earlier product was the LOCO location-based search app at 40tasks.com. The company appears defunct - upcodeacademy.com serves a Cloudflare 522 dead-origin error (a bare default server page by December 2025) and 40tasks.com no longer resolves in DNS (domain-squatted since about 2023). No public API surface was found.

providers.name: Upthere
providers.description: Upthere was a consumer cloud-storage company backed by GV and founded by former Apple software engineering chief Bertrand Serlet. Its Upthere Home app was designed as "one home" for photos, videos, music, and documents, stored directly in the Upthere cloud with fast search, private sharing, and shared "Loops". Western Digital acquired Upthere in 2017 and later discontinued the service; upthere.com now 302-redirects every path to a retired Western Digital support notice. Upthere never published a public developer API, and no API surface remains — this profile records the company identity and the posture of the surviving domain.

providers.name: Ureeka
providers.description: Ureeka was a community and mentorship platform for small businesses, surfaced as a Bullpen Capital portfolio company. The company no longer operates a standalone product - the ureeka.biz domain (www and apex) now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to zenbusiness.com, and no developer, documentation, or API surface remains. Probed 2026-07-21 by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: Ursula
providers.description: Ursula is a Brazil-based AI startup building AI-native characters. Founded by an Emmy-winning team with experience at Pixar, Unity, Blizzard, and Google, it combines LLMs, symbolic AI, and long-term memory to power emotionally aware digital beings that evolve and connect with users across games, apps, and digital worlds. Ursula is a seed-stage Prosus Ventures portfolio company surfaced for the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API program, and at enrichment time its Framer-hosted website at ursula.ai returned HTTP 404 (site unpublished) while the domain retained valid TLS and SPF/DMARC records.

providers.name: Usermind
providers.description: Usermind was a Seattle-based journey and experience orchestration platform that captured and analyzed contextual data at every touchpoint of the customer journey to personalize experiences across channels, and was named a Leader in The Forrester Wave Journey Orchestration Platforms, Q2 2020. Backed by a16z and Menlo Ventures, the company was acquired by Qualtrics (announced July 20, 2021); usermind.com now redirects to qualtrics.com and no independent Usermind API surface remains.

providers.name: UTURN
providers.description: UTURN Entertainment is a Saudi Arabian digital media and entertainment company founded in 2010 that has grown into the largest Arabic Multi-Channel Network (MCN) in the MENA region. It produces original digital content — comedy sketches, gaming (Saudi Gamer), women's lifestyle (Unseen), sports (MLM), and MMA (MMAnia) shows — distributed across YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, and other social platforms, and offers content creation, sponsored content, branded content, and digital production services to brands. A 500 Global portfolio company, UTURN publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: ValueCo
providers.description: ValueCo (ValueCo Metrics SAS) is a Paris-based fintech building an objective ESG market view from the proprietary ESG scores of asset managers and institutional investors. Its platform aggregates investor-side scoring into a consensus view so listed and non-listed companies can understand how the market actually perceives their ESG performance and improve their strategies. A Techstars portfolio company, ValueCo serves asset managers, institutional investors, enterprises, and ESG contributors; it currently publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Veo Robotics
providers.description: Veo Robotics built FreeMove, a 3D depth-sensing computer vision safety system that lets standard industrial robots work safely alongside people by monitoring workcells and dynamically restricting or resuming robot motion. Backed by GV and Lux Capital, the company's assets - including FreeMove and related intellectual property - were acquired by Symbotic in July 2024, and veobot.com now redirects to symbotic.com. Veo Robotics published no public API surface; this profile records the company in the API Evangelist network graph.

providers.name: Vistel
providers.description: Vistel (Beijing Zhiyuan Huitu Technology, 致远慧图) is a Beijing-based medical AI company founded in 2016 that applies computer vision and deep learning to ophthalmology. Its NMPA Class III and EU CE certified software analyzes fundus images to screen for diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and age-related macular degeneration, paired with its RC350 and RX350 fundus cameras and VS550 vision screener, plus telemedicine and image management systems. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, Cyberport Hong Kong, and Redhill Capital. Vistel publishes no public developer portal or API surface.

providers.name: Westwing
providers.description: Westwing is Europe's number one "Beautiful Living" e-commerce company, present in more than 20 European countries. It is a premium one-stop Home & Living destination that offers design lovers a carefully curated selection of the best design brands alongside its own Westwing Collection, created by an in-house team in Munich, spanning furniture, sofas, lighting, beds, rugs, textiles, outdoor and home accessories. Westwing (Westwing Group SE) is a publicly listed company and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Point Nine. It publishes no public developer API; its primary machine-facing surface is a root-level /llms.txt policy that governs how LLMs and agents may use its catalog and editorial content.

providers.name: WorkAmerica
providers.description: WorkAmerica was a skilled-labor hiring marketplace that connected job seekers, employers, and educators to close the skills gap - "connecting education to employment, exclusively for the skilled labor force" (archived homepage, 2017). A 500 Global portfolio company, it appears defunct - the workamerica.co domain expired (registrar suspension page captured December 2018) and now 301-redirects to an unrelated Indonesian website. No public API, developer portal, GitHub organization, or packages were found.

providers.name: wutwut
providers.description: wutwut is a former Slow Ventures portfolio company listed on the firm's portfolio page. Its domain, wutwut.com, is suspended - HTTPS refuses connections and HTTP has served a registrar ICANN contact-verification suspension page since 2021 - and no public product, developer program, or API surface could be found. This profile remains in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead record documenting that probe result.

providers.name: Wuxi Vision Pro
providers.description: Wuxi Vision Pro Co., Ltd. (无锡蕾明视康科技有限公司, "蕾明视康"), founded in 2010, is a Chinese ophthalmic medical device company that develops, manufactures, and sells intraocular lenses (IOLs) and other high-end ophthalmic consumables, focused on foldable IOL R&D and domestic substitution of imported lenses. Headquartered in Wuxi with a Shanghai branch, and backed by Qiming Venture Partners. No public API or developer surface was found.

providers.name: Xirrus
providers.description: Xirrus was an enterprise Wi-Fi company that made high-density wireless access points and arrays managed through the Xirrus Management System (XMS), which exposed a management API that community client libraries were built against. Backed by Canaan Partners, Xirrus was acquired by Riverbed Technology in April 2017 to power cloud-managed Wi-Fi in SteelConnect, and Riverbed sold the Xirrus Wi-Fi business to Cambium Networks in 2019. The Xirrus brand has since been absorbed into Cambium Networks' enterprise Wi-Fi portfolio, and xirrus.com now redirects to cambiumnetworks.com, leaving no independent Xirrus API surface.

providers.name: XtremIO
providers.description: XtremIO was an Israeli all-flash enterprise storage company founded in 2009 and acquired by EMC in May 2012 for $430 million, with the technology continuing as the Dell EMC XtremIO all-flash array product line. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners, XtremIO no longer operates independently and publishes no public developer program — xtremio.com is a parked domain retained under Dell brand protection, with DNS still actively managed by Dell.

providers.name: Y&S
providers.description: Y&S is the company behind ReservaTurno, an Argentine consumer appointment-booking platform (active circa 2014-2023) that let users reserve turnos at hair salons, beauty and aesthetics centers via web and mobile apps, and gave centers a free online agenda and client-communication system. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of 2026-07-21 the website returns 404 on all pages and no public API or developer surface was found.

providers.name: Zions Bancorporation
providers.description: Zions Bancorporation, National Association is a nationally chartered bank and bank holding company headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, with roughly $87 billion in total assets. It is a super-regional operating a single national bank charter across seven regional divisional brands - Zions Bank, Amegy Bank, California Bank & Trust, National Bank of Arizona, Nevada State Bank, Vectra Bank Colorado, and The Commerce Bank of Washington - serving consumers, small business, and commercial/treasury clients across the Western United States. On the open-finance front Zions runs NO public first-party developer API portal: developer.zionsbank.com and api.zionsbank.com do not resolve, and its business digital-banking surface (Treasury Internet Banking at treasurygateway.zionsbank.com) is credential-gated with no published API reference or downloadable OpenAPI. As a large depository institution it is subject to the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule, but Zions has not published a first-party data-access API or a documented FDX-conformant endpoint; consumer-permissioned data sharing in practice reaches Zions through third-party aggregators (Plaid/MX/Finicity/Akoya) rather than a first-party API surface.

providers.name: Avistone
providers.description: Beijing Avistone Biotechnology Co., Ltd. is a commercial-stage innovative biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Beijing, China, focused on the research, development, and commercialization of first-in-class and best-in-class oncology therapies. Founded in 2012 (originally Beijing Pearl Biotechnology) and renamed Avistone in 2018, the company has two approved cancer drugs on the market: Vebreltinib (万比锐®), a MET inhibitor approved for non-small cell lung cancer and glioma indications and included in China's National Reimbursement Drug List, and Andamertinib (安比锐®), an EGFR exon 20 insertion inhibitor approved in 2026 for advanced NSCLC. Avistone maintains a pipeline of additional candidates (ANS01 through ANS09) across solid-tumor indications and is backed by IDG Capital. The company publishes no public developer API or programmatic surface; this profile captures its corporate and investor identity.

providers.name: Blackcart
providers.description: Blackcart is a Try Before You Buy (TBYB) platform for ecommerce merchants that lets online shoppers order products, receive them at home, and pay only for what they keep during a trial window. The platform pairs a proprietary fraud and AI order-decisioning engine with storefront integrations for Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, WordPress, and custom storefronts, and charges merchants a revenue share on kept items rather than upfront or integration fees. Founded circa 2019 and backed by a 2021 US$8.8M Series A (investors include 500 Global), Blackcart exposed a Beta REST API (order cancellation, refunds, product/store endpoints) documented on Stoplight. As of this enrichment pass its primary domains (blackcart.com and its *.blackcart.com subdomains) return Fastly "unknown domain" errors and blackcart.co serves only a JavaScript redirect shell, indicating the public product and developer surface is offline or the company has wound down.

providers.name: Brainspec
providers.description: BrainSpec is a medical software company whose FDA-cleared, cloud-based platform BrainSpec Core makes MR spectroscopy (MRS) accessible to clinicians and researchers, turning standard MRI scanners into a non-invasive "virtual biopsy" that measures brain-chemistry metabolite concentrations. The web application ingests MRS data in DICOM, RDA, TWIX, SDAT and G-file formats across GE, Siemens and Philips 3T scanners, applies a linear-combination post-processing model, and interfaces directly with hospital PACS to pull companion images and push screenshots and reports back. BrainSpec is backed by DCVC and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass BrainSpec publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; integration is delivered as a managed clinical/PACS service.

providers.name: Breathe Technologies
providers.description: Breathe Technologies, Inc. is a California-based medical device company that develops wearable and continuous ventilation systems for patients with chronic respiratory insufficiency and neuromuscular disease. Its flagship Life2000 Ventilation System is an FDA-cleared, ultra-lightweight ventilator that adapts from a stationary compressor to a wearable device, supporting both acute and chronic respiratory failure in home and institutional settings. Breathe Technologies is a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company and is now part of the Hillrom family (acquired by Baxter), with the Life2000 system distributed under Baxter respiratory care. This is a hardware medical device manufacturer with no public developer, API, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: BSOS
providers.description: BSOS is a Web3 infrastructure company building compliant financial rails across emerging markets and institutional finance. It operates two core lines of business - compliant stablecoin payment networks for cross-border USD settlement in emerging markets (starting with Latin America), and institutional-grade real-world asset (RWA) tokenization systems for leading financial institutions in Asia. Its products include Velaro for cross-border USD payments, RWA SuiteX for asset tokenization, and SUPLEX for supply chain finance. BSOS is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Cabot Oil & Gas
providers.description: Cabot Oil & Gas was an independent oil and gas company engaged in the development, exploitation, exploration, production, and marketing of natural gas and oil properties in the United States. In 2021 it merged with Cimarex Energy to form Coterra Energy, which operates across the Permian Basin, Marcellus Shale, and Anadarko Basin.

providers.name: Causera
providers.description: Causera was an early-stage Palo Alto, California startup surfaced as a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. Enrichment probing found no operating public surface: the company's own domain, causera.com, resolves to a GoDaddy parked-domain lander rather than a product site, and the only verified live property is the dormant "Causera Engineering" GitHub organization (github.com/causera, created 2011-06-22), which holds a single public repository — a fork of mbleigh/princely, a Rails wrapper for the PrinceXML PDF library — last pushed in August 2011 with no public members. Causera therefore appears to be a defunct 2011-era company with no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no published specifications. This profile records the negative result so future enrichment rounds do not re-probe from scratch.

providers.name: Intello
providers.description: Intello was a SaaS management platform providing SaaS discovery, usage analytics, and spend optimization for IT teams seeking visibility and control over their software portfolio. The product line is now offered by Zylo, an enterprise SaaS spend optimization and AI consumption cost management platform. There is no separate public developer API.

providers.name: Jewelbots
providers.description: Jewelbots makes smart, codable friendship bracelets designed to teach kids (primarily tween girls) to code. The wearable is an Arduino-compatible, Bluetooth Low Energy device built on a Nordic nRF chipset that friends can program with an Arduino IDE library and firmware, with a companion iOS/Android app for pairing and messaging. The project is largely open source: the Jewelbots GitHub organization publishes the Arduino library, firmware, companion app, and hardware/toolchain repositories. Jewelbots was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company; jewelbots.com now runs as a Shopify storefront. It is a hardware/firmware and education company rather than a web API provider, and exposes no first-party public HTTP/OpenAPI API.

providers.name: Lawdingo
providers.description: Lawdingo is a New York City legal-technology company founded in 2012 by Nikhil Nirmel and Dan Langevin, and a Y Combinator Winter 2013 alum backed by Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst and AltaIR Capital. It launched as a consumer marketplace for talking to a lawyer on demand, then pivoted to serving law firms and corporate legal departments with remote paralegals and contract attorneys — legal research, litigation drafting, court filing and discovery support — delivered through an online platform where clients assign work, share documents, deposit funds and track hours. Lawdingo publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs, and as of this enrichment pass its lawdingo.com and www.lawdingo.com domains both return HTTP 404 "Site Not Found" from an unpublished Framer site, leaving no live web surface to harvest.

providers.name: LessonLeap
providers.description: LessonLeap was a group-learning platform for children, offering small-group online classes and tutoring aimed at helping kids keep learning outside of school. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. LessonLeap has since been acquired by Preply, the language-learning and tutoring marketplace, and no longer operates as an independent product. lessonleap.com now serves only a single-page acquisition notice directing visitors to Preply. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no developer portal, no documentation, no API, no SDKs or packages, no public GitHub repositories, and no published .well-known discovery documents — this profile is retained as a historical company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: MisterBnB
providers.description: misterb&b (operated by SFO84 inc.) is the world's largest LGBTQ-focused travel and accommodation booking platform, connecting gay and queer travelers with LGBTQ-friendly rentable lodging including private rooms, apartments, hotels, and homestays across more than 200,000 cities worldwide. Founded in Paris in 2014 by Matthieu Jost, François de Landes, Marc Dedonder, and Julien Delon and now headquartered in San Francisco, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. Enrichment found no public developer/API surface: the consumer site is Cloudflare-protected (403 to non-browser clients), the github.com/misterbnb organization holds only open-source Ruby/JS forks, and no well-known, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP artifacts are published. Host-partner connectivity is offered indirectly via channel managers such as Guesty rather than a documented public API.

providers.name: Notch
providers.description: Notch (formerly OrderEZE/ChefHero) brings the restaurant supply chain online, digitizing the paper-driven process of wholesale food ordering and order taking between restaurants and their distributors. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Toronto, the platform spans four product surfaces — Order Manager and Invoice Manager for buyers, AP Manager for restaurant accounts payable, and AR Manager for distributor accounts receivable — handling order placement, invoice management, reconciliation, payment collection, and payment processing for food and beverage suppliers and buyers. Notch keeps ordering and finance workflows in sync through one-way and two-way connectors to accounting and ERP systems including QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, NetSuite, Xero, and Microsoft Dynamics 365, plus CSV import/export. Notch does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its accounting/ERP connectivity is delivered through its own connectors and the third-party Rutter unified accounting API, so Notch operates as an API consumer rather than an API provider. (This profile covers Notch the restaurant-to-supplier ordering and AR/AP automation company at notch.financial, and is unrelated to "Notch Pay," the African payments company at developer.notchpay.co.)

providers.name: Remarkable AI
providers.description: Remarkable AI is an AI-powered customer engagement platform for consumer and ecommerce brands, delivering 1:1 personalized messaging across email, SMS, and social channels. Its products span Retain (personalized win-back campaigns for lapsed customers), Support (24/7 AI-plus-human customer service that converts tickets into sales), and Acquire (AI-driven social engagement on TikTok, YouTube, X, and Reddit). The platform is used by 1,000+ ecommerce brands including SAXX, Hyper Skin, Nomadica, Kindra, StoryWorth, and Hot Topic, with plans starting at $1,500/month. Remarkable AI was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Riggs Distler
providers.description: Riggs Distler & Company is an energy and utility infrastructure construction firm operating since 1909. Now part of Centuri Group, the company delivers electric transmission and distribution, natural gas, renewable energy, emergency response, and heavy civil services across the United States and Canada. Riggs Distler is a field-services contractor with no public developer APIs or developer portal.

providers.name: Shennon Biotechnologies
providers.description: Shennon Biotechnologies is a San Francisco based biotechnology company accelerating drug development by screening millions of single cell-cell interactions to identify novel therapeutic agents for cancer and autoimmune disease. Its proprietary TCELERATOR platform combines ultrafast single cell-cell interaction mapping with proprietary AI models to discover new targets and develop more effective medicines. The company is backed by DCVC and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes a corporate marketing site but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: SmartRent
providers.description: SmartRent, Inc. (NYSE: SMRT), founded in 2017 and headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a leading provider of smart home and smart property technology for the multifamily and single-family rental industries. Its platform pairs smart hardware — smart locks, thermostats, water/leak sensors, access control and hubs (Alloy, Fusion) — with cloud-based SaaS for property operators to manage connected devices at scale. Products span smart apartments, building and common-area access control, asset protection and leak monitoring, parking management, self-guided tours, Virtual Intercom (browser-based WebRTC entry), and community/resident WiFi. SmartRent exposes a partner-gated REST API and a Phoenix Sockets real-time API for integrations, but publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI; API credentials are provisioned on request via api@smartrent.com. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: 58.com
providers.description: 58.com (58同城, "58 Tongcheng") is China's largest online classifieds and local-services marketplace, often called the "Chinese Craigslist." Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Beijing, it operates listings across recruitment and jobs, real estate and housing (Anjuke), used goods (Zhuanzhuan), automobiles, local services, and yellow-pages business directories. Formerly listed on the NYSE (WUBA), it was taken private in 2020 by a Warburg Pincus / General Atlantic consortium. Its 58 Open Platform (open.58.com) exposes payment, recruitment/jobs data, housing, local-service information, security risk-control, marketing, and social capabilities to approved third-party partners via reviewed developer accounts and API keys. Backed historically by DCM Ventures.

providers.name: Aerohive
providers.description: Aerohive Networks was a cloud-managed networking company founded in 2006 by Changming Liu and headquartered in Milpitas, California. It pioneered controller-less, cloud-managed Wi-Fi and edge networking, managed through its HiveManager NG (later ExtremeCloud IQ) platform and access points. Aerohive went public on the NYSE under the ticker HIVE and was acquired by Extreme Networks in a deal that closed on 2019-08-09 for approximately $272 million. The company operated an Aerohive Developer Program with a public developer portal (developer.aerohive.com) and REST APIs for the HiveManager NG / ACS platform, plus a GitHub organization of reference applications. Following the acquisition the products were folded into ExtremeCloud IQ, and the legacy Aerohive API and its developer portal were retired (shutdown dated 2026-07-12), with integrators directed to migrate to the Extreme Platform ONE Developer Portal. This profile enriches the historical Aerohive API surface; it is a retired/acquired provider.

providers.name: American Tire Distributors Holdings
providers.description: American Tire Distributors (ATD) is one of the largest independent suppliers of replacement tires in North America, distributing passenger, light truck, medium truck, and specialty tires from more than 110 distribution centers. ATD delivers over 30.5 million tire units annually to more than 85,000 delivery points across the United States and Canada, serving independent tire dealers, automotive service centers, and retailers.

providers.name: Apollo Education Group
providers.description: Apollo Education Group is a private education provider that operates the University of Phoenix and other institutions offering associate's, bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degree programs. The organization focuses on providing accessible higher education to working adult learners through online and in-person formats.

providers.name: Apollo Global Management
providers.description: Apollo Global Management is a global alternative investment manager providing private equity, credit, and real assets strategies to institutional and individual investors. With over $840 billion in assets under management, Apollo focuses on delivering excess returns through its private equity, credit, and real assets business segments. Apollo does not have a public developer API program.

providers.name: Area 1 Security
providers.description: Area 1 Security was a cloud-native email security company that built preemptive anti-phishing and business-email-compromise (BEC) protection, discovering and blocking phishing campaigns before they reached inboxes. It could be deployed inline (MX/journaling) or via API connectors to Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. Cloudflare acquired Area 1 Security in February 2022 for approximately $162 million and folded the technology into its Zero Trust / Cloudflare One platform, where it is now sold as Cloudflare Email Security. The independent area1security.com developer surface has been retired and now redirects to Cloudflare; the product API and documentation live under the Cloudflare developer platform.

providers.name: Armstrong World Industries
providers.description: Armstrong World Industries (NYSE: AWI) is a leading global designer and manufacturer of innovative commercial and residential ceiling, wall, and suspension system solutions. Armstrong offers a broad portfolio of ceiling and wall products across mineral fiber, fiberglass, wood, metal, and specialty substrates for use in commercial construction and renovation projects worldwide. The company provides BIM content, product data, and specification tools for architects and designers but does not offer a public developer API.

providers.name: Astraea
providers.description: Astraea is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) clinical trial automation platform that gives pharmaceutical sponsors, biotechs, and CROs an AI operating system for clinical development. Founded by Joshua Wang and Sanmay Sarada, the platform orchestrates specialized AI agents across the full biometrics lifecycle - standards mapping, data normalization, CDISC mapping, SDTM and ADaM dataset generation, TFLs/TLFs, SAP, eCRFs, Define-XML, QC, and submission documents - turning a protocol and raw study data into FDA-submission-ready output. Astraea is positioned as sponsor-run software rather than a CRO: it runs inside the customer's own secure environment so clinical data never reaches Astraea's servers, with 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and audit-ready, standards-native traceability. The company reports serving 10+ global pharma and biotech sponsors with 30-50% faster reporting cycles.

providers.name: Bash Shell
providers.description: GNU Bash (Bourne Again SHell) is the default Unix shell and command-line interpreter on most Linux distributions and macOS. Developed by Brian Fox for the GNU Project as a free replacement for the Bourne shell, Bash provides a rich scripting language with variables, control structures, functions, I/O redirection, job control, and process management. Bash scripts are the foundational automation tool for system administration, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps tooling, and software build systems.

providers.name: Belk
providers.description: Belk is a privately-held American department store chain headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, serving the southeastern United States. The company sells clothing, handbags, jewelry, beauty products, and home goods. Belk operates an omnichannel retail model with physical stores and an online marketplace. Supplier and marketplace integrations are handled via EDI through value-added networks, with order management integration available through Rithum (formerly CommerceHub) and other channel management platforms.

providers.name: Bitfusion
providers.description: Bitfusion (Bitfusion.io) was a GPU virtualization startup whose FlexDirect software pooled and disaggregated GPUs across a network so machine learning and AI workloads could share accelerator hardware on demand. VMware acquired Bitfusion in August 2019 and folded the technology into vSphere as "vSphere Bitfusion." VMware/Broadcom later declared End of Availability for vSphere Bitfusion effective May 2023, with end of maintenance in May 2025. The independent company no longer operates and the bitfusion.io domain no longer resolves; there is no independent, active public API surface remaining for this provider.

providers.name: Bizible Marketing Analytics
providers.description: Bizible was a B2B marketing attribution and revenue analytics platform that connected marketing activity to pipeline and revenue across advertising, web, CRM, and marketing-automation channels. Acquired by Marketo in 2018 and subsequently by Adobe, the product now ships as Adobe Marketo Measure (formerly Bizible); the bizible.com domain 301-redirects to Adobe and its product documentation has moved to the Adobe Experience League. It has no standalone public developer portal, OpenAPI, or API reference of its own — integration is handled through Adobe/Marketo Measure and CRM connectors.

providers.name: Bringy, Inc.
providers.description: Bringy, Inc. is a digital insurance brokerage operating in Egypt, founded in 2019 and licensed by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA License #100). Through its website and iOS/Android mobile apps, Bringy lets consumers compare, select, purchase, and manage insurance policies online, positioning itself as a digital insurance advisor that guides customers from policy selection through claims and compensation. Coverage lines include car, business, medical, personal-accident, and home insurance, with payment via Visa, Mastercard, Meeza, mobile wallets, and installment providers (ValU, Sympl, Souhoola). Bringy was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a consumer marketing site and blog but no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Brinker International
providers.description: Brinker International is a leading casual dining restaurant company that owns, operates, and franchises Chili's Grill & Bar and Maggiano's Little Italy. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Brinker operates over 1,600 Chili's locations across 29 countries and over 50 Maggiano's locations in the United States. The company leverages digital ordering platforms, loyalty programs, mobile apps, in-restaurant kiosks, and point-of-sale integrations for restaurant operations, running a unified open-source e-commerce environment built on Red Hat (RHEL, Satellite, Lightspeed) and using Prismic CMS for digital content management. Brinker operates an SSO-gated partner/franchise API developer portal at developer.brinker.com for onboarding partners; there is no public, self-service developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open GitHub organization. Consumer-facing surfaces are the Chili's and Maggiano's mobile apps and websites and their loyalty programs.

providers.name: Clarabridge
providers.description: Clarabridge was a customer experience management (CEM) and conversational analytics company known for its natural-language-understanding platform that analyzed unstructured customer feedback — contact-center transcripts, chat, email, surveys, social media, and online reviews — to surface sentiment, emotion, effort, intent, and emerging topics. Qualtrics acquired Clarabridge in 2021, and the technology has since been integrated and rebranded inside the Qualtrics XM platform: Clarabridge Studio became Qualtrics XM Discover and Clarabridge Engage became Qualtrics Connect. Clarabridge no longer operates an independent developer portal or public API; its capabilities are now delivered through Qualtrics. This profile is retained as a company/brand record in the API Evangelist network with an acquisition pointer to Qualtrics.

providers.name: ClimateAI
providers.description: ClimateAi (climate.ai) is a climate-intelligence company that turns global weather, climate and extreme-event modeling into decision-grade forecasts for agriculture, food and beverage, manufacturing, energy, finance, retail and federal/defense customers. Its ClimateLens products cover risk screening, monitoring and adaptation, and its developer surface is the LensConnect API — a REST weather and climate data API addressed by latitude and longitude that returns 30+ years of history (1995-present, ERA5-backed), a fixed 30-year climatology baseline, and AI-stitched probabilistic forecasts running from short-term through seasonal (~6 months) in a single continuous timeline, at ~25 km resolution with optional 1 km downscaling for select variables. A separate ClimateAI Platform gateway handles accounts, users, roles, permissions, device API keys and product routing.

providers.name: CloudCraze
providers.description: CloudCraze was an enterprise B2B commerce platform built natively on the Salesforce Platform, letting businesses launch online B2B storefronts fast and scale them on top of Salesforce CRM data. Brands including Coca-Cola, Cummins, Ecolab, Land O' Lakes, and WABCO ran global B2B commerce on it. Salesforce acquired CloudCraze in 2018 and folded it into the Salesforce B2B Commerce product line (now the legacy "B2B Commerce for Visualforce" managed package), where its Apex/JavaScript developer surface continues to be documented on Salesforce Developers. CloudCraze no longer operates as an independent company or developer portal — www.cloudcraze.com redirects to Salesforce B2B Commerce.

providers.name: CSX Corporation
providers.description: CSX Corporation is a Class I freight railroad operating one of the largest rail networks in the eastern United States, serving 23 states with roughly 20,000 route miles of track. CSX moves bulk commodities, intermodal shipments, and merchandise for industrial customers and operates the ShipCSX customer portal for shipment management, EDI integration, and freight tracking.

providers.name: Dada
providers.description: Dada Group (Dada Nexus, NASDAQ: DADA) is a leading Chinese instant retail and local on-demand delivery platform, headquartered in Shanghai and founded in 2014. It operates an open, crowdsourced delivery network of more than one million rider partners serving supermarkets, pharmacies, fresh-food and restaurant merchants across thousands of counties and cities, alongside merchant fulfillment products such as the Haibo in-store logistics system and the Dada Youjian picking service. Now integrated into the JD.com ecosystem, its core delivery brand was rebranded to JD Instant Delivery (京东秒送) in May 2024. Dada runs a merchant Open Platform (开放平台) for order, delivery-tracking and fulfillment integrations. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Doubleclick
providers.description: DoubleClick was a pioneering digital advertising technology company founded in 1995 and backed by Canaan Partners; it went public in 1998 and was acquired by Google in 2007-2008. Its products were absorbed into what is now the Google Marketing Platform: DoubleClick Campaign Manager became Campaign Manager 360, DoubleClick for Publishers (DFP) became Google Ad Manager, and DoubleClick Bid Manager became Display & Video 360. DoubleClick no longer operates as an independent company and maintains no independent developer portal, website, or API host of its own. The surviving developer/API lineage (dfareporting / doubleclick-advertisers) is served entirely through Google's developer platform. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; there is no independent provider surface to enrich.

providers.name: Edgeware
providers.description: Edgeware AB was a Swedish video-delivery technology company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Stockholm, known for its TV CDN, origin and media server, and streaming video-delivery products used by telecom operators and broadcasters to run OTT and IPTV services. Backed by Creandum, it listed on Nasdaq Stockholm in 2016 and was acquired by Agile Content (Agile Content S.A.) in 2020. The Edgeware brand has since been consolidated into AgileTV: edgeware.tv now redirects to agiletv.com/edgeware/, and its developer/technical documentation lives under docs.agilecontent.com (AgileTV Origin & Media Server, CDN Solutions, Subtitling). Edgeware no longer operates as an independent company or publishes an independent developer API surface.

providers.name: EMCOR Group
providers.description: EMCOR Group is a Fortune 500 mechanical and electrical construction, energy, and facilities services company headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut. It operates through three segments, EMCOR Construction Services, EMCOR Building Services, and EMCOR Industrial Services, delivering hyperscale data center construction, hospital support services, energy efficiency programs, and green building solutions. This repository captures the public APIs, developer resources, and machine-readable artifacts associated with EMCOR Group.

providers.name: Ermetic
providers.description: Ermetic is a cloud security company founded in 2019 that pioneered cloud infrastructure entitlement management (CIEM) as part of a unified, identity-first cloud-native application protection platform (CNAPP) spanning AWS, Azure, and GCP. The platform provides full visibility into permissions and entitlements across multi-cloud environments, least-privilege and just-in-time access controls, anomaly detection against behavioral baselines, and compliance and cloud security posture management (CSPM). Ermetic raised roughly $100M from investors including Accel, Norwest Venture Partners, Glilot Capital Partners, and Target Global, and was acquired by Tenable in October 2023 for approximately $265M. The product now ships as Tenable Cloud Security; the ermetic.com domain redirects to Tenable, and the former Ermetic customer application (us.app.ermetic.com) exposes a login-gated REST API.

providers.name: Excelero Storage
providers.description: Excelero was a software-defined storage company whose flagship product, NVMesh, delivered distributed, low-latency shared NVMe block storage across a server cluster with a Kubernetes CSI driver and a management CLI. Excelero was acquired by NVIDIA in 2022 and no longer operates as an independent company; its NVMesh product and documentation are now part of NVIDIA. The former excelero.com domain 301-redirects to nvidia.com/en-us/excelero/. This profile was surfaced as a battery-ventures portfolio company; the enrichment pipeline found no independent Excelero API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal to harvest.

providers.name: Flowcharts
providers.description: Flowcharts are a visual modeling technique used across software engineering, systems analysis, business process design, and education to depict the steps, decisions, and flow of a process or algorithm. Within an API context, flowcharts are used to model workflows, integration patterns, retry logic, authentication flows, and the orchestration of services. This topic indexes the standards, notations, libraries, and rendering tools that practitioners use to create and exchange flowcharts as part of API documentation, design, and operations.

providers.name: FTP
providers.description: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is a standard network protocol used to transfer files between a client and a server over a TCP-based network. FTP is a protocol specification rather than a vendor or HTTP API, and is documented primarily in IETF standards (RFC 959 and follow-ups) and in widely deployed server implementations such as vsftpd, ProFTPD, Pure-FTPd, and FileZilla Server. This index links to the canonical specifications and documentation for the protocol; no OpenAPI is generated because FTP is not an HTTP API.

providers.name: FUNDING.yml
providers.description: GitHub configuration file specifying funding platforms and links for project sponsorship, displayed as a Sponsor button on the repository page. Supports platforms including GitHub Sponsors, Patreon, Open Collective, Ko-fi, Liberapay, Tidelift, Buy Me a Coffee, IssueHunt, Polar, thanks.dev, LFX Mentorship, and custom URLs.

providers.name: General Electric
providers.description: General Electric Company has reorganized into separate publicly traded companies: GE Aerospace, focused on jet engines and aviation systems, and GE Vernova, focused on energy and power generation. GE HealthCare was spun off in 2023. No unified public developer API portal is currently published by GE Aerospace or GE Vernova.

providers.name: igetget
providers.description: igetget is the English name for 得到 (Dedao), a Chinese knowledge-service and lifelong-learning platform operated by Beijing Siwei Zaowu Information Technology Co., Ltd. (北京思维造物信息科技股份有限公司), the company behind Luojisiwei (罗辑思维) founded by Luo Zhenyu. The app sells curated courses, expert lectures, ebooks, and audiobooks across finance, economics, law, management, psychology, and self-improvement, alongside an enterprise edition, a web edition, and the annual "Time's Friend" (时间的朋友) New Year's Eve lecture. It is a consumer content product; enrichment found no public API specification or developer documentation, only an open-platform (开放平台) login surface at open.igetget.com. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Indoo Rs
providers.description: indoo.rs (indoo.rs GmbH) was a Vienna, Austria based Indoor Positioning System (IPS) startup founded in 2010 that built indoor mapping, localization, and routing technology plus a mobile SDK for developers and device manufacturers. Its solution combined Wi-Fi, BLE/iBeacon, sensor fusion, and dead-reckoning (SLAM-style) navigation to deliver real-time indoor positioning with accuracy down to roughly two meters. Backed early by Speedinvest, indoo.rs was acquired by Esri on February 28, 2019; its software became part of Esri's ArcGIS Indoors and its Vienna headquarters became the Esri R&D Center Vienna focused on IPS. The indoo.rs domain now redirects to the ArcGIS Indoors product, and the company no longer operates an independent public API or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Speedinvest portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: JD Business
providers.description: JD Business is the enterprise-facing arm of JD.com (Jingdong), one of China's largest technology and retail companies, offering B2B procurement, supply-chain, and corporate purchasing services to businesses. JD.com operates across retail, logistics, technology, health, and industrials, and runs the JD Open Platform (JOS / "Zeus" Developer Center) at jos.jd.com, where third-party merchants and partners integrate with JD's e-commerce, order, product, and logistics systems. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and is being enriched from JD's public surface; JD's developer platform and enterprise services are primarily China-market and Chinese-language.

providers.name: JDBC
providers.description: JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) is a Java API that defines how a client may access a database. It provides methods for querying and updating data in a database and is oriented towards relational databases. JDBC is part of the Java Standard Edition platform via the java.sql module (with enterprise extensions in javax.sql), and every JDBC driver implements the Driver interface to enable database connectivity in Java applications.

providers.name: Joint Fire Science Program
providers.description: The Joint Fire Science Program (JFSP) funds scientific research on wildland fires and distributes results to help policymakers, fire managers and practitioners make sound decisions. Operated jointly by the U.S. Departments of the Interior and Agriculture, JFSP coordinates the Fire Science Exchange Network across regional knowledge nodes. JFSP does not publish a self-service developer portal or OpenAPI; research outputs are surfaced through the firescience.gov website.

providers.name: Keurig Dr Pepper
providers.description: Keurig Dr Pepper is a leading North American beverage company formed by the 2018 merger of Keurig Green Mountain and Dr Pepper Snapple Group. It operates a portfolio of more than 125 owned, licensed, partner, and allied brands across hot and cold beverages, including Keurig single-serve brewing systems and brands such as Dr Pepper, 7UP, Snapple, Mott's, Bai, Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, and Peet's Coffee.

providers.name: Lean Management
providers.description: Lean Management is the discipline of planning, organizing, and overseeing lean-related activities to achieve optimal outcomes. Drawing on the Toyota Production System and the broader lean manufacturing tradition, lean management emphasizes continuous improvement (kaizen), respect for people, elimination of waste (muda), value-stream thinking, and pull-based flow. In a software and API context, lean management informs how product, platform, and operations teams plan, ship, and improve digital capabilities, and is a foundational input for adjacent disciplines such as DevOps, agile delivery, and platform engineering.

providers.name: Matchday
providers.description: Matchday is a consumer mobile platform for collecting officially licensed digital football (soccer) player cards and building a squad, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The product is a business-to-consumer collecting and squad-building experience delivered through its mobile apps and website at matchday.com. As of this enrichment pass, Matchday does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or documentation surface: probing api.matchday.com, docs.matchday.com, and developer.matchday.com returned no reachable developer hosts, and the marketing site is a single-page application. This profile therefore carries company identity plus a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts, and remains a lead to revisit if a public API surface is launched.

providers.name: Midas
providers.description: Midas is an onchain asset-management protocol that brings institutional-grade investment strategies onchain as tokenized real-world assets (RWAs).
