Its work centers on the NOVA microhypervisor and virtual machine introspection (VMI) tooling, using machine-checked mathematical proofs written in Coq to establish strong security guarantees for virtualization, edge, and embedded platforms. The company open-sources core components — including the NOVA microhypervisor, the tenjint VMI platform, and supporting Coq libraries — on GitHub, and does not publish a public web/REST API surface.

providers.name: Beme
providers.description: Beme Inc. (stylized "beme") was an American multimedia company founded in 2014 in New York City by YouTube filmmaker Casey Neistat and engineer Matt Hackett. Its mobile app, released on iOS in July 2015 and on Android in May 2016, let users capture and instantly share unedited two-to-eight-second videos without previewing or editing them, aiming at a more authentic alternative to curated social video. Beme raised a seed round backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Vayner/RSE, and CNN acquired the company in November 2016 in a deal reported at $25 million. The consumer app was shut down on January 31, 2017, and on January 25, 2018 the founders departed and Beme was folded into CNN Digital Studios. The company is defunct. Beme never published a public API, developer portal, or API documentation; its only public technical artifact is an open-source Go testing utility. The beme.com domain has since changed hands and now redirects to an unrelated company.

providers.name: Blue Vision Labs
providers.description: Blue Vision Labs was a London-based computer-vision company that built the first city-scale augmented reality cloud — crowdsourcing centimetre-accurate 3D maps of entire cities from images captured by car-mounted smartphone cameras, then letting developers use visual positioning to place shared and persistent AR content that every device sees in the same real-world spot. It emerged from stealth in March 2018 with a $14.5M round led by GV, alongside Accel and Horizons Ventures, and offered invite-only early access to iOS and Android SDKs covering San Francisco, New York City and London. Lyft acquired the company in October 2018 and made it the UK hub of its Level 5 self-driving division. The developer platform is retired: bluevisionlabs.com no longer resolves to a web host, the documentation and SDK downloads are offline, and no public API surface remains.

providers.name: Broadsoft
providers.description: BroadSoft was a cloud unified-communications (UCaaS) and VoIP software provider whose BroadWorks and BroadCloud platforms powered hosted PBX, calling, messaging, and contact-center services for telecom carriers and service providers worldwide. Its developer surface centered on the Xtended Services Interface (XSI) and OCI (Open Client Interface) provisioning APIs. Cisco acquired BroadSoft in February 2018 and folded the products into its Collaboration portfolio; the platform now ships as Cisco BroadWorks. The independent developer presence has been retired — www.broadsoft.com 301-redirects to cisco.com — so this profile carries no standalone live API surface. Originally surfaced as a bessemer-venture-partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Bump
providers.description: Bump Technologies was a Mountain View, California mobile software company (2008-2014) behind Bump, an iOS and Android app that let two people exchange contacts, photos and files by physically bumping their phones together. Bump servers correlated accelerometer, location and network signals from two handsets to match the pair, then brokered the transfer. The company published a first-party Bump API and iOS/Android SDKs so third-party apps could embed the same proximity-matching handshake. Backed by Y Combinator, Sequoia Capital and a $16M Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz in January 2011, Bump was acquired by Google in September 2013 and both the app and its developer API were discontinued on January 31, 2014. The company's bu.mp domain still serves its shutdown notice and the archived SDK repositories remain public under the bumptech GitHub organization; there is no live API surface.

providers.name: Datos Io
providers.description: Datos IO was a Silicon Valley data-management startup, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that built RecoverX — an "application-centric" backup, recovery and data-mobility platform for cloud-native and distributed databases. RecoverX targeted NoSQL and cloud data stores including Apache Cassandra, DataStax, MongoDB, Couchbase and Amazon DynamoDB, alongside relational sources such as Microsoft SQL Server, and used parallel data streaming, semantic deduplication and a distributed metadata catalog to back up in native formats and recover across private, hybrid and public cloud. Datos IO was acquired by Rubrik in 2018 and operated for a period as "Rubrik Datos IO" before the brand was retired. The company has no independent presence today: the datos.io domain has lapsed and is listed for sale through a domain broker, and no live developer portal, documentation or API surface remains. This profile is retained as an archival lineage record within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Edgar Online (OTC Markets Group)
providers.description: Edgar Online (OTC Markets Group) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: fintech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Eltek
providers.description: Eltek is a Norwegian power-electronics and telecom power-systems manufacturer (DC power rectifiers, industrial and telecom energy systems, the Flatpack product family) now operating as part of Delta Electronics. Its primary domain eltek.com 301-redirects to Delta's standard telecom power solutions catalog (www.delta-emea.com). This is a physical-hardware brand: no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or well-known discovery surface was found. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub via the sierra-ventures VC pipeline; profile retained for domain-security signal and future re-check.

providers.name: FazWaz
providers.description: FazWaz is a Thailand-based property technology company operating one of the most comprehensive real estate portals in Southeast Asia. Through fazwaz.com it aggregates residential and investment property listings — condos, houses, villas, and land for sale and rent — connecting buyers, sellers, renters, and agents across Thailand and neighboring markets, and pairs the consumer marketplace with agent tools, market data, and property-management services. FazWaz is backed by 500 Global. It runs an internal application API and a GraphQL endpoint that power its own web and mobile clients (both disallowed to crawlers in robots.txt); no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal has been published at this time.

providers.name: FindMeCure
providers.description: FindMeCure is a Sofia, Bulgaria healthtech company (founded 2015, backed by Techstars) that connects patients with clinical trials through a patient-facing search engine often described as "the Google of clinical trials," letting people search, find, and join a trial within a few clicks. Its sister B2B product, TrialHub, is a clinical-trial strategy, feasibility, and patient-recruitment intelligence platform covering 70 countries and serving pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs including Takeda, Novartis, and Syneos Health. No public developer API is currently documented; this profile captures the company's identity and probed domain security posture.

providers.name: GOAT
providers.description: GOAT (operated by GOAT Group) is a global online marketplace for authentic sneakers, apparel, and accessories, launched in 2015 and headquartered in the Los Angeles area. The platform pairs a consumer buying-and-selling experience with in-house authentication that verifies new and used footwear and streetwear from thousands of brands, and GOAT Group also operates the Flight Club consignment stores and the alias seller platform. GOAT was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, accel, index-ventures, initialized-capital, matrix-partners, and sv-angel and added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed company profile. It runs a consumer commerce platform rather than a public developer API, so this enriched profile focuses on verified company identity and the security surface probed from its public domain.

providers.name: Homzmart
providers.description: Homzmart is a Cairo, Egypt-based online marketplace for furniture, home decor, appliances, and workspace products that connects thousands of local manufacturers, brands, and merchants with consumers across Egypt and the wider MENA region. Founded in 2019 by Mahmoud Ibrahim and Ibrahim Mohamed, the platform lists more than 55,000 products and layers in flexible financing, delivery, and assembly services. Homzmart runs consumer web and mobile storefronts alongside merchant-facing "Sell With Us" and "Homzmart For Business" programs, and has raised roughly $40M in venture funding including a $15M Series A, with 500 Global among its backers. No public developer API program, SDK, or API documentation was found during enrichment; the company publishes a vulnerability-disclosure page and standard trust/policy pages.

providers.name: Infra.Market
providers.description: Infra.Market is a technology-enabled building materials platform serving India's construction and real estate sectors across the entire project lifecycle. Operating as a house of brands, it supplies concrete, aggregates, steel, AAC blocks, plywood, tiles, sanitaryware, paints, plumbing, modular kitchens, hardware, electricals, appliances, and rental equipment through both B2B (direct corporate sales with site delivery) and B2R (retail via dealers and distributors across 17,000+ touchpoints). It is backed by 280+ manufacturing facilities across 22 Indian states under brands including Shalimar Paints, RDC, IVAS, Robo, and Ultrafine, and is headquartered in Thane, Maharashtra. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio company; no public developer API surface has been identified to date.

providers.name: Integration Patterns
providers.description: Integration Patterns are design patterns and best practices for integrating different software systems and applications, including messaging, data transformation, and service orchestration approaches. Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIP), as cataloged by Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf, provide a technology-independent vocabulary and visual notation harvested from proven solutions to recurring integration problems, organized into Messaging Channels, Message Construction, Message Routing, Message Transformation, Messaging Endpoints, and System Management.

providers.name: LE TOTE
providers.description: Le Tote was an online women's clothing rental and subscription-box business founded in San Francisco in 2012 by Brett Northart and Rakesh Tondon, and a member of the Y Combinator Summer 2013 batch. Unlike Rent the Runway, which concentrated on high-end event wear, Le Tote rented everyday apparel and accessories through a rotating personalized "tote" driven by its own sizing and recommendation data. In August 2019 it agreed to acquire the Lord & Taylor department-store chain from Hudson's Bay Company; both businesses filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 2 August 2020, and Saadia Group bought the assets that October. Saadia Group was reported effectively shut down in March 2024 and the letote.com site went offline that spring. Le Tote is defunct: the domain no longer resolves, and the company never published a public API or developer portal. This profile is retained as a historical record of its open-source engineering output.

providers.name: Lready
providers.description: Lready, Inc. was the original 2007 incorporated name of Life360 — the family safety and location-sharing company that rebranded to Life360, Inc. in October 2011. Life360 operates a consumer mobile platform (iOS and Android) for real-time family location sharing, driving safety, crash detection, roadside and emergency response, and is publicly traded. This profile resolves the "Lready" venture-portfolio lead to its operating entity, Life360, and captures the security posture the company exposes at its production domain. Life360 does not publish a public first-party developer API program or OpenAPI, so no API-surface artifacts are derived here.

providers.name: Marvell Technology
providers.description: Marvell Technology, Inc. is a Fortune 500 fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company designs and develops data infrastructure semiconductor solutions including custom ASICs, data processing units, Ethernet controllers, optical and copper PHYs, switches, and storage controllers used in data centers, enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, automotive, and consumer markets. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Marvell. Public developer documentation is gated behind a customer support portal and is not openly accessible.

providers.name: Mashgin
providers.description: Mashgin builds an AI-powered, computer-vision self-checkout system that identifies multiple items simultaneously without barcodes, letting customers check out in seconds. Its touchless kiosks are deployed across 5,000+ locations including convenience stores, stadiums, arenas, universities, and healthcare facilities, and integrate with 50+ payment networks, POS systems, and loyalty programs. Mashgin does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integrations are handled through direct partnerships and its support and knowledge-base channels. Backed by Matrix Partners, SUSA Ventures, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Masmovil
providers.description: Masmovil (MasMovil Group) is a Spanish telecommunications operator providing mobile, fiber optic internet, and fixed-line services to consumers and businesses across Spain, with bundled fiber-plus-mobile packages, device sales, roaming, and international calling. The group operates a family of consumer telecom brands and, following its 2024 combination with Orange Spain, is part of the MasOrange joint venture. As of this enrichment pass Masmovil publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification; the network profile carries the identity and a domain security posture probe only.

providers.name: MetroPCS
providers.description: MetroPCS is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Old National Bancorp
providers.description: Old National Bancorp is a regional bank holding company headquartered in Indiana and a Fortune 1000 firm that provides consumer banking, commercial banking, mortgage, and wealth management services across the U.S. Midwest and Southeast. The bank operates branch and digital banking channels including mobile and online banking, bill pay, and Zelle. Old National does not publish a public developer portal or external open banking API.

providers.name: Organon
providers.description: Organon & Co. is a Fortune 500 global healthcare company focused on improving the health of women throughout their lives. Spun off from Merck in 2021, Organon's portfolio spans women's health, biosimilars, and established medicines across more than 140 markets worldwide. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Organon. No public developer APIs or documentation portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Orion Health
providers.description: Medical platform which allows the development of applications for different healthcare scenarios

providers.name: Rolls-Royce
providers.description: Rolls-Royce plc is a British multinational aerospace and defense company manufacturing aero engines (Trent series), defense propulsion, and power systems. Rolls-Royce does not publish a public developer API. The company operates supplier portals at suppliers.rolls-royce.com and maintains a small GitHub presence with the qc-cfd open-source repository covering quantum computing for computational fluid dynamics research.

providers.name: Saint-Gobain
providers.description: Saint-Gobain is a French multinational corporation founded in 1665, headquartered in Courbevoie, France. It designs, manufactures, and distributes materials and solutions for the construction, mobility, healthcare, and industrial markets. The group operates through well-known brands including CertainTeed (North American roofing, insulation, gypsum), Norton (abrasives), Weber (mortars and facades), Placo (plasterboard, France), and ISOVER (insulation). Saint-Gobain trades on Euronext Paris under the ticker SGO and is a component of the CAC 40 and Euro Stoxx 50 indices. As a building materials and industrial manufacturer, Saint-Gobain operates no public developer program, API portal, or machine-readable surface. The GitHub organization at github.com/saint-gobain exists but hosts zero public repositories. Any digital integration with customers, distributors, or partners happens through private B2B channels (EDI, custom integrations, e-commerce portals for trade buyers) rather than a documented public API. This repo exists in the API Evangelist network as a placeholder record for the company — to mark that the surface area was assessed and found to be absent — rather than to catalog APIs.

providers.name: Springboard
providers.description: Springboard is an online education company offering mentor-led, career-focused bootcamps and courses in software engineering, data science, data analytics, UX/UI design, cybersecurity, and machine learning. Programs pair a structured, self-paced curriculum with 1:1 industry mentorship, career coaching, and a job guarantee on eligible tracks. Springboard was surfaced from a 500 Global portfolio list and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it operates as a consumer/B2B learning platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, so this profile carries identity and security-posture signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Stan
providers.description: Stan (stan.store) is an all-in-one creator storefront and link-in-bio commerce platform that lets creators sell digital products, online courses, coaching calls, memberships, and webinars directly from a single mobile-first store link. The platform bundles checkout and payments, email marketing, an AutoDM tool, analytics, and integrations with third-party tools such as Zoom and Google Meet. Backed by Forerunner Ventures, General Catalyst, and Norwest Venture Partners, Stan targets the creator economy. As of this enrichment pass Stan publishes no public developer API, webhook specification, or SDKs — the surface is a consumer product plus a help center; this profile captures the identity and a probed domain-security profile.

providers.name: Sun Basket
providers.description: Sun Basket is a San Francisco-based meal-kit and prepared-meal delivery service offering organic, chef-designed recipes and ingredients shipped as weekly subscription boxes, with menus spanning dietary programs such as paleo, keto, vegetarian, gluten-free, and diabetes-friendly options. Surfaced as a portfolio company of sapphire-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, Sun Basket operates a consumer e-commerce and subscription-delivery product; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment probing.

providers.name: Sygaldry
providers.description: Sygaldry Technologies builds quantum-accelerated AI servers — augmenting classical data-center infrastructure with quantum processors purpose-built for AI to deliver exponential speedups on specific training and inference tasks. Founded in 2024 in Ann Arbor, Michigan by Chad Rigetti (founder of Rigetti Computing), Idalia Friedson, and Michael Keiser, the company combines multiple qubit types within a single fault-tolerant architecture to accelerate model training, fine-tuning, and token generation while cutting compute cost and energy use. A Y Combinator Spring 2025 company, Sygaldry has raised $139M ($34M seed led by Initialized Capital and a $105M Series A led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, with Bloomberg Beta among its investors). Sygaldry currently publishes no public developer API; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network discovery.

providers.name: Takenos
providers.description: Takenos is a Latin American fintech offering a digital dollar wallet built for freelancers, remote workers, and businesses who need to receive cross-border payments. It lets users get paid from abroad, hold and save in digital dollars with daily yield, and spend via international (TakeCard) and local (SpicyCard) debit cards plus QR payments. Riding the LATAM stablecoin and onchain-finance wave, it targets remittance friction and local-currency inflation across markets including Argentina and Bolivia. Backed by a $5M seed round (investors include 500 Global). No public developer API is documented; this profile was enriched from public sources.

providers.name: The GEO Group
providers.description: The GEO Group, Inc. (NYSE: GEO) is a publicly traded private corrections and community supervision company headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida. Founded in 1984 as Wackenhut Corrections Corporation and rebranded in 2004, it is the largest private prison operator in the United States and a primary contractor to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the U.S. Marshals Service, the Federal Bureau of Prisons, and numerous state departments of corrections. As of 2024 the company owned or managed approximately 80,000 beds across roughly 99 facilities and reported $2.424 billion in revenue. Its wholly owned subsidiary BI Incorporated operates the federal Intensive Supervision Appearance Program (ISAP) and builds the ankle monitors, GPS trackers, voice-verification systems and SmartLINK smartphone app used to monitor people in immigration proceedings and community supervision. GEO Group publishes no public developer API and has no GitHub presence; the only "platform" surfaces it exposes are customer-facing operational systems (BI TotalAccess for officers, BI SmartLINK for supervised individuals) used inside its own contracts. This repository documents the corporate footprint, the technology subsidiary, and the public-record controversies surrounding the firm under the second Trump administration's 2025+ ICE detention expansion, for purposes of the API Evangelist network's coverage of API absence in sensitive sectors.

providers.name: Tradegecko
providers.description: TradeGecko was a Singapore-based cloud inventory and order management platform for SMEs, wholesalers, and online retailers, launched in 2013 with integrations into Shopify, WooCommerce, and Xero. Intuit acquired TradeGecko in August 2020 and rebranded it QuickBooks Commerce; the standalone platform and its public REST API were subsequently discontinued. Its API hosts no longer resolve and tradegecko.com is no longer operated by the company, though first-party Ruby client libraries remain published on RubyGems.

providers.name: TrueFlip
providers.description: TrueFlip was an international anonymous blockchain lottery with instant payouts, open-source draw code, and a transparent prize fund, launched in 2017 with an Ethereum token ICO and backed by Pantera Capital. The company's GitHub organization has been dormant since 2018, and the trueflip.io domain is suspended at the registrar (clientHold) with no DNS records; by early 2026 the domain was serving unrelated crypto-casino affiliate content. No public API, developer documentation, SDK packages, or machine-readable surface was found. Profile retained as a Pantera Capital portfolio record.

providers.name: Unbound
providers.description: Unbound (Unbound Finance) was a DeFi protocol describing itself as "The DeFi Treasury for Liquidity Pool Tokens," enabling liquidity providers to collateralize LP tokens on Ethereum. It is a Pantera Capital portfolio company (sector: crypto). As of 2026-07-21 the project appears inactive: unbound.finance returns HTTP 404, its documentation host (wiki.unbound.finance) no longer resolves, and its GitHub organization contains only forked repositories - no public API surface, developer portal, or first-party packages were found.

providers.name: Unidesk
providers.description: Unidesk was a Marlborough, Massachusetts software company backed by Matrix Partners that pioneered application layering for virtual desktop infrastructure, packaging Windows applications and operating-system components into shareable virtual disk layers. Citrix acquired Unidesk in January 2017 and the technology lives on as Citrix App Layering. unidesk.com now 301-redirects to the Citrix App Layering product page, the GitHub organization has been dormant since the acquisition, and the company maintains no standalone API surface of its own.

providers.name: Ursa Computing
providers.description: Ursa Computing was a startup founded in 2020 by Wes McKinney (creator of pandas, co-creator of Apache Arrow) to accelerate Apache Arrow and open source data science tooling, backed by GV. In late 2021 Ursa Computing and Ursa Labs joined forces with other teams to form Voltron Data, and the company no longer operates independently: ursacomputing.com no longer resolves, and its remaining public footprint is the ursacomputing GitHub organization, whose crossbow repository still runs extra CI for Apache Arrow. No public API surface was ever published under the Ursa Computing name.

providers.name: vestiairecollective
providers.description: Vestiaire Collective is a global online marketplace for pre-owned luxury and designer fashion, founded in Paris in 2009. The platform lets members buy and sell authenticated second-hand clothing, bags, shoes, watches, and accessories, with in-house physical authentication and quality control on higher-value items and a mission centered on circular fashion and sustainable consumption. It operates a consumer marketplace across web and mobile apps in dozens of countries. It is backed by Balderton Capital among other investors. This API Evangelist profile was added as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment probes found no public developer/API program, but did verify the company's published security disclosure surface and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Voltron Data
providers.description: Voltron Data is a Mountain View-based data infrastructure company (founded 2021) behind Theseus, a GPU-accelerated, composable distributed SQL query engine for petabyte-scale analytics and AI pipelines, distributed embedded through partners rather than as a self-serve public API. The company is a major steward of the open-source composable data stack — Apache Arrow, Ibis, Substrait, Arrow Flight SQL, and ADBC — acquired Claypot AI in January 2024, and is backed by Battery Ventures, GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Walden Catalyst, with an Accenture investment in 2025. As of 2026-07-21 the company website (voltrondata.com) is unreachable — the domain is registered but its DNS zone is lame-delegated — leaving the GitHub organization as the live public surface; no public API, SDK packages, or developer portal are published.

providers.name: 360 Commerce
providers.description: 360 Commerce is a New Zealand and Australia B2B ecommerce platform that helps wholesalers, distributors and manufacturers bring customer ordering, account self-service and ERP-connected workflows online. More than a standard ecommerce website, it gives customers a secure ordering portal for contract and customer-specific pricing, ERP stock visibility, repeat ordering, quotes, approvals, invoices, credit notes and aged balances. The platform (built on its EcomCore product) integrates with leading ERP, accounting, inventory and CRM systems including Odoo, MYOB Advanced and NetSuite so online ordering reflects the way a business actually trades.

providers.name: 858 Therapeutics
providers.description: 858 Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego, California, developing first-in-class and best-in-class small-molecule therapies that target tumor dependencies in DNA damage response (DDR) pathways. Its lead program, ETX-19477, is an oral, potent, and selective PARG (poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase) inhibitor being evaluated in a Phase 1/2 study for patients with advanced solid tumors, exploiting cancer-cell vulnerabilities tied to replication stress and defects in replication-fork protection. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage therapeutics company it publishes a corporate and scientific web presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so API artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Abe AI
providers.description: Abe AI was a conversational-AI platform for banks and credit unions, delivering a financial virtual assistant (chatbot and voice) across web, mobile, SMS, and smart-speaker channels so consumers could check balances, track spending, and bank by natural language. Founded in Orlando, Florida and backed by Techstars, Abe AI was acquired by Envestnet | Yodlee in 2019; its conversational-banking technology was folded into Yodlee's fintech data platform. The abe.ai domain now 301-redirects to yodlee.com/fintech/conversational-ai and no longer operates an independent developer or API surface.

providers.name: Acacia
providers.description: Acacia (Acacia Communications) is a coherent optical networking company, an early Matrix Partners portfolio company that was acquired by Cisco. Acacia designs and manufactures high-speed coherent optical interconnect solutions built on silicon photonics, low-power DSP, and 3D siliconization, including performance-optimized modules (AC1200, CIM 8), MSA pluggable modules (CFP, CFP2, OSFP, QSFP-DD, QSFP28), and client optics components (PAM4 DSP, optical engines). These power AI scale-out and scale-across fabrics, data center interconnect, metro and long-haul networks, submarine cables, access and cable networks, and space communications. Acacia is a hardware/components provider and does not publish a public developer API or programmatic platform.

providers.name: Airborne Entertainment
providers.description: Airborne Entertainment was a Montreal, Quebec mobile entertainment company founded in 2000 that published and distributed premium mobile content and applications for carrier decks and early smartphones, including games, ringtones, ring-back tones, images, video and informational content, often under licensed consumer brands. The company raised a $22M round in July 2004 with participation from Insight Partners and Verizon, sold a majority stake to Japan's CYBIRD Co., Ltd. in 2005, was taken back by management in a 2008 buy-out, operated afterwards as Airborne Mobile, and was acquired by Bandsintown in October 2010. It no longer operates as an independent company: both airborneentertainment.com and airbornemobile.com are parked domain-sale listings, and the company never published a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as an API Evangelist network history record.

providers.name: AkashX
providers.description: AkashX is a Techstars-backed data and AI company building an Online Cognitive Processing (OLCP) Database and a declarative "Cognitive SQL" engine for reasoning over structured and unstructured data at scale. Its platform runs small language models in-database to deliver low-latency, token-efficient, deterministic inference as an alternative to probabilistic RAG, with semantic operations such as Cognitive Join, Cognitive Classify, and Cognitive Topic Discovery, plus Ontology Views that turn files into queryable tables for agents. It integrates with lakehouse environments like Databricks and targets financial intelligence, sales analysis, healthcare and clinical-trial, and talent-screening use cases. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline; no public API, SDK, or developer documentation is published yet.

providers.name: AliciaBots
providers.description: AliciaBots is a maritime robotics company, backed by Techstars, that builds autonomous robot teams for cleaning and inspecting ship hulls. Its flagship Roverclean robot operates independently to remove marine growth and monitor hull condition in real time without interrupting a vessel's voyage, using self-learning adaptive systems, precision cleaning, and remote monitoring and control to improve fuel efficiency and help operators meet IMO regulatory standards. AliciaBots does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile tracks the company as a network lead.

providers.name: Alooma
providers.description: Alooma was a cloud data-pipeline (ETL) platform founded in 2013 in Palo Alto and Tel Aviv that let enterprises stream and migrate data from sources such as SQL Server, Oracle, Amazon Aurora, Salesforce, Zendesk, and Zuora into data warehouses including Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, and Snowflake. It offered a hosted pipeline with a REST API input connector and a first-party Python client (alooma.py) for programmatic management of inputs, mappings, and tables. Google Cloud acquired Alooma in February 2019 and wound the standalone product down; the alooma.com developer surface no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record surfaced from the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio.

providers.name: Altitude Software
providers.description: Altitude Software is a contact center and unified customer interaction (uCI) software company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal. Its flagship Altitude uCI suite provides omnichannel contact center capabilities — inbound/outbound campaigns, IVR and self-service, routing, dialer, recording and quality management, and CRM/ERP integration — with the Altitude uAgent SDK exposing Java, C/C++, .NET, SOAP, XML-RPC and web-service APIs for on-premises and cloud deployments. Altitude Software was a portfolio company of Insight Partners and was acquired by Enghouse Systems (TSX: ENGH) on 2020-12-30; the product line is now developed and maintained by Enghouse Interactive, and the brand continues to operate regionally (e.g. Altitude Software APAC). The company does not publish a modern public REST API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; integration is delivered through the proprietary uAgent SDK and packaged CRM/ERP connectors.

providers.name: Andrenam
providers.description: Andrenam is a defense technology company building an AI-powered maritime sensing network for undersea surveillance. It develops mass-manufacturable, low-cost buoy-based autonomous sonar systems that deploy from manned and unmanned vessels to detect, track, and identify real-time maritime traffic using cloud and edge AI, then dispatch resources to priority areas. Its product line spans deployment, AI-enhanced detection, and integration with naval command-and-control systems, targeting government and military maritime-domain-awareness customers. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Aquafortus
providers.description: Aquafortus Technologies is a New Zealand-based deep-tech water treatment company that develops patented non-thermal, zero-liquid-discharge (ZLD) desalination technology for high-salinity industrial brines. Its ABX system uses a solvent-extraction and membrane-filtration process at ambient temperatures to turn up to 98% of high-salinity brine into fresh water while using significantly less energy than thermal alternatives, and can expose, isolate and extract valuable metals and minerals (lithium, copper, magnesium salts and others) from the treated brine. The company targets cooling towers, mining, oil and gas, inland desalination, flue-gas desulphurisation and other high-volume, high-salinity industrial processes. Aquafortus is backed by deep tech venture firm DCVC and Novo Holdings, and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: ArrePath
providers.description: ArrePath is an AI-driven pharmaceutical company based in Princeton, New Jersey, applying machine learning to accelerate small-molecule drug discovery in infectious disease. Its platform treats heterogeneous, small, and noisy bioactivity datasets as a modeling opportunity, enabling work on novel chemical classes where conventional approaches struggle; a public-data oral bioavailability model lifted a lead series from roughly 22% to 89% bioavailability. Lead programs include an oral LpxH inhibitor for outpatient urinary tract infections (pre-IND targeted mid-2026) and antibacterial programs against non-tuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) lung disease and tuberculosis, plus an early non-infectious discovery effort. ArrePath is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Astro Mechanica
providers.description: Astro Mechanica is a San Francisco aerospace company, founded in 2021 by Ian Brooke, reinventing supersonic flight for a new jet age. Its flagship Duality electric combined-cycle engine is engineered to stay efficient from takeoff through Mach 3+ by reconfiguring between turbofan, turbojet, and ramjet modes using a hybrid turboelectric architecture. The company designs engines, airframes, and flight systems in-house, has been selected to develop an engine for the U.S. Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, and is backed by a16z, Lowercarbon Capital, and Y Combinator. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As an aerospace hardware manufacturer, Astro Mechanica publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web and identity surface only.

providers.name: AstroForge
providers.description: AstroForge is a commercial space startup founded in 2022 and based in Huntington Beach, California, focused on asteroid mining and the in-space extraction and refining of platinum group metals and other critical minerals. Backed by Initialized Capital and a Y Combinator alum, the company designs low-cost, autonomous, replicable interplanetary spacecraft to prospect and mine near-Earth asteroids, with its DeepSpace-2 mission targeting the first commercial rendezvous with a body outside Earth's gravity well. AstroForge does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a frontier-tech lead and will be enriched further if and when a developer program appears.

providers.name: Ateios
providers.description: Ateios Systems is an Indianapolis-based advanced battery manufacturer that produces high-energy, recyclable, PFA-free battery electrodes for global battery makers. Its proprietary RaiCure platform is a solvent-free, cure-on-command coating process using energy-curable polymers instead of solvent-based thermal drying, enabling thicker electrodes (>10 mAh/cm2), higher energy density, and roughly 5x faster coating throughput at lower cost and emissions. Ateios targets medical device, IoT, mobility, and defense markets. Founded in 2017 and backed by Techstars, TitletownTech, Good Growth Capital and others, the company is a materials/hardware manufacturer and publishes no developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer platform.

providers.name: ATMI Sales
providers.description: ATMI Sales (Advanced Technical Marketing Inc.) is a manufacturers' representative and technical sales firm serving the electronics and semiconductor industry across the Pacific Northwest and Western Canada. The company connects customers with component suppliers through a research, development, and build model — identifying suitable technology solutions, building supplier relationships, and ensuring component availability and supply-chain sourcing in the regions where products are manufactured. ATMI maintains a line card of partner technologies and works with distributors to fulfill orders. This is a non-developer B2B sales and distribution company; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of sierra-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Atom Semiconductor
providers.description: Atom Semiconductor (Atom Semiconductor Technologies Limited) is a fabless mixed-signal chip design company founded in Hong Kong in October 2020, with offices in Shenzhen and Shanghai. It designs high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for consumer and industrial IoT systems across three product lines: digital sensor chips (temperature/humidity, pressure, optical), analog-to-digital converters (24-bit Sigma-Delta, high-precision SAR, and high-speed GSPS ADCs), and microprocessors. Its first product, the AS1412 24-bit Sigma-Delta ADC, shipped for customer trials in late 2021. The company raised roughly 100M yuan in a pre-A round led by Qiming Venture Partners (with Venus Medtech and Alibaba Entrepreneurs Fund) and was named to the Forbes Asia 100 To Watch 2022. It is a hardware chip designer and does not publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Atropos Health
providers.description: Atropos Health is a Stanford-spinout, New York / Bay Area real-world evidence (RWE) company founded in 2020 by Nigam Shah, Brigham Hyde, and Saurabh Gombar to close the medical "evidence gap" by converting routine healthcare data into publication-grade observational studies in minutes instead of months. Its flagship platform GENEVA OS (Generative Evidence Acceleration Operating System) is a federated, cloud-agnostic operating system that installs behind the customer's firewall, ingests longitudinal patient records as in-memory patient-timeline objects, and exposes a Temporal Query Language (TQL) and Advanced Cohort Engine (ACE) for rapid observational analyses without moving PHI. On top of GENEVA OS, Atropos offers ChatRWD, a conversational chat-to-database application that generates full observational studies from natural-language clinical questions, the Atropos Evidence Agent (an agentic AI deployed at Stanford Health Care and developed in collaboration with Microsoft to surface RWE directly inside clinical workflows and notes), Green Button (the original on-demand consult-style evidence service that gave rise to the company), Forge (study automation), and Alexandria, marketed as the world's largest body of precision evidence-based findings with 33M+ entries used for clinical decision support and LLM training. The company sells into health systems (pharmacy, research informatics, value-based care, GME) and life sciences (brand planning, HEOR, medical affairs, R&D, commercial analytics, precision-medicine AI/ML), is backed by Valtruis, Emerson Collective, Breyer Capital, McKinsey Ventures, Cencora Ventures, Presidio Ventures, Merck Global Health Innovation, Samsung Next, and others, and partners with Stanford Health Care, Mayo Clinic Platform, and Microsoft. Atropos has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; GENEVA OS, TQL, ACE, ChatRWD, and the Evidence Agent are proprietary enterprise software delivered under contract to health-system and life-sciences customers, and the company's public GitHub org contains only forks (FAISS, HELM, security-policy-templates, terraform-aws-github-runner) and a small number of internal research notebooks rather than any shippable client library.

providers.name: Autolus *
providers.description: Autolus is a life-sciences (biopharmaceutical) company operating in the cell-therapy space, developing programmed / engineered T cell (CAR-T) therapies for cancer and other serious diseases. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a clinical/commercial-stage biopharma, its public web presence (autolus.com) is a corporate marketing and investor-relations site rather than a developer platform: no public API, developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment. The only machine-discoverable artifact is a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Axcelius I/II
providers.description: Axcelius I/II is a biopharmaceutical company-creation vehicle backed by Canaan Partners, formed to found and incubate drug-development companies pursuing treatments for cancer, rare diseases, and neurodegenerative disorders. It is led by managing partner Dennis Podlesak and sponsored at Canaan by general partner Brent Ahrens, and operates from San Francisco, California, with an associated holding entity registered in Connecticut at Canaan's Westport office. Rather than operating as a product company, Axcelius assembles management teams and capital around licensed therapeutic assets and spins them out as standalone biopharma companies; Transposon Therapeutics, developing therapies for ALS and Alzheimer's disease, is its best-documented creation. As of this enrichment pass the vehicle remains in stealth mode with no public developer surface -- no product website beyond a holding page, no documentation, developer portal, SDKs, GitHub organization, or API of any kind.

providers.name: Axera Tech
providers.description: Axera Intelligence (爱芯元智), operating as Axera Tech, is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company building AI-inference SoCs for edge and endpoint computing. Its chips pair the Axera Tongyuan mixed-precision NPU with the Axera Zhimu AI-ISP to power on-device vision perception, smart-vehicle autonomous-driving and intelligent-cabin platforms, and multi-tier edge-AI inference across IoT and industrial scenarios. Axera Tech was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; it is a hardware/silicon provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Basecamp Research
providers.description: Basecamp Research is a London-based biotech company mapping global genetic biodiversity to power AI-based design of biological systems. Its core asset is BaseGraph, a Neo4j-backed knowledge graph of billions of biological relationships assembled from novel protein and genome sequences collected under access-and-benefit-sharing partnerships with biodiversity-rich countries. On top of this data it builds foundation models and tools including EDEN (a large-scale biology sequence model), BaseFold (3D protein structure prediction that improves on AlphaFold2 for large, complex structures and small-molecule interactions), and BaseScan (an automated annotation pipeline). Basecamp works with pharma and biotech partners on drug discovery and enzyme/protein design, and has collaborated with NVIDIA to bring BaseFold to the BioNeMo platform. Backed by True Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Basecamp Research currently exposes no public self-serve developer API - data and models are accessed via partnerships, and product docs sit behind an authenticated portal.

providers.name: BigHat Biosciences
providers.description: BigHat Biosciences is a biotechnology company that pairs machine learning with a high-throughput, fully integrated wet lab to design next-generation antibody-based therapeutics. Its platform closes the loop between in-silico antibody design and in-house synthesis and characterization, generating proprietary experimental data that trains its models and speeds the discovery of biologics with improved developability. The company has publicly discussed its Reccy antibody design studio (RADS) and has entered machine-learning-enabled biologics collaborations with Eli Lilly (including Lilly TuneLab), Johnson & Johnson, and Lonza/Synaffix. BigHat is a private, venture-backed company (8VC, a16z) and maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source computational-biology tooling. It does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: BlackBuck
providers.description: BlackBuck, operated by Zinka Logistics Solutions and incorporated in 2015, runs India's largest digital trucking platform, digitizing the truck-operator lifecycle for roughly a million truck operators (about 28% of India's truckers) across 100,000+ villages. Its super-app spans a loads marketplace, FASTag toll payments, fuel, GPS/telematics, vehicle and working-capital financing, and a used-trucks marketplace. Listed on the NSE as BLACKBUCK since November 2024, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer program, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment; this profile carries the company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Blue Jeans Network
providers.description: Blue Jeans Network (later BlueJeans by Verizon) was a cloud-based video conferencing company founded in 2009 in Mountain View / San Jose, California. It delivered interoperable video meetings across desktop, mobile, and conference-room systems, and offered a developer surface that included the onVideo/Meetings REST API and a WebRTC Embed SDK for embedding live video into applications. Verizon acquired BlueJeans in 2020; Verizon subsequently discontinued the BlueJeans service and the bluejeans.com website and developer portal are no longer reachable. This profile preserves the company's published package artifacts, which persist in public registries even though the hosted service is retired. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Borqs
providers.description: Borqs Technologies Inc. is a global Internet of Things (IoT) platform solution provider delivering customizable, differentiated and scalable smart-connected IoT software, hardware and cloud-service platforms. Founded in 2007, Borqs is a Google-licensed Android and Android Wear partner with R&D centers in the U.S., India and China, and debuted publicly on Nasdaq (BRQS) in August 2017. Its BorqsWare platform powers smartphones, tablets, wearables, in-vehicle infotainment (IVI), M2M and smart-appliance solutions, and in 2021 it expanded into solar and energy storage systems (ESS) via its Holu Hou Energy acquisition. Borqs is now a Sasken Group company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published; this profile carries company identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Busy Ming Group
providers.description: Busy Ming Group (Hunan Mingming Busy Commercial Chain Co., Ltd. / 湖南鸣鸣很忙商业连锁股份有限公司) is a mass-market snack retail chain operator headquartered in Changsha, Hunan, China, and a consumer-sector portfolio company of HongShan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). It operates two discount snack store brands — Snacks Are Busy (零食很忙, founded 2017) and Zhao Yiming Snacks (赵一鸣零食, founded 2019) — which combined into a network of more than 21,000 retail locations, heavily concentrated in county-level cities and townships. The group publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate, franchising, and investor-relations web presence.

providers.name: Calxeda
providers.description: Calxeda was an Austin, Texas semiconductor startup — founded in 2008 as Smooth-Stone by Barry Evans, Larry Wikelius and David Borland — that built ARM-based EnergyCore system-on-chip server processors (ECX-1000, ECX-2000/Midway) aimed at low-power, high-density data center workloads. It raised roughly $90-103M from venture investors including Battery Ventures, and its silicon shipped in Boston Limited Viridis appliances and HP Project Moonshot systems. Calxeda ceased operations in December 2013 after a refinancing round fell through, and its ARM server IP resurfaced under Silver Lining Systems in December 2014. The company published no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts, and calxeda.com is now a parked domain listed for sale, so there is no live API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.

providers.name: Cerberus Tech, Inc.
providers.description: Cerberus Tech, Inc. (C7 Security) is a Central Asian cybersecurity firm combining practical offensive security with research-backed methodology. Its flagship product, Cerberus, is an IDE and programming language purpose-built for ethical hackers to run faster penetration-testing assessments. Services span security assessment (penetration testing, audits, red teaming), secure development (code, design, and architecture reviews), OSINT reconnaissance, R&D grounded in type theory, and consulting. The company also runs C7 Academy, an elite penetration-testing training program, alongside free education and community initiatives. It reports 150+ security audits with a 95%+ penetration rate and 300+ students trained. Backed by 500 Global; surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Cerexa
providers.description: Cerexa was a privately held biopharmaceutical company founded in the mid-2000s (its cerexa.com domain was registered in March 2005) to develop anti-infective therapies for serious, drug-resistant bacterial infections in the hospital setting. Its lead program was ceftaroline fosamil, a fifth-generation cephalosporin antibiotic active against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), in-licensed from Takeda Pharmaceutical Company and carried forward by Forest Laboratories; the compound was approved by the FDA on October 29, 2010 and marketed as Teflaro in the United States and Zinforo in Europe. Cerexa was backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners, and its programs ultimately passed through Forest Laboratories into the Actavis/Allergan combination (Forest Laboratories was acquired by Actavis on July 1, 2014) and on to AbbVie. Cerexa no longer operates as an independent company and has no developer surface: it publishes no API, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no documentation, and its historical cerexa.com domain is now registered and operated by AbbVie, 301-redirecting to AbbVie's Allergan page. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chaos
providers.description: CHAOS Industries is a U.S. defense-technology company founded in 2022 that builds advanced sensing and detection systems for military, border, and critical-infrastructure defense. Its Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN) technology powers a multi-product portfolio - including the Vanquish radar for early warning and tracking of unmanned aerial systems and missile threats, and HYDRA, a software-defined multi-application platform for detection, communications, and electronic effects. CHAOS markets domain dominance through counter-drone (counter-UAS) radar that detects threats up to ten minutes faster and tracks targets to 250 km. The company has raised roughly $1 billion from investors including 8VC, Accel, Valor Equity Partners, and NEA, with offices in Los Angeles, Washington DC, San Francisco, San Diego, London, and Amman. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; CHAOS publishes a marketing and newsroom presence but no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Cheetah
providers.description: Cheetah (Cheetah Technologies, with its software platform also marketed as Kimelo) is an AI-enabled, app-based restaurant supply and wholesale ordering marketplace launched in 2015 to bridge the digital gap in foodservice. Its eCommerce platform gives small to medium-sized food distributors and restaurants tools for online ordering, process automation, delivery route optimization, supply chain management, and customer retention, with next-day delivery of daily supplies. In June 2024 the company divested its physical distribution business (Pleasanton, CA) to Palo Alto Foods to focus on commercializing its software platform nationwide. The platform provides digital product catalogs, personalized purchasing insights, integrated payment processing, routing management, and automated inventory tracking, and lets distributors integrate directly with their ERP or inventory management and point-of-sale systems to automate order placement. Cheetah does not appear to publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is offered through direct ERP, inventory, and POS system connections arranged with the company rather than self-service documented endpoints.

providers.name: ChurchTrac
providers.description: ChurchTrac is all-in-one church management software (ChMS) for small and large churches, covering people and member management, church directory, groups, attendance and check-in, event registration, worship planning and volunteer scheduling, online giving, and fund accounting/budgeting. ChurchTrac does NOT publish a public or partner developer API - there is no documented REST API, API keys, OAuth, or webhooks for building against ChurchTrac data. Its "integrations" are ChurchTrac consuming third-party services (Stripe for giving, SendGrid/Mailchimp for email, Twilio for texting, QuickBooks for accounting, Zoom); member-facing access is via the Church Connect app and embeddable online giving forms, not a programmable API surface. This entry is documented as an honest stub.

providers.name: CIX Technology
providers.description: CIX Technology (此芯科技) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2021 that designs high-performance, general-purpose heterogeneous intelligent CPU chips for AI computing. The company builds low-power, high-efficiency compute platforms spanning personal computing (PC), vehicle/automotive computing, and edge computing, and partners across the Arm ecosystem (Arm, Arm China, Lenovo and others). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. CIX is a silicon/hardware company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Claimglide
providers.description: Claimglide (ClaimGlide) is an AI-powered software platform that automates the end-to-end prior-authorization process for private medical practices and healthcare providers. It generates prior-auth submissions using payer-approved language, auto-pulls clinical data from EMR systems, follows up with payers, tracks authorization timelines, and auto-generates appeal letters to increase the share of prior-auths approved and shorten turnaround time. Claimglide integrates with major EMR/EHR platforms including eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, NextGen Healthcare, and ModMed, and states HIPAA compliance. Founded in 2025 in Seattle by Nami Lindquist and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch), the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. No public API, developer documentation, or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: Coolso
providers.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: COSY
providers.description: COSY (CosyRobo) is a retail-technology robotics company that builds autonomous inventory robots for physical stores. Its flagship robot, SCOUT, roams store aisles using AI and machine vision to scan shelves, map products, audit stock levels, and check planogram compliance, feeding the results into a cloud-based management system so retailers can reduce out-of-stocks and improve on-shelf availability. Backed by 500 Global, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: CrawlGraph
providers.description: A backlink-intelligence SaaS built on Common Crawl's open hyperlink graph (~120M domains / 4.4B links). Provides referring-domain lookups, competitor gap analysis, and outreach-target discovery as a low-cost alternative to Ahrefs/Moz/Semrush.

providers.name: Daqstra
providers.description: Daqstra is an AI-native operating platform for complex test infrastructure, giving aerospace, energy, and robotics teams observability and orchestration for the physical world. The platform connects data-acquisition hardware (National Instruments, PLCs, and custom equipment) at the edge, centralizes and versions test data in the cloud, and orchestrates hardware sequences and test logic as code through Python and REST APIs. Daqstra Edge streams live signals from physical hardware, Daqstra Hub (Strata Hub) organizes test-campaign data with AI-powered insight, and the Daqstra API lets engineers drive test runs programmatically instead of through manual CSV workflows. The company was founded by aerospace-propulsion and avionics engineers and is backed by Y Combinator (S26 batch).

providers.name: DaVita HealthCare Partners
providers.description: DaVita HealthCare Partners is the legacy name for the combined entity of DaVita and HealthCare Partners following their 2012 merger. The HealthCare Partners group operated medical groups and physician networks managing Medicare Advantage and other coordinated care patients before being divested by DaVita in 2019. DaVita continues to provide kidney care and dialysis services. No public developer API has been identified for the combined entity or the historical HealthCare Partners group.

providers.name: DEM Bio
providers.description: DEM BioPharma is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing first-in-class cancer therapeutics that target the signals solid tumors use to evade immune destruction. The company pioneers next-generation macrophage and innate-immune immunotherapies discovered through its proprietary CHoMP (Co-culture with Human Myeloid Phagocytes) functional-genomics platform, which uses CRISPR-based screening to identify novel "don't-eat-me" and activating targets on myeloid cells. DEM launched in 2022 with $70M in Series A financing and is backed by Longwood Fund, Emerson Collective, Pfizer Ventures, Astellas, and Insight Partners. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile; DEM publishes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Digitalk
providers.description: Digitalk, Inc. was an American object-oriented software tools vendor and a Trinity Ventures portfolio company, best known for Smalltalk/V — a commercial Smalltalk development environment first released in 1986 for MS-DOS, preceded by "Digitalk Methods" in 1983. It was founded by George Bosworth, Jim Anderson, Mike Teng and Barbara Noparstak, and its product line grew into Visual Smalltalk Enterprise. In July 1995 Digitalk merged with its principal competitor ParcPlace Systems; the combined company was later renamed ObjectShare, announced a shift away from Smalltalk toward Java in 1997, and active development of the Digitalk line ended shortly after. The final release, Visual Smalltalk Enterprise 2000, shipped in September 2000. Cincom retains the right to sell and support VSE 2000 for existing licensees and Seagull Software owns the virtual machine. Digitalk predates the public web API era and operates no developer platform, public API, or live web presence today; this profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ditto Biosciences
providers.description: Ditto Biosciences (Ditto Bio) is a San Francisco biotechnology startup, founded in 2025 and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch), that discovers drugs for autoimmune diseases by identifying and engineering immune-controlling proteins that parasites, viruses, ticks, and worms have naturally evolved over millions of years to modulate the human immune system. The company pairs an AI platform with wet-lab biology to mine more than a million natural proteins, identify candidates predicted to hit clinically validated human immune-disease targets, and transform them into therapeutic candidates. Ditto is an early-stage, three-person team led by founders Dennis Sun (CEO), Adair Borges (CSO), and Emily Weiss (CTO). This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Ditto Bio currently publishes a marketing and science website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: Dyna
providers.description: DYNA Robotics builds commercial-grade, general-purpose robots for real-world automation across factories, restaurants, and laundromats. Its flagship DYNA-1 is a dual-arm robotic system powered by a vision-language-action (VLA) foundation model, running 24/7 in production with a reported 99.4% success rate and human-level dexterity. The company positions itself as building embodied AGI through high-performance robots that adapt across environments and learn new skills rapidly with minimal custom engineering. Backed by CRV, DYNA closed a $120M Series A in 2025. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface has been published to date; this profile tracks the company as an AI/robotics lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Eco Gear
providers.description: Eco Gear (에코기어) is a South Korean food-technology company that develops natural biomaterial-based nano-coating preservation agents which extend the freshness of fresh produce and reduce food waste across the cold chain. Its product line — Flowting for cut flowers, Ecocell for stevia tomatoes, and Fruiting for citrus — forms an invisible, food-safe protective layer that slows moisture loss, browning, and mold without synthetic waxes or harmful emulsifiers, with field trials showing spoilage reduced by up to 71%. The company markets a physical-products and R&D business and does not currently publish a public developer API. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Element Zero
providers.description: Element Zero is a green-materials technology company decarbonizing the production of iron and other critical metals. Its patented non-aqueous electrochemical process converts any grade of metal ore (iron, nickel, titanium, lithium) into high-purity metal with zero carbon emissions, using 30-40% less energy than conventional smelting and operating at low temperatures so it can run on intermittent renewable energy (wind, solar, hydro). Based in Perth and northern Western Australia near the world's largest iron-ore ports, the company is scaling a modular platform aimed at the roughly 8% of global CO2 emissions from iron and steelmaking, including its Pilbara Iron Super Hub at Port Hedland. Backed by a US$10M seed round led by Playground Global. This is an industrial deep-tech company with no public API or developer platform; the profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Embark Veterinary
providers.description: Embark Veterinary is a canine genomics and biotechnology company that sells at-home dog DNA test kits for breed identification, ancestry, and genetic health screening. Using a cheek-swab sample and a proprietary genotyping platform that analyzes over 200,000 genetic markers, Embark reports 400+ breeds, 270+ genetic health conditions, allergy risk, coat and trait predictions, a relative finder, and a breeder dashboard with a Pair Predictor tool. Embark is a direct-to-consumer service delivered through its website, mobile apps, and a research partner program (Cornell University, NIH, Morris Animal Foundation). As of this review it does not publish a documented public or partner developer API; results are consumed through Embark's own web/app dashboards, and customers can download their dog's raw genetic data file for personal use and sharing.

providers.name: emergen
providers.description: emergen (智昌科技集团股份有限公司, Zhichang Technology Group) is a Chinese industrial intelligence company founded by Dr. Gan Zhongxue, an expert in intelligent manufacturing. Built around its proprietary "ternary control" technology and cluster (swarm) robotics, the company positions itself as "AI + Control," delivering integrated "industrial agent" solutions that install a control "brain" into individual machines, production lines, and whole factories. Its portfolio spans robot controllers, ubiquitous controllers, industrial and collaborative robots, life-science robots, GVision 2D/3D machine vision, the GSC-AI100 sense-compute-control AI controller, a swarm-intelligence network controller, a micro-control cloud platform, and the "Jiangxin" family of industrial large models (design, production, service, and management). emergen serves automotive, electronics, equipment manufacturing, steel, metallurgy, textile, furniture, and shipbuilding sectors, plus Robotics-as-a-Service. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass no public developer/API surface was found.

providers.name: Epirus
providers.description: Epirus is a Torrance, California-based defense technology company building solid-state, software-defined high-power microwave (HPM) directed-energy systems for counter-electronics and counter-unmanned-aerial-systems (cUAS) missions. Its flagship product is Leonidas, a non-kinetic HPM weapon system designed to defeat single drones and large drone swarms by disabling their onboard electronics, with a growing product family that includes Leonidas IFPC-HPM (Indirect Fire Protection Capability — High-Power Microwave) for the U.S. Army, Leonidas Expeditionary (ExDECS) for the U.S. Marine Corps, Leonidas H2O for maritime interdiction, the portable Leonidas Pod, and Stryker Leonidas (with General Dynamics Land Systems). Epirus also collaborates with Anduril, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris, Kodiak AI, Peraton, and Palantir, and has received contracts from the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, DARPA, ONR, and Singapore's DSTA. The company is privately held, has raised more than $550M across Series B/C/D, and operates under CMMC Level 2 certification. Its product surface is classified defense hardware and embedded firmware — there is no public developer portal, REST API, SDK, or open-source software offering.

providers.name: Europass
providers.description: EuroPass is a Paris-based digital agency founded in 2016 that specializes in Chinese outbound tourism, describing itself as the European leader in implementing Chinese digital solutions for destinations, retailers, transportation, attractions, and hospitality brands. Its services span Chinese social-media management (notably WeChat and Weibo), WeChat mini-programs and stores, e-commerce, digital ticketing, destination marketing, and mobile payment acceptance via WeChat Pay and Alipay so European businesses can serve and transact with Chinese travelers. EuroPass operates as a services and marketing company rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and enriched with the identity and domain-security data available from its public web presence.

providers.name: Everyone Medicines
providers.description: Everyone Medicines is a therapeutics company listed in the Khosla Ventures portfolio under the Therapeutics category, where it is described as "individualized precision therapeutics." The company has no public developer or API surface as of July 2026. Its original web address, everyonemedicines.com, now issues a 301 redirect to www.eomeds.com, a domain registered through GoDaddy on 2024-05-11 that currently resolves to no DNS A record, so the site is dark and no page, documentation, or .well-known document can be retrieved. Probes of the package registries (npm, PyPI), GitHub organizations (everyonemedicines, eomeds), and the .well-known discovery surface all returned nothing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed life-sciences lead; it carries probed domain-security data only and should be re-run once the company publishes a live site.

providers.name: Fabheads
providers.description: Fabheads is a carbon fiber and composite manufacturing company (Fabheads Automation) that delivers end-to-end composite product development — design, analysis, tooling, prototyping, and production — using its own fiber-printing and automated-layup technology alongside traditional craftsmanship. It serves aerospace, mobility, marine, robotics, medical, and sports customers from aerospace-grade facilities, and publishes the C6 Slicer tool for composite fiber printing. Backed by Accel. As a hardware manufacturer it exposes no public developer API; this profile captures identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: FairMoney
providers.description: FairMoney is a credit-led digital bank for emerging markets, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Paris, France, with operating subsidiaries in Nigeria and India. The company began life as a France-incubated micro- lending app and pivoted to focus on Africa, becoming one of the largest digital lenders in Nigeria after the Central Bank of Nigeria granted its subsidiary a Microfinance Bank (MfB) license. FairMoney's consumer mobile app offers near-instant collateral-free personal loans, FlexiCredit, asset finance, savings products (FairLock, FairSave, FairTarget, FairDollar), a current account, debit cards, bill payments, and peer-to-peer transfers. Its Business Banking arm extends current accounts, payments, and credit to Nigerian SMEs. In India, FairMoney operates as a digital lender disbursing small-ticket personal loans through its mobile app. FairMoney does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a third-party developer portal; integration is internal and partner- driven, and the company's only public technical surface is its engineering GitHub organization, which mirrors infrastructure-as-code and open-source tooling forks (Terraform AWS modules, GitHub Actions, rubocop, puma plugins, salesforce_bulk_api) rather than a product API.

providers.name: finern
providers.description: Finern (Finern Automation) is a China-based industrial automation company that designs and builds fully automated production lines and intelligent measurement systems for manufacturing. It serves five sectors — automotive, electronics, new energy (battery/EV), healthcare/pharmaceutical equipment, and consumer goods — with automated assembly, testing, and inspection systems. The company reports 600+ personnel, 30,000+ square meters of facilities, 100+ global clients, 8 international sites, and 4 R&D centers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Finern publishes a corporate marketing website but does not currently expose any public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface (no /.well-known/*, llms.txt, or OpenAPI found on probe).

providers.name: Fixed Format
providers.description: Fixed format (also known as fixed-width) is a data interchange approach where every field has a predefined column width and is space-padded as needed. It contrasts with delimiter-separated formats like CSV, and is widely used in legacy mainframe systems, banking files, healthcare claims, government filings, and Unix system files such as /etc/passwd. While not an API in the REST sense, fixed-format files remain a critical data exchange medium that modern APIs and ETL pipelines must read and write.

providers.name: Floward
providers.description: Floward is a leading online flowers and luxury gifting company headquartered in Kuwait and operating across the Middle East and the United Kingdom. Founded in 2017, the company delivers fresh flower arrangements, curated gift boxes, chocolates, cakes, and personalized gifts to more than 40 cities across 9 countries, sourcing blooms daily from ethical growers worldwide and offering same-day and scheduled delivery through its web store and mobile apps. Floward is backed by investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks Floward as a company in the network; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and corporate site but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: Fluent.ai
providers.description: Fluent.ai is a Montreal-based speech recognition software company, founded in 2015, that voice-enables the world's devices with embedded, offline voice AI. Its patented "speech-to-intent" technology maps a user's speech directly to their intended action using acoustic deep neural networks, with no speech-to-text transcription and no cloud connection required. The result is a small-footprint, private-by-design engine that runs fully on-device, is robust to noise, and works across languages and accents. Fluent.ai licenses two core products to OEMs and ODMs: Fluent.ai Air (Automatic Intent Recognition), an on-device command-recognition engine, and Fluent.ai Wakeword, a small-footprint wake-word / keyword-spotting solution. Target markets include smart-home devices, wearables and hearables (including True Wireless Stereo), and industrial IoT and robotics.
