providers.description: Datacurve is a San Francisco-based AI infrastructure company that positions itself as "the data engine for frontier AI," building high-quality, expert-annotated datasets, reinforcement-learning environments, long-horizon agent tasks, benchmarks, and supervised fine-tuning demonstrations used to train and evaluate frontier AI models. Its offerings include off-the-shelf and custom datasets, agent-trajectory capture (tool calls, pivots, recovery attempts), and domain-sensitive evaluations across software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, machine learning, and research. Datacurve is backed by Homebrew and publishes research such as the DeepSWE long-horizon coding benchmark. The company sells through direct engagement (contact@datacurve.ai) and currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: DataFox
providers.description: DataFox was a San Francisco company-intelligence and sales-prospecting startup, backed by GV among others, that used machine learning to collect and score signals about private and public companies (funding rounds, hiring, news, growth signals) and delivered them to sales and marketing teams through a web application, CRM integrations, and a company-data API. Oracle acquired DataFox and folded its company-and-signals data into the Oracle Cloud CX / Oracle Fusion Marketing stack. The independent product has been fully retired: as of this profile the datafox.com apex and www hosts are served from Oracle infrastructure and every path under www.datafox.com issues a blanket HTTP 301 to Oracle marketing pages, while api.datafox.com and app.datafox.com resolve to a parked Oracle address that accepts no connections. There is no surviving DataFox developer portal, documentation, API reference, or specification to harvest, so this profile is retained as a historical/acquired company record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Datost
providers.description: Datost Inc. is a New York applied research lab building hardware and intelligent systems that operate in your environment without demanding constant attention — "computers that come after the screen." Its first public product is ED1TH, a 25-gram pair of AI augmented-reality smart glasses with a 640x480 green Micro-LED in-lens display readable in direct sunlight, hot-swap battery cells, a companion steel smart ring for gesture control, and a privacy-first design with zero cameras and a single hardware-mutable microphone. ED1TH runs ED1TH-OS and handles email, calendar, turn-by-turn navigation, live translation, and meeting transcription in the wearer's field of view. Datost is backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and OpenAI. As a consumer hardware and applied-research company, Datost does not currently publish a public web API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Diablo Technologies
providers.description: Diablo Technologies Inc. was an enterprise memory technology company backed by Battery Ventures. It developed Memory Channel Storage (MCS), an architecture that placed flash storage directly on the DDR memory bus, and productized it as Memory1, a flash-as-DRAM DIMM the company marketed as delivering up to 256 GB of memory per module and 4 TB per dual-socket server. Diablo positioned itself as a silicon and module vendor selling through server and storage OEM partners rather than as a software or platform company: it never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or any machine-readable specification, and no developer surface appears anywhere in the archived record of its website. The company appears to be defunct. Its corporate site is last archived intact in 2017, the domain subsequently served unrelated SEO spam, the diablo-technologies.com registration lapsed and was re-registered on 2023-10-08 through a different registrar, and the hostname today serves an unrelated consumer-gadget review blog with no connection to the memory business. No GitHub organization exists under either diablo-technologies or diablotechnologies. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface.

providers.name: Discovery Communications
providers.description: Discovery Communications was a global media company providing original and purchased programming across multiple distribution platforms before merging with WarnerMedia in 2022 to form Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), a leading global media and entertainment company whose portfolio spans HBO Max, Discovery Channel, CNN, Warner Bros. film studios, DC, Food Network, HGTV, and other television, film, and streaming brands. No public developer APIs are documented at the corporate level; technical and partnership inquiries are handled at the individual brand or business-unit level.

providers.name: docin
providers.description: docin (豆丁网, docin.com) is a Chinese C2C document-sharing platform operated by Beijing Docin Century Network Technology (北京豆丁世纪网络技术有限公司) that faces the global market. The platform hosts over 1.3 billion documents, books, magazines, and publications spanning education, architecture and construction, business and contracts, medical and psychological materials, industry reports, and legal documents, supporting both learning and practical application. It offers a "豆丁书房" (Docin Reading Room) mobile reading app and VIP membership tiers. docin was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Probing found no public developer or API platform: open.docin.com 301-redirects to the homepage, /app/api returns 404, and no /.well-known discovery documents are published.

providers.name: Dollar Shave Club
providers.description: Dollar Shave Club is a direct-to-consumer men's grooming brand founded in 2011 and best known for its subscription razor and blade service that ships razors, blades, shave butter, and personal-care products to members on a recurring schedule. Acquired by Unilever in 2016 and later sold to Nexus Capital Management in 2023, the company sells online through its storefront at dollarshaveclub.com. Its e-commerce experience runs on Shopify; the storefront host exposes Shopify Customer Account OAuth2/OIDC discovery documents (including Shopify's customer-account-api and customer-account-mcp-api scopes) but Dollar Shave Club publishes no first-party public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation of its own. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub of a16z, Cowboy Ventures, Dragoneer, and Forerunner Ventures.

providers.name: Domtar
providers.description: Domtar is committed to turning responsibly sourced wood fiber into essential products like paper, pulp, recycled packaging, tissue, and lumber. No public developer-facing APIs have been identified at this time; this index will be updated if any are made available.

providers.name: Duetto
providers.description: Duetto is a San Francisco–headquartered hospitality technology company providing a cloud-based Revenue and Profit Operating System (RP-OS) for hotels, casinos, resorts, and independent properties. Duetto's platform combines dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, group business optimization, benchmarking, and reporting to help hospitality operators optimize room rates, profitability, and total revenue performance. Core products include GameChanger (real-time dynamic pricing engine), ScoreBoard (forecasting and reporting dashboard), BlockBuster (group business optimization), Advance (AI-powered demand forecasting), HotStats (profitability benchmarking), and GameTime (select-service hotel revenue management). Duetto serves over 7,500 properties in more than 100 countries, with customers including Meliá, Sonesta, Virgin Hotels, and Sandman Hotel Group. Duetto integrates with major property management systems (PMS), central reservation systems (CRS), booking engines, and channel managers including Cloudbeds, Oracle OPERA / OHIP, Mews, Sabre, Amadeus, SiteMinder, and Infor. Duetto exposes an Open API for technical integration partners but does not publish a public, self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification — API access is partner-only and gated through a structured onboarding process with a self-testing toolkit. Revenue is generated through SaaS subscriptions to its revenue management products.

providers.name: eBPF Foundation
providers.description: The eBPF Foundation is a Linux Foundation project that advances eBPF technology by guiding upstream development, promoting its benefits, and enhancing its security and reliability. eBPF enables programmable kernel functionality for networking, observability, tracing, and security without changing kernel source code. The Foundation itself does not operate a public API; it stewards the technology and community.

providers.name: Eeki Foods
providers.description: Eeki Foods is a food company listed in the General Catalyst portfolio and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer surface: eekifoods.com serves a pre-launch "Launching Soon" placeholder page, there are no api./docs./developer. subdomains in DNS, no /.well-known/ discovery documents, no llms.txt, no first-party client libraries on npm or PyPI, and no GitHub organization or repositories. The domain is held and mail-enabled (Google Workspace MX) and serves valid TLS 1.3 with HSTS, so this remains a live lead worth re-checking once the company launches a public product surface.

providers.name: Enel X
providers.description: Enel X is the advanced-energy-services business line of the Enel Group, an Italian multinational utility headquartered in Rome. Enel X delivers smart energy products and services across electrification, e-mobility, demand response, virtual power plants, and distributed energy resource (DER) management for residential, commercial, industrial, public-sector, and utility customers. Its principal offerings include the Enel X Way app and network for electric-vehicle charging (the consolidated successor to JuicePass and JuiceNet), the JuiceBox and JuicePedestal hardware lines, the JuiceNet Utility Edition managed-charging platform, the DER.OS / DER optimization software (now run as Calibrant Energy in North America after Enel's 2023 divestiture of its North American demand-response business), Enel X Flex flexibility management software, and VPP Connect, a set of API endpoints that lets third-party DER operators — OEMs, automation providers, and equipment manufacturers — aggregate EV chargers, batteries, HVAC systems, heat pumps, and other controllable assets into Enel's virtual power plant and earn revenue from demand-response and grid-services programs via either the open Automated Demand Response (oADR) protocol or a custom Enel API. Enel X exposes additional non-public surfaces — including the emobility.enelx.com OAuth/charging endpoints used by the Enel X Way mobile apps — but does not publish OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal; VPP Connect documentation is delivered under partnership agreement after a guided onboarding process. The official Enelx GitHub organization has effectively no public engineering presence, and the legacy JuiceNet public API has been deprecated as part of the platform migration to Enel X Way.

providers.name: Entity Relationship
providers.description: Entity-Relationship (ER) modeling is a data modeling technique used to describe the data requirements for an information system. ER diagrams visually represent entities (objects or concepts), their attributes, and the relationships between them. ER modeling is a fundamental tool in database design and system analysis, with notation variants including Chen's original notation, Crow's Foot notation, and Barker's notation.

providers.name: EpiBiologics
providers.description: EpiBiologics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Mateo, California, developing bispecific antibodies for directed extracellular protein degradation. Its proprietary EpiTAC platform leverages an atlas of 270+ degradation-inducing cell-surface receptors to build tissue-selective therapies that degrade disease-causing proteins while sparing healthy tissue, targeting cancer, autoimmune, and other serious diseases. The company dosed its first patient with EPI-326 (an EGFR-driven solid-tumor bispecific) in a Phase 1 study in April 2026 and closed a $107M Series B round in January 2026. Backed by GV, EpiBiologics was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile; it publishes a corporate website but no public developer/API surface.

providers.name: FAI & GLOBAL SOLUTIONS HOLDING LIMITED
providers.description: FAI & GLOBAL SOLUTIONS HOLDING LIMITED is a Saudi Arabian holding company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its site at fai.sa is a WordPress property served from nginx behind a WAF that returns HTTP 403 to every external request except /robots.txt, so no company description, developer portal, documentation, or API surface could be retrieved during the enrichment pass. No public API, specification, SDK, or event surface has been observed to date; the domain-security posture was probed successfully and is recorded in security/. Re-probe from an allowed network on a later round to confirm whether a developer surface exists behind the block.

providers.name: Filmgrail
providers.description: Filmgrail is an Oslo, Norway based software company offering an AI-powered digital platform for cinema operators. Its product suite bundles a cinema content management system (CMS), native iOS and Android mobile apps, branded cinema websites, and marketing and analytics tooling into a single managed offering, with a loyalty system, festival platform, push notifications, and a planning tool layered on top. Filmgrail markets these capabilities as a way to automate cinema operations and grow digital ticket sales and moviegoer engagement, and describes API-based integration between its platform and cinema point-of-sale systems, websites, and mobile apps. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from Oslo, Norway and Delaware, USA. Filmgrail does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: First Solar
providers.description: First Solar is a leading global provider of comprehensive photovoltaic (PV) solar energy solutions, designing and manufacturing thin-film solar modules. No public developer portal or open APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: FMC Technologies (now TechnipFMC)
providers.description: FMC Technologies was a Houston-based energy services and equipment company serving the upstream oil and gas industry, particularly subsea, surface, and measurement solutions for hydrocarbon production. In January 2017 FMC Technologies completed its merger with Technip to form TechnipFMC, a global energy services company serving the subsea, surface, and offshore project markets. This repository tracks the legacy FMC Technologies brand and any successor APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with the merged TechnipFMC entity. No public APIs or developer programs are currently published.

providers.name: Forge Robotics
providers.description: Forge Robotics is a Galway, Ireland and San Francisco based robotics company building modular autonomous factories for metal fabrication. Its shipping container sized, software configurable units combine a vision system, sub millimeter 3D scanning, and robotic intelligence to autonomously handle, position, weld, laser engrave, and finish metal assemblies, turning conventional human programmed industrial welding robot arms into autonomous members of the workforce. The company targets the skilled welder shortage in US manufacturing with continuously operating, snap together production modules. Forge Robotics was co founded by Eoin Cobbe (CEO) and Robert Cormican (CTO) and is a Y Combinator backed pre seed startup. As of this profile the company exposes a marketing and product website only, with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Fox Corporation
providers.description: Fox Corporation is a U.S. media company whose portfolio includes Fox News Media, Fox Sports, Fox Entertainment, Fox Television Stations, and the ad-supported streaming service Tubi. Fox is a Fortune 500 consumer of cloud, AI, and media technology APIs (notably AWS as preferred AI cloud provider) but does not publish a public developer portal at the corporate level.

providers.name: GigaCloud Technology
providers.description: GigaCloud Technology (NASDAQ: GCT) operates the GigaCloud Marketplace, a global B2B e-commerce platform for large-parcel merchandise such as furniture, home furnishings, fitness equipment, and appliances. The marketplace connects manufacturers, primarily in Asia, with resellers across the United States, Europe, and Japan, integrating product discovery, transactions, and end-to-end cross-border logistics including ocean freight, warehousing, and last-mile delivery. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a dcm-ventures portfolio lead. Enrichment probes found no public developer portal, API documentation, or well-known discovery surface; the corporate site is behind bot protection (HTTP 403), so this profile is limited to verified domain-security posture and company identity.

providers.name: Gimme Media
providers.description: Gimme Media is the Techstars-backed music company behind Gimme Radio, the heavy-metal streaming and live-DJ radio platform that later expanded into Gimme Metal and Gimme Country. The standalone streaming apps were wound down, and the brand now operates as a Shopify-hosted storefront at gimmemetal.com selling vinyl, merchandise, and exclusive releases to the metal community. As of this enrichment pass Gimme Media publishes no first-party public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation; the only machine-readable surfaces served at its domain are the Shopify Customer Accounts platform OIDC endpoints, which belong to the hosting platform rather than to a Gimme Media API.

providers.name: Givemetap
providers.description: GiveMeTap is a UK-based social-enterprise consumer brand that designs and sells reusable, BPA-free stainless-steel and insulated water bottles (500ml and 700ml, plus custom co-branded bottles for businesses). For every bottle sold, GiveMeTap funds five years of clean drinking water for a person in Ghana, giving 20% of its revenue to water projects in Africa; the company reports 116,391 people reached with clean water for life. It operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront on the Shopify platform. GiveMeTap is a physical-products company with no first-party developer API, developer portal, or public API documentation; it was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub.

providers.name: GM OnStar
providers.description: GM OnStar is General Motors' connected vehicle services platform, originally launched in 1996 as an in-vehicle safety, security, and concierge service and since extended into a commercial data platform under OnStar Business Solutions. The OnStar Business Solutions API and Data Services product delivers near-real-time embedded telematics straight from properly equipped 2015-model-year-or-newer GM vehicles — Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac — without aftermarket hardware, exposing vehicle location, speed, ignition status, odometer, fuel level, EV state-of-charge and charging status, tire pressure, seatbelt status, diagnostic trouble codes, and driver-behavior events such as hard brake and hard acceleration. The product is packaged into tiered plans (commonly referenced as API Starter and API Pro) and is distributed primarily through OnStar's enterprise channel under the GM Envolve commercial brand, plus integrations with fleet management providers including Samsara, Geotab, Wheels, Verizon Connect, and other approved telematic service providers. There is no public self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI specification — access is gated through GM/OnStar sales (developer.gm.com is a request-access endpoint) or via an authorized integration partner. Consumer-facing OnStar mobile features (remote start, remote lock, vehicle locate, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, Super Cruise telemetry) are delivered through GM's myChevrolet, myBuick, myGMC, and myCadillac apps and are not part of the published API surface.

providers.name: Halp
providers.description: Halp was a conversational ticketing and help-desk tool that let teams turn Slack and Microsoft Teams messages into trackable tickets, founded in Boulder, Colorado and backed by Techstars. Atlassian acquired Halp in February 2020 and folded its capabilities into Jira Service Management; the standalone Halp product and its API were subsequently discontinued. The halp.com domain now resolves to Atlassian and is served from Atlassian's edge, so no independent Halp developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or MCP surface remains to enrich. This profile records the company's history and the (Atlassian-operated) security posture still observable on the halp.com domain.

providers.name: Hawk-Eye Innovations
providers.description: Hawk-Eye Innovations is a Basingstoke, UK-headquartered sports technology company and part of the Sony Group, specializing in precision optical tracking, electronic officiating, video replay, and performance analytics across 25+ professional sports in 100+ countries. Founded in 2001 by Paul Hawkins and acquired by Sony in 2011, Hawk-Eye operates alongside Pulselive and Beyond Sports within Sony's sports division. The company is the standard for ball-tracking in tennis (Electronic Line Calling, now used in place of human line judges at the major tours), goal-line technology and semi-automated offside in football (Premier League, FIFA), video replay in cricket (DRS), NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, rugby, and PGA Tour shot-tracking. Core product platforms include SMART Replay, SMART Track, SMART Insight, HawkAR, iHawk, HawkREPLAY, HawkNEST, HawkVISION, SkeleTRACK, Electronic Line Calling, Goal Line Technology, Semi-Automated Offside Technology, and VAR systems. Revenue comes from long-term contracts with leagues, federations, and broadcasters; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hawk-Eye products. All integrations are bespoke and delivered through Sony Sports Business / Hawk-Eye operations teams.

providers.name: Headgum
providers.description: Headgum is an American comedy podcast network founded in 2015 by Marty Michael, Amir Blumenfeld, and Jake Hurwitz, with studios in Los Angeles and New York. It produces and distributes premium comedy and entertainment podcasts including Doughboys, Not Another D&D Podcast, Dead Eyes, Hey Riddle Riddle, and Why Won't You Date Me?, and operates Gumball, a host-read podcast and YouTube advertising marketplace that lets brands buy ads directly from creators. Headgum is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Headgum publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Health Standards
providers.description: Health Standards covers the collection of technical standards and specifications used in healthcare interoperability, including HL7 FHIR, HL7 v2, CDA, DICOM, IHE profiles, ICD codes, SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, US Core, and other health data exchange and coding standards. This index curates the canonical specifications, reference implementations, registries, and developer resources for building interoperable healthcare applications.

providers.name: Helion Energy
providers.description: Helion Energy is an Everett, Washington fusion power company building commercial fusion electricity generators using a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed configuration (FRC) approach burning deuterium and helium-3. Helion forms two FRC plasmas at opposite ends of its machine, accelerates them toward each other, merges them, and uses pulsed magnetic compression to drive them to fusion conditions; the expanding plasma pushes against the confining magnetic field and induces current directly back into the machine's capacitor bank via Faraday's Law, recapturing electricity without a steam cycle. Founded in 2013 by David Kirtley, John Slough, Chris Pihl, and George Votroubek, Helion is chaired by Sam Altman and has progressed through seven generations of prototypes (IPA, Venti, Trenta, and most recently Polaris) on its way to commercial generators. Polaris, brought online in late 2024, is the company's seventh-generation machine and the first privately developed fusion device to demonstrate measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, reaching 150 million degrees Celsius in February 2026. In May 2023, Helion signed the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement, committing to deliver 50 MWe to Microsoft starting in 2028, with the Orion plant planned for the Malaga, Washington area; a subsequent agreement with Nucor targets a 500-MWe facility. Helion is funded by Sam Altman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Nucor, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and others, with a reported $5.4B valuation as of early 2025. The company's revenue model is fusion electricity sales under long-term PPAs; Helion has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source software product, and its public GitHub organization (Helion-Energy) contains only forks of plasma-physics simulation tools (WarpX, FerroX, pyamrex, maestrowf).

providers.name: HelloFresh
providers.description: HelloFresh SE is a publicly listed (Frankfurt Stock Exchange: HFG), Berlin-headquartered global meal-kit and food-solutions company that ships recipes and pre-portioned ingredients to households across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. Its brand portfolio includes HelloFresh, Factor, Green Chef, EveryPlate, Chefs Plate, Youfoodz, and Good Chop. HelloFresh does not publish a public consumer developer API; its engineering organization is active in open source on GitHub, maintaining widely used infrastructure tooling such as the Janus API gateway, the health-go healthcheck library, and the goengine event-sourcing framework. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Insight Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd.
providers.description: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd. (海兴电力 / Hexing) is a Chinese energy-technology company focused on smart power distribution and utilization, new energy, smart water and gas, water treatment and clean water, and marine electrification. Beyond hardware, Hexing delivers integrated solutions and project delivery spanning metering devices, communication networks (RF, PLC, cellular, NB-IoT), MDC / MDM / AMI platforms, billing systems, distribution automation, energy storage (BESS), EV charging, water metering, seawater desalination and electric marine propulsion. The company reports 34 years of industry experience, operations across 110+ countries and 17 global manufacturing hubs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; Hexing publishes no public developer/API surface today, so this profile captures corporate identity plus the AI knowledge file (llms.txt) the company publishes for AI search / RAG.

providers.name: HiddenLayer
providers.description: HiddenLayer is an Austin, Texas-based AI security company founded in March 2022 by Chris Sestito (CEO), Tanner Burns (Chief Scientist), and Jim Ballard (CIO) — former Cylance researchers who encountered a real-world attack on production ML models. HiddenLayer builds an AI Security Platform that protects machine learning and generative AI systems across their entire lifecycle, comprising four integrated modules: AI Discovery (catalogs AI assets and eliminates shadow AI), AI Supply Chain Security (Model Scanner inspects models, weights, and pickle/RDS files for malicious payloads and backdoors), AI Attack Simulation (continuous adversarial red-teaming for agentic and generative systems), and AI Runtime Security / AIDR (a real-time detection-and-response firewall using deterministic classifiers that sit outside the model inference path to detect prompt injection, jailbreaks, indirect attacks, data leakage, and malicious tool calls in agentic and MCP systems). The platform exposes native connectors for CI/CD, MLOps, SIEM/SOAR, API gateways, and major data and cloud platforms, plus guardrail integrations for OpenAI Agents, LangChain, AWS Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework, Azure APIM, and a GitHub Action for Model Scanner. HiddenLayer publishes Python, TypeScript, and Java/Kotlin SDKs and research-grade tooling such as HiddenPickle (Python pickle disassembler/patcher) and HiddenPromise (R .rdx/.rdb/.rds disassembler). The company has raised $56M total ($50M Series A in September 2023 led by M12 / Microsoft's Venture Fund and Moore Strategic Ventures, with Booz Allen Ventures, IBM Ventures, Capital One Ventures, and Ten Eleven Ventures participating) and serves Fortune 500 enterprises, financial services, and US Federal agencies. The HiddenLayer SaaS console and REST API are gated behind enterprise sales and not publicly self-serve, placing this profile in Tier-3 (enterprise-gated) coverage.

providers.name: Humans
providers.description: humans& is a human-centric frontier AI lab founded in 2025 and publicly announced on January 20, 2026, building large-scale AI models centered on people and their relationships rather than raw autonomy. Its research spans long-horizon and multi-agent reinforcement learning, memory, and user understanding, tightly integrating science and product so that AI acts as connective tissue that strengthens organizations and communities. The founding team comes from frontier industry and academic labs including xAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, Reflection, AI2, Stanford, and MIT. Its seed round is led by SV Angel and co-founder Georges Harik, with investors including NVIDIA, GV (Google Ventures), Emerson Collective, Forerunner, S32, DCVC, and Jeff Bezos. As a pre-product research lab it publishes no public API yet; this profile captures its verified public identity surfaces.

providers.name: IA Ventures
providers.description: IA Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm based in New York City, at 920 Broadway, 15th Floor. It backs founders building data-driven businesses across financial technology, machine learning, and infrastructure, typically at the seed and early stage. IA Ventures was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent firm within the API Evangelist network and is profiled here as a venture-capital company rather than an API producer: it publishes a minimal single-page website and does not expose a public API, developer portal, or event surface. This profile captures the firm's identity and the security posture of its public domain.

providers.name: Iambic Therapeutics
providers.description: Iambic Therapeutics is a San Diego, California AI-driven drug discovery company founded in 2019 by Thomas Miller (CEO) and Fred Manby (CTO) that designs small-molecule therapeutics for oncology and other indications. Iambic builds proprietary AI models for drug discovery, including Enchant, a multimodal transformer that predicts clinical properties (pharmacokinetics, cellular and biochemical activity) of candidate molecules from early discovery data, and NeuralPLexer (now NeuralPLexer3), a flow-based generative model for protein-ligand complex structure prediction used to identify cryptic pockets and guide structure-based design. Both lines of work have been published at venues including NeurIPS 2025. The company's internal pipeline is oncology-led: IAM1363, a brain-penetrant selective HER2 / HER2-mutant inhibitor, completed Phase 1/1b dose escalation in 2025 and is in dose optimization with clinical activity reported at ESMO 2025; IAM-K1 (KIF18A) and IAM-C1 (CDK2/4) are preclinical, alongside undisclosed neurology, gastrointestinal, and inflammation discovery programs. In February 2026 Iambic announced a discovery and technology collaboration with Takeda worth up to ~$1.7B plus royalties, following a $100M+ private financing in November 2025 and total disclosed funding of approximately $334M. The company has been named to the CNBC Disruptor 50 list in 2025 and 2026 and has signaled intent to access public markets, including via a SPAC. Iambic's public GitHub footprint is limited to np-bench, a BSD-3 benchmark library for 3D biomolecular structure prediction; the underlying NeuralPLexer and Enchant models are proprietary and there is no public developer API, SDK, or commercial platform offering.

providers.name: ICF (ICF International)
providers.description: ICF (NASDAQ: ICFI), formerly ICF International, is a global consulting and digital services firm headquartered in Reston, Virginia, delivering management, technology, and policy consulting to US federal agencies, state and local governments, utilities, and commercial clients. ICF serves markets spanning government, energy, environment, infrastructure, transportation, health, education, social programs, public safety, and disaster management, with approximately 9,000 employees worldwide. The firm has invested in an in-house AI offering branded "ICF Fathom," but no public REST APIs, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation have been identified. ICF's work is delivered under contract rather than through a productized developer platform.

providers.name: IDEX Corporation
providers.description: IDEX Corporation (NYSE: IEX) is a global engineered products company that designs and manufactures pumps, flow meters, valves, fluidics systems, precision components, and fire and safety equipment. IDEX serves health, science, water, energy, semiconductor, aerospace, fire and safety, and industrial markets through three segments: Fluid and Metering Technologies, Health and Science Technologies, and Fire and Safety / Diversified Products.

providers.name: Imbue
providers.description: Imbue is a San Francisco AI research lab building agentic foundation models for reasoning and the human tooling around them, with a stated mission of AI that is loyal to its user. The team trains large reasoning models in-house (including a 70B model trained from scratch with open-sourced tooling and evaluation datasets) and publishes research on agent and reasoning architectures, reinforcement learning, data generation, and the scientific theory of deep learning. Imbue ships practical tools that emerge from the research, including Sculptor and mngr for orchestrating parallel coding agents, Bouncer for filtering social feeds, and Blueprint and Vet. There is no public commercial inference API; integration happens through open-sourced repositories, model artifacts on Hugging Face, and research releases.

providers.name: Inkbox
providers.description: Inkbox is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce company selling semi-permanent temporary tattoos. Its proprietary "For Now Ink" formula is made with Genipa plant extract and develops into the skin to last up to about two weeks, longer than surface-level temporary tattoos. Inkbox sells thousands of pre-designed tattoos from independent artists and offers a custom service where customers upload their own artwork to create personalized designs. The business operates as a consumer retail brand with an online store, and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Insilico Medicine
providers.description: Insilico Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company applying generative AI and robotic automation to drug discovery and development. Its Pharma.AI software suite includes PandaOmics (target discovery from multi-omics data), Chemistry42 (generative chemistry with retrosynthesis, property prediction, and ADMET), Generative Biologics, inClinico (clinical trial outcome prediction), Science42 DORA (research assistant), Nach01, and PreciousGPT-family models for life sciences. The company runs its own therapeutic pipeline spanning oncology, fibrosis, and inflammation, with programs targeting TNIK, USP1, QPCTL, PHD, MAT2A, TEAD, ENPP1, KAT6 and others through Phase II. Insilico monetizes through Pharma.AI software licensing, partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies, and progression of its in-house assets. Pharma.AI tools are commercial SaaS products accessed via web UI; the company publishes open-source research code on GitHub (GENTRL, fcd_torch, BiAAE, DD-VAE, DORA) but does not expose a public commercial API.

providers.name: Ion Mobility
providers.description: ION Mobility is a Singapore-headquartered technology and automotive company that designs and builds affordable, zero-emission smart electric motorcycles for riders across Southeast Asia, with its flagship M1-S model and a companion rider mobile app. The company combines advanced hardware and software with human-centred design, spanning electric two-wheelers and energy charging and storage solutions, with additional offices in Jakarta and Shenzhen and backing from investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and identity surface; ION Mobility currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification, operating a consumer waitlist/test-ride site and an internal open-source tooling estate on GitHub.

providers.name: Isono Health
providers.description: iSono Health is a Sunnyvale, California medical device company behind ATUSA, described as the first AI-driven portable and automated 3D breast ultrasound scanner. ATUSA performs fully automated whole-breast imaging in about two minutes per breast without a trained sonographer, pairing a 3D ultrasound scanner and wearable accessory with a Windows desktop/tablet application and HIPAA-compliant cloud storage for real-time 2D and 3D visualization, lesion localization, and remote monitoring. The system is FDA 510(k) cleared and targets more accessible point-of-care breast cancer screening and monitoring. iSono Health is a Y Combinator-backed company. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: J.C. Penney
providers.description: J.C. Penney Company, Inc. (JCPenney) is an American department store chain offering apparel, accessories, beauty, jewelry, footwear, and home goods. The company emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in late 2020 and continues to operate hundreds of department stores across the United States and Puerto Rico.

providers.name: Jumbo Privacy
providers.description: Jumbo (Jumbo Privacy) was a mobile-first consumer privacy and security assistant founded in 2019 by Pierre Valade, the co-founder of the Sunrise calendar app acquired by Microsoft. The iPhone/Android app helped everyday users take control of their online privacy by automatically hardening privacy settings across services like Google, Facebook, Twitter/X, Amazon, and LinkedIn, cleaning up old social posts, monitoring data breaches, and bundling identity-theft insurance. It was explicitly designed to process user data locally on-device with no server-side processing, so it never exposed a public developer API, SDK, or documented integration surface. Jumbo was backed by investors including Balderton Capital and Thrive Capital before being acqui-hired by cyber-insurer Coalition in 2023; the standalone consumer app was wound down and fully discontinued by 2024. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record - there is no active API to enrich.

providers.name: Kairos Power
providers.description: Kairos Power is an Alameda, California-based advanced nuclear fission company developing the KP-FHR (Kairos Power Fluoride salt-cooled High-temperature Reactor), a Generation IV reactor design that uses TRISO (tri-structural isotropic) fuel pebbles cooled by molten fluoride salt (FLiBe) at low pressure and high temperature. Kairos Power is building Hermes, a low-power demonstration reactor at the East Tennessee Technology Park in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, which became the first non-light-water reactor authorized for construction by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission in over 50 years (construction permit issued December 2023). A second unit, Hermes 2, will pair two reactors with a 28 MWe electricity-generating turbine. In October 2024 Google signed a corporate power purchase agreement with Kairos Power for up to 500 MW of nuclear electricity from multiple small modular reactors, with the first deployment targeted by 2030 and additional capacity through 2035 — the first corporate PPA for new advanced nuclear in the United States. The company's revenue model is reactor sales, electricity PPAs, and federal cost-share partnerships (DOE Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program). Kairos Power is privately held, does not expose a public developer API or SDK, and operates under NRC regulatory oversight as a safety-critical nuclear licensee.

providers.name: Kencko Foods
providers.description: Kencko is a direct-to-consumer functional-food company that makes no-fuss instant smoothies and other whole-food products from 100% organic, vegan, freeze-dried fruits and vegetables with no added sugars. Customers subscribe and shop through a Shopify-hosted online store at kencko.com. Kencko is a Techstars-backed portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead for the enrichment pipeline. It publishes no first-party developer API; the only machine-readable discovery surface on its domain is the Shopify Customer Account API OIDC/OAuth well-known configuration that backs storefront customer login.

providers.name: Kodit.io
providers.description: Kodit.io was a Helsinki-based proptech and "iBuyer" that used machine learning and automation to make instant cash offers on residential property, buying homes directly from sellers and reselling them, with operations in Finland, Spain and Poland. Founded in 2017 and backed by Speedinvest among others, the company rebranded to Rive in 2022 after a EUR 23M Series A aimed at simplifying home buying and selling across Europe. In January 2024 Rive (formerly Kodit.io) transferred its entire Finnish real estate brokerage business to Neliöt Liikkuu LKV, and the Kodit.io LKV entity subsequently entered bankruptcy proceedings in late 2024. The company operated a consumer-facing marketplace only; it never published a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts, and the kodit.io domain has since lapsed to an unrelated registrant. This profile is retained as a historical network record.

providers.name: Koo
providers.description: Koo was an Indian microblogging and social networking platform built by Bombinate Technologies, positioned as a multilingual, India-first alternative to Twitter/X with support for Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi and other regional languages. Backed by Accel and Tiger Global, it grew during the 2021 Indian social-media policy disputes before ceasing operations in 2024 after funding and acquisition talks fell through. Koo never published a public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs, and its domain no longer serves a site — this profile is retained as a verified-defunct historical record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Kuwo Music
providers.description: Kuwo Music (酷我音乐) is a Chinese online music streaming service, founded in Beijing in 2005, that grew from a desktop music player into one of China's major consumer streaming apps across desktop, web, and mobile. Kuwo merged with Kugou under China Music Corporation, which was subsequently acquired by Tencent Music Entertainment Group, and Kuwo now operates as one of TME's music apps alongside QQ Music and Kugou. Kuwo entered the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead via Qiming. It is a consumer-facing streaming property rather than an API-first provider, and no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface has been verified for it.

providers.name: Kyndryl
providers.description: Kyndryl is a Fortune 500 IT infrastructure services company spun off from IBM in 2021. The company designs, builds, manages, and modernizes mission-critical technology systems across cloud, mainframe, networking, digital workplace, security, applications, data, and AI. Kyndryl operates the Kyndryl Bridge integration and observability platform, runs the Kyndryl Vital design studios, and partners with hyperscalers including AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and SAP. No public developer API has been documented.

providers.name: Layer By Layer
providers.description: Layer By Layer was a San Francisco 3D-printing software startup founded in 2012 and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2013 batch. It operated a marketplace for buying, selling, and sharing printable 3D designs, and built streaming and digital rights management technology that let licensed content partners distribute 3D-printable intellectual property without handing over raw model files. MakerBot (Stratasys) announced its acquisition of the company in November 2014 and folded the streaming and DRM technology into the MakerBot Digital Store. The company no longer operates independently: layerbylayer.com is a parked domain, and there is no developer portal, documentation, public API, or GitHub organization to enrich.

providers.name: Leidos
providers.description: Leidos, a Fortune 500 digital and mission innovator, delivers solutions at the intersection of national security, health, and critical infrastructure. With a global workforce of approximately 47,000, the company is executing its NorthStar 2030 strategy focused on five growth engines: space and maritime, energy infrastructure, digital modernization and cyber, mission software, and managed health. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified.

providers.name: Lenda
providers.description: Lenda was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment on 2026-07-19 found no operating surface: lenda.com returns HTTP 200 but serves only a parked single-page notice offering the domain for sale via a contact form, hosted on AWS and registered through Amazon Registrar. Every developer-facing subdomain probed (api, developer, developers, docs, app, status, blog) is NXDOMAIN, the full /.well-known/ discovery surface plus /llms.txt, /openapi.json and /robots.txt all return 404, and there is no first-party package on npm or PyPI and no company GitHub organization. This company is treated as defunct with no API to catalog; no artifact pointers are wired because no artifacts genuinely exist.

providers.name: Likeplum
providers.description: Likeplum (likeplum.com) was an online expert-knowledge and task marketplace that billed itself as "expert knowledge and skills at your fingertips" and invited users to "ask experts to answer your questions and hire skilled engineers, programmers, designers, writers, marketers and more on the world's largest information trading marketplace." Members posted either a free-to-ask question or a paid task, received answers and completed work from the site's expert pool, and paid only after approving the result under a post-pay model, with optional fully private posts and card or PayPal settlement. Its busiest categories were writing, programming, graphic design, and marketing and SEO. By late 2014 the company had folded the brand into the "Createpool" network, splitting its four most popular categories into dedicated sites — hackerpool.com for programming tasks, studypool.com for academic and homework Q&A, mechanicpool.com for auto repair, and counselpool.com for legal questions — and migrated every likeplum account, question, answer, and profile across. Only the academic property survives today: likeplum.com now 301-redirects to www.studypool.com, while createpool.com fails TLS negotiation and hackerpool.com, mechanicpool.com, and counselpool.com no longer resolve. The Likeplum brand exposes no developer portal, documentation, SDK, package, or public API, so this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record for a rebranded 500 Global portfolio company rather than as an API provider.

providers.name: Lotus
providers.description: Lotus (Lotus Health AI) is a consumer healthcare company delivering AI-driven medical care backed by real physicians through an iOS app. The service offers an AI Doctor that analyzes a member's health, prescriptions sent to any U.S. pharmacy, lab orders across 6,000+ test sites, centralized medical-record storage, and 24/7 care. Founded by KJ Dhaliwal (CEO) and Zekka Nelson (CTO) with clinicians from UCLA Health, UCSF, and Johns Hopkins, and backed by CRV among others. As of this enrichment pass Lotus publishes no public developer/API surface: no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, well-known discovery, or security.txt were found. Only an end-user Intercom help center and a careers page are public.

providers.name: LotusFlare
providers.description: LotusFlare is a cloud-native digital commerce and monetization platform for telecommunications operators. Its Digital Network Operator (DNO) Cloud provides charging, product catalog, ordering, and digital customer-experience (BSS) capabilities as a managed SaaS to mobile carriers, and powers eSIM and travel-connectivity brands. The platform is delivered to enterprise telecom customers rather than through a public self-serve developer API; no public developer portal or API definition was discoverable at profile time. Backed by GV and Social Capital.

providers.name: LuxCreo
providers.description: LuxCreo is a hardtech company delivering same-day dental 3D printing through an integrated ecosystem of hardware, materials, and cloud software. Its dental line pairs the FDA Class II 510(k)-cleared iLux Pro Dental printer, iLuxWash cleaning, and iLuxCure curing hardware with proprietary resins and ActiveMemory polymer technology (4D Aligner, 4D Bright). The software stack — LuxFlow Pro print prep, LuxDesign AI design automation, LuxLink fleet management, and the LuxCloud Dental platform — runs the in-house aligner and appliance workflow. Backed by Kleiner Perkins. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; no public developer API surface was found.

providers.name: Magic
providers.description: Magic (magic.dev) is a San Francisco frontier AI research lab building frontier-scale code models - an "AI coworker" for software engineering, and ultimately a path to safe AGI - rather than a shipping developer product. It has raised roughly $515M from Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, CapitalG, Elad Gil, Sequoia, Jane Street, and Eric Schmidt, and has published research on ultra-long-context models (LTM-1 at a 5M token context window, and the unreleased LTM-2-mini research prototype claimed to handle up to 100M tokens). As of this review Magic does not publish a public, self-serve developer API, API reference, SDK, or waitlist; its website and careers pages describe mission, research, and open roles only, with no product access model, pricing, or documented endpoints. Its GitHub organization (magicproduct) hosts research tooling (e.g. hash-hop, a long-context evaluation harness) and infrastructure forks, not an API client or SDK.

providers.name: Marathon Oil
providers.description: Marathon Oil was an independent international energy company that engaged in the exploration, production, and marketing of liquid hydrocarbons and natural gas. The company was acquired by ConocoPhillips in 2024, and its public web presence now redirects to ConocoPhillips. No public developer APIs have been identified.

providers.name: MatX
providers.description: MatX is an AI-hardware company designing specialized semiconductors optimized for large language model workloads. Its flagship MatX One chip targets high-throughput, low-latency training, inference, and reinforcement learning for large dense and Mixture-of-Experts models, storing weights in SRAM to cut latency and reaching over 2,000 output tokens per second on large models. MatX is a hardware and research company with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity, research/blog output, open-source codebases, and domain-security posture. Backed by Jane Street, Spark Capital, and Situational Awareness LP.

providers.name: MAYD
providers.description: MAYD (Meds At Your Doorstep) is a Berlin-based on-demand medication delivery service building a digital healthcare platform for Europe. Founded in 2021 by Hanno Heintzenberg and Lukas Pieczonka (previously McMakler), MAYD partners with local pharmacies to deliver over-the-counter and prescription medications to consumers' doors in about 30 minutes, 365 days a year, across German cities including Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Frankfurt, Cologne and Düsseldorf. The company operates a consumer mobile app and website (getmayd.com) and raised a ~EUR 30M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners in January 2022, with participation from Target Global, 468 Capital and Earlybird Venture Capital. MAYD is a consumer-facing (B2C) delivery business and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface; it is a Stripe payments customer for its checkout and billing.

providers.name: Meridianfleetservices
providers.description: Meridian Fleet Services is a holding company that acquires and partners with exceptional fleet service businesses, positioning itself as a permanent home for them. It focuses on preserving each acquired company's legacy and culture while supporting long-term organic growth through stronger teams, better planning and tooling, and scalable operational systems. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment confirmed a marketing website only (About, FAQs, Contact) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or programmatic surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Moss
providers.description: Moss is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of y-combinator and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Motif Analytics
providers.description: Motif Analytics was a startup (founded 2021 by Mikhail Panko and Theron Ji, with Sean Taylor as chief scientist) building interactive sequence analytics for growth and operations teams. Its product let analysts explore event sequences — user journeys, funnels, order-management flows — with a purpose-built Sequence Operations Language (SOL) and in-browser WebAssembly so data never had to leave the browser, backed by a $5.7M seed round led by Amplify Partners and Felicis (2024). As of this enrichment pass the product site and the docs.motifanalytics.com subdomain no longer resolve and motifanalytics.com serves a MarkMonitor brand-protection holding page, indicating the company has wound down. No public REST/GraphQL API, SDK, OpenAPI, CLI, or developer surface was ever published; the sole public GitHub repo is a 2023 bug reproduction.

providers.name: Moven
providers.description: Moven (Movencorp Newco Inc.) is a New York City fintech founded in 2011 by Brett King and Alex Sion. Originally a direct-to-consumer mobile banking and financial-wellness app, the company pivoted in 2020 to a business-to-business model, licensing its spending-analytics and financial-wellness technology to banks, credit unions, and other fintechs through open APIs and SDKs. Its data-driven engagement modules power companion and challenger-bank experiences such as TD Bank's MySpend and Westpac's CashNav. Moven's API and SDK surface is partner-gated behind a demo/sandbox request rather than a self-serve public developer portal, so no public OpenAPI, reference documentation, or GitHub organization is available for catalog harvesting.

providers.name: Moxion Power
providers.description: Moxion Power was a Richmond, California-based mobile battery energy storage (BESS) company founded in 2020 that designed, manufactured, and deployed large-scale mobile lithium-iron-phosphate battery units (the MP-75 and related platforms) intended to displace diesel generators across construction sites, film and television production, live events, utility work, and emergency response. The company built a 40,000 square-foot factory in Richmond, raised approximately $100 million in a Series B at a reported $1.5 billion valuation led by Tamarack Global with participation from Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund and Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, and signed a multi-year fleet partnership with Sunbelt Rentals. After delivering 400+ units it announced cessation of operations on July 29, 2024, laid off its entire workforce, and filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware in August 2024 with approximately $201,980 in cash on hand and estimated liabilities of $100M–$500M. In September–October 2024, Viridi Parente acquired Moxion's Richmond facility, battery inventory, intellectual property, patents, and the Sunbelt Rentals relationship through the bankruptcy auction for approximately $7 million. Moxion Power had no public developer API, SDK, or open source release; its GitHub organization (github.com/moxion-power) contains zero public repositories. This profile is preserved for historical reference.

providers.name: Muro AI
providers.description: Muro AI is an early-stage construction-technology startup building PrecOS, a pre-construction operating system marketed as a pre-con manager's AI assistant that carries general contractors from scoping through handover. The platform applies domain-adapted large language models, image models, agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, and document/plan parsing (OCR and computer vision) to automate bid comparison, estimation, bill-of-materials, and budget updates for teams that still run on spreadsheets. Muro is backed by Techstars and integrates with industry tools such as Procore. As of this profiling the company publishes a marketing site, a blog, and careers pages, but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so this record captures identity and a domain-security probe rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Mushroom Material
providers.description: Mushroom Material is a New Zealand and Singapore based sustainable-packaging startup founded in 2020 by Shaun Seaman and Jotinder Singh that grows a biodegradable, home-compostable alternative to expanded polystyrene (Styrofoam) from fungal mycelium. The company combines agricultural byproducts such as wood chips, sawdust, hemp straw and cardboard with mycelium to grow millions of pellets, coats them in a biopolymer binder, and uses compression molding to shape protective packaging that drops into existing Styrofoam production lines. The material offers shock absorption, low density and natural water resistance while composting in months. A Techstars-backed company, Mushroom Material raised a US$5M+ (NZ$8.5M) seed round led by Wavemaker Partners and Singapore's SEEDS Capital (with Icehouse Ventures, K1W1 and Black Kite Capital) to build a pilot plant in Auckland. This profile is a materials/manufacturing company in the API Evangelist network; it has no public API surface.

providers.name: MUSINSA
providers.description: MUSINSA is South Korea's leading online fashion platform, founded in 2001 by Cho Man-ho as a streetwear community and now operating a marketplace that connects more than 10,000 brands with over 16 million members. The company reported roughly USD 3.3 billion in GMV and USD 907 million in revenue for 2024, returned to operating profit, and is pursuing a KOSPI IPO. MUSINSA runs domestic and global storefronts (musinsa.com, global.musinsa.com), a partner/seller program for K-fashion brands, and an engineering organization that publishes on the MUSINSA tech blog. It has raised funding from investors including KKR, Sequoia/Peak XV (formerly Sequoia Capital China / HongShan) and IMM Investment. No genuine public product/developer API or OpenAPI-backed developer portal was found during enrichment; a corporate CMS Swagger UI at dev-api.corp.musinsa.com is an internal tool (its public spec still points at the Swagger petstore demo), so this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Ndata
providers.description: nData (ndata.cz) is a European pharmaceutical software company operating since 2005 that builds GxP-compliant, AI-assisted systems for the pharma lifecycle: portfolio and project management (ePM), regulatory affairs (eRA), quality control planning (eQCP), artwork and packaging management (eAW), controlled documentation (eDOCS), clinical trial documentation / eTMF, plus eLAB (R&D lab operations), and eGO and eTRANSFER (launching Q3/2026). Its public web presence is a marketing and product-catalog site; nData publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specifications. Note: this repo was seeded as a bain-capital-ventures ai-infrastructure portfolio stub, but the ndata.cz surface is a pharmaceutical GxP software vendor — the portfolio match appears to be a mismatch.

providers.name: Ndea
providers.description: Ndea is an AI research and science laboratory building artificial general intelligence through program synthesis. Ndea describes its work as blending intuitive pattern recognition with formal reasoning in a unified architecture, combining deep-learning intuition with discrete program search to achieve stronger generalization from minimal training data. As a frontier research organization, Ndea presents itself through its public website, an about page, a careers/jobs page, and a podcast; it currently publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or commercial developer platform, so this profile captures its corporate and web-security surface rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Nestlé
providers.description: Nestlé S.A. is the world's largest food and beverage company by revenue, headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland. Its product portfolio spans coffee (Nescafé, Nespresso), water, pet food (Purina), baby and infant nutrition (Gerber, Cerelac), confectionery (KitKat), dairy, and health science. No public developer portal or external API offering has been identified for Nestlé; integrations with retailers and partners are handled through private B2B systems rather than a self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory
providers.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is the largest US Department of Energy science and energy laboratory. ORNL provides public data and scientific computing resources for research including neutron science, materials science, computing, energy, and national security.

providers.name: Operand
providers.description: Operand is an AI-enabled pricing and commercial strategy platform for consumer retail, founded in 2024 and backed by Felicis, Y Combinator, SV Angel, and Soma Capital. It applies proprietary AI systems — an autonomous "agent swarm" — to set pricing and promotion strategy for mid-market and enterprise brands and retailers managing thousands of SKUs, volatile demand, and thin margins, running simulations to benchmark margin, revenue, and inventory-turn objectives before automating price changes. Operand is delivered as a managed platform with expert support and request-a-quote pricing rather than a public developer API; it currently publishes no OpenAPI, developer portal, or self-serve SDKs. An earlier Operand product at operand.ai offered an embeddings / semantic-search API with Python, Go, and TypeScript SDKs, now discontinued.

providers.name: Pachama
providers.description: Pachama is a San Francisco–based climate technology company founded in 2018 that built a satellite- and machine-learning-powered platform for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of nature-based carbon projects — including forest conservation, reforestation, afforestation, and improved forest management. Pachama combined satellite imagery, LiDAR, remote sensing, and deep-learning models to measure aboveground biomass, detect deforestation, and track project performance against verified baselines, surfacing that intelligence through an online marketplace where corporate buyers (including Microsoft, Shopify, Salesforce, Flexport.org, Mercado Libre, Boom Supersonic, and Nespresso) could discover and purchase high-integrity carbon credits. In November 2025, Pachama was acquired by Carbon Direct, and its proprietary digital MRV platform and forest-carbon science team were folded into Carbon Direct's science-backed carbon management offering; pachama.com now redirects to carbon-direct.com. Throughout its life as an independent company Pachama operated a buyer marketplace and discussed plans for a partner API to embed project selection and retirement data into third-party products, but never shipped a public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification — its GitHub organization contains only forks and archived internal tooling.

providers.name: Panacea
providers.description: Panacea is an AI-native FDA regulatory services firm (Y Combinator Spring 2026, operating as withpanacea.com) that pairs experienced ex-FDA regulatory consultants with a proprietary AI platform to accelerate medical device and pharmaceutical companies through FDA approval. Panacea supports the full range of U.S. regulatory pathways - 510(k), De Novo, PMA, IDE, IND, NDA, BLA, ODD, Pre-Subs, and BDD - handling regulatory strategy, pre-FDA meetings, and submission authoring through to clearance and approval. The company differentiates on milestone-based, outcome-aligned pricing rather than hourly billing, claiming results roughly 60% faster than traditional firms while keeping 100% expert oversight. Panacea is a professional services / consulting company; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: petkit
providers.description: PetKit is a consumer smart pet-technology company that designs and sells connected pet-care hardware — automated feeders, smart water fountains, self-cleaning litter boxes, cameras, and health-monitoring accessories — paired with the PetKit mobile app that controls the devices over the cloud. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass, PetKit publishes no dedicated first-party developer portal or public API; petkit.com is operated as a Shopify storefront, so the only machine discoverable surface on the domain is Shopify's Customer Account OAuth/OIDC discovery documents. Third-party (community, reverse-engineered) integrations exist for the mobile-app backend but there is no officially documented API.

providers.name: PG Studios
providers.description: PG Studios is a full-service creative media company offering animation, film production, and creative media services. The studio operates specialized divisions spanning animation production, filmmaking, audio and music composition, and game development. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, PG Studios is a creative-services business rather than an API provider: its public website markets studio capabilities and a client portfolio, and it publishes no developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal. This profile has been through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; the honest result is that there is no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Physical Intelligence
providers.description: Physical Intelligence (often styled "Pi" or "π") is a San Francisco-based research company building general-purpose foundation models for robotics with the stated goal of producing learning algorithms that can control any robot to do any task. The company has published a continuing line of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: π0 (October 2024, first generalist multi-task multi-robot policy), π0-FAST (autoregressive variant via Real-time Action Chunking / FAST tokenization), π0.5 (April 2025, open-world generalization), π*0.6 (November 2025, reinforcement-learning from experience), and π0.7 (April 2026, steerable model with emergent capabilities). Physical Intelligence releases significant work as open source: the openpi repository (~12K stars) is the canonical home for π0 weights and code, with companion repos including real-time-chunking-kinetix, pi-data-sharing, aloha, augmax, and rlds_dataset_builder. The company does not yet offer a hosted commercial API; access to the platform is via open-weight models and research collaborations.

providers.name: Pinduoduo
providers.description: Pinduoduo is a China-focused social commerce and agriculture-first e-commerce marketplace operated by PDD Holdings (Nasdaq: PDD), the multinational commerce group that also runs the cross-border marketplace Temu. Pinduoduo pioneered the "team purchase" (group-buy) model, connecting hundreds of millions of consumers directly with farmers, manufacturers, and merchants at scale. For developers, Pinduoduo runs a merchant-facing Open Platform (open.pinduoduo.com) that exposes gateway-style APIs for goods, orders, logistics, promotions, and store management to ISVs and merchant tools; that platform is geo-restricted to mainland China and was not directly reachable for artifact capture in this pass. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China) and enriched with verifiable corporate identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Pony.ai
providers.description: Pony.ai is a global autonomous-mobility company founded in Silicon Valley in 2016 and dual-headquartered in Guangzhou and Fremont. Its core technology is the Pony "virtual driver", a Level 4 autonomous driving stack deployed across three business lines: Robotaxi (PonyPilot+ ride-hailing service operating in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen, plus pilots in California and Arizona), Robotruck (autonomous heavy-duty trucking in China), and Personally Owned Vehicle (POV) intelligent driving software for production passenger cars. The company is publicly listed on NASDAQ under PONY and reports more than 32 million kilometres of autonomous road testing. Pony.ai does not publish a traditional public developer API; its public GitHub presence includes infrastructure tooling such as pony_aim (experiment tracker) and bazel-buildfarm rather than the AV stack itself. This profile captures the company surface and any developer-relevant artifacts.

providers.name: Prevenotics, Inc.
providers.description: Prevenotics, Inc. is an AI-powered preventive healthcare and diagnostics company working toward "a zero cancer world powered by AI." Its flagship solution provides real-time identification of pre-cancerous risks during gastroscopy, helping physicians move beyond diagnosis to effective prognosis management and stomach cancer prevention. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global and cites partnerships with NVIDIA, LG Electronics, Kakao, and Korean research and government institutions (NIPA, NIA, Seoul AI Hub). No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation was found during enrichment; this profile currently tracks the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Props
providers.description: Props (Props Project, operated by Props PBC / Open Props, founded by YouNow's Adi Sideman) was a blockchain-based loyalty and rewards network that let consumer apps grant users a shared crypto token (the Props Token) as a stake in the networks they helped grow. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Borderless Capital, Venrock and Comcast Ventures, it raised ~$2M and was the first Regulation A+ consumer token qualified by the SEC, reaching over three million users across its app network. In August 2021 the team announced it would wind down commercial operations at year end, citing the regulatory constraints of running a qualified security, and open-sourced the Props Protocol contracts on GitHub. The propsproject.com domain no longer resolves; there is no live developer portal, API, documentation, or maintained SDK. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record.

providers.name: Qphox
providers.description: QphoX is a Delft, Netherlands-based quantum technology company founded in 2021 and spun out of Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). It develops quantum networking hardware to tackle the scaling challenges of quantum computing, centered on its Quantum Transducer, described as the first quantum interface between single optical and single microwave photons, enabling optical interconnects between superconducting quantum processors. Alongside the transducer, QphoX offers an Optical Control System for delivering RF signals into extreme cryogenic environments and a CryoSwitch Control Module for use with Radiall's cryogenic latching actuator. The company publishes open-source Python instrument-control libraries (QCoDeS drivers) on GitHub for operating its hardware. QphoX is backed by Speedinvest. QphoX exposes no public web API or developer portal.

providers.name: Quince
providers.description: Quince is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce retailer selling high-quality essentials at radical prices across apparel, home goods, bedding, furniture, accessories, jewelry, beauty, and travel. It uses a factory-direct model that bypasses traditional retail markups to offer affordable luxury. Quince was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc, GGV Capital, ICONIQ Capital, and Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer retail brand it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or .well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Realtor.com
providers.description: Realtor.com is a real estate listings website operated by Move, Inc., a subsidiary of News Corp, headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The platform is the official site of the National Association of REALTORS (NAR) under a long-term operating agreement and is one of the largest U.S. property search portals, serving home buyers, sellers, renters, and real estate professionals. Realtor.com aggregates for-sale, for-rent, and off-market listings sourced primarily from Multiple Listing Services (MLSs) via Move's listings distribution subsidiary ListHub, and surfaces them through consumer web and mobile apps alongside neighborhood, school, mortgage, and market data. The professional side of the business sells lead-generation and marketing products such as Connections Plus, ReadyConnect Concierge, and Market VIP to agents and brokers, while ListHub provides MLS-to-portal syndication, broker reporting, and listing feed management. Adjacent Move properties include Doorsteps, Moving.com, and SeniorHousingNet, and the company publishes a public economic research arm at realtor.com/research that releases monthly housing market reports and downloadable historical datasets. Realtor.com does not publish a first-party public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; programmatic access to listing data is gated through MLS membership and ListHub's broker/vendor agreements, while the only widely available HTTP APIs branded as Realtor.com are unofficial third-party scrapers hosted on RapidAPI and Apify.

providers.name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) is a Salt Lake City-based AI-enabled drug discovery company that operates the Recursion Operating System (Recursion OS), a vertically integrated platform combining automated wet-lab cellular phenomics, transcriptomics (Trekseq), proteomics, ADME, chemistry, and patient data with machine learning to map biology and design drug candidates. The platform runs on BioHive-2, a NVIDIA-built supercomputer ranked among the top global systems and dedicated to biopharma workloads, and is fed by 50+ petabytes of proprietary biological and chemical data. In November 2024 Recursion completed the acquisition of Exscientia, folding Exscientia's generative AI chemistry, Centaur Chemist, and clinical pipeline into the combined company; Recursion now runs more than 10 clinical and preclinical programs (REC-4881 for FAP, REC-3565 MALT1 inhibitor, REC-1245 RBM39 for biomarker-enriched solid tumors and lymphomas, REC-617 CDK7 inhibitor, REC-994 for cerebral cavernous malformation, REC-2282 for NF2- mutated meningiomas, REC-4209 for IPF, REC-7735 for HSD obesity), 10+ advanced discovery programs, and 10+ partnered programs across Roche (Genentech), Bayer, Sanofi, and Merck KGaA (Darmstadt). Recursion does not currently expose paid commercial APIs to external developers; assets and data access are delivered through licensing, scientific collaborations, and the MapApp web product. Externally, Recursion ships substantial open tooling: the RxRx family of open phenomics datasets (RxRx1, RxRx2, RxRx3, RxRx3-core, RxRx19a, RxRx19b) hosted at rxrx.ai and Hugging Face, the OpenPhenom-S/16 foundation model (released on Hugging Face and Google Cloud's Model Garden, with Phenom-Beta on NVIDIA BioNeMo), the MolE molecular foundation model, the gflownet library for graph and molecular generative modeling, SynFlowNet/synflownet-boltz for retrosynthesis-aware molecular design, maes_microscopy (NeurIPS 2023 spotlight masked autoencoders for cell microscopy), and rxrx1-utils for the NeurIPS 2019 CellSignal competition. The combination positions Recursion as a Tier-2 AI drug discovery provider with no commercial API surface but a meaningful open-source and open-model presence aimed at the computational biology research community.

providers.name: Red RidgeBio
providers.description: RedRidge Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company that identifies and develops biparatopic antibodies, an antibody class engineered to bind two distinct sites (epitopes) on a single target protein for greater potency and selectivity. Its programs span oncology (antibody-drug conjugates for solid tumors) and autoimmunity (immune-cell modulators), pursued through partnerships and internal discovery. The company operates from Basel, Switzerland with additional presence in Cambridge, Massachusetts and San Francisco. RedRidge Bio was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web presence.

providers.name: Reniac
providers.description: rENIAC Inc. is a Santa Clara-based data acceleration company whose flagship product, the rENIAC Data Engine (rDE), is a drop-in accelerator for open source and NoSQL databases such as Apache Cassandra.
