Combining FPGAs with proprietary software, rDE speeds storage, network, and compute operations and can be deployed as a hardware-optimized cache, a transparent data-acceleration proxy, or a scalable storage engine on-prem, hybrid, or in the cloud (including early availability on AWS). rENIAC targets ultra-low-latency, real-time workloads — AI/ML, fraud prevention, payment processing, electronic trading, and recommendation engines — claiming up to 10x throughput, 13x lower latency, and significant TCO and CPU reductions. rENIAC ships an infrastructure/hardware acceleration product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Rockport Trade Systems
providers.description: Rockport Trade Systems is a global trade management (GTM) software company providing customs compliance, import and export management, and trade-content solutions to enterprises. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners, it was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the company operates a corporate marketing website but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specification surface, and the site actively blocks automated access (HTTP 403), so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: RUUT
providers.description: RUUT (ruut.mx) is a Mexican fintech and mobile-first investment platform that lets everyday people invest in the US stock markets. Marketed as "la plataforma de inversion para no inversionistas" (the investment platform for non-investors), it gives users access to 8,000+ US stocks and ETFs, personalized risk-based portfolios (safe, moderate, aggressive), goal-based investing, and AI-tailored market news. Accounts are protected up to $500,000 USD via SIPC insurance through its US brokerage partner Alpaca Securities LLC (FINRA/SIPC). RUUT is registered with Mexico's CNBV as an independent investment advisor (Folio #30174) and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. RUUT is a consumer product with no public developer API; this profile was enriched from its public website and live domain probes.

providers.name: Salduu (Profe Social)
providers.description: Salduu, operating as Profe Social at profe.social, is a 500 Global-backed social networking platform. The live host serves Mastodon's default robots.txt (Disallow /search, sitemap.xml.gz) and a Ruby on Rails error stack, indicating the platform runs on Mastodon / ActivityPub fediverse technology, so it exposes the standard Mastodon client REST API and ActivityPub federation endpoints under /api. Both the site and its API surface sit behind a Cloudflare managed challenge, so the instance's own instance metadata, OpenAPI, and developer pages could not be retrieved by a non-browser client during enrichment. This profile records what was directly observed via DNS/TLS/HTTP and well-known probes; the API contract itself remains to be captured once the challenge is cleared or the provider publishes a spec.

providers.name: Seasats
providers.description: Seasats designs and manufactures autonomous uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs) for ocean intelligence, maritime domain awareness, and defense missions. Its platform lines include the hand-deployable Lightfish (6-month endurance), the fast-response Quickfish (35+ knots with an integrated drone bay), and the heavy-payload Heavyfish. Vessels carry modular payloads, run persistent autonomous surveys, and integrate with existing command-and-control (C2) architectures. Seasats is a Techstars-backed company. As of this enrichment pass Seasats publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; its integration story is C2 interoperability, not a web API.

providers.name: Seed&Spark
providers.description: Seed&Spark is a crowdfunding and streaming platform for independent film and episodic content, combining a project crowdfunding marketplace for filmmakers with a subscription streaming service for independent films and series. Founded in 2012 and backed by Techstars, the company helps independent creators raise funds, build audiences, and distribute their work. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment (homepage and app paths sit behind Cloudflare bot protection; no api.* or developers.* subdomain resolves and no well-known API documents are published).

providers.name: Shelby.tv
providers.description: Shelby.tv was a Techstars-backed social video discovery startup that let people find, share, and watch videos surfaced from their social networks. The company has shut down; shelby.tv now serves only a founders' farewell page and no longer operates any product, developer program, or public API. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Silk and Sonder
providers.description: Silk and Sonder is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global, redpoint-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: SnapDeal
providers.description: Snapdeal is an Indian e-commerce marketplace founded in February 2010 by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal and headquartered in Gurugram/New Delhi. It began as a daily-deals platform and grew into a value-focused online marketplace that connects third-party sellers with buyers across categories such as fashion, home and kitchen, electronics accessories, and general merchandise, primarily serving price-sensitive shoppers in India's smaller cities and towns. Sellers onboard and manage catalog, orders, and payouts through the Snapdeal seller portal (seller.snapdeal.com). Snapdeal has been backed by investors including SoftBank, Bessemer Venture Partners, Nexus Venture Partners, and Kalaari Capital. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners; enrichment found no public developer portal, no api.snapdeal.com or developer.snapdeal.com host, and no published API specification or well-known discovery surface — the seller portal is login-gated behind SSO.

providers.name: Snips
providers.description: Snips was a Paris-based artificial intelligence company that built a private-by-design, on-device voice assistant platform and natural language understanding (NLU) technology, letting developers add offline voice interfaces to connected devices without sending audio to the cloud. Snips was acquired by Sonos in November 2019 and its team became the Sonos Voice Experience group; the developer platform, hosted APIs, and console were subsequently discontinued. snips.ai now serves only a static acquisition-announcement page, and the company's open-source libraries (notably the Snips NLU engine) remain archived under the github.com/snipsco organization.

providers.name: Snowcap Compute
providers.description: Snowcap Compute is building the world's first commercial superconducting computing platform, operating at 4.5 Kelvin to deliver breakthrough energy efficiency and performance for AI and data-center workloads. Launched in June 2025 with $23 million in seed funding led by Playground Global, the company is developing superconducting chips and systems aimed at the next era of AI and quantum-adjacent compute. As a hardware and deep-tech company it publishes a marketing and careers presence but no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Sportlogiq
providers.description: Sportlogiq is a Montreal, Quebec-based sports analytics company that applies patented computer vision and machine learning to broadcast video to generate high-resolution player tracking, event, and performance datasets across ice hockey, soccer/global football, American football, and youth sports. Founded in 2015 by Olympic figure skater Craig Buntin and computer-vision PhD Mehrsan Javan, the company is led by CEO Mitchell Wasserman and employs roughly 75 people, including a research team of ~13 AI scientists with 180+ patents and publications. Sportlogiq describes itself as the global leader in hockey analytics, with adoption across the majority of NHL franchises, 150+ professional and amateur hockey clubs worldwide, international hockey federations and leagues (SHL, PWHL, IIHF), NCAA hockey programs, NFL franchises, and global football organizations — collectively serving 220+ clients. In November 2024 Sportlogiq acquired 8BY8, a sports video infrastructure platform that combines multi-angle video, data streams, and audio for officiating, coaching, and player health workflows. In January 2026 Sportlogiq was itself acquired by Teamworks, where it continues to operate as the AI analytics layer of Teamworks' broader operating system for sport. Sportlogiq exposes its tracking and event data to teams, leagues, broadcasters, and analytics partners through a private partner API and bulk data feeds; there is no public developer portal, no self-service signup, no published OpenAPI specification, and no public SDKs or open-source repositories. Access is sold as part of commercial contracts and integrated directly into partner workflows.

providers.name: Standard Intelligence
providers.description: Standard Intelligence (si.inc) is an aligned AGI research lab based in San Francisco building AI models that explore and learn like humans do. Its work includes hertz-dev, an open-source 8.5B-parameter autoregressive base model for interactive, full-duplex conversational audio; a fully general computer-action model that navigates websites, executes CAD sequences, and drives autonomously at 30 FPS; and The Heap, a 30-petabyte data-storage system built in San Francisco for under $500,000. The company has raised $75M from Sequoia and Spark Capital. It publishes research posts and open-source code on GitHub but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Stickies
providers.description: Stickies (stickies.wtf) was a Los Angeles-based consumer web3 company, built by BYO Labs, that made "dumb stickers and GIFs starring your favorite NFTs" — users connected a crypto wallet holding their NFTs and generated custom stickers and GIFs of those avatars for use in messaging and social apps. Founded around 2022 by Tom Wright (CEO) and Sterling Barnett (COO), it raised roughly $5.5M with backing from Lightspeed Venture Partners (Jeremy Liew). The product was a closed consumer web app with no public developer API, documentation, or SDK. The company appears defunct: the stickies.wtf site was last captured live in 2023, returned 403s by mid-2024, and the domain no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN) as of July 2026; co-founder Sterling Barnett has since moved on to other ventures.

providers.name: Superset
providers.description: Superset is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of y-combinator and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Swimply
providers.description: Swimply is a peer-to-peer marketplace that lets people book private swimming pools and other recreational spaces (family, party, and luxury pools plus tennis, pickleball, and basketball courts) by the hour, and lets owners list and monetize their spaces as hosts. Operating across the US, Canada, and Australia, the platform reports over 4 million five-star experiences, 15,000+ active hosts, and 15,000+ available spaces, and offers a 2026 Summer Pass membership. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. No public API or developer program was found at the time of enrichment; this profile documents the company's public web surface only.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment. The company operates through its publishing labels: Rockstar Games (Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption), 2K (NBA 2K, Borderlands, Civilization, BioShock, Mafia), Private Division, and Zynga (mobile games). Headquartered in New York City, Take-Two is a Fortune 500 company with studios across North America, Europe, and Asia. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Talentpluto
providers.description: Talentpluto (Pluto) is an AI voice-agent platform for professional discovery and recruitment, founded in 2025 and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch out of New York City. Professionals talk to Pluto for about ten minutes about what they have done, what they are great at, and what they want next; Pluto turns that private conversation into a discoverable professional profile that the person controls and that can be shared with people and AI agents. For hiring, companies describe what they need and Pluto searches its network and the broader market, evaluates fit on both sides, privately confirms interest, and facilitates warm introductions when there is mutual alignment. The company positions Pluto as a source of truth for career context in an internet increasingly built for agents. As of profiling it is a consumer- and recruiter-facing product with no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or other machine-facing surface; this profile is a network stub awaiting a real API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Tara Ai
providers.description: Tara AI (Y Combinator W15, originally Gradberry) was a San Jose-based engineering efficiency platform that used fine-tuned LLMs over source control and project data to measure cycle times, benchmarks, and delivery velocity, integrating with GitHub, GitLab, Jira, and Slack. Backed by Aspect Ventures, Y Combinator, and Slack Fund (~$13M raised). As of July 2026 the company is listed as permanently closed on Crunchbase and tara.ai is a parked domain; no public API, developer docs, or SDKs were ever published, and the TARAAI GitHub org has no public repositories.

providers.name: TerraPower
providers.description: TerraPower is a Bellevue, Washington-based advanced nuclear innovation company founded in 2006 with Bill Gates as founder and chair. Its flagship product is the Natrium reactor, a 345 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor co-developed with GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy and paired with an integrated molten salt energy storage system that can boost output to 500 MWe for up to five-plus hours to follow renewable grid load. TerraPower broke ground in 2024 on the first commercial Natrium demonstration plant in Kemmerer, Wyoming under the U.S. Department of Energy's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP), a 50/50 cost-share with up to $2 billion in federal funding. The company's second business line, TerraPower Isotopes (TPI), produces research-grade actinium-225 — an alpha-emitting radionuclide used in targeted alpha therapy for cancer — from DOE thorium-229 stockpiles in partnership with Isotek, with a lab in Everett WA and a cGMP manufacturing facility under construction in Philadelphia's Bellwether District. TerraPower has no commercial developer API, SDK, or public partner integration platform; its revenue model is reactor sales, plant operation, and isotope supply contracts with pharmaceutical partners including Aktis Oncology, Advanced Accelerator Applications, Cardinal Health, and Point Biopharma. The company does maintain a meaningful open-source nuclear engineering footprint on GitHub — most notably ARMI (Advanced Reactor Modeling Interface), an Apache 2.0 Python framework for nuclear reactor design and analysis automation used internally to design Natrium and made available to the wider reactor engineering community.

providers.name: The Rainmaker Group Ventures (letitrain.com)
providers.description: letitrain.com was the corporate domain of The Rainmaker Group Ventures, LLC, an Atlanta-based hospitality revenue and profit optimization software vendor serving hotels, resorts and casinos. Rainmaker sold an "intelligent profit platform" built around three products: guestrev for transient pricing and science-based revenue management, grouprev for group pricing and evaluation, and revintel for business intelligence and reporting, with a demand forecast marketed to operators including Caesars Entertainment, Atlantis Casino Resort Spa and Two Roads Hospitality. The company was backed by Norwest Venture Partners and ran offices in Atlanta, Las Vegas, Singapore and Dubai. The brand is retired: letitrain.com now serves a blanket redirect to Cendyn, the acquiring company, its TLS certificate expired in December 2022, and no Rainmaker developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification was ever published or archived. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record with no active API surface.

providers.name: The RealReal
providers.description: The RealReal is the world's largest online marketplace for authenticated, resale luxury goods, operating a managed consignment marketplace across women's and men's fashion, fine jewelry and watches, handbags, fine art, and home. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco, the company employs in-house gemologists, horologists, art curators, and brand authenticators to verify every item, pairing that expertise with data-driven pricing and demand insights. The RealReal is a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: REAL) and has processed tens of millions of consigned items. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass The RealReal publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: TotSpot
providers.description: TotSpot was a mobile resale shopping marketplace for kids' clothes, letting parents buy and sell gently used children's fashion (brands like Burberry, Nike, GAP, Gymboree) with peer-to-peer listings and a concierge selling service. A 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company, TotSpot appears to be defunct - as of July 2026 totspot.me serves only a web-hosting placeholder page, and no public API or developer surface was found.

providers.name: Traverse
providers.description: Traverse is a San Francisco data research lab, founded in 2025 by Lance Yan and backed by Y Combinator (W26) along with angel investors from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and Meta. Traverse partners with frontier AI labs to solve "non-verifiable" work: the ambiguous, taste-dependent, long-horizon tasks in domains like law, healthcare, sales, and writing where reinforcement learning lacks the clean deterministic feedback loops it has in math and coding. The lab captures real human expert behavior in highly controlled settings and turns judgment, taste, and reasoning into high-fidelity training environments for frontier models. As of mid-2026 Traverse is an early-stage research lab with no public API, developer platform, SDKs, or product documentation — its public surface is a manifesto-style website, a blog, careers pages, and a contact CTA for prospective lab partners.

providers.name: Trella
providers.description: Trella is a Cairo-headquartered B2B trucking marketplace and digital freight platform that connects shippers with carriers across the Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan (MENA-P). Founded in 2019 by Omar Hagrass, Ali El Atrash, and Pierre Saad and backed by Y Combinator, Trella runs a digital load marketplace, a carrier mobile app, and a shipper web dashboard that together replace the traditional broker-driven, paper-based long-haul trucking workflow. Core platform services include load posting and carrier matching, instant quoting, GPS tracking and live shipment visibility, electronic proof of delivery (ePODs), load insurance, a control-tower operations layer for carrier quality and performance, and integrated payments and invoicing between shippers and carriers. The network spans 30,000+ carriers and operates from major freight hubs including Cairo, Alexandria, Port Said, Damietta, Sokhna, Jeddah, Dammam, Riyadh, and Dubai, serving industries such as FMCG, construction, manufacturing, agriculture, mining, e-commerce, retail, electronics, ceramics, and freight forwarding. Trella's revenue model is marketplace take-rate and value-added logistics services; there is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks catalog, or open-source platform release for the Trella marketplace.

providers.name: Tribes
providers.description: Tribes (Tribes Protocol, Inc.) is a web3-native social wallet and messaging application that lets people co-own and manage digital assets together while communicating directly from within the wallet itself. Its "co-wallets" combine group messaging and shared custody so crypto communities, creators, and DAOs can coordinate and make decisions without relying on external tools like Discord or Twitter. Founded by former Coinbase engineer Hish Bouabdallah, Tribes raised a $3.3M pre-seed round in January 2023 led by Kindred Ventures, with South Park Commons and Script Capital. It is a consumer crypto product; its public code surface is the tribes-protocol GitHub organization (smart-contract libraries and tooling) rather than a hosted REST/GraphQL developer API.

providers.name: Triblio
providers.description: Triblio is an account-based marketing (ABM) platform now owned by Foundry, the marketing services and data unit of International Data Group (IDG). Originally founded in Reston, Virginia, Triblio was acquired by IDG/Foundry in June 2020 as the cornerstone of a multi-year strategy to combine first- party publisher data, third-party intent signals, and ABM advertising, web personalization, and sales acceleration into a single platform. The product combines account-based advertising, intent-driven audience segmentation, website personalization, and a Smart Score that ranks accounts using behavioral signals from first-party web visits, third-party intent providers (notably Bombora Company Surge and G2 intent), CRM data, and Foundry's own publisher network. Triblio integrates with major CRMs and marketing automation systems including Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics 365, SugarCRM, Marketo, Pardot, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Analytics, and Slack. Foundry positions Triblio as the engine behind its broader Sales Acceleration and Foundry ABM offerings, with intent data feeds from Bombora ingested weekly and G2 intent ingested nightly. Triblio does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI specification, or open-source SDKs; the GitHub organization at github.com/triblio was archived in January 2026 with no public repos. Customer integrations are delivered through pre-built CRM and MAP connectors, an Apps Marketplace, and platform-internal automation rather than a self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Trustid
providers.description: TRUSTID was a Portland, Oregon telephone caller-authentication and call-center anti-fraud company led by CEO Patrick Cox, authenticating inbound callers pre-answer without knowledge-based interrogation of the caller. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures, TRUSTID was acquired by Neustar (closed January 2019), and Neustar was itself acquired by TransUnion in December 2021, where the caller-authentication capability lives on in Trusted Call Solutions. TRUSTID no longer operates independently and publishes no public API surface — trustid.com is unresponsive and www.trustid.com returns HTTP 503 from Neustar redirect infrastructure.

providers.name: TTM Technologies
providers.description: TTM Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTMI) is a leading global manufacturer of technology products, including mission systems, radio frequency components, RF microwave and microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced printed circuit boards (PCBs). TTM serves aerospace and defense, data center computing, medical, industrial and instrumentation, automotive, and networking and communications markets. The company reported approximately $2.9B in FY2025 revenue, operates 24 specialized facilities across North America and Asia Pacific, and employs more than 18,000 people. TTM expanded its defense electronics footprint with the 2022 acquisition of Telephonics from Griffon Corporation.

providers.name: Tuza
providers.description: Tuza is a banking automation platform that orchestrates AI agents, customers and workflows to eliminate the manual processes that slow banks down. Originally launched in the UK at tuza.co.uk as a card-payment fee comparison and switching service for merchants, the company has repositioned as Tuza AI, delivering agentic automation for banks. It is an early-stage, venture-backed fintech (backed by Northzone) building a product that connects AI agents with core banking operations and customer-facing workflows. As of this profile Tuza publishes a marketing and careers site only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface has been released yet, so this record captures verified company identity plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: TXN
providers.description: TXN (TXN Solutions, Inc.) was a San Francisco consumer spending analytics company that captured transactions directly from the credit and debit cards of an opt-in research panel, layering demographics and targeted surveys on top to give merchants competitive intelligence and share-of-wallet insight. Founded by Alex Rampell, Pasha Bitz, and Jonathan Wolf and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Bloomberg Beta, General Catalyst, Homebrew, SV Angel, and Slow Ventures, it is listed as exited in the Bloomberg Beta portfolio. As of July 2026 txn.com serves only a parked "Launching Soon" page on an Alibaba Cloud host with a self-signed TLS certificate — no product, developer, or API surface remains.

providers.name: Ubiquisys
providers.description: Ubiquisys was a UK-based developer of intelligent 3G/LTE/Wi-Fi small cells and femtocells for mobile operators, with products like ActiveRadio, ActiveSON, CloudBase, and EdgeCloud deployed by carriers such as SFR and SoftBank, and was ranked #1 in ABI Research's Small Cell Vendor Matrix. Backed by Accel, Cisco announced its intent to acquire Ubiquisys on April 3, 2013, and the company was absorbed into Cisco's small cell portfolio; ubiquisys.com is now Cisco-owned and redirects to Cisco's acquisitions page. Ubiquisys published no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Upteam
providers.description: Upteam is a 500 Global portfolio company whose public web presence now points at Luxclusif: upteamco.com returns an HTTP 302 redirect to luxclusif.com, the B2B luxury resale platform offering wholesale distribution of pre-owned luxury goods, stock acquisition, and resale-as-a-service programs. Enrichment probing found no developer portal, no API documentation, and no machine-readable API artifacts on either the Upteam domain or the Luxclusif site; /.well-known/ discovery paths on upteamco.com return 403 and site paths redirect to Luxclusif.

providers.name: Vancity
providers.description: Vancity (Vancouver City Savings Credit Union) is a member-owned financial co-operative headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, and the largest community credit union in Canada, with over 543,000 members, roughly CA$35 billion in assets, and about 60 branches across the Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island. Founded in 1946 as an open-bond credit union, it is provincially chartered and cooperatively governed, offering retail and business banking, mortgages, foreign exchange, Visa cards, insurance, and investment advice, with values-based and impact-lending positioning. Vancity exposes no first-party public developer API portal: developer.vancity.com and developers.vancity.com do not resolve. It participates in Canada's shared payment rails through Central 1 (its banking-technology and payments provider, including enhanced Interac e-Transfer real-time payments) and Payments Canada, while third-party consumer data access is provided through aggregators such as Plaid and Flinks. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework is legislated but not yet operational, so any programmatic account access today is voluntary and aggregator-mediated rather than served by a documented Vancity API.

providers.name: WeDidIt
providers.description: WeDidIt was a Brooklyn, New York fundraising platform founded in 2012 by Su Sanni and Benjamin Lamson that gave small nonprofits online donation pages, crowdfunding, peer-to-peer, ticketing, and fiscal-sponsorship tools, plus a mobile app for in-person card donations. A 500 Global portfolio company and 43North winner, it was acquired by Allegiance Fundraising Group in June 2019 and its product folded into the Allegiance suite. No public developer API was ever documented, and the wedid.it domain has since lapsed to an unrelated site, so no API surface remains to profile.

providers.name: Wing
providers.description: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary, spun out of Google X in 2018, with operating headquarters in Palo Alto, California and significant operations in Australia, Finland, Ireland, and the United States. Wing designs, builds, and operates a fleet of small fixed-wing electric VTOL aircraft that autonomously pick up and deliver packages to customers' homes, and it operates an unmanned traffic management (UTM) stack used by drone pilots and aviation authorities. Wing was the first company to receive an FAA Part 135 Air Carrier Certificate for drone delivery (2019) and is an approved LAANC USS in the United States and an approved drone airspace authorization provider for CASA in Australia. Wing's commercial surface is split across two main platforms — the Wing Delivery Platform, a partner-only API and UI suite that lets retailers, restaurants, and logistics providers embed drone delivery into their own order flows (Walmart, DoorDash, Papa Johns, and others), and OpenSky, a consumer drone airspace authorization app and partner API. Wing also co-founded the InterUSS Platform open-source UTM project, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. Wing's revenue comes from per-delivery fees charged to merchant partners and from drone-as-a-service operations rather than from public developer APIs; the Delivery Platform API and OpenSky API are not openly published and there is no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at the time of profiling.

providers.name: WorkClass
providers.description: WorkClass is (or was) a Singapore-based job marketplace founded in 2020 that matched frontline and blue-collar workers with employers, promising placement within 24 hours via matching algorithms. Backed by 500 Global, Goodwater Capital, Antler, and Kistefos, it surfaced here as a 500 Global portfolio lead. As of July 2026 its primary domain workclass.co redirects to an unrelated UK website and workclass.com is parked for sale; no public API, developer portal, client packages, or GitHub organization were found.

providers.name: Ximian
providers.description: Ximian was a Boston-based open source software company founded on October 19, 1999 by Miguel de Icaza and Nat Friedman -- originally incorporated as International GNOME Support, then Helix Code, and renamed Ximian in January 2001. It advanced the GNOME desktop, built the Evolution email and collaboration client and Ximian Connector, ran the Red Carpet software-update service, and launched the Mono open source .NET implementation. Surfaced via the Battery Ventures portfolio, Ximian was acquired by Novell on August 4, 2003 to strengthen Novell's enterprise Linux business; after Attachmate acquired Novell in 2011 the founders went on to create Xamarin (acquired by Microsoft in 2016). Ximian no longer operates: www.ximian.com still resolves on Novell infrastructure but permanently redirects every path to novell.com/linux/ximian.html, which forwards to suse.com -- there is no live website, developer portal, or public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical identity record.

providers.name: YOOX NET-A-PORTER (YNAP)
providers.description: YOOX NET-A-PORTER (YNAP) is a leading digital multi-brand luxury fashion group operating the online stores NET-A-PORTER, MR PORTER, YOOX, and THE OUTNET. Following the 2025 acquisition by Mytheresa, the group operates under the parent LuxExperience B.V. (NYSE ticker "LUXE"), pairing full-price curated luxury with off-price destinations. YNAP was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The group runs an engineering organization (YNAP Tech) and maintains public GitHub open-source tooling, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or partner developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Zibra Labs
providers.description: Zibra Labs is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building distributed compute infrastructure for AI workloads at scale. The platform gives teams access to the cheapest CPUs and GPUs across hyperscalers and neoclouds, orchestrating clusters of 100 to 50,000 mixed hardware nodes with sub-50ms task-dispatch overhead and millions of parallel tasks on spot instances across regions. Target workloads include quantitative-trading backtesting and parameter sweeps, AI post-training and reinforcement-learning pipelines, multi-modal data processing, batch and high-volume inference, and long-horizon agentic workflows. The founding team previously built three LinkedIn databases (Venice, Liquid, Espresso) and were tech leads on the open-source Ray compute framework. As of this profile Zibra Labs publishes only a corporate marketing site; no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs are available yet.

providers.name: Amount
providers.description: Amount is a Chicago-based financial technology company that provides banks, credit unions, and fintechs with a digital lending and account-origination platform. Spun out of the consumer lender Avant in 2020 and backed by QED Investors, Amount delivers configurable software for personal loans, point-of-sale and buy-now-pay-later financing, deposit and account opening, and integrated fraud, identity verification, and decisioning. Its product API is delivered to enterprise banking customers through a private, credentialed developer portal (docs.amount.com) rather than a public self-serve API.

providers.name: AssetVault
providers.description: AssetVault is a London-based consumer fintech platform that helps individuals and families catalogue, protect, and grow their valuable assets in one secure digital vault. It spans physical items (homes, vehicles, jewelry), digital assets (passwords, investment portfolios), and financial holdings, layering on digital estate planning (eWill), insurance claims support, analytics, and concierge services. The platform emphasizes bank-grade security with encrypted transmission, two-factor authentication, and biometric access, and is available as an App Store, Google Play, and web app. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API surface is published yet.

providers.name: BetterDoctor
providers.description: BetterDoctor Inc. was a San Francisco health-technology company (founded 2012) that built a provider data verification and directory-accuracy platform, helping health plans keep their provider directories current while letting clinicians attest to and manage their own practice information. Its original public API surfaced physician, practice-location, specialty, and insurance-plan data for building healthcare provider-directory applications. Backed by 500 Global and Uncork Capital, BetterDoctor was acquired by Quest Analytics, where the product continues as a provider-attestation and network-adequacy service used by 700,000+ healthcare professionals across 360,000+ locations. The standalone developer API has since been retired; betterdoctor.com now redirects to Quest Analytics.

providers.name: Blockspring
providers.description: Blockspring was a data integration and enrichment platform that let developers and spreadsheet users run cloud functions and connect to hundreds of third-party APIs and data services from Google Sheets, Excel, and via its own API. Founded around 2014 and originally Y Combinator backed, it was acquired by Coda (Krypton) in 2017 and surfaced here as an a16z portfolio-associated company. All Blockspring services -- the website tooling, integrations, plugins, APIs, and data enrichment -- were permanently shut down on December 29, 2022, with active subscriptions cancelled and prorated refunds issued. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no live developer surface, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Canadian Western Bank
providers.description: Canadian Western Bank (CWB) is a Schedule I domestic chartered bank founded in 1988 (through the merger of the Bank of Alberta and Western & Pacific Bank) and headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta at Canadian Western Bank Place. Historically the largest publicly traded Schedule I bank headquartered in Western Canada and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: CWB), it held roughly CA$43 billion in assets and focused on full-service business and commercial banking, personal banking, equipment financing and leasing, trust services, and wealth management across a network of affiliated entities. In June 2024 National Bank of Canada agreed to acquire CWB in an all-share deal valued at roughly CA$5 billion, and the acquisition closed in early 2025; CWB now operates as a subsidiary of National Bank of Canada and its branches and brand are being wound down and rebranded under National Bank. Consistent with Canada's voluntary and still fragmented open-finance landscape — the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework was legislated in 2024 (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement, overseen by the FCAC) but is not yet operational — CWB publishes no first-party public developer portal and no documented public API. Its developer and API hostnames do not resolve, and the entire cwbank.com domain now 301-redirects to National Bank of Canada (nbc.ca). Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached only indirectly through third-party data aggregators (Plaid is confirmed via aggregator coverage directories). No first-party FDX-conformant data-access API was found. This is an honest identity-only, aggregator-only record for an institution now absorbed into National Bank of Canada.

providers.name: CareMerge
providers.description: CareMerge is a senior living technology company that builds family engagement, care coordination, community engagement, and communications software for senior living and long-term / post-acute care communities. Its platform connects residents, families, and care staff so communities can coordinate care, share activities and calendars, and keep families informed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass CareMerge publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface; its marketing site sits behind a SiteGround (sg-captcha) challenge and its GitHub organization contains internal tooling and open-source forks rather than a first-party client SDK.

providers.name: Celgene
providers.description: Celgene Corporation was a global biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of innovative therapies for cancer and immune-inflammatory diseases. Celgene was acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) in November 2019 and its operations are now consolidated under BMS. No public developer API has been identified; engagement is organized through BMS clinical trials, study connect, and investigator-sponsored research portals.

providers.name: Denali Therapeutics
providers.description: Denali Therapeutics is a South San Francisco-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, and delivers therapeutics for people living with serious neurodegenerative and lysosomal storage diseases. Its proprietary Transport Vehicle (TV) platform is engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier so that large-molecule therapies can reach the brain and body. Denali maintains a public GitHub organization publishing open-source computational-biology and cheminformatics research tools (archs4, basechem, napari-mito-hcs), but publishes no public developer API. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: Desaisiv Inc.
providers.description: DESAISIV is a corporate InsurTech platform focused on health insurance in Saudi Arabia and the wider MENA region. Founded in 2022, the company builds AI and automation products for insurers and third-party administrators (TPAs), including smart underwriting automation, a real-time quotation engine, OCR-powered claims intelligence, a corporates insurance marketplace, and SME portals. Its platform bridges data, systems, insurers, and corporates to streamline underwriting, quoting, and claims. DESAISIV is backed by 500 Global, Terra VC, Oqal, and other MENA/UK/US investors via a US$2M pre-seed round. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: doc.ai
providers.description: doc.ai, Inc. was a privacy-first enterprise artificial intelligence platform for healthcare, founded by Sam De Brouwer and Walter De Brouwer. It ran decentralized "data trials" that let individuals contribute and train models on their own genomic, pharmacogenomic, exposomic, wellness and hematology data, and it issued the $NRN (Neuron) token in a sale that closed in October 2017 — which is why it is carried in the Pantera Capital portfolio under the crypto sector despite being a digital-health AI business. Sharecare, Inc. completed its acquisition of doc.ai on 2021-02-23, absorbing the Unwinding Anxiety, Serenity, VERIFIED and Passport products and retaining both founders as executives. The doc.ai brand is retired: the apex domain no longer resolves to a website (last archived HTTP 200 on 2023-04-16) and no doc.ai developer portal, API, or specification could be located.

providers.name: First Horizon Corporation
providers.description: First Horizon Corporation (NYSE: FHN), headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee, is a regional financial-services holding company operating across 12 southeastern U.S. states through its principal subsidiary, First Horizon Bank. The franchise reports roughly $84 billion in total assets, $67 billion in deposits, and approximately 410 banking centers as of Q1 2026. Business lines include consumer and small-business banking, commercial and specialty lending, private banking and wealth management, and FHN Financial fixed- income capital markets. The company was founded in 1864 as First National Bank of Memphis, rebranded as First Tennessee in 1977, became First Horizon National Corporation in 2004, and shortened its name to First Horizon Corporation following the 2020 IberiaBank merger. In February 2022 First Horizon announced a $13.4 billion all-cash acquisition by Toronto-Dominion Bank; the parties mutually terminated the merger on May 4, 2023, citing regulatory uncertainty around the deal's closing timeline, with TD paying a $225 million termination fee plus a previously agreed $25 million reimbursement to First Horizon. First Horizon does not publish a public developer API portal. Customer account data is reachable for fintech use cases only through US open-banking aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) and through emerging Financial Data Exchange (FDX) APIs that will be required of covered data providers under the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule. Commercial APIs for treasury management, ACH origination, wire initiation, and host-to-host file transfer are available to corporate clients under direct contract through First Horizon Treasury Management Services but are not publicly documented.

providers.name: Healthcaresource.com
providers.description: HealthcareSource is a healthcare-focused talent management software provider whose recruiting, applicant tracking, onboarding, behavioral assessments, learning, and employee performance-management products are used across U.S. healthcare organizations. HealthcareSource was acquired by symplr in July 2021 (from Francisco Partners) and its products are now delivered as part of symplr's healthcare talent-management suite, including symplr Recruiting. No public developer program, API documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface was found for the brand at profiling time; the healthcaresource.com domain 301-redirects to symplr.com/healthcaresource.

providers.name: Independence Health Group
providers.description: Independence Health Group is the Philadelphia-headquartered parent holding company of Independence Blue Cross (the Blue Cross and Blue Shield licensee for southeastern Pennsylvania), AmeriHealth Administrators (a national third-party benefits administrator), and AmeriHealth New Jersey. Through its subsidiaries the group serves approximately seven million members and is one of the largest health insurers in the Philadelphia region. Independence Health Group itself does not publish a developer portal or APIs; all CMS Interoperability and Patient Access surfaces are operated by the subsidiary plans (notably Independence Blue Cross and AmeriHealth New Jersey).

providers.name: IQVIA
providers.description: IQVIA empowers life sciences organizations to accelerate innovation, improve patient outcomes, and bring treatments to market faster through advanced analytics and technology. IQVIA is a Fortune 500 company offering data, analytics, clinical research, and connected intelligence services.

providers.name: Kemper
providers.description: The Kemper family of companies is one of the nation's leading insurers. With approximately $13 billion in assets, Kemper is improving the world of insurance by offering personalized solutions for individuals, families and businesses.

providers.name: Korn Ferry
providers.description: Korn Ferry is a global organizational consulting firm that helps companies design optimal organization structures, recruit and develop talent, and drive performance. The firm offers services across executive search, leadership development, organizational strategy, total rewards, and talent acquisition. Korn Ferry serves clients across industries with a combination of consulting, data, and digital products.
