The firm has historic depth in consumer financial services, real estate, public finance, and IP, and runs widely read thought-leadership properties including the Consumer Finance Monitor blog (with public RSS feed) and the Business Better podcast. Ballard Spahr does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is the Consumer Finance Monitor RSS feed.

providers.name: Calpine
providers.description: Calpine Corporation was a major U.S. energy company headquartered in Houston, Texas, and was the largest generator of electricity from natural gas and geothermal energy in the United States. It operated 80 power plants with approximately 26,035 megawatts of generation capacity, including The Geysers, the world's largest geothermal complex. Calpine also operated the Champion Energy retail electricity subsidiary serving deregulated markets. As of January 2026, Constellation Energy completed its acquisition of Calpine for $16.4 billion, making it a business unit of Constellation. Calpine does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Coinsuper
providers.description: Coinsuper presents itself as a cryptocurrency exchange offering USD-compliant crypto trading, spot markets, an exchange and trade interface, a token listing application process, a referral program, and blockchain products (LENS and Blockchain+). The public site markets white-label trading-system solutions, enterprise cold and hot wallet asset management, and industrial blockchain technical services, citing patents in crypto trading and blockchain core technology. Coinsuper was originally a Hong Kong exchange surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the current site is a WordPress-hosted brand presence with no publicly documented developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at the time of this pass.

providers.name: Covestor
providers.description: Covestor was an online investment management and social investing platform, backed by Union Square Ventures, that let everyday investors mirror the portfolios of vetted model managers through managed brokerage accounts. Interactive Brokers acquired Covestor in 2015 and later rebranded it as Interactive Advisors; the covestor.com domain now 301-redirects to interactiveadvisors.com. No public Covestor developer or API surface exists, so this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub with only a live domain-security probe recorded.

providers.name: Data.ai
providers.description: Data.ai (founded as App Annie in 2010, rebranded to data.ai in 2022) was a mobile app market-data and analytics provider, offering estimates of app downloads, revenue, usage, and competitive market intelligence across the iOS App Store and Google Play for publishers, brands, and investors. The company historically exposed a market-data API (api.data.ai) for programmatic access to app performance and store intelligence. Data.ai was acquired by Sensor Tower in 2024 and now operates as a Sensor Tower company; its standalone site is a gated login and the former public API host serves a default page, so its independent API surface has been consolidated into Sensor Tower and effectively retired. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an ivp portfolio company.

providers.name: Day & Zimmermann
providers.description: Day & Zimmermann is a privately held, family-owned diversified industrial services company founded in 1901 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The company operates across four primary business segments — Maintenance & Construction (power, nuclear, fossil, renewable, and chemical plants), Munitions (ammunition manufacturing, storage, and demilitarization for the U.S. military, including operation of the Lake City Army Ammunition Plant), Government Services (security, EOD, facility management, and architecture/engineering for federal agencies), and Workforce Solutions (staffing and talent placement via Yoh). The Yoh family has controlled the company since 1961; Harold L. Yoh III serves as Chairman and CEO. Day & Zimmermann reported approximately $2.7 billion in revenue in 2023 with roughly 43,000–52,000 employees across approximately 150 global locations. Day & Zimmermann does not publish any public developer APIs; its business is delivered through long-cycle service contracts, government-owned contractor-operated (GOCO) facilities, and direct client engagements.

providers.name: Fraudio
providers.description: Fraudio is an Amsterdam-based payments fraud detection and financial-crime scale-up founded in 2019 by João Moura (CEO), Nathan Trousdell (COO), and team, with additional offices in London, Lisbon, and Barcelona. Fraudio delivers AI- and machine-learning-driven fraud detection as a managed service to merchant acquirers, payment service providers, card issuers, and banks, with a product line that covers card payment fraud, merchant initiated fraud, anti-money laundering, authorised push payment (APP) fraud, and money mule detection. The company markets itself as "Generation 3" fraud detection, advancing past rule-based (Gen 1) and bespoke per-customer ML (Gen 2) approaches by training a single centralized "patent pending AI super brain" on the pooled transaction history of all of its customers, claiming network-effect performance gains versus single-tenant models. Fraudio integrates with customers through a plug-and-play real-time scoring API with sub-100ms response times, configurable risk-appetite thresholds, and no upfront integration or setup cost. Customers include Viva Wallet, Silverflow, Pismo, Bancontact, Fazz, PayTabs, IXOPAY, Bold.co, SaltPay, WiPay, ePayco, and LOQR. Fraudio is ISO 27001 certified, was selected for the Visa Innovation Program (2023), is co-financed by the EU Lisboa 2030 programme, has raised roughly $3.3M seed plus a Series A round (March 2025), and counts BigStar Ventures, BYND Venture Capital, Teya, Viva Wallet, Portugal Ventures, Iberis Capital, Shilling, and CTT among its investors. There is no public developer portal, no open API reference, no public OpenAPI spec, no SDK, and no GitHub organization — the fraud-scoring API is delivered as a gated B2B integration through a commercial sales process.

providers.name: Holtec International
providers.description: Holtec International is a privately held American supplier of equipment and systems for the nuclear, solar, geothermal, and fossil power-generation industries. The company is best known for its spent-fuel storage and transport casks (HI-STAR, HI-STORM, HI-STORE CISF), decommissioning services through Holtec Decommissioning International (HDI), and its in-development SMR-300 small modular reactor — a roughly 320 MWe two-loop pressurized water reactor with an 80-year design life. Holtec is currently pursuing the first-ever restart of a permanently shut-down U.S. commercial nuclear power plant at Palisades in Michigan, which is also designated as the first deployment site for the SMR-300. The company runs manufacturing facilities in Camden, NJ, Pittsburgh, PA, and Orrville, OH, and partners with Hyundai Engineering & Construction (HDEC) on SMR-300 detailed design and full-scope plant construction.

providers.name: KelAI
providers.description: KelAI (Kelai) is an AI quant research platform for hedge funds and institutional investors that positions itself as an autonomous alpha engine. Its AI agents run the full systematic-research workflow — generating trading-signal ideas, writing and testing research code, analyzing market data, running backtests and validation, and monitoring live signal performance — consolidating what normally runs across siloed systems and inefficient workflows. Founded by Jeremie Cohen, a former WorldQuant portfolio manager and head of event-driven systematic strategies who also led machine learning teams at Millennium Management, KelAI is part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch and is deployed with institutional investors. As an early-stage company it does not yet publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Koinex
providers.description: Koinex was an Indian digital-asset exchange launched in 2017, describing itself as India's first and largest cryptocurrency exchange with more than one million users. It offered spot trading across multiple crypto assets with INR pairs before regulatory uncertainty around Indian banking access forced it to shut down all services in June 2019, asking users to withdraw their holdings by July 15, 2019. The company is DEFUNCT: koinex.in now serves only a single static wind-down notice directing former users to claim any crypto assets left on the platform through CoinDCX, with which Koinex partnered for the transition. There is no live product, developer portal, documentation, or API surface; the domain's TLS certificate expired in March 2025 and every path other than the notice returns 403. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record of a shut-down crypto exchange and as a Pantera Capital portfolio lead.

Its Luna BESS is described as the first repurposed-battery system to achieve UL 1973, UL 9540, and UL 9540A certifications, and is applied to demand-charge management, grid backup, EV-charging support, and energy arbitrage across data centers, public institutions, transportation, food & beverage, manufacturing, and forestry. Moment Energy is a hardware and energy-services company and publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Nse-india
providers.description: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), operating at nseindia.com, is one of the world's largest stock exchanges by number of trades and derivatives contracts, headquartered in Mumbai. It runs electronic equity, derivatives, debt, and currency markets, publishes market data and corporate filings, and maintains the Nifty family of indices via NSE Indices. NSE exposes market data primarily through licensed data feeds and the undocumented endpoints powering nseindia.com rather than a published public developer API program; this profile was surfaced as an enrichment lead and has no documented public REST API surface at this time.

providers.name: NuScale Power
providers.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

providers.name: Oddup
providers.description: Oddup (now operating as Oddup Markets) is a Singapore-based platform founded in 2015 by James Giancotti. It began as a data-driven startup-rating and intelligence service — a 500 Global portfolio company scoring startups and crypto projects — and has since pivoted to prediction markets, letting users trade on real-world outcomes across crypto, FX, indices, and commodities using a distinctive Yes / No / Maybe outcome model. The current product is a client-side single-page web application hosted on Vercel at oddup.app (and oddup.com). As of this enrichment pass the live site is geo-restricted (HTTP 451, x-blocked-country: US) and exposes no public developer, API, documentation, or .well-known surface — no OpenAPI, no API subdomains, and no published packages were discoverable. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe only; it will be re-enriched if a public API surface appears.

providers.name: Pacific Fusion
providers.description: Pacific Fusion is a fusion energy company based in Fremont, California developing commercial fusion power using pulsed magnetic inertial fusion. Its modular system pairs a fast electric pulser, a meter-scale fusion chamber, and centimeter-scale fuel targets to pursue net facility gain with practical, affordable manufacturing. Building on breakthroughs from US National Laboratories (Lawrence Livermore, Sandia) and partners such as General Atomics, the company aims to deliver limitless, clean, on-demand power. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, this profile has been enriched through the API Evangelist network. Pacific Fusion is a hardware and energy company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

Around was acquired by Miro in June 2022, operated for a period as Around by Miro Labs, and was shut down on 31 March 2025, with features such as echo prevention and reactions folded into Miro's own video collaboration surface. Asula has raised roughly $6.7M from Electric Capital, Framework Ventures, and Figment Capital, and ships two products, Bedlam and Dawn. providers.name: Atlas Discovery
providers.description: Atlas Discovery is an AI-powered biotechnology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building foundation models of human patient biology to predict how people will respond to drugs in clinical trials. Nine of ten drugs fail in trials because no animal model or cell in a dish reliably predicts a human response; Atlas Discovery trains models on preclinical and clinical data to improve trial design and rescue stalled drug programs. Its research spans single-cell representation learning (ExpressionVAE) and clinical response prediction, with work presented at ICLR '26, ICML '26, and CSHL '26. The company is an early-stage research lab with no public API, developer program, or product surface yet; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting a public developer offering.

providers.name: Atom Computing
providers.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

providers.name: Atomwise
providers.description: Atomwise pioneered the use of deep convolutional neural networks for structure-based drug discovery, with its AtomNet platform applying AI to virtual screening of small molecules against protein targets. The company ran the Artificial Intelligence Molecular Screen (AIMS) academic collaboration program, partnered with biotech and pharma companies on discovery contracts, and built an internal pipeline of small-molecule programs. As of 2026, atomwise.com redirects to Numerion Labs (numerionlabs.ai), reflecting an apparent rebrand or successor entity that positions itself as an AI superplatform exploring drug-like chemical space with programs in immune and inflammatory diseases. Atomwise never exposed a public commercial API; AtomNet screening was delivered to partners as a service. The legacy GitHub organization (github.com/atomwise) hosts no public repositories.

Its Network AI platform ingests telemetry from network devices, applies machine-learning anomaly detection (including gray failures), eliminates noise, performs incident root-cause identification, noiseless ticket creation, and auto-mitigation/remediation for data-center and enterprise networks. The platform exposed a Topology REST API for device discovery/lifecycle and DevOps/ITSM integration. Augtera was acquired by NVIDIA in December 2024 and folded into the NVIDIA Spectrum-X networking portfolio; its standalone augtera.com site now 301-redirects to nvidia.com, so no independent public developer/API surface remains. Added to the API Evangelist network as a bain-capital-ventures portfolio lead.

It raised a $1.8M seed round in May 2013 from Highland Capital Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Freestyle Capital, and Draper Associates, and was acquired by Yahoo in January 2014. Yahoo discontinued the Aviate launcher on March 8, 2018. The company is defunct: it never shipped a public API, developer portal, or SDK, aviate.com is now a parked domain listed for sale, aviate.yahoo.com redirects to downloads.yahoo.com, and the ThumbsUp Labs GitHub organization has no public repositories.

providers.name: Bouffalo Lab
providers.description: Bouffalo Lab (博流智能) is a fabless chip design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nanjing, China, focused on ultra-low-power AIoT (AI + IoT) and edge-computing system chips. Its product line centers on RISC-V based microcontrollers with integrated wireless connectivity — the BL602/BL604 (Wi-Fi 2.4G + BLE 5.0), BL702/BL704/BL706 (Zigbee 3.0 + BLE 5.0), BL606P (quad-mode dual-core Wi-Fi/BT/BLE/Zigbee), and the BL616/BL618 and BL808 families — combining wireless radios, audio/video processing, and on-device AI algorithms. The company ships the open-source BouffaloSDK (a merge of bl_mcu_sdk and bl_iot_sdk) under Apache 2.0 through its public GitHub organization, along with hardware abstraction drivers, Matter/Thread support, and NuttX RTOS ports. Bouffalo Lab is a hardware/firmware provider rather than a web-API provider; it exposes no public HTTP/REST developer API, so the enrichment pipeline captures its developer surface (GitHub SDK org) and domain security posture. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

Once valued at roughly $2.3 billion and backed by investors including Bloomberg Beta and SV Angel, the company ceased operations in November 2024 and its facilities and equipment entered liquidation through 2025-2026. providers.name: Boxee
providers.description: Boxee, Inc. was a New York and Tel Aviv based consumer media company founded in 2007 by Avner Ronen, Tom Sella, Idan Cohen, Gidon Coussin and Roy Vulcan. Its cross-platform media-center software began as a fork of the open-source XBMC project and bridged local media libraries with internet streaming sources. Boxee shipped a Python-based application API in April 2009 that let third parties build Boxee apps in Python with XML-defined interfaces, distributed through the Boxee app directory and documented at developer.boxee.tv. Hardware followed with the D-Link Boxee Box (2010) and Boxee TV with a cloud DVR service (2012). Backed by Union Square Ventures and Spark Capital, Boxee was acquired by Samsung Electronics in July 2013; the cloud DVR was shut down on 10 July 2013 and Samsung wound down the Boxee team in 2015. The company is defunct and no API surface, developer portal, or documentation remains reachable.

Butter Systems raised roughly $120K across two seed rounds in 2013 from Y Combinator and Fenox Venture Capital, and shut down in 2014. Y Combinator lists the company as inactive, and its buttersystems.com domain is now a parked "domain may be for sale" page. Built on a proprietary WebRTC-based real-time video distribution network, Caffeine positioned itself as a low-latency, social-first alternative to Twitch for gaming, entertainment, and — in its later years — live sports, partnering with roughly 200 sports organizations and reaching tens of millions of monthly users. The company published open-source broadcasting tooling under its caffeinetv GitHub organization (libcaffeine, caffeine-rtc, an OBS plugin, and the CaffQL GraphQL code generator) but never shipped a public, documented developer API program. Caffeine announced it was ceasing operations, and its web presence is now a shutdown notice; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead and is archival rather than an active, integrable API provider.

Its enterprise platform let financial institutions deliver strong digital identities to end users while meeting KYC/AML and data privacy obligations (including European GDPR), giving individuals control over their own personal identity data shared across institutions. The company was backed by investors including Partech and PayPal, and was acquired by Blockchains, Inc. in December 2020, after which its team and identity technology were folded into Blockchains' digital identity product. The former company website (cambridge-blockchain.com) is no longer served; the surviving public developer surface is its GitHub organization and two first-party npm cryptographic libraries. No public HTTP API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or hosted documentation was ever published.

providers.description: CoreOS was a San Francisco-based container infrastructure company founded in 2013 that built a lightweight, automatically-updating Linux distribution (Container Linux, originally CoreOS Linux) and a family of now-foundational cloud-native open source projects: etcd (the distributed key-value store at the heart of Kubernetes), the Quay container registry, the Tectonic enterprise Kubernetes platform, the rkt container engine, flannel networking, Clair image-vulnerability scanning, and Ignition provisioning. Red Hat acquired CoreOS in January 2018 for approximately $250 million. Its technologies were folded into Red Hat's portfolio — Container Linux became Red Hat CoreOS and the community Fedora CoreOS, Tectonic merged into OpenShift, Quay continues as Red Hat Quay, and etcd and rkt were donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. The company no longer operates independently; coreos.com redirects to Red Hat OpenShift. The github.com/coreos organization remains active as the upstream home for Fedora CoreOS components such as Ignition, Butane, and fleetlock.

providers.description: Cornershop is an on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service founded in 2015 in Chile by Oskar Hjertonsson, Daniel Undurraga, and Juan Pablo Cuevas, simultaneously launching in Santiago, Chile and Mexico City, Mexico. The platform connects consumers with personal shoppers who pick and deliver groceries, pharmacy items, and other goods from local supermarkets, specialty stores, and big-box retailers. After a 2018 acquisition attempt by Walmart was blocked by Mexican regulators, Uber agreed in October 2019 to acquire majority ownership, completing full acquisition in July 2021 at a reported valuation north of US$3 billion — Chile's first unicorn exit. At its peak Cornershop operated in eight countries across the Americas: Chile, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Peru, Canada, and the United States. Beginning in 2021 Uber merged the Cornershop brand into Uber Eats, migrating the grocery vertical ("Uber Eats Grocery") into its main consumer app and progressively shutting down the standalone Cornershop apps and websites. As of 2026 cornershopapp.com and cornershop.io redirect to ubereats.com, the Cornershop LLC GitHub organization (archived October 2024) has zero public repositories, and there is no public developer API, SDK, partner program, or technical documentation under the Cornershop brand — Cornershop survives only as engineering history and as the LatAm backbone of Uber Eats Grocery. Community-built unofficial Python wrappers exist on GitHub but reverse-engineer the consumer mobile app and are not sanctioned by Uber.

providers.name: DHCP
providers.description: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) is a network management protocol used to automate the process of configuring devices on IP networks. DHCP dynamically assigns IP addresses and other network configuration parameters to each device on a network, enabling them to communicate with other IP networks. Defined in IETF RFC 2131, the protocol supports automatic, dynamic, and manual allocation modes and uses message types including DHCPDISCOVER, DHCPOFFER, DHCPREQUEST, DHCPACK, DHCPNAK, DHCPDECLINE, DHCPRELEASE, and DHCPINFORM. DHCP builds on BOOTP (RFC 951) and is supplemented by RFCs covering options and clarifications.

Its platform combined generative chemistry (Centaur Chemist) with patient tissue-based screening (EVE, an automated single-cell platform for testing drug candidates directly against patient-derived tumor samples) to design small-molecule drug candidates faster and at lower cost than conventional pharma R&D. Notable firsts included EXS-21546 (an A2A antagonist developed with Evotec), DSP-1181 (the first AI-designed molecule to enter human clinical trials, with Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma), and DSP-0038 (a dual 5-HT1A/5-HT2A modulator for Alzheimer's psychosis). Exscientia maintained active pharma partnerships with Sanofi, Bristol Myers Squibb, Bayer, Sumitomo, and Merck KGaA. Exscientia was acquired by Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) in an all-stock deal that closed in November 2024; the combined company operates under the Recursion brand and the legacy exscientia.ai website now redirects to recursion.com. The Exscientia name persists primarily through its GitHub organization, which continues to host open-source scientific Python packages for molecular predictive modelling (molflux), physics-based ML potentials (physicsml), antibody structure prediction (abodybuilder3), and biomolecular simulation (biosimspace) used by the wider computational chemistry and structural biology community. Exscientia did not expose any public commercial APIs, SDKs, or developer products before or after the merger; platform access was always delivered through collaborative drug-discovery agreements.

Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York City, Flex operates a consumer mobile app and partners with property-management platforms; it is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and surfaced in the 500 Global portfolio. providers.name: Kitchensurfing
providers.description: Kitchensurfing was a New York City marketplace that booked professional chefs to shop for, cook, and serve meals in customers' own kitchens, founded in 2012 and backed by roughly $20M from Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital, and Tiger Global. It began as an advance-booking platform for private dinner parties and pivoted in 2015 to a flat-rate on-demand model in which a chef arrived and cooked dinner within a fixed window. Neither model produced sustainable demand against better-capitalized meal-kit and delivery competitors, and the company discontinued service and shut down on April 15, 2016. It never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Its GitHub organization survives with eleven public repositories - open-source Ruby/Rails forks and internal hackathon projects, last active in 2016 - but contains no client library or API definition. The kitchensurfing.com domain was subsequently re-registered by an unrelated cooking-products affiliate publisher and no longer represents this company.

providers.name: Kitchit
providers.description: Kitchit was a San Francisco on-demand private-chef marketplace founded in 2011 by Brendan Marshall and Ian Ferguson. The service matched consumers with vetted professional chefs who shopped, cooked, served, and cleaned up a multi-course meal in the customer's own home, booked through the kitchit.com web and mobile storefront. In 2015 the company pivoted from fully customized menus to a lower-priced standardized product marketed as "Kitchit Tonight," priced around $39 per person with a two-person minimum. Kitchit served more than 100,000 meals across roughly five years of operation and reported a net promoter score of 87. It raised approximately $8.1M, with investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Crosslink Capital, Javelin Venture Partners, and Otter Rock Capital. The company announced its shutdown in April 2016, with the founders citing a finite investment runway that ended amid broad upheaval in food-tech, alongside contemporaneous failures at SpoonRocket, Dinner Lab, and Kitchensurfing. Kitchit is defunct: it operates no website, developer portal, or public API today, and no public API surface was ever published. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record for network completeness.

providers.name: Klout
providers.description: Klout was a San Francisco social-analytics company, founded in 2008 by Joe Fernandez and Binh Tran, that scored individuals on their online social influence. The "Klout Score" was a single number from 1 to 100 derived from the size of a person's social network and how other people engaged with the content they published across connected accounts such as Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, and Google+. Klout operated a public REST API — the Klout API v2 at api.klout.com — that let developers resolve a social handle to a Klout identity, look up a user's score and score history, and retrieve influence graphs (who a user influences and is influenced by) and topic affinities; access was key-based and widely used by marketing, CRM, and social-listening tools, and a large community of third-party client libraries grew up around it in Ruby, Node.js, Python, and PHP. Lithium Technologies acquired Klout on 27 March 2014 for approximately $200 million. Lithium retired Klout as a standalone service on 25 May 2018 — the day the EU General Data Protection Regulation took effect — stating that Klout's AI and machine-learning capabilities were valuable to Lithium but the consumer service was not aligned with its long-term strategy. The Klout API was shut down with the service. Lithium has since been rebranded as Khoros, and klout.com now redirects into the Khoros website. The company is defunct and operates no live API; this profile is retained as a historical provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kobo360
providers.description: Kobo360 is a Nigerian-founded, pan-African B2B digital freight marketplace and logistics technology platform headquartered in Lagos, with operations across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Togo, Uganda, and other African countries. Founded in 2017 by Obi Ozor and Ife Oyedele II, Kobo360 operates an "Uber for trucks" long-haul logistics model that matches cargo owners and enterprise shippers with truck owners and drivers through a single digital ecosystem. The company runs the Global Logistics Operating System (G-LOS), an enterprise-grade logistics SaaS / digital freight forwarding platform that provides shipper dashboards, end-to-end shipment visibility, driver and truck ratings, embedded credit and working-capital products for carriers, and route and load optimization across the Kobo network of registered drivers and trucks. Kobo360 serves large FMCG, manufacturing, and commodities customers including Dangote, DHL, Honeywell, Olam, and Unilever, and has raised funding from investors such as Goldman Sachs, IFC, TLcom Capital, and Western Asset. Kobo360 does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open developer portal; integrations with shippers and partners are delivered through enterprise onboarding rather than a self-service API program.

providers.name: Kuva Space
providers.description: Kuva Space is a Finnish space-data company headquartered in Espoo that operates a fleet of hyperspectral Earth observation microsatellites and delivers AI-driven planetary intelligence through its Kuva Sense platform. Founded in 2016 (originally as Reaktor Space Lab) by Tuomas Tikka and Janne Kuhno in collaboration with Reaktor, the company designs, builds, and operates its own 6U CubeSat-class spacecraft carrying a patented in-orbit tunable Fabry-Perot 2D snapshot hyperspectral imager. Its operational Hyperfield-1A (launched August 2024 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg) and Hyperfield-1B (launched June 2025) cover the 475–950 nm VNIR range with up to 160 tunable spectral bands at 25 m spatial resolution and a 50 km swath from a 500 km polar sun-synchronous orbit. The larger 70 kg Hyperfield-2 microsatellite, scheduled for H2 2026, expands coverage to 450–1,650 nm at 15 m resolution with an additional 3.6 m GSD RGB camera. By 2030 Kuva Space plans to grow the constellation to roughly 100 satellites to enable sub-daily revisit anywhere on Earth. Onboard AI handles cloud filtering, spectral band alignment, and compression so that downlinked products feed directly into Kuva Sense, where automated analytics generate insights-as-a-service for agriculture (crop identification, yield forecasting, harvest timing), aquaculture (water quality, algal bloom detection, biomass), environment and carbon (sequestration monitoring, deforestation, pollution tracking), and safety and security (vessel detection and tracking, illegal activity warning, rapid change detection). Kuva Space is part of the European Space Agency InCubed-co-funded HYPERFIELD program, was awarded a €1.8M ESA Civil Security from Space contract within the SMART-CONNECT consortium to demonstrate rapid hyperspectral insights for crisis response, and in 2026 signed a Letter of Intent with SSC Space to strengthen Nordic space capabilities. The commercial model is subscription-based insights-as-a-service rather than pay-per-pixel imagery sales, with current access offered through the Kuva Sense Early Adopter Program; the company markets "robust APIs and customizable data formats" for system integration but does not currently publish open public API reference documentation, an OpenAPI specification, or a self-service developer portal. The only public engineering surface is the open-source kuva-data-processing Python toolkit (kuva-metadata, kuva-reader, kuva-geometry) on GitHub and PyPI, which reads Kuva GeoTIFF-based L0/L1AB/L1C/L2A data products and their metadata sidecars.

providers.name: Kwest
providers.description: Kwest was a Berlin-based B2B SaaS platform for the operations behind renewable-energy installations. Founded by Robin Dechant, Marco Holst and Constantin Ehren, it gave solar, heat-pump and smart-meter installers a workflow platform covering project management, inspection documentation, automated report creation and incident management, plus integrations that synced installation data with the CRM, ERP and field-service tools those companies already ran (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Dynamics 365, Odoo, Xentral, weclapp, Zoho, Aurora Solar, Solytic, Praxedo, Zapier and others). Speedinvest invested in 2021. In 2024 Kwest was acquired by Kraken Technologies, the technology arm of Octopus Energy Group, which folded the Kwest workflow platform into the Kraken stack and opened its first development hub in Berlin around the seven-person team. Kwest published no public API or developer program, and the company no longer operates independently - its former getkwest.com domain has lapsed and now serves unrelated third-party content, so it is recorded here as historical only and is not linked as a live website.

The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Leade.rs
providers.description: Leade.rs, Inc. was a two-sided marketplace that matched keynote, motivational, and business speakers with the conferences, corporate events, brands, and press that wanted to book them. Event organizers could search a curated roster and create an event, while speakers maintained a profile covering their availability and topics — the platform's stated aim was to remove the cold-outreach grind from conference programming and surface newer and more diverse voices. The company was co-founded by Loïc Le Meur, the French entrepreneur behind the LeWeb conference and a Silicon Valley angel investor; at acquisition its network was reported at roughly 300 speakers across 11 core fields including crypto, AI, and entrepreneurship. ASX-listed Animoca Brands acquired 100% of the equity on 6 May 2019 for US$0.5 million upfront, intending to grow the roster into a mentor and investor network bridging East and West alongside its Zeroth accelerator, with Le Meur joining Animoca as a venture partner. The product did not survive the acquisition. Leade.rs never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable documentation, and as of the July 2026 enrichment pass the leade.rs domain no longer resolves — it remains registered through December 2026 and is delegated to EuroDNS nameservers, but the zone is not served, so there is no live surface of any kind to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

Common applications include contactless payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay), transit ticketing, access control, device pairing, smart posters, and secure identification. NFC defines several technical specifications including NDEF (data exchange format), NCI (controller interface), LLCP (link layer), SNEP (data exchange), and the Tag Type 1-5 operation specifications.

providers.name: OpenBazaar
providers.description: OpenBazaar is an open-source, decentralized peer-to-peer marketplace protocol that let buyers and sellers trade goods and services directly with one another using cryptocurrency, with no central company, listing fees, or intermediaries taking a cut. Trades were coordinated over a distributed network built on IPFS and libp2p, settled with Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, and secured with multisignature escrow and third-party moderation. The project originated from the DarkMarket proof-of-concept and was developed and funded by the company OB1 (backed by a16z, Union Square Ventures, and others). The OpenBazaar server daemon exposed a local JSON REST API on the node that desktop, mobile, and web clients used to manage listings, orders, wallets, and profiles. OB1 wound down commercial operations and the hosted services in early 2021, and the code was open-sourced to the community. The openbazaar.org site now advertises an in-development "OpenBazaar 3.0" successor, and the GitHub organization hosts the legacy Python (1.0) and Go (2.0) daemons alongside newer Rust and browser-based clients.

Its application keeps a user's data on their own device by default, offering personal search, offline content archives, multiple personas, trust-based connections via tokens, information-centric collaboration, and community moderation. The project is grounded in four principles: transparency, accountability, personal control, and security (cryptographic verification). It is a revival of the original OpenCola (1999), and the current release is a local desktop application rather than a hosted service. OpenCola publishes no public web API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time; this profile captures its identity and open-source posture for the API Evangelist network.

Backed by Insight Partners and other growth investors, it operates a consumer education platform and does not publish a public developer API program; its public GitHub organization holds internal open-source engineering forks rather than client SDKs.

Optimyze was acquired by Elastic N.V. in October 2021 and its Prodfiler technology was folded into Elastic Observability as Elastic Universal Profiling. The independent company no longer operates: the optimyze.cloud domain no longer resolves, the GitHub organization was archived in 2024, and the Prodfiler developer sub-sites (documentation, app, community) are offline. No independent public Optimyze API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal exists to enrich; this profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Orbital Insight
providers.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program). The company applied computer vision and machine learning to satellite imagery, aerial photography, AIS vessel signals, and IoT/mobile location data to produce intelligence on supply chains, global commodities (notably oil storage via its Global Geospatial Crude Index), geopolitical events, demographics, retail foot traffic, disaster damage, and national-security questions. Its flagship product was the GO platform (later rebranded TerraScope), a self-service geospatial intelligence platform layering proprietary models over commercial satellite imagery from partners including DigitalGlobe, Airbus, Planet Labs, and e-GEOS. Orbital Insight raised funding from In-Q-Tel, GV (Google Ventures), Sequoia Capital, CME Ventures, and others, and acquired Boston-based FeatureX in 2018. After a period of financial distress in 2023, Orbital Insight was acquired by Privateer (co-founded by Apple's Steve Wozniak and Alex Fielding) on May 6, 2024. Following the acquisition, the standalone orbitalinsight.com brand was wound down and the TerraScope platform is now offered by Privateer alongside its Wayfinder space-domain-awareness data engine, fused into Privateer's "Elements" all-domain data platform. As of 2026 there is no public self-service Orbital Insight developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the orbitalinsight GitHub organization has only two archived repositories (a region-aggregation reference and a fork of tileserver-gl) and no current developer portal.

providers.name: Orby AI

Founded by former DeepMind and Google researchers, Orby was backed by Wing Venture Capital and NEA before being acquired by Uniphore in August 2025, where its technology now powers the Uniphore Business AI Cloud. Orby publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; its capabilities are delivered as an enterprise platform accessed via demo and sales engagement.

Orca Bio's lead program TREGZI is a precision-engineered allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy for hematological malignancies, alongside investigational programs Orca-T and Orca-Q. As a clinical/therapeutics company it does not publish a public developer or API surface; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and enriched with verified company identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: PsiQuantum
providers.description: PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California photonic quantum computing company founded in 2016 by Jeremy O'Brien, Terry Rudolph, Pete Shadbolt, and Mark Thompson, building utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers based on single-photon qubits at telecom wavelength. Its Omega chipset — a silicon photonic system integrating on-chip single-photon sources, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, barium-titanate optical switches, and low-loss fiber couplers — is manufactured on 300mm wafers at GlobalFoundries' flagship fab in Malta, NY, leveraging mature semiconductor processes rather than exotic cryogenic fabrication. The company is constructing two utility- scale, million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum computing sites: one at Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia (in partnership with the Australian and Queensland governments) and one at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago, Illinois (with additional R&D at PsiLabs in Daresbury, UK and assembly at PsiFactory in Milpitas, CA). PsiQuantum exposes a developer surface aimed at fault-tolerant quantum algorithm researchers: Construct, an enterprise platform for FTQC algorithm development, resource analysis, and training; Circuit Designer, a free web tool for prototyping and visualizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits; Circuit Hub, a shared library of `.circuit` files; and two open-source Python projects on GitHub — Bartiq, a symbolic quantum resource estimator that compiles subroutine-level costs to global T-gate, Toffoli, qubit, and circuit-volume estimates, and QREF, an open JSON-Schema-based format for representing quantum algorithms as hierarchical DAGs with a Pydantic validation library and a `qref-render` visualization tool. NVIDIA's CUDA-Q is integrated into Construct for accelerated simulation. PsiQuantum does not currently publish a commercial cloud-access REST API, OpenAPI specification, or a general-purpose quantum-execution SDK comparable to those of gate-model quantum cloud providers — its public developer artifacts are confined to FTQC resource-estimation tooling and algorithm-design surfaces — and there is no public pricing or self-serve tier for the underlying quantum hardware.

Its ReSOLVE platform combines AI/ML, protein science, structural biology, and biophysics to accelerate discovery; the pipeline includes VENT-03 (cGAS inhibitor), VENT-02 (NLRP3 inhibitor), and VENT-04 (caspase-4/5 inhibitor). Headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts with a site in Saint-Laurent, Quebec, and backed by GV and the SoftBank Vision Fund. Formed in July 2014 through the merger of International Paper's xpedx division with Unisource Worldwide, Veritiv operated as a publicly traded company on the New York Stock Exchange until it was acquired and taken private by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) in November 2023 in a transaction valued at approximately $2.3 billion. The company is headquartered in Sandy Springs, Georgia, and operates roughly 125 distribution centers across the United States and Mexico. Veritiv does not publish any public developer APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal — its commercial surface is built around sales reps, account managers, and large-account customer portals rather than a programmable API.

View makes View Dynamic Glass, electrochromic architectural windows whose tint adjusts automatically to sunlight, glare, and heat, alongside a connected Smart Building Platform in which each pane is individually IP-addressable and app-controllable and layered with sensors and services such as SmartProtect (an Azure IoT integration that alerts building managers when glass breaks). Backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund, View went public via SPAC in 2021 and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2024, transitioning back to private ownership under its lenders. View exposes no public developer API surface; its GitHub organization (viewinc) mirrors third-party C/C++ and IoT firmware libraries used internally rather than first-party SDKs.

The company is a regional fresh-food, beverage, and fuel brand with a strong loyalty program (Wawa Rewards) and a mobile ordering app. Wawa operates an internal API management platform (built with MuleSoft) used to connect to third-party services such as Uber Eats, Grubhub, and DoorDash for delivery, but does not publish a public developer portal or expose public APIs.

Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) announced its acquisition of WayPay in July 2019, after which the independent brand was retired. providers.description: Wheels Up Experience Inc. (NYSE: UP) is a leading on-demand private aviation provider in the U.S., offering charter and membership programs, commercial travel benefits through a strategic partnership with Delta Air Lines, and cargo services. Founded in 2013 by Kenny Dichter, Wheels Up was rescued from potential bankruptcy in September 2023 when a Delta Air Lines-led consortium (Delta, Certares, Knighthead, Cox) closed a $500M financing package and took a ~95% controlling equity stake. In November 2024 the company acquired the Embraer Phenom 300/300E fleet of GrandView Aviation ($105M) and secured $332M in equipment financing from Bank of America as part of a multi-year fleet modernization toward two core aircraft types (Phenom 300 series and Challenger 300/350). In 2025 it launched a new Signature membership portfolio and an industry-first integrated self-booking of Delta commercial flights inside the Wheels Up members app. Wheels Up does not publish a public developer API — its booking surface is a members-only mobile app and members.wheelsup.com web portal, with B2B operator connectivity historically routed through its acquired Avianis platform (2019).

The company operates multiple brands including Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn, Pottery Barn Kids, PBteen, West Elm, Rejuvenation, Mark and Graham, and Green Row. Williams-Sonoma does not offer a public developer API. The company uses internal APIs and third-party platforms for e-commerce, registry services, and supply chain management.

providers.name: American Financial Group
providers.description: American Financial Group (AFG) is a holding company engaged primarily in property and casualty insurance, focusing on specialized commercial products for businesses, and in the sale of fixed and indexed annuities through its Great American Insurance Group and Great American Life subsidiaries. AFG serves businesses across more than 40 specialty markets including agriculture, aviation, cyber, environmental, equine, ocean marine, professional liability, and transportation.

providers.name: American International Group (AIG)
providers.description: American International Group (AIG) is one of the world's most extensive international insurance organizations, operating in more than 200 countries and jurisdictions. AIG provides a broad range of property casualty insurance, life insurance, retirement solutions, and other financial services to commercial and individual customers worldwide. The company's offerings include casualty, property, cyber, professional liability, management liability, marine, aviation, energy, trade credit, and private client insurance.

providers.name: American National Insurance
providers.description: American National Insurance Company is a multi-line insurance holding company founded in 1905 and headquartered in Galveston, Texas. The company offers life insurance, annuities, pension risk transfer, health insurance, and property and casualty insurance through multiple subsidiary companies operating in all 50 states. American National holds A-level ratings from A.M. Best, Fitch, and S&P.

providers.name: Amodo
providers.description: Amodo was a European connected-insurance and telematics company founded in Zagreb, Croatia, that helped insurers and brokers build and distribute personalized usage-based insurance (UBI) products. Its Connected Insurance Platform combined a mobile telematics SDK, driver-behavior scoring, customer segmentation, and profiling analytics to power models ranging from try-before-you-buy to pay-as-you-drive and pay-per-mile. Over roughly nine years Amodo ran nearly 50 telematics programs worldwide with insurers including AIG, Porsche Versicherungs, Tower Insurance, and P&V, and was named one of the Financial Times' top five insurtech companies. Backed by Speedinvest, Amodo was acquired by Cambridge Mobile Telematics (CMT) in March 2023 and folded into CMT's European operations; the amodo.eu domain now redirects to CMT, and the company no longer maintains an independent public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Bright Health
providers.description: Bright Health Group was a Minneapolis-based healthtech and health-insurance company founded in 2016 by former UnitedHealthcare CEO Bob Sheehy, offering individual, family, and Medicare Advantage plans on the ACA exchanges through its Bright HealthCare brand. Backed by Redpoint Ventures and other venture investors, the company went public in 2021, then exited the insurance business, rebranded to NeueHealth in January 2024 to focus on value-based care delivery (NeueCare) and provider enablement (NeueSolutions), and shut down all remaining Bright HealthCare health-plan operations effective December 31, 2024. NeueHealth was subsequently taken private by New Enterprise Associates. Bright Health never published a public developer program, API, or documentation surface; runout operations are handled under the NeueHealth corporate brand.

providers.name: Brighter
providers.description: Brighter is a Santa Monica, California digital health technology company founded in 2010 by internet entrepreneur Jake Winebaum that built a consumer-driven dental benefits platform connecting dentists, patients, and dental insurers. Brighter licensed digital engagement solutions to insurance carriers, including online and mobile provider directories, patient reviews, and its proprietary Brighter Schedule online appointment scheduling feature, along with the Brighter PRO self-insured dental plan launched in 2014. Its platform powered member-engagement tools for major dental insurers including Cigna, Delta Dental, and Aetna. Backed by roughly $49M from General Catalyst, Mayfield, Benchmark, DAG Ventures, and Tenaya Capital, Brighter was acquired by Cigna in December 2017 and its technology folded into Cigna's digital health offerings. The brand persists as a Cigna dental provider experience.

providers.name: Carro
providers.description: Carro is a Singapore-headquartered used-car marketplace and automotive fintech platform, founded in 2015 and widely described as Southeast Asia's largest online used-car retailer. It operates a data-driven marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned vehicles across Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and Japan, and pairs it with adjacent services: car financing (Genie Financial Services), motor insurance, aftersales servicing and workshops (Carro Care), and car subscription. Carro reached unicorn status in 2021 in a round led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund; as of this pass Carro publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition, so this profile is company-identity only.

providers.name: Corpay
providers.description: Corpay (formerly FLEETCOR) is a corporate payments company that provides commercial cards, accounts payable automation, cross-border payment solutions, fuel and fleet cards, and workforce travel management services. The company serves over 800,000 customers globally through its Corpay Complete spend management platform and ERP integrations. A public, openly accessible developer API portal could not be confirmed from the corporate website at the time of this review.

providers.name: CUNA Mutual Group (TruStage)
providers.description: CUNA Mutual Group, now operating as TruStage, is an insurance and financial services company that provides insurance, retirement, and investment products to credit unions and their members. Founded in 1935 to serve the credit union movement, the company rebranded to TruStage in 2023, unifying its consumer-facing brands under a single identity. TruStage offers life insurance, auto and home insurance, AD&D, retirement planning, annuities, lending solutions, compliance services, and analytics tools to credit unions and their members.

providers.name: getdinghy
providers.description: Dinghy (getdinghy.com) was a UK insurtech offering on-demand professional indemnity and business insurance for freelancers and contractors, and a Balderton Capital portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the domain no longer serves an independent site - its TLS certificate and HTTP responses resolve to Kingsbridge Group infrastructure (kingsbridge.co.uk / kingsbridgegroup.com / kng.io) and every path returns HTTP 502, indicating the brand has been absorbed by Kingsbridge. No public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or well-known discovery surface is exposed, so no spec-grounded artifacts could be searched or derived. Retained as a network lead with evidence of the successor.

providers.name: Gigmile
providers.description: Gigmile is an African mobility platform and gig-economy fintech that gives riders, drivers, and fleet operators a pathway to financial independence through affordable vehicle financing and operational support. It offers lease-to-own and flexible financing for motorcycles, tricycles, cars, and electric vehicles (via its Gamma Mobility asset-financing brand), alongside earned-wage access, vehicle insurance, health cover, maintenance, and working-capital/micro-credit for independent gig workers. Founded by Kay and Sam out of Africa's e-commerce sector, Gigmile operates across Nigeria and Ghana (Lagos, Accra) and helps mobility entrepreneurs onboard and scale managed fleets of riders.

providers.name: Globe Life (Torchmark)
providers.description: Globe Life Inc. (NYSE: GL), formerly known as Torchmark Corporation, is an S&P 500 financial services holding company headquartered in McKinney, Texas. Founded in 1900, the company provides life insurance, supplemental health insurance, and annuity products through direct-to-consumer and agent distribution channels across the United States. Subsidiaries include Globe Life Liberty National Division, American Income Life Insurance Company, United American Insurance Company, Globe Life And Accident Insurance Company, and Globe Life Family Heritage Division. Revenue in 2024 was $5.78 billion with total assets of $29.1 billion. No public developer API is available; the company uses MuleSoft Anypoint Platform internally for API management and integration.

providers.name: Harris Computer
providers.description: Harris Computer is a constellation of companies acquiring and operating vertical market software businesses across the public sector, healthcare, utilities, financial services, education, and insurance markets. Harris Computer itself does not publish a unified public developer portal; APIs and integrations are delivered through its individual portfolio companies (such as Harris Local Government, Harris Utilities, Harris Healthcare, and Harris School Solutions). Harris Computer is a subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc.

providers.name: Healf
providers.description: Healf (healf.mx) is a Mexico City-based InsurTech startup founded in 2022 that offers an AI-based SaaS platform to simplify, explain, and manage medical / health insurance policies. Using generative AI, natural language processing, and information-retrieval models, the platform automates repetitive inquiries, provides 24/7 conversational support to insurance brokers, and gives the insured comprehensive insight into their policy details for better-informed decisions. For brokers and doctors it streamlines communication and automates processes, improving transparency and traceability for insurers. Healf is a 500 Global portfolio company (Somos Lucha Batch 19), also backed by Blue Zone Ventures. This profile currently has no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface.

providers.name: Health Net
providers.description: Health Net is a managed care organization offering health benefits to individuals, families, businesses, and beneficiaries of government sponsored programs. Health Net is a wholly owned subsidiary of Centene Corporation, one of the largest managed care companies in the United States.

providers.name: Huscarl
providers.description: Huscarl is an AI-native actuarial advisory firm focused on corporate self-insurance and captive insurance programs. The company provides actuarial intelligence and independent advisory for captive managers and owners, including feasibility studies for captive insurance entities, pricing and underwriting of uncommon risks with limited data, and reserve estimation and actuarial opinions. It helps large corporations determine whether they are paying the right amount for coverage and optimize their insurance strategy. Huscarl was founded by Alex Musy (CEO) and Paulien Jeunesse, who previously built cyber parametric insurance at Descartes Underwriting, and is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company based in San Francisco. As a professional-services actuarial firm it currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Kettle
providers.description: Kettle is a reinsurance company that uses machine learning to model climate risk, according to the venture portfolio listings of its investors. Its focus is climate and catastrophe risk modeling applied to reinsurance underwriting. Kettle is backed by Anthemis, DCVC, Homebrew and True Ventures, and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface has been verified for this provider yet; this profile remains a stub awaiting a successful enrichment run with network access.

providers.name: LeapStack
providers.description: LeapStack (栈略数据 / Stack Strategy Data) is a Shanghai-based insurance technology and data-analytics company operating in China's health-insurance sector, applying big-data and risk-control intelligence to help insurers with claims, underwriting, and healthcare-cost analysis. It is a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and Qiming Venture Partners. Its public web presence (www.leapstack.tech) is a client-rendered marketing site; as of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or other public API surface was found. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Liazon
providers.description: Liazon was a Buffalo, New York based operator of private benefits exchanges, best known for the Bright Choices Exchange, which helped small and mid-sized employers move to a defined-contribution benefits model and let their employees shop for health, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage through an online marketplace. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Bessemer Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Towers Watson — now WTW — and no longer operates as an independent business. As of a 2026-07-19 probe, liazon.com publishes no A record and serves no website over HTTP or HTTPS, while the domain's MX records resolve to willistowerswatson-com.mail.protection.outlook.com and the registration is held through MarkMonitor, indicating WTW retains the domain defensively rather than operating a product on it. There is no Liazon developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDK, or public API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record; enrichment beyond domain-level DNS evidence is not applicable.

providers.name: Lima
providers.description: Lima launches Linux virtual machines on macOS with automatic file sharing, port forwarding, and containerd integration for running containers.

providers.name: Loews Corporation
providers.description: Loews Corporation is a diversified holding company with subsidiaries operating in commercial property and casualty insurance (CNA Financial), natural gas pipelines (Boardwalk Pipelines), packaging products (Altium Packaging), and hotels (Loews Hotels). Loews Corporation does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this index tracks the company website and consumer-facing properties for reference.

providers.name: Loews Corporation
providers.description: Loews Corporation (NYSE: L) is a diversified holding company headquartered at 9 West 57th Street, New York. Controlled by the Tisch family, the corporation pursues long-term shareholder value through four operating subsidiaries spanning insurance, energy infrastructure, hospitality, and rigid plastic packaging. The parent entity itself publishes no developer APIs, SDKs, or technical artifacts — its public surface is investor-relations, SEC filings, and press communications. This apis.yml therefore documents the parent's portfolio structure and points to each operating subsidiary for any API-bearing surface.

providers.name: Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance
providers.description: Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Company (MassMutual) is a leading mutual life insurance company providing life insurance, disability income insurance, long-term care insurance, retirement and annuity products, and investment management services. This repository is an alias for the MassMutual API Evangelist profile and tracks publicly available APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Medi Assist
providers.description: MediBuddy (Medi Assist) is a Bessemer Venture Partners-backed digital healthcare platform based in India that lets consumers and corporate health-benefit members book online doctor consultations, order lab tests and diagnostic health checkups, buy medicines, and access cashless hospitalization and insurance-linked care through a single app and website. It operates as a consumer-facing health services marketplace; at the time of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification. This profile records what could be verified from the public web surface.

providers.name: Melon Digital Insurance
providers.description: Melon is a digital-first insurance agency based in Saudi Arabia, building modern Insurtech products for individuals across the Kingdom. The company has received preliminary approval from the Saudi Insurance Authority (IA) to operate as a digital insurance agency, with final licensing pending, and is currently pre-launch ("launching soon"). Melon uses technology and AI to deliver transparent, fair pricing, simple policies, and a seamless, fully digital customer experience. It is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass, Melon publishes only a marketing landing page (melon.sa) with no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: National General Holdings
providers.description: National General Holdings was a specialty personal lines insurer offering auto, RV, motorcycle, homeowners, and accident & health coverage. Acquired by Allstate in January 2021 for approximately $4 billion and folded into Allstate as the "National General, an Allstate company" brand. No standalone developer program, public APIs, or technical portal exists; the corporate domain redirects to nationalgeneral.com which is now an Allstate-operated consumer site.

providers.name: Neqabty
providers.description: Neqabty (NeQabty / نقابتي, "my syndicate") is an Arabic-language (RTL) web and mobile application serving members of professional syndicates in Egypt, backed by 500 Global. The public surface at neqabty.com is a single-page application aimed at end users; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface. This profile is retained as a company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: New York Life
providers.description: New York Life Insurance Company is the largest mutual life insurance company in the United States, headquartered in Manhattan, New York. The company provides life insurance, fixed and variable annuities, long-term care, and investment management (through subsidiaries such as New York Life Investments / NYLIM). New York Life has maintained the highest financial-strength ratings from major rating agencies for more than a century. No public developer portal or external APIs have been identified; agent, partner, and reinsurer integrations occur through private B2B channels.

providers.name: New York Life Insurance
providers.description: New York Life Insurance Company is the largest mutual life insurance company in the United States, founded in 1845. The company provides whole, term, universal, and variable universal life insurance, long-term care and disability insurance, annuities, and asset management through New York Life Investments. Ranked #69 on the Fortune 500. No public APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Nordstrom
providers.description: Nordstrom is a leading fashion retailer offering compelling clothing, shoes, and accessories for men, women, and children through Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack stores and online. Nordstrom does not currently operate a public developer portal or expose general-purpose APIs to third-party developers; this repository captures the company profile and any future developer-facing artifacts.

providers.name: Ohio National (Acquired by Constellation Insurance / Rebranded as AuguStar)
providers.description: Ohio National Financial Services was a Cincinnati-based mutual life insurance and annuities provider, historically operating through Ohio National Mutual Holdings, Inc. (ONMH). In March 2021 Constellation Insurance Holdings announced a sponsored demutualization of ONMH and Ohio National Financial Services for total consideration of approximately US$1 billion, including member consideration and new capital. The transaction closed on March 31, 2022, after a member vote on March 11, 2022, converting ONMH to a stock company renamed Ohio National Holdings, Inc. On July 17, 2023 Constellation repositioned and rebranded Ohio National's life insurance business as AuguStar Life, with the Ohio National Life Insurance Company and Ohio National Life Assurance Corporation expected to change their names to AuguStar Life Insurance Company and AuguStar Life Assurance Corporation in Q4 2023. Constellation Insurance is owned by long-term institutional investors CDPQ (Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec) and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, and Constellation's family of insurance companies collectively held over US$34 billion in assets under management as of December 31, 2022. The product surface remains traditional life insurance, indexed life, and annuities distributed through agents and independent marketing organizations; no public developer APIs or OpenAPI specs are published.

providers.name: Ornikar
providers.description: Ornikar is a French online driving school and insurance company that guides consumers from earning their driving permit through to car, home, and pet insurance. Founded in France, it offers highway-code (code de la route) training, driving lessons, accelerated permit programs, point-recovery courses, and corporate road-safety training, alongside auto, home, and pet insurance products and CPF financing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: Consumer. No public developer API surface was found during the enrichment pass; only domain-security signals were probed.

providers.name: Pacific Life
providers.description: Pacific Life is a U.S.-based insurance company providing life insurance, annuities, mutual funds, and investment products and services to individuals, businesses, and pension plans. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: Poppins Health
providers.description: Poppins Health is a health insurance provider offering a modern health plan built for small businesses. Headquartered in Ohio, the company focuses on affordability, transparent coverage, and a better member experience for small business owners and their employees. Poppins Health is a portfolio company of the venture firm Anthemis. As of this profile, Poppins Health publishes a public marketing website but does not expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation surface for third-party integration.

providers.name: Protective Life
providers.description: Protective Life Corporation is a U.S.-based financial services holding company offering life insurance, annuities, and asset protection products through its subsidiaries. This repository tracks any APIs, SDKs, and developer-facing resources associated with Protective Life and its product lines.

providers.name: Raincoat
providers.description: Raincoat builds embedded, highly scalable parametric climate insurance products and the automated infrastructure that powers them. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Juan, Puerto Rico, the company combines real-time environmental and geospatial data with parametric risk models to automatically trigger coverage and deliver instant, direct payouts to beneficiaries after natural disasters such as hurricanes, earthquakes, floods and excess rainfall. Raincoat operates as B2B2C infrastructure, connecting insurers, reinsurers and distribution partners so they can offer embedded disaster protection across Latin America, the Caribbean, the United States and other climate-exposed markets. The company is backed by Anthemis and Two Sigma Ventures. Raincoat publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time; integration is handled directly through partnership.

providers.name: Raven Risk AI
providers.description: Raven Risk AI is an AI platform for credit managers and investment professionals that automates credit analysis workflows — financial data analysis, due diligence, risk assessment, and report generation — to help teams assess and monitor investments with greater speed and precision. Founded in 2023 by Blair Fleming and based in Manhattan, New York, the company is backed by 500 Global. The platform integrates internal and external data sources, applies fine-tuned AI models for credit assessment, and supports deal tracking and firm knowledge management. No public API, developer portal, or documentation is currently published; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network lead pending an eventual developer surface.

providers.name: Rote
providers.description: Rote is an AI-native insurance department for auto body shops, backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2027 batch). The platform uses AI agents to handle the entire negotiation lifecycle between collision-repair shops and insurance carriers, autonomously filing and defending claims using technical repair data so that shops recover revenue lost to denied or undervalued estimates. Founded in San Francisco by Aditya Mittal and Gabriel Castillo, Rote is an early-stage company presenting a marketing website only; no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface has been published to date. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: ScoreData
providers.description: ScoreData Corporation is a Palo Alto based predictive-analytics and AI/ML platform company founded in 2014 by Danny Yang, Vas Bhandarkar, Mudit Chandra and Prasanta Behera. Its flagship ScoreFast platform, paired with iMaaS (intelligent Models as a Service), lets cross-functional AI teams develop, deploy, monitor, manage and govern machine-learning models in production across Banking, Insurance and Healthcare. ScoreFast uses patented dynamic machine learning that learns continuously, removing the need to manually regenerate predictive models, and its applications can be deployed across in-store, mobile, web, kiosk, chatbot and cloud contact-center touchpoints. ScoreData is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company awaiting a public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Singulate
providers.description: Singulate is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Stable
providers.description: Stable is an insurtech company that provides price risk management and price insurance for agricultural and food commodities, helping farmers, food producers, buyers, and businesses hedge against the volatility of commodity prices. Backed by Anthemis and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub, Stable operates a price-stabilization platform rather than a public developer API surface.

providers.name: The Zebra
providers.description: The Zebra is an Austin, Texas based consumer insurance comparison marketplace that lets people compare car, home, renters, and life insurance quotes from many carriers in one place. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. Sector: consumer. Enrichment (2026-07-21) found no public developer or API surface: no api./developer./developers./partners. subdomains resolve, the public site sits behind a WAF, and docs.thezebra.com is an internal Google Workspace redirect rather than API docs.

providers.name: True Link
providers.description: True Link Financial provides financial management tools for people with complex needs and their caregivers. Its offerings include the True Link Visa prepaid card with caregiver-configurable spending controls and transaction monitoring, investment and trust administration for representative payees, fiduciaries, guardians and non-profit trustees, white-label family banking for financial institutions, and AI-powered merchant fraud prevention (Retina AI). The company reports serving more than 250,000 families. No public developer API or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Vontier
providers.description: Vontier is a global mobility technology company serving convenience stores, fleet operators, and auto repair shops. Its portfolio spans traditional fueling, alternative energy (EV, CNG, RNG), repair tools, and car-wash technology through brands including Gilbarco, DRB, Driivz, Matco Tools, Teletrac Navman, ANGI Energy, and Invenco.

providers.name: Wagmo
providers.description: Wagmo is a modern pet healthcare company offering three consumer products: Wagmo Wellness (a reimbursement plan covering routine and preventative care such as wellness visits, vaccines, dental cleanings, grooming, and supplements), Wagmo Insurance (accident-and-illness pet insurance for cats and dogs), and VETalk (24/7 virtual televet consultations).
