Wagmo also distributes its wellness and insurance products as an employee benefit through HR teams and brokers, and partners with pet brands. The company is a Techstars portfolio company. It operates as a direct-to-consumer and B2B2C brand and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Wayco
providers.description: Wayco (Wayco AI, Inc.) is a Y Combinator (W26) startup building an AI operator for medical-legal cases. Its platform automates personal-injury and mass-tort case workflows end to end: AI voice agents answer and triage intake calls, match patients to medical providers by case type and location, coordinate telemedicine, summarize and analyze medical records at scale, and manage lead follow-up from first intake toward settlement. Founded by Iqbol Temirkhojaev and based in New York City, the company serves law firms, medical-billing, and insurance-claims teams. As of July 2026 Wayco is early stage and publishes a marketing site (wayco.ai) only, with no public developer API, documentation, or machine-readable specifications yet.

providers.name: Webfinanceholding
providers.description: Web Finance Holding AD is a Bulgarian financial-services holding company established in 2002 (formerly Finance Consulting AD). It specializes in the consultation and management of debt portfolios, acquisition of receivables, collection risk management, restructuring, and the management of enterprises in liquidation, and holds stakes across insurance, banking, and leasing subsidiaries including Saglasie Insurance, Texim Bank, and BM Leasing. The public web presence is a corporate and investor-relations site; no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: Willing
providers.description: Willing was an online estate-planning and will-making platform (a 500 Global portfolio company) that let consumers create wills, living wills, and related documents. The brand has since been absorbed into MetLife Legal Plans; as of this enrichment pass willing.com live-redirects (HTTP 302) to legalplans.com. Willing publishes no independent public API, developer portal, or GitHub organization of its own, so it carries no API artifacts beyond a domain-security probe of the surviving willing.com host.

providers.name: Yuanbao (元保)
providers.description: Yuanbao Inc. (元保) is a technology-driven online insurance distribution platform in China, founded in 2019 and listed on NASDAQ under the ticker YB. It distributes medical, critical illness, accident, property, and pet insurance products directly to consumers and provides system services to partnered insurance carriers, embedding proprietary large language models into core functions including risk identification, customer acquisition, product design, personalized recommendation, policy management, and claims processing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, Yuanbao operates a consumer-facing web and mobile experience (yuanbaobaoxian.com, redirecting to yuanbaobaoxian.cn) and does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or open API platform at this time.

providers.name: yuanxinjituan
providers.description: Yuanxinjituan (Beijing Yuanxin Technology Group Co., Ltd. / 圆心科技集团) is a Chinese healthcare-technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Beijing, dedicated to delivering value across the full patient care cycle. It operates an integrated online-and-offline platform spanning three core scenarios — medical consultation, medication, and payment — connecting doctors, patients, pharmaceutical companies, and insurers. Its businesses include the Miaoshou (妙手) internet hospital, hospital-side and DTP pharmacies (圆心药房), a prescription-sharing platform, pharmaceutical distribution, and the Yuanxin health-insurance arm (圆心惠保). Backed by Tencent, Sequoia China, and Qiming Venture Partners, Yuanxin is one of China's largest full-chain service providers for the commercialization of innovative drugs and has pursued a Hong Kong Stock Exchange main-board listing. The company presents a consumer/enterprise healthcare surface; no public developer API, open platform, or documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Aepona
providers.description: Aepona was a telecommunications software company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Belfast, Northern Ireland, with additional offices in Dublin, the United States, and Sri Lanka. Its Network-as-a-Service platform let mobile network operators and cloud service providers expose carrier network capabilities — messaging, voice, location, identity, and carrier billing — to third-party developers through common-language REST APIs, and merchandize them through multi-sided business models. Backed by Amadeus Capital Partners and Sapphire Ventures, Aepona was acquired by Intel in April 2013 for approximately $124 million and folded into Intel's software and services group alongside the Mashery API-management acquisition. The company is no longer operating independently and its developer surface is defunct; this profile is retained as a historical record within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Alcatel-lucent
providers.description: Alcatel-Lucent was a French-American telecommunications equipment company formed in 2006 from the merger of Alcatel (France) and Lucent Technologies (USA, the former Bell Labs / AT&T systems business). It supplied fixed, mobile, and converged broadband networking hardware, IP routing, optical transport, and communications services to carriers and enterprises worldwide. Nokia acquired Alcatel-Lucent in 2016 and its product lines and Bell Labs research arm were absorbed into Nokia; the standalone brand and developer surface have since been retired. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio lead and is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network; no independent public API developer portal is currently operated under the alcatel-lucent.com domain.

providers.name: Allergan
providers.description: Allergan was a global pharmaceutical company that developed, manufactured, and commercialized branded therapeutics, devices, and biologic products across medical aesthetics, eye care, central nervous system, and gastroenterology. The company was the maker of Botox (botulinum toxin), Juvederm (injectable filler), CoolSculpting, Alphagan, Vraylar, Linzess, and Ubrelvy. AbbVie completed its $63 billion acquisition of Allergan in May 2020. The company now operates as Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company. Allergan Data Labs, the digital innovation arm, built the Alle loyalty platform serving over 3 million users across nearly 20,000 medical offices and spas in the US, using machine learning for personalized consumer engagement in medical aesthetics. Allergan Aesthetics does not maintain a public developer API program.

providers.name: Alpha Technologies
providers.description: Alpha Technologies is a power-systems manufacturer providing AC, DC, and renewable powering solutions for the telecom, cable-broadband, traffic, security, industrial, and alternative-energy industries. Its product line spans uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), standby and non-standby power systems, batteries, enclosures, network/fiber powering gear, and renewable-energy products. Founded in the 1980s and now part of EnerSys, Alpha operates as a hardware and stored-energy solutions provider rather than a public API platform; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel-associated portfolio lead and carries no public developer or API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Altruist (iConnectiva)
providers.description: iConnectiva (Connectiva Analytics and Insights Ltd), part of Altruist Technologies Pvt. Ltd., is a telecom analytics product and services company focused on subscriber-data monetization. Its RAFMS platform delivers Revenue Assurance and Fraud Management to telecom, media and utility operators, alongside Big Data analytics to lower churn, boost ARPU and reduce revenue leakage. iConnectiva reports managing 350+ million subscribers for Revenue Assurance and Fraud Management, handling 500+ million customers, processing 15+ billion CDR/day, a repository of 400+ KPIs across RA and FMS, and 1000+ adaptors, delivered through advisory, tool-based and managed services. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface is published.

providers.name: American Tower
providers.description: American Tower Corporation is one of the largest global REITs and a leading independent owner, operator, and developer of multitenant communications real estate. The company owns and operates approximately 225,000 communications sites globally, providing tower space and related services to wireless carriers and broadcasters across the United States, Latin America, Europe, Africa, India, and Asia-Pacific. American Tower enables wireless communications networks by leasing antenna space on its towers to mobile network operators.

providers.name: Amphiform
providers.description: Amphiform is an energy technology company redefining the future of energy by developing new materials and manufacturing processes that create clean, abundant, and dense energy sources. Rather than scaling existing technologies, Amphiform engineers entirely new materials using precise manufacturing tools to address energy demands for decarbonization, computing, and space exploration. A General Catalyst portfolio company in the energy-infrastructure sector, it is pre-product and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Arcturus
providers.description: Arcturus (Arcturus Technologies) is a Los Angeles advanced-materials company founded by Amir Mashal that infuses carbon nanomaterials into metals to create a new class of conductors, using lasers to embed carbon into copper and dramatically improve its electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance. Positioned in frontier climate/energy tech, its drop-in materials target motor windings, bus bars, heat sinks, data-center infrastructure, electric motors, drones, robotics, and — over time — transmission lines and grid infrastructure. The company emerged from stealth in June 2026 with an $8M seed round led by Initialized Capital, with 1517, Breakthrough Energy Discovery, Toyota Ventures, and Wireframe Ventures participating. This is a deep-tech hardware/materials company with no public API or developer program; the profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Azuria
providers.description: The website wired to this profile (azuria.com) resolves to Azuria Water Solutions, an infrastructure-rehabilitation company that has operated for over 50 years in the water, wastewater, and stormwater sector. It renews aging pipeline infrastructure through cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) technology, water main renewal, cathodic protection, and spray-on lining, operating through brands including Insituform, Underground Solutions, MTC, and Corrpro. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface: it is not an API provider. NOTE: this stub was surfaced as a norwest-venture-partners portfolio lead, but that linkage is unverified — Norwest's public portfolio does not list an "Azuria", and this water-infrastructure company may be a different entity than the intended Norwest-backed one.

providers.name: Blueprint Power
providers.description: Blueprint Power was a New York City software company, founded in 2017 by Robyn Beavers, that turned commercial real estate portfolios into virtual power plants. Its cloud platform connected to distributed energy assets in buildings — solar, batteries, cogeneration — and used data-driven and machine-learning models to aggregate, orchestrate and transact that surplus capacity into wholesale energy markets. It raised a $3.5M Series A (Congruent Ventures, MetaProp, Fifth Wall, Fred Wilson, Brad Burnham) and was acquired by bp in October 2021, joining the bp Launchpad portfolio. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no independent public surface: www.blueprintpower.com returns a 301 permanent redirect to bp.com/retailenergy, and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or public GitHub organization could be found. Retained in the network as an acquired-company record with no API surface.

providers.name: CDI Corp
providers.description: CDI Corp (CDI Corporation) is a multidisciplinary engineering and technical resourcing firm founded in Philadelphia in 1950 as Comprehensive Designers, Inc., later listed on the NYSE from 1988 to 2017. After being taken private by AE Industrial Partners in September 2017 for approximately $176M ($8.25 per share), AE divested CDI's aerospace business to Belcan (2017), talent and technology services to Artech (2018), and architecture/engineering subsidiary L.R. Kimball to TranSystems (2021), refocusing the remaining CDI Engineering Solutions on integrated engineering, design, project support, procurement, and construction management for the energy and chemicals industries. On January 1, 2025 CDI Engineering Solutions, LLC became a wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Consulting Engineers and now trades as Tata Consulting Engineers USA, LLC, headquartered in Houston, TX with 650+ employees across ten engineering centers. CDI Corp has no public developer APIs; the company delivers engineering services and staff augmentation rather than software products. The tagline carried by the operating business is "Quality Results. Sustainable Solutions. Safely Delivered."

providers.name: Cedar Point Communications
providers.description: Cedar Point Communications, Inc. is a telecommunications software company that enables cable, wireline, and wireless operators to simplify the cost-effective delivery of VoIP and multimedia services. Its flagship SAFARI C3 is an integrated switching platform supporting up to 250,000 voice lines, complemented by the SafariView management tool and the SafariFusion suite (Application Platform, Residential Communication Application, Registration Routing Application, and Visual Communications Suite). Cedar Point Communications became a subsidiary of GENBAND following its 2010 acquisition. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications were found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: Chariot Defense
providers.description: Chariot Defense is a San Francisco-area defense technology company building high-voltage, hybrid-electric power systems for the modern battlefield. Its AMPHORA family (the 24 VDC / 5 kW A24 and the 400 VDC / 35 kW A400) and the upcoming VANGUARD platform deliver quiet, high-density, transportable power that replaces loud, fuel-hungry diesel generators, cutting energy signature and fuel use while powering distributed systems such as drones, sensors, electronic warfare, command and control, additive manufacturing, and directed-energy weapons. Founded in 2022 by Adam Warmoth, the company has raised $41M (a $34M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz plus an $8M seed) and its systems are fielded by the U.S. Army and the Defense Innovation Unit. This is a hardware/defense company profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Chesapeake Energy
providers.description: Chesapeake Energy Corporation was an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, focused on unconventional natural gas and oil fields onshore in the United States. In October 2024, Chesapeake combined with Southwestern Energy to form Expand Energy Corporation, which now operates as the largest natural gas producer in the United States. Chesapeake Energy does not currently expose a public developer API; royalty owners and partners interact through the Owner Online Accounts portal, and investors are served via the Expand Energy investor relations site.

providers.name: Chevron
providers.description: Chevron Corporation is one of the world's largest integrated energy companies, with operations across upstream exploration and production, downstream refining and marketing, and the production and transportation of crude oil, natural gas, refined fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals, and renewable fuels. Chevron is headquartered in Houston, Texas, and operates globally under brands including Chevron, Texaco, and Caltex. Chevron does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; supplier and partner integrations are handled through the Chevron Invoice and Payment Status (CIPS) system and the Supplier Relations channels, and investors and stakeholders are served through corporate, sustainability, and IR websites.

providers.name: cordproject
providers.description: Cord Project Inc. was a New York based startup founded around 2014 by former Google Creative Lab designers Thomas Gayno and Jeff Baxter. Its flagship product, Cord, was a voice messaging app that let people send short audio clips as a middle ground between texting and phone calls. The company raised seed funding from investors including Google Ventures, Greycroft, Lerer Hippeau, Metamorphic Ventures and Slow Ventures, and was acquired by Spotify in January 2016 to explore new ways of interacting with audio. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation; this profile is retained as a Slow Ventures portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Crestwood Equity Partners
providers.description: Crestwood Equity Partners LP was a master limited partnership that owned and operated midstream energy assets across the United States, including natural gas, NGL, and crude oil gathering, processing, storage, and transportation businesses. Crestwood was acquired by Energy Transfer LP in November 2023, with Crestwood common and preferred units ceasing trading on the NYSE on November 3, 2023; ongoing operations and partner contracts have been integrated into Energy Transfer's pipeline and midstream network. Crestwood does not publish a public developer API program; technical interfaces such as nominations, scheduling, and capacity portals are now handled through Energy Transfer's commercial systems.

providers.name: DCP Midstream Partners
providers.description: DCP Midstream Partners is a midstream energy company that gathers, processes, transports, stores, and markets natural gas and natural gas liquids (NGLs) across major U.S. producing regions. Following Phillips 66's acquisition of the remaining public units in 2023, DCP Midstream now operates as part of Phillips 66's midstream segment. The company does not publish a public developer API; integration with shippers and customers is handled through customer portals (tariffs, electronic flow measurement) rather than a self-service API.

providers.name: Dominion Energy
providers.description: Dominion Energy is one of the nation's largest producers and transporters of energy, providing electricity and natural gas to customers across multiple U.S. states including Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, and Utah. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Dominion Resources
providers.description: Dominion Resources is the former name of Dominion Energy, one of the nation's largest producers and transporters of energy, providing electricity and natural gas to customers across multiple U.S. states. The company rebranded from Dominion Resources to Dominion Energy in 2017. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Ecovate
providers.description: Ecovate (Ecovate Energy Indices) is an Israeli energy-data company that operates a platform for the wholesale electricity market price index. It publishes benchmark indices and analytics tracking wholesale electricity market prices, giving energy suppliers, large consumers, traders, and regulators a transparent reference for the cost of electricity in the wholesale market. Ecovate was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. The company's public presence is a marketing/product site (Hebrew and English editions) and it does not currently publish a developer program, public API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Edviro
providers.description: Edviro is an AI platform for building operations and energy optimization, aimed at facility managers and building operators of large commercial buildings. It pulls scattered building data - utility bills, smart meters, building management systems (BMS), submeters, sensors, and work-order platforms - into one place, then follows an Ingest, Detect, Act, and Verify workflow: it consolidates the data, catches energy waste and anomalies in real time, dispatches work orders and adjusts setpoints, and proves the resulting savings against meter data and utility bills. The platform also builds a digital twin of each building to simulate capital projects and forecast ROI before purchase, and produces audit-grade Measurement and Verification (M&V) reporting. Edviro is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Electroflow
providers.description: Electroflow Technologies is a United States deep-tech company (founded 2023, headquartered in San Bruno, California) developing an electrochemical direct lithium extraction (DLE) process that pulls lithium from dilute North American brines containing under 200ppm lithium using renewable electricity and minimal chemicals. Its cell uses anodes that absorb lithium ions from brine on one pass and release them into a carbonate solution on the reverse pass, producing battery-grade lithium carbonate that is reacted with iron and phosphate to make lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode powder domestically — a three-step route versus the traditional ten-step process, targeting LFP material at roughly 40% below Chinese producers. The company raised a $10M seed round in October 2025 led by Union Square Ventures with Voyager Ventures, Fifty Years, and Harpoon Ventures, and counts Breakthrough Energy among its backers. Electroflow is a hardware and battery-materials company; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Eli Lilly
providers.description: Eli Lilly and Company is a Fortune 500 global pharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells human pharmaceutical products in therapeutic areas including diabetes, oncology, immunology, and neuroscience. Eli Lilly does not currently publish a public developer API portal; the company exposes selected machine learning models through its Lilly TuneLab platform to partner biotechs but does not offer general purpose, self-serve APIs.

providers.name: Enbala
providers.description: Enbala Power Networks was a distributed-energy-resource (DER) and grid-flexibility software company (Concerto DER management platform). It was surfaced as an obvious-ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass the company has no live public developer or API presence. enbala.com serves an expired TLS certificate and 301-redirects to www.generacgs.com (Generac Grid Services), which no longer resolves in DNS. No OpenAPI, docs host, developer portal, SDK, MCP server, or webhook surface could be located. Treat this profile as a defunct/acquired lead rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Endurance Energy
providers.description: Endurance Energy is a renewable-energy developer building subsea geothermal power systems that harness volcanic activity beneath the seafloor to generate continuous, weather-independent electricity. Its first product, Adelie, is a planned 100 kW subsea power system slated for deployment in September 2026 at the Axial Seamount caldera off the Oregon coast, targeting island nations, industrial facilities, and data centers that need firm baseload power. The company is venture-backed (a Series A led by Founders Fund) and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Felicis portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public developer surface, API, SDK, or documentation; this entry captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: EnerSys
providers.description: EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial applications, manufacturing batteries, chargers, accessories, and outdoor equipment enclosures. EnerSys serves motive power, reserve power, aerospace and defense, and specialty markets. While EnerSys offers a number of customer-facing web tools (Battery Sizing Program, Motive Power configurator, CARB Compliance Calculator) and product-level telemetry such as the Wi-iQ battery monitoring system and NexSys iON connected fleet platform, no public developer APIs or open specifications have been published as of this index.

providers.name: Enghouse
providers.description: Enghouse Systems Limited (TSX: ENGH) is a publicly traded Canadian enterprise software and services company headquartered in Markham, Ontario and founded in 1984. It builds mission-critical, communications-focused software delivered on-premise and via the cloud, organized into two segments: the Interactive Management Group (Enghouse Interactive — omnichannel contact centre, customer experience, IVR, video collaboration and AI-assisted agent tooling) and the Asset Management Group (Enghouse Networks — telecom OSS/BSS, media and broadcast, and network monitoring; plus transportation, public-safety and transit systems). The company grows largely through acquisition of specialized software brands.

providers.name: ENGIE Insight Services
providers.description: ENGIE Insight Services (formerly Ecova, now operating as ENGIE Impact) is a sustainability and resource-management company that helps corporations, cities, and governments reduce their environmental footprint and operating costs. It provides energy, water, and waste expense management, utility bill auditing and payment, data management, sustainability consulting, and decarbonization strategy across a large portfolio of client sites. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, this profile has been enriched with domain-security and discovery probes; the company publishes no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Envision Energy
providers.description: Envision Energy is a Chinese green-technology company founded in 2007 by Lei Zhang and headquartered in Shanghai. It designs and manufactures smart wind turbines, operates one of the world's largest fleets of connected wind and solar assets, and builds net-zero industrial parks. Its business spans energy storage and batteries (through Envision AESC), green hydrogen and green ammonia, and the EnOS AIoT operating system delivered by its Envision Digital arm, which connects and manages energy and IoT devices at scale. Envision was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (formerly Sequoia China) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; its public digital surface is a marketing site and the EnOS platform, which is documented on region-restricted hosts not reachable for spec discovery in this pass.

providers.name: EP Energy
providers.description: EP Energy Corporation was an independent exploration and production company engaged in the acquisition and development of unconventional onshore oil and natural gas properties in the United States. EP Energy filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2019 and emerged in October 2020, with assets later acquired by IKAV in March 2022. The company does not maintain any public APIs, SDKs, or developer resources.

providers.name: EQT Corporation
providers.description: EQT Corporation is the largest producer of natural gas in the United States, headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. EQT operates in the Appalachian Basin and combines exploration and production technology with environmental stewardship initiatives, including a Scope 1 and Scope 2 net-zero commitment. EQT does not maintain a public developer program or open APIs; data access is limited to investor relations, ESG reporting, and partner-facing portals such as Equitrans Midstream customer services.

providers.name: FaxSav
providers.description: FaxSav Incorporated was an Edison, New Jersey internet-fax company that designed, developed and marketed store-and-forward and real-time fax transmission services over a hybrid telephony and Internet network, letting customers bypass international long-distance rates. Its products included the faxLauncher Windows desktop client, the faxMailer email-to-fax service built on the company's patented e-mail security technology, and Serverlink, a partner integration that let third-party fax software and application developers route documents through the FaxSav Network. FaxSav went public in 1996, renamed itself NetMoves Corporation in February 1999, and was acquired by Mail.com, Inc. in early 2000; Mail.com became EasyLink Services Corporation in 2001 and the business was acquired by OpenText in 2012. The company is defunct and operates no API, developer program, or public developer portal today. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: FlexEngage
providers.description: FlexEngage is a retail customer-engagement company that powered transactional and triggered customer communications for retailers and brands, including digital receipts, order and shipping notifications, and omnichannel messaging across email, SMS, and print. The company was backed by Bullpen Capital and was acquired by Narvar in 2019. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the Bullpen Capital portfolio; the public site (www.flexengage.com) is currently served behind CloudFront and returns HTTP 403 to automated clients, so no public developer/API surface could be captured during enrichment.

providers.name: Fourth Power
providers.description: Fourth Power is a grid-scale thermal energy storage company building a "thermal battery" that stores electricity as heat. Surplus wind and solar power is used to heat blocks of graphite to roughly 2,400 degrees Celsius; molten tin, circulated by an all-ceramic pump, moves that heat in and out of storage, and thermophotovoltaic (TPV) cells convert the stored heat back into electricity when the grid needs it. The company positions the system as a cheaper, longer-duration alternative to lithium-ion for firming a clean grid, and operates a megawatt-scale demonstration facility near Boston. Fourth Power raised a Series A led by DCVC in 2023. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Fourth Power is a hardware and energy company and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Greenchoice
providers.description: Greenchoice is a Dutch energy supplier focused on green electricity and gas, offering renewable energy contracts, solar panels, heat pumps, and EV charging services to consumers and businesses in the Netherlands.

providers.name: Gtctowers
providers.description: GTC Towers is a telecommunications infrastructure company based in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida, positioning itself as a customer-focused tower owner built by a team of wireless industry veterans. It develops and operates digital connectivity infrastructure including cell towers, small cells, and in-building wireless systems, alongside tower operations management, tower safety services, and Eco Power Wheels power solutions. GTC Towers leases tower space and supports carriers and enterprises through the various stages of tower siting, deployment, and growth. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate marketing website only, with no developer portal, API, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: GTS Central Europe
providers.description: GTS Central Europe, operating in Romania as GTS Telecom (a member of Deutsche Telekom AG since 1993), is an IT&C service provider delivering cloud solutions (virtual hosting, private cloud, VPS, dedicated storage), cyber security (DDoS mitigation, firewalls, endpoint protection, backup and disaster recovery), connectivity (internet access, IP transit, leased lines, Ethernet VPN, dark fiber, DWDM), unified communications, managed services (LAN, server, network security, Wi-Fi), physical security systems, and IT hardware/software. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Hawaiian Electric Industries
providers.description: Hawaiian Electric Industries (HEI) is a Hawaii-based holding company whose primary subsidiaries provide electric utility service to roughly 95% of Hawaii's residents through Hawaiian Electric, and clean-energy investments through Pacific Current. HEI does not publish public developer APIs at this time; this index tracks the company and its subsidiaries for API discovery purposes.

providers.name: Hess Corporation
providers.description: Hess Corporation was an independent global energy company engaged in the exploration, development, production, transportation, purchase, and sale of crude oil, natural gas liquids, and natural gas. Its core operations centered on onshore unconventional production in the Bakken Shale of North Dakota and a major offshore position in the Stabroek Block in Guyana, with additional interests in the Gulf of Mexico, Canada, and Southeast Asia. Chevron Corporation completed its $53 billion all-stock acquisition of Hess on July 18, 2025, after a regulatory and arbitration delay that included a Federal Trade Commission consent order barring former CEO John B. Hess from serving on Chevron's board and a parallel ExxonMobil/CNOOC arbitration over Guyana right-of-first-refusal claims. Hess is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of Chevron, and the ONE GUYANA FPSO at Stabroek has come online to produce approximately 250,000 barrels of oil per day. Hess Corporation has never offered public developer APIs; its technology integrations were handled through enterprise partner systems and joint-venture operator portals.

providers.name: HF Sinclair
providers.description: HF Sinclair is an independent energy company that produces and markets gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, specialty lubricant products, and renewable diesel fuel through refineries and a brand network of branded fuel stations.

providers.name: Hotmail
providers.description: Hotmail was one of the first free web-based email services, launched in 1996 by Sabeer Bhatia and Jack Smith and among the earliest venture-backed consumer web companies (funded by Draper Fisher Jurvetson and Menlo Ventures). Microsoft acquired Hotmail in December 1997 and operated it as MSN Hotmail and later Windows Live Hotmail. In 2013 Microsoft folded Hotmail into Outlook.com; hotmail.com mailboxes remain fully active but are served by Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 infrastructure. Hotmail exists today only as a legacy consumer email brand and domain, with no standalone developer program. Programmatic access to hotmail.com mailboxes is provided through Microsoft Graph (Outlook Mail) and the standard IMAP, POP, and SMTP protocols, not a dedicated Hotmail API.

providers.name: Icahn Enterprises
providers.description: Icahn Enterprises L.P. is a diversified holding company engaged in the investment, energy, automotive, food packaging, real estate, home fashion, and pharmaceutical industries through its operating subsidiaries. The company does not currently publish public developer APIs; investor relations, SEC filings, and corporate communications are provided through its corporate website.

providers.name: IHS
providers.description: IHS was a global information and analytics company providing critical insight to customers across industries including aerospace, defense, automotive, chemicals, energy, and financial services. IHS merged with Markit in 2016 to form IHS Markit, which was subsequently acquired by S&P Global in 2022. The legacy ihs.com domain now redirects to S&P Global. No public IHS-branded APIs are tracked here; current API offerings live within S&P Global product lines.

providers.name: Infocast
providers.description: Infocast is an event management company (acquired by Clarion Events in 2024) that has produced premier deal-making conferences and summits for more than 35 years across energy, finance, infrastructure, manufacturing, and emerging technology sectors. Infocast does not currently publish a public API.

providers.name: Lansing Trade Group
providers.description: Lansing Trade Group was an international merchandiser, marketer, and logistics company specializing in bulk commodities including grains, biofuels, and energy products. In 2022, The Andersons completed the acquisition of Lansing Trade Group; its commodities business now operates as part of The Andersons' Trade Group.

providers.name: Level 3 Communications
providers.description: Level 3 Communications was a multinational telecommunications and Internet service provider that operated one of the largest fiber networks in the world, delivering Tier-1 IP transit, managed services, and content delivery. In 2017 it was acquired by CenturyLink, which later rebranded the combined company as Lumen Technologies. No public API program is documented under the legacy Level 3 brand.

providers.name: Liberty Energy
providers.description: Liberty Energy Inc (NYSE: LBRT), formerly Liberty Oilfield Services, is a Denver-based energy services company. It is one of the largest providers of completion services (hydraulic fracturing, wireline, sand and logistics) to onshore oil, natural gas, and enhanced geothermal producers in North America, and it is rapidly pivoting into distributed power generation for data centers and AI infrastructure via its Liberty Power Innovations (LPI) subsidiary. Founded in 2011 by Chris Wright, who left in 2025 to become the 17th US Secretary of Energy under the Trump administration. Ron Gusek is now President and CEO. The company does not publish any public developer APIs; this profile documents the organization, its proprietary internal platforms (FracTrends, Sentinel, digiTechnologies), and the Liberty Power data center pivot.

providers.name: Linear Labs
providers.description: Linear Labs is an industrial motor technology company headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, building high-torque motor systems for wind, nuclear, pumps, actuators, mining, and defense applications. Its patented Hunstable Electric Turbine (HET) permanent-magnet architecture uses a circumferential flux design the company states delivers 2x torque density, 97% peak efficiency, and 50% weight reduction versus conventional motors, scaling from 10 kW to 2.2 MW. Its PitchPro 2000 is a complete pitch-system replacement for aging GE 1.5 wind turbines, pairing the HET motor with KEBA drive electronics, a Bachmann PLC controller, and ultracapacitor backup power. Linear Labs is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable technical surface; this profile is maintained for network coverage and identity only.

providers.name: Marathon Petroleum
providers.description: Marathon Petroleum is one of the largest petroleum product refiners, transporters, and marketers in the United States, with operations including refineries, pipelines, terminals, and retail outlets. No public developer APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Marianaminerals
providers.description: Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated critical-minerals company supplying the metals essential to modern energy, artificial intelligence, and defense technologies. The company currently develops copper and lithium production projects, with plans spanning cobalt, aluminum, graphite, uranium, and rare earth metals, and is headquartered in San Francisco with an engineering office in Houston. Backed by Khosla Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; an enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: MarkWest Energy Partners
providers.description: MarkWest Energy Partners was a master limited partnership engaged in the gathering, processing, and transportation of natural gas and natural gas liquids. The company was acquired by MPLX in 2015 and its operations have since been consolidated under the MPLX brand. No public developer APIs are offered under the MarkWest Energy Partners name.

providers.name: Meta Platforms
providers.description: Meta Platforms is a multinational technology conglomerate that builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses, including Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, and Reality Labs.

providers.name: National Oilwell Varco
providers.description: National Oilwell Varco (NOV) is a global provider of equipment, technology, and services for the oil and gas drilling industry. NOV designs and manufactures rigs, drilling tools, downhole equipment, and provides digital solutions for drilling operations worldwide.

providers.name: National Security Agency
providers.description: The National Security Agency (NSA) is a U.S. intelligence agency responsible for global monitoring, collection, and processing of information and data for foreign intelligence and counterintelligence purposes.

providers.name: Nerviom
providers.description: Nerviom is a Y Combinator-backed startup building AI workflows for infrastructure site predevelopment. Its platform deploys AI-assisted workflows tailored to each stage of predevelopment across data centers, energy, manufacturing, telecom, commercial, and mining sites — helping teams surface permitting, zoning, compliance, and interconnection risks earlier, make repeatable execution processes that do not scale linearly with headcount, and consolidate scattered PDFs, portals, and spreadsheets into a single operating view. Nerviom is an early-stage company; it currently publishes a marketing and demo-booking site and does not yet expose a public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: New Jersey Resources
providers.description: New Jersey Resources (NJR) is a Fortune 1000 energy services holding company that provides natural gas distribution through New Jersey Natural Gas, retail energy services, midstream assets, and clean energy investments. No public APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: NextEra Energy
providers.description: NextEra Energy, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American energy company and one of the largest electric utility holding companies in the United States. It is the world's largest generator of renewable energy from the wind and sun, and a world leader in battery storage. NextEra Energy operates principally through its two subsidiaries, Florida Power & Light (FPL) and NextEra Energy Resources. This repository captures the public-facing digital surface, corporate touchpoints, and any developer or data resources for NextEra Energy. No public REST APIs, developer portal, or machine-readable data feeds have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Niko
providers.description: Niko (Niko Energy) is a Mexican clean-energy company focused on energy efficiency for multi-site enterprises. It designs, installs, and finances commercial and residential solar photovoltaic systems and battery storage, wrapping them in embedded financing options that include cash purchase, 12-month interest-free plans, multi-year subscriptions, and power purchase agreements (PPAs). Its Niko Hub dashboard centralizes energy-portfolio management across locations, Niko Care provides 24/7 monitoring and maintenance, and Niko Insurance covers panel hardware. Backed by fintech venture firm QED Investors, Niko pairs solar deployment with consumption analytics and ESG / consolidated reporting. No public developer API, documentation, or specification surface was found on niko.mx as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: NPco
providers.description: NPco (NP Company) is an AI-native physics-simulation startup building AI-powered simulation for aerospace, defense, and energy engineering. Backed by Partech, it positions itself around accelerating physics simulation with AI. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing site (careers plus a contact@npco.ai address) with no public developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs surfaced. This profile remains a lead in the Industrial, Energy & IoT sector pending any future developer/API surface.

providers.name: Oklo
providers.description: Oklo Inc. is a Santa Clara, California advanced fission company designing and deploying small modular reactors under the Aurora powerhouse brand. The Aurora is a liquid-metal (sodium) cooled, metal-fueled fast reactor derived from the Experimental Breeder Reactor-II (EBR-II) lineage, engineered as a "walk-away safe" passively cooled system that is self-stabilizing and self-controlling under loss-of-coolant and loss-of-shutdown conditions. Oklo's reactors are intended to run on recycled high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel, including legacy EBR-II material, with the company building out three vertically integrated fast-reactor businesses: clean power generation, advanced nuclear fuel fabrication and recycling, and medical radioisotope production. The first commercial Aurora is targeted for operation at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in late 2027 to early 2028, supported by selection into the DOE Reactor Pilot Program and Fuel Line Pilot Projects, and the company has completed an NRC Phase 1 pre-application assessment. Oklo went public in May 2024 via merger with AltC Acquisition Corp (a SPAC co-founded by Sam Altman, who serves as chairman) and trades on the NYSE under ticker OKLO. Oklo's commercial posture is utility-scale and industrial — selling power, fuel cycle services, and isotopes to data center operators, defense customers, and industrial offtakers — and the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or open source software.

providers.name: Ola Electric
providers.description: Ola Electric is an Indian electric-vehicle manufacturer building electric scooters (the S1 family), electric motorcycles (the Roadster line), and home energy solutions (Ola Shakti battery systems), all designed and produced in India around its in-house 4680 Bharat Cell and ferrite-motor technology. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates a nationwide Hypercharger fast-charging network and Hyperservice center footprint across India. As a consumer EV and energy hardware manufacturer, Ola Electric publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API reference; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Par Pacific Holdings
providers.description: Par Pacific Holdings is an entrepreneurial liquid fuels company focused on owning and operating energy and infrastructure businesses in logistically- complex markets. The company operates refining, retail, and logistics businesses across Hawaii, Washington, Wyoming, and Montana, with retail brands including 76, Hele, and nomnom.

providers.name: PBF Energy
providers.description: PBF Energy is one of the largest independent petroleum refiners and suppliers of unbranded transportation fuels, heating oils, lubricants, petrochemical feedstocks, and other petroleum products in the United States, operating refineries and a logistics network across the country.

providers.name: Plains GP Holdings
providers.description: Plains GP Holdings owns an interest in Plains All American Pipeline, a publicly traded master limited partnership that owns and operates midstream energy infrastructure in the United States and Canada. No public developer API or developer portal has been published; this repository tracks corporate and investor resources.

providers.name: PPL
providers.description: PPL Corporation is a U.S. energy company that delivers electricity and natural gas to customers through its regulated utilities in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, and Rhode Island. PPL is a Fortune 500 company.

providers.name: Praxair
providers.description: Praxair was an American multinational industrial gases company that merged with Linde AG in 2018 to form Linde plc. Praxair operations in the United States now operate as Linde. The company supplies atmospheric, process, and specialty gases, along with related equipment and services to a range of industries.

providers.name: ProPetro Holding
providers.description: ProPetro Holding Corp (NYSE: PUMP) is a Midland, Texas-based oilfield services company that "provides hydraulic fracturing and other complementary services to leading upstream oil and gas companies engaged in the exploration and production of North American unconventional oil and natural gas resources," operating principally in the Permian Basin. Service lines include hydraulic fracturing, the FORCE electric fleet (eFleet), Silvertip Wireline, cementing, PROPWR power solutions, and Aqua Prop water management. ProPetro does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or technology developer portal.

providers.name: Pulse Space
providers.description: Pulse (Pulse - Space Power Solutions) is a Techstars-backed space technology company building power solutions for spacecraft and satellites. The company operates a WebGL marketing site at pulsespace.com and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; enrichment probing confirmed a marketing-only web presence (TLS 1.3 with HSTS) and no developer or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Quanta Services
providers.description: Quanta Services is a Fortune 500 specialty contracting company that delivers infrastructure solutions to the electric power, renewable energy, oil and gas, pipeline, and communications industries throughout North America and Australia.

providers.name: Radiant
providers.description: Radiant is a nuclear technology company developing portable, transportable microreactors designed to deliver clean, reliable power to remote sites, military installations, disaster-relief operations, and industrial locations that today depend on diesel generators. Its flagship Kaleidos reactor is a factory-built, containerized ~1 MW microreactor intended to ship by truck, plane, or ship and be operational quickly on-site. Founded by former SpaceX engineers and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Radiant is backed by DCVC and Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer program, API, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Resilient Power Systems
providers.description: Resilient Power Systems is a power-electronics hardware company known for solid-state and medium-voltage power distribution and conversion systems, including solid-state transformers for grid, EV fast-charging, and industrial applications. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass its web presence (resilientpower.com) has moved and now redirects to Eaton, following acquisition; the company publishes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or other API-consumable surface, so this profile is identity-only. Enrichment probes confirmed the redirect and captured live domain-security posture for the remaining host.

providers.name: Revvity
providers.description: Revvity is a life sciences and diagnostics company providing instruments, software, reagents, and services to support drug discovery, development, diagnostics, and applied research. Formed from the former life sciences and diagnostics businesses of PerkinElmer, Revvity serves pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical, academic, and applied markets with offerings spanning reproductive health screening, omics, imaging, and laboratory automation.

providers.name: Salient Energy
providers.description: Salient Energy is a Dartmouth, Nova Scotia based clean-energy hardware company developing zinc-ion batteries as a safer, lower-cost alternative to lithium-ion for renewable energy storage and grid applications. Its cells use a non-toxic, water-based electrolyte that eliminates fire risk, and are built from low-cost zinc and manganese materials sourced in North America, with a roughly 50% lower production carbon footprint than lithium-ion. The company positions its technology as a scalable answer to lithium supply constraints for stationary energy storage. Salient Energy manufactures physical battery hardware and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Sedona Systems
providers.description: Sedona Systems was an Israeli deep-tech networking company (multi-layer / multi-domain network optimization and hierarchical control for optical and IP transport networks) surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners. As of this enrichment pass the company no longer operates independently: its website sedonasys.com issues a permanent 301 redirect to Cisco, where the product now lives as Cisco Crosswork Hierarchical Controller. No independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface exists for Sedona Systems; there is nothing to enrich beyond domain posture. Any live API surface belongs to Cisco Crosswork and is out of scope for this profile.

providers.name: Shoretel
providers.description: ShoreTel was a Sunnyvale, California business communications company founded in 1996 that built IP-based unified communications (UC), VoIP phone systems, and contact-center products for the enterprise, spanning on-premises ShoreTel systems and the cloud-hosted ShoreTel Sky platform. Mitel Networks acquired ShoreTel in September 2017 for roughly USD 530 million and folded its products into the Mitel Connect line. ShoreTel no longer operates as an independent company: the shoretel.com domain now 301-redirects to mitel.com, and there is no independent ShoreTel developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface. Legacy integration surfaces (for example the ShoreTel Sky Hosted API and Exchange Web Services integrations) are now documented and hosted under Mitel. This record was surfaced as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company and enriched to reflect its acquired, defunct-as-independent status.

providers.name: Solactron
providers.description: Solactron, Inc. is a Silicon Valley solar technology company developing high-performance, monolithically integrated thin-film solar modules on glass substrates. Its proprietary "Thin Film 2.0" process uses a tunable compound chemistry targeting greater than 34% efficiency by capturing over 95% of the solar spectrum, aiming for the highest efficiency and lowest cost at gigawatt scale. Backed by 500 Global, Solactron is a deep-tech hardware and materials manufacturer positioned in the renewable energy and utility-scale photovoltaic market. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only (Home, Technology, Company, Careers, Contact) and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: SolarBridge Technologies
providers.description: SolarBridge Technologies was a solar power-electronics company that developed AC photovoltaic (ACPV) technology for residential and commercial solar, including its TrueAC modules, the Pantheon and Pantheon II microinverters, and the SolarBridge Management System for monitoring installed systems. The company was acquired by SunPower in 2014 and no longer operates as an independent business; its former marketing site is preserved at solarbridgetech.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. SolarBridge was a hardware and embedded-electronics company and does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Solstice
providers.description: Solstice is a community solar platform that lets households, renters, and businesses benefit from renewable energy without installing rooftop panels. Subscribers reserve a portion of a nearby solar farm and earn monthly savings on their electric bill through solar credits, while businesses can purchase community solar subscriptions and renewable energy credits (RECs). Solstice also offers subscriber-management solutions for solar developers and asset owners. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Sonantic
providers.description: Sonantic was a London-based AI voice company that built hyper-realistic, emotionally expressive text-to-speech models for entertainment, gaming, and film. The company is best known for recreating Val Kilmer's voice for Top Gun: Maverick after he lost his speaking voice to throat cancer. Spotify acquired Sonantic in June 2022 for a reported 93 million euros, and the underlying TTS technology has since been folded into Spotify products, most visibly the Spotify AI DJ feature launched in 2023. As of 2026, Sonantic no longer operates as a standalone product or public API. This apis.yml entry exists as a historical and archival record of the company, its technology, and its acquisition.

providers.name: SparkCharge
providers.description: SparkCharge operates one of the world's largest off-grid and mobile EV charging networks, delivering on-demand electric vehicle charging to commercial and fleet operators without fixed grid infrastructure. Its offerings span mobile battery-based charging dispatched by technicians, portable off-grid power hubs, and permanent charging installations, serving delivery, rideshare, automotive, ports, and event customers. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Spectra Energy
providers.description: Spectra Energy was a Fortune 500 American energy company headquartered in Houston, Texas, focused on natural gas transmission and storage, distribution, and gathering and processing. Founded in 2007 as a spin-off from Duke Energy, Spectra Energy operated the Texas Eastern Pipeline and other major North American natural gas infrastructure. In February 2017, Spectra Energy was acquired by Enbridge Inc. in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $28 billion and no longer operates as an independent entity.

providers.name: Superior Energy Services
providers.description: Superior Energy Services is a leading provider of specialized oilfield services and equipment for oil and gas exploration, production, and well services. The company operates a portfolio of global brands providing drilling equipment rentals, completion tools, well intervention, and production services across 47 countries. Superior leverages digital transformation technologies including SAP, Azure, and field data platforms to deliver integrated wellbore technology and wellsite solutions.

providers.name: Terranox AI
providers.description: Terranox AI is the first vertically integrated, AI-powered uranium discovery company, founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch. The company finds high-grade uranium deposits in North America by training machine learning models on more than seventy years of exploration outcomes locked in thousands of legacy PDFs, drill logs, and hand-drawn geological maps. Traditional uranium exploration has a hit rate below one percent and timelines measured in decades; Terranox aims to raise that hit rate and compress discovery time to help supply the fuel a global nuclear-energy resurgence needs — the world must roughly quadruple uranium production by 2050. Terranox is a private operating company focused on geoscience and mineral exploration and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. It is backed by General Catalyst, 776 Ventures, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Traffix
providers.description: Traffix Systems was an Israeli 4G network-signaling company, founded in 2005, that offered Diameter signaling products (routing, load balancing, and gateway functions) for telecommunications service providers. Bessemer Venture Partners partnered with the company in 2011, and in 2012 Traffix was acquired by F5 Networks, which absorbed its Diameter signaling technology. The company no longer operates independently: its legacy domain traffixsystems.com is parked on F5 Networks infrastructure with no web presence, and Traffix publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: UGI Corporation
providers.description: UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) is a King of Prussia, Pennsylvania-based natural gas and electric utility and propane distribution company. UGI Utilities serves Pennsylvania natural gas and electric customers, AmeriGas is the largest retail propane distributor in the United States, and UGI International markets LPG across Europe through brands including Antargaz, Flaga, and AvantiGas. The corporation also operates midstream and energy marketing businesses. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specs, or third-party developer APIs have been identified. Customer self-service runs on a Smart Energy Water (SEW)-powered Online Account Center (Android package com.sew.ugi) with CheckFree Pay handling bill payments; AmeriGas operates the separate MyAmeriGas portal at myamerigas.com. Large commercial customers use an Oracle APEX-based TCP platform at apex.ugi.com. UGI Utilities is not listed as a supported utility by UtilityAPI or other Green Button aggregators at the time of profiling.

providers.name: UUNET Technologies
providers.description: UUNET Technologies was one of the first commercial Internet service providers, founded in 1987 by Rick Adams in Virginia to commercialize Usenet and email, launching the AlterNet IP backbone in 1990. Backed by Accel Partners, Menlo Ventures, and NEA, it IPO'd on NASDAQ in 1995, was acquired by MFS Communications for $2B in 1996, which WorldCom bought that same year; after the MCI merger and Verizon's 2006 acquisition the UUNET brand was retired into Verizon Business. The brand is defunct today - its legacy domains (uu.net, uunet.com) remain Verizon-operated DNS zones whose web hosts only redirect to verizon.com/business, and it publishes no APIs or developer surface.

providers.name: Wi Charge
providers.description: Wi-Charge is a long-range wireless power company that transmits electricity over the air using infrared light, delivering safe, automatic charging to smart devices from thirty or more feet away without cables, batteries, or charging pads. The company sells consumer products such as the Encode Wireless Power Kit for smart locks and licenses its transmitter platform and compact receiver modules to OEMs building smart-home, commercial, IoT, retail, and consumer-electronics devices. Wi-Charge is venture-backed, including by Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Wi-Charge publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a hardware and OEM-licensing business rather than an API-first provider.

providers.name: Wiom
providers.description: Wiom is an Indian consumer internet company offering recharge-based home broadband: shared WiFi delivered over a community mesh network so households can pay only for the internet they actually use, without a mobile-data plan or a traditional fixed-line broadband contract. It was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of Accel. As of this enrichment pass Wiom operates a consumer marketing website (a React single-page application) but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface, so this profile carries verified identity and a live domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Wupima
providers.description: Wupima, Inc. was a Virginia-based mobile social intelligence company that did business as Hook Mobile, backed by 500 Global (500 Startups). Its App Growth Engine (AGE) product offered iOS and Android SDKs and an API that let mobile app and game developers grow their user base through word-of-mouth SMS/MMS social invitations, device targeting, and conversion analytics. The company, founded by Terry Hsiao, was active roughly 2010-2016 and is now defunct - wupima.com is a dead S3 bucket (403 AllAccessDisabled) and hookmobile.com has been taken over by an unrelated domain squatter serving spam, so no live website, developer portal, or API surface remains. Profile retained as a historical 500 Global portfolio record.

providers.name: yinglisolar
providers.description: Yingli Energy Development Co., Ltd. (Yingli Solar) is one of the earliest companies in China to commit to the photovoltaic industry, operating as an integrated photovoltaic smart-energy solution provider spanning technology research and development, smart manufacturing of high-efficiency solar PV modules (PANDA 3.0 and YLM 3.0 series), and the development, construction, and operation of power stations for residential, commercial, and utility-scale applications. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As a solar-hardware manufacturer, Yingli publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its only online service surfaces are a product anti-counterfeiting verification tool and product-specification downloads.

providers.name: ylhyoil
providers.description: ylhyoil is an upstream oilfield services provider backed by Qiming Venture Partners, serving traditional and unconventional reserves across domestic and overseas markets. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or software product surface for this company; it operates as an oilfield services business rather than an API provider. Only its registrable domain was probed for baseline DNS/TLS security posture.

providers.name: Zap Energy
providers.description: Zap Energy is a Seattle, Washington fusion energy company pursuing commercial fusion power via the sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch — a compact, magnet-free pulsed-power approach in which a flowing column of deuterium plasma is compressed (pinched) to fusion conditions inside a roughly two-meter metal tube, with shear in the axial flow stabilizing the pinch in place of the heavy superconducting magnets used by tokamak and stellarator designs. Founded in 2017 by Benj Conway, Brian A. Nelson, and Uri Shumlak as a spinout of University of Washington and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory research, the company has developed a lineage of devices — ZaP, ZaP-HD, FuZE, FuZE-Q, and FuZE-3 — culminating in 2024 with Century, a 100-kW-scale repetitive pulsed-power test platform with liquid-metal walls intended to demonstrate plant-relevant technologies. In November 2025 FuZE-3 reported plasma electron pressures of 830 MPa (1.6 GPa total), the highest pressure measured in any sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch and a marker on the path to scientific energy gain (Q>1). Zap Energy was selected for the U.S. Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program in May 2023 and received DOE approval of the preconceptual design of its Fusion Pilot Plant. The company has raised over $325 million across Series A–D from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, Energy Impact Partners, Chevron Technology Ventures, Shell Ventures, DCVC, Valor Equity Partners, and Addition. As of April 2026, Zabrina Johal serves as CEO with Conway as President, and the company has expanded its mandate to also pursue small modular fission alongside its fusion roadmap. Zap Energy has no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release; the technical surface is published as peer-reviewed papers and DOE milestone reports.

providers.name: Zeno Power Systems
providers.description: Zeno Power Systems (Zeno Power) develops radioisotope power systems — compact "nuclear batteries" that convert the decay heat of radioisotopes into long-duration electricity for extreme environments such as the lunar surface, deep-sea infrastructure, and remote defense installations. Backed by Techstars and other investors, Zeno is a hardware and energy-systems company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public web API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or GitHub organization, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: abbisko
providers.description: Abbisko Therapeutics (上海和誉生物医药科技有限公司) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of innovative small-molecule therapeutics, primarily in oncology. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or agent surface — this is a biopharmaceutical R&D company, not an API provider — so no API artifacts apply; only a live domain-security probe was captured.

providers.name: AbleTo
providers.description: AbleTo is a virtual behavioral health company delivering structured, evidence-based cognitive behavioral therapy and coaching programs for anxiety, depression, and stress, typically delivered through health insurance benefits. Founded in 2008 and acquired by Optum (UnitedHealth Group) in 2020, AbleTo now operates as part of Optum Behavioral Care; its www.ableto.com domain 301-redirects to optumbhcare.com. Originally backed by Bain Capital Ventures, the company is patient-facing and publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or OpenAPI. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio and market tracking.

providers.name: Acceleron
providers.description: Acceleron is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: aceabio
providers.description: ACEA Biosciences (aceabio) is a life-sciences company known for cell-analysis instrumentation that was acquired by Agilent Technologies; its aceabio.com.cn domain now redirects to an Agilent landing page (explore.agilent.com/ACEA-joins-Agilent). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the Qiming venture firm and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or public API surface for the standalone entity — the operating web presence has been folded into Agilent.

providers.name: aceatherapeutics
providers.description: ACEA Therapeutics (aceatherapeutics.com) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing innovative small-molecule and antibody-drug-conjugate treatments across oncology, autoimmune, and antiviral therapeutic areas, with product candidates including Olgotrelvir, Abivertinib, AC0058, STI-6129, and AC0939. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a pharmaceutical company oriented toward patients, physicians, and investors, ACEA Therapeutics publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or technical integration surface at this time; this profile captures its verifiable web/domain footprint only.

providers.name: Achira
providers.description: Achira is a digital-biology company building molecular world models to transform drug discovery and the physical sciences. Founded by John Chodera, Theofanis Karaletsos, and Zavain Dar, it blends geometric deep learning, generative AI, physics, quantum chemistry, and statistical mechanics into foundation simulation models that enable out-of-distribution prediction at the atomistic scale — a "third path" between pure machine-learning approaches and traditional molecular dynamics simulation. Achira raised a $33M Series A from Dimension, Amplify Partners, NVIDIA NVentures, and Compound. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: acxel
providers.description: ACXEL is a digital cell biology company building advanced microfluidics platforms and productivity tools for life sciences research and drug development. Its self-developed AP-LOC (Active Pixel Lab-on-Chip) technology enables high-throughput, parallel, and precise microdroplet manipulation, alongside AM-EWOD and AM-DMF digital microfluidic platforms supporting cell sorting, cell therapy, antibody therapy, synthetic biology, and chemical synthesis with full-process chip integration and real-time feedback monitoring. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. ACXEL is a hardware and platform provider and publishes no public developer/API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Adim
providers.description: Adim is an entertainment-technology and web3 media company co-founded in 2022 by It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia creator Rob McElhenney alongside Richard Rosenblatt, Chase Rosenblatt, Melissa Kaspers, and Spencer Marell. Adim invites a community of storytellers, writers, and fans to collaboratively create, develop, and co-own a new generation of intellectual property — stories, characters, and narrative universes known as the Adimverse — rewarding contributors with ownership stakes and a say in how the community is governed. The company raised a $5M seed round led by Chris Dixon of a16z crypto. Adim is a consumer creative platform rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Aethero
providers.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AI-Prime (Paidao Intelligence)
providers.description: AI-Prime (Paidao Intelligence / 湃道智能) is a Shanghai-based industrial-safety AI company founded in 2017 that builds computer-vision, deep-learning, and knowledge-graph platforms for high-hazard industries. Its full-stack products span an AI industrial-safety monitoring cloud platform, 40+ safety-scenario models (PPE detection, unsafe behavior, equipment leaks, fire/smoke, work-process compliance), a self-learning AI model-development platform, and Prime-Edge smart hardware (edge-computing boxes, inspection robots, AR work mirrors, and edge cameras) serving the chemical, steel, coal, oil & gas, energy, and mining sectors. AI-Prime is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It is an enterprise B2B provider with no public developer API program; this profile captures its identity and web presence.

providers.name: AirEye
providers.description: AirEye is a wireless airspace security company delivering Wireless Detection and Response (WDR) for enterprise IT and OT environments. Its AI-driven, agentless SaaS platform individually protects every Wi-Fi-enabled asset without isolating it from the network, identifying and classifying devices and wireless interactions, visualizing wireless communications in real time, automatically preventing threats through policy enforcement, and providing forensic analysis of incidents. AirEye addresses unauthorized wireless access, data leakage, network-segmentation circumvention, and device hijacking, with a focus on healthcare providers, defense manufacturers, and general enterprises. The company has been recognized in multiple Gartner market guides for medical device security and operational technology protection. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead; AirEye publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: aistarfish
providers.description: aistarfish (aistarfish.com) is the web home of Haixin Health (海心健康), a Chinese digital-health company operated by Zhejiang Haixin Zhihui Technology Co., Ltd. that provides full-course disease management and support services for cancer patients across their entire treatment journey. Its consumer-facing products are iOS and Android mobile apps built around a patient community, peer-support networks, patient and official medical diaries, and patient-to-doctor connections, under the mission of "helping cancer patients live longer and live better." The company holds an Internet Pharmaceutical Information Service qualification. It is surfaced here as a portfolio company of the Qiming venture network. As of this pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Allena Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Allena Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Allevi
providers.description: Allevi is a bioprinting company that designs and manufactures 3D bioprinters, bioinks, and accompanying software for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and life-sciences research. Its desktop bioprinters and biomaterials let researchers fabricate living tissue constructs for drug discovery, disease modeling, and organ-on-chip work. Allevi was acquired by 3D Systems and operates as part of its regenerative medicine portfolio. The company publishes bioprinting protocols, application notes, webinars, and white papers, but exposes no public web API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Alliance
providers.description: Alliance (also known as AllianceDAO) is an early-stage accelerator and founder community for crypto, fintech, and AI startups. Its flagship 10-week program pairs two weeks in-person in New York City with eight weeks remote, providing admitted teams $500k in initial funding (with follow-on capital), weekly lectures and 1:1 mentorship from experienced founders, 90+ partner perks (AWS, Google Cloud, OpenAI, Anthropic, and others), and a Demo Day that connects startups with venture and angel investors. Alliance is backed by firms including Kindred Ventures and Multicoin Capital, and its alumni include Rain, Pump, Synthetix, Pendle, Tensor, and Seismic. Alliance is a services and accelerator organization and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Alliant Credit Union
