Originally Acorn Systems, the product is now owned and operated by IgniteTech (an ESW Capital enterprise-software company); the acornsys.com domain 301-redirects into IgniteTech's software library. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification is published for the product.

providers.name: Acre Homes
providers.description: Acre Homes is a North Carolina-based homeownership company whose mission is to "create the best way to experience homeownership." Acre enables individuals to buy quality homes in desirable neighborhoods while sharing in ownership appreciation and reducing costs, notably without requiring traditional debt financing. Positioned in the wealth and asset management corner of fintech and proptech, the company reframes owning a home as a less financially burdensome decision than the conventional mortgage path, letting residents build equity through a shared-appreciation model rather than a conventional debt-financed purchase. Acre Homes is an early-stage venture-backed company and a portfolio company of Anthemis Group. It operates a consumer-facing homeownership offering and does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or developer documentation; this profile captures verified company identity and public links.

providers.name: Actuate
providers.description: Actuate Corporation was an enterprise business intelligence and reporting software company founded in 1993 and backed by Accel (partner Arthur Patterson). It was the original developer of BIRT (Business Intelligence and Reporting Tools), building a developer community measured in millions of downloads, and traded on NASDAQ under the ticker BIRT. OpenText acquired Actuate in January 2015 and folded its analytics and reporting technology into OpenText Analytics Cloud. The standalone actuate.com site is no longer an active product presence (all paths return HTTP 404) and the company publishes no independent, live API or developer portal today. A separately named company at actuate.ai (AI video/threat detection) is unrelated to this Accel-portfolio entity and likewise exposes no public API.

providers.name: Adap.tv
providers.description: Adap.tv was a global programmatic video advertising platform founded around 2007 and backed by Redpoint Ventures, offering brands, agencies, and publishers tools for planning, executing, and measuring video ad campaigns programmatically, including real-time bidding (RTB), audience targeting, campaign management, and analytics through its Pathway video-intelligence platform. AOL acquired Adap.tv in September 2013 for approximately $405 million and folded its technology into ONE by AOL; the business subsequently passed to Verizon Media and then Yahoo. Adap.tv no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, public API, or SDKs; the www.adap.tv domain now 301-redirects to yahooinc.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Adjoint
providers.description: Adjoint Inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts fintech (founded 2016) that built distributed-ledger and smart-contract software for corporate treasury and insurance. Its flagship platform, Uplink, let financial firms onboard assets onto a permissioned ledger, manage balances, and author self-executing agreements in Adjoint's Financial Core Language (FCL), with SDKs to bridge to traditional systems. The company raised roughly $10.4M and competed with Kyriba, Trovata, and Modern Treasury. As of this enrichment pass the company appears dormant: its adjoint.io domain now resolves to a parked/expired Namecheap page, its GitHub organization returns 404, and no first-party client SDKs are published to public registries. This profile is a VC-portfolio enrichment stub; see the data-quality note below regarding the originally-attached website.

providers.name: AdKnowledge
providers.description: Adknowledge, Inc. was a performance-based digital advertising and marketing technology holding company founded in 2004 by Scott Lynn and headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri. It ran a response-based targeting marketplace that connected advertisers to consumers across email, search, domains, social and app inventory, and it exposed a publisher-facing AdStation platform with an automated offer engine and creative library. Ben Legg served as Group CEO from 2011 to 2016, during which the company consolidated a long acquisition run (Super Rewards, Miva, Cubics, Lookery, Hydra Group, AdParlor, Giant Media, TriVu Media and others) into video and social units that were then sold off; AdParlor was subsequently acquired by Fluent in 2019. Third-party company registries now list Adknowledge as out of business. It entered the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub via kleiner-perkins. Contemporary integration write-ups confirm a historical RESTful AdStation / Publisher Platform API, but as of this enrichment pass no live surface survives: the adknowledge.com zone is still registered (AWS Route 53 nameservers, Microsoft 365 mail with an SPF record) yet publishes no A record for the apex or for www, api, developer, developers, docs or publisher, so there is no reachable website, developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification from which to harvest provider artifacts.

providers.name: Adku
providers.description: Adku was a big-data e-commerce personalization startup founded around 2010 by former Googlers (CEO Ajit Varma with co-founders Carlos Whitt and Jesse Shieh), and an AngelPad alumnus. It built machine-learning technology to personalize the online shopping experience for visitors to e-commerce sites such as eBay, Amazon, and Zappos. Backed by Battery Ventures, Greylock Partners, and True Ventures (roughly $1.49M raised), Adku was acquired by Groupon in February 2012 and is no longer an operating, independent company. It has no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface; this record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead for historical/enrichment tracking only.

providers.name: adludio
providers.description: Adludio is an AI-powered interactive mobile advertising company founded in 2015 in London by Paul Coggins (originally Future Ad Labs). Its "Sensory Ad Science" platform builds rich, interactive mobile ad units using touch, motion and haptic interaction, sold on a cost-per-engagement rather than CPM model, with brand clients including Nike, Microsoft, Coca-Cola and Estee Lauder. The company was backed by Balderton Capital. As of 2026 the adludio.com domain 301-redirects to permate.com (an unrelated Vietnamese partnership-automation platform), indicating the original company is no longer operating a public web presence; no public API or developer surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: AdMeld
providers.description: AdMeld was a New York City advertising-technology company founded in 2007 (by Ben Barokas and Brian Adams) that ran a supply-side platform / private ad exchange helping premium digital publishers optimize and monetize their ad inventory (serving 500+ publishers including FOX News and The Weather Channel). Google acquired AdMeld in 2011 for roughly $400M and folded its technology into the DoubleClick Ad Exchange. AdMeld no longer operates as an independent product and exposes no standalone public API; the admeld.com domain now serves a Google-maintained legacy landing page for DoubleClick Ad Exchange (Google nameservers, Google-hosted).

providers.name: administrative-divisons-db
providers.description: Get all administrative divisions of a country

providers.name: AdNectar
providers.description: AdNectar was a social advertising startup founded in 2008 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, that built a sponsored virtual-gifts network for Facebook applications and other social platforms. Its product let agencies and brands run campaigns in which consumers gave branded virtual gifts drawn from a catalog, paired with an embedded rich-media landing unit plus viral distribution, optimization, and reporting, so social-app publishers could monetize their virtual-goods inventory. The company raised roughly $5.3M from investors including Battery Ventures before being acqui-hired by Lockerz in November 2011. AdNectar is now defunct; its original adnectar.com domain is parked and serves no live product, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record and is not an active API provider. Note that the unrelated adnectar.io (performance marketing) and addnectar.com (Addnectar Solutions) are separate companies and are not associated with this entity.

providers.name: Adphorus
providers.description: Adphorus was an Istanbul- and Berlin-based travel marketing-science company and an official Facebook and Instagram Marketing Partner (certified since 2014) that specialized in automated, scalable Dynamic Ads for Travel, helping brands such as Expedia, Trivago, and Kayak scale full-funnel performance on Facebook and Instagram. The company was acquired by Sojern in November 2017 and subsequently absorbed; it operates no independent public website or developer API today, so this network profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record rather than an active API provider. The enrichment pipeline found no live domain, developer portal, or specification to harvest.

providers.name: Advanced Analogic Technologies (AnalogicTech)
providers.description: Advanced Analogic Technologies Incorporated (AnalogicTech, formerly NASDAQ: AATI) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1997 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, with design centers in Santa Clara and Shanghai. The company designed total power-management solutions built on proprietary analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits and discrete power MOSFETs, shipping a portfolio of more than 500 power-management application-specific standard products (ASSPs) and general-purpose analog ICs across four application areas: display and lighting, voltage regulation and DC/DC conversion, interface and power management, and battery management, primarily for mobile and portable consumer electronics. Advanced Analogic Technologies was acquired by Skyworks Solutions, Inc. in January 2011 and no longer operates as an independent company; it is a hardware semiconductor manufacturer with no public web API, developer platform, or API artifacts. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a company record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Advanced Metal Research
providers.description: Advanced Metal Research is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company based in Los Angeles building machine intelligence for American welding. The company develops American-made robotic welding cells that pair computer vision with real-time seam tracking and post-weld inspection, turning welding from a scarce manual craft into a closed-loop manufacturing system that learns from every weld as it happens. Founded in 2025 by Julian Fried, Stephen Lin, and Angus Muffatti, it targets the projected shortage of skilled welding professionals across US industrial manufacturing. The company is early-stage and hardware-focused; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Advent Solar
providers.description: Advent Solar was a silicon photovoltaic company founded in 2002 and headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico, that designed and manufactured crystalline-silicon (c-Si) solar cells and modules, pioneering emitter-wrap-through cell architectures and streamlined back-contact module assembly. Backed by Battery Ventures, EnerTech Capital, @Ventures and others across roughly $109M in venture funding (including a $70M Series D in 2007), the company's assets and intellectual property were acquired by Applied Materials in late 2009 / 2010. As a physical solar-hardware manufacturer that is no longer operating independently, Advent Solar exposes no public API, developer portal, or software surface; this profile is retained as a network identity record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Advolve.AI
providers.description: Advolve.AI is an AI-driven performance-marketing and customer-acquisition platform for e-commerce brands and marketplaces, offering an end-to-end solution to automate, scale, and optimize paid media and digital advertising, including a patent-pending creative-optimization capability that tunes interactive ad elements (messaging, graphics, colors, fonts). Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Sao Paulo, Brazil, Advolve was backed by Prosus Ventures and Valor Capital and was acquired by iFood (Prosus group) in November 2025 to power iFood Ads across Latin America. Advolve publishes a marketing website only; as of enrichment it exposes no public developer program, API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Aelita Software
providers.description: Aelita Software Corporation was an enterprise systems-management software company founded in 1998 by Ratmir Timashev (who later co-founded Veeam Software). Headquartered in the Columbus, Ohio area (Dublin/Powell, OH), Aelita built Windows infrastructure management tooling for Microsoft Active Directory and Microsoft Exchange environments — including migration, directory management, auditing, reporting, security analysis, systems monitoring, and disaster recovery. Marquee products included Migration Manager for Active Directory, Migration Manager for Exchange, Secure Copy, Enterprise Reporter, Recovery Manager for Active Directory, ActiveRoles Server, and InTrust. Insight Partners was an early investor. Aelita was acquired by Quest Software in March 2004 for approximately $115 million and its technology was folded into Quest's Windows Management line (much of which is now part of One Identity). The company has had no independent operation since 2004; it exposed no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface, and there is no live web presence today (the aelita.com domain is parked/for sale). This profile is retained as a historical Insight Partners portfolio record — there is no active developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Aemon
providers.description: Aemon is an autonomous AI research-and-development engineer founded in 2025 by Ray Xu and Richard Zhou and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Given an engineering problem and a measurable objective, Aemon reads state-of-the-art research, then generates, tests, and evolves thousands of candidate approaches at machine speed to discover optimal solutions that can exceed what human experts find. The team demonstrated the approach by setting a new world record on the NP-hard circle-packing optimization problem for under $10 of compute, beating a prior Google DeepMind result. Aemon is an early-stage, demo-first enterprise product headquartered in San Francisco; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Aerodome
providers.description: Aerodome was a Drone-as-First-Responder (DFR) company founded in 2023 by former California police officer Rahul Sidhu (CEO) and Kenaniah Cerny (Chief Architect). It built a fully integrated, automated, and remotely operated software platform that let public-safety agencies dispatch autonomous drones directly from 911 calls, pairing DJI drone hardware, robotic battery-swap docking nests, and radar with Aerodome DFR software featuring augmented-reality street overlays, automated flight operations, computer-aided-dispatch integration, and live airspace awareness. The company reported average 86-second response times to 911 calls. Backed by a16z, CRV, and 2048 Ventures across a seed (Oct 2023) and $21.5M Series A (May 2024), Aerodome was acquired by Flock Safety in October 2024 for over $300 million; its technology and software now ship as the Flock Safety "Flock DFR" product line, and the aerodome.com domain redirects to that product page.

providers.name: AeroFS
providers.description: AeroFS was an enterprise file sync-and-share and secure collaboration product built by Air Computing Inc., founded in 2010 out of Y Combinator with seed backing from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z Seed), SV Angel, Avalon Ventures, and angels including Chris Sacca, Maynard Webb, Jerry Yang, and Paul Buchheit. Its differentiator was peer-to-peer, private-cloud file sync that kept data on a company's own devices rather than a vendor's servers. Air Computing later pivoted to a team collaboration app called Amium. In 2017 the company merged with Redbooth (CEO and co-founder Yuri Sagalov became CEO of Redbooth), Amium was shut down on December 15, 2017, and the AeroFS technology was folded into Redbooth's product line. The standalone AeroFS product, developer program, and API are no longer operated; the aerofs.com domain is now a parked GoDaddy "for sale" page. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical/defunct-company record rather than an active developer surface.

providers.name: Affinity Labs
providers.description: Affinity Labs was a consumer social-networking company founded in 2006 by Christopher Michel (founder of Military.com) that built online communities for niche professional groups including firefighters (FireLink), police officers (PoliceLink), nurses (NursingLink) and the Armed Forces (HMForces.co.uk). Backed by Trinity Ventures and the Mayfield Fund, it grew past one million registered members before being merged into Monster Worldwide (Monster.com) in a $61 million transaction in January 2008. Its European operations shut down in 2012 and its domains and content were amalgamated into the Monster brand. The company is defunct and publishes no developer/API surface; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record. Not to be confused with Affinity (affinity.co), the unrelated relationship-intelligence CRM.

providers.name: afujingyou
providers.description: afujingyou (阿芙 / AFU) is a Chinese consumer essential-oil, aromatherapy and skincare brand founded in 2006, backed by Qiming Venture Partners (Series C, 2017). It sells single and blended essential oils, base/carrier oils, masks, emulsions and face creams through retail and e-commerce channels (Tmall/JD/Weibo storefronts). Enrichment finding (2026-07-17): this is a consumer packaged-goods brand, not an API provider — no public developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or other API artifacts exist to harvest, and the catalog domain afujingyou.net.cn does not resolve (NXDOMAIN). Retained as an identity-only record; no API artifacts are applicable.

providers.name: Aggra
providers.description: Aggra Technologies Private Limited operates Moneytor, an autonomous, self-learning platform for stressed loan recovery. Founded in 2017 in Mumbai, India by Ayush Srivastava and Anubhav Singh, Moneytor delivers debt management, collections, enterprise collections software, and distressed-debt / portfolio purchase solutions to lenders. The SaaS platform applies machine learning and automation to digitize the collections process — automating settlements, offering borrowers customized repayment plans, orchestrating multi-channel borrower communications, tracking overdue accounts, sending automated reminders, and surfacing real-time reporting and analytics — helping lenders collect and liquidate their consumer loan portfolios. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Agile Software
providers.description: Agile Software Corporation was an American product lifecycle management (PLM) software company founded in 1995 and headquartered in San Jose, California. Backed by Accel, it IPO'd on the NASDAQ in 1999 and built enterprise software that helped manufacturers manage product records, bills of materials, engineering change orders, quality, compliance, and supply-chain data across a product's development and production lifecycle. Oracle Corporation acquired Agile Software in July 2007 for approximately US$495 million; its products were rebranded as Oracle Agile PLM and folded into Oracle's supply-chain and applications suite. The company no longer operates independently: agilesoft.com now redirects to Oracle, and the only surviving developer surface is the legacy Oracle Agile PLM SDK (a Java API set) hosted on docs.oracle.com. This profile is retained as an acquired/historical record; there is no live, independent public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Agillion
providers.description: Agillion, Inc. was an Austin, Texas web-based customer relationship management (CRM) company founded in 1998 by Steve Papermaster. It offered small and mid-sized businesses a hosted, continuously updated online database that consolidated customer information as businesses and their customers interacted, an early software-as-a-service CRM offering. The company raised roughly $40M from investors including Cisco, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley and is carried as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. Agillion has since been permanently closed; its agillion.com domain no longer serves a website and the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record.

providers.name: AgLocal
providers.description: AgLocal was a venture-backed food-technology startup (founded 2011 by Mike Hsieh and Naithan Jones, Kansas City / San Francisco) that built an online marketplace connecting small family ranchers and sustainable meat producers directly with buyers. It launched in 2013 as a ranch-to-restaurant marketplace serving chefs, then pivoted in 2014 to a consumer-facing monthly meat subscription service. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Chicago Ventures and others across roughly $3.8M in funding, the company shut down in 2015, stating it could not reach a self-sustaining business model. It is added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead; the company is now defunct and its domain (aglocal.com) is parked/for sale, so no live developer portal, API, or specifications exist to enrich.

providers.name: Ahana
providers.description: Ahana was a venture-backed SaaS company founded in 2020 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, that provided a managed, cloud-native offering of PrestoDB — the open source distributed SQL query engine originally created at Facebook — positioned as the query and analytics layer of the open data lakehouse. Ahana raised roughly $32M in seed and Series A funding from investors including GV (Google Ventures), Lux Capital, Third Point Ventures, Leslie Ventures, and Liberty Global Ventures, and was a leading contributor and steward of the Presto Foundation. In April 2023 Ahana was acquired by IBM, which joined the Presto Foundation and folded Ahana's SaaS Presto capabilities into IBM watsonx.data. The independent Ahana product and developer surface no longer exist: the ahana.io domain now 301-redirects to https://www.ibm.com/products/watsonx-data. This profile is retained as a historical network record for the acquired company; there is no live first-party API to enrich.

providers.name: Ahlijasa
providers.description: Ahlijasa was an Indonesian on-demand home services startup founded in 2015 in the Greater Jakarta area by Jay Jayawijayaningtiyas and Made Dimas Astra Wijaya. It originally offered laundry, air-conditioning repair, and home cleaning before pivoting in late 2016 to focus exclusively on on-demand laundry by partnering with premium and traditional laundrettes to give them a digital storefront and online customer base. The company won Startup World Cup Indonesia in 2016 and raised seed funding in May 2017 from 500 Startups (500 Global), Fenox VC, and Indogen Capital, but secured no further funding afterward. Its primary domain (ahlijasa.com) now resolves to a domain-parking/for-sale page, indicating the business is no longer operating. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts were found for this provider during enrichment.

providers.name: Aiden.ai
providers.description: Aiden.ai was a London-based marketing-analytics startup, founded in 2016 by Marie Outtier and Pierre-Jean Camillieri, that built what it billed as the first AI-powered marketing analyst: a machine-reading assistant that ingested large volumes of paid-advertising data to surface actionable insights, detect anomalies, predict campaign performance, and proactively act to improve ROI. It raised a $1.6M seed round led by Partech in 2018 and was acquired by Twitter (now X) on 2019-11-21. The company no longer operates as an independent business, ships no public product or developer API, and the aiden.ai domain is now parked and listed for sale (Afternic). This profile is retained as a Partech portfolio lead but is defunct: there is no live developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Aikito
providers.description: Aikito is a New York-based company (founded 2021) operating a commercial real-estate platform that helps business owners design, build, finance, and manage their commercial spaces. It pairs a suite of AI-driven tools with non-dilutive financing so tenants can build out a space and pay over time, covering the project lifecycle from lease execution through move-in. Aikito was founded by Amol Sarva and its investors include Bloomberg Beta, Gaingels, Calm Ventures, FJ Labs, and Northzone. As of this profile Aikito publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface, so it remains a company/identity record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Ailumia
providers.description: Ailumia is an AI-driven retail operations platform that helps brands and sellers grow on the world's most valuable marketplaces, with a focus on Amazon. The platform applies artificial intelligence across the retail workflow to manage marketplace sales, inventory, supply chain, and finances, giving operators data-driven guidance and automation to navigate the challenges of modern e-commerce. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Taipei, Taiwan, Ailumia is backed by 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio; enrichment probing found a Cloudflare-fronted WordPress marketing presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: AIM
providers.description: AIM is an artificial-intelligence company based in North America and backed by General Catalyst, where it is surfaced as an active portfolio company in the AI sector (sponsoring partners Quentin Clark and Max Rimpel). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline. No public developer surface, website, product documentation, or API artifacts have been located for AIM yet; this profile records only what General Catalyst publicly publishes and will be enriched once a verified company domain and developer presence are identified.

providers.name: Aim Security
providers.description: Aim Security was an Israeli cybersecurity company (founded 2022) that built a security platform for enterprise adoption of generative AI and large language models — covering GenAI/LLM data-loss prevention, prompt-injection and jailbreak defense, shadow-AI discovery, and governance guardrails for employee use of AI applications. The company was acquired by Cato Networks and its standalone site (aim.security) now permanently redirects to catonetworks.com; its technology has been folded into the Cato SASE Cloud platform. As of this enrichment pass Aim Security exposes no independent public developer API, documentation portal, SDKs, or MCP server of its own.

providers.name: AInnovation
providers.description: AInnovation (创新奇智, Qingdao AInnovation Technology Group) is a Chinese enterprise artificial-intelligence company founded in 2018 and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (02121.HK). It focuses on "AI + Manufacturing", delivering industrial AI through its AInnoGC platform — an industrial large-language-model and AI-agent application-development platform — and its MMOC technology stack: ManuVision machine-vision, MatrixVision edge-video intelligence, and the Orion distributed machine-learning platform. It serves manufacturing verticals including semiconductors, steel, 3C electronics, automotive, energy, food and materials, construction, and financial services. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, the company reports 1,400+ patent applications. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Airespace
providers.description: Airespace, Inc. (formerly Black Storm Networks) was an American enterprise networking systems company founded in 2001 by Pat Calhoun, Bob Friday, Bob O'Hara and Ajay Mishra, manufacturing wireless LAN access points and the controllers that managed them. Airespace pioneered the centralized AP-controller architecture for rapid enterprise Wi-Fi deployment and authored the Lightweight Access Point Protocol (LWAPP), the direct precursor to the IETF CAPWAP standard, and was first to market with integrated Wi-Fi location tracking. It was venture backed by Storm Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners, Fidelity Investments and Battery Ventures, and shipped OEM equipment through NEC, Alcatel and Nortel. Cisco Systems acquired Airespace in 2005 for $450 million and merged its products into the Cisco Aironet line. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no API, developer portal or documentation; the airespace.com domain is parked and listed for sale.

providers.name: AirKit
providers.description: AirKit (Airkit.ai) was a low-code platform for building customer-facing digital experiences and, later, AI-powered customer service agents, backed by Accel and Emergence Capital. The company was acquired by Salesforce (announced 2023) and its technology now underpins Salesforce Agentforce. As of this enrichment pass, www.airkit.com 301-redirects to salesforce.com/agentforce and the domain's CAA records point to salesforce.com, so AirKit no longer operates an independent developer surface, API, documentation, or portal of its own — all first-party discovery URLs resolve into Salesforce properties. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record; enrichment beyond domain-level DNS/TLS evidence is not applicable.

providers.name: AirMap
providers.description: AirMap was a drone airspace-management and unmanned traffic management (UTM) platform that provided airspace intelligence, flight planning, digital notice, and geofencing services for drones and their operators, exposed through a developer platform of airspace and flight APIs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07) the company appears defunct: airmap.com no longer serves a developer portal or API and now resolves to a parked Squarespace-hosted page with a mismatched TLS certificate, and the legacy developer.airmap.com / api.airmap.com / docs.airmap.com hosts no longer resolve. No live API surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Airplane
providers.description: Airplane was a Benchmark-backed developer platform for building internal tools, dashboards, and operational workflows by turning scripts into shareable tasks and UIs. It was acquired by Airtable in 2023 and the product was subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct: the website www.airplane.dev no longer connects, the airplane.dev apex resolves to a domain-parking IP, and the airplanedev GitHub organization was archived on 2026-02-03 with no public repositories. No live API, developer portal, documentation host, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: airquality
providers.description: AirQuality (爱优特) is a Shanghai-based manufacturer of high-efficiency electrostatic air purification and disinfection products, including central air filtration systems, commercial kitchen exhaust (hood) cleaners, odor-elimination units, and smart air-quality detection systems for schools, hospitals, offices, shopping malls, and hotels. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is a hardware/manufacturing business that publishes a consumer website and online shop but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so most enrichment artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Airside
providers.description: Airside (formerly Airside Mobile) is a digital identity and mobile credential product whose website airsidemobile.com now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to Entrust's Airside app page, indicating the product and its assets were acquired by Entrust. As of this enrichment pass no public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, developer portal, or developer documentation surface could be discovered: developer/api/docs subdomains do not resolve and the root domain and /.well-known/security.txt both redirect off-site to Entrust. The company was originally surfaced as a bain-capital-ventures portfolio lead (sector ai-apps) and remains a stub pending any first-party developer program.

providers.name: Airware
providers.description: Airware was an enterprise commercial-drone (UAV) software and aerial-data-analytics company founded in 2011 by Jonathan Downey and headquartered in San Francisco. It began by building an operating system and autopilot for commercial drones, then pivoted to a cloud-based "Aerial Information Platform" that captured, processed, and analyzed drone imagery for enterprise verticals such as mining, quarrying, insurance, and construction. Airware acquired French drone-analytics firm Redbird in 2016 and raised roughly $118M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, GV (Google Ventures), Intel Capital, and Next World Capital. The company ceased operations in September 2018. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no live developer surface, API, or public specification is currently discoverable (the airware.com domain no longer resolves), so this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.

providers.name: AirWatch
providers.description: AirWatch was an enterprise mobility management (EMM) and mobile device management (MDM) company founded in 2003 in Atlanta, Georgia and backed by Accel. It provided cloud-based device, application, content, and email management for enterprise mobile fleets. VMware acquired AirWatch in February 2014 for roughly USD 1.5 billion, folding it into the VMware Workspace ONE Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform, and the brand was fully retired. In 2024 VMware End-User Computing (including Workspace ONE) was divested to Omnissa. As an independent brand AirWatch no longer operates a developer portal or public API: airwatch.com now redirects to the Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM product page, and the historical AirWatch REST API lives on as the per-tenant Workspace ONE UEM REST API served from customer *.awmdm.com consoles. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aitme
providers.description: Aitme was a Berlin-based deep-tech robotics company that built a platform for automated food preparation, deploying robotic kitchen and canteen systems that cooked and assembled meals autonomously for foodservice and workplace-catering settings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, the company has since been acquired and exposes no public developer surface: no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or hosted domain could be located during enrichment. This profile is retained as an honest catalog record with no fabricated API artifacts.

providers.name: Akash Systems
providers.description: Akash Systems is an Oakland, California deep-tech semiconductor company that pioneers Diamond Cooling thermal-management technology, integrating synthetic diamond directly with semiconductors such as Gallium Nitride (GaN) to remove heat up to five times faster than copper. Its Chip-on-Diamond and diamond-cooled server products target AI and data-center compute, while its GaN power amplifiers and satellite radios serve space communications, radar, cellular, and automotive/EV markets. Akash Systems is a hardware and materials company with no public developer API or documentation surface; it was surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Alassio
providers.description: Alassio is a French financial-technology company building a next-generation payroll software platform (logiciel de paie nouvelle generation) for businesses. Alassio positions itself as offering the functional depth expected of a specialist payroll and HR tool, with added transparency and control for finance and people teams. The company is backed by venture-capital firm Partech and operates from France, serving the French and European payroll, compensation, and human-resources market. As of this profile the company publishes only a marketing landing page and a legal notice; no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or integration surface has been located. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub awaiting a public developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Albedo
providers.description: Albedo is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of initialized-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: frontier-tech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Alibaba Local Services
providers.description: Alibaba Local Services (阿里巴巴本地生活) is Alibaba Group's on-demand local-life services business, formed in 2018 by integrating the Ele.me food-delivery platform with the Koubei local-services and restaurant-discovery platform. It operates on-demand food and grocery delivery, local merchant services, reviews and reservations, and last-mile logistics across China, and received a major financing round led by the SoftBank Vision Fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the network as a lead; no distinct public developer API surface has been confirmed for the holding entity under this name (its consumer platforms Ele.me and Koubei operate their own separate open platforms).

providers.name: Aliena
providers.description: Aliena is a Singapore-based space-technology company, incorporated in 2018, that designs and manufactures compact electric propulsion systems for small satellites. Its MUSIC plasma thruster line delivers high thrust-to-power ratios at very low power budgets with high specific impulse, enabling small satellites to operate and sustain very low Earth orbit (VLEO) for high-resolution remote sensing. Aliena is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: All Day Kitchens
providers.description: All Day Kitchens is a San Francisco-based cloud-kitchen (ghost kitchen) infrastructure company that operates a network of delivery-optimized commissary kitchens, letting restaurant brands expand into new markets and fulfill online delivery orders without building out their own physical locations. Often positioned as a "Kitchen as a Service" platform, it pairs shared kitchen capacity with software and operations for order routing, food preparation, and last-mile delivery hand-off. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it publishes only a marketing landing page at www.alldaykitchens.com with no public developer portal, API, documentation, or event surface.

providers.name: All Def Digital
providers.description: All Def (formerly All Def Digital) is a YouTube-focused digital content studio founded by Russell Simmons that produces unscripted original programming for Gen Z, Millennial, and multicultural audiences across comedy, food, hip-hop, and culture. Its owned-and-operated channels have amassed 15M+ fans and more than 2 billion video views, and it produces branded content for partners including Sprite, Snickers, Hyundai, Lexus, and McDonald's. All Def is a portfolio company of a16z, surfaced in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Alliance Holdings
providers.description: Alliance Holdings GP, L.P. (AHGP) was a limited partnership formed to own and control Alliance Resource Management GP, LLC, the managing general partner of Alliance Resource Partners, L.P. (ARLP), the second largest coal producer in the eastern United States. AHGP held a general partner interest and incentive distribution rights in ARLP, along with a substantial direct ownership stake in ARLP common units. In 2018, Alliance Holdings GP became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Alliance Resource Partners as part of a simplification transaction, with AHGP unitholders receiving ARLP common units in exchange. Alliance Resource Partners (NASDAQ: ARLP) continues as a diversified energy company generating income from coal production and mineral royalties from coal, oil, and gas interests across the United States. As an energy holding company, Alliance Holdings did not maintain a public developer API program.

providers.name: AllSome
providers.description: AllSome is a Malaysia-based cross-border e-commerce fulfillment, warehousing, and supply-chain company serving online marketplace sellers across Southeast Asia. It operates a fulfillment network and order-management platform that helps sellers source, store, and ship goods (notably China-to-SEA cross-border trade) across channels such as Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop. AllSome is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; no public developer API surface was discoverable during enrichment (the primary website is WAF-protected and returns 403 to automated clients, and no api/developer/docs subdomains resolve).

providers.name: AllTaster
providers.description: AllTaster Limited (trading as Taster) is a UK-registered, digital-first food-brand creator that imagines and operates virtual and physical restaurant concepts in collaboration with chefs, creators, and franchise partners, distributed largely through third-party delivery apps and its own consumer mobile apps. Its brand portfolio includes Pepe Chicken, Out Fry, La Vie Dirty Burgers, Sheesh!, and others. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, developer portal, or technical documentation, so no API artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived; this profile captures verified company identity only.

providers.name: AllTrails
providers.description: AllTrails is an outdoor recreation platform for discovering, mapping, and navigating hiking, trail running, mountain biking, and backpacking routes. It offers a searchable database of hundreds of thousands of trails worldwide with maps, elevation profiles, community reviews, photos, and conditions, plus GPS turn-by-turn navigation, offline downloadable maps, and route planning through its AllTrails+ subscription. AllTrails is a consumer mobile and web application; it does not publish a public developer API program, and its web surface is served behind a Cloudflare WAF that blocks automated discovery. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched with the verifiable public signals available.

providers.name: Ally
providers.description: Ally.io was an OKR and goal-management SaaS platform for people and performance teams, helping organizations set, align, and track objectives and key results across the workforce. Backed by Accel, Greylock, Tiger Global and Addition, the company was acquired by Microsoft in October 2021 and its product was folded into Microsoft Viva Goals. The ally.io domain remains actively hosted but no longer exposes a public developer/API surface; developer, docs and API subdomains do not resolve. This API Evangelist profile is retained as an hr-tech portfolio lead with a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: AllyO
providers.description: AllyO is an HR-tech company, founded in 2016 in Palo Alto, California, that built a conversation-first, AI recruiting chatbot and automation platform for high-volume hiring. Its chatbot let candidates apply to jobs, answer common questions, get screened, and schedule interviews via text and web chat 24/7, with integrations into applicant tracking systems, job boards, and background-check providers. AllyO raised roughly $64M in venture funding (including a $45M round in 2019 backed by investors such as Sapphire Ventures) before being acquired by HireVue in October 2020. The AllyO product now lives inside HireVue as its Conversational AI and Automation offering; www.allyo.com 301-redirects to HireVue and AllyO no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Almentor
providers.description: Almentor is a Dubai (UAE) based video e-learning platform delivering the largest high-quality Arabic continuous-learning video library, founded in 2016 and launched in January 2018 by Ihab Fikry and Ibrahim Kamel. It serves both individual learners (B2C) and organizations (B2B via business.almentor.net) with paid courses, free talks, crash courses, and books across health, humanities, technology, entrepreneurship, business management, lifestyle, and corporate communication, delivered by hundreds of experts and educators across the MENA region. Backed by Partech, Almentor has delivered more than three million learning experiences. Almentor publishes no public developer/API program; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Alongside
providers.description: Alongside is an a16z-backed crypto company (alongside.xyz) founded in 2022. It originally launched the Alongside Crypto Market Index (AMKT), the first on-chain broad crypto market index token with a 0% annual fee, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Coinbase Ventures, and Franklin Templeton. The company has since pivoted to AI-native compliance automation for scaling crypto firms, unifying fragmented KYC/AML/KYT tooling into a single system and reducing manual analyst burden for autonomous financial agents. As of this enrichment pass Alongside publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: Alpharel
providers.description: Alpharel, Inc. was a Camarillo, California document-management and imaging company founded in 1981 that built turnkey digital document transmission and management systems (scanners, optical disks, terminals, LANs) for industrial, commercial, and government use. It acquired Optigraphics in 1993, renamed itself Altris Software in October 1996, and its business was ultimately succeeded by Spescom Software, Inc. of San Diego. Alpharel appears in the Battery Ventures portfolio list. The company is DEFUNCT under this name: it has no active first-party website, developer portal, API, or SDKs, so there is no API/developer surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Alphion
providers.description: Alphion Corporation is a broadband access equipment manufacturer that develops fiber-optic and wireless networking solutions for network operators, enterprises, and community networks. Founded in 2000 and based in Princeton Junction, New Jersey, the company builds GPON-based fiber-to-the-x (FTTx/FTTH) access systems, optical network terminals (AONT/ONT), and secure GigaWi-Fi broadband access products that deliver voice, data, video, and wireless services over passive optical networks. Alphion is a photonics and telecommunications hardware provider; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It does not currently publish a developer portal, public API, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Alterya
providers.description: Alterya is an AI-powered fraud-prevention company founded in 2022 (Y Combinator; seed round led by Battery Ventures, ~$9.8M) that detects authorized-fraud scams — authorized push-payment (APP) scams, pig-butchering and romance scams, money-mule and synthetic accounts, and social-engineering-driven withdrawals — before victims send funds. It connects fraud signals across crypto rails and traditional fiat/bank rails, and prior to acquisition monitored more than $8B in transactions per month for exchanges and fintechs including Binance, Coinbase, and Block, protecting roughly 100M end users. Chainalysis acquired Alterya in January 2025 for a reported ~$150M; it now ships as the "Alterya by Chainalysis" fraud-prevention product. The standalone alterya.com domain is parked and the company operates entirely inside Chainalysis, with no independent public developer portal, API, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: AltSchool
providers.description: AltSchool was an American education-technology company founded in 2013 by former Google executive Max Ventilla to build a network of small private "lab" schools around a personalized, student-directed learning model, using those campuses to develop a K-12 software platform for assignments and progress tracking. It raised more than $170 million from investors including Founders Fund, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Mark Zuckerberg's CZI, and Peter Thiel. In 2017-2019 the company closed or handed off its for-profit schools (to Higher Ground Education) and pivoted to selling the software as "Altitude Learning," with Ventilla stepping down as CEO. The venture is now defunct as an independent operation: the altschool.com domain no longer resolves and altitudelearning.com redirects to Guidepost Montessori. No public developer, API, or documentation surface was found; this record is retained as a historical VC-portfolio company profile.

providers.name: Alwans
providers.description: Alwans is a Saudi technology investment and startup-development company based in Al Khubar, Saudi Arabia, and launched in January 2010. The firm is focused on enriching local Arabic technical content and competing globally by investing in and building startup ideas and technology projects, with an emphasis on e-commerce, online marketing, mobile applications, and mobile games. Alwans is a small team (2-10 employees) and is itself backed by 500 Global; its portfolio includes companies such as Foodics and Fnjalah. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs -- this profile is an identity record within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Amalfi Semiconductor
providers.description: Amalfi Semiconductor was a fabless developer of high-performance CMOS radio frequency (RF) and mixed-signal semiconductors for cellular handsets. Its proprietary CMOS-based AdaptiveRF architecture delivered power amplifiers that extended battery life and talk time while reducing the size and cost of front-end cellular handset designs, shipping over 100 million CMOS power amplifiers. Battery Ventures led the company's $24M Series C in 2009, with further investment in 2012 alongside DCM and Globespan Capital Partners. Amalfi Semiconductor was acquired by RF Micro Devices (now part of Qorvo) in November 2012 for $47.5M in cash. The company is defunct as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; this profile is retained for network and portfolio-graph completeness rather than API enrichment.

providers.name: Amber Bio
providers.description: Amber Bio is a San Francisco biotechnology company developing an RNA-based gene-editing platform capable of making multi-kilobase edits — rewriting thousands of bases on a single RNA strand in one step — to reach previously undruggable patient populations. Because edited RNA eventually degrades in the body, the approach is designed to be safer and reversible compared with permanent DNA editing. The platform pairs multi-kilobase RNA writing with AI foundation models to target diverse pathogenic variants across patients with a single product, initially focused on ophthalmology and central nervous system diseases. Founded by CRISPR-field researchers from the Broad Institute and UC Berkeley (co-founder and CTO Basem Al-Shayeb, advised by Nobel Laureate Jennifer Doudna), Amber Bio launched in 2023 with a $26M seed round co-led by Playground Global and Andreessen Horowitz. It has no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Amber Wave
providers.description: AmberWave, Inc. (formerly AmberWave Systems Corporation) is a Lowell, Massachusetts deep-technology company that researches, develops, and licenses semiconductor and photovoltaic materials technology. It originated strained-silicon and aspect-ratio-trapping techniques from MIT and Bell Labs research, and today develops Ultra-Thin Silicon (UTSi) flexible solar cells and modules that weigh roughly 90% less than conventional panels, targeting lightweight commercial rooftops, off-grid power, building integration, vehicle, and aerospace applications. AmberWave is a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It publishes a corporate website but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface, so there are no machine-readable API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: amberjack
providers.description: Amberjack is a direct-to-consumer men's footwear brand based in Brooklyn, New York, that designs and manufactures dress shoes engineered with athletic-inspired technology such as heat-activated arch support and dual-density outsoles for all-day comfort in hybrid work settings. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify storefront and is backed by Slow Ventures. Enrichment found no public developer or API surface (no docs portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, OAuth, or /.well-known endpoints); it remains catalogued as a consumer-brand company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Amberpoint
providers.description: AmberPoint was an enterprise software company founded in 2001 that provided runtime management, monitoring, and governance solutions for Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) and distributed web-services applications. Its products let organizations discover, secure, monitor, and enforce policy across complex multi-application business processes and message flows, and competed in the SOA management space alongside vendors integrated into enterprise middleware stacks. AmberPoint was acquired by Oracle on February 8, 2010, with its technology folded into Oracle Fusion Middleware and Oracle Enterprise Manager. The company no longer operates independently; the amberpoint.com domain is held by Oracle and no longer serves a public developer surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record surfaced from a venture-capital portfolio.

providers.name: AMCC
providers.description: AMCC (Applied Micro Circuits Corporation, also known as AppliedMicro or APM) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1979 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It designed network and embedded Power ISA processors, ARMv8-A server processors (the X-Gene line), and optical transport, connectivity, and storage silicon for telecommunications, data center, and industrial markets. Backed by Matrix Partners, U.S. Venture Partners, and other venture investors, AMCC traded on NASDAQ under the ticker AMCC. It was acquired by MACOM Technology Solutions (NASDAQ: MTSI) in January 2017 and no longer operates as an independent company. As a fabless chip designer with no public developer platform, AMCC exposes no APIs, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is retained as a historical company record and Matrix Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: AMCC (Applied Micro Circuits Corporation)
providers.description: Applied Micro Circuits Corporation (AMCC) was a California-based semiconductor company founded in 1979, originally producing application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) for the military market before diversifying into commercial mixed-signal, networking, storage, and embedded processor products. AMCC went public on NASDAQ in 1997, acquired MMC Networks in 2000, and bought IBM's PowerPC 400 processor line in 2004. Under the AppliedMicro brand it later developed the X-Gene ARM 64-bit server-on-chip family. AMCC ceased to exist as an independent entity when MACOM completed its acquisition on January 26, 2017; the X-Gene compute business was subsequently spun out to form Ampere Computing. As a fabless silicon/hardware company (now defunct), AMCC published no public developer API surface, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: American Aerospace Advisors
providers.description: American Aerospace Technologies, Inc., doing business as American Aerospace Advisors, is a defense and critical-infrastructure monitoring company based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. It provides end-to-end airborne intelligence systems that combine unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), airborne sensors, analytics, and communications to deliver near-real-time data through a cloud-based intelligence gateway. Its flagship AiRanger medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aircraft and InstiMaps sensor technology support pipeline and linear-asset patrol, beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) flight services, sensor integration, and aviation policy consulting. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Amiato
providers.description: Amiato was a Palo Alto, California big-data startup founded in 2011 by Nathan Binkert and Mehul A. Shah, originally incubated at Y Combinator in 2012 under the name Nou Data. Amiato built a real-time analytics pipeline around its Schema-lift technology, which extracted records from NoSQL data stores such as MongoDB and Couchbase, automatically inferred and transformed them into a relational schema, and loaded them continuously into Amazon Redshift so that unstructured operational data could be queried by conventional business-intelligence tools. The company raised roughly $2M from investors including Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz, Ignition Partners, Data Collective (DCVC) and angel Bobby Yazdani. Amazon Web Services quietly acquired Amiato in May 2014 (reported publicly in April 2015) in what was widely characterized as a talent acquisition; most of the team joined Amazon's database and Redshift product groups and Amiato ceased independent operations. The company is defunct: the amiato.com domain no longer resolves and there is no surviving public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich.

providers.name: Amino
providers.description: Amino is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of techstars, union-square-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Amixr.io
providers.description: Amixr was an incident-response and on-call management startup that provided alerting, escalation, and on-call scheduling for engineering and DevOps teams, integrating with monitoring stacks such as Grafana and Prometheus. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Grafana Labs in December 2021 and its product was folded into Grafana OnCall (now part of Grafana IRM). The standalone amixr.io product and developer surface have been retired; the domain no longer serves an active website, developer portal, or API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record following enrichment.

providers.name: Analytical Flavor Systems
providers.description: Analytical Flavor Systems is the startup behind Gastrograph AI, a sensory-science and machine-learning platform that modeled human flavor, aroma, and texture perception to help food and beverage companies predict consumer preference, benchmark products, and optimize formulations before physical prototyping. It was a Techstars-backed portfolio company. Its gastrograph.com domain now 301-redirects to NielsenIQ, which acquired the technology and folded it into its BASES AI Product Developer solution; no independent public API, developer portal, or SDK surface remains.

providers.name: Anchor *
providers.description: Anchor was a podcast creation, hosting, distribution, and monetization platform (anchor.fm), founded in 2015 and backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others. Spotify acquired Anchor in 2019 and folded it into its creator tooling, later rebranding the product to Spotify for Podcasters and then Spotify for Creators. The anchor.fm domain now 302-redirects to Spotify's creator product (podcasters.spotify.com / creators.spotify.com); Anchor never published a standalone public developer API, and it no longer operates as an independent company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead; enrichment confirms it is an acquired/absorbed brand with no independent developer surface to harvest.

providers.name: Anchor FM
providers.description: Anchor FM was a podcast creation, hosting, distribution, and monetization platform founded in 2015 that let anyone record, edit, publish, and monetize a podcast for free from a phone or browser. Spotify acquired Anchor in 2019 and folded the product into Spotify for Podcasters, later rebranded Spotify for Creators; the anchor.fm domain now redirects to creators.spotify.com. Anchor never published a public developer API or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity and domain-security posture only. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel (consumer sector).

providers.name: andjaro
providers.description: Andjaro is a French SaaS platform for replacement management and workforce flexibility, helping organizations handle short-notice absences, staff shortages, and operational continuity across the private and public sectors. The product gives HR and operations teams real-time visibility of available personnel across an employment ecosystem, matches available workers (CDI/CDD employees, freelancers, and temps) to urgent replacement needs, and automates the administrative workflow by integrating with payroll, ERP, planning, and HRIS systems. It serves facility management, healthcare and social services, the public sector, retail, collective catering, and transport and logistics. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of balderton-capital; no public API, developer portal, or SDK was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Angelic
providers.description: Angelic (Angelic: Dark Symphony) is a dark, story-rich cinematic turn-based Strategy-RPG from Angelicore Game Studios, where players lead neo-human angels through tactical missions, impossible choices, and cosmic horror. Originally launched as a Web3 / metaverse gaming project backed by Pantera Capital, the title is now distributed as a premium PC game on Steam and the Epic Games Store. Angelic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface as of this profile; it is a consumer game studio rather than an API provider.

providers.name: AnimeChan
providers.description: Anime quotes (over 10k+)

providers.name: Anobit Technologies
providers.description: Anobit Technologies was an Israeli fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2006, that developed flash-memory Memory Signal Processing (MSP) controller technology to extend the endurance, reliability, and performance of consumer-grade NAND flash used in SSDs and mobile devices. Backed by Battery Ventures among others, Anobit was acquired by Apple in early 2012 and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer surface, API program, or live web presence, and remains in the API Evangelist network only as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Anon
providers.description: Anon is an enterprise AI agent platform that builds production-ready AI agents for companies. Its offerings include computer-use agents that automate long-running browser workflows, hosted web agents that perform tasks across multiple systems, and an agent authentication toolkit that gives developers tools to authenticate agents across third-party services. Originally positioned as an automated authentication layer for the gen-AI age, Anon has raised $14M from Forerunner Ventures, Union Square Ventures, and Abstract Ventures. As of this profile the company does not publish a public self-serve API, SDK, developer portal, or MCP server; engagements are handled directly (hello@anon.com).

providers.name: AnswerSoft
providers.description: AnswerSoft, Inc. was a privately-held computer-telephony integration (CTI) software company based in Richardson, Texas. Its Concerto product line automated interactions between telephony systems and business applications, covering smart screen pop, intelligent call routing, data mining, and early internet-enabled call centers. Davox Corporation acquired AnswerSoft in a stock-for-stock transaction in 1998 to pair AnswerSoft's inter-application automation with Davox's Unison outbound call center line, taking the combined company into the emerging CRM market. Davox renamed itself Concerto Software in 2002, merged with Aspect Communications to form Aspect Software in 2005, and merged with Noble Systems to become Alvaria in 2021. AnswerSoft has not operated independently for over twenty-five years, publishes no API, developer program, or documentation, and the answersoft.com domain is now listed for sale on the GoDaddy aftermarket. This profile is retained as a historical acquired-company lead only.

providers.name: Anycart
providers.description: Anycart is a consumer grocery delivery and store-pickup platform that lets shoppers enter a zip code, choose a favorite local grocery store, and shop for anything they need with no price markups and no service fees. The service spans multiple U.S. retailers and focuses on transparent pricing for everyday grocery ordering, delivery, and pickup. Anycart was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It operates a consumer web and mobile storefront (anycart.com) and does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI definition, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Apex (Apex Security)
providers.description: Apex Security was an AI security startup founded in 2023 in Tel Aviv by Matan Derman (CEO) and Tomer Avni (CPO), backed by Sequoia Capital, Index Ventures and angel investors including Sam Altman. Its platform gave enterprises visibility into generative-AI and LLM usage — public tools like ChatGPT and Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and in-house AI applications — then let them define policy, detect violations and shadow AI, and respond to attacks across the AI attack surface. Tenable announced its intent to acquire Apex on 2025-05-29 and closed the acquisition in June 2025 for approximately $47.8M; the technology was folded into the Tenable One exposure management platform and now ships as Tenable One AI Exposure. Apex no longer operates as an independent company: the apexhq.ai domain has lapsed and was re-registered by an unrelated party on 2026-05-13, and now serves a Namecheap parking page. There is no Apex developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Apex Space
providers.description: Apex Space (Apex) is a Los Angeles based satellite manufacturing company that builds productized, configurable spacecraft bus platforms for proliferated constellations across LEO, MEO, and GEO orbital regimes. Apex offers three product lines: Aries (small satellites up to 150 kg payload), Nova (medium satellites up to 300 kg payload), and Comet (large satellites up to 3,000 kg payload), and operates Factory One, a high-rate manufacturing facility in Los Angeles with the capacity to produce more than 200 satellites annually. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Apex does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; customers configure satellite platforms through the on-site Configurator and direct sales inquiries.

providers.name: API Fortress
providers.description: API Fortress was an API testing and monitoring platform that let engineering teams author, run, and continuously monitor functional and integration tests against REST and SOAP APIs, in the cloud or via an on-premise Docker-based agent. It was acquired by Sauce Labs in January 2020 and its capabilities were folded into the Sauce Labs API Testing product. The standalone apifortress.com developer surface has since been retired; as of this enrichment pass the domain no longer resolves (parked Route53 nameservers, no A records), the apifortress GitHub organization returns 404, and there is no live first-party API, docs, SDK, or well-known surface remaining to enrich.

providers.name: Apigy
providers.description: Apigy, Inc. is the company behind Lockitron, an early keyless smart-lock startup that let people lock, unlock, and share access to their doors from a smartphone. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and known for a large 2012 crowdfunding campaign, Apigy built connected door-lock hardware and companion mobile apps before the Lockitron product line was wound down. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; its public website (lockitron.com) is currently unreachable and no active developer or API surface could be located.

providers.name: Apla, Inc.
providers.description: Apla, Inc. (aplahub.com) was an AI-based accounting and bookkeeping platform based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 2023. Aplá targeted early-stage startups and accountants working in QuickBooks Online, offering automated expense categorization, transaction and expense management, bookkeeping, and financial reporting, and shipped a "Vendor Search" Chrome extension that retrieved vendor details inside QuickBooks Online. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass the company appears inactive: the aplahub.com origin is unreachable (HTTP 522/525 behind Cloudflare) and third-party trackers list it as deadpooled. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface could be found; the only developer-facing artifact located was the QuickBooks Online Chrome extension.

providers.name: aplum
providers.description: aplum (branded Plum, Chinese 红布林) is a Beijing-based online marketplace for second-hand and pre-owned luxury fashion, founded in 2017. It runs C2B2C and B2B2C models — authenticating, grading, photographing, and reselling used designer apparel, handbags, watches, and accessories through its mobile app and website. Plum raised a $100M Series C from Zhuanzhuan Group in 2022, and earlier venture rounds from Qiming Venture Partners and Matrix Partners China. The platform is consumer-facing (Android app com.aplum.androidapp and mobile web m.aplum.com); it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal, so it is catalogued here as a company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Apollo Shield
providers.description: ApolloShield develops counter-drone (counter-UAS / cUAS) systems that detect, classify, and neutralize unauthorized aerial threats. Its product suite spans RF detection sensors (omnidirectional Omni RF Sensor up to 1.5 km and directional sensors 2-5 km with triangulation), active-defense jammers (portable RF Gun under 4 kg, stationary, mobile, and vehicle-mounted RF Jammers), the integrated RF Sense&Block system, a CUAS vehicle, and a centralized Command Center that manages sensors and issues real-time alerts via SMS, email, and API. The platform uses AI-assisted RF fingerprinting to identify drone communications and can force unauthorized drones to return home. Command Center runs on-premise or cloud-based. Note: jammers cannot be sold in the United States except to federal government entities and require regulatory compliance in other jurisdictions. ApolloShield exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or portal today; the only programmatic surface referenced is outbound Command Center alert delivery. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech.

providers.name: Aporeto
providers.description: Aporeto was a zero trust cloud security company providing machine identity-based microsegmentation, a distributed firewall, and Kubernetes network security for hybrid and multi-cloud application workloads. Backed by DCVC and Wing Venture Capital, Aporeto was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in December 2019 (~$150M) and its identity-based microsegmentation platform was folded into Prisma Cloud. The company no longer operates an independent product, brand, or developer surface; aporeto.com now redirects to Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Cloud. This profile is retained as a network record of the acquired company; no standalone API, developer portal, or specification surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: APP Group  Ness Czechia
providers.description: APP Group (renamed Ness Czechia after its acquisition by Ness Digital Engineering) is an enterprise IT services and systems-integration company headquartered in Prague, Czech Republic, with offices in Brno and Ostrava. Operating today as Ness Czech s.r.o., it is one of the most significant SAP providers (SAP Gold Partner) in the Czech Republic and the wider CEE region, delivering system integration, ERP and SAP S/4HANA implementation, business intelligence, data analytics, eGovernment / eHealth registers, core banking, pricing and billing, CRM and portals, IoT, and digital-platform engineering to large enterprises and the public sector. It is not a public API provider: it does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a self-serve API program. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record.

providers.name: AppAssure Software (Dell)
providers.description: AppAssure Software was a data-protection vendor (backup, replication, and recovery for physical, virtual, and cloud systems) funded by Bain Capital Ventures before Dell acquired it in 2012. Its flagship AppAssure 5 platform shipped a bundled service-management REST API for programmatically driving backup, replication, and recovery from the Management Console. The product line has since been retired and folded into what is now Quest Rapid Recovery; there is no active public developer portal, hosted API host, or machine-readable specification. This profile is retained for network completeness and lineage rather than as a live, integrable API surface.

providers.name: AppBistro
providers.description: AppBistro, operated by MMTG Labs, was an application marketplace for the Facebook Pages platform that let brands and page administrators discover, install, and manage third-party apps to boost engagement and reach on their fan pages. It also built AppGalleries, a white-label app-store platform. A TechCrunch Disrupt 2010 finalist, the San Francisco startup raised a $550K convertible note (Sand Hill Angels, 500 Startups, i/o Ventures, Zelkova Ventures, Seraph Group, and angels including Alfred Lin) and was acquired by mobile ad network InMobi on 2012-07-13, after which the product and its five-person team (co-founders Ryan Merket and Nalin Mittal) wound down. The company is defunct and appbistro.com no longer resolves; no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: appconomy
providers.description: Appconomy was a mobile-commerce platform company, founded in 2010 and dual-headquartered in Austin, Texas and Shanghai, China, that let brands, retailers, service providers, and mobile carriers add commerce functionality (daily deals, coupons, loyalty and rewards, mobile gifting, and merchant app generation for marketplaces such as Taobao) to their mobile apps. It was venture-backed with strategic investors including Qiming Venture Partners (lead of a $10M Series A), True Ventures, Neusoft Holdings, and WTI. The company is now permanently closed and publishes no live developer surface. The appconomy.cn domain does not resolve, appconomy.com returns 404, and no public API, documentation, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ endpoint could be found. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-graph record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Appionics
providers.description: Appionics Holdings Limited is a Hong Kong mobile applications and games company that operated under the consumer brand name "Animoca". Co-founded by Yat Siu and David Kim, and emerging out of the Outblaze group, Appionics developed and published cross-platform games and apps for iOS and Android, claiming more than 150 titles and over 40 million downloads during 2011. In 2014 the company spun off part of its app portfolio, along with a set of licensed intellectual-property game rights, into Animoca Brands Corporation Limited (ASX AB1), which listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in January 2015 and later pivoted to blockchain gaming and NFTs. Appionics itself never published a developer program, and today has no live web or API surface of its own.

providers.name: Appirio
providers.description: Appirio is a global cloud services and consulting company founded in 2006 and headquartered in Indianapolis, acquired by Wipro for USD 500 million in 2016 and now operating as "Appirio, a Wipro company." Appirio is a strategic implementation partner for Salesforce, Workday, Google, and Amazon, helping over 3,000 enterprises across healthcare and life sciences, banking, higher education, manufacturing, and retail adopt cloud-based solutions. Its services span Salesforce ecosystem consulting, CRM and platform implementation, cloud application development, and digital transformation. Appirio is a consulting and systems-integration firm rather than an API producer: it does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or a developer portal, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: Application Environment Verification
providers.description: Android library and API to verify the safety of user devices, detect rooted devices and other risks

providers.name: Applimation
providers.description: Applimation was a provider of application Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) and enterprise data archiving software for packaged applications including SAP (ERP, HR, CRM, SRM, SCM, APO) and Oracle environments, helping customers manage the full data lifecycle from test-data management through archiving of inactive data to lower storage and database costs and improve application performance. Informatica acquired Applimation for approximately $40 million in an agreement announced in February 2009, folding its ILM and database-archiving technology into Informatica's data management portfolio. Applimation no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer surface, API, or documentation.

providers.name: Appurify
