providers.description: Appurify was a mobile app and website testing platform that let developers automate testing and optimization of native and web apps on real iOS and Android devices across OS versions and simulated network conditions. Founded and backed by DCVC and GV, Appurify was acquired by Google in June 2014 and its technology was folded into Firebase Test Lab (formerly Google Cloud Test Lab). The company no longer operates independently; the appurify.com domain now redirects to the Firebase Test Lab documentation and Appurify's standalone developer API and product have been discontinued.

providers.name: Apropose
providers.description: Apropose, Inc. was a Mountain View, California startup spun out of the Stanford University Computer Science Department in 2013 to bring data-driven software to web design. Founded by Ranjitha Kumar, Jerry Talton, Maxine Lim, and Arvind Satyanarayan, the company built tools for large-scale visual page search and web design analytics — letting teams track design trends, compare a site's design against demographics, and surface prevalent design patterns to inject concrete data into the design process. It raised a roughly $1.875M seed round in 2014 led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA) and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), with angels including Pat Hanrahan and Nick McKeown. The company has since ceased operations and is permanently closed; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and its primary domain (apropose.com) is now parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained as an a16z portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Apsalar
providers.description: Apsalar was a mobile marketing analytics and attribution company (founded 2010, headquartered in San Francisco, backed by Battery Ventures and 500 Startups/500 Global) that provided a mobile measurement platform (MMP) for app install attribution, campaign analytics, and marketing data unification. In 2017 Apsalar merged into Singular (singular.net); the Apsalar brand and its developer/API surface were retired as part of that acquisition. The apsalar.com apex domain no longer resolves to a live site and www.apsalar.com now redirects to Singular, so there is no active first-party API, OpenAPI, or developer portal to enrich. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead pointing to its successor, Singular.

providers.name: Apteligent
providers.description: Apteligent (originally Crittercism, founded 2011 by Andrew Levy, Robert Kwok, and Jeeyun Kim, rebranded to Apteligent in 2016) was a mobile application performance management platform that provided real-time crash reporting, diagnostics, service monitoring, and user-engagement analytics across iOS, Android, hybrid, and HTML5 apps. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Opus Capital, and Shasta Ventures (~$48.7M raised), the company was acquired by VMware on 2017-05-15 and folded into the Workspace ONE digital-workspace platform. Following VMware's 2024 end-user-computing spin-off, the technology now ships under the Omnissa Intelligence brand. The independent Apteligent developer surface has been retired: apteligent.com no longer resolves at the apex and www.apteligent.com 301-redirects to omnissa.com; there is no live standalone API, documentation, or developer portal to enrich.

providers.name: AquaShield
providers.description: AquaShield is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26 batch) startup building AI-driven water leak detection for buildings and large real estate portfolios. Non-invasive sensors clamp onto existing pipes in minutes with no pipe cutting, retrofits, or downtime; the platform learns each building's normal water-flow patterns and flags anomalies in real time before they escalate into costly damage. Water damage is the largest preventable loss in real estate — more than fire and theft combined. Founded by former MIT and Harvard/EPFL robotics researchers Paul Beckers (CEO) and Marguerite Benoist (CTO), the company is based in San Francisco and works with some of the largest residential portfolios in the world. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; AquaShield currently publishes a marketing site only and does not yet expose a public API or developer program.

providers.name: ArbiLex
providers.description: ArbiLex is a legal-fintech startup founded at the Harvard Innovation Labs in 2018 by Isabel Yang that brings AI and predictive analytics to high-stakes international arbitration and litigation finance. Its Bayesian machine learning and NLP models — trained on a dataset of over nine million cases — produce empirical, explainable case ratings that help counsel quantify uncertainty, reduce errors, and value claims. ArbiLex also operates the ArbiLex Funding Exchange (AFX), a data-driven marketplace pairing AI-rated cases with litigation-finance capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; no public developer API surface was found at time of enrichment.

providers.name: Arbor Software
providers.description: Arbor Software Corporation was an enterprise business-intelligence and OLAP software company founded in 1991 in Sunnyvale, California by Bob Earle and Jim Dorian. It created Essbase, the pioneering multidimensional online-analytical-processing (OLAP) server first released in 1992, and went public on NASDAQ under the ticker ARSW in 1995. Arbor merged with Hyperion Software in 1998 to form Hyperion Solutions Corporation, which Oracle Corporation acquired in 2007; the Essbase technology lives on inside Oracle. Arbor Software no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface, so there is nothing to enrich.

providers.name: Ares Interactive
providers.description: Ares Interactive is a game developer and publisher founded in 2024 by veteran industry leaders, operating studios in San Francisco and Berlin. The company builds player-first games designed to evolve with their communities and grow into enduring franchises, with a current portfolio that includes Baseball Hits, Heroes vs. Hordes, and The Walking Dead: Aftermath. Ares Interactive is backed by General Catalyst and was added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer/gaming portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and careers website but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Arilinc
providers.description: Aril Inc. (Arilinc) is a fabless semiconductor company in Los Gatos, California designing efficient AI processors and memory technology for edge inference. Its two core products are the Aril Standard Cell Memory, a patented on-chip memory offering roughly 40% lower active power and 3.6x smaller area, and a scalable RISC-V-based AI Processor Engine delivering hundreds of TOPS of inference per block with integrated vector and matrix engines. The company targets robotics, industrial automation, drones, defense and aerospace, autonomous vehicles, and edge vision systems where power efficiency is critical. Founded by a team of engineers who have collectively shipped 20M+ processors and worked on silicon for Cisco, Intel, AMD, and Google. Arilinc sells custom silicon and IP to hardware makers rather than a public developer API; it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Arimo
providers.description: Arimo (formerly Adatao) was a Palo Alto, California AI and big-data startup building a distributed deep-learning and "Behavioral AI" analytics platform on top of Apache Spark, backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Bloomberg Beta. The company was acquired by Panasonic in 2017 and folded into Panasonic's AI/innovation efforts, and it no longer operates as an independent provider. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead for the API Evangelist network, this profile has no surviving developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich - the arimo.com and arimo.ai domains no longer resolve.

providers.name: Ario
providers.description: Ario is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures, wing-venture-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ai-apps. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Ark.com
providers.description: Ark.com was a people search engine founded in San Francisco in March 2012 by Patrick Riley and Yiming Liu, and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2012 batch. Ark indexed over a billion public social network profiles — aggregating "ghost profiles" from Facebook, LinkedIn, AngelList and other networks — and let users search across them with filters such as hometown, current city, high school, college, employer and interests, to reconnect with classmates and acquaintances or find new business contacts. The company raised a $4.2M seed round in April 2012 from Andreessen Horowitz, Greylock Partners and SV Angel, and reached the finals of TechCrunch Disrupt NYC 2012. Ark is no longer operating: Y Combinator lists the company as Inactive and PitchBook lists it as Out of Business. As of a July 2026 probe the ark.com domain no longer serves the company — it redirects to www.ark-invest.com, the unrelated ARK Investment Management site — and no api., developer. or docs. subdomain resolves. Ark never published a public API, developer portal or SDKs, so there is no API surface to catalog. Retained as a historical a16z portfolio record only.

providers.name: ArrowPoint
providers.description: ArrowPoint Communications, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARPT) was a networking company based in Acton, Massachusetts that built content switches — Layer 4-7 "web switches" that inspected HTTP content, cookies and URLs to route and load-balance traffic across web server farms, CDNs and hosting providers. Founded in 1997 and backed by Matrix Partners, North Bridge Venture Partners and Accel Partners, it IPO'd in early 2000 and was acquired by Cisco Systems in a stock deal announced 2000-05-05 and completed 2000-06-23, valued at roughly $5.7 billion. Its CSS 11000 series and WebNS software became a Cisco product line that has since reached end-of-life and been retired. ArrowPoint no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no documentation, no APIs and no SDKs, and the arrowpoint.com domain — still delegated to Cisco nameservers — serves no live web or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Matrix Partners portfolio exit.

providers.name: ArrowPoint Communications
providers.description: ArrowPoint Communications, Inc. was a Massachusetts-based content-networking company that built "content smart" web switches for server load balancing, content delivery, and web caching in the late 1990s. After a January 2000 IPO it was acquired by Cisco Systems in 2000 for approximately $5.7 billion in stock, and its technology became the basis of the Cisco Content Services Switch (CSS) product line. It has not operated as an independent company since the acquisition, and it exposes no public developer program, API, documentation, or other machine-readable surface today; this record is retained for network/portfolio lineage rather than active API enrichment.

providers.name: Artillery Games
providers.description: Artillery Games (also known as Artillery) was an early-stage technology startup backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) that built browser-based, real-time multiplayer strategy games and an associated JavaScript game engine. The company was acquired by GitHub in 2017 and no longer operates as an independent entity; its former artillery.com domain now redirects to a domain-sale marketplace. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead, but exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or other surface to enrich via the pipeline.

providers.name: Artivest
providers.description: Artivest was a New York-based alternative investments technology company founded in 2012 that gave financial advisors and high-net-worth investors a curated digital experience for discovering, evaluating, and subscribing to private investment funds, including its "Open Network" platform serving roughly 1,800 advisors and management of 28 proprietary alternative investment funds. iCapital Network announced the acquisition of substantially all of Artivest's assets — technology, operating platform, fund management, and enterprise relationships — on 2020-05-13 and closed the transaction in August 2020. The Artivest brand, platform, and public web presence were fully absorbed into iCapital; as of this enrichment pass artivest.co does not resolve and artivest.com is registered to an unrelated third party. Artivest never published a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts, and there is no live surface remaining to enrich.

providers.name: asgoodasnew
providers.description: asgoodasnew is a German e-commerce retailer of refurbished and pre-owned consumer electronics, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, cameras, and related accessories, sold with warranty through its online store at asgoodasnew.de (asgoodasnew.com redirects there). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Probing the public surface found no developer portal, API documentation, or API host — this is a consumer-facing storefront with no public API program at this time. The profile is retained as a portfolio lead; only mechanical domain-security signals for the web host could be captured.

providers.name: Associated Content
providers.description: Associated Content was an open content publishing platform founded in 2005 by Luke Beatty that paid contributors to publish articles, video, audio, and images on any topic, then distributed that library through associatedcontent.com and a network of syndication partners. At its peak it hosted over one million pieces of content from roughly 250,000 contributors and adopted Thomson Reuters OpenCalais for automated classification of that library. It raised a $5.4M Series A from SoftBank Capital (2006), a $10M Series B from SoftBank, Canaan Partners, and Tim Armstrong (2007), and $6M more in 2009, before Yahoo acquired it in May 2010. Yahoo rebranded the property as Yahoo Voices in December 2011 and shut it down on July 31, 2014, retiring the Yahoo Contributor Network the following month. The company is defunct: it never published a public developer API, and associatedcontent.com is now a parked domain that refuses HTTPS.

providers.name: Astrid *
providers.description: Astrid was a popular cross-platform social to-do list and task-management app (Todoroo, Inc.), known for its Android and web productivity service and a lightweight task-sync API. It was a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the consumer sector. Yahoo acquired the Astrid team in May 2013 and discontinued the service later that year; the astrid.com domain now resolves to Yahoo and the original developer surface (apidoc / api_keys) is dead. The Android client was open-sourced (todoroo/astrid) and later revived by the community as tasks.org (tasks/tasks). No live first-party API, developer portal, or documentation exists to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct portfolio lead.

providers.name: Atexto
providers.description: Atexto was a speech-recognition data company (self-described "the accuracy platform for speech recognition") based in Mexico City, founded around 2016 by Brenda Mana Pastrian and Esteban Gorupicz. It helped machine-learning and voice-assistant teams create, collect, annotate, transcribe, and benchmark audio/speech datasets, combining an enterprise data platform with a global paid crowdsourcing community that transcribed and labeled audio across roughly 24 languages and their regional accents. The company also offered a hybrid human-plus-machine audio-to-text transcription service and ASR training-data services. It was backed by 500 Global, Redwood Ventures, MC Capital, and a Start-Up Chile grant. The company now appears inactive: its former domain atexto.com has been repurposed to an unrelated third-party site, and no live developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification could be located. This profile captures verified historical identity only; no API artifacts were enriched because no live API surface exists.

providers.name: AtheroMed
providers.description: AtheroMed, Inc. was a privately-held medical device company based in Menlo Park, California, founded to treat peripheral artery disease (PAD). Its sole product was the Phoenix Atherectomy System, an over-the-wire, low-profile atherectomy catheter that uses a rotating front-cutting element at the distal tip to shave diseased material directly into the catheter, where an internal Archimedes screw continuously captures and removes the debulked material without requiring specialized capital equipment. The Phoenix system received FDA 510(k) clearance in January 2014 and CE Mark approval in Europe. AtheroMed was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and U.S. Venture Partners, and was acquired by Volcano Corporation in June 2014 for $115 million upfront plus milestone payments; Volcano was in turn acquired by Royal Philips in February 2015. AtheroMed no longer operates as an independent company, its atheromed.com domain is parked and listed for sale, and it has no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind. The Phoenix catheter is now sold as a Philips Volcano product.

providers.name: Athletes First
providers.description: Athletes First is a full-service sports representation and management agency founded in 2001 and headquartered in Southern California, with additional offices in New York City, Gainesville, Austin, and Atlanta. The firm represents elite NFL players, coaches, front-office executives, collegiate athletes, and sports broadcasters, and operates specialized departments spanning football contract negotiation, career management, pre-draft preparation, talent marketing and brand building, broadcasting and new media, media development and sales, and properties and events. In February 2023, Mastry Ventures in partnership with General Catalyst acquired a majority stake in the agency. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company (sector: consumer) and added to the API Evangelist network. Athletes First publishes no public developer, API, or technical surface.

providers.name: AtmoSec
providers.description: AtmoSec was an Israel-based SaaS security startup founded in January 2021 that built a platform for securing hyperconnected SaaS ecosystems. Its technology discovered authorized and shadow SaaS applications, controlled risky SaaS-to-SaaS and third-party OAuth app communication, detected and disconnected malicious apps, remediated SaaS misconfigurations, and governed non-human identities (API keys, OAuth apps, service accounts, and tokens) via native IAM APIs. Founded by former Armis and Google executives and backed by Battery Ventures and Glilot Capital, AtmoSec was acquired by Check Point Software Technologies in September 2023 and folded into the Check Point Infinity / SASE platform for continuous SaaS posture management. It no longer operates as a standalone company and publishes no public developer API; atmosec.com now redirects into checkpoint.com.

providers.name: Atrisa
providers.description: Atrisa (formerly Refortifai) is a Y Combinator (P26) startup building AI agents for analog circuit design. The product is a chat-based assistant engineer that lets hardware and analog design teams ask it, in natural language, to create a design, debug a circuit, or run simulations. Atrisa is designed to fit into existing workflows: teams bring their own toolkit, PDKs (process design kits), and design documents, which Atrisa reads, understands, and adopts to produce schematic-level outputs and iterate on analog designs. As an early-stage company it currently ships a hosted web application rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public surface pending any future API release.

providers.name: atSpoke
providers.description: atSpoke was a modern workplace service desk / internal helpdesk SaaS (formerly askSpoke) that let teams triage and resolve employee support requests across HR, IT, and operations. It was a portfolio company of Accel and was acquired by Okta in August 2021 for approximately $90M to seed Okta's identity governance (IGA) roadmap. The standalone atSpoke product and its entire domain footprint have since been sunset: atspoke.com, askspoke.com, help.atspoke.com and the former public API host api.askspoke.com/api/v1 no longer resolve or serve. This profile is retained as a historical network record; there is no live developer surface left to enrich.

providers.name: Auditude
providers.description: Auditude was a Palo Alto video advertising technology company founded in 2007 that let premium publishers, content owners and media companies manage, serve and monetize advertising around online video across multiple platforms and devices via its proprietary Auditude Connect platform. Backed by Redpoint Ventures and Greylock Partners with roughly $38M raised, its customers included Comcast, Sony Music and Universal Music Group. Adobe acquired Auditude in November 2011 for a reported ~$120M and folded the technology into Adobe Primetime (ad decisioning / ad insertion), since rebranded under Adobe Pass. Auditude no longer operates as an independent company: auditude.com does not resolve, and the only surviving public footprint is the legacy com.auditude.ads.* namespace inside Adobe's Primetime Player SDK documentation. This profile is retained as a defunct / acquired historical record; there is no Auditude API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Audos
providers.description: Audos is a New York-based AI-native startup studio and "publishing house for everyday entrepreneurs," founded in 2024 by Henrik Werdelin and Nicholas Thorne (the team behind Prehype, BarkBox, Ro, and Managed by Q). It helps non-technical solo founders turn expertise into million-dollar AI businesses, giving them AI-powered business-building tools, up to $25,000 in funding, and paid-social distribution in exchange for a ~15% revenue share, aiming to launch startups at massive scale. Audos raised an $11.5M seed round led by True Ventures (with backing from Niklas Zennstrom) and acquired No Cap. Its product surface is a consumer/entrepreneur web platform; the api.audos.com backend is private and auth-gated, with no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Augur
providers.description: Augur, Inc. was a Boulder, Colorado startup (founded 2012) that offered a cross-device attribution API using machine learning to recognize a unique device and its owner across laptops, phones, and tablets without relying on cookies, serving ad-tech and security customers to personalize experiences and improve conversion. Techstars-backed (also iGan Partners and Right Side Capital), Augur raised roughly $1.16M before being acquired by Wunderkind (formerly Bounce Exchange / BounceX) on 2017-05-04. The augur.io domain no longer resolves to a live product origin (Cloudflare edge returns HTTP 522) and no developer portal, API reference, or SDKs remain publicly reachable, so this profile is retained as an inactive/acquired historical record rather than a live API provider.

providers.name: Aurigin Systems
providers.description: Aurigin Systems, Inc. was an intellectual-property management software company founded in 1992 and headquartered in Cupertino, California. It built online patent and trademark information services and business-automation software for intellectual-asset management, raising roughly $54M in venture funding (investors included Battery Ventures) over its lifetime. The company operated under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection before substantially all of its assets were acquired by Information Holdings Inc. in May 2002. It is defunct, has no surviving website, developer portal, or public API, and was surfaced only as a historical portfolio lead from a Battery Ventures scrape.

providers.name: Aurora Therapeutics
providers.description: Aurora Therapeutics is a CRISPR gene-editing biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing scalable, personalized genetic medicines for rare diseases. Founded by gene-editing pioneers including Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Fyodor Urnov and led by CEO Edward M. Kaye, the company uses an "umbrella" approach that bundles multiple rare disease-causing mutations under a single regulatory pathway, combining guide RNA design, AI-engineered editors, and delivery systems to correct mutations at scale. Backed by Menlo Ventures, Aurora is profiled in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass it publishes a corporate website and news surface but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other technical/developer surface.

providers.name: Autobutler
providers.description: Autobutler is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Autochess VNG
providers.description: Rest Api for Autochess VNG

providers.name: Automatic Labs
providers.description: Automatic Labs was a connected-car company (the Automatic OBD-II adapter and companion app plus a developer platform / REST API for trip, vehicle, and driving-behavior data), founded circa 2011 and backed by a16z. It was acquired by SiriusXM in 2017 and wound down: the service and its developer API were discontinued around May 2020. As of this enrichment pass the automatic.com domain (and its api./developer. subdomains) 301-redirects to automattic.com, the unrelated WordPress company, so no live API, documentation, or developer surface remains to harvest. This profile is retained as a defunct a16z portfolio lead.

providers.name: AutoTrader.com
providers.description: AutoTrader.com is an American online automotive marketplace headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, and owned by Cox Automotive. Launched in 1997, it connects car buyers and sellers by aggregating listings for new, used, and certified pre-owned vehicles from franchise dealers, independent dealers, and private sellers. The site provides vehicle search and comparison, pricing and valuation tools, financing and trade-in estimates, dealer reviews, and lead-generation connections between shoppers and dealerships. It is a consumer-facing marketplace and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile tracks its public web and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Avegant
providers.description: Avegant is an augmented reality display technology company that develops light engine technology bringing high-performance visuals to lightweight AR glasses designed for everyday wear. Its flagship product, the AG-30L2 LED light engine, is described as the world's smallest LED light engine for augmented reality. Avegant is a venture-backed hardware company (a portfolio company of 500 Global) focused on the optical and display components that power the next generation of AR eyewear rather than on a public developer platform. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Avere Systems
providers.description: Avere Systems was a Pittsburgh-based enterprise storage company building hybrid cloud NAS technology, best known for its FXT Series Edge filers and the vFXT virtual appliance that accelerated and tiered file workloads across on-premises NAS and public cloud object storage. The company was acquired by Microsoft in January 2018 and folded into Microsoft Azure, where the technology lives on as Avere vFXT for Azure. Avere Systems no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal or public API of its own; its former domain (averesystems.com) now 301-redirects to Microsoft's Avere landing page.

providers.name: Avnera
providers.description: Avnera Corporation was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon, that designed low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits and audio system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for wireless headphones, headsets, soundbars, speakers, and gaming audio devices. Backed by venture investors including Redpoint Ventures, Avnera was acquired by Skyworks Solutions in 2017 and now operates as part of Skyworks. It maintains no independent developer program or public API surface; the avnera.com domain resolves to a parked/inactive page with no product site.

providers.name: AVS
providers.description: AVS (listed by Battery Ventures as "AVS, Inc.") is a former Battery Ventures portfolio company. Battery's public list of all companies marks the entry with an asterisk, which its own legend defines as "Denotes an exited investment," so AVS is a historical holding rather than an active one. Enrichment research on 2026-07-20 — Battery's company list and WordPress API, targeted web search, and probes of battery.com/company/avs and battery.com/portfolio/avs (both HTTP 404) — surfaced no company website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API, specification, SDK, or other machine-readable artifact that can be attributed to this specific AVS with confidence. The name is heavily overloaded across unrelated firms (medical device, life-science services, audio-visual, voice recognition), and none of those could be tied back to the Battery investment. This profile is therefore retained as an identity-only record with no API surface; it is not a scored API provider.

providers.name: Awake
providers.description: Awake Security was a cybersecurity company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, backed by Greylock Partners. Its network detection and response (NDR) platform applied network traffic analysis, behavioral modeling, and entity resolution to surface malicious activity, insider threats, and compromised devices across enterprise, IoT, and cloud environments without requiring endpoint agents. Arista Networks acquired Awake Security in October 2020 and the technology now ships as Arista NDR. This company profile was surfaced as a Greylock portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the standalone awakesecurity.com domain is behind a bot-challenge and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Awake Security (Arista Networks)
providers.description: Awake Security was a network detection and response (NDR) company founded in 2014 that used AI and machine learning to analyze network traffic and detect threats, compromised devices, and malicious insiders without relying on agents or signatures. Arista Networks acquired Awake Security in 2020 and the technology now ships as Arista NDR within Arista's security portfolio. The former awakesecurity.com domain redirects to Arista's security solutions site; the product has no distinct public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or SDK program of its own. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures. Sector: security.

providers.name: Awavesemi
providers.description: Awavesemi (Awave Semiconductor) is a semiconductor company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass, its domain awavesemi.com issues a 301 redirect to https://www.qualcomm.com/data-center, indicating the company and its data-center silicon effort have been absorbed into Qualcomm. Awavesemi publishes no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or MCP surface — it is a hardware/silicon company, not an API provider, so the enrichment pipeline finds no API artifacts to harvest beyond domain-level security posture.

providers.name: Axelrod
providers.description: Axelrod is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an autonomous operating layer for boutique, independent, and luxury hotels and resorts. Its software runs daily front-of-house and back-of-house operations, coordinating arrivals, rooms, rates, access, maintenance, supplies, and owner reporting inside the systems and teams a property already has in place, integrating with existing PMS, channel, pricing, and accounting platforms rather than requiring net-new tooling. Founded by Adrian Stoica and Saman Sayahpour, the company markets itself as "boutique hotels that run themselves" and reports being live across four continents with Michelin Key awarded and Marriott Luxury Collection properties. Axelrod does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Axiometrix Solutions
providers.description: Axiometrix Solutions is a global test and measurement company serving technology-intensive industries through three specialist brands - GRAS Sound & Vibration (acoustic and vibration sensors for challenging environments), imc Test & Measurement (modular data acquisition, signal conditioning, and shock/vibration solutions), and Audio Precision (audio and RF analyzers for quality validation). Its integrated portfolio of sensors, data acquisition systems, control software, analysis software, and test fixtures supports advanced research, R&D, and production/manufacturing test across aerospace, defense, automotive, consumer electronics, audiology and medical technology, communications, semiconductor, and environmental monitoring markets. Backed by Battery Ventures. No public web API or developer program has been identified for this provider.

providers.name: Axis Network Technology
providers.description: Axis (axisnet.asia) is a Malaysia-based e-commerce enabler, incorporated in 2009, providing an end-to-end managed e-commerce solution that consolidates business digitalization, inventory solutions, automated e-fulfillment, express and cross-border logistics across 98+ countries, e-commerce marketing, multi-marketplace selling, and training via Axis Academy for individuals and SMEs. It was surfaced as a portfolio lead of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Axis Security
providers.description: Axis Security was a Security Service Edge (SSE) and Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) vendor founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, with research and development in Israel. Its cloud-delivered Atmos platform combined ZTNA, a Secure Web Gateway (SWG), Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) controls, and digital experience monitoring to connect users to private applications and the internet without a traditional VPN. The company was backed by Canaan Partners, Ten Eleven Ventures, Cisco Investments, and Dell Technologies Capital, and was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Aruba Networking in 2023, where the Atmos technology now lives on as HPE Aruba Networking SSE. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead; the standalone axissecurity.com developer surface has been decommissioned following the acquisition, so no live API or developer portal is currently published under the Axis Security brand.

providers.name: Axon
providers.description: Axon is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building real-time predictive intelligence on a brain-inspired architecture. Its approach centers on small, efficient "world models" that learn continuously on-device rather than depending on large models or the cloud, giving an edge-first design lower latency and lower cost. The initial focus is high-frequency trading and capital markets, where real-time prediction is decisive, with future applications targeted at wearables, edge devices, and robotics. Axon is backed by Northzone, Concept Ventures, a16z Speedrun, and EWOR. As of this profile the company is pre-product with no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal; this repository tracks it in the API Evangelist network for enrichment as its developer surface emerges.

providers.name: Azarus
providers.description: Azarus was a consumer startup that built an interactive engagement and rewards layer for live game streaming and esports, letting viewers take part in real-time interactive experiences and earn blockchain-based crypto rewards while watching streams on platforms like Twitch. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Azarus was acquired by Coinbase in April 2021 to build interactive experiences into its consumer products. The former azarus.io domain now 302-redirects to a YouTube video and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, packages, or other machine-readable surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead with no live API to enrich.

providers.name: B2B-Center
providers.description: B2B-Center is one of Russia's largest electronic trading platforms (ETP) for business-to-business procurement, operating at b2b-center.ru. The platform hosts electronic tenders, auctions, and competitive sourcing procedures that connect corporate and commercial buyers with a broad network of suppliers across many industries. It provides tools for organizing purchases, publishing procurement notices, qualifying and managing suppliers, and running the full electronic bidding lifecycle. B2B-Center is backed by Insight Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company awaiting deeper enrichment.

providers.name: Babel Finance
providers.description: Babel Finance was a Hong Kong-based crypto financial services provider offering crypto asset lending and borrowing, asset management, brokerage and derivatives trading, and mining-related financing to institutional and high-net-worth clients. It reached a USD 2B valuation on an USD 80M Series B in May 2022 with backing that included Multicoin Capital, then froze customer redemptions and withdrawals weeks later in June 2022 amid the Three Arrows Capital and Celsius contagion. The company disclosed roughly USD 766M in losses, pursued a Singapore court moratorium and a scheme of arrangement, and floated a crypto-backed stablecoin to repay creditors. As of this enrichment pass the company is listed as permanently closed and its primary domain babel.finance no longer resolves (no NS delegation), so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct crypto-lending provider.

providers.name: Babycare
providers.description: Babycare is a Chinese mother-and-baby (母婴) consumer brand offering a broad range of maternity and infant-care products, including diapers, wipes, strollers, baby carriers, feeding bottles, toys, and maternal care goods. It operates primarily as a direct-to-consumer brand, selling through major Chinese e-commerce marketplaces (Tmall, JD.com, Douyin) alongside its own channels and offline retail, and is one of the leading new-generation mother-baby brands in China. Babycare is backed by venture investor Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). This profile is a consumer-brand entry in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been identified for this provider.

providers.name: Backtype
providers.description: BackType was a San Francisco social-media analytics startup (backed by 500 Startups/500 Global) whose BackTweets product helped publishers measure the reach and conversion of their Tweets and content for clients including The New York Times, HubSpot, bitly, and SlideShare. The BackType team also built Storm, the distributed real-time stream-processing system later open-sourced as Apache Storm. Twitter acquired BackType on July 5, 2011 and folded the team into its platform group; the standalone product and public API were discontinued after the acquisition. The company is defunct and backtype.com is now a parked domain, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: BackWeb
providers.description: BackWeb Technologies Ltd. was an Israeli-American enterprise software company founded in 1995 by Eli Barkat, Nir Barkat, Yuval Rakavy, Iftah Sneh and Lior Hass, with offices in Ramat Gan, Israel and San Jose, California. BackWeb pioneered "Polite" push technology — background delivery of software updates, patches, alerts and marketing content to desktops using only idle bandwidth so it did not disrupt the user or the corporate network. Its Polite Communication Server, Offline Access Server, e-Accelerator and Proactive Portal products were deployed by Cisco, Hewlett-Packard, IBM, Ericsson, Compaq and SAP, and integrators used the BackWeb Server Extension API and BackWeb Automation SDK to publish content from external data sources into the Polite server. The company IPO'd on NASDAQ (BWEB) in June 1999 after raising roughly $13M privately from investors including Goldman Sachs, Intel and Trinity Ventures, peaking near $38M in annual revenue. It never recovered from the dot-com collapse, was delisted from NASDAQ and moved to the OTC Bulletin Board, approved a voluntary liquidation in 2012, suspended operations and divested its patents in 2014, and began distributing remaining cash to shareholders. BackWeb is defunct: there is no operating company, no developer portal, and no live API. The backweb.com domain is a parked Afternic for-sale lander. This profile is retained as a historical record only.

providers.name: Baicai
providers.description: Baicai (白菜二手车, "Baicai Used Cars") is a Chinese used-vehicle trading platform operating a new-retail model that pairs online used-car marketplaces with offline chain "used-car supermarket" stores. Vehicles listed on the platform are inspected by third-party agencies (100+ point checks that exclude major accident, water-damaged, and fire-damaged cars) and carry a return guarantee plus a warranty on major components. The business was spun out of and operates under 58.com (via Tianjin 58 Cloud Car / 天津五八云车) and became independently operated in 2021. It received early seed backing from Ribbit Capital. Baicai is a consumer-facing marketplace and does not publish a public developer platform, API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and public web presence for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Baker Technologies
providers.description: Baker Technologies (Baker) was a Denver, Colorado based customer relationship management (CRM) and marketing platform built for the cannabis industry, founded in 2014 by David Champion, Joel Milton, and Roger Obando. A graduate of the 500 Startups accelerator, Baker helped licensed dispensaries grow revenue and build customer relationships through online ordering, loyalty programs, SMS/text messaging, and analytics, and launched an expanded integrations program with a developer API connecting dispensaries to 20+ ancillary cannabis services. The company raised approximately $11.75M (including an $8M Series A) before being acquired by TILT Holdings in 2018. The trybaker.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, indicating the product has been discontinued; no live developer portal, API documentation, or specifications are publicly available.

providers.name: BAMA TEA
providers.description: BAMA TEA (八马茶业), a brand of Fujian Bama Tea Industry Co., Ltd., is a large-scale Chinese tea enterprise founded in 1997 and headquartered in Anxi County, Quanzhou, Fujian Province. It integrates tea plantation cultivation, production and processing, branded retail-chain distribution, and export, and is best known for Tieguanyin oolong. The company operates a nationwide network of branded retail stores across China and sells oolong, black, green, white, and dark teas. It is a publicly listed company and a portfolio investment of IDG Capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector lead: BAMA TEA publishes a consumer e-commerce website but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so the API-artifact enrichment recipes do not apply.

providers.name: BANIQL CORP.
providers.description: BANIQL CORP. (BANiQL) is developing a sustainable process for selectively extracting nickel and cobalt for use in lithium-ion battery production. Its core technology uses a chemical process to selectively extract nickel and cobalt from raw materials at lower temperatures and atmospheric pressure, producing high-quality nickel at roughly 30% lower cost than High Pressure Acid Leaching (HPAL) with net-zero waste, cutting energy consumption and carbon dioxide emissions by around 80% while repurposing leftover materials into products like fertilizers and construction materials. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; this materials/cleantech company publishes no developer or API surface, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security data only.

providers.name: BankOns
providers.description: BankOns was a San Mateo, California mobile savings startup founded in the summer of 2010 by Joshua Greenough, a former VP of Operations at PowerReviews. Launched in May 2011, the app connected a user's bank transaction history to their location, analyzing spending habits to surface the nearby merchant deals and rewards best suited to them, drawing on Foursquare and other local deals data. The name was a contraction of "bank" and "coupons". BankOns was seed funded by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) plus a friends-and-family round. In May 2012 Capital One acquired select BankOns software through a limited asset purchase agreement, and several team members including Greenough joined Capital One Labs. The product was wound down and the company no longer operates a consumer service or a developer platform. The bankons.com domain resolves to a GoDaddy parking lander with no content, and no API, documentation, SDK, or developer surface exists.

providers.name: baoyugame
providers.description: baoyugame (Guangzhou Baoyou Network Technology) is a Chinese game development and publishing studio founded in 2011 and headquartered in Guangzhou, focused on the research and development of mobile games and web (browser) games. Its founding team came from established studios including NetEase, and it operates multiple internal game studios with a development team of roughly 100 people, shipping turn-based RPG, ARPG, and strategy titles. The company is venture-backed, appearing in the portfolios of Qiming Venture Partners, Morningside Venture Capital, and Jiuhe Capital. baoyugame publishes a consumer game website only and exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface, so this profile carries company identity rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Barneyscan
providers.description: Barneyscan was a San Leandro, California color imaging company founded in 1986 that built one of the first high-quality 24-bit color film scanners and related graphic-arts software for the press and prepress industry. It is best known as the origin of Adobe Photoshop, whose early version 0.87 shipped bundled with Barneyscan scanners as "Barneyscan XP" before Adobe licensed it. Backed by Battery Ventures, Bay Partners, and OSCCO Ventures, the company was acquired by PixelCraft on March 1, 1993 and no longer operates. It has no live website, developer portal, or public API surface, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Barter.VG
providers.description: Provides information about Game, DLC, Bundles, Giveaways, Trading

providers.name: Basalt
providers.description: Basalt (Basalt Technologies Corp.) is a San Francisco spacecraft-software company building Dispatch, a simulation-based operating system for satellites that makes flight software portable across dissimilar spacecraft hardware — pitched as "Windows for spacecraft" and "Constellations as a Service." Dispatch provides a common control layer so fleets of different satellites can work together on tasking (visible, infrared, and radar imaging), in-orbit networking and telecom, signals intelligence, and monitoring or inspecting other on-orbit assets, including autonomous re-tasking for national security missions. Founded in 2023 by Max Bhatti and Alex Choi (ex-SpaceX engineers, MIT CubeSat program), Basalt is a Y Combinator W24 company that raised a $3.5M seed round led by Initialized Capital in May 2024, with participation from Y Combinator, Liquid 2 Ventures, and General Catalyst. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security. Sector: frontier-tech / space / defense.

providers.name: Bass Associates
providers.description: Bass Associates is an early- and growth-stage venture capital firm historically based at 435 Tasso Street, Palo Alto, California, and appears on the Battery Ventures "list of all companies" as an exited entry. Public investor databases record roughly 32 investments and 10 exits alongside co-investors such as Accel Partners, Kleiner Perkins and CRV, with its last recorded investment (Teloquent, growth equity) in January 2002 and its last recorded exit in December 2003. The 2026 enrichment pass found no operating website, no developer portal, no documentation and no API surface of any kind: the firm appears dormant and is not an API provider. It was surfaced into the API Evangelist network by the VC-portfolio crawl as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead, but the underlying entity is itself an investor rather than an operating software company.

providers.name: Baton
providers.description: Baton is a supply-chain and logistics technology company that operates as Ryder System's Silicon Valley innovation lab following its 2022 acquisition. Founded in 2019 out of 8VC's build program, Baton originally built a network of freight "drop zones" that let long-haul truckers hand off loads for local pickup and delivery, coordinating vehicles, drop zones, warehouses, and local drivers. Today the team builds RyderShare, a collaborative logistics platform combining real-time supply-chain visibility with exception management across shipments in transit. As of this enrichment pass, baton.io publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or integration surface (the site exposes only marketing and careers pages); this profile is maintained for network discovery.

providers.name: Battlebound
providers.description: Battlebound was a Los Angeles-based blockchain / play-to-earn game studio founded in May 2021 by former Riot Games technical artist Adam Hensel (pseudonym Damos), with a team drawn from Blizzard, Ubisoft, NCSoft and Riot Games. In March 2022 it raised a $4.8M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from Play Ventures and Dapper Labs. Its titles were Evaverse, a Steam-published social metaverse game using NFTs as playable avatars, and an in-development RPG codenamed Anterris (also referenced as "Project A"). The studio wound down amid the collapse of the web3 gaming market; as of 2025 it is defunct and the battlebound.com domain is parked and listed for sale. The company never published a public API, SDK, or developer platform, so there is no API surface to catalog or enrich.

providers.name: BBA
providers.description: BBA is a name-only entry harvested from the Andreessen Horowitz public investment list (https://a16z.com/investment-list/), where it appears alphabetically between Bayesian Health and Beacons.ai. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the entry could not be resolved to an operating company: a16z publishes no link, description, or category for it, the name does not appear in the a16z portfolio detail pages, and web searches surface no startup, funding round, or press coverage matching it. Candidate domains (bba.com, bba.ai, bba.co, getbba.com) either fail to resolve or are parked for sale, so there is no website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to profile. This profile is retained as an unresolved venture-portfolio lead rather than an API provider; it should be re-checked if a16z ever attaches a link to the entry or the company emerges publicly under this name.

providers.name: BBN
providers.description: BBN (RTX BBN Technologies, formerly BBN Technologies and Raytheon BBN) is an American research and development organization based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1948 and now a division of RTX Corporation. BBN has a storied history in computer networking, having built the original ARPANET Interface Message Processors and pioneered early email. Today it delivers advanced technology for national security across AI and machine learning, all-domain command and control, applied biosciences, cyber operations, spectrum dominance, maritime autonomy, multi-domain sensing, resilient networking, planning and logistics, quantum and photonics, and voice and language processing. General Catalyst has backed BBN since 2004. BBN serves government and defense customers and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Bear Flag Robotics
providers.description: Bear Flag Robotics is an autonomous-tractor company that retrofits existing farm tractors with sensors, onboard compute, and path-planning software to enable driverless field operations such as tillage and row-crop work. Founded in 2017 and backed by Y Combinator and True Ventures, the company was acquired by John Deere in August 2021 and now advances Deere's autonomy roadmap. It is a hardware and agricultural-robotics business with no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or GitHub surface; its website redirects to John Deere.

providers.name: Beast Industries
providers.description: Beast Industries is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of social-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: creator-economy. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: BeautyDate
providers.description: BeautyDate (beautydate.com.br) is a Brazilian beauty and wellness marketplace that connects consumers with salons and independent beauty professionals for discovering and booking appointments online. It was surfaced as a 500 Global venture-portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. At the time of this enrichment pass the public website and application endpoints were unreachable (HTTP 530 behind Cloudflare, with api.beautydate.com.br redirecting to a down app.beautydate.com.br origin), so no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable specification could be captured.

providers.name: Bebop
providers.description: Bebop (bebop.co) was a stealth-mode enterprise software startup founded by Diane Greene, co-founder and former CEO of VMware, building a development platform intended to make it easier to build and maintain enterprise applications. The company never shipped a public product, developer portal, or API, and was acquired by Google on November 19, 2015 for approximately $380 million, at which point Diane Greene was named head of Google's newly consolidated enterprise cloud business (Google for Work, Cloud Platform, and Google Apps). The acquired technology was later folded into Google Hire, which Google shut down in 2019. Bebop is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical a16z portfolio record; it has no live domain, no public API surface, and no developer artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: BeBop Sensors
providers.description: BeBop Sensors was a Berkeley, California smart-fabric sensor company founded in 2014 that designed and manufactured flexible, fabric-based pressure and touch sensors for OEMs across robotics, medical devices, automotive interiors, and virtual reality. Its best known products were haptic VR gloves and "intelligent sensing technology" surfaces that turned ordinary materials into multi-touch, pressure-sensitive inputs. The company raised a $10M+ Series A led by Bullpen Capital and shipped custom sensor hardware paired with bespoke firmware and integration software for enterprise customers. BeBop sold engineered hardware under contract rather than a self-serve developer product, and never published a public API, developer portal, or SDK. The company is no longer operating and its former domain has been repurposed by an unrelated third party.

providers.name: Beckon
providers.description: Beckon was a marketing analytics and marketing performance measurement SaaS platform, founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. Its product automated the ingestion, harmonization, and normalization of marketing data from across paid, owned, and earned channels into a single unified set of metrics and dashboards, giving marketing teams a "total marketing intelligence" view of spend, performance, and ROI. Beckon was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and Storm Ventures, and was subsequently acquired into the IgniteTech (ESW Capital / Trilogy) portfolio. The independent beckon.com domain now redirects to its acquirer, IgniteTech, and the company no longer operates a public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal of its own.

providers.name: Bed Bath And Beyond
providers.description: Bed Bath & Beyond was a chain of domestic merchandise retail stores selling home furnishings, bedding, kitchenware, and other home goods. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2023. The brand was subsequently acquired by Beyond Inc. (formerly Overstock.com), which relaunched Bed Bath & Beyond as an online retail destination. Beyond Inc. also owns Overstock, buybuy BABY, and related brands.

providers.name: Bedrock Materials
providers.description: Bedrock Materials was a Chicago-based deep-tech startup founded in 2023 by Spencer Gore (CEO, previously Tesla and Enovix) and Rafael Vila (CTO, Stanford battery scientist) to manufacture engineered sodium-ion cathode active materials as a low-cost, easy-to-source alternative to lithium-ion — built from abundant sodium, manganese, iron and aluminum, and designed to drop into existing lithium-ion cell manufacturing lines for low-voltage, starter-lighting-ignition, micromobility and industrial-traction applications. It raised a $9M seed round led by Trucks Venture Capital with Refactor Capital and Version One Ventures. In April 2025 the company wound down and returned the majority of that seed capital to its investors: CEO Spencer Gore concluded that sodium-ion could not be produced cheaply enough to beat lithium iron phosphate (LFP) after lithium oversupply collapsed prices, and that energy-density gains carried steep trade-offs. Bedrock Materials was a materials-science manufacturer and never operated a developer program, public API, or developer portal; both bedrockmaterials.com and its former bedrock.inc website are now parked/for-sale domains with no company content. This profile is retained as a verified-defunct record in the API Evangelist network — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Beek
providers.description: Beek was a Spanish-language audiobook and ebook streaming platform serving Latin America and Spain, backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners. At its peak it reached over 4 million users who streamed nearly 200 million minutes of audio content, including its exclusive Beek Originals catalog. The service has since shut down: Amazon's Audible acquired a significant portion of the Beek Originals catalog, and Beek now redirects listeners to Audible to continue their libraries. Beek ran a private backend service (api.beek.io) but published no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation, so it has no consumable API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Beervana International Limited
providers.description: Beervana International Limited is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: beijingyuanxin
providers.description: beijingyuanxin (Beijing Yuanxin) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its primary domain beijingyuanxin.com is served over HTTPS (TLS 1.3) and 301-redirects to www.yuanxinjituan.com (Yuanxin Group). During this enrichment pass no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL) was discoverable; the domain answered TLS/DNS security probes, but its content host was not reachable from the probe location. This remains a portfolio lead pending a discoverable API surface.

providers.name: Belanjaparts
providers.description: Belanjaparts is an Indonesian e-commerce platform for automotive spare parts, operating primarily as a mobile application with a searchable catalog of vehicle components, user accounts, shopping cart, order tracking, and location-based services. It serves the automotive aftermarket retail sector and is backed by 500 Global. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer, API, or integration surface at this time (consumer app and website only).

providers.name: Believer
providers.description: The Believer Company (Believer) is a global games company headquartered in Los Angeles that develops and publishes player-focused interactive entertainment for players worldwide. Assembled from veterans behind titles such as Words With Friends, League of Legends, Destiny, and Plants vs. Zombies, and backed by a16z and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Believer builds next-generation game worlds with an emphasis on community, player investment, and immersive experiences. As of this profile, Believer publishes a company site and a careers surface but no public developer portal, API, documentation, or programmatic developer surface — so this entry carries company identity only, with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Belle International
providers.description: Belle International Holdings (百丽国际) is one of China's largest women's footwear and fashion retailers, designing, manufacturing, and distributing shoe brands such as Belle, Teenmix, Tata, and Staccato alongside a sportswear-distribution business, across thousands of directly operated retail outlets and a growing e-commerce presence. Formerly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the group was taken private in 2017 by a consortium led by Hillhouse Capital and CDH Investments in one of the largest Hong Kong take-private deals. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hillhouse; enrichment found no public developer portal, API program, or machine-readable API surface for this consumer-retail company. This remains an identity and domain-security profile rather than an integratable API provider.

providers.name: Bemis
providers.description: Bemis Company, Inc. was a global leader in developing and producing flexible packaging solutions for food, beverage, and pharmaceutical applications. Founded in 1858 and headquartered in Neenah, Wisconsin, Bemis completed a $6.8 billion merger with Amcor Limited in June 2019, creating the global leader in consumer packaging. The combined entity operates as Amcor, and the Bemis brand continues as Bemis Manufacturing for FDA-compliant healthcare and pharmaceutical packaging, serving customers across 50+ countries with ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certified manufacturing operations.

providers.name: Benny
providers.description: Benny is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of matrix-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: fintech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Berry Plastics Group
providers.description: Berry Plastics Group was a manufacturer and marketer of plastic packaging products, nonwoven specialty materials, and engineered materials serving customers across consumer and industrial markets. The company was renamed Berry Global Group in 2017 to reflect its global operations and diversified product portfolio beyond plastics. As Berry Global, the company subsequently merged with Amcor in 2024.

providers.name: BetGenius
providers.description: BetGenius is the sportsbook-operator brand of Genius Sports, a London- and New York-listed sports data, technology, and commercial-services group. Founded in 2000 and operating as a Genius Sports business unit since the 2015 corporate consolidation, BetGenius provides licensed sportsbooks with an end-to-end B2B platform spanning official data and odds feeds, fully managed trading and risk management (Genius Trading Services), low-latency live video and interactive in-play streaming (BetVision and Genius Live Player), BetBuilder same-game-parlay pricing, ScoreCentre widgets, acquisition and retention marketing (FANHub, media buying, dynamic creative optimisation), and back-office sportsbook platform services (used by operators such as OPAP, 888, Betway, and Hard Rock Bet). Genius Sports sources official data from 400+ league partners — including the NFL, English Premier League, Serie A, EuroLeague, and PGA Tour — and serves 300+ licensed sportsbooks across regulated markets worldwide. BetGenius itself does not expose a self-service developer portal; its APIs (Booking API, Fixtures API v2, Matching API v2, Warehouse REST/Streaming/Publish APIs, LiveStats In-Arena and Licensing APIs, BetVision and Live Player integration SDKs) are documented at developer.geniussports.com and delivered to contracted operators via UAT and production environments using API-key authentication.

providers.name: Betty Labs
providers.description: Betty Labs was the startup behind Locker Room, a live-audio app that launched focused on live sports conversations before broadening into general social audio. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Spotify in 2021, after which Locker Room was rebuilt into Spotify's live-audio product (Greenroom / Spotify Live). Betty Labs no longer operates as an independent company; its primary domain (bettylabs.io) now redirects to Spotify, and it publishes no independent developer portal, API, documentation, or other public developer surface of its own. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company lead with no active API footprint.

providers.name: Bev
providers.description: Bev is a female-focused beverage company disrupting the male-dominated alcohol industry with premium, low-sugar canned wines made from California grapes. Sold direct-to-consumer at drinkbev.com, its lineup spans Bubbly Rosé, Bubbly White, Rosé, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Grigio and Pinot Noir, each with less than 1g of sugar per serving. Founded on a mission to transform drinking culture and promote female empowerment in business, Bev is a seed-stage Canaan Partners portfolio company. This is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce brand with no public API, developer program, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Beyond Reach Labs
providers.description: Beyond Reach Labs is a Brooklyn, New York aerospace company building deployable solar arrays and thermal radiators for spacecraft that expand from compact launch sizes to enormous structures in orbit. Its patented geometry-changing panels grow from the size of a dining table to a football field once deployed, giving satellites, orbital data centers, commercial space stations, and lunar outposts up to 10x more usable power without adding launch mass or volume. Founded by two aerospace engineers, the company is targeting its first in-space demonstration in Q2 2027 and is a Y Combinator portfolio company. Beyond Reach Labs is a hardware manufacturer and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Bharat Matrimony
providers.description: Bharat Matrimony is one of India's largest online matrimonial and matchmaking services and a flagship brand of Matrimony.com Ltd, a publicly listed Indian consumer-internet company. It helps prospective brides and grooms find life partners through profile creation, community- and region-specific matrimony sites, search and matching, messaging, and premium assisted-matchmaking and wedding services. Added to the API Evangelist network via VC-portfolio discovery (Bessemer Venture Partners, Canaan Partners); no public developer API program or OpenAPI surface was found at the time of enrichment. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Big Fish Games
providers.description: Big Fish Games is a casual-games publisher and digital storefront offering downloadable and online casual, hidden-object, match-3, puzzle, card, and social-casino titles for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. Founded in Seattle in 2002 and now part of Aristocrat's Pixel United, the company distributes thousands of games through its bigfishgames.com storefront and mobile apps. It operates as a consumer-facing games company and does not currently publish a public developer API program, OpenAPI definition, or partner API surface; this profile tracks its public web presence for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Big Heart Pet Brands
providers.description: Big Heart Pet Brands was a producer and marketer of branded pet food and snacks with brands including Meow Mix, Milk-Bone, Kibbles 'n Bits, 9Lives, Natural Balance, Pup-Peroni, Gravy Train, Nature's Recipe, Canine Carry Outs, and Milo's Kitchen. Big Heart Pet Brands was acquired by The J.M. Smucker Company in 2015 and no longer operates as an independent entity. All brands are now managed under J.M. Smucker's Pet Foods division.

providers.name: Big Lots
providers.description: Big Lots is a discount retailer offering a wide assortment of brand-name closeout merchandise including furniture, food, consumables, seasonal products, soft home, hard home, and electronics. Big Lots operated hundreds of stores across the United States. In 2024, Big Lots filed for bankruptcy and its brand and operations were acquired by Nexus Capital Management.

providers.name: Big Sur Ai
providers.description: Big Sur AI is an AI-powered SaaS platform for e-commerce merchants, founded in 2023 by Vinod Ramachandran (CEO) and Arnaud Weber (CTO). Its flagship product is an AI Sales Agent that delivers an assisted, conversational shopping experience to online shoppers, guiding product discovery and answering questions in real time to increase merchant conversion rates and average order sizes. The company raised a $6.9M seed round in March 2024 led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with Guru Chahal as the lead partner. This profile was surfaced from the Lightspeed portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Bigger Games
providers.description: Bigger Games is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of index-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: entertainment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Bilimber Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Bilimber Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore-based private company (exempt private company limited by shares) incorporated on 2020-11-17, operating in research and experimental development on electronics. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (an early/seed-stage investor alongside a Hong Kong government program) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface -- the bilimber.com domain is currently unregistered and does not resolve -- so no first-party API artifacts could be searched, derived, or generated. This profile remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: BillGuard
providers.description: BillGuard was a consumer personal-finance and transaction-security company whose mobile app scanned bank and credit-card transactions for hidden fees, billing errors, grey charges, and fraud, and let users flag or dispute suspicious charges. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company was acquired by Prosper Marketplace in 2015 and folded into the Prosper Daily app; billguard.com now 301-redirects to prosper.com and no independent BillGuard developer, API, or documentation surface remains. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead with no live API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Billion Hearts
providers.description: Billion Hearts is a consumer-sector company backed by General Catalyst (2024) and based in Asia, with an investor group that includes Neeraj Arora, Rahul Garg, and Abishek Chopra. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of general-catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. At the time of profiling the company publishes no public developer surface — no API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal — and its website resolves to a placeholder, so this profile remains an identity-only lead awaiting a real API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Bionic
providers.description: Bionic was the pioneer of Application Security Posture Management (ASPM), offering a platform that mapped application architecture, services, and data flows in production without requiring source-code access or repository integration, in order to eliminate vulnerability noise and prioritize business-critical risk. CrowdStrike announced its acquisition of Bionic on September 19, 2023 (estimated $350M) and folded the technology into Falcon Cloud Security as its ASPM capability. The bionic.ai domain now wildcard-redirects to CrowdStrike; Bionic no longer maintains an independent developer portal, API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bionic Panda Games
providers.description: Bionic Panda Games was a cross-platform mobile social games company founded in March 2010 by Charles Hudson (CEO) and Mike Jimenez (CTO), headquartered in San Francisco, California. The studio focused on Android-first social and casual titles, shipping Aqua Pets (a fishing and aquarium simulation that reached several million downloads and a top-100 grossing spot on Android), Vacation Slots, and PicAPic Camera. It raised seed funding from SoftTech VC, Norwest Venture Partners, Google Ventures, 500 Startups, and angel investors before ceasing operations. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; the studio published no public developer API, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Bionic Stork
providers.description: Bionic Stork Ltd. (operating as Bionic, bionic.ai) was an Application Security Posture Management (ASPM) company founded in Tel Aviv, Israel. Its agentless platform mapped application architectures in production — services, APIs, dependencies, data flows and SBOMs — to surface and prioritize security, data-privacy and operational risk for cloud-native applications. Backed by Insight Partners, Cyberstarts and Battery Ventures (including a $65M Series B), Bionic was acquired by CrowdStrike in 2023 for a reported ~$350M and folded into CrowdStrike Falcon ASPM. bionic.ai now 301-redirects to CrowdStrike and the company has no independent public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Bison Trails
providers.description: Bison Trails was a blockchain infrastructure company founded in 2018 by Joe Lallouz and Aaron Henshaw, offering infrastructure-as-a-service for participating in and securing proof-of-stake and other blockchain networks across dozens of protocols (staking, validators, and node infrastructure). Backed by Initialized Capital, Kleiner Perkins, and others, it was acquired by Coinbase in January 2021 and folded into Coinbase Cloud. The bisontrails.co domain now redirects to Coinbase's cloud/node infrastructure offering at coinbase.com/cloud, and no independent developer portal, documentation, or public API surface remains under the Bison Trails brand.

providers.name: Bit.io
providers.description: Bit.io was a serverless, shareable PostgreSQL database platform that let developers spin up cloud Postgres databases in seconds, load and query data, and share them via a link, with programmatic access over the standard Postgres wire protocol. Founded by Adam Fletcher and Jonathan Mortensen and backed by Battery Ventures, bit.io was acquired by Databricks in May 2023; the standalone product was sunset on June 29, 2023 (database exports available through July 29, 2023) and the team moved to Databricks. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired network record — there is no live API, developer portal, documentation, or discovery surface to enrich.

providers.name: Bitcasa
providers.description: Bitcasa, Inc. was an American cloud storage company (founded 2011 in St. Louis, Missouri; later based in Mountain View, California) known for its converged/infinite storage model and, for developers, the CloudFS API — a white-label cloud-storage platform that let third-party applications integrate file management, secure sharing, media transcoding, instant streaming, and zero-knowledge client-side encryption. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), CrunchFund, Pelion Venture Partners, Horizons Ventures, Samsung Ventures, and First Round Capital, Bitcasa wound down its consumer Bitcasa Drive service in 2016 and shut down all services in 2017. The company is defunct and the bitcasa.com domain is now parked, so no live developer surface, API documentation, or specifications remain to enrich.

providers.name: Bitfusion Io
providers.description: Bitfusion (bitfusion.io) was an Austin, Texas startup, backed by DCVC, that built "elastic AI" infrastructure software. Its FlexDirect platform was a transparent GPU/CPU virtualization layer that pooled network-attached accelerators (GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs) across TCP, RoCE, and InfiniBand into a single elastic compute cluster for sharing, scaling, and management of AI/ML workloads. VMware acquired Bitfusion in 2019 and folded FlexDirect into vSphere as vSphere Bitfusion (subsequently end-of-lifed). The independent company no longer operates, the bitfusion.io domain no longer resolves, and it exposes no public API, developer portal, or discoverable artifacts. Retained here as a DCVC portfolio record; defunct as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: BitYota
providers.description: BitYota was a Data-Warehouse-as-a-Service (DWaaS) startup founded around 2011 in Santa Clara, California, offering a SaaS analytics data warehouse that ran on top of Amazon Web Services and Rackspace infrastructure and natively queried semi-structured JSON data. The company's team of data-processing engineers was acqui-hired by LifeLock in August 2015 for approximately $12.8 million, and the standalone BitYota product and company were subsequently wound down. The primary domain bityota.com no longer resolves (no DNS records), no public API, developer portal, documentation, source repositories, or client SDKs survive, and there is no active API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest. This profile is retained for historical/network completeness and is flagged defunct.

providers.name: Bix
