providers.description: Bix was an online talent-competition community founded in 2006 by Mike Speiser (co-founder of Epinions), where users created and judged web-based contests across karaoke, dance, photography, writing, beauty, and comedy. Backed by Trinity Ventures, the roughly 16-person startup grew to over one million users within months and was acquired by Yahoo! in November 2006; Yahoo later shut the service down. This API Evangelist profile documents Bix as a historical, defunct consumer company with no live website, developer platform, or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: black-unique
providers.description: Black Unique (全球购骑士特权, "Global Shopping Knight Privilege") is a membership-based consumer e-commerce and discounts platform founded in 2018 and headquartered in Guangzhou, China. Its core product is a privileges/membership card that aggregates discounts and special offers across a wide range of consumer categories: online shopping on major marketplaces such as Tmall, JD.com and Kaola, in-person shopping at international duty-free shops, outlets and supermarkets across 24-plus countries, plus dining, entertainment, travel and fuel. The company operates a consumer-facing app and website rather than a public developer program, and is backed by Qiming Venture Partners along with CCV, Eastern Bell Venture Capital and INCE Capital. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Qiming portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other developer surface.

providers.name: Blekko
providers.description: Blekko was a web search engine founded in 2007 by Rich Skrenta, Tom Annau, and Mike Markson and launched publicly in 2010. It was best known for "slashtags" — user-applied /slashtag filters that curated and narrowed search results by category as a spam-resistant alternative to mainstream search engines — and it exposed a developer search API. Blekko was acquired by IBM in March 2015, where its technology and team were folded into the IBM Watson group and its consumer search engine was shut down. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical/defunct record; the company no longer operates a live website or public API (blekko.com resolves in DNS but no longer serves HTTPS).

providers.name: Blink Booking
providers.description: Blink Booking was a Madrid, Spain based mobile application for last-minute hotel booking, founded in 2011 by Rebeca Minguela and Miguel Ortega Rodriguez. The app presented travellers with a curated daily selection of four discounted hotels for same-day stays, working with more than 2,000 hotel partners across eight European countries, and competed directly with HotelTonight. The company raised approximately $2.5M in a Series A round in May 2012 from Ventech, Uncork Capital (then SoftTech VC), 500 Global (then 500 Startups) and Kibo Ventures. Groupon acquired Blink Booking in September 2013 to strengthen its Groupon Getaways travel division; the app was rebranded "Blink by Groupon" and was wound down over the following months. The company is defunct and publishes no developer surface, no API, and no documentation. Its former blinkbooking.com domain lapsed and was re-registered in August 2020 by an unrelated party; it now redirects to a third-party gambling site and must not be treated as a company property.

providers.name: Blinkist
providers.description: Blinkist is a Berlin-founded subscription learning app that condenses the key ideas of thousands of nonfiction books and podcasts into roughly 15-minute text and audio summaries called "Blinks." Launched in 2012, it is used by millions of readers to learn on the go across categories such as productivity, business, psychology, personal growth, and science, and it also offers Blinkist for Business for teams and organizations. The consumer product is delivered through the web and iOS/Android apps backed by a private mobile backend at api.blinkist.com; Blinkist does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. Blinkist was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by Insight Partners) and enriched with the provider signals that could be verified from its public surface.

providers.name: BlockTower Capital
providers.description: BlockTower Capital was an institutional digital-asset investment management firm founded in 2017, running crypto hedge fund and venture strategies and backed by investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Union Square Ventures. As of April 30, 2025 the firm was acquired by and rebranded as Arca; blocktower.com now 301-redirects to ar.ca and BlockTower no longer operates as a standalone brand. The firm published no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface, so there is no API artifact set to enrich here beyond identity and a domain-security probe of the still-resolving legacy domain.

providers.name: BlockVigil
providers.description: BlockVigil was a blockchain / Web3 developer platform company, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the enrichment pass on 2026-07-18, the company's website (https://blockvigil.com) publishes only a wind-down notice stating that "BlockVigil has concluded its active service offerings," directing remaining custom-contract customers to their designated representative. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or well-known/ metadata are published; this profile therefore captures only live domain-security posture and the discontinuation status.

providers.name: Bloomin' Brands
providers.description: Bloomin' Brands, Inc. (NASDAQ: BLMN) is one of the largest casual dining restaurant companies in the world, headquartered in Tampa, Florida and founded in 1988. It owns and operates four restaurant concepts — Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill, and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar — across the United States and internationally (Brazil, South Korea, Hong Kong, and China). The company's consumer technology centers on the Web-based Dine Rewards loyalty program, per-brand mobile apps (iOS/Android) for online ordering, curbside takeaway, delivery, table payment, reservations, and waitlist, and corporate supplier portals (BBI Connect). Bloomin' Brands does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; the apis collection below is intentionally empty.

providers.name: BloomThat
providers.description: BloomThat was an a16z-backed, San Francisco same-day flower and gift delivery startup, surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. It operated a consumer (B2C) mobile and web ordering experience and never published a public developer API. As of this enrichment pass its domain (bloomthat.com) 301-redirects to ftd.com/bloomthat, indicating the brand has been acquired by / absorbed into FTD and no longer operates an independent developer surface.

providers.name: Blooom
providers.description: Blooom was an independent robo-advisor that provided automated, flat-fee management of employer-sponsored retirement accounts — 401(k), 403(b), 457, and TSP plans — analyzing holdings, rebalancing allocations, and flagging hidden fund fees on accounts it advised but did not directly custody. Founded in 2013 and backed by QED Investors, the Kansas-based company operated a consumer web application rather than a public developer API. The consumer service has since wound down: blooom.com no longer resolves to a website and the domain is now served by Morgan Stanley nameservers with a locked-down, mail-disabled defensive DNS posture (null MX, SPF -all, DMARC p=reject). Retained here as a historical wealth-management profile; no live API or developer surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Blue Bottle Coffee *
providers.description: Blue Bottle Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and retailer founded in 2002 in Oakland, California by James Freeman, known for freshly roasted single-origin beans, seasonal blends, cafes, and a direct-to-consumer subscription service that ships coffee within 48 hours of roasting. A majority stake was acquired by Nestle in 2017. The company operates cafes across the United States and Asia and sells whole-bean coffee, brewing equipment, and gift subscriptions through its e-commerce site. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv, kindred-ventures and true-ventures; no public developer API program has been found. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Blue Flame Data
providers.description: Blue Flame Data was an early-2000s consumer-preference analytics company (founded around 2000 in New York City) that built web-based software for real-time measurement of consumer market preferences, marketed as TrueChoice Preference Technology for quantifying the preference structures of individual consumers and employees. The company appears to be defunct: its domain (blueflamedata.com) resolves to a parked/unresponsive IP and does not serve a live site. It was surfaced to the API Evangelist network via Battery Ventures portfolio mining. During enrichment no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, packages, MCP server, or other machine-readable artifacts could be located, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Blue Frog Gaming
providers.description: Blue Frog Gaming is a small independent game studio founded in 2007 by Matt Maroon and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2007 batch), based in Akron, Ohio. The company builds browser-based and social strategy games, best known for Starfleet Commander — a persistent, multi-universe game of resource management, alliance building, and fleet combat — along with Stardrift Empires (built with Syfy Games) and the sci-fi MMO ShadowRift. Blue Frog Gaming is a consumer game developer rather than an API-first platform: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API description. This record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it will be upgraded if and when a public API surface is discovered.

providers.name: Blue Kai
providers.description: Blue Kai (BlueKai) was a cloud-based big-data and data management platform (DMP) for audience, marketing, and advertising data, founded in 2008 and backed by Battery Ventures. Oracle acquired BlueKai in 2014 and folded it into Oracle Data Cloud / Oracle Advertising; the bluekai.com domain now 301-redirects to oracle.com (verified 2026-07-18, HTTP 403 at www.oracle.com). No independent Blue Kai developer portal, API, OpenAPI, documentation, changelog, or event surface remains, so no live provider API artifacts can be enriched. This record is retained as an acquired-company / VC-portfolio node rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Blue Studios.io, BlueStudios
providers.description: Blue Studios (bluestudios.io), tagline "Where Families Flourish," is a family-focused technology company backed by 500 Global that builds consumer digital products and experiences for households. Its portfolio spans Wallio, a collaborative finance app for couples and families; Blue Studios Education, an edutainment streaming and learning platform; Blue Studios Entertainment, a family-oriented media production division; and Blueniverse, the ecosystem tying the products together. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation — this profile is a consumer-company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Bluebirds
providers.description: Bluebirds is an AI-powered outbound sales and go-to-market (GTM) prospecting platform, founded in 2022 by Rohan Punamia (CEO) and Kunal Punera (CTO). The product helps sales teams create, test, and scale AI-driven prospecting triggers, letting representatives target and personalize outreach in a unified workflow so they reach the right personas with the right message at the right time. Bluebirds was seed-funded by Lightspeed Venture Partners (invested 2023). As of July 2026 the primary domain bluebirds.com 301-redirects to Salesforce's AI prospecting agent page, indicating the Bluebirds team and technology have been absorbed into Salesforce. Bluebirds exposes no public developer or API surface — no docs, developer, api, status, or trust subdomains resolve, and the application host (app.bluebirds.com) is login-gated behind bot protection — so this profile is identity-only and carries no API artifacts.

providers.name: bluebottlecoffee
providers.description: Blue Bottle Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and retailer that sells single-origin beans, blends, and brewing equipment through its ecommerce storefront, subscriptions, and cafes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, the company operates a consumer-facing storefront (bot-protected) with no public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface at the time of this pass; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Bluebox
providers.description: Bluebox (Bluebox Security) was an enterprise mobile and application security startup founded around 2012 that let organizations secure corporate data on employee-owned smartphones and tablets without managing the whole device. It raised roughly $27.5M, with Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) leading its Series A and returning for the Series B alongside Tenaya Capital, Andreas Bechtolsheim, and SV Angel. Its technology assets were acquired by Lookout on April 8, 2016, after which Bluebox ceased operating as an independent company. It was a packaged security product vendor, not a public API provider, and it maintains no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface today.

providers.name: Bluedata Software Inc
providers.description: BlueData Software Inc was a big-data infrastructure company whose EPIC platform ran Hadoop, Spark, and other analytics workloads in Docker containers on-premises and in the cloud. It was a dcvc (Data Collective) portfolio company and was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in 2018; its technology now lives on as the HPE Ezmeral Container Platform. The original www.bluedata.com domain 301-redirects to HPE's container-platform page, and the company no longer operates an independent developer, API, or documentation surface, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Bluefin Labs
providers.description: Bluefin Labs was a social TV analytics company founded in 2008 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Deb Roy and Michael Fleischman, spun out of research at the MIT Media Lab. Its platform semantically interpreted public social media commentary from Twitter, Facebook and blogs and automatically linked those comments to the television shows and advertisements people were watching, producing audience engagement measurement for networks, agencies and brands. Its product, Bluefin Signals, gave media buyers a tool for accessing and analyzing social TV response data. The company raised a Series A led by Redpoint Ventures in 2010 and a $12M Series B led by Time Warner Investments in January 2012, with SoftBank Capital and Lerer Ventures participating. Twitter acquired Bluefin Labs on February 6, 2013 for a reported ~$100 million and absorbed the team and technology into its TV advertising and analytics products. The company is DEFUNCT: it operates no independent product, developer program or API, and the bluefinlabs.com domain no longer belongs to the company — it now redirects to an unrelated news site. This profile is retained as a historical / portfolio-graph record only.

providers.name: BlueKai
providers.description: BlueKai was a data management platform (DMP) and third-party audience data marketplace founded in 2008 that let marketers collect, organize, and activate first- and third-party audience data for programmatic advertising and targeting. Oracle acquired BlueKai in 2014 and folded it into the Oracle Data Cloud; Oracle wound down its advertising business (including the former BlueKai and Data Cloud assets) in 2024. The company operates no independent developer program today — the bluekai.com domain 301-redirects to Oracle's advertising pages and exposes no live public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: BlueLabs
providers.description: BlueLabs (withbluelabs.ai) is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building toward "emotional intelligence at scale." Its core technology, Blue-JST, is described as a novel dual reward mechanism designed to balance relationships and utility — an approach grounded in reward modeling and reinforcement learning. The company is backed by Forerunner Ventures and is actively hiring research talent. As of this profile it publishes a single marketing site (built on Webflow) with no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface; this record will be enriched as a developer- or agent-facing surface emerges.

providers.name: Bluelearn
providers.description: Bluelearn was an India-based community-driven learning and edtech startup backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears inactive - its primary domain (bluelearn.in) no longer serves a product site and instead resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander page, with no reachable HTTPS endpoint, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. No OpenAPI, SDK, or other machine-readable API artifacts were found to search, generate, or derive from. This profile remains a lead pending any revived public developer surface.

providers.name: Bluestone
providers.description: BlueStone is one of India's largest online retailers of fine jewellery, founded in 2011 by Gaurav Singh Kushwaha and headquartered in Bangalore. It runs an omnichannel model spanning its e-commerce storefront and 125+ physical stores across India, offering 7,000+ BIS-hallmarked and certified designs in gold, diamond, gemstone, and platinum, plus services such as lifetime exchange, buyback, 30-day returns, and personal video consultations. The company is backed by Accel. BlueStone publishes no public developer portal or API; this profile captures the company's identity and a probed domain-security posture for the network.

providers.name: BlueStripe Software
providers.description: BlueStripe Software was an application performance management (APM) vendor headquartered in the Research Triangle Park area of North Carolina. Its flagship product, FactFinder, provided application-aware infrastructure performance monitoring and end-to-end transaction tracing across distributed servers, letting operations teams map and troubleshoot how applications behaved across physical, virtual, and cloud infrastructure. The company was backed by Trinity Ventures and other venture investors before being acquired by Microsoft in April 2015, after which its technology was folded into Microsoft System Center and the Operations Management Suite (OMS) and the standalone BlueStripe product and developer surface were discontinued. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record; the company no longer operates an independent website, developer portal, or API.

providers.name: BlueTalon Data Systems
providers.description: BlueTalon Data Systems was a data-centric security company that built dynamic, policy-based access control, data masking, filtering, and auditing for enterprise data platforms such as Hadoop, relational databases, and big-data stores. It let organizations enforce fine-grained authorization and privacy controls at the point of data access. Founded around 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, BlueTalon was acquired by Microsoft in July 2019, after which its team and technology were absorbed into Microsoft's data-governance and security efforts (Azure). BlueTalon no longer operates as an independent company; the bluetalon.com domain is parked on Azure DNS with no active web, developer, or API surface, so this network profile carries identity only and has no live artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: BMC Stock Holdings
providers.description: BMC Stock Holdings, Inc. was one of the largest professional building materials distributors in the United States, serving homebuilders, remodelers, and contractors with lumber, structural components, millwork, doors, windows, and installed services. The company was formed in December 2015 through the merger of Stock Building Supply and Building Materials Holding Corporation (BMHC) and traded on NASDAQ under the ticker BMCH, headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina. On January 1, 2021, BMC Stock Holdings completed an all-stock "merger of equals" with Builders FirstSource (NYSE: BLDR), creating the nation's largest supplier of structural building products to the professional homebuilding market. The combined company retained the Builders FirstSource name, BLDR ticker, and Irving, Texas headquarters. The merger had an enterprise value of approximately $2.5 billion and produced a company with more than $11 billion in annual sales, approximately 26,000 employees, and roughly 550 distribution and manufacturing locations across more than 40 U.S. states. BMC Stock Holdings no longer exists as an independent entity. The legacy buildwithbmc.com domain redirects to bldr.com, and BMC product lines and branches have been absorbed into the Builders FirstSource network. This profile is retained as a historical Fortune 1000 record (BMC ranked #677 prior to the merger) and as a redirect to the successor profile at api-evangelist/builders-firstsource. BMC operated as a commodity-and-services distributor and did not publish public developer APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal. No API surface is documented for this provider.

providers.name: bomming
providers.description: Zhuhai Boming Vision Technology Co., Ltd. (珠海博明视觉科技有限公司) is a Chinese high-tech industrial machine-vision company founded in September 2016 and headquartered in the Zhuhai High-tech Zone. It develops optical and machine-vision inspection technology for manufacturing quality control, including 3D structured-light sensors, flash measuring instruments (闪测仪), 2D/3D profile measurement systems, PCB back-drill thickness gauges, surface-defect inspection systems, glue-dispensing systems, and an AI deep-learning algorithm platform for automated visual inspection. Its solutions serve the lithium-battery, magnetic-materials, 3C electronics, semiconductor, photovoltaic, metalworking, and pharmaceutical industries. This is a hardware/equipment manufacturer with no public developer or API surface; the profile is retained as a VC-portfolio company lead.

providers.name: Bon-Ton Stores
providers.description: The Bon-Ton Stores was a regional department store chain in the United States that operated stores across the Midwest, Northeast, and upper Great Plains. Founded in 1898 in York, Pennsylvania, the company sold apparel, accessories, cosmetics, home furnishings, and other merchandise under banners including Bon-Ton, Bergner's, Boston Store, Carson's, Elder-Beerman, Herberger's, and Younkers. The company filed for bankruptcy and ceased operations in 2018.

providers.name: Bonfire Studios
providers.description: Bonfire Studios is an independent video game development studio based in Irvine, California, focused on building original interactive entertainment, including its announced title Arkheron. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, Bonfire Studios does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other programmable developer surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich; this profile is maintained as a company record and an ongoing lead should a developer surface emerge.

providers.name: BoomTrain
providers.description: BoomTrain was a machine-learning marketing technology startup that used AI to power personalized, cross-channel messaging (email, web, and push notifications) for brands, predicting individual content and send-time recommendations for each consumer. Backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) among others, BoomTrain raised roughly $15M before being acquired by Zeta Global in July 2017 (reportedly $35-40M), which folded its machine-learning, decisioning, and personalization technology into the Zeta Marketing Platform. The boomtrain.com domain now redirects to Zeta Global; there is no standalone BoomTrain developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Boost Media
providers.description: Boost Media (formerly BoostCTR) was a digital-advertising creative-optimization SaaS platform that paired machine-learning analysis with a curated marketplace of more than 1,000 human writers and designers to test and improve ad creative across paid search, social, video, and display campaigns. Its technology powered roughly $1 billion in paid-search advertising for around 100 global brands across retail, education, financial services, healthcare and insurance, gaming, auto, and travel. Backed by Battery Ventures (Series C, $19M, 2014), Founder Collective, and 500 Global, the company raised about $42.8M total before being acquired by AdLabs Technology in April 2019. The company is now closed and its former domain (boostmedia.com) no longer resolves; this profile is retained as a Battery Ventures portfolio record. No public API, developer portal, or specification surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Bop.fm
providers.description: Bop.fm was a music-sharing and playlist startup that let people share and play individual songs across streaming services — building a link for a track that would resolve to whichever service (Spotify, Deezer, SoundCloud, YouTube, Rdio) each listener used. Founded out of Y Combinator, it reportedly reached several million monthly listeners and raised roughly $2M before being acquihired by identity-protection company LifeLock in October 2015, at which point the website, mobile apps, and embedded players were shut down. The company is defunct: the bop.fm domain no longer serves the product (it now redirects to an unrelated parked site) and no developer portal, documentation, or API surface remains online. This profile is retained as a historical record within the API Evangelist network; there are no live API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Born
providers.description: Born (formerly Slay) is a Berlin-based consumer AI company founded in 2022 by Fabian Kamberi (CEO), Jannis Ringwald, and Stefan Quernhorst. Born builds AI characters and companions designed for shared, social experiences rather than isolating one-to-one chatbots. Its flagship product Pengu is a co-parented virtual pet with more than 15 million registered users, and the company is expanding into a multi-character platform called Friends and a photorealistic voice-and-video companion experience called Life. Since 2022 Born has launched five consumer social apps that reached #1 globally on the App Store. It raised a $15M Series A in September 2025 (participants include Accel, Tencent, and Laton Ventures), bringing total funding to roughly $25M. Born is a consumer mobile-app maker and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Boss
providers.description: Boss (BOSS Zhipin / BOSS直聘) is the largest online recruitment platform in China by average monthly active users, operated by Kanzhun Limited (NASDAQ: BZ, HKEX: 2076) and founded in 2014 in Beijing. It pioneered the "Direct Recruitment" model, a mobile-native experience that connects employers (bosses) and job seekers through instant direct chat rather than static resume exchange, with candidate and job matching powered by proprietary AI algorithms and big-data insights. The consumer job-search product at zhipin.com does not publish a public developer/job-data API; an authorized enterprise developer surface (BossHi mini-program open platform) exists for partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Boston Properties (BXP)
providers.description: BXP (formerly Boston Properties) is the largest publicly traded developer, owner, and manager of premier workplaces in the United States. The company develops, owns, and manages Class A office properties across six major U.S. markets: Boston, Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington DC. BXP is a self-administered and self-managed REIT focused on premier urban workspace.

providers.name: Botd
providers.description: Botd is a browser library for JavaScript bot detection

providers.name: Bounty Hunter
providers.description: Bounty Hunter (獎金獵人) is Taiwan's largest creative-competition platform, founded in 2011 to help young creators discover and enter contests. It aggregates and curates design, illustration, photography, short-film, writing, music, business-planning, programming, and academic competitions from Taiwan and around the world for its several-hundred-thousand registered creator members. Through its Contest Builder (contest.bhuntr.com) and brand-services arm (desk.bhuntr.com) it also runs sponsored competitions for clients including Google, Microsoft, Lexus, McDonald's, and E.SUN. The company established a U.S. headquarters in 2014 and is backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) and Silicon Valley angel investors. It exposes no documented public developer API; api.bhuntr.com is an undocumented first-party backend.

providers.name: Boyd Gaming
providers.description: Boyd Gaming is a multi-jurisdictional casino entertainment company that owns and operates 28+ gaming properties across 10 U.S. states. The company offers casino gaming, hotel accommodations, dining, entertainment, and sports betting through its Boyd Sports platform. Boyd Rewards is the company's loyalty program spanning all properties, accessible via web portal and mobile app.

providers.name: Bracket Computing
providers.description: Bracket Computing was a cloud computing and enterprise security company founded in 2011 by Tom Gillis and Jason Lango (both formerly of IronPort Systems) and based in Mountain View, California. It built a cloud workload-isolation platform that extended encryption, integrity protection, and micro-segmentation across heterogeneous public and private cloud environments. The company raised roughly $130 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Fidelity, Goldman Sachs, and Sutter Hill Ventures before VMware acquired its intellectual property and key engineers on May 1, 2018, folding the technology into the VMware NSX networking and security portfolio. Bracket Computing no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; its primary domain now resolves to a parked domain-for-sale page.

providers.name: Braid
providers.description: Braid Networks was a creator-economy startup that let creators build customizable landing pages unifying their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts and commerce links), build mailing lists, and engage followers via text and push notifications. Founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro, it raised a $6.8M seed round from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Initialized Capital. Braid was a consumer direct-to-fan product and never published a public developer API. The company was acquired by Laurel on 2026-01-01 to power Laurel's Signal product and has since shut down; the braid.network domain no longer serves a site.

providers.name: Brainient
providers.description: Brainient was a London-based advertising technology company founded in 2009 by Emi Gal that specialized in interactive video advertising and Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO). Its platform made online video ads more personalized and interactive by matching creative to real-time context such as socio-demographics, geolocation, device, time of day, and weather. Brainient was acquired by Teads in September 2016 and folded into the Teads Studio division; the standalone Brainient brand and its brainient.com domain are now defunct. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. No public API surface, developer documentation, or machine-readable specification was located for Brainient during enrichment.

providers.name: BrandCT
providers.description: BrandCT (品牌CT) is an offline-retail market-monitoring service operated by Mashangying (马上赢市场调查 / yikuaigao), a Chinese retail-data company. It has built a national offline-retail monitoring network based on POS data from a panel of sample stores, and delivers brand owners a "BrandCT" service that scans more than 10 million products across offline retail formats to quantify market share, distribution (铺市率), and product sell-through. The platform supports quantitative analysis of product innovation, channel competition, and category trends to speed up and sharpen client decision-making. The product is delivered through a login-gated web dashboard (WeChat, phone, and email verification sign-in); no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Bravado
providers.description: Bravado is a community platform for sales professionals, best known as the War Room, which it describes as the world's largest online sales community with more than 400,000 members. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, Bravado offers career networking, anonymous peer Q&A, a jobs and hiring marketplace that matches sales talent with companies, an AI recruiter called Hunter, and a virtual "commission points" rewards currency, delivered through the web and a mobile app. The company is backed by Redpoint Ventures. Bravado does not publish a public developer API; its product is built on an internal GraphQL backend. As of this profile's enrichment date the primary domain bravado.co resolves to a Gandi parking page ("this domain name is unavailable") and is not serving the live product.

providers.description: Some Breaking Bad quotes

providers.name: Brewster
providers.description: Brewster was a New York-based mobile contacts startup founded by Steve Greenwood that launched an iOS app in July 2012 offering a "hyperconnected mobile address book" — it merged phone contacts with Google Apps, Facebook, Twitter, Foursquare and LinkedIn profiles, deduplicated them, and kept them self-updating in the cloud while surfacing relationship signals about who a user actually engaged with. The company was backed by Union Square Ventures and Slow Ventures. In October 2015 the founding team was acqui-hired by Restaurant Brands International (owner of Burger King and Tim Hortons) without the app or its data, and in March 2016 FullContact acquired Brewster's self-updating address book technology and shut the consumer product down within 30 days. Brewster never published a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI definition or developer portal, and no API surface survives today. This profile is retained as a historical record only.

providers.name: Bridgeco
providers.description: BridgeCo Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 that built networked-audio silicon and software for consumer electronics. Its JukeBlox platform — a system-on-a-chip paired with a software development kit — let wireless speakers, A/V receivers, home-theater systems and docking stations stream music from tablets, smartphones and PCs, and was designed into products from Pioneer, Philips, Denon, Marantz, JBL and Harman/Kardon. Earlybird Venture Capital was the company's first institutional investor in 2000. BridgeCo was acquired by Standard Microsystems Corporation (SMSC) on 19 May 2011 in a deal worth up to $67.5 million, and SMSC was in turn acquired by Microchip Technology on 2 August 2012, where the JukeBlox wireless-audio line was folded into Microchip's portfolio. BridgeCo no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation or public API; the bridgeco.com domain today is an unrelated domain-for-sale parking page.

providers.name: BrightBytes
providers.description: BrightBytes was a San Francisco-based K-12 education data and analytics company founded in 2012 by Rob Mancabelli, best known for Clarity, a decision-support and analytics platform used by schools and districts to connect technology spending and classroom use to student learning outcomes, and for DataSense, a data-integration platform that captured, cleaned, and synced student data between disparate school systems. The company sold DataSense and its team to Microsoft in February 2019 and was itself acquired by Google in 2022. BrightBytes no longer operates independently: as of July 2026 www.brightbytes.net returns an expired-site placeholder and no developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or status surface remains. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: BrightFunnel
providers.description: BrightFunnel was a San Francisco-based B2B marketing analytics company founded in 2012 that built a revenue attribution and forecasting platform. Its Revenue Intelligence Suite gave B2B marketers multi-touch attribution, revenue-funnel analysis, account-based measurement, web analytics, and predictive forecasting so they could quantify marketing's impact on pipeline and revenue and align plans with business priorities. BrightFunnel was acquired by account-based marketing vendor Terminus in January 2018, and its multi-channel analytics were folded into the Terminus platform. It no longer operates as a standalone product: the brightfunnel.com domain now serves only a redirect, and there is no live developer portal, public API, documentation, SDK, or discovery surface (.well-known, llms.txt) to enrich. This profile remains a historical company stub, originally surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: BrightRoll
providers.description: BrightRoll was a programmatic video advertising platform founded in 2006 in San Francisco that ran one of the largest independent real-time bidding marketplaces for digital video ads (RTB/DSP/SSP), connecting brand advertisers and agencies with publisher video inventory across web, mobile, and connected devices. The company was acquired by Yahoo in November 2014 and its technology was folded into Yahoo's advertising stack, later branded under Oath / Verizon Media and now Yahoo Advertising. BrightRoll no longer operates as an independent provider and publishes no standalone developer program or public API. As of this enrichment pass its former domain, brightroll.com, returns an HTTP 301 redirect to Yahoo's advertising platforms page, and the domain is served from Yahoo-owned DNS and mail infrastructure. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired / absorbed company record rather than an active API producer.

providers.name: Briko Robotics
providers.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

providers.name: Brilliant Planet
providers.description: Brilliant Planet is a carbon-removal company that grows microalgae in open-air ponds on otherwise-unproductive coastal desert land, using seawater rather than fresh water, to sequester atmospheric carbon dioxide at scale. Harvested algal biomass is dried and stored to lock the captured carbon away durably, while the process also deacidifies the seawater it returns. The company operates research and demonstration facilities in coastal Morocco and is developing measurement, reporting, and verification approaches for its nature-based carbon capture. It is backed by Union Square Ventures and other climate-focused investors. This API Evangelist profile is a company/provider record; Brilliant Planet publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time (its primary web presence is access-restricted).

providers.name: Britesemi
providers.description: Britesemi (Brite Semiconductor / 灿芯半导体（上海）股份有限公司, Shanghai, stock ticker 688691) is a one-stop custom chip and silicon IP supplier. It provides ASIC design services spanning chip specification definition, SoC and mixed-signal design architecture, backend design, and final product delivery, alongside a family of proprietary YouIP interface IP cores (YouDDR, YouSerdes, YouUSB, YouMIPI, YouPCIe, YouONFI, YouIO, YouRF, YouADC). This is a semiconductor / ASIC design-services business, not a public web-API provider: enrichment found no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners.

providers.name: Broadbus Technologies
providers.description: Broadbus Technologies was a video-on-demand (VOD) streaming infrastructure company based in Boxborough, Massachusetts. It developed RAM-based VOD streaming server technology (the B-1 server) used by cable operators to deliver on-demand video at scale. The company was acquired by Motorola in 2006 and folded into Motorola's Connected Home / cable video business. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As a defunct hardware and infrastructure vendor with no surviving corporate or developer presence, it exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or discoverable web surface to enrich.

providers.name: Bromium
providers.description: Bromium was an endpoint-security company founded in 2010 that pioneered application isolation through hardware-enforced micro-virtualization, running each untrusted task (a web page, email attachment, or downloaded file) inside its own disposable CPU-level micro-VM so malware could not escape to the host. Bromium was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Hewlett-Packard (HP Inc.) acquired Bromium in September 2019 and folded the micro-virtualization technology into HP Sure Click and the HP Wolf Security endpoint-protection line; bromium.com now permanently redirects to HP's endpoint-security pages. Bromium no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no standalone public developer API, so this profile carries company identity only rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: BTR New Material Group
providers.description: BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd. (贝特瑞新材料集团股份有限公司) is a globally leading supplier of lithium-ion battery materials headquartered in China. The company produces anode materials for high-capacity batteries across soft-pack, aluminum-shell, and cylindrical formats; cathode materials for consumer electronics, power tools, energy storage, and electric vehicles; and advanced new materials used in smartphones, tablets, PCs, and displays. BTR operates a central research institute of roughly 50,000 square meters staffed by about 900 researchers. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. BTR is a materials manufacturer and publishes no developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface; this profile captures its public web and domain-security footprint.

providers.name: budcreate
providers.description: BUD (budcreate.xyz, app at joinbudapp.com) is an AI-powered 3D UGC (user-generated content) interactive content platform where millions of creators build, play, and share immersive experiences and games. It is a consumer mobile creation and social platform spanning avatars, 3D worlds, mini-games, and AI-assisted content generation. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass, BUD publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or discovery/.well-known surface — it is a consumer application, not an API provider.

providers.name: Buddy Media
providers.description: Buddy Media was a social media marketing and advertising platform (founded 2007, backed by ggv-capital, insight-partners and ivp) that helped brands manage publishing, engagement and paid campaigns across Facebook, Twitter and other social networks. It was acquired by Salesforce in 2012 and folded into the Salesforce Marketing Cloud (Social Studio) product line; the buddymedia.com domain now redirects to salesforce.com/marketing. No standalone Buddy Media public API, developer portal or first-party SDK remains — this network entry is retained as a historical martech company stub.

providers.name: buddybuild
providers.description: buddybuild was a mobile continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform for iOS and Android apps, offering automated builds, testing, user feedback, and over-the-air deployment to testers. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Kleiner Perkins, it was acquired by Apple in January 2018; the standalone service was wound down through 2018-2019 and its capabilities were folded into Apple's Xcode Cloud. The buddybuild.com domain now redirects to developer.apple.com/xcode-cloud/, and no independent developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface remains. Retained as a network record of an acquired/defunct provider rather than an active enrichment target.

providers.name: Buffd
providers.description: Buffd is a gaming and esports consumer application, delivered as an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) at buffd.gg, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The company was linked in the venture-portfolio source to the now-defunct juked.gg esports property; buffd.gg is the live product surface. As of this enrichment pass, Buffd publishes no public developer program, API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only, awaiting a developer surface to enrich further.

providers.name: Bufferbox
providers.description: BufferBox was a Waterloo, Ontario startup that operated self-service parcel-pickup lockers for online shoppers, letting people route e-commerce deliveries to a nearby locker and collect them with a PIN. Google acquired BufferBox in November 2012 and wound the service down in early 2015. The company is defunct and operates no developer or API surface; the bufferbox.com and bufferbox.ca domains are parked (resolving to a Bizland placeholder host), so this profile carries no API artifacts. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical logistics / last-mile-delivery record.

providers.name: Builder.ai
providers.description: Builder.ai was a London-based AI-assisted software development platform, originally founded in 2016 as Engineer.ai by Sachin Dev Duggal, that let customers assemble custom web and mobile applications from reusable building blocks orchestrated by an AI assistant branded "Natasha." Positioned as a no-code/low-code "human-assisted AI" app factory, it raised large rounds from investors including Insight Partners, Microsoft, the Qatar Investment Authority and SoftBank's DeepCore. The company collapsed into insolvency and entered administration in 2025 amid a revenue-restatement controversy, and its public web and developer surfaces are no longer operational. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record; no live API, developer portal, or documentation could be verified during enrichment.

providers.name: Buildspace
providers.description: Buildspace was an online education platform and community that billed itself as "the biggest school in the world for people who wanted to work on their own ideas," running six-week cohort-based programs to help entrepreneurs and builders ship their own projects and startups. Backed by a16z, the company wound down its operations; its site now serves only a farewell letter and final video. It was a consumer education and community product, not an API provider, and exposes no public developer surface, API, documentation, or SDKs. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Bumblebee Spaces
providers.description: Bumblebee Spaces is a San Francisco smart-home robotics company that builds app-controlled motorized storage systems for compact urban living. Its ceiling-mounted robotic units lift beds, closets, and storage bins up and out of the way, reclaiming floor space in small apartments, while a built-in camera and mobile app track and retrieve stored belongings on demand. The company sells and installs hardware plus a companion consumer mobile application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Canaan Partners, the profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Bumped
providers.description: Bumped was a Portland, Oregon-based fintech that rewarded consumers with fractional shares of publicly traded stock in the brands and companies they shop with, turning everyday spending and loyalty into equity ownership. Backed by Canaan Partners, the company operated a consumer investing and rewards application before winding down its consumer product. It was surfaced through the Canaan Partners portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. During enrichment no live public developer surface, API, documentation, package, or well-known discovery endpoint could be located -- the primary domain (bumped.com) no longer resolves and related domains are parked -- so this remains an identity-only profile with no active API artifacts.

providers.name: Burberry & Hicks
providers.description: Burberry & Hicks is a company listed on the Battery Ventures "List of All Companies" portfolio page, where it is flagged with an asterisk denoting an exited investment as of the Q1 2026 edition of that list. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-derived lead awaiting enrichment. A July 2026 enrichment pass searched the open web, venture databases, and candidate domains and found no active corporate website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no public API surface of any kind for this company. Battery's own listing carries no outbound link. The profile is retained as an historical portfolio record rather than as an active API provider, and carries no API artifacts.

providers.name: Buysight
providers.description: Buysight, Inc. was a Silicon Valley advertising technology startup founded in 2008 that built intent-based audience targeting, retargeting, and Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO) for display advertising, using machine learning to select both the audience for an impression and the creative shown to that user. The company raised approximately $16 million from ONSET Ventures, Rembrandt Venture Partners, Uncork Capital (SoftTech VC / Jeff Clavier), Reid Hoffman, and AOL. On December 4, 2012 Buysight was acquired by AOL's Advertising.com Group, with the entire team joining AOL and the DCO and machine-learning technology folded into AOL's AdLearn optimization engine alongside Advertising.com, ADTECH, the AOL On Network, goviral, and Pictela. Buysight no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API, documentation, or SDKs. The buysight.com domain is held by MarkMonitor and redirects to a registrar placeholder page. This profile is retained as a historical acquisition record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: BuyWithMe (Gilt Groupe)
providers.description: BuyWithMe (Gilt Groupe) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: commerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Buzzer
providers.description: Buzzer was a mobile live-sports streaming startup founded in 2020 by Bo Han, formerly director of live content at Twitter. Its consumer app, launched in 2021, sold micropayment access — as low as $0.99 to $1 — to short in-game moments of live sporting events, targeting Gen Z fans who would not buy a full cable or league subscription. Buzzer secured streaming rights covering the NBA, WNBA, NHL, PGA Tour and ATP Tour, and raised roughly $44 million in total, including a $20 million Series A in June 2021 co-led by Sapphire Sport and Canaan Partners alongside a large group of athlete and team-owner investors. On 19 May 2023 the company shut down the direct-to-consumer app and pivoted to a business-to-business model branded "Powered by Buzzer", announced as API licensing, custom development and consulting for leagues, teams and networks streaming direct to fans. That offering never reached public availability: Buzzer ceased all operations on 30 June 2023, citing "recent fundraising developments and market dynamics". No public developer portal, API documentation, specification, SDK or package was ever published. The buzzer.com domain no longer hosts the company and now redirects to an Atom.com domain-for-sale listing. Retained in the network as a historical record of a defunct company; not an active API provider.

providers.name: BYBE
providers.description: BYBE, Inc. is a promotion platform for the beer, wine, and spirits industry, connecting alcohol beverage brands, retailers, and consumers through digital rebates and promotional offers. Backed by Techstars, BYBE operates in the regulated alcohol marketing space where compliance and channel constraints shape how promotions reach shoppers. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable specification; this record captures its identity plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Byjus
providers.description: Byju's is an Indian educational technology company founded in 2011 by Byju Raveendran and Divya Gokulnath and headquartered in Bengaluru, India. It offered app-based adaptive learning for K-12 students and preparation for competitive exams such as JEE, NEET, and civil services, and expanded through acquisitions including Aakash, WhiteHat Jr, Toppr, Osmo, Epic, and Great Learning. Once among the world's most valuable edtech startups, the company entered insolvency proceedings in India following a widely reported financial collapse. Byju's does not publish a public developer program or API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: C16 Biosciences
providers.description: C16 Biosciences is a New York City based synthetic biology company producing high-performance, sustainable ingredients for consumer goods manufacturers through its proprietary Palmless platform. Using microbial fermentation and biotechnology, C16 designs plant-free, deforestation-free alternatives to palm oil and petroleum-derived commodity ingredients for beauty and personal care, food, and home and personal care markets. Its flagship Palmless Torula Oil is a bioactive super-emollient with antioxidant properties for skincare formulations, alongside designer fats, oils, fatty acids, triglycerides, and alcohols. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCVC; it is an ingredients and biomanufacturing business and does not currently publish a public developer platform or API.

providers.name: Cabletron Systems
providers.description: Cabletron Systems, Inc. was an American manufacturer of networking and network-management equipment, founded in 1983 by Craig Benson and Robert Levine and headquartered in Rochester, New Hampshire. It rose to prominence in the 10BASE5 and Ethernet switching markets, shipped the ST-500 transceiver and the LAN-MD field test set, built the SPECTRUM network-management platform, and passed one billion US dollars in annual sales in 1996 at a peak of roughly 6,600 employees. In 2000 the company announced a split into four businesses: Enterasys Networks (enterprise switching), Riverstone Networks (metro service provider), Aprisma Management Technologies (SPECTRUM software), and GlobalNetwork Technology Services. The Cabletron holding company merged into Enterasys, which went public in 2001, was taken private by The Gores Group in 2006, and was acquired by Extreme Networks in 2013. Riverstone was acquired by Lucent and later liquidated. Cabletron Systems no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API, or documentation: the cabletron.com and enterasys.com domains both redirect to extremenetworks.com. This record is retained as a historical company profile only.

providers.name: CAD Solutions
providers.description: CAD Solutions, Inc. is a historical Battery Ventures portfolio company that appears in the firm's all-companies list. Research during the API Evangelist enrichment pass found no operating business, no developer surface, and no live web presence behind the name - public records indicate the company was acquired by microCAD Solutions on 1995-05-29, and the closest matching domain, cadsolutions.com, now resolves to a GoDaddy parked "for sale" page rather than a company site. The many unrelated "CAD Solutions" businesses currently trading under similar names (CAD Solutions LLC, CAD Solutions Inc of Dassault partner fame, CADD Solutions, CAD-E Solutions) are separate entities and are not this Battery portfolio record. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Cakeshop
providers.description: Cakeshop is a commerce-enablement platform that helps creators monetize their expertise, selling digital products, courses, and services directly to their audiences. It was a San Francisco-based startup operating in the creator-economy and content-monetization space, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass its public site (getcakeshop.co) returns an expired Squarespace notice, and no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or GitHub organization could be discovered; the domain still resolves over TLS and was probed for baseline security posture.

providers.name: CalAtlantic Group
providers.description: CalAtlantic Group was a U.S. homebuilder formed on October 1, 2015 through the merger of Standard Pacific Homes and Ryland Homes. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, it became the fourth largest homebuilder in the United States before being acquired by Lennar Corporation in February 2018, which made Lennar the nation's largest homebuilder. CalAtlantic no longer operates as an independent entity and does not offer public APIs or developer resources.

providers.name: Caleres
providers.description: Caleres is an American footwear company headquartered in Clayton, Missouri, established in 1878 (rebranded from Brown Shoe Company in 2015). It designs, develops, sources, manufactures, and distributes footwear through its Famous Footwear retail segment (approximately 900 U.S. locations) and Brand Portfolio segment which includes Sam Edelman, Stuart Weitzman, Allen Edmonds, Naturalizer, Vionic, LifeStride, Dr. Scholl's, Rykä, Franco Sarto, and Blowfish Malibu. Caleres does not currently publish a public developer API program; integrations are typically handled through B2B EDI and partner channels.

providers.name: Calista Technologies
providers.description: Calista Technologies was a desktop and GPU virtualization startup founded in 2006 in San Jose, California by Neal Margulis, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Greylock, and Western Technology Investment. Its software improved the user experience of 3-D and multimedia delivery for virtualized desktop deployments and server-hosted applications running on Windows Server Terminal Services (Remote Desktop). Microsoft acquired the company in 2008 and folded its GPU-virtualization technology into RemoteFX. The company is defunct and publishes no live developer, documentation, or API surface; its former domain (calistatechnologies.com) is now a parked domain listed for sale.

providers.name: Callidus Software
providers.description: Callidus Software Inc. (branded CallidusCloud) was an enterprise SaaS provider of sales performance and lead-to-money solutions, including Enterprise Incentive Management (EIM) / sales commissions, configure-price-quote (CPQ), contract lifecycle management (CLM), marketing automation, sales enablement, learning management, and gamification. Incorporated in Delaware in 1996 and headquartered in Dublin, California, it went public on Nasdaq (CALD) in 2003. SAP acquired CallidusCloud for $2.4 billion in January 2018, rebranded parts of it (e.g. SAP Litmos for the learning suite), delisted the company, and later divested pieces in 2022. As an independent developer surface CallidusCloud is defunct — the former docs portal (docs.calliduscloud.com) no longer serves a valid TLS certificate and calliduscloud.com now redirects to SAP's acquired-brands page.

providers.name: Callin
providers.description: Callin was a social podcasting and live-streaming platform founded by David Sacks and Axel Ericsson, backed by Craft Ventures, that let creators stream live audio, take listener questions, then record, edit, publish and share the result as a podcast episode. The company was acquired by Rumble (NASDAQ: RUM) in May 2023 and the standalone consumer app was subsequently wound down. As of enrichment the callin.com domain returns only a Cloudflare-gated placeholder and the provider exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cambridge Aerospace
providers.description: Cambridge Aerospace is a UK-based defense technology company, incorporated in September 2024, developing scalable interceptor missiles and sovereign air-and-missile-defense systems for European nations. Its first product, Skyhammer, is a tube-launched subsonic interceptor with a Cambridge-developed radar seeker, positioned as an affordable, mass-producible counter to drones and cruise missiles (often likened to an Iron Dome-style layered air defense). The company operates in the aerospace and defense/security sector and is backed by a venture syndicate including Accel, Lakestar, Lux Capital, Spark Capital, and the D3 fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel; it is a hardware-first defense company with no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Campanja
providers.description: Campanja was a Stockholm-based advertising-technology company founded in 2010 that built a high-frequency paid-search bid-optimization engine. Its platform placed millions of automated bids per day across Google AdWords, Google Shopping, and Yahoo/Bing search campaigns, using real-time tracking and predictive big-data modeling to improve return on ad spend for large online advertisers while cutting media cost. Campanja raised a $5M Series A (Hoxton Ventures, DFJ Esprit) and was acquired by [24]7.ai in 2015, where its technology was folded into the [24]7 Customer Acquisition Cloud. The independent company is effectively defunct and campanja.com no longer resolves to a live site. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Canopy Labs
providers.description: Canopy Labs was a customer analytics and predictive marketing SaaS company founded in 2012 in the Toronto, Ontario area (Thornhill) by Wojciech Gryc and Jorge Escobedo, with an additional office in San Francisco. A Y Combinator alumnus, it built machine-learning software that helped businesses model and predict customer behavior, optimize purchase funnels, and personalize marketing across the customer journey. The company raised seed funding from investors including BDC Venture Capital's IT Fund and Valar Ventures. In 2018 Canopy Labs was acquired by Drop Technologies (the customer-loyalty app Drop), after which the independent product, website (canopylabs.com), and any developer/API surface were wound down. This profile is retained as a historical company record; the entity no longer operates independently and publishes no live API.

providers.name: Canvas Networks
providers.description: Canvas Networks was a consumer social media and image-sharing startup founded by Christopher "moot" Poole (the founder of 4chan). Launched in private beta in early 2011 at canv.as, the platform let users share, annotate, and remix images on moderated, topic-based boards, positioning itself as a friendlier, more creative take on imageboard culture. It raised roughly $3.6M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Union Square Ventures, SV Angel, Lerer Ventures, Founder Collective, Ron Conway, and Joshua Schachter, and later pivoted to the mobile drawing app DrawQuest. The company shut down on January 21, 2014, citing its inability to build a sustainable business model. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirms it is defunct with no surviving developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Cap Hill Brands
providers.description: Cap Hill Brands was a Seattle-based e-commerce brand aggregator founded in 2020 by Kevin Saliba and Jason LeeKeenan (both former Zulily leaders). Operating as a "tech-first" Amazon aggregator, it acquired and operated digitally-native consumer/CPG brands sold on Amazon, Walmart, and Shopify, handling supply chain, marketing, and warehousing. It raised roughly $250M in debt and equity and acquired nearly 35 brands (including Butterfly Craze, merka, and LilGadgets). In March 2024 Cap Hill Brands merged with product developer Juvo+ to form Infinite Commerce, which has since been absorbed into Razor Group. Cap Hill Brands is a consumer operating company, not an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specs, SDKs, or partner integration surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Version One Ventures and retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record.

providers.name: Capacity Bio
providers.description: Capacity Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing mitophagy therapeutics to restore mitochondrial quality control in age- and disease-related conditions. Its platform advances small molecules, peptides, and nanoparticles that enhance identification and clearance of dysfunctional mitochondria. With operations in Los Angeles and Tokyo, the company closed a $35M financing round in 2023 and is backed by Insight Partners. As a drug-development firm, Capacity Bio publishes no public API, developer platform, or SDK surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: CapriCoast
providers.description: CapriCoast (CapriCoast Home Solutions Pvt Ltd) was a Bengaluru, India based online modular-furniture and modular-kitchen retailer, founded in 2014 and backed by Accel Partners and RB Investments. It offered an online 3D catalog of kitchens and wardrobes with designs pre-customized for project floor plans. The company was acquired by HomeLane in November 2017 and no longer operates independently; its domain (capricoast.com) is now parked/for-sale and it publishes no developer, API, or documentation surface. Sector: consumer. Retained in the network as an Accel portfolio record; no API artifacts are available to enrich.

providers.name: Capriza
providers.description: Capriza was an enterprise mobility software company founded in 2011 in Palo Alto, California, backed by a16z and others across roughly $73.5M in funding. Its platform took a no-code approach to mobilizing workflows from legacy enterprise applications such as SAP, Oracle and PeopleSoft by driving their existing user interfaces, explicitly WITHOUT requiring APIs, new infrastructure or custom code. The company has permanently closed and never published a public API surface, so this record is retained as a historical network entry rather than an enrichable provider profile.

providers.name: Carbonated
providers.description: Carbonated Inc. is a mobile game developer founded in 2015 by industry veterans from Zynga, Electronic Arts, and Blizzard. The studio builds hardcore PvEvP (player-versus-environment-versus-player) games for phones and uses AI to help drive moment-to-moment gameplay. Its debut title is Mad World, currently in early-access sign-up. Carbonated also operates Carbyne, a proprietary live-ops platform that lets the team instantly modify almost every part of the game experience through a comprehensive set of web tools, built to support multiple games. Carbonated is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). As of this profile Carbonated publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this record captures the company identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CarbonData
providers.description: CarbonData is a seed-stage company that appears in Bloomberg Beta's publicly published portfolio manual, listed under the Bloomberg Beta 2013 L.P. fund (covering investments made roughly 2013-2016) with Matthew Moore named as the associated founder. Bloomberg Beta's own portfolio listing carries no website link for the company, and enrichment searches and DNS/HTTP probes in July 2026 found no attributable company website, developer portal, documentation, API, or source repository. The company appears to be dormant or wound down; no API surface exists to catalog at this time.

providers.name: CardMonster Inc.
providers.description: CardMonster turns ideas and brands into games. The company designs and publishes premium IP-based tabletop titles with global partners such as Disney and Krafton, and builds CardMonster Forge, an AI-powered tool that helps creators turn their own ideas into playable digital prototypes. From physical board games to an online playtesting platform, CardMonster connects creativity and technology to make game creation faster, smarter, and more accessible. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass CardMonster publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Cardmunch
providers.description: CardMunch was a mobile business-card scanning service that used human transcription to turn photographed business cards into contact records on iOS. Founded as a Y Combinator and 500 Global backed startup, it was acquired by LinkedIn in January 2011 for a reported sum under $3 million and operated as a free LinkedIn-branded iPhone app. LinkedIn discontinued the app on July 11, 2014, migrating its users to Evernote's business-card scanning feature. CardMunch never published a public developer program, API, or SDK, and the cardmunch.com domain was re-registered by an unrelated party in April 2016 and now hosts an affiliate content blog. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cargon Tech B.V.
providers.description: Cargon Tech B.V. is a supply-chain and logistics technology company backed by 500 Global. Its public presence at cargon.com positions Cargon as a fast, innovative supply-chain platform with powerful analytical tools for shippers and carriers, while the related Cargon TMS product (cargon.tech) offers a cloud transport-management system for small carriers and freight forwarders covering dispatch, fleet management, invoicing and Timocom integration. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment (the cargon.com site is a client-rendered single-page app that returns its index shell for unknown paths), so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Carmera *
providers.description: CARMERA was a New York City based road-intelligence and HD mapping company that provided "change-as-a-service" map maintenance for autonomous driving, mobility-as-a-service and consumer navigation. It used consumer-grade cameras mounted on commercial fleet vehicles as crowdsourced visual probes to detect permanent road inventory change (signs, signals, lane markings) and temporary closure events (construction), then regenerated both HD and SD maps in near real time. Its commercial offering was described as detection APIs that identify map-impacting events plus vector APIs that deliver map updates, layered over a customer-supplied or CARMERA-supplied base map. The company was backed by GV and was acquired in July 2021 by Woven Planet (now Woven by Toyota), the advanced mobility subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation. Its APIs were sold under enterprise agreements and were never published as a public developer program; as of this enrichment pass the carmera.com domain no longer resolves and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API artifact survives.

providers.name: Carousell
providers.description: Carousell is a Singapore-headquartered classifieds and recommerce marketplace founded in 2012 that lets people buy and sell secondhand and new goods, cars, and property across Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. The Carousell Group operates a family of consumer marketplace brands including Carousell, Cho Tot, Mudah, OneShift, Laku6, Refash, and Ox Street, spanning general classifieds, automotive, and recommerce verticals. Carousell was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; it is a consumer marketplace with no publicly documented developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Carpooling
providers.description: Carpooling.com GmbH was one of Europe's largest ridesharing / carpooling platforms, founded in Munich, Germany and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital. It connected drivers with empty seats to passengers travelling the same route across Europe. In April 2015 the company was acquired by the French ridesharing operator BlaBlaCar and its operations were merged into that platform. The carpooling.com domain and every developer-facing subdomain (developer / api / docs) now redirect to BlaBlaCar (blablacar.co.uk), and no independent Carpooling developer portal, API, or specification remains. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record; there is no live API surface of its own to enrich.

providers.name: Carr, Riggs & Ingram (CRI)
providers.description: Carr, Riggs & Ingram (CRI) is a top-25 nationally ranked accounting and advisory firm headquartered in Alabama, operating 70+ locations across 13 states plus Mexico. The firm delivers audit and attest, tax, and advisory services (cybersecurity, fraud and forensics, valuations, and transaction advisory) to more than 18 industries, alongside value add-on subsidiaries including CRI Advanced Analytics, CRI CFO Hub, and CRI M&A Advisors, and is a member of PrimeGlobal. It was surfaced via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched here; note that criadv.com is a professional-services accounting firm, not a Bessemer-backed fintech startup, so the portfolio-lead tagging is a domain false-positive. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface exists.

providers.name: Carsome
providers.description: Carsome is Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, with operations across Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Singapore. The company runs an online marketplace where consumers can sell, buy, and finance pre-owned vehicles, combining a consumer-facing storefront with B2B dealer auctions, vehicle inspection and certification, logistics, insurance, and financing services. Carsome is a venture-backed technology company (a regional unicorn) counted among the portfolio of 500 Global. No public developer program, API documentation, or API surface has been found; this profile remains a company/lead record awaiting any published API.
