providers.name: Cascade
providers.description: Cascade (www.cascade.io) was a no-code data analysis platform founded in 2019 by Jake Fuentes and Jon Brelig that let non-technical business teams import large datasets, transform and combine them with no-code tools, then visualize and present findings as interactive data apps (positioned as a cloud-native, collaborative alternative to Alteryx). The company wound down in 2023 after failing to reach breakout growth; www.cascade.io now serves a retrospective "What Cascade Did" page. As of the 2026-07-18 enrichment probe there is no public API, developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or documentation surface to enrich, so this profile carries identity only.

providers.name: cashbus
providers.description: CashBus (现金巴士), operated by Micro-Credit Speed Express (Group) Co., Ltd. (微额速达集团有限公司) of Shanghai, is a Chinese mobile financial-technology platform providing quick microloans to underserved consumers who lack access to traditional banking. The company runs an automated, AI-driven credit decision engine that scores applicants in seconds using thousands of risk factors and big-data analysis, with risk management spanning pre-loan, in-loan, and post-loan stages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. The public presence is a corporate marketing site (company vision, team, careers, contact) with no published developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cashforce
providers.description: Cashforce is a fintech platform focused on cash flow forecasting and working-capital analytics for corporate treasury and finance teams, connecting ERP systems, bank accounts, and financial data to give companies real-time visibility into cash positions, liquidity, and forecasting scenarios. Originally a Techstars-backed portfolio company, Cashforce was acquired by Billtrust and its standalone product surface is no longer independently operated; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public footprint. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definitions are currently reachable at the cashforce.com origin (the site returns HTTP 522), so this record carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Caspida
providers.description: Caspida was a cybersecurity company specializing in user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), applying unsupervised machine learning to network, endpoint, and identity data to detect insider threats and advanced attacks without predefined rules. Splunk acquired Caspida in July 2015 and folded its technology into Splunk User Behavior Analytics (Splunk UBA). Caspida no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone developer program, API, or documentation surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record.

providers.name: Caviar
providers.description: Caviar is a premium restaurant food-ordering and delivery marketplace that connects diners with local, higher-end and popular restaurants for on-demand delivery and pickup. Originally launched in 2012 and later owned by Square, Caviar was acquired by DoorDash in 2019 and now operates on DoorDash's logistics and marketplace platform under the trycaviar.com brand. The service focuses on curated restaurant selection, quality-oriented ordering, courier delivery, and catering. Caviar does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead and captures whatever public, agent-relevant surface exists.

providers.name: Cavium
providers.description: Cavium, Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 and headquartered in San Jose, California, that designed multicore processors and networking silicon for enterprise, data center, cloud, and service-provider infrastructure. Its product families included OCTEON multicore MIPS and ARM network and security processors, ThunderX ARM-based server SoCs, Nitrox security processors, LiquidIO intelligent adapters and smart NICs, and the FastLinQ Ethernet and Xpliant switch lines it gained through its 2016 acquisition of QLogic. Cavium was a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: CAVM) before being acquired by Marvell Technology Group in July 2018 for roughly 6 billion US dollars. Its technology now ships as part of Marvell's networking and infrastructure processor portfolio. As a silicon and hardware vendor, Cavium never operated a public developer API program or web API surface.

providers.name: Cazena
providers.description: Cazena was a Waltham, Massachusetts-based enterprise software company, founded in 2014, that delivered a fully-managed SaaS data platform — a "Big Data as a Service" cloud data lake that let enterprises run analytics, machine learning, and data-lake workloads on managed cloud infrastructure without operating the underlying stack themselves. The company was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), North Bridge Venture Partners, and Formation 8. Cloudera agreed to acquire Cazena (alongside Datacoral) in June 2021, folding Cazena's managed SaaS data-lake technology into the Cloudera platform. Cazena no longer operates as an independent provider; its domain cazena.com now redirects to cloudera.com, and it exposes no independent public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: CE 140
providers.description: CE 140 is a placeholder record surfaced from a 500 Global portfolio scrape and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The name is a scrape artifact rather than a real company name, and the only identifying detail carried on the stub was the website https://siftery.com. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found that domain no longer serves the company it was recorded for: it returns an unrelated WordPress site (title "About Us", meta description describing US-focused casino guides) behind Cloudflare, and every API and discovery path probed returned 404 (/.well-known/security.txt, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, /.well-known/api-catalog, /.well-known/ai-plugin.json, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /api, /docs). There is no API surface, no developer portal, and no verifiable operating company behind this record. It is retained as a dead lead so future enrichment runs do not re-spend search budget on it.

providers.name: cehome
providers.description: cehome (铁甲工程机械网, "Tiejia") is a Chinese digital platform for the construction and engineering machinery industry, operated at cehome.com and m.cehome.com. It is a professional information hub and community serving equipment owners, operators, dealers, and manufacturers: industry news and price data, product reviews, buying guides and detailed product listings across brands (Sany, Caterpillar, Komatsu, Doosan, and others) and equipment types (excavators, loaders, bulldozers, cranes), a used-machinery marketplace, operator job listings, and the active 铁甲论坛 community forum. cehome is a consumer/community web platform rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or programmatic API surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Celequest
providers.description: Celequest was a business intelligence software company that built an appliance-based platform for real-time operational BI — streaming dashboards and continuous analytics over live transactional data rather than batch data-warehouse reporting. The company was acquired by Cognos in 2007, and its technology was folded into the Cognos Now! operational BI appliance; Cognos itself was acquired by IBM in 2008. Celequest no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer surface. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe, celequest.com and www.celequest.com resolve to IBM redirect infrastructure (redirect.www.ibm.com) and issue a blanket HTTP 301 to the IBM Cognos Now! product page for every path, including /.well-known/* and /llms.txt. There is no portal, no documentation, no API, and no artifacts to harvest. This record is retained as a historical/acquired-company entry in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cencorp
providers.description: Cencorp (Zhuhai) Industrial Technology Co., Ltd. is a process-automation equipment manufacturer that designs and builds high-end laser processing, dispensing, automated optical inspection (AOI), and system-integration & automation systems for the consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor, and new-energy industries. Formed in 2020 and combining the acquired Finland-based Cencorp automation business with operations headquartered in Zhuhai, China, the company runs 12 offices worldwide with 400+ R&D engineers and 300+ patents, and is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this is a physical automation-equipment business.

providers.name: CenterForce Technologies
providers.description: CenterForce Technologies was a Bethesda, Maryland software company that built workforce-optimization, workforce-management, and performance-analytics software for contact centers. It partnered with Concerto Software for nearly a decade before Concerto acquired it on 2004-04-26 to pair CenterForce's workforce and contact-center management tools with Concerto's ACD, IVR, and email contact-channel products. Concerto was itself taken private in 2005 and rebranded as Aspect Software in 2007, absorbing the former CenterForce workforce-optimization product line. The company raised roughly $6.01M; investors included Battery Ventures, Piper Sandler, Aspect Software, and SightLine Partners. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead. Enrichment (2026-07-18) confirmed it is a long-defunct, acquired entity with no independent website, developer portal, or API surface; there is nothing to catalog.

providers.name: Chaart
providers.description: Chaart (주식회사 차트, Chaart Inc.) is a Seoul-based art-trading and art-asset-management platform for South Korea's art collectors and investors. Its iOS and Android apps let collectors buy and resell artworks in the secondary market with transparent price/valuation information, automatic artwork matching, authenticity checks, secure delivery, and integrated payments. Chaart reports 5,000+ registered collectors and thousands of artworks traded, and raised pre-seed funding from 500 Global. Chaart is a consumer mobile app: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Chalkable
providers.description: Chalkable was a K-12 education technology company that provided a cloud-based student information system (SIS), learning management, and an education "app store" letting schools run third-party classroom apps on top of shared student data. Its developer platform exposed a RESTful API (OAuth 2.0) over school data points such as student and teacher scheduling, real-time attendance, grading and discipline records, announcements, messaging, and notifications, with partner apps rendered inside an iframe within the Chalkable classroom. Chalkable was acquired by PowerSchool on October 12, 2016, and the product line was absorbed into PowerSchool; the original developer surface (dev.chalkable.com and classroom.chalkable.com/Developer) is no longer operational. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: changeducation
providers.description: ChangEducation is an integrated teaching-service provider of artificial-intelligence and STEAM curriculum systems, surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It builds AI and STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Mathematics) curriculum products and teaching services for the Chinese K-12 education market. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing website (changeducation.cn, which redirects to a JavaScript-rendered landing page) with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this profile remains an identity-only lead with no technical API artifacts.

providers.name: Chart Industries
providers.description: Chart Industries is a leading global manufacturer of highly engineered equipment servicing multiple market applications in clean energy and industrial gas. The company provides cryogenic equipment, process technologies, and aftermarket services for hydrogen, LNG, biogas, CO2 capture, and traditional industrial gases. Chart Industries does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: chatail
providers.description: Chatail is a Shanghai-based SaaS company (founded 2016) that provides private-domain livestream and video sales software for high-end and luxury retail brands across fashion, jewelry, beauty, automotive, and home-goods verticals, pairing intelligent customer acquisition with conversion tooling ("智能获客与高效转化双轮驱动"). The product is delivered as a hosted web application at chatail.com; no public developer API, documentation portal, or OpenAPI surface is published at this time (api.chatail.com serves a default nginx placeholder). Chatail raised a Series B round led by Qiming Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Qiming portfolio company.

providers.name: Checkin
providers.description: Checkin (checkin.cc) was a Bloomberg Beta-backed social-connection platform that brought thousands of people together for structured, timed 8-minute weekly one-on-one conversations intended to spark meaningful human connection. The consumer service ceased operations on June 30, 2023; the domain now serves a shutdown notice and the only remaining contact is support@checkin.cc. The company published no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this profile has no API artifacts to enrich beyond a live domain-security probe of the remaining host.

providers.name: Chemtura
providers.description: Chemtura Corporation was a global specialty chemicals company that developed, manufactured, and marketed chemical intermediates, additives, specialty chemicals, urethanes, organometallics, and modern plastics. In April 2017, Chemtura was acquired by LANXESS AG, the German specialty chemicals company headquartered in Cologne, and its operations were integrated into LANXESS's Performance Materials and other business segments. Chemtura products are now marketed and supported through LANXESS, which continues to serve agriculture, animal care, mobility, consumer goods, electrical and electronics, energy, food, and healthcare end markets.

providers.name: Cherwell Software
providers.description: Cherwell Software was an IT service management (ITSM) vendor founded in 2004 and headquartered in Colorado Springs, Colorado. Its flagship Cherwell Service Management (CSM) platform, first released in 2007, let IT departments automate routine tasks, manage incidents, problems, changes, and assets, and build codeless workflows, later expanding into enterprise service management for HR, Facilities, Information Security, and Project Management. Cherwell was acquired by Ivanti on March 25, 2021, and its products were folded into the Ivanti Neurons portfolio: Cherwell ITSM became Ivanti Neurons for ITSM, Cherwell ITAM became Ivanti Neurons for ITAM, and Cherwell CORE became Ivanti's Enterprise Service Management offering. The cherwell.com domain now 301-redirects to Ivanti, and no standalone Cherwell-branded developer portal, API, or public specification remains. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chery
providers.description: Chery Automobile Co., Ltd. is a Chinese state-owned automobile manufacturer headquartered in Wuhu, Anhui, and one of China's largest passenger-vehicle exporters, conducting business in more than 130 countries and regions. Its brand portfolio spans the core Chery marque (TIGGO and ARRIZO SUV and sedan series), the Fengyun and OMODA/JAECOO new-energy lines, and the QQ city-car brand, with a growing emphasis on the CSH (Chery Super Hybrid) powertrain and connected-vehicle technology. Chery was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As an automotive manufacturer, Chery publishes corporate and consumer web properties but no public developer portal or API surface was found during this pass.

providers.name: Chi Forest
providers.description: Chi Forest (marketed as CHI FOREST) is the US-facing consumer beverage brand of the Chinese drinks company Genki Forest (元气森林), backed by Hongshan (Sequoia China) and IDG Capital. The company produces zero-sugar, zero-calorie, zero-caffeine sparkling refreshers with Asian-inspired, fruit-forward flavors such as guava and lychee, distributed through retailers including Costco, Amazon, and H Mart. It is a direct-to-consumer and retail beverage brand with a marketing/e-commerce web presence and no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface at this time. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector company record.

providers.name: Chickin
providers.description: Chickin is an Indonesian poultry-technology company operating a full-stack, integrated ecosystem for chicken farmers across Indonesia. It combines closed-house smart-farming hardware (IoT climate and environmental controllers), day-old-chick and feed supply, farmer financing, and guaranteed offtake and distribution of live birds, aiming to modernize and de-risk small and mid-scale poultry farming. Backed by 500 Global, Chickin runs its operations through a mobile and web application at chickin.id. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile records its public web presence and domain-security posture and remains a lead for further enrichment should a developer surface be published.

providers.name: Chordiant Software
providers.description: Chordiant Software Corporation was an enterprise software vendor founded in 1991 and based in California, known for customer relationship management (CRM) and customer decision management software used by large banks, insurers, telecommunications carriers, and healthcare organizations. Its products included Chordiant Decision Management, Marketing Director, and Recommendation Advisor, delivering real-time predictive decisioning and next-best-action recommendations across customer channels. The company went public on NASDAQ (CHRD) in 2000 and was acquired by Pegasystems in 2010, with its decisioning technology folded into Pega's Customer Decision Hub. Chordiant no longer operates as an independent company and exposes no public developer portal or API; the chordiant.com domain now redirects to pega.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record and carries no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: chowbotics
providers.description: Chowbotics was a food-robotics company known for "Sally," a fresh-food and salad vending robot that assembled customized bowls on demand for cafeterias, hospitals, campuses, and grocery locations. The company was acquired by DoorDash in early 2021 and no longer operates as a standalone business; its domain (chowbotics.com) now redirects to DoorDash (get.doordash.com). As of this enrichment pass Chowbotics publishes no independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or other machine-readable developer surface, so this remains an identity-only record in the API Evangelist network rather than an active API provider profile.

providers.name: Chrono24
providers.description: Chrono24 is one of the world's leading online marketplaces for luxury and pre-owned watches, connecting tens of thousands of professional dealers and private sellers with buyers across more than 100 countries. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, the platform lists hundreds of thousands of watches and offers buyer protection through its Trusted Checkout escrow service, authentication, and integrated payment and shipping. Chrono24 operates as a consumer web and mobile marketplace and does not publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence and demand tracking. Backed by Insight Partners and General Atlantic.

providers.name: chushou
providers.description: Chushou (触手TV / 触手直播) was a China-based mobile game live-streaming platform, at one point among the largest mobile-focused game streaming services in China, letting players broadcast and watch mobile gameplay. It was backed by Qiming Venture Partners and Tencent and is surfaced here as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company's public web presence at chushou.tv is unreachable (the server returns empty replies) and it exposes no documented developer API, SDK, or portal, so this profile remains an inactive/defunct lead with no live API surface to enrich beyond DNS/TLS-level signals.

providers.name: Chute
providers.description: Chute was a visual marketing automation platform (getchute.com) that helped brands discover, collect, rights-manage and publish consumer and user-generated visual content. Its product line spanned visual insights, digital asset management and content publishing, and it exposed a public REST API documented on Apiary (docs.chute.apiary.io) with first-party Ruby and Node.js client libraries. The company is defunct: the canonical domain no longer serves a site, the API and developer hosts do not resolve, the Apiary documentation returns 502, and the github.com/chute organization has been deleted. Only the abandoned package-registry entries survive. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record of a former API provider.

providers.name: Cinder
providers.description: Cinder is a Trust & Safety platform — an operating system for online Trust & Safety and content moderation teams. It unifies policy management, content review and moderation queues, investigations, automated detection, and reporting into a single workflow so platforms can enforce their rules consistently and at scale. The company (originally at cinder.co, now cinder.ai) was founded by operators with backgrounds at Meta, Palantir, and US national-security teams, and applies AI and agentic automation to content classification, case management, and enforcement. Cinder is venture-backed (Accel, and additional investors) and sits in the security / trust & safety sector. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company and enriched by the pipeline; the company's public surface is behind bot protection, so API artifacts remain to be confirmed.

providers.name: CipherCloud
providers.description: CipherCloud was a cloud security company, founded in 2010, that pioneered the cloud access security broker (CASB) category. Its platform provided encryption and tokenization, data loss prevention, cloud discovery and shadow IT visibility, threat protection, and compliance controls for SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Office 365, ServiceNow, and Box. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Index Ventures among others, CipherCloud was acquired by mobile and cloud security vendor Lookout in early 2021, and its CASB technology was folded into Lookout's Secure Cloud Access offering. The standalone ciphercloud.com developer and product surface has since been retired; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record. No live public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface could be located during enrichment (ciphercloud.com returns HTTP 404 and no developer/docs subdomains resolve).

No public API, developer platform, SDKs, or developer documentation are published by Circa Labs at this time.

providers.name: Circular
providers.description: Circular was a Spanish hiring community that connected tech recruiters with software developers, describing itself as a "Hiring Community for Tech Recruiters & Developers." It operated a referral-driven talent network in which recruiters shared vetted candidates they could not place themselves, and developers received job opportunities through that trusted pool rather than through cold outreach. The company was backed by Point Nine Capital and ran its candidate and recruiter landing experiences on a Next.js application served from circular.io and static.circular.io. Circular has since shut down and merged into Manfred (getmanfred.com), the largest tech community in Spain, with its own migration notice stating "Circular cierra sus puertas para integrarse en Manfred." The circular.io domain remains registered to Singular People Europe S.L. but has been fully undelegated, and Point Nine no longer lists Circular in its portfolio. Circular never published a public developer program, API, SDK, or specification. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Circularity Fuels
providers.description: Circularity Fuels builds AI-controlled, mass-manufacturable reactors that turn waste carbon and cheap renewable power into drop-in hydrocarbons, starting with affordable sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Its Ouro Reactor reforms waste carbon (methane and CO2 off-gassed by dairy farms, agricultural plants, and industrial facilities) into clean syngas, and its Aion Reactor uses next-generation Fischer-Tropsch synthesis to assemble that syngas into liquid fuels. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It is a hardware and process company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Citadel
providers.description: Citadel (also branded Citadel Defense / Drone Citadel) is a counter-unmanned-aircraft-system (C-UAS) company founded in 2016 that built an automated, modular drone-defense solution using proprietary machine-learning algorithms to detect, classify, and defeat unauthorized drones. It raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series A in 2017 and was subsequently acquired by BlueHalo. The company operates no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, and its standalone domains (citadeldefense.com, dronecitadel.com) are now parked or no longer resolve.

providers.name: Citadel Securities
providers.description: Citadel Securities is one of the world's leading market makers and electronic trading firms, providing liquidity and price discovery across equities, options, exchange-traded funds, fixed income, currencies, and commodities for institutional and retail investors globally. Founded in 2002 by Ken Griffin, the firm operates a high-performance, technology-driven trading platform. It is a privately held financial-services company and does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity and public infrastructure posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Civitas Resources
providers.description: Civitas Resources is an independent exploration and production company focused on developing oil and natural gas resources in Colorado's Denver-Julesburg Basin and the Permian Basin. The company emphasizes carbon-neutral operations and sustainable production practices. Civitas Resources does not currently publish a public developer portal or API. The company has announced a merger with SM Energy Company.

providers.name: Clarity
providers.description: Clarity (clarity.fm) is an on-demand business advice marketplace that connects entrepreneurs and startup founders with a curated network of vetted experts, advisors, and industry leaders for paid, one-on-one phone consultations booked by the minute. Founded by Dan Martell and now part of the Startups.co family, Clarity lets members search experts by topic, schedule calls, and pay per-minute for coaching on fundraising, marketing, sales, product, and growth. As of this enrichment pass Clarity publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's identity and a live domain-security probe of clarity.fm.

providers.name: Cleanwise
providers.description: Cleanwise (Cleanwise, Inc.) is a Jan/San procurement management company serving multi-location national and regional businesses. The company applies janitorial supply category knowledge and custom procurement management systems to help customers manage, measure, and control their janitorial and sanitation spend. Cleanwise describes itself as technology-enabled and customer-driven, combining in-house procurement systems, industry expertise, and supplier partnerships to deliver product efficiencies and standardized best practices across distributed facility footprints. Its published customer examples include the US Postal Service, JCPenney, and Best Buy, with claimed first-year savings of 10-20% of total Jan/San spend. Insight Partners has listed Cleanwise in its portfolio since 2022. No public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API artifact has been found for Cleanwise; the company operates as a procurement services provider rather than an API producer.

providers.name: ClearMix
providers.description: ClearMix was a technology startup founded by Gabriel Ruttner and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It is listed in Bloomberg Beta's public portfolio with an exit marker, indicating the company has since exited (acquired or wound down). providers.name: Clearstory Data
providers.description: Clearstory Data was a big-data analytics startup (Menlo Park / Mountain View, CA) that built a cloud service for blending and visualizing enterprise and third-party data, backed by a16z, GV (Google Ventures), Kleiner Perkins and Khosla Ventures. It was acquired by Alteryx in 2016 and is no longer an independent company. Its former domain (clearstorydata.com) has lapsed and now 301-redirects to unrelated parked/spam sites, so it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/defunct portfolio record; no live artifacts are producible.

providers.name: Clinovas LTD
providers.description: Clinovas LTD (Clinova, clinova.ai) is an AI-powered patient recruitment platform for clinical trials. Per the company's own site, it matches eligible patients to trials in minutes rather than months using AI-powered patient matching against hospital electronic health records (EHR). The solution is hospital-based and HIPAA-compliant, targeting clinical research organizations and trial sponsors operating in emerging markets including Eastern Europe and the CIS region. Backed by 500 Global. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: CliQr Technologies *
providers.description: CliQr Technologies was a San Jose, California cloud management software company, backed by GV (Google Ventures) and Google Capital, that built the CloudCenter platform for application-defined hybrid cloud orchestration. Its single application profile let enterprises model, deploy, and manage workloads across bare-metal, virtualized, and container environments and across public clouds (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, IBM SoftLayer, Rackspace) and private clouds (OpenStack, CloudStack, VMware vCloud). Cisco announced its intent to acquire CliQr for $260 million in March 2016 and folded the product into Cisco CloudCenter as part of its hybrid cloud strategy; CliQr no longer operates as an independent company and maintains no active developer surface, API, or documentation.

providers.name: Clothes Horse
providers.description: Clothes Horse was a New York-based, data-driven size-and-fit recommendation company for online apparel shopping. It matched a shopper's body measurements and brand preferences against retailers' actual garment measurements to recommend the right size at the point of sale, sold to retailers as SaaS. The company merged with Fits.me in December 2014 to form a virtual-fitting-room solutions provider, and no longer operates as an independent entity. It exposed no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and the clotheshor.se domain now resolves to an unrelated Swedish fashion/lifestyle WordPress blog. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; enrichment found no live API surface.

providers.name: Cloud Commerce
providers.description: Cloud Commerce (CloudCommerce) is a Bangkok, Thailand-based venture tech builder helping small and medium enterprises across Southeast Asia sell globally. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups) at the seed stage, it operates three commerce platforms: FastShip, a cross-border e-commerce logistics platform; CloudMall, an e-commerce distribution platform to build, run, and scale online marketplaces; and KOLLAB, an influencer-commerce platform connecting brands with over 100,000 KOLs across Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook. The company connects SME product data to global online marketplaces and logistics providers. No public developer/API surface was found during enrichment (no docs, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery endpoints).

providers.name: Cloudflare Trace

providers.name: CloudPhysics
providers.description: CloudPhysics is a SaaS-based big-data analytics platform for virtualized IT infrastructure, founded in 2011 and acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise in 2021. Deployed as the CloudPhysics Observer virtual appliance against VMware vSphere / vCenter, it collects IT metadata and delivers data-driven insights for capacity planning, cost optimization, migration assessment, and infrastructure health. It is now part of HPE; cloudphysics.com redirects to HPE storage. CloudPhysics exposes no public developer API of its own — the product consumes the VMware vCenter API to gather metadata rather than publishing a developer-facing API, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Cloudpipes
providers.description: Cloudpipes was a Sofia (Bulgaria) and London-based iPaaS (integration platform as a service) that provided a cloud-based integration and workflow-automation platform for connecting SaaS applications and automating business processes without code. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups / 500 Istanbul), BrightCap Ventures and LAUNCHub Ventures, the company was acquired by Vista-backed Quickbase (Quick Base) in August 2019 and its standalone product and developer surface were subsequently wound down. This API Evangelist profile is a historical/portfolio record: the cloudpipes.com origin is offline (Cloudflare 522) and no live API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts remain available to harvest.

providers.name: Cloudsimple
providers.description: CloudSimple was an enterprise software company that ran secure, dedicated VMware workloads (VMware Cloud Foundation - vSphere, vSAN, NSX) as a managed service on public clouds, originally partnering with Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. Google Cloud acquired CloudSimple in November 2019 and folded the technology into Google Cloud VMware Engine; the standalone company, product, and developer surface no longer exist. The former domain (cloudsimple.com) resolves to a Google-owned IP but serves no live website, documentation, or API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and Redpoint Ventures and remains in the API Evangelist network as a historical / defunct-provider record; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: CloudSwitch
providers.description: CloudSwitch was a cloud-infrastructure software startup founded in 2008 by Ellen Rubin and John Considine and headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts. Its flagship product, CloudSwitch Enterprise, was a downloadable software appliance that installed into VMware and Xen environments and enabled enterprises to migrate and run existing Windows and Linux virtual machines in public clouds such as Amazon EC2 and Terremark without re-architecting them, preserving networking and security boundaries. The company raised roughly $15.4M across two rounds from Matrix Partners, Atlas Venture, and Commonwealth Capital Ventures, and was acquired by Verizon in August 2011 and folded into its Terremark cloud services unit. The company is defunct: it operates no independent website, developer portal, or API, so this profile remains a historical portfolio-lead stub with no live surface to enrich.

providers.name: Club Factory
providers.description: Club Factory was a Chinese-owned cross-border e-commerce marketplace app that grew to roughly 70 million users globally, with India its largest market at around 40 million users. In June 2020 the Government of India banned Club Factory alongside 58 other Chinese apps citing data and privacy concerns, and the company withdrew from the Indian market shortly after. It was originally added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead surfaced from Qiming's portfolio. Enrichment finds the company effectively defunct - clubfactory.com no longer serves a company site (it is parked for sale via Afternic nameservers and redirects to a /lander page), there is no live developer or API surface, no published SDKs, and no discoverable /.well-known documents.

providers.name: Clusterk
providers.description: ClusterK was a cloud cost-optimization startup founded in 2013 in Palo Alto, California by Dmitry Pushkarev. Its software let AWS users run production and batch workloads on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances at up to 90% savings versus on-demand pricing, by predicting spot-market prices and continuously rebalancing capacity across instance types. ClusterK shipped two products: ClusterK Balancer, which arbitraged the AWS Spot Market for cost savings, and ClusterK Cirrus, a cloud-native HPC grid scheduler. The company was backed by DCVC (Data Collective), Rally Ventures, and the Mayo Clinic Business Accelerator, raising roughly $1.2M. Amazon acquired ClusterK in April 2015 and absorbed the team and technology into AWS; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Clustree
providers.description: Clustree was a French HR-technology startup founded in 2014 that built an AI-powered skills engine and a multilingual skills ontology (over 53,000 verified skills consolidated from more than one billion job skills) used to match employees to internal roles and mobility opportunities. It was acquired by Cornerstone OnDemand in early 2020 (approximately $18.5M, all-cash) and its technology was folded into Cornerstone's People Intelligence / Skills platform. The independent Clustree brand is discontinued: clustree.com no longer serves a website and there is no live developer portal, public API, documentation, SDK, or package registry presence under the Clustree name. This profile is retained as a network identity/lead record only.

providers.name: Clutch Learning
providers.description: Clutch Learning (Clutch Prep) was a Miami-based education-technology startup founded in 2011 that helped more than two million college students learn through thousands of short-form, topic-based video tutorials and practice problems across subjects such as chemistry, physics, biology, accounting, and calculus. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), the company was acquired by Pearson in 2022 and folded into the Pearson+ study platform, where the offering now lives as Pearson Channels. The standalone clutchprep.com product is no longer independently operated. The domain 301-redirects to pearson.com/channels, and the company exposes no independent developer portal, public API, SDKs, or event surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record.

providers.name: Cmd *
providers.description: Cmd was a Vancouver, Canada-based cybersecurity startup founded in 2016 that built runtime security and observability purpose-built for Linux infrastructure, giving security and DevOps teams real-time visibility and policy-based control over user activity across cloud workloads. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), which led its $15M Series B in 2019, Cmd raised roughly $21.6M total before being acquired by Elastic in August 2021, where its technology was folded into the Elastic Security cloud workload protection and Limitless XDR offering. Co-founders Jake King (CSO) and Santosh Krishan joined Elastic through the acquisition. Cmd no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live API, developer portal, or public API surface; this profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: cn
providers.description: cn is the China-region web presence (cn.ausperbio.com) of AusperBio Therapeutics (Hangzhou Ausper Bio / 杭州浩博医药有限公司), a Phase II clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming HBV treatment toward a functional cure and advancing oligonucleotide therapeutics. AusperBio leverages its proprietary Med-Oligo ASO platform with targeted delivery technologies to apply antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapeutics across viral infections, metabolic conditions, genetic disorders, and immune diseases; its lead candidate AHB-137 is an unconjugated ASO advancing through Phase II/III trials for chronic hepatitis B. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; the company publishes a marketing website but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: CNANO
providers.description: CNANO (Jiangsu Cnano Technology Co., Ltd., Shanghai STAR Market 688116) is a carbon nanotube and graphene materials manufacturer founded in 2011 and headquartered in Zhenjiang, China, with a US arm (Cnano USA) in Santa Clara, California. It develops and mass-produces multi-wall and single-wall carbon nanotube powders, conductive pastes, graphene composite pastes, and conductive masterbatches used as additives in lithium-ion batteries, conductive polymer composites, antistatic coatings, and tire rubber reinforcement. It is one of the largest global producers of multi-wall carbon nanotubes for battery applications. Backed by IDG Capital. This is a physical-materials manufacturer with no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface.

providers.description: Online Compiler for Various Languages

providers.name: Cogito
providers.description: Cogito Corp was a Boston-based real-time artificial-intelligence company that provided emotional-intelligence and conversation-guidance software for contact-center agents, analyzing voice signals during live phone calls to coach agents in the moment and surface customer-experience and agent-wellbeing insights. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by Battery Ventures), Cogito's primary domain cogitocorp.com now 301-redirects to verint.com and its developer subdomains no longer resolve, reflecting the product's absorption into Verint's customer- experience automation portfolio. Cogito no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface; this record is retained as an identity and acquisition profile. The enrichment pass found no standalone Cogito public API, OpenAPI, documentation, developer portal, SDK, or well-known surface to catalog.

providers.name: Cohesion
providers.description: Cohesion is a New York City-based financial intelligence company (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building AI agents that automate investment research for hedge funds and institutional investors. The platform continuously monitors public companies across earnings reports, news, podcasts, and social media such as X/Twitter to surface differentiated investing signals that fundamental equity analysts would otherwise spend hours a week tracking manually. Founded by Devon Krapcho (CEO), Matthew McBrien, and Matt Munns, its agents are used by 10+ long/short and long-only equity funds managing over $10 billion in assets. Marketed as "Modern Intelligence for Finance," Cohesion currently ships only a single-page marketing site with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its verified company identity as an API Evangelist network lead.

providers.name: Coho Data
providers.description: Coho Data was a scale-out enterprise storage startup based in Sunnyvale, California, founded in 2011 (originally as Convergent.io) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz among others. It built a software-defined storage platform that combined commodity flash and software-defined networking to deliver scalable NFS/object storage for private clouds. The company ceased operations and wound down in 2017. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is defunct: it operates no live developer portal, documentation, or API, and the cohodata.com domain has since lapsed to a third-party parked/content-farm site unrelated to the original company, so there is no public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Coinbooks
providers.description: Coinbooks is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto-web3. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Coinmine
providers.description: Coinmine is a consumer cryptocurrency-mining hardware company known for the Coinmine One, a plug-and-play home mining device that let non-technical owners mine and hold crypto assets from a simple companion app. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the coinmine.com storefront is offline (the Shopify store returns "unavailable"), so no live developer portal, API, or documentation surface could be confirmed. The registrable domain remains active for email (SPF/DMARC configured), and this profile captures the honest, probed security posture of that domain.

providers.name: Colfax Corporation (Historical)
providers.description: Colfax Corporation was a diversified global manufacturer founded in 1995 in Richmond, Virginia by Steven and Mitchell Rales. In April 2022, Colfax completed the spin-off of its fabrication technology business as ESAB Corporation (NYSE: ESAB) and renamed itself Enovis Corporation (NYSE: ENOV), refocusing on specialty medical technologies. The Colfax brand and corporate entity no longer exists as an operating company. This profile is preserved for historical reference and routes to the two successor entities. No Colfax-branded developer APIs were ever published; any successor APIs would fall under Enovis or ESAB.

providers.name: Collaborate *
providers.description: Collaborate.com was a mobile-first team collaboration service — unified document sharing, task management and team messaging across iPhone, iPod Touch, Android and the web, with integrations into Box, Dropbox and Google Drive. It was a service of Boston-based Kibits Corp, founded in 2011 by Matt Cutler (CEO) and David Greenstein (CTO), and was backed by GV (Google Ventures), Charles River Ventures, General Catalyst, SOS Ventures, Commonwealth Capital Ventures and Launch Capital. The company exited via acquisition by Cisco (December 2013), and its collaboration technology was folded into Cisco's communications portfolio. The company no longer operates independently: collaborate.com is now a MarkMonitor-managed redirect that sends plain-HTTP traffic to https://www.webex.com/ and serves nothing over HTTPS. There is no developer portal, documentation, SDK, package, webhook or API surface to catalog — the asterisk in GV's portfolio listing marks the exit.

providers.name: Collectivemedical
providers.description: Collective Medical was a Salt Lake City-based healthtech company that operated a real-time care-collaboration network connecting hospitals, emergency departments, health plans, and provider organizations to identify and coordinate care for high-risk and complex patients. It is best known for its EDIE (Emergency Department Information Exchange) and PreManage platforms. Collective Medical was acquired by PointClickCare in 2020, and the brand now operates as a product line within PointClickCare; collectivemedical.com resolves to a PointClickCare marketing page. This profile has no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface.

providers.name: Color Labs Inc. (Apple)
providers.description: Color Labs Inc. was a Palo Alto, California social photo-sharing startup founded in 2011 by Bill Nguyen and Peter Pham. Its Color mobile app let people photograph and browse photos taken nearby, grouping content by proximity and social graph. The company raised roughly $41 million before launch — $25 million from Sequoia Capital, $9 million from Bain Capital Ventures, and $7 million in venture debt from Silicon Valley Bank — and reportedly declined a $200 million acquisition offer from Google. After a March 2011 launch that drew about a million downloads but fell under 100,000 active users by September 2011, the board voted in October 2012 to wind the company down and the service closed at the end of that year. Apple then acqui-hired the remaining engineering team in a talent acquisition reported at roughly $2–7 million. Color Labs never shipped a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, and it has had no live web or API surface since 2012. Its former domain, color.com, is today operated by the unrelated Color Health, Inc. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Bain Capital Ventures portfolio company; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Comfy *
providers.description: Comfy (comfyapp.com) was a workplace-experience platform built by Building Robotics Inc. that let employees control lighting, temperature, room booking and office navigation from a mobile app, surfaced here as a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio lead. During enrichment the domain comfyapp.com was found to permanently 301-redirect to Enlighted Inc. / Building Robotics Inc., a Siemens Company, where the product has been rebranded as Siemens Building X space and workplace management; the Enlighted/Comfy site further states operations are ramping down. No independent public API, OpenAPI, SDK, developer portal, well-known discovery surface, or security.txt was found for Comfy or its successor as of this pass. This profile is retained as an acquired/defunct stub with domain-security probe data.

providers.name: Command E
providers.description: Command E was a universal search startup that built a keyboard-driven (Cmd+E) desktop tool for searching across the cloud applications people use at work — Google Drive, Slack, Notion, email, and more — from a single command bar, returning unified results without switching apps. The company was backed by Amplify Partners in the ai-ml / productivity search space. Command E was acquired by Dropbox in 2021, and its team went on to help build Dropbox Dash. Its former developer/marketing site at getcommande.com no longer resolves, so no live API, OpenAPI, or developer documentation surface is available to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Commercial Metals Company
providers.description: Commercial Metals Company (CMC) is a Fortune 500 manufacturer, recycler, and marketer of steel and metal products serving the construction, energy, and manufacturing industries. CMC was the first US steel company to launch an online customer portal (myCMC), but does not currently publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI specifications. Programmatic integrations with myCMC (order management, shipping, invoicing) are typically established through direct contracts with CMC's IT organization rather than via a self-service developer program.

providers.name: CommonGround
providers.description: CommonGround is an early-stage (seed) AI company listed in the Matrix Partners portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-derived lead. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the company has no reachable public web presence: the URL Matrix publishes for it (https://www.commonground-ai.com/) has no A record and serves no site, and WHOIS shows that domain is registered to Apple Inc. through the Com Laude corporate registrar rather than to CommonGround. The adjacent domains commonground.ai and commongroundai.com are parked for sale on Afternic, and getcommonground.com resolves only to a registrar lander. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI or other machine-readable API artifact, GitHub organization, or published client library could be located. This profile is retained as an identity-only stub and should be re-checked if the company establishes a public presence.

providers.name: Compaq
providers.description: Compaq Computer Corporation was a personal-computer manufacturer founded on February 16, 1982 in Houston, Texas by Rod Canion, Jim Harris and Bill Murto, three former Texas Instruments executives. It legally reverse-engineered the IBM PC BIOS and shipped the Compaq Portable in March 1983, then built out the Deskpro desktop line, the LTE notebook line, the Presario consumer line, and the SystemPro and ProLiant server lines, becoming the world's largest PC maker by 1994. Losing ground to Dell's direct-sales model and hit by the dot-com collapse, Compaq agreed to merge with Hewlett-Packard on September 4, 2001 in a $24.2 billion deal that closed on May 3, 2002. HP retired the Compaq brand entirely in North America and Europe in 2013 and has since licensed it regionally to third parties (Positivo Tecnologia in Brazil, Grupo Newsan in Argentina, Triden Corp in Mexico, Ossify Industries in India). Compaq predates the public web-API era and never published a developer program, public API, or SDK of its own; the compaq.com domain is still registered to HP Inc. but serves no website. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Compaq Computer Corporation
providers.description: Compaq Computer Corporation was an American personal-computer company founded in 1982 in Houston, Texas by Rod Canion, Jim Harris, and Bill Murto. It pioneered IBM PC-compatible portable computers with the 1983 Compaq Portable and grew into one of the largest PC manufacturers of the 1990s, acquiring Digital Equipment Corporation in 1998. Compaq merged with Hewlett-Packard in 2002; the brand was gradually retired and its operations absorbed into HP. It survives in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company profile (backed by kleiner-perkins); it operates no present-day developer portal, public API, or SDK surface, as compaq.com now resolves to HP infrastructure.

providers.name: complexpolygon
providers.description: Complex Polygon is listed by name only on the Slow Ventures portfolio page (https://slow.co/portfolio/) with a link to complexpolygon.com and no description or category. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 found no live company presence: complexpolygon.com is delegated to Gname's expired-domain nameservers (expire1/expire2.gname-dns.com), fails TLS entirely, and returns HTTP 503 with a registrar parking script over plain HTTP. The Internet Archive shows the domain was already a parked page in February 2025 and, before that, an SEO essay-mill content farm rather than a startup site. No GitHub organization or repositories, no npm, PyPI or crates.io packages, and no developer, documentation or API surface of any kind could be found. This record is retained as an unverified venture-portfolio lead with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Computer Sciences Corporation
providers.description: Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC) was a multinational information technology services and professional services company. On April 1, 2017, CSC merged with the Enterprise Services line of business of Hewlett Packard Enterprise to form DXC Technology, retiring the standalone CSC brand. This profile is preserved as a historical record; CSC did not publish any public developer APIs and the entity is no longer actively operated under this name.

providers.name: Comtravo
providers.description: Comtravo was a Berlin-based business travel management company (a TMC) that combined booking technology with human travel agents to handle corporate flights, hotels, rail and expense workflows for European businesses. It was backed by Creandum and other investors. As of this enrichment pass the standalone company is no longer operating: the comtravo.com domain returns a 301 redirect to navan.com, consistent with Comtravo having been acquired/wound into Navan (formerly TripActions). No independent Comtravo developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or public API surface could be found, so this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Con-way
providers.description: Con-way Inc. was a North American freight transportation and logistics company best known for its Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) carrier Con-way Freight along with Menlo Logistics, Con-way Truckload, and Con-way Multimodal. On October 30, 2015, XPO Logistics completed a $3 billion acquisition of Con-way; by May 2017 the Con-way brand had been fully retired in favor of XPO. This profile is preserved as a historical record; Con-way no longer operates under this name and modern shipping APIs are surfaced under XPO.

providers.name: Concept
providers.description: Concept is an unresolved company name harvested from the Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) public investment list, where it appears alphabetically between Compound and Convex as a bare list item with no linked website, category, stage, or description. No authoritative public source tying the name "Concept" to a specific company, domain, or product could be verified during enrichment, so this record remains an identity stub with no API surface, no developer portal, and no artifacts. It is retained as a lead so a future enrichment pass with working search can resolve the company behind the a16z listing and, if it publishes APIs, profile them properly.

providers.name: Concord Communications
providers.description: Concord Communications was surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. The July 2026 enrichment pass found no live company web presence and no API surface. The candidate domain concordcommunications.com resolves to a GoDaddy/Afternic domain-for-sale parking lander (no company content), and concord.com belongs to an unrelated business (Concord, the independent music company). No developer portal, documentation, API reference, specification, package, or /.well-known surface could be probed, and the APIs.io catalog holds no matching provider record. This profile is retained as an inactive historical lead; there is nothing to enrich until a live successor surface is identified.

providers.name: Concurrent Real-Time
providers.description: Concurrent Real-Time, Inc. is a provider of high-performance real-time computing systems, software, and solutions, headquartered in Pompano Beach, Florida. Its portfolio centers on RedHawk Linux, a real-time operating system based on Linux; iHawk multiprocessor computer platforms; the NightStar suite of development, debugging, and analysis tools; and SIMulation Workbench, a real-time simulation framework used for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and model-based design. Concurrent Real-Time serves aerospace, defense, automotive, transportation, financial, and industrial simulation markets. The company traces its lineage to the real-time division of Concurrent Computer Corporation and is backed by Battery Ventures. It operates as a systems and embedded-software vendor rather than a public web-API provider, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Confer Technologies
providers.description: Confer Technologies, Inc. was an enterprise endpoint security company that marketed what it called the "Converged Endpoint" — a single lightweight sensor combining attack prevention, detection, and incident response across endpoints, servers, cloud workloads, and mobile devices. The product gathered endpoint telemetry across the enterprise and applied data science to analyze attacker behavior and adapt automatically, positioned as an EDR and next-generation antivirus alternative for organizations without large security teams. Confer was venture-backed (Matrix Partners, Foundation Capital) and raised roughly $17M before being acquired by Carbon Black in 2016. Its site at confer.net began permanently redirecting to carbonblack.com by mid-2016 and the domain no longer resolves to a host. Carbon Black was subsequently acquired by VMware (2019) and then by Broadcom (2023). Confer never published a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is retained as a historical record of an acquired company and has no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Confluera
providers.description: Confluera was a cybersecurity company founded in 2018 in Palo Alto, California, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that built a Cloud eXtended Detection and Response (CxDR) platform for autonomous, real-time detection and response across cloud and on-premises infrastructure. Its technology correlated low-level security signals into progressing cyberattack storylines. Confluera was acquired by Zscaler (announced December 2022, closed early 2023); the standalone confluera.com domain has since been retired and no independent developer portal, API, or documentation surface remains publicly reachable.

providers.name: Congruent
providers.description: Congruent builds AI-native radar hardware and simulation tooling for self-driving cars and end-to-end autonomy. The company pairs a radar architecture that exposes raw sensor data with a world-model-based generative simulator, producing both real and synthetic raw radar returns to train autonomy stacks. Radar is the only depth sensor cheap enough to scale to every vehicle while still working in rain, fog, snow, and dust, where camera and lidar systems degrade. Congruent is an early-stage Y Combinator (W26) company founded in 2025 by Clement Barthes and Evan Scope Crafts, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this profile the company operates a single marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or specification.

providers.name: Conjectag
providers.description: Conjectag (Conject AG / Conject Holding GmbH) was a Munich-based German construction technology company founded in 2000 that provided cloud-based software for the built environment, covering project management, collaboration, document control, and construction cost management for the AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) sector. It was surfaced as a historical Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company. Conject was acquired by the Australian construction collaboration platform Aconex in March 2016, and Aconex was subsequently acquired by Oracle in December 2017; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no live website or developer/API surface. This profile is retained for network provenance rather than active enrichment.

providers.name: ConnectCapital
providers.description: ConnectCapital is a private equity investment firm, established in 2000, that made investments in early and expansion stage companies providing enterprise application and infrastructure software and solutions. It was surfaced as a portfolio entry of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating web presence - the connectcapital.com domain is parked on GoDaddy nameservers and redirects every path to a lander, and connect-capital.com is listed for sale. ConnectCapital is an investor, not an API producer, and has no developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Connected
providers.description: Connected (Connected HQ, Inc.) was a social CRM and contact-management startup that pulled a user's address book, email and social accounts together into a single continuously-updated relationship manager. Backed by 500 Global, it was acquired by LinkedIn in October 2011 and folded into the LinkedIn-branded "Connected" product, after which the standalone service was retired. Connected never shipped a public developer program, API, SDK or documentation. The connectedhq.com domain is still defensively held by the acquirer (MarkMonitor registrar, Azure DNS and NS1 nameservers, SPF and DMARC p=reject, RFC 7505 null MX) but publishes no A record and serves no content. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Consona
providers.description: Consona Corporation was an Indianapolis, Indiana enterprise software company founded in 1986 as Made2Manage Systems and taken private by Battery Ventures in 2003. Operating a roll-up strategy, it acquired multiple ERP and CRM product lines (DTR, Cimnet, AXIS, Encompix, Intuitive, Relevant, SupplyWorks) serving small and midsize manufacturers and field-service businesses. On August 7, 2012 Consona merged with CDC Software to form Aptean, and the Consona brand was retired from commercial use. The company is defunct, has no live web domain (consona.com does not resolve) and no public API or developer surface; its former products live on inside Aptean.

providers.name: Contactually
providers.description: Contactually was a cloud-based CRM (customer relationship management) platform focused on helping real estate agents, brokers, and other relationship-driven professionals nurture their networks through follow-up reminders, contact bucketing, pipelines, and automated outreach. Founded around 2011, it was acquired by real estate brokerage Compass on February 27, 2019, and had already been powering Compass's own CRM. Contactually permanently ceased operations on March 31, 2022. It historically exposed a v2 REST API (api.contactually.com) documented at developers.contactually.com for contacts, buckets, notes, tasks, and webhooks, but that developer surface, the API hosts, and all SDKs are now offline. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct provider; no live API, documentation, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Conteller
providers.description: Conteller is a user-generated content (UGC) marketplace where brands pay for authentic media directly from their own customers and everyday, non-famous creators. Brands publish media briefs and the platform lets creators capture, submit, and store photos, videos, and TikTok-style content, then handles paying those creators for approved submissions. A Mexican/Spanish startup (Madrid) selected for Batch 19 of 500 Global's Somos Lucha accelerator program in Latin America, Conteller has run pilots spanning roughly 1,400 creators and a dozen brands. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of 500 Global. As of this profile the public site is a disabled Vercel deployment and no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface has been found.

providers.name: Convertro, Inc.
providers.description: Convertro, Inc. was a marketing analytics company based in Santa Monica, California, providing a multi-touch attribution platform that measured the ROI of marketing touchpoints across online and offline media using algorithmic attribution models. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Convertro was acquired by AOL in 2014 and folded into the AOL/Verizon (now Yahoo) advertising stack. It no longer operates an independent public developer surface: convertro.com redirects to yahooinc.com, and no developer portal, documentation, API, or reachable API host was found during enrichment. This profile is retained as a network record; there is no live provider API surface to enrich.

providers.name: coohua
providers.description: Coohua (酷划在线) is a Beijing-based Chinese mobile advertising company founded in 2014 and backed by Qiming Venture Partners. It pioneered the incentive- and lock-screen-advertising model in China, rewarding users with cash for unlocking their screens, reading content, and engaging with ads. Its flagship products include Coohua Lockscreen (酷划锁屏) and the Tao News (淘新闻) reading-rewards app, serving advertisers across internet, finance, automotive, and e-commerce verticals. At its peak Coohua captured a majority share of China's lock-screen advertising market and returned billions of yuan in cash rewards to users annually. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification could be found during enrichment; this profile is retained as a company/provider record surfaced from the Qiming portfolio.

providers.name: Copan Systems
providers.description: Copan Systems was an enterprise data-storage company founded in 2002 and based in Longmont, Colorado, known for pioneering MAID (Massive Array of Idle Disks) technology for long-term persistent and archival storage. Its Enterprise MAID architecture powered down idle disks to cut power, cooling, and floor-space costs in the data center. Backed by Battery Ventures and other investors, the company raised more than $100 million in venture funding before filing for bankruptcy in 2009; SGI acquired its assets in 2010 (that storage lineage now sits within Hewlett Packard Enterprise). The company is defunct and operates no public developer surface, API, or documentation, so there is nothing to enrich in the API Evangelist artifact pipeline.

providers.name: Copia Global
providers.description: Copia Global was a Kenyan B2C e-commerce and last-mile distribution company founded by Tracey Turner and Jonathan Lewis to serve middle- and low-income consumers across rural and peri-urban Africa. Rather than a consumer website, it ran an agent-network model in which customers placed catalog orders through local agents using mobile and USSD technology, and Copia processed, aggregated, and delivered goods within days. Backed by investors including DCVC and Goodwell, the company raised a $50M Series C in 2022 to expand, but suspended Uganda operations in 2023, entered administration in May 2024, and was subsequently placed into liquidation. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or specification; its primary domain now resolves to a parked page. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead for network coverage.

providers.name: Core Labs
providers.description: Core Labs is an early-stage product studio based in New York City building the future of professional identity and connection for the digital economy. Founded by serial entrepreneur Ajay Rajani (previously Grovo and Tala), the company operates in rapid-experimentation mode, incubating and testing consumer and productivity products. Its portfolio includes Mural, a simple portfolio-building tool for product managers, marketers, and digital workers that turns shared URLs into rich embeds; Core, a peer-and-expert mentorship platform used in university entrepreneurship programs and fellowships; and Makeshop, an on-demand marketplace for creative services. Core Labs is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: Core Loop
providers.description: Core Loop is a game studio founded in 2020 by Vincenzo Alagna and Dan Chao, veterans of Machine Zone, GREE, and Funzio, building a modern cross-platform MMO at the intersection of massively multiplayer online games and web3. The studio is developing an AI-directed, dynamic world that evolves based on the actions of the community, with a blockchain-based, player-driven virtual economy in which participants truly own the assets they craft or earn and can potentially make a living in the game long-term. The game targets both PC and mobile. Core Loop raised a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Galaxy Digital, Block.one, 1Up Ventures, Dune Ventures, and others, and operates as a remote-first team headquartered in Oakland, California. As a game studio, Core Loop does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Coremetrics
providers.description: Coremetrics was a web analytics software company founded in 1999 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. It delivered a cloud-based (SaaS) digital marketing analytics platform used by more than 2,100 online brands to capture and analyze visitor and shopper behavior across web, social, and mobile channels for marketing optimization, attribution, and personalization. Backed by Accel and other venture investors, Coremetrics was acquired by IBM in 2010 and folded into IBM Digital Analytics and the IBM Watson Marketing / Enterprise Marketing Management suite. The standalone coremetrics.com developer surface is no longer operational, and no live public API, documentation, or SDK could be found during enrichment.

providers.name: Corillian
providers.description: Corillian Corporation was a leading provider of Internet banking software and services, headquartered in Hillsboro, Oregon. The company was formed in 1997 when CheckFree spun off InteractiveSolutions Corporation, and it went on to build the Corillian Voyager online banking platform used by many U.S. banks and credit unions for online banking, bill payment, and real-time financial services integration. Backed by Battery Ventures, Corillian became a public company and expanded through the acquisitions of InteliData Technologies (2005) and qbt Systems (2006). In February 2007 CheckFree agreed to acquire Corillian for approximately $245 million; CheckFree was itself acquired by Fiserv later that same year, after which the Corillian brand was retired. The company no longer operates independently and maintains no public API, developer portal, documentation, or other live developer surface.

providers.name: Corio, Inc.
providers.description: Corio, Inc. was an enterprise Application Service Provider (ASP) founded in September 1998 in San Carlos, California, and incorporated in Delaware, formed by acquiring the capital stock of Data Systems Connectors, Inc. Corio implemented, hosted and managed packaged enterprise business software from Oracle, PeopleSoft, SAP, Ariba and Siebel Systems on behalf of medium and large public, private, non-profit and public sector customers, delivering ERP, CRM and e-business functionality as a service from secure third-party data centers over IP networks. The company operated two lines of business — Application Management Services and Professional Services — and partnered with (i)Structure, XO Communications and Qwest for data center and network infrastructure. Backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (29.5% pre-IPO across the KPCB Java Fund, KPCB VIII, KPCB VIII Founders Fund and KPCB Information Sciences Zaibatsu Fund II, with Vinod Khosla and Ted Schlein on the board) and Cap Gemini Ernst & Young, Corio went public on NASDAQ in 2000. IBM agreed to acquire Corio on 24 January 2005 for $2.82 per share in cash via Nike Acquisition Corp.; Corio filed its Form 15 deregistration on 15 March 2005 and was absorbed into IBM. The company is defunct, publishes no API, developer portal or documentation, and corio.com is a parked domain — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cornami
providers.description: Cornami is a Santa Clara, California high-performance computing company building morphable silicon and a stream-centric software stack for privacy-preserving and AI workloads. Its FracTLcore Fabric and TruStream dataflow programming model power the Tigris 16nm ASIC, MX8 board, and rack-scale MX64 system, delivering real-time Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), private LLM inference, blockchain, and signal-processing acceleration at greatly reduced power and latency. Cornami is a frontier-tech company backed by SoftBank Vision Fund; this profile tracks its public developer and API surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Corporate Buzz Words
providers.description: REST API for Corporate Buzz Words

providers.name: Corrent
providers.description: Corrent (listed by Battery Ventures as "Corrent Corporation *", where the asterisk denotes an exited investment) was surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. A July 2026 enrichment pass found no operating company behind the name: corrent.com resolves to an Efty domain-for-sale parking page, corrent.io / corrent.ai / getcorrent.com do not resolve, corrent.co is an unrelated Shopify wellness storefront, there is no github.com/corrent organization (404), no npm or PyPI packages under the name, and no English Wikipedia entry for Corrent Corporation. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or any other API surface exists to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead only.

providers.name: CORS Proxy
providers.description: Get around the dreaded CORS error by using this proxy as a middle man

providers.name: Cortera
providers.description: Cortera was a business (trade) credit data provider that turned anonymized, contributed accounts-receivable and B2B payment data into forward-looking payment-risk insight, credit scores, and firmographics on private companies so credit teams could spot changes in a customer's financial health. Founded in Massachusetts, Cortera was acquired by Moody's (Moody's Analytics) in 2021 and its product line has since been folded into Moody's Company Reference Data / Trade Credit offering, marketed as "Moody's Pulse (formerly Cortera)". The standalone cortera.com domain now 301-redirects to Moody's; there is no independent Cortera developer portal or public self-serve API today — data is delivered through Moody's data-delivery APIs, CRM/ERP connectors, and file feeds. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and is retained as an acquired-company record.

providers.name: Counterpane
providers.description: Counterpane Internet Security, Inc. was a managed security services provider founded by cryptographer Bruce Schneier, growing out of his Counterpane Systems cryptography consultancy. Counterpane pioneered Managed Security Monitoring (MSM) — outsourced, 24x7 human-staffed security operations centers that monitored customer networks and devices for intrusions, rather than selling security products. It was venture-backed, with Accel among its investors, and was acquired by BT Group in 2006, after which its operations were folded into BT's managed security business. The company is defunct as an independent entity: it operates no product, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface today. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe, counterpane.com resolves (209.17.116.163, Network Solutions nameservers) but refuses HTTPS on port 443, and plain HTTP redirects to https://www.schneier.com/ — Bruce Schneier's personal site. www.counterpane.com returns HTTP 404.
