There is no MX, SPF, DMARC, or CAA record on the domain. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Court Buddy
providers.description: Court Buddy is a legal services marketplace that connected consumers and small businesses with independent attorneys for flat-fee, on-demand legal help, aiming to make legal representation more affordable and accessible. It operated under the LawChamps brand (lawchamps.com) and was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface was found during enrichment, and the primary web property is currently unreachable.

providers.name: Cover
providers.description: Cover (Cover Technologies Inc.) is a Los Angeles-based construction technology company that designs and builds custom, architect-grade backyard homes, accessory dwelling units (ADUs), and residential spaces using a prefabricated, factory-manufactured building system. Cover handles the full development process end to end, from initial consultation and design through permitting, manufacturing, and on-site installation, delivering custom spaces in weeks rather than years. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of General Catalyst. Cover is a physical-product homebuilder and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures verifiable company identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Craftsvilla
providers.description: Craftsvilla was an India-based online marketplace for ethnic and handcrafted products — sarees, ethnic apparel, jewelry, footwear, accessories, beauty and home decor sourced from artisans, weavers and small sellers across India. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Mumbai, it was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, Nexus Venture Partners and Global Founders Capital before winding down its consumer operations around 2019 amid financial difficulties. It was surfaced as a Lightspeed portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment found no live public developer surface: the storefront domain now serves a broken AWS S3 redirect (www.craftsvilla.com is NXDOMAIN) and there is no API, developer portal, documentation, /.well-known/ discovery, or llms.txt to harvest.

providers.name: Cray
providers.description: Cray is the high-performance computing (HPC) and supercomputing brand, originally Cray Research and later Cray Inc., now part of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) following HPE's 2019 acquisition. The cray.com domain 301-redirects to HPE's HPC/compute pages, and Cray no longer operates an independent public developer portal, API reference, or API surface — its supercomputing systems, ClusterStor storage, and Slingshot interconnect are marketed and supported under HPE. Enrichment found no first-party Cray API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation to harvest. The norwest-venture-partners backing recorded on this stub is a legacy venture-history association, not a current independent company relationship.

providers.name: Creator Cabins
providers.description: Creator Cabins (operating as Cabin, at cabin.city) is a crypto-web3 community project that built globally distributed, coliving neighborhoods uniting members through shared culture, economy, and token-based governance via the Cabin DAO. It began in 2020 with a 28-acre Texas Hill Country property known as Neighborhood Zero and grew into a multi-property network for remote workers before members voted to wind down the formal DAO structure in 2025; individual neighborhoods continue operating independently, and a related Neighborhood Village Project now serves over 100 communities globally. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: CrediFi
providers.description: CrediFi is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-18 and 2026-07-20 found no independent live surface for CrediFi — credifi.com redirects to actovia.com, a commercial real estate data provider — so this profile is retained as a historical record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Creopop
providers.description: CreoPop is a consumer 3D-printing pen that lets you draw three-dimensional objects freehand. Unlike filament 3D pens it has no hot parts or melting plastic; instead it uses photopolymer "cool ink" cartridges that are solidified by built-in LEDs, and it is battery operated and charged over mini-USB. The product line includes specialty inks (elastic, magnetic, glow-in-the-dark, aromatic, temperature-sensitive, and electrically conductive). CreoPop is a hardware/consumer-electronics brand with a marketing and direct-to-consumer e-commerce website; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Crew32
providers.description: Crew32 was a stealth-stage technology startup based in Santa Monica, California, working in the human resources, employment, and workplace-culture space. It was founded by Jason Nazar (previously co-founder and CEO of Docstoc), George Ishii (co-founder of Betterworks, Geni, and Yammer), and Yadid Ramot, and raised roughly $5.8 million in early funding around 2016. The company is publicly associated with the comparably.com workplace-culture and compensation review platform. Crew32 was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; no public API, developer portal, or SDK has been identified for this company.

providers.name: Crews By Core *
providers.description: Crews by Core was a construction field-execution platform based in Palo Alto, California (with a Tokyo office), founded and led by CEO Di-Ann Eisnor. Branded "Mission Control for the Field," its mobile-first product gave superintendents and foremen a single tool for lookahead scheduling, jobsite logistics, drawings, and field-to-office messaging, layered with AI-driven risk detection to quantify and mitigate schedule and financial risk on the jobsite. The company was backed by GV (Google Ventures) among ten investors and was acquired by construction IoT company WakeCap on July 1, 2024, folding its scheduling and communication tooling into WakeCap's worker-productivity sensor platform. Crews by Core did not expose a public developer API; this profile documents the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: crob.at
providers.description: Free, no-login web tool for sharing Pokémon Showdown teams as visual pages, with a public REST API for creating/retrieving teams, generating random teams, and fetching sample teams.

providers.name: Crocodoc
providers.description: Crocodoc built an HTML5-based document viewing and annotation API that converted PDF, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files into HTML5 for plugin-free, in-browser viewing, embedding, and markup. A 500 Startups / Y Combinator-lineage company, Crocodoc was acquired by Box in 2013, and its document-rendering technology became the foundation of the Box View API (later Box Content Preview / UI Elements). The standalone Crocodoc API was subsequently deprecated and the crocodoc.com domain is no longer active. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cross Access
providers.description: Cross Access was a data-integration software company backed by Battery Ventures that was acquired by IBM on 2003-10-17 and folded into IBM's information-integration portfolio. It is defunct and has no independent web presence, developer portal, API, or documentation surface today; DNS for candidate domains (crossaccess.com, cross-access.com, crossaccess.io) does not resolve. This profile is retained as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio record, not an active API provider, and there are no live artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Crossbar
providers.description: Crossbar, Inc. is a Santa Clara semiconductor company founded in 2010 that develops resistive random-access memory (ReRAM), a non-volatile memory built on RRAM patents licensed from the University of Michigan. Its CMOS-compatible ReRAM targets faster write performance, lower power consumption, and higher endurance than NAND flash at roughly half the die size, and is offered as embedded and standalone memory IP to OEMs and system-on-chip developers across consumer, mobile, enterprise, industrial, and IoT markets. Crossbar is a hardtech portfolio company backed by Kleiner Perkins. As a silicon-IP provider it exposes no public developer API surface; this profile carries company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Crossref Metadata Search
providers.description: Books & Articles Metadata

providers.name: CrowdAnalytix
providers.description: CrowdAnalytix (CAX) is a crowdsourced data science and predictive analytics platform that connects enterprises with a global community of data scientists to build, test, and compare machine learning models through hosted modeling competitions. The company runs prediction and classification contests across industries such as consumer packaged goods, retail, banking, insurance, and healthcare, and has extended into AI/ML model development, data annotation and labeling, and packaged AI solutions. Headquartered in Frisco, Texas with operations in Bangalore, India, CrowdAnalytix is backed by Accel.

providers.name: crowdcube
providers.description: Crowdcube is a UK-based equity crowdfunding platform that lets everyday and professional investors buy shares in early-stage and growth-stage private companies, and lets founders raise capital directly from their community and the wider crowd. Founded in 2011 in Exeter by Darren Westlake and Luke Lang, it is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and has helped hundreds of startups and scale-ups raise funding from a large base of retail investors. The platform covers pitch discovery, investment processing, share issuance, nominee shareholding, and a secondary-market cashout facility. Crowdcube surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its company identity and observable domain-security posture.

providers.name: Crowdery
providers.description: Crowdery was a consumer retail and e-commerce startup backed by a16z, listed on the a16z investment list. Its product inverted the traditional retail sales model: shoppers voted on product designs from a curated set, Crowdery assembled a personalized marketplace from each shopper's top picks, and the highest-voted products were opened for pre-order at a discount. For brands it offered consumer feedback loops, pre-production demographic analytics, and pre-orders intended to de-risk manufacturing runs. The company never shipped a public API or developer program. As of July 2026 Crowdery appears defunct: the apex domain crowdery.com serves a Doteasy hosting placeholder page, www.crowdery.com still delegates to a decommissioned Heroku prelaunch application that returns 404, and no developer portal, documentation, GitHub organization, or API surface could be found. This profile is retained as a historical a16z portfolio record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: CrowdMob
providers.description: CrowdMob was a mobile gaming and app-monetization startup surfaced as an a16z portfolio company. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating API surface: the company no longer appears in the a16z portfolio listing, and the crowdmob.com domain is now operated by an unrelated affiliate-marketing publisher (AffiliateBay) as a WordPress "growth marketing agency" landing page. No developer portal, documentation, API reference, specs, SDKs, packages, or /.well-known/ discovery documents exist. Retained as a historical/defunct record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Cruise
providers.description: Cruise was an autonomous-vehicle (robotaxi) company founded in 2013 and majority-owned by General Motors, building self-driving technology and operating driverless ride-hail services in San Francisco and other U.S. cities. Backed by GM, Honda, SoftBank Vision Fund, Spark Capital, Y Combinator and others, Cruise suspended operations after a 2023 incident and, in December 2024, GM announced it would end robotaxi development and fold the Cruise team into GM's own autonomous and driver-assistance programs. As of 2026 the getcruise.com domain 301-redirects to GM's autonomous-driving pages. Cruise never published a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Cruise Technologies
providers.description: Cruise Technologies was a wireless thin-client computing company founded in 1997 and based in Arlington Heights, Illinois. It developed the CruiseConnect platform, which enabled server-class and wireless thin-client computing delivered through OEM and licensing partners worldwide. The company raised roughly $12M from Battery Ventures and Bessemer Venture Partners, was acquired in 1999, and has since ceased operations. It was surfaced as a historical entry on the Battery Ventures list-of-all-companies roster and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Enrichment confirmed the company is defunct: it has no live website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. The former cruisetechnologies.com domain is a parked HugeDomains for-sale listing, not a company property. This profile is retained as a historical record only and requires no further enrichment.

providers.name: Crystal
providers.description: Crystal (Crystal Semiconductor) was a hardtech company that designed audio and mixed-signal semiconductor chips. Kleiner Perkins partnered with the company in 1986 at the early stage, and Crystal was subsequently acquired by Cirrus Logic. The company was surfaced from the Kleiner Perkins portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. It operated as a fabless chip designer rather than a software or platform business, and no longer exists as an independent entity: it publishes no website, no developer portal, and no public API surface of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record and is not an API provider.

providers.name: CubeTree
providers.description: CubeTree was an enterprise social collaboration software startup (founded 2008, Redwood City, California) offering a business social network with wikis, blogs, file sharing, and activity feeds. It was acquired by SuccessFactors in 2010 (deal valued up to $50M) and folded into the SuccessFactors Business Alignment suite; SAP subsequently acquired SuccessFactors in 2012 and the product was absorbed into SAP SuccessFactors / SAP Jam. CubeTree no longer operates as an independent company: the cubetree.com domain is parked under SAP nameservers with no live web presence, developer portal, documentation, or API. Surfaced as a trinity-ventures portfolio company; retained as a historical/defunct network record with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: CucumberTown
providers.description: Cucumbertown was a recipe network and food-blogging platform ("a Tumblr for recipes") founded around 2011-2012 in Palo Alto, California by Cherian Thomas, Chris Luscher, Arun Prabhakar and Dan Hauk, and backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) among other angel investors. It let home cooks and food bloggers publish, structure, and share recipes on a hosted network. Cucumbertown was acquired by the Japanese recipe network Cookpad in June 2015 and was fully shut down by March 31, 2017 for lack of a sustainable business model. The company is defunct and operates no public API or developer program. The cucumbertown.com domain now 302-redirects to Samsung Food (app.samsungfood.com, formerly Whisk), an unrelated successor product; none of the artifacts served on that host belong to Cucumbertown.

providers.name: Culinarybrands
providers.description: Culinary Brands is an Indian foodservice and beverage operator on a mission to prove that fresh, quality food is possible without compromising on taste. The company builds and runs a portfolio of well-known food and coffee brands across India, including Subway (sandwiches / QSR), Lavazza (coffee), and Fresh & Honest (coffee and vending), with a stated focus on sustainability, diversity and inclusion, governance, and CSR. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the public web presence is a WordPress corporate site with no developer portal, documentation, or product API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cullinet Software
providers.description: Cullinet Software (formerly Cullinane Database Systems) was a database and application software company based in Westwood, Massachusetts, best known for the IDMS/IDMS-DB mainframe database management system, the IDD data dictionary, and the ADS/Online application development environment for IBM mainframes. Backed by Battery Ventures, Greylock, and Morgenthaler Ventures, it was one of the first software companies to go public (1978) and was acquired by Computer Associates (CA) on June 30, 1989. The company is defunct and publishes no developer portal, API, or documentation surface today; this record is retained as a historical portfolio-graph node with no enrichable API artifacts.

providers.name: Cult of the North
providers.description: Cult of the North (established November 2022 under the codename "Seidr") is a Stockholm, Sweden-based video game studio co-founded by former EA general manager Adam Schaub and former King SVP Marcus Jacobs, and backed by a seed investment from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The studio drew talent from King, Activision Blizzard, EA, Embark Studios, Resolution Games, and FunPlus, and set out to build large-scale, next-generation multiplayer PvP experiences for PC and console in Unreal Engine 5 — first the debut title codenamed "Project Gundalf" and later the free-to-play strategy war game "We Will Be Gods." As a consumer game studio it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile carries company identity only. Industry reporting in 2025 indicated the studio wound down operations.

providers.name: Cultivaet Technologies Holding Ltd.
providers.description: Cultivaet Technologies Holding Ltd. is an AI-driven agricultural technology ("AgriTech for Humanity") startup based in Egypt serving smallholder farmers across the Middle East. Its products include a Farmer AI Companion delivering personalized weather, crop-planning, pest-control and soil-health insights, a Knowledge Platform that collects/analyzes/distributes social and scientific agricultural data, and a Business SaaS connecting farmers with food-industry buyers for sustainable procurement and traceability. The company is backed by 500 Global and Sanabil and is part of the Google Cloud Startups Program (pre-seed, 2024). As of this enrichment pass Cultivaet publishes only a marketing site (cultivaet.ai) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or other developer surface, so no API artifacts were generated.

providers.name: Cultivate
providers.description: Cultivate was an AI-powered digital leadership and coaching platform that analyzed leaders' own opt-in digital communication data to deliver hyper-personalized, privacy-preserving coaching insights and recommendations for people managers. Founded through an Entrepreneur in Residence program at Samsung NEXT by Joseph Freed, Samir Meghani, and Andy Horng, and backed by Trinity Ventures, Silicon Valley Data Capital, and Bloomberg Beta, Cultivate was acquired by employee listening and people-analytics company Perceptyx on February 15, 2022, where it became the basis for Perceptyx's "Cultivate Intelligent Coaching" product. Cultivate operated as an enterprise HR/leadership SaaS and did not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the company no longer exists as an independent entity.

providers.name: Curio Labs
providers.description: Curio (curio.io), operated by Curio Labs, was a London-based audio-journalism subscription app founded in 2016 by Govind Balakrishnan and Srikant Chakravarti. It turned articles from premium publishers into professionally narrated audio and later added AI-generated personalized episodes. Backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), EarlyBird, Draper Esprit, Cherry Ventures and Horizons Ventures, it raised over $15M before the founders wound the company down after eight years, citing AI and big-tech competition; they have since moved on to a new venture (Gibran). Enrichment probe finds no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface — curio.io now serves a closure/landing page only.

providers.name: Curious Ai
providers.description: The Curious AI Company was a Helsinki, Finland-based artificial intelligence research company founded in 2015 by Harri Valpola (previously founder of ZenRobotics) along with Antti Rasmus, Mathias Berglund, Tapani Raiko, and Timo Haanpaa. The company pursued artificial general intelligence, real-world computer vision for robots, and interactive, autonomous, and semi-supervised machine learning, and is best known for foundational research on Ladder Networks for semi-supervised deep learning. It raised roughly 4.7M USD from investors including DCVC, Lifeline Ventures, and Invus, and was acquired by Apple in January 2021. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer platform, API, documentation, or SDKs. This record is retained as a DCVC portfolio identity profile; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Curlie
providers.description: Curlie is a multilingual, human-edited web directory and the official successor to the Open Directory Project (ODP), also known as DMOZ. After the DMOZ directory was shut down in March 2017, the editor community relaunched the project as Curlie to continue cataloging websites by topic across more than 90 languages. Curlie is maintained entirely by volunteer editors who review and categorize submitted sites into a hierarchical taxonomy used as a reference by search engines and researchers.

providers.name: Currency-api
providers.description: Free Currency Exchange Rates API with 150+ Currencies & No Rate Limits

providers.name: Curtiss-Wright
providers.description: Curtiss-Wright is a global integrated business that provides highly engineered products, solutions, and services mainly to the aerospace, defense, commercial power, process, and general industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans rugged embedded computing, mission-critical avionics, electronic packaging, naval propulsion, reactor coolant pumps for nuclear power, surface treatment services, industrial valves, sensors, data acquisition systems, telemetry ground stations, emergency arresting systems for military aircraft, and electronic systems for naval shipbuilding programs. The company traces its lineage to the aviation pioneers Glenn Curtiss and the Wright brothers and today operates across the Defense Electronics, Naval & Power, and Aerospace & Industrial segments.

providers.name: Custom Chat API | MirrorFly
providers.description: MirrorFly is a self-hosted CPaaS providing token-authenticated REST Chat Platform APIs (User and Admin) plus SDKs for in-app chat, HD video/voice calling, VoIP, contact center, chatbot/conversational AI, and live streaming for web and mobile apps.

providers.name: Customer Database
providers.description: Customer Database is the topic dedicated to APIs, schemas, vocabularies, and reference designs for the systems of record that store customer identity, profile, contact, preference, consent, and account data. A customer database underpins CRM, marketing automation, customer data platforms (CDPs), customer service, billing, and analytics use cases, and is increasingly expected to support API-first access, schema-on-write data quality, real-time eventing, GDPR/CCPA consent and erasure workflows, and identity resolution across web, mobile, and offline channels. This repository tracks the vendors, standards, and patterns that make customer data accessible, governed, and portable.

providers.name: Customer Portals
providers.description: Customer Portals is the topic dedicated to the architecture, APIs, schemas, and reference designs behind self-service customer portals. A customer portal is a secure web or mobile experience where authenticated customers can manage their profile, view orders and invoices, pay bills, submit and track support tickets, download documents, manage notification preferences, and access account-specific resources. Modern customer portals are typically composed of multiple back-end APIs - authentication and identity, profile and preference management, billing and invoicing, support and ticketing, notifications, and document delivery - surfaced through a single front-end shell. This repository tracks the vendors, patterns, and standards that make customer portals reliable, accessible, and API-driven.

providers.name: CYGIA
providers.description: CYGIA (Zhuhai CYGIA Automation Equipment Co.) is an intelligent-factory equipment and solution provider founded in 2006 and headquartered in Zhuhai, China. It develops, manufactures, and services intelligent automation and automated-test equipment for consumer electronics, semiconductor and integrated-circuit, automotive, medical, and new-energy industries. Once backed by Qiming Venture Partners, CYGIA became a subsidiary of publicly traded CYG (Changyuan Group, Shanghai Stock Exchange 600525.SH) in 2015. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface for CYGIA, which is a hardware/automation-equipment manufacturer rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Cymbal
providers.description: Cymbal was a consumer blockchain data startup founded in 2022 in Menlo Park by Eric Feng, Nick Chang and others, building a "human readable" Ethereum block explorer with a visual, social interface and AI-generated conversational summaries of wallets, NFTs and transactions. The company raised $18.5M in 2023 from investors including First Round Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Solana Ventures, Patron, Acrew and GV. In July 2025 Yahoo acqui-hired the Cymbal team into a new AI research group. Cymbal published no public developer API or documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile is a GV-portfolio company record.

providers.name: Cyota, Inc
providers.description: Cyota, Inc was a cybersecurity company founded in 1999 in New York City by Naftali Bennett, Lior Golan, Michal Tzur, and Amir Orad, focused on online banking fraud, e-commerce fraud, and anti-phishing protection. Cyota pioneered token-less consumer authentication and risk-based fraud detection for financial institutions, reportedly holding a majority share of the US and UK e-commerce authentication markets. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, the company was acquired by RSA Security on December 30, 2005 for approximately $145 million, after which its technology was folded into RSA's Identity and Fraud portfolio (RSA Adaptive Authentication / FraudAction). Cyota no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no live developer surface, API, or documentation. This profile is retained for historical/network provenance only.

providers.name: Cyvera
providers.description: Cyvera was an Israeli cybersecurity startup, founded in 2011 and backed by Battery Ventures, that pioneered exploit-prevention endpoint security. Its flagship product, TRAPS (Targeted Remote Attack Prevention System), blocked unknown, zero-day attacks by obstructing the exploitation techniques attackers rely on rather than relying on signatures. Cyvera was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in April 2014 for roughly $200M, and TRAPS was folded into Palo Alto's endpoint offering that ultimately became Cortex XDR. The independent company no longer operates; the cyvera.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live developer portal, public API, or artifact surface to enrich.

providers.name: D2iQ
providers.description: D2iQ (formerly Mesosphere, maker of DC/OS) was an enterprise Kubernetes company whose flagship product, the D2iQ Kubernetes Platform (DKP), delivered production-grade Kubernetes cluster provisioning, day-2 operations, and application management across cloud, on-premises, edge, and air-gapped environments. D2iQ was acquired by Nutanix in early 2024; DKP was folded into and rebranded as the Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP), which launched in May 2024. The independent D2iQ web and developer surfaces are now retired: d2iq.com redirects to nutanix.com/d2iq and docs.d2iq.com redirects to the Nutanix support portal, so D2iQ no longer operates a first-party public API, developer portal, or artifact surface of its own. This profile is retained as a historical / acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dabchy
providers.description: Dabchy is a Tunisia-based online marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned and new lifestyle goods including fashion and clothing, accessories, home decor, sporting equipment, and books. Serving the Tunisian market in French (fr_TN), it lets individuals list their own items and discover deals from other sellers, positioning itself as a simple, fast, and secure platform for giving everyday objects a second life. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Dabchy publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; api.dabchy.com is a locked-down (HTTP 403) application backend and the public site is a client-rendered single-page app with no exposed spec.

providers.name: Dairyqueen
providers.description: Dairy Queen (International Dairy Queen, Inc.) is an American chain of soft-serve ice cream and fast-food restaurants operating thousands of franchised locations worldwide, known for its Blizzard treats, cones, sundaes, and grill menu. A subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway, it reaches consumers through its website, mobile app, and loyalty program. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead; Dairy Queen publishes no public developer API program, so this repo currently carries only a probed domain-security profile and identity metadata.

providers.name: dajiabao
providers.description: dajiabao is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of the Chinese venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no reachable public surface: dajiabao.com resolves in DNS (139.196.207.93, an Alibaba Cloud Shanghai address, nameservers at eName) but both TCP/80 and TCP/443 time out, so there is no website, developer portal, documentation, or /.well-known/ discovery surface to profile. Mail is delegated to Tencent Exmail (mxbiz1/mxbiz2.qq.com), which indicates the registration is still actively used even though the web presence is dark. Searches of npm, PyPI, and crates.io returned no packages under this name, and the company publishes no OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, or MCP surface that the network can index. This profile is retained as a verified-dark lead and should be re-probed on a later round in case the company relaunches a public site.

providers.name: Damon Motorcycles
providers.description: Damon Motorcycles (Damon Inc.) is a Vancouver, British Columbia electric motorcycle company founded in 2017 by Jay Giraud and Dominique Kwong, and an alumnus of the Techstars accelerator. Damon builds high-performance electric motorcycles led by the HyperSport and HyperFighter models, and is known for two safety and ergonomics technologies: CoPilot, a 360-degree advanced warning system that uses radar, cameras, and sensors to alert riders to surrounding hazards, and Shift, a transformable ergonomics system that adjusts the riding position between commuter and sport stances. The company has faced significant financial and going-concern difficulties, and its public web presence at damon.com currently returns errors, so no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be verified during enrichment. This profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dangdang
providers.description: Dangdang (当当, dangdang.com) is a Chinese business-to-consumer e-commerce company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Beijing. It began as one of China's largest online booksellers and expanded into a broad general-merchandise marketplace spanning books, e-books and e-readers, digital reading, consumer electronics, apparel, home goods, and maternal and baby products. Once listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker DANG) before being taken private, Dangdang was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No active public developer program, open platform, or machine-readable API surface was reachable during enrichment (the site is geo-restricted); this profile carries a probed domain-security posture and awaits any discoverable API artifacts.

providers.name: Danger
providers.description: Danger, Inc. was a Palo Alto, California mobile computing company founded on December 9, 1999 by Andy Rubin, Joe Britt, and Matt Hershenson, all former Apple, WebTV, and Philips engineers. Danger built the Danger Hiptop, sold in the United States as the T-Mobile Sidekick, an early client-server ("cloud") smartphone whose downloadable application catalog prefigured the app stores later shipped by Android and iOS. Andy Rubin left Danger in 2003 to found Android. Microsoft acquired Danger on February 11, 2008 for a price reported at roughly $500 million and folded the team into "Project Pink," which shipped as the short-lived Microsoft Kin. Most former Danger staff had left Microsoft by October 2009 and the company was wound down by approximately 2011. Danger was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a historic Redpoint Ventures portfolio holding. It is defunct: the danger.com domain no longer resolves and there is no developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: DAOex
providers.description: DAOex (DAO Exchange, product-branded "Commune") was a web3 community relationship management platform positioned as an all-in-one tool for understanding, engaging, and growing DAO and NFT communities. Its advertised surface covered member directories bridging on-chain and off-chain data, referral programs with unique member/affiliate links, quests, contests and bounties as rewards infrastructure, Discord-native engagement and role assignment, and payouts of tokens, NFTs or Discord roles on Ethereum mainnet and Polygon via an automatically provisioned Gnosis Safe, with a points-and-CSV fallback for pre-token communities. Surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the company appears DEFUNCT: daoex.app no longer resolves in DNS (NXDOMAIN, no SOA), the site was a single-page Webflow marketing site last published 2022-09-22 and last archived 2023-03-21, and no API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, package or GitHub organization was ever published.

providers.name: Dapper
providers.description: Dapper was an advertising-technology and web-data company founded in 2006 by Jonathan Aizen and Eran Shir, seed-funded by Accel. It ran two surfaces: Dapper Ads, an intent-driven dynamic-ad product that pulled live product and inventory data from an advertiser's own site into targeted creative without IT integration; and open.dapper.net (the "Dapp Factory" / Dapper: The Data Mapper), a hosted tool that turned any web page into structured feeds, web services and widgets — XML, RSS, JSON, YAML, CSV, iCalendar, Google Gadgets, Netvibes modules and image loops — effectively letting anyone "create an API for any site" before providers published their own. Dapper was acquired by Yahoo! in 2010 and both surfaces were shut down; dapper.net now resolves to Yahoo nameservers with no host, and open.dapper.net no longer resolves. There is no live API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Dasera
providers.description: Dasera is a data security company in the data security posture management (DSPM) and data governance space, founded by Ani Chaudhuri and backed by Sierra Ventures. Its platform was built to continuously discover, classify, and monitor sensitive data across cloud and on-premises data stores (databases, warehouses, data lakes) and to surface data security, privacy, and compliance risk across the data lifecycle. As of this enrichment pass the standalone dasera.com origin is unreachable (a Cloudflare 1001 origin error with a failed TLS handshake), so no live developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface could be harvested; this profile records the domain-security posture that could still be probed via DNS/TLS and remains a stub awaiting a live API surface.

providers.name: dashmobile
providers.description: dashmobile (listed by Slow Ventures as "Dash Labs") was surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 found no operating public surface: the listed domain dashmobile.co has no DNS records at all (no A record, no NS delegation) and returns no HTTP response, and the Internet Archive holds exactly one capture of the domain (2022-05-24), which was itself a .CO registry domain-expired parking page rather than company content. The company therefore has no website, no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no discoverable artifacts of any kind. This profile is retained as a verified-defunct portfolio lead and is not a candidate for further enrichment unless the company relaunches on a new domain.

providers.name: Dasient
providers.description: Dasient was a web anti-malware company founded in 2008 in Sunnyvale, California by ex-Google engineers Neil Daswani and Shariq Rizvi with McKinsey consultant Ameet Ranadive. It sold cloud-based protection against web-based malware and malvertising, scanning customer websites and ad networks with its Malware Analysis Platform. It shipped a JSON-RPC over HTTP "Web Protection API" that let customers schedule and run on-demand malware scans of individual domains and URLs, with tiered pricing by scans per day. Twitter acquired Dasient in January 2012 for a reported $19.1 million; the product was retired, dasient.com went dark in late 2012, and the domain is now a parked defensive registration held by Twitter. This company is DEFUNCT and has no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Data Elite Services
providers.description: Data Elite Services, Inc. was a San Francisco company associated with Data Elite, a venture lab and early-stage accelerator for big-data startups and data scientists founded in 2013 at 135 Main Street, San Francisco, California. The entity was registered in California on 2013-08-27 as a foreign stock corporation and its filing status is recorded as forfeited by the Franchise Tax Board, indicating the business is no longer active. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live company website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. The dataelite.com domain resolves but redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale parking lander rather than a company site, and no other candidate domain resolved. This record is retained as an inactive historical entry in the API Evangelist network with no API artifacts to enrich; it should not be treated as an active API provider.

providers.name: Datafleets
providers.description: DataFleets was a privacy-preserving data science and federated computation platform that let organizations run analytics and machine learning across distributed, siloed, or regulated datasets without centralizing or exposing the underlying raw data, using techniques such as federated learning and differential privacy to keep data in place while still enabling cross-silo insight. Founded as a venture-backed startup and backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, DataFleets was acquired by LiveRamp in early 2021. Its former datafleets.com domain now redirects to liveramp.com, and the company operates no independent public developer portal, API, or documentation, so there is no live API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: DataGravity
providers.description: DataGravity was a data management and security software company founded in April 2012 in Nashua, New Hampshire by Paula Long (co-founder of EqualLogic) and John Joseph. It pioneered the "data-aware storage" category, shipping hybrid storage arrays that indexed, classified, and audited data in place so that security, governance, and search became properties of the storage tier rather than bolt-on tooling. The company raised venture funding from Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, CRV and others, won Best of Show at VMworld 2014, and began shipping in October 2014. In February 2016 it pivoted from appliances to a software-only behavioral data-security product. DataGravity ceased operations in June 2017 and its assets were assigned to a liquidator; HyTrust acquired the technology and roughly twenty employees, folding the product into HyTrust CloudAdvisor (HyTrust was itself acquired by Entrust in 2021). The datagravity.com domain no longer belongs to the company and now 301-redirects to an unrelated business (anomalo.com). No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification survives, so there is no API surface for this profile to describe.

providers.name: Datalogix
providers.description: Datalogix was a consumer-purchase and marketing data company that connected offline buying behavior to digital advertising audiences, enabling measurement and targeting for brands and ad platforms. Backed by General Catalyst and IVP, it was acquired by Oracle in 2014 and folded into the Oracle Data Cloud. The datalogix.com domain now 301-redirects to Oracle's acquisitions page, and no standalone Datalogix developer portal, API, or documentation remains publicly available.

providers.name: DataSine
providers.description: DataSine was a London-based AI personalization startup, founded in 2015 and backed by Techstars, that applied machine learning and behavioral psychology to help marketers tailor content, imagery, and copy to audience personality traits. The company was acquired by Shutterstock and folded into Shutterstock's AI/creative-intelligence work; its datasine.com domain is now registered to Shutterstock, Inc. (MarkMonitor) and HTTP 301-redirects to shutterstock.ai. DataSine no longer operates an independent product or a developer/API surface, so this profile is retained as an acquired-company record rather than an active provider awaiting API artifacts.

providers.name: Dataxu
providers.description: DataXu was a Boston-based programmatic advertising technology company, founded in 2009, that built a cloud-based demand-side platform (DSP) for automated, data-driven media buying across display, video, mobile, and connected TV. The company was acquired by Roku in 2019 and its technology was absorbed into Roku's OneView advertising platform (now Roku Ads). DataXu no longer operates as an independent brand: its primary domain (dataxu.com) 301-redirects into Roku's advertising site, and there is no independent DataXu developer portal, public API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical / acquired-company record surfaced from the Menlo Ventures portfolio.

providers.name: Datorama
providers.description: Datorama was a cloud-based marketing intelligence and analytics platform founded in 2012 in Tel Aviv and New York. It unified marketing, advertising, and sales data from thousands of disparate sources into a single AI-powered reporting and dashboarding layer, using its "Genius" machine-learning engine to automate data harmonization across ad, social, web, and CRM APIs. Salesforce acquired Datorama in August 2018 for a reported ~$800 million and rebranded it as Salesforce Marketing Cloud Intelligence (Marketing Intelligence). The standalone datorama.com domain now 301-redirects to the Salesforce Marketing Intelligence product page, and the former standalone developer/API surface has been folded into Salesforce documentation. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a lightspeed-venture-partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: Datrium
providers.description: Datrium was a Sunnyvale, California enterprise infrastructure company founded in 2012 by Brian Biles and Hugo Patterson (both formerly of Data Domain / EMC). Its flagship DVX ("Distributed Virtual X") platform introduced an "open convergence" architecture that separated compute from durable storage for virtualized data centers, and the company later pivoted toward cloud disaster-recovery-as-a-service (Datrium DRaaS with DRaaS Connect and ControlShield). Datrium was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, NEA, and others, and was acquired by VMware in July 2020, with its technology folded into VMware Cloud Disaster Recovery. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no active developer portal or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record surfaced from Lightspeed Venture Partners' portfolio.

providers.name: DaWanda.com
providers.description: DaWanda.com was a German online marketplace for handmade, unique, and custom-made products, founded in 2006 in Berlin. It connected independent makers and small designers with buyers across Germany and Europe, comparable to Etsy in the DACH region. DaWanda ceased operations on 30 August 2018 and partnered with Etsy to migrate its sellers and buyers; the www.dawanda.com domain now redirects to Etsy Germany. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. No public developer program or API surface was found during enrichment; the company is defunct and retained here as a historical/portfolio record.

providers.name: Dazz
providers.description: Dazz is a cloud security company specializing in Application Security Posture Management (ASPM) and code-to-cloud risk remediation. Its platform correlates findings across code, cloud, and on-prem infrastructure into a single unified view, maps vulnerabilities back to their root cause in source code, and gives security and engineering teams a remediation engine to prioritize and fix issues across the application lifecycle. Co-founded and led by CEO Merav Bahat, Dazz was backed by Insight Partners, Greylock, Cyberstarts, and others. Wiz announced its acquisition of Dazz on November 21, 2024 to extend its Cloud Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) with Dazz's remediation capabilities; the dazz.io domain now redirects into Wiz. This profile has no independent public developer/API surface.

providers.name: DCB Technologies
providers.description: DCB Technologies is a company name that appears on the Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) published investment list, and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-derived stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass no public company website, developer portal, documentation, API reference, or machine-readable API artifact could be attributed to the a16z-listed entity: the a16z investment list publishes the name with no accompanying URL or sector, and open-web search surfaces only unrelated same-name businesses (a French IT services firm at dcb-technologies.fr, plus several unaffiliated US LLCs registered in Florida, Delaware, Wisconsin, New Jersey and Maryland). No base host was therefore available to probe for /.well-known/ discovery documents, domain security records, package registries, or specifications. This profile is retained as an identity-only lead and should be revisited when a canonical domain for the a16z-backed entity is published.

providers.name: DCHQ
providers.description: DCHQ (Data Center HQ) was a cloud automation and Docker container management platform out of San Francisco, offering both a hosted PaaS (DCHQ.io) and self-hosted on-premise editions for modeling, deploying, and managing container-based applications across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Rackspace, and OpenStack. The platform covered application modeling (Docker Compose / JSON), infrastructure automation, multi-tenant governance and access controls, and lifecycle management including monitoring, backup, and auto-scaling, with integrations for Docker, GitHub, and Jenkins. The company is now defunct — its primary domain (dchq.co) no longer resolves and dchq.io serves a frozen 2020 marketing snapshot with no live developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record; no live API artifacts were available to enrich.

providers.name: DCS-Touristik (DCS Travel)
providers.description: DCS-Touristik GmbH, trading as DCS Travel (dcs.travel), is a German river- and sea-cruise operator based in Nagel, Germany. The company organizes river cruises on major European waterways — primarily the Danube and the Rhine — as well as sea cruises along the Croatian coast, operating its own vessels including the DCS Amethyst 1 and DCS Amethyst 2. Its business is direct consumer travel booking: multi-day cruise packages (roughly 3 to 12 days), organized transfers and shore excursions, themed sailings, travel-insurance partnerships, and early-booking discounts. This is a consumer-facing tourism brand with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer documentation. It was originally added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio stub; that classification appears to be a false match (the "early-bird" cruise discount wording rather than the Earlybird venture firm), and no API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: DealCart
providers.description: DealCart is a Pakistan-based social-commerce and group-buying startup offering discounted groceries and everyday household goods, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As a consumer mobile-commerce business it publishes no public developer program. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-18 found the primary domain dealcart.io parked/expired (a Namecheap landing page) and dealcart.pk serving a password-gated Shopify storefront, with no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or API surface to harvest. This profile carries a live domain-security probe and remains a lead pending any future public API program.

providers.name: Dealflo
providers.description: Dealflo was a UK-based financial-technology company that provided an automated agreement, identity-verification, and e-signature platform used by lenders and financial institutions to capture, verify, and legally bind financial agreements end to end. It was acquired by OneSpan (formerly VASCO Data Security) in September 2018 for roughly USD 55 million and folded into OneSpan's Digital Agreements / electronic-signature product line. The dealflo.com domain now 301-redirects to onespan.com and Dealflo no longer operates an independent developer program, public documentation, or API. This record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio/company lead surfaced from the HV Capital portfolio; no independent API artifacts exist to enrich because the product surface has been absorbed by OneSpan.

providers.name: Dean Foods
providers.description: Dean Foods was a leading U.S. food and beverage company and one of the largest processors and direct-to-store distributors of fresh fluid milk and other dairy products. After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2019, most of Dean Foods' assets were acquired by Dairy Farmers of America (DFA) in 2020. Dean Foods no longer operates as an independent company and does not publish a public developer API; surviving brands are now managed under DFA. This profile is retained for historical reference.

providers.name: DecisionPoint Software
providers.description: DecisionPoint Software was a San Mateo, California-based enterprise software company that provided packaged financial performance management (FPM) and financial data warehousing software, built primarily around the Oracle ERP stack. Its systems captured and moved continuously changing data from financial source systems into a data warehouse, automatically configuring the analytic environment as the source systems changed, and shipped as far as Release 11 with operations in both the United States and the United Kingdom. The company was named one of the 50 fastest-growing private companies in Silicon Valley in 2004 and raised a $5M Series B round from Battery Ventures that same year. It was acquired in December 2005 by NCR's Teradata data warehousing division, which folded the FPM and data warehousing technology into the Teradata enterprise data warehouse offering. DecisionPoint Software has not operated as an independent company for roughly two decades: it publishes no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface, and this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Deep Render
providers.description: Deep Render is an artificial-intelligence company that developed neural-network-based ("learned") video and image compression technology, aiming to replace traditional hand-engineered codecs such as H.264/HEVC/AV1 with deep-learning models for higher compression efficiency. Founded as a London-based startup, it was backed by Speedinvest and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network through VC-portfolio discovery. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain, deeprender.ai, issues a blanket HTTP 301 redirect to InterDigital's Video Lab (https://www.interdigital.com/video-lab/), indicating the company and its compression technology have been absorbed into InterDigital. Deep Render publishes no independent developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface for enrichment at this time.

providers.name: deepfactor
providers.description: Deepfactor was an application security (AppSec / ASPM) platform for cloud-native and containerized applications. Its integrated approach combined software composition analysis (SCA), software bill of materials (SBOM) generation, container image scanning, and container runtime security into a single developer-security platform. Its differentiating capability was runtime software composition analysis / runtime reachability, correlating static scans with observed runtime application behavior so teams could prioritize vulnerability remediation based on true usage. Use cases spanned Shift-Left & DevSecOps, supply chain security, SBOM, container runtime security & compliance (SOC 2), and cloud-native application security. Backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07) the public website is offline — the apex domain (deepfactor.io) returns a Cisco 503 error page and the WP Engine-hosted www/docs hosts return "Site is not available", and DNS for the apex resolves to Cisco infrastructure; there is no live developer portal, API, SDK, CLI, GitHub organization, or published package to harvest.

providers.name: DeepMap
providers.description: DeepMap was a high-definition mapping and localization software company for autonomous vehicles, building HD maps, real-time localization, and map-update infrastructure that let self-driving cars know precisely where they were. Backed by a16z and Accel, DeepMap was acquired by NVIDIA in 2021 and folded into NVIDIA's autonomous-vehicle platform; the deepmap.ai domain now resolves to NVIDIA's self-driving solutions page. No independent DeepMap developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists post-acquisition. This profile is retained as a network/portfolio record.

providers.name: DeepSparks
providers.description: DeepSparks was a Bangkok, Thailand fintech offering a lending-as-a-service platform built on AI-driven alternative credit scoring. It analyzed non-traditional data to help financial institutions, microlenders, and enablers approve and acquire underbanked borrowers, and offered a data API, lead generation, and a rejected-applicant exchange. Founded in 2018 and backed by 500 Global and J Ventures, the company has since ceased operations (deadpooled); its official site at deepsparks.ai no longer resolves.

providers.name: DeepWay 深向
providers.description: DeepWay (深向科技 / Shenxiang Technology) is a Chinese intelligent new-energy heavy-truck company, backed by Baidu and Qiming Venture Partners, that designs and manufactures electric autonomous freight trucks it calls RoboTrucks. Its vehicle line includes the Xingchen II (深向星辰 II) and Xingtu (深向星途) electric heavy trucks paired with the Tianji (天玑) driver-assistance and autonomous driving stack, an AI-based fleet management platform, and a vehicle-owner mobile app. DeepWay reports 7,500+ activated L2 vehicles, a 30%+ subscription rate, and 300M+ km of assisted-driving operation, and follows a roadmap from L2 assistance (2023) to L4 platooning (2025) to single-vehicle L4 autonomy (2028). Its business model progresses from vehicle sales to subscription services to large-scale autonomous logistics capacity. As of this enrichment pass DeepWay publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification — this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: DeepWeave
providers.description: DeepWeave is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of homebrew and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ai. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency
providers.description: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is the largest security agency in the federal government, dedicated to protecting America's trusted workforce and trusted workspaces. DCSA conducts personnel vetting and background investigations, oversees the National Industrial Security Program, delivers counterintelligence and insider threat support, and operates systems such as the Defense Information System for Security (DISS) and the National Background Investigation Services (NBIS). DCSA does not currently expose a public developer API; access to its mission systems is limited to authorized government users and cleared industry partners.

providers.name: Defense.net
providers.description: Defense.Net was a cloud DDoS-mitigation company founded in 2012 by Barrett Lyon (also the founder of Prolexic, the original DDoS-mitigation provider). It operated a global constellation of scrubbing/mitigation sites that filtered distributed-denial-of-service attacks against Internet-facing infrastructure in real time. Bessemer Venture Partners led a $9.5M Series A in 2012. In May 2014 the company was acquired by F5 Networks and folded into the F5 Silverline DDoS Protection managed service. Defense.Net no longer operates as an independent business: the defense.net domain now returns an HTTP 301 redirect to the F5 Silverline product page, and there is no independent developer portal, public API, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Degla Inc
providers.description: Degla is a Y Combinator (Fall 2026) startup building an autonomous aerial intelligence layer that turns natural language into multi-drone mission execution. Operators describe an objective in plain language and Degla plans the mission, assigns aircraft, defines coverage patterns, and deploys a fleet that adapts in real time — with no waypoints, flight plans, or specialized training required. The platform targets search and rescue, emergency response, infrastructure inspection, and other critical field operations. Founded in 2026 by Aziz Hanafi and based in Boston, the company is in early access and has not yet published a public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Dehash.lt
providers.description: Hash decryption MD5, SHA1, SHA3, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512

providers.name: Deice
providers.description: De-Ice Technologies is an aviation deep-tech company that develops a fast, chemical-free aircraft de-icing system to replace traditional glycol chemical spray methods. Spun out of MIT in 2015 by co-founders Alexander Bratianu-Badea and Ruben Toubiana, the Somerville, Massachusetts company uses gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductors to generate high-frequency electric current through tape-like strips attached to an aircraft's exterior, melting snow and ice during the boarding window instead of the usual 30-45 minute glycol spray delay. The approach eliminates glycol spraying costs and the carbon emissions from idling and chemical production/transport, improving airline on-time performance. Air Canada is the launch customer, and the technology was featured in Time's Best Inventions of 2024. De-Ice is a portfolio company of Playground Global. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; De-Ice publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Deliverr
providers.description: Deliverr was an e-commerce fulfillment company founded in 2017 (Harish Abbott and Michael Krakaris) that offered fast, affordable outbound fulfillment for online sellers across marketplaces such as Shopify, Amazon, Walmart, eBay, and Wish, backed by 8vc and other investors. Shopify acquired Deliverr in 2022 and folded it into Shopify Logistics / the Shopify Fulfillment Network; in 2023 Shopify sold that logistics business to Flexport. Deliverr no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone developer portal or API — its former domain (deliverr.com) now redirects to flexport.com, and its fulfillment capabilities live inside Flexport's platform. This profile is retained as a historical network stub; there is no live Deliverr API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Delta Tucker Holdings
providers.description: Delta Tucker Holdings was the holding company for DynCorp International, a provider of specialized mission-critical professional and support services to government and commercial customers, including aviation services, logistics, and training. DynCorp's operations were acquired and integrated into Amentum in 2020. Delta Tucker Holdings does not publish public APIs; this profile is preserved as a corporate-history index.

providers.name: Deployco
providers.description: Deployco (the OpenAI Deployment Company, DeployCo) is a ~$10B enterprise-AI joint venture launched by OpenAI in May 2026 to help organizations put frontier AI into production. It is an engineering-heavy consulting and deployment business: Forward Deployed Engineers and Deployment Specialists embed in client companies to connect OpenAI models to their data, tools, controls, and core workflows (RAG, fine-tuning/distillation, infrastructure, and safety/compliance). It is backed by a founding-investor group including Emergence Capital. DeployCo is a services/consulting entity and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs of its own; any API surface it uses is the OpenAI platform. No API artifacts are available to enrich at this time.

providers.name: Dexterra
providers.description: Dexterra was a mobile workforce management software startup that built a mobile application platform for managing and optimizing field/mobile operations. Backed by Canaan Partners along with New Enterprise Associates, Intel Capital, Motorola Solutions Venture Capital, and Mesirow Financial, the company raised roughly $108M across its rounds. Dexterra was acquired by Antenna Software in June 2009 and no longer operates as an independent entity; it has no active developer program, public API, or developer portal. This profile is retained as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead for network completeness.

providers.name: Diamanti
providers.description: Diamanti was a San Jose, California infrastructure company (founded 2014) that built hyperconverged, bare-metal infrastructure purpose-built for containers and Kubernetes. Its flagship Ultima platform paired plug-and-play appliances with hardware-accelerated networking and storage I/O cards, and its Spektra software added multi-cluster, hybrid-cloud Kubernetes management across on-premises and public-cloud environments. As of this enrichment pass the company appears to be defunct / to have ceased operations: www.diamanti.com resolves but returns a captcha-walled placeholder (HTTP 202, noindex) with no reachable developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or public API surface.

providers.name: Diapers.com
providers.description: Diapers.com is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ecommerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Dictum
providers.description: API to get access to the collection of the most inspiring expressions of mankind

providers.name: DiDi Autonomous
providers.description: DiDi Autonomous Driving (滴滴自动驾驶) is the autonomous-driving subsidiary of Chinese mobility giant DiDi. Founded as an internal research unit in 2016 and spun out as an independent company in 2019, it develops Level 4 self-driving technology and operates robotaxi services integrated into the DiDi ride-hailing platform in Chinese cities including Shanghai and Guangzhou. In 2020 SoftBank Vision Fund led a roughly $500M funding round into the unit. As a hardware- and fleet-oriented autonomous mobility operator it does not currently publish a public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Digby
providers.description: Digby was an Austin, Texas software-as-a-service provider of mobile commerce and mobile engagement solutions for large retailers, operating under parent company 30 Second Software Inc. Its platform — including the Localpoint location-based marketing product — delivered branded mobile web experiences and native shopping apps, connecting digital engagement to physical stores for customers such as Cabela's, Kohl's, Catalina Marketing and Hasbro. Digby raised venture funding from Battery Ventures, S3 Ventures, Daylight Ventures, Relay Ventures and the BlackBerry Partners Fund. The company was acquired by fellow Austin mobile company Phunware in May 2014 (along with its Movaya subsidiary in Seattle and Chengdu), terms undisclosed, and the Localpoint technology was folded into Phunware's product line. Digby no longer operates as an independent company: digby.com no longer resolves to a live site (last Internet Archive capture February 2015) and there is no current developer portal, documentation, API, SDK or other public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Digiflex
providers.description: Digiflex (listed by Battery Ventures as "Digiflex, Ltd.") is a former Battery Ventures portfolio company, marked on the firm's list-of-all-companies page as an exited investment. The API Evangelist enrichment pipeline could not resolve an operating web presence for this entity: digiflex.com does not resolve (NXDOMAIN), and the live domains sharing the name are unrelated third parties — digiflex.io is a UK web-design agency, digiflex.co.uk is a separate UK business, and digiflex.ai returns HTTP 403 with no verifiable link to the Battery investment. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, package-registry presence, or any other API artifact could be located for this company. This profile is retained as an honest record of an exited/defunct portfolio lead with no discoverable API surface rather than being enriched with speculative attribution.

providers.name: Digital Market
providers.description: Digital Market was an enterprise-software company that built electronic-components B2B commerce software, backed by Trinity Ventures. It was acquired by Agile Software and no longer operates as an independent provider. It is not an API provider and publishes no live developer surface, documentation, or specifications; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio record rather than an active, enrichable API.

providers.name: Digital Mortar
providers.description: Digital Mortar is an in-store and physical-location people-journey analytics company. Its DM1 platform measures shopper and visitor journeys - path, queue, occupancy, throughput, dwell and space utilization - using LiDAR and stereoscopic-camera sensors, delivering heat mapping, funnel analysis, real-time queue and occupancy tracking, display and merchandising measurement, and door/people counting as a SaaS analytics tool. It serves retail, airports, malls, stadiums and events. Digital Mortar is now part of PMY Group; its digitalmortar.com domain is dormant (mail-only, no live website) and it exposes no public developer or API program.

providers.name: Digital Room
providers.description: Digital Room is a marketing and printing services company that for nearly three decades has helped small and medium-sized businesses reach customers, promote products, and build their brands. It operates a family of online printing and marketing brands serving SMBs with print, signage, and promotional products. Backed by Insight Partners, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Dija
providers.description: Dija is a consumer-sector company surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-18 enrichment pass the company has no live web or developer surface: its candidate domains do not resolve (dija.co, dija.com) and dija.co.uk is a parked domain listed for sale by a third-party broker. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or any other API artifact could be located, so no provider artifacts were generated or derived. The 2026-07-20 pass re-verified this independently: dija.co and dija.com return NXDOMAIN, dija.co.uk resolves to an Aftermarket.com parking page advertising the domain for sale (Nominet registration active to 2026-12-10) and returns 404 for every /.well-known/ discovery path and /llms.txt. Note for future runs: the github.com/dija organization and the dija.now and dija.sa domains are UNRELATED name collisions (Dija, a Saudi Arabia software firm, and a separate reminder app) and must not be attributed to this company. This profile remains a lead with no active public API surface.

providers.name: Diligent Software
providers.description: Diligent Software is an entry harvested from Battery Ventures' public "list of all companies" (https://www.battery.com/list-of-all-companies/), where it is marked with an asterisk denoting an EXITED investment. Battery publishes only the company name for this entry — no URL, no sector, no description, and no acquisition or IPO detail — so the underlying company could not be positively identified during enrichment. It appears to be a legacy/defunct or long-since-acquired enterprise software investment rather than an operating API provider. The only live host at diligentsoftware.com is an unrelated single-proprietor custom .NET software consultancy in Liberty Hill, Texas (Peter Stephens), whose static site has not been updated since February 2014; it is NOT treated as this company. This profile is explicitly NOT Diligent Corporation, the GRC/board-management vendor at diligent.com — that company is catalogued separately in the network as diligent-boards (developer.diligent.com, HighBond/Entities/ESG/Workflow APIs) — and it is NOT Diligent AI (godiligent.ai), the KYC/AML compliance API catalogued as diligent. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, package, well-known surface, or event surface was found for this entry. No artifacts were produced because none exist to harvest.

providers.name: Dillard's
providers.description: Dillard's is an American department store chain offering apparel, footwear, cosmetics, handbags, menswear, and home goods from top brands. The retailer operates stores across the United States and an e-commerce site, with no publicly documented developer APIs at this time.

providers.name: Dimeq
providers.description: Dimeq is a Norwegian maritime safety technology company working to prevent loss of life at sea and set new health, safety and environmental (HSE) standards for the maritime sector. Its Eye-D System is an IoT-based digital ecosystem that delivers real-time positioning of crew and passengers to one-meter accuracy during emergencies, man-overboard detection using environmental sensors, automatic mustering that registers people in seconds, and statistical analysis for accident documentation and prevention, while keeping data anonymous and GDPR-compliant outside of emergencies. The D-Router gateway supports Wi-Fi, Ethernet, PLC, fiber optics, UWB, Bluetooth, LoRa, ZigBee and MATTER connectivity. This is a hardware/IoT product company with no public developer portal, API, SDK or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Dingdong
providers.description: Dingdong (Dingdong Maicai / 叮咚买菜) is a Shanghai-based on-demand fresh-grocery e-commerce company operating a front-warehouse (dark-store) model that delivers fruit, vegetables, meat, seafood and prepared foods to consumers, typically within about 30 minutes, through its mobile app. The company is publicly listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker DDL) and is backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). Its public surface (ddxq.mobi) is a consumer mobile-app backend rather than a developer platform; no public developer portal, API documentation, or open API program was found during enrichment, and the host is not reachable outside of China.

providers.name: Dingdong Maicai
providers.description: Dingdong Maicai (叮咚买菜), operated by Shanghai Yibai Mi Network Technology Co., Ltd., is a Chinese on-demand fresh grocery e-commerce and delivery platform. It runs a mobile-app marketplace for fresh produce, meat, seafood, prepared foods, and daily groceries, backed by a network of front-line neighborhood micro-fulfillment stations that enable fast, same-hour delivery in major Chinese cities. The company is publicly listed on the NYSE (ticker DDL) and was backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It is a consumer-facing operation with no public developer program or open API surface; this profile is a network lead maintained by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Direct Revenue
providers.description: Direct Revenue was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead. A July 2026 enrichment pass found no live corporate or developer surface for this company: directrevenue.com resolves to an Efty domain-for-sale parking lander (domain registered 2002, held at Tucows, listed for sale); direct-revenue.com is a squatted domain that 302-redirects to baidu.com; directrevenue.co returns Cloudflare 522 (origin unreachable); and directrevenue.net, directrevenue.ai and getdirectrevenue.com do not resolve at all. There is no website, no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no matching provider in the APIs.io catalog. This profile is retained as a historical lead record only and carries no API artifacts.

providers.name: Dirig Software
providers.description: Dirig Software, Inc. was a Nashua, New Hampshire software company that built application and system management software for eBusiness — agent-based performance monitoring and automated problem correction for J2EE application servers (WebLogic, WebSphere), web infrastructure, and hosted service-provider environments, sold both direct to enterprises and through OEM and service-provider channels. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures. Its web presence at dirig.com carried full product, partner, and support content through roughly 2003, degraded to a broken holding page under the name "Dirig Corporation" from early 2004, and by late 2006 the domain was a parked Sedo for-sale page. As of this enrichment pass the company has no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind; dirig.com now resolves to an unrelated third-party endpoint returning a bare "OK" health response. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network — there is nothing to enrich and nothing to score.

providers.name: Discovered Materials
providers.description: Discovered Materials (legally matforge inc) is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) startup based in San Francisco building AI scientists for the semiconductor industry. The company uses swarms of AI agents to run the full materials-discovery pipeline - generating candidate materials, synthesizing them, and testing them in physical laboratories - to find novel materials for datacenters and fabrication facilities. Their stated goal is to compress a process that traditionally takes 10+ years of lab work into months, targeting 10x-better alternatives for applications such as nanoscale interconnects. Founded by Akash Ramdas (Stanford materials-science PhD/postdoc) and Advaith Sridhar (Carnegie Mellon AI, formerly Luma Labs and Persona AI). At the time of profiling the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; this entry is an enrichment lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DISH Network
providers.description: DISH Network is a U.S. television provider offering satellite and streaming TV services, as well as wireless services through its Boost Mobile and DISH Wireless brands. DISH is now part of EchoStar following the 2024 merger that brought DISH and Hughes back together under one parent. No public consumer-facing developer APIs are documented; the Boost Mobile and DISH Wireless networks are operated on a 5G Open RAN architecture.

providers.name: Distil Networks
providers.description: Distil Networks was a bot detection and mitigation company founded in 2011 and backed by Techstars, providing automated-threat protection, web scraping defense, account-takeover prevention, and API security that blocked malicious bots and credential stuffing across web, mobile, and API surfaces. Distil Networks was acquired by Imperva in 2019 and its technology now lives on as Imperva Advanced Bot Protection; the distilnetworks.com domain redirects to Imperva and there is no independent Distil Networks developer surface or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record.

providers.name: Distributedspectrum
