providers.description: Distributed Spectrum, self-described as "The World's First AI Signals Expert," builds edge-AI radio-frequency sensing technology that detects and identifies RF signals to autonomously map threats without expensive hardware or trained operators. Its sensors process data locally to deliver real-time alerts on threat types such as tactical radios, GPS jammers, and drones, and can be deployed anywhere using commercial components to form distributed detection networks. The company is headquartered at 99 Madison Ave, New York, NY, raised a $25M Series A, and is a Felicis portfolio company. No public API or developer program is published at this time; this profile carries the identity and domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Divide *
providers.description: Divide was a bring-your-own-device (BYOD) mobile management product, built by Enterproid, that created a secure, separate work persona (dual-persona / work profile) on an employee's personal Android and iOS phone. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), the company was acquired by Google on May 19, 2014 and folded into the Android for Work / Android Enterprise program. The standalone Divide product and any developer or API surface have been discontinued; divide.com now serves a Google-owned tombstone page that redirects visitors to android.com/work. No independent API, developer portal, SDK, or specification remains to enrich — this record is preserved as an acquired-company profile.

providers.name: DMall
providers.description: DMall (多点数智, Dmall Inc.) is an Asia-Pacific retail digitalization service provider that pairs consulting with technology to deliver an all-in-one digital retail operating system for supermarkets, grocery chains, and other retailers. Its cloud-native SaaS platform (Dmall OS) spans supply chain, point-of-sale, store operations, membership, e-commerce, and O2O fulfillment, helping traditional retailers modernize into data-driven omnichannel businesses. The company is backed by IDG Capital among other investors. DMall does not currently publish a public developer portal, open-platform documentation, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile captures its public web identity and domain security posture while awaiting a documented API surface.

providers.name: DNA Games
providers.description: DNA Games was a social game studio founded in 2009 by Jon Lee and Shaun Haase in the San Francisco Bay Area, building technology for real-time social game optimization on the Facebook platform. The studio shipped Casino City, Bar World, and Slot City, casino and lifestyle simulation titles that together reached more than 20 million players, with Casino City becoming a leading casino simulation game on Facebook. The company raised roughly $2 million in venture funding from Battery Ventures and Bain Capital Ventures before being acquired by Zynga in May 2011, one of a rapid series of Zynga studio acquisitions during that period. Post-acquisition the founders and core team were absorbed into Zynga to seed a new internal game studio, and DNA Games ceased to operate as an independent company. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company publishes no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface; the dnagames.com, dna.games, and dnagames.io domains are all parked or listed for sale by third parties and are not operated by the company.

providers.name: DogVacay
providers.description: DogVacay was a consumer marketplace for dog boarding, pet sitting, dog walking, and doggy daycare that connected pet owners with a network of vetted, background-checked pet sitters and hosts across the United States and Canada. Founded in 2012 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), the company was acquired by and merged into Rover in 2017; the DogVacay brand has since been retired and dogvacay.com now redirects to Rover. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was ever published, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: Dolly
providers.description: Dolly was a Seattle-based on-demand moving and last-mile delivery marketplace that connected people who needed help moving furniture and large items with independent "Helpers" who owned pickup trucks and vans, coordinated through consumer and retail-partner mobile apps. It grew a same-day big-and-bulky delivery network used by retailers such as IKEA, Costco, Lowe's, West Elm, and Peloton. Dolly was acquired and folded into TaskRabbit (owned by IKEA / Ingka Group); as of 2026 the dolly.com domain 301-redirects entirely to taskrabbit.com/delivery, and the service now operates under the "Taskrabbit Delivery" brand. No standalone Dolly-owned developer portal, public API, or well-known discovery surface survives — every dolly.com path redirects into TaskRabbit. This profile records the honest disposition of the company; the developer/API footprint now lives (if anywhere) under TaskRabbit, not Dolly.

providers.name: DolphinSearch
providers.description: DolphinSearch was an eDiscovery, information lifecycle management, and compliance company surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. As of enrichment it has no active public developer or API surface - the dolphinsearch.com domain is parked/for-sale (302 to HugeDomains) and the Insight Partners portfolio record marks it as not an API provider - so no API artifacts could be produced.

providers.name: Donnerwood Media
providers.description: Donnerwood Media was an early-stage social gaming and social entertainment company founded in 2005 by Sean Ryan and based in San Francisco. It operated Meez.com, an avatar-building platform that let consumers create customized 3D avatars usable across the web as personal identifiers, alongside a portfolio of social game properties. The company raised roughly $15.7M from Battery Ventures, transcosmos, and Allen & Company. It is now defunct — the Meez service went offline in December 2017 and its domain expired in March 2018 — so it exposes no live website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: Doodle Mobile
providers.description: Doodle Mobile (Asia) Limited is a developer and publisher of casual mobile games for Android, founded in 2010 and backed by KPCB and Innovation Works, with research and development centers in Beijing and Shanghai and more than 300 million downloads across its catalog. Its titles include Restaurant Live, Dino Island (Dragon), and Fast Racing 3D, and it also partners with third party developers to publish games worldwide. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a static brochure website with no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or portal.

providers.name: Door-to-Door Organic
providers.description: Door to Door Organics was an organic and natural grocery home-delivery service founded in 1997 and headquartered in Louisville, Colorado. It delivered fresh local and organic produce boxes along with pantry staples, dairy, eggs, meat, and bread to homes and offices across roughly 17 states in the West, Midwest, and East Coast (including Washington, D.C.). Backed by Battery Ventures among others, the company raised about $44.4M over six rounds before abruptly ceasing operations in 2017. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no public developer surface (no portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or API host); the company is defunct and publishes no API.

providers.name: Dooyoo De
providers.description: Dooyoo was a German consumer product-review and price-comparison platform built on user-generated reviews, best known for its "dooyooMiles" rewards program that paid users for writing reviews. It was acquired by the French shopping-guide publisher LeGuide.com in 2008, and the LeGuide group (Ciao, Dooyoo, and others) was in turn acquired by Kelkoo in 2016 to form Kelkoo Group. The dooyoo.de domain no longer operates as an independent brand and now 301-redirects to kelkoogroup.com; there is no active developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a defunct/absorbed portfolio lead with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Dot Product
providers.description: Dot Product is a San Francisco AI startup founded in 2024 by Usman Masood (former CTO of Pipe and engineering manager at Stripe) and Maksim Stepanenko (previously at Coinbase, Primer, Locu, and the MIT Media Lab). The company builds "Operator," a platform of voice-first AI coworkers (agents) for operations and customer-support teams: AI agents that follow company-specific playbooks, provide 24/7 phone/voice support, and scale to fluctuating demand as an alternative to traditional call centers. Dot Product raised a $6M seed round led by Index Ventures with participation from Lachy Groom. As of this enrichment pass the company operates in stealth: the product surface (operator.xyz) does not resolve publicly and dotproduct.xyz is parked, so no public API, developer docs, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications could be verified. Sector: ai-ml.

providers.name: Double Click
providers.description: DoubleClick was an interactive marketing and advertising technology company founded in 1996 by Kevin O'Connor and Dwight Merriman. It pioneered ad serving, targeting, and campaign measurement for publishers and advertisers, went public on NASDAQ as DCLK, and was acquired by Google in 2008 for roughly $3.1 billion. Its products were folded into Google's advertising stack — DoubleClick for Publishers became Google Ad Manager and DoubleClick Digital Marketing became the Google Marketing Platform. DoubleClick no longer exists as an independent company or API provider; doubleclick.com now redirects to Google Marketing Platform. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical venture-portfolio record (surfaced via lightspeed-venture-partners) rather than a live, enrichable developer surface.

providers.name: Drafted
providers.description: Drafted is a network-recruiting and employee-referral platform, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company. The product helps companies tap their collective network to source, qualify, and hire talent: a Drafted Slackbot delivers weekly intelligent referral recommendations and lets teams submit referrals straight into their ATS from Slack, while NLP, machine learning, and a graph database of the company network extend matching beyond first-degree employee connections to surface higher-quality referrals. Drafted has been used by thousands of companies ranging from startups to large enterprises. This profile was seeded from a VC-portfolio lead; at enrichment time the public web surface (drafted.us) was not serving a live product site and no public API, developer documentation, or specification could be found.

providers.name: Drawbridge
providers.description: Drawbridge, Inc. was a San Mateo, California cross-device identity and digital advertising company founded in 2011 by Kamakshi Sivaramakrishnan (a former AdMob scientist). It built a people-based identity graph that used machine learning to probabilistically match individuals across their connected devices (desktops, smartphones, tablets, and connected TVs) so brands could serve and measure relevant advertising across devices. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Northgate Capital, and Mitsui & Co., the company raised roughly $69M across five rounds before it was acquired by LinkedIn in 2019 and folded into LinkedIn Marketing Solutions. Drawbridge no longer operates as an independent company and never published a public developer API or developer portal, so there is no live API surface to enrich; this profile records its identity as a historical Kleiner Perkins portfolio company.

providers.name: Drawbridge Networks
providers.description: Drawbridge Networks was a network microsegmentation cybersecurity startup founded in 2014 in New York by John Terrill and Tom Cross. Its product, PathProtect, applied fine-grained, identity- and workload-aware security policies inside corporate networks to learn, detect, and automatically quarantine lateral (east-west) attacker movement before it could spread. The company raised a $1.7M seed round from Antecedent Ventures, Bloomberg Beta, and Bowery Capital, and was acquired by OPAQ Networks in May 2017 (OPAQ was itself later acquired by Fortinet in 2020). Drawbridge Networks was surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment finds the company defunct: no domains resolve, and there is no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Dream Voyage Inc.
providers.description: Dream Voyage Inc. is an AI-driven consumer studio founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz through its Speedrun accelerator alongside Soma Capital. Led by co-founder and CEO Coco Chen, a former TikTok founding product manager and Tinder PM, the studio builds viral AI-powered consumer applications spanning spiritual wellness, dream interpretation, gaming, and social payments. Its products include SINE Daily Manifest (an AI spiritual-health app offering daily affirmations, astrology, birth-chart analysis, and tarot readings that went viral on TikTok), Dreamore (AI-powered dream interpretation), Vdrop (turning social media into a payment network), and RPS (a Solana-based social game). Dream Voyage ships consumer mobile apps rather than a public developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documented API surface. This record is a network stub retained for discovery and future enrichment.

providers.name: Drippi
providers.description: Drippi (trydrippi.com) was a New York City-based platform that helped young content creators navigate the complexities of running their creator businesses. The company has been acquired and has closed its service to both current and new customers, directing its community to Instagram (@trydrippi) for future updates. It does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. NOTE FOR ENRICHMENT — this entity is distinct from the similarly named drippi.ai, a separate, bootstrapped Twitter/X cold-outreach DM automation SaaS (founded 2021 by Alex Penunuri, no venture funding); do not attach drippi.ai's API artifacts to this Bloomberg Beta portfolio profile.

providers.name: Drishti
providers.description: Drishti was an AI and computer-vision company that turned manual assembly-line activity into continuous streams of process data for discrete manufacturers. Cameras securely streamed factory-floor video into proprietary neural networks that generated cycle-time data and detected the sequence of human actions within each cycle, giving plant teams system-wide visibility into variability, bottlenecks, and improvement opportunities. Founded in 2017 in Mountain View, California and backed by Emergence Capital, Drishti counted Ford, Honeywell, and Nissan among its customers before being acquired by Apple in September 2023. The company operated no public developer API, and all of its web and developer domains are now offline.

providers.name: Drishti Technologies
providers.description: Drishti Technologies was a Mountain View, California company (founded 2016 by Prasad Akella, Krishnendu Chaudhury, and Ashish Gupta) that applied AI-powered computer vision and video analytics to manual assembly lines in manufacturing. Its platform digitized human actions on the production floor to enable time-and-motion studies at scale, quality traceability, and continuous improvement, with products including Drishti Trace (video capture and traceability) and Drishti Flow (line analytics). The company was acquired by Apple in September 2023 and no longer operates an independent public website, developer portal, or API surface — its domains (drishti.com, drishti.ai) no longer resolve to a live product.

providers.name: Driveway Corporation
providers.description: Driveway Corporation was a dot-com-era online file storage and sharing service that operated driveway.com from roughly 1998 until 2001. Its consumer product let members "store and access files from any Web-connected computer" and share documents, photos and MP3s with friends and colleagues, with up to 100 MB of free storage on sign-up; it also marketed a white-label "Driveway Private Label Storage" offering to other websites. Battery Ventures lists Driveway Corporation as an exited investment. The company is defunct and no longer operates any web, developer or API surface. NOTE: the driveway.com domain today belongs to an unrelated business — Lithia Motors' Driveway online car marketplace — and must not be attributed to this company.

providers.name: Drone Capital I
providers.description: Drone Capital I is an entry harvested from the Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) public investment list at https://a16z.com/investment-list/ and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. Enrichment probing found no operating company, no developer surface, and no API behind this name. The naming pattern ("<theme> Capital I") matches a fund or special-purpose investment vehicle rather than an operating startup, and no corresponding corporate website, documentation portal, or public repository could be located. Candidate domains were probed directly and none belong to this entity. This profile is retained as a catalog record of the a16z investment-list entry only; it is not an API provider and carries no API artifacts.

providers.name: Dropcam
providers.description: Dropcam is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, bessemer-venture-partners, kleiner-perkins, menlo-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: dstzc
providers.description: dstzc (地上铁, DiShangTie Green Technology, Shenzhen) is a leading Chinese provider of digitalized operations-management solutions for new-energy (electric) logistics vehicles. It operates a full-lifecycle fleet platform covering vehicle sales and leasing, digital fleet management, safety and risk management, maintenance, charging and battery-swap services, and residual-value management, reporting 224,000+ operational vehicles across 3,246 service locations spanning all 333 prefecture-level regions of mainland China. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company has no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dubsmash
providers.description: Dubsmash was a video-selfie and lip-sync mobile application that let users record short videos set to a library of popular audio clips, quotes, and songs. Founded in Germany in 2014 by Jonas Druppel, Roland Grenke, and Daniel Taschik, it grew into one of the most downloaded social video apps, particularly among younger creators in the United States. Reddit acquired Dubsmash in December 2020, integrated its video-creation technology into the Reddit platform, and discontinued the standalone Dubsmash app on February 22, 2022. Dubsmash never offered a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; its consumer domain (dubsmash.com) no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical, defunct company record surfaced from venture-capital portfolio data.

providers.name: Dulcetta
providers.description: Dulcetta is the company behind Focus@Will (focusatwill.com), a functional-music streaming service that curates instrumental soundtracks scientifically designed to improve concentration and productivity during focused work. Backed by 500 Global, Dulcetta operates a consumer subscription product marketing measurable gains in focus for knowledge workers, students, and creative professionals who work with music. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced lead; no public developer API or documentation surface has been identified to date, so this profile carries company identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Dune
providers.description: A simple API which provides you with book, character, movie and quotes JSON data

providers.name: Dverse
providers.description: Dverse is the API Evangelist network profile for Symmetry Dimensions Inc. (株式会社SYMMETRY), a Tokyo-based technology company whose "DVERSE" digital-twin lineage evolved into a portfolio of DX solution services, infrastructure operations and maintenance support (インフラ維持管理支援), and SDTC data services. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the network as an enrichment lead. The branded domain symmetry-dimensions.com now redirects to the company's live site at symmetry-inc.co.jp. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate/marketing site (a Nuxt single-page app on Google Cloud) but no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, CLI, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface — so no machine-readable API artifacts could be harvested. This record therefore carries company identity plus a probed domain-security profile only, and remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Dvlp Medicines
providers.description: DVLP Medicines is a drug-development software company building an end-to-end, configurable platform that moves molecules from discovery to commercialization with speed. The platform pairs a single data repository for pharmaceutical assets with specialized AI agents for pharma operations, document automation, knowledge synthesis, and decision support for portfolio management. It is positioned as a software co-pilot for drug development and a marketplace connecting project leaders with investors and outsourced R&D and manufacturing vendors, targeting underserved therapeutic markets such as new antibiotics for antimicrobial resistance and rare-disease therapies. DVLP Medicines is a portfolio company of DCVC (Computational Bio & Chem), first funded in 2022. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the company publishes a marketing site but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: DwellSocial
providers.description: DwellSocial is a Techstars-backed, Chicago-area community food service that brings iconic city restaurants to suburban neighborhoods. Members browse curated restaurant offerings, place group orders for scheduled dates, and meet for a convenient neighborhood pickup to enjoy city-quality meals at home. The service also runs fundraisers for local causes and non-profits, and currently serves suburbs such as Naperville and Elmhurst. DwellSocial operates as a consumer web and mobile application; no public developer API, OpenAPI, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment (dwellsocial.com serves a JavaScript single-page app and api.dwellsocial.com returns the same marketing site rather than a machine API).

providers.name: E8 Storage Systems
providers.description: E8 Storage Systems was an Israeli enterprise storage startup that built rack-scale NVMe flash arrays, separating high-performance shared flash from compute so that data-intensive workloads could reach local-NVMe latency over the network. The company was backed by Accel and was acquired by Amazon; the acquisition was reported on 2019-07-31. E8 no longer operates as an independent vendor and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API. Its historical domain, e8storage.com, is retained defensively but does not resolve: there are no address or mail records, and DMARC aggregate reports are directed to dmarc.amazon.com. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical big-data and storage-infrastructure record with no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Earendil Robotics
providers.description: Earendil Robotics is a Y Combinator-backed defense technology company registered in England and Wales that builds AI-powered situational-awareness and counter-drone systems for tactical units. Its product line includes IVAS, an edge-AI vision-augmentation system fusing night vision, thermal imaging, and laser ranging for total-darkness operation; Aeglos, an autonomous high-speed (300+ km/h) interceptor drone for counter-UAS defense with autonomous target locking and all-weather thermal tracking; and Holo, an ultra-lightweight dual-mode tactical sight combining high-resolution thermal imaging with a fiber-optic reticle. As of this profile the company exposes only a public marketing website and a contact form, with no published developer surface, API, SDKs, documentation, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: East Range Group
providers.description: East Range Group is a team of high purity water systems and service companies serving North America. The group is dedicated to building phenomenal places to work for its employees and to building the best high purity water service company on the continent, delivering proactive customer service and deep technical expertise across the most intricate complexities of high purity water technology. Its operating companies include Atlas High Purity Filter & Water Technologies, Pure Flow High Purity Water Services, and H2O Solutions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer/API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Eatsii
providers.description: Eatsii is a Jakarta, Indonesia based foodtech startup operating a cloud kitchen platform. It runs a cloud kitchen concept that offers takeaway and delivery alongside dine-in service, and markets cloud kitchen space to F&B operators under a franchise partnership model, positioning itself as helping food and beverage companies run a more efficient kitchen in the food delivery era. The company describes itself as combining a heartfelt touch with data and business strategy, and lists 11-50 employees in Food and Beverage Services. It was surfaced through the 500 Global (500 Durians) portfolio. Eatsii publishes no developer program, public API, or technical documentation, and as of July 2026 its eatsii.com domain does not serve a live website.

providers.name: Eaze
providers.description: Eaze is a California-based cannabis marketplace and delivery platform that connects licensed dispensaries and cannabis brands with adult consumers, offering online ordering and same-day delivery of flower, edibles, vapes, and related products across the state. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in San Francisco, Eaze operates a consumer marketplace plus a technology and logistics stack for compliant retail. Backed by 500 Global and DCM Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. Eaze does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; its api.eaze.com host is an internal, bot-protected surface.

providers.name: Ebates
providers.description: Ebates is a consumer cash-back and rebate shopping platform founded in 2000 in San Francisco that pays members a percentage of their purchases back as cash when they shop through its links at thousands of partner retailers. Rakuten acquired Ebates in 2014 and rebranded the U.S. service as Rakuten Rewards in 2019; the ebates.com domain now redirects to rakuten.com. The business is a consumer-facing rewards and affiliate-commerce brand and does not operate an independent public developer API program. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: eBureau
providers.description: eBureau was a predictive analytics and big-data scoring company founded in 2004 and headquartered in St. Cloud, Minnesota, providing real-time predictive scores, identity verification, and fraud-prevention products (eScore, eIDverifier, eIDcompare) to lenders, insurers, and marketers. eBureau was acquired by TransUnion in December 2015 and its capabilities were absorbed into TransUnion's fraud and identity solutions; the ebureau.com domain remains live (behind Cloudflare) but exposes no independent public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Redpoint Ventures and enriched with a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: EchoStar
providers.description: EchoStar Corporation (Nasdaq: SATS) is a global, fully integrated communications and content delivery leader and provider of technology, spectrum, and connectivity. Through its DISH, Boost Mobile, Hughes, and EchoStar Mobile brands, EchoStar delivers satellite communications, wireless services, and IoT connectivity to consumers, enterprises, governments, and aviation customers worldwide.

providers.name: Ecobites Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Ecobites Pte. Ltd. operates Rec Rec, a Vietnamese consumer packaged-goods brand producing cricket-based snack foods marketed as high-protein, nutrient-dense alternatives to conventional snacks. Its product line spans cricket noodles (Mi Dam De), cricket puffs (Banh Phong De) in flavors such as Gochujang and Mala, and seasoned dried crickets (De Say). Products emphasize complete protein with a full amino-acid profile plus iron, zinc, magnesium, and potassium while keeping sodium low. Rec Rec is distributed through 7-Eleven, Farmers Market, Galaxy Cinema, BHD Cineplex, Naman Market, LS Place, Shopee, and TikTok Shop. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. It publishes a consumer e-commerce website but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Ecolab
providers.description: Ecolab is a Fortune 500 global leader in water, hygiene, and infection prevention solutions and services. The company helps customers in food, healthcare, hospitality, industrial, and energy markets keep their environments clean, safe, and healthy while protecting people and vital resources.

providers.name: EcoMom
providers.description: EcoMom was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead for enrichment. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating company surface behind the ecomom.com domain. The domain's nameservers are ns1/ns2.afternic.com and every request to ecomom.com issues a 307 redirect to an Afternic listing headlined "The domain name ecomom.com is for sale!" with no published price. The host serves a wildcard soft-200 parking page - arbitrary paths, including a deliberately nonsense control path, all return HTTP 200 with text/html that redirects to /lander - so the 200 status codes returned for /.well-known/security.txt, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, /.well-known/api-catalog, /.well-known/ai-plugin.json, /llms.txt and /openapi.json are parking artifacts and not real documents. The api, developer, docs and www subdomains resolve to the same two parking IPs. There is no developer portal, no documentation, no specification and no API surface to catalog, so no enrichment artifacts were written for this company.

providers.name: eCredit.com
providers.description: eCredit.com was an online trade-credit and credit-decisioning company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It no longer operates independently. The ecredit.com domain is delegated to Moody's nameservers and 301-redirects in full to Moody's trade-credit offering, where "Moody's eCredit" now exists as a platform within Moody's Trade Credit product line. Enrichment probes confirm no independent developer portal, documentation, API specification, or /.well-known surface remains on ecredit.com. Any live API capability for this product is delivered through Moody's, which is profiled separately in the network as the successor company.

providers.name: Eden Robotics
providers.description: Eden Robotics is a Y Combinator-backed robotics company building autonomous robots for industrial operations, delivered on a robots-as-a-service model that starts at roughly $10 per hour with no setup fees. The offering is positioned as plug-and-play, requiring no on-site engineers or specialized robotics hires, and is powered by the company's Theta OS platform. As of this profile the company publishes a single marketing and sales-contact website and does not expose a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this record captures the verified company identity and domain-security posture and will be upgraded if and when a developer surface is published.

providers.name: Edfa3ly
providers.description: Edfa3ly is an Egyptian cross-border e-commerce and online shopping platform that lets consumers in Egypt and the wider MENA region buy products from international retailers and marketplaces, then handles the international shipping, customs clearance, and local delivery on their behalf. It bridges shoppers to overseas stores by managing purchasing, logistics, and payment in local currency. Edfa3ly is a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; the company does not publish a public developer program or API at this time.

providers.name: EDGE Sound Research
providers.description: EDGE Sound Research is an audio technology company building intelligent audio infrastructure, as stated by its own tagline. Backed by Techstars, the company operates from edgesoundresearch.com. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API, SDK, CLI, MCP server, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI) was found on its web presence, and the site is a fully client-rendered Next.js application. This profile captures the company's identity and web/domain security posture within the API Evangelist network pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: EdgeSpring
providers.description: EdgeSpring is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins, lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Edgix
providers.description: Edgix (Edgix Corporation) is a former, exited Battery Ventures portfolio company surfaced from Battery's public list-of-all-companies page and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment stub. Battery lists the investment as exited (marked with an asterisk on their all-companies list), and the portfolio harvest recorded is_api_provider: false. No artifacts were produced this round because there is nothing published to search, generate, or derive against without fabrication. This record is retained as a verified-defunct lead so future pipeline runs can skip it rather than re-probe.

providers.name: Edia
providers.description: Edia is an AI platform for K-12 school districts focused on improving student outcomes. Its products span AI math tutoring (reported 8-23% score improvements), attendance intervention to reduce chronic absenteeism (up to 30% reduction), and District Intelligence analytics that consolidate data from student information systems (SIS), learning management systems (LMS), behavior, and wellness sources into a single view for educators and administrators. Edia reports serving 200+ districts and 500K+ students. The company is backed by Felicis and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile. Edia does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or API specification, so this profile carries only verifiable company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: edisn.ai

providers.name: Edmodo
providers.description: Edmodo was an education technology company that operated a K-12 social learning network and learning management platform connecting teachers, students, and parents, and at its peak ran a developer platform and app store for third-party education apps. It was acquired by NetDragon in 2018 and the service was shut down in September 2022. Surfaced as a portfolio company of union-square-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the edmodo.com domain resolves only to a parked lander page and exposes no live developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: eduFire
providers.description: eduFire was an online education startup surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-19 found that the company's primary domain, edufire.com, no longer resolves (no DNS A or NS records), indicating the company is defunct. No live developer portal, API surface, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or any other artifact could be located to enrich, so this profile remains an identity-only stub.

providers.name: Edukart
providers.description: EduKart was an Indian online education startup, backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), that sold certificate, diploma and degree courses from partner universities and training institutes to Indian learners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company is now defunct — repeated probes of edukart.com find a parked hosting placeholder rather than a live business, and no developer, API, documentation or SDK surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: EduPristine
providers.description: EduPristine is a Mumbai-based finance, accounting, and analytics training institute founded in 2008, offering classroom and online certification-prep and professional up-skilling programs. Its catalog spans financial modeling, CFA, FRM, ACCA, US CPA and US CMA, business analytics and data science, digital marketing, financial accounting (Big 4 aligned), and healthcare/medical coding. EduPristine runs training centers across India alongside self-paced and instructor-led online courses, and is part of Adtalem Global Education. Sector: edtech. No public developer API or documented API surface was found during enrichment; the corporate website sits behind a WAF that blocks automated discovery of a well-known or developer surface.

providers.name: eEye Digital Security
providers.description: eEye Digital Security was an American cybersecurity company and an early pioneer of commercial vulnerability management and vulnerability research. BeyondTrust acquired eEye Digital Security in May 2012, and the company no longer operates as an independent entity or brand. Its former domain, eeye.com, now resolves to BeyondTrust infrastructure — the www host no longer presents a valid TLS certificate, and the domain's DMARC reporting addresses point at beyondtrust.com. eEye publishes no developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, package, or discovery surface of its own; the successor product surface, including the BeyondTrust Password Safe API, is catalogued in the API Evangelist network under the beyondtrust profile. This record is retained as a historical company entry and an acquisition pointer rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Effa
providers.description: Effa is a sustainable consumer goods company that makes the world's first 100% recyclable paper toothbrush, a disposable, plastic-free alternative to conventional plastic toothbrushes aimed at hotels, airlines, and retail consumers. Founded in Ukraine by Dasha and Ilya Kichuk and headquartered in San Francisco, California, the company supplies eco-friendly personal care and amenity products to hospitality and travel clients, with reported customers including Netflix and Radisson. Effa is backed by 500 Global and Startup Wise Guys. Effa does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Efficient Frontier
providers.description: Efficient Frontier was a digital advertising optimization and search marketing company founded in 2002 that applied algorithmic, finance-inspired bid optimization to manage over $1 billion in annual marketing spend across search, display, and social (notably Facebook ad buying) for enterprise clients such as Discover, Travelodge, and Match.com. Adobe acquired the company in late 2011 (announced November 30, 2011; completed January 2012) and folded its multi-channel ad forecasting, execution, and optimization capabilities into the Adobe Digital Marketing / Advertising Cloud. The efrontier.com domain now redirects to adobe.com and the company has no independent website, developer portal, or public API.

providers.name: Eggrock
providers.description: Eggrock (Eggrock Modular Solutions; legally Innovative Modular Pre-Fabrication LLC) is a North American manufacturer of prefabricated "bathroom-in-a-box" pods — complete, custom, ready-to-install bathrooms built off-site using BIM-driven design and lean manufacturing for hotels, hospitals, dormitories, military barracks, and other multi-unit construction projects. Off-site fabrication compresses construction schedules and improves quality versus building bathrooms on site. In 2012 Eggrock licensed exclusive North American manufacturing and distribution to Oldcastle Precast. It is a construction / building-products manufacturer with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: eigencomm
providers.description: Shanghai Eigencomm Technology Co., Ltd. is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2017 and headquartered in the Zhangjiang district of Shanghai, China, dedicated to the research, design, and sale of cellular Internet of Things (IoT) communication chipsets and their supporting software. Eigencomm has mass-produced NB-IoT and Cat.1bis chip series that power smart meters, smart security, mobile payment, shared devices, asset trackers, charging piles, wearables, smart firefighting, and smart home appliances, and is developing 5G silicon. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund II, Qiming Venture Partners, and others, having raised roughly USD 171M across multiple rounds. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it publishes no public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Eigentech
providers.description: Eigentech (eigentech.ai) is an artificial intelligence technology company, reported to have been founded around 2016 and headquartered in Hangzhou, China, that applies AI and machine learning to business and industrial domains. Its platform is positioned to help enterprises improve operational efficiency, optimize workflows, and strengthen data-driven decision-making by embedding AI into existing business processes. Eigentech is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for the enrichment pipeline. NOTE - as of the latest enrichment pass the company website (https://eigentech.ai) does not resolve and no public developer, documentation, or API surface could be reached, so no API artifacts could be harvested without fabrication.

providers.name: Eka Robotics
providers.description: Eka Robotics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts robotics-AI company founded in 2025 that is building intelligence for the physical world in its native language: force. Its Vision-Force-Action (VFA) model combines vision, force sensing, and action to give robots generality, performance, and safety for close human-robot interaction. The team pioneers self-supervised robot learning, large-scale robot learning, world models, reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer, drawing talent from MIT, Berkeley, Harvard, DeepMind, and Boston Dynamics. Co-founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal (Improbable AI Lab), the company is an early-stage research-and-hardware venture and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with the company's public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Elastica
providers.description: Elastica was a Silicon Valley cloud security startup that pioneered the Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) category, using data science and machine learning to give enterprises visibility into and control over Shadow IT and sanctioned SaaS applications. Its CloudSOC platform combined an API-based control mode (connecting directly to cloud apps such as Office 365, Box, Salesforce, and Google Workspace) with an inline gateway mode for data-loss-prevention, threat detection, and compliance. Backed by Mayfield, Pelion Venture Partners, and Third Point Ventures, Elastica was acquired by Blue Coat Systems for $280 million in November 2015; Blue Coat (with Elastica and Perspecsys) was in turn acquired by Symantec in 2016, where the technology became the Symantec CloudSOC CASB, later part of Broadcom's enterprise security portfolio. Elastica no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no active public developer surface, API, or SDK.

providers.name: Elastifile
providers.description: Elastifile was an enterprise cloud file-storage company founded in 2013 in Tel Aviv, Israel. It built a software-defined, scale-out distributed file system (the Elastifile Cloud File System / ECFS) that delivered elastic, high-performance NFS-compatible shared storage for enterprise-grade applications running at scale in the public cloud, with the ability to scale capacity out or in on demand. Backed by Battery Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners (among others), Elastifile was acquired by Google Cloud in August 2019 (reported at roughly $200M) and its technology was folded into Google Cloud Filestore, powering the Filestore High Scale / Enterprise tiers. Elastifile no longer operates as an independent company or brand: elastifile.com redirects to Google Cloud Filestore, and there is no standalone Elastifile developer portal, API, or SDK surface to enrich.

providers.name: Element AI
providers.description: Element AI was a Montreal, Quebec-based artificial intelligence company founded in 2016 by Jean-Francois Gagne, Yoshua Bengio, Nicolas Chapados, Philippe Beaudoin, Anne Martel, and Jean-Sebastien Cournoyer. It operated as an AI systems integrator and professional-services firm with the mission of putting advanced AI capabilities - natural language processing, computer vision, document intelligence, and conversational AI - in reach of traditional enterprises. After raising roughly US$102M plus Canadian government funding and reaching an estimated US$600-700M valuation in 2019, the company ran short of runway and was acquired by ServiceNow (announced November 30, 2020; closed January 8, 2021 for approximately US$230M). Its research group became ServiceNow Research and its former domain now redirects there. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no standalone public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Elephint
providers.description: Elephint is an electronics-photonics integration company building integrated photonic systems-on-a-chip (SoC) technologies. Its focus areas span photonic integrated circuits, silicon photonics, free-space optical communication, fiber optics, optical amplifiers, coherent beam combining, wavefront control, photonic signal processing, photonic computing, and artificial intelligence. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, Elephint is a deep-tech hardware company that presently publishes only a company website (https://elephint.ai) and does not expose a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Elevation Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Elevation Pharmaceuticals was a San Diego specialty pharmaceutical company founded in 2008 by Cam Garner, Bill Gerhart, and Ahmet Tutuncu to develop next-generation aerosol/inhalation therapies for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It raised a $30 million Series A in 2010 backed by Canaan Partners, TPG Growth, Care Capital, and Mesa Verde Venture Partners, and was acquired by Sunovion Pharmaceuticals in August 2012. The company is no longer independently operating; its domain now resolves to Sunovion nameservers and it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio record.

providers.name: Elite Business Ventures
providers.description: Elite Business Ventures, LLC (EBV, ebvinc.com) is a San Diego-based workplace compliance company founded in 2005 that has helped over one million businesses stay compliant with federal and state labor laws and workplace safety regulations. It operates through two primary brands: PosterElite, a white-label labor-law-poster compliance platform embedded by HR, payroll, HCM, PEO, and workforce-management providers under their own brand; and Osha4Less.com, an ecommerce store of affordable OSHA and labor-law compliance products for small businesses. EBV is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. The company exposes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or documentation surface — partner integration is handled through direct white-label / reseller arrangements rather than a self-service developer program.

providers.name: Elmawkaa
providers.description: Elmawkaa (الموقع) is an Egyptian B2B online marketplace that digitizes construction-materials procurement. Founded in Cairo in 2017 by Ebrahem Anwar, Mahmoud Habib, and Mohamed Thabet, the platform lets construction companies request and compare competitive supplier quotations for materials such as cement, steel, and gypsum board, using proprietary matching algorithms to replace slow, manual bidding with a documented, automated process. A 500 Startups (500 Global) accelerator graduate that raised a seed round led by Flat6Labs with Oqal and other regional backers, Elmawkaa was fully acquired by Saudi PropTech / real-estate-appraisal platform Ayen in a seven-figure deal in October 2024, with its marketplace folded into Ayen's services. Elmawkaa publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation, and its standalone domain (elmawkaa.com) no longer resolves following the acquisition.

providers.name: EmojiHub
providers.description: Get emojis by categories and groups

providers.name: Encore Music Technologies
providers.description: Encore Music Technologies, Inc. ("Encore") is a consumer live-music technology company based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2020 by Ian Edelman, Jonathan Gray, and recording artist Kid Cudi. Its mobile app lets artists perform live inside custom augmented-reality environments directly from a phone while fans join, react, and pay artists in real time through gamified microtransactions such as a ten-cent "clap." The company raised a $9M seed round led by Battery Ventures in February 2022, with participation from 468 Capital, Kayak Ventures, Parade Ventures, and others. Encore ships consumer iOS and Android apps rather than a public developer platform; as of this pass it exposes no documented public API, and its marketing website (clapforencore.com) does not currently resolve to a live server.

providers.name: Endeavor
providers.description: Endeavor was a global sports and entertainment company representing talent and owning and operating events, with subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group. This repository tracks Endeavor as a corporate entity; no public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Endeavor Group Holdings
providers.description: Endeavor Group Holdings was a global sports and entertainment company that represented talent, owned and operated events, and provided licensing, marketing, and media services through subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent representation, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group, which now operates WME, 160over90, Pantheon Media Group, and IMG Licensing. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Endo International
providers.description: Endo International was a specialty pharmaceutical company best known for Xiaflex (collagenase clostridium histolyticum), branded urology and orthopedic products, and a large sterile-injectables and generics business (Par Pharmaceutical). Endo filed Chapter 11 in August 2022 amid mass opioid litigation tied to its legacy Opana ER franchise, and emerged in April 2024 as the private company Endo, Inc., owned by its former creditors. On July 31, 2025, Endo combined with Mallinckrodt; the merged group then separated in November 2025 into two independent companies — Keenova Therapeutics (specialty branded therapeutics, including the former Endo Xiaflex/urology/orthopedics portfolio and Mallinckrodt specialty brands) and Par Health (generics, sterile injectables, and pharmaceutical Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients manufacturing). Endo no longer operates as a standalone public-facing pharmaceutical company. There is no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or technology API surface associated with Endo, the post-emergence Endo Inc, Keenova Therapeutics, or Par Health. Any references to "API" on the successor companies' sites refer to pharmaceutical Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, not software application programming interfaces.

providers.name: Energy Micro
providers.description: Energy Micro was a Norwegian fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2007 and headquartered in Oslo, best known for its EFM32 "Gecko" family of energy-friendly 32-bit ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers and the EFR radio products targeting low-power embedded and IoT applications. The company was acquired by Silicon Labs in 2013 and fully absorbed into that company's product lines; its former energymicro.com domain now redirects to silabs.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no independent, first-party API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface for Energy Micro as a standalone entity — the developer tooling for its EFM32 line lives under Silicon Labs today.

providers.name: English Central
providers.description: English Central is an online English language learning platform that combines a large library of authentic video content with speech-recognition-driven pronunciation practice, adaptive vocabulary and quiz tools, and live one-on-one lessons with tutors. It serves individual learners as well as schools, universities, and enterprise/partner programs (including regional partners in Japan and elsewhere). Backed by GV (Google Ventures), it operates in the consumer education / EdTech sector. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment; partner integrations appear to be handled privately.

providers.name: Engram
providers.description: Engram is an early-stage AI company building models that learn from an organization's unique context and data, with the pitch that they can match or beat frontier models while using only 1%-10% of the tokens ("AI has learned the world. Now it should learn yours."). Positioned as a learned AI memory layer and backed by Kleiner Perkins, Engram is at a pre-product / research stage: as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, documentation, pricing, blog, sign-up, or GitHub organization. This profile captures the company's public identity only; there is no developer or API surface available to enrich.

providers.name: Enhanced Radar
providers.description: Enhanced Radar is a San Francisco-based applied AI company building intelligent systems for aviation, the world's most complex transportation domain. Its work centers on pilot-controller communications, where the company owns the full pipeline from data collection through in-house labeling and quality assurance to produce high-quality aviation AI training datasets. Products include Pattern, an aviation operational intelligence platform; ATC.com, a live air traffic control radio service; and Y4, an aviation understanding model announced in February 2026. Enhanced Radar has demonstrated real-time detection of runway incursion risks and raised $7 million in May 2026. It is backed by DCVC and Initialized Capital. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Enjoy Technologies
providers.description: Enjoy Technology (Enjoy Technologies) was a "commerce at home" mobile-retail startup founded in 2014 by Ron Johnson, the former Apple senior vice president of retail and JCPenney CEO, and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company brought the retail store experience to customers' homes, dispatching mobile experts to deliver, set up, and demonstrate consumer electronics on behalf of partners such as carriers and device makers. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Oak Investment Partners, and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Enjoy went public via SPAC in 2021 and declared bankruptcy in 2022, with its assets subsequently acquired. Enjoy never operated a public developer program or API; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: EnjoyHQ
providers.description: EnjoyHQ was a centralized user-research and customer-feedback repository — a single source of truth where product and UX teams stored, tagged, searched, and analyzed qualitative and quantitative research (interviews, surveys, support tickets, NPS scores, and app-store reviews). Backed by Point Nine Capital, it was acquired by UserTesting in 2021 and folded into the UserTesting Human Insight Platform. Its brand domain getenjoyhq.com now issues a permanent (HTTP 308) redirect to usertesting.com/platform/enjoyhq, and EnjoyHQ no longer operates an independent developer, documentation, or API surface.

providers.name: Enpirion
providers.description: Enpirion was a fabless semiconductor company specializing in high-frequency power-management integrated circuits, best known for its PowerSoC family of integrated DC-DC converters that combined the controller, MOSFETs, and inductor in a single package for point-of-load power conversion in networking, computing, and industrial systems. The company was acquired by Altera in 2013 and subsequently absorbed into Intel with Altera in 2015; the Enpirion brand and its enpirion.com developer/product site are now defunct. It never operated a public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK program, so this record is retained as a company identity stub rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Ensilo
providers.description: enSilo was an endpoint-security company founded in 2014 (San Francisco and Herzliya, Israel) that delivered automated endpoint detection and response (EDR), real-time post-infection protection, and data-exfiltration prevention in a single agent. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and other investors, enSilo was acquired by Fortinet in October 2019 and its technology was folded into the FortiEDR product line. The independent enSilo brand, developer surface, and public API no longer exist; the ensilo.com domain now redirects to Fortinet's site. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company lead and carries no live API artifacts.

providers.name: Entergy
providers.description: Entergy Corporation is an integrated energy company headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, providing electricity to more than 3 million utility customers across Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Texas. The company operates power generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure including nuclear, renewable, and hydroelectric resources. While Entergy does not publish a public developer API portal, it operates customer-facing digital tools (myEntergy account portal, outage map, energy efficiency toolkit) that interact with internal systems via private APIs.

providers.name: Enuma, Inc.
providers.description: Enuma, Inc. is a Berkeley, California educational technology company that builds award-winning, self-guided digital learning apps for young children, including the Todo Math series, Todo Classroom, and the Kitkit School / Enuma Global program. Founded by Sooinn Lee and Gunho Lee, Enuma designs research-based, game-like early literacy and numeracy experiences that work for all learners, including children with special needs and those in low-resource settings. The company co-won the $10M Global Learning XPRIZE for its open-source Kitkit School tablet curriculum. Enuma is a consumer and classroom education company that ships mobile applications through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or event surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with verified company identity by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Envariant
providers.description: Envariant is building the control layer for foundation models — an AI interpretability SDK that lets teams inspect, steer, and control model behavior. The SDK exposes a compact set of primitives: detect and causally trace behaviors like hallucinations or invariant violations, reason inductively and steer outputs programmatically, extract human-readable domain principles, and synthesize targeted edge cases — moving verification upstream, directly into the model's latent space, with no bespoke engineering required. Envariant is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in San Francisco. The SDK is in pre-release beta, so no public API, OpenAPI, or developer documentation is available yet; this profile captures the company identity ahead of a public developer surface.

providers.name: Enviri (formerly Harsco)
providers.description: Enviri Corporation, formerly known as Harsco Corporation, is a trusted global leader in environmental solutions, developing and refining methods of recycling and beneficial reuse for industrial customers. Enviri operates through three divisions: Clean Earth (hazardous waste management and recycling), Harsco Environmental (services to the global steel industry), and Harsco Rail (rail-track maintenance equipment and services). Enviri does not currently publish a public developer portal or open APIs.

providers.name: Eo Computer
providers.description: Eo Computer (EO, Inc.) was an early-1990s hardtech company, backed by Kleiner Perkins, that built the EO Personal Communicator - a pen-based tablet computer running GO Corporation's PenPoint operating system. AT&T became the principal backer and later shut the company down in 1994. The company is defunct: it has no website, developer program, public API, SDKs, or any published developer surface, so there is nothing for the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline to search, generate, or derive. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record of a dead, non-API hardware company.

providers.name: Ephemeral
providers.description: Ephemeral is a body-art company that makes semi-permanent, made-to-fade tattoos using a proprietary vegan, medical-grade polymer ink engineered to fade from the skin over roughly one to two years. Backed by Canaan Partners, the company sells direct-to-consumer through certified partner tattoo artists in select cities and business-to-business by supplying its Generation-3 ink to professional artists. It is a consumer and physical-product business, not a technology or API provider - as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: ePIT
providers.description: ePIT (listed by Battery Ventures as "ePIT, Inc.") is a former Battery Ventures portfolio company that appears on the firm's public list-of-all-companies page marked as exited. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no current public web presence for the company: no corporate website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. The obvious candidate domains are not operated by the company — epit.com returns a parked "this domain may be for sale" page (HTTP 200) and epit.net redirects to a Saw.com domain-broker listing (HTTP 403 without a browser user agent). Web search returned no company profile, industry, headquarters, or acquisition record. This profile is retained as an honest, no-API-surface record of a Battery Ventures portfolio lead rather than as an active API provider, and carries no artifacts because none exist to harvest.

providers.name: EQL Games
providers.description: EQL Games is a Louisville, Kentucky based lottery-industry technology company that operates as an original game studio, third-party content aggregator, and boutique licensor for the global iLottery market. Its iLottery Marketplace aggregates a catalog of 300+ games from 24 partner studios behind a single integration point for lottery operators, while its EQL Labs innovation division builds original instant-win and eInstant titles that fold in licensed intellectual property and live sports. The company also represents brands across lottery verticals (instant scratch and eInstant) and reports serving 8 lottery clients. EQL Games was surfaced through Bullpen Capital's portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing and corporate web presence but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: EquiLibre
providers.description: EquiLibre Technologies is a Prague-based frontier AI trading research lab building self-learning reinforcement-learning agents that trade equities autonomously across the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Founded by ex-DeepMind researchers Martin Schmid, Matej Moravcik, and Rudolf Kadlec — the trio behind the DeepStack poker AI — the company applies the same game-solving and continual-learning techniques to financial markets, with its agents trading billions of dollars daily in partnership with quantitative firm Tower Research Capital. In 2026 EquiLibre raised a Series A led by Creandum at a reported ~EUR 438M / $500M+ valuation. It operates as a proprietary trading and research lab and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: EraDrive
providers.description: EraDrive is a space technology company building compact, AI-powered self-driving modules that give spacecraft onboard autonomy — vision-based navigation, control, collision avoidance, and situational awareness computed at the edge. A Stanford Space Rendezvous Laboratory (SLAB) spinoff founded by Sumant Sharma (CEO), Justin Kruger (CTO), and Prof. Simone D'Amico (CSO), EraDrive integrates flight-proven autonomy software with existing satellite infrastructure for space traffic management, on-orbit servicing and logistics, and advanced remote sensing across commercial and defense missions. The company closed an oversubscribed $5.3M seed round in December 2025, co-led by Haystack Ventures with participation from Point Nine, Harpoon Ventures, Brave Capital, 2100 VC, and Entropy Industrial Capital. As an early-stage hardware/software company, EraDrive currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Escher Reality
providers.description: Escher Reality was an augmented reality and computer vision startup founded in 2016 by Ross Finman (CEO) and Diana Hu (CTO), with roots in the MIT Sandbox program. It built cloud backend services for cross-platform, persistent, multi-user mobile AR — shared experiences that neither Apple ARKit nor Google ARCore offered at the time — letting multiple users interact with the same virtual objects anchored to the real world. The company raised roughly $3 million and was based in Sunnyvale, California. In February 2018 Escher Reality was acquired by Niantic (creator of Pokemon GO); its team and technology were folded into the Niantic Real World Platform (now Lightship), and the standalone company and its developer/SDK offering were discontinued. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record; there is no independent, active API or developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: ESPL
providers.description: ESPL (Esports Players League) is a Singapore-headquartered global esports tournament network and platform, founded in 2019, building an open, grassroots-focused ecosystem for amateur competitive gaming. It runs ESPL-branded online and on-ground tournaments across Asia, Europe, and the Americas with a mobile-first focus alongside PC and console titles, operated from its Singapore headquarters with regional offices in Cologne and Los Angeles. ESPL is a portfolio company of 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), which led its seed round in 2020. As of this enrichment pass ESPL publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface, and its espl.co domain did not resolve (DNS SERVFAIL) at probe time; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: EST
providers.description: EST (EST Media) is a Los Angeles-based media holding company founded by Jaeson Ma and Eric Tu that amplifies Asian stories and talent for global audiences. It operates three divisions: EST Studios, which develops, finances, produces, and sells Asian film and television projects; Eastern Standard Times, a Gen Z digital video platform sharing untold stories from Asia and its diaspora; and Established, a content studio partnering with global brands on advertising campaigns, influencer collaborations, commercials, and experiential events. EST Media is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile carries company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Estamp
providers.description: E-Stamp Corporation (eStamp) was a dot-com era Internet-postage company, a Canaan Partners seed-stage portfolio company that competed with Stamps.com to let users buy and print official U.S. Postal Service postage online. The company is defunct: on April 30, 2001 Stamps.com acquired E-Stamp's name, 31 Internet-postage patents, and the estamp.com domain, which today 301-redirects to stamps.com. There is no live company, product, developer portal, or API surface to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Ethereal Exploration Guild
providers.description: Ethereal Exploration Guild (EtherealX) is an Indian spacetech company founded in 2022 in Bengaluru by Manu J. Nair, Prashant Sharma, and Shubhayu Sardar, building fully reusable medium-lift launch vehicles. Its lead product, the Razor Crest Mk-1 (RCM1), targets roughly 25 tons to low Earth orbit with high launch cadence, up to 16 orbit insertions per flight, and 72-96 hour turnaround. The company has manufactured its 80kN reusable upper-stage engine (Pegasus) using a proprietary Full Flow Segregated Cooling Cycle (FFSCC) and operates a large private rocket testing facility in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu. EtherealX has raised on the order of $26M across multiple rounds, including a Series A in December 2025. The company offers launch services rather than any developer-facing API or platform.

providers.name: Ethplorer
providers.description: Ethereum tokens, balances, addresses, history of transactions, contracts, and custom structures

providers.name: EV3
providers.description: Escape Velocity (EV3) is an early-stage crypto and web3 venture capital firm based in New York, co-founded by Mahesh Ramakrishnan and Salvador Gala, that backs founders building frontier-technology companies across programmable money, programmable molecules, and programmable intelligence. EV3 writes early-stage checks and concentrates on crypto-enabled and decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN) businesses spanning advertising and attention, credit and liquidity, machine maps, and energy and bandwidth. Its funds have drawn backing from investors including Multicoin Capital. EV3 is an investment firm rather than a product company and publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Eve Com
providers.description: Eve.com was a dot-com era e-commerce retailer of prestige beauty and personal care products, founded in 1998 by Mariam Naficy and Varsha Rao. It raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners (1999) and reached a Series B before being acquired by Idealab in 2000, after which the business ceased independent operations. It is retained in the API Evangelist network only as a historical Lightspeed portfolio lead; it published no developer program, API, SDKs, or documentation. The eve.com domain is today operated by an unrelated entity (CCP Games / the EVE Online game universe) and is not a surface for this company, so no live API or developer artifacts can be harvested for it.

providers.name: Everdream
providers.description: Everdream Corporation was an on-demand desktop and IT asset management SaaS provider founded in 1998 and headquartered in Fremont, California. It offered hosted remote management, monitoring, and security services that gave organizations visibility into their hardware and software assets over the internet. Backed by Canaan Partners and other venture investors, Everdream was acquired by Dell in December 2007 and folded into Dell's managed-services offerings. The company is defunct; the everdream.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, and there is no active public API, developer portal, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Everest
providers.description: Everest is an early-stage Y Combinator (Fall 2025 / F25) startup based in San Francisco building agent-ready technical support for developer tools. Its premise is that a growing share of a devtool's users will be coding agents rather than humans, and Everest helps devtool companies sell to and support those coding agents with instant technical support. The company was founded in 2026 by co-founders Yolanda Cao and Spencer McKee. As of this profile Everest operates a single marketing landing page (everestagi.com) with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or other developer surface yet published; this record is maintained as a lead for the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: eVestment Alliance
providers.description: eVestment Alliance is an institutional investment data, analytics, and market-intelligence platform founded in 2000 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. Institutional asset managers report performance, holdings, and firm data into the platform, while investment consultants, asset owners, and allocators use it to research, screen, and compare managers, funds, and strategies across traditional and alternative asset classes. eVestment was acquired by Nasdaq in 2017 and is now delivered as part of Nasdaq's investment-intelligence solutions; its primary website redirects to nasdaq.com/solutions/evestment/. Originally backed by Insight Partners, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Evident.io
providers.description: Evident.io was a cloud security posture management company, founded in 2013, best known for the Evident Security Platform (ESP) — an agentless SaaS service that continuously monitored Amazon Web Services (and later Microsoft Azure) accounts for security misconfigurations, compliance drift, and risk across services like IAM, S3, EC2, and CloudTrail. ESP scored findings against frameworks such as CIS Benchmarks, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2, and exposed its analysis programmatically through a REST API so teams could automate remediation and wire results into their DevSecOps pipelines. Palo Alto Networks acquired Evident.io in March 2018 for roughly $300M and folded the technology into what became Prisma Cloud. The standalone evident.io product, developer portal, and API have been retired; the domain is now defensively held with no live website or API surface. This record is retained for historical/network-graph completeness — there is no live API to enrich.

providers.name: Evident.io (Palo Alto Networks)
providers.description: Evident.io was a cloud security posture management (CSPM) company whose Evident Security Platform (ESP) continuously monitored AWS and other public-cloud accounts for misconfigurations and compliance drift via an agentless, API-driven control engine. Palo Alto Networks acquired Evident.io in March 2018 and folded the ESP technology into its Prisma Cloud offering; the standalone evident.io brand, website, and ESP API have since been retired. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a security-sector lead.

providers.name: Evolv Technology
providers.description: Evolv Technologies Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: EVLV), headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, builds AI-based touchless security screening systems used to detect concealed weapons at venues, schools, hospitals, workplaces, and stadiums. Its flagship Evolv Express walk-through system uses sensor fusion and machine learning to screen people at high throughput without requiring them to stop, empty pockets, or remove bags, and the companion Evolv Insights analytics product reports on screening volume, alert rates, and operational performance. Evolv Technology is a portfolio company of DCVC and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDK, MCP server, or open developer portal; its public web presence is served behind bot protection and its status surface is gated behind SSO.

providers.name: Exact Target
providers.description: ExactTarget was a digital marketing and email-marketing automation SaaS company founded in 2000 in Indianapolis, Indiana. It built the Fuel developer platform and Interactive Marketing Hub for email, mobile, and social campaign automation, went public on the NYSE (ticker ET) in March 2012, and was acquired by Salesforce in December 2013 for approximately 2.5 billion dollars. ExactTarget became the foundation of Salesforce Marketing Cloud; the exacttarget.com domain now redirects to the Salesforce Marketing Cloud email-marketing product and the former developer.exacttarget.com Fuel/Code@ API platform (REST and SOAP APIs) has been retired and folded into the Salesforce Marketing Cloud developer surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/acquired-company record.

providers.name: Excite@Home
providers.description: Excite@Home (At Home Corporation) was a broadband cable-internet provider and web-portal company formed when the @Home Network merged with the Excite web portal in 1999. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, it delivered high-speed residential internet over cable partners and operated the Excite consumer portal, before filing for bankruptcy and ceasing operations in 2001.
