It is a defunct pre-API-era consumer company surfaced from a venture portfolio; it publishes no developer platform, OpenAPI, or live API surface, so this profile remains an identity-only stub with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Expanse
providers.description: Expanse (originally founded as Qadium) was a cybersecurity company specializing in internet attack surface management, continuously discovering and monitoring an organization's internet-connected assets to find exposures and unmanaged risk. The company was backed by IVP, Susa Ventures, and Y Combinator, and was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in 2020. Its technology now ships as Cortex Xpanse, part of the Palo Alto Networks Cortex platform, and the expanse.co domain 301-redirects to the Cortex Xpanse product page. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network; the company no longer operates an independent developer program or public API surface.

providers.name: Expeditors International of Washington
providers.description: Expeditors International is a global logistics company offering freight forwarding, customs brokerage, supply chain management, warehousing, and other related logistics services. As of this update no public developer portal or openly-published APIs were located; integrations are typically delivered via private partner connectivity (EDI/B2B) and account-managed channels.

providers.name: Eyeview
providers.description: Eyeview (Eyeview Digital) was a New York-based personalized and programmatic video advertising technology company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - its primary domain (eyeviewdigital.com) is registered on AWS nameservers but serves no website (no DNS A record) and no email (no MX record), and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or public GitHub spec surface could be located. No API artifacts could be harvested; this remains a defunct-company stub.

providers.name: Fable Therapeutics
providers.description: Fable Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company developing protein-engineered biologics for obesity and metabolic disease. Its lead candidate, FBL-140, is an infrequently dosed monoclonal antibody antagonizing the activin receptor type II (ActR2) pathway to reduce body weight and fat while preserving lean muscle mass and improving cardiometabolic health, with clinical trials expected to begin in early 2027. The company is also advancing a combination therapy pairing ActR2 antagonism with an incretin mimetic. Fable Therapeutics is a deep-tech portfolio company backed by DCVC. It operates as a traditional drug-development company and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or technical platform.

providers.name: Fabraix
providers.description: Fabraix builds red-teaming AI agents that continuously find security vulnerabilities in customer-facing AI systems. Its flagship product, Nyx, autonomously discovers exploits across chat, voice, browser, and coding agents without needing source-code access, drawing on a library of more than 10,000 jailbreaks and adaptive attack strategies that pursue promising approaches across hundreds of interactions. Fabraix also created ACE (Adversarial Cost to Exploit), a game-theoretic benchmark that measures AI security by the cost of a successful attack, enabling continuous, lower-cost vulnerability testing that re-assesses systems with each update. Fabraix is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; no public API, developer documentation, or machine-readable surface has been published by Fabraix at this time.

providers.name: Facet
providers.description: Facet was a consumer AI image-editing and creative tool, backed by Accel and originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass, its domain facet.ai (HTTP) 301-redirects to www.vsco.co/features/canvas ("VSCO Canvas | AI Mood Board Maker for Photographers"), indicating the product has been acquired by / absorbed into VSCO. Facet exposes no independent developer platform, public API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface of its own; its HTTPS endpoint is unreachable.

providers.name: Fact Base Inc.
providers.description: Fact Base Inc. (株式会社Fact Base) is a Japanese manufacturing-technology company on a mission to make manufacturing seamless by driving the digitization of small and mid-sized factories (町工場). Its corporate site presents the company mission and vision for connecting Japan's fragmented small-factory manufacturing base through digital tooling. Surfaced through the API Evangelist network as an Insight Partners portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass no public developer program, API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation is published on the corporate domain.

providers.name: Faircraft
providers.description: Faircraft is a biotechnology company creating a new class of cultivated materials, starting with real leather grown in the lab from animal cells rather than raised on farms. Using cell biology and protein engineering, it produces genuine leather (product lines FCL_001 through FCL_006) with the look, feel, and performance of traditional hides but with a lower environmental footprint and no animal farming, and customizable properties for fashion, automotive, and luxury brands. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Faircraft is a materials-science company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Fakespot
providers.description: Fakespot was an AI-powered fake-review detection service, founded in 2016, that graded the trustworthiness of product reviews on Amazon and other online marketplaces through a browser extension, mobile apps, and website. Mozilla acquired Fakespot in 2023 and integrated its technology into Firefox as the Review Checker. Mozilla discontinued the product in 2025 — the Firefox Review Checker on June 10, 2025 and the Fakespot browser extension, mobile apps, and website on July 1, 2025 — and fakespot.com now redirects to a Mozilla announcement. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface exists; this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.

providers.name: FamilyLeaf
providers.description: FamilyLeaf was a private social network for families, launched in 2012 and marketed as "a place to share your life with your family" — a closed, invite-based space for sharing photos and updates among relatives rather than a public feed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-20 found no operating company: familyleaf.com is registered (GoDaddy, registry expiry 2027-03-09) but delegated to no nameservers at all, so it has no A record, no mail, no website and no API surface. The last live archived snapshot of the product (2014) carries a banner announcing that FamilyLeaf had become part of Origami; by the 2023 archived snapshot the domain was serving a registrar parking page. There is no developer portal, documentation, SDK, GitHub organization, or any other API artifact to capture. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Fan Controlled Football
providers.description: Fan Controlled Football (FCF) was a professional indoor American football league in which fans voted on play calls in real time through a mobile app, playing a fast, 7-on-7 format staged at Pullman Yards in Atlanta and streamed to social and live-video audiences. The league drew high-profile athlete and celebrity team owners and investors and positioned itself as a fan-interactive, tech-driven sports and entertainment property. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. FCF paused operations and its public web presence (fcf.io) no longer serves a live site, so it currently exposes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface.

providers.name: Fanatics
providers.description: Fanatics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of softbank-vision-fund, thrive-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Fanatics Holdings
providers.description: Fanatics Holdings, Inc. is a global digital sports platform that connects fans with the teams, leagues, players, and events they love. Founded in 2011 and led by Michael Rubin, the company operates across several business segments: Fanatics Commerce (licensed sports merchandise, e-commerce, and manufacturing), Fanatics Collectibles (trading cards and memorabilia, including Topps), and Fanatics Betting & Gaming (the Fanatics Sportsbook and online casino). It has no public developer API program or published API specification; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile surfaced from a16z's venture portfolio.

providers.name: Fanbridge
providers.description: FanBridge was an email and SMS marketing platform for musicians, artists, bands, and creators, letting them grow and message their fan mailing lists, run newsletters, and capture subscribers from shows and social channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-19) confirmed FanBridge is defunct - it was acquired by Kit (formerly ConvertKit) and ceased operations on April 11, 2022, with active accounts migrated to the Kit platform. The domain fanbridge.com now 302-redirects to kit.com/fanbridge. There is no standalone FanBridge developer API, documentation, SDK, or event surface; the developer docs linked from the destination site belong to Kit, not FanBridge.

providers.name: FangTek
providers.description: FangTek (Shanghai Fangtek Electronics Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Shanghai. It designs highly integrated analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits for mobile phones, portable devices and consumer electronics, with a product line spanning audio power amplifiers, voice and audio processing, image processing, LED drivers, power management ICs, analog switches and DC boost converters. Qiming Venture Partners lists FangTek in its portfolio as "a leading provider of highly integrated circuit solutions for cell phone, portable device, voice processing, audio processing and image processing." FangTek is a silicon component vendor that reaches customers through electronics distributors; it publishes no public developer platform, web API, SDK or machine-readable API surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security data only.

providers.name: Fanhouse
providers.description: Fanhouse was a creator-subscription social platform, backed by a16z, that let fans pay creators directly for exclusive posts, photos, and community access rather than through ad-driven feeds. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The original product operated at fanhouse.app, which no longer resolves to the company (it now redirects to an unrelated domain), indicating the a16z-backed platform is defunct. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API surface could be located for the original Fanhouse product, so no scored API artifacts could be produced without fabrication. This profile is retained as a company/lead record.

providers.name: Fanimal
providers.description: Fanimal was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Re-verified on 2026-07-20, the primary domain fanimal.com remains a parked, Cloudflare-fronted redirect — every path probed (root, /llms.txt, /.well-known/security.txt, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /.well-known/api-catalog, and the api./developer./docs. subdomains) returns HTTP 301 to https://tickpick.com/?fanimal=y. The ?fanimal=y attribution marker on a redirect into a ticket-resale marketplace indicates the property is defunct or has been absorbed by TickPick. No package was found on npm, PyPI, RubyGems, or crates.io; the github.com/Fanimal organization exists but is empty (0 public repos, no profile metadata) and cannot be verified as the same company. No independent Fanimal API, developer portal, OpenAPI spec, MCP server, or reachable /.well-known/ surface exists to enrich; there is no spec-bearing developer surface to ground any artifact against. The registered domain is still administered (live TLS, HSTS, SES SPF, Google and Klaviyo site-verification TXT records), which is captured in the probed domain-security artifact.

providers.name: fanli
providers.description: fanli (返利网, fanli.com) is a Chinese cashback and shopping-rewards platform that aggregates promotions, coupons, and rebate offers across major online retailers, letting consumers earn money back on purchases they route through the site. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, fanli.com is a live consumer-facing web property; no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API definition, /.well-known discovery surface, llms.txt, or published security/vulnerability-disclosure program was found.

providers.name: Farfetch
providers.description: Farfetch is a global luxury fashion technology platform and online marketplace connecting consumers with boutiques, brands, and department stores across more than 190 countries, offering designer womenswear, menswear, kidswear, shoes, bags, and accessories. Beyond its consumer marketplace, Farfetch historically operated a B2B arm, Farfetch Platform Solutions (FPS), providing e-commerce, fulfilment, and logistics technology to luxury retailers; the group was acquired by Coupang in early 2024. No public developer portal or API documentation is currently reachable for the marketplace or the platform arm.

providers.name: Farm Credit Administration
providers.description: The Farm Credit Administration (FCA) is an independent federal agency responsible for regulating and supervising the Farm Credit System, a nationwide network of cooperatively owned institutions that provide credit and financial services to farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural borrowers. The FCA ensures that the Farm Credit System operates in a safe and sound manner and provides fair and competitive services. FCA does not publish a public REST API; however, the FCS Data Portal and downloadable Call Reports provide programmatic access to financial data on Farm Credit System institutions.

providers.name: Farmeron
providers.description: Farmeron was a dairy herd-management and farm-analytics SaaS founded in 2011 in Osijek, Croatia, that helped dairy producers track animals, feed, milk production, and farm operations through a web platform and data integrations. The company went through the 500 Startups accelerator and was acquired by the machine-vision agriculture firm Cainthus in 2016, after which the standalone Farmeron product was wound down. This network profile is retained as a historical/portfolio lead; the farmeron.com domain is registered but no longer serves a live website or API, so there is no public developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fashion, Inc. (Fab.com)
providers.description: Fashion, Inc. was the legal entity behind Fab.com, the design-focused e-commerce and flash-sale marketplace founded in 2010 by Jason Goldberg and Bradford Shellhammer after pivoting from the Fabulis social network. Fab raised roughly $150M across rounds led by Menlo Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and Atomico, listed Battery Ventures among its backers, and passed ten million members by December 2012 before layoffs and a collapse in growth. PCH International acquired Fab's digital assets in March 2015; the site was later repositioned around health and fitness goods and went offline in December 2022. The company is defunct and operated no public developer program or API. The fab.com domain is today registered to Epic Games, Inc. and serves Epic's unrelated Fab digital-asset marketplace, so nothing currently published at that host belongs to this company.

providers.name: Fashionara
providers.description: Fashionara was an Indian premium online fashion retailer that launched in 2012 as a curated "e-fashion mall" selling ladies, men's and kids apparel, footwear and lifestyle goods. It ran a flash-sale "events" model on a Magento storefront, carried more than 200 international labels alongside Indian brands including Kenneth Cole, Calvin Klein, Fossil, Adidas, Benetton, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Clarks and Arrow, and operated a quirky in-house sub-brand called F.lea Bazaar. It offered free shipping over Rs. 799, free returns, next-day delivery in eight Indian cities, a style-advisor booking service and an Android app (com.fnara.main). The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Fashionara never published a public API, developer portal, SDK or OpenAPI definition — a scan of more than 8,000 archived fashionara.com URLs found no /api, /developer, /docs, /swagger, /oauth or /graphql paths, and no api/developer subdomain was ever archived. The storefront went dark in mid-2016 and the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: FashionLab Nordic Inc.
providers.description: FashionLab Nordic Inc. is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Fast Break Labs
providers.description: Fast Break Labs is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Fastenal
providers.description: Fastenal is a leading distributor of industrial and construction supplies, offering fasteners, tools, safety equipment, and other industrial products through stores, vending, and e-commerce. While Fastenal provides EDI integrations and supply chain programs like FAST 360, FASTBin, and FASTStock to enterprise customers, no publicly documented API specifications are available.

providers.name: FavStay
providers.description: FavStay is a hotel and accommodation booking company in the travel and hospitality sector, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the public site at favstay.com is offline (the host returns a Microsoft Azure Web App 404 error and its TLS certificate does not match the domain), indicating the product is defunct or the web presence has been retired. The domain still resolves with Google Workspace email and an SPF record delegating to the Juniper (ejuniper.com) hospitality booking engine, but no public developer surface, API documentation, or machine-readable specification could be found.

providers.name: FBG Capital
providers.description: FBG Capital is a digital asset management firm operating in blockchain-based capital markets, founded in 2015 by Vincent Zhou. One of the earliest and largest blockchain-focused investment firms in Asia, FBG runs a venture arm that backs early-stage blockchain and Web3 startups and a trading/asset-management arm active across cryptocurrency markets. Its portfolio spans DeFi, Layer-1 and Layer-2 protocols, gaming, metaverse, and infrastructure projects (Terra, NEAR, Livepeer, Filecoin, Maple, Origin Protocol, Zilliqa, and many others). FBG Capital publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile tracks the firm as a company/investor node in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fenxiang Life
providers.description: Fenxiang Life (分享生活) is a Hangzhou-based Chinese social e-commerce and shopping-guide platform that combines cashback rebates with AI-driven price comparison. It returns platform commissions to consumers as cashback and analyzes historical price trends across major Chinese marketplaces including Taobao, JD.com, Pinduoduo, Douyin, and VipShop to help shoppers save money. Founded in 2018, the company reports 50M+ users and is backed by DCM Ventures, Xiaomi, and Toutoushidao Fund. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; the company is consumer-facing and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Ferguson
providers.description: Ferguson is a Fortune 500 distributor of plumbing supplies, HVAC products, pipe, valves and fittings, waterworks, and building supplies serving professional contractors, residential homeowners, and commercial customers across the United States.

providers.name: Fern Bot
providers.description: Fern (operating as Ishiki Labs) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) physical-AI startup building high-fidelity, custom robot world models that let robotics companies evaluate and train their robot policies at scale in software. Fern provides plug-and-play reinforcement-learning environments generated from a foundational world model: robotics teams seed varied starting scenes from their production environments, test and improve policies entirely in simulation, and Fern generates RL heads on top of existing policies to raise speed and success rates — a continual-learning flywheel where production robots improve every week. Founded in 2025 by CEO Amit Yadav (ex-Meta LLaMA / Reality Labs research scientist) and CTO Robert Xu (ex-Meta Reality Labs and Citadel Securities). As of this profile Fern publishes a marketing site, a whitepaper, and case studies but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Fidelity National Financial
providers.description: Fidelity National Financial (FNF) is a leading provider of title insurance, escrow, and other title-related services, as well as transaction services to the real estate and mortgage industries. FNF also operates F&G Annuities & Life and owns technology providers including SoftPro and ServiceLink that serve the title, real estate, and mortgage workflow.

providers.name: FiftyThree
providers.description: FiftyThree, Inc. was a New York City-based technology company that built tools for mobile creativity, best known for Paper (Apple's 2012 iPad App of the Year), the Pencil Bluetooth stylus, and Paste, a collaborative presentation tool. The company raised a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) in 2013 and, in July 2014, shipped the FiftyThree SDK so third-party iOS apps such as Procreate and Noteshelf could integrate the Pencil stylus (pairing, palm rejection, surface pressure). FiftyThree's assets and patents were acquired by WeTransfer on August 21, 2018, and the standalone products and developer surface were subsequently wound down. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no live public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI to enrich.

providers.name: Figure
providers.description: Figure is a Sunnyvale, California humanoid robotics company building general-purpose bipedal robots for the home and the workplace. Its current flagship product is Figure 03, marketed as an everyday general-purpose humanoid robot, succeeding Figure 01 and Figure 02. Figure develops Helix, an in-house Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that unifies perception, language understanding, and learned control to drive a full upper humanoid body at 35 degrees of freedom and 200 Hz, with capabilities including novel-object manipulation from natural-language commands and multi-robot task coordination. Figure has run commercial pilots with partners such as BMW and previously collaborated with OpenAI on language models. The company's revenue model is robot sales/leasing and enterprise deployments; Helix is a proprietary on-board model and there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Figure or Helix.

providers.name: FileUp
providers.description: Temporary file hosting with upload API, expiration times, and view limits

providers.name: Finisar
providers.description: Finisar Corporation was a manufacturer of optical communications components and subsystems (optical transceivers, semiconductor lasers, and related fiber-optic hardware). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. Finisar was acquired by II-VI Incorporated in 2019, and the combined company was subsequently rebranded as Coherent Corp. The Finisar brand is retired (finisar.com issues a 301 redirect to coherent.com, verified 2026-07-19) and has no independent public developer, API, or documentation surface. No API artifacts are applicable to this stub.

providers.name: Finmark
providers.description: Finmark was a financial planning, modeling, and forecasting SaaS platform for startups and small businesses, backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, letting founders build budgets, cash-flow runway, hiring plans, and scenario models without spreadsheets. It was acquired by BILL (bill.com) and wound down as a standalone product: as of this enrichment pass finmark.com and www.finmark.com return a 301 permanent redirect to https://www.bill.com/. There is no longer an independent Finmark developer portal, API, documentation, pricing, or status page to enrich; the domain-security probe below reflects the residual finmark.com DNS/TLS surface only.

providers.name: Finnomena
providers.description: Finnomena is a Thailand-based wealth-technology and investment platform, headquartered in Bangkok, that lets retail investors research, buy, hold, and rebalance mutual funds and other investment products through a single mobile and web application. The platform combines a robo-advisory experience and model portfolios with an active investment community and a large body of Thai-language market education and analysis content. Finnomena Funds operates as a licensed investment intermediary, and the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Finnomena publishes a consumer-facing WordPress marketing site and a mobile app but no public developer program, API, or OpenAPI surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security data only.

providers.name: Fintool
providers.description: Fintool is an AI-powered equity research analyst and financial copilot built for institutional investors such as hedge funds, asset managers, and buy-side and sell-side analysts. Its assistant ingests SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K), earnings-call transcripts, and financial data to answer research questions with source citations, accelerating fundamental analysis and due diligence. Fintool is a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery; Fintool operates as an enterprise SaaS product and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal that could be harvested.

providers.name: Fintura
providers.description: Fintura is a company name that appears on Battery Ventures' full list of all companies (https://www.battery.com/list-of-all-companies/) with no linked website, sector, or status, and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-derived stub awaiting enrichment. A July 2026 enrichment pass probed every plausible domain and found no confirmed, live company presence that can be attributed to this Battery-listed entity - fintura.com resolves to an empty placeholder page, fintura.de is parked for sale through a domain broker, and fintura.ai is a parked lander. A live SaaS at fintura.io exists (workflow and CIPC-compliance automation for South African accounting firms) but nothing publicly ties it to the Battery listing, so it is deliberately NOT claimed here. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or any other API artifact was found, and no API surface is asserted. This profile remains an unverified lead rather than a producer profile.

providers.name: Fireglass
providers.description: Fireglass was an Israeli browser-isolation cybersecurity startup, a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners, whose remote-browser-isolation product removed active web content threats by rendering pages in an isolated cloud environment. The company was acquired by Symantec in 2017 and its technology folded into Symantec Web Isolation (now part of Broadcom); it no longer operates as an independent brand. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment probe the fireglass.com domain has been re-registered and now serves Technical Glass Products, an unrelated fire-rated architectural glass manufacturer. No surviving Fireglass developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, MCP server, or /.well-known surface exists to enrich; this stub is retained as a resolved Lightspeed portfolio lead.

providers.name: FireVisor
providers.description: FireVisor is an AI-based manufacturing analytics platform that helps manufacturers leverage their production data beyond traditional defect detection and process control methods. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Singapore (with a secondary office in Toronto, Canada), FireVisor works toward "self-aware factories powered by artificial intelligence," applying machine learning to manufacturing and industrial-automation data. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this profile the public firevisor.com site returns a 404 from its load balancer and exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: First Person Labs
providers.description: First Person Labs, Inc. is a Palo Alto, California-based startup that appears on Andreessen Horowitz's (a16z) public investment list, and was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead pending discovery of a public API or developer surface. As of this profile, no public developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or other machine-readable API artifact has been verified for the company, so this record remains an identity-only stub. It will be enriched further once a confirmed product, developer portal, or API surface is located and attributed to this entity; no domain, product, or API has been attached here without verification.

providers.name: Flagcat
providers.description: Flagcat is a Paris-based animation and webtoon production studio building ambitious action-fantasy anime and webtoon series (including "Writers," "Deadly Hour," and "Impure Blood Regression") while redesigning the production pipeline around artist wellness. Its proprietary tool, Flagcat Colors, is an AI-powered coloring product for webtoon artists that learns from uploaded character references and batch-colorizes line art in one click, exporting layered files for final touch-ups. Flagcat Colors is in a pre-beta, waiting-list stage and the studio publishes no public API, developer platform, SDKs, or documentation as of this profile. Backed by Seedcamp.

providers.name: Flagship
providers.description: Flagship is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of index-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: retail. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Flapping Airplanes
providers.description: Flapping Airplanes describes itself as a frontier data efficiency lab that is currently in stealth. It is an AI-sector company backed by GV and Index Ventures, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a single stealth landing page (flappingairplanes.com) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this profile will be enriched further as a developer-facing surface appears.

providers.name: Fleetsmith
providers.description: Fleetsmith was a San Francisco-based startup (founded 2016) that provided cloud-based Apple device management (MDM) for IT teams — automated zero-touch setup, patching, app deployment, and security enforcement across Macs, iPhones, iPads, and Apple TVs. Backed by Menlo Ventures and others, Fleetsmith was acquired by Apple in June 2020; Apple subsequently discontinued the standalone product and folded its capabilities into Apple Business Essentials. The company no longer operates an independent developer program or public API, and fleetsmith.com now redirects to Apple Business Essentials. This profile is retained for network history.

providers.name: Fleetzero
providers.description: Fleetzero is a Houston-based maritime technology company, founded in 2021 and led by U.S. Navy veterans and shipping-industry experts, building battery-electric energy and robotics systems to decarbonize ocean shipping at cost parity with fossil fuels. Its Leviathan modular marine energy storage system, 3.8 MWh marine battery containers, and 55 MWh battery barges provide propulsion power and mobile charging infrastructure for cargo vessels. Backed by Obvious Ventures, Fleetzero was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it currently publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so this profile carries company identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: FlightCar
providers.description: FlightCar was a United States peer-to-peer car-rental marketplace built around airport travel, surfaced into the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating company behind the name and no API surface of any kind. The domain flightcar.com is registered but publishes no A, AAAA or MX records, resolves to no host, and sits on Njalla privacy nameservers with a SOA serial dated 2026-07-18; the api, developer and docs subdomains do not resolve; there is no GitHub organisation at github.com/flightcar; and no first-party client library exists on npm or PyPI. The Internet Archive shows the consumer site returning 200 through May 2016 and an Internal Server Error by July 2017, with no successful captures in 2017 or 2018. FlightCar is therefore carried in the network as a defunct company retained for portfolio-graph and historical continuity rather than as an active API provider, and should not be re-queued for artifact enrichment.

providers.name: Flipagram
providers.description: Flipagram is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Fliptop
providers.description: Fliptop was a San Francisco-based predictive marketing and customer intelligence startup that applied data science and machine learning to CRM and marketing-automation data to score leads, predict conversion, and prioritize sales pipelines. Founded around 2009, it was acquired by LinkedIn in August 2015 and folded into LinkedIn's Sales Solutions (Sales Navigator) product. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its former domain fliptop.com now 301-redirects to business.linkedin.com/sales-solutions. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Flirtey
providers.description: Flirtey was a drone-delivery technology company founded in 2013 by Matthew Sweeny and Tom Bass, backed by Y Combinator. It pioneered autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle delivery, conducting the first FAA-approved drone delivery in the United States in 2016 (Nevada) and running early delivery trials with partners including Domino's (the first pizza delivered by drone, in New Zealand) and 7-Eleven. Flirtey developed the Flirtey Eagle delivery drone and portable landing/loading systems aimed at medical, food, and retail last-mile logistics. The company is now defunct: it did not maintain a public developer program or API, and the flirtey.com domain has since been sold and now redirects to an unrelated business (us-stemcell.com). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Flixster
providers.description: Flixster is an American movie-discovery and social entertainment brand founded in 2007 that let people rate and review movies, browse local showtimes, watch trailers, and share what they were watching. It grew into one of the largest movie communities on the web and mobile, and in 2011 was acquired by Warner Bros. together with Rotten Tomatoes; Fandango Media later acquired both Flixster and Rotten Tomatoes from Warner Bros. in 2016. The Flixster Video digital-locker service (built on UltraViolet) was shut down in 2019. The flixster.com property no longer operates as an independent consumer site — it now redirects to Fandango, and Flixster does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/brand record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: float
providers.description: Float is a design-led product lab founded by David Okuniev and Neil Kinnish, the ex-Typeform Labs team, building new consumer and creator software products under the mantra "we make new products float." Its first product is Supercut, an AI-assisted video tool entering beta. Float raised a EUR 1.6M seed round led by Point Nine Capital with angels including Koen Bok (Framer), Christian Reber and Niklas Jansen (Interface Capital), Soleio, and Robert Munoz (Typeform). As of this enrichment pass Float publishes only a marketing site (float.build) and product landing pages and exposes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or developer platform.

providers.name: Floracene
providers.description: Floracene is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) health-tech startup that optimizes medical-device purchasing for independent surgery centers. Its platform surfaces clinically equivalent implant options based on a physician's manufacturer contracts, helping independent orthopedic and spine surgery centers choose lower-cost, clinically interchangeable devices and recoup an estimated 20-30% of implant spend while protecting case margins and patient care. US surgery centers spend roughly $7 billion annually on implants, which represent 40-60% of procedure costs. The company is at an early, pre-product stage with a placeholder marketing site and no public API, developer portal, or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Flourish
providers.description: Flourish (Flourish Labs) is a New York City based artificial intelligence research company building, in its own words, "human-level intelligence with human-level efficiency." Backed by GV (Google Ventures), the lab concentrates on advanced machine learning systems and foundational AI research rather than a public developer platform. At the time of profiling it publishes a marketing website but exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, documentation, MCP server, or other developer surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio-lead stub and enriched with a live domain-security probe of its website host.

providers.name: FlowWise Networks
providers.description: FlowWise Networks was a computer-networking hardware company founded in 1996 and headquartered in San Jose, California, that built layer 2, 3, and 4 wire-speed, self-configuring router-acceleration products designed to boost enterprise network performance with minimal disruption of service. Backed by Alta Partners, Battery Ventures, InveStar Capital, Mitsubishi Electric, and TL Ventures (roughly $21M-$27.5M raised), the company was acquired by Network Equipment Technologies (N.E.T.) in January 2000. It is long defunct and operates no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this record is retained for VC portfolio-graph provenance only and is not an enrichable API provider.

providers.name: Fluidly
providers.description: Fluidly was a London-based intelligent cashflow forecasting fintech founded in 2016 by Caroline Plumb, providing SME cash-flow prediction, scenario planning, and working-capital tools used by roughly 1,300 UK accountancy firms. OakNorth Bank acquired Fluidly in December 2021 and folded the product into its Credit Intelligence Suite; the independent Fluidly brand has since been retired and fluidly.com now redirects to OakNorth's partnerships page. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record — no independent Fluidly developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface remains.

providers.name: Flutter
providers.description: Flutter was an early-stage gesture-recognition startup founded in 2010 by Mehul Nariyawala and Navneet Dalal and based in California. Its consumer app used computer-vision hand-gesture recognition over a built-in webcam to control media players such as iTunes, Spotify, VLC, and QuickTime; it launched in 2012, reached number one free app in dozens of countries on the Mac App Store, and was named by Apple among the best free apps of 2012. The company raised early funding from Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and NEA before Google acquired it on October 2, 2013, after which the product was discontinued. It has no active developer program, public API, or maintained developer portal today. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; there is no live provider surface to enrich.

providers.name: Flye
providers.description: Flye was a San Francisco social-audience and brand-marketing analytics startup (500 Global / 500 Startups Demo Day Batch 19, founded 2016) that helped brands build and understand their audiences from social data (an "audience fingerprint") and run targeted, personalized engagement campaigns using machine learning. The company appears defunct — its original domain (flye.co) has lapsed and now hosts an unrelated online-casino review/affiliate site. No developer platform, API, documentation, SDK, or other technical surface exists for this provider, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication.

providers.name: FogHorn Systems (Johnson Controls)
providers.description: FogHorn Systems was a Sunnyvale, California developer of edge AI and machine learning software for the industrial and commercial Internet of Things (IIoT). Its Lightning Edge AI platform and Lightning EdgeML brought real-time streaming analytics and ML inference to constrained on-premises edge hardware for predictive maintenance, machine optimization, and operational intelligence use cases. Johnson Controls acquired FogHorn in January 2022 and folded its team and technology into the OpenBlue suite of smart, autonomous building solutions, with the former Sunnyvale headquarters operating as a Johnson Controls "AI Hub." FogHorn no longer operates as a standalone brand and publishes no independent public developer surface — no developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization resolve as of this enrichment pass; the former foghorn.io/foghorn.ai domains are parked. This profile is retained as a network company record with no public API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Folhamatic
providers.description: Folhamatic (IOB Folhamatic Group) is a Brazilian developer of integrated accounting, payroll, and fiscal/tax software for accounting firms and businesses, founded in 1990 and headquartered in Americana, Sao Paulo. Its product line includes Folhamatic Payroll for personnel management and electronic files, Electronic Point Control for time-clock management, the Folhamatic Accounting system for management reporting, and Folhamatic Written Tax for tax departments. At acquisition it served more than 11,000 companies with 500-plus employees. Folhamatic was acquired by the UK's Sage Group in June 2012 and now operates as part of Sage in Brazil. The company publishes no first-party public developer API, and the historic folhamatic.com.br domain no longer serves a live site.

providers.name: Folia Water
providers.description: Folia Water, Inc. is a clean-water social enterprise founded in 2016 by Jonathan Levine, Theresa Dankovich, and Cantwell Carson with the goal of bringing safe drinking water to 100 million people for pennies a day. The company manufactures Folia Filters, an affordable antimicrobial filter paper embedded with silver nanoparticles that kills 99.9999% of bacteria and 99.7% of viruses while removing protozoa and iron. Folia Water sells through distribution partners in emerging markets such as Bangladesh and is backed by 500 Global. It is a physical consumer-products manufacturer with no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface as of this profile.

providers.name: Food Advisor
providers.description: Food Advisor (FoodAdvisor.my) is a Malaysia-based food discovery application founded in 2014 by Kenny Hew and headquartered in Selangor, Malaysia. The service helps users find dishes and restaurants by searching dish names as keywords alongside locations. It is backed by 500 Global through the 500 Durians Southeast Asia fund. As of this profile the public web presence at foodadvisor.my returns HTTP 404 and no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation could be located for enrichment.

providers.name: Foodish
providers.description: Random pictures of food dishes

providers.name: Foodzie
providers.description: Foodzie was an online marketplace, founded in 2008 and based in San Francisco, that let people discover and buy food directly from small artisan producers, and later ran a monthly tasting-box subscription service. It raised roughly $1M from investors including Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC) and Jeff Clavier, and was acquired by the video-commerce company Joyus in June 2012, becoming "Joyus Food" before the subscription service was wound down. The company is defunct; the foodzie.com domain is no longer operated by the original business, and no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Football Standings
providers.description: Display football standings e.g epl, la liga, serie a etc. The data is based on espn site

providers.name: Foreword Fund
providers.description: Foreword Fund is an early-stage venture capital firm led by solo general partner Declan Kelly, backing daring founders in their first chapters. Foreword writes first checks of up to $250,000 at the pre-seed and seed stage, partnering with roughly ten exceptionally focused teams each year across B2B software, fintech, crypto, enterprise software, AI, marketplaces, and consumer sectors in the US and Europe. A partner fund of Seedcamp, its portfolio spans 40-plus companies including unicorns Sorare, Jeeves, and Localyze.

providers.name: Forrst
providers.description: Forrst was a community for designers and developers to share work in progress and give and receive detailed feedback, founded in 2009 by Kyle Bragger with seed funding from 500 Startups (500 Global) and other angels. It was acquired by Colourlovers in 2012, then by product-design firm ZURB in January 2013, and was shut down on April 14, 2014. The company is defunct; forrst.com now redirects to zurb.com and there is no active API, developer portal, or public API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Fortigo
providers.description: Fortigo Network Logistics Pvt. Ltd. (4TiGO) was a Bengaluru, India technology-enabled logistics and supply-chain network platform, founded in 2015, operating an online marketplace for freight/truck transportation alongside a Digital Supply Chain Control Tower SaaS. It was backed by Accel and Nandan Nilekani's NRJN Family Trust, raising roughly $23.5M across five rounds. As of this enrichment pass the company appears deadpooled/defunct: its 4tigo.com site is unreachable (connection refused across all hosts) and no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition could be located. No API artifacts were enriched because there is no live developer surface.

providers.name: Fortune Brands Innovations
providers.description: Fortune Brands Innovations (formerly Fortune Brands Home & Security) is a leading home products company with a portfolio of brands across water innovations (Moen, House of Rohl, Aqualisa), outdoors (Therma-Tru, Larson, Fiberon), and security (Master Lock, SentrySafe, Yale Residential).

providers.name: Fortune Technology (China FIF)
providers.description: Fortune Technology, listed by Qiming Venture Partners as one of the largest commercial factoring companies in China, historically operating at china-fif.com. Commercial factoring is a trade-finance business: purchasing accounts receivable from suppliers at a discount to provide working capital. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe the company publishes no developer surface of any kind — no public API, no documentation portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents. The china-fif.com domain no longer serves the company: HTTPS is refused outright (port 443 closed) and plain HTTP returns an unrelated Chinese Premier League sports-streaming site running EmpireCMS. This record is retained as an honest negative result for the API Evangelist network rather than deleted.

providers.name: Fortunes
providers.description: ForTunes was a Vienna-based mobile music data analytics application for self-publishing and DIY artists, managers, and small labels. The app collected and visualized performance data across Spotify, Apple Music, SoundCloud, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and other platforms into a single intelligent feed, with notifications for playlist adds and follower growth, a Spotify playlist recommendation engine, public artist profiles, and team collaboration. Backed by Speedinvest (2018), the company was acquired by Utopia Music in 2023. As of this profile the primary web domain (fortunes.io) no longer resolves and no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; the product surface is the consumer iOS and Android apps.

providers.name: Fossil Group
providers.description: Fossil Group is a global designer, marketer, and distributor of consumer fashion accessories including watches, jewelry, handbags, small leather goods, belts, and sunglasses sold under owned and licensed brands such as Fossil, Skagen, Michele, Relic, Misfit, and licensed lines for Michael Kors, Diesel, Emporio Armani, Tory Burch, and others.

providers.name: FounderDating
providers.description: FounderDating was an online network that helped entrepreneurs find co-founders, advisors, and early team members to start companies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-19) confirms FounderDating has been merged into CoFoundersLab: the founderdating.com domain now redirects to cofounderslab.com, a founder-matching and startup-community platform. Neither the legacy FounderDating brand nor the CoFoundersLab successor publishes a public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, developer portal, SDK/package, or any /.well-known discovery surface, so there are no API artifacts to search, generate, or derive. The founderdating.com host is additionally unreachable over HTTPS (connection times out; DNS points at a parked Tucows IP). This profile is retained as a historical company record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Foxconn Industrial Internet
providers.description: Foxconn Industrial Internet Co., Ltd. (FII, 工业富联) is a Shanghai Stock Exchange-listed subsidiary of Hon Hai Precision Industry (Foxconn), headquartered in Shenzhen, China. It is a smart-manufacturing and industrial-internet company producing cloud computing infrastructure and AI servers, communication and networking equipment, and precision tooling, and it offers factory-automation, lighthouse-factory, and industrial-internet platform services for global electronics OEMs. FII operates as a contract manufacturer and industrial platform rather than a public API provider: it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal. This profile tracks the company's corporate identity in the API Evangelist network; there is no API artifact surface to enrich.

providers.name: Foxtrot
providers.description: Foxtrot (Foxtrot Market, foxtrotco.com) is a Chicago-based retail chain of upscale convenience stores and cafes combining a neighborhood corner store with a coffee shop and a curated selection of local and specialty food, drink, and grocery goods, plus on-demand delivery and pickup. Surfaced as a portfolio company of d1-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. At the time of enrichment the public site (foxtrotco.com) is a minimal placeholder and the company exposes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Frame
providers.description: Frame Technology Corp. was a software company that developed FrameMaker, a structured desktop-publishing and technical-documentation authoring application widely used for long, complex documents. Founded in the 1980s and taken public, Frame Technology was acquired by Adobe Systems in 1995; FrameMaker continues today as an Adobe product. This is a historical/acquired portfolio company of Canaan Partners with no independent developer or API surface of its own.

providers.name: Framed *
providers.description: Framed (framed.io), formerly Framed Data, was a GV-backed predictive-analytics / customer churn-prediction machine-learning startup. As of 2026 the framed.io domain no longer hosts a product or developer surface: it serves a static Squarespace landing page titled "Framed + Square" that points visitors to Square Capital (squareup.com/capital), indicating the team/product moved to Square. No API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable artifact surface survives, so there is nothing to enrich against; this record is retained as a dormant/acquired lead.

providers.name: Freejit
providers.description: Freejit (styled FREEjit) was an early-stage startup founded around 2010 in Newport Beach, California, that attempted to turn browser autocomplete into a marketable service. It was backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) and other early investors. Per public company registries the business is now closed/defunct, and its domain (freejit.com) no longer resolves. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; enrichment found no live developer surface, API, documentation, SDKs, or specifications to harvest.

providers.name: Freeport-McMoRan
providers.description: Freeport-McMoRan is a leading international mining company with headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona, operating large, long-lived geographically diverse assets with significant proven and probable reserves of copper, gold, and molybdenum.

providers.name: Freescale Semiconductor
providers.description: Freescale Semiconductor, Inc. was an American semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Austin, Texas, created in 2004 from the spin-off of Motorola's Semiconductor Products Sector. Freescale designed and produced embedded processing hardware — microcontrollers (Kinetis, S08), i.MX applications processors, ColdFire and QorIQ/PowerPC communications processors, digital signal processors, RF, analog, and sensor products — for the automotive, networking, industrial, and consumer markets. In December 2015 Freescale merged with NXP Semiconductors in a roughly $11.8B deal and ceased to exist as an independent company; its freescale.com domain now redirects to nxp.com. Freescale was a hardware/silicon company, not a web-API provider: it published no public REST/HTTP API, developer portal, or OpenAPI, so there is no live API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Freestyle
providers.description: Freestyle is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of foundry-group and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: venture-capital. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Freqens
providers.description: Freqens is an early-stage financial planning and analysis (FP&A) startup building software that helps finance teams leave spreadsheets behind in the agentic era, giving CFOs and finance leaders a better way to work with their numbers. Backed by Seedcamp, the company is currently in a private, invitation-only phase, inviting a small initial group of CFOs and finance leaders. There is no public API, developer portal, or documentation yet; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network as it moves toward a public product.

providers.name: FreshDish
providers.description: FreshDish (Fresh Dish, Inc.) was a Santa Monica meal-kit delivery startup founded in 2012 by Steve Goldstein (formerly SVP/GM at Provide Commerce, the ProFlowers and Shari's Berries operator). Incubated by Science Inc. and seeded with $500,000 from Battery Ventures, it shipped ready-to-cook dinner kits with chef-designed recipes and pre-portioned ingredients (two-person kits at $24, family-of-four at $32, free shipping). The company was deadpooled and is no longer operating; the freshdish.com domain now resolves to a parked/for-sale lander. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. FreshDish never operated a developer program, public API, or SDKs, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Freshmenu
providers.description: FreshMenu is a Bengaluru-based full-stack food-technology company that operates its own cloud kitchens and cooks, packages, and delivers a daily-changing menu of fresh gourmet meals directly to consumers. Unlike aggregator marketplaces, FreshMenu owns the end-to-end experience — from culinary R&D and kitchen operations to its consumer ordering website and mobile apps — serving Bengaluru, Mumbai, and the Delhi/NCR region (New Delhi and Gurgaon). The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. It publishes a consumer ordering experience but no public API or developer program; this profile captures its identity and infrastructure posture for the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Freshplum
providers.description: Freshplum was a San Francisco data-science startup (founded 2010) that built cloud-based predictive analytics for e-commerce, gauging online shopper behavior in real time to surface personalized promotional offers and discounts to visitors who might otherwise abandon a purchase. During its private alpha it was already processing over 10M requests a day. Freshplum raised roughly $1.7M from investors including DCVC and GV (Google Ventures) before being acquired by ad-targeting company TellApart in July 2014 (TellApart was in turn acquired by Twitter in 2015). The company is defunct: it ships no live product, developer portal, documentation, or public API, and the freshplum.com domain is now a parked listing offered for sale via Afternic. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Friend.ly
providers.description: Friend.ly was a social question-and-answer service that let people meet and connect by answering fun, get-to-know-you questions, launched around 2010 by a team led by Ed Baker. It raised roughly $5M from Lightspeed Ventures, Balderton Capital, SoftTech VC (now Uncork Capital), and a range of angels, and was acquired by Facebook (now Meta) on October 10, 2011 — primarily an acqui-hire, with the founding team moving to Facebook to work on growth and new products. The consumer service was wound down after the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record for Uncork Capital; the friend.ly domain is now parked and the company operates no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Friend.tech
providers.description: Friend.tech is a decentralized social application built on Base, Coinbase's Ethereum layer-2 network, that lets users tokenize their social graph by buying and selling "keys" (originally "shares") which grant access to private chat rooms and gated content with individual creators. Launched in August 2023 and backed by Paradigm, a key's price rose as more people bought into a given creator. In 2024 the team disabled protocol fees and relinquished control of the on-chain smart contracts to the community. Friend.tech operates a live web frontend (www.friend.tech) but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI definition; this profile was surfaced as a Paradigm portfolio company and enriched with the real signals available (live-site domain security posture).

providers.name: Friends with Benefits
providers.description: Friends with Benefits (FWB) is a token-gated social DAO and cultural community at the intersection of web3, art, music, and technology. Membership is gated by holding the $FWB ERC-20 token, which unlocks access to the community's Discord, local city chapters, IRL events, and editorial and creative programming. Backed by a16z crypto, FWB is one of the most cited examples of a social DAO. It is a community organization rather than an API provider: as of this profile it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal, and its primary web presence (fwb.help) is a membership site. This entry was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Friendster
providers.description: Friendster is a mobile-first social network for real-life friends, operating at friendster.com with a native iOS app and a web experience. The service positions itself around privacy and intentional design — no ads, no algorithms, no spam, and an explicit promise never to sell user data — and centers on connecting people with the friends they actually know in real life. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass Friendster publishes a consumer marketing site and a native iOS app, but exposes no public developer program, API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — so there are no API artifacts to harvest, only company identity and live domain-security posture.

providers.name: Frontier Car group
providers.description: Frontier Car Group (FCG) was a Berlin-based startup, founded in 2016, that built, launched, and operated online and offline used-car marketplaces across high-growth emerging markets including Nigeria, Mexico, Chile, Pakistan, Indonesia, India and Poland, offering vehicle inspections, pricing guides, financing, warranties and insurance. OLX Group (Prosus/Naspers) invested up to $400M at a $700M valuation in 2019 and folded FCG into its OLX Autos brand; the Berlin operations were shut down in 2021 and Prosus later moved to exit the car-classifieds business. As of this enrichment pass the frontiercargroup.com domain no longer resolves (registered and ACTIVE through 2027 but serving no DNS A/NS records), the api.frontiercargroup.com host does not resolve, and the company publishes no developer, API, documentation, or other machine-readable surface. Originally surfaced as a Partech portfolio lead.

providers.name: frontiercargroup
providers.description: Frontier Car Group was a Berlin-based company (founded 2016 by Ricardo Donoso, Andre Kussmann and Daniel Esponda) that built and operated consumer-to-business (C2B) online marketplaces for used cars in emerging markets, including Cars45 (Nigeria), CarFirst (Pakistan), BeliMobilGue (Indonesia), and local brands in Chile, Mexico and Turkey. Sellers got instant online quotes, booked inspections at physical centers, and received competitive offers from a dealer network. The company raised roughly $553M and was acquired by OLX Group (Prosus/Naspers), where it was folded into the OLX Autos business. Its standalone domain (frontiercargroup.com) is no longer live and it exposes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Fuego
providers.description: Fuego, Inc. (maker of FuegoBPM) was an enterprise business process management (BPM) and service-oriented architecture software company founded circa 1999 in Plano, Texas. It was backed by Trinity Ventures among others (Series A, 2004) and was acquired by BEA Systems in March 2006, where FuegoBPM became the basis of BEA AquaLogic BPM; BEA was subsequently acquired by Oracle in 2008 and the technology folded into the Oracle BPM product line. Fuego no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: Fulfil
providers.description: Fulfil (Fulfil Solutions) is an automation company that builds robotic online-grocery fulfillment systems. Its ShopBot robots perform zero-labor pick-and-pack across all grocery temperatures and categories (ambient, refrigerated, frozen, and produce), providing item-level data and control with claimed 99% order accuracy and roughly 50% lower operating costs. The company operates automated micro-fulfillment facilities and partners with grocery and delivery operators. Backed by DCVC, Fulfil was surfaced as a portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing website but no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Full Truck Alliance
providers.description: Full Truck Alliance Co. Ltd. (Manbang Group / 满帮集团, NYSE: YMM) operates a leading digital freight platform in China that connects truckers and shippers to make road transportation more efficient. It runs the Yunmanman (运满满) and Huochebang (货车帮) mobile apps, applying mobile internet, big data, and artificial intelligence to freight matching, brokerage, transaction services, and value-added offerings across hundreds of cities and tens of thousands of routes. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures, hongshan, and softbank-vision-fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or open platform on its corporate site; this profile carries verified company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Funderful
providers.description: Funderful was an alumni fundraising software platform for universities and higher-education advancement teams, founded in 2013 by Raimonds Kulbergs and headquartered in Riga, Latvia. It helped advancement offices run donation campaigns, track donors, and pioneer conversational chatbots to re-engage alumni, with clients including UC Berkeley, Georgetown, London Business School, and Oxford and Cambridge colleges. Funderful joined 500 Startups (Batch 20) and raised seed funding before being acquired by Ruffalo Noel Levitz (RNL) in February 2019. The company is defunct as an independent entity and its domain (funderful.com) no longer resolves; enrichment found no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: FunFair
providers.description: FunFair began as FunFair Technologies, a blockchain gaming company that built Ethereum-based casino infrastructure (the Fate Channels state-channel technology and the FUN ERC-20 token) to let operators run provably-fair, on-chain casino games. The funfair.io domain now redirects (302) to FunFair Ventures (funfair.ventures), an early-stage Web3 venture firm run by the same team that invests across DeFi, gaming, infrastructure, NFTs, CeFi, social, travel, and DePIN, and sponsors the Blockchain Gaming Alliance. FunFair exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documentation portal; its historical surface was on-chain smart contracts rather than a hosted REST/HTTP API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and enriched with live domain-security probe data.

providers.name: Fungible
providers.description: Fungible Inc. was a Santa Clara, California startup founded in 2015 by Pradeep Sindhu (Juniper Networks co-founder) and Bertrand Serlet that built Data Processing Units (DPUs) — programmable microprocessors (the F1 and S1 chips plus the FS1600 NVMe storage array) designed to offload networking, storage, and security workloads from data-center CPUs. Its DPU cluster control plane ran Linux and exposed internal REST APIs for management, but Fungible never published a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK registry. Microsoft acquired the company in January 2023 (reported ~$190M), folded the team into its Azure data-center infrastructure engineering organization, and wound down the independent product line. The fungible.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fusion I/O
providers.description: Fusion-io (branded Fusion I/O) was an enterprise storage company founded in 2005 and based in the Salt Lake City area of Utah, best known for its ioMemory and ioDrive PCIe flash acceleration cards that placed NAND flash directly on the server bus to speed databases and data-center workloads. Steve Wozniak served as chief scientist; the company listed on the NYSE in 2011 and was acquired by SanDisk in 2014, later becoming part of Western Digital. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface today; fusionio.com no longer resolves to a live site. Retained in the network as a defunct a16z portfolio company for record.

providers.name: Fusion-io
providers.description: Fusion-io was a computer hardware and software systems company founded in 2005 in Salt Lake City, Utah, that pioneered PCIe-based flash memory (NAND) storage for enterprise data centers under the ioMemory, ioDrive, ioFX and ioScale product lines. Steve Wozniak served as its Chief Scientist. The company IPO'd on the NYSE under the ticker FIO in June 2011 and was acquired by SanDisk in 2014 for roughly 1.1 billion dollars; SanDisk (and the Fusion-io technology) was in turn acquired by Western Digital in 2016. It was venture-backed by New Enterprise Associates, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Accel. Fusion-io no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no public developer API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record.

providers.name: Future Nostalgia Studios
providers.description: Future Nostalgia Studios, Inc. is a consumer software company that builds AI-powered mobile applications and companion experiences for iOS and Android. Its published apps include Kindred (AI stories and roleplay), Muze (AI fashion photography), Booboo (long-distance relationship tracker), Pocket Frens (self-care and habit tracker), and Minime (AI motivational buddy). Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, documentation, or /.well-known surface — it is a business-to-consumer app studio rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Futureadvisor
providers.description: FutureAdvisor was a Y Combinator-backed robo-advisor that provided automated, algorithm-driven investment management and portfolio recommendations to retail investors. It was acquired by BlackRock and folded into the firm's digital wealth offerings; the consumer FutureAdvisor product has since been wound down. As of this enrichment pass the domain futureadvisor.com is controlled by BlackRock (its nameservers resolve to blackrock.com) but publishes no live website, developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or any public developer surface. No API artifacts could be searched, fetched, or derived — this remains an identity-only record for a defunct/absorbed provider.

providers.name: Futurtec
providers.description: Futurtec (鑫君特) is a Chinese medical-device company founded in 2015 and recognized as a national high-tech enterprise, focused on orthopedic surgical robotics. Its flagship ORTHBOT surgical system combines navigation with automatic robotic execution — intelligent needle placement, non-invasive positioning, dual-camera navigation, and visual force-feedback pressure protection — and holds Chinese regulatory approval (Feb 2021) and EU MDR CE certification (May 2023). The company reports 251+ patents filed or granted, including 84+ invention patents and 25+ PCT applications. As of this enrichment pass, Futurtec publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or software surface: it is a clinical hardware manufacturer, so the enrichment pipeline found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Fuze
providers.description: Fuze was a cloud unified-communications-as-a-service (UCaaS) provider offering enterprise cloud voice, video conferencing, team messaging, and contact-center capabilities for the mobile and distributed workforce. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Insight Partners, Fuze was acquired by 8x8 in 2022; its website (www.fuze.com) now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to 8x8.com/fuze and the Fuze product line has been folded into the 8x8 platform. No independent Fuze developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or public API surface could be found during enrichment. This profile remains in the API Evangelist network as a stub; the only artifact that could be enriched from real signal is a live domain/DNS/TLS security probe of fuze.com.

providers.name: Fyodor Biotechnologies
providers.description: Fyodor Biotechnologies is a Baltimore, Maryland based biotechnology company focused on making malaria diagnosis fast, affordable, and non-invasive. Its flagship product, the Urine Malaria Test (UMT), is a rapid diagnostic that detects active malaria infection from a urine sample in minutes without a blood draw, working much like a home pregnancy test so it can be used at the point of care or at home in regions where malaria is endemic. The test has been validated through partnerships with Johns Hopkins University, Duke University, and the University of Lagos, carries a CE Mark, and has secured regulatory approvals in Nigeria, Cote d'Ivoire, Kenya, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Fyodor was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It currently publishes no public developer platform, API, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.
