providers.description: API to retrieve song information from Gaana

providers.name: GAGO Group
providers.description: GAGO Group (Beijing Jiage Tianyu Technology Co., Ltd.) is a China-based frontier-technology company focused on agricultural and rural big data applications. Its homepage positions the business around agricultural and rural big data, applying remote-sensing and data-analytics techniques to agriculture. GAGO Group is backed by DCM Ventures and was added to the API Evangelist network from that portfolio. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate website at gagogroup.cn but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification could be verified, so no spec-derived API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: galbot
providers.description: Galbot (银河通用机器人, "Galaxy Universal Robotics") is the official site of a general-purpose, embodied-AI robotics company. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and profiled here for API and developer-surface enrichment. As of this enrichment pass Galbot publishes only a marketing website rendered as a client-side single-page app; no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or MCP surface could be discovered. The only machine-readable signals captured are the DNS, TLS, and email-authentication (SPF/DMARC) posture of the galbot.com domain.

providers.name: Galileo Technology
providers.description: Galileo Technology was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1993 that designed and marketed complex semiconductor devices for high-performance embedded control systems, principally in the area of data communications. Co-founded by Avigdor Willenz (CEO), Manuel Alba (President), and Eyal Waldman (VP Engineering), the company completed an IPO in 2000 and was acquired by Marvell Technology, Inc. in 2001 for approximately $2.7 billion. It was an early Lightspeed Venture Partners investment (1995). The company no longer operates independently and exposes no public developer surface, API, or documentation; this profile is retained for network/portfolio lineage only.

providers.name: Gamefam
providers.description: Gamefam is a gaming studio that builds and operates high-quality branded games and interactive experiences for Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences on platforms such as Roblox and Fortnite. It develops games, media campaigns, and amplification programs for 50+ brand partners (including LEGO, Adidas, Disney, and Netflix) and runs creator-facing programs such as Dev X and its Creator Fund. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Gamefam publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — its products are consumer game experiences distributed through third-party platforms.

providers.name: GamerzClass
providers.description: GamerzClass was a Copenhagen, Denmark-based online esports education platform, founded in 2018, that offered structured masterclasses and one-on-one coaching from professional players across titles such as Counter-Strike, League of Legends, and Dota 2. Backed by 500 Global, ByFounders, Bumble Ventures, and TrueSight Ventures, the company raised roughly USD 2.5M before being acquired by US-based esports coaching marketplace Metafy in May 2022. The gamerzclass.com domain no longer serves a live site and the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Gantto
providers.description: Gantto was a web-based Gantt chart and project scheduling SaaS launched in August 2010, backed by Y Combinator and 500 Startups (500 Global). It let teams create and share project schedules in the browser as an alternative to Microsoft Project, with a customer base that reportedly included Twitter, Lucasfilm, and Fujitsu. Gantto was acquired by Dutch competitor Tom's Planner on July 9, 2013, and the product was subsequently discontinued, with users migrated to Tom's Planner. gantto.com now redirects to tomsplanner.com. This company is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record; it publishes no developer program, API, or technical surface to enrich.

providers.name: Garaji
providers.description: Garaji was an online auto-services marketplace based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, founded in 2018, that connected car owners with local workshops for routine maintenance and repairs. Customers selected a service and a vetted garage, and a Garaji valet or tow truck collected the vehicle, delivered it to the workshop, and returned it once work was complete. Garaji was a 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) portfolio company. The company is permanently closed, and its domain garaji.com is now a parked, for-sale listing served via GoDaddy/Afternic with no live product or developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct portfolio-lead record; there are no APIs or developer artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Gateways
providers.description: A curated index of API, AI, data, and event gateways including cloud-managed services, open source projects, and commercial platforms that route, secure, and manage traffic across APIs, AI models, data pipelines, and event-driven architectures.

providers.name: GCL
providers.description: GCL System Integration Technology Co., Ltd. (GCL SI, Shenzhen: 002506) is one of the four listed companies of China's GCL Group and a global leading provider of photovoltaic and clean-energy solutions. Headquartered in Suzhou Industrial Park, Jiangsu Province, the company manufactures high-efficiency solar cells, large-size photovoltaic modules, energy-storage systems, and next-generation perovskite solar technology, with operations spanning six continents. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and added to the API Evangelist network; GCL SI is an industrial manufacturer and publishes no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: Geek-Jokes
providers.description: Fetch a random geeky/programming related joke for use in all sorts of applications

providers.name: Geekatoo
providers.description: Geekatoo was a Walnut Creek, California on-demand, in-home technology support marketplace that connected consumers to a nationwide network of vetted local technicians for computer repair, network troubleshooting, TV mounting, and home-theater/smart-home installation using a fixed-price and competitive-bid model positioned as an alternative to retail services like Geek Squad. Founded in 2013, it went through the 500 Startups accelerator (sixth batch) and raised roughly $2.2M from backers including 500 Startups, CRCM Venture Capital, DeNA, MicroVentures, and Wefunder. In May 2016 Geekatoo merged with Los Angeles-based HelloTech to form one of the largest on-demand in-home tech support networks in the US; the standalone Geekatoo brand and website (geekatoo.com) are no longer operational. This API Evangelist profile is a 500 Global portfolio lead retained for historical record; the enrichment pipeline found no live developer surface, API, or documentation to harvest.

providers.name: Gemvara
providers.description: Gemvara was a Boston-based direct-to-consumer custom fine-jewelry e-commerce retailer, founded in 2006 by Matt Lauzon and Jason Reuben (Babson College), known for made-to-order jewelry customization software that let shoppers configure gemstones and metals on demand. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners among others, it was acquired by Richline Group (a Berkshire Hathaway company) in 2013 and shut down in February 2023. The company published no public developer API, and the gemvara.com domain no longer resolves to a live site. This profile is retained as a defunct-company record.

providers.name: GenArts
providers.description: GenArts, Inc. was a Cambridge, Massachusetts developer of visual effects software for the film, broadcast, and advertising industries, best known for its flagship Sapphire plug-in suite used in Oscar-nominated visual effects work since 1996. GenArts was acquired by Boris FX in September 2016; the genarts.com domain now redirects to borisfx.com and the Sapphire product line is developed and sold under the Boris FX brand. The company published no public developer API, SDK, or documented programmatic surface — its products are desktop editing plug-ins. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: General Aviation
providers.description: General Aviation is a Y Combinator-backed startup (Spring 2026 batch) building a new air traffic control (ATC) system by connecting aircraft to the internet. Founded by Ben Frank, the company develops remote ATC tower technology aimed at the roughly 90 percent of airports in the U.S. National Airspace System that currently operate without control towers, giving smaller airfields an affordable path to the safety and efficiency benefits of tower services without the cost of traditional tower infrastructure and staffing. As of this profile the company operates a single marketing landing page and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: General Cable
providers.description: General Cable Corporation was a global developer and manufacturer of copper, aluminum, and fiber optic wire and cable products. The company was acquired by Prysmian Group in 2018 and integrated into the Prysmian portfolio. No public developer APIs are documented for General Cable.

providers.name: General Growth Properties
providers.description: General Growth Properties (GGP) was a major U.S.-based commercial real estate company and the second-largest shopping mall operator in the United States before being acquired by Brookfield Property Partners in 2018. The GGP portfolio is now operated under Brookfield Properties. No public developer APIs are documented for the legacy GGP entity.

providers.name: General Instinct
providers.description: General Instinct is a San Francisco company (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building the deployment layer for physical AI. Founded in 2026 by Bill Jiao and Guanming Wang, it distills, quantizes, and deploys large frontier AI models onto constrained edge hardware so robotics, drone, and physical-AI teams can run low-latency models fully offline on devices like NVIDIA Jetson, mobile NPUs, ARM CPUs, the Apple Neural Engine, and Snapdragon. Its first product, Instinct Edge, takes a model, a target device, and a latency budget and returns an offline runtime that hits the budget on-device with no cloud calls, handling model compression, custom kernel optimization (CUDA, Metal, ARM NEON), and the data-to-serving pipeline. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment searched the public web and found a marketing landing page but no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or public API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested. This profile captures the company identity plus the security posture of its public web surface, and remains an identity-only lead pending a discoverable API.

providers.name: General Radar
providers.description: General Radar Corp. (GenRad) is a Belmont, California hardtech company founded in 2016 that designs and manufactures fully solid-state, high-resolution active electronically scanned array (AESA) phased-array radar systems built largely on commercial off-the-shelf hardware. Its products include the C-band GenRad GFC multi-mission AESA radar with a GaN front-end and digital beam-forming, and the Mark-IV 76-81GHz millimeter-wave 3D imaging radar producing LIDAR-like point clouds. The company serves aerospace and defense (U.S. Air Force, Navy, NORAD), counter-drone, airfield foreign-object-debris (FOD) detection, autonomy, wind energy, and weather markets, and has raised over $35M from investors including Kleiner Perkins and Octave Ventures. General Radar publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness.

providers.name: Generalastro
providers.description: General Astronautics (Generalastro) is a Y Combinator (W26) space-robotics company founded in 2025 by Bram Schork, based in San Francisco, building autonomous dexterous robotic arms that perform laboratory research and manufacturing tasks in microgravity without astronaut intervention. Its systems handle work like pipetting, sample prep, plate handling, and reagent mixing, targeting microgravity production of pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and fiber optics where crew time on orbital stations is the bottleneck (NASA estimates ISS crew time at ~$130K/hour). The company is pre-product hardware, backed by Y Combinator and Planet Ventures (~$7.1M raised), and currently exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Gens de confiance
providers.description: Gens de confiance is a French online classified-ads marketplace built around trust rather than anonymity. Members reach listings and other members through the communities and networks they already belong to and their mutual connections, so buyers and sellers of goods, housing, jobs, services, and holiday rentals transact with people vouched for by a shared circle instead of strangers. The company operates a consumer web and mobile marketplace and is backed by Partech. No public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Gentle Monster
providers.description: Gentle Monster is a South Korean luxury eyewear brand founded in 2011 and operated by parent company IICOMBINED, headquartered in Seoul. The brand designs and sells avant-garde sunglasses and optical frames, and is widely recognized for its immersive, art-installation flagship stores and experiential retail spaces. Its sister brands include Tamburins (fragrance and body care) and Nudake (conceptual dessert and patisserie). Gentle Monster sells globally through flagship stores, department-store concessions, and its direct-to-consumer site at gentlemonster.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it is a consumer retail brand and publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Genvec
providers.description: GenVec was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 1992 and headquartered in Gaithersburg, Maryland, that pioneered adenovector (AdenoVerse) gene-delivery technology to develop gene-based therapeutics and vaccines, including programs for hearing loss and balance disorders. Backed by Canaan Partners, ARCH Venture Partners, EDF Ventures and HealthCare Ventures, GenVec was acquired by Precigen (formerly Intrexon) on June 16, 2017 and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; the genvec.com domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: Geometer
providers.description: Geometer is a San Francisco-based business incubator that builds and launches innovative, technology-driven companies. It provides founding leadership, physical facilities, guidance, camaraderie, and funding to early-stage teams building game-changing products, in San Francisco and around the world. Geometer operates as a company studio and accelerator rather than a software vendor; as of this profile it publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or technical documentation. It was surfaced through the Bloomberg Beta portfolio graph and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead. Contact is via contact@geometer.io, and the studio is located at 530 Jackson St, 3F, San Francisco, CA 94133.

providers.name: Get Satisfaction
providers.description: Get Satisfaction was a customer-community and engagement SaaS platform that gave companies a hosted online community where customers, employees, and prospects could ask questions, report problems, share ideas, and offer praise in public topic threads. Founded in 2007, it popularized the customer-powered support community model and offered widgets, community moderation, and integrations that companies embedded on their websites and product pages. Get Satisfaction was acquired by the social customer experience management company Sprinklr in 2015 and folded into Sprinklr's platform; the standalone product and its developer program have since been discontinued. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record (backed by Uncork Capital); it no longer operates a live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Getable
providers.description: Getable is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Historically Getable operated a construction and equipment rental marketplace/software platform (getable.com). As of this enrichment pass the original company appears inactive; the getable.com domain resolves to a general home-services and equipment-rental lead-generation marketplace with no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or other public API surface. No OpenAPI, MCP, or agent-facing artifacts could be sourced, so this profile remains an identity stub rather than a scored API provider.

providers.name: Getaway
providers.description: Getaway was a consumer hospitality startup that operated a network of minimalist tiny cabins ("Outposts") in nature within a couple hours' drive of major US cities, letting people book short, disconnected nature escapes. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of cowboy-ventures (sector: consumer). The company was acquired by Marriott International and rebranded as "Postcard Cabins" under Marriott's Outdoor Collection; the getaway.house domain now 301-redirects entirely to the Marriott Postcard Cabins brand page. Getaway operates a consumer booking website only and publishes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface, so this profile carries identity metadata rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: GetGlue
providers.description: GetGlue was a social-entertainment "check-in" network where users checked in to TV shows, movies, sports, music, and books to earn stickers and badges and see what friends were watching. Founded by Alex Iskold and backed by Union Square Ventures, it offered a public API and social graph for entertainment. GetGlue was acquired by i.TV in late 2013, rebranded to tvtag, and the service was discontinued. The getglue.com domain is now a parked lander with no live product, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Getlinks
providers.description: GetLinks is an AI-powered hiring operating system for Southeast Asia, operating across Thailand, Singapore, and Vietnam. For employers it provides job posting, AI-driven candidate screening, structured interview tooling with video/audio scoring, and recruiter consulting services; for job seekers it offers job search (14,200+ active jobs in Thailand), salary intelligence sourced from real placements, AI CV readiness analysis, and mock interview training. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal was found; the platform is an end-user recruitment and career product.

providers.name: Ghost Robotics
providers.description: Ghost Robotics designs and manufactures quadrupedal unmanned ground vehicles (Q-UGV), with its flagship Vision 60 platform deployed across defense, public safety, law enforcement, industrial, construction, and education customers. The platform supports modular payloads for sensing, comms, and manipulation. Ghost Robotics provides a developer SDK only to vetted partners and integrators and does not operate a public developer portal, open API, or public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Gilmour Space
providers.description: Gilmour Space Technologies is an Australian venture-backed space company headquartered on the Gold Coast in Queensland, founded in 2012 by brothers Adam and James Gilmour. The company designs and manufactures hybrid-propulsion orbital launch vehicles (the Eris rocket) and satellite platforms (the G-class / ElaraSat bus), and operates the Bowen Orbital Spaceport in North Queensland from which it is pursuing Australia's first sovereign orbital launch. Gilmour Space is backed by investors including Blackbird Ventures, Main Sequence Ventures, 500 Global, Fine Structure Ventures and HESTA. It is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the company operates in aerospace and space launch and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Gilt
providers.description: Gilt (Gilt Groupe) is a members-only flash-sale e-commerce retailer offering limited-time sales on designer and luxury fashion, accessories, home goods, and travel at discounted prices. Founded in 2007, Gilt pioneered the flash-sale model in the United States, hosting time-boxed curated sales events for a member base. The company was acquired by Hudson's Bay Company in 2016 and later combined with Rue La La to form Rue Gilt Groupe. Gilt operates primarily as a consumer-facing web and mobile shopping experience; it does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Gilt Groupe
providers.description: Gilt Groupe is a New York-based online retailer that pioneered the "flash sale" model in the United States, offering limited-time, members-only sales of discounted designer fashion, luxury goods, home items, and travel. Founded in 2007, Gilt was acquired by Hudson's Bay Company in 2016 and subsequently sold to Rue La La in 2018, forming Rue Gilt Groupe; the gilt.com storefront remains operational. Gilt's engineering team was an influential early adopter of Scala and microservices and open-sourced roughly fifty JVM libraries (the "gfc" Gilt Foundation Classes, Handlebars-Scala, sbt plugins) to Maven Central under the com.gilt groupId. Gilt operated no public REST API at the time of this enrichment pass - its historical developer.gilt.com API and the github.com/gilt organization are both retired. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.description: Add dynamically generated statistics to your GitHub profile ReadMe

providers.name: Gitprime
providers.description: GitPrime was a software engineering analytics and developer-productivity company founded in 2015 in Durango, Colorado, backed by Y Combinator and DCVC. Its product mined data from Git repositories, code review, and ticketing systems to give engineering leaders visibility into team throughput, code churn, and delivery health. Pluralsight acquired GitPrime in 2019 (~$170M) and rebranded it as Pluralsight Flow; in February 2025 Appfire acquired Flow from Pluralsight, and Appfire has announced that Flow will be discontinued on December 31, 2027. The independent gitprime.com domain no longer resolves and www.gitprime.com redirects to appfire.com/flow/info, so there is no standalone GitPrime developer portal, public API, or specification to enrich; any surviving API functionality now lives under the Appfire Flow product. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct company record.

providers.name: Glintinc
providers.description: Glint (Glint Inc), founded in 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, built a people-success and employee-engagement platform centered on frequent pulse surveys, engagement analytics, and manager action-planning to help organizations measure and improve employee experience. LinkedIn acquired Glint in November 2018, and the product was subsequently folded into Microsoft Viva as Viva Glint. There is no standalone Glint developer portal or public API: the former glintinc.com domain now 302-redirects to Microsoft's Viva Glint community, and the offering is delivered and documented through Microsoft Viva. This profile is retained for network lineage as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company that was acquired rather than an independently operating API provider.

providers.name: Glints
providers.description: Glints is a talent recruitment and career development platform headquartered in Singapore and operating across Southeast Asia, including Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Taiwan and the Philippines. Founded in 2013, it runs an online job marketplace connecting job seekers with employers, a curated headhunting service (TalentHunt), and a cross-border managed-talent / remote-hiring offering that lets companies build and employ distributed teams across the region. Glints also publishes career resources and expert classes. It is one of the largest talent ecosystems in Southeast Asia and is backed by investors including DCM Ventures, Monk's Hill Ventures and PERSOL. This API Evangelist profile was added as a portfolio-company lead; Glints exposes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Glo Pharma
providers.description: GLO Pharma is a beauty and aesthetics company developing next-generation products for at-home use, best known for the subtopical skincare brand Ourself. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (Series A, 2020), the company operates as a direct-to-consumer beauty and personal-care business rather than a technology or API provider: it sells physical skincare and aesthetic products to end consumers and does not publish a developer platform, public API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed portfolio company profile; enrichment found no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Glow
providers.description: Glow (glow.fm) was a podcast subscription and membership monetization platform that let podcasters run paid, listener-supported premium feeds. The standalone product has since been folded into Libsyn: as of this enrichment pass the glow.fm domain issues a 301 redirect to Libsyn's podcast-monetization offering, its TLS certificate has expired, and no active developer portal, API, documentation, or SDK surface remains under the Glow brand. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead (a16z, Norwest Venture Partners, Union Square Ventures) and has no live API to enrich.

providers.name: GlowRoad
providers.description: GlowRoad is an Indian social-commerce and reselling platform, headquartered in Bengaluru and founded in 2017, that enabled individuals — predominantly home-based women entrepreneurs — to resell fashion, home, and lifestyle products to their social networks over WhatsApp and Facebook without holding inventory. The company was acquired by Amazon India in 2021 and its reselling model was subsequently folded into Amazon's operations. GlowRoad runs a consumer mobile app and a supplier-onboarding funnel rather than a public developer program; as of this enrichment pass no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or partner API surface is published, and the public web endpoints return HTTP 503.

providers.name: GLP
providers.description: GLP is a leading global logistics real estate and investment management company, developing and operating warehouses, distribution centers, and supply-chain infrastructure alongside a large fund and asset-management business. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of hillhouse and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Sector: logistics. As of this enrichment pass GLP publishes a WAF-protected corporate website but no discoverable public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal; this profile remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: GMR
providers.description: GMR (General Mining Research) is a crypto and Web3 company backed by Multicoin Capital and tracked in the API Evangelist network. Its public presence is a single-page web application at gmr.xyz identifying it as "General Mining Research" with a general contact at info@gmr.xyz. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, well-known discovery surface, or SDK/CLI could be found — the only machine-verifiable signal is the domain's TLS/DNS security posture. This profile remains a lead awaiting a published API or developer surface to enrich further.

providers.name: Gnip
providers.description: Gnip was a social media data aggregation company founded in 2008 in Boulder, Colorado by Eric Marcoullier and Jud Valeski. It became the first authorized reseller of the Twitter "firehose" and delivered enterprise-grade access to real-time and historical social data from Twitter, Tumblr, WordPress, Disqus, StockTwits and many other sources through products such as PowerTrack, Historical PowerTrack, the Search API, the Audience API and the Engagement API. Twitter acquired Gnip in April 2014 and folded its technology into Twitter's enterprise data platform; the Gnip brand and standalone APIs were retired and gnip.com now 301-redirects to the Twitter/X enterprise developer documentation. This profile is preserved for historical/network completeness — Gnip is no longer an independent provider.

providers.name: Go Deed
providers.description: Go Deed (legally Deed Inc.) is a workplace-giving and corporate social responsibility platform founded in 2016 that helps enterprises engage employees around volunteering, charitable giving, donation matching, and everyday social-impact actions. With teams in New York, San Francisco, and Berlin, Deed served Fortune 500 and mid-market employers before being acquired into Bonterra, where it now ships as the "Deed" employee-engagement product. The joindeed.com domain 301-redirects to bonterratech.com/product/deed. Deed was surfaced as an Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company (investment 2021) and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no independent public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification for the standalone Go Deed / Deed brand.

providers.name: GoatChat AI - Adaptive Plus Inc.
providers.description: GoatChat AI - Adaptive Plus Inc. is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: GoDays
providers.description: GoDays is an AI-powered workforce analytics platform for enterprises that predicts and helps prevent employee burnout. It analyzes internal company data — keyboard usage behaviors, employee sentiment, interactions, performance, and feedback — to measure and forecast burnout risk, then surfaces recommendations to improve workflow, productivity, and employee wellbeing. Founded in 2021 and based in Seoul (Gangnam), South Korea, the company was co-founded by CEO Yelnur Kai and Adiar Bopov, and raised a seed round in 2024 with participation from 500 Global and Domino VC. GoDays was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site only, with no public API, developer portal, or specification surface.

providers.name: gohoo
providers.description: gohoo was a boutique e-commerce company based in Hangzhou, China (founded circa 2001) that linked high-quality goods to supplier channels by integrating the factory supply chain to reduce brand premium. It raised a seed round in 2018 and a Series A in March 2019 with backing from Qiming Venture Partners and Bertelsmann Asia Investments. The company is no longer active (deadpooled), and its gohoo.com domain now redirects to an atom.com domain-for-sale landing page. No live company website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists, so there is nothing to enrich beyond this honest identity record.

providers.name: GoInstant
providers.description: GoInstant was a Canadian (Halifax, Nova Scotia) real-time collaboration startup, founded in 2011, that provided a JavaScript API and backend-as-a-service for building multi-user, real-time web applications — shared browsing / co-browsing, live data synchronization, and presence. Developers embedded a hosted client library to add real-time collaboration (shared cursors, forms, and widgets) to a web page without plugins. Salesforce acquired GoInstant on 2012-07-09 (reported at ~$70M) and folded the technology into its platform; the standalone GoInstant developer service and website were subsequently discontinued (gone by late 2014). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record — GoInstant is a defunct provider with no live API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Good & Co.
providers.description: Good & Co. (Good&Co Labs, Inc.) was a Techstars-backed startup that built a research-driven psychometric and culture-fit platform for hiring and employee engagement, using Big Five-based personality assessments to match candidates, teammates, and workplaces via a proprietary FitScore. As of this enrichment pass the original company appears defunct with no live developer or API surface, and the good.co domain now resolves to an unrelated third-party logistics (3PL) fulfillment business.

providers.name: Good Glamm Group
providers.description: Good Glamm Group is an India-based content-to-commerce conglomerate in the personal care and cosmetics sector, founded in September 2021 by Darpan Sanghvi, Priyanka Gill, and Naiyya Saggi and briefly valued as a unicorn after 2021 Series D funding. Its house of brands includes MyGlamm, St.Botanica, The Moms Co, Sirona, Organic Harvest, POPxo, ScoopWhoop, BabyChakra, MissMalini, and Tweak, spanning India, Dubai, Singapore, and the USA. The group was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Prosus Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the goodglamm.com domain serves a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) stakeholder portal, and no public developer API or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Good Manufacturing Practices
providers.description: A system of processes, procedures, and documentation that ensures products are consistently produced and controlled according to quality standards, commonly used in pharmaceutical, food, and medical device manufacturing. Proper implementation reduces legal and operational risk while supporting audit readiness.

providers.name: Good Technology
providers.description: Good Technology was an enterprise mobile security company whose Good Dynamics platform provided app-level encryption, data loss prevention, secure inter-app communication, and a secure application-development SDK/API used by ISVs, systems integrators, and enterprises to build secured mobile apps across iOS and Android. The company served more than 6,200 organizations, including over half of the Fortune 100. Good Technology was acquired by BlackBerry in October 2015 for approximately $425 million and folded into BlackBerry's enterprise mobility (UEM) portfolio; it no longer operates as an independent entity and its former developer surface (good.com) now redirects to blackberry.com. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Goodlegal
providers.description: Goodlegal was a Bucharest-based legal-tech startup founded in 2021 by Vasile Tiple (former UiPath Head of Legal Automation) building a legal infrastructure platform and "one-stop shop for legal compliance" — a drag-and-drop document builder, out-of-the-box document templates, an editor with text analysis, e-signature, workflow automation, and integrations aimed at standardizing legal work for individuals and organizations. It raised a ~EUR 1.2M pre-seed round in 2022 led by Earlybird's Digital East Fund. The company wound down and shut off its platform at the end of 2023 (per founder Vasile Tiple's "Final thoughts on Goodlegal" post), and the goodlegal.io domain is now parked / listed for sale. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API surface was ever published, and none exists today. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Goodme
providers.description: Goodme (brand "Good me", Chinese: 古茗; legal entity Guming Holdings Limited) is one of China's largest freshly-made tea-beverage franchise chains, founded in 2010 by Wang Yun'an and headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang. It sells fruit tea, milk tea, and coffee through a franchise model concentrated in China's lower-tier cities, and had grown to roughly 9,800 outlets nationwide by late 2024. The company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (SEHK: 1364) in February 2025, raising about US$233 million. It is a consumer-sector portfolio company of HongShan and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a food-and-beverage retail franchise, Goodme publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or agent-facing surface at this time.

providers.name: GoodsMart International
providers.description: GoodsMart is a Cairo-based premium grocery and household e-commerce delivery startup serving compounds across 6th of October, Sheikh Zayed, and New Cairo. Founded by Rami Fawzi and co-founders (soft-launched 2014, officially launched 2015), it pioneered contactless overnight grocery delivery in Egypt, dropping orders into a pre-installed GoodsMart box outside the customer's home between midnight and 6am. The company operates a consumer-facing mobile app and web storefront for groceries, personal care, and home-care products. It has raised roughly $4.37M from investors including 500 Global, Sawari Ventures, Algebra Ventures, and Savour Ventures. As of this profile, GoodsMart publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this remains a company/lead record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Gotiger
providers.description: GoTiger is a Berlin-based food company that operates multiple delivery-first food brands out of modern ghost kitchens, including Bok Bok Chicken, GoDumpling and Kyoo Chicken. Founded in 2022, the company began as GoTiger Asia Grocery Delivery, a same-day app-based service delivering Japanese, Korean and Chinese groceries and everyday essentials across Berlin and Potsdam on a Shopify Plus backend, before pivoting to a portfolio of virtual restaurant brands. GoTiger is a consumer product company backed by Speedinvest, Adjacent, Nucleus Capital and Shio Capital; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time.

providers.name: GoTiny
providers.description: A lightweight URL shortener, focused on ease-of-use for the developer and end-user

providers.name: Gowalla
providers.description: Gowalla is a location-based social check-in application that lets people keep up with their friends in the real world by checking in at places, sharing their location, and collecting stamps and passport-style travel memories. Originally launched in 2007 as a pioneering location-based social game, Gowalla was acquired by Facebook in 2011 and wound down in 2012, then relaunched by founder Josh Williams in March 2023 as an iOS app before active development was paused in April 2023. The app remains available on the App Store and continues to operate on a limited basis, recruiting early testers through its Street Team program. Gowalla historically published a Check-In API with OAuth 2 support (2010), but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation is available today. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector lead.

providers.name: Goyaz Silver Jewellery
providers.description: Goyaz Silver Jewellery is a Hyderabad-based Indian jewellery retail brand founded in January 2023 by Priyanka Vemuluri, specializing in 92.5 premium and gold-plated silver jewellery that blends traditional Indian craftsmanship with contemporary, occasion-led design. Operating a chain of 18 retail stores across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka (including Kukatpally, Punjagutta, Suchitra Circle, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam), Goyaz positions gold-plated silver as an accessible luxury alternative to gold. In October 2025 the company raised a Rs 130 crore (~$14.6M) Series A round led by Norwest Venture Partners, its first institutional funding, to expand its retail footprint, strengthen design and manufacturing, and enhance its omnichannel experience. The company operates an online storefront and social commerce presence but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: Graft
providers.description: Graft was a San Francisco-based AI platform company founded in 2021 by Adam Oliner (former Head of Machine Learning at Slack and Splunk) and Eric Schkufza. Its "Intelligence Layer" operationalized foundation models — LLMs and multimodal models over text, images, audio, video and graphs — connecting internal documents, databases and knowledge bases so organizations could build production-grade generative, predictive and structured-analytics solutions without deep machine-learning expertise or infrastructure. Graft raised a $4.5M pre-seed led by GV (2022) and a $10M seed led by Radical Ventures (2023). In October 2025 the Graft team and technology were acquired by You.com, with Adam Oliner joining as Field CTO; the graft.com domain is no longer operated by the company and no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remains.

providers.name: Graft Concepts
providers.description: Graft Concepts was a consumer-electronics accessories company best known for the "Leverage" modular iPhone case, a latched aluminum-and-polycarbonate bumper frame with interchangeable backplates that let owners swap in kickstands, bike mounts, and 3D-printed backs. The company was a Y Combinator startup based in the San Francisco Bay Area and was acquired by Inseego (formerly Novatel Wireless) in January 2014, after which the independent product and brand were wound down. This profile was surfaced by the venture-portfolio scraper and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found no live developer surface, API, SDK, or documentation for the company. The original graftconcepts.com domain no longer serves the company and now resolves to a parked content page, so there are no API artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: Grana
providers.description: Grana was a Hong Kong-based direct-to-consumer fashion brand founded in October 2014 by Luke Grana and Pieter-Paul Wittgen, selling premium wardrobe basics made from directly-sourced fabrics — Peruvian pima cotton, Chinese silk, Japanese denim, European linen, cashmere, merino and baby alpaca — online without retail middlemen. It raised roughly US$16M across seed and Series A rounds from investors including Alibaba's Hong Kong Entrepreneurs Fund, 500 Startups (now 500 Global), Golden Gate Ventures, MindWorks Ventures and the Bluebell Group. The company has since wound down; grana.com now resolves to a parked domain with no live storefront, developer program, or public API.

providers.name: Graph Countries
providers.description: Country-related data like currencies, languages, flags, regions+subregions and bordering countries

providers.name: graphenest.com
providers.description: Graphenest is a Portuguese nano-cleantech company that develops sustainable, high-performance graphene-based materials for electromagnetic interference (EMI/EMC/RF) shielding. Its proprietary, scalable and low-energy graphene production process powers two industrial-ready product lines: HexaShield, a sprayable conductive coating for high-frequency applications, and G-Shield, a family of conductive thermoplastics for extrusion and injection moulding, plus the G-Prime graphene material. The solutions deliver higher shielding performance at lower cost and weight (up to 75% lighter than metal alternatives) for Tier 1/Tier 2 manufacturers in batteries, electronics, telecom (radar, LiDAR, 5G/6G), and cables & wires. Graphenest is a materials and manufacturing company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars-linked portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Graphicly
providers.description: Graphicly was a digital-comics and e-book distribution and self-publishing platform, founded around 2009 in Austin, Texas, that let independent creators and publishers convert their work and distribute it across major reading platforms including Amazon Kindle, Apple iBooks, Barnes & Noble Nook, and Google Play. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) among other investors, the company was acquired by Blurb in 2014 and its distribution service was subsequently discontinued. The graphicly.com domain no longer serves a live product, and the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph and historical reference; enrichment found no live API, SDK, event, or security surface to harvest.

providers.name: Graphiq
providers.description: Graphiq was a creative-technology startup founded in 2015 that set out to disrupt the traditional agency model by connecting companies with vetted graphic designers through a flexible design-subscription service. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Klingit in July 2024 and its brand folded into Klingit; the graphiq.design domain now redirects to klingit.com. Graphiq operated as a design-services marketplace and offered no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GraphQL Pokemon
providers.description: GraphQL powered Pokemon API. Supports generations 1 through 8

providers.name: Graviti
providers.description: Graviti is a Mexico City-based consumer fintech founded in 2020 that unlocks affordable access to essential home utilities for unbanked and underserved Mexican families, starting with solar water heaters financed through a pay-as-you-go (PayGo / BNPL) model of small recurring payments. Backed by 500 Global, Clocktower Technology Ventures, Mucker Capital, Active Capital, and BFA Global's Catalyst Fund, the company combines hardware installation with embedded consumer lending. Graviti is a consumer-facing product company and does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with an honest no-API-surface result.

providers.name: Gravity Sketch
providers.description: Gravity Sketch is a 3D design and modeling application built for spatial creation, letting designers sketch, model, and iterate on concepts in virtual reality (Meta Quest, PC VR) and on tablet. It is widely used across automotive, footwear, industrial, and product design for early-stage ideation and collaborative review, backed by a cloud collaboration platform (LandingPad) for sharing and version history. The company is a creative-tools maker rather than an API-first provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, or documented webhook surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel, GV, and Point Nine and captures the company identity plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: GreatHorn
providers.description: GreatHorn was a cloud-native email security company founded in 2015 in Waltham, Massachusetts, providing anti-phishing, spear-phishing, business email compromise (BEC), and account-takeover protection for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. Backed by Uncork Capital, it was acquired by Hornetsecurity in 2021. As of enrichment (July 2026) the greathorn.com domain returns HTTP 404 (Cloudflare, acquired/retired) and the company publishes no live developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface. No public API artifacts were found to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record.

providers.name: GreenBytes
providers.description: GreenBytes was a data-storage and desktop-virtualization company (patented VDI IO-offload and inline data deduplication) backed by Battery Ventures, and was acquired by Oracle in June 2014. Its product line was absorbed into Oracle and the former green-bytes.com domain now redirects to Oracle Support. The company has no independent, active developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or public API surface, so the enrichment pipeline found no real API artifacts to add. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio-lead stub.

providers.name: Greenfield Online
providers.description: Greenfield Online, Inc. (Nasdaq SRVY) was an independent provider of Internet-based survey solutions and online market-research panels, headquartered in Wilton, Connecticut. Founded in 1994, it pioneered online panel sampling and data collection for the marketing-research industry, went public in 2004, and grew by acquiring sampling firms worldwide (including European comparison-shopping service Ciao). Microsoft acquired the company in 2008 for roughly $486 million to obtain Ciao, then divested the survey and sampling assets to Toluna in 2009. Greenfield Online no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer program, public API, or live web presence today. This record is retained as a portfolio-lead profile surfaced from the Insight Partners portfolio.

providers.name: Greif
providers.description: Greif is an industrial packaging products and services leader with a vision to be the best performing customer service company in the world. Greif also offers digital tools such as the Greif Green Tool carbon footprint calculator and the Greif+ online platform for customers.

providers.name: Greypoint Industries
providers.description: Greypoint Industries is a Canadian defense-technology company (Y Combinator S26) building passive RF mapping software that charts the electromagnetic spectrum so operators can see every signal, track every threat, and act first — "built in Canada for those who protect." Founded in 2026 by Nic Chu, Jordan Khoo, Steven Xu, and Darcy Zhang, the company also develops mass-produced autonomous counter-drone interceptors designed to defeat drone-swarm saturation at a fraction of the cost of the targets. As an early-stage hardware and software startup, Greypoint currently publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures the company's identity for the API Evangelist network and awaits a developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Gridsnap
providers.description: Gridsnap is a Los Angeles-based gaming studio founded in 2024 and part of the a16z Speedrun Cohort 002. The studio builds interactive worlds for community, powered by user-generated content (UGC), primarily using Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN). Its work spans three areas - developing original IP, partnering with influencers to create community spaces inside Fortnite, and investing in emerging game developers by taking stakes in their projects while providing development support. Gridsnap publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation; this profile is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Grokstyle
providers.description: GrokStyle was a visual-search / computer-vision startup (a Cornell Tech spinout) that let users find products such as furniture and home decor from a photo, backed by Canaan Partners. It was acquired by Facebook in early 2019 and wound down. As of this enrichment pass its domain (grokstyle.com) is registered but resolves to no nameservers, there is no live website, developer portal, API, SDK, or GitHub organization, so there is no public API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Group Nine Media
providers.description: Group Nine Media was a New York-based digital-media holding company formed in 2016 through the merger of Discovery Digital with the original Group Nine, uniting the news brand NowThis, the animal brand The Dodo, the lifestyle brand Thrillist, and the science brand Seeker under one roof (it later added PopSugar). Backed by Discovery Inc. and venture investor IVP, it built large social-video and branded-content audiences before it was acquired by Vox Media in February 2022 and folded into that portfolio. Group Nine operated as a consumer media publisher, not an API provider: it did not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable API surface, and its groupnine.com domain now resolves to a third-party domain-sale landing page. This profile is retained as a VC-portfolio identity record with no scorable API artifacts.

providers.name: Groupalia
providers.description: Groupalia was a Spanish group-buying / daily-deals company (a Groupon-style local commerce marketplace) founded in 2010 and backed by investors including Insight Partners, operating across Spain, Italy and parts of Latin America before consolidating in the group-buying downturn. The brand's only active surface today is the Italian domain groupalia.it, a gift-card storefront whose checkout is operated by EPIPOLI S.p.A. (mygiftcard.it); the original www.groupalia.com domain no longer resolves. No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or agent-facing surface is published, so this profile remains a consumer-company identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Growth Networks
providers.description: Growth Networks was a networking-silicon startup founded in the late 1990s that developed a new category of switching hardware it branded Internet Switching Fabrics — scalable, multi-service capacity silicon for high-speed network switches and routers. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (co-founded by Barry Eggers), the company was acquired by Cisco Systems in 2000 and folded into Cisco's core routing and switching business. It operates no independent developer platform or public API today; this profile is retained as a venture-portfolio historical record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: GTR
providers.description: GTR (Global Top Round) was a mobile game accelerator program that annually selected roughly ten indie mobile game studios, providing them global publishing connections, real global game-market and network access, mentorship, and fundraising support through a six-month accelerator program and the Global Top Round global mobile game conference. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of enrichment (July 2026) the company website globaltopround.com no longer resolves (no DNS A/NS records) and GTR appears to be defunct; it exposes no public API, developer platform, documentation, or SDK, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Guardicore
providers.description: Guardicore is a micro-segmentation and Zero Trust network security company, founded in 2013 and backed by Battery Ventures and Partech, best known for its Centra platform for software-defined segmentation, application dependency mapping, and lateral-movement threat containment across data center, cloud, and hybrid environments. Guardicore was acquired by Akamai in 2021 and its technology now ships as Akamai Guardicore Segmentation; the guardicore.com domain redirects to the Akamai Segmentation product. This profile tracks Guardicore as a distinct company in the API Evangelist network. Its API reference is delivered through Akamai TechDocs and is login-gated, so no public OpenAPI or standalone developer surface was discoverable during enrichment.

providers.name: Guesser
providers.description: Guesser was a startup surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Per Version One Ventures' own portfolio listing, Guesser was acquired by Gemini in 2021 and no longer operates as an independent company. During the enrichment pass no live company website, developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or other public developer surface could be located (its likely domain guesser.io does not resolve), so no provider artifacts were produced. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record.

providers.name: Guild Technologies
providers.description: Guild Technologies was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass (2026-07-20) confirmed against Battery Ventures' own company list (battery.com/list-of-all-companies) that Guild Technologies is an exited investment, and found no discoverable live website, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface. All plausible domains (guildtech.com, guildtechnologies.com, guild.io, guild.tech) are parked/for-sale or dead. This is not the open-source GraphQL group "The Guild" (the-guild.dev), whose products are already catalogued separately (graphql-hive, graphql-mesh, graphql-yoga, graphql-codegen). No API artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived — this remains an unresolved historical lead.
