providers.name: Gurú de Viaje
providers.description: Gurú de Viaje is a Mexico-based travel-deals company and flight-deal hunter ("cazador de ofertas de viaje") that publishes daily cheap-flight promotions and airfare offers so travelers can fly cheaply and see the world. Its Spanish-language consumer website and mobile/push experience surface daily discounted airline tickets and travel promotions, with a focus on departures from Mexican cities such as Guadalajara and Mexico City. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass Gurú de Viaje operates a consumer Next.js web property (gurudeviaje.com) and publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: GW2Spidy
providers.description: GW2Spidy API, Items data on the Guild Wars 2 Trade Market

providers.name: GYENNO
providers.description: GYENNO is a medical technology company that designs assistive devices and digital-health tools for people living with Parkinson's disease and other movement disorders. Its consumer product line includes the GYENNO Bravo anti-tremor eating utensil (a stabilizing, weighted spoon/fork that counteracts hand tremor) and the GYENNO Skywalk portable freezing-of-gait mobility aid that projects a visual laser cue to help users resume walking, alongside a range of adaptive and weighted utensils and daily-living aids. GYENNO was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer marketing site only and exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Gymboree
providers.description: Gymboree is a children's apparel and accessories retailer selling clothing for babies, toddlers, and kids up to age 12 through its consumer e-commerce site at gymboree.com. The brand is owned and operated by The Children's Place, Inc. (headquartered at 500 Plaza Drive, Secaucus, NJ). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Gymboree publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine interface: its site is a purely consumer-facing retail storefront, so no API artifacts (OpenAPI, MCP, SDKs, webhooks) exist to harvest. This profile carries only the identity and infrastructure-security probe of the gymboree.com domain.

providers.name: H World Group
providers.description: H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group) is one of the world's largest multi-brand hotel operators, headquartered in Shanghai, China and founded in 2005 by Ji Qi. It franchises, manages, and leases-and-operates thousands of hotels across economy-to-luxury tiers under brands including HanTing, Ji Hotel, Orange, Hi Inn, Elan, Starway, Crystal Orange, Manxin, Madison, Blossom House, CitiGO and Ni Hao, plus the upscale European Deutsche Hospitality portfolio (Steigenberger, IntercityHotel, MAXX, Jaz in the City, Zleep) and the H Rewards loyalty program. The company is dual-listed on NASDAQ (HTHT) and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (1179). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; H World is a consumer hospitality operator and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: H.B. Fuller
providers.description: H.B. Fuller is a leading global adhesives provider focused on perfecting adhesives, sealants, and other specialty chemical products for consumer, durable assembly, electronics, hygiene, packaging, and other industrial markets. No public developer portal or production APIs are advertised on the corporate website.

providers.name: Habeas
providers.description: Habeas was an email reputation and deliverability services provider that helped legitimate senders monitor and manage their sending reputation to maximize inbox deliverability, using a trademark-based accreditation and safelist model to certify permission-based email. Founded in the mid-2000s and backed by Canaan Partners through a Series B round, Habeas was acquired by Return Path in 2008 (habeas.com now redirects to returnpath.com); Return Path was in turn acquired by Validity in 2019. The company is defunct as an independent brand and publishes no live public API or developer surface, so this profile is retained as a Canaan Partners portfolio-history record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: HackerNews
providers.description: Social news for CS and entrepreneurship

providers.name: HAGS
providers.description: HAGS is a consumer-sector company listed in the portfolio of GV (Google Ventures) and tracked in the API Evangelist network. Its website, hags.com, is live but served behind Cloudflare, which challenge-blocks automated crawling (HTTP 403 on every path), so no public developer program, OpenAPI definition, API reference, or documentation surface could be located during enrichment. This profile is maintained as a lightweight company lead and will be expanded if and when HAGS publishes a developer or API surface.

providers.name: Hain Celestial Group
providers.description: The Hain Celestial Group is a leading organic and natural products company providing consumers with A Healthier Way of Life through a portfolio of natural, organic, and better-for-you brands. No public APIs or developer programs have been identified for Hain Celestial Group at this time.

providers.name: Hanqi Group
providers.description: Beijing Hanqi Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. (Hanqi Group) is a Beijing-based environmental technology company specializing in full-process chemical and oily wastewater treatment for the petrochemical, coal-chemical, new-energy, industrial-park, and municipal sectors. With roughly 17 years of operating history, 140+ client references, and 80+ patents across physicochemical, biochemical, and oxidation process categories, Hanqi delivers engineered water-treatment technologies and services rather than software. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Public research confirms no developer, API, SDK, or agent surface exists for this provider.

providers.name: haoyiku
providers.description: Haoyiku (好衣库) is a Chinese private-domain social e-commerce and brand flash-sale platform operated by Haoyiku (Hangzhou) Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. and associated with Jingling Group, founded in December 2017. It equips millions of individual store owners with a one-click storefront, dropship supply chain, private-domain traffic tooling, operations training, and after-sales services, spanning apparel, footwear, bags, cosmetics, personal care, mother-and-baby, and daily-necessities categories across more than 15,000 brand partnerships. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, Haoyiku is a consumer mobile-app business with no public developer platform or API program; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Happy Elements
providers.description: Happy Elements is a mobile game developer and publisher, backed by DCM Ventures, best known for free-to-play titles such as the Ensemble Stars! rhythm/idol franchise and Merc Storia. Operating across China and Japan, the company builds consumer entertainment games distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play rather than a public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector portfolio profile; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface, so the only machine-verifiable artifact is a probed domain-security posture for happyelements.com.

providers.name: Hardware Intelligence
providers.description: Hardware Intelligence is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup based in San Francisco building an end-to-end, agent-native toolchain for chip design. Founded in 2026 by Athreya Anand, the company applies agentic AI and ultrafast feedback loops to the semiconductor design and verification workflow. Its first product, Wave, is a terminal-native waveform debugger with a verification agent built in, aimed at accelerating hardware debugging and design iteration. At the time of profiling the company is pre-launch with early-access pilots and a waitlist; it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity only and awaits a developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Harvard Art Museums
providers.description: Art

providers.name: Hassle
providers.description: Hassle.com was a London-based on-demand home-cleaning marketplace, founded in 2012 by Alex Depledge and Jules Coleman, connecting households with vetted local cleaners for one-off and recurring bookings. Backed by Accel Partners, it was acquired by Rocket Internet-backed Helpling in July 2015 for a reported EUR 32 million to form one of the world's largest home-cleaning marketplaces. The Hassle.com brand was subsequently folded into Helpling, whose UK operations have since ceased; the domain now redirects to Helpling. The company operates a consumer-facing web/mobile booking product and exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Hatcheri
providers.description: Hatcheri (Hatcheri Foods) is a food-focused incubator-accelerator based in San Leandro, California that partners with emerging food and beverage brands to build and scale them. Founded in 2013, it operates through three arms: Hatcheri Brands (leading day-to-day operations alongside founders), Hatcheri Advisory Services (hands-on strategic support across supply chain, marketing, sales, financial management, food safety, and product innovation), and Hatcheri Capital (investment and funding partnerships). Portfolio and partner brands include Sonoma Gourmet, Snapdragon, Fra' Mani, Sukhi's, and Sonoma Specialty Foods. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Hatcheri publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or technical documentation; this profile is a company/provider identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: HauteLook
providers.description: HauteLook was a members-only, flash-sale e-commerce destination for fashion, beauty, and home goods, founded in 2007 in Los Angeles. It was acquired by Nordstrom in 2011 and operated as a standalone flash-sale brand before being folded into Nordstrom Rack; www.hautelook.com now redirects to the Nordstrom Rack Flash storefront. The provider publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, so no API artifacts could be enriched during the pipeline pass.

providers.name: Haven
providers.description: Haven, Inc. was an ocean freight technology company founded in 2014 that built software to automate quoting, booking, document management, and shipment management for commodity producers, traders, and freight forwarders moving international ocean cargo. Backed by DCVC, Haven was acquired by supply-chain visibility platform FourKites in April 2021, and its technology became the foundation of FourKites' Dynamic Ocean product for end-to-end international ocean shipment visibility. Haven no longer operates an independent public developer program or API; the Haven brand survives only as the "Haven Marketplace" login at app.haveninc.com, now operated as part of FourKites.

providers.name: Hawaiian Holdings
providers.description: Hawaiian Holdings was the parent company of Hawaiian Airlines, the largest and longest-serving airline of Hawaii, providing scheduled passenger service to destinations across the Pacific. In 2024 the company combined with Alaska Air Group, and Hawaiian Holdings became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Alaska Air Group. No public developer portal or production-facing APIs are advertised.

providers.name: HawkEye 360
providers.description: HawkEye 360 is a Herndon, Virginia-based radio frequency (RF) data analytics and geospatial intelligence company that operates the first commercial satellite constellation purpose-built to identify, process, and geolocate a broad range of RF signals from space. Founded in 2015 by Chris DeMay, Charles Clancy, and Bob McGwier, the company flies clusters of three small satellites in formation that use time- and frequency-difference-of-arrival triangulation to pinpoint emitters across VHF through Ku-band. As of 2025, HawkEye 360 has placed 36 Hawk satellites on orbit across 12 operational clusters. Its core products include RFGeo (the underlying RF signal mapping and geolocation data product), RFIQ (its RF intelligence data product recently selected by NASA Commercial LEO programs), and Mission Space, a web-based RF geospatial intelligence analysis platform. The company also offers a Regional Awareness Subscription (RAS) service providing persistent monitoring of high-interest regions such as the Mediterranean, South China Sea, and the Korean Peninsula. In December 2023 HawkEye 360 acquired Maxar Intelligence's RF Solutions business (formerly Aurora Insight), expanding its spectrum-mapping capabilities. Customers are concentrated in defense, intelligence, national security, and maritime domain awareness — including the US Government, allied partners, and foreign military sales (a 2025 FMS to India was approved by the Defense Security Cooperation Agency). HawkEye 360 has filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO. There is no public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open-source release; data access is delivered through gated commercial and government contracts via the Mission Space platform and a customer-facing API for ordering and integration of RF analytics into customer systems.

providers.name: hayneedle.com (formerly know as NetShops)
providers.description: Hayneedle (formerly NetShops) was an online retailer of home goods, furniture, and outdoor products, founded as NetShops in Omaha, Nebraska in 2002 and rebranded to Hayneedle.com in 2009. It grew into a large specialty e-commerce operator running hundreds of niche home-and-lifestyle storefronts, and was acquired by Jet.com in 2016 for roughly $90 million, becoming a Walmart subsidiary after Walmart bought Jet.com. The standalone brand was subsequently wound down and hayneedle.com now redirects into walmart.com. It was listed as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no first-party public developer surface (no API docs, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or event surface); the only signal captured is honest DNS/TLS domain-security data for the still-resolving redirect domain.

providers.name: HD Supply Holdings
providers.description: HD Supply is one of the largest industrial distributors in North America, providing maintenance, repair, and operations products and value-added services to multifamily, hospitality, healthcare, and government facilities. HD Supply operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of The Home Depot following its acquisition in 2020.

providers.name: Hearst
providers.description: Hearst is a privately held, diversified American media, information, and services conglomerate headquartered in the Hearst Tower in New York City. Founded in 1887 by William Randolph Hearst, the company spans more than 360 businesses across magazines, newspapers, broadcast television, cable networks, business and financial information, healthcare information, automotive data, and venture investments. Hearst reported approximately US$13B in revenue (2024) with ~22,000 employees worldwide.

providers.name: HeartThis
providers.description: HeartThis was a mobile fashion shopping and discovery app, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and GV and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company appears defunct/absorbed: heartthis.com and www.heartthis.com now return a 301 redirect to an OpenSky content page (www.opensky.com/content/general/heartthis), the host serves a long-expired stale wildcard TLS certificate (CN wildcard auctivacommerce.com, expired 2022-12-16), and no api, developer, or docs subdomains resolve (NXDOMAIN). No public developer portal, documentation, or API surface could be found, so no API artifacts could be enriched without fabrication.

providers.name: HeartyyFresh
providers.description: HeartyyFresh is a mobile-first Indian grocery delivery service that lets customers order fresh Indian groceries and household staples for home delivery through its iOS and Android apps. The consumer offering centers on convenience and quality, promoting a first-time incentive of 20% off the first five orders placed through the app. HeartyyFresh operates as a direct-to-consumer grocery app (published under the com.rahein.heartyyfresh Android package and the "HeartyyFresh - Indian Grocery" iOS listing) rather than a developer platform; it exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched for identity only.

providers.name: Hedgeye
providers.description: Hedgeye Risk Management is an independent investment-research and financial-media firm founded in 2008 by Keith McCullough and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut. Hedgeye sells subscription research and market analysis to investors across macroeconomics, sector/vertical coverage, and individual securities, delivered through daily notes, models, and its Hedgeye TV video platform, newsletters, and live events. The company is best known for its data-driven, process-oriented "GIP" (growth, inflation, policy) macro framework and its independent, no-conflicts positioning relative to traditional Wall Street sell-side research. As surfaced in the API Evangelist network, Hedgeye operates a consumer/subscriber web application at app.hedgeye.com but does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface; this profile captures the identity and domain-security posture that could be verified without authenticated access.

providers.name: Heights Labs
providers.description: Heights Labs is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital, techstars and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Hello Alice
providers.description: Hello Alice is a free, multichannel digital platform that helps small business owners start, grow, and fund their businesses. Founded in 2017 by Carolyn Rodz and Elizabeth Gore, it connects millions of entrepreneurs to capital (grants and loans), a peer network, business-health tools, and educational resources, and partners with enterprises, financial institutions, and government programs to distribute grant funding and support to underserved small business owners. Backed by QED Investors among others. The company operates a consumer web application at helloalice.com; no public developer API or documented API program was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Hello Gold
providers.description: HelloGold is a Malaysian fintech company operating a mobile gold-savings app that lets everyday users buy, save, sell, send, and redeem 99.99% investment-grade gold starting from as little as RM1, with physical redemption from a minimum of 1 gram. Its SmartSaver feature runs an automated 12-month savings plan that buys gold at the lowest weekday price on the user's behalf. The service is Shariah-compliant (certified by Amanie Advisors), with gold stored in an insured and audited Singapore vault. HelloGold is a portfolio company of 500 Global and a recognized Islamic-fintech player. This profile is a consumer mobile-app company with no public developer/API surface identified during enrichment.

providers.name: HelloFlo
providers.description: HelloFlo was a women's-health startup (a 500 Global / 500 Startups portfolio company) known for its subscription boxes and viral marketing. As of this enrichment pass its helloflo.com domain returns a permanent 301 redirect to theflowspace.com (Flow Space), a women's-health digital media platform owned by Penske Media Corporation. HelloFlo no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any technical / developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct/redirected network lead; there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Herbeast
providers.description: Herbeast is a sustainable skin care and lifestyle brand based in China, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company explores the application of Chinese herbal essence to the skin, grounding its formulations in the concepts and technical principles of biomedicine. Founded and led by CEO Yisa He with Chief Scientist and co-founder Yanjing Bai, Herbeast operates as a consumer skin care and lifestyle products brand rather than an API-first technology provider. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; its only observed web property (herbeast.com) resolves to a deactivated Shopify storefront. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed portfolio identity record, not as an active API producer.

providers.name: Heroic Story
providers.description: Heroic Story was a Web3 gaming studio building a collaborative, community-owned tabletop role-playing game world — a Dungeons & Dragons-style on-chain MMORPG powered by smart contracts and NFTs on Polygon. Founded by Jay and Scott Rosenkrantz, it raised a $6M seed round in November 2022 led by Upfront Ventures with participation from Multicoin Capital and Polygon, bringing total financing to roughly $7.4M. As of this profiling the primary domain heroicstory.com resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander with no active product, documentation, developer, or API surface, indicating the project is dormant or defunct.

providers.name: Hexion
providers.description: Hexion is a global leader in thermosetting resins, providing a broad range of adhesive, structural, and specialty resins to a wide variety of industries including coatings, construction, electronics, and automotive. Their purpose is to activate science to change our world.

providers.name: Heygo
providers.description: Heygo (formerly GoGuides) was a London-based consumer platform for live, interactive virtual tours, where local guides livestreamed real-time walking tours of destinations around the world to remote audiences on a tip-based model. It was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Point Nine. As of this enrichment pass the public site origin is unreachable (HTTP 522 behind Cloudflare) with no mail (MX/SPF/DMARC) records, indicating the service is no longer operating; no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or other machine-readable API surface could be located.

providers.name: Heytea
providers.description: Heytea is a Chinese premium modern tea-beverage chain founded in 2012 in Jiangmen, Guangdong. It pioneered cheese-topped tea and fresh-fruit "new-style tea" and has grown to thousands of stores across mainland China and international markets including Singapore, the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and the United States. Backed by investors including Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China) and IDG Capital, Heytea runs its own mobile ordering app and retail loyalty program. As a consumer food-and-beverage retailer it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; this profile is retained in the network as a company identity lead.

providers.name: HiCustomer
providers.description: HiCustomer (ハイカスタマー) was a Japanese Customer Success Management (CSM) SaaS built specifically for SaaS companies. Its platform aggregated customer data scattered across BI tools, CRMs, and chat tools to visualize product usage, communication history, revenue, and contract information in one place. Teams used configurable health-score rules to monitor account health across the customer lifecycle, and custom alerts to surface churn and upsell signals at the right moment, with time-series analysis to make customer-success outreach repeatable. The company also offered customer-success consulting. As of this enrichment pass the hicustomer.jp domain no longer resolves to a live site (its authoritative AWS Route 53 zone is empty) and the product appears discontinued; the last archived homepage (Oct 2024) shows only a minimal "About the company" page. No public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal was ever published.

providers.name: Hidden Leaf Games
providers.description: Hidden Leaf Games is an independent video game development studio founded in 2019 and based in the United States. The studio builds competitive multiplayer games centered on competition, progression, and social play, with a stated mission of delivering a world-class experience where games are meant to be played together regardless of skill level or platform. The company is led by CEO David Li and President Bao Lam and raised seed funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2021. Hidden Leaf Games is a consumer gaming company and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile tracks it as a portfolio-sourced lead in the API Evangelist network for ongoing enrichment.

providers.name: High Jump Software
providers.description: HighJump Software was a Minneapolis-based provider of supply chain execution software, best known for its warehouse management system (WMS) and its extensible, configurable architecture for distribution, direct-store-delivery, and manufacturing operations. The company was acquired by Battery Ventures in 2014, expanded through acquisitions (Accellos, Nexus, TrueCommerce lines), then acquired by Körber in 2017 and folded into Körber Supply Chain Software. As of 2024 the portfolio was rebranded Infios. The standalone HighJump brand is retired: highjump.com now 301-redirects to infios.com, and the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification. This profile is retained as a historical / acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Highfive
providers.description: Highfive was a video collaboration and conferencing company (highfive.com) surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of gv and lightspeed-venture-partners. The brand was acquired by and folded into Dialpad: highfive.com now issues a 301 redirect to dialpad.com/highfive, and developer.highfive.com no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN). Highfive exposes no independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or /.well-known/ discovery surface of its own; any current programmatic capability lives under the Dialpad platform. This profile is retained as an enrichment lead; only a domain-security probe of the surviving highfive.com domain yielded real data.

providers.name: Highlight
providers.description: Highlight is a General Catalyst portfolio company added to the API Evangelist network as a stub via the VC-portfolio harvest. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no active developer API surface to catalog: the company's primary domain (highlightyourbrand.com) now returns only a JavaScript redirect to a parked "/lander" page, and the source portfolio harvest already flagged the entry as a non-API provider (is_api_provider false, no URL captured). Note that the developer-observability platform highlight.io is a DISTINCT company (YC-backed, acquired by LaunchDarkly) and is NOT this General Catalyst portfolio company, so its API artifacts were deliberately not attributed here.

providers.name: Hitwise
providers.description: Hitwise was an online competitive-intelligence and audience-measurement company that tracked website traffic, clickstream behavior, and search-term data to help marketers benchmark share of visits, referral sources, and competitor performance across industry verticals. Originally an Australian firm, it was later owned by Experian and then Connexity. The Hitwise brand has since been retired -- as of this enrichment pass the hitwise.com domain no longer serves a live product (it returns a lapsed-host "Site is not available" page with a mismatched TLS certificate) and exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of insight-partners; enrichment found no active API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Hlabs
providers.description: Hlabs (Harrison Laboratories, Inc., operating as hlaboratories.com) is a US-based, Y Combinator-backed (Winter 2026) manufacturer of plug-and-play robotics components. The company produces a domestically-manufactured, integrated hardware ecosystem for robot builders — including the RB1 main board (powered by Nvidia Jetson), wireless communication modules, field-oriented control (FOC) boards, pancake motors, and actuators. Its stated goal is to eliminate the complexity of sourcing mismatched components from overseas and integrating them, so roboticists can focus on design rather than electronics debugging. Hlabs targets teams building medium-to-large robots such as quadrupeds, humanoids, and robot arms, and serves customers across household robotics, defense, and other robotic platforms. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer/API surface at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Hologix
providers.description: Hologix, Inc. (formerly MBA Technologies, founded 1989) was a Phoenix, Arizona software company that developed Attricom, a business-to-business eCommerce order management solution built for manufacturers with complex, attribute-based product lines in the metals, textile, and paper and forest products industries. Attricom streamlined configuration, quoting, and order management so large-scale producers could offer closer, self-service ordering relationships to their customers. Hologix was venture-backed by Insight Partners, Adams Capital Management, Integral Capital Partners, and Kemper Ventures, and has since ceased operations. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public API, developer portal, or product website is currently reachable.

providers.name: Holor Media
providers.description: Holor Media was an integrated immersive media technology company founded in 2015 and based in Los Angeles and San Francisco. It focused on 360/VR content creation and distribution, building augmented and virtual reality authoring tools aimed at the next generation of social, interactive XR (extended reality) experiences, including interactive 360 apps for the Transformers film franchise. It raised seed funding from 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), Skyline Ventures, and WI Harper Group. The company is now permanently closed and its former domain (holor.com) is a parked, for-sale listing on Afternic, so there is no active developer surface, API, documentation, or SDK to profile. This record is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Homary
providers.description: Homary is a direct-to-consumer home furnishings retailer that sells furniture, faucets, lighting, outdoor, kitchen, bath, storage and organization, decor and rugs sourced straight from manufacturers to shoppers' homes. The brand positions itself around "affordable luxury" home decor, operating an online storefront (homary.com) with category catalogs, deals, best sellers, a design service, and a business-to-business program. Homary was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As a consumer e-commerce brand it exposes only internal storefront endpoints (/hm-api/, /chart-api/, disallowed in robots.txt) and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Home Account
providers.description: Home-Account (Home Account) was a consumer financial-services startup focused on mortgage management and consumer credit-risk analytics, backed by Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC). Per its LinkedIn profile, the company built patent-worthy consumer risk-analytic tooling to help homeowners manage mortgages and understand consumer credit risk, operating in the Consumer Services sector with roughly 11-50 employees and a base in the Fort Mill, South Carolina (ZIP 29708) area. Its original website, home-account.com, no longer resolves, and Uncork Capital's portfolio record associates the company with Bills.com. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API artifacts were found during enrichment; this record remains an identity-only profile of a legacy/defunct portfolio company added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Homeboodle
providers.description: Homeboodle was a San Francisco rental marketplace startup that rebranded as "Lovely" around 2012. The product let renters search, apply for, and pay for apartments online, while giving landlords and property managers tools to list units, screen applicants, and collect rent. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) among other investors, Lovely (livelovely.com) was acquired by RentPath (the owner of Apartment Guide and Rent.com) for roughly $13M in April 2014. The company is now defunct as an independent product; livelovely.com issues a 301 redirect to apartmentguide.com and the former developer/API surface (hub.livelovely.com) is offline. This record is retained for historical and network-graph completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Homeis
providers.description: Homeis was a social networking platform for immigrant and foreign-born communities, founded in January 2017 by Ran Harnevo and Hanan Laschover with offices in New York City and Tel Aviv. The app matched users by country of origin and current city so newcomers could find their community for tips, jobs, dating, events, and local services, serving groups such as Israelis in the U.S., Latinos in Canada, French-speaking Africans in France, and South Asians in the Emirates. It reached more than one million users and raised roughly $16 million, including a $12 million Series A led by Canaan Partners and Spark Capital. The consumer app shut down in Summer 2021 and never reopened; homeis.com is now a parked domain listed for sale. Homeis published no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich for this profile.

providers.name: HomeJoy
providers.description: Homejoy, Inc. was an online home-services marketplace that connected customers with vetted house cleaners and handymen through its website and mobile apps. Founded in 2010 by siblings Adora and Aaron Cheung, the Y Combinator-backed company raised roughly $40M (Google Ventures, Redpoint, First Round, Max Levchin) and expanded to more than 30 cities across the US, UK, Canada, France and Germany. Battered by high customer churn, discount-driven growth and worker-misclassification lawsuits, Homejoy ceased operations on July 31, 2015; much of its product and engineering team was acqui-hired by Google. This is an archival API Evangelist profile of a defunct company: it operates no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, and its former homejoy.com domain now redirects to an unrelated cleaning service.

providers.name: Homigo
providers.description: Homigo was a Toronto-based home-services startup, founded in 2016, that later rebranded to Setter and operated a concierge platform giving each homeowner a dedicated concierge to manage home maintenance and repairs — plumbing, HVAC, electrical, landscaping, roofing, pools, masonry, appliances, and handyman work — at the touch of a button. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Thumbtack in December 2020. Its website (setter.com) no longer resolves, and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation were ever published, so there is no live provider surface to enrich.

providers.name: Honest Food Company
providers.description: Honest Food Company GmbH is a Berlin-based cloud-kitchen / ghost-restaurant operator founded in 2017 that produced and delivered food under a portfolio of virtual delivery-only brands (Mamacita, Blattgold, Baba Noni, Beste Freunde, Holy Chicken, Clubkitchen) ordered through its own sites and third-party delivery platforms. Backed by Creandum and Index Ventures, it was acquired by Delivery Hero SE in February 2020 and folded into the Delivery Hero group; it operates no independent public developer/API surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Creandum portfolio lead. Sector: consumer / food delivery.

providers.name: Honey
providers.description: Honey was a modern intranet and internal-communications SaaS platform (honey.is) built to connect distributed teams, streamline company-wide communication, drive and quantify employee engagement, and replace outdated intranets. Launched in 2013, it was incubated by the design agency Huge and its parent Interpublic Group in Brooklyn, and raised a $1M seed round from Point Nine Capital in 2015; customers included Capital One, Coca-Cola Hellenic, Lowe's, and Sesame Street. The company is now defunct: the honey.is domain no longer resolves and it publishes no live website, developer portal, API, or documentation. This profile is retained as a Point Nine portfolio lead with no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Honor
providers.description: Honor (Honor Technology, Inc.) is a San Francisco-based home care company that pairs a high-touch, non-medical in-home care network for aging adults with a proprietary technology and operations platform - the Honor Care Platform - covering caregiver ("Care Pro") scheduling and matching, client care plans, visit management, and back-office operations. In August 2021 Honor acquired Home Instead, the world's largest senior home care franchise network, which now operates as a subsidiary of Honor; the Honor Care Platform powers both the Honor Care Network and Home Instead franchise offices. Honor exposes its platform to internal staff and to caregivers and families through the Honor Care Pro and Honor Family mobile apps and a client web portal. As of this writing Honor publishes NO public or partner developer API, developer portal, or API reference documentation - the platform is a closed, first-party care-delivery operations system rather than an API product. This entry is therefore a documentation stub kept for catalog completeness; it will be updated if Honor ever ships a documented public or partner API.

providers.name: Hop Aero
providers.description: Hop Aero is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) aerospace and defense company based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2024 by Jacob Balaj and Matija Milenovic. The company develops hypersonic rocket cargo vehicles that deliver payloads point-to-point into austere, contested environments hundreds of miles away in minutes, aiming to give the United States and its allies an asymmetric logistics advantage. Hop Aero has raised a $3M pre-seed round and won a $1.25M U.S. Air Force SBIR award; its team draws on experience from SpaceX, Virgin Orbit, Masten Space Systems, SpinLaunch, and Destinus. This is a hardware-stage company with no public API or developer surface at the time of profiling; this record was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and is maintained for network discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: HopShop Inc.
providers.description: HopShop Inc. is a consumer AI fashion-discovery and creator-monetization platform, often described as "Shazam for Fashion." Shoppers upload or screenshot an outfit and HopShop's visual-search AI finds the exact item plus similar matches across 600+ brand partners, including Bloomingdale's, Nordstrom, Levi's, and Tommy Hilfiger. Creators and influencers build personalized shops, link the outfits they feature on Instagram to shoppable products, grow their communities, and earn affiliate commissions. The company is backed by 500 Global. As surfaced to the API Evangelist network, HopShop operates as a consumer-facing mobile and web application and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: Hortor Games
providers.description: Hortor Games (Beijing Haoteng Chuangxiang Technology Co., Ltd. / 北京豪腾创想科技有限公司) is a Chinese mobile game developer and publisher focused on casual, word, and mini-game titles distributed as standalone apps and as WeChat / Douyin mini-games. Its catalog includes idiom and word puzzle games such as 成语小秀才, plus casual titles like 肥鹅健身房 (Goose Gym), 咸鱼之王, 海岛来了, and 稻田路. The company operates consumer game landing and distribution sites across the hortorgames.com, hortorcx.com, and 666youxiting.com domains. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API program, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Host Hotels & Resorts
providers.description: Host Hotels & Resorts is a leading lodging real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns luxury and upper-upscale hotels operating under premium brands in major U.S. and international markets. No public APIs are offered.

providers.name: HouseTrip
providers.description: HouseTrip was a London-based online vacation-rental marketplace founded in 2009 by Arnaud Bertrand and Junjun Chen, backed by Accel and Balderton Capital, that grew to roughly 300,000 European holiday properties before being acquired by TripAdvisor in April 2016. The standalone HouseTrip brand and its developer surface (formerly dev.housetrip.com) have since been retired; the housetrip.com domain now serves TripAdvisor's HolidayLettings marketplace. This profile is retained as a historical consumer-sector company record in the API Evangelist network; no live first-party API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published under the HouseTrip brand.

providers.name: Howard
providers.description: Howard was the world's first flex-use real estate platform, co-founded by Michael Jaindl (CEO) and Derek Lee, aiming to bring flexibility to commercial real estate. It was an early-stage (seed) company backed by Bloomberg Beta out of its 2016 fund. The company has since permanently closed and operates no public developer surface, API, documentation, or live host. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio record and is not an active API provider.

providers.name: Huaun
providers.description: Huaun (华云安, Huayun'an) is a Beijing-based cybersecurity company specializing in attack surface management, vulnerability research, and adversarial (offensive/defensive) security. Its product line centers on three AI-driven systems: Ai·Vul (灵洞), an adaptive threat and vulnerability management platform that discovers and inventories host, web, IoT, and container-cluster assets along with eighteen classes of digital exposure including APIs; Ai·Radar (灵知), a threat-intelligence engine built on natural-language processing and knowledge graphs across thirty-plus data sources; and Ai·Bot (灵刃), an intelligent penetration-testing and attack-simulation system backed by a library of over 160,000 vulnerabilities and 2,000+ proof-of-concept exploits. Backed by DCM Ventures and other investors, Huaun helps enterprises continuously discover and validate their external and internal attack surface.

providers.name: Huddl
providers.description: Huddl (huddl.ai) was an AI meeting-collaboration platform founded in 2017 in Mountain View, California by CEO Krishna Yarlagadda and CTO Nava Davuluri. The product acted as a collaboration hub layered over Zoom, Webex, and Microsoft Teams, using automatic speech recognition to turn meeting audio into searchable text alongside real-time collaborative note-taking and AI-generated meeting summaries. The company raised roughly $8.7M in venture funding. As of this enrichment pass the huddl.ai domain no longer resolves (delegated to Namecheap parking nameservers with no A/AAAA/MX/TXT records), indicating the service is discontinued; no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or GitHub organization could be located.

providers.name: Huixiaoer
providers.description: Huixiaoer (会小二) is a Chinese online platform for booking meeting venues, hotel conference rooms, and event spaces, operated by Beijing Yundong Digital Media Technology (北京云动数字媒体技术有限公司). It connects companies with a network of conference hotels and specialty venues across China and 20+ overseas cities, offering venue matching, price negotiation, and one-on-one meeting-planning advisors, plus bundled catering, accommodation, transportation, staging, team-building, incentive travel, and exhibition booth services on a free-to-client, commission-based model. Backed by DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Humane
providers.description: Humane was a consumer AI hardware startup, founded by former Apple engineers, best known for the AI Pin — a screenless, wearable AI-powered device — and its companion Cosmos operating system and Humane.Center cloud service. The company was acquired by HP in early 2025, the AI Pin was discontinued, and its cloud services and humane.com domain were taken offline. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the company has no reachable web, developer, or API surface.

providers.name: Humanoid
providers.description: Humanoid was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass its associated domain speakertext.com no longer serves a live product. The domain resolves (HTTP 200) but sits on GoDaddy parking infrastructure (IPs 15.197.148.33 / 3.33.130.190, ns65/ns66.domaincontrol.com nameservers) and every path — including /.well-known/* and fabricated paths — returns an identical parking lander that redirects to /lander (wildcard soft-404). No API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or discovery surface could be found. The company appears defunct/inactive; there is no enrichable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Hundeland
providers.description: Hundeland was a German direct-to-consumer online shop for dog supplies — dog food, treats, accessories, and pet-care products — and a portfolio company of the Point Nine venture capital firm. The hundeland.de storefront has been permanently closed ("dauerhaft geschlossen") and now 302-redirects to Pets Premium (petspremium.de), operated by the same company, which carries the same brands and product range; former customers must re-register there. Hundeland publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs, so the enrichment pipeline found no API surface to harvest. This record is retained as a Point Nine portfolio lead with the real closure status captured; the only machine-verifiable artifact is the domain-security probe of the still-resolving hundeland.de host that serves the redirect.

providers.name: Hydro Wind Energy
providers.description: Hydro Wind Energy develops offshore renewable energy infrastructure at the convergence of dispatchable clean power, grid-scale energy storage, and freshwater production. Its OceanHydro Omni deep-sea offshore wind platform converts wind into mechanical lift with built-in storage; SubSea RO Wind couples wind energy directly to subsea reverse-osmosis desalination; and the Offshore AI Power Plant integrates both with floating data centres for off-grid AI infrastructure. The company also ships QuenchSea, a portable hand-powered desalination device deployed across 60+ countries. Backed by Techstars, Republic, and Shell StartUp Engine. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: HYLA
providers.description: HYLA (HYLA Mobile) was a mobile device trade-in and reverse-supply-chain company that ran buyback, trade-in, and device-recommerce programs for carriers, retailers, and manufacturers, reselling and redistributing used smartphones into secondary markets. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, it was acquired and its business folded into Assurant: its site hylamobile.com now permanently redirects to Assurant's mobile/broadband unit. HYLA is not a public API provider — it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API, so this profile is an identity-only company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API catalog entry.

providers.name: Hyper 4
providers.description: Hyper (heyhyper.ai) is a Y Combinator-backed startup building "the self-driving company brain" — a knowledge-management platform that assembles a centralized, self-maintaining knowledge graph from a team's emails, Slack, GitHub, calendars, and other work sources, then feeds that context back into AI agents and tools so they act with accurate company memory and require fewer repeated corrections. Founded in 2026 by Shalin Shah and Kanyes Thaker and based in San Francisco, the company was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this profile Hyper is very early-stage, publishing only a marketing landing page at heyhyper.ai with no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface yet available; this record captures verified company identity and will be re-enriched as a developer platform is published.

providers.name: Hypersonica
providers.description: Hypersonica is a European defence and aerospace company developing sovereign hypersonic strike systems for both military and civilian applications. Founded to give Europe an independent technological edge to deter aggression, the company tested what it describes as Europe's first sovereign hypersonic missile prototype in February 2026, focusing on fast, modular, maneuverable deep-strike capabilities delivered in months rather than years at a claimed 80% cost reduction. Headquartered in Munich with UK offices, Hypersonica raised a EUR 23.3M Series A backed by Plural, SPRIND, and General Catalyst. As a business-to-government defence contractor it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so no API artifacts could be enriched.

providers.name: Hyperspace
providers.description: Hyperspace is a crypto/blockchain venture backed by Pantera Capital, added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. As of July 2026 its domain hyperspace.xyz 301-redirects to joinearlybird.com, where the project now operates as "Earlybird" — a pre-mainnet blockchain effort ("When Mainnet? Soon") with a private devnet at dev.joinearlybird.com (access-restricted, HTTP 403). There is no public API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, developer portal, documentation, pricing, or terms surface published yet; no /.well-known discovery documents are served on either host. This profile remains a lead awaiting a real developer surface before the enrichment pipeline can capture substantive API artifacts.

providers.name: Hyphen
providers.description: Hyphen was a mobile-first employee engagement and pulse-survey platform that let organizations collect anonymous employee feedback, run continuous sentiment surveys, and give managers analytics on engagement and culture. Founded as a 500 Global-backed startup, Hyphen was acquired by Betterworks and folded into the Betterworks Engage product line. Its original domain, gethyphen.com, now 301-redirects to betterworks.com/product/engage-overview/, and the company no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network; the live successor product is Betterworks Engage.

providers.name: Hyrule Compendium
providers.description: Data on all interactive items from The Legend of Zelda: BOTW

providers.name: I2 Technologies Inc (THINK SYSTEMS)
providers.description: i2 Technologies Inc was a Dallas-based supply-chain management software company founded in 1988 by Sanjiv Sidhu and Ken Sharma; "THINK SYSTEMS" refers to Think Systems Inc, a supply-chain planning software firm i2 acquired in 1997. i2 Technologies was itself acquired by JDA Software in 2010, which rebranded to Blue Yonder in 2020 and is now owned by Panasonic. This is a defunct/historical entity with no independent, live developer or API surface. The enrichment pass found no attributable API to enrich; the live i2group.com intelligence-analysis APIs belong to a different, unrelated company (a name collision), and the "insight-partners" backing appears to be an erroneous VC-portfolio match.

providers.name: IAM
providers.description: Identity and Access Management (IAM) is a framework of policies and technologies that ensures the right users have appropriate access to technology resources. IAM encompasses authentication, authorization, and the management of digital identities across systems. This index tracks IAM-related APIs, standards, and developer resources.

providers.name: IBEX Process Technology
providers.description: IBEX Process Technology was a semiconductor-industry technology company based in Lowell, Massachusetts, founded around 2000, that developed neural-network-based process control systems for semiconductor fabrication. The company raised roughly $6.8M across two funding rounds and is now defunct (deadpooled), with an Involuntary Revocation status on its Massachusetts registration. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub from battery-ventures data; enrichment finds no live website, no developer/API surface, and no machine-readable specifications to harvest.

providers.name: Icarus
providers.description: Icarus is an aerospace and defense company building autonomous, solar-powered stratospheric aircraft for persistent surveillance and connectivity. Its APOLLO platform operates continuously above 60,000 feet, delivering rapid aerial intelligence, wide-area coverage across 1,000+ square miles, and always-on, low-latency (5-10ms) direct-to-device communications for weeks-long missions without ground infrastructure. Founded in 2023 and based in El Segundo, California, Icarus was part of Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch. The company operates in the defense/aerospace hardware space and does not currently publish any public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical developer surface; this profile captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Iceberg Quantum
providers.description: Iceberg Quantum is a quantum architecture firm building fault-tolerant quantum computing systems around LDPC (Low-Density Parity-Check) error-correction codes. Its designs aim to cut the hardware overhead of quantum error correction by more than an order of magnitude, and its Pinnacle architecture claims roughly 10x lower overhead through modular lattice surgery and time-overhead compression. The company is hardware- and architecture-focused rather than a software/API provider; it partners with qubit hardware makers (PsiQuantum, Diraq, Oxford Ionics) and is backed by DCVC, Blackbird, and LocalGlobe. Surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking; there is no public API, SDK, or developer surface to enrich at this stage.

providers.name: iceonline
providers.description: iceonline (冰场联盟) operates an enterprise-grade backend management platform for ice rinks in China, published at www.iceonline.cn as a login-gated single-page administrative console branded "冰场联盟 企业级后台管理系统" (Ice Rink Alliance Enterprise Management System). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the public surface is a private SPA with no discoverable API: no OpenAPI/Swagger, SDK, developer portal, changelog, or security.txt was found — every probed path (including /.well-known/*, /swagger.json, /openapi.json) returns the SPA shell rather than a real document. Only live domain-security posture (TLS/DNS) could be captured this round.

providers.name: icerasemi
providers.description: Icera Semiconductor (icerasemi.com) was a British fabless semiconductor company known for soft-modem and baseband processor chipsets for wireless devices, and was acquired by NVIDIA in 2011. It was surfaced as a portfolio lead of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company no longer operates independently; as of this enrichment pass the domain www.icerasemi.com returns a shared-hosting error page with no live product, developer, API, or documentation surface, so there is nothing beyond domain-level metadata to enrich.

providers.name: IControl Networks
providers.description: IControl Networks was a smart-home and home-security platform company (OpenHome / Connect, Piper) backed by Kleiner Perkins. It was acquired by Comcast in 2017 (the platform underpinned Xfinity Home) with its residential SaaS business sold to Alarm.com; it no longer operates as an independent entity. Enrichment probe (2026-07-20): the icontrol.com domain no longer serves a website and is now delegated to Comcast nameservers (dns10x.comcast.net); icontrolnetworks.com, developer.icontrol.com, and api.icontrol.com do not resolve. No live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists to harvest. Sector: hardtech / IoT.

providers.name: Id Analytics
providers.description: ID Analytics was a San Diego-based identity risk and fraud analytics company founded in 2002. It operated the ID Network, a cross-industry consortium of consumer identity behavior, and productized it as ID Score and related fraud-detection, credit-risk, and identity-verification analytics used by financial services, telecommunications, and government. The company was acquired by LifeLock in 2012, passed to Symantec when it bought LifeLock in 2017, and was sold to LexisNexis Risk Solutions in 2020, where its capabilities are now delivered. It no longer operates an independent developer portal or public API; idanalytics.com now redirects to LexisNexis Risk Solutions.

providers.name: Identify Software
providers.description: Identify Software Ltd. was an Israeli enterprise-software company founded in 1996 in Petah Tikva by Yochi Slonim, backed by earlybird (invested 2001). It built application performance management, software-testing, and business-process-automation tooling that helped IT teams reproduce, diagnose, and resolve production application problems, best known for its AppSight problem-resolution suite. It is a legacy portfolio entry rather than an active API provider: the identify.software domain is parked/for-sale, there is no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich, so this profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead only.

providers.name: Identify3D
providers.description: Identify3D developed software to secure the digital (additive / 3D-printing) manufacturing supply chain by encrypting, distributing, and tracing digital part files, so that a part could only be produced by an authorized user, machine, and material and non-conforming or counterfeit parts could not enter the physical supply chain. The suite coupled part designs with production criteria (designated user, machine, material) and provided intellectual-property protection, digital-rights management, and traceability for distributed manufacturing. Founded in San Francisco and backed by Uncork Capital, Identify3D was acquired by Materialise NV in October 2021 and its technology was folded into the Materialise CO-AM distributed-manufacturing platform. The company no longer operates a standalone product, developer portal, or public API; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for historical and VC portfolio-graph purposes.

providers.name: iDigBio
providers.description: Access millions of museum specimens from organizations around the world

providers.name: idsmanager
providers.description: IDSManager (Jiuzhou Yunteng, 九州云腾) is a Chinese enterprise cybersecurity vendor providing unified identity management and zero-trust security. Its IDaaS platform centralizes account lifecycle, authentication, and authorization around a 5A framework (application center, unique accounts, single sign-on, centralized authorization, transparent auditing). The product line spans the IPG identity authentication series, MFA combining biometrics and digital certificates, the SPG secure application authentication series with Web and API gateways, and an SDP identity-defined perimeter for zero-trust access. It targets cloud migration, mobile-office security, and regulatory compliance across internet, finance, government, manufacturing, and education sectors. No public developer portal, API, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Ihaveu
providers.description: Ihaveu (优众网, ihaveu.com) was a Chinese business-to-consumer luxury fashion e-commerce platform founded in 2010 by Sun Tongyu (a former president of Alibaba's Taobao) and Chen Xiao. Based in China, it sold curated high-end designer apparel and accessories from international couture brands such as Prada, Hermes, and Marc Jacobs to Chinese consumers. It raised a Series A of roughly $11M in December 2010 led by IDG Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners, followed by a Series B in 2012 that added The CID Group and JAFCO Asia. The company is no longer active and its ihaveu.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, so it exposes no live website, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record for a defunct Lightspeed portfolio company; it has no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: iHeartMedia
providers.description: iHeartMedia is America's #1 audio company, reaching 9 out of 10 Americans every month through broadcast radio, digital streaming, podcasts, live events, and on-demand entertainment. Public API documentation, developer programs, or open API artifacts have not been identified for iHeartMedia. This repository exists to track APIs, SDKs, and developer resources should they become available.

providers.name: Illinois Tool Works
providers.description: Illinois Tool Works (ITW) is a Fortune 500 global multi-industrial manufacturer of value-added consumables and specialty equipment with related service businesses across automotive OEM, food equipment, test and measurement, electronics, welding, polymers and fluids, construction products, and specialty products. ITW does not publish a public API or developer program. This repository exists to track APIs, SDKs, and developer resources should they become available.

providers.name: illuminem
providers.description: illuminem is a global sustainability platform that brings together news, expert opinion, and ESG and sustainability data in a single place for professionals, investors, and organizations working on the energy transition and the broader climate and sustainability agenda. It publishes editorial and community-contributed "Voices" articles, curates sustainability and clean-energy news, and maintains a data hub of ESG and sustainability metrics. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the network as an enrichment lead; the provider does not currently expose a public, machine-readable developer API surface that could be discovered during this pass (its web properties sit behind a bot-challenge), so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only, awaiting a documented API to deepen it.

providers.name: Illusive Networks
providers.description: Illusive Networks was a cybersecurity company specializing in deception technology and identity threat detection and response (ITDR) — discovering and remediating identity vulnerabilities and detecting attacker lateral movement across on-premises and cloud environments using deceptive traps and agentless deception tactics. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Innovation Endeavors, TPG and others, the company was acquired by Proofpoint in December 2022. Its technology now ships as Proofpoint Identity Threat Defense (previously Illusive); the standalone illusive.com property redirects to Proofpoint and the company no longer operates an independent developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Illustra
providers.description: Illustra Information Technologies was an object-relational database company founded in 1992 by Michael Stonebraker, Gary Morgenthaler and several of Stonebraker's students to commercialize the Postgres research project. Its DataBlade extensibility modules let structured and unstructured multimedia data (text, geospatial, web content) be stored and indexed as true objects. NASA selected it in 1995 to store millions of satellite images. Informix Corporation acquired the company in 1996 and folded the object-relational engine and DataBlades into what became Informix Universal Server; that lineage passed to IBM and is now maintained by HCL Technologies. Illustra no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no standalone website, developer portal, or API. This record was surfaced from a historical Trinity Ventures portfolio list; enrichment found no live API surface.

providers.name: Imara
providers.description: Imara Corporation was a lithium-ion battery technology startup founded in 2006 in Menlo Park, California, that grew out of research at SRI International. It designed and manufactured high-power lithium-ion battery cells and packs based on patented cathode materials science, targeting power tools, outdoor power equipment, hybrid electric vehicles, specialty applications, and power-grid energy storage. Backed by Battery Ventures and Nth Power, it raised roughly $15.65M and reached commercial cell production in 2009 before shutting down around 2010-2011 for lack of manufacturing funding. It is a hardware company with no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface, and is now defunct.

providers.name: IMDbOT
providers.description: Unofficial IMDb Movie / Series Information

providers.name: iMedeon
providers.description: iMedeon, Inc. was a mobile workforce management software company based in Atlanta, Georgia, providing wireless web applications to optimize scheduling, routing, and the dispatch and management of mobile field workforces (the iM:Work suite). It was acquired by ViryaNet Ltd. in February 2002 (later rolled into Verisae) and no longer operates independently. The domain imedeon.com does not resolve and there is no live website, developer portal, or API surface. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a defunct/legacy company profile; there is nothing to enrich.

providers.name: Immunity Project
providers.description: Immunity Project was a San Francisco nonprofit and Y Combinator company (batch Winter 2014, one of YC's first non-profits alongside Watsi) that set out to develop a free HIV/AIDS vaccine. Its approach studied naturally immune "HIV controllers" and applied machine learning to reverse-engineer the immune response, aiming to deliver a crowdfunded, virus-free vaccine via nasal spray. Founders included Reid Rubsamen, Naveen Jain, and Ian Cinnamon. The organization surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; enrichment found no developer portal, documentation, or API surface, and its former domain (immunityproject.org) has lapsed and now redirects to an unrelated third-party news outlet, indicating the project is effectively defunct.

providers.name: Impossible Aerospace
providers.description: Impossible Aerospace is a deep-tech aerospace hardware company founded in 2016 by Spencer Gore in Santa Clara, California. It builds the US-1, a long-range all-electric quadcopter whose lithium-ion cells form part of the airframe structure, giving it up to roughly two hours of flight time for aerial imaging, surveillance, and public-safety missions with law enforcement and first responders. The US-1 runs the third-party Auterion OS flight stack (built on the PX4 open autopilot). The company was later acquired and operates as a small team. Enrichment note (2026-07-19): the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface, and its primary domain impossible.aero no longer resolves in DNS.

providers.name: Impossiblefoods
providers.description: Impossible Foods is a food technology company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Redwood City, California that develops plant-based substitutes for meat products, including the Impossible Burger, Impossible Sausage, and Impossible Chicken. Its products use soy leghemoglobin (heme) to mimic the taste and texture of animal meat and are distributed through grocery retail and foodservice channels. The company is backed by investors including Khosla Ventures. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile is currently identity- and domain-security-only.

providers.name: Incognito Technologies
providers.description: Incognito Technologies Private Limited is a Jaipur, India-based information technology services and software consultancy (incorporated December 2011, CIN U72200RJ2011PTC036364, offices in Bani Park, Jaipur). The firm offers custom software development, web and mobile application development, cloud and data services, IT infrastructure management, digital transformation, and enterprise ERP consulting. It is a professional-services provider rather than a public API producer; as of this enrichment pass no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI) has been located, and the corporate website (inctech.in) was unreachable when probed.

providers.name: Industrial Safety Technologies
providers.description: Industrial Safety Technologies (IST) was a hardware-focused industrial safety platform, founded in 2011 and built by Battery Ventures through acquisitions of gas-detection and hazard-monitoring businesses including Gas Measurement Instruments (GMI), Detcon, DSA Detection, and Simtronics. Its products centered on fixed and portable gas detectors, flame detectors, and hazardous-environment safety instrumentation for industrial sites. IST was acquired by Scott Safety, a Tyco business, from Battery Ventures for $329.5 million in December 2014 and no longer exists as an independent company; the enrichment pipeline found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface to profile.

providers.name: infarm
providers.description: infarm (Indoor Urban Farming GmbH) is a Berlin-based vertical/indoor farming company, surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The company builds modular, cloud-connected growing systems for herbs, leafy greens, and produce placed in grocery stores and distribution hubs. This profile was enriched by the pipeline; infarm publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface, and its website is bot-blocked (HTTP 403) to automated access, so only domain-level security posture could be probed. It remains a company/identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Inferact
providers.description: Inferact is an AI inference infrastructure startup founded by the creators and core maintainers of vLLM, the most popular open-source LLM inference engine. Its mission is to grow vLLM as the world's AI inference engine and to make serving AI models effortless — as simple as spinning up a serverless database — by optimizing inference performance across diverse hardware, supporting emerging model architectures (mixture-of-experts, multimodal, and agentic), and expanding accelerator compatibility while keeping all optimizations flowing back to the open-source community. vLLM supports 500+ model architectures across 200+ accelerator types with 2,000+ contributors. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with verifiable public identity and domain-security signals; the company does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or specification.

providers.name: Inferact
providers.description: Inferact is a startup founded by the creators and core maintainers of vLLM, the widely adopted open-source large language model inference engine. The company exists to supercharge vLLM adoption, developing inference and serving optimizations at the frontier where models meet hardware at scale and flowing those improvements back into the open-source community. As of January 2026 the company had raised roughly $150M at an $800M valuation and is recruiting engineers and researchers. As of this enrichment pass Inferact publishes only a company announcement page at inferact.ai and does not yet expose a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or commercial product docs.

providers.name: Infiot
providers.description: Infiot was a secure access service edge (SASE) and intelligent edge networking startup that combined SD-WAN, zero trust network access (ZTNA), security service edge, and cloud-delivered edge intelligence into a single-vendor, AI-driven service for connecting branch, remote, and IoT sites. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Netskope in August 2022 and its technology was folded into Netskope's Borderless SD-WAN and Converged Access product line. Infiot no longer operates an independent brand, developer portal, API reference, or public API host; the former infiot.com domain now 301-redirects to Netskope's Converged Access product page, so there is no standalone API surface to enrich. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed portfolio lead with its acquisition status recorded.

providers.name: Information Technology Infrastructure
providers.description: Information Technology Infrastructure encompasses the hardware, software, networks, and facilities used to support the delivery, management, and operation of IT services. This includes servers, storage, networking, data centers, and cloud infrastructure components.

providers.name: Inloop Robotics
providers.description: Inloop Robotics (InLoop) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup in San Francisco offering robotics-as-a-service for warehouses, fulfillment centers, and light manufacturing. Its bimanual "Loop V1" robot performs box assembly, kitting, visual inspection, content preparation, unpackaging, and order pick-and-pack. The system runs a hybrid-autonomy, human-in-the-loop model: onboard AI handles routine work while remote teleoperators take over on edge cases, and production failures feed continuous learning. InLoop sells this as a flat monthly subscription that bundles the hardware, ongoing AI updates, and 24/7 teleassistance fallback, rather than selling robots outright. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site only, with no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this record tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending any future developer/API program.

providers.name: Innovium
providers.description: Innovium, Inc. was a Santa Clara, California semiconductor company founded in 2014 that designed high-bandwidth Ethernet switch silicon (the TERALYNX family) for cloud and enterprise data centers, competing with Broadcom on high-radix, low-latency switching with deep buffers and built-in telemetry/analytics. Backed by Greylock and other deep-tech investors, Innovium was acquired by Marvell Technology in 2021 (~$1.1B) and its switching technology continues inside Marvell's portfolio. The company shipped hardware silicon, not a public developer API — innovium.com now redirects to marvell.com, and there is no developer portal, OpenAPI, or programmatic API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Inphi
providers.description: Inphi Corporation (formerly NYSE: IPHI) was a fabless semiconductor company that designed high-speed analog and mixed-signal interconnect components -- SerDes, PAM4 DSPs, optical DSPs, and coherent DSPs -- used to move data across networks and inside data centers, from cloud and telecom infrastructure to long-haul and metro optical transport. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Inphi was acquired by Marvell Technology in April 2021 and folded into Marvell's data-center and connectivity portfolio; its former inphi.com domain now 301-redirects to marvell.com. As a semiconductor hardware company, Inphi did not publish a public developer API, portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company record.

providers.name: Insamo
providers.description: Insamo is a biotechnology company building membrane-permeable, orally available cyclic peptides that combine the binding affinity of antibodies with the pharmacology of small molecules for drug discovery. Its platform automates the design, synthesis, and testing of peptides at large scale and applies machine learning across vast chemical spaces to identify therapeutic candidates. Founded in February 2024 with $12M from Playground Global, venBio, and MRL Ventures Fund, the company operates from Berkeley, California and Chippendale, New South Wales, Australia. Insamo currently publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Insent.ai
providers.description: Insent.ai was a Boston-based, Techstars-backed B2B conversational marketing platform that let marketing and sales teams engage website visitors in real time with human-first chat, visitor identification, routing, and meeting booking. ZoomInfo acquired Insent in July 2021 and rebranded the product as ZoomInfo Chat; the insent.ai domain now serves ZoomInfo Chat. As a standalone company Insent.ai no longer operates its own developer portal, documentation, or public API surface, so the enrichment pipeline found no first-party API artifacts to harvest.
