providers.name: InstaEDU
providers.description: InstaEDU was an online, on-demand tutoring platform founded in 2011 in San Francisco that connected students with tutors for live one-on-one help across a range of academic subjects. Backed by Battery Ventures and Social Capital, the company was acquired by Chegg in 2014 and folded into the Chegg Tutors service, which Chegg subsequently wound down in 2021. There is no independent InstaEDU developer program, public API, developer portal, or live domain today (instaedu.com no longer resolves) — this profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Instante
providers.description: Instante (also listed as Istante Software) is a data-warehousing software company that received a seed investment from Canaan Partners, with John Balen listed as the sponsoring partner on Canaan's portfolio page. The company is profiled as an application software provider building tools for data warehousing. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist VC-portfolio pipeline as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no public developer surface. No reachable company website, API, developer documentation, SDKs, OpenAPI, or event/webhook surface could be verified. The candidate domains instante.com (a parked domain listed for sale) and instante.io (an unrelated Brazilian consumer photo-gallery app) are not this company.

providers.name: Instart Logic
providers.description: Instart Logic was a web application performance and security company founded in 2010 (originally as Zettata) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. It pioneered an endpoint-integrated cloud delivery architecture that paired a cloud service with a client-side JavaScript engine (the Nanovisor) running in the browser to accelerate web and mobile web applications, optimize and stream images (SmartVision), and defend applications with bot management and a web application firewall. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, Tenaya Capital, Greylock, Sutter Hill Ventures and others across roughly $140M+ in venture funding, the company's technology assets were acquired by Akamai Technologies in early 2020, after which the business wound down. No live developer or API surface remains: the instartlogic.com domain resolves to no website host and is served by Akamai nameservers.

providers.name: Institut für Produktqualität
providers.description: Institut für Produktqualität (ifp) is an independent analytical testing laboratory based in Berlin, Germany, providing laboratory analysis, testing, and consulting services for food, feed, cosmetics, and pharmaceutical products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the provider publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or machine-readable discovery surface; its public website is served behind bot-protection (HTTP 401) and exposes no /.well-known documents. This profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Intelligence Factory
providers.description: Intelligence Factory is a San Francisco robotics and embodied-AI startup (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building general-purpose foundation models for robotic manipulation. Its stated mission is "Human Intelligence for Robots" — deploying bots with human-level dexterity and reasoning in the real world. The team trains models on human demonstration data captured through custom gloves that record what a person sees, does, and feels, retargets that human motion onto robot motion, and deploys the resulting models across robot platforms from dexterous hands to grippers, with early focus on warehouses, grocery stores, and data centers. The company was founded by Yash Sinha (CEO) and Jalaj Shukla (CTO), with a team drawn from ETH Zurich, University of Pennsylvania, Harvard, NVIDIA, Formula 1, and Ansys. As of this profile it publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or GitHub organization — it is an early-stage lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Intellimize
providers.description: Intellimize was an AI-powered website optimization, personalization, and conversion-rate optimization platform (an amplify-partners portfolio company in the ai-ml sector) that let marketing teams continuously test and machine-learn the best-performing landing-page and website experience for each visitor. It was acquired by Webflow in 2024 and folded into the Webflow Optimize product; the entire intellimize.com domain now 301-redirects to webflow.com/feature/optimize. As a standalone brand Intellimize no longer operates an independent developer portal, public API, documentation, or SDK surface — enrichment therefore found no OpenAPI, packages, well-known documents, MCP server, or security/trust program of its own. Only live domain-security posture for the retained intellimize.com domain could be probed.

providers.name: Internal Control Standards
providers.description: Internal Control Standards are frameworks of policies and procedures designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the achievement of objectives in operational effectiveness, reliable financial reporting, and compliance with laws and regulations. The COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework (originally released in 1992 and refreshed as ICIF-2013) is the most widely adopted standard for internal controls and underpins SOX 404 compliance, with supplemental 2023 guidance for internal control over sustainability reporting (ICSR) addressing modern risks including generative AI and robotic process automation.

providers.name: International Flavors & Fragrances
providers.description: International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF) is a global creator of flavors, fragrances, and ingredients for consumer products including perfumes, cosmetics, food, beverages, and household goods. IFF is a Fortune 500 company with no documented public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: International Network Services
providers.description: International Network Services (INS) was one of the world's largest independent network consulting and security services providers, delivering enterprise network design, infrastructure, and network security solutions to financial services, pharmaceutical, aerospace, energy, and transportation customers. Backed by Canaan Partners (Series C) alongside investors including Sequoia Capital, Cisco Investments, and Lucent Technologies, the company was acquired by Lucent. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed portfolio company; it does not currently operate a public API developer surface.

providers.name: International Paper
providers.description: International Paper is a Fortune 500 producer of fiber-based packaging, pulp, and paper products serving customers in more than 150 countries. The company does not currently publish a public developer API program; business integrations are handled through customer and supplier portals.

providers.name: Internet Security Systems
providers.description: Internet Security Systems (ISS) was an Atlanta-based network and internet security company, founded in 1994, that provided vulnerability scanning, intrusion detection, and managed security services (Internet Scanner, RealSecure, Proventia, BlackICE). It was acquired by IBM in 2006 for approximately $1.3 billion and folded into IBM as IBM Internet Security Systems (later IBM Security / X-Force); it no longer exists as an independent company. Surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, ISS operates no active, independent public developer or API surface today, so there is nothing live to enrich against.

providers.name: Intraware
providers.description: Intraware, Inc. was a software delivery and entitlement-management company founded in 1996 and headquartered in Orinda, California. Its flagship SubscribeNet service gave enterprise software publishers a web-based electronic software delivery (ESD) and license-management platform, delivering applications through an encryption, compression, and multi-server distribution engine while giving corporate IT subscribers account-specific entitlement, update, and download information. Intraware went public on NASDAQ under the ticker ITRA in 1999 during the dot-com boom, was backed by investors including Canaan Partners, and was acquired in 2009 by Acresso Software (later Flexera Software). Its SubscribeNet software-monetization capabilities live on today as part of Revenera; there is no independent Intraware developer program, public API, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Canaan Partners portfolio company and is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Intrepida Bio
providers.description: Intrepida Bio, Inc. is a preclinical biotechnology company (founded 2019, headquartered in Encinitas / San Diego, CA) developing medicines that modulate the innate immune system to fight cancer and other diseases. Working with Biouniversa s.r.l., the company holds worldwide rights to develop proprietary monoclonal antibodies against the novel targets BAG3 and its receptor IFITM-2 — a signaling axis tumors hijack to build a growth-promoting, immune-evasive microenvironment (notably in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PDAC). Intrepida raised roughly $9.5M from Canaan, Sofinnova, Indaco Venture Partners and Vertis to fund IND-enabling studies of its lead oncology program. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. NOTE: this is a therapeutics/drug-discovery company with no public API, developer portal, or software product surface; its website (intrepidabio.com) no longer resolves and the entity appears dormant/defunct, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: IntruVert Networks
providers.description: IntruVert Networks was a network intrusion-prevention company founded in 2000 in San Jose, California, and backed by Trinity Ventures. Its IntruShield product line combined purpose-built inline intrusion-prevention appliances with the IntruShield Manager to detect and block network attacks in real time. McAfee (then Network Associates) acquired IntruVert in May 2003 for approximately $103 million, folding the technology into its intrusion-prevention portfolio. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no live developer or API surface; this record is retained for historical/portfolio-graph purposes only.

providers.name: Invidica
providers.description: Invidica is an Oakland-based B2B wholesale ecommerce marketplace (founded 2019) that upgrades the wholesaler-retailer relationship for the reseller economy. It pairs a marketplace where resellers order wholesale products directly from brands with AI-driven analytics that combine Amazon sales data to predict an item's profitability, sales velocity, and competition, helping small sellers find the most profitable products to resell. Founded by CEO Sean Bovell and backed by 500 Global and 1517 Fund (pre-seed, 2021). The company appears to be pivoting under the Reroute Retail brand (rerouteretail.com, "launching soon"); its original invidica.com domain no longer resolves. No public API or developer surface is currently published.

providers.name: Invisible Universe
providers.description: Invisible Universe is a consumer entertainment company building AI-powered animated intellectual property for social platforms — described by FastCompany as "building the Pixar of the internet one TikTok at a time." It has launched multiple animated franchises reaching millions of followers and billions of views across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube, and created Invisible Studio, a proprietary AI engine that compresses short-form animated content production from weeks to hours. Backed by Initialized Capital, it operates in the consumer/media sector. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: InVisionApp
providers.description: InVision (InVisionApp, Inc.) was a digital product design collaboration platform founded in 2011 by Clark Valberg and Ben Nadel. It built a suite of tools for prototyping, design handoff, and real-time collaboration — including interactive prototypes, Inspect/Specs for developer handoff, DSM (Design System Manager), Boards, and the Freehand online whiteboard. At its peak InVision was valued near two billion dollars and backed by Battery Ventures, Accel, Tiger Global, and others, serving product design teams as a challenger to Adobe. As Figma surged, InVision's business declined: it sold the Freehand whiteboard product to Miro in 2023, and wound down all remaining services on December 31, 2024, after which customer content was permanently deleted. The invisionapp.com domain now redirects to Miro. InVision historically exposed a public REST API with OAuth and webhooks for its design platform, but that developer surface has been retired along with the product.

providers.name: Iomob
providers.description: Iomob (The Internet of Mobility) was a Barcelona-based Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) technology company founded in 2017. Its platform let cities, transport operators, and corporations orchestrate multimodal, door-to-door journeys — combining public transit, ride-hailing, taxis, micromobility, parking, and demand-responsive transport — through unified journey-planning APIs, native iOS/Android SDKs, and customizable white-label apps. Iomob's MaaS platform and SDK were acquired by Busup in January 2025 to build a corporate mobility platform; the Iomob UK entity was dissolved in September 2025 and the public website (iomob.net) is currently offline (Cloudflare 526 origin error). No public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK packages, or GitHub organization could be verified during enrichment — Iomob's APIs and SDKs were delivered under B2B/partner agreements.

providers.name: Iprint
providers.description: iPrint.com was an early online print shop, launched in 1996 out of Larkspur, California, that let consumers and small businesses design and order customizable printed products (business cards, stationery, invitations, promotional items) over the web. Backed by Canaan Partners, the company went public on the NASDAQ under the symbol IPRT in March 2000, merged with promotional-products firm Wood Associates in 2001, was delisted in 2002, and its assets were ultimately acquired by Harland Clarke in 2009. The iprint.com domain today hosts a live consumer print e-commerce storefront operated out of Richmond Hill, Ontario, offering business cards, marketing materials, signs, banners, stickers, and design services. The company exposes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is identity-only and carries no API artifacts.

providers.name: IPtronics
providers.description: IPtronics A/S was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2003 in Copenhagen, Denmark, designing integrated circuits (laser drivers, transimpedance amplifiers, and CMOS ICs) for parallel optical interconnects used in high-speed computing, storage, and datacenter communications. Backed by Creandum, Sunstone, and 10i10, the company was acquired by Mellanox Technologies in 2013 (now part of NVIDIA) and no longer operates as an independent entity. It is a hardware chip vendor with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic surface; the former iptronics.com domain now redirects to NVIDIA Networking. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio identity record only.

providers.name: IQI Inc (Beijing AIQI Technology)
providers.description: IQI Inc, operating as Beijing AIQI Technology Co., Ltd. (北京爱其科技有限公司), is a mobile-internet company founded in April 2013 that develops smart hardware and robotics products under a "Create more & More fun" philosophy. It is best known for its ONEBOT building-block robots and construction sets — including the Mi Tu (米兔) block robots in the Xiaomi ecosystem and heritage-architecture sets such as the Millennium Mortise-and-Tenon (千年榫), Qinian Hall (祈年殿) and Forbidden City Corner Tower kits. The company sells through its own store, Tmall (ONEBOT flagship) and JD.com. It is a consumer smart-hardware/toy brand; as of this profile it publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK or documentation surface.

providers.name: Iridium
providers.description: Iridium Communications Inc. (NASDAQ: IRDM) is a McLean, Virginia satellite communications company operating a constellation of 66 cross-linked Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that deliver truly global L-band voice, data, IoT, and positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) services across every region of the Earth, including the polar oceans. Iridium sells satellite phones (Iridium Extreme), satellite messengers, satellite IoT modules and modems (Iridium 9602/9603, Iridium Certus 9770/9810/9704, Iridium Edge, Iridium Edge Pro, Iridium Edge Solar), Short Burst Data (SBD) messaging, broadband Certus terminals, and next-generation Iridium NTN Direct 5G Non-Terrestrial Network services built on 3GPP NB-IoT for direct-to-device smartphone and IoT connectivity. Iridium CloudConnect — co-developed with Amazon Web Services — pipes satellite IoT data as JSON into customer-owned Amazon SQS queues inside their own AWS VPC over a dedicated private Iridium-AWS interconnect, making Iridium the first global cloud-native satellite IoT backhaul. The company serves aviation, maritime, government/defense, land-mobile, autonomous systems, and IoT markets through a partner ecosystem of more than 500 service providers, value-added resellers, and hardware OEMs, and in May 2026 announced a planned acquisition of Aireon, operator of the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance network. Iridium's business model is airtime/subscription revenue plus hardware module licensing and engineering services; there is no public, self-service developer API or OpenAPI — network access is mediated through Iridium-authorized service providers, the Iridium CloudConnect AWS integration, and hardware-level AT-command and SBD interfaces on Iridium modems.

providers.name: Iris Automation
providers.description: Iris Automation was a Reno, Nevada deep-tech company that built Casia, a computer-vision detect-and-avoid (DAA) system enabling beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) drone operations. Its onboard products (Casia, Casia X) and the ground-based Casia G used industrial cameras and machine-learning to detect non-cooperative intruder aircraft and prevent near mid-air collisions, integrating with MavLink-based autopilots and UAS ground control systems. Iris Automation was acquired by uAvionix in late 2023; the irisonboard.com domain now 301-redirects to uAvionix and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or well-known surface of its own.

providers.name: Ironport
providers.description: IronPort Systems was an email and web security gateway company founded in 2000 in San Bruno, California, known for its anti-spam, anti-virus, anti-phishing, and URL-filtering appliances and its SenderBase email reputation service. Cisco Systems acquired IronPort in 2007 for approximately $830 million; the products were rebranded as Cisco Email Security and Cisco Web Security and the standalone IronPort brand and pricelist were fully retired by late 2012. IronPort no longer operates an independent public website, developer portal, or API surface — its domain now resolves into Cisco — so this profile is retained as a historical Menlo Ventures portfolio company rather than an active API provider awaiting enrichment.

providers.name: Isidor
providers.description: Isidor is a frontier enterprise-AI company, founded in 2025 and headquartered in San Francisco with a London presence, building secure, vertically-integrated data pipelines that transform unstructured proprietary enterprise data into training- and evaluation-ready material for foundation models. Its platform spans five capabilities it describes as evaluation (industry-specific and agentic benchmarks), verifiers for generative-AI outputs in critical workflows, reasoning-trace data capture, foundation-model post-training (fine-tuning and alignment on proprietary data), and enterprise-grade security and privacy. Isidor raised an oversubscribed $3.6M pre-seed led by Gradient Ventures, futurepresent, and Seedcamp, with angels from Google DeepMind, Perplexity, and others. The company has no public API or developer surface yet; this profile tracks it as an enrichment lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: iSIGHT Security
providers.description: iSIGHT Security is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: cybersecurity. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: ITA Software
providers.description: ITA Software is a travel technology company, now part of Google, that builds airfare pricing, shopping, and availability software for airlines, online travel agencies, and travel management companies. Founded in 1996 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by MIT computer scientists (notably Jeremy Wertheimer) and backed early by Battery Ventures, General Catalyst, and Sequoia Capital, the company was acquired by Google in 2011. Its flagship QPX engine powers pricing, revenue shopping, ticket rebooking, award-flight search, ancillary merchandising, and flight schedule/seat availability for carriers including Air Canada, American Airlines, Delta, United, and Virgin Atlantic, and its technology underpins Google Flights. ITA Software also operates the consumer ITA Matrix flight-search tool at matrix.itasoftware.com. The former public QPX Express REST API was retired by Google in April 2018; today ITA Software's QPX solutions are delivered as an enterprise engagement through Google account teams, with no public self-service developer program, portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Itch
providers.description: Itch is a UK direct-to-consumer pet wellness brand, backed by Seedcamp, offering a subscription service that delivers vet-approved flea, tick and worm treatments to pet owners on a recurring schedule, alongside pet health guidance and related care products. It was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification could be found; the consumer website sits behind bot protection, so this profile carries provider identity plus a probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Itemfield
providers.description: Itemfield was an enterprise data-integration software company known for its Complex Data Exchange (CDE) and B2B data-transformation technology, which parsed, mapped, and transformed complex, unstructured, and industry-standard message formats into structured data. Itemfield was acquired by Informatica in 2006, and its technology was absorbed into Informatica's B2B Data Transformation product line. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no surviving independent Itemfield developer surface: the itemfield.com domain now resolves under Informatica-managed DNS and serves no HTTP content, so there is no live API, documentation, portal, or specification to harvest.

providers.name: Iyuno
providers.description: Iyuno is one of the world's leading media localization companies, providing dubbing, subtitling, and access services for film, television, and streaming platforms across dozens of languages and markets worldwide. It was formed from the combination of Iyuno Media Group and SDI Media and is backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. Iyuno operates as an enterprise content and media-services provider; as of this profiling it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Izif
providers.description: Izif (إعزف) is an online music education platform for the Arabic-speaking world, positioning itself as the largest platform for teaching music in Arabic. It offers a subscription library of more than 2,000 instructional videos across roughly ten popular Arabic instruments — oud, guitar, violin, piano, ney, darbuka, qanun, vocals, and music theory — taught by elite Arab musicians, alongside music sheets and iOS/Android apps. A 500 Global portfolio company, Izif is a consumer EdTech subscription service and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: J.Crew Group
providers.description: J.Crew Group, Inc. is an American multi-brand specialty retailer offering women's, men's, and children's apparel, shoes, and accessories under the J.Crew, Madewell, and Crewcuts brands. The company operates retail stores, factory outlet stores, and direct-to-consumer e-commerce sites.

providers.name: J.M. Smucker
providers.description: The J.M. Smucker Company is a leading marketer and manufacturer of consumer food and beverage products and pet food and pet snacks in North America, with brands including Smucker's, Folgers, Jif, Milk-Bone, and Meow Mix.

providers.name: Jacobs Engineering Group
providers.description: Jacobs Engineering Group, now operating as Jacobs Solutions, is one of the world's largest providers of professional, technical, and construction services, offering full-spectrum support to industries including aerospace, energy, environmental, infrastructure, and transportation. This entry is retained for legacy continuity; current activity is tracked under Jacobs Solutions.

providers.name: JAKA
providers.description: JAKA (Shanghai JAKA Robotics Co., Ltd.) is a collaborative robot (cobot) manufacturer founded in 2014 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, with origins in robotics research at Shanghai University. The company designs and builds lightweight, human-collaborative industrial robot arms — including its JAKA Zu series and MiniCobo — used across manufacturing, 3C electronics, automotive, healthcare, education, and commercial service applications. JAKA robots are programmed through the company's on-device control software and a robot SDK (C++/Python) that communicates with the robot controller over TCP/IP on the local network, rather than a public cloud web API. As of this profile JAKA does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or hosted REST/MCP API surface; this repository is a company profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Jask Labs
providers.description: Jask Labs (JASK) was a cybersecurity company that built an Autonomous Security Operations Center (ASOC) platform — applying machine learning and analytics on top of network and security telemetry to triage and prioritize security alerts and reduce SOC analyst workload. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors, JASK was acquired by Sumo Logic in 2019 and folded into Sumo Logic's cloud SIEM / Cloud SOC offering. Jask Labs no longer operates as an independent company: its domains (jask.ai and jask.com) now permanently redirect (HTTP 301) to sumologic.com, and there is no standalone Jask Labs developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or live product surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead stub with the acquisition recorded.

providers.name: Jaunt *
providers.description: Jaunt (Jaunt VR, later Jaunt XR) was a cinematic virtual-reality and immersive-media technology company founded in 2013 and based in Santa Clara, California. It built end-to-end tools for capturing, stitching, streaming, and viewing 360-degree cinematic VR, including the Jaunt ONE professional camera and a cloud rendering pipeline, before pivoting toward volumetric AR/XR in 2018. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) among other investors, the company wound down its XR business and sold its underlying technology assets to Verizon in late 2019. This profile was surfaced as a GV portfolio company; the company is now defunct and its domains (jaunt.us, jauntxr.com) are parked/for-sale or reassigned, so there is no live developer or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: JCR
providers.description: JCR (Java Content Repository) is a Java specification (JSR-283, "Content Repository for Java Technology API 2.0") that provides a vendor-neutral, implementation-independent way to access content bi-directionally on a granular level within a content repository. It defines features for hierarchical content modeling, versioning, access control, search, locking, and observation, with the javax.jcr package as its core. The reference implementation is provided by the Apache Jackrabbit project.

providers.name: Jelli
providers.description: Jelli was a programmatic advertising technology company focused on terrestrial and broadcast radio, building a real-time platform that let advertisers buy and manage radio spots programmatically across broadcast station inventory. Backed by Battery Ventures (among other investors), Jelli was acquired by iHeartMedia in 2016 and its technology went on to power programmatic and automated audio advertising. The independent Jelli brand is now defunct - the jelli.com domain 301-redirects to tritondigital.com, and no Jelli-branded developer portal, API reference, or public API host remains. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the enrichment pipeline found no live Jelli developer or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Jerpix
providers.description: Jerpix is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The primary web domain jerpix.com resolves to a live, actively hosted site (Google Workspace email, DNSimple nameservers), but as of this pass the company publishes no discoverable public API surface — no api/docs/developer/status subdomains, no OpenAPI, and no developer portal were found. This profile currently carries only verifiable identity and domain-security signals; it remains a lead awaiting a published API to enrich.

providers.name: Jet
providers.description: Jet.com was an American e-commerce company and online marketplace founded in 2014 by Marc Lore and headquartered in Hoboken, New Jersey. It offered a membership-style shopping model with dynamic, real-time pricing that lowered the total as shoppers added items to their cart. Walmart acquired Jet.com in 2016 for roughly USD 3.3 billion and folded its operations into Walmart's own e-commerce platform, discontinuing the Jet.com brand in 2020. The jet.com domain now redirects to walmart.com; Jet operates no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation. This record is retained as a defunct portfolio lead for network completeness.

providers.name: Jet (Walmart)
providers.description: Jet (Walmart) was a US e-commerce marketplace founded by Marc Lore and backed by Bain Capital Ventures, acquired by Walmart in 2016 for roughly 3.3 billion USD and subsequently wound down. The jet.com domain now 302-redirects to walmart.com (confirmed 2026-07-19) and no standalone Jet developer portal, API, documentation, or SDK surface exists; the brand and its commerce technology were absorbed into Walmart. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is retained for lineage/graph purposes but has no live public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Jet Com
providers.description: Jet.com was an American e-commerce marketplace founded in 2014 by Marc Lore that used dynamic, real-time pricing to lower cart totals as shoppers combined orders. Walmart acquired Jet.com in 2016 for approximately 3.3 billion dollars, folded its technology and talent into Walmart's online operation, and fully shut down the Jet.com brand and site in 2020. The jet.com domain now redirects to walmart.com, and no Jet-branded developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface remain online.

providers.name: Jetway
providers.description: Jetway was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead pointing at nextravel.com. Enrichment found that nextravel.com now 301-redirects to TravelPerk (www.travelperk.com), which itself redirects to www.perk.com, an all-in-one business travel and expense-management platform. NexTravel was a US corporate-travel startup acquired by TravelPerk; it no longer operates as an independent brand and publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery documents at nextravel.com (every probed path soft-404s to the Perk marketing site). This profile is retained as an acquired/redirected lead with no independent developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: jiayuan
providers.description: Jiayuan (世纪佳缘, jiayuan.com) is one of China's largest online dating and serious-relationship matchmaking platforms, connecting members seeking marriage and long-term relationships through profile matching, search, messaging, and offline matchmaking services delivered on web and mobile apps. Founded in 2003 and later part of the Baihe Jiayuan group, it operates as a consumer-facing social/dating product. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not appear to publish a public developer API program, so this profile carries company identity and probed domain-security signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Jibe
providers.description: Jibe was an HR-tech / talent-acquisition and recruitment-marketing SaaS company, surfaced as a portfolio company of sapphire-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company no longer operates independently: its domain www.jibe.com issues a blanket HTTP 301 redirect to www.icims.com (Jibe was acquired by iCIMS), and no independent Jibe developer portal, API, OpenAPI, or .well-known surface exists to harvest. No API artifacts could be enriched without fabrication.

providers.name: JioSaavn
providers.description: API to retrieve song information, album meta data and many more from JioSaavn

providers.name: Jiumaojiu
providers.description: Jiumaojiu (Jiu Mao Jiu International Holdings, HKEX: 09922) is a Chinese casual-dining restaurant group headquartered in Guangzhou and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange since January 2020. Founded roughly three decades ago, it operates 600+ restaurants across mainland China, Southeast Asia and North America under five brands: Jiumaojiu (Shanxi handmade-noodle cuisine), Tai Er (sour cabbage fish, 400+ locations), Song Hot Pot (Chongqing hot pot), Shan Wai Mian (Guizhou sour-soup hot pot) and Chao Na Bian (Chaoshan grilled beef). Backed by IDG Capital. As a consumer food-and-beverage operator it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity lead.

providers.name: Jjgmachining
providers.description: JJG (JJG Aero Pvt Ltd, JJG Machining Pvt Ltd, and JJG Special Processing Pvt Ltd) is a precision contract-manufacturing group founded in 2004 that produces machined components for the aerospace, automotive, and industrial sectors. It offers 2-5 axis CNC machining alongside high-volume turned and turn-mill parts in ferrous, aluminum, copper alloys, and titanium, backed by 30+ NADCAP-approved special processes such as electroplating, anodizing, paint, and NDT. This is a physical manufacturing company with no public API, developer program, or machine-readable API artifacts; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record only.

providers.name: Jobedu
providers.description: Jobedu is a Jordanian pop-culture creative retail and merchandise brand known for Arabic-language streetwear, apparel, prints, and consumer goods, operating a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront hosted on Shopify. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the jobedu.com storefront returns HTTP 404 (Shopify-hosted, DNS points to shops.myshopify.com) and no public API, developer portal, documentation, or /.well-known surface could be found, so no API artifacts were produced beyond a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Jopwell
providers.description: Jopwell was a career advancement and diversity-recruiting platform that connected Black, Latinx, and Native American students and professionals with employers for jobs, internships, and career resources. Founded in 2015 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors, it was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of an enrichment probe on 2026-07-19, the jopwell.com domain returns an HTTP 301 redirect to trueplatform.com (True, an executive search and talent-management firm), indicating the standalone Jopwell product is no longer operating. No public developer program, API, OpenAPI specification, documentation, or /.well-known/security.txt surface was found, so no API artifacts could be produced.

providers.name: Joyride
providers.description: Joyride was a mobile audio service that made driving more fun and more interesting, offering an in-car audio/entertainment experience for drivers and passengers. Founded by Jeff Chen (co-founder & CEO) and James Zhang (co-founder & CTO), the company raised a seed round from Cowboy Ventures and was subsequently acquired by Google, marking a successful exit. As a consumer mobile application it exposed no public developer API surface, and the product is no longer independently operated following the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: jsgaiya
providers.description: Jiangsu Gaiya Environmental Engineering Co., Ltd. (江苏盖亚环境工程有限公司) is a Suzhou-based environmental engineering and technology company, described on its site as the region's first firm specializing in contaminated-soil remediation, with offices at the Nanjing University Suzhou High-Tech Research Institute. Its business covers environmental engineering design and construction, environmental testing and risk assessment, R&D and sale of environmental-protection equipment, product distribution, and environmental technology consulting. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the Qiming venture network. Enrichment probes found a static Chinese-language marketing website (IIS, GB2312) and no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or other machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Jubilee Inc
providers.description: Jubilee Inc (Jubilee Media) is a Los Angeles-based digital media production company that creates discussion-based and dating video shows designed to provoke thoughtful conversation and foster human connection across social and ideological divides. Its flagship YouTube programs include Middle Ground, Odd One Out, and Ranking, alongside sister dating channels such as Love Comma Nectar (Versus 1) and the reaction and behind-the-scenes brand TwoBilee. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API or developer platform at this time, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Julu Mobile
providers.description: Julu Mobile was a Shanghai, China based mobile advertising network that served targeted, personalized ads to Chinese mobile users by analyzing mobile interactions to profile user interests. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Zhubajie on November 1, 2012 and no longer operates an independent product or developer platform. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, documentation, MCP server, or developer surface, and julumobile.com resolves to a Cloudflare block page.

providers.name: Jump Ramp Games
providers.description: Jump Ramp Games was a New York City casual mobile gaming company best known for Lucktastic, a free scratch-card, rewards, and instant-win app that launched on Android in 2014 and grew to roughly 10 million US installs across Android and iOS, consistently ranking near the top of the lifestyle category. Founded by Alex Betancur and Tony Vartanian and backed by Bullpen Capital, the company paired free-to-play casual gaming with performance-marketing and rewards technology. Jump Ramp Games was acquired by MobilityWare in September 2019, which took over the Lucktastic franchise; the jumprampgames.com domain now redirects to mobilityware.com. The company exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

providers.name: JumpCam
providers.description: JumpCam was a consumer mobile video startup (San Francisco, founded 2013 by former Yammer/YouTube product leader David Stewart) that let groups of friends collaboratively shoot and edit a single video from up to thirty short clips. It raised $2.7M led by Google Ventures (GV) and shipped an iOS app. The company is no longer active and jumpcam.com is now a parked domain listed for sale (Afternic); no developer portal, API, documentation, or other public API surface exists. Surfaced as a GV portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirmed there is no live API to profile.

providers.name: Jumpcut
providers.description: Jumpcut (Jumpcut, Inc.) is a Y Combinator-backed, remote-first digital-media company founded in 2014 in Los Angeles that produces online courses about entrepreneurship and content creation — teaching viral YouTube growth, audience building, and launching digital products with marketing automation. It reached the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Canaan Partners. Jumpcut is a consumer education/creator business, not an API producer: it publishes no developer platform, API reference, or machine-readable API specification, so there is no API surface to onboard here. As of this profile its primary domain jumpcut.com does not resolve (registered via Namecheap through 2032 but serving no DNS/website), and customers reported losing account access in late 2025, indicating the product has wound down. Retained as an identity-only network stub.

providers.name: Jumprope
providers.description: Jumprope was a how-to video creation app backed by lightspeed-venture-partners that let creators produce and share step-by-step, swipeable instructional videos. The company (formerly at getjumprope.com) was acquired by Snap Inc. in early 2021 and the standalone product was subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass it operates no independent website, developer portal, or public API surface — the getjumprope.com and jumprope.co domains no longer resolve, and the unrelated jumprope.com domain is a physical jump-rope retailer on Shopify (not this company). No API artifacts could be discovered or derived; this profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record only.

providers.name: Jumptap
providers.description: Jumptap was a mobile advertising and audience-targeting platform founded in 2005 and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It matched ads to signals such as time of day, carrier network, site content, and device type, helping app developers acquire users and helping developers and publishers maximize ad revenue. In August 2013 Jumptap was acquired by Millennial Media (valued at roughly $210-232M in stock); Millennial Media was subsequently acquired by AOL/Verizon and folded into what is now Yahoo. Jumptap no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API.

providers.name: Junlebao
providers.description: Junlebao Dairy Group (Shijiazhuang Junlebao Dairy Co., Ltd., 君乐宝乳业) is one of China's largest dairy processors, founded in 1995 and headquartered in Shijiazhuang, Hebei Province. Its business spans the full dairy value chain: infant and toddler formula, low-temperature (chilled) yogurt, room-temperature liquid milk, fresh milk, cheese and dairy-farming/animal-husbandry operations. Junlebao is the largest dairy company in Hebei and ranks among China's top dairy producers, leading domestic infant-formula sales volume and holding a top position in low-temperature yogurt. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hongshan (HSG). As a consumer packaged-goods / food manufacturer it publishes no public developer program, API, or open-data surface; this profile tracks its corporate web presence and company identity.

providers.name: juren
providers.description: Juren (巨人教育 / Juren Education) is a Chinese comprehensive basic-education training institution founded in 1994 and headquartered in Beijing (Zhongguancun, Haidian District). It is a B2C education and tutoring business — spanning brands such as Juren School, Juren 1-on-1, Xiao Juren, and Juren online school — offering courses in Chinese, English, mathematics, arts, study tours, and seasonal camps, plus education publishing and franchising. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found NO public developer, API, or technical-integration surface: the historic official domain juren.com does not resolve (DNS), juren.ai is a parked for-sale domain, and juren.cn is a Chinese-language marketing mirror with no developer section. This is a non-API B2C company lead retained for network completeness rather than API artifact enrichment.

providers.name: JustBook
providers.description: JustBook was a Berlin, Germany based mobile hotel booking startup that offered same-day and last-minute hotel deals at discounted rates, in a model similar to HotelTonight. Founded in 2012, it grew to cover last-minute inventory across more than 120 cities in Europe and the United States through its iOS, Android, and web apps. The company was backed by Creandum, DN Capital, and Earlybird Venture Capital (among roughly 21 investors, raising about $3.74M) and was acquired by UK luxury-travel company Secret Escapes in January 2014 to strengthen its German-market and mobile presence. JustBook no longer operates as an independent brand and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation; this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct, acquired Creandum portfolio company. Note: the justbook.de domain is now an unrelated book price-comparison site (BookFinder) and is not connected to this company.

providers.name: Juxta Labs
providers.description: Juxta Labs, Inc. was a San Francisco social and mobile applications startup founded around 2011 by Jared Allgood and Jayson Ahlstrom, building social games and light-social apps for teens (titles such as Zoomed In, Shadow Shapes, and Pick the Song) that reportedly reached tens of millions of users. In June 2015 the company raised roughly $1.7M from investors including 500 Global (then 500 Startups), Monashees, Alta Ventures, and Atua Ventures, which is why it surfaces in the 500 Global portfolio. The company is now inactive/deadpooled and its site (juxtalabs.com) is offline, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. Note: an unrelated current company at juxtalabs.io (enterprise AI document automation) is a different entity and is not this 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Jüsto
providers.description: Jüsto is a Mexican online-only supermarket founded in 2019 by Ricardo Weder, headquartered in Mexico City. It operates a direct-to-consumer grocery e-commerce and delivery model with no physical stores, sourcing produce and pantry goods directly from farmers, producers, and brands and fulfilling orders from micro-fulfillment dark stores. The company sells its catalog through web and mobile apps and has raised venture funding from investors including General Atlantic, SoftBank, Foundation Capital, and 500 Global. Jüsto has no public developer program or documented API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: K2 Space
providers.description: K2 Space (K2 Space Corporation) is a Los Angeles / Torrance, California aerospace startup that designs and manufactures high-power "Mega Class" satellite buses. Its platforms deliver roughly 20kW of array power and up to one metric ton of payload capacity - about ten times the power and payload of conventional buses - to maximize the throw-weight of next-generation launch vehicles like SpaceX Starship and Blue Origin New Glenn. K2 builds radiation-tolerant, vertically integrated (80% in-house) spacecraft with redundant avionics and high-delta-v propulsion for LEO, MEO, GEO and cislunar missions, serving commercial and U.S. government / defense customers. Backed by First Round Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint Ventures, the company raised a $250M Series C at a $3B valuation and is preparing its first production satellite, GRAVITAS. K2 Space is a hardware company with no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: kaiheikeji
providers.description: Kaiheikeji Digital (开黑科技) is a Chinese mobile entertainment and esports social platform operating an online game "sparring"/companion marketplace, where players post demands (game, skill level, and price) and qualified players selectively take orders to play alongside clients. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, which led a roughly $15M Series A+ round in 2018. The company operates a consumer-facing mobile app rather than a public developer API program; no public API, developer portal, or API documentation surface has been identified. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record surfaced from the Qiming portfolio.

providers.name: Kairos Aerospace
providers.description: Kairos Aerospace is a methane-detection company founded in 2014 in Sunnyvale, California that provides cost-effective, high-frequency aerial methane detection for the oil and gas industry. Its patented LeakSurveyor spectrometer is flown over upstream and midstream infrastructure to image methane plumes, and proprietary software turns those flights into actionable emissions data so operators can find, prioritize, and fix leaks. The company rebranded as Insight M in March 2024 and was subsequently acquired by Zeitview. Kairos Aerospace was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile is an identity record rather than an API catalog entry.

providers.name: Kairos Sports Tech
providers.description: Kairos Sports Tech was a Belfast and Dublin based sports technology startup that built a team operations and communication platform for professional sports, integrating team planning, daily communication, and player management into one centralized system used by more than 100 football and rugby organizations. Founded by Andrew Trimble and Gareth Quinn and backed by Techstars, Kairos was acquired by Teamworks in January 2024 and its product was folded into the Teamworks Hub athlete operating system. The standalone kairostech.io site now redirects entirely to teamworks.com/hub/, and Kairos no longer operates an independent public API, developer program, or discoverable API artifacts.

providers.name: Kaixin001
providers.description: Kaixin001 (开心网) is a Chinese social networking website launched in March 2008 by founder Cheng Bingao, a former senior executive at Sina. It rose to mass popularity in 2009-2010 on the back of viral social games such as "Friends for Sale" and "Parking Wars" before losing ground to Renren, Sina Weibo, and WeChat. After the parent company was acquired by a listed company in 2016, the founder departed and the business pivoted toward enterprise services and internet finance, marginalizing the original social network. Kaixin001 discontinued its Flash-based social gaming on November 18, 2023, and now persists mainly as a low-activity nostalgia platform. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub of Qiming and exposes no current public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Kalpana
providers.description: Kalpana, Inc. was a Sunnyvale, California networking hardware company founded in 1990 by Vinod Bhardwaj and Larry Blair that built the first Ethernet switch, the seven-port EtherSwitch, and pioneered EtherChannel link aggregation and the Virtual LAN (VLAN) concept. The company was acquired by Cisco Systems in 1994 and has been defunct as an independent entity ever since, with its technology absorbed into Cisco's Catalyst switching product line. There is no surviving developer portal, API, or public developer surface associated with the original Kalpana, Inc.

providers.name: Kamcord
providers.description: Kamcord was a San Francisco-based mobile technology company (Y Combinator, Summer 2012) founded by Aditya Rathnam, Kevin Wang, and Matt Zitzmann. It offered an iOS and Android SDK that let game developers embed in-app gameplay recording, live streaming ("appcasting"), and social sharing to YouTube, Twitter, and Facebook, and grew to roughly 200 million device installs. The company later pivoted to a short-form mobile screen-content social network ("shots"). In November 2017 Lyft acquihired most of the ~15-person team, including co-founders Rathnam and Wang, and Kamcord wound down its consumer app, live streaming, and developer SDK by the end of 2017. The company is DEFUNCT and no longer operates any developer program or API. The kamcord.com domain has since been repurposed by an unrelated lifestyle/blog publisher and is NOT associated with the original Kamcord.

providers.name: Kanler
providers.description: Kanler was a Redwood City, California home-improvement marketplace and construction technology company that connected homeowners with vetted home-improvement professionals and managed their projects end to end, positioning itself around price transparency and project peace of mind. Seed-funded in 2016 with backing from Battery Ventures, Floodgate Fund, TriplePoint Capital and Flight VC, the company later operated as a custom-home and whole-house remodeling firm. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (kanler.com) returns HTTP 404 and no public developer, API, or documentation surface could be found, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Kanoodle
providers.description: Kanoodle was an online advertising network founded in 1999 by Kent Keating, specializing in search-targeted and later content-targeted (contextual) sponsored links, adding partners such as CBS MarketWatch in January 2004. In August 2006 it restructured under a new parent company, Seevast Corp - the search-advertising business kept the Kanoodle brand, the content-targeted contextual ad product was spun out as Pulse 360, and the newly acquired Moniker.com domain registrar ran as a separate unit. Listed here as an Insight Partners portfolio company, Kanoodle/Seevast is defunct and exposes no surviving public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation - the seevast.com domain now resolves to a parked-domain lander. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Kansas City Southern
providers.description: Kansas City Southern (KCS) was a transportation holding company that operated freight rail networks across the United States and Mexico. On April 14, 2023, KCS merged with Canadian Pacific Railway to form Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC), the first single-line rail network connecting Canada, the United States, and Mexico. CPKC operates approximately 32,000 km (20,000 mi) of rail and is headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, with U.S. headquarters in Kansas City, Missouri.

providers.name: Kaodim
providers.description: Kaodim was a Southeast Asian on-demand home and local services marketplace founded in 2014 that connected consumers with service providers such as cleaners, plumbers, electricians, aircon technicians, movers, tutors, and event professionals. Headquartered in Malaysia, it operated regionally under Kaodim.com (Malaysia), Kaodim.sg (Singapore), Gawin.ph (Philippines), and Beres.id (Indonesia), and raised venture funding from investors including 500 Global (500 Startups), Venturra Capital, and Square Peg. The company ceased all operations on July 1, 2022, citing prolonged COVID-19 lockdowns, labor shortages, rising costs, and weakened demand. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer program or API surface exists for the defunct company, so there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: KapStone Paper and Packaging
providers.description: KapStone Paper and Packaging Corporation was a producer of containerboard, corrugated products, and specialty paper based in Northbrook, Illinois. In November 2018, KapStone was acquired by WestRock for approximately $4.9 billion, ending its existence as an independent public company. WestRock subsequently merged with Smurfit Kappa in July 2024 to form Smurfit Westrock, the global combined entity that today inherits the legacy KapStone operations.

providers.name: karmaloop
providers.description: karmaloop is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Kashya
providers.description: Kashya Inc. was a data-protection software company providing continuous data protection (CDP) and heterogeneous, storage-agnostic data replication for enterprise disaster recovery and business continuity. Founded around 2000 with headquarters in San Jose, California and research and development in Israel, and backed by Battery Ventures among other investors, Kashya was acquired by EMC Corporation in 2006 for a reported ~$153 million. Its technology became the foundation of EMC RecoverPoint. The company has been defunct since the acquisition and operates no independent website, developer portal, or public API surface today.

providers.name: Katango
providers.description: Katango was a Palo Alto, California mobile software startup whose smartphone app automatically organized a user's phone and social contacts into intelligent groups (circles) using clustering algorithms, so people could share and message the right subset of friends without manually building lists. The company was backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (through its sFund social initiative) and was acquired by Google in November 2011, with the team joining Google to work on the Google+ Circles experience. The standalone product was discontinued after the acquisition. This API Evangelist profile was created as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio lead; enrichment confirms the company is defunct with no public developer surface, API, or documentation. The katango.com domain now resolves to Google-owned infrastructure with no live site.

providers.name: Katch
providers.description: Katch is a Speedinvest-backed agricultural technology and embedded-finance platform serving agribusiness supply chains. It offers essential digital services for its partners, including e-commerce, grain procurement, and business intelligence, and layers embedded financial solutions such as factoring and credit directly within transactions. This lets agricultural partners manage cash flow, access working capital, and streamline supply-chain operations from a single platform. Katch was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; an enrichment pass found no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI, or machine-readable API surface for the company at this time.

providers.name: Kazadi Enterprises
providers.description: Kazadi Enterprises develops grid-independent renewable energy systems for cold chain management and energy-intensive dehumidification. Its patented Ring Regenerator technology unlocks environmental heat from ambient air to regenerate liquid desiccant, reducing conventional energy consumption for food processing, controlled environment agriculture (CEA), and HVAC applications. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: KB Home
providers.description: KB Home is one of the largest and most recognized homebuilders in the United States, building single-family homes, townhomes, and condominiums for first-time, move-up, and active adult buyers across more than 45 markets.

providers.name: KBR
providers.description: KBR is a Fortune 500 company that delivers science, technology, and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world, spanning defense, intelligence, space, energy transition, and sustainable infrastructure markets.

providers.name: kechowpharma
providers.description: Kechow Pharma (Shanghai Kezhou Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Shanghai's Zhangjiang High-Tech Park. It focuses on innovative small-molecule drug research and development in oncology and free-radical-related diseases, pursuing Best-in-Class therapeutics based on independent intellectual property. Its lead approved product is Kelopin (tolametinib), a MEK inhibitor for advanced NRAS-mutant melanoma. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; no public developer or API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Keepe
providers.description: Keepe operates a US nationwide service-provider network of vetted technicians covering HVAC, plumbing, electrical, furnace and heating, air conditioning, home appliances, and EV charger installation and repair. The platform streamlines the full home-services workflow end to end - recruiting, sourcing, dispatching, authorizing, and paying qualified technicians - so property managers, warranty companies, and insurers can get high-quality repair work completed reliably across markets. Keepe runs a consumer/technician mobile app and a private application backend at api.keepe.com; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline with the infrastructure signals that are publicly observable.

providers.name: Kelly Services
providers.description: Kelly Services is a global leader in providing workforce solutions, connecting talented people to companies in need of their skills across a variety of industries including staffing, talent management, and outsourcing.

providers.name: Kennametal
providers.description: Kennametal is a leading provider of productivity solutions for metalworking, earth cutting, and wear components, coatings, and powders. Kennametal offers online integration services including Punch-Out / OCI (Open Catalog Interface), EDI, and a Product Data Portal for catalog and product information.

providers.name: Keno
providers.description: Keno is an on-demand, doorstep car-wash and vehicle-care mobile application operating in the United Arab Emirates, billing itself as the "No.1 car wash app in the UAE". Customers download the iOS or Android app, add their vehicle, select from wash, maintenance, and detailing services (priced by vehicle class from bike to luxury SUV), and a mobile team of "ninjas" arrives at the customer's location to perform the work with a choice of payment methods. Keno is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer mobile application with no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kenvue
providers.description: Kenvue is the world's largest pure-play consumer health company by revenue, formed from the consumer health spin-off of Johnson & Johnson. Everyday care is a powerful catalyst in making you feel better, inside and out. Kenvue's iconic brands include Tylenol, Neutrogena, Listerine, Aveeno, Band-Aid, and Johnson's.

providers.name: Kerning Cultures
providers.description: Kerning Cultures is a Middle East and North Africa media company producing narrative journalism and audio storytelling podcasts in Arabic and English. Based in Dubai, UAE and backed by 500 Global, the Kerning Cultures Network creates original shows, branded audio, and advertising for a regional listener audience. It operates as a consumer media and content brand and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future API surface.

providers.name: Keurig Green Mountain
providers.description: Keurig Green Mountain was a leader in specialty coffee and coffee makers, producing the Keurig single-serve brewing system and partnering with leading coffee brands. In 2018 Keurig Green Mountain merged with Dr Pepper Snapple Group to form Keurig Dr Pepper, a Fortune 500 beverage company. This repository preserves the historical API and developer footprint of Keurig Green Mountain prior to that merger.

providers.name: Keychain
providers.description: Keychain is an AI-powered operating system and manufacturing network for the consumer packaged goods (CPG) industry. The platform connects brands, retailers, and private-label buyers with vetted contract manufacturers and co-manufacturers, helping teams discover production partners, source ingredients and packaging, benchmark supplier capabilities, and bring new products to market faster. Keychain aggregates data across the fragmented CPG supply chain into a searchable network so brands can find who makes what and manufacturers can surface available capacity. The company is headquartered in New York and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Keynexus
providers.description: KeyNexus was an enterprise encryption key management company based in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, providing centralized key management, Bring Your Own Key (BYOK), and Key Management as a Service for cloud, on-premises, and hybrid deployments. Its platform helped enterprises generate, store, distribute, and control the lifecycle of encryption keys used to protect data across applications and infrastructure. KeyNexus was acquired by StorMagic in January 2021, and its technology was folded into the StorMagic SvKMS (Secure Virtual Key Management Service) product; the keynexus.com domain now redirects to StorMagic's encryption key management offering. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking. KeyNexus no longer operates as an independent developer platform.

providers.name: Kezaihui
providers.description: Kezaihui (再惠 / Zaihuihui (Shanghai) Network Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Shanghai-based Chinese SaaS platform for local-life-service commerce, providing offline merchants — primarily mid-tier restaurants plus entertainment, beauty, and hospitality businesses — with one-stop store-opening and digital-operations tooling. Founded around 2012, the company offers private-domain member and community management, trading-platform shop diagnostics and automated strategy recommendations, content-creator (influencer) marketing, multi-channel precision ad delivery, and the Hui Shenghuo (惠生活) rights-aggregation platform, helping merchants operate across Meituan, Douyin, Xiaohongshu, and Taobao. It reports serving hundreds of thousands of merchants across dozens of Chinese cities with more than 1,000 employees. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer program or API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Khazenly
providers.description: Khazenly is a Cairo, Egypt based cloud order-fulfillment and e-commerce enablement platform that helps online merchants and brands manage the full post-checkout journey. Its stack combines an order management system, warehousing and pick-pack-ship fulfillment, last-mile delivery, and cash-on-delivery collection so sellers can outsource operations while retaining visibility. Khazenly connects to popular e-commerce storefronts and marketplaces to sync orders, inventory, and shipping status. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network; its public developer/API surface is not openly documented, so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signals rather than harvested API artifacts.

providers.name: Kimono Labs
providers.description: Kimono Labs was a developer-tools startup that let users turn any website into a structured API without writing code, using a visual point-and-click tool to define data selectors that Kimono would crawl on a schedule and expose as JSON/CSV endpoints and RSS feeds. Founded in 2014 by Pratap Ranade and Ryan Rowe and backed by Cowboy Ventures, the company was acquired by Palantir Technologies in February 2016, after which the hosted cloud service at kimonolabs.com was shut down on 29 February 2016; a downloadable Kimono Desktop application was released as a farewell so existing scrapers could continue running locally. The company is defunct and operates no live API today; this profile is retained for historical and network completeness.

providers.name: Kindred Ai
providers.description: Kindred AI (Kindred Systems) was an artificial-intelligence and robotics company that applied reinforcement learning and teleoperation to autonomous piece-picking robots for warehouse and retail-fulfillment automation. Founded by D-Wave alumni and backed by DCVC among other investors, Kindred was acquired by Ocado Group in 2020 and folded into Ocado's advanced-robotics operations. It no longer operates an independent public developer surface: the kindred.ai brand domain remains under corporate (CSC) DNS with active Google Workspace mail, but serves no live homepage, developer portal, documentation, or public API. This profile is retained as an enrichment lead surfaced from the DCVC portfolio; no OpenAPI, SDK, or hosted API artifacts could be verified.

providers.name: Kinecta
providers.description: Kinecta Corporation was a venture-backed provider of software infrastructure for content distribution, funded by Canaan Partners and reaching a Series B stage. It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. The company is no longer operating as an independent provider and publishes no active developer surface, API, documentation, or developer portal, so there are no API artifacts to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio identity record.

providers.name: Kinetic Apps
providers.description: Kinetic (kineticapps.ai) is a Brooklyn-based venture studio and consumer-software portfolio-company builder that uses AI to let small teams ship products that previously required much larger ones. Rather than long planning cycles, Kinetic launches focused consumer apps, watches real user behavior, and feeds those learnings back into a shared engine of creative, distribution channels, data, and product patterns to accelerate the next launch. Its portfolio of consumer applications includes Nested, Prove It, PayMe, Relay, and Tempo. Backed by GV (Google Ventures). Kinetic publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile is a company/provider lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kings
providers.description: Kings International Olympiads (kings.lt) is an international educational olympiads organization that runs academic competitions for students, operating a multi-language web platform served from kingsolympiad.com. It was surfaced through the 500 Global venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the organization publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery artifacts (/.well-known/*, llms.txt all resolve to the SPA shell, i.e. soft 404s).

providers.name: Kinnek
providers.description: Kinnek was a B2B purchasing marketplace that helped small and mid-sized businesses buy from suppliers. Buyers could describe what they needed, collect competitive quotes from vetted suppliers, read unbiased reviews, and get expert purchasing advice in one place, under the tagline "Purchasing Made Painless." The company operated at kinnek.com but is no longer active: the domain no longer resolves (no DNS A, MX, NS, or SOA records) and the site survives only via the Internet Archive (strongest snapshot circa 2017). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead (backed by 500 Global and Version One Ventures); the enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specifications for this provider.

providers.name: Kippt
providers.description: Kippt was a social bookmarking and link-saving service (kippt.com) that let people save, organize, and share bookmarks in lists and follow other users' collections. It exposed a public REST API over the kippt.com domain, which produced a small ecosystem of community-authored client libraries in Python, Ruby, and JavaScript. Kippt was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The service has since been discontinued: the kippt.com domain resolves to a legacy IP but no longer responds, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to harvest. What remains real and capturable is the set of third-party API wrapper packages still published on the public registries.

providers.name: Kishlay Foods
providers.description: Kishlay Foods is a snack-food manufacturing company based in Guwahati, Assam, India, operating since 2003. The company produces premium potato chips, namkeens, and traditional Indian savory snacks, with regional varieties such as Aloo Bhujia, Bengali Mix, Chakna Mix, Cocktail Peanut, and Chana Jor Garam. Kishlay Foods runs a consumer/distributor marketing website and recruits distributor partners across the region; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, webhook, or developer-portal surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Kitch
providers.description: Kitch was a Lisbon, Portugal based restaurant technology company founded in 2019 by Rui Bento and Nuno Rodrigues, both former Uber executives for southern Europe. After starting as a delivery-first "dark kitchen" operator, Kitch pivoted during the 2020 pandemic into a SaaS platform that let restaurants consolidate and manage digital orders arriving from multiple third-party delivery marketplaces — Glovo, Uber Eats, Bolt Food and Just Eat among them — on a single tablet, alongside their own direct-ordering storefront, so operators could keep control of their menus, pricing and customer identity instead of depending on the aggregator apps. Kitch raised roughly EUR 1 million in pre-seed funding led by Seedcamp and Mustard Seed MAZE, followed by a EUR 3.25 million seed round led by Atlantic Food Labs. The company was acquired by Barcelona-based delivery platform Glovo in a deal signed in January 2022 and announced in March 2022, and the standalone Kitch brand has since been retired. Kitch never published a public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or status page was ever published on kitch.io, and none appears in the Internet Archive's record of the domain. The kitch.io domain registration has since lapsed and now resolves to an unrelated third-party gambling site, so no live link is carried in this profile.

providers.name: Kiva Software
providers.description: Kiva Software Corporation was a pioneer of the internet application server, founded in May 1994 by chairman and CEO Keng Lim and headquartered in Mountain View, California. In January 1996 Kiva shipped what is widely credited as the industry's first web application server, giving companies a platform for developing and deploying transaction-oriented business applications on the web — and the first Java application server to market, with C++ application development supported alongside it. The product line comprised the Kiva Enterprise Server (deployment and management runtime), the Kiva Application Builder (graphical development tool), and the Kiva SDK with Java and C++ foundation classes; the company also ran the Kiva Enterprise Alliance Program (KEAP) for end-to-end partner solutions. Customers included Bank of America, E-Trade, Travelocity, Internet Shopping Network, Hong Kong Telecom, and Pacific Bell Internet. Kiva raised roughly $13.9 million across two rounds from Weiss Peck & Greer, Greylock, Discovery Ventures, Sippl MacDonald Ventures, Norwest Venture Capital, and Trinity Ventures, and is listed in the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio as a 1996 early-stage investment. In December 1997 Netscape Communications acquired Kiva for approximately $180 million in stock (6.3 million Netscape shares), and the Kiva Enterprise Server became the Netscape Application Server — which went on to become the iPlanet Application Server under the AOL/Netscape–Sun Microsystems alliance, then Sun ONE Application Server and Sun Java System Application Server. Kiva has not operated independently since 1997, published no public developer API in the modern sense, and has no live web presence today (the historical www.kivasoft.com domain is now parked and listed for sale). This profile is retained as a historical Lightspeed and Trinity Ventures portfolio record — there is no active developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: KNO
providers.description: Kno, Inc. was a digital textbook and student learning platform founded in May 2009 in Santa Clara, California by CEO Osman Rashid (co-founder of Chegg) and CTO Babur Habib. Kno began as a dual-screen tablet built for students, abandoned hardware in 2011, and pivoted to eTextbook software delivered across iPad, Android, Windows and the web in partnership with textbook publishers. The company raised roughly $93 million from Andreessen Horowitz, Intel Capital, Goldman Sachs, FLOODGATE, First Round Capital, SV Angel, Advance Publications and GSV Capital before being acquired by Intel in November 2013 for approximately $15 million and rebranded as Intel Education Study, which has itself since been discontinued. As of enrichment the kno.com domain is parked and redirects to a third-party domain brokerage, and the provider exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other artifact surface to enrich.

providers.name: Knote
providers.description: Knote is a small New York-based startup backed by 500 Global, surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.
