Third-party company databases describe it inconsistently: Tracxn profiles Knote as a knowledge-management platform that raised roughly $150K from 500 Global, while Dealroom describes it as an AI-powered email summarization and management tool. No first-party description could be confirmed. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass the knote.com web property is offline — the domain resolves (Cloudflare nameservers, an EC2 A record, live Google Workspace MX and an SPF record including Mailgun and Mailchimp) but refuses connections on both port 80 and port 443, so no homepage, developer portal, documentation, API reference, or machine-readable specification could be retrieved. No corporate GitHub organization, package-registry client library, or public API surface was found; the GitHub repositories named "Knote" are unrelated third-party note-taking and Kubernetes-course projects. This profile therefore carries only what could be independently verified: the funding and identity facts above plus a live DNS/TLS domain-security probe. It should be treated as a dormant or defunct lead and re-checked if the domain returns to service.

providers.name: Koan
providers.description: Koan was a goal-management SaaS at koan.co that billed itself as "The Free OKR and Status Tracking Platform", pairing OKR goal setting with a weekly "Reflections" status-update loop and an Insights layer so teams tracked progress as a habit rather than a quarterly spreadsheet exercise. The product shipped a Goal Metrics API — enabled per goal via an API integration toggle on the goal edit page — so teams could push their most important numbers into Koan goals in real time, alongside a Zapier app and native integrations with Slack, Jira, and Okta SSO. Koan was acquired by Gtmhub, an acquisition announced on its own homepage and blog by January 2022, and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Uncork Capital portfolio company. As of enrichment the koan.co domain no longer serves the product: it redirects to a GoDaddy domain-for-sale lander, and there is no live developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDK, or status surface left to harvest.

providers.name: Koru Careers
providers.description: Koru (joinkoru.com) was a Seattle-based predictive hiring and people-analytics SaaS company. Its platform built a per-employer "predictive hiring fingerprint" and scored candidates against the Koru7 Impact Skills assessment — Grit, Rigour, Impact, Teamwork, Curiosity, Ownership and Polish — via a 20-minute online pre-interview that produced a Candidate Fit Score, with the stated goal of increasing quality of hire and reducing screening bias. Products were marketed as Koru Hire and Koru Develop. The company was acquired by Cappfinity: between February and November 2020 joinkoru.com began redirecting to koru.cappfinity.com, where the Koru7 Impact Skills Assessment was carried as a Cappfinity product. That subdomain now redirects to cappfinity.com, which carries no remaining Koru branding, and the joinkoru.com domain has lapsed and currently serves unrelated online-gambling affiliate content. Koru published no public developer portal, documentation, or API; this profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct company and no live endpoints are catalogued.

providers.name: Kosmix
providers.description: Kosmix Corporation was a Mountain View, California topic-discovery and search company operating from roughly 2005 to 2011. Rather than returning a ranked list of links, Kosmix automatically assembled a topic "home page for the web" for any subject, aggregating and categorizing content across health, science, food, sports, politics, travel, finance and other verticals. The company also shipped the RightHealth, MeeHive and Tweetbeat properties, the last of which filtered and organized real-time Twitter activity by topic. Kosmix was acquired by Walmart in 2011 and became the nucleus of @WalmartLabs; kosmix.com later 301-redirected to walmartlabs.com and the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record. There is no live Kosmix developer surface, API, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Kubota Corporation
providers.description: Kubota Corporation is a Japanese multinational manufacturing agricultural, construction, and industrial machinery, including compact tractors, excavators, mowers, utility vehicles, engines, and water and environmental infrastructure systems sold in over 120 countries. Kubota does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; equipment telematics (KubotaNOW) and dealer integrations are handled through partner channels rather than open APIs.

providers.name: Kyndoo
providers.description: Kyndoo Inc. was a San Francisco based influencer-marketing software platform that let brands find, connect to and work with social-media influencers. Its differentiator was audience authenticity: Kyndoo built a database of vetted influencers and published the "Kyndex" score, described as a credit score for influencers, which measured whether a following was made of real people with buying intent rather than purchased bot accounts. Around that database it sold campaign management, attribution and brand-safety tooling to brands, taking a service fee on the influencer deals brands negotiated through the platform. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Kyndoo was acquired by CIPIO (cipio.ai) and its web property is now offline - kyndoo.com has not served a page since early 2022. Kyndoo never published a public API, developer portal or SDK, so this profile is an identity and lifecycle record rather than an API profile.

providers.name: Kyte
providers.description: Kyte was a full-stack technology-operations company that delivered rental cars on demand to the customer's door, positioning itself for any trip longer than a rideshare — a car for a day, a few days, or longer — with no rental counters, no lines and no paperwork. Headquartered in San Francisco, the company combined a consumer mobile and web booking experience with its own fleet and delivery operations ("bits and atoms"), and at its peak operated in 14 US markets delivering tens of thousands of trips per month. It was a growth-stage portfolio company of Anthemis under that firm's Data, Tech and Infrastructure thesis. Kyte was a consumer-facing operator and never published a public developer program, API, SDK or developer portal, and as of this enrichment pass its web properties no longer serve the company.

providers.name: L Brands
providers.description: L Brands was a Fortune 500 specialty retail holding company best known for Victoria's Secret, PINK, and Bath & Body Works. In 2021 the company split into two independent publicly traded companies, with Bath & Body Works, Inc. retaining the original NYSE listing and Victoria's Secret & Co. spun off as a standalone retailer. The L Brands brand is no longer in active use; this repository preserves the historical corporate record. No public developer API has been documented.

providers.name: L2
providers.description: L2 Inc was a subscription research and business intelligence firm founded in New York City in 2010 by NYU Stern marketing professor Scott Galloway and co-founder Maureen Mullen. L2 benchmarked the digital competence of consumer brands, publishing more than 25 Digital IQ Index reports each year covering over 2,200 brands across fashion, luxury, retail, beauty, financial services, hospitality and consumer packaged goods. Its research scored brands on site experience, e-commerce, digital marketing, social media and mobile execution, and was sold as a subscription to CMOs and senior marketing leaders. The firm raised roughly $16.5 million in venture funding, including backing from General Catalyst (Larry Bohn and Paul Sagan) from 2014. Gartner acquired L2 in March 2017, when it had about 150 employees across New York and London, and folded the Digital IQ research into Gartner for Marketers. L2 never operated a public developer program or API: its research was delivered through a subscriber web platform and published reports. The l2inc.com domain is registered but no longer resolves, and no L2-branded developer, documentation or API surface remains online. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Lagoa
providers.description: Lagoa was a cloud-based 3D visualization, rendering, and CAD publishing platform built by TeamUp Technologies Inc., billed as the first web-based platform for photoreal 3D visualization and rendering. It let artists, designers, engineers, and architects import over 40 native CAD formats, build kinematic assemblies, produce photoreal renders in the browser via its MultiOptics interactive rendering engine, publish interactive 3D product configurators, and collaborate on scenes in real time — with no local hardware or installed software. Lagoa also ran a developer platform exposing server-side Platform APIs (geometry and image transcoding, asset management, thumbnailing, user authentication, versioning) alongside an Application Framework with Application, Collaboration, and Real-time Persistence APIs for embedding browser-based 3D into third-party apps. The company acquired browser CAD tool 3DTin in September 2013. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company is defunct: the marketing site (home.lagoa.com), support and API documentation (support.lagoa.com) and application host all stopped resolving, the github.com/lagoa organization is empty, and lagoa.com is now a parked listing offered for sale on atom.com. No live developer, API, or documentation surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Lancope
providers.description: Lancope was an Atlanta, Georgia based network security company best known for StealthWatch, a NetFlow-based network visibility and security analytics platform that used flow telemetry from existing routers and switches to detect internal threats, lateral movement, and anomalous behavior without deploying inline sensors. Lancope was acquired by Cisco Systems on December 22, 2015 for approximately $452.5 million to advance Cisco's "Security Everywhere" strategy. StealthWatch was folded into Cisco's security portfolio, rebranded Cisco Stealthwatch Enterprise and later, from version 7.4.0, Cisco Secure Network Analytics. Lancope no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, API, or SDK of its own - lancope.com now redirects to the Cisco Secure Network Analytics product page. The programmable surface descended from StealthWatch (the Secure Network Analytics REST APIs, plus the deprecated SOAP Web Services API) is documented by Cisco on developer.cisco.com and is catalogued in the API Evangelist network under the Cisco provider repositories rather than here.

providers.name: Lara Networks
providers.description: Lara Networks, Inc. (founded as Lara Technology) was a fabless semiconductor company headquartered at 110 Nortech Parkway, San Jose, California, that architected, designed, and marketed silicon-based packet-processing solutions for high-speed Internet and networking infrastructure. Its products were built on a patent-pending Associative Processing Technology (APT) and manufactured on 0.18-micron process technology: Network Database Search Engine (NDSE) devices, network coprocessors, and NDSE subsystems, with Content-Aware Switching (CAS) solutions in development. The devices were content-addressable memory search engines that offloaded ultra-large table lookups from network processors — holding tables of more than three million addresses and sustaining over 100 million lookups per second so switches and routers could process packets from Layer 2 to Layer 7 at full line rate at OC-48 (2.5Gbps) and above. The company raised a $40 million second round in October 2000 led by Raza Ventures with Battery Ventures, InveStar Capital, and TeleSoft Venture Partners, alongside a long-term co-development agreement and minority equity investment from STMicroelectronics. Lara Networks no longer operates independently: by January 2003 its laranetworks.com domain served Cypress Semiconductor Corporation content, and today every path on the domain 301-redirects to Infineon Technologies, which acquired Cypress in April 2020. As a fabless chip company selling silicon to network equipment manufacturers, Lara Networks never operated a web or developer API program, and no public API surface exists to enrich. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Launchbit
providers.description: LaunchBit was an advertising startup founded in 2012 and incubated through 500 Startups, co-founded and led by CEO Elizabeth Yin. It launched as an email ad network that let B2B and software-as-a-service advertisers reach audiences through niche email newsletters, and helped publishers monetize email — a medium BuySellAds founder Todd Garland described as "pretty tricky to monetize." In March 2014 LaunchBit pivoted toward a customer-acquisition and lead-generation platform for SaaS companies. BuySellAds.com acquired LaunchBit in September 2014 for undisclosed terms, and the company no longer operates independently: as of a July 2026 probe, launchbit.com serves the BuySellAds corporate website for every path. LaunchBit published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so this profile is retained as a historical/acquired record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Leaba Semiconductor
providers.description: Leaba Semiconductor was an Israeli fabless semiconductor startup founded in 2014 in Caesarea by Eyal Dagan (CEO) and Ofer Iny (CTO), the founders who had previously sold Dune Networks to Broadcom in 2009. Leaba designed high-end networking silicon — switch and router ASICs for carrier-class packet processing — and was backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Pitango Venture Capital. Cisco announced its intent to acquire the roughly 45-person company on 2 March 2016 for about $320 million in cash and assumed equity awards plus retention incentives, before Leaba had shipped a product; the deal was widely characterized as an acquisition of next-generation semiconductor talent and design IP. The Leaba team became the anchor of Cisco's Israel silicon engineering center, and its technology underpins Cisco Silicon One, launched in December 2019 as the programmable networking chip family behind the Cisco 8000 Series carrier-class routers. Leaba never operated an independent developer program, public API, or SDK surface, and the leaba.com domain no longer serves a website. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: LeanMarket
providers.description: LeanMarket was a mobile advertising technology company headquartered in Mountain View, California, that brought real-time bidding (RTB) display advertising to small and mid-sized advertisers through a self-serve platform. Its pitch was transparency and operator control: advertisers could pull reports showing in-depth data on every mobile app and mobile website their ads appeared in — in contrast to blind ad networks — and could tweak, optimize and scale campaigns themselves through a self-serve interface with up-to-the-second reporting, rather than waiting on an account manager to make changes. The company went through the Y Combinator Summer 2012 (S12) batch and appears on the Andreessen Horowitz investment list, with seed participation also reported from Initialized Capital. LeanMarket is defunct and operates no live product, developer portal or API today; this profile is retained for historical and network completeness.

providers.name: LearnSprout
providers.description: LearnSprout was a San Francisco edtech company founded in 2012 by Franklyn Chien, Anthony Wu and Joe Woo out of the Imagine K12 accelerator. It built LearnSprout Connect, an API layer that unlocked K-12 student data held in student information systems (SIS) through direct database integration rather than the SIS application layer, giving edtech developers a single "once and done" integration plus a change-log endpoint for incremental syncs. It also sold a district-facing analytics product covering attendance, grades and college readiness, reaching over 2,500 schools across 42 states on roughly $4.7M raised from Andreessen Horowitz, Formation 8 and Samsung Ventures. Apple acquired the company in January 2016 and the public API was retired; learnsprout.com no longer resolves and is parked on Apple nameservers.

providers.name: Legato Systems
providers.description: Legato Systems, Inc. was a storage management software company founded in 1988 in Palo Alto, California by four former Sun Microsystems engineers — Jon Kepecs, Bob Lyon, Joe Moran, and Russell Sandberg. Its flagship product, NetWorker, was introduced for Unix in 1990 and became one of the defining enterprise backup, recovery, and archiving platforms of the client-server era, centralizing scheduled backup, media management, and disaster recovery across heterogeneous Unix, Windows, and NetWare environments. Backed by Mayfield, the company went public in July 1995. EMC Corporation announced its acquisition of Legato in July 2003 and completed it in October 2003 for an estimated $1.3 billion, folding the product line into EMC's information-management portfolio. NetWorker survives today as Dell EMC NetWorker following Dell's 2016 acquisition of EMC. No Legato-branded developer or API surface remains: the legato.com domain carries Akamai nameservers but publishes no website, and the company predates modern package registries, so no first-party client libraries exist. This profile is retained as a historical Mayfield portfolio record.

providers.name: LightCyber
providers.description: LightCyber was an Israeli-American cybersecurity company that pioneered a category it called Behavioral Attack Detection — using behavior-based profiling of network traffic and endpoint activity, rather than malware signatures or technical artifacts, to detect attackers already operating inside an enterprise network. Its LightCyber Magna platform shipped as a set of appliances and services (Magna Detector, Magna Probe, Magna Master, Magna Pathfinder, and the Magna Cloud Expert System) and was positioned for user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), network traffic analysis, security visibility, and PCI compliance. The company was backed by Battery Ventures, Glilot Capital Partners, Amplify Partners, and angel investor Shlomo Kramer. Palo Alto Networks announced the completed acquisition of LightCyber for $105 million in cash on February 28, 2017, and engineered its automated behavioral analytics into the Palo Alto Networks security platform. The independent LightCyber brand, product line, and web presence no longer exist; the lightcyber.com domain has since lapsed from Palo Alto Networks' control and now resolves to an unrelated third-party site.
