providers.name: Linear Technology
providers.description: Linear Technology Corporation was an American semiconductor company founded in 1981 by Robert H. Swanson Jr. and Robert C. Dobkin and headquartered in Milpitas, California. It designed and manufactured high-performance analog integrated circuits across data conversion (ADCs and DACs), signal conditioning (operational amplifiers, comparators, voltage references), power management (switching and linear regulators, battery management, LED drivers), interface (RS232, RS485), radio frequency, oscillators, and space and military ICs, shipping a catalog of more than 7,500 products. Analog Devices agreed to acquire Linear Technology in July 2016 in a cash-and-stock deal valued at approximately $14.8 billion, and the acquisition closed on March 10, 2017. Linear Technology no longer operates as an independent company: the linear.com domain permanently redirects to Analog Devices, and the Linear name survives only as the "Power by Linear" product brand. Linear Technology publishes no independent developer portal, documentation, or API surface of its own; its developer-facing successor in this network is analog-devices.

providers.name: Linear Technology Corporation
providers.description: Linear Technology Corporation (listed as "Linear Technologies" in the Mayfield portfolio harvest) was an American analog semiconductor company founded in 1981 and headquartered in Milpitas, California, designing and manufacturing high-performance analog integrated circuits — power management, data converters, amplifiers, voltage references, interface and RF products — for industrial, automotive, communications, computing, and military/aerospace markets. Backed early by Mayfield and Kleiner Perkins, it went public on NASDAQ in 1986 under the ticker LLTC and was acquired by Analog Devices in March 2017. The company no longer operates independently: its linear.com domain 301-redirects to www.analog.com, and its product lines, datasheets, and design tools (including LTspice) are now distributed through Analog Devices. As an analog component manufacturer it never operated a web/developer API program, and no public API surface exists to enrich. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead; the successor developer surface is catalogued in the API Evangelist network under analog-devices.

providers.name: Link A Media
providers.description: Link_A_Media Devices (LAMD) was a privately-held fabless semiconductor company founded in March 2004 by storage industry veterans and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It built signal-processing and data-recovery technology — read channels, error correction and System-on-Chip blocks — that storage OEMs combined with their own proprietary logic to build custom controller SoCs for hard disk drives and NAND flash. Its product lines were MagLINK (magnetic/HDD) and FlashLINK (NAND/SSD), sold as IP and silicon to drive manufacturers rather than as a developer-facing service. The company targeted higher areal density, lower cost per gigabyte, improved drive robustness and higher manufacturing yields. LAMD is no longer an operating independent company: its website was live through January 2013 and the domain is today a parked for-sale listing. It never published a public API, developer portal, or SDK, so there is no API surface for the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline to capture.

providers.name: LittleFund
providers.description: LittleFund (styled Littlefund) was a New York City-based consumer fintech mobile app that let families create long-term savings and gift funds for their children. Instead of physical presents, relatives and friends could contribute money toward a child's fund for birthdays, holidays, and milestones, with funding from bank accounts or credit/debit cards and savings goals tracked in-app. The company was backed by 500 Global (500 Startups) and was acquired by UNest, a children's investment and savings platform, around 2020. LittleFund operated as a B2C mobile product and never published a public developer platform, API, or documentation. Its original site at littlefund.co is offline and littlefund.com is now a parked domain; this record is retained as a historical company profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Livsho Holdings Limited
providers.description: Livsho Holdings Limited operates LIVSHO, described as the GCC's first live auction marketplace for collectibles, where users buy, sell, and connect around the things they love through interactive live shopping experiences. The consumer-facing platform is delivered primarily through a mobile app, with a Wix-hosted marketing presence at livsho.tv and livsho.com and a Linktree for app downloads. Livsho is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation is currently published.

providers.name: LNKO
providers.description: LNKO is a Moroccan direct-to-consumer eyewear brand and e-commerce retailer selling prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, and children's eyewear (LNKO KIDS) for men and women, plus accessories such as tote bags, pouches, hats, and eyeglass chains. It operates physical retail locations alongside an online storefront with two-day delivery across Morocco. LNKO is a consumer fashion/retail brand backed by 500 Global; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation, so it carries no API artifacts in the API Evangelist network at this time.

providers.name: Lo Que Necesito
providers.description: Lo Que Necesito (loquenecesito.co) is a Colombian real estate technology platform that lets people request and purchase housing online, accompanying customers through the buying process. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. A July 2026 enrichment pass found a live consumer website but no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Local Kitchens
providers.description: Local Kitchens is a restaurant company that operates multi-brand "food hall" locations where a single kitchen prepares menu items from a curated set of local and national restaurant brands for on-demand pickup and delivery, ordered through its consumer website and mobile app. Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, it is a consumer-facing hospitality and food-ordering business. As of this pass it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation — its web presence is a Cloudflare-fronted marketing and ordering site (Google Workspace email, Klaviyo, Twilio, Zoom in its DNS records).

providers.name: Locker Room *
providers.description: Locker Room was a live-audio social app for sports fans built by Betty Labs, a seed-stage startup backed by GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Precursor Ventures. Launched in October 2020, it let insiders and fans hold real-time voice conversations about sports. Betty Labs and Locker Room were acquired by Spotify in March 2021 and folded into Spotify Greenroom / Spotify Live, which Spotify has since discontinued. Locker Room no longer operates as an independent product and exposes no public developer API or portal; this profile is retained as a GV portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Loftium
providers.description: Loftium was a Seattle-based real-estate technology startup (founded 2017) that helped renters and aspiring homebuyers cover a down payment by hosting a room or unit on Airbnb and sharing the short-term rental income. It later pivoted to a rent-to-own model. Loftium was acquired by Flyhomes in February 2023. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of threshold-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment pass (2026-07-20) found no public API, developer portal, or documentation: the loftium.com domain no longer serves company content and 301-redirects to unrelated parked domains, and no api/docs/developer subdomains resolve. No API surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: LogicLoop
providers.description: LogicLoop was a low-code / no-code operations-automation platform that let non-engineering teams write SQL-based business rules on top of their company data to trigger alerts, reviews, and automated actions for use cases like fraud and risk monitoring, logistics, and customer onboarding. Founded in 2021 by Jesika Haria and Jackie Xu, it raised roughly $4.5M from Accel and First Round Capital, offered an AI SQL Copilot (plain-English-to-SQL) and a REST API for managing rules, schedules, notifications, and embedded dashboards. LogicLoop was acquired by Hummingbird (risk and compliance) on 2024-09-18; its website (www.logicloop.com), docs (docs.logicloop.com), and API hosts no longer resolve, so no live API surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: LogicNow
providers.description: LogicNow (styled LOGICnow) was a global provider of integrated, cloud-based IT service management (ITSM) software for managed service providers (MSPs), best known for its MAX product suite — MAX Remote Management (RMM), MAX Backup & Disaster Recovery, MAX Mail, MAX Risk Intelligence and MAX Service Desk. On June 1, 2016 LOGICnow was acquired by SolarWinds and merged with SolarWinds N-able to form SolarWinds MSP, later spun out as the independent public company N-able. LogicNow no longer operates as an independent entity: its logicnow.com domain no longer serves a website (NXDOMAIN, MX only, handled by n-able.com) and it publishes no independent developer or API surface.

providers.name: Loku
providers.description: Loku was a travel and local-experiences recommendation startup, founded around 2010, that provided personalized recommendations from local experts. The company raised roughly $2.1M in seed funding and was acquired by Groupon in July 2013, after which the product was shut down. Loku is no longer an operating company. Its former domain, loku.com, no longer hosts a product and now redirects to an Afternic "domain for sale" listing. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; enrichment confirms there is no live API, developer portal, documentation, or product surface to catalog.

providers.name: Long Lake
providers.description: Long Lake is an AI-enabled roll-up holding company founded in 2023 that acquires and modernizes established American services businesses — spanning homeowners association (HOA) management, construction and infrastructure services, and corporate travel — by deploying its proprietary horizontal AI platform, Nexus. Backed by General Catalyst, Alpha Wave, D1 Capital, Thrive, and Elad Gil, the company has raised over $670 million and acquired more than 30 businesses, including a $6.3 billion agreement to take American Express Global Business Travel private. Long Lake operates as a private holding company (llmh.com) with no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Loose Cubes
providers.description: Loosecubes, Inc. was a membership-based marketplace often described as the "Airbnb for shared office space" — it connected people looking for a place to work with companies that had vacant desks and coworking space. Founded in 2010 in Brooklyn, New York by Campbell McKellar (Walmsley) and Anna Thomas, it raised roughly $9M total, including a $7.8M Series A led by New Enterprise Associates with Revolution Ventures and Battery Ventures participating. The company shut down and permanently closed in late 2012. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead; enrichment found no live API surface — the business is defunct and the loosecubes.com domain is now held by an unrelated owner.

providers.name: Lorillard
providers.description: Lorillard Tobacco Company was the third-largest cigarette manufacturer in the United States, marketing cigarettes under brand names including Newport, Kent, True, and Old Gold. In 2015, Lorillard was acquired by Reynolds American Inc. (RAI), and its operations and brands have since been integrated into the Reynolds American family of companies. Lorillard does not operate a public developer program or API platform.

providers.name: Loris
providers.description: Loris was an AI-powered customer service and conversation intelligence platform that analyzed voice, chat, and email interactions to surface contact drivers, sentiment shifts, and quality signals for support teams. Originally a Techstars-backed startup, Loris was acquired by Contentsquare and its product has been folded into the Contentsquare Conversation Intelligence offering. The standalone loris.ai property now 301-redirects to contentsquare.com and the company no longer publishes an independent public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record.

providers.name: Lost Lake Games
providers.description: Lost Lake Games is a Seattle-based independent video game studio building narrative-driven games. The studio raised a $5.1M seed round in 2022 led by BITKRAFT Ventures with participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners, 1Up Ventures, and Moon Holdings, and describes itself as being at the beginning of its next big adventure. As a consumer game developer, Lost Lake does not currently operate a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; its web presence is a marketing site with an email signup and links to Steam, Discord, and Twitter/X. This profile captures the company's identity and public footprint within the API Evangelist network, surfaced originally as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: Lowkey
providers.description: Lowkey (lowkey.gg) was a San Francisco social gaming platform that let players automatically record, review, and share their gameplay highlight clips across titles like League of Legends, VALORANT, and Among Us. Backed by Y Combinator and an a16z Series A, the company was acquired by Niantic (the developer of Pokemon GO) and the consumer product was subsequently discontinued. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no live public developer surface: the lowkey.gg domain no longer resolves/serves, and there is no public API, OpenAPI, documentation portal, SDK, or MCP server to harvest.

providers.name: LPL Financial Holdings
providers.description: LPL Financial Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: LPLA) is the parent company of LPL Financial LLC, one of the largest independent broker-dealers in the United States and a leading retail investment advisory firm. The company supports thousands of independent financial advisors, banks, credit unions, and registered investment advisors. LPL Financial Holdings does not operate a public developer program; APIs and integrations are operated under the LPL Financial subsidiary brand for partners and advisors.

providers.name: LSI
providers.description: LSI Corporation (formerly LSI Logic) was a semiconductor and storage-technology company that designed custom and standard chips, storage adapters, and RAID controllers for enterprise storage and networking systems. It was a Kleiner Perkins hardtech portfolio company and later a public company (NYSE: LSI). LSI was acquired by Avago Technologies in 2014 and its assets are now part of Broadcom Inc.; the legacy lsi.com domain redirects into Broadcom infrastructure. LSI operated no independent public developer program or web API, and no LSI-branded API surface exists today.

providers.name: LSI Logic
providers.description: LSI Logic Corporation was an American semiconductor company known for application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), custom system-on-chip designs, and storage/RAID controller silicon. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. The company was acquired by Avago Technologies in 2014 and its assets are now part of Broadcom; its former lsi.com domain redirects to broadcom.com. LSI Logic operates no independent public developer API program.

providers.name: Lu Pu Investment (陆浦投资)
providers.description: Lu Pu Investment (陆浦投资), operating through Shanghai Luxiang Fund Sales Co., Ltd. (上海陆享基金销售有限公司), is a China-based wealth-management and public mutual-fund distribution business serving retail investors. It offers fund subscription and purchase (认/申购), automatic investment plans (定投), and wealth-advisory services through dedicated financial advisors, delivered via its website and mobile app. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. No public developer, API, or technical integration surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Lucifer Quotes
providers.description: Returns Lucifer quotes

providers.name: Luckin Coffee
providers.description: Luckin Coffee (瑞幸咖啡) is a Chinese multinational coffee company and coffeehouse chain headquartered in Xiamen, China. Founded in 2017, it runs a technology-driven, mobile-app-first retail model in which nearly all ordering, payment, and membership happen through its native app and mini-programs rather than at a counter. As of 31 March 2026 the company operated 33,596 stores globally. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Luckin Coffee publishes no public developer program, open platform, or API — its digital surface is a consumer ordering app, not a documented API product.

providers.name: Luckypai
providers.description: Luckypai (乐酷天 / LuckyPai Ltd) was a Chinese television home-shopping company founded around 2006-2007 that grew into a leading nationwide TV and online shopping network, selling home appliances, cosmetics, apparel, food, and digital devices. It raised roughly $25M from investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Intel Capital, and the LOTTE Group, and was acquired by Lotte Home Shopping in 2010 for approximately $160M. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As an acquired, no-longer-operating consumer commerce business it has no public developer program, API, or independent web presence; the luckypai.com domain is parked and listed for sale.

providers.name: Ludlow Ventures
providers.description: Ludlow Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2010 and based in Detroit, Michigan. Led by partners Jonathon Triest and Brett deMarrais, the firm invests in exceptional founders across sectors with a relationship-driven, people-first philosophy, backing companies at the earliest stages rather than chasing trends. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Foundry Group. Sector: venture-capital.

providers.name: Lulus
providers.description: Lulus (Lulus Fashion Lounge Holdings) is a direct-to-consumer online fashion retailer offering women's apparel, dresses, shoes, and accessories, operating primarily through lulus.com and mobile apps. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IVP and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Lulus publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface: developer.lulus.com does not resolve and no /.well-known/ discovery documents are served. This profile therefore captures company identity plus a live domain-security posture probe rather than any API artifacts.

providers.name: Luma Home
providers.description: Luma Home was a smart-home networking startup, backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), best known for its Luma whole-home mesh WiFi system that paired consumer routers with mobile-app network management, parental controls, and security features. The company was acquired by Newell Brands and its product line was subsequently discontinued. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no live company website and no public developer, documentation, or API surface (candidate domains return HTTP 404), so no API artifacts were produced. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: LumaTax
providers.description: LumaTax is a US and Canadian sales tax automation platform that helps businesses automate sales tax filings, manage nexus exposure, and streamline remittance across multiple state and federal jurisdictions. The product imports transaction data from sources such as Amazon, Stripe, Shopify, and Excel, validates that data and assigns correct tax jurisdictions, generates categorized return summaries, files returns automatically, and stores past filings for audit preparation. Originally an independent Seattle fintech backed by Cowboy Ventures, LumaTax was acquired and is now offered as a product line under Taxually alongside CrossTax, EcoTax, and OneTax. As of enrichment it exposes no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Lumina
providers.description: Lumina (Lumina Innovations) is a San Francisco-based startup building all-electric, autonomous heavy construction equipment. Founded by Ahmed Shubber and Federico Di Palma, the company develops both the hardware and the self-driving software in-house, taking a Tesla/Waymo-style approach to the excavation and earth-moving industry. Its flagship Moonlander ML6 is a 32-ton fully autonomous electric bulldozer with roughly 750 horsepower of peak output and a 414 kWh battery pack. The broader product lineup spans Roadrunner, Moonlander, Bladerunner, and a Powerpack energy system. Lumina does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Luminus Devices
providers.description: Luminus Devices is an optoelectronics manufacturer ("Improving Life with Photons") producing solid-state lighting and photonics hardware: COB arrays, specialty and color SMD LEDs, UV/IR/horticulture LEDs, green/blue/red multi-mode lasers, and power semiconductors (SiC MOSFETs and Schottky barrier diodes) for retail, industrial, medical, life-sciences, display, and automotive applications. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment confirmed this is a hardware/components company that publishes no public developer API, REST API, or developer portal — only a product resources/tools portal.

providers.name: Luna Park
providers.description: Luna Park is a consumer-sector company surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network. Its registered domain lunapark.com now redirects (HTTP 301) to meetquinn.ai — Quinn, described on-site as an AI training platform focused on "operational readiness for the trades." As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a minimal marketing landing page with no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or other machine-readable API surface. Domain-security posture was probed live: TLS 1.3 with SPF and DMARC (quarantine) present; no HSTS, DNSSEC, or CAA records.

providers.name: Lunasonde
providers.description: Lunasonde is a Techstars-backed deep-tech space company building a satellite constellation for subsurface Earth imaging. Its sensing technology aims to scan beneath the surface from orbit to detect groundwater, minerals, and other underground features, delivering the resulting geophysical data to mining, agriculture, water, and natural-resource customers. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, documentation portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this record captures its verifiable web and domain-security footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lunchclub
providers.description: Lunchclub is an AI-powered professional networking platform that matches members for one-to-one meetings and warm introductions based on their goals, background, and interests. Members set what they are looking for — hiring, fundraising, sales, mentorship, or making new connections — and Lunchclub's matching system proposes relevant people to meet over video. The company is consumer/prosumer facing and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched in the API Evangelist network; probing confirmed no public API surface, no OpenAPI, and no /.well-known discovery documents.

providers.name: Luvocracy *
providers.description: Luvocracy was a social-shopping and recommendation marketplace where people discovered, shared, and bought products curated by friends and trusted tastemakers, with the service handling the purchasing on the buyer's behalf. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) and Kleiner Perkins, the company was acquired by @WalmartLabs in 2014 and subsequently wound down; its website (luvocracy.com) now serves an archived static page announcing the acquisition. No developer program, public API, or SDK was ever published, and none exists today. This profile is retained as a network record of a defunct consumer startup. Sector: consumer / social commerce.

providers.name: Luxe
providers.description: Luxe was an on-demand valet parking service that let users request a valet through a mobile app to pick up, park, and return their vehicle, operating in San Francisco, Chicago, and New York. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, Luxe is a consumer mobility service with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; this profile records that honest finding.

providers.name: Luxe Nomad
providers.description: The Luxe Nomad is a luxury travel booking company offering curated villas, private residences, and boutique hotels across Asia-Pacific and beyond. It operates as a consumer-facing booking platform rather than a developer-first API provider. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, this profile was probed for a public API surface, developer portal, and discovery documents; none were found (the site is bot-protected and returns no developer, API, or /.well-known resources). It remains catalogued as a company lead with a probed domain-security profile.

providers.name: Luxvisions Innovation Limited
providers.description: Luxvisions Innovation Limited is a camera module and imaging technology manufacturer established in March 2018, headquartered in Hong Kong with operations in Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Shangrao, China. The company designs and produces optical camera modules and audio-video integration technology for mobile phones, tablets, PCs and notebooks, automotive systems, AIOT devices, and 3D/ToF VR/AR/MR applications, and states it launched the industry's first triple camera module for mobile phones. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (HongShan Capital) and added to the API Evangelist network. As a hardware/component manufacturer, Luxvisions publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Lydian
providers.description: Lydian (Lydian Labs) develops modular, turnkey plants that produce sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from captured CO2 and hydrogen. Its technology converts carbon dioxide and electrolytic hydrogen into jet fuel via a syngas production process compatible with existing aircraft, targeting deployment in under two years and capital costs roughly 50% lower than conventional SAF plants. The company markets to airlines, fuel buyers, and facility operators. Based in Charlestown, Massachusetts, Lydian is backed by Union Square Ventures. This is a hardware/industrial company with no public API, SDK, or developer portal surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Lynda.com
providers.description: Lynda.com was an online video learning platform founded in 1995 by Lynda Weinman and Bruce Heavin, offering courses in software, creative, and business skills. LinkedIn acquired Lynda.com in 2015 (~$1.5B) and folded it into LinkedIn Learning; the standalone Lynda.com service has been retired and www.lynda.com now 301-redirects to linkedin.com/learning. The brand exposes no public developer program or API surface of its own. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and enriched as a lead; the honest result is a defunct brand with no first-party API.

providers.name: Lyracollective
providers.description: Lyra Collective is a consumer-products holding company that owns and operates a portfolio of everyday care brands across skincare, feminine care, and family and pet products, including LOLA, EVER, QRX Labs, TriLASTIN, Nuvadermis, Natemia, Leash Boss, and Lusso Gear. It positions itself around "Exceptional Care, For Everyday Moments," emphasizing clean, quality essentials sold direct-to-consumer and through retail. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer-brands operator it publishes no public developer portal, API, or API documentation; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Lytmus
providers.description: Lytmus was a technical-interview and coding-assessment platform for hiring engineers. Candidates worked live in a browser-based, fully functional Ubuntu virtual machine (Terminal, editors, Chrome) so recruiters could run pair-programming phone screens and evaluate real coding skills across languages and full-stack scenarios, priced in per-session plans. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment probing (2026-07-20) found no developer portal, API, documentation, or ./.well-known surface; the company was acquired by GitHub in 2019 and its product has since been shut down, so lytmus.io now serves stale content and lytmus.com is a parked, for-sale domain. No API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Lytro
providers.description: Lytro was a light-field (plenoptic) imaging company founded in 2006 by Ren Ng and based in Mountain View, California. It shipped the first consumer light-field cameras (the Lytro and the Lytro Illum), which captured the entire light field so images could be refocused after the fact, and later pivoted to professional light-field capture for cinema and VR with Lytro Cinema and Lytro Immerge. Backed by a16z, Greylock, NEA and Qualcomm Ventures, the company wound down in March 2018 with much of its technology and talent moving to Google. It is defunct and publishes no public developer program or API; the lytro.com domain now 301-redirects to an unrelated light-field vendor (raytrix.de).

providers.name: Madison-reed
providers.description: Madison Reed is a female-founded and female-led direct-to-consumer hair color company offering 8-Free permanent, demi-permanent, and root touch-up hair color crafted in Italy, sold as at-home kits and delivered as professional services at 95+ Hair Color Bar locations across the United States. The company blends e-commerce retail, subscription replenishment, and in-person salon booking. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and True Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Madrone
providers.description: Madrone is a data center cooling technology company (Y Combinator Spring 2026, NVIDIA Inception) building modular thermodynamic cooling systems that sit outside the data center and chill water to the dew point, eliminating the need for mechanical chillers and cooling towers. The company claims roughly 30% less power and water than a conventional chiller-plus-cooling-tower setup in Texas installations, freeing that power and capital for additional GPU compute. It is an early-stage hardware and infrastructure company with a sales-and-partnerships motion; as of this profiling it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, documentation, or other machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Mafengwo
providers.description: Mafengwo (马蜂窝, "Honeycomb") is a Chinese travel social and user-generated-content platform offering travel guides, destination reviews, trip notes (游记), community Q&A, and online booking for flights, hotels, tours, and local activities. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. No public developer or open-platform (开放平台) API surface was discoverable during this enrichment pass; the site is protected by anti-bot measures and exposes no OpenAPI, well-known discovery documents, or security.txt.

providers.name: Magic Circle Studio
providers.description: Magic Circle Studio is a venture-backed consumer mobile game developer building social games designed to nourish relationships through cooperation, creativity, and playful shared experiences. Its flagship title, Magic Garden, launched on iOS in July 2025 and reached one million players in its first year, following the studio's earlier titles Truffle Hogs and a Magic Circle Discord activity that won Discord's Best Chill/Party Game award. The studio received pre-seed funding from General Catalyst in 2022 and joined the a16z Games SPEEDRUN accelerator in 2023. It is a direct-to-consumer game company with no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained as a network identity record.

providers.name: Magmatic Games
providers.description: Magmatic Games is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Magnetis
providers.description: Magnetis is a Brazilian digital wealth management and automated investment (robo-advisor) platform, backed by 500 Global, that offered goal-based portfolio recommendations and managed investment accounts to retail investors in Brazil. The company was acquired by BTG Pactual, and the magnetis.com.br domain now redirects to BTG Pactual's investimentos platform; no independent public developer program or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: MAGNiTT
providers.description: MAGNiTT is a venture data platform covering startups, investors, and funding activity across emerging venture markets, with a focus on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and adjacent emerging ecosystems. It aggregates data on startup companies, venture capital and corporate investors, funding rounds, and exits, and publishes market research and analytics reports used by founders, investors, and enterprises to track venture activity. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass MAGNiTT publishes no discoverable public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; the platform is a subscription-based data product served behind login and bot protection.

providers.name: Maimai
providers.description: Maimai (脉脉) is a Chinese professional networking and workplace social platform operated by Beijing Taoyou Tianxia Technology Development Co., Ltd. It combines professional networking, recruitment and talent matching, job referrals, company reviews and workplace community, and career-development learning (脉课堂) for the Chinese-language market. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Maimai publishes no public developer program, open platform, or API documentation, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Main Street Hub
providers.description: Main Street Hub was a marketing platform for local and small businesses, founded in Austin, Texas around 2010, that managed social media, review sites, and online customer engagement on behalf of restaurants, salons, and other Main Street merchants. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, it was acquired by GoDaddy in 2018 and folded into the GoDaddy Social product; the former mainstreethub.com domain now 301-redirects to godaddy.com/online-marketing/godaddy-social. No independent developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface remains, and api.mainstreethub.com does not resolve.

providers.name: Mainframe
providers.description: Mainframe (Mainframe Group, Inc.) is a software development and marketing services company building products for the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem. It offers three service areas — Risk Management (protocol parameter optimization and stability), Development (DeFi and blockchain financial solutions), and Marketing (brand reach and audience engagement) — and has produced projects including Hifi, Pooled NFT, Sheet Heads, and Crown Ribbon. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Mainframe publishes a Webflow marketing site only, with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Make School
providers.description: Make School was a San Francisco-based computer science college and coding bootcamp, backed by a16z, that offered an applied computer science bachelor's program. As of August 2021 the degree program moved to Dominican University of California, and Make School.org now operates as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit running a scholarship program for former Bachelor in Applied Computer Science students. The organization publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and this enrichment pass confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Makeably
providers.description: Makeably was an online marketplace for custom-made and handmade goods (apparel, jewelry, furniture, household items, wedding and arts products), later pivoting to a "remixes" model that let shoppers request variations of reference products rather than fully bespoke commissions. It raised roughly $650K in seed funding in 2013 from Great Oaks Venture Capital, 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and others. The company appears to be defunct — its domain no longer resolves and no developer or API surface exists. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub.

providers.name: Makelog
providers.description: Makelog was a product changelog and release-notes platform that helped software and product teams collect, curate, and publish product updates to communicate releases with customers and internal stakeholders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment (sector: productivity). As of this enrichment pass the makelog.com domain no longer resolves (DNS NXDOMAIN) and no live web, developer, or API surface could be reached, indicating the product has been discontinued.

providers.name: Maker Comms
providers.description: Maker Communications was an early networking-silicon company that designed high-performance programmable communications processors and related software for ATM and Internet Protocol data, voice, and video networks. Founded in 1994 and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (early investment in 1997, Barry Eggers), the company went public in 1999 on NASDAQ under the ticker MAKR and was acquired by Conexant Systems (NASDAQ CNXT) in 2000. It exists in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it is a defunct, fully-exited hardware/semiconductor company with no surviving public developer program, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Maker.me
providers.description: Maker.me is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: makespace
providers.description: makespace was a New York-founded, full-service consumer storage company (professional pickup, packing, digital photo cataloging, and on-demand redelivery) added to the API Evangelist network as a slow-ventures portfolio-lead stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the makespace.com domain 301-redirects to clutter.com, the storage brand now operated as Clutter by Iron Mountain, and the company exposes no public developer program, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or documented API surface. This profile records the honest result of the pipeline: identity plus a live domain-security probe, with no API artifacts available to harvest.

providers.name: Malaeb
providers.description: Malaeb (ملاعب) is the #1 sports pitch and facility booking application in the MENA region, letting players discover and reserve stadiums, courts, and pitches around them across Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, and Oman. Backed by 500 Global, Malaeb connects players and venue operators through a consumer mobile marketplace. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface; its web presence is a WordPress marketing site fronting a React single-page application.

providers.name: Mammoth Biosciences
providers.description: Mammoth Biosciences is a genetic medicines company co-founded by CRISPR co-inventor Jennifer Doudna, developing in vivo gene-editing therapeutics and CRISPR-based diagnostics. The company discovers and engineers novel CRISPR systems and proteins to overcome delivery challenges in genetic medicine, with the goal of creating permanent cures. It is a therapeutics- and diagnostics-focused biotechnology company rather than an API/platform provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or programmatic access. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc, Mayfield and SV Angel and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mamut
providers.description: Mamut was a Norwegian business software company (Mamut ASA / Mamut AS) that provided accounting, ERP, CRM, e-commerce and online-presence software to small and medium-sized businesses across the Nordics and parts of Europe. It was acquired by Visma in 2011 and the Mamut product line has since been absorbed into the Visma family of business software. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass the mamut.com web server is unreachable (both HTTP and HTTPS time out) and there is no reachable public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface under the Mamut brand; enrichment therefore captured only what could be probed from DNS/TLS. Sector: enterprise.

providers.name: Mandatory Reserves Requirement
providers.description: A central bank regulation requiring commercial banks to hold a minimum percentage of customer deposits as reserves, either as cash in their vaults or as deposits with the central bank, to ensure liquidity and stability in the banking system.

providers.name: Manicube (Elizabeth Arden Red Door)
providers.description: Manicube (Elizabeth Arden Red Door) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: commerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Manifest OS
providers.description: Manifest OS is an AI-native law firm building an operating system for legal work that replaces the traditional billable hour with transparent fixed-fee pricing. It is profiled by Kleiner Perkins as an early-stage (2026) Enterprise AI company that applies AI to deliver predictable legal services. As of this enrichment pass Manifest OS does not publish a public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal, so it carries no API artifacts.

providers.name: Manifold Bio
providers.description: Manifold Bio is a biotechnology company developing tissue-targeted biologic medicines. It runs a high-throughput in vivo discovery engine that pairs massively multiplexed in vivo screening — using mCode protein barcodes read out by DNA sequencing — with AI-powered protein and antibody design (mBER) and engineered mShuttle delivery vehicles. Its pipeline targets CNS diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's (amyloid-beta, tau, alpha-synuclein) and peripheral cardiometabolic disease. Backed by Playground Global. The company publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or event surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Manime
providers.description: ManiMe (Manime) is a direct-to-consumer beauty company offering custom-fit semi-cured gel manicure and pedicure kits. Customers scan their nails with a smartphone and ManiMe manufactures made-to-measure gel nail sets shipped to the home for at-home application. The company was backed by Canaan Partners and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass the manime.co storefront (a Shopify store) returns HTTP 402 "Store unavailable", indicating the store is currently closed or inactive. No public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or webhook surface could be found.

providers.name: Manitowoc
providers.description: Manitowoc Cranes is one of the world's largest providers of lifting equipment for the global construction industry, including lattice-boom crawler cranes, tower cranes, mobile hydraulic cranes, and boom trucks. No public developer APIs have been documented.

providers.name: Manpower
providers.description: Manpower is a global workforce solutions brand of ManpowerGroup that delivers innovative staffing and workforce services to organizations worldwide and helps talent find meaningful, sustainable employment. No public developer APIs have been documented.

providers.name: ManpowerGroup
providers.description: ManpowerGroup is a global workforce solutions company that connects talented people with innovative companies through its family of brands including Manpower, Experis, and Talent Solutions. No public developer APIs have been documented.

providers.name: Mantari
providers.description: Mantari is a weather-intelligence and earth-sensing company building a decision-intelligence platform that fuses a distributed network of sensors with AI to turn environmental data across oceans, skies, and space into mission-critical, actionable intelligence. It initially targets government and defense decision support, with plans to extend into broader economic and commercial applications. As of this profile Mantari publishes a marketing homepage and a careers page but no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this record captures its identity plus a live domain-security probe, pending a future developer surface.

providers.name: MapReduce
providers.description: MapReduce is a programming model and processing technique for computing large data sets in parallel across a distributed cluster. Originally developed by Google and popularized by Apache Hadoop, it splits data processing into map and reduce phases to enable scalable big data analytics.

providers.name: Markato
providers.description: Markato (legally On Your Marks) is a brand builder and distributor for health, beauty, and wellness brands across Asia, positioning itself as a next-generation distribution disruptor. From bases in Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, Thailand, and Australia, it helps high-potential brands enter, grow, and dominate the region's most competitive markets. Its capabilities span strategic channel development into top-tier offline and online retailers (Sephora, Watsons, Mannings, SaSa), e-commerce and social commerce operations across Shopee, TikTok, and Lazada, 360-degree marketing and brand building, and end-to-end local operations, logistics, product registration, and compliance. Markato is backed by a roughly US$4M seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with a team drawn from L'Oreal, P&G, McKinsey, and Lane Crawford. Markato is a services and distribution business and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Markhor
providers.description: Markhor is a direct-to-consumer commerce company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Y Combinator and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its site at markhor.com runs on Shopify and is currently offline, returning an HTTP 402 "Store unavailable" response. A July 2026 enrichment pass probed the domain and well-known paths and found no public API, developer platform, documentation, or SDK surface; only live DNS/TLS/HTTP domain-security signal was captured.

providers.name: MarkIt
providers.description: MarkIt is a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) startup based in Atlanta, GA building AI agents that automate international trade compliance workflows. The platform performs defensible HS and HTS tariff-code classification, OCR processing of shipping documents, tariff management, and customs issue resolution, with agents that work directly inside the tools trade professionals already use every day such as Excel, PDFs, and broker portals. MarkIt also publishes a free web-based HTS code classification tool at markittrade.com/hts. As of this enrichment pass MarkIt is an early-stage, landing-page-only product with no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Markov
providers.description: Markov (Markov Studios) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building data and environments for training computer-use AI. The company captures how people actually use computers - screen recordings with synchronized mouse and keyboard inputs, annotations, and open datasets across real workflows in tools like Salesforce, Blender, and Photoshop, plus gaming data from Valorant, Minecraft, and GTA. Markov sources high-quality tasks and data to train the next generation of computer-use and reinforcement-learning models, releasing much of its work in public on Hugging Face (150k+ dataset downloads). Founded in 2026 by Dev Mandal (CEO) and Harish Ashok, Markov distributes its datasets through Hugging Face rather than a first-party API; this profile currently tracks no public API surface.

providers.name: Markup Language
providers.description: A markup language is a system for annotating a document in a way that is syntactically distinguishable from the text. Examples include HTML, XML, Markdown, LaTeX, and others that add semantic meaning or formatting instructions to text content.

providers.name: Masco Corporation
providers.description: Masco Corporation is a global leader in the design, manufacture, and distribution of branded home improvement and building products, including faucets, plumbing fixtures, cabinets, paints, and architectural coatings under brands such as Delta, Behr, Hansgrohe, KILZ, and Liberty Hardware.

providers.name: Masergy
providers.description: Masergy Communications was a managed networking and security provider offering software-defined networking (SD-WAN), secure networking (SASE), managed security services, and unified communications as a service (UCaaS/CCaaS) to enterprises over a global software-defined platform. Masergy was acquired by Comcast Business in October 2021 and folded into Comcast Business; the masergy.com web properties now redirect to business.comcast.com/masergy/. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners. Enrichment found no live standalone developer portal or API surface (api.masergy.com returns HTTP 502; developer/docs subdomains do not resolve), so this profile documents identity and the probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Massive Dynamic
providers.description: Massive Dynamic is an AI-powered advertising platform that bills itself as "The Advertising Copilot" and "the human-AI interface for massive scale." It helps media and advertising teams coordinate large-scale digital ad campaigns by pairing an AI Analysis Copilot (automating daily analytics checks, quarterly business reviews, and Media Mix Modeling) with Execution Delegation, where an AI agent handles operational campaign setup so strategists can focus on decisions. The tool works inside existing Slack and email workflows as a conduit between strategy and activation teams, and emphasizes enterprise-grade data governance with ring-fenced customer data and an explicit commitment not to use customer data to train or improve models. The company was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Mavrck
providers.description: Mavrck is an influencer marketing platform, founded in Boston, that helps consumer brands and agencies discover creators, activate influencer and advocacy campaigns at scale, manage relationships and content workflows, and measure campaign performance across social channels. As of January 17, 2024 Mavrck rebranded and now operates as part of Later's influencer marketing offering (later.com). This record was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead (surfaced via Techstars) and enriched by the pipeline; probing confirms a marketing-SaaS web presence with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Maxion Therapeutics
providers.description: Maxion Therapeutics is a UK biotechnology company developing protein therapeutics using its proprietary KnotBody technology, which fuses venom-derived knottin miniproteins with antibodies to drug previously untreatable ion channel- and GPCR-driven diseases across autoimmune, inflammatory, and related therapeutic areas. Maxion is a preclinical-stage drug-discovery company, not an API or developer-platform provider; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-tracking purposes and has no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Mayflower
providers.description: Mayflower is an early-stage (Y Combinator, Fall 2025) startup building an AI-powered HR plug-in that automates immigration screening, visa eligibility assessment, and compliance for international hiring. The platform parses candidate documents, classifies visa pathways, and generates attorney-ready forms, integrating directly with existing HR systems so companies can surface only compliant candidates and reduce legal risk. Founded in 2025 by Naren Chittem and Aryan Gulati and based in San Francisco, the company currently operates a marketing landing page with a book-a-call motion and publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or GitHub organization. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; the enrichment pipeline found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: MBX
providers.description: MBX (formerly Memebox) is a global, multi-brand beauty and personal care company founded in 2012 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2014 batch. Headquartered in San Francisco with operations in Seoul, Shanghai, and Taipei, MBX uses data-driven consumer insights and Korean beauty innovation to build and scale a portfolio of cosmetics brands — including Kaja, I Dew Care, Pony Effect, I'm Meme, and Nooni — sold through retail partners such as Sephora and Ulta. The company has raised over $190M from investors including Cowboy Ventures, Y Combinator, Formation 8, Goodwater Capital, Johnson & Johnson, and Pear VC. MBX operates as a direct-to-consumer and wholesale CPG business; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: MCA Solutions
providers.description: MCA Solutions was a service parts planning and optimization software company founded in 1999 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Its Service Planning and Optimization (SPO) suite helped aerospace and defense, high-tech, and capital-equipment firms reduce spare-parts inventory, lower support costs, and improve service levels across the service supply chain. Backed by Battery Ventures and Longworth Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Marlin Equity Partners in March 2012 and merged into Servigistics (later part of PTC). It no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: McCormick
providers.description: McCormick spices and products have been kitchen must-haves since 1889. Learn about seasoning and cuisine while discovering tons of delicious recipes today. No public developer APIs are currently documented.

providers.name: MCU Countdown
providers.description: A Countdown to the next MCU Film

providers.name: Mediaspectrum
providers.description: Mediaspectrum is a cloud-based SaaS provider of multichannel advertising, content management, and publishing software for media companies and publishers. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Miami, its platform manages the full advertising lifecycle -- proposal generation, packaging, scheduling, rating, workflow, trafficking, optimization, and billing -- alongside an integrated CRM and the ContentWatch content management system spanning print, web, mobile, video, social, and broadcast channels. The company raised a $35.8M investment from Insight Venture Partners in 2013 and counts Gannett, Dow Jones, and Trinity Mirror among its clients. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: MediaSpike
providers.description: MediaSpike was an AdTech startup founded in 2011 by Blake Commagere and headquartered in Mountain View, California, that built a native monetization platform for dynamic, programmatic product placement inside social, mobile, and virtual-reality games. Its API let game developers surface contextual in-game sponsorships and brand placements, and the network reportedly reached roughly 20 million unique users at its peak. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Google Ventures, CMEA Capital, 500 Startups, and others (a $5.2M Series A in November 2013), the company ceased operations around June 2017. mediaspike.com no longer hosts the product and currently serves only a "coming soon" placeholder; no live API, developer portal, or discovery surface remains.

providers.name: MEDICAL INTELLIGENCE CO
providers.description: Medicarri (operated by Medical Intelligence Co) is a B2B healthtech marketplace based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia that connects clinics and healthcare facilities with medical suppliers, letting buyers source medical supplies and equipment from many vendors in one place. The company was selected for Batch 4 of the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator Program run by 500 Global and Sanabil Investments. As of this profile Medicarri operates a customer-facing e-commerce web application at medicarri.com and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Meet Cute
providers.description: Meet Cute is a New York-based media company founded in 2019 by Naomi Shah that produces and distributes original scripted romantic-comedy audio programming, releasing bite-sized 15-minute rom-com stories as podcasts across platforms such as Apple Podcasts and Spotify. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Advancit Capital, and LocalGlobe, the company was acquired by Fox Entertainment in November 2025 to serve as a rapid-development content incubator for scripted and unscripted series. Meet Cute is a consumer media/content brand with no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile is retained as a company record.

providers.name: meetdavis
providers.description: Davis (meetdavis.com) is an AI-native real estate technology company, backed by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, that compresses early-stage real estate development from months to days. Davis combines proprietary AI models with human architect expertise to deliver feasibility studies (site analysis, regulatory diagnostics, volumetrics, financial modeling) and architectural designs (floor plans, unit-mix optimization, space planning) directly to developers and investors. Its first proprietary model, Gaudi-1, performs automated architectural generation under regulatory and financial constraints. Davis operates as a service model rather than selling software, and publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs at this time. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from the Balderton Capital portfolio and has been through the enrichment pipeline; no API surface was found.

providers.name: Mekan
providers.description: Mekan (somosmekan.com) is a Latin American software platform serving the automotive sector, with solutions organized around two product lines - Autos (vehicles) and Repuestos (auto parts / spare parts) - to help dealers, parts sellers, and automotive businesses manage and grow their operations. Backed by 500 Global, the company was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network. At the time of enrichment the public surface is a Spanish-language marketing site centered on a "Agenda tu demo" (schedule-a-demo) flow, with WhatsApp and LinkedIn contact channels and no publicly documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Mem Protocol
providers.description: Mem Protocol (mem.so) was a San Francisco based startup, founded in 2021, building tools for the social layer of web3 - a decentralized social-media protocol focused on user data sovereignty, portable social graphs, and verifiable on-chain identity. The company raised a ~$3.1M seed round in 2021 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z crypto), with participation from Balaji Srinivasan and Polychain's Olaf Carlson-Wee. As of this enrichment pass the project appears dormant/defunct - the official domain mem.so resolves only to a parking IP and times out, and the alternate domain memprotocol.xyz redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page. No live website, developer portal, API documentation, GitHub organization, SDK packages, or public API surface could be found. This profile remains an identity-only company record; there is nothing to enrich beyond the historical facts below.

providers.name: Mensa Brands
providers.description: Mensa Brands (rebranded BRND.ME) is an India-based, technology-led house of brands founded in 2021 by Ananth Narayanan (former Myntra CEO), building and scaling digital-first consumer brands across fashion, beauty, personal care, home and FMCG. Backed by Accel, Tiger Global and Prosus Ventures, it reached unicorn status and operates a portfolio of acquired D2C brands. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of prosus-ventures; a public developer API surface was searched for and none was found — the company exposes a corporate/consumer web presence rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Mensabrands
providers.description: Mensa Brands (now operating as BRND.ME) is a Bangalore, India based "house of brands" / digital-first brand aggregator founded in 2021 by Ananth Narayanan. Following the Thrasio model, it acquires, operates and scales digital-native consumer brands across fashion, beauty, personal care, home and general merchandise, selling through marketplaces such as Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra as well as direct-to-consumer channels. The company reached unicorn status in 2021 and is backed by investors including Norwest Venture Partners, Accel, Prosus Ventures, Tiger Global and Alpha Wave. Its original domain mensabrands.com now redirects to brndme.in. This is a consumer-brands operating company; enrichment found no public developer or API surface (no docs/developer/api subdomains, no /.well-known documents, no llms.txt) beyond the marketing site's WordPress CMS, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Mentor Graphics
providers.description: Mentor Graphics was a leading electronic design automation (EDA) software vendor whose tools span integrated-circuit design and verification, PCB and electronic-systems design, and manufacturing analysis. Battery Ventures held a position in the company. In 2017 Mentor Graphics was acquired by Siemens and its portfolio now ships as Siemens EDA (part of Siemens Digital Industries Software), including Calibre for physical verification and DFM, the Questa functional verification platform, and the Xpedition / PADS PCB design suites. The mentor.com domain now redirects to the Siemens EDA site. Siemens EDA delivers desktop and cloud-hosted engineering software and managed services; it does not publish a public developer REST API, OpenAPI definition, or self-serve developer portal, so there is no public API surface to enrich for this provider.

providers.name: Meolaa
providers.description: Meolaa is an AI-first, digitally native FMCG company based in India, founded in 2023 by Ishita Sawant. It began as a curated e-commerce marketplace for clean, sustainable, direct-to-consumer brands across fashion, beauty, home, and baby care, and is expanding into building a portfolio of purpose-driven in-house microbrands (including HIRA) powered by a shared AI and data platform for cross-brand innovation, supply-chain resilience, and marketing. The company raised a $6M Pre-Series A round led by General Catalyst with Claypond Capital, Colossa Ventures, Turbostart Global, and Kunal Shah. Meolaa is a consumer company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: MeowFacts
providers.description: Get random cat facts

providers.name: Meridian Data
providers.description: Meridian Data, Inc. was a Battery Ventures-backed maker of network-attached storage (NAS) appliances, best known for the Snap! Server workgroup NAS line and one of the industry's first storage operating systems for entry- and workgroup-level appliances. Quantum Corporation acquired Meridian Data in a stock swap valued at roughly $85M, completed June 1, 1999, folding its technology into Quantum's storage systems strategy. The company has not operated independently since and publishes no current developer or API surface; this profile is retained for API Evangelist network completeness as a historical, acquired entity.

providers.name: Merkle
providers.description: Merkle Data is a risk-management and analytics platform for crypto institutions, founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York. The platform aggregates proprietary market data (its Pulse dataset), public blockchain data, and third-party feeds to give funds, trading desks, and other digital-asset institutions actionable analytics across portfolio risk, liquidity risk, and counterparty risk, delivered through both interactive dashboards and programmatic APIs. Merkle Data is backed by Pantera Capital. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API reference, or SDK is discoverable and merkledata.io resolves to a login-gated institutional dashboard, so this record captures identity only.

providers.name: Merklebase, Inc.
providers.description: Merklebase provides data-driven infrastructure for institutional digital-asset finance, spanning enterprise data management, a core portfolio management system, reporting and accounting, risk management, a trade capture system, and a digital-asset loan management system. It advertises connectivity to 220+ custodians, trading venues, and data providers, and is used by hedge funds, asset managers, and financial institutions to streamline front-to-back operations across fiat, crypto, derivatives, and stablecoins. A developer API and connectivity layer is referenced by customers, but the public developer surface (docs.merklebase.io on Theneo) is currently unpublished and the API (api.merklebase.io, AWS API Gateway) is gated, so no public OpenAPI/SDK artifacts are harvestable yet.

providers.name: Messaging Protocol
providers.description: Messaging Protocol is a networking technology or protocol that facilitates communication, data transfer, or traffic management between systems and devices. Examples include AMQP, MQTT, STOMP, and other protocols that enable reliable, efficient, and secure connectivity across distributed environments.

providers.name: Metacloud
providers.description: Metacloud was an OpenStack-based private-cloud company founded in 2011 in Pasadena, California by former infrastructure engineers from Yahoo! and Ticketmaster. It let enterprises run production OpenStack private clouds on their own hardware, fully operated as a managed service. Metacloud raised a $10M Series A led by Canaan Partners (with Storm Ventures and AME Cloud Ventures) and was acquired by Cisco in 2014, where it became Cisco Metapod and later Cisco Metacloud before the product line was retired. There is no independent Metacloud company or first-party developer API surface today; the platform exposed standard OpenStack APIs rather than a proprietary API.

providers.name: Metaldyne Performance Group
providers.description: Metaldyne Performance Group was a leading provider of components for use in powertrain and safety-critical platforms for the global light, commercial, and industrial vehicle markets before being acquired by American Axle.

providers.name: Metaphor
providers.description: Metaphor was an active-metadata / data-catalog platform (metaphor.io) that combined a social, agent-assisted data governance experience with a large library of open-source Python "connectors" that extracted metadata (schemas, lineage, usage, ownership, documentation, data quality) from warehouses, BI tools, and data pipelines to populate the Metaphor app. Founded by ex-LinkedIn DataHub engineers and backed by Amplify Partners, Metaphor's technology platform was acquired by KPMG; the metaphor.io site now redirects to the KPMG acquisition announcement and the standalone developer surface (docs.metaphor.io, api.metaphor.io, the MetaphorData GitHub org) has been decommissioned. The first-party open-source metadata packages (metaphor-connectors, metaphor-models) still resolve on PyPI.

providers.name: Mettler-Toledo International
providers.description: Mettler-Toledo is a global manufacturer of precision instruments and services for use in laboratories, manufacturing, and food retailing applications. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for Mettler-Toledo International.

providers.name: MeUndies
providers.description: MeUndies is a direct-to-consumer apparel brand based in Los Angeles, selling underwear, loungewear, socks, and basics online through a subscription membership and one-time purchase model. It operates as an e-commerce retailer at meundies.com rather than a developer platform: an enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 probed the domain and found no public API surface (api.meundies.com and developer.meundies.com both return 404, and no /.well-known/, /llms.txt, or OpenAPI documents were discoverable). This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and carries the domain-security probe result; it will gain API artifacts only if MeUndies publishes a developer program.
