providers.name: Microagi
providers.description: Microagi (stylized microagi) is a data research lab building end-to-end physical, embodied AGI, with a stated focus on reliable real-world deployments; its public positioning is "Accelerating embodied AGI." Backed by Northzone, the company is early-stage: as of this profile its public presence is a single marketing site at microagi.ai with no published developer API, documentation, SDKs, CLI, or agent surface. This API Evangelist profile tracks Microagi as a portfolio lead; artifacts here are limited to a live domain-security probe of the marketing host until a developer surface is published. (Note: the unrelated github.com/microagi org, "µAGI / microagi.dev" by Vitakka Consulting, is a separate entity and is deliberately not attributed here.)

providers.name: micropointbio
providers.description: MicroPoint Biotechnology (Shenzhen MicroPoint Biotechnology Co., Ltd. / 微点生物) is a biochip technology company focused on the R&D, manufacturing and sale of MEMS-based Lab-on-a-Chip products. It is one of the few firms to master microfluidic-chip core technology at mass-production scale, and describes itself as the only POCT manufacturer that develops and produces both the biochips and their companion detection instruments, spanning fluorescence immunoassay, electrochemical coagulation testing and infectious-disease (including COVID) diagnostics. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and enriched here; no public developer, API, SDK or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Microservice Architecture
providers.description: An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services organized around business capabilities. Widely used by developers to build, maintain, and scale software applications efficiently.

providers.name: Microservice Design
providers.description: Architectural approach for building applications as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services that are organized around business capabilities. Covers principles, patterns, and best practices for designing effective microservice-based systems.

providers.name: microTERRA
providers.description: microTERRA is a Mexico-based food-ingredient company that develops functional ingredients derived from Lemna (duckweed). Its MAS product line delivers natural flavor enhancers and texture modifiers for the food and beverage industry, positioned as sustainable, clean-label alternatives that support salt and sugar reduction in formulations. A Techstars-backed B2B startup, microTERRA sells to food formulators and manufacturers and does not currently expose any public developer API, SDK, CLI, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Mighty AI *
providers.description: Mighty AI was an AI training-data / data-labeling company surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Sector: AI. The enrichment pipeline probed its web and DNS surface on 2026-07-20 and found no live API: the apex domain mighty.ai now 301-redirects to aurora.tech (the company was absorbed/acquired), and no api/developer/docs subdomains resolve. This profile is retained as a portfolio-graph lead with no active developer or API surface.

providers.name: MightyHive
providers.description: MightyHive was a data and digital media consultancy that helped brands take control of their programmatic advertising, media buying, data strategy, and marketing technology. Founded as an independent programmatic trading and media consultancy, it was acquired by S4 Capital and rebranded to Media.Monks in August 2021; the S4 Capital operating company has since consolidated under the single "Monks" brand (monks.com). Its offerings spanned digital media transformation, campaign launch and measurement, customer data platform (CDP) work, Amazon eCommerce solutions, and marketing/AI transformation services for enterprise brands. It is a professional-services / consulting business, not an API product company: it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDK, or open-source GitHub organization. Added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z-portfolio lead; enrichment confirms no API surface exists.

providers.name: miim
providers.description: mi|im (pronounced "mime", for Movement Imaging | Intelligence Matters) develops proprietary machine-learning and computer-vision technology that turns movement into intelligence for retail. Its movement-imaging platform analyzes and optimizes how people flow through physical space, helping retailers improve customer experience, drive operational efficiency, and detect and respond to events. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital; no public API, developer portal, or documentation was found during enrichment (the miim.ai domain currently returns a parked WordPress error page).

providers.name: Milano Vice
providers.description: Milano Vice is a Berlin-based virtual restaurant company founded in 2021 by Rudolf Donauer and Dennis Murselovic (both ex-Delivery Hero) that operates a digitally-powered, delivery-first pizza brand. It partners with professional kitchens across German cities including Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg and Frankfurt to prepare and deliver handmade pizzas and pinsa to homes and offices, orderable through its own website and third-party delivery platforms such as Lieferando, Wolt and Uber Eats. It is a consumer food brand backed by Speedinvest, Coefficient Capital, True and Geschwister Oetker, and does not currently publish a public developer API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub.

providers.name: Milk *
providers.description: Milk, Inc. was a mobile application development lab founded in 2011 by Kevin Rose, Daniel Burka, and Jeff Hodsdon, and backed by GV (Google Ventures). Its only shipped product was Oink, an app for rating and discovering real-world things. Milk shut down Oink in early 2012 and the product team was acqui-hired by Google in March 2012, after which the company ceased to exist. It is defunct with no active website, developer portal, SDKs, or public API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; enrichment confirmed there is no API to catalog.

providers.name: Milk Moovement
providers.description: Milk Moovement is a dairy supply chain software company that provides cloud-based logistics, scheduling, routing, quality tracking, and automated payroll tools for dairy cooperatives and processors across North America. The platform digitizes the movement of milk from farm to processor, giving producers, haulers, and cooperatives real-time visibility into the dairy supply chain. The company was surfaced via the techstars portfolio and enriched into the API Evangelist network; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or status page.

providers.name: Millennial Media
providers.description: Millennial Media was a mobile advertising / adtech company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The enrichment probe (2026-07-20) found the company is defunct: millennialmedia.com now CNAMEs to rc.yahoo.com via AWS Global Accelerator on oath.cloud (Yahoo / Verizon Media / Oath infrastructure, consistent with the AOL acquisition of Millennial Media), and every host returns HTTP 404. There is no independent millennial-media developer portal, API, developer.* or api.* subdomain (NXDOMAIN), and no /.well-known/ or /llms.txt discovery surface. No API artifacts exist to enrich; this record is retained as a historical/company lead only.

providers.name: Milliray
providers.description: Milliray is an airspace-security company building millimeter-wave radar technology to detect, track, and classify the small drones that conventional radar systems miss — from $50 quadcopters to autonomous swarms. Its DroneTector product fuses multiple sensor types into all-weather, 24/7 units that operate standalone or in networked mesh configurations, protecting airports, critical infrastructure (substations, refineries, water-treatment facilities), and forward-deployed defense operations. The company is backed by Y Combinator, NATO DIANA, the UK Defence and Security Accelerator, and the Royal Academy of Engineering. As of this enrichment pass Milliray publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — it is a hardware/defense provider without a programmable interface.

providers.name: Mind Robotics
providers.description: Mind Robotics is an industrial robotics company building intelligent robotic systems for real-world industrial deployment. The company focuses on clearly defined, high-impact environments — narrowing scope to the settings with the greatest operational need as a path toward broadly capable robots. Mind Robotics is a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company in the hardtech sector. As of this profile the company operates a single-page marketing website and an Ashby-hosted careers page and publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Mindsay
providers.description: Mindsay (formerly Destygo) was a Paris-based conversational AI platform that built chatbot and virtual-assistant automation for customer service and support teams, with a focus on travel and hospitality use cases. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the standalone mindsay.com brand is no longer serving a live site or developer surface (the company was acquired by Laivly), so no public API, developer portal, or documentation could be located to profile.

providers.name: Mindstrong
providers.description: Mindstrong (Mindstrong Health) was a digital mental health company backed by General Catalyst that combined a virtual behavioral-health care team with a research program in "digital biomarkers" — passively measuring cognition and mood from smartphone interaction patterns. The company wound down its consumer care operations around 2023. It never published a public developer API, documentation portal, or API reference; its primary domains no longer serve a live site. The one first-party software artifact located is a Python research library (digital biomarker model fitting) published to PyPI by the company's data science team. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an enriched company record with no public API surface.

providers.name: Minerva Labs
providers.description: Minerva Labs was an Israeli endpoint-security company known for its anti-evasion and ransomware-prevention technology, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of amplify-partners. It was acquired by Rapid7 in 2023; as of a 2026-07-20 probe the minerva-labs.com domain issues a 301 redirect to www.rapid7.com and operates no standalone developer portal, docs, or API surface. No developer/docs/api subdomains resolve and no APIs.json artifacts are enrichable from this defunct property. Sector: cybersecurity.

providers.name: Miniswap
providers.description: Miniswap is a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) startup building an online marketplace for complex hobbies, starting with tabletop gaming miniatures such as Warhammer. The platform maintains a catalog of more than 20,000 unique miniatures with detailed product information, and lets sellers photograph an item and have Miniswap automatically generate an accurate, detailed listing. It targets the roughly $20 billion tabletop games industry and was founded by Zak Singh and Will Hanna, who met at Cambridge. Miniswap is a consumer-facing web marketplace at miniswap.gg; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, documentation portal, or discovery artifacts.

providers.name: Minit
providers.description: Minit was a process-mining software company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Bratislava, Slovakia. Its platform ingested event-log data from systems of record (ERP, CRM, service desks) to reconstruct, visualize, and analyze how business processes actually run, surfacing bottlenecks, rework, compliance gaps, and automation opportunities. Backed by Earlybird Venture Capital (among other investors), Minit was acquired by Microsoft in March 2022, and its process-mining technology was folded into Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining (process advisor). The standalone Minit product, developer surface, and minit.io site have been retired; the domain now resolves through Microsoft-controlled Azure DNS and no longer serves a public site or API. This profile is retained as a network record of an acquired company; there is no independent Minit API to enrich.

providers.name: Mint
providers.description: Mint was a personal finance, budgeting, and money-management product originally built by Aaron Patzer and backed by First Round Capital and Uncork Capital (then SoftTech VC) before its 2009 acquisition by Intuit. Intuit shut the standalone Mint service down and reimagined its features (transaction review, spending tracking, net-worth monitoring, account linking across 17,000+ financial institutions) inside Credit Karma. Mint exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API reference; this profile is retained as a network company record. Sector: fintech.

providers.name: Miracle Miles
providers.description: Miracle Miles (Miracle Miles Group) is a consumer footwear e-commerce company backed by Hongshan (Sequoia China). It designs, manufactures, and sells affordable fashion footwear and accessories direct-to-consumer through a family of online brands, including DREAM PAIRS (launched 2009), Bruno Marc (men's footwear), Nortiv 8 (outdoor), and Dream Pairs Kids, selling primarily via its own storefronts and large online marketplaces. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is maintained as a company/lead record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mirendil
providers.description: Mirendil is a frontier AI research lab founded by veterans of Anthropic, xAI, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI and led by CEO Behnam Neyshabur and CTO Harsh Mehta. The company is building self-accelerating AI R&D: training frontier models that are exceptional at AI research and then redesigning the entire research loop around them to make it faster, more capable, and more autonomous. Its stated goal is to put frontier AI R&D in everyone's hands so people closest to a problem can stay on it, with applications spanning drug discovery, chemistry, biology, materials science, and robotics. Mirendil raised a $200M seed round at roughly a $1B valuation co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins with participation from Nvidia. As of mid-2026 the company has no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Miru Labs
providers.description: Miru Labs is a San Francisco / Bay Area cybersecurity startup founded in 2024 by Eoghan McKee, Quang Pham, and David Pigott, building a graph-native investigation and insider-threat prevention platform. Miru unifies cloud and endpoint sources into a living graph so human analysts and AI agents can investigate together, using behavioral intelligence to distinguish malicious intent from accidental violations and an "Agentic Dispatch" capability that runs autonomous investigations that triage, escalate, and counter-act across alerts and domains. The platform targets cybersecurity, trust and safety, and national-security investigation use cases, detecting AI leakage, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, reconnaissance, and espionage, and generating legal-grade case reports. The company raised a $2.7M pre-seed round led by Dreamcraft and Cadenza alongside Seedcamp, with participation from Inovia, Notion, and Alphagraph. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio lead; as of this pass Miru publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Mitro *
providers.description: Mitro was a password manager for individuals and teams, founded in 2012 in New York City by Vijay Pandurangan, Evan Jones, and Adam Hilss (former Google/Serious Eats engineers). It let multiple people securely share and control logins to a single account, architected around cloud storage with password databases encrypted client-side using keys derived from the user master password. Mitro raised $1.2M in seed funding from Google Ventures (GV) and Matrix Partners. On July 31, 2014 the team joined Twitter and released the Mitro source code on GitHub as free software under the GPL. The hosted Mitro service shut down on October 6, 2015; its open-source successor is Passopolis. The company is defunct and publishes no live API, developer portal, or reachable domain today.

providers.name: Mixer Labs
providers.description: Mixer Labs was a San Francisco startup, backed by Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC), best known for building GeoAPI, a geolocation and geodata web API that let developers resolve places, points of interest, and location context from coordinates. The company was acquired by Twitter in December 2009, where its technology and team (co-founders Elad Gil and Othman Laraki) went on to power Twitter's location and geo features. Mixer Labs no longer operates as an independent company, its mixerlabs.com domain no longer resolves, and it publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface today. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record rather than an active provider awaiting enrichment.

providers.name: Moat
providers.description: Moat was an advertising measurement and analytics company, backed by Insight Venture Partners and Mayfield, that measured ad viewability, attention, and brand safety across digital and video advertising. Oracle acquired Moat in 2017 and folded it into Oracle Advertising (Oracle Moat / Oracle Data Cloud). The independent moat.com brand no longer operates a standalone developer program: www.moat.com now 301-redirects to oracle.com/advertising, and the bare moat.com host no longer negotiates TLS. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/absorbed company lead with no independent public API surface.

providers.name: mobike
providers.description: Mobike (Chinese 摩拜单车 / 摩拜科技, "Mobike Technology") was a Beijing-based dockless bicycle-sharing company founded in 2015. Riders located, unlocked, and paid for GPS smart-lock bikes through a mobile app and QR codes. Mobike was acquired by Meituan in 2018 and its standalone brand was subsequently folded into Meituan Bike; the public site (www.mobike.com) is now a bare ICP-filing landing page with no developer API, SDK, documentation, or portal surface. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: MODIVO
providers.description: MODIVO is a Polish multibrand online fashion retailer operating one of the largest fashion e-commerce platforms in Central and Eastern Europe, offering more than 300,000 products from over 1,700 brands across women's, men's, and children's clothing, footwear, accessories, and beauty. Part of the MODIVO Group (alongside eobuwie.pl), the company is a consumer-technology portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and also runs MODIVO Platform (a commerce technology offering) and MODIVO Advertising (a retail-media network). As of this enrichment pass MODIVO publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Modsy *
providers.description: Modsy was a consumer interior-design startup founded in 2015 offering online interior design with 3D room visualization technology. In 2022 it shifted away from consumer design services to focus on its core 3D home technology, and on August 30, 2023 its IP and team became part of Lennar to pursue the next generation of 3D innovation for the home. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer or API surface exists.

providers.name: Modular Wind Energy
providers.description: Modular Wind Energy is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Module
providers.description: Module is a vertically integrated sustainable housing company that designs, manufactures, and builds modular homes. Operating across design (architecture and engineering with BIM), manufacturing (its Last Mile Facility in Pittsburgh), and construction (licensed general contracting), Module focuses on infill and "missing middle" housing, small-footprint and energy-efficient affordable homes, and mixed-income developments through its Last Mile Network of design, construction, and mission-driven developer partner programs. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; Module publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Modus
providers.description: Modus (Modus Technologies, formerly Modus Closing) was a real estate closing, title, and escrow technology startup backed by 500 Global and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It built software to modernize the home-closing experience for buyers, sellers, and real estate agents. Modus was acquired by Compass in 2021; its standalone product was wound down and folded into Compass. As of this enrichment pass, modusclosing.com serves only a Compass-branded placeholder page (titled "Modus Technologies") that loads Compass CDN assets, and the company publishes no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs, SDKs, or any other public API surface. This profile is retained as an honest historical company record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Moglix
providers.description: Moglix is an Indian B2B commerce platform for industrial and MRO (maintenance, repair, and operations) procurement, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Noida, India, with a Singapore base. Through MoglixBusiness it supplies enterprises with industrial products — safety equipment, electricals, power tools, fasteners, packaging, and office supplies — alongside supply-chain, procurement-software, and financing services. A unicorn backed by Accel and other investors, Moglix operates across manufacturing supply chains in India and international markets. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; enrichment probing found an internal API host (api.moglix.com) but no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or documented API surface.

providers.name: mogujie
providers.description: Mogujie (蘑菇街), operated by Mogu Inc. (NYSE MOGU), is a Chinese online fashion and lifestyle social-commerce destination that pairs a shopping marketplace with live video streaming and influencer-led content across apparel, beauty, and accessories. The company was formed from the 2016 merger of Mogujie and Meilishuo, is headquartered in Hangzhou, China, and listed on the New York Stock Exchange in December 2018. Mogujie's historical third-party open platform (open.mogujie.com) has been retired and now redirects away, and no active public API developer surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: MojiLala
providers.description: MojiLala was a marketplace for stickers, GIFs, and emoji that offered a content API and mobile SDKs so developers could embed searchable sticker and animated-sticker packs into messaging and social apps. Backed by 500 Global, the team subsequently pivoted to LEO AR (leoapp.com), a consumer augmented reality application for creating, transforming, and sharing AR experiences. As of this profiling the original MojiLala developer surface at mojilala.com is offline (returns HTTP 403/530) and the active property, leoapp.com, is a single-page marketing/app site that publishes no public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery endpoints. This profile is retained as a network lead; no live API artifacts were discoverable.

providers.name: Molagri
providers.description: Molagri is a Toronto-based biotechnology startup building next-generation biopesticides for agriculture. The company designs pest-control molecules that target specific molecular pathways unique to pest insects while preserving pollinators and other beneficial organisms, and uses predictive modeling to stay ahead of the evolution of pest resistance. Molagri emphasizes higher efficacy and biobased production to reduce emissions across both manufacturing and field application. Founded in 2026 by University of Toronto PhD biochemists Zaky Hassan and Min Jin, the company was part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking; as an early-stage biotech it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Molten Industries
providers.description: Molten Industries is a West Oakland, California climate-technology company that uses methane pyrolysis to split natural gas into clean hydrogen and solid graphite using electrical resistive heating, consuming significantly less energy than conventional methods. Founded by Stanford researchers Kevin Bush and Caleb Boyd, the company produces US-made graphite for lithium-ion battery anodes and hydrogen for heavy industry. It is a hardware and materials manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: MomMom
providers.description: MomMom (맘맘) is a South Korean consumer parenting and family-activity platform that helps parents discover places to go with their kids and products to buy for them. The mom-mom.net website and app curate kid-friendly destinations by region, family accommodation and resort deals, restaurant and class discounts, and community-driven product rankings (국민템랭킹) covering baby and childcare essentials, alongside parenting tips. It is a B2C curation, deals, and recommendation service, backed as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface is currently published (probed 2026-07-20).

providers.name: Moncler
providers.description: Moncler S.p.A. is an Italian luxury fashion house best known for its high-end down jackets and technical outerwear, founded in 1952 in Monestier-de-Clermont, France and today headquartered in Milan, Italy. The Moncler Group operates the Moncler and Stone Island brands, sells globally through directly operated retail boutiques, department-store wholesale and a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront, and is listed on Borsa Italiana (MONC). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; probing found a consumer e-commerce storefront but no public developer API program.

providers.name: MoreTickets
providers.description: MoreTickets (摩天轮票务), operated by Shanghai Juqitech, is a next-generation internet performance ticketing marketplace founded in 2015. The platform lets consumers buy and sell tickets to concerts, stage plays, musicals, and sports events through a transparent, competitive pricing marketplace with standardized ticketing services. It operates primarily as a consumer-facing web and mobile marketplace and does not publish a public developer API or open platform. The company is backed by Qiming Venture Partners and has raised a reported $108M in funding.

providers.name: Morta Security
providers.description: Morta Security was a stealth-mode cybersecurity startup founded in 2012 by a team with backgrounds in threat intelligence and protecting national critical infrastructure (widely reported as ex-NSA engineers). The company was building a new paradigm for detecting and countering advanced, targeted cyber threats. Morta raised roughly $1.9M in venture funding from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), DCVC (Data Collective), Greylock, Norwest, and Wing Venture Capital, and was acquired by Palo Alto Networks (NYSE: PANW) in 2013-2014, where its technology and team were folded into Palo Alto's threat-detection products. Morta Security no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio record; enrichment found no API artifacts.

providers.name: Mosaic Building Group
providers.description: Mosaic (Mosaic Building Group) is a full-stack construction technology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. It is a national leader in build-to-rent residential construction and pre-development, pairing in-house software with local homebuilding partners to deliver personalized homes faster and at lower cost across Arizona and Texas. Its Mosaic Hub platform applies AI to construction planning and operations management. Backed by a16z (Series A lead) alongside Greylock, Innovation Endeavors, Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, SV Angel, and 8VC. Mosaic operates as a hybrid construction-plus-software business and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Motion Math
providers.description: Motion Math was an educational math-games company (500 Global portfolio) whose products were acquired by Curriculum Associates and folded into the i-Ready learning platform. As of the enrichment probe (2026-07-20) the motionmathgames.com domain and every subdomain (developer/api/docs) return a 301 redirect to curriculumassociates.com/products/i-ready/i-ready-learning/motionmath-shutdown, and the site shares a wildcard TLS certificate with i-ready.com. The company publishes no independent API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface — this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct/acquired provider with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Mountaintop.gg
providers.description: Mountaintop (Mountaintop.gg) was a remote-first independent video game studio founded in 2020 by veterans of Blizzard, Respawn, Riot, and Bungie, led by Oculus co-founder Nate Mitchell. Backed by a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), the studio built Spectre Divide, a free-to-play 3v3 tactical PvP shooter featuring its signature "Duality" two-body mechanic. The game launched in 2024, but the studio wound down and Spectre Divide's online services were shut down in 2025. Mountaintop is a consumer game studio, not an API provider, and publishes no developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and its public web and support surfaces are now offline. It remains cataloged in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company with no active API surface.

providers.name: Movie Quote
providers.description: Random Movie and Series Quotes

providers.name: Moxxie Ventures
providers.description: Moxxie Ventures is an early-stage (pre-seed and seed) venture capital firm founded in 2019 by Katie Jacobs Stanton, backing exceptional, technical founders building a better future. The firm writes $500K-$2M checks (typically ~$1.5M for roughly 10% ownership) across enterprise software, climate, consumer, fintech, healthcare, infrastructure (dev platforms, robotics, autonomy) and vertical AI, and has raised three funds including a $95M third fund in 2024. Its 100+ portfolio companies include Airtable, Calm, Carta, Coinbase, Lime, Opendoor and Tipalti. Moxxie publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Mozilla http scanner
providers.description: Mozilla observatory http scanner

providers.name: Mozilla tls scanner
providers.description: Mozilla observatory tls scanner

providers.name: Mporium
providers.description: Mporium (Mporium Group plc, formerly MoPowered) was a London-based, "mobile first" data-driven marketing and advertising-technology company founded in 2012. Its proprietary IMPACT platform delivered software-as-a-service that helped agencies and advertisers identify and act on consumer "micro-moments" across search, social, and display media, reacting to real-time signals from TV, news feeds, sports, financial data, and social media to optimise ad pricing, timing, and selection. The group also acquired the digital agency Fast Web Media. Mporium was a portfolio company of the fintech venture firm Anthemis and was previously listed on the London Stock Exchange. The company is now defunct: it has been delisted, publishes no developer portal or public API, and its primary domain (mporium.com) is parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: MRU
providers.description: MRU Holdings, Inc. (operating as MyRichUncle) was a specialty education-finance company founded in 2001 and headquartered in New York that became one of the largest private student-loan providers in the United States. It ceased offering student-loan products in September 2008 and filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in February 2009. Battery Ventures participated in the company's 2005 PIPE financing. The company is defunct and publishes no live website, public API, or developer surface.

providers.name: mSpot
providers.description: mSpot was a mobile cloud-based content service provider founded in 2004 by Daren Tsui (CEO) and Ed Ho (CTO) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company offered a cloud music locker that let users upload their music library and stream it from PCs, Macs, iPhone, iPad and Android devices, alongside a full-length movie rental service with content deals across Sony, Disney, Paramount, NBC/Universal, Lionsgate, Warner and others. mSpot raised roughly $2.3M in venture funding from Trinity Ventures and was acquired by Samsung Electronics in May 2012 (reported ~$8.8M) to power the Samsung Music Hub. The standalone mSpot product and brand were subsequently wound down and folded into Samsung; there is no active mSpot developer portal, API, or product surface today. This profile is retained as a historical network record.

providers.name: mucho
providers.description: Mucho (Mucho Indonesia) was an Indonesian social-commerce startup founded in 2018 and headquartered in South Jakarta, positioned as Indonesia's first social online shopping application and often described as an aspiring "Pinduoduo for Indonesia." Its mobile app let users buy together with friends to unlock group-buying discounts, cutting distribution layers by working directly with brand owners and pairing frictionless payment with logistics support. The company raised early / seed funding with participation from Qiming Venture Partners. Mucho has since shut down; its app is no longer distributed and the mucho.asia domain now resolves to a parked placeholder page with no product, API, or developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct-company record surfaced through the Qiming portfolio graph.

providers.name: Muir Test Systems
providers.description: Muir Test Systems is a company in the Battery Ventures portfolio, operating in the test-and-measurement space. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 searched the web, npm/PyPI/Maven/other package registries, and probed for a developer/API surface and found no publicly discoverable developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or hosted MCP server. No production website domain for the company resolved during probing, so domain, well-known, and security probes could not be run. This profile remains a company-only lead with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Multi
providers.description: Multi (originally launched as Remotion in 2019) was a macOS-native multiplayer collaboration application for software teams, offering multi-person screensharing for up to ten participants, shared cursor and keyboard control with sub-100ms latency, session recording, and AI-generated summaries and action items. Backed by Greylock and First Round Capital, the company was acqui-hired by OpenAI in June 2024; the product was shut down and user data deleted, with the founding team joining OpenAI's ChatGPT desktop group. The multi.app site remains live as a static marketing page but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Muni
providers.description: Muni was a Latin American social-commerce and community group-buying platform founded in 2019 in Bogota, Colombia by Maria Echeverri Gomez, aiming to transform e-commerce across LATAM by letting community leaders aggregate neighborhood demand and buy everyday grocery and household items at prices up to 40 percent below competitors, with no added shipping or service fees. It raised a Series A from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2021 and at its peak served over 15,000 communities across Colombia, Brazil, and Mexico. As of this enrichment pass the company's primary domain (munitienda.com) resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander with no active product, developer portal, or public API surface, so the profile remains a consumer-app portfolio lead with no discoverable API.

providers.name: Murmur Technologies INC
providers.description: Murmur Technologies INC (Murmur) is a Chicago, Illinois out-of-home advertising technology company operating a mobile digital billboard platform. It mounts smart LCD screens on car-tops and pedestrian backpacks to display geo-targeted ads on city streets, using sensors, computer vision, and location data to segment audiences by demographics, location, and behavior, measure ad performance in real time, and retarget viewers across other channels such as Facebook and Google. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass its public web hosts (murmurcars.com / murmurads.com) do not resolve to a live web server and the operation appears dormant; it exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: musical.ly
providers.description: musical.ly was a short-form lip-sync and music video social app, popular 2014-2018, that was acquired by ByteDance and merged into TikTok on 2 August 2018. The service and brand are defunct. It never published an official first-party public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI; the only known interfaces are unauthorized community reverse-engineering projects. It was surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no first-party API surface to profile.

providers.name: Mutto Optronics
providers.description: Mutto Optronics (Mutto Inc) is a Taipei, Taiwan-based provider of resistive and capacitive touch panels for the mobile phone and tablet market. Formerly a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company, it is now publicly held. It is a hardware/optronics manufacturer with no public API, developer program, or documented software surface. The registered domain (muttoinc.com) has lapsed and now resolves to a domain-parking and ad-monetization landing page across all hosts, so there is no first-party developer, docs, or API infrastructure to enrich.

providers.name: Mya Systems
providers.description: Mya Systems was a San Francisco based HR-tech company, founded in 2012 by Eyal Grayevsky and James Maddox, that built Mya, a conversational-AI recruiting assistant automating candidate outreach, screening, scheduling and communications across the hiring lifecycle, integrating with major ATS, CRM and HRIS platforms such as Workday and SAP SuccessFactors. Backed by Emergence Capital, the company was acquired by The StepStone Group (Totaljobs) in May 2021, when its founders and engineering team joined StepStone; the standalone mya.com and hiremya.com developer, product and API surfaces are retired and mya.com now redirects to thestepstonegroup.com. No independent public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification remains for Mya Systems.

providers.name: myBOX
providers.description: myBOX was an on-demand self-storage service founded in 2015 in Seoul, South Korea, and backed by 500 Global. It delivered storage boxes to a user's door for storing unused luggage and goods, offering free pickup and a range of container sizes for documents, clothes, and bulky items. The company has since permanently closed; its site (my-box.kr) no longer resolves and it exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical surface. Retained in the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead; no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: Mybuys
providers.description: MyBuys was a San Mateo, California cross-channel retail personalization company founded in 2002 that delivered coordinated product recommendations and targeted offers across websites, email, and display advertising using a patented portfolio of real-time optimization algorithms and an Active Shopper Database. MyBuys merged with digital advertising firm Magnetic in 2015, and Magnetic sold the MyBuys merchandising/personalization business to Evergage in January 2018. The company is defunct as an independent entity; the mybuys.com domain resolves but serves no live product, and there is no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Mycoworks
providers.description: MycoWorks is a San Francisco Bay Area biotechnology and advanced-materials company founded in 2013 by artist Philip Ross and Sophia Wang, headquartered in Emeryville, California. It engineers premium leather-alternative biomaterials from mycelium using its patented Fine Mycelium process, sold under the Reishi brand to luxury fashion, automotive, and design partners. The company was backed by DCVC and other investors; it entered insolvency and was wound down through an Assignment for the Benefit of Creditors in late 2025. MycoWorks operates as a physical-materials manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: MyGlamm
providers.description: MyGlamm is an Indian direct-to-consumer beauty and cosmetics brand operated by Sanghvi Beauty and Technologies Private Limited (the Good Glamm Group), backed by Accel. It sells makeup, skincare and personal-care products online and through retail. As of mid-2026 the parent company is undergoing corporate insolvency proceedings and its primary domain serves an insolvency stakeholder notice portal. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: MyLife
providers.description: MyLife (formerly Stop, Breathe & Think) was a meditation and mindfulness mobile app backed by 500 Global that guided users through short check-ins and recommended meditations based on how they were feeling. As of this enrichment pass the company's primary web presence at stopbreathethink.com no longer resolves to a live site (DNS and CAA records remain but there is no reachable HTTPS host), and no public developer, API, documentation, or SDK surface could be located. The company appears defunct.

providers.name: Mynd
providers.description: Mynd is a tech-enabled property management and real estate investing company offering full-service management for single-family rental (SFR) homes. It manages more than 20,000 homes across 40-plus U.S. markets, handling tenant screening, leasing, rent collection, maintenance, and portfolio management for individual and institutional investors, and provides a proprietary Investor Portal for real-time portfolio visibility. Mynd is owned by Roofstock and integrates with partner platforms such as Stessa. As of this enrichment pass Mynd publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile remains a company/portfolio lead with no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: MyNewPlace
providers.description: MyNewPlace is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: real-estate. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Myntra
providers.description: Myntra is one of India's largest fashion and lifestyle e-commerce platforms, offering apparel, footwear, accessories, and beauty products across its own and third-party brands. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Bengaluru, Myntra was acquired by Flipkart (Walmart) in 2014 and operates a consumer marketplace at myntra.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Myntra does not publish a public developer API program; its developer/API hosts resolve behind Akamai but are not openly documented.

providers.name: MYSALE GROUP PLC
providers.description: MySale Group PLC is a former AIM-listed online retailer that operated flash-sale and outlet e-commerce marketplaces across Australia, New Zealand and Southeast Asia under brands including MySale, OzSale, BuyInvite and Cocosa. The group was delisted and its corporate operations wound down; the surviving consumer brand, OzSale (ozsale.com.au), now runs as a Shopify-hosted storefront. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer program, API, SDK, or webhook surface: the corporate domain mysalegroup.com no longer resolves and the remaining brand sites are consumer retail storefronts only. This record is retained as a portfolio-lead profile surfaced from the Insight Partners portfolio; it has no API artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: MySpace
providers.description: Myspace (Myspace LLC, part of the People / Entertainment Weekly Network) is a music and culture social platform focused on artist networking, music streaming, and editorial entertainment coverage. Originally one of the largest social networks of the 2000s, it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Myspace operates a consumer music/entertainment website only — its former developer platform (developer.myspace.com, OpenSocial-based) has been retired and no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or API documentation surface could be found. This profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only, with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Myxt
providers.description: Myxt is a consumer music streaming platform operated by Paper Phones Inc., built around the tagline "Musicians. Fans. Nothing in between." Instead of forced monthly subscriptions, Myxt uses an "unlock" model that lets artists monetize audio, session files, project files, images, and videos directly, while fans support creators without a recurring commitment and can chat with the artist after each unlock. Native iOS and Android apps extend access beyond the web. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network; during enrichment no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface was found.

providers.name: N3twork
providers.description: N3TWORK Studios Inc is a mobile and blockchain gaming studio behind role-playing titles including Legendary: Game of Heroes, Legendary: Heroes Unchained, and Triumph. N3TWORK was previously known for its mobile game network and free-to-play publishing/user-acquisition platform, and was backed by GV (Google Ventures) among other investors. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record. Sector: consumer / gaming.

providers.name: Na Kd
providers.description: Na Kd (NA-KD) is a Swedish online fashion retailer for women, selling clothing, shoes, and accessories direct-to-consumer through na-kd.com. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead, backed by Northzone and Partech. As of this enrichment pass NA-KD publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures the company identity and its live domain-security posture.

providers.description: Memes on Narendra Modi

providers.name: Nanno
providers.description: Nanno was an on-demand babysitting and childcare marketplace startup, founded in 2016 and based in Denver, Colorado, that connected parents with vetted, background-checked sitters through a consumer mobile app (a "childcare on demand" model). Backed by 500 Global among others, the company paused operations at the end of 2021 amid pandemic-driven labor and childcare-market disruption, and its technology and assets were acquired by household-management startup Call Emmy in May 2022. The Nanno corporate entity persists but no longer operates its platform; nanno.com no longer serves a live site. Nanno was a consumer app and never published a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. This profile is retained as a network stub for historical/lineage purposes and carries no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Nanoconduction
providers.description: Nanoconduction, Inc. was a Sunnyvale, California hardware startup that developed carbon-nanotube-based thermal management (chip-cooling) solutions for the microprocessor industry. The company licensed NASA Ames-developed Nano Engineered Thermal Material — vertically aligned carbon nanotube array composites that act as a high-efficiency thermal interface at the junction where processors meet heat sinks. Backed by Battery Ventures, Jerusalem Venture Partners, Phoenix Venture Partners, Western Technology Investment, and Woodside Fund (roughly $23M raised), Nanoconduction was acquired by Unidym in July 2008 and is permanently closed. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no public API, developer, or specification surface — a defunct materials-science hardware company with no digital API footprint.

providers.name: Naranga
providers.description: Naranga is a cloud-based franchise management platform for franchisors and multi-location brands, covering franchise sales CRM and lead management (emaximation), operations and multi-location support (nCompass), employee and franchisee training (nSpire), field audits and inspections, task and job scheduling, and local/multi-channel marketing. API access model: Naranga does NOT publish a documented public or self-serve developer API. There is no developer portal, no published API reference, no OpenAPI/Swagger definition, no SDKs, and no self-serve API keys as of this entry. Integrations with third-party systems (for example Twilio, RingCentral, Microsoft 365, AssureSign, and lead-capture/Zapier-style connectors) exist but are delivered through Naranga's partner and professional-services onboarding (typically a multi-week implementation scoped per brand), not through open, documented, developer-facing endpoints. Pricing is quote-based / contact-sales.

providers.name: Narrative Science
providers.description: Narrative Science was a Chicago-based artificial-intelligence company known for its Quill natural-language-generation (NLG) platform, which automatically turned structured data into written narratives and data stories. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Sapphire Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company no longer operates independently: Salesforce acquired Narrative Science in December 2021 and folded its technology into Tableau. The former corporate domain (www.narrativescience.com) now 301-redirects to Tableau's AI/augmented-analytics pages, and no developer, api, or docs subdomains resolve. There is no independent public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface remaining to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical/acquisition record.

providers.name: nasn-auto
providers.description: NASN Automotive Electronics Co., Ltd. is a Shanghai-based automotive chassis electronic-control manufacturer founded in 2016, developing brake-by-wire and steer-by-wire systems for smart and assisted driving. Its products include the NBooster intelligent braking system, brushless electric power steering (EPS) controllers, and motion-control solutions for autonomous vehicles. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, Matrix Partners China, Hillhouse and CATL, NASN has raised roughly $231M and is a Tier-1 supplier pursuing a Hong Kong listing. Surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company; NASN is an automotive hardware manufacturer with no public developer API surface at nasn-auto.com.

providers.name: Natalist
providers.description: Natalist is a direct-to-consumer fertility and pregnancy products brand founded in 2019 by Halle Tecco, selling prenatal vitamins, ovulation and pregnancy tests, fertility supplements, and pregnancy and postpartum products online. The company was acquired by Everly Health in 2021 and its storefront now redirects to Everlywell; it is a consumer e-commerce brand with no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or webhook surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with live domain-security probing of natalist.com.

providers.name: Natero
providers.description: Natero was a customer-success and predictive-analytics platform (an Andreessen Horowitz portfolio company) that helped SaaS teams reduce churn, monitor account health, and drive expansion using machine learning. It was acquired by Freshworks in 2019 and folded into the Freshsuccess product line. As of this enrichment pass the standalone company is defunct - the natero.com domain no longer resolves to a website, and there is no live developer portal, API reference, or public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Natron Energy
providers.description: Natron Energy was a Santa Clara, California sodium-ion battery company spun out of Stanford University in 2012 by Colin Wessells, building cells based on a Prussian blue analog (PBA) chemistry that promised long cycle life, fast charge and discharge, non-flammability, and a domestic supply chain free of lithium, cobalt, and nickel. Natron's product line was aimed at critical power and industrial backup applications, including the BlueTray 4000 — a 48 VDC, 4 kW (6 kW peak), 50 V rack-mounted sodium-ion battery tray — and the BlueRack 250 / 500 kW battery cabinets targeted at data center UPS, peak shaving, and EV fast-charging support. The company stood up the first U.S. sodium-ion mass-production line in Holland, Michigan in 2024 (a converted Clarios facility, ~600 MW/yr nameplate) and announced a planned $1.4 billion factory in Kingsboro (Rocky Mount), North Carolina that was expected to create more than 1,000 jobs. Investors included Khosla Ventures, Chevron Technology Ventures, United Airlines Ventures, Aramco Ventures, and Sherwood Partners. After ~$373M raised, on August 27, 2025 Natron's board determined that ongoing fundraising and order-pipeline efforts were unsuccessful; the company filed a WARN notice and permanently ceased operations on September 3, 2025, terminating staff at both the Holland, MI and Santa Clara, CA sites and cancelling the North Carolina factory. Sherwood Partners, the largest shareholder, took over wind-down and asset disposition. Natron was a battery hardware OEM with no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or programmable cloud surface.

providers.name: Natural Intelligence Systems
providers.description: Natural Intelligence Semiconductor (Natural Intelligence Systems) is a fabless semiconductor startup founded in 2016 and headquartered in Boise, Idaho, led by founder and CEO Paul Dlugosch. The company is developing the Natural Neural Processor (NNP), a novel processor architecture inspired by the human neocortex to deliver disruptive performance for artificial intelligence and big-data analytics workloads. Its roadmap spans the chips, system boards, and a software tool chain of compilers, drivers, and low-level APIs needed to bring the NNP into customer systems. It exposes no public web API today; the developer surface is chip- and driver-level tooling. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead.

providers.name: naturalmotion
providers.description: NaturalMotion is a mobile game developer founded in 2001 and now operating as part of Zynga under Take-Two Interactive, with games downloaded over six billion times across more than 175 countries. Known for titles such as CSR Racing, Star Wars Hunters, and the Euphoria and Morpheme animation technologies, the company builds and publishes consumer mobile games. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass NaturalMotion publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Neeva
providers.description: Neeva was an ad-free, subscription-based consumer search engine founded in 2019 by former Google executives Sridhar Ramaswamy and Vivek Raghunathan, backed by Greylock and Sequoia. It positioned itself as a privacy-first alternative to Google, later adding an AI-powered answer engine (NeevaAI). Neeva was acquired by Snowflake in May 2023, and its consumer search product was shut down on June 2, 2023, with the team and technology folding into Snowflake to power enterprise search and generative-AI features. The company no longer operates an independent product, developer program, or public API; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Neolane
providers.description: Neolane was a marketing automation and cross-channel campaign management company, backed by Battery Ventures, that Adobe acquired in 2013 for roughly $600M and rebranded as Adobe Campaign. The former neolane.com domain now 301-redirects to Adobe's Campaign product page, and the company no longer operates an independent developer portal, API, or artifact surface of its own. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; its live API footprint, if any, belongs to Adobe Campaign rather than a standalone Neolane brand.

providers.name: Neon Wild
providers.description: Neon Wild is a personalized children's entertainment platform backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) through its SPEEDRUN games program. Founded in New York by Troy Kirwin, it uses AI to transform a child's likeness into the hero of interactive digital books and narrative experiences distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface, and its former neonwild.com Squarespace site has expired. This profile remains a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Neoteris
providers.description: Neoteris was a Sunnyvale, California networking-security company backed by Battery Ventures and New Enterprise Associates, best known for its SSL VPN / Instant Virtual Extranet (IVE) appliances. It was acquired by NetScreen Technologies in 2003, and subsequently rolled into Juniper Networks when Juniper acquired NetScreen in 2004. The company no longer operates as an independent entity: the neoteris.com domain is registered but parked with no live host (nameserver records only, no A/AAAA/MX), and there is no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; enrichment found no live API to catalog.

providers.name: Nervana Systems
providers.description: Nervana Systems was a deep-learning and AI-hardware startup founded in 2014 (founders Naveen Rao, Amir Khosrowshahi, and Arjun Bansal) that built the open-source "neon" deep-learning framework and a custom AI training ASIC (the Nervana Engine). Backed by DCVC (Data Collective) and others, the company was acquired by Intel in August 2016 and folded into Intel's AI effort, where its work became the Intel Nervana Neural Network Processor (NNP-T / NNP-I); Intel wound that product line down in early 2020 following its Habana Labs acquisition. Nervana Systems no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no live developer surface: its primary domains (nervanasys.com, nervana.com, nervanasystems.com) no longer resolve, and it is not present in the APIs.io catalog. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: nested
providers.description: Nested is a modern, technology-enabled UK estate agency that helps people sell, buy, and let residential property. It pairs hyper-local human agents with a digital platform and mobile app that give sellers transparency across the transaction, listing homes on major portals such as Rightmove, Zoopla, and OnTheMarket. Nested was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. The company operates a consumer-facing service and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation at this time.

providers.name: Net Effect Systems
providers.description: Net Effect Systems is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise-software. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Network Alchemy
providers.description: Network Alchemy, Inc. was a Santa Cruz, California networking-security company backed by Trinity Ventures that developed non-stop IP infrastructure for secure private communications, commerce and collaboration. It marketed what it described as the industry's first secure IP clustered networking (IPsec/VPN) solution, delivering scalability, high availability and price/performance with no single point of failure. The company was acquired by Nokia in February 2000 and its products were folded into Nokia's network-security line. It is a defunct dot-com-era entity with no active website, developer portal, or public API surface; this profile is retained as a historical Trinity Ventures portfolio record. Enrichment found no live API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Network Engines
providers.description: Network Engines, Inc. was an early venture-backed (Canaan Partners) server and storage appliance maker that built application platforms and OEM appliance integration hardware for software vendors. The company was later acquired by UNICOM Global and rebranded UNICOM Engineering — its original networkengines.com domain now redirects to www.unicomengineering.com, where the business is positioned around Dell-based appliances and OEM engineering / build-to-order application platform integration. It is a hardware and manufacturing-services business, not an API producer: an enrichment probe on 2026-07-20 found no public developer program, no OpenAPI, no /api or /developers surface, and no /.well-known discovery documents on either host. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Neuron23
providers.description: Neuron23 is a clinical-stage precision-medicine biotechnology company developing genetically targeted small-molecule therapies for neurological and immunological diseases, with a lead precision-medicine program focused on Parkinson's disease. It combines machine-learning-driven genetic biomarker discovery with drug development to match patients to the therapies most likely to help them. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund, Neuron23 is a therapeutics company that publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Neversitup
providers.description: Neversitup is a Bangkok, Thailand based software development and IT outsourcing company delivering end-to-end digital software along with web, mobile, and backend engineering and dedicated developer placement for clients. It also builds and operates its own consumer fintech products, including the Piggipo and Piggipo Go credit-card management apps and the Fast Loan lending platform, on a stack spanning Python, Node.js, React, Kotlin, and Swift running on AWS and Firebase. As of this enrichment pass Neversitup publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or SDKs; it operates as a services and product company rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Neverware
providers.description: Neverware was a New York-based software company, backed by Thrive Capital, best known for CloudReady — a ChromiumOS-based operating system that converted aging PCs and Macs into fast, secure, cloud-first Chromebook-like endpoints for schools and enterprises. Google acquired Neverware and folded CloudReady into ChromeOS Flex: the neverware.com domain now 301-redirects to Google's ChromeOS Flex product pages (chromeos.google/products/chromeos-flex) and its certificate issuance is controlled by Google (CAA pki.goog). The company operates no standalone public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface today.

providers.name: Newfold
providers.description: Newfold Digital is a web presence and technology solutions company serving small and medium businesses worldwide with domain registration, web hosting, website building, e-commerce, security, and digital marketing. It was formed in 2021 from the merger of Web.com Group and Endurance International Group and operates a portfolio of consumer and reseller brands including Bluehost, HostGator, Network Solutions, Register.com, Web.com, and Domain.com. The corporate site newfold.com is an investor and company presence rather than a unified developer portal; public developer and API surfaces live within the individual operating brands, not at the holding-company level.

providers.name: Newmark Group
providers.description: Newmark Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: NMRK) is a global commercial real estate advisory and services firm headquartered in New York City. Founded in 1929 and acquired by BGC Partners in October 2011, Newmark provides capital markets, leasing, valuation & advisory, global corporate services (GCS), property management, industrial and logistics, multifamily, and retail services. The firm expanded its international footprint with the 2023 acquisition of UK-based Gerald Eve and its multifamily platform via Open Realty Advisors. Newmark publishes recurring industry research under the MarketBeat / market-report brand but does not operate a public developer program or expose machine-readable APIs.

providers.name: Newsle
providers.description: Newsle was a news-alerting startup that used disambiguation, natural language processing, and machine-learning algorithms to find blog posts and articles mentioning people in a user's professional and social network, notifying them seconds after publication. Founded around 2011 and backed by Bloomberg Beta, it grew to more than two million users before being acquired by LinkedIn in July 2014, after which its team and features were folded into LinkedIn and the standalone product was retired. The newsle.com domain no longer resolves to a live site and the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface today. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company lead.

providers.name: Nexite
providers.description: Nexite is a retail technology company (website nexite.io) surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It operates in the connected-retail / IoT-for-physical-retail space. This profile was added as a stub lead and has been through one local enrichment pass: the public web presence is live but fully gated behind a bot / CAPTCHA challenge, and no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or discovery (/.well-known/) surface could be reached. No public API surface is catalogued at this time; the entry is retained as a company record pending a discoverable API.

providers.name: NexLP
providers.description: NexLP was a Chicago-based legal artificial intelligence company known for its Story Engine platform, which applied data science, machine learning, and natural language processing to legal, investigations, compliance, and eDiscovery workflows. NexLP was acquired by Reveal Data in 2020 and folded into Reveal's AI-powered eDiscovery and legal intelligence platform. The nexlp.com domain no longer hosts a public website and exposes no developer API surface; live DNS probes show its security/abuse contact (CAA iodef) now points to revealdata.com, corroborating the acquisition. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched via the pipeline; no live API, documentation, or SDK surface was found.

providers.name: Next Big Sound
providers.description: Next Big Sound was a music-industry analytics company founded in 2009 out of Techstars Boulder that tracked artists' social, streaming, and airplay signals (plays, fans, engagement across Spotify, YouTube, SoundCloud, radio and social platforms) and exposed them through a REST developer API used by labels, managers and media. It was backed by Foundry Group, Uncork Capital (SoftTech VC), Alsop Louie and IA Ventures, and was acquired by Pandora in August 2015. Its analytics became Pandora's artist tools and were folded into the Pandora / SiriusXM Artist Marketing Platform (AMP). The standalone developer API and portal (developer.nextbigsound.com) have been deprecated; nextbigsound.com now resolves to Pandora infrastructure and HTTP redirects to amp.pandora.com. This profile is retained as a network identity record for a defunct/acquired provider — no independent live API surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Nextbite
providers.description: Nextbite is a virtual-restaurant / ghost-kitchen company that operates delivery-only food brands out of existing restaurant kitchens, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It reaches consumers through third-party delivery marketplaces rather than a public developer platform; its sister restaurant-ordering-aggregation product Ordermark has since merged into UrbanPiper (a DoorDash Preferred Integrations Partner). As of this enrichment pass Nextbite publishes only a thin marketing website (nextbite.com, "We Put Food on The Table") and exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Nexus Lab Technologies, Inc.
providers.description: Nexus Lab (Nexus Lab Technologies, Inc.) is a contrail-reduction software company founded in 2022 and backed by 500 Global. Operating from nexuslab.fr, it applies machine learning to satellite imagery, flight traffic data, and meteorological parameters to help airlines optimize flight paths and reduce contrail formation, mitigating aviation's non-CO2 climate impact. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing website with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; no developer surface was found to catalog.

providers.name: Ngmoco *
