providers.name: Nicira Networks
providers.description: Nicira Networks was a software-defined networking (SDN) and network virtualization pioneer founded in 2007 out of research by Martin Casado, Nick McKeown, and Scott Shenker on OpenFlow. Its Network Virtualization Platform (NVP) decoupled virtual networks from underlying physical hardware. VMware acquired Nicira on August 24, 2012 for approximately $1.26 billion; the technology was folded into VMware vSwitch and relaunched as VMware NSX in 2013, and VMware was itself acquired by Broadcom in November 2023. Nicira no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no first-party developer portal or API. Its only historical API footprint is the third-party Nicira NVP plugin integrated into Apache CloudStack. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of a16z and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Nimsoft
providers.description: Nimsoft was a SaaS-based IT infrastructure and application monitoring and service-desk company, founded in 1998 as Nimbus Software in Oslo, Norway and later headquartered in Redwood City, California. Backed by Northzone and JMI Equity, it was acquired by CA Technologies in March 2010 for roughly $350 million, after which its products were folded into CA Unified Infrastructure Management (UIM). CA was in turn acquired by Broadcom in 2018, and the former Nimsoft monitoring capability now lives on as Broadcom DX Unified Infrastructure Management. The www.nimsoft.com domain today resolves to Broadcom infrastructure, and Nimsoft has no independent developer portal, public API, or OpenAPI surface of its own.

providers.name: Nistevo
providers.description: Nistevo was a Collaborative Logistics Network — a web-based, on-demand (ASP/SaaS) transportation management platform that let manufacturers, retailers, and carriers plan, tender, execute, and settle inbound and outbound truckload freight collaboratively. Founded in 1996 in Eden Prairie, Minnesota (originally TransView Corporation) and backed by Insight Partners, it served shippers such as General Mills, Land O'Lakes, Georgia-Pacific, Cargill, and Baxter, and was acquired by Sterling Commerce (an AT&T subsidiary) in May 2006. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; nistevo.com is parked and serves no live web application.

providers.name: Nizthewiz
providers.description: NizTheWiz Technology Sdn Bhd is a Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia based logistics startup founded in 2015 that operates a crowd-sourced, on-demand same-day local courier and delivery platform. Its consumer mobile app connects senders with a crowd-sourced fleet of couriers and provides live GPS tracking and full last-mile transparency across the delivery lifecycle. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass NizTheWiz publishes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs — its product is a consumer-facing courier app rather than a developer platform, so there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Noah
providers.description: Noah (originally founded as Patch Homes in 2016 and rebranded to Noah in 2020) was a US-based home-equity investment fintech backed by Union Square Ventures. It offered homeowners up-front financing in exchange for a share of their home's future appreciation, as an interest-free, no-monthly-payment alternative to a HELOC or cash-out refinance. The company raised roughly $156M across five rounds from seven investors before ceasing operations in 2024. This record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio lead; no live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Nobell Foods
providers.description: Nobell Foods is a molecular-farming food-technology company founded by Magi Richani that produces animal-free cheese from plant-grown casein. The company engineered soybean plants to grow the same dairy caseins found in animal milk, working with independent Midwest farmers to raise the crop from seed to flower, then converting the plant-derived proteins into cheese that melts, stretches, and tastes like conventional dairy. Backed by DCVC, Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz, and investors including Bill Gates and Robert Downey Jr., Nobell raised a $75M Series B and has since rebranded to Alpine Bio, with Nobell Foods continuing as the animal-free cheese brand and product unit. It is a consumer-packaged-goods and biotech company with no public API or developer program; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with verified public identity only.

providers.name: NOD Games
providers.description: NOD Games is a Seoul-based blockchain game studio founded in 2019 by CEO Chanki Lee, building entertaining game content and open, player-owned game platforms where gamers and communities own and trade in-game digital assets as NFTs. Its marquee titles are League of Kingdoms, a free-to-play 4X MMO strategy game with tradable Land NFTs and the LOKA token, and Crypto Sword & Magic, an RPG whose heroes, equipment, and pets are recorded on-chain with game logic running in smart contracts. The company is backed by a16z crypto. As of this enrichment pass NOD Games publishes no first-party developer program, public API, SDK, or GitHub organization; its official domain nodgames.com resolves to an unconfigured Wix parking page and the League of Kingdoms domain no longer resolves, so there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Node.io
providers.description: Node (Node.io, legally Node Inc.) was an artificial-intelligence startup founded in 2014 by former Google executive Falon Fatemi. Node marketed an "artificial intuition" platform that combined a customer's CRM data with a large external graph of people and companies to score and predict which prospects, partners, employees, or investors a business should engage next. The company raised roughly $16M from investors including 500 Global, Mark Cuban, Avalon Ventures, Canaan Partners, and Bee Partners. On 2020-08-24 Node Inc. was acquired by SugarCRM, which folded the technology into its sales and CX products rather than continuing to sell it as a standalone product. Node.io no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; the node.io domain is now a parked GoDaddy/Afternic "for sale" listing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: NodeFlair
providers.description: NodeFlair is a Singapore-based technology career-transparency platform, founded in 2018 by Ethan Ang, that gives Asia's tech talent access to verified salary data, company reviews, tech-stack insights, benefits, and job listings across the APAC region. Salaries are verified against actual employee payslips, differentiating NodeFlair from other job boards, and the platform serves over 500,000 monthly visitors across eight Asian countries while helping companies hire tech talent. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment; the profile currently carries live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Noise & Vibration Technologies
providers.description: Noise & Vibration Technologies (NVT Group) is a Battery Ventures-backed platform of test-and-measurement companies that design, manufacture, and support equipment for measuring, simulating, and analyzing vibration, noise, shock, and other environmental variables. Its operating brands include Data Physics (SignalCalc dynamic signal analyzers and vibration controllers), Team Corporation (electrodynamic and hydraulic shakers), and Lansmont (package and product-testing systems), serving aerospace, defense, commercial space, automotive, and industrial customers worldwide. The company ships hardware and desktop analysis/control software rather than any public web API, REST service, SDK, or developer portal, so it has no programmable API surface for the API Evangelist network at this time.

providers.name: Nok Nok Labs
providers.description: Nok Nok Labs is a passwordless and strong authentication vendor and a founding member of the FIDO Alliance, known for the Nok Nok S3 Authentication Suite that lets enterprises deploy FIDO-based (UAF/U2F/FIDO2/passkey) multi-factor and passwordless authentication across mobile and web. Its offering is an enterprise, server-side authentication platform sold to banks, telcos, and large organizations rather than a self-serve public API product. As of this enrichment pass the company has no independent public developer portal: the noknok.com domain (every path probed) 301-redirects to OneSpan's security platform at onespan.com/security, indicating its web presence has been consolidated under OneSpan. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures.

providers.name: nomiku
providers.description: Nomiku (Y Combinator W15, backed by Slow Ventures) was a consumer-hardware startup that built an affordable WiFi-connected sous-vide immersion circulator and the companion Tender recipe app, later pivoting to the Nomiku Meals ready-to-cook subscription paired with the Nomiku Smart Cooker. The company emailed customers on December 13, 2019 that it was discontinuing the Smart Cooker and Meals and suspending operations. It exposed no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; the device was controlled through a private mobile app and cloud backend. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead identity record for historical and investor-graph completeness only.

providers.name: Normalyze
providers.description: Normalyze was a data security posture management (DSPM) company that helped organizations discover, classify, and protect sensitive data across SaaS, PaaS, multi-cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments, mapping data access paths and prioritizing risk. Backed by Battery Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Normalyze was acquired by Proofpoint in 2024 and its capabilities are now delivered as part of the Proofpoint Data Security Posture Management product line; the normalyze.ai domain redirects to Proofpoint. Normalyze never published a standalone public developer portal, API reference, or SDK, so this profile has no independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Normunity
providers.description: Normunity is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel anti-cancer therapies that work at the interface of the immune system and the tumor. In collaboration with the Lieping Chen lab at the Yale School of Medicine, Normunity has identified a novel class of "Immuno-smart targets" — tumor-specific, cell-surface proteins co-opted by cancer cells to drive local immune suppression — and is building a pipeline of biologic medicines including therapeutic antibodies, bispecific antibodies, and payload-carrying biologics. Its lead program, NRM-823, is a T cell engager that has entered clinical trials. Normunity is backed by Canaan Partners. This is a corporate/scientific company with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: Norstel
providers.description: Norstel AB was a Swedish semiconductor materials company that produced silicon carbide (SiC) wafers for power electronics, high-frequency and high-temperature electronics, and sensors, using its patented High Temperature Chemical Vapor Deposition (HTCVD) crystal-growth technology. Backed by Creandum among other investors, Norstel was acquired by STMicroelectronics in December 2019 and folded into ST's silicon carbide operations; it no longer operates as an independent company. As a hardware and materials manufacturer, Norstel published no developer platform, API, or SDK, so this API Evangelist record is an identity-only profile with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: North
providers.description: North (formerly Thalmic Labs) was a wearable-computing hardware company founded in 2012 in Kitchener, Ontario by University of Waterloo graduates Stephen Lake, Matthew Bailey, and Aaron Grant. It first shipped the Myo gesture-control armband, which read electrical muscle activity to wirelessly control computers and other devices, and later pivoted to Focals, consumer smart glasses with a heads-up display. A Y Combinator Winter 2013 company that raised over $140M, North was acquired by Google in January 2020 and wound down; its products and consumer-facing website (bynorth.com) were discontinued. This profile is retained as a network record. North published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Northstar Technology
providers.description: Northstar Technology (Northstar Technologies, Inc.) was a marine navigation electronics company and an exited Battery Ventures portfolio investment. It was a leader in premium marine GPS/chartplotter hardware and was acquired by Brunswick Corporation in December 2002 to form Brunswick New Technologies, and later sold to Navico in 2007. It is a defunct hardware company with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface; the enrichment pipeline found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Nosh Bio
providers.description: Nosh.bio is a Berlin-based sustainable food-technology company founded in 2022 by Tim Fronzek and Felipe Lino that produces nutritional, highly functional proteins from non-GMO fungi via proprietary precision fermentation. Its flagship Koji Protein and Koji-Beef mince hybrid are mycelium-derived, clean-label mycoprotein ingredients with binding, gelling and texturizing properties, sold B2B to manufacturers across meat alternatives, seafood, dairy, sauces, confectionery, wellness and pet food. The company is a foodtech portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital and closed a EUR 3.2M seed round. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Nosh.bio publishes no developer API, SDK, developer portal, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: NotePass
providers.description: NotePass (notepass.ai) is an early-stage, stealth-mode startup that is pre-launch: its only public web presence is a "Coming Soon" landing page inviting visitors to follow its journey and sign up for launch updates. The product has not been publicly announced and no developer platform, API, documentation, or SDK is published yet. NotePass was surfaced as a portfolio company of Electric Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead to monitor for a future API surface. Public contact is james@notepass.ai.

providers.name: Nova Instruments
providers.description: Nova Instruments is a test-and-measurement platform company that designs, develops, and manufactures instruments and systems for analyzing fluid and solid mechanics. It operates a family of established brands — Brookhaven Instruments, Dantec Dynamics, DegreeC, NDT Systems, Phoenix Inspection Systems, Technology Design, and Stresstech — spanning particle characterization, optical measurement, thermal management, and non-destructive testing. A portfolio company of Battery Ventures since 2010, it operates as part of the Nova Ventures Group. As a hardware-focused instruments manufacturer, Nova Instruments does not currently publish a public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Nova Metrix
providers.description: Nova Metrix is a geotechnical, environmental, and materials-testing instrumentation company headquartered in Wakefield, Massachusetts and founded in 2009. It designs and manufactures sensors, instruments, monitoring software, and consumables for structural-health monitoring, construction, civil engineering, energy, and medical markets, operating in more than 90 countries. Nova Metrix is the parent of a family of specialist geotechnical and fiber-optic brands including Roctest, Sensornet, Sherborne Sensors, Soil Instruments, Westbay Instruments, DGSI, Waterloo Hydrogeologic, and Van Essen Instruments. It is backed by Battery Ventures, Commonwealth Capital, and Ascent Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Nova Metrix publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile carries verified company identity rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Novira Therapeutics
providers.description: Novira Therapeutics was a biopharmaceutical company developing direct-acting antivirals for chronic hepatitis B (HBV), notably HBV capsid assembly modulators. It was acquired by Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) in 2015 and no longer operates as an independent entity. Its domain (noviratherapeutics.com) is now run on Johnson & Johnson DNS and mail infrastructure with no public website, developer portal, or API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners; the enrichment pipeline confirms there is no API or developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: Novocall
providers.description: Novocall was a Singapore-based callback and lead-conversion SaaS (a click-to-call and callback-scheduling widget that turned website visitors into inbound phone calls and booked meetings), surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company's public web presence is unreachable. The apex novocall.co has live email DNS (SPF, DMARC quarantine, CAA) but no web host, www.novocall.co returns a Cloudflare 530 (origin down), novocall.com is a parked/for-sale domain, and getnovocall.com refuses connections. providers.name: NTT DATA
providers.description: NTT DATA is a global IT services and consulting firm offering strategic consulting, cloud services, cybersecurity, data analytics, application development, and managed infrastructure across industries including banking, healthcare, manufacturing, public sector, and retail. The company operates in more than 50 countries and serves Fortune 500 enterprises with digital transformation, AI, and systems integration capabilities. NTT DATA does not publish a general public REST API; integrations are typically delivered through bespoke engagements and partner-specific solutions.

providers.name: Nuance Labs
providers.description: Nuance Labs is an early-stage AI research company based in Seattle, Washington, building a human foundation model with emotional intelligence. It is developing a real-time, full-duplex audiovisual system that sees, hears, reasons, speaks, and expresses simultaneously, reading tone, facial expression, and hesitation to enable face-to-face AI interaction that feels human. Backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company is pre-product: as of this enrichment pass it publishes only a marketing site (About, Press, Contact, Careers) with a "Get Demo" / early-access call to action, and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or other developer surface.

providers.name: Nubis
providers.description: Nubis Communications is a co-packaged optics (CPO) and silicon-photonics semiconductor startup building high-density, low-power optical interconnects for AI, machine-learning, and hyperscale data-center systems. Its technology places optics directly next to switch and accelerator ASICs to move data at very high bandwidth with dramatically lower energy per bit than pluggable optics. The company (originally at nubis-inc.com) has been absorbed into Ciena, whose optics-for-co-packaged-applications product line now carries the work; the former Nubis domain redirects to Ciena. As a fabless hardware / photonics-IP company it exposes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so no API artifacts apply to this record.

providers.name: Nucor
providers.description: Nucor Corporation is a Fortune 500 American steel and steel products manufacturer headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. It is the largest steel producer in the United States and the largest recycler of any material in North America. Nucor does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; this index captures the corporate, sustainability, and certification resources that are publicly available.

providers.name: Numerify
providers.description: Numerify was an IT business analytics company that provided a cloud-based System of Intelligence for IT operations, applying AI and machine learning to data from ITSM, DevOps, and application-performance tools to predict change risk, reduce incidents, and improve software delivery. Numerify was acquired by Digital.ai in 2020, and its capabilities now live inside Digital.ai's Change Risk Prediction / Intelligence product line. The standalone numerify.com domain 301-redirects to digital.ai, and the company publishes no independent public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Nuvia
providers.description: Nuvia was a semiconductor startup founded in 2019 to design high-performance, energy-efficient Arm-based CPU cores for data-center and client computing, backed by Mayfield among other investors. Qualcomm acquired Nuvia in 2021 and its core technology became the Qualcomm Oryon CPU. Nuvia has no independent developer, API, or product surface today; its former site nuviainc.com now redirects to qualcomm.com. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio identity record rather than an active API provider.

providers.description: nvxclouds is the web home of 锘崴科技 / NVX, whose legal entity is Hangzhou Nuowei Information Technology Co., Ltd. (杭州锘崴信息科技有限公司), an information technology company based in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming. The public website at nvxclouds.com is a single-page web application served over TLS from Alibaba Cloud infrastructure.
