providers.name: nWay
providers.description: nWay is a San Francisco-based multiplayer game developer and publisher founded in 2011, known for real-time synchronous PvP titles including Power Rangers: Legacy Wars (70M+ downloads), Power Rangers: Battle for the Grid, and the Web3 mech-combat game Wreck League. Its proprietary nWayPlay engine powers fast-paced cross-platform multiplayer across mobile, PC, and console. nWay was surfaced as a portfolio lead of cowboy-ventures. As a consumer gaming studio it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented API surface; enrichment probes of its website, /.well-known/security.txt, and /llms.txt returned no API artifacts.

providers.name: O11
providers.description: O11 is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building custom AI software for financial services firms. Rather than forcing teams onto a new external platform, O11 embeds AI-driven automation directly into the tools finance teams already use every day — Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and other enterprise applications — so users can generate presentations, spreadsheets, and documents and automate workflows without switching contexts. The company positions itself against the observation that a majority of firms still rely on legacy software where generic bolt-on AI features fail to deliver real value. As of this profile O11 publishes a marketing site (o11.ai) but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation could be found; this remains an early-stage identity profile in the API Evangelist network awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Observo
providers.description: Observo AI built an AI-native data pipeline (telemetry pipeline) platform that optimizes security and observability data in flight, filtering, enriching, and normalizing logs, metrics, and traces into standard schemas like OCSF to cut SIEM and observability data volume and cost before ingestion into the SOC. Founded in 2022 and backed by Felicis, Observo AI was acquired by SentinelOne; the observo.ai domain now 301-redirects to SentinelOne's Singularity AI Data Pipelines product, its documentation host (docs.observo.ai) is authentication-gated, and there is no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or programmatic surface to enrich.

providers.name: Observo Ai
providers.description: Observo AI was an AI-powered data pipeline platform for observability and security telemetry. Its product reduced log and event volume (filtering low-value data by up to ~80%), normalized diverse telemetry formats into standardized schemas such as OCSF, and enriched data at ingest before it reached a SIEM or observability backend. Founded to tame the roughly 35% annual growth of security and observability data, the company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was subsequently acquired by SentinelOne, where the technology now ships as Singularity AI Data Pipelines. The former observo.ai domain now 301-redirects to SentinelOne and the company no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Octapulse
providers.description: Octapulse (OctaPulse) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup applying computer vision and robotics to automate quality inspection in finfish farms. Its AI vision platform integrates into existing aquaculture workflows starting at the hatchery stage, using off-the-shelf cameras to perform broodstock phenotyping and juvenile deformity detection. The system reduces per-fish inspection time from roughly five minutes to under thirty seconds while achieving over 90% accuracy, standardizing QA processes and building proprietary multi-species datasets for the aquaculture industry. At this stage Octapulse is an early hardware-and-vision product company with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; this profile tracks it as a lead in the API Evangelist network for future enrichment should a developer platform emerge.

providers.name: Octarine
providers.description: Octarine was a cloud-native application security startup that built a security platform for Kubernetes and service-mesh environments, providing runtime visibility, policy enforcement, and threat detection for containerized workloads and microservices. Backed by Accel and Samsung NEXT, Octarine was acquired by VMware in May 2020 and its technology was folded into VMware Carbon Black Cloud and the Tanzu portfolio to deliver Kubernetes and container security. As an independent company Octarine no longer operates a public developer or API surface; its former domain octarinesec.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company / acquisition record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Odyssey Therapeutics
providers.description: Odyssey Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing small-molecule and biologic therapeutics for autoimmune, inflammatory, and oncology indications. The company targets upstream immune signaling mechanisms to prevent pathological inflammation rather than only suppressing downstream responses, advancing a pipeline of precision medicines. It operates as a private, venture-backed drug-discovery company with no public developer or API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: OFF
providers.description: OFF (Off-Live, off.live) is an enterprise AI software company building intelligent applications that help organizations streamline, innovate, and grow. Its products include AiVee, a smart scheduling assistant that uses computer vision to turn calendar images into digital events and manage invitations across popular calendar apps, and Pumky, a text-to-image generation platform with customizable artistic styles for both beginners and professionals. The company builds on computer vision, multilingual large language models, and domain-specialized AI models. Backed by Coinbase Ventures, Samsung Next, and Electric Capital. Surfaced as a portfolio company of electric-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Offerfit
providers.description: OfferFit is an AI decisioning company whose reinforcement-learning platform automated marketing experimentation and 1:1 personalization (replacing manual A/B testing with self-learning agents). OfferFit was acquired by Braze in 2025 and its product now ships as the BrazeAI Decisioning Studio. The offerfit.ai domain 301-redirects entirely to braze.com, and OfferFit publishes no independent developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal of its own. This profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio company and enriched via live DNS/TLS/HTTP domain probes.

providers.name: OGSystems
providers.description: OGSystems was a geospatial intelligence, data analytics, and advanced technology company based in Chantilly, Virginia, serving the United States intelligence community and Department of Defense with threat analytics, machine learning, and geospatial exploitation solutions. The company was acquired by Parsons Corporation in 2019 and folded into Parsons' national security and intelligence portfolio. Its former domain (ogsystems.com) now redirects to parsons.com, and it maintains no independent public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity/lead record surfaced from VC-portfolio data; there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Okera
providers.description: Okera was a data access governance and data security platform providing fine-grained, attribute-based access control, data discovery and classification, dynamic masking, and audit for analytics and machine-learning workloads across data lakes and warehouses. Founded around 2016, Okera was acquired by Databricks in May 2023 and folded into the Databricks governance stack (Unity Catalog). Okera no longer operates as an independent product: the okera.com domain now 301-redirects to databricks.com, and there is no standalone Okera developer portal, documentation, or public API surface remaining. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record.

providers.name: Okol
providers.description: Okol operates propiedades.com, an online real estate marketplace serving Mexico where buyers and renters search residential and commercial property listings and connect with agents, developers, and brokers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, the company runs its consumer-facing listings platform on AWS but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specifications at this time.

providers.name: Old Town Media
providers.description: Old Town Media is a New York City media consulting and investment firm founded in 2017 by journalists Tom McGeveran and Josh Benson together with media operations executive Katherine Lehr. The firm helps launch and grow journalist-founded news organizations (The Colorado Sun, Block Club Chicago, Documented), consults with established media companies (Chalkbeat, The Marshall Project, Medium) on revenue and sustainability, brokers media-technology partnerships, and runs a venture fund for early-stage media investments. It publishes no public API, developer platform, SDK, or technical product surface.

providers.name: Olin
providers.description: Olin Corporation is a leading global manufacturer and distributor of chemical products and ammunition. Olin operates three business segments: Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls, Epoxy, and Winchester. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: Olix
providers.description: Olix (OLIX Computing) is a stealth-stage hardware company building a new computing architecture that integrates SRAM with photonics to address the computational bottlenecks of large-scale AI deployment. The company positions its SRAM-plus-photonics design to surpass HBM-based architectures on throughput-per-megawatt and total cost of ownership while outperforming silicon-only alternatives on speed and latency as frontier-model demand compounds faster than today's infrastructure can scale. Backed by Creandum, Olix is currently pre-product and hiring across the US and UK; it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Omeat
providers.description: Omeat (rebranded as Evergreen Select) is a cultivated-beef company that partners with global meat producers to create price-predictable, industrial-scale beef supply. It produces 100% real beef without antibiotics, hormones, or plant-based fillers, positioning cultivated meat as a practical supplement to conventional supply chains while holding pricing at parity with commodity ground beef. Founded by tissue-engineering researcher Ali Khademhosseini and backed by GV, the company targets restaurants and meat processors seeking supply-chain stability and consistent quality. As of this enrichment pass Omeat operates as a food/biotech producer with a marketing website only: no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or GitHub organization were found, so there is no machine-readable API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a company/lead record surfaced from the GV venture portfolio.

providers.name: Omen
providers.description: Omen (omen.ai) delivers real-time asset intelligence through continuous fluid analysis, monitoring the health of mission-critical machinery in data centers and heavy industry. Its two offerings are a non-invasive permanent sensor that attaches to equipment for continuous, automated fluid (oil, coolant, water) analysis and real-time health tracking, and a portable canister lab that performs on-site, off-site, and field spectroscopic testing. The platform detects wear, contamination, and degradation before failures occur, targeting the machines the world depends on. Backed by CRV. As of this enrichment pass Omen publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Omniscient
providers.description: Omniscient is an AI intelligence platform for organizational decision-making, describing itself as a new class of AI that masters an organization's data and context to deliver decision-moving insights. Its focus areas include corporate reputation and narrative monitoring, geopolitical and regulatory risk tracking, marketing and narrative measurement, and supply chain and ESG risk, with an emphasis on early detection of weak signals and coordinated response. A Seedcamp portfolio company, it is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes a marketing site (Azure Static Web Apps) with no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Omniture
providers.description: Omniture was a web analytics company founded in 1996 in Orem, Utah and backed by Battery Ventures. It went public in 2006 and was acquired by Adobe Systems in 2009 for approximately 1.8 billion dollars. Its flagship SiteCatalyst product became Adobe Analytics within the Adobe Experience Cloud, and the DataWarehouse and reporting interfaces were folded into Adobe's Analytics APIs. The omniture.com domain now redirects to adobe.com and no independent Omniture API surface exists. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Omvana
providers.description: Omvana was a meditation and personal-growth audio app developed by Mindvalley, offering guided meditations, ambient soundscapes, and mixable audio tracks for daily mindfulness practice. The standalone Omvana product has since been folded into Mindvalley; omvana.com now permanently redirects (HTTP 308) to mindvalley.com/free-meditations. No public developer, API, or partner surface is published for Omvana or the successor free-meditations offering.

providers.name: One Raven
providers.description: One Raven is a Phoenix, Arizona smart-home technology company building a local-first home automation platform designed for homeowners who want simplicity, privacy, and control. Its core product is the One Raven Home Server, which processes and stores home data locally rather than in the cloud, and ships pre-paired with a curated set of devices such as thermostats, smart locks, leak-detection and security sensors. The platform emphasizes local data storage, encrypted remote access, and a subscription-free model. Backed by a $5M seed round led by proptech investor Fifth Wall. One Raven does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: OneASP
providers.description: OneASP (Application Security Protection) is the runtime application security product line of OneAPM (Beijing Blue Ocean Xuntong Technology / 蓝海讯通), a Qiming-backed Chinese IT operations management (ITOM) and application performance monitoring vendor founded in 2008. OneASP delivered runtime application self-protection (RASP) for web applications, and was also marketed internationally under the OneRASP brand. As of enrichment (2026-07), no standalone OneASP developer portal, public API, or SDK surface resolves - the oneasp.com brand domain no longer resolves and OneASP appears to be a legacy/absorbed product line of the parent OneAPM platform.

providers.name: OneCommand
providers.description: OneCommand is a cloud-based customer marketing and loyalty-automation platform built for automotive dealerships. Founded in 1999 and headquartered in Mason, Ohio, it helps dealers drive service and sales traffic, increase owner retention, and lower marketing costs through data-driven, multichannel outreach across voice, text, email, and direct mail. Its product family includes the OneCommand loyalty-automation platform, the Higher Gear CRM, and the TrafficAccelerator service. OneCommand was acquired by Affinitiv and its capabilities are now part of Karmotive, a CDK Global company. OneCommand operates as a marketing-services provider and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Oneforty
providers.description: Oneforty was a Twitter application marketplace and app store founded by Laura Fitton in 2009, letting users discover, review, and purchase third-party apps and services built on the Twitter API. It raised roughly $1.9M (Flybridge Capital, Javelin Venture Partners, and angels including Dave McClure) and grew to thousands of listed apps before being acquired by HubSpot in 2011. The company is defunct — the oneforty.com domain now 301-redirects to hubspot.com and exposes no developer surface, API, documentation, or SDKs. Retained in the network as a historical portfolio-lead record only.

providers.name: OneKitchen
providers.description: OneKitchen is a Dubai-based cloud/ghost-kitchen enablement startup founded in 2018 that provided chefs, restaurants, and food entrepreneurs with shared kitchen space, equipment, and operating technology to launch delivery-only restaurant brands in about 48 hours at a fraction of traditional restaurant capital cost. It was backed by 500 Global, Chernovetskyi Investment Group, and Savour Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company appears dormant - its primary domain joinonekitchen.com no longer resolves to a live product (it now redirects to a domain-sale parking page) and no public developer portal, API, documentation, or other API surface could be found.

providers.name: Onera (acquired by Lyniate in 2021)
providers.description: Onera, Inc. was a San Francisco-based retail technology company that built a real-time inventory availability and omnichannel order fulfillment platform. Its "Onera Decision Engine" connected inventory events across siloed retail systems into a single real-time source of inventory truth and used machine learning to determine optimal fulfillment locations for orders, serving retailers such as Gap, Old Navy, Torrid, rue21, and Zumiez. Founded circa 2014 and backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Founder's Collective, Onera was acquired by supply-chain planning and optimization vendor ToolsGroup in June 2022, where its real-time inventory and fulfillment capabilities were folded into the ToolsGroup retail platform. NOTE: the "acquired by Lyniate in 2021" in this record's slug/name is incorrect harvested metadata; the verified acquirer is ToolsGroup (2022). The company no longer operates a standalone public developer portal or API surface.

providers.name: OneRoom
providers.description: OneRoom was an online-learning startup founded in 2014 in San Francisco by Scott Forman and Jeff Kolesky and backed by Bloomberg Beta's 2013 fund with a roughly $750K seed round. It operated joinoneroom.com as a marketplace of live, video-based writing courses (fiction, non-fiction, playwriting, poetry, and prose) taught in intimate online classrooms featuring break-outs, head-to-head debates, content sharing, and co-annotation. The company appears defunct — co-founder Jeff Kolesky departed in 2016, and its domain now 302-redirects to a domain-sale listing (hugedomains.com). No product, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface remains. This profile records the honest identity so the API Evangelist network does not re-research a dead portfolio lead.

providers.name: OneSpot
providers.description: OneSpot was an Austin, Texas adtech and content-marketing startup that built a machine-learning platform to personalize and sequence branded content across websites, email, and paid media. Founded around 2010 and backed by early investors including 500 Startups, RSL Venture Partners, and Austin angels, it raised multiple venture rounds before being acquired. The onespot.com domain (and its developer, api, and app subdomains) now redirects to IgniteTech, and the company no longer operates an independent public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: OneSwoop
providers.description: OneSwoop is a UK car-buying and new-car price-comparison website, founded in 1999 and based in Liverpool, England, that lets consumers compare prices on brand-new cars and buy them online at a discount. It operates as a consumer-facing e-commerce and comparison property and publishes no public developer platform, API, documentation, or SDK surface. Backed historically by Insight Partners and other venture investors, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: OnFarm
providers.description: OnFarm Systems, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Fresno, California, was an agriculture IoT data-integration company that offered a customizable dashboard aggregating in-field sensor and remotely gathered data (weather, soil, irrigation) into a single view for farming operations across the US, Europe, and Asia. OnFarm was acquired by SWIIM System in July 2018, at which point CEO Lance Donny became SWIIM's COO. The onfarm.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, and no live public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface remains. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; enrichment found no active API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Open English
providers.description: Open English is an online English-language learning platform for Spanish-speaking learners across Latin America and the US Hispanic market. It sells consumer and corporate English courses built around unlimited live classes available 24/7 with native-speaking teachers, plus self-paced lessons and conversation and accent practice, delivered through its website and mobile apps. Backed by Redpoint Ventures; surfaced into the API Evangelist network as an edtech company profile. The enrichment probe found no public developer, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Open Skills
providers.description: Job titles, skills and related jobs data

providers.name: OpenInvest
providers.description: OpenInvest was a values-based / ESG investing fintech (Y Combinator and a16z backed) that let advisors and investors build and manage portfolios aligned to social and environmental causes. It was acquired by J.P. Morgan Chase in 2021 and folded into J.P. Morgan's wealth-management and Private Bank offerings. Its standalone product and any developer surface were discontinued: the openinvest.com domain now resolves to J.P. Morgan (www.openinvest.com is a CNAME to privatebank.jpmorgan.com), and no public OpenInvest developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDKs, or .well-known metadata could be found during enrichment. Retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record with no live API surface.

providers.name: OpenNetwork Tech.
providers.description: OpenNetwork Technologies was an identity and web access management software company known for web-based single sign-on (SSO), authentication, authorization, and federated identity products for web-enabled enterprise applications. Based in Clearwater, Florida, it raised venture funding led by Battery Ventures (with JP Morgan and SI Ventures). BMC Software acquired the company in March 2005 for roughly $18 million and folded it into BMC's Identity Management Business Unit. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: OpenToken
providers.description: OpenToken (OpenToken Inc.) was a San Francisco based cryptocurrency startup founded in 2017 that operated a token-fundraising and token-project aggregation platform, generating a secure, per-buyer funding address for each contributor so token projects could collect and distribute assets during their sales. The company was backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Pantera Capital, and Moonwhale Ventures. It is no longer active: the opentoken.com domain is parked (it refuses HTTPS connections and resolves to OnlyDomains parking nameservers), and no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification, or first-party SDK could be located for the company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and remains a defunct-company record in the API Evangelist network; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: opsmatic
providers.description: Opsmatic was a San Francisco-based infrastructure monitoring startup founded in 2013 that delivered a cloud service for real-time visibility into configuration changes and configuration "drift" across dynamic cloud infrastructure, alerting DevOps and operations teams so they could troubleshoot and reduce downtime. New Relic acquired Opsmatic in November 2015 to enter the infrastructure monitoring market, and the company no longer operates as an independent entity. The opsmatic.com domain now redirects to newrelic.com and there is no live independent developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. This record is retained as a historical VC-portfolio profile.

providers.name: Optiant
providers.description: Optiant, Inc. was a Boston-area supply chain optimization software company founded in 2000 on multi-echelon inventory optimization technology developed by researchers at MIT. Its flagship PowerChain suite (Network Design, Inventory, and Planner) let global manufacturers and distributors model multidimensional supply chains and free up working capital trapped across multi-echelon networks. Optiant was acquired by Logility, Inc. in 2010 (~$3.3M) and its technology was folded into Logility's Voyager Solutions suite as Voyager Inventory Optimization. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API surface; the optiant.com domain no longer resolves. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched as a historical/defunct lead.

providers.name: Optimotive
providers.description: Optimotive is an autonomous-robotics company building a vertically integrated fleet of advanced robots for the toughest, most extreme environments across construction, mining, and oil and gas. Its robots take on the mundane, repetitive, and hazardous tasks that burden human workers, doing it cost-effectively. Two products are already deployed with major market players: IRIS, a wheeled autonomous robot that captures large-scale site data, and BOX, which provides a reliable home base and on-site infrastructure for entirely self-sufficient robots. Two more robots are joining the fleet: MULE for onsite material handling and SCRUBBLES for site cleanup. The company is vertically integrated from developing its own AI to 3D printing its robots, owning the full hardware and software stack. Founded by CEO Scott Fairley and based in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, Optimotive raised a 2M USD seed round led by Version One Ventures in September 2024, with participation from Garage and NewLab. As a physical robotics hardware business, Optimotive publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: OptoAtmospherics
providers.description: OptoAtmospherics, Inc. is an Ann Arbor, Michigan company (founded 2009, spun out of Michigan Aerospace Corporation) that develops UV-based Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR) systems for the wind energy industry. Its laser-based atmospheric measurement products deliver continuous wind speed, direction, temperature, and density reporting from turbine-mounted or ground-based platforms, with real-time detection of wind gusts, shear, and turbulence to improve site assessment, increase energy output, and protect turbine equipment. The business is a hardware and atmospheric-sensing venture; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or software platform. Its former domain (optoatmospherics.com) is now parked/for-sale and the product line lives on under michiganaerospace.com/optoatmospherics/.

providers.name: Oratomic
providers.description: Oratomic is a Pasadena, California quantum computing company where leading researchers from Caltech and Harvard are building utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers with neutral atoms and optical systems. Launched from stealth in March 2026, the company advances quantum error correction with the aim of making practical, cryptographically relevant quantum computation possible with far fewer qubits than previously believed (on the order of ~10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits rather than millions). Oratomic is a deep-tech hardware and research organization; at this time it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic access surface.

providers.name: Orbicle Bio
providers.description: Orbicle Bio is an agricultural biotechnology startup developing carbon-negative, microbial-based organic fertilizers derived from soil microbes to replace synthetic fertilizers. Backed by 500 Global, the company targets rice-farming productivity and soil sustainability across Southeast Asian markets such as Vietnam and Thailand, with a commercial product launch planned for 2026. Orbicle Bio publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness and enrichment.

providers.name: Orbital ATK
providers.description: Orbital ATK was an American aerospace manufacturer and defense industry company formed in February 2015 by the merger of Orbital Sciences Corporation and the defense and aerospace divisions of Alliant Techsystems. The company produced launch vehicles, satellites, missiles, ammunition, precision-guided munitions, rocket motors, and the Cygnus spacecraft for ISS resupply before being acquired by Northrop Grumman on June 6, 2018 and rebranded as Northrop Grumman Innovation Systems.

providers.name: Orchard
providers.description: Orchard (Orchard Platform Markets) was a New York City online-lending technology company founded in 2013 that provided data, analytics, reporting, and an order-management system connecting institutional investors with marketplace-lending originators. Backed by Canaan Partners and Spark Capital, Orchard was acquired by Kabbage in April 2018 (substantially all assets); its team joined Kabbage's data-science org and the standalone product and its developer surface were wound down. The orchardplatform.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live API, documentation, or developer portal to enrich.

providers.name: Orgspace
providers.description: Orgspace, Inc. was a B2B people-operations software company offering org design, staffing, and workforce analytics tools that integrated alongside existing HR/HRIS systems. Its product let teams create team configurations, propose org charts, visualize cost projections, and build headcount plans framed around assigning people into roles rather than tracking open positions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass the orgspace.io domain no longer resolves (no DNS records) and the company appears defunct; no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface could be found.

providers.name: Origami Logic
providers.description: Origami Logic was a marketing-intelligence / big-data analytics company (backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners) surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the origamilogic.com web surface is defunct: DNS resolves only Google Workspace mail (MX + SPF/DMARC) with no A record on the apex or www host, so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. Domain-security posture was probed and recorded; no other public API artifacts exist. Retained as a historical company profile.

providers.name: Origami Robotics
providers.description: Origami Robotics is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) hardware startup based in Millbrae, California building advanced robotic hands designed specifically for machine learning and general-purpose robotic manipulation. The company designs a high-degrees-of-freedom hand with in-joint motors, co-designed with a matching data-collection glove that eliminates the embodiment gap between human and robot manipulation so that real-world training data transfers directly to deployed robots. Its focus areas include force transparency, avoiding the sim-to-real problems of high-ratio gearboxes, and scaling real-world manipulation data by deploying devices "in the wild." Origami Robotics targets industrial automation in manufacturing and logistics and has sold hands to Physical AI research labs including Amazon. Origami Robotics is a hardware and robotics company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Ornadyne
providers.description: Ornadyne is a Los Angeles hard-tech startup building autonomous flapping-wing UAVs (ornithopters) that look and fly like real birds for covert reconnaissance and surveillance. Its near-silent, AI-powered, man-portable drones are engineered for low acoustic and visual signatures, hour-class flight times, and natural bird-like flight, contrasting with easily detected quadcopters and fixed-wing aircraft. Founded by Geourg Kivijian (CEO, ex-NASA JPL and Astrolab) and Armen Arakelyan (CTO, ex-SpaceX Starship), the company is a Y Combinator Spring 2026 company operating in the hardware, robotics, drones, aerospace, and defense space. It is a hardware/defense company with a marketing website and no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Osyva
providers.description: Osyva is a B2B commerce and procurement platform for the veterinary supply sector in Colombia and Latin America ("Gestiona tus compras veterinarias"), connecting veterinary clinics, distributors, and buyers to manage the ordering and purchasing of veterinary products and pharmaceuticals. Backed by 500 Global, Osyva runs a web and mobile application (osyva.com, osyva2go.com) and the related Hubu brand (hubu.com.co). Its platform is powered by internal API hosts (api.osyva.com, api.osyva2go.com), but as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, documentation, or API specification, so its API surface is private.

providers.name: Otis
providers.description: Otis was an alternative-asset investing platform that let retail investors buy fractional shares in collectibles such as contemporary art, sneakers, trading cards, comics, and cultural memorabilia, backed by Kindred Ventures and Union Square Ventures. Otis was acquired by Public Holdings (Public.com) in 2022 and folded into Public's alternative-assets investing product; its former domain withotis.com now 301-redirects to public.com. The standalone Otis brand is defunct and exposes no independent developer or API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Outfittery
providers.description: Outfittery is a European personal-shopping and personalized-fashion e-commerce service that curates and ships tailored outfits to customers based on a style questionnaire and human stylist recommendations. Headquartered in Berlin, Germany, it operates across the UK, Spain, France, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands and Sweden. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. An enrichment probe found a consumer web/e-commerce presence with no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: OutlookSoft
providers.description: OutlookSoft was a corporate performance management (CPM) software company providing budgeting, planning, consolidation, forecasting, and financial reporting software. Originally surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, enrichment confirmed OutlookSoft was acquired by SAP in 2007 and folded into SAP Business Planning and Consolidation (SAP BPC). The outlooksoft.com domain is now controlled by SAP (SAP nameservers) and serves no live site, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no independent API to enrich.

providers.name: Outrider
providers.description: Outrider is an autonomous yard technology company that automates distribution yard operations with self-driving, all-electric yard trucks (hostlers). The Outrider System combines autonomous driving software, robotics for connecting and disconnecting trailers, and site operations software to move trailers between docks, parking spots, and staging lanes in large logistics yards. Headquartered in Golden, Colorado, Outrider targets shippers and logistics operators seeking to improve safety, sustainability, and throughput in the supply chain. The company is backed by investors including 8VC. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal has been identified for Outrider.

providers.name: Outside.in
providers.description: Outside.in was a hyperlocal news aggregation service that clustered blog posts and local news by geography ("placeblogging"), founded in 2006 and backed by Union Square Ventures and Milestone Venture Partners. It was acquired by AOL in 2011 and folded into the Patch local-news network; the standalone product and its geo-tagging API were subsequently shut down. The company is defunct: the outside.in domain no longer serves a website and there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Outsmart
providers.description: Outsmart (Outsmart Education) is an early-stage EdTech startup building a consumer, mobile-first learning experience for higher education in the age of AI — "the university of the future." Founded by former Duolingo executives and backed by roughly $38M from investors including Forerunner, Khosla, Lightspeed, DST, Abstract, Karman, Latitud, and Reach, with teams in LA, SF, and Salt Lake City. The product is a pre-launch waitlist app (iOS and Android, built with React Native, Rive, and Unity) emphasizing content generation at scale, gamification, and benchmarking. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing/waitlist site only; it exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Outsmart
providers.description: Outsmart (formerly branded Outsmart College; site joinoutsmart.com, with outsmartcollege.com redirecting there) is a pre-launch consumer education-technology company founded by former Duolingo executives Jorge Mazal (Chief Product Officer) and Gina Gotthilf (VP of Marketing & Growth) and backed by roughly $38M from top investors. Operating across LA, SF, and Salt Lake, Outsmart is building an AI-native, mobile-first "university of the future" — a gamified consumer learning experience for iOS and Android that combines large-scale AI content generation, psychometric assessment, benchmarking, and multi-modal behavior classification. As of this profile the product is at waitlist stage and the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this remains an API Evangelist network lead surfaced from the Khosla Ventures portfolio.

providers.name: OYO
providers.description: OYO (Oravel Stays Limited) is an India-headquartered hospitality company that operates a franchise and aggregator platform for budget and mid-market hotels, homes, and vacation rentals across India, Southeast Asia, Europe, and other markets. Founded in 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, OYO standardizes independent properties under its brands and distributes them through its consumer apps and website. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector company; as of this enrichment pass OYO publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Oyster.com (TripAdvisor)
providers.description: Oyster.com is a hotel review and travel-photography website owned by TripAdvisor, known for its in-person "Photo Fakeout" investigations and professionally shot, unedited hotel photos across destinations worldwide. It operates as a consumer-facing WordPress-based review and booking-referral site rather than a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or well-known discovery documents. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Packagd *
providers.description: Packagd * is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Packfleet
providers.description: Packfleet was an all-electric last-mile parcel courier based in London, delivering for hundreds of merchant customers using a zero-emission electric-van fleet with a focus on sustainable, reliable next-day delivery. Backed by Creandum as a venture-funded climate-logistics company, Packfleet wound down its independent brand in March 2025, with its deliveries transitioned to DHL. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was ever published; this profile is retained as a network record. Enriched: no API surface (company now operates as DHL).

providers.name: Padminivna
providers.description: Padminivna (padminivna.com resolves to Padmini VNA Mechatronics Ltd.) is an automotive component manufacturer established in 1991, specializing in innovation and manufacturing of technologies for the auto components industry across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles (M&HCV, LCV), two- and three-wheelers, tractors, and off-road vehicles. Its offerings span ICE, hybrid, and EV powertrains plus sensors and agnostic technologies, with a focus on fuel efficiency, quality, and environmental sustainability. Surfaced as a portfolio lead of norwest-venture-partners; the public site exposes only a vendor portal and employee login and publishes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: PaintZen
providers.description: PaintZen is a residential painting services platform that connects homeowners with vetted professional painters, offering instant online quotes and booking for interior and exterior painting, deck staining, epoxy flooring, and drywall repair. Backed by Bullpen Capital, the company operates its proprietary Zenify platform and now runs under Arch Painting out of Woburn, Massachusetts. As of this enrichment pass PaintZen publishes a consumer-facing website with online quoting and financing but no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: PaperX.com
providers.description: PaperX.com was a dot-com-era B2B online marketplace for the European paper industry, a former Insight Partners portfolio company that ceased operations in early 2001. The paperx.com domain is now a parked domain (Bodis/ztomy parking nameservers serving an error page) with no live company site, developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and processed by the enrichment pipeline; the honest result is that there is no discoverable API to enrich.

providers.name: Paragon Solutions
providers.description: Paragon Solutions Ltd is an Israeli cyber-intelligence and surveillance software vendor founded in 2019 in Tel Aviv by former Unit 8200 commander Ehud Schneorson together with Idan Nurick, Igor Bogudlov and Liad Avraham, with Ehud Barak among its backers. Its flagship product, Graphite, is mobile-device intelligence software marketed to government and law-enforcement agencies. Battery Ventures took an early-stage stake in the company; in 2024 Paragon was acquired by AE Industrial Partners and merged with the US cybersecurity firm RED Lattice. Surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead, Paragon operates no public developer platform: it publishes no API, SDKs, documentation, or self-service sign-up, and its domain (paragonsolutions.io) currently serves no website. There is no public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Parative
providers.description: Parative was an AI-powered customer intelligence / customer behavior platform (founded 2017, Boston, MA) that surfaced product-usage signals to define ICP fit, forecast net revenue retention, and predict churn, renewal, and expansion for go-to-market and customer success teams. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures (sector: ai-apps). Parative was acquired by Totango on 2024-10-22 and no longer operates independently; its domain parative.com no longer resolves (no DNS/NS records) and it exposes no reachable public API, developer portal, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Parature
providers.description: Parature was a cloud-based customer service and self-service knowledge base company founded around 2000 (originally as Cyracle) and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. Its SaaS suite covered a customer self-service knowledge base, ticketing/case management, live chat, and social customer service, and it exposed a developer API for managing knowledge base articles, tickets, and related data. Microsoft acquired Parature for a reported $100 million in January 2014 and folded its capabilities into Microsoft Dynamics CRM / Dynamics 365 for Customer Service. Parature from Microsoft stopped selling to new customers on November 1, 2016 and the standalone service was fully retired (end of support) on May 15, 2018. This is a historical/defunct company profile: the parature.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: parenthoods
providers.description: Parenthoods was a Y Combinator-backed mobile social network for parents, founded in 2014 by Siobhan Quinn and Jeni Axline in San Francisco, that helped local moms and dads discover nearby parents and share parenting experiences to counter the social isolation of early parenthood. The company raised a $1.32M seed round in November 2014 with participation from Slow Ventures, Lowercase Capital, 500 Global, and Y Combinator. The product shipped as an iOS mobile application and never published a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or documentation portal. The parenthoods.com domain now redirects to Wonderschool, and this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Slow Ventures portfolio lead with no discoverable API surface.

providers.name: Parhelion Studio Co.
providers.description: Parhelion Studio Co. is an anime-focused game studio based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and a portfolio company of a16z (Speedrun Cohort 002). Founded by a team that met at the University of Michigan, the studio builds live-service anime mobile and PC games — including gacha titles and the tactical anime trading card game Echoes of Astra — publishing across Steam, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. Their mission is to make anime a global medium and to create long-lasting IP through games and technology. Parhelion Studio is a consumer entertainment company; a public, scan of its website (parhelion.gg), app-store listings, and the a16z Speedrun profile found no developer-facing API, SDK, MCP server, webhook, or other machine-readable API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead and enriched to confirm it has no public API program at this time.

providers.name: Parkway Corp
providers.description: A Philadelphia-based real estate and parking infrastructure company that develops, owns, and manages parking facilities and mixed-use properties across the greater Philadelphia region. Parkway operates one of the largest privately held portfolios of urban parking and structured real estate assets in the Mid-Atlantic, providing on-street and off-street parking, monthly parking programs, validation services, and selective property development. The company does not publish a public developer API or partner integration portal.

providers.name: Parlia
providers.description: Parlia is the "encyclopedia of opinion," a London-based collaborative content platform founded by Turi Munthe and J. Paul Neeley that maps the world's arguments and opinions the way Wikipedia maps facts. Launched in January 2020 from Somerset House Exchange, it lets a community document, compare, and debate perspectives across politics, technology, and culture in calm, descriptive language, and publishes the "On Opinion with Turi Munthe" podcast. Parlia is a consumer-facing web product; the enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface. It is tracked here as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company.

providers.name: Parstream
providers.description: ParStream was a big-data analytics database company founded in 2011 in Cologne, Germany by Michael Hummel, Joerg Bienert and Norbert Heuber. Its columnar, GPU-accelerated OLAP database was built for Internet-of-Things environments, filtering and analyzing billions of records in sub-second time at the edge of the network, with query access via SQL and a JSON query format plus a C++ API for user-defined query nodes. Cisco acquired ParStream on October 26, 2015 and folded the team into its Data and Analytics Group; the standalone product was declared obsolete and retired in 2018. The former parstream.com domain now redirects to a Cisco end-of-life product page, and no independent developer portal, API, SDK, or discovery surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Partnered
providers.description: Partnered was a cloud-based co-selling and partner-introductions platform that let sales teams request and exchange warm customer introductions with their partners' sales teams, enabling partner-powered co-selling at scale. Founded by Adam Michalski and Tim Sherwood and backed by Slow Ventures among other early investors, Partnered was acquired by Crossbeam on May 18, 2022, and its product was folded into Crossbeam's Ecosystem-Led Growth platform. The partnered.com domain now redirects to crossbeam.com; Partnered no longer operates as an independent company and exposes no independent public API surface.

providers.name: Partyphile
providers.description: Partyphile (formerly Guestlist.ph) is a Manila, Philippines nightlife and events startup that built a consumer mobile app for discovering clubs, bars, parties, and events, getting on club guest lists to waive cover charges and skip lines, and booking VIP tables. Founded by Ron Baetiong out of a University of Santo Tomas thesis, it raised seed funding from 500 Startups (500 Global) and Kickstart Ventures and planned Southeast Asia expansion. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company presents no public developer or API surface — its primary domain partyphile.com no longer resolves and partyphile.ph is unreachable — so no API artifacts exist to harvest; this remains a company identity profile.

providers.name: Passwordinator
providers.description: Generate random passwords of varying complexities

providers.name: Patch Biosciences
providers.description: Patch Biosciences was a synthetic-biology and machine-learning company, founded in 2020 and based in New York, that built an AI platform for genetic sequence design — computationally engineering DNA "cargos" and regulatory elements to make gene and RNA therapies more effective, specific, and durable. It was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Bio + Health, Casdin Capital, and S32. Patch Biosciences was acquired by Ginkgo Bioworks in early 2024 and folded into Ginkgo's genetic-medicine services; it no longer operates as an independent company. Its former standalone website (patch.bio) is now parked and no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface exists. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record surfaced from a16z portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: PatPat
providers.description: PatPat is a direct-to-consumer children's and family apparel retailer founded in 2014 by Albert Wang and Ken Gao, selling baby, toddler, and kids' clothing along with matching family outfits, shoes, women's clothing, bags, and accessories to consumers in more than 100 countries and regions. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, PatPat operates as an online marketplace and mobile-first shopping app, and is one of the largest direct-to-consumer players in the children's apparel segment. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; PatPat does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Pattern
providers.description: Pattern was an early-stage team-collaboration startup founded by ex-Googlers and backed by Uncork Capital (SoftTech VC). It was acqui-hired by Workday in August 2017, with the team folded into Workday and its independent product and website discontinued; pattern's former web presence now redirects to workday.com. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record for the Uncork Capital graph, but it exposes no independent developer surface, API, documentation, or specification of its own, so the enrichment pipeline has no provider artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Pawdly
providers.description: Pawdly (포들리) is a South Korean pet e-commerce marketplace and mobile app operated by KCC I&C, offering pet product shopping across categories, saved/wishlist items, and pet-care service reservations, alongside pet-care tips and member benefits delivered through its app. KCC I&C operates as a payment intermediary and mail-order sales broker rather than the direct seller, with individual merchants fulfilling orders, shipping, and refunds. Pawdly was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass found a consumer web/mobile marketplace with no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Pawsh
providers.description: Pawsh is a consumer marketplace that connects pet owners with top-rated local dog and cat groomers. Pet owners browse groomer profiles, read real reviews, compare transparent pricing, and book grooming appointments online in minutes. Backed by 500 Global, Pawsh runs as a Firebase-backed web application at pawsh.app and serves 2,000+ pet owners. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface — it is a consumer-facing booking platform with no programmable interface to catalog.

providers.name: Pazpo
providers.description: Pazpo was an Indonesian property-technology (proptech) marketplace that billed itself as the country's first property search engine ("Mesin Pencari Properti Pertama di Indonesia"), letting users buy, sell, and rent homes, shophouses (ruko), apartments, warehouses, offices, and land across Jakarta, Tangerang, and the wider Indonesian market via web and a companion mobile app. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (500 Startups) and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for the enrichment pipeline. The enrichment pass found the company defunct: the pazpo.id domain no longer resolves (DNS lookup fails), and by 2024 the lapsed domain had been taken over by an unrelated Indonesian online-gambling ("togel") site. No live website, developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists to harvest; historical detail here is reconstructed from Internet Archive captures (2015-2017).

providers.name: PCH International
providers.description: PCH International (pchintl.com) is a global supply chain solutions provider that helps brands bring innovative physical products to market across the entire product lifecycle. Its services span new product introduction (NPI) planning, design and development, validation and manufacturing (EVT/DVT/PVT), and post-production revenue optimization, plus global logistics, direct-to-consumer (D2C) transformation, supply-chain financing, and sustainability programs. PCH serves personal care and beauty, health and fitness, home and lifestyle, accessories, audio and entertainment, and smart retail sectors. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners, PCH is a B2B services provider with no public developer API or platform at this time.

providers.name: Peak Games
providers.description: Peak (Peak Games) is a global mobile game developer headquartered in Istanbul, Turkey, best known for the casual puzzle titles Toon Blast and Toy Blast, which reach roughly 40 million monthly active users worldwide. The studio was acquired by Zynga in 2020 and operates teams across game development, art, big data and data science, and cloud platform engineering. Peak publishes consumer mobile games and does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Pearlbio
providers.description: Pearl Bio is a synthetic biology company developing next-generation biomaterials for smart biologics. Its proprietary platform unites genome and ribosome engineering to produce novel biologics with diverse chemistries previously inaccessible, creating template-directed biomaterials with tunable properties by combining biological precision with chemical diversity. The company partnered with Merck on cancer-related biologics (announced March 2024) and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Pearl Bio operates as a research-and-partnership organization and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Peel
providers.description: Peel Technologies Inc (peel.com) is a Redpoint Ventures-backed consumer technology company known for the Peel Smart Remote mobile app, which turned smartphones into universal remote controls for TVs, set-top boxes, and home-entertainment devices with a TV guide and content discovery layer. As of this enrichment pass the peel.com website resolves over HTTPS but serves only a single-logo placeholder page (frameset redirecting to an S3-hosted logo), indicating the company is dormant. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface was found; developer/api/docs subdomains do not resolve.

providers.name: Peerflix Media Network
providers.description: Peerflix Media Network was a Palo Alto, California online movie vertical advertising network that grew out of Peerflix, a peer-to-peer DVD-trading marketplace backed by Battery Ventures, 3i Group, and BV Capital (~$10M raised across two rounds). Peerflix shut down its DVD trading marketplace in April 2008 and continued briefly as the ad-focused Peerflix Media Network before being acquired by LiveUniverse in September 2008. The company is defunct; its domain (peerflixmedianetwork.com) no longer resolves and it exposes no developer platform, documentation, or API surface. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio-history record.

providers.name: Peerless Systems
providers.description: Peerless Systems Corporation is a technology company that describes itself as a leader in embedded imaging solutions. Historically focused on embedded imaging and printing controller technology and intellectual-property licensing for digital document, printer, and multifunction-device OEMs, the company operates as a corporate and licensing entity rather than a developer-facing API platform. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub associated with Battery Ventures; an enrichment pass found a corporate marketing website (peerless.com) but no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: PeerStreet
providers.description: PeerStreet was a two-sided marketplace for real estate debt investing that connected individual and institutional investors with short-term, high-yield real estate loans originated by a nationwide network of private lenders. The platform let investors build diversified portfolios of loan positions, earn monthly interest, and access loan-level documentation and performance data, along with a "Pocket" cash account and self-directed IRA options for accredited investors. Operating as a licensed California finance lender (License 60DBO-45398) and backed by a16z, PeerStreet transacted more than $5B across 47 states before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2023. The company is profiled in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Penguint
providers.description: PenguinT (penguin.travel) is a licensed Thai travel agency and tour operator (registration 11/08856) specializing in online flight search and booking for domestic and international routes. The consumer-facing site lets travelers compare round-trip and one-way fares across major carriers such as Thai Airways, Emirates, and Qatar Airways, in cabin classes from economy through first, departing from Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket and other Thai cities. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or programmatic booking surface.

providers.name: Penn National Gaming
providers.description: Penn National Gaming (now operating as Penn Entertainment) is one of the largest and most diversified regional gaming and racing companies in the United States, operating casinos and racetracks across multiple states. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: Penske
providers.description: A diversified transportation services conglomerate operating truck leasing, logistics, automotive retail, and professional motorsports across North America. Penske Corporation spans Penske Truck Leasing (full-service leasing, rental, and contract maintenance), Penske Logistics (supply chain management, warehousing, distribution, dedicated contract carriage), Penske Automotive Group (retail automotive dealerships in the US, UK, Germany, Italy, Japan, Australia, and New Zealand), and Team Penske (motorsports). The corporate parent has 73,000+ employees and approximately $43B+ in consolidated revenue. Customer self-service is delivered through web and mobile portals (Penske Fleet Insight, Penske Truck Leasing app, Penske Truck Rental); Penske does not publish a public developer API or partner integration portal. Penske Automotive Group is the publicly traded subsidiary (NYSE - PAG).

providers.name: Pento
providers.description: Pento was a European (UK/Danish) automated payroll platform that let companies run payroll, sync with accounting and HR tools, and pay employees in a few clicks; it was backed by Point Nine and Seedcamp. As of this enrichment pass the pento.io domain (HTTP 301) redirects to HiBob (www.hibob.com) and serves HiBob's HR-software marketing site with no remaining Pento branding, indicating Pento's payroll product has been folded into HiBob. There is no independent Pento developer program, API, or documentation surface to enrich; any live payroll API now lives under HiBob. This profile is retained as a network lead with its acquisition/redirect status recorded.

providers.name: Pepperfry
providers.description: Pepperfry is an Indian online marketplace for furniture and home products, founded in 2011 and headquartered in Mumbai. It sells furniture, decor, lamps, kitchen and dining goods, furnishings, and modular home solutions to consumers across India through its website, mobile apps, and a network of physical studio showrooms. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/GraphQL specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface: the consumer site is fully bot-protected (HTTP 403) and there is no evidence of an externally documented API program. The one artifact captured is a live domain-security probe of pepperfry.com.

providers.name: Performance Drone Works
providers.description: Performance Drone Works is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lux-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: defense. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Peribit
providers.description: Peribit (Peribit Networks) was a wide-area network (WAN) acceleration and optimization company backed by Mayfield. It built appliances that reduced bandwidth consumption and accelerated application performance across enterprise WAN links. Peribit Networks was acquired by Juniper Networks in 2005 and is listed as an exited "Milestone" company in the Mayfield portfolio. The company is defunct: it has no active corporate website, developer portal, public API, SDKs, or other machine-readable surface. This API Evangelist profile was created as a VC-portfolio stub for enrichment; the enrichment pass confirmed there is no live API or developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: Periodic Labs
providers.description: Periodic Labs builds AI scientists and autonomous laboratories to accelerate discovery in the physical sciences. Its systems formulate hypotheses, run real-world experiments in self-driving labs, and learn from the results, targeting materials design and the search for higher-temperature superconductors, and helping industrial partners such as semiconductor manufacturers analyze experimental data to iterate faster. The company is backed by Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners and SV Angel. As of this profile Periodic Labs publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface; this record captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Periscope
providers.description: Periscope was a consumer live video streaming application (pscp.tv) that let people broadcast and watch real-time video from their mobile devices, later operated by Twitter. The service was discontinued in March 2021 and the site (https://www.pscp.tv/) now serves only a farewell notice with archived past broadcasts; it publishes no API, developer portal, or documentation. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub (backers: bessemer-venture-partners, gv, menlo-ventures) in the API Evangelist network. Enrichment confirms there is no active API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Periscope Data
providers.description: Periscope Data was a cloud business-intelligence and analytics platform (SQL-based dashboards, data exploration, and reporting for data teams), backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, SuSa Ventures and Threshold Ventures. It was acquired by Sisense in 2019; the product is now Sisense for Data Teams and the periscopedata.com domain 301-redirects to sisense.com. No standalone Periscope Data developer portal, documentation, or public API surface remains as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Persistent
providers.description: Persistent Systems Limited is a global digital engineering and enterprise modernization company with 35+ years of experience, ~27,500 employees across 21 countries, and roughly $1.65B in annual revenue. It provides consulting, software product engineering, cloud and infrastructure, data and analytics, and applied-AI services to enterprises across banking and financial services, insurance, healthcare and life sciences, industrial, software and hi-tech, and telecom and media. Publicly listed in India, Persistent operates an AI Hub (GenAI Hub, iAURA, SASVA) and a products marketplace, but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specifications, SDKs, or API reference documentation as of this enrichment pass; this profile therefore captures company identity and probed domain-security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: PerTrac
providers.description: PerTrac was a hedge-fund and alternative-investment analytics software provider (portfolio analytics, asset allocation, and manager/database research for institutional investors), surfaced as an insight-partners portfolio company. As of this enrichment the PerTrac brand has been folded into Nasdaq eVestment — www.pertrac.com redirects to nasdaq.com/solutions/evestment/ — and there is no standalone PerTrac developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI definition, or public API surface. This profile is retained as a network record; any live API surface now lives under the Nasdaq eVestment product.

providers.name: Petrarch
providers.description: Petrarch is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) data-marketplace company based in San Francisco that unlocks enterprise data for the AI economy. Petrarch sources proprietary, enterprise-facing datasets from distressed businesses and legacy industries such as construction, manufacturing, and logistics, clears and anonymizes them, and brokers them to AI companies and research labs building for the physical world. Notable data types transacted include construction plans, autonomous-driving recordings, and codebases. The company was founded by Harvard graduates Ian Lee, Samuel Hahn, and Sudhish Swain, with prior experience at organizations including Scale AI. As of this profile Petrarch operates a public marketing website but does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Phia
providers.description: Phia is a personal shopping assistant that helps consumers build their closet and find the best prices instantly across the web. Co-founded by Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni, the product spans a mobile app and a browser extension that compares prices for a given item across new and resale marketplaces, tracking more than 700 fashion, beauty, and lifestyle brands. The public phia.com site is a consumer storefront (a brand directory plus editorial style edits) and exposes no developer API, documentation, or programmatic surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of GGV Capital and enriched from live probes of the public site.

providers.name: Philly Shipyard
providers.description: Philly Shipyard (now Hanwha Philly Shipyard, Inc.) is a commercial shipbuilder based at the former Philadelphia Naval Shipyard, constructing Jones Act-compliant container ships, product and Aframax tankers, and National Security Multi-Mission Vessels (NSMVs) for the U.S. Maritime Administration and state maritime academies. In December 2024, Hanwha Systems and Hanwha Ocean (subsidiaries of South Korea's Hanwha Group) completed the acquisition of Philly Shipyard for approximately $100M, rebranding the operation as Hanwha Philly Shipyard Inc. (HPSI). No public developer APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Philz Coffee
providers.description: Philz Coffee is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of cowboy-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Phoenix Tailings
providers.description: Phoenix Tailings is a clean rare earth and critical minerals refining company working to restore U.S. industrial independence by building domestic refining capacity for the metals behind every major technology. It recovers rare earth elements and other critical minerals from mining waste (tailings) and low-grade feedstocks using a low-emission, zero-landfill process, supplying materials for medical devices, electric vehicles and automotive systems, electronics, and defense applications. The company operates as a materials producer and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks its identity and web/domain security posture.
