providers.name: Phood Solutions
providers.description: Phood Solutions is a New York City-based food-waste technology company founded in 2015 by Luc Dang and Nick Kruczek. Its computer-vision platform, PhoodX, pairs a countertop scale and camera system with a waste-analytics dashboard to automatically identify, weigh, and categorize discarded food in commercial kitchens, grocery prepared-foods operations, and food-service venues. The platform reports product-level margins, recommends demand-based production volumes, and helps operators cut food waste by up to 50 percent, reduce kitchen labor, and lower food-inventory costs. Phood also offers Phood Lab, custom digital solutions built by its food technologists. The company is backed by Techstars. Phood publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Physera
providers.description: Physera was a virtual physical therapy (musculoskeletal) startup that provided members video access to a nationwide network of licensed physical therapists for diagnosis and treatment, along with in-application 3D exercise animations, voice prompts, computer-vision range-of-motion measurement, and asynchronous messaging. Backed by Lux Capital, Physera was acquired by Omada Health in May 2020 (reported ~$30M) and now operates as the "Omada MSK by Physera" digital care program; the physera.com domain redirects to omadahealth.com/musculoskeletal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI surface, or documented event/webhook surface — it is a member-facing clinical product with no first-party developer program.

providers.name: Pick1
providers.description: Pick1 was a real-time survey and social analytics platform founded in 2010 in San Francisco by Paolo Privitera (with Armando Biondi and Lorenzo Barbantini Scanni). It let brands run white-label surveys and augment respondent profiles with data from a dozen-plus social networks for audience segmentation, CRM enrichment, and retargeting, working with brands such as IKEA, Toyota, Telefonica, and American Express. The company was seed-backed by 500 Global and others, and was acquired by Evensi around 2017; its operating status is now closed and the pick1.com domain no longer resolves. This record is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub — there is no live API or developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: PiCloud
providers.description: PiCloud was a cloud-computing startup founded in 2009 that offered a pay-as-you-go, serverless platform for running Python workloads across public (AWS) and private clouds without provisioning, configuring, or managing virtual servers — popular for batch processing, high-performance computing, and scientific computing. It raised a seed round from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, Plug and Play, and Greylock. The team was acquired by Dropbox in November 2013 and the PiCloud service was shut down on February 25, 2014 (its platform lived on briefly as the open-source Multyvac project). The picloud.com domain is now parked, and there is no live API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: PICT
providers.description: PICT was a San Francisco startup (founded 2012 by Brent Locks, Kele Dobrinski, and Gregory Nicholas) that built a platform to make images shoppable, letting publishers tag and monetize products within photos. It raised a $1.4M seed round in 2013 backed by 500 Global, Opus Capital, Lowercase Capital, and Forerunner Ventures, and was acquired by PopSugar in January 2014. The pict.com domain no longer resolves and the company exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: PictureWorks
providers.description: PictureWorks (PictureWorks Technology) was a digital imaging technology company based in Danville, California that built imaging tools and services for the real estate and e-commerce industries, enabling online visual presentation of products and properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. The company was acquired by Internet Pictures Corporation (IPIX) in 2000. No public developer API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or SDK surface could be located for this entity during enrichment; the active pictureworks.com (Pictureworks Group, Singapore theme-park imaging) is a separate, unrelated company and is not linked here to avoid mis-attribution.

providers.name: Pienza
providers.description: Pienza is a Seattle-based B2B software startup studio and early-stage venture fund founded in 2020 by Aaron Bird (founder of Bizible, later sold to Marketo). Pienza partners with entrepreneurs to ideate, fund, and build category-defining SaaS companies, and later operated a Pienza Ventures accelerator focused on helping Indian SaaS and AI startups scale into the U.S. market. It raised $5.1M from MHS Capital, Version One Ventures, and Vulcan Capital plus angel investors. Pienza is a company-building and investment firm rather than an API provider; enrichment found no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal, and the primary pienza.com domain no longer serves an active site.

providers.name: Pine Street Labs
providers.description: Pine Street Labs is a crypto / blockchain infrastructure company surfaced as a portfolio company of Polychain and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: infrastructure. Enrichment probes of pinestreetlabs.com found no live developer or API surface: the domain currently serves unrelated content and publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or security programs. This profile is retained as a lead pending a verified developer surface.

providers.name: Pinhome
providers.description: Pinhome is an Indonesian proptech real estate marketplace for smart buying, selling, and renting of houses, apartments, offices, and shop-houses (Pintar Jual Beli Sewa Rumah). The platform spans property listings and search, mortgage (KPR) and loan-takeover facilitation with partner banks, an automated property valuation tool (Pinvalue), and a marketplace of household and property services. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Pinhome operates a consumer-facing web and mobile product and does not publish a public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Pinshape
providers.description: Pinshape is an online marketplace and community for 3D-printable designs, where makers, designers, and hobbyists browse, download, and sell STL and other printable model files for use on desktop 3D printers. The platform hosts both free and premium designs across categories such as toys, gadgets, art, jewelry, and functional parts, and was acquired by desktop 3D-printing manufacturer Formlabs. This profile was surfaced as a venture portfolio lead and enriched through the API Evangelist network; Pinshape publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Pitch Aeronautics
providers.description: Pitch Aeronautics provides AI-powered weather intelligence and drone-deployable line solutions for electric utilities, helping them boost grid capacity, increase reliability, and reduce wildfire risk. The company pairs aerial hardware that installs and inspects power-line equipment with software that turns real-time atmospheric and grid data into dynamic line-rating and operational intelligence. Pitch Aeronautics is a Techstars-backed company; this API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public website. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment (July 2026).

providers.name: Pixate
providers.description: Pixate was a code-free, drag-and-drop mobile prototyping platform that let designers build sophisticated, fluid interactive prototypes running natively on iOS and Android devices. Founded as an interaction-design startup and backed by a16z, Pixate was acquired by Google in July 2015 and discontinued on October 31, 2016. The pixate.com domain now serves only a Google-hosted farewell notice; there is no product, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface remaining to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record.

providers.name: Pixelworks
providers.description: Pixelworks, Inc. (NASDAQ: PXLW) is a San Jose, California based semiconductor company founded in 1997 that designs video and pixel processing integrated circuits and software for digital video applications. Its technology spans digital displays, mobile devices, projection systems, digital signage, and video conferencing and surveillance, including the Iris visual processing line and TrueCut Motion cinematic-quality video platform. Pixelworks sells chips and IP to device makers rather than operating a public developer API platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and coverage tracking.

providers.name: PixOwl
providers.description: PixOwl is a mobile game studio, originally known for the early mobile version of The Sandbox and titles such as Doodle Grub, later acquired by Animoca Brands. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the pixowl.com domain is a defunct redirect loop behind Cloudflare with no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface; only live domain-security posture (TLS/DNS) could be probed.

providers.name: Piñata Farms
providers.description: Piñata Farms is a Los Angeles-based consumer entertainment company behind an AI video and meme-making mobile app that turns chats, photos, and trending templates into personalized memes and short AI-generated video messages. Backed by Index Ventures and Founders Fund, the product is delivered as an iOS/mobile consumer app served by a private backend at api.pinatafarm.com; the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead with a monitored (currently unavailable) marketing site and a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Placeholder
providers.description: Placeholder is a venture capital partnership based in New York City that invests in decentralized information networks — crypto protocols and Web3 infrastructure. It was added to the API Evangelist network via the VC-portfolio pipeline. The firm publishes a marketing website (Squarespace-hosted) but no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; this profile therefore carries firm identity and live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Placemeter
providers.description: Placemeter was a New York City computer-vision analytics startup (a Techstars company) that turned live video feeds into real-time measurements of pedestrian and vehicle activity in physical places, offering a data API for foot-traffic and movement counts. The standalone product and developer API are no longer operational: placemeter.com no longer serves a website (the apex domain has no address record, carries no mail exchanger, and is defensively parked under Netgear's corporate registrar, CSC Corporate Domains), so there is no live API surface, documentation, SDK, or event stream to enrich.

providers.name: Planetly
providers.description: Planetly was a Berlin-based carbon accounting and climate software startup, backed by speedinvest, that helped companies measure, reduce, and offset their carbon footprint. It was acquired by OneTrust and subsequently absorbed; as of this enrichment pass the planetly.com domain 301-redirects to onetrust.com/solutions, and Planetly operates no independent website, developer portal, or public API surface. This profile is retained as a network stub documenting the company and its outcome.

providers.name: Plantner Inc.
providers.description: Plantner Inc. (PLANTNER) is a South Korean biotechnology company specializing in the extraction and manufacturing of alginic acid, a biodegradable marine-derived biomaterial. Operating as a bio-industry platform provider, Plantner supplies alginic acid-based solutions across medical devices (wound dressings, nutraceuticals), pharmaceuticals (gastroprotective agents, drug-delivery systems), cosmetics (modeling masks, hydrogels), advanced biotech (bio-ink, organoids, delivery carriers), and agriculture (controlled-release fertilizers, mulching films, eco-friendly herbicides). Headquartered in Seoul with an R&D center in Suwon, the company is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a materials/biotech manufacturer and does not currently publish a developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: plated
providers.description: Plated was a meal-kit delivery company surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company was acquired by Albertsons in 2017 and later wound down; the plated.com domain now 301-redirects to safeway.com, and no independent developer portal, API reference, SDK, or well-known surface remains. This profile records the honest state of a defunct provider with no active API surface.

providers.name: Platespin
providers.description: PlateSpin is a workload virtualization, migration, and protection product line (PlateSpin Migrate, PlateSpin Protect, PlateSpin Forge) originally built by PlateSpin Ltd., acquired by Novell in 2008, subsequently owned by Micro Focus and then OpenText. It is not an independent company: the platespin.com domain 301-redirects to Novell's virtualization/workload solutions page and resolves to a Novell IP (130.57.66.19), with the TLS certificate owned by Micro Focus (*.microfocus.com, *.netiq.com). This record was created from an insight-partners VC-portfolio scrape and is a false match against the legacy PlateSpin brand; there is no independent developer portal, public API, or discoverable developer.* / docs.* / api.* surface for PlateSpin as a standalone provider.

providers.name: Platfora
providers.description: Platfora was a big-data analytics company founded in 2011 by Ben Werther that provided in-memory business intelligence and data visualization directly on top of Apache Hadoop, letting analysts run interactive queries, build "lenses," and share dashboards without ETL into a separate warehouse. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Battery Ventures, In-Q-Tel and others, it raised roughly $65M before Workday acquired the company in July 2016 and folded the technology into Workday's analytics stack. The standalone Platfora product and platfora.com developer surface were subsequently discontinued; the domain no longer resolves and no public API or developer program remains.

providers.name: Plato
providers.description: Plato was a mentorship and leadership community for engineering leaders (platohq.com), operating from 2018 until its sunset on December 19, 2025. It ran a global network of 500+ engineering leaders and 1,000+ mentors, the annual Elevate conference, and dozens of meetups, webinars, and dinners. Its parent company Coda was acquired by Grammarly (rebranded Superhuman), which wound down Plato's programs to focus on an AI-native productivity suite. The company is now deactivated: platohq.com redirects to a Substack sunset announcement and no developer API, SDK, documentation, or integrations are or were published. Surfaced as a partech portfolio lead; enrichment found no API surface.

providers.name: Platogo
providers.description: Platogo Interactive Entertainment GmbH is a Vienna, Austria based social casino gaming studio that builds and operates free-to-play slot and casino apps for mobile and web. Its flagship titles are Slotpark, a premium Vegas-style social slots app used by millions daily, and Gaminator, one of the largest social casino gaming communities on the web. The company localizes its games into more than 13 languages and works alongside industry partners including Greentube and Novomatic. Platogo is backed by Seedcamp. No public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Platypus
providers.description: Platypus is a Danish HR-technology company (a Speedinvest portfolio company, invested 2019) that built a talent lifecycle management solution for HR managers. Its people-analytics product helped HR professionals measure what employees value at every stage of the talent lifecycle - from attraction through management to retention - using a value-centric approach to company culture built on 12 work-related values across 3 core areas of organizational culture, surfacing individual needs and priorities while protecting employee anonymity. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment; the company's former domains (getplatypus.com, platypus.ai) are now parked / listed for sale, indicating the product appears to be inactive/defunct.

providers.name: Playcurio
providers.description: PlayCurio is a Seoul-based educational technology company that builds AR (augmented reality) play-learning products for children, pairing physical educational tools with digital content. Its catalog includes AR titles such as Curio Safari, Phonics Pop, Dictionary Pop, and Math Mates, alongside a content-IP business spanning characters like Detective Pete, Dino Tales, and 100+ Curio Safari animals, plus B2B production services (character development, 2D/3D animation, UI/UX, and live-action video). PlayCurio is consumer- and partnership-facing and publishes no developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation. Surfaced via the 500 Global portfolio and enriched here; a domain-security probe of play-curio.com is the only technical artifact this pass produced.

providers.name: PleasrDAO
providers.description: PleasrDAO is a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) formed in 2021 by a collective of digital artists, NFT collectors, and DeFi investors. It is known for acquiring and stewarding culturally significant digital and physical assets, including the sole copy of Wu-Tang Clan's album "Once Upon a Time in Shaolin," the original "Doge" meme image, and Edward Snowden's "Stay Free" NFT. The organization pioneers fractionalized, on-chain ownership of art and cultural artifacts. PleasrDAO operates as a community-governed collective rather than a conventional software or API company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Plenty
providers.description: Plenty is an American indoor vertical farming company that grows produce such as leafy greens and strawberries in controlled, climate-independent indoor facilities using proprietary vertical growing systems, automation, and robotics. Headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area and founded in 2014, Plenty is backed by investors including SoftBank Vision Fund and DCM Ventures. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a frontier-tech portfolio-company profile; the public enrichment pass found no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Plerk
providers.description: Plerk was a Mexican fintech startup offering an employee-benefits and perks platform ("beneficios para colaboradores") for companies in Mexico, backed by 500 Global. During 2023 Plerk merged with minu to consolidate the employee benefits offering in Mexico, and the standalone Plerk product was wound down. Its primary domain plerk.com no longer resolves (DNS fully lapsed; last web archive May 2023) and plerk.io redirects to the now-defunct plerk.com. Support was handled at soporte@plerk.io. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired lead; the surviving product and any API surface live under minu. No live developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists for Plerk.

providers.name: Plexistor
providers.description: Plexistor was an enterprise storage startup that built Software-Defined Memory (SDM) - a converged memory-and-storage architecture delivering ultra-low latency and millions of IOPS on commodity servers by tiering across DRAM, NVDIMM-N, Intel/Micron 3D XPoint, flash, and spinning disk. It positioned SDM as a persistent-memory storage layer for big-data workloads such as Cassandra, Couchbase, and Spark, adding enterprise features like snapshots, clones, high availability, and clustering. The company was acquired by NetApp in 2017 and its technology was folded into NetApp's memory/storage roadmap. The plexistor.com site survives as a static legacy marketing page with no active product download, API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the honest result is that Plexistor exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: Plexxi *
providers.description: Plexxi was a software-defined networking (SDN) startup building data-center fabric and network orchestration, backed by GV and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and folded into the Aruba Networks / HPE data-center portfolio; plexxi.com now 301-redirects to arubanetworks.com. As of this enrichment pass Plexxi has no independent, live developer surface: no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, SDKs, or other API artifacts remain reachable. This record is retained for network lineage and its venture-portfolio provenance rather than any active API.

providers.name: Pliant Technology
providers.description: Pliant Technology, Inc. was a data-center storage company that pioneered the introduction of high-performance enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs) into mission-critical data-center environments. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by SanDisk in 2011 and its product line was folded into SanDisk's enterprise storage solutions. The company operated as a hardware/semiconductor storage vendor and published no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer surface; its former domain now redirects to SanDisk. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Pluto Mobility

providers.name: Pointy
providers.description: Pointy was an Irish retail-technology startup (pointy.com), founded by Mark Cummins and Charles Bibby and backed by Seedcamp, that helped independent brick-and-mortar retailers put their in-store inventory online by connecting a simple barcode-scanning device or point-of-sale integration to a searchable online product page. Google acquired Pointy in 2020 and has since fully folded the product into Google's own tooling: pointy.com now redirects to Google Business Profile support, and the former Pointy app is now Google's Local Inventory app, which syncs in-store products to Google Search and Maps via POS systems such as Clover, Square, and Lightspeed. Pointy no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this API Evangelist profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record and historical marker rather than an active API provider.

It surfaces in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. The firm publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security posture only.

providers.name: Polyvore
providers.description: Polyvore was a community-powered fashion and lifestyle social-commerce website where members created and shared outfit "sets" by clipping product images into collages. Founded in 2007 and backed by Matrix Partners, it was acquired by Yahoo in 2015 (~$200M), passed to Verizon/Oath, and its assets were acquired by Canadian e-commerce retailer SSENSE in April 2018, which shut the site down immediately. The polyvore.com domain now 301-redirects to ssense.com; there is no live product, developer portal, or public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Pomelo fashion
providers.description: Pomelo Fashion is an omnichannel fashion retailer headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand, selling women's apparel and accessories across Southeast Asia through its website and mobile app. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront (pomelofashion.com, served via CloudFront) but exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface (all probed paths returned HTTP 405). This profile therefore carries only probed domain-security signal; it remains a lead for revisiting should a developer program launch.

providers.name: Pond5
providers.description: Pond5 is a royalty-free stock media marketplace where creators buy and sell video footage, music tracks, sound effects, motion graphics, images, and other digital assets. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this profile has been through a local enrichment pass: the public web presence sits behind DataDome bot protection with no discoverable public API, developer portal, SDKs, OpenAPI, or security.txt at the time of the pass. Only live DNS/TLS/HTTP domain-security posture could be probed. Sector: media.

providers.name: Pop Mart
providers.description: Pop Mart International Group is a Chinese pop-culture and designer-toy company best known for its blind-box collectibles and character IP such as Labubu (The Monsters), Molly, Skullpanda and Dimoo. Headquartered in Beijing and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, it operates retail stores, robot-shop vending machines, and a consumer e-commerce presence across China and international markets. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (HongShan/Sequoia China). Consumer sector; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment (no developer portal, /.well-known documents, or llms.txt).

providers.name: Pop Up Archive
providers.description: Pop Up Archive was a startup that provided audio and podcast transcription, speech-to-text, and searchable spoken-word archiving tools, making audio content discoverable and machine-readable. It was acquired by Apple in 2017 and its independent products, developer surface, and popuparchive.com domain were retired. The domain now resolves to Apple nameservers with no active host, so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API to enrich. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Bloomberg Beta and is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record; no live API surface remains.

providers.name: Pop-Up Magazine
providers.description: Pop-Up Magazine is a live magazine created for a stage, a screen, and a live audience, produced by the team behind The California Sunday Magazine. Each production combines original nonfiction storytelling, live music, illustration, animation, and photography performed on tour in theaters across the United States. The company also operates Pop-Up Magazine Brand Studio, producing custom live and multimedia storytelling for brand partners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Pop-Up Magazine is a consumer media and live-events brand; it publishes a public promotional website but exposes no developer program, public API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface, so this profile is identity- and security-posture-only.

providers.name: Populr.me
providers.description: Populr.me was a self-service website builder that let users create and host single-page personal and marketing pages on free and paid subscription tiers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found the consumer service permanently shut down on June 1, 2023 (users directed to Wix, Weebly, Squarespace, GoDaddy) and no public API, developer program, documentation, or event surface remains — only a static shutdown page on the domain.

providers.name: Portal Software
providers.description: Portal Software was an Accel-backed billing and revenue-management software company whose portal.com domain now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to Oracle WebCenter Portal, indicating the business and its assets have been absorbed into Oracle. It was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, but the enrichment pass finds no independent developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or published security program under portal.com — the domain serves only an Oracle marketing redirect, so there is no standalone API surface to enrich beyond the domain-level TLS/DNS security probe.

providers.name: Portal Terreno
providers.description: Portal Terreno is an online marketplace for land and parcels ("terrenos" and "parcelas") in Latin America, operating localized classifieds portals for Chile (portalterreno.cl) and Mexico (portalterreno.com.mx) with tens of thousands of land listings. The Next.js web platform lets buyers search, filter, and contact sellers to find land for sale, while sellers and real-estate agents publish listings. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer, API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found during the enrichment pass; the domain-security posture was probed live.

providers.name: Portals
providers.description: Portals (theportal.to) is a consumer platform organized around three activities — play, collect, and create — surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a Greylock portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the public site is a single-page consumer application: no published developer API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, documentation, or /.well-known discovery documents were found. The only machine-verifiable surface is the web domain itself (HTTPS with TLS 1.3, HSTS, SPF, and DMARC present). This profile will be upgraded if and when a public API surface appears.

providers.name: Portals
providers.description: Portals (theportal.to) is a browser-based, Web3 metaverse and social gaming platform where users can play, collect, and create in a connected universe of interoperable virtual worlds. Players embark on quests, collect rare loot and digital collectibles, and build their own spaces, all directly in the browser without a download. Built on the Solana blockchain, Portals is a consumer-facing metaverse experience backed by Multicoin Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as of this enrichment pass Portals publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this remains a company/identity profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Pose
providers.description: Pose (pose.vn) is a Vietnamese entertainment and lifestyle media publication based in Ho Chi Minh City, covering celebrity news, beauty pageants (including Miss Universe Vietnam), fashion, beauty, health, and film and television. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a company stub. As of this enrichment pass the site is a consumer-facing content publication monetized through advertising and sponsored content, with no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: POSIX
providers.description: POSIX (Portable Operating System Interface) is a family of IEEE and Open Group standards that define a consistent operating system API, command line shell, and utility interfaces for maintaining compatibility between Unix and Unix-like systems. It is a specification rather than a network API, and there is no public REST or HTTP interface for the standard.

providers.name: Post.news
providers.description: Post.news was a social-news and microblogging platform positioned as a Twitter/X alternative, backed by a16z and founded by former Waze CEO Noam Bardin. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company has no discoverable public API surface, developer program, or documentation, and the consumer web property appears to be offline (see x-website-status). This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Postini
providers.description: Postini was an email security and message-management company founded in 1999, providing hosted spam and virus filtering, email archiving, encryption, and web security for businesses. Google acquired Postini in 2007 (roughly $625M) and folded its capabilities into Google Apps (now Google Workspace); the standalone Postini service was discontinued and customers were transitioned to Google Apps by around 2012. The postini.com domain is now Google-owned and redirects to google.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; the company has no live, standalone API surface, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Power Lattice
providers.description: Power Lattice (Powerlattice) is a semiconductor and power-management startup building power delivery solutions for AI accelerators and GPUs. Its core product is an industry-first power delivery chiplet that integrates voltage regulation directly into the processor package, addressing the data-center "power wall" as AI chips push past 2,000 watts. The Rainier micro-IVR architecture combines miniaturized on-die magnetic inductors, advanced control-circuit innovations, a vertical design, and a programmable software layer to deliver 50%+ power reduction, 2-3X performance-per-watt gains, and extended system lifetime. Backed by Playground Global, the company raised $25M to break the AI power wall. This is a hardware company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: PPG Industries
providers.description: PPG Industries is a Fortune 500 global supplier of paints, coatings, and specialty materials serving customers in construction, consumer products, industrial, transportation markets, and aftermarkets. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with PPG Industries. As of the last review, no public APIs or developer portal have been identified.

providers.name: PPS (pps.tv)
providers.description: PPS (pps.tv), originally the PPStream peer-to-peer online-video client, is a Chinese internet-video brand backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The pps.tv domain now issues a permanent HTTP 301 redirect to suike.cn, the home of iQIYI Suike (爱奇艺随刻) — a video-sharing and short-video community operated by iQIYI. It is a consumer video product; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface, so there is no API artifact set to harvest for this profile.

providers.name: Pratt & Whitney
providers.description: A major American aerospace manufacturer designing, manufacturing, and servicing aircraft engines for commercial, military, and business aviation applications. A division of RTX Corporation (formerly Raytheon Technologies), Pratt & Whitney is known for its geared turbofan (GTF) engine technology (PW1000G family) powering the Airbus A220 and A320neo, the F135 powering the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter, and the PT6 turboprop family. Customer-facing digital services - EngineWise health monitoring, FAST (Full-flight data Acquisition Storage and Transmission), and the Customer Portal - are operated privately for airline, MRO, and military customers behind credentialed access and are not exposed as a public developer API or open partner integration portal.

providers.name: Precidian Investments
providers.description: Precidian Investments is an industry leader in the creation of innovative financial products, specializing in exchange-traded fund (ETF) and mutual fund development. The firm is best known for ActiveShares, its patented non-transparent actively managed ETF structure, and licenses its proprietary processes, technologies, and structures to financial institutions or acts as sponsor for products. Its expertise spans product development, trading, clearance, sales, technology, and securities law. Precidian operates as a business-to-business partner to asset managers and ETF providers and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Precision Castparts
providers.description: Precision Castparts Corp. is a worldwide manufacturer of complex metal components and products including investment castings, forgings, and fasteners and structurals for aerospace and industrial gas turbine markets. The company is owned by Berkshire Hathaway.

providers.name: Prelay
providers.description: Prelay is a deal collaboration ("team selling") platform that helps B2B revenue teams coordinate the internal stakeholders behind complex enterprise deals — sales engineers, legal, deal desk, finance, and leadership — inside a shared workspace that plugs into the CRM. It is a SaaS application aimed at sales and revenue operations, not a developer/API product: as of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or developer subdomains (api./developers./docs.) were found. Prelay was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Prevalent
providers.description: Prevalent is a third-party risk management (TPRM) software vendor whose platform automates vendor risk assessment, continuous monitoring, and compliance workflows across the third-party lifecycle. Surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment (sector: cybersecurity). Prevalent has since been acquired by Mitratech; www.prevalent.net now redirects to mitratech.com/products/prevalent/. Enrichment found no public developer portal, REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or webhook surface — the only documented integration is a DocuSign connector inside the Contract Essentials module.

providers.name: PriceBaba
providers.description: PriceBaba is an India-based consumer price-comparison and gadget research platform, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Mumbai. It helps shoppers compare mobile phones, consumer electronics and other gadgets by aggregating specifications, expert and user reviews, and prices across online and offline local retail stores, so buyers can find the best available deal near them. PriceBaba is backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups). No public developer program or API surface was discoverable during this enrichment pass. The website is served behind Cloudflare and blocks automated access, and no api.pricebaba.com host resolves.

providers.name: Primary Data
providers.description: Primary Data was a software-defined storage and data-virtualization startup best known for its DataSphere platform, a metadata engine that abstracted files across heterogeneous storage tiers (flash, disk, cloud) behind a single global namespace and moved data automatically by policy. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors, the company ceased operations in 2017, with much of its team and technology continuing at Hammerspace. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass the company is defunct and primarydata.com is a parked domain (GoDaddy lander), so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: PrimaryBid
providers.description: PrimaryBid was a UK-based fintech that gave retail investors access to public capital markets — IPOs, follow-on equity raises, and public offerings that were historically restricted to institutional investors. It partnered with exchanges, banks, and issuers to broadcast live capital-raising events to individual investors, powering retail participation in listings such as Deliveroo, PensionBee, and Soho House. PrimaryBid's technology was acquired by SoFi Technologies, Inc. in May 2026; the standalone consumer platform has been wound down and its public website now redirects former shareholders to third-party share registrars. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Primavera Systems
providers.description: Primavera Systems, Inc. was a project-management and project-portfolio-management software company best known for the Primavera P6 scheduling platform used in construction, engineering, and capital-projects industries. It was acquired by Oracle Corporation in 2008 and folded into Oracle's Construction and Engineering business, where the products live on as Oracle Primavera. As an independent company it no longer exists, its primavera.com domain now redirects to oracle.com/primavera, and it publishes no independent public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation of its own. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead, but that association does not match the acquired-by-Oracle entity and appears to be a name-matching artifact.

providers.name: Prism Skylabs
providers.description: Prism Skylabs was a cloud-based visual monitoring and video analytics company that turned surveillance and IP-camera feeds from physical retail and commercial spaces into searchable, time-lapse imagery and business intelligence. Backed by a16z and Draper Nexus, it was acquired by Cisco in 2016 and folded into the Cisco Meraki smart-camera (MV) computer-vision line; the standalone company is defunct. The prismskylabs.com domain now 301-redirects to prism.com, an unrelated domain-licensing/holding page, and no live Prism Skylabs developer portal, API documentation, or API specifications exist to enrich. This profile is retained as an a16z portfolio identity record.

providers.name: Prismlab
providers.description: Prismlab (Shanghai Prismlab Technology / 上海普利生) is an industrial-grade 3D printing equipment provider founded in Shanghai, China, and a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company develops high-precision additive manufacturing systems built on its proprietary SMS (Scan-Mode Slicing / sub-pixel micro-scanning) photocuring technology, including the Rapid 600 and Rapid 400 industrial printer series, the SP high-accuracy series, and MP micro-nano printers for research. Its systems serve dental and orthodontics (clear aligners, dentures), precision medical devices, jewelry, education and research, electronics, and mold/prototype manufacturing. As a B2B hardware manufacturer, Prismlab publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Privalia
providers.description: Privalia is a members-only online outlet and flash-sales retailer offering time-limited private sales on fashion, footwear, accessories, sportswear, and home goods from major brands at discounts of up to 70 percent. Operating consumer storefronts across Spain, Italy, Mexico, and Brazil (es/it/mex/br.privalia.com), Privalia is part of the Veepee (vente-privee) group and was an early Insight Partners portfolio company. It runs as a business-to-consumer e-commerce brand and publishes no public developer or API program.

providers.name: Privitar
providers.description: Privitar was a UK-founded data privacy and data provisioning company known for its Data Privacy Platform, which applied de-identification, anonymization, tokenization and policy-based data access controls to sensitive data at scale for enterprises in financial services, healthcare and government. Privitar was acquired by Informatica in 2023 and folded into Informatica's data governance and privacy portfolio. As of this enrichment pass the privitar.com domain (and docs.privitar.com) permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to informatica.com, and no independent Privitar developer portal, API documentation, or API surface remains online. This profile is retained as a network lead record for the former company; live API artifacts now belong to Informatica.

providers.name: prmeasure
providers.description: prmeasure (Precision Measurement & Control, 精实测控) is a Zhuhai, China based high-tech enterprise specializing in measurement, control, and artificial intelligence technologies for flexible manufacturing. The company builds industrial-grade testing and control equipment for the consumer electronics, automotive, and home-appliance industries, and offers consumer-level customized production through a C2M (customer-to-manufacturer) model. Its WowNow platform (iwownow.com) provides creative prototyping tools and flexible manufacturing equipment for individuals. prmeasure was surfaced as a portfolio company of the Qiming Venture Partners investment graph and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate marketing website only, with no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Process Sensing Technologies
providers.description: Process Sensing Technologies (PST) is a measurement instrumentation group that designs and manufactures precision sensors and analyzers for moisture, humidity, dew point, oxygen, and trace gas measurement across industrial, pharmaceutical, food, and life-science applications. Its brand portfolio includes Michell Instruments, Rotronic, Analytical Industries, Ntron, SensoScientific, and Isensix, spanning process gas analysis and real-time environmental monitoring. The company now operates under the DwyerOmega brand following its combination with Dwyer Instruments. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; probing of its public web surface found hardware, software downloads, calibration tooling, and monitoring platforms but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Prodigy Software
providers.description: Prodigy Software was a San Francisco-based provider of cloud-based automotive retail software, offering a SaaS digital-retailing platform that let car dealerships move the sales process online (web-store services, deal structuring, and financing workflows). Founded in 2015 by Marty Hu and Michia Rohrssen, it raised seed funding from Battery Ventures, SV Angel, 8VC, and CrunchFund, and was acquired by Upstart Holdings in March 2021. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its former domain is parked.

providers.name: Product Backlog
providers.description: A product backlog is a prioritized list of features, enhancements, and fixes that serves as the single source of requirements for product development. It is most commonly used in Agile and Scrum methodologies, where the product owner is responsible for ordering items based on business value, customer feedback, dependencies, and technical considerations. The backlog evolves continuously as new requirements emerge and priorities shift, providing development teams with a clear, ordered view of upcoming work.

providers.name: Product Backlog Items
providers.description: Product backlog items (PBIs) are the individual units of work that make up a product backlog, representing features, enhancements, bug fixes, and technical tasks in Agile and Scrum methodologies. Each PBI typically includes a description, acceptance criteria, priority, and an estimate of effort. PBIs are continuously refined through grooming and refinement sessions, and the highest-priority items are pulled into sprints by development teams to be implemented and delivered as increments of working software.

providers.name: Project Management Methodology
providers.description: A systematic approach or framework for planning, executing, and controlling projects to achieve specific goals within defined constraints of time, budget, and resources. It helps teams plan, execute, and deliver projects on time and within scope through structured methodologies.

providers.name: Prologue
providers.description: Prologue (Prologue AI) is a multimodal creative operating system that lets teams create, edit, and organize AI-generated images, video, audio, and text in a single workspace. Powered by "Prologue Intent" and a best-in-class catalog of third-party generative models, it targets professional creative workflows for agencies and brands ("crafted, not generated"). It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was discoverable — the product site is a consumer/pro web application behind bot protection.

providers.name: Propagate
providers.description: Propagate (Propagate Brands) is an e-commerce accelerator and equity syndication platform founded by JD Jernigan and backed by 500 Global. It partners with early-stage direct-to-consumer brands selling on Shopify and Amazon — typically those under $1M in annual revenue and overlooked by larger aggregators — providing working capital plus growth marketing, branding, data collection, customer service, and supply-chain support to help them scale and reach acquisition-ready exits. It simultaneously lets individual investors take equity stakes in these growing private commerce brands to earn passive income. Propagate operates as a services-and-investment business rather than a software company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical platform surface.

providers.name: Prospera
providers.description: Prospera Technologies was an Israeli agricultural-technology company, founded in 2014 and headquartered in Tel Aviv with US offices in Austin, TX, that applied machine learning and computer vision to continuously monitor plant development, health and stress from crop-field imagery and deliver irrigation and crop-growth recommendations to growers through mobile and web dashboards. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Cisco and Qualcomm, Prospera was acquired by Valmont Industries for roughly $300M in 2021 and its technology was folded into Valmont's Valley Insights and the Valley 365 connected crop-management platform. Prospera no longer operates an independent public developer surface: the prospera.ag domain still resolves in DNS but its HTTPS endpoint is unreachable, and no public API, developer portal, or API documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Protent
providers.description: Protent is a San Francisco based Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building a real-time video intelligence platform for law enforcement and public safety teams. Its software monitors many live surveillance, CCTV, and bodycam feeds at once, automatically prioritizing critical streams when escalation or volatility is detected, and lets teams run natural-language searches across active feeds (for example, "a person in a red hoodie with a backpack"). Founded in 2025 by Srihan Balaji (ex-Lockheed Martin Research, AWS) and Abhisheik Sharma (CTO, NLP/sentiment analysis), the company works with police departments in the Atlanta, Chicago, and St. Louis metro areas. As of this profile, Protent publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Proterra
providers.description: Proterra is a US-based manufacturer of high-energy lithium-ion battery systems for electric vehicles and commercial equipment, including transit buses, trucks, and off-highway EVs, with charging and fleet solutions. Originally an electric transit bus and powertrain manufacturer founded in 2004, the battery-systems business (Powered by Proterra) continues under the proterra.com domain following the 2023 restructuring. It is a physical hardware and energy-storage company backed by Obvious Ventures under its planetary-health thesis, and publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Pseudolithic
providers.description: PseudolithIC is a semiconductor company specializing in heterogeneous integration technology for cost-effective, high-performance silicon RFICs (radio frequency integrated circuits). The company combines compound semiconductor chiplets with large-diameter, low-cost silicon wafers to deliver mm-wave power amplifiers, low-noise amplifiers, and transmit/receive (T/R) front-end modules for RF and wireless applications. PseudolithIC is a hardware/chipset manufacturer targeting the RF and semiconductor industries; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or programmatic surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PulteGroup
providers.description: PulteGroup is one of America's largest homebuilding companies, building homes under the Centex, Pulte Homes, Del Webb, DiVosta Homes, John Wieland Homes, and American West brands. No public developer APIs have been identified at this time; this index tracks the company's public web properties.

providers.name: Punchd
providers.description: Punchd was a mobile customer-loyalty rewards application for small businesses, founded in 2009 at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo by Reed Morse and Grantland Chew, that let merchants run digital punch-card loyalty programs. Google acquired the company in June 2011 and retired the product in June 2013, folding features into other Google products. The getpunchd.com domain now serves only a static Google-hosted closure announcement. The company is defunct with no active product, developer program, or public API surface; this profile is retained for network completeness as a historical record.

providers.name: Pure Networks
providers.description: Pure Networks is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners, mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: PurismEV Inc.
providers.description: PurismEV Inc. is an AI-driven electric-vehicle energy optimization platform that processes real-time vehicle data to help fleets, OEMs, leasing companies, and operators reduce energy consumption, extend battery lifespan, and lower operating costs. Its products include Smart Throttle Control technology (range extension), Battery-Aware Smart Charging, a Smart Mobility energy management system (EMS), and a Fleet Management Dashboard for real-time monitoring across cars, delivery trucks, forklifts, scooters, and drones. PurismEV is backed by 500 Global. The company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Puyo Nexus
providers.description: Puyo Puyo information from Puyo Nexus Wiki

providers.name: PwC
providers.description: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is one of the Big Four professional services firms providing audit and assurance, tax, and management consulting services globally. PwC operates as a network of member firms across approximately 150 countries with hundreds of thousands of professionals. Service lines include audit, deals and transactions, tax compliance and advisory, risk assurance, cybersecurity and privacy, ESG and sustainability assurance, workforce transformation, and digital/technology consulting (cloud, data, AI, ERP). PwC publishes thought-leadership content and operates client portals for engagement delivery and document exchange, but it does not publish a public developer API or open partner integration portal at the corporate level - client connectivity is bilateral and project-scoped rather than offered as a self-serve API product.

providers.name: Qapa
providers.description: Qapa (qapa.fr) is a Paris-based French online recruitment and temporary-work (interim) marketplace that matched companies with job seekers for permanent and temp placements. Backed by Index Ventures and Partech, it was majority-acquired by the Adecco Group. The qapa.fr web property is now gated behind an Azure Application Gateway (HTTP 403) and exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface; this profile is retained as an API Evangelist network record.

providers.name: Qerja
providers.description: PT Qerja Manfaat Bangsa (Qerja) is an Indonesian human-resources company operating an end-to-end HR product ecosystem for employers, established in 2007 and later part of the PT M Cash Integrasi Tbk technology group. In 2019 it acquired Karir.com, Indonesia's first job portal (since 1998), and reports serving over 50,000 clients and 8 million member users across the country. The public presence is a corporate marketing site (qerjagroup.com) covering its HR services, clients, and user demographics; no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: QikPod
providers.description: QikPod was an Accel-backed Indian startup that built an automated parcel locker network for last-mile e-commerce delivery, letting shoppers collect and return packages from unattended smart lockers placed in apartments, offices, and retail locations. The company has since rebranded and pivoted to Leapmile Robotics, a nano-warehouse automation and intelligent fulfillment platform that uses robotics to handle storage, retrieval, picking, auditing, and dispatch inside compact autonomous warehouse facilities. The legacy qikpod.com domain now redirects to leapmile.com/qikpod. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead; no public developer API surface has been found for either the QikPod or Leapmile properties.

providers.name: QLC
providers.description: QLC is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Its listed website resolves to NewCampus (newcampus.com), an education and financial operator that supports organizations across the innovation lifecycle — from early-stage incubation and acceleration through grants and treasury operations to leadership training, governance design, and operating-model consulting. Notable programs include the Open Campus Accelerator (OC-X) and the seachange HR and Web3 tracks. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, MCP server, or machine-readable specification — there is no developer surface to catalog beyond the corporate marketing site.

providers.name: QoS
providers.description: Quality of Service (QoS) is the description or measurement of overall performance of a service, particularly in computer networking and telecommunications. QoS encompasses traffic prioritization, packet loss management, latency control, and bandwidth allocation to ensure reliable performance for applications such as VoIP, video streaming, and real-time systems.

providers.name: QOSMIC
providers.description: QOSMIC builds optical ground station infrastructure, a frontier-tech play backed by prosus-ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network. Its public presence (qosmic.space) is a single-page marketing site with no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable surface at the time of enrichment. This profile captures the company identity and probed domain security posture; it remains a lead awaiting a public API before deeper artifact enrichment.

providers.name: Quantum
providers.description: Quantum is a Saudi Arabian advertising-technology (adtech) enabler that bridges online publishers and advertisers with data and technology. Its Quantum One omnichannel platform connects online and offline retail experiences across programmatic ads, in-app media buying, e-sampling, on-ground activations, influencer marketing, and out-of-home media, with goal-attainment tracking, ROI measurement, customer-engagement analytics, and conversion-rate analysis. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Quantum Effect Dev
providers.description: Quantum Effect Devices (QED, originally Quantum Effect Design) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1991 by former MIPS Computer Systems managers Tom Riordan, Earl Killian, and Ray Kunita. QED designed MIPS-based 32- and 64-bit embedded RISC microprocessors (the RM5200 and RM7000 families) for networking and communications systems including routers, switches, and optical transport equipment. The company completed an IPO in 2000 and was acquired the same year by PMC-Sierra for approximately $2.3 billion. It has no independent operations, developer platform, or API surface today; the former corporate site (qedinc.com) is defunct. This record was surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company and is retained as a historical/no-API-surface entry.

providers.name: Quantum Motion
providers.description: Quantum Motion is a UK-based full-stack quantum computing company building scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers using silicon (CMOS) technology, the same manufacturing process used for conventional microchips. Spun out of University College London and the University of Oxford, the company develops qubit control hardware, cryogenic electronics, and quantum architecture aimed at manufacturing quantum processors at scale. It is a research- and hardware-focused company rather than an API or developer-platform provider; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface could be verified (the corporate site sits behind bot-challenge protection and web search was unavailable), so the profile remains identity-only.

providers.name: QuBit
providers.description: QuBit was a London-based ecommerce personalization and product-discovery platform — customer-experience optimization, recommendations, A/B testing, and behavioral big-data analytics — backed by Accel, Balderton Capital, and Sapphire Ventures. QuBit was acquired by Coveo in 2021 and fully absorbed into the Coveo Merchandising Hub. The qubit.com domain, its developer docs (docs.qubit.com), and every API and /.well-known/ endpoint now redirect to coveo.com and docs.coveo.com, so QuBit no longer operates an independent public API surface.

providers.name: Quickoffice
providers.description: Quickoffice was a mobile office productivity suite (document, spreadsheet, and presentation editing for iOS, Android, and Symbian) that was acquired by Google in June 2012, folded into Google Docs / Google Drive, and formally discontinued in 2014. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 confirmed there is no independent Quickoffice API surface. The quickoffice.com domain now resolves to Google infrastructure and www.quickoffice.com 301-redirects to google.com/docs/about/, developer.quickoffice.com does not resolve (NXDOMAIN), and no developer portal, documentation, or API remains. The product capabilities live on inside Google Workspace (Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides).

providers.name: Quirky
providers.description: Quirky was a crowdsourced consumer-product invention platform (founded by Ben Kaufman) that let inventors submit ideas the community helped design, manufacture and sell; it was backed by a16z among others. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2015. As of this enrichment pass the quirky.com domain is a parked "domain name is for sale" page with no operating product, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained as a defunct a16z portfolio-company lead; no API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Qumranet
providers.description: Qumranet was an Israeli software company that developed the Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) hypervisor and the SPICE remote-desktop protocol, along with the SolidICE virtual desktop infrastructure product. It was acquired by Red Hat in September 2008, after which its technologies were folded into Red Hat's virtualization portfolio (Red Hat Enterprise Virtualization / RHEV) and contributed upstream to the Linux kernel and open-source communities. Qumranet no longer exists as an independent company: the qumranet.com domain now issues a permanent (301) redirect to Red Hat's enterprise virtualization page, and there is no independent Qumranet developer program, API surface, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Qunar Com
providers.description: Qunar (去哪儿网, "where to go") is a Chinese online travel platform founded in 2005 and headquartered in Beijing. It operates a travel search and booking service covering domestic and international flight tickets, hotel reservations, train and bus tickets, vacation packages, and travel deals. Qunar was NASDAQ-listed (QUNR) and is majority owned by Trip.com Group (formerly Ctrip). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; no public developer portal or API program was discoverable at open.qunar.com, developer.qunar.com, or api.qunar.com during this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Quotable Quotes
providers.description: Quotable is a free, open source quotations API

providers.name: Quran-api
providers.description: Free Quran API Service with 90+ different languages and 400+ translations

providers.name: RACI
providers.description: A responsibility assignment matrix that defines roles and responsibilities using four key designations - Responsible (those who do the work), Accountable (the ultimate decision maker), Consulted (those whose input is needed), and Informed (those who need to be kept updated). RACI matrices help clarify ownership, reduce confusion, and improve project coordination by mapping stakeholders to specific tasks or deliverables.

providers.name: Radiant Entertainment
providers.description: Radiant Entertainment was an independent video game studio co-founded by brothers Tom and Tony Cannon, who also created the Evolution Championship Series (EVO), the premier fighting-game tournament. The studio was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and is known for the free-to-play fighting game Rising Thunder and the voxel city-building title Stonehearth. Radiant Entertainment was acquired by Riot Games in 2016 and its team was folded into Riot; the studio no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Radionomy (Azerion)
providers.description: Radionomy (Azerion) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ai-apps. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Raised
providers.description: Raised (joinraised.com) is an AI-powered recruiting platform founded in 2022 and backed by 500 Global. It delivers vetted candidates to venture-backed startups — particularly in AI, deep tech, and Web3 — at a fraction of the cost and time of traditional recruitment agencies, using proprietary AI to match candidates to roles. The company is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, and operates as a software-enabled alternative to traditional staffing firms. Raised publishes a marketing website only; no public developer API, documentation, or developer platform surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Ralph Lauren Corporation
providers.description: Ralph Lauren Corporation (NYSE: RL) is a global premium-lifestyle company founded by Ralph Lauren in 1967 and headquartered in New York City. The company designs, markets, and distributes apparel, accessories, home, and fragrances across a portfolio of brands including Polo Ralph Lauren, Ralph Lauren Collection, Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Double RL (RRL), Lauren Ralph Lauren, and Chaps, along with Polo Golf, RLX, Pink Pony, Ralph Lauren Home and Paint, Ralph Lauren Watches and Fine Jewelry, and Ralph Lauren Restaurants. Direct-to-consumer commerce runs on Adobe Commerce, and category-extension brands are operated through licensing partners (eyewear via Luxottica, fragrances via L'Oréal). The corporation operates retail stores in dozens of countries with no publicly documented developer APIs, partner program portal, affiliate API, or open OpenAPI/Postman/GraphQL surface as of the profiling date.

providers.name: Raphe Mphibr
providers.description: Raphe mPhibr is an Indian deep-tech aerospace company revolutionizing unmanned aviation through in-house carbon fiber composites, UAV airframes, propulsion, and end-to-end manufacturing. The company designs and builds heavy-lift and tactical unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs/drones) for defense and industrial applications, emphasizing research-driven innovation and vertically integrated production. Raphe mPhibr is a B2B / defense-oriented manufacturer surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface — its digital presence is a corporate marketing site only.

providers.name: Rapportive
providers.description: Rapportive was a browser extension that added a contact-intelligence sidebar to Gmail, surfacing a person's name, photo, job, and social profiles alongside their email. Founded in 2011 and backed by 500 Global (then 500 Startups), it was acquired by LinkedIn in 2012 and later folded into LinkedIn Sales Navigator. The rapportive.com domain now 301-redirects to LinkedIn's "Sales Navigator for Gmail" feature page. Rapportive published no standalone developer API and operates no independent developer surface today; this profile records that defunct/absorbed status for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rapsphere
providers.description: RAPsphere was a mobile IT company that developed mobile information management solutions enabling CIOs to contend with BYOD (bring-your-own-device) in the enterprise and the critical need to protect corporate applications and data on mobile devices. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by AppSense in May 2012 and no longer operates as an independent entity. Its former domain (rapsphere.com) is now a parked / for-sale domain and there is no live developer surface, public API, documentation, or reachable web presence to enrich. This profile is retained as a portfolio-history lead and is not an active API provider.

providers.name: RareLee
providers.description: RareLee (Rarelee) is a Seoul-based premium personal style consulting company founded in 2017, offering data-driven hair, makeup, and fashion analysis. Its consultants classify a client's face shape, features, and skeletal structure across millions of type combinations to recommend personalized hairstyles, makeup designs, and coordinated outfits, both online and in person. Rarelee serves celebrity clientele and has collaborated with brands such as Shinsegae and Marriott. It is a direct-to-consumer service with no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead for enrichment.

providers.name: Rascal Games
providers.description: Rascal Games is a game development studio founded by Rick and Jon, both experienced entrepreneurs previously at Blitz.gg and Discord. The studio is building "Project Wayward," a group-based PvE action-adventure game inspired by Sea of Thieves, Valheim, and Fortnite, with an emphasis on cooperative multiplayer experiences. Rascal Games raised a Series Seed round backed by a16z SPEEDRUN and industry veterans including Mitch Lasky. As a pre-launch game studio, Rascal Games publishes a marketing and careers site but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; the enrichment pass confirms there is currently no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Rasyonet
providers.description: Rasyonet is a Turkish fintech company providing integrated financial software solutions and capital markets data platforms for institutional clients, asset managers, and financial analysts. Founded in 2000 and headquartered at ITU ARI Teknopark in Istanbul, Rasyonet offers tools for analyzing global equity markets, economic indicators, mutual and pension funds, fixed-income securities, portfolio analytics, and automated financial reporting. Their flagship EquityRT platform delivers equity research, company valuation, and peer benchmarking capabilities via desktop and Excel integration. No public developer API or machine-readable specification has been documented at this time.

providers.name: Raw Apothecary
providers.description: Raw Apothecary is a Mexico-based consumer brand that operated a Shopify storefront at rawapothecary.mx (Spanish-language, powered-by Shopify), surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the storefront returns "Tienda no disponible" (HTTP 402, "Store Unavailable"), and the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification surface. This profile is retained as a company record; there is no API to enrich beyond a live domain-security probe of the storefront host.

providers.name: Rawsome Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Rawsome Pte. Ltd. (trading as Rawsome Asia Beverages) is a Singapore-based producer and distributor of small-batch, handcrafted raw kombucha sold under the Wild Boocha brand. The company brews fermented tea beverages -- including Citrus Green, Strawberry Mint, and Harmony Adaptogenic flavors -- available in one-liter bottles and refillable mini kegs, and markets them as a functional wellness drink rich in probiotics, polyphenols, B vitamins, vitamin C, organic enzymes, and amino acids. Rawsome operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront (built on Odoo) and was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile currently has no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; it is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.description: Standard repository documentation file providing project overview, setup instructions, and usage examples. Automatically displayed on repository landing pages by GitHub, GitLab, and other hosting platforms.
