providers.description: Websocket API to access realtime stock data

providers.name: Reality Reflection
providers.description: Reality Reflection is a technology studio, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, whose website (realityreflection.com) is currently "under recovery" and points to two active projects, MOSS LAND (moss.land, which describes itself as "Infrastructure for the AI Civilization") and ROCKET.RUN (rocket.run). An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK, .well-known metadata, llms.txt, or security program for the company; the only machine-verifiable surface is the domain's live TLS/DNS security posture.

providers.name: Realy
providers.description: Realy is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto-web3. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Rebookify
providers.description: Rebookify is a travel-technology company that helps travel agencies and travel management companies save money on hotel bookings by continuously monitoring the price of existing hotel reservations and automatically rebooking them at lower rates whenever prices drop, capturing the savings without changing the guest's stay. Backed by 500 Global, Rebookify operates a business-facing web product at rebookify.com. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface has been identified.

providers.name: Rec Room
providers.description: Rec Room is a cross-platform social gaming and user-generated-content platform where players hang out, play, and build their own rooms and games using in-app creation tools (Rec Room Studio and the visual Circuits scripting system). It runs on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Meta Quest VR, iOS, and Android with a shared avatar and economy. Founded in 2016 (originally as Against Gravity) and headquartered in Seattle, the company is backed by Index Ventures among other investors. Rec Room publishes a consumer platform at rec.net; no official public developer API or documented developer program was found during enrichment (the site is served behind Cloudflare and an internal api.rec.net host exists but is undocumented/unofficial).

providers.name: Recommind
providers.description: Recommind was an enterprise information analytics and eDiscovery software company founded in 2000, best known for its CORE predictive-analytics platform and its Axcelerate eDiscovery and information-governance products used by legal and enterprise customers. OpenText acquired Recommind in 2016, and the Recommind brand and its technology are now folded into OpenText's Discovery and information-management portfolio. The standalone recommind.com domain now redirects to the OpenText brand page, and no independent Recommind developer portal, API reference, or API surface remains.

providers.name: Recordgram
providers.description: Recordgram is a mobile music-creation platform, now operating as Cre8tor (cre8tor.app), that lets aspiring artists record songs, write lyrics, access a library of beats, and collaborate with professional producers directly from a smartphone. The company won the TechCrunch Disrupt SF 2017 Startup Battlefield and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. It is a consumer iOS/Android application with no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal surfaced at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment confirmed the consumer-app nature and the rebrand to Cre8tor.

providers.name: Recount Media
providers.description: Recount Media operates The Recount, a political news and media outlet that distributes government and political coverage across social platforms (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Snapchat, and X) plus the "Who Broke It" newsletter on Substack, under the tagline "More signal, less noise, and zero spin." It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer media brand it publishes no public developer platform, API, or specification surface; this profile captures its identity and the domain-security posture probed from its live website.

providers.name: Recursive
providers.description: Recursive (Recursive Superintelligence) is an AI research company founded in 2025 and backed by Earlybird, building recursive self-improving systems designed to automate knowledge discovery and accelerate scientific progress, beginning with AI research itself. Its team of researchers and entrepreneurs previously worked at OpenAI, DeepMind, Google Brain, Meta, Salesforce and Uber, and works on open-ended algorithms, AI-generating algorithms and self-improving systems. The company is based in San Francisco with an additional presence in London. Recursive currently publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable developer surface; this profile captures its identity as a lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Red Beacon
providers.description: Redbeacon was a consumer home-services marketplace that connected homeowners with local service professionals — for home repair, cleaning, landscaping, handyman and similar jobs — letting people describe a job and receive quotes from vetted local pros. The company was an early venture-backed startup (with Mayfield among its investors) and was acquired by The Home Depot in 2012. The standalone Redbeacon consumer service was subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass the redbeacon.com domain still resolves (Cloudflare DNS, Google Workspace email) but serves no live website (origin returns HTTP 525 / 400) and publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio-graph node.

providers.name: Red Tricycle
providers.description: Red Tricycle (redtri.com) was a digital parenting media company publishing local family activity guides, things-to-do listings, product roundups, and lifestyle content for parents across major US cities. It was acquired by Tinybeans, and the redtri.com domain now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to tinybeans.com, a family photo-sharing app. Red Tricycle was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface for either the Red Tricycle or Tinybeans consumer property.

providers.name: Red Ventures
providers.description: Red Ventures is a privately held digital marketing and media holding company headquartered in Fort Mill, South Carolina, operating a portfolio of high-growth consumer brands and comparison, commerce, and content businesses including Bankrate, The Points Guy, Lonely Planet, and Allconnect. The company combines proprietary technology, data science, and performance marketing to acquire customers on behalf of its brands and partners. It is a corporate/media holding company and publishes no public developer API program, developer portal, or SDKs on its primary web presence.

providers.name: RedCap
providers.description: RedCap is an automotive dealer service software company that built an on-demand vehicle pickup-and-delivery, loaner, and shuttle platform for dealership fixed-operations (service) departments — offering live vehicle tracking, automated dispatching, at-home loaner contracting, on-demand parts fulfillment, and Uber-integrated shuttle coordination that plug into a dealership's existing DMS and service tools. Backed by Uncork Capital, RedCap was acquired by Solera and is now operated as Solera Service Suite; its former site (getredcap.com) redirects to the Solera Service Suite product. RedCap does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: RedDoorz
providers.description: RedDoorz is a Southeast Asian budget-hospitality technology company that operates a franchise and management network of economy hotels and rooms across Indonesia, Singapore, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Thailand. Through its consumer website and mobile apps travelers can search, book, and pay for value-priced stays, while its "List your property" program onboards independent hotel owners onto the RedDoorz brand, distribution, loyalty, and property-management platform. Backed by 500 Global and Qiming Venture Partners, the company operates a consumer booking product rather than a public developer platform; as of this pass it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile tracks the company's digital and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: reetian
providers.description: reetian (Chinese brand 瑞天数智, Reetian Digital Intelligence) is a China-based digital-intelligence company surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. Its public presence is a JavaScript single-page marketing site at reetian.com fronted by Cloudflare; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or source repositories that could be discovered and harvested. This profile remains a company-level lead pending a public API surface.

providers.name: refresh
providers.description: Refresh (refresh.si) is a digital marketing agency focused on building and growing digital brands. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found a minimal public web footprint with no API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface; the profile is retained as a company lead with domain security captured from live TLS/DNS probes.

providers.name: Regulatory DataCorp
providers.description: Regulatory DataCorp (RDC) was a risk and compliance intelligence company whose flagship GRID (Global Regulatory Information Database) powered KYC, AML, and third-party/financial-crime screening. RDC was acquired by Moody's Corporation in 2020 and fully absorbed into Moody's risk and KYC product line; it no longer operates as a standalone entity. The former rdc.com and regulatorydatacorp.com domains are parked on Moody's nameservers with no live site, developer portal, or public API. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of bain-capital-ventures; no independent API surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Rei do Pitaco
providers.description: Rei do Pitaco is a Brazilian online sports betting, daily fantasy sports, and casino platform founded in 2019 and headquartered in Brazil. The service offers competitive sports odds, live in-play betting, daily fantasy sports contests, and casino games aimed at the Brazilian market. As a regulated iGaming operator its consumer web and mobile properties are geo-restricted outside Brazil (the primary domains return HTTP 451 to non-Brazilian visitors), and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface. Rei do Pitaco is backed by Bullpen Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile.

providers.name: Reinfer
providers.description: Reinfer was a London-based communications intelligence company, backed by Seedcamp, that built a natural-language-processing platform for mining structured insight and automation triggers from unstructured conversational data such as emails, support tickets, and chat. Reinfer was acquired by SS&C Blue Prism and its technology folded into SS&C's intelligent-automation product line; the original developer surface (reinfer.io, docs.reinfer.io, api.reinfer.io) is now defunct and no longer resolves, so there is no live public API to catalog. This profile is retained as a portfolio and acquisition lead for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Relish
providers.description: Relish is a consumer product operated at hellorelish.com and backed by Bullpen Capital, added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. Live enrichment probing found the marketing site sitting behind a bot/captcha challenge and marked noindex, with no developer, API, or documentation subdomains resolving, no first-party GitHub organization, no published SDK packages, and no machine-readable well-known files. No public API surface was discovered during enrichment; the only verified technical artifact is a domain-security posture probe (TLS 1.3, SPF and DMARC present, no HSTS/DNSSEC/CAA records).

providers.name: Remedy Corporation
providers.description: Remedy Corporation was an IT service management (ITSM) software company founded in 1991 by Lawrence Garlick, David Mahler, and Doug Mueller, and backed by Accel with a Series A investment. Its flagship Action Request System (AR System) became a leading help-desk and IT service management platform. The company went public on NASDAQ under the ticker RMDY, was acquired by Peregrine Systems in 2001, and its ITSM assets were subsequently acquired by BMC Software in 2002, where the Remedy ITSM product line continued for many years. Remedy Corporation no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no active developer portal, documentation, or public API.

providers.name: Remote Calc
providers.description: Decodes base64 encoding and parses it to return a solution to the calculation in JSON

providers.name: Renotag, Inc.
providers.description: Renotag, Inc. is a Calgary, Canada based construction-technology startup (founded 2020, backed by 500 Global) that builds home-renovation and construction cost-estimation software. Its product produces localized renovation estimates and material takeoffs in minutes by combining user inputs with regional labor and material pricing data, helping contractors quote and close more business. As of this enrichment pass Renotag publishes no public developer program, API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documentation surface; the primary web properties (renotag.com and api.renotag.com) currently return HTTP 301 redirect loops, and the app is a private login at app.renotag.com. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio.

providers.name: Renoviso
providers.description: Renoviso is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Renren
providers.description: Renren (人人网), originally launched as Xiaonei in 2005 and renamed in 2009, was one of China's largest social networking platforms and was widely described as the "Facebook of China," especially popular among university students. Renren Inc. listed on the NYSE in 2011; the social-networking business later declined and the assets were sold in 2018. The site is now operated by Chengdu Renren Interactive Entertainment Technology Co., Ltd. and is undergoing a service upgrade. Historically Renren ran an Open Platform with an OAuth2 REST API (wiki.dev.renren.com) for third-party login and social integration; that developer surface is now defunct and no live API endpoints respond.

providers.name: rentify
providers.description: Rentify was a London-based property technology (PropTech) startup founded in 2011 that built an online lettings and property-management platform for landlords, letting them list, market, price, and manage rental properties directly without a traditional high-street agent. It raised a Series A from Balderton Capital and later a crowdfunding round before ceasing operations. Surfaced as a balderton-capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface (the company is no longer operating and rentify.com no longer serves an application).

providers.name: Rentlytics
providers.description: Rentlytics was a multifamily real estate data analytics company founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, CA (with offices in Sacramento and Denver). Its platform consolidated operational and financial data scattered across multifamily assets into a unified business-intelligence layer, and it shipped products such as Open Data Services and Renovation Manager for per-unit and per-property yield visibility. Rentlytics was acquired by RealPage in 2018 for roughly $57 million and folded into RealPage's real-estate platform. As of this enrichment pass the standalone rentlytics.com domain is parked (it redirects to a generic lander) and the company operates no independent public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: RentMineOnline
providers.description: RentMineOnline was a San Francisco-based software-as-a-service company, founded in 2007, that brought resident referral programs online for the multifamily rental housing industry by leveraging leading social networking sites. Its platform sent community-branded emails to apartment residents and paid them referral bonuses for recommending their buildings to friends across their social networks. In 2011 it was voted "Best New Company in Apartment Marketing." RentMineOnline was acquired by RealPage in July 2012 and folded into RealPage's multifamily marketing portfolio; it no longer operates an independent website or developer program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this profile was processed by the enrichment pipeline, which confirmed no public API surface, developer documentation, or discovery artifacts exist for the defunct entity.

providers.name: Reply.ai
providers.description: Reply.ai was a conversational AI and customer-experience platform founded in 2016 in New York City, building software to automate repetitive customer-service processes and deliver instant, personalized support across a customer's preferred communication channels. The company was acquired by Kustomer in May 2020 and folded into that platform. As of this enrichment pass the reply.ai domain is a parked "for sale" listing with no active product, developer portal, or public API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Replyr.ai
providers.description: Replyr.ai (Replyr Sdn Bhd, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia) is an AI-powered customer engagement and lead-acquisition platform. It builds GPT-style chat assistants that reply instantly in multiple languages across WhatsApp and other chat channels to qualify leads, answer FAQs, recommend products, and book appointments 24/7. The company packages this with Meta and Google advertising campaigns and a BookAClinic discovery marketplace, positioning itself as a patient-acquisition solution for specialised clinics. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Replyr.ai publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: ResearchGate
providers.description: ResearchGate is a professional network and social platform for scientists and researchers, founded in 2008 in Berlin, Germany. Members use it to share and discover research publications, connect and collaborate with colleagues, ask and answer questions, and track the reach and citations of their work. The platform hosts tens of millions of researcher profiles and a large corpus of full-text papers, and is operated by ResearchGate GmbH. It exposes no publicly documented developer API surface; this profile was surfaced via the dragoneer portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Reserve *
providers.description: Reserve was a restaurant-reservation startup backed by GV and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector portfolio lead. Its domain reserve.com now issues an HTTP 301 redirect to resy.com, the Resy restaurant-reservation platform, indicating the product has been folded into Resy. During enrichment no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI, or developer documentation was found for Reserve, and no security.txt, bug bounty, or trust center is published on the domain. The profile is retained as an acquired/redirected consumer-sector lead.

providers.name: Resonado Labs
providers.description: Resonado Labs is a high-velocity innovation and hardware development lab focused on improving the acoustic performance of the next generation of audio products through speaker hardware design and engineering. Backed by 500 Global, the company designs novel loudspeaker and transducer technology for consumer electronics and audio OEMs. Resonado Labs is a hardware and acoustics company; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Resourcely
providers.description: Resourcely is an a16z-backed company reachable at resourcely.io, surfaced as a portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public web presence is served on Webflow with Google Workspace email (SPF/DMARC configured). As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, documentation portal, first-party SDK/CLI packages, or status/trust subdomains were discoverable, and its former documentation host (docs.resourcely.io) no longer resolves, so this remains an identity-and-security profile rather than a scored API surface.

providers.name: Restorando
providers.description: Restorando was a Latin American online restaurant-reservation platform (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, and other markets), originally backed by Emergence Capital and later acquired by TripAdvisor. The Restorando brand has since been absorbed into TheFork: as of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass, restorando.com returns a 301 redirect to thefork.es and the standalone Restorando product no longer exists. It exposes no independent developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable surface to enrich.

providers.name: Retailigence
providers.description: Retailigence is a retail technology company that applies artificial intelligence and machine learning to category management and store operations. Its ML Engine powers an AI suite for assortment optimisation, space modelling, store clustering, customer segmentation, and an X-Ray control-tower hub (web and mobile) that tracks and helps remove in-store operational issues. The platform is delivered as a proof-of-concept engagement rather than a public self-serve developer API. Retailigence was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: RetailMeNot *
providers.description: RetailMeNot is a consumer savings destination that aggregates coupons, promo codes, cash-back offers, and deals from thousands of retailers and brands, helping shoppers in the United States save money when they buy online and in-store. It operates a website, mobile apps, and browser extensions that surface verified discount codes and cash-back at checkout, and it monetizes through retailer affiliate relationships rather than a self-serve developer platform. As of this profile RetailMeNot publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; probing found no reachable developer portal or well-known discovery documents, and partner activity is handled through whitelabel affiliate infrastructure.

providers.name: Rev1
providers.description: Rev1 (REV1, Inc.) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building an AI-powered platform that automatically converts 3D CAD models into fully annotated, production-ready 2D manufacturing drawings in minutes instead of hours. The software applies ASME Y14.5-2018 geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) standards, captures design intent, and lets mechanical engineers review the design rationale before sharing with manufacturers, reportedly recovering roughly 25% of engineering time at hardware companies across robotics, aerospace, automotive, medical devices, and consumer electronics. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes only a marketing site and a demo-request flow — there is no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface to catalog.

providers.name: Reveal Imaging
providers.description: Reveal Imaging (Reveal Imaging Technologies) is a security-screening hardware company known for CT-based explosives-detection and checkpoint screening systems for aviation and critical infrastructure. Founded around 2002 and backed by General Catalyst since 2003, the company was acquired into SAIC and its detection business is now part of Leidos. It is a physical-security systems provider, not an API provider - enrichment found no public developer portal, API, developer documentation, or machine-readable specification hosted under its own name (its former revealimaging.com domain now serves Leidos, and the General Catalyst portfolio entry points to saic.com).

providers.name: Revolution Precrafted
providers.description: Revolution Precrafted is a Manila, Philippines-based prefabricated design and proptech company founded in 2015 by Robbie Antonio. It designs and sells limited-edition prefab homes, pavilions, modular hotels, pop-up retail spaces, glamping structures, and furniture created by more than 80 leading global architects, designers, and artists under exclusive partnership. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Durians) and K2 Global, it reached a reported unicorn valuation. The company runs a consumer real-estate and construction business and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and mislabeled "Strategic Grow" in the source stub; the website revolutionprecrafted.com is authoritative.

providers.name: Revolv
providers.description: Revolv was a smart-home company that built a connected home hub and mobile application to unify control of disparate smart-home devices and wireless protocols from a single app. The company was acquired by Nest (Google) and the Revolv hub and service were subsequently discontinued; owners of purchased Revolv hubs were directed to Nest support for refunds through a deadline of October 31, 2018. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical portfolio record. The company publishes no active API, developer portal, SDKs, or public developer surface, so this entry carries only a domain-security probe of its remaining web presence.

providers.name: Revolving Games
providers.description: Revolving Games is a mobile-first game studio and publishing company operating two independent gaming studios with a team of 150+ gaming-industry veterans. Its flagship title is War of Nova, a sci-fi 4X space-strategy mobile game for iOS and Android spanning base-building, empire-building, and competitive multiplayer live-ops gameplay. Backed by Pantera Capital, the company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it publishes a consumer marketing website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Ricursive
providers.description: Ricursive (Ricursive Intelligence) is a frontier AI lab building self-improving systems, starting with chip design. The company combines modern AI methods with semiconductor and electronic design automation (EDA) workflows to create a feedback loop between AI systems and the hardware that runs them. It was founded by veterans from Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and NVIDIA (including researchers behind AlphaChip) and is backed by leading investors. As of this profile Ricursive publishes a public marketing and careers site but no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or developer product surface — so there is no API artifact to harvest. This company profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Ricursive Intelligence
providers.description: Ricursive Intelligence is a frontier AI laboratory building self-improving systems to reinvent chip design, closing the loop between artificial intelligence and the hardware that powers it. Founded by researchers behind work such as AlphaChip (Nature 2021), RL-CCD (DAC Best Paper 2023), Insta (DAC Best Paper 2025), and C3PO (ASP-DAC Best Paper 2026), and contributors to major AI models and accelerators (Gemini, Claude, Grok, TPUs), the company raised $335M from Sequoia, Lightspeed, DST Global, and NVentures. As of this profile the company operates as a research lab with a public marketing site and careers page but no publicly documented developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Right Hear
providers.description: Right Hear (RightHear) is an accessibility technology company, backed by Techstars, that helps people who are blind, have low vision, or face orientation and wayfinding challenges navigate indoor and complex public spaces more independently. Its solution pairs location sensors installed at points of interest with a companion smartphone app that delivers spoken, audible orientation cues and accessibility information to visitors, and is marketed primarily to businesses, venues, and public institutions seeking to make their physical environments more inclusive. At the time of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API documentation surface, and its website sits behind a bot-protection challenge; this profile tracks the company's identity and public web presence for API and agentic-access discoverability.

providers.name: Rightpoint
providers.description: Rightpoint is a global experience consultancy, now fully integrated into the Genpact brand, that designs and builds customer and employee experiences for enterprise organizations. Its practice spans agentic experience, digital workspace, experience advisory, intelligent content, omnichannel experience, and personalization and experimentation, delivered through deep platform partnerships with Adobe, Microsoft, Optimizely, and Sitecore. As a services and consulting firm rather than an API product company, Rightpoint publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and web presence within the API Evangelist network. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

providers.name: Riide
providers.description: Riide manufactures connected electric bicycles combining a street-legal 500W ebike (the Riide 2) with built-in GPS tracking, 4G cellular connectivity, remote lock/disable theft prevention, and a removable battery with state-of-charge monitoring. The company pairs hardware with a mobile app and connected-vehicle services. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this pass the public site is a consumer product/pre-order page ("coming soon") with no documented developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Rimac
providers.description: Rimac Group is a Croatia-based holding company bringing together exclusive hypercars and advanced electrification technology. Its portfolio spans Bugatti Rimac (the hypercar joint venture behind the all-electric Rimac Nevera), Rimac Technology (design, engineering and production of EV components — battery systems, powertrains, battery management systems and electronic control units supplied to OEMs including Porsche, Hyundai, BMW and others), and Verne (autonomous urban mobility / robotaxi). Rimac is a B2B automotive and electrification supplier and vehicle manufacturer; it does not currently operate a public developer program, API, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio tracking.

providers.name: Rise Reforming
providers.description: Rise Reforming is a climate-technology company that converts underutilized and flared waste biogas into valuable chemicals such as dimethyl ether (DME) and methanol. It deploys a modular, on-site reforming process at biogas sources like wastewater treatment plants, enabling localized, supply-secure chemical production and reducing dependence on centralized, fossil-fuel-based chemical manufacturing. A Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company, it is building the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demonstration in the Americas at a Chicagoland wastewater facility. As a hardware and chemical-process company, it currently publishes no public web API, developer portal, or software SDK surface.

providers.name: Rise Robotics
providers.description: RISE Robotics develops industrial linear-actuation technology designed to replace traditional hydraulic systems. Its flagship Beltdraulic Cylinder is a fluid-free hydraulic alternative delivering faster actuation, higher reliability, no fire hazard, and fuel-source flexibility for large-scale industrial applications. The company builds actuation products (Beltdraulic Cylinder, Railgate, SuperJammer, CLD) for Tier 1 suppliers, OEMs, and the US Department of Defense. RISE Robotics is a hardware and heavy-equipment company backed by Techstars; it publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: RiskIQ
providers.description: RiskIQ was a San Francisco-based external threat intelligence and attack surface management company, known for its PassiveTotal platform (passive DNS, WHOIS, SSL certificate and host-pair intelligence), Digital Footprint external asset discovery, and External Threats brand/phishing detection. It exposed a developer REST API at api.riskiq.net and a research console at community.riskiq.com. Microsoft acquired RiskIQ in 2021 and folded its technology into Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence (MDTI) and Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM). As of this enrichment pass the riskiq.com domain runs on Microsoft/Azure infrastructure and www.riskiq.com issues a 301 redirect to the Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence product page; the standalone RiskIQ/PassiveTotal API hosts (api.riskiq.net, community.riskiq.com) no longer accept connections. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record with no live, independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: riskmethods
providers.description: riskmethods was a supply-chain risk management SaaS company (Munich, Germany) that helped enterprises monitor, assess, and mitigate risk across their supplier networks using AI-driven risk intelligence, supplier monitoring, and disruption alerting. Backed by Point Nine Capital, riskmethods was acquired by Sphera in 2022 and its product now lives inside Sphera's Supply Chain Risk Management suite; the former riskmethods.net domain 301-redirects to sphera.com. riskmethods did not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or discovery endpoints, so this profile carries the identity and a probed domain-security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: RiskPulse
providers.description: RiskPulse was a supply chain risk and weather-intelligence company (also known by its Stormpulse brand) that scored and forecast weather, transit, and logistics disruption risk across supply chain networks. It was acquired by Everstream Analytics; the riskpulse.com and stormpulse.com domains now 301-redirect to everstream.ai, where the capability lives on as Everstream's Weather Intelligence and Analytics product. As of this enrichment pass there is no standalone RiskPulse public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or discovery surface, and Everstream exposes no public API either. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company lead.

providers.name: Riverpool
providers.description: Riverpool (riverpool.ai) is an early-stage, pre-launch startup building what it describes as the "post-modern analytics data stack" — a continuously circulating, self-refreshing approach to analytics data rather than a stagnant warehouse. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the public site is a "coming soon" landing page hosted on GitHub Pages with no launched product, developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or other API surface to catalog yet. This profile captures verified company identity and domain-security posture; API artifacts will be added when the product and its developer surface go live.

providers.name: Rivet Design
providers.description: Rivet is a design agent that works alongside your coding agent: given a prompt or an existing application, it explores dozens of distinct visual and UI design directions in parallel so you can compare them side by side and pick the one that fits, instead of iterating on a single design by hand. As of this profile it is an early-stage product presented through a marketing landing page at tryrivet.design; no public API, SDKs, CLI, MCP server, or developer documentation are published yet, so the API Evangelist network tracks it as an identity-only company profile.

providers.name: Rivos
providers.description: Rivos is a Santa Clara-based silicon startup founded in 2021 that designs data-center class GPUs and AI accelerators around the open RISC-V instruction set architecture, fabricated on TSMC's 3nm process. The company is also developing a CUDA-to-RISC-V translation layer to ease migration of Nvidia-based AI workloads onto its silicon. Rivos raised a 250 million dollar Series A in 2024 led by Matrix Capital Management with Walden Catalyst and Dell Capital Partners, followed by additional rounds bringing total funding above 370 million dollars at a valuation north of 2 billion dollars. In October 2025 Meta announced an agreement to acquire Rivos to bolster its in-house custom silicon program. The company has operated in near-stealth mode and currently exposes no public website content, SDKs, or APIs, so this profile is intentionally an empty apis list with external press and acquisition references.

providers.name: RJMetrics
providers.description: RJMetrics was a Philadelphia-based business intelligence and analytics company (founded 2008, backed by Trinity Ventures, SoftTech VC and others) that helped online businesses centralize, model and visualize data from databases and SaaS tools. In 2016 the company was acquired by Magento; its analytics product became Magento Business Intelligence and now lives inside Adobe Commerce, while the data-pipeline team spun out the standalone product Stitch (later acquired by Talend). The RJMetrics brand no longer operates independently: rjmetrics.com issues a 301 redirect to the Adobe/Magento Business Intelligence product page, and there is no surviving RJMetrics developer portal, public API, SDK or documentation surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Roadrunner
providers.description: RoadRunner is a tech-enabled managed waste and recycling services company operating across all 50 US states, serving 14,000+ commercial customers in hospitality, healthcare, retail, logistics and manufacturing. It consolidates multi-location waste programs and layers proprietary optimization tooling (Oversite, Waste Metering, BillCheck, Priceshield) plus the RecycleMORE and CleanStream recycling programs on top of hauler networks. Backed by Fifth Wall and Kleiner Perkins in the climate sector. As of this enrichment pass RoadRunner publishes a marketing site and a customer + payment portal but no public developer/API surface, so no OpenAPI, SDK, MCP or event artifacts were found.

providers.name: roadster
providers.description: Roadster was a Palo Alto digital automotive retail commerce platform (its Express Storefront let dealers sell and finance vehicles fully online) that was acquired by CDK Global in 2021 and folded into CDK's automotive digital-retailing suite. The roadster.com domain now serves CDK Global's Automotive Digital Retailing product and no longer exposes a standalone Roadster developer portal, API reference, or public API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public API artifacts are discoverable.

providers.name: Rocana
providers.description: Rocana (formerly ScalingData) was an IT operations analytics company founded in 2014 in San Francisco and backed by GV. Its product captured and analyzed all machine data from all sources across data-center infrastructure, keeping it online and queryable for years so operations teams could perform root-cause analysis and surface emerging IT problems before they caused outages. The company raised roughly $19.4M before being acquired by Splunk in 2017, after which the independent Rocana product and brand were wound down. It was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment on 2026-07-21 confirmed there is no live public website (rocana.com no longer resolves), no developer portal, no API, and no client packages — the company no longer operates independently.

providers.name: Rocket Lab
providers.description: Rocket Lab (Rocket Lab Corporation, formerly Rocket Lab USA; Nasdaq RKLB) is an American aerospace manufacturer and end-to-end space company founded in 2006 by Peter Beck. It designs and launches the Electron small-lift orbital rocket, is developing the reusable Neutron medium-lift vehicle, and builds the Photon spacecraft platform along with satellites, spacecraft components, solar cells, reaction wheels, star trackers, separation systems and other space systems. Rocket Lab operates launch complexes in Mahia, New Zealand and at Wallops Island, Virginia, providing dedicated and rideshare launch services plus on-orbit management for commercial, civil and national-security customers. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures; this profile is enriched from public identity and live domain probes only, as Rocket Lab publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Rocketable
providers.description: Rocketable acquires profitable SaaS products and infuses them with AI, operating a portfolio of software businesses that are run, improved, and grown by AI agents. Backed by Y Combinator, True Ventures, Bloomberg Beta, and INDIE.vc, the San Francisco company buys established SaaS products generating at least $500K in annual revenue and works toward support that resolves problems in seconds and features and fixes that ship in minutes or hours instead of quarters. The public site runs two intake flows — apply to join the team, and submit a SaaS product to be acquired — plus a newsletter on automating software businesses with AI agents. No public API or developer surface is published.

providers.name: Rocketrip
providers.description: Rocketrip was a New York City corporate travel cost-savings platform that gave business travelers a personalized budget (a "Price to Beat") and rewarded employees who booked flights, hotels, and rail below it, sharing the savings between the traveler and the company. It was backed by Canaan Partners, GV, Bessemer, and Y Combinator. As of this enrichment pass the rocketrip.com and www.rocketrip.com domains 301-redirect to Tabhi (tabhi.ai / tabhi.com), the developer, docs, and api subdomains no longer resolve, and no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI could be found — the standalone Rocketrip product and its API surface appear to have been retired or folded into Tabhi.

providers.name: Rockmelt
providers.description: Rockmelt was a Chromium-based social web browser startup founded in 2008 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), designed to integrate Facebook, Twitter, and web feeds directly into the browser chrome. The company was acquired by Yahoo in August 2013 and its products were discontinued shortly after. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment confirms the company is defunct with no live web, developer, or API surface.

providers.name: Rodeo
providers.description: Rodeo is a consumer social app that helps people wrangle their social life: save the things you want to do — social posts, screenshots, links and photos — and then do the things you saved together with friends, while Rodeo wrangles the details and keeps you organized. Tagline: "Save it. Do it." Backed by Foundry Group and Seedcamp. As of this enrichment pass Rodeo publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs or .well-known discovery surface — it is a consumer mobile/web product, not an API provider.

providers.name: Rogue Wave Software
providers.description: Rogue Wave Software was a developer-tools and high-performance-computing software company known for products such as TotalView, Klocwork, IMSL numerical libraries, PV-WAVE, and its Zend PHP and open-source support lines. It was acquired by Perforce Software in 2019 and the brand has since been fully absorbed into Perforce; the historical roguewave.com domain now 301-redirects wholesale to perforce.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. This enrichment pass found no independent Rogue Wave API surface, developer portal, documentation, or well-known endpoints — everything resolves to Perforce.

providers.name: Rohm and Haas
providers.description: Rohm and Haas Company was an American specialty chemicals manufacturer founded in 1909 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The company produced electronic materials, specialty polymers, adhesives, coatings, paints, and process chemicals. On April 1, 2009, Rohm and Haas was acquired by The Dow Chemical Company for approximately $18.8 billion in cash and stock. The Rohm and Haas brand has since been largely retired and its product lines, technologies, and businesses have been integrated into Dow (now Dow Inc., NYSE: DOW). Some legacy product brands persist under Dow but the standalone company no longer exists.

providers.name: RolePoint
providers.description: RolePoint was an employee referral, internal mobility, and talent-acquisition software company that helped recruitment teams source, refer, and redeploy talent through referral programs and internal mobility marketplaces, with a "Connect" API layer for integrating into ATS/HRIS systems such as iCIMS. The company was acquired by Jobvite in 2019 and folded into the Jobvite Talent Acquisition Suite; the standalone rolepoint.com domain no longer resolves and no independent developer portal or API surface remains reachable. It is tracked here as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Rooster
providers.description: Rooster is a subscription mobile reading app built by Plympton, Inc., a literary studio co-founded by Jennifer 8. Lee, Yael Goldstein Love, and Jacky Chang. Rooster delivers serialized fiction to readers' phones in short, commute-sized installments for a flat monthly fee, drawing on Plympton's DailyLit heritage of serialized reading. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Rooster is a consumer-facing app; Plympton publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or webhook surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Rothys
providers.description: Rothy's is a San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer footwear and accessories brand founded in 2012, known for washable shoes and bags 3D-knitted from recycled materials such as post-consumer plastic water bottles and marine plastics. Its catalog spans flats, loafers, sneakers, Mary Janes, clogs, sandals, heels, and boots for women, men, and kids, alongside totes, crossbody bags, wallets, and backpacks. The company ships to 40+ countries and emphasizes sustainable, seamless-knit manufacturing that reduces waste. Rothy's was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer retail brand it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and web presence for the catalog.

providers.name: Rovilus
providers.description: Rovilus is a seed-stage hardware startup founded in 2018 by YenChe Huang and Katherine Kan, developing thermal management technology for industrial battery packs. The company raised roughly $150K from 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) and appears in that firm's portfolio. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass the company's website (rovilus.com) no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN, no NS/MX records), and no public API, developer portal, SDK, documentation, or other developer surface could be found; Rovilus is a physical battery-thermal hardware company with no API footprint.

providers.name: Rowspace
providers.description: Rowspace builds AI infrastructure for major asset managers, converting fragmented institutional knowledge into clean, structured data that AI can reliably operate on. Founded in 2024 by Michael Manapat (former CTO of Notion and Head of Applied ML at Stripe) and Yibo Ling (former Chief Business Officer of Binance), the company operates under Emergence Capital's "Agentic Software" thesis with the positioning "You built your firm's edge. Compound it with AI." As of this enrichment pass Rowspace publishes only a marketing website (www.rowspace.ai) and has no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: roxmotor
providers.description: ROX Motor (roxmotor.com) is a Chinese electric-vehicle manufacturer, a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, best known for the ROX 01 electric off-road SUV. It is a consumer automotive brand with no public developer API surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with a domain-security probe. The site is hosted on Tencent Cloud and was not reachable from the enrichment environment for content search.

providers.name: RPX
providers.description: RPX Corporation is a San Francisco-based patent risk management company that provides defensive patent aggregation, patent market intelligence, and litigation-risk services to member companies. Its member platform is served from gated hosts (api.rpxcorp.com and docs.rpxcorp.com) that require subscription authentication, so no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface is accessible for enrichment. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of crv. Sector: enterprise / intellectual property.

providers.name: RTFKT
providers.description: RTFKT (pronounced "artifact") was a digital-fashion and collectibles studio founded in 2020 by Benoit Pagotto, Chris Le, and Steven Vasilev, known for NFT-based virtual sneakers, wearables, and the CloneX avatar collection created with artist Takashi Murakami. Backed by an a16z-led seed round, the company was acquired by Nike in December 2021 and operated as a Web3 / metaverse brand. Nike announced it was winding RTFKT down in December 2024, with operations ceasing by the end of January 2025. RTFKT was a consumer/collectibles brand and never published a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; its remaining web presence is a frozen static archive page. This profile records that verified absence of an API surface.

providers.name: Rtv
providers.description: Rtv (Return to Vendor) is a materials-innovation company building a circular recycling system for nylon-6. Its patented molecular design regenerates nylon that can be recycled infinitely without quality loss, yielding production-ready recyclable yarn, monomaterial stretch fabric, and regenerated pellets for injection molding and extrusion. The company also offers end-of-life textile collection, waste reprocessing, and regulatory-compliance support (EPR, California SB 707, EU textile regulations) for apparel, automotive, and technical industrial applications. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Third Sphere, Teknor Apex, and NSF SBIR grants.

providers.name: Rudus
providers.description: Rudus is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI-powered takeoff and estimation platform for concrete contractors and subcontractors. The software automatically detects and classifies concrete structures (footings, walls, columns, and slabs) from architectural plan sets, expands them into detailed assembly line items, and integrates into existing estimator workflows rather than replacing them. Rudus reports a 70-80% reduction in takeoff and estimation time, letting estimators submit more bids. Founded by Rishi Pankhaniya (ex-Airbnb) and Sahil Goel (ex-Amazon). As of this enrichment pass Rudus operates a lead-generation marketing site at rudus.ai with no public developer program, API, documentation, or self-service sign-up; this profile records that verified state.

providers.name: ruhnn
providers.description: Ruhnn Holding Limited (如涵控股) is a Hangzhou-based Chinese influencer (KOL) incubation, marketing, and e-commerce company. It pioneered the "internet celebrity" (wanghong) commercialization model, signing and developing influencers and monetizing their audiences through self-operated online stores on marketplaces such as Taobao and Tmall, as well as through a platform/advertising business that connects its network of KOLs with third-party brands for social-marketing campaigns. The company listed on NASDAQ under the ticker RUHN in 2019 and was subsequently taken private. It is surfaced here as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. Ruhnn is a consumer-facing influencer marketing and commerce operator and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Ruka.ai
providers.description: Ruka.ai is a Spanish-language AI company, backed by 500 Global, that builds AI agents giving businesses control and visibility over their operating margin. Its agents automate operational processes, process invoices, detect cost-saving opportunities and anomalies, and alert teams to variations in real time so they can reduce operational costs and make better data-driven decisions. Ruka.ai is a SaaS product presented through a marketing website at ruka.ai; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Russian Calendar
providers.description: Check if a date is a Russian holiday or not

providers.name: RVDS Inc.
providers.description: RVDS Inc. is a South Korean food and beverage company that describes itself as growing into Korea's representative Multi-K-Food Brand Operator, building and operating a portfolio of consumer dining brands including Dodo Korea, Butai, and Salad Monster. Based in Cheongju-si, Chungcheongbuk-do, the company is backed by 500 Global. As a consumer food-brand operator it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so this profile carries only identity and probed domain-security signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: S3 Graphics
providers.description: S3 Graphics, Inc. is a legacy graphics, video, and multimedia accelerator company known for its GPU architectures (Savage, Chrome and DeltaChrome, plus the earlier ViRGE and Trio chipsets) and its display drivers. Originally founded as S3 Incorporated in 1989, the graphics business later operated as S3 Graphics under VIA and HTC ownership. Its public web presence is a legacy marketing and driver-download site (still Flash/Ruffle based); it exposes no modern web API, SDK, or developer platform. The historical "Developers" area was a hardware developer-relations channel offering GPU sample cards during the DeltaChrome era, not a programmatic API.

providers.name: S4S Technologies
providers.description: S4S Technologies operates what it describes as India's only full-stack food processing platform, running tech-driven farm-gate procurement and processing for the food and beverage industry. The company sources fresh produce from farmers through Village Level Collection Centres, processes it through climate-clean micro food-processing units, and supplies convenience-driven ingredients (fruits, vegetables, pulses, grains, and spices) to more than 1,100 food and beverage customers. It is a B2B agritech and food-supply-chain business rather than a software or API provider; no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Sabanto
providers.description: Sabanto is an agricultural autonomy company known for retrofitting existing farm tractors and equipment with an autonomy kit and an autonomy-as-a-service model, enabling unmanned tillage, planting, and field operations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 the company's primary domain (sabanto.com) no longer resolves to a live site — it redirects to a GoDaddy parked/for-sale page — so no developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, GitHub organization, or other public API surface could be found. This profile is retained as a lead with no live API surface at this time.

providers.name: Sabi
providers.description: Sabi ("Just Think") presents itself at sabi.com as a consumer neural-interface company building a wearable (a beanie) that transforms a wearer's thoughts directly into text — "no typing, no voice, just think." As of this enrichment pass the company operates a single marketing landing page with no public developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, changelog, or status surface; the only outbound links are its social accounts on X and Instagram. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub lead; there is currently no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Sabrix
providers.description: Sabrix was a transaction (indirect / sales & use) tax determination and compliance software company whose engine calculated sales, use, VAT and GST taxes for enterprise ERP and billing systems. Sabrix was acquired by Thomson Reuters in 2009 and folded into the Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE Indirect Tax product line. As an independent brand Sabrix no longer operates: the sabrix.com domain is now owned by Thomson Reuters (Thomson Reuters nameservers) and issues a 301 redirect to tax.thomsonreuters.com/en/onesource/indirect-tax. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical fintech / tax-tech lead; there is no independent Sabrix developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or well-known surface to enrich. Any live tax API surface lives under the Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE brand.

providers.name: Safire
providers.description: Safire (Safire Technology Group, Inc.) is a Canaan Partners portfolio company operating in battery and energy-materials deep tech. It develops impact-resistant, safety-focused electrolyte technology aimed at making lithium-ion batteries more resistant to fire and physical damage. Added to the API Evangelist network as a stub from Canaan's portfolio, it is a hardware and materials-science business rather than a software vendor; an enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 probed the company's likely domains and found no public developer portal, API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Sailplane
providers.description: Sailplane is an early-stage, true-ventures-backed AI startup building agentic automation. As of July 2026 the company is in stealth / pre-launch: sailplane.ai serves only a teaser page rendering an agent execution trace ("A signal has been sent. An agent is listening. The trace begins here.") describing plan initiation, support agents, branch generation, trajectory proposal/approval, and execution. No public API, developer docs, SDKs, or well-known endpoints are published yet. This profile remains a lead pending a public developer surface.

providers.name: Saks Global (fka Saks Fifth Avenue)
providers.description: Saks Global (fka Saks Fifth Avenue) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Saks OFF 5TH
providers.description: Saks OFF 5TH is an American off-price retailer of designer and luxury fashion, footwear, accessories, and home goods, historically operated as the discount banner of Saks Fifth Avenue and later folded into Saks Global (Hudson's Bay Company / HBC). It sold marked-down designer merchandise through outlet stores and an e-commerce site at saksoff5th.com. As of this enrichment pass the public website resolves to a shutdown notice with only a store-locations link, and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface. It was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub of Insight Partners in the consumer sector.

providers.name: Salad Ventures
providers.description: Salad Ventures is a crypto and web3 investment firm operating in the digital-asset, blockchain, and web3 gaming ecosystem. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital. As an investment and ecosystem firm rather than an API producer, Salad Ventures exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; its primary web presence (salad.ventures) sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and publishes no machine-readable API surface. This profile captures the firm's identity and domain-security posture for the network.

providers.name: Saleo
providers.description: Saleo is an AI-powered demo experience platform for go-to-market teams, enabling sales and pre-sales engineers to run high-stakes live demos inside their native product, build self-serve interactive product tours, and deliver autonomous AI-driven demos around the clock. Its products include Live (real demos backed by AI-generated demo data), Demo Agent (autonomous AI discovery agents), and Capture (interactive product tours). Saleo serves enterprise customers including SAP, Salesforce, 6sense, Seismic, and SailPoint, and is backed by Emergence Capital. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Samara
providers.description: Samara is a residential design and construction company that builds prefabricated, factory-made homes. Founded as an independent venture by Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia, Samara designs and delivers backyard accessory dwelling units (ADUs) in configurable Studio, One Bedroom, Two Bedroom, XL 8 and XL 10 models, alongside "Locale by Samara" single-family homes and a modular "kit of parts" for higher-yield multifamily infill. The company pairs a consumer-facing online configurator, property-eligibility checks, financing options and regional showrooms with factory production and installation. Backed by General Catalyst, Samara operates in the housing, construction technology and real-estate space. It is a physical-product company with no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Samastha Synergy Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Samastha Synergy Pte. Ltd. operates Djoin (djoin.id), positioning itself as a "digital partner for sustainable scale" that helps financial institutions and organizations in Indonesia grow through an adaptive product ecosystem. Djoin's named products are Coopmax (a platform aimed at cooperatives / koperasi), Kocek, and ProofyLink. The company runs a private backend API at api.djoin.id, which sits behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to unauthenticated requests; as of this profile there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, documentation, or SDK surface published. Samastha Synergy was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; this profile captures what is publicly verifiable from the djoin.id site and DNS/TLS probes.

providers.name: Sample6
providers.description: Sample6 was a food-safety technology company (a Canaan Partners portfolio company) that developed rapid, bioluminescence-based pathogen detection and environmental monitoring products for the food industry, aimed at catching contamination such as Listeria, Salmonella, and E. coli before product shipped. The business was acquired and absorbed into IEH Laboratories & Consulting Group; the sample6.com domain now redirects to iehinc.com. No independent developer portal, public API, or machine-readable API artifacts survive, so this record is retained as a historical company profile rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Sampler
providers.description: Sampler is a digital product-sampling platform used by consumer packaged goods (CPG) and retail brands to run targeted sample-distribution campaigns, collect first-party consumer data and reviews, and measure the impact of sampling on purchase behavior. It is operated as a business-facing marketing SaaS (Webflow marketing site, Salesforce Pardot marketing automation) and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, documentation host, or machine discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Samunnati
providers.description: Samunnati is an integrated agri-enterprise platform working to de-fragment India's agricultural value chain by connecting farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and agri enterprises. It combines financial solutions (lending to farmers, FPOs, and agri businesses), trade facilitation and market linkages, and digital marketplaces (FPO Next, Trade Next, and input, output, credit, and consumer marketplaces), alongside innovation, research, and foundation-led community work. Operating across Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Jaipur, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar, it positions itself as one of India's largest agri enterprises. Samunnati runs several customer-facing digital platforms but does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time.

providers.name: Sandforce
providers.description: SandForce was a fabless semiconductor company (Canaan Partners-backed) that designed flash memory / SSD controller processors. It was acquired by LSI Corporation in 2012 and its flash-controller business was subsequently folded into Seagate; the sandforce.com domain now redirects to seagate.com. As a defunct, absorbed brand it operates no independent website, developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation, so there is no live API surface to enrich. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a canaan-partners portfolio lead; retained as a historical/company record.

providers.name: Sandhill Markets
providers.description: Sandhill Markets (formerly Stonks.com) was a private-markets investment platform founded in 2020 by serial entrepreneur Ali Moiz, backed by a16z. It let accredited investors buy and sell shares of leading pre-IPO companies through a secondary marketplace, Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs), and a planned exchange, aiming to democratize an asset class historically gated by high minimums and opaque pricing. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, and its primary web presence appears defunct/misconfigured: the apex domain sandhillmarkets.com returns a GitHub Pages "Site not found" 404, the former stonks.com domain now redirects to an unrelated product, and no api/docs/app subdomains resolve. Only a beehiiv-hosted newsletter subdomain (blog.sandhillmarkets.com) remains observable. This profile is retained as a company/portfolio-lead stub with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Santa Cruz Operation
providers.description: Santa Cruz Operation (SCO) was an American software company founded in 1979 in Santa Cruz, California, best known for its Unix operating systems for Intel x86 hardware — Xenix (developed with Microsoft), SCO UNIX, SCO OpenServer, and UnixWare. The company later reorganized as Tarantella, Inc. and The SCO Group, which became widely known for the SCO v. IBM Linux litigation beginning in 2003. The SCO Group filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2007, and its Unix product assets were subsequently sold to UnXis, later renamed Xinuos. The historic Santa Cruz Operation is defunct and operates no modern developer platform or public API; this record is retained for network completeness.

providers.name: Sapho
providers.description: Sapho was a San Bruno, California micro-apps startup (founded 2014) that let enterprises build employee-facing "micro apps" and workflow notifications on top of legacy and SaaS systems. It was acquired by Citrix in November 2018 and folded into the Citrix Workspace product line as Citrix Microapps; the standalone product, developer portal, and any API surface were retired. The sapho.com domain now resolves only to a MarkMonitor brand-protection holding page (HTTPS refused, HTTP returns the registrar notice), so there is no live public API, documentation, or developer surface to enrich. This record is retained as a portfolio-company history stub for bloomberg-beta and uncork-capital.

providers.name: Saturnbird Coffee
providers.description: Saturnbird Coffee (三顿半) is a Chinese specialty coffee company known for premium instant coffee made with its proprietary REPUS extraction technology (cold extraction plus intelligent drying) using 100% Arabica beans. Its numbered Number Series and Express Series products, a Red Dot Design Award winner and Specialty Coffee Association member, are sold direct-to-consumer online and through collaborations with roasters including April Coffee, Kurasu, Monogram Coffee, and Fritz Coffee Company. Backed by Hongshan (HSG), it was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce brand with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Saudara Ai
providers.description: Saudara AI is an AI-native sourcing brokerage, founded in 2024 and based in Spokane, Washington, that connects American brands with vetted Indonesian manufacturers. Buyers submit requests for quotes (RFQs) and the company pairs human brokers with AI agents that scan factories, verify certifications, benchmark pricing against market data, and prepare quotes, returning vetted supplier options within 48 hours. Saudara AI also handles quality control, logistics, improved payment terms (30/70 and net-60), and vendor financing. As of its launch the company reports having sourced over $1M for 40+ brands. It operates as a brokerage service and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Savioke
providers.description: Savioke is a robotics company, backed by GV, that built the Relay autonomous delivery robot used by hotels and hospitals to move items such as amenities, medications, lab samples, and supplies through facilities without human assistance. The company now operates as Relay Robotics (savioke.com redirects to relayrobotics.com). It publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface; enrichment found only a marketing/contact site.

providers.name: Scaleio
providers.description: ScaleIO was a software-defined block storage startup (an early Norwest Venture Partners investment) that was acquired by EMC in 2013 and folded into Dell EMC as ScaleIO, later renamed VxFlex OS and then PowerFlex. It is no longer an independent company: the scaleio.com domain is Dell-managed and 301-redirects to the Dell EMC software-defined storage product page, and there is no independent developer portal, API, or SDK surface under this brand. Any current API surface lives under Dell PowerFlex, not scaleio.com.

providers.name: Schematic Labs
providers.description: Schematic Labs was a San Francisco consumer music startup founded in 2010, best known as the maker of SoundTracking, an "Instagram for songs" mobile app for sharing the music you are listening to. Backed by Google Ventures (GV), Accel Partners, and SoftBank Capital with roughly $5.9M raised, it was acquired by Rhapsody in August 2014 and wound down as a standalone company. Today soundtracking.com redirects to napster.com (Rhapsody's successor brand) and schematiclabs.com is a parked domain. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; this profile records the company's place in the GV portfolio graph.

providers.name: SCiFi Foods
providers.description: SCiFi Foods was a San Francisco Bay Area food-technology startup, founded in 2019 by Joshua March (CEO) and Kasia Gora (CTO), that developed cultivated (cell-cultured) beef blended with plant-based ingredients to make burgers close to the taste of conventional meat. The company used a proprietary platform built on gene-editing tools such as CRISPR to create and screen hundreds of animal cell lines each month. Backed by a16z among others, SCiFi Foods raised roughly $40M before ceasing operations in June 2024; its cell lines were later released to academia via the Good Food Institute. The company is defunct and exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical surface.

providers.name: Scoop
providers.description: Scoop (Scoop Technologies, Inc.) is a San Francisco based future-of-work company backed by Index Ventures whose Scoop for Work product is a hybrid-work scheduling assistant. It plugs into employees existing calendar and Slack so teams can coordinate great in-office days, sync schedules, and see who will be in, while giving HR and workplace leaders analytics on office usage and hybrid work trends. Originally launched in 2015 as a carpool/commute service (takescoop.com), the company pivoted to hybrid workplace coordination. Note: as of this enrichment pass the product domain scoopforwork.com returns HTTP 410 Gone with a broken TLS certificate, and the legacy takescoop.com domain is parked for sale; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface could be found.

providers.name: Scoopola
providers.description: Scoopola was an early-stage consumer startup backed by 500 Startups (Batch 2, June 2011), pitched as "the HotelTonight for live music and theater" — a mobile app for discovering and buying last-minute, discounted tickets to local live-music and theater events. The company appears defunct; its associated web domains (getwillcall.com and scoopola.com) no longer resolve, and there is no surviving developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This record is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; the enrichment pipeline found no live API to catalog.

providers.name: Scoreloop
providers.description: Scoreloop was a Munich, Germany based mobile social gaming company that provided a cross-platform SDK adding social features to mobile games - online leaderboards, achievements, player challenges, friend invites, and in-game virtual currency and monetization. The Scoreloop SDK supported Android, iOS, Windows Phone, Samsung Bada, Marmalade/AirPlay, and Unity 3D, and at its peak was used by more than 3,000 game developers. The company was backed by earlybird and was acquired by Research In Motion (BlackBerry) in 2011; the standalone Scoreloop platform and its developer service were subsequently wound down. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead - there is no live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remaining (the scoreloop.com domain now serves a suspended page and no developer host resolves), so no API artifacts are available to harvest.

providers.name: Scout.fm
providers.description: Scout.fm (Scout FM) was a podcast-curation startup whose iOS, Android, Alexa and CarPlay apps turned podcasts into personalized, radio-like stations using AI-driven recommendations across genres such as news, sports and true crime. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, Precursor Ventures, Advancit Capital and Samsung NEXT (roughly $1.4M raised), the company was acquired by Apple in September 2020 and subsequently shut down, with its apps pulled from every platform. The scout.fm domain no longer resolves and the company publishes no developer, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as a historical network record; there is nothing left to enrich.

providers.name: Screenhero
providers.description: Screenhero was a Y Combinator (W13) startup that built interactive screen sharing with voice and video, letting remote users share and control any application together. It was acquired by Slack in January 2015; the six-person team joined Slack and the standalone Screenhero product was discontinued, with its screen-sharing, voice, and video capabilities folded into Slack (today surfaced as Slack Huddles). The screenhero.com domain now 301-redirects to slack.com/features/huddles. No independent Screenhero developer portal, API, or SDK exists; this record is retained as a historical a16z portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Scriptlogic
providers.description: ScriptLogic was an IT systems-management software vendor known for Active Directory administration, desktop/Group Policy management, and Microsoft platform administration tooling. The brand and its products were acquired by Quest Software and fully absorbed; the scriptlogic.com domain now issues a 301 redirect to Quest's Microsoft Platform Management solutions page. ScriptLogic operates no independent website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface today. This profile was seeded as a VC-portfolio stub; enrichment found no first-party API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: SDSA
providers.description: SDSA (stylized as /dev/agents) is a stealth-stage startup building what it describes as a next-generation operating system for AI agents, aiming to make agentic applications a robust part of everyday consumer software through new UI patterns, a reimagined privacy model, and a developer platform for shipping more capable apps. The company was founded by David Singleton (former Stripe CTO), Ficus Kirkpatrick, Hugo Barra, and Nicholas Jitkoff, and is backed by SV Angel. As of this profile the company is pre-product: sdsa.ai is a single marketing/recruiting page with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or developer portal yet available. This entry was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with what is publicly verifiable.

providers.name: SE3 Labs
providers.description: SE3 Labs is a European artificial intelligence company building spatial AI for autonomous systems, with a mission to enable machines to perceive, reason, and act autonomously in the physical world. Its technology performs real-time 3D reconstruction of operational environments, spatial understanding to orchestrate fleets of autonomous machines, and natural-language interfaces for commanding multiple machines at once. Early applications target the defence sector, including vision-based autonomy and multi-drone reconnaissance. SE3 Labs is backed by Seedcamp and works directly with government and military partners; it does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Seam AI
providers.description: Seam AI was an AI-native account-based marketing (ABM) platform that used AI agents to research target accounts, monitor buying signals, and automatically execute outbound marketing and sales campaigns.
