Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, the company has been acquired and is merging its product into Clarify as "Clarify Signals" — a signals-aware CRM. As of this enrichment pass the getseam.ai site serves an acquisition/transition notice directing users to the Clarify Signals waitlist, and the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or .well-known discovery surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Seculert
providers.description: Seculert was an Israeli cybersecurity company that provided cloud-based automated threat and attack detection, analytics, and breach-detection services, correlating outbound traffic and threat intelligence to identify compromised devices. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, it was acquired by Radware in January 2017 and folded into Radware's cloud security portfolio; the independent seculert.com brand is now defunct. This enrichment pass found no live independent API surface: the apex domain no longer serves TLS, www.seculert.com redirects to a dead HubSpot landing page, and no /.well-known, llms.txt, or developer/API documentation is published. Retained as a network profile of an acquired, now-inactive provider; DNS records (DMARC ruf to dmarc@radware.com) corroborate the Radware ownership.

providers.name: SecureInfo Corporation
providers.description: SecureInfo Corporation was a cybersecurity and information-assurance company focused on FISMA and federal compliance, surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the domain www.secureinfo.com no longer serves an independent site — its TLS certificate resolves to kratosdefense.com (Kratos Defense), indicating the business was acquired/absorbed. No independent public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface was found; this profile records that honest finding.

providers.name: SeeCommerce
providers.description: SeeCommerce was a supply-chain performance management software company that provided analytics and management software focused on supply-chain visibility and problems. It raised roughly $47-58M across multiple venture rounds from investors including Insight Partners and Integral Capital Partners, and was acquired in February 2006. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct/acquired with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface (seecommerce.com no longer resolves to the company and other candidate domains do not resolve), so there are no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: SeedFi
providers.description: SeedFi was a U.S. consumer fintech that offered credit-building loans and savings products (its "Credit Builder Prime" and "Borrow & Grow" plans) aimed at helping financially underserved borrowers build credit history and cash savings simultaneously. Backed by a16z and other investors, SeedFi was acquired by Cross River Bank in 2022, and its consumer offerings were subsequently folded into Credit Karma (Intuit). The seedfi.com domain now 302-redirects to a Credit Karma support article; SeedFi operates no independent developer portal, public API, documentation, or OpenAPI surface. This profile is retained as a network company record with no API to enrich.

providers.name: Seek AI
providers.description: Seek AI was a New York City generative-AI enterprise data analytics company, backed by Battery Ventures, that built a conversational analytics agent letting business users query enterprise data in natural language and receive trustworthy answers (translating plain-language questions into SQL and narrative results over a company's own databases and warehouses). In 2025 Seek AI was acquired by IBM and folded into IBM watsonx AI Labs, a developer-first agentic-AI innovation hub in New York City; the company no longer operates an independent product, developer program, or public API. Its former developer subdomain (developers.seek.ai) now redirects to IBM's watsonx AI Labs, and the standalone seek.ai marketing site is no longer served. This API Evangelist profile records Seek AI as an acquired portfolio company and carries no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: SeeMexico
providers.description: SeeMexico is a B2B corporate travel management platform and business travel agency in Mexico that lets companies book flights, hotels, and car rentals from a single platform. It offers corporate rates, business credit, cashback, direct invoicing (facturacion), and a dedicated account executive to streamline managed business travel. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; the public site is a Duda-built marketing site and no public developer portal, API documentation, or programmatic surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Semmle
providers.description: Semmle was a semantic code-analysis company whose engine let developers write queries (in its QL query language) to find security vulnerabilities and their variants across large codebases, and which powered the free open-source code review platform LGTM.com. Its technology was adopted by Uber, NASA, Microsoft, and Google. GitHub acquired Semmle in September 2019 and folded the QL engine into what is now CodeQL and GitHub code scanning; the standalone Semmle and LGTM.com products were retired and www.semmle.com now redirects to the GitHub acquisition announcement. This profile is retained as a historical (acquired) company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SenSage
providers.description: SenSage was a security information and event management (SIEM) and log/event analytics company backed by Battery Ventures and Canaan Partners. Its platform focused on collecting, warehousing, and analyzing very large volumes of security event and log data for threat detection, forensics, and regulatory compliance reporting. SenSage was later acquired by KEYW Holding Corporation and the brand was retired; its former domain, sensage.com, now redirects to IgniteTech (an ESW Capital software-acquisition operator). This profile was surfaced as a venture portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. No active developer portal, public API, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; the company is treated as defunct with no live API footprint.

providers.name: Sequence Holdings
providers.description: Sequence Holdings is a technology holding company that acquires established businesses and transforms them with artificial intelligence. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc, it operates as an investment and operating group that buys mature companies and applies AI to modernize their products and operations. The company publishes a single marketing site and no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Serena & Lily
providers.description: Serena & Lily is a home furnishings and design brand founded in 2003 and based in Sausalito, California, known for its coastal-inspired furniture, bedding, rugs, wallpaper, lighting, and home decor sold through its e-commerce site and a network of design shops. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a direct-to-consumer retail and interior-design brand, Serena & Lily publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface at the time of this enrichment pass; this profile captures its identity and domain security posture only.

providers.name: Seriously
providers.description: Seriously Digital Entertainment is a mobile game studio best known for the Best Fiends match-3 puzzle franchise, a bug-versus-slug adventure set in the world of Minutia and available on iOS and Android. Founded in Helsinki with a Los Angeles presence and backed by Northzone, the studio was acquired by Playtika. It is a consumer entertainment company: its public web presence (seriously.com, which now redirects to bestfiends.com) is a game marketing and community site with app-store download links and social channels. Seriously publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Servo7
providers.description: Servo7 is a Y Combinator-backed warehouse robotics company that builds AI-powered robots for automating physical material-handling tasks such as loose-loaded container unloading, mixed-pallet palletizing, depalletizing, sortation, and case handling (up to a 20kg payload). Its differentiator is a no-code, demonstration-based deployment model in which an operator shows the robot the task to automate, with no engineers or integration project and no facility redesign required. Servo7 works with logistics providers including CEVA, Stord, DHL, and PostNL. It is a physical-robotics/hardware company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Sessions
providers.description: Sessions (Session Technologies, formerly Flow OS) was a Bucharest-based unified communication and collaboration platform founded in 2021 by Radu Negulescu and Radu Tintescu, backed by earlybird's Digital East Fund (invested 2022, lead Dan Lupu). The product bundled voice, video, chat, webinars and meetings with third-party productivity integrations on a proprietary "Flow OS" framework at sessions.us. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07-21) the company appears defunct: the sessions.us domain no longer serves the product (it resolves to an unrelated parked/casino-spam page behind a bare-IP TLS certificate), the docs, developers and api subdomains do not respond, and no live developer, API, OpenAPI, SDK or documentation surface could be located to enrich. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead record; no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: Seventh Spark
providers.description: Seventh Spark was a proprietary mobile platform powered by social engagement, curated content, and interactive live experiences, building customizable mobile applications for faith-based organizations and churches to expand and interact with their communities across times and locations. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and co-founded by Brian Lee and Marissa Bell, the company was acquired by Romans535. It is a consumer/mobile-app business with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or programmatic surface, and its domain (seventhspark.com) now resolves to an unclaimed Squarespace placeholder.

providers.name: SGI (Silicon Graphics)
providers.description: SGI, or Silicon Graphics, was a workstation, server, supercomputing, and computer-graphics company founded in 1982 and one of Mayfield's landmark early portfolio companies. It pioneered high-performance 3D graphics hardware, the IRIX operating system, and the OpenGL API. The independent company was acquired by Rackable Systems in 2009 (which adopted the SGI name) and that business was in turn acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in 2016. There is no longer an independent SGI developer program or public API surface; the historic sgi.com domain now redirects to HPE's high-performance-computing product line. This profile is retained as a historic Mayfield portfolio record; it is not an active API provider.

providers.name: Shara
providers.description: Shara (Shara Technology Management Nigeria Ltd) is a Lagos-based fintech that provides collateral-free working-capital loans of up to NGN 10 million to Nigerian small and medium-sized businesses. Sole traders, partnerships, and limited companies apply through Shara's website or Android app with basic business details and a bank statement, and receive a free loan estimate in seconds with approval typically in 48 hours to two weeks. The company reports over NGN 50 billion disbursed across 100,000+ loans to 7,000+ business customers. Shara publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: ShareRoot
providers.description: ShareRoot is an Australian digital marketing and technology company based in St Kilda, Victoria, that helps brands understand market opportunities and engage audiences across digital channels. It operates through several subsidiary brands: the ShareRoot platform for user-generated content (UGC) and brand ambassador programs (social walls, contests, and e-commerce optimization), The Social Science marketing agency focused on Australia's life sciences and health technology sectors, and Ludomade, which builds digital experiences spanning web design, mobile games, VR/AR, and experiential activations. ShareRoot publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures the company identity and a live domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ShearShare
providers.description: ShearShare is a B2B2C marketplace that lets salon and barbershop owners rent out unused chairs, booths, and suites to licensed beauty and barbering professionals on a flexible, on-demand basis — space-as-a-service for the hair, beauty, and grooming industry. Through its mobile app and web platform, independent stylists, barbers, and cosmetologists discover and book professional space by the day, while shop owners monetize idle capacity. Founded in 2015 by Dr. Tye Caldwell and Courtney Caldwell and headquartered in McKinney, Texas, the company has been featured on ABC's Shark Tank and is backed by 500 Global among other investors.

providers.name: Shelf Engine
providers.description: Shelf Engine was a Seattle-based technology company that used machine learning and AI-driven demand forecasting to help grocery retailers reduce food waste and optimize ordering of perishable and fresh food items. It offered a guaranteed-order model where its forecasting engine predicted demand and absorbed the risk of unsold inventory. Shelf Engine was acquired by / merged into Crisp (gocrisp.com), the retail data platform, and its independent brand is now defunct: shelfengine.com 301-redirects to gocrisp.com. No independent public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface is published under the Shelf Engine brand.

providers.name: Shellworks
providers.description: Shellworks is a materials-science company that produces VIVOMER, a home-compostable, biodegradable alternative to conventional plastic made through a natural fermentation process from agricultural waste. VIVOMER runs on standard plastic-manufacturing equipment, is certified for food contact (FDA and EU 10/2011), and biodegrades without leaving microplastics or toxic residue. Shellworks supplies these sustainable packaging materials to consumer brands across the UK, EU, and US. Backed by Version One Ventures, the company was surfaced as a portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a B2B climate / materials supplier with no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Sheroes
providers.description: Sheroes is a women-only social network and community platform based in India, founded in 2014 by Sairee Chahal. It gives women a safe, moderated space to connect, ask questions anonymously, seek support, learn, and grow across communities spanning careers, health, relationships, parenting, entrepreneurship, and personal finance. The platform operates a mobile app and website, offers helpline and expert support, and has expanded into women-focused financial services (MahilaMoney). Sheroes was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Sheroes exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or documented event/webhook surface; the site is a fully client-side single-page application. This profile therefore captures the company identity plus a live domain-security probe of its public host.

providers.name: ShoeDazzle
providers.description: ShoeDazzle is a California-based online fashion subscription retailer offering curated shoes, handbags, and accessories through a VIP membership model. Founded in March 2009 (early backers included Andreessen Horowitz and Lightspeed Venture Partners), it was acquired by JustFab in August 2013 and is now operated as a brand of TechStyle Fashion Group alongside Fabletics, JustFab, FabKids, and Savage X Fenty. ShoeDazzle is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation.

providers.name: Shoppr
providers.description: Shoppr was a Malaysia-based consumer fashion-discovery mobile app (launched May 2015, often described as the "Tinder of fashion") that let shoppers swipe through personalized clothing recommendations. The founding team, led by Kendrick Wong, subsequently pivoted the business into Omnilytics, a B2B fashion retail market-intelligence and analytics platform serving brands and retailers. As of this enrichment pass the associated domain omnilytics.co is a parked domain (nameservers lander.d.parity.domains) and neither Shoppr nor Omnilytics exposes any public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal. This entry originated as a 500 Global portfolio lead and is retained for record; it has no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Shopzilla
providers.description: Shopzilla is a comparison-shopping brand that lets consumers search across thousands of merchants to compare products, prices, and merchant ratings. Originally launched as BizRate and later Shopzilla, Inc., the business rebranded its corporate entity to Connexity in 2014 and is today operated by Connexity, a Taboola company, alongside sibling properties such as Bizrate, Beso, and PriceGrabber. Historically Shopzilla ran the Shopzilla Publisher Program, a CPC affiliate program whose Catalog API (the Bizrate and Beso APIs) exposed catalogued products, merchant offers, and ratings/reviews over a query-based RESTful web service returning XML or JSON. That legacy publisher API is no longer a documented, publicly onboardable developer program; the consumer shopzilla.com site remains live but publishes no current public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched with a domain-security probe pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Short Link
providers.description: Short URLs support so many domains

providers.name: Shots Mobile
providers.description: Shots Mobile, Inc. is the company founded by John and Sam Shahidi that built the Shots selfie photo-sharing app (2013) and grew from mobile-game studio RockLive into a podcast and media business. Today shots.com presents SHOTS as a media company that helps creators turn shows into businesses through partnerships, distribution, and growth resources. It publishes a marketing/content website on WordPress.com and exposes no first-party developer or API product surface; there is no public documentation, SDK, or hosted API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: SHRAPNEL
providers.description: SHRAPNEL is a AAA free-to-play extraction first-person shooter developed by Neon Machine and built on a dedicated Avalanche blockchain subnet. Early access launched on PC in February 2024, with a Steam listing and a player-driven economy: modding and creator tools for building skins and maps, a marketplace for tradable in-game items, and the SHRAP token. Neon Machine has publicly announced a Web3 developer API platform named GameBridge, but as of this profile it is not yet publicly documented — SHRAPNEL exposes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or docs portal, and shrapnel.com sits behind Cloudflare bot protection. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Polychain and tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Shriram City
providers.description: Shriram City (Shriram City Union Finance Ltd) was a leading Indian non-banking financial company (NBFC) in the Shriram Group, offering personal, business, two-wheeler, gold and small-enterprise loans plus fixed deposits. Founded 1986 in Chennai, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners. In November 2022 the company was amalgamated into Shriram Finance Ltd; its www.shriramcity.in host no longer resolves and the shriramcity.in apex now redirects to shriramfinance.in. No public developer or API program was found. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline: web search + live domain/security/well-known probes.

providers.name: Shunra
providers.description: Shunra Software (founded 1997, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) was an application performance engineering and network virtualization vendor whose products let teams emulate real-world network conditions to test application and mobile performance before deployment. Hewlett-Packard acquired Shunra's network virtualization business in March 2014 to expand its LoadRunner and Performance Center mobile-testing capabilities; the technology moved to HPE's software division and then to Micro Focus in 2016 (now part of OpenText). Shunra no longer operates as an independent company: the shunra.com domain redirects to HPE's domain-redirect 404 handler (nameservers softwaregrp.com) and there is no live product, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead but resolves to a defunct/absorbed company with nothing to enrich.

providers.name: Sibeam
providers.description: SiBEAM, Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company that pioneered 60GHz millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless technology and helped drive the WirelessHD standard for uncompressed wireless HD video and multi-gigabit data links. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment (sector: semiconductors). The enrichment pass found no independent public surface: SiBEAM was acquired by Silicon Image in 2011, and Silicon Image was in turn acquired by Lattice Semiconductor in 2015, so there is no live SiBEAM website, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Sigstr
providers.description: Sigstr was an Indianapolis-based email signature marketing and account-based marketing (ABM) platform that turned employee email signatures into a targeted marketing channel, backed by Battery Ventures and other investors. It was acquired by Terminus in September 2019 and folded into the Terminus platform as its Email Experiences / signature marketing product; the standalone Sigstr brand has since been retired. As of this enrichment pass the sigstr.com domain is a parked WP Engine page (HTTP 404), no api./developer. hosts resolve, and app.sigstr.com CNAMEs to Terminus infrastructure (email2.terminusplatform.com) — the company publishes no public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Silagroup
providers.description: SILA is a next-generation business services and real estate platform based in India, backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It delivers strategic solutions across Facility Management, Material Handling Services, Food & Catering, Real Estate Advisory, and Real Estate Development, supporting corporate entities, real estate funds, landowners, and developers throughout the entire real estate lifecycle. SILA runs a WordPress-based corporate website (silagroup.co.in) and publishes no public developer API surface; the only exposed HTTP API is the internal WordPress REST (wp-json) endpoint used to render the CMS. Enrichment confirmed no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, no /.well-known discovery documents, and no developer portal, SDKs, or docs as of this pass.

providers.name: Silicon Clocks
providers.description: Silicon Clocks is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lux-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: semiconductors. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Silicon Optix
providers.description: Silicon Optix Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company that designed image- and video-processing chips, best known for its Realta HQV (Hollywood Quality Video) processor for high-definition video scaling, de-interlacing, and noise reduction, and for the Teranex line of professional video processors. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners, it was acquired by Integrated Device Technology (IDT) in 2008 (IDT was subsequently acquired by Renesas). The company operated as a hardware/chip vendor and did not publish a public developer API; its historical primary domain (siliconoptix.com) no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a network stub with no live API surface.

providers.name: Silk
providers.description: Silk (Silk Security) was a cybersecurity company backed by Insight Partners that built an exposure, vulnerability and security-finding correlation / risk-prioritization platform. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain silk.security issues a verified 301 redirect to armis.com, indicating the company and product have been absorbed into Armis; no standalone Silk developer or API surface (developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or status page) is currently published, so there is no independent API to enrich beyond a domain-security probe of the still-live silk.security host.

providers.name: Silver Tail
providers.description: Silver Tail Systems was a website fraud and abuse detection company founded in 2008 in Menlo Park, California by Mike Eynon and Laura Mather, both formerly on the anti-fraud team at eBay/PayPal. Its product collected and analyzed real-time web traffic to deliver web session intelligence and predictive analytics that detected fraud, account takeover, and abuse on banking and commerce websites. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) among others, the company raised roughly $20M across three rounds before being acquired by RSA, the security division of EMC, in 2012 and rebranded as RSA Web Threat Detection. It no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no live developer or API surface.

providers.name: Silveredge
providers.description: Silveredge was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub from the 500 Global venture portfolio; the website property wired to this record (silverpush.co) presents Silverpush, an AI-powered contextual intelligence company that helps advertisers deliver contextually relevant, brand-safe video advertising across YouTube, CTV, TikTok, Meta, and the open web through its Mirrors contextual intelligence suite and Parallels moment-marketing platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface — developer subdomains do not resolve and developer paths return 404 — so there is no API artifact surface to harvest. This profile remains a company lead.

providers.name: Simple Feast
providers.description: Simple Feast was a Danish plant-based, ready-to-eat meal company surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the consumer app host food.simplefeast.com no longer resolves and the root domain simplefeast.com is parked on one.com nameservers, so the company appears defunct. No developer portal, API, documentation, or other machine-readable API surface could be discovered during enrichment; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Simplex
providers.description: Simplex (سيمبلكس) is an Egyptian industrial company representing local manufacturing and contributing to industrial development across Egypt, the Middle East, and Africa. Its public website (simplexarabia.com) is an Arabic catalog site focused on industrial spare parts and representation of Egyptian industry; it exposes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, or machine-readable specification. This profile was surfaced as a stub via VC-portfolio scraping and has no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: simplifile
providers.description: Simplifile is a real estate document collaboration and electronic recording (e-recording) network that connects settlement agents, lenders, and county recording offices to submit, track, and record property documents electronically. Its platform also covers post-closing collaboration, lien release, and trailing-document management for the mortgage and title industry. Simplifile is part of ICE Mortgage Technology (Intercontinental Exchange). This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched via live domain and endpoint probing; no public developer API surface was found.

providers.name: Simply
providers.description: Simply (hellosimply.com) is a consumer creative-learning company that makes AI-powered mobile apps for teaching music and art to beginners, with the stated mission of making the pursuit of creative hobbies simple and fun for all. Its product suite spans Simply Piano, Simply Guitar, Simply Sing, and the free Simply Tune tuner for music, plus Simply Draw for art, and a set of emerging extended-reality experiences including Simply Piano XR, Simply Piano for Apple Vision Pro and Google Android XR, and Simply Draw for Meta AI Glasses. Backed by GV, Simply is a direct-to-consumer subscription business and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; press inquiries are handled at press@hellosimply.com.

providers.name: Simply Measured
providers.description: Simply Measured was a Seattle-based social media analytics and reporting platform, founded in 2010 and backed by Trinity Ventures, that measured brand performance across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and other social channels. It was acquired by Sprout Social in December 2017 and its product, brand, and developer surface were sunset and folded into Sprout Social. The simplymeasured.com domain now 301-redirects to sproutsocial.com and no independent Simply Measured API, developer portal, or documentation remains online. This record is retained as a defunct/acquired portfolio-lead marker; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: SimplyCook
providers.description: SimplyCook is a UK-based recipe-box and meal-flavoring subscription service (tagline "For simple pleasures, SimplyCook.") that ships monthly boxes of flavor pots, stocks, and spice blends alongside curated recipes so subscribers can cook varied meals at home in around twenty minutes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. SimplyCook operates as a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand; it runs an internal application backend at api.simplycook.com but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile therefore carries only what could be genuinely probed: DNS/TLS/HTTP domain-security posture for the company domain.

providers.name: Simpo
providers.description: Simpo is a no-code digital adoption platform (DAP) that lets enterprise product and customer-success teams build in-app onboarding flows, guided walkthroughs, announcements, surveys, and contextual help without writing code. End users are guided at the point of need inside the software they already use, driving feature adoption, engagement, and retention. Founded in 2016 by Yohanan Hruschev and Yuval Karmi and headquartered in San Francisco, Simpo raised a $4.5M seed round led by Redpoint Ventures in 2019 and was acquired by WalkMe in October 2021. The product is a snippet/embed-installed browser layer rather than a public developer REST API; it exposes no OpenAPI, SDK, or public developer documentation surface, and the primary web host is no longer reachable following the acquisition.

providers.name: simsim
providers.description: simsim was an Accel-backed India-based social / video commerce startup (sector: consumer) that let creators sell products through short shoppable videos; it was acquired by Google in 2021 and wound down. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-21 confirm the simsim.in zone is live for email only (Google Workspace MX + SPF), with no resolving web host (apex or www), no api/app/developer/docs subdomains, and no reachable HTTPS, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: SingleHop
providers.description: SingleHop was a Chicago-based managed hosting, dedicated server, and cloud infrastructure provider, historically known for its LEAP customer control panel and API. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The SingleHop brand was acquired by INAP (Internap) in 2016 and has since been fully absorbed; the singlehop.com domain now HTTP 301-redirects to horizoniq.com (HorizonIQ, the successor infrastructure brand). No independent SingleHop developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface remains publicly reachable under the SingleHop brand.

providers.name: Singularity
providers.description: Singularity (Singularity Defense Corp) is a defense-technology company building low-cost, mass-producible air-defense and counter-weapon systems to protect warfighters and civilians from drones and cheap aerial munitions. Founded by engineers from SpaceX, Tesla, and Anduril alongside operators who have deployed air defenses in combat, the company emerged from stealth in July 2026 with an $80M Series A at a $400M valuation led by Khosla Ventures and Felicis, with Menlo Ventures, NEA, Y Combinator, Harpoon Ventures, and others participating. It emphasizes in-house manufacturing of major subsystems combined with commercial-volume components for rapid production and field deployment, including active conflict zones. Singularity is a hardware defense company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio lead and enriched with verified company identity by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Singularity Defense
providers.description: Singularity Defense Corp (operating on singularityus.com) is a defense-technology company building affordable, scalable counter-weapon air defense systems that protect warfighters and civilians from drones and low-cost, mass-produced munitions. Led by CEO Jack Oswald with COO Shail Giroux, the company is backed by Khosla Ventures, New Enterprise Associates, Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, Menlo Ventures, and Felicis. It ships physical air-defense hardware and publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; this enrichment pass confirmed the company has no public API surface.

providers.name: sinocelltech
providers.description: Sinocelltech (Beijing Sino Cell Biotechnology Group Co., Ltd.; Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market code 688520) is a biopharmaceutical research and development company founded in 2002 by Dr. Xie Liangzhi. It develops and commercializes recombinant protein and monoclonal antibody therapeutics across oncology, autoimmune disease, and infectious disease, together with preventive vaccines including a recombinant 14-valent HPV vaccine and COVID-19 vaccines. The company has multiple marketed products in China and a pipeline of clinical-stage candidates. It publishes no public developer platform, API, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: SIQ Basketball
providers.description: SIQ Basketball is a Techstars-backed sports-technology company that builds a FIBA-approved, sensor-embedded smart basketball and companion mobile app that automatically tracks shooting mechanics, makes and misses, shot arc and other performance data to coach players. Its technology is now marketed under the Spalding brand as the Spalding TF DNA Smart Basketball, sold with an app subscription. The company operates as a direct-to-consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its network identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Siri
providers.description: Siri began as Siri Inc., a spinout of SRI International's CALO artificial-intelligence program, backed by Menlo Ventures and Morgenthaler Ventures. The company shipped an iOS virtual-assistant app in February 2010 and was acquired by Apple in April 2010. Siri now ships as Apple's built-in voice assistant across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and HomePod. There is no independent public REST API or developer portal for Siri; the developer surface is SiriKit, an on-device Apple framework (Intents/App Intents) that lets iOS apps expose actions to Siri rather than call Siri as a web service.

providers.name: Sisu Data
providers.description: Sisu Data was an a16z-backed augmented-analytics / decision-intelligence startup that automatically surfaced key drivers and anomalies in structured business data. It was acquired by Snowflake in October 2023 and the standalone product and developer surface were subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass the sisudata.com domain no longer hosts a product, developer portal, API, or documentation — it 301-redirects to the LinkedIn "Sisu is joining forces with Snowflake" announcement, and its TLS certificate expired in November 2024. No public API surface exists to enrich; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio record only.

providers.name: SiteAdvisor, Inc.
providers.description: SiteAdvisor, Inc. is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: cybersecurity. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: SK Finance Ltd
providers.description: SK Finance Ltd (skfin.in) is a Jaipur, India-based non-banking financial company (NBFC) providing asset-backed retail lending. Its products span commercial vehicle, car, tractor, construction-equipment and two-wheeler loans alongside secured business loans and home-renovation / mortgage finance, delivered through a physical branch network with EMI calculators, online EMI payment, a branch locator, a loan-application portal and a customer "Refer and Earn" referral program. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate/marketing website (Next.js) with no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Skillbridge
providers.description: Skillbridge (skillbridge.co) was a New York-based online marketplace for freelance consultants and independent professionals, connecting organizations from Fortune 500 companies to early-stage startups with vetted specialists for short-term engagements. Founded in 2013, it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. Skillbridge was acquired by Toptal in 2016 and folded into what became Toptal Business; the skillbridge.co domain now 301-redirects to toptal.com/finance. The company operates no independent developer API, documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or event surface, so there are no technical artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Skims
providers.description: SKIMS is an American shapewear, loungewear, and apparel brand co-founded in 2019 by Kim Kardashian with Jens and Emma Grede, headquartered in Los Angeles. It sells solutionwear, underwear, loungewear, swim, and ready-to-wear direct-to-consumer through skims.com and via wholesale partners, and is the official underwear partner of the NBA, WNBA, and USA Basketball. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Thrive Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. This consumer retail brand publishes no public developer API surface; the profile carries a live domain-security probe of its web infrastructure.

providers.name: Skinseoul Lab
providers.description: Skinseoul Lab operates skin-seoul.com, a direct-to-consumer Korean beauty (K-beauty) e-commerce brand selling skincare and cosmetics to international customers, backed by 500 Global. Its public presence is a Next.js storefront fronted by Cloudflare with an Express commerce backend; enrichment probing (2026-07-21) found no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. The api.skin-seoul.com host returns only a plaintext "OK" health response, indicating an internal storefront backend rather than a documented public API.

providers.name: Skip Scooters
providers.description: Skip Scooters (operated by Skip Transport / Waybots) was a San Francisco-based dockless shared electric scooter (micromobility) startup and one of the early operators permitted in San Francisco, also running fleets in Washington, D.C. Backed by Accel, the company wound down and its assets moved to Helbiz around 2020. It is no longer operating: its former consumer app and rider domains (rideskip.com is a parked for-sale domain, skip.com now resolves to an unrelated retailer) have no live developer, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record; the enrichment pipeline found no public API to harvest.

providers.name: Skipjaq
providers.description: Skipjaq, Inc. was a machine-learning performance-optimisation startup that marketed itself as "Performance Optimisation as a Service" and was backed by Accel. Its proprietary automated workload-optimisation software ran repeated optimization tests against a customer's application (hosted in the cloud on AWS EC2 instances behind Elastic Load Balancers) and used machine learning to tune configuration for better application performance, throughput, and latency without manual, expert tuning. The product was delivered as a cloud SaaS and was offered under a beta test agreement. The company is now defunct: the skipjaq.com domain no longer resolves on any common TLD (.com/.io/.ai/.co.uk all return no A/NS records as of 2026-07-21), the last archived snapshot of the site dates to May 2025, and there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, first-party SDK, or live API surface. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio lead.

providers.name: Skybox Imaging
providers.description: Skybox Imaging was a high-resolution Earth-observation smallsat startup founded in 2009 out of Stanford University, building the SkySat constellation of small satellites to capture sub-meter commercial imagery and video. Backed by Canaan Partners among other venture investors, it was acquired by Google in 2014 for roughly $500M, renamed Terra Bella in 2016, and then sold to Planet Labs in 2017. The company no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no live developer API, docs, or discovery surface; this profile is retained as a portfolio-graph node for canaan-partners.

providers.name: Skyboximaging
providers.description: Skybox Imaging was a satellite imaging and geospatial-analytics company (founded 2009, Mountain View, CA) that built a constellation of small high-resolution Earth-observation satellites (SkySat) and the analytics to turn frequent imagery into commercial insight. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Bessemer, Khosla Ventures and others, it was acquired by Google in 2014 (~$500M), renamed Terra Bella, and its satellite business was sold to Planet Labs in 2017. The skyboximaging.com domain is no longer a live product surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph and historical reference.

providers.name: SkyGiraffe
providers.description: SkyGiraffe was an enterprise-grade mobility platform that let companies build customized, job-specific mobile apps with no coding, connecting mobile workforces to corporate systems of record such as SAP, Oracle, Salesforce and ServiceNow. In 2016 the company added developer access, exposing a single secure endpoint for third-party apps to read from and write to those backend enterprise systems through the SkyGiraffe platform. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global), Microsoft Ventures, and Trilogy Equity Partners across ~$10.5M in funding, SkyGiraffe was acquired by ServiceNow on October 25, 2017 and its technology and team were absorbed into ServiceNow's Now Platform mobile capabilities. The independent skygiraffe.com domain no longer hosts a product, developer portal, or API — it 301-redirects to ServiceNow's acquisition announcement — so there is no live, independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Skyport Systems *
providers.description: Skyport Systems was a cloud infrastructure security startup, backed by GV and other investors, best known for SkySecure — a hyperconverged secure server appliance that enforced workload isolation and firewall policy in dedicated hardware for critical enterprise data-center workloads. Cisco acquired the company on January 24, 2018 and did not continue the standalone SkySecure offering, so Skyport Systems no longer operates as an independent company. Enrichment found no live developer surface: skyportsystems.com is a parked/for-sale domain and skyportsystems.net now serves an unrelated cybersecurity news aggregator. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record (surfaced as a GV portfolio company) with no public API, developer portal, or SDKs to catalog.

providers.name: Skypunk
providers.description: Skypunk is an independent game studio headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2021 to build new science-fiction multiplayer games. The studio is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and has raised approximately $750K in early funding. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Skypunk is a consumer game developer, not an API producer: its public presence is a studio marketing site and it publishes no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or any external API surface at this time.

providers.name: Slauson & Co.
providers.description: Slauson & Co. is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Los Angeles, founded in 2020 by Austin Clements and Ajay Relan and named for the South LA avenue where the two first met. Rooted in economic inclusion, the firm invests at the pre-seed and seed stage in SMB software tools for the next generation of small-business owners and in culturally relevant consumer products and services, backing founders who have historically been overlooked by traditional venture capital. Slauson & Co. has raised a $100M Fund II — backed by tech companies including Google, Meta and PayPal — and runs the Friends & Family accelerator that pairs non-dilutive grants with hands-on programming. Portfolio companies include Sienna Naturals, Pressed Roots, A-Frame Brands, Charger Help, Bags and Prado.

providers.name: SLF
providers.description: German city, country, river, database

providers.name: Slime Sandwich
providers.description: Slime Sandwich was an online gaming company that developed in-browser 3D games. It was founded in 2009 in Englewood, Colorado by Douglas Glover, Vadim Ugov, and former Photobucket CEO Alex Welch, and raised a $2.75M Series A round backed by Battery Ventures. The company has since permanently ceased operations and its slimesandwich.com domain is no longer active (now a parked/for-sale listing). It was originally surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; enrichment confirms there is no live company website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to profile.

providers.name: Small Giant Games
providers.description: Small Giant Games is a Helsinki, Finland based mobile game studio best known for the hit puzzle-RPG Empires & Puzzles. Founded in 2013, the studio was acquired by Zynga in 2018 (now part of Take-Two Interactive) and continues to operate its live free-to-play mobile titles. As a consumer mobile gaming company it publishes player-facing games and support resources rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and EQT Ventures and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline, which found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, package/SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface — only a live consumer marketing website.

providers.name: Smalt
providers.description: Smalt is a Berlin-based training academy and technology platform for the green-energy installation trades. It combines a B2B installation services business (solar and, increasingly, heat pumps and other climate-trade work) with an education platform that upskills and certifies installers, plus a franchise model that lets trained installers run their own training businesses on Smalt's learning materials and tooling. Founded in 2023 and backed by General Catalyst, noa, Owl Ventures, Heartfelt, La Famiglia and Loric Ventures, Smalt is a workforce/services company rather than an API provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface to catalog.

providers.name: Smart Reno
providers.description: Smart Reno is a Montreal-based home-renovation marketplace, founded in 2012 by Andrei Uglar, that connects homeowners with qualified, available local contractors. Homeowners post a project and receive up to three competing quotes from vetted renovation professionals through a proprietary contractor-matching platform. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), Anges Quebec, and BDC, Smart Reno was acquired by RBC Ventures in 2019 and now operates its consumer marketplace under the soumissionrenovation.ca brand across Quebec, Ontario, and Alberta. The company exposes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or webhook surface; smartreno.com 301-redirects to the successor site and no /.well-known discovery documents were found.

providers.name: Smarterer
providers.description: Smarterer was a Boston-based skills-assessment company that used crowdsourced, adaptive tests to rapidly quantify people's proficiency across 400+ technical, social, and business skills. Backed by Google Ventures (GV), it opened a REST API in March 2015 that let partners embed tests, pull score data, and build leaderboards and profiles on top of its assessment engine. Pluralsight acquired Smarterer for roughly $75M in November 2014, absorbed its test engine into the Pluralsight learning platform, and wound down the standalone product. The smarterer.com domain no longer serves a site (defensively held via MarkMonitor, no DNS A record) and there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Smith
providers.description: Smith (GoSmith, Inc.) was an app- and web-based marketplace for home-improvement and remodeling services, founded in 2012 in Sunnyvale, California and part of the 500 Startups (500 Global) accelerator's 8th batch in 2014. Homeowners listed a project to receive quotes from up to five researched and vetted local contractors, with scheduling and payment tooling for the professionals. As of this enrichment pass the gosmith.com domain still resolves (AWS/Google Workspace DNS) but serves no website (HTTP/HTTPS connections time out), and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Snapette
providers.description: Snapette was a mobile fashion-discovery and local-shopping application that operated from 2011 to 2013, letting users photograph, share, and discover fashion items and nearby boutique inventory. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), it was acquired by PriceGrabber in 2013 and subsequently ceased operations. This API Evangelist profile is retained as an archival portfolio-company record; the company publishes no developer program, API, or SDK surface. The snapette.com domain now serves only an archival page documenting the app's history, founders, and business model.

providers.name: Snapfinger
providers.description: Snapfinger was an online and mobile food-ordering platform that let diners browse menus and place takeout and delivery orders across a network of restaurant brands. The snapfinger.com domain now 301-redirects to Tillster, the restaurant-commerce company (ordering, kiosk, loyalty, menu, and data solutions for 40,000+ restaurants), so Snapfinger operates today as a defunct brand absorbed into Tillster. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published under the Snapfinger name. It remains in the API Evangelist network as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio lead pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: SnapShyft
providers.description: SnapShyft is an on-demand staffing marketplace that connects hospitality, food-and-beverage, and events venues with vetted gig workers for short-notice shifts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (snapshyft.com) serves a coming-soon placeholder page and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, changelog, or /.well-known discovery surface. The only machine-verifiable signal harvested was domain/transport security (TLS 1.3, HSTS, DMARC quarantine); the profile remains a lead awaiting a live developer surface.

providers.name: Soasta
providers.description: SOASTA was a web and mobile performance-testing company known for CloudTest (cloud-based load and performance testing) and mPulse (real user monitoring / RUM). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. SOASTA was acquired by Akamai Technologies (its products were folded into Akamai's mPulse and CloudTest offerings); the former soasta.com domain now 301-redirects to akamai.com, so SOASTA no longer operates an independent developer portal, API surface, or product presence of its own.

providers.name: Socialcam
providers.description: Socialcam was a mobile social video application (iPhone, Android, Windows Phone) for capturing, editing, and sharing short videos across social networks. Founded by Michael Seibel, Ammon Bartram, and Guillaume Luccisano out of Y Combinator (W2012) and backed by a16z, it reached roughly 16 million downloads and was acquired by Autodesk in July 2012 for $60 million. The consumer service was discontinued on October 28, 2015, and socialcam.com no longer resolves to a live web host (AWS Route 53 nameservers only, no A record), so there is no developer portal, API, documentation, or agent surface to enrich.

providers.name: Socialee
providers.description: Socialee is a beauty shopping platform that blends social media with e-commerce, letting shoppers discover and buy products through shoppable videos, write reviews, and earn rewards as creators. Its catalog spans makeup, skincare, fragrance, haircare, and bath & body, with next-day delivery and 7-day returns. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; an enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public API, developer portal, or .well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Sockeye Networks
providers.description: Sockeye Networks was a network-management software company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. It provided intelligent internet routing and connectivity-optimization services, combining real-time global internet traffic data with customer-specific measurements to optimize enterprise IP connectivity for improved network performance, efficiency, and visibility. The company appears to be defunct or long-inactive; no active website domain resolves and no public developer/API surface, documentation, or specifications could be found during enrichment.

providers.name: Socra AI
providers.description: Socra AI operates Socra Tutor (소크라 튜터), a Korean-market, AI-powered education service that describes itself as an intelligent AI answer-comparison service — students submit problems and Socra compares and evaluates candidate answers using AI to help them learn. It is a consumer-facing edtech mobile/web application rather than a developer platform; as of this profile no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation could be found. Socra AI was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Socrates
providers.description: Socrates (socrates.ai) was an AI-powered virtual employee assistant that answered day-to-day employee questions across HR, IT, and workplace services. It has been acquired by Simpplr and is no longer a standalone product: the socrates.ai domain now redirects to simpplr.com/socrates-ai/ and the technology ships as the Simpplr "AI Assistant" within their employee experience platform. No independent Socrates developer portal, API reference, or public API surface exists; developer resources, if any, live under Simpplr. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record surfaced from the Norwest Venture Partners portfolio.

providers.name: Socratic
providers.description: Socratic is an AI-powered homework help and learning app that lets students photograph or type a question and receive curated explanations, videos, and step-by-step resources across math, science, literature, and social studies. Founded in 2013 and backed at the early stage by investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Socratic was acquired by Google in 2018 and now operates as "Socratic by Google," a free consumer mobile app whose homework-help capabilities have largely been folded into Google Lens. Socratic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documented developer surface; this profile records it as an acquired consumer product with no independent API footprint.

providers.name: SODA
providers.description: SODA Inc. (株式会社SODA) is a Japanese consumer-technology company that operates SNKRDUNK (スニーカーダンク / スニダン), one of Japan's largest consumer-to-consumer marketplaces for sneakers, trading cards ("トレカ"), apparel, and accessories. The SNKRDUNK app lets users buy and sell collectible and secondary-market goods with professional in-house authentication (真贋鑑定 by プロ鑑定士) and a full purchase-protection / compensation guarantee, alongside a buyback service. SODA is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. As a consumer marketplace app, SODA publishes no public developer program or API at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Soff
providers.description: Soff is an AI-powered quoting platform for U.S. distributors that turns inbound RFQs into won deals. It automatically captures requests for quotes from email, generates instant quotes and PDFs, tracks quote performance (won vs. lost), logs activity into ERP/CRM systems, and analyzes customer behavior and lost-deal reasons. Backed by Y Combinator (S24) and General Catalyst, based in San Francisco, and SOC 2 Type II certified. As of this enrichment pass Soff publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Soha Systems
providers.description: Soha Systems was a cloud-delivered secure application access company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California. Its "Soha Cloud" service let enterprises grant users and third parties fast, secure, per-application access to internal apps without a traditional VPN, an early software-defined perimeter / zero-trust network access (ZTNA) approach. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Menlo Ventures, and Cervin Ventures, Soha Systems was acquired by Akamai Technologies in October 2016, and its technology became the basis for Akamai Enterprise Application Access (EAA). The company no longer operates independently and publishes no standalone developer portal, documentation, or public API; its former domain (soha.io) now resolves only to Akamai edge infrastructure and serves no content.

providers.name: Sold *
providers.description: Sold * was a consumer resale service (a mobile app that sold your unwanted items on your behalf, handling pricing, listing, and fulfillment). Backed by GV, the Sold team was acqui-hired by Dropbox; the service was shut down and no longer accepts items. The homepage at usesold.com now serves only an acquisition/shutdown notice. No developer portal, API, documentation, or well-known surface exists (all api/developer/docs subdomains fail to resolve; /.well-known/*, /llms.txt, and /openapi.json return 404). Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Soldsie
providers.description: Soldsie was a social-commerce platform founded in 2012 in San Francisco by Chris Bennett and Arrel Gray that let retailers sell directly through social media: customers bought products by commenting "Sold" on a merchant's Facebook or Instagram post, while a backend dashboard handled invoicing, customer tracking, and waitlists. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and e.ventures, it raised roughly $1M in seed funding and a $4M Series A (2014), and had processed over $25M in transactions across more than 1,000 merchants. The product is now defunct: the soldsie.com apex no longer resolves and www.soldsie.com returns a broken redirect, so there is no live developer portal, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Sole Society
providers.description: Sole Society is a women's footwear, handbags, jewelry, and accessories e-commerce brand, surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the standalone brand no longer operates its own storefront. The domain solesociety.com resolves to MarkMonitor-managed nameservers, its HTTPS endpoints do not respond, and http://solesociety.com redirects (HTTP 200) to https://www.dsw.com/, so the domain appears to have been folded into DSW / Designer Brands. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, MCP server, or other machine-readable API surface was found for this brand. This profile remains a lead-stage company record with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Solugen
providers.description: Solugen is a chemical manufacturing company that produces sustainable industrial chemicals through its proprietary Bioforge platform, which combines engineered enzymes, metal catalysis, and modular process design to convert renewable feedstocks into products with minimal waste. Solugen serves markets including oil and gas, renewable fuels, aerospace and defense, water treatment, cleaning, agriculture, concrete, and personal care. Backed by Founders Fund, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass Solugen publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Solvvy
providers.description: Solvvy was a conversational-AI and customer-support automation platform that let companies deploy self-service virtual agents to understand end-customer questions, resolve issues, and deflect support tickets across chat and web channels. Zoom announced a definitive agreement to acquire Solvvy in May 2022 and folded its natural-language and workflow-automation technology into Zoom Contact Center and the Zoom Virtual Agent product. As of this profile the standalone Solvvy brand is discontinued: solvvy.com no longer serves a site (HTTPS connection refused) and the company publishes no independent, live public API, developer portal, or documentation. This repo is retained as a historical company record; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Sonera
providers.description: Sonera is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of amplify-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ai-ml. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Sonoma Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Sonoma Biotherapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing engineered regulatory T cell (Treg) therapies to restore immune balance in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Building on Nobel Prize-winning Treg biology, its lead program SBT-77-7101 is in Phase 1 clinical trials for conditions including refractory rheumatoid arthritis and hidradenitis suppurativa. Backed by 8VC and GV, the company operates in cell therapy and does not publish a public developer API surface. Sector: biotech.

providers.name: Sooth
providers.description: Sooth (Sooth Labs, Inc.) is an AI research company building a "World Model for Global Foresight" — a continuously trained forecasting engine that integrates economic, geopolitical, and operational signals into calibrated probability forecasts for high-stakes decisions. Its platform is described in three parts: the Sooth Engine (a world model that reasons across domains), Sooth Chronology (autonomous agents that collect and prioritize signals), and Sooth Proof (cryptographically committed, calibrated forecasts with an auditable track record). Founded by veterans of frontier AI at Meta and Carnegie Mellon and backed by Felicis, the company is pre-product as of mid-2026 and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Sora
providers.description: Sora Schools is a fully online, project-based independent middle and high school (soraschools.com), backed by Union Square Ventures. Students learn through interdisciplinary, interest-driven projects and live small-group expeditions rather than traditional grade-level classes, with an accredited diploma path. It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Union Square Ventures portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the public site is served behind a Cloudflare bot challenge and Sora publishes no public developer, API, or integrations program, so this profile carries only probed infrastructure signals (DNS/TLS/security) rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Sosh
providers.description: Sosh was a San Francisco-based social-discovery mobile app (founded 2010) that acted as a "social concierge," giving members a personalized collection of local activities, events, and places to do and share. It was backed by Battery Ventures and Khosla Ventures among others. Sosh was acqui-hired by on-demand delivery service Postmates in November 2015 and the consumer app was subsequently discontinued. Enrichment research (WebFetch) found no surviving product, developer portal, documentation, or public API; the sosh.com domain is now a parked "for sale" listing. There is no live API surface to enrich, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Soufflé Therapeutics
providers.description: Soufflé Therapeutics is a genetic medicine company developing nucleic acid (siRNA) therapeutics that use proprietary cell-specific ligand-conjugation technology to target and deliver treatments to specific cell types. Its initial programs address muscle and heart disorders, with first therapies targeting Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy (FSHD) and genetically-driven cardiomyopathies, with clinical trials expected to begin in 2026. The company is headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts and was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. It is a therapeutics/pharmaceutical company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Space Ape
providers.description: Space Ape Games is a London-based mobile game studio founded in 2012 and now part of Supercell, known for live-service mobile titles including Beatstar, Fastlane: Road to Revenge, Transformers: Earth Wars, Samurai Siege, and Rival Kingdoms. The studio operates in the consumer gaming sector and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; its primary web presence redirects to Supercell. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which found no public API surface and captured domain-security posture for the studio domain.

providers.name: Space Runners
providers.description: Space Runners is a digital fashion company that designs and launches digital wearable NFTs for metaverses in collaboration with celebrities and brands. Positioned at the intersection of Web3, gaming, and consumer fashion, the company produces branded digital sneakers, apparel, and wearable collectibles for use across metaverse platforms. Backed by Accel and Pantera Capital, Space Runners operates a consumer-facing brand and marketplace rather than a developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Spaceape
providers.description: Space Ape Games is a London-based mobile game developer, founded in 2012, that became part of Supercell after Supercell took a majority stake in 2017 and fully acquired the studio. As a consumer mobile-gaming studio it ships player-facing game titles rather than a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass the former company site spaceapegames.com returns an HTTP 302 redirect to supercell.com, and no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published for Space Ape Games or its parent Supercell (Supercell references only a Developer Grants Program, not an API). This profile was surfaced as a northzone portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; it currently exposes no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Spacejoy
providers.description: Spacejoy is an online interior design platform that pairs customers with professional designers to reimagine their spaces. Users share a room photo and requirements, then receive photo-realistic 3D renderings, curated furniture and decor recommendations, and shoppable design boards that link directly to retailers such as Wayfair, Article, Crate & Barrel, and CB2. The service covers living rooms, bedrooms, dining rooms, home offices, nurseries, entryways, and outdoor spaces, and operates an integrated storefront at shop.spacejoy.com plus an iOS mobile app. Spacejoy is a direct-to-consumer design service with no public developer program, API, or documentation surface as of this profile. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel.

providers.name: Spacemaker
providers.description: Spacemaker was a Norwegian proptech startup (founded 2016 in Oslo) that built cloud-based, AI-assisted generative design software for early-stage real estate and urban site planning, letting architects, developers, and urban planners rapidly explore massing, sunlight, wind, noise, and view analyses to optimize buildable sites. Backed by investors including Northzone, Spacemaker was acquired by Autodesk in November 2020 (reported ~$240M) and its technology was continued and rebranded as Autodesk Forma. The standalone spacemaker.ai domain now permanently (301) redirects to the Autodesk Forma product page, so there is no longer an independent Spacemaker developer portal, API, or documentation surface; developer/API access is provided through Autodesk Forma and the broader Autodesk Platform Services ecosystem.

providers.name: SpeedHome
providers.description: SpeedHome is a Malaysian online property rental marketplace that connects landlords and tenants directly, best known for its zero-deposit rental model backed by tenancy protection. The platform covers listing, tenant screening, digital tenancy agreements, rent collection, and landlord protection through its consumer-facing web and mobile applications. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Spenny
providers.description: Spenny is an Indian personal-finance and micro-investing app that works like a digital piggy bank, rounding up everyday spending on cards, UPI, and netbanking and automatically investing the spare change. Users can put round-ups and lump sums (from as little as Rs. 10) into digital gold and curated mutual fund baskets, with no lock-ins and anytime withdrawals. Spenny is a consumer mobile application and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: SPES (speschina)
providers.description: SPES (诗裴丝) is a China-based consumer personal-care and beauty brand operating a direct-to-consumer business across Chinese e-commerce and social-commerce channels, including its Tmall flagship store, a JD.com storefront, and Douyin, Xiaohongshu (RED), and Weibo social accounts, with a WeChat official account. The brand runs a marketing website (a Vue.js / Element UI single-page app served from Alibaba Cloud) and was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It does not currently publish any public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation; the only HTTP API referenced by its site is a private content backend for the marketing pages. This profile records the enrichment pass that confirmed there is no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Spider Fleet
providers.description: Spiderfleet (Spider Fleet) is a Mexico-based intelligent fleet-management platform that helps businesses run and maintain their vehicle fleets. Its public site (spider.com.mx, in Spanish) markets fleet onboarding ("Flotillas"), preventive maintenance scheduling ("mantenimientos"), and quote requests ("cotizacion") for fleet operators, and is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a static marketing website with no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specification; two navigation links (contact and login) return 404 and the site's TLS certificate is expired.

providers.name: Spiff
providers.description: Spiff was a sales commission and incentive compensation management (ICM) platform that automated commission calculations, gave sales reps real-time earnings visibility, and streamlined finance-side reconciliation for revenue teams. Founded in Utah and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Norwest Venture Partners, Spiff was acquired by Salesforce in 2024 and folded into Sales Cloud as "Salesforce Spiff" / Incentive Compensation Management. As of this profile the standalone spiff.com and app.spiff.com properties redirect to salesforce.com, and no independent Spiff public API, developer portal, documentation, or OpenAPI surface remains discoverable — its capabilities are now delivered through the Salesforce platform.

providers.name: Spindle Technologies
providers.description: Spindle Technologies (spindle.ai) was an Accel-backed AI startup that was acquired by Salesforce; as of this enrichment pass its entire domain — including the docs, developer, api, and app subdomains — issues a 301 redirect to salesforce.com/agentforce, so it no longer operates an independent developer portal, API, documentation, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as a network record of the company and its acquisition. No standalone API artifacts could be harvested. Domain-level security posture (TLS/DNSSEC/SPF/DMARC on spindle.ai) was probed and captured.

providers.name: SpinLaunch
providers.description: SpinLaunch is a space technology company developing a kinetic launch system that uses a rotating carbon-fiber arm inside a large vacuum chamber to accelerate launch vehicles to thousands of kilometers per hour before ignition, aiming to eliminate up to 70 percent of the fuel and structure of a conventional rocket. It operates a Suborbital Accelerator test facility at Spaceport America in New Mexico that doubles as a customer payload-testing platform, and is developing an Orbital Launch System alongside its Meridian satellite broadband constellation for enterprise connectivity. Backed by GV, the company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Spiritus
providers.description: Spiritus Technologies is a climate-tech company building low-cost direct air capture (DAC) technology that removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Its core carbon-dioxide-removal system and its Orchard Power product (pairing DAC with waste heat for net-zero power) target dramatically lower energy use and capital cost than existing DAC. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Aramco Ventures, and Mitsubishi, with carbon-removal customers including Shopify, Stripe, and Frontier. Based in White Rock, New Mexico. This is a physical carbon-removal hardware company and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: Spoke
providers.description: SPOKE (spoke-london.com) is a London-based direct-to-consumer men's fashion retailer specializing in tailored menswear engineered for precise fit, with the tagline "A flawless fit, delivered." Its range spans trousers, denim, shirts, knitwear, shorts, tailoring (suits and jackets) and accessories, sold through an e-commerce storefront with a "Fit Finder" sizing tool. Backed by Seedcamp and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. An enrichment pass found no public developer program, API, or developer documentation; the company operates a standard retail e-commerce storefront only.

providers.name: Spoon University
providers.description: Spoon University is a food and lifestyle content platform for the next generation of college students, publishing recipes, food news, restaurant reviews, cooking how-tos, and campus dining coverage across hundreds of university chapters. It is owned and operated by Her Campus Media, LLC (Boston, MA), the media company behind Her Campus, College Fashionista, InfluenceHer Collective, and Generation Hired. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and Uncork Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Spoon University publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation — it is a consumer content brand, not an API provider — so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: SpoonRocket
providers.description: SpoonRocket was an on-demand, prepared-meal delivery startup backed by a16z that delivered low-cost ready-to-eat meals on demand. The company has since ceased operations and its spoonrocket.com domain no longer resolves to a live website (AWS Route53 nameservers remain delegated, but there is no A record). It publishes no developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or public API surface. This profile remains in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead with no active API to enrich.

providers.name: Springpath
providers.description: Springpath Inc. was a Sunnyvale, California hyperconverged infrastructure startup, backed by Redpoint Ventures, whose distributed data-platform technology became the basis for Cisco HyperFlex Systems. Cisco moved to acquire the company (announced 2016) and folded its software into the HyperFlex product line. Cisco announced the discontinuation of HyperFlex infrastructure products in September 2023, and Springpath no longer operates as an independent company. The springpathinc.com domain is now served by Cisco nameservers and no longer hosts a live website, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an historical/acquired-company record; there is no independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: SpringRole
