providers.description: SpringRole was a blockchain-based professional reputation and attestation platform — an endorsement and verified-resume network that let people attest to each other's skills and work history on-chain — and was a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Its primary domain, springrole.com, now issues a 301 redirect to Springworks (springworks.in), an HR-technology company whose products include SpringVerify (background verification), Goodfit (AI-native recruitment), and EngageWith (employee engagement). An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, developer portal, SDK/package, MCP server, llms.txt, or /.well-known discovery documents for SpringRole (the well-known paths return the Webflow marketing SPA, not real artifacts), and no separate developer or docs subdomain resolves.

providers.name: Sqreen
providers.description: Sqreen was a Paris- and San Francisco-based application security company offering Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP), an in-app Web Application Firewall, and account-takeover and attack protection delivered through language agents for Node.js, Python, Ruby, PHP, Java and Go. Backed by Y Combinator, Greylock and Point Nine, Sqreen was acquired by Datadog in 2021 and its technology was folded into Datadog Application Security Management. The standalone sqreen.com product, dashboard and developer APIs have since been decommissioned; the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical company lead and has no live, independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: St. Bernard Software
providers.description: St. Bernard Software was a San Diego-based web-security company (iPrism web-filtering appliances) that rebranded to EdgeWave and whose technology and domains now resolve to the successor cybersecurity provider GoSecure (gosecure.ai / gosecure.net). The St. Bernard Software brand is defunct: an enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 confirmed stbernard.com presents a *.gosecure.net certificate and edgewave.com 301-redirects to gosecure.ai. The successor company GoSecure offers 24/7 managed detection and response services and publishes no developer portal or public API. This company therefore has no independent, live API surface to enrich, and no API artifacts were created (attributing GoSecure's surface to this legacy slug would conflate two distinct companies).

providers.name: Stabilitas
providers.description: Stabilitas was a Techstars-backed crisis and risk-intelligence startup whose stabilitas.io domain now issues a 301 redirect to crisis24.com/lp/onsolve. The company was absorbed into OnSolve, which is today part of Crisis24 (a GardaWorld company) providing critical event management, mass notification, travel risk, and security intelligence. Stabilitas no longer operates as an independent brand and exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal of its own. This profile is retained as an acquired/defunct portfolio lead; there is no standalone API surface left to enrich.

providers.name: StableBrowse
providers.description: StableBrowse is a San Francisco startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building browser infrastructure and real-world data pipelines for AI agents and AI labs. Its platform transforms dynamic websites into structured knowledge and execution graphs so agents can reliably complete web-based tasks — form filling, data extraction, authentication flows, and website change detection — without relearning workflows on every run, and it sources, labels, and enriches hard-to-find long-tail, gated, and ephemeral web data until it is worth training on. StableBrowse markets performance gains including large reductions in token usage, faster workflow execution, and high task success rates across use cases such as price monitoring, loan applications, CRM updates, travel booking, and navigation of legacy enterprise systems. The company was founded by Jay Mehta, Deepit Shah, and Somansh Shah (all formerly of Amazon). As of this profile the public site is a marketing landing page with no published API, developer documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: StackSocial
providers.description: StackSocial is a consumer e-commerce and daily-deals marketplace operated by StackCommerce, selling software, online courses, gadgets, and digital goods at discounted prices. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The public surface is a bot-protected single-page storefront; enrichment probes found no publicly documented API, OpenAPI specification, SDK packages, MCP server, well-known metadata, or llms.txt on the stacksocial.com host as of this pass.

providers.name: Stailer
providers.description: Stailer (ステイラー) is a retail-commerce platform built by 10X, Inc. (株式会社10X) that lets Japanese supermarket, drugstore, and other retail chains vertically launch and operate their own branded e-commerce and online-grocery services. It provides the consumer storefront apps, order management, in-store picking and fulfillment, and delivery operations that let established brick-and-mortar retailers stand up online shopping quickly. Stailer is a B2B SaaS offering sold through direct enterprise engagement; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, documentation portal, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Staked
providers.description: Staked was an institutional cryptocurrency staking and delegation provider that ran validator infrastructure and non-custodial staking services across proof-of-stake networks including Ethereum, Solana, Polkadot, and Cosmos. Founded in 2018 and backed by Pantera Capital, Staked was acquired by Kraken in December 2021 and its products have since been folded into Kraken Staking. The former staked.us domain now serves a static notice redirecting users to staking.kraken.com and kraken.com/institutions/staking; no independent developer portal, public API, or documentation surface remains under the Staked brand.

providers.name: StalkBuyLove
providers.description: StalkBuyLove was an India-based online women's fashion e-commerce retailer, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the brand appears defunct as an independent property, since the stalkbuylove.com domain now returns a 301 permanent redirect to styched.in (Styched, an unrelated Shopify-powered Indian youth-fashion retailer). No public developer portal, API, SDK, MCP server, changelog, or other machine-readable API surface could be found for StalkBuyLove on any registry or well-known path. The only honest signal available is the domain, DNS, and TLS security posture of the redirecting host, captured in the domain-security artifact.

providers.name: Standard Chartered
providers.description: A British multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in London with a strong focus on Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. Provides corporate, institutional, and consumer banking across more than 50 markets globally.

providers.name: Standard Economics
providers.description: Standard Economics is building an "economic computer" aimed at financial inclusion and intelligent capital allocation at global scale, describing a system with memory, judgment, and the ability to improve its own decisions to deliver economic security. Its product surface is Uno (uno.global). The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Paradigm, and was added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery. As of the latest enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this profile currently carries only a domain-security posture probe.

providers.name: Star Analytics
providers.description: Star Analytics is a business-intelligence software company described as a market leader in process automation and application integration across hybrid computing environments, with products built to address the automation and integration requirements of business intelligence software. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public developer platform, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; the primary domain (staranalytics.com) resolves to a parking IP and does not serve HTTPS, consistent with a legacy company that is no longer independently operating.

providers.name: StarOfService
providers.description: StarOfService is an online local-services marketplace that connects consumers with vetted service professionals across home improvement, events, wellness, lessons, and business services. Headquartered in France and operating across multiple European markets, the platform matches customer project requests to nearby providers and facilitates quotes and messaging between them. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company exposes a consumer web marketplace and has no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Stateless
providers.description: Stateless was a Boulder, Colorado network-infrastructure startup (founded 2016) that built a software platform for network automation in the hybrid multi-cloud era, delivering network functions such as firewalls and load balancers through an "as a service" consumption model with an emphasis on simplicity, scalability, and evolvability. Backed by Speedinvest, the National Science Foundation, Drive Capital, and Matchstick Ventures, with its last funding announced in December 2022. The company now appears defunct — its former domains (stateless.net, getstateless.com) redirect to domain-parking "for sale" pages and no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface remains.

providers.name: Statwing
providers.description: Statwing was a self-serve statistical-analysis SaaS tool that let non-statisticians run and interpret analyses on survey and spreadsheet data through a point-and-click interface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-21) found no live company or developer surface. Statwing was acquired by Qualtrics in 2015 and the product discontinued, and the statwing.com domain now serves an unrelated Thai-language lifestyle site. No API, documentation, SDKs, or developer resources exist.

providers.name: Steelbrick
providers.description: SteelBrick was a Configure-Price-Quote (CPQ) SaaS vendor backed by IVP and Shasta Ventures before it was acquired by Salesforce (announced December 2015, closed 2016) and folded into the product now shipped as Salesforce CPQ (formerly Salesforce Revenue Cloud). The steelbrick.com domain is no longer an independent surface: its apex 301-redirects to salesforce.com/sales/cpq/ and the www host serves a broken default CloudFront certificate. There is no standalone SteelBrick developer portal, documentation, or public API — any live API surface belongs to Salesforce CPQ. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead / acquisition record; enrichment found no independent API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Stoicism Quote
providers.description: Quotes about Stoicism

providers.name: Storability
providers.description: Storability Software was an enterprise storage resource management (SRM) company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Southborough, Massachusetts. It built software to simplify and centralize the management of complex, multi-site, multi-vendor storage infrastructures, raising roughly $67M from investors including Battery Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Madison Dearborn Partners. The company was acquired by Storage Technology Corporation (StorageTek) on October 11, 2004, and no longer operates as an independent entity. It has no surviving website, developer portal, or public API surface.

providers.name: Storemaven
providers.description: Storemaven was an app-store-optimization (ASO) and app-marketing platform founded in Tel Aviv in 2015 that pioneered App Store / Google Play A/B testing of icons, screenshots and videos using predictive, machine-learning-driven creative testing to lift install conversion rates for mobile app publishers. It was acquired by Zynga (Take-Two) in September 2022 and folded into the company's growth org, now operating as "mavens, a Zynga company." Storemaven shipped a login-gated SaaS dashboard and published no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal; the original storemaven.com domain has since lapsed and been repurposed into an unrelated third-party review site. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead with no independent API surface.

providers.name: Storia Originals, Inc.
providers.description: Storia Originals, Inc. (doing business as Storiaverse) was a Los Angeles-based consumer mobile entertainment startup founded in 2023 by Agnes Kozera and David Kierzkowski. Its Storiaverse app pioneered a patent-pending "read-watch" format blending short-form reading, animation, and audio, connecting writers and animators to publish and monetize original stories across sci-fi, fantasy, horror, mystery, and comedy, including adaptations of HarperCollins titles. It raised a pre-seed round led by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; both its marketing site (storia.io) and its iOS/Android app store listings are no longer reachable (all HTTP 404), indicating the product is inactive or has been wound down.

providers.name: Storicity
providers.description: Storicity Inc. was a Seoul, South Korea-based travel-technology startup, founded around 2020 and backed by 500 Global, that built Yoda Trip (Korean brand "여다") — an AI-assisted consumer travel-planning mobile app offering customized itineraries and mobile audio guides for tourist destinations, shipped on iOS and Android. It was a consumer B2C mobile product rather than an API platform provider. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 (web search plus a live domain/TLS probe) found no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK packages, GitHub organization, or other developer surface. Public records indicate the Yoda Trip service was discontinued in April 2025 and the company is listed as out of business; the yodatrip.com domain still resolves but serves a broken TLS certificate.

providers.name: Storigen Systems
providers.description: Storigen Systems was an Internet infrastructure company founded in 2000 and based in Lowell, Massachusetts, that pioneered the Distributed Storage Network — a class of infrastructure intended to improve the economics and performance of bandwidth-intensive applications by enabling efficient storage, delivery, and management of data across distributed environments. The company raised roughly $49M from investors including Battery Ventures, Charles River Ventures (CRV), Flagship Pioneering, and Pilot House Ventures before ceasing operations; it is now permanently closed. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no live domain, developer portal, documentation, or API surface — the company is defunct and publishes nothing to harvest.

providers.name: Stranger Things Quotes
providers.description: Returns Stranger Things quotes

providers.name: Stratim
providers.description: Stratim (originally incorporated as Zirx in 2014, rebranded to Stratim in 2017) was a San Francisco-based SaaS company that built an enterprise fleet-operations and logistics platform for transportation companies, autonomous-vehicle operators, and urban fleets. Its three product lines were the Stratim Platform (fleet operations software), the Stratim Exchange (on-the-ground vendor fulfillment), and the Stratim Marketplace (fleet-owner/vendor transactions), and it advertised API access, a workforce app, processing-engine integration, and SMS updates. Founded by Shmulik Fishman and Sean Behr and backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures ($36.4M raised), Stratim was acquired by ACV Auctions in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the stratim.com domain is held in custodial parking (CSC Corporate Domains) with no live website, developer portal, documentation, or reachable API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Strattic
providers.description: Strattic was a static and headless WordPress hosting platform that pre-rendered WordPress sites into static assets for improved security, performance, and scalability, while preserving the familiar WordPress admin experience via SFTP and WP-CLI developer access. Strattic was acquired by Elementor in 2022 and folded into Elementor Hosting; Elementor announced the sunset of its dedicated static hosting service in 2025, and strattic.com now 301-redirects to elementor.com/hosting/. No independent Strattic public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remains.

providers.name: Streamonce
providers.description: StreamOnce was a cloud-based enterprise collaboration platform founded in 2012 in San Jose, California by Ilan Twig and Ariel Cohen (who later co-founded TripActions/Navan). The product connected business systems into a social enterprise layer so teams could reply to emails, read documents, and post to Yammer and Chatter from a single unified interface. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (~$1.25-1.36M raised), the company was acquired by Jive Software in 2013, less than a year after its initial funding. StreamOnce is no longer an operating company and publishes no active product, developer portal, or API; the streamonce.com domain now redirects to a domain-sale marketplace. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record surfaced via Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Strella Biotechnology
providers.description: Strella Biotechnology is a Seattle-based produce-quality intelligence company that uses ethylene gas sensors and predictive analytics to reduce food waste across the fresh-produce supply chain. Its product line spans Storage (predicting produce maturity in cold storage), Ripen (automating the ripening process), Sequence (optimizing shipment order to cut shrink), and Monitor (real-time environmental monitoring in logistics). The company reports tracking over two billion pounds of produce across 26 countries and is backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of this enrichment pass, Strella exposes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhook surface.

providers.name: StrikeAd
providers.description: StrikeAd was a mobile advertising technology company surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (strikead.com) resolves to a parked lander page rather than an active product or developer surface - every path, including the homepage, /.well-known/ discovery endpoints, and common API paths, returns the same domain-parking redirect to /lander. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API surface could be found, indicating the company is no longer operating an active public API.

providers.name: StructionSite
providers.description: StructionSite was a construction-technology company providing jobsite reality-capture and progress-documentation software (360-degree walkthrough video and photo documentation of construction sites, tied to project plans). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the standalone StructionSite brand has been absorbed by its acquirer DroneDeploy - structionsite.com, www.structionsite.com, and api.structionsite.com all HTTP 301-redirect to www.dronedeploy.com. No independent StructionSite developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, package, or /.well-known discovery surface could be found; any API surface now lives under the DroneDeploy brand.

providers.name: StudentFinance
providers.description: StudentFinance is a European fintech company, backed by Seedcamp, focused on financing access to education and career development (income-share and deferred-payment models for students and upskilling programs). Surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, its public presence is currently a minimal Webflow marketing site; an enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Studio
providers.description: Studio (formally Studio of America, Inc.) is a creative collective that develops art through software, describing its mission as creating together, from and for the heart. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV in the consumer sector and added to the API Evangelist network, the public site at s-tud.io is a static Gatsby marketing presence (Home, Beliefs, and Team pages plus an audio player) and exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, documentation, or well-known discovery surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Studio Moderna
providers.description: Studio Moderna is one of the largest multichannel direct-to-consumer retailers across Central and Eastern Europe, the Middle East, and beyond, founded in 1992 and headquartered in Emmen, Switzerland, with major operations based in Ljubljana, Slovenia. The company reaches consumers through TV direct-response (Top Shop), e-commerce, print catalogs, call centers, and physical retail stores in roughly twenty countries. Its portfolio of house brands spans sleep and home (Dormeo), kitchenware (Delimano), footwear and wellness (Walkmaxx), and health and lifestyle products (Kosmodisk, Rovus, WellNeo). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company exposes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: StudySoup
providers.description: StudySoup is a consumer education-technology platform that provides college and university students with study tools for better grades. It offers custom study guides written by student notetakers, step-by-step textbook solutions (AnswerED videos), video overviews of core curriculum (PreparED), and community features including a Discord channel and YouTube livestreams, alongside a notetaker monetization program that pays students to share their notes. StudySoup was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass the live site (studysoup.com) is an active B2C study-resources product with no publicly documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or integration surface.

providers.name: StyleSage
providers.description: StyleSage was a fashion and retail market-intelligence startup (Techstars-backed) that applied computer vision and data science to track apparel pricing, assortment, discounting, and trend signals across e-commerce retailers. The stylesage.co domain now redirects to Centric Software, which acquired the product and folded it into its Centric Market Intelligence platform for fashion, footwear, home, and beauty brands. As of this enrichment pass no standalone public developer API, documentation, SDK, or well-known surface is published for StyleSage.

providers.name: StyleSaint
providers.description: StyleSaint is a Los Angeles-based direct-to-consumer luxury women's fashion brand, originally an a16z-backed social-commerce startup and now an independent e-commerce label selling silk, lace, and other luxury-fabric apparel that is handmade in LA, ethically made, and sustainably sourced. The storefront runs on Shopify. As of this enrichment pass StyleSaint publishes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or agent-facing surface of its own; it is catalogued here as an a16z portfolio company. Any programmable commerce capability would be provided by the underlying Shopify platform rather than by a first-party StyleSaint API.

providers.name: Styleup
providers.description: StyleUp was a Y Combinator (Winter 2013) fashion advisory startup that delivered personalized daily outfit recommendations tailored to the user's local weather and individual style preferences, learning from feedback to improve suggestions over time. It operated as a consumer styling service out of the San Francisco Bay Area rather than as an API or developer platform. The company is now defunct and no longer operates: its former domain (thestyleup.com) has been repurposed by an unrelated third party and serves a Turkish sports-streaming site, so there is no live product, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface remaining to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical stub with no active API artifacts.

providers.name: SumAll
providers.description: SumAll was a New York-based social media and business analytics startup, surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct - its primary domain sumall.com no longer resolves to a live product and is parked/listed for sale on Afternic. There is no live developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface to harvest, so no provider artifacts were produced.

providers.name: SunFarmer
providers.description: SunFarmer is a solar energy company operating primarily in Nepal that designs, installs, finances, and services solar power systems for health facilities, schools, agriculture, and businesses. Its mission is to make reliable solar energy affordable across underserved communities, powering water pumping, clinics, and irrigation. SunFarmer reports over 3.2 million cubic meters of water pumped, 1.5+ million units of clean electricity generated, and nearly 1.8 million kilograms of CO2 offset. It offers a "Get Solar" customer path and a "Give Solar" donation program. It is a direct-to-customer solar services and social-impact provider with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: SUNWODA
providers.description: Sunwoda Electronic Co., Ltd. (欣旺达电子股份有限公司, Shenzhen Stock Exchange 300207) is a global lithium-ion battery manufacturer headquartered in Shenzhen, China. Its business spans consumer batteries (smartphone and laptop battery packs), electric-vehicle power batteries, energy-storage systems, energy services, smart hardware, and an innovation ecosystem. Sunwoda supplies battery cells and packs to major consumer-electronics and automotive OEMs worldwide. As a hardware and manufacturing company it operates corporate, investor, supplier (SRM), and bidding platforms, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirms there is no public API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Super
providers.description: Super (super.gs) is an early-stage consumer entertainment application built by Outpace Studios and backed by Bullpen Capital, positioned around the tagline "Entertainment you can cash out." As of mid-2026 the product is pre-launch: the public site is a single-page marketing and waitlist experience with no published developer platform, API, SDKs, or documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks Super as a portfolio lead and currently carries only a live domain-security probe of super.gs; it will be enriched further if and when the company ships a public API surface.

providers.name: Super Sports Media
providers.description: Super Sports Media Group is an IDG Capital-backed Chinese sports-media company best known for holding the English Premier League broadcast rights in mainland China and operating consumer sports streaming and content services under the ssports.com brand. Its platform was subsequently absorbed into iQiyi Sports (爱奇艺体育), and ssports.com now redirects there. This is a business-to-consumer sports streaming and media-rights operation with no public developer program: no API documentation, developer portal, SDKs, OpenAPI, or open platform surface could be found during enrichment. Profile retained as a network company record.

providers.name: Superjampad
providers.description: Superjampad is a consumer product company surfaced as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network. Its site at superjampad.com serves a Next.js single-page application branded "Breaking - News from friends," a social news product, and the site robots.txt references sitemaps for breaking.im and whatsgood.im, indicating a family of consumer news and social applications. As of this enrichment pass Superjampad publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, llms.txt, or .well-known discovery documents; the domain's request paths all resolve to the SPA catch-all rather than to any machine-readable API surface. This profile therefore captures verifiable identity and domain-security posture only, and remains a lead awaiting a real developer surface to enrich further.

providers.name: supermag
providers.description: Suzhou Supermag Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. is a Chinese deep-tech manufacturer specializing in magnetic levitation (maglev) motion and fluid-handling systems. Its product lines include SCM maglev wafer turntables for ultra-clean semiconductor rotation, SCP maglev pumps for contamination-free fluid transport, MSS maglev stirring systems for low-shear mixing, and SCT maglev turbomolecular pumps for high-vacuum applications, serving the semiconductor, biopharmaceutical, chemical, and energy industries. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, the company markets physical industrial hardware and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Superplastic
providers.description: Superplastic is a designer-toy and entertainment brand that creates animated synthetic celebrities and collectible vinyl art toys, including the characters Janky, Guggimon, and Staffie, sold through its Shopify-powered online store. Based in Burlington, Vermont, the company blends animation, streetwear-style limited-edition drops, and collectible figures. It is a direct-to-consumer commerce and social-media brand and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its web and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: SuperValu
providers.description: SuperValu was one of the largest grocery retail and wholesale distribution companies in the United States before being acquired by United Natural Foods (UNFI) in 2018 for $2.9 billion. SuperValu operated retail grocery stores under multiple banners and provided wholesale distribution services. The supervalu.com domain now redirects to UNFI's wholesale food distribution platform. Suppliers interact with UNFI/SuperValu distribution through EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) and the myUNFI supplier portal.

providers.name: Surfboard
providers.description: Surfboard (teamsurfboard.com) was a workforce management (WFM) SaaS for customer support teams — scheduling, forecasting, and real-time staffing for contact centers — backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest. As of this enrichment pass the standalone product no longer operates independently; teamsurfboard.com returns an HTTP 301 permanent redirect to Dialpad's workforce management software page (dialpad.com/features/workforce-management-software), indicating Surfboard was acquired by / folded into Dialpad. No standalone Surfboard developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface is publicly reachable; all probed /.well-known/ discovery endpoints return 404.

providers.name: Surtr Defense Systems
providers.description: Surtr Defense Systems is a Y Combinator-backed defense technology company building ParallaxOS, an open operating system for counter-UAS (counter-drone) command-and-control. Surtr positions itself outside the incumbent C2 tension by not competing with hardware partners on contracts and not monetizing partner data: hardware partners decide what data the platform sees, customers decide what data is kept, and every byte is visible to partners and customers in real time. ParallaxOS ingests any sensor (radar, RF, EO/IR, acoustic) over open defense-interoperability standards such as NATO SAPIENT, Link 16, Cursor on Target, and ATAK; tasks any compatible kinetic, EW, or directed-energy effector with human-in-the-loop authorization on every engagement; and performs multi-sensor fusion, autonomous track correlation, and AI threat classification at millisecond latency on the tactical edge. Customer data, integration code, and decisions remain the customer's, deployed on-prem or in GovCloud. Founded by Anshul Ahluwalia (CEO, ex-Shield AI) and Cameron Fiore (CTO, ex-Anduril, ex-Shield AI). Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public developer API surface is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Survata
providers.description: Survata was a San Francisco market-research and brand-measurement company, backed by Bloomberg Beta, that ran online surveys and brand-lift studies to measure advertising effectiveness across digital channels. Survata was acquired by Upwave in 2019 and the brand has since been fully absorbed — survata.com now 301-redirects to upwave.com, the enterprise brand-measurement platform. No public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or well-known discovery surface is published for Survata or its Upwave successor; this profile is retained as a network lead with no live API surface.

providers.name: Survios
providers.description: Survios is a virtual reality game studio that develops and publishes immersive VR titles across major platforms including PlayStation VR, Steam, Meta Quest, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch. Known for award-winning games such as Raw Data, Creed: Rise to Glory, The Walking Dead: Onslaught, Sprint Vector, Electronauts, and Alien: Rogue Incursion, the studio describes itself as one of the world's leading VR games studios. Backed by Lux Capital, Survios operates as a consumer games company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: SV Academy
providers.description: SV Academy is a tech-sales training and talent-placement platform that trains job seekers to become Sales Development Representatives (SDRs) through a tuition-light, income-share program and connects its graduates with hiring tech companies. It positions itself as "not an agency," charging employers no placement fees and instead earning revenue through the training and placement of its graduates. As a training and workforce-development service it exposes no public developer platform, API, or developer documentation; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Sverve
providers.description: Sverve was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. During the enrichment pass the company's website (sverve.com) was offline — the origin returned HTTP 522 behind Cloudflare, and its DNS (NameBright registrar-parking MX/SPF and a "comingsoon.namebright.com" DMARC target) indicates the domain is parked and the company appears inactive. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or public API surface could be found, so there is nothing to enrich beyond a probed domain-security record. Left as an inactive lead.

providers.name: Swag.com
providers.description: Swag.com is a custom branded-merchandise and promotional-products platform that lets businesses design, order, warehouse, and distribute company swag such as apparel, drinkware, tech accessories, and curated "Swag in a Box" kits. A Techstars-backed company (acquired by Custom Ink in 2021), it operates a self-serve online storefront and fulfillment service. No public developer API or developer portal is currently published; this profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Swarm Technologies
providers.description: Swarm Technologies is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of social-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: space. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Sweetgreen
providers.description: Sweetgreen is a fast-casual restaurant company (NYSE: SG) building healthy, plant-forward food through a network of company-owned locations and its digital ordering platform. It reaches customers primarily via its consumer website and mobile app for pickup, delivery, and its Sweetgreen Rewards loyalty program, and operates automated "Infinite Kitchen" locations. As of this enrichment pass, Sweetgreen publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture only. Backed by D1 Capital and True Ventures.

providers.name: Swiftkey
providers.description: SwiftKey is a predictive on-screen keyboard for Android and iOS that uses machine learning to improve autocorrect, next-word prediction, and swipe-to-type (SwiftKey Flow). Founded in London as TouchType, it was acquired by Microsoft in 2016 and is now shipped as Microsoft SwiftKey. The former SwiftKey SDK for embedding its prediction engine has been discontinued, and www.swiftkey.com now permanently redirects to microsoft.com/swiftkey. As of this enrichment pass the product exposes no public developer API, SDK registry package, or developer portal.

providers.name: SwitchMe
providers.description: SwitchMe was a Mumbai, India based fintech startup founded in 2012 and backed by 500 Global that helped consumers evaluate and switch their home loans and mobile service providers, handling document collection and submission on their behalf. The company appears to be defunct: no public developer program, API, or documentation could be found, and its switchme.in domain currently resolves to unrelated content. This profile records what could be verified during the enrichment pass; there is no API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Syenta
providers.description: Syenta is an Australian deep-tech semiconductor company (founded 2022, spun out of the Australian National University, with teams across Australia, Europe and the United States) building manufacturing equipment for advanced chip packaging. Its proprietary Localized Electrochemical Manufacturing (LEM) technology combines material deposition and 3D patterning in a single step to produce sub-micron High-Resolution Interconnects on large (>1000 mm2) packages, targeting the chip-to-chip bandwidth bottleneck in AI computing; its Achyon production tool delivers wafer-level system integration at high density. Backed by Playground Global and Australia's National Reconstruction Fund (Series A), Syenta is a hardware / fabrication-equipment maker and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Syft
providers.description: Syft (originally Syft Online Ltd, later branded "Syft by Indeed") is a UK-founded flexible-staffing marketplace launched in London in 2015 by Jack Beaman and Novo Abakare. Its platform connects employers across hospitality, retail, industrial, care and facilities-management directly with vetted, rated temporary and part-time workers, removing the traditional recruitment agency and charging a flat fee on top of worker wages. Creandum led Syft's Series A in 2017; the company was acquired by Indeed in 2019 and now operates as part of Indeed Flex. Syft is a consumer/employer staffing marketplace and exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Sygate
providers.description: Sygate Technologies was an endpoint-security software company founded in 1995 in Fremont, California, and backed by Trinity Ventures among other investors. Its products included enterprise server and end-user firewalls (Sygate Personal Firewall), automated network discovery, network access control (NAC), and security monitoring. Symantec acquired Sygate in 2005 for its Universal Network Access Control technology; the end-user products were subsequently discontinued and the enterprise NAC technology folded into Symantec (now Gen Digital). Sygate is a defunct entity with no active company website, developer portal, or public API surface; this profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Symbio Robotics
providers.description: Symbio Robotics is an AI industrial-automation company founded in 2014 and based in Emeryville, California. Its flagship product, SymbioDCS, is a robot-agnostic middleware and Python programming framework that lets automation teams build, deploy, and continuously improve AI-driven assembly applications on existing factory robots. Symbio has publicly worked with automakers including Ford, Nissan, and Toyota to speed transmission and vehicle assembly. SymbioDCS is deployed on-premises inside manufacturing lines rather than offered as a public web API; as of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, SDK/package registry presence, MCP server, or API surface, and its former web domains (symb.io, symbiorobotics.com) now resolve to parked/for-sale landing pages.

providers.name: Symmorphix
providers.description: Symmorphix, Inc. was a materials-science company founded in 1998 and based in Sunnyvale, California, that developed and manufactured advanced amorphous dielectric and optical thin films for the optical-networking and communications industries. Its core technology was a proprietary wide-area physical vapor deposition (PVD) process performed at low temperatures, enabling deposition of a broad range of material compositions onto metal, ceramic, and polymer substrates for use as physical barriers, dielectric layers, and optical layers. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures and Crescendo Ventures and was acquired by Springworks on February 6, 2004. It is a defunct hardware/materials company with no public API, developer portal, or software developer surface, and is retained in the API Evangelist network only as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Synplicity
providers.description: Synplicity, Inc. was a supplier of software for the design of programmable logic devices (FPGAs, PLDs and CPLDs) used in communications, military/aerospace, consumer, semiconductor and computer systems. Its tools provided logic synthesis, physical synthesis, ASIC prototyping and verification for FPGA and DSP designers (Synplify, Synplify Pro, Identify). Synplicity was acquired by Synopsys for approximately $227 million, with the transaction completed on 2008-05-15, and no longer operates as an independent company. The legacy domain synplicity.com now 301-redirects to synopsys.com. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners; it has no independent public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: SynQuest
providers.description: SynQuest, Inc. (formerly Nasdaq: SYNQ) was an Atlanta, Georgia based supply-chain planning and logistics software company that provided e-business solutions to optimize the financial and operational performance of the supply chain, including transportation, distribution, and inventory planning and simulation for customers such as Ford Motor Company. SynQuest reverse-merged with Viewlocity, Inc. in November 2002 (Viewlocity merged into SynQuest as the surviving entity) and was delisted from the Nasdaq SmallCap Market shortly after. Insight Partners (formerly Insight Venture Partners) was an early investor, which is why the company appears in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead. The company is inactive today and publishes no live website, developer portal, or public API surface; enrichment searches found only historical SEC filings and press coverage.

providers.name: Syntertainment
providers.description: Syntertainment was an entertainment technology startup founded in 2012 in Berkeley, California by game designer Will Wright (creator of SimCity and The Sims), Avi Bar-Zeev, and Anya Wright, emerging from the Stupid Fun Club collective. The company set out to explore the intersection of entertainment and reality, blending real-world data and player experiences with game-like interactive media. It raised roughly $5M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Mayfield, SV Angel, and former Electronic Arts CEO John Riccitiello. The venture never shipped a public consumer product and is no longer active; its website (syntertainment.com) is offline and it exposes no public developer program, documentation, or API surface. This profile was surfaced from an a16z portfolio list and enriched to reflect the company's real, historical status.

providers.name: Synthetic Design Lab
providers.description: Synthetic Design Lab is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2022 developing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for cancer therapy. Its SYNTHBODY platform and SYNTHBODY Engine engineer multispecific biologics with layered BIO-LOGIC control mechanisms and targeted payload delivery reported at 10x or more versus conventional ADCs. The company emerged from stealth in April 2025 with a $20M seed round led by Playground Global and Godfrey Capital, and is led by CEO Daniel S. Chen (formerly Global Head of Cancer Immunotherapy Development at Genentech) and CSO Ramesh Baliga. This is a therapeutics research company with no public API, SDK, or developer surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Syrup
providers.description: Syrup (Syrup Tech) is an AI-powered inventory optimization and demand-forecasting platform for retail and apparel brands. Its machine-learning decision-support engine combines transactional, marketing, and inventory data with external signals such as social trends and weather to recommend how brands produce, buy, and allocate inventory across omnichannel commerce, reducing stockouts and overproduction. Founded in 2021 by James Theuerkauf and Ferdinand Stockmann, Syrup raised a $17.5M Series A led by Accel and was acquired by Anaplan in September 2025; syrup.tech now redirects to anaplan.com. Syrup exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Systems Center
providers.description: Systems Center, Inc. was a mainframe and enterprise systems-management software vendor best known for the NetMaster network-management product line. The company was acquired by Sterling Software of Dallas in a 1993 deal (approximately $185M), after which NetMaster was folded into Sterling's data-communications portfolio and rebranded (Connect:Direct lineage); Sterling Software was itself acquired by Computer Associates in 2000. Systems Center was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass (2026-07-21) searched for any live website, developer portal, or API surface and found none: the company is defunct with no independent public presence, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: t4game
providers.description: t4game (呈天游 / Bstonegames) is the brand of Beijing Chengtian Network Technology Co., Ltd., a Chinese online-game developer and operator founded in 2008 and headquartered in Beijing. The company designs, publishes, and operates mobile, PC, and web-based games — including titles such as 醉江湖online (Drunk Rivers and Lakes Online) and 诛神传奇/诛神online (Zhushen Online) — spanning role-playing, real-time strategy, and shooting genres. Its public presence at t4game.com is a consumer-facing game portal (player login, registration, and recharge), company and culture pages, a product catalog, game/media news, and recruitment listings. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, MCP server, or other machine-readable API surface could be found.

providers.name: Taascom
providers.description: Taascom (branded "The As A Service Company", taascom.com) is a San Jose, California company founded in 2019 that provides an IoT-based servitization SaaS platform helping equipment makers shift from transactional capex sales to recurring subscription, pay-per-use, and outcome-based revenue models. Its packaged offerings include Device-as-a-Service, Auto-Replenishment-as-a-Service, and Uptime-as-a-Service. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found a marketing-stage web presence only — no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or OpenAPI surface at the time of this pass.

providers.name: Tacit
providers.description: Tacit Networks was an early-2000s enterprise networking vendor and one of the leading providers of WAN Optimization technology for Wide Area File Services (WAFS), letting distributed offices access centralized file servers over the wide area network at LAN-like speeds. Backed by Canaan Partners (Series A led by Maha Ibrahim), JP Morgan, Chevron Technology Ventures and RRE Ventures, the company was acquired by Packeteer in May 2006 (subsequently absorbed into Blue Coat Systems and Symantec). It is defunct: it operated no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface, so this profile carries company identity only and has no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: TacoFancy
providers.description: Community-driven taco database

providers.name: Tactic
providers.description: Tactic was a cryptocurrency and digital-asset accounting platform founded in 2021 in New York and backed by Lux Capital. Its product aggregated on-chain activity and exchange/custody data (Coinbase and others) into a unified treasury view and crypto sub-ledger, automatically categorizing transactions, calculating USD gain/loss and taxable events, and reconciling the crypto sub-ledger to traditional accounting software such as QuickBooks. Tactic launched from stealth in 2022 (originally on choosetactic.com, later the exact-match tactic.com) and raised roughly $13.6M before being acquired by TaxBit in January 2023 to augment TaxBit's digital-asset accounting suite. The standalone product, developer portal, and API surface have been retired; the tactic.com domain is now listed for sale and no independent developer surface remains.

providers.name: Taggle Internet Ventures
providers.description: Taggle Internet Ventures Private Limited was an Indian online group-buying / daily-deals platform (taggle.com) incorporated in 2010 in Bangalore, Karnataka, that brought consumers together to purchase discounted products and services from merchants across food & beverage, wellness, and beauty. It raised an early venture round in 2010 and is now reported as permanently closed. The enrichment pass found no live developer program, public API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or documentation for this entity. Note: the taggle.com domain is now operated by an unrelated Australian digital water-metering company, Taggle Systems, which is a distinct company and not the subject of this record. This profile was surfaced during VC-portfolio mining and is retained as a historical/closed-company stub with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: TakeLessons
providers.description: TakeLessons was an online and in-person lessons marketplace founded in 2007 by Steven Cox and headquartered in San Diego, California. It connected students with independent instructors for music, languages, academic subjects, cooking, and professional training, handling scheduling, payments, and instructor discovery. Microsoft acquired TakeLessons in September 2021 to expand its edtech offerings, then wound the service down: the last day to book lessons was August 15, 2024 and the consumer site closed on November 15, 2024. The company is now defunct and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface; this record is retained as a portfolio-lineage stub for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TakeWheels
providers.description: TakeWheels (branded "Wheels", operated by Wheels Labs) was a shared electric micromobility platform based in Los Angeles, founded in 2018, that offered seated pedal-assist e-bikes and dockless light electric vehicles for short-distance urban trips. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital, which participated in the company's 2019 Series A. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable developer surface for this company. As of this pass the primary domain (takewheels.com) no longer resolves to the company: it issues a 301 redirect to an unrelated third-party site, indicating the business is defunct and the domain has been repurposed. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead with no active API surface.

providers.name: Talaria Technologies
providers.description: Talaria Technologies, Inc. was a developer-tools startup based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2011, that built a dynamic web application server and runtime infrastructure for web developers — notably a just-in-time (JIT) compiler and runtime for PHP intended to help developers build and run websites more efficiently. It was surfaced as an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) portfolio/investment-list company. Per public company-intelligence sources (indexed.vc, PrivCo, Bloomberg, CB Insights), Talaria was acquired by Google in 2013 and ceased operating as an independent company; it maintains no active website, developer portal, or public API surface today.

providers.name: Talasim
providers.description: Talasim was a Jordanian user-generated-content website that curated photographs of funny signs on cars, stores, and roads, positioned as an online comedy and self-expression channel. Backed by Seedcamp, it was acquired by the regional reviews-and-listings community Jeeran (Amman, Jordan) in March 2010, with its engineering team absorbed into Jeeran's localisation efforts. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer, API, or documentation surface; the referenced jeeran.com domain no longer serves a live site (TLS handshake failure). This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio stub and has been enriched to reflect its acquired, no-API status.

providers.name: Talking Computers
providers.description: Talking Computers is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building Facility, described as "The Workplace for AI" and delivering autonomous organizations for enterprises. The company deploys fleets of AI Infrastructure Engineers that collaborate over week-long time horizons, run hundreds of experiments in parallel, and learn from them to optimize customers' training and inference infrastructure to their specific workloads. Talking Computers reports partnering with companies to speed up GPU kernels to 6x state-of-the-art and to cut the latency of voice models to roughly half that of competitors. As of enrichment, the company is an early-stage two-person team and publishes only a marketing presence at talkingcomputers.ai (a single-page application); it exposes no public API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from verified public sources.

providers.name: Tallan
providers.description: Tallan was a Hartford, Connecticut technology consultancy, founded in 1985, that built custom Microsoft- and Azure-powered solutions — application modernization, e-commerce and web development, user experience, mobile, cloud, data, and AI/ML — for clients in manufacturing, consumer packaged goods, pharma, healthcare, and state and local government. In February 2023 Tallan was acquired by EY US and folded into EY's Microsoft services group; the tallan.com domain now 301-redirects to EY's Microsoft alliance page. Tallan operated as a professional-services consultancy and never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or event surface, so there is no API to enrich.

providers.name: Talon
providers.description: Talon (Talon Cyber Security) was an enterprise browser security company that built a secure, isolated Chromium-based browser for protecting SaaS and web application access on managed and unmanaged devices, with controls for data loss prevention, zero-trust access, and endpoint posture. Surfaced as a portfolio lead of Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in December 2023 and its product was folded into the Palo Alto Networks Prisma Access Browser (Prisma SASE). Talon no longer operates as an independent company: its former domain (talon-sec.com) redirects to the Palo Alto Networks Prisma Browser product page, and no independent public developer portal, API documentation, or public API surface was found during enrichment. This profile is retained as a company record for network history.

providers.name: Tandem
providers.description: Tandem is a virtual office for remote and distributed teams, backed by Y Combinator and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), that recreates the presence and spontaneity of an in-person office online. It shows who is available and who is in a conversation, and lets teammates drop into low-friction voice and video rooms with screen sharing, plus integrations with tools like Notion, GitHub, and Trello. Surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network, Tandem is a consumer/team collaboration product with app integrations but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal at the time of enrichment (verified 2026-07-21 against https://tandem.chat).

providers.name: Tantan
providers.description: Tantan (探探) is a Chinese location-based social discovery and online dating application, launched in 2014 and widely described as "China's Tinder" for its swipe-based matching mechanic. The app pairs nearby users who mutually express interest and layers on messaging, moments, live streaming, and interest-based social features. An early DCM Ventures portfolio company, Tantan was acquired by Momo Inc. (now Hello Group) in 2018 and operates as a consumer mobile product across China and several international markets. Tantan is a mobile-first consumer app and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Tapastic
providers.description: Tapastic is the former brand of Tapas, a digital storytelling platform (Tapas Entertainment, a Kakao company) that hosts webcomics and web novels across romance, fantasy, action, drama, and other genres. Readers access serialized episodes through a free-with-premium model using an in-app "Ink" currency, and creators publish original and user-generated stories via the creators.tapas.io publishing portal. The original tapastic.com domain has been retired and now rebrands to tapas.io. As of this enrichment pass the platform exposes only a consumer web/mobile application and a content-creator publishing surface; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, developer portal, or documented webhook/event surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and remains a lead in the API Evangelist network with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Tapchief
providers.description: Tapchief was an India-based online marketplace that connected businesses and professionals with a vetted network of freelance experts, consultants, and advisors for project-based work, on-demand consultations, and expert advice. Founded in Bengaluru and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), the platform let companies discover, book, and collaborate with independent talent across functions such as marketing, finance, product, and technology. Tapchief was acquired by Chargebee in 2021, and the tapchief.com domain is now dormant. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; probing found no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: TapCommerce (Twitter)
providers.description: TapCommerce was a mobile app-retargeting and advertising technology company acquired by Twitter in July 2014 and folded into Twitter's MoPub mobile ad exchange; it no longer operates as an independent entity. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Sector: commerce / adtech. Enrichment pass (2026-07-21) found no live domain (tapcommerce.com does not resolve) and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Tapingo
providers.description: Tapingo was a mobile ordering and pickup app for college campuses and local restaurants, surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures. It was acquired by Grubhub in 2018 and folded into Grubhub Campus; as of the 2026 enrichment pass the tapingo.com domain 301-redirects to onsite.grubhub.com and Tapingo no longer operates as an independent company or publishes any developer or API surface. Sector: consumer / food ordering. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; there are no live APIs to enrich.

providers.name: Tapsense
providers.description: TapSense was a mobile advertising and real-time-bidding platform surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The 2026-07-21 enrichment pass found no live developer or API surface - the tapsense.com domain resolves to a parked page with no content, the docs.tapsense.com host presents an expired TLS certificate, and developer.tapsense.com returns no documentation. No OpenAPI, SDK, package, MCP, or webhook surface was discoverable. The company appears defunct (mobile-ad platforms of this era were commonly acquired and wound down), so there is nothing to enrich beyond this identity record.

providers.name: Tapshots
providers.description: Tapshot, Inc. (marketed as Videokits) is a Cupertino, California company founded in 2012 that builds a mobile-first video capture and survey platform. Its Videokits Pro apps guide users through structured "kits" of survey questions and shot lists to capture video interviews and NPS/demographic survey responses in the field, then upload them to a web portal for storage, transcoding, streaming, and analysis. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the public website (videokits.com) does not respond and no developer/API surface (OpenAPI, SDK, developer portal, or GitHub organization) could be found; the iOS/iPad app was last updated June 2023, indicating a dormant product.

providers.name: taptrip.co
providers.description: TapTrip (taptrip.co) was a UK-based self-serve business travel and expense booking platform for SMEs, founded in 2018 in Manchester and part of the Barclays Accelerator powered by Techstars. It let smaller businesses book and manage flights, hotels, rail, and ground transportation without a travel management company. TapTrip was acquired by TripStax in July 2022 and folded into the TripStax platform as an SME online-booking module for travel management companies; the standalone brand was absorbed. As of this enrichment pass the taptrip.co domain no longer hosts an active product — it resolves to a ParkingCrew domain-parking service and the TLS endpoint does not respond. No public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface was found for the standalone company.

providers.name: Targa Energy
providers.description: Targa Energy is a midstream natural gas and natural gas liquids (NGL) services company operating in North America. The company provides gathering, compression, treating, processing, and selling of natural gas; storing, fractionating, treating, transporting, and selling of NGLs. Targa Energy operates as part of the broader Targa Resources enterprise, which is a Fortune 500 midstream infrastructure company focused on the Permian Basin and other major production areas.

providers.name: Targa Resources
providers.description: Targa Resources Corp. is a Fortune 500 and S&P 500 midstream energy infrastructure company and one of the largest independent midstream companies in North America. The company provides midstream services including gathering, compression, treating, processing, and selling of natural gas; fractionating, treating, transporting, and selling of natural gas liquids (NGLs); gathering, storing, terminaling and selling crude oil; and storing and selling refined petroleum products. Targa operates primarily in the Permian Basin, Anadarko Basin, and South Texas production areas, and owns the Grand Prix NGL Pipeline.

providers.name: Target Arm
providers.description: Target Arm is a robotics company building systems to autonomously launch and recover drones from moving vehicles without stopping. Its Ralar robotic arm captures drones mid-air, recharges them, and relaunches them, while TRACKR sensor-fusion, TurboFly autopilot, and Maestro mission-control software coordinate drone fleets across commercial delivery, first-responder, agriculture, energy-inspection, and defense/ISR use cases. A Techstars-backed hardware startup with no public API or developer program at this time; this network profile captures identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Taskty
providers.description: Taskty (تاسكتى) is an Egypt-based online marketplace for on-demand home services, connecting customers with vetted service providers for residential cleaning, furniture and upholstery care, eco-friendly pest control, and home maintenance including plumbing, electrical, painting, carpentry, marble, aluminum, and air-conditioning work. The platform is delivered primarily through consumer iOS and Android mobile apps plus a web presence, with booking, dispatch, and WhatsApp/phone support. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Taskty publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Tastemade
providers.description: Tastemade is a modern media company producing food, travel, and home & design video programming for a global millennial and Gen-Z audience. Founded in 2012, it distributes short- and long-form video across social platforms, connected-TV apps, and its ad-supported and subscription Tastemade+ streaming service, and runs a branded-content studio for advertisers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of redpoint-ventures; enrichment found no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Tasty Labs
providers.description: Tasty Labs, Inc. was a social-software development studio founded in 2010 by Joshua Schachter (creator of Delicious), Nick Nguyen, and Paul Rademacher. Backed by a $3M Series A from Union Square Ventures and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), it built experimental consumer products including Jig.com (a marketplace for needs), Human.io (a micro-task service), and Skills.to. The company was acquired by @WalmartLabs in May 2013, with its team and technology folded into WalmartLabs; the tastylabs.com domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record and exposes no public API surface, developer documentation, or specifications.

providers.name: Tastykake
providers.description: Tastykake is a Philadelphia-area baked snacks brand founded in 1914, known for Kandy Kakes, Krimpets, Juniors, and snack pies. It has been owned by Flowers Foods (NYSE: FLO) since 2011 and operates as a consumer packaged goods brand within the Flowers Foods portfolio alongside Nature's Own, Wonder, and Dave's Killer Bread. No public, developer-facing APIs have been identified for the Tastykake brand; partner, retailer, and distribution integrations are handled through Flowers Foods' internal EDI and account-managed channels rather than a public developer portal.

providers.name: TastyUrban
providers.description: TastyUrban is a Berlin-based virtual restaurant franchise and digital-first food-brand licensing company founded in 2022 by Felix Chrobog, Marc Hansell, and Gerry Pidgeon (alumni of Gorillas, Tier, and Deliveroo). It pursues an asset-light model in which existing restaurants and retail partners license and operate TastyUrban's digital food brands, using otherwise idle kitchen capacity to add revenue without major investment or operational complexity. The company is backed by Earlybird and raised a EUR 1.5M seed round in 2023 and a EUR 6.5M Series A in 2025 (led by IBB Ventures). TastyUrban operates a consumer/partner web presence at tastyurban.com but publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Tattvam
providers.description: Tattvam AI (Tattvam Labs) is an early-stage, Seedcamp-backed deep-tech startup building the intelligence layer of chip design, applying artificial intelligence to semiconductor and electronic design automation (EDA) workflows. As of this profile the company operates a single marketing landing page at tattvamlabs.ai (a Vercel-hosted React single-page app) with no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs; it is in a pre-product, team-building stage. Contact hello@tattvamlabs.ai.

providers.name: Tcell Io
providers.description: Tcell Io (tCell.io) was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no active web presence - its former domain tcell.io now resolves to a third-party domain-parking page (parklogic.com) and returns no company site, developer portal, documentation, or API surface. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, well-known discovery documents, SDKs, or other machine-readable API artifacts could be found. This profile is retained as a network record; there is nothing enrichable until the company publishes an active developer surface.

providers.name: TeachStreet
providers.description: TeachStreet was an online learning marketplace that, in its own words, "helps people find great classes, courses, teachers, and instructors who help them learn new things," while "teachers use TeachStreet to find more students" (teachstreet.com homepage, archived June 2011). Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company, TeachStreet was acquired by Amazon on February 2, 2012 and subsequently wound down. The teachstreet.com domain is now a dormant, Amazon-controlled brand-protection asset — MarkMonitor nameservers, a locked-down mail posture (SPF "v=spf1 -all", DMARC "p=reject" reporting to dmarc.amazon.com), and no A/AAAA/MX records — so there is no live website, developer portal, or API surface to enrich. This record is retained as a historical, defunct-company profile.

providers.name: Teamnote
providers.description: TeamNote is an enterprise mobile productivity and secure communication platform founded in Hong Kong in 2014 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2015 batch. Positioned as "Slack for mobile workforces," it gives corporations a mobile-first workspace for team messaging, collaboration, workflow forms, announcements, and content distribution to frontline and deskless staff, with enterprise security and administration controls. The product originally shipped at teamnoteapp.com (its first customer was Cheung Kong Holdings) and the company now presents at teamnote.ai. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documentation surface was discoverable during enrichment; both web properties are bot-protected.

providers.name: TeamUp Inc.
providers.description: TeamUp Inc. operates fanZ (fanzapp.io), a gamified football (soccer) fan-engagement mobile app for iOS and Android. fanZ combines fantasy football (fantaZ), social following of teams, leagues and players, prediction challenges and mini-games, a rewards system of points, badges and digital collectibles, an official merchandise store, and global leaderboards, plus news, match highlights and video content. The product is a consumer-facing mobile application operated by Wathbah for Information Technology and backed by 500 Global; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Technion Seed
providers.description: Technion Seed is an early-stage Israeli technology incubator and seed investment vehicle jointly owned by four venture capital funds — Vertex Ventures Israel, Battery Ventures, SCP-Vitalife and ProSeed — together with the Technion Research & Development Foundation. Through Technion Seed these funds invest up to roughly $1,000,000 in high-market-potential, early-stage technological ideas and ventures emerging from and around the Technion, helping entrepreneurs prove the viability of their idea at a stage of very high uncertainty. It is an investment firm and incubator rather than an API producer, and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: Telaria
providers.description: Telaria was an independent supply-side platform (SSP) for premium video and connected TV (CTV) advertising, formerly known as Tremor Video's sell-side business. Its Video Management Platform (VMP) combined an ad server built for advanced/OTT TV with real-time analytics, automated decisioning, yield optimization, and integrated programmatic plus direct-sold monetization for publishers of digital video inventory. On April 1, 2020 Telaria completed an all-stock merger of equals with Rubicon Project to form Magnite, now the largest independent sell-side advertising platform spanning CTV, desktop, and mobile. Telaria no longer operates as a standalone company: the telaria.com domain redirects to magnite.com, and the "Telaria" name survives publicly only as a Prebid.js header-bidding bidder adapter routed through Magnite. This profile documents the historical company; there is no independent public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or documentation portal to harvest.

providers.name: TellApart
providers.description: TellApart was a predictive-marketing and cross-device retargeting technology company founded in 2009 by former Google AdWords-API engineers Josh McFarland and Mark Ayzenshtat. Its cloud-based customer data platform unified shopper profiles across channels and devices and used machine-learning scoring to power dynamic product ads and direct-response retargeting for retailers such as Neiman Marcus, Wayfair, Sur La Table and Pottery Barn. TellApart was acquired by Twitter in April 2015 for roughly $533M in stock and folded into Twitter's advertising business; it no longer operates as an independent company and the tellapart.com domain is now parked with no live developer or API surface. Surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: TellApart (acquired by Twitter in 2015)
providers.description: TellApart (acquired by Twitter in 2015) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ai-apps. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Tello
providers.description: Tello (Tello Applications, Inc.) was a customer-feedback and customer-service ratings startup founded in 2010 in Palo Alto, California by Joe Beninato and backed by 500 Global. It offered a free web and mobile application that let consumers rate and comment on their in-person service experiences at businesses (including feedback on specific employees), and sold businesses paid dashboard access to monitor how their staff were rated. The company has since shut down; no live product, developer program, or public API surface remains, so this record is retained as a defunct-company profile rather than an active provider for enrichment.

providers.name: TellTail
providers.description: TellTail was a community-first platform providing community, education, and business support to dog breeders, connecting certified breeders with families seeking puppies. Backed by a $3.4M seed round led by General Catalyst (April 2022, with Scribble Ventures and Companion Fund). Surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company has since ceased operations ("TellTail is closing its doors"); it operated a consumer marketplace and community product with no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or event surface.

providers.name: Tempo Automation
providers.description: Tempo Automation is a San Francisco-based software-automated printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) manufacturer, founded in 2013 and formerly publicly traded on Nasdaq as TMPO. Its software-driven manufacturing platform was built to take complex electronics from design to physical prototype and new product introduction in as little as a few days, serving customers in aerospace, medical technology, semiconductor, industrial, and automotive. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and Uncork Capital. The company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its current website is a single-page placeholder offering on-demand circuit board manufacturing through a contact form.

providers.name: tempow
providers.description: Tempow was a Paris-based startup (founded 2016) building software to improve Bluetooth audio connectivity, including an operating system for true-wireless earbuds and multi-device audio streaming licensed to chipset makers and Android device manufacturers such as Motorola and TCL. Backed by Balderton Capital and C4 Ventures, Tempow was acquired by Google in 2021. The company operated as a B2B embedded-software and licensing business and never published a public developer API. Its website (www.tempow.com) no longer resolves. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirms there is no live API surface.

providers.name: Tenet Industries
providers.description: Tenet Industries is a Swedish defense-technology startup founded in 2026 by Hugo Frisk, Fabian Andersson, and Emil Falk (students from KTH Royal Institute of Technology and the Stockholm School of Economics) building low-cost, mass-producible defense systems. Applying design-for-manufacturing and first-principles engineering, the company starts with strike/attack drones — a kamikaze quadcopter that assembles in two minutes with roughly half the parts of comparable systems — and extends the same hardware/software platform to loitering munitions, jammers, radars, and missile systems. Backed by Y Combinator ($500K). As a defense hardware manufacturer, Tenet Industries currently publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tennis Channel
providers.description: Tennis Channel is a United States-based cable television network and direct-to-consumer streaming service dedicated to tennis and racquet sports, including live coverage and highlights from the ATP Tour, WTA Tour, Grand Slam events, and related pickleball and padel programming.
