Alongside its linear TV channel it operates a subscription streaming product (Tennis Channel / formerly Tennis Channel Plus) delivering live matches, on-demand video, news, rankings, and instructional content across web, mobile, and connected-TV apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Tennis Channel publishes a consumer streaming platform but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: tenXer *
providers.description: tenXer was a San Francisco productivity-analytics startup that helped engineering leads measure and improve team performance by pulling data from the tools engineers already used (GitHub, JIRA, Pivotal Tracker, etc.) and turning it into manager-facing views, stats and insights. Backed by True Ventures, GV (Google Ventures) and Khosla Ventures (~$5M raised), the company was acquired by Twitter in April 2015 for under $50M and folded into Twitter's internal engineering-tools effort. The standalone product and public developer surface no longer exist; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. No live API, developer portal, or documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Terbium Labs
providers.description: Terbium Labs was a Baltimore-based dark web data intelligence and digital risk protection company (founded 2013) best known for Matchlight, a fully private, automated platform that used patented data-fingerprinting to detect a customer's sensitive data (PII, credentials, intellectual property) as it appeared for sale or leak across the open, deep, and dark web. Matchlight was offered through a web console and a REST API, plus an "Unstructured Data Pipe" that streamed raw crawled dark-web source data to partners. Terbium Labs was acquired by Deloitte in June 2021, with its technology, most staff, and customers folded into Deloitte's Detect & Respond cyber practice. The independent company no longer operates and its developer surface at terbiumlabs.com is offline (the domain resolves no A records and there is no public GitHub organization), so no live API artifacts can be harvested.

providers.name: Terra Bella (fka Skybox Imaging)
providers.description: Terra Bella, originally founded in 2009 as Skybox Imaging (Mountain View, California), was a satellite imaging and geospatial analytics company that built and operated the SkySat constellation of high-resolution Earth-observation satellites. Google acquired Skybox Imaging in 2014 for roughly $500 million and rebranded it Terra Bella. In 2017 Alphabet/Google sold Terra Bella and its SkySat satellites to Planet Labs, folding the business into Planet's Earth-observation operations. Terra Bella no longer exists as an independent operating entity and publishes no independent developer portal, API, or SDK surface; its capabilities live on inside Planet Labs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners.

providers.name: Terra Industries
providers.description: Terra Industries is a Nigeria-based defense-technology company, positioning itself as Africa's first defense prime, that designs, manufactures, and deploys autonomous multi-domain security systems across air, land, and eventually sea. Founded in 2024 by Nathan Nwachuku and Maxwell Maduka, the company builds ArtemisOS (an AI-powered operating system for infrastructure security), the Archer long-range VTOL surveillance drone, the Iroko modular UAV, the Duma autonomous unmanned ground vehicle, and the Kallon solar-powered AI sentry tower to monitor, detect, and respond to threats such as terrorism, sabotage, and armed attacks on critical infrastructure including hydropower plants, mines, and power assets. Terra raised $11.75M led by 8VC in January 2026. As a hardware and defense-systems manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained as a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tetra
providers.description: Tetra (Tetra AI) was a Seattle, Washington startup building on-device AI models for vision, audio, and speech, optimized to run efficiently on mobile, compute, automotive, and IoT hardware. Backed by Wing Venture Capital and Shield Capital, the company was acquired by Qualcomm on October 1, 2023 and its technology and team were absorbed into Qualcomm's AI model and Snapdragon efforts. As an independent company Tetra no longer operates a standalone website, developer portal, or public API surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich. This profile is retained as a Wing Venture Capital portfolio record with its identity reconciled to the acquired entity.

providers.name: The Backplane
providers.description: The Backplane, Inc. was a US social-network-builder startup (founded 2011) that built branded social networks for fan groups and organizations, most notably Lady Gaga's Little Monsters community, and later pivoted to the Place.xyz network-building platform. Backed by Battery Ventures, GV, Sequoia, Greylock and others, it raised roughly $18.9M before running out of money, going out of business in April 2016 and selling all of its assets (patents, code, trademarks, URLs). The company is defunct; enrichment found no live website, developer portal, API, specification, or SDK surface to catalog.

providers.name: The Boring Company
providers.description: The Boring Company is an American infrastructure and tunnel-construction company founded by Elon Musk in 2016 that designs and builds underground transportation, utility, and freight tunnels to reduce urban traffic congestion. Its Prufrock tunnel-boring machines dig low-cost tunnels roughly a mile a week, and its all-electric, zero-emissions Loop system carries passengers in Tesla vehicles through those tunnels — the Las Vegas Convention Center Loop is its first commercial deployment. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; its web presence is marketing, careers, Vegas Loop ticketing, and a merchandise store.

providers.name: The Echo Nest
providers.description: The Echo Nest was a music-intelligence company, spun out of the MIT Media Lab, that ran a developer platform and API for music understanding — machine-listening audio analysis (tempo, key, energy, danceability, valence), artist and song metadata, automated playlisting and taste profiles, and the Rosetta Stone service for translating artist and track IDs across music services. It was acquired by Spotify in March 2014 (reported at roughly €49.7M / ~$100M). Spotify consolidated onto its own Web API: The Echo Nest API stopped issuing new keys on 2016-03-29 and stopped serving requests on 2016-05-31, with developers directed to the Spotify Web API (whose audio-features and audio-analysis endpoints descend from Echo Nest technology). The developer.echonest.com portal no longer resolves; the echonest.com domain now redirects to an unrelated WordPress site. This profile was surfaced as a matrix-partners portfolio company; it is retained for historical/lineage reference and has no live, public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: The Inside
providers.description: The Inside is a direct-to-consumer, made-to-order home furnishings brand founded in 2017 by Christiane Lemieux and Britt Bunn, offering customizable upholstered furniture — sofas, chairs, beds, headboards, and decor — in 100+ fabrics and patterns. Backed by Canaan Partners along with Corigin Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Forerunner Ventures, and BAM Ventures, it was acquired by Havenly in February 2022. Surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network; during enrichment no public developer API, OpenAPI, or well-known metadata surface was found — theinside.com serves an e-commerce storefront with no documented programmatic interface.

providers.name: The League
providers.description: The League is an American social and dating mobile application founded in 2014 by Amanda Bradford and launched in 2015. It positions itself as a selective, career-oriented dating community ("Date. Intelligently."), using an application/waitlist model and LinkedIn/Facebook-based verification to curate its membership. The League was acquired by Match Group in 2022 and operates as a consumer iOS/Android app. It is a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures. As a consumer mobile app it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or partner API surface.

providers.name: The OK Company
providers.description: The OK Company was a consumer technology startup, backed by Obvious Ventures, best known for OK Play - a mobile app for iOS and Android that turned screen time into a catalyst for real-world, parent-and-child play activities designed to build empathy, kindness, and creativity in young children. It was founded by CEO JJ Aguhob and President Chris Ovitz (previously co-founders of the mobile video app Viddy), with developmental psychologist Dr. Colleen Russo Johnson as Chief Scientist. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - its domain theokcompany.com no longer resolves to a product site and instead redirects to a third-party domain-sale listing. The OK Company was a consumer mobile app business and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer platform, so there is no API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company lead.

providers.name: The Old Reader
providers.description: RSS reader

providers.name: The Players' Tribune
providers.description: The Players' Tribune is a sports-media company that gives athletes a platform to connect directly with fans in their own words, publishing first-person stories, essays, letters, and video from professional players across football, basketball, soccer, baseball, and other sports. Founded in 2014 and backed by GV and IVP, it operates as a digital publisher rather than an API provider: an enrichment probe of theplayerstribune.com found a public sports-content website with no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface (no docs/api/developer subdomains, no /.well-known/ metadata, no llms.txt). This profile captures the company identity and the results of a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: The Report of the Week
providers.description: Food & Drink Reviews

providers.name: The Rounds
providers.description: The Rounds was a membership-based sustainable grocery and household-goods delivery startup (backed by a16z and Redpoint Ventures) built around reusable packaging and reducing single-use waste. The company has since been wound down and folded into Misfits Market — as of this enrichment pass https://www.therounds.co/ returns an HTTP 301 redirect to a Misfits Market "welcome-new-rounds" landing page ("Same Mission, More Groceries"). No developer portal, API, documentation, or public API surface was found; api./docs./developer.therounds.co do not resolve. This profile is retained as a network lead with an acquired/defunct status.

providers.name: The Sentience Company
providers.description: The Sentience Company builds a consumer AI product at sentience.company under the tagline "Build the digital version of you" — a personal AI persona / digital-twin experience where an individual creates and shares a digital version of themselves. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures (sector: ai-apps) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API surface, or /.well-known/ discovery documents were found — the site is a client-rendered single-page app that returns identical HTML (soft-404) for every path, so this remains an identity-only lead with no API to catalog.

providers.name: TheFind (Meta)
providers.description: TheFind (Meta) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: commerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Theres Camping
providers.description: Theres (데얼스, Theres Co., Ltd.) is a South Korean e-commerce marketplace for outdoor and camping gear, where customers buy both new and second-hand equipment in one place. The platform aggregates brands and vendors (Grape Box, Camping Khan, Ridge Mountain Gear, Matador, and others), offering product search, a shopping cart, deal notifications, a community section, and vendor/product listing tools. Based in Seoul (Seocho-gu), Theres is a portfolio company of 500 Global. The company publishes a consumer web/app storefront and does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or integration surface.

providers.name: thetab
providers.description: The Tab (thetab.com) is a UK-based digital media and entertainment publication operated by Digitalbox Publishing Ltd (Co Reg No. 09909897). It covers celebrity and reality-TV news, viral trends, gaming, politics, and university and campus culture across a network of youth-focused verticals, monetized primarily through advertising (advertise.thetab.com). Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, /.well-known/ discovery surface, or llms.txt (all probed and returned HTTP 404); this remains an editorial/advertising media property with no developer-facing product.

providers.name: Thing Labs
providers.description: Thing Labs was an early consumer social-software startup founded in 2008 by Jason Shellen (previously a product lead on Blogger and a co-creator of Google Reader at Google). The company built browser-based social tools including Plinky (daily writing prompts), Brizzly and the Brizzly Guide (a web-based Twitter/social client), and Let's Be Trends. Backed by SoftTech VC (now Uncork Capital) alongside angel investors, Thing Labs was acquired by AOL in September 2010, after which Shellen became VP of Product for AOL's AIM & Messaging group. Thing Labs no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no public developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ThirdLove
providers.description: ThirdLove is a San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer women's intimate apparel brand best known for its online Fit Finder quiz and half-cup bra sizing, selling bras, underwear, and loungewear direct to consumers through its e-commerce site. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of a16z and Felicis. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public developer or API surface — no developer subdomain, no documented API, no /.well-known/ discovery documents, and no security.txt or trust-center program. Only a domain-security probe of thirdlove.com yielded real data (TLS 1.3, HSTS, SPF, DMARC).

providers.name: Thistle Technologies
providers.description: Thistle Technologies provides security tools, libraries, and services for the developers who build connected and embedded devices. Founded by security veteran Window Snyder and backed by DCVC, the company offers a turnkey embedded-device security platform whose two headline products are the Thistle Update Solution (end-to-end over-the-air firmware and software updates for Embedded Linux on ARM/ARM64 and x86-64 as well as Infineon PSoC 6 microcontrollers) and Thistle Secure Boot Enablement (tools and services for enabling secure/verified boot with managed key handling and firmware signing on hardware such as Espressif ESP32, Infineon OPTIGA Trust M secure elements, and U-Boot targets including the Raspberry Pi 4 and BeagleBone). Thistle helps device makers add mechanisms that keep IoT and edge/AI hardware updatable and resistant to compromise without building the security infrastructure themselves. The offering is delivered as SDKs, libraries, and managed services integrated into a customer's device firmware rather than as a public web API.

providers.name: Thomas
providers.description: Thomas is a Y Combinator-backed startup (Spring 2026 batch) based in San Francisco, building what it describes as the world's first AI founder: an autonomous AI agent that starts, runs, and grows its own companies on the internet end to end. Founded by Thomas Cloarec (the company was formerly named HireThomas, Inc. / MadeByThomas), it operates a public marketing site at madebythomas.ai. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, CLI, or developer documentation; the site is a single-page marketing application and its internal /api/ and /events/ routes are explicitly disallowed to crawlers via robots.txt.

providers.name: thorough
providers.description: thorough (透彻未来 / Thorough Future) is a China-based company surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its site at thorough.ai serves a Chinese-language single-page web application over HTTP only (HTTPS is unreachable at the time of this pass) and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification surface. This profile remains a lead awaiting a public developer surface.

providers.name: Thread
providers.description: Thread (thread.com) was a UK-based fashion technology company that combined AI with human expert stylists to deliver personalized clothing recommendations for men and women. Founded by Kieran O'Neill and Ben Phillips and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Balderton Capital, Thread's brand, technology and data were acquired by Marks & Spencer. The company subsequently entered administration and has ceased trading; its site now serves only a shutdown notice. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or event surface. This profile is retained as a network record of a defunct portfolio company.

providers.name: Threadless ( Skinny CM Holdings)
providers.description: Threadless (operated by Skinny CM Holdings) is an online design community and print-on-demand apparel marketplace founded in 2000 in Chicago. Artists and designers submit artwork, the community scores and votes on submissions, and winning designs are printed on t-shirts, apparel, wall art, home goods, and accessories sold through the site. Threadless also runs Artist Shops, free hosted storefronts that let independent creators sell their designs on a print-on-demand basis without holding inventory. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer API surface was reachable during this pass (the storefront aggressively blocks automated access).

providers.name: Three Squirrels
providers.description: Three Squirrels (三只松鼠) is a Chinese consumer snack company founded in 2012 by Zhang Liaoyuan and headquartered in Wuhu, Anhui Province. Positioned as one of China's first internet-native food brands, it sells nuts, seeds, dried fruits, baked goods, and other leisure snacks primarily through e-commerce channels (Tmall, JD.com, and its own storefronts) alongside a growing offline retail footprint. The company is publicly listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange ChiNext board (stock code 300783). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; as a consumer packaged-goods retailer it does not publish a public developer API, open platform, or API documentation. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Three Wheels United
providers.description: Three Wheels United is a fintech-driven electric vehicle financing company in India, founded in 2017 by Cedrick Tandong, Kevin Wervenbos, and Apurv Mehra. It works to remove the financial barriers to clean mobility by providing loans for two- and three-wheeler electric vehicles — starting with auto-rickshaws — disbursed through its RBI-registered NBFC lending partner Shabri Investments Private Limited. The company pairs credit with a mobile app that helps drivers manage their loans and connect to services, and reports over 4,000 vehicles financed, 20,000+ customers served, and thousands of tonnes of CO2 reduced across Bangalore, Mumbai, and the Delhi NCR (Noida) region. It is backed by Techstars, Delta Corp Holdings, Asian Development Bank Ventures, Microsoft, and other global investors, having raised roughly $10 million in Series A funding. It is a consumer-facing lender with no public developer program, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Tiamat
providers.description: Tiamat is a frontier-technology startup backed by DCM Ventures. It closed a Series A round of nearly $10 million co-led by DCM and Vitalbridge (announced May 2023). The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead from dcm-ventures. Its primary web presence, tiamat.com, is served entirely behind a Chinese CDN (Tencent EdgeOne) and was not reachable from the enrichment environment; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or other API surface was discoverable during this pass. This profile remains a stub awaiting a reachable API surface before artifact enrichment can proceed.

providers.name: Ticketfly
providers.description: Ticketfly was a San Francisco-based event-ticketing platform for independent music venues, promoters, and festivals, founded in 2008. It was acquired by Eventbrite in 2017 and, following a June 2018 data breach, was shut down in November 2018 with its music-oriented features folded into Eventbrite Music. The company is defunct: as of 2026 every Ticketfly host (www.ticketfly.com, developer.ticketfly.com) returns HTTP 301 redirects to eventbrite.com. No independent Ticketfly API, developer portal, documentation, or specification survives. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Ticketmonster
providers.description: Ticketmonster (TMON) is a South Korean e-commerce and social-commerce platform founded in 2010 as "Ticket Monster." Operating primarily at tmon.co.kr (the legacy ticketmonster.co.kr brand), TMON sells deals, daily bargains, fashion, travel, and a broad retail catalog to Korean consumers via web and mobile apps. It grew into one of Korea's leading online marketplaces and was later brought under the Qoo10 group. TMON is a consumer-facing retail/marketplace business; it does not publish a public developer program, API portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documented API surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed the absence of any public API surface.

providers.name: Tidal Metals
providers.description: Tidal Metals is a deep-tech materials company that extracts decarbonized magnesium directly from seawater and desalination brine using only electricity from renewable sources, without mining, chemical additives, or brine waste. The company's patented process concentrates and extracts magnesium salt to address a critical supply-chain vulnerability: the United States currently produces no primary magnesium while China controls roughly 91% of global supply. Founded by Ph.D. physicists and engineers with backgrounds in nuclear engineering and plasma physics from MIT, Princeton, and Wisconsin-Madison, and backed by DCVC, Tidal Metals aims for carbon-neutral, domestically scalable magnesium production. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface at this time.

providers.name: TidalScale
providers.description: TidalScale built software-defined server technology that aggregated the CPU, memory, and I/O of multiple commodity servers into a single large virtual machine (an inverse hypervisor / software-defined memory approach), enabling in-memory computing for very large workloads without specialized hardware. The company was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in early 2022, and the tidalscale.com domain now redirects into HPE infrastructure (its TLS endpoint serves an HPE certificate). This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline; TidalScale exposes no independent public developer API surface today.

providers.name: Tidemark
providers.description: Tidemark is enterprise financial and operational planning software for continuous, extended, and driver-based planning. It provides scenario ("what-if") modeling, workflow and approvals, and real-time data integration across 140+ ERP and EPM systems for budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning. Founded as a venture-backed cloud analytics and enterprise performance management (EPM) company and counted among the Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) portfolio, Tidemark was later acquired and is now offered as a product within the insightsoftware family. It has no publicly documented API, SDK, or developer portal; integration is delivered through pre-built ERP/EPM connectors rather than a public developer program.

providers.name: Tiebaobei
providers.description: Tiebaobei (铁甲二手机) is a used construction-machinery C2C trading platform operated by Beijing Tiejialong Technology Co., Ltd. (北京铁甲龙科技有限公司). Founded in 2009 out of the Tiebaobei (Cehome) construction-equipment forum, it lets individuals buy and sell used excavators, loaders, bulldozers, cranes, rotary drills and other heavy equipment, backed by a network of ~400 regional "city manager" brokers across 30 Chinese provinces who verify and co-inspect machines. The platform layers industry news, equipment inspection/detection, price rankings and financing services on top of the marketplace. It raised A financing from Qiming Venture Partners, a DCM-led Series B (¥100M, 2015) and a Yuansheng-led Series C (¥200M, 2016). This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public developer API or open platform was found.

providers.name: TimeBlocks
providers.description: TimeBlocks is a consumer calendar and personal scheduling mobile app developed by Day2Life Inc., a South Korean company backed by 500 Global. Marketed as Korea's #1 decoration calendar, it brings calendar, to-do, memo, and habit tracking together in a single view, with patented drag-and-drop time-block scheduling (US Patent 10,409,474 B2), roughly 1,000 customization items (themes, stickers, fonts), shared and group calendars with real-time notifications, seven home-screen widgets, and cloud sync across devices. It is a native iOS and Android app; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Timeful
providers.description: Timeful was a smart time-management and scheduling application surfaced as a portfolio company of dcvc. Per dcvc's own portfolio listing it is an EXIT — acquired by Alphabet/Google — and no longer operates as an independent company. There is no standalone Timeful website, developer portal, or public API surface to enrich; its scheduling technology was absorbed into Google's calendar products after the acquisition.

providers.name: Times Adder
providers.description: With this API you can add each of the times introduced in the array sended

providers.name: Tiny Comet
providers.description: Tiny Comet is an educational games studio building history-based simulation RPGs for school-aged children, founded by Emily Tierney and Anca Agapi. Its first title, Nation Survival, is an immersive educational role-playing game on the Roblox platform. The studio came out of the a16z SPEEDRUN accelerator and has raised additional venture capital from Andreessen Horowitz and Roble Ventures. Tiny Comet is a consumer gaming and edtech company with no public developer or API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tipp24
providers.description: Tipp24 is a German consumer online-lottery brand — a business-to-consumer service where players place bets on the outcomes of state and international lottery draws (secondary lottery / lottery brokerage) over the web and mobile apps. The brand is operated by ZEAL Network SE, a publicly listed company headquartered in Hamburg, Germany, whose email infrastructure (SPF/DMARC) still resolves to zealnetwork.de. Tipp24 is a regulated consumer gambling product; it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs, and its web properties (tipp24.de, tipp24.com) sit behind Cloudflare bot protection. This profile originated as an Earlybird VC portfolio lead and was processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline, which confirmed the absence of an API surface and captured the domain security posture of the brand.

providers.name: To Summer
providers.description: To Summer (观夏 / Guanxia) is a Chinese premium home-fragrance and lifestyle brand founded in Beijing, known for its Eastern-inspired scented candles, incense, diffusers, perfumes, and bath and body products. Positioned as a direct-to-consumer scent brand, it sells primarily through its own website, WeChat mini-program, Tmall flagship store, and a growing footprint of physical concept stores across China. To Summer is backed by IDG Capital and was surfaced through the API Evangelist venture-portfolio pipeline. As a consumer retail brand it exposes a customer-facing e-commerce experience rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and the outcome of an enrichment probe that found no public API surface.

providers.name: Toasty
providers.description: Toasty (toasty.family, published by Wenose) is a French consumer mobile application for responsible, sustainable, and ethical shopping. The app curates committed brands and makes conscious consumption engaging through a gamified experience of daily private sales, quizzes, challenges, gifts, and rewards. It reports a 4.9-star rating across the app stores and more than 400,000 downloads. Toasty is a business-to-consumer mobile product with no public developer program, API, or documentation surface at this time; it was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. This profile captures its public identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Toolsvilla
providers.description: Toolsvilla is an India-based e-commerce marketplace for machinery, tools, and equipment, positioning itself as one of India's largest online stores for industrial, agricultural, and power tools serving small businesses, farmers, and trade buyers. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs were found during this enrichment pass; the site's internal backend at api.toolsvilla.com is undocumented and returns a bare JSON response.

providers.name: Tops Friendly Markets
providers.description: Tops Friendly Markets is a regional supermarket chain headquartered in Amherst, New York operating 152 grocery stores and 58 gas station and convenience stores across upstate New York, northern Pennsylvania, and Vermont. In November 2021 Tops Holding II merged with Price Chopper / Market 32 to form Northeast Grocery Inc, a roughly 300-store regional alliance under common ownership. The Tops consumer brand continues to operate an e-commerce platform with online grocery pickup and DoorDash delivery, the BonusPlus loyalty card program with digital coupons and gas rewards, the MoolahVille cash back rewards program, in-store pharmacies, gift cards, and iOS and Android mobile apps. Vendor and supplier engagement is handled through Northeast Shared Services. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, webhook, EDI portal, status page, RSS feed, or changelog is published for the Tops brand.

providers.name: TopXGun
providers.description: TopXGun (Nanjing TopXGun Robotics / 拓攻机器人) is a Chinese unmanned aerial vehicle manufacturer specializing in the research, development, and production of agricultural spray drones, heavy-lift delivery drones, industrial and cleaning drones, firefighting and emergency UAVs, tethered drones, eVTOL and large unmanned aircraft, and the professional flight-control and avionics hardware, payload equipment, and software systems that power them. Its whole-aircraft capability spans all airspace below 5,000 meters and payloads up to 1.5 tons across core industries, and it offers ODM/OEM customization and education support. Its overseas agricultural line is marketed as TopXGun Agriculture (topxgunag.com) with CE, FCC, RoHS, and KC certifications. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. No public web API, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment; this is a hardware manufacturer.

providers.name: Torbit
providers.description: Torbit was a web-performance-optimization startup (real-user monitoring and automated front-end optimization) backed by 500 Startups, acquired by Walmart Labs in 2013. The product has long been discontinued; the enrichment pass found no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface. torbit.com no longer serves a site and now resolves to Walmart brand-protection infrastructure (MarkMonitor registrar, UltraDNS nameservers, Proofpoint mail), with both HTTP and HTTPS requests timing out.

providers.name: Toyota Connected
providers.description: Toyota Connected is Toyota Motor Corporation's global connected mobility technology arm, building the data, telematics, and software platforms that power Toyota and Lexus connected vehicle services worldwide. The group operates as a federation of regional subsidiaries — TOYOTA Connected Corporation (Japan), Toyota Connected North America (TCNA, Plano, Texas), TOYOTA Connected Europe (TCEU, United Kingdom), TOYOTA Connected India (TCIN), TOYOTA Connected Asia Pacific, and Toyota Tsusho Connected Middle East — and runs Toyota's Mobility Service Platform (MSPF) and the Drivelink telematics backbone behind Safety Connect, Service Connect, Remote Connect, Destination Assist, Wi-Fi Connect, and the "Hey Toyota" in-vehicle voice assistant. TCNA reports surpassing five million connected customer calls across Toyota and Lexus and runs Toyota's Big Data Center for connected-vehicle data. KINTO — Toyota's mobility services brand for car subscription, car-sharing, ride-hailing, and carpooling (KINTO One, KINTO Flex, KINTO Share, KINTO Ride, KINTO Join) — sits adjacent in Toyota's mobility portfolio and is powered by KINTO Technologies on AWS. Toyota exposes developer portals at developer.eig.toyota.com (Toyota API Portal covering TMC, TMNA, TEMA, TFS, NAMC, and other entities) and developer.toyotaconnected.eu (Toyota Connected EU API services, including Telematics and Vehicle APIs documented with Swagger/OpenAPI), but access is gated to partners and internal Toyota teams — no public, unauthenticated OpenAPI specifications are published. Third-party access to Toyota vehicle data for individual developers is typically brokered through partners such as Smartcar and High Mobility rather than directly via Toyota's own portals.

providers.name: Tracksby
providers.description: Tracksby (Tracks.by) was a music marketing startup that helped artists and their managers release new music and videos through deep Facebook integration, social launch campaigns, fan email capture, and YouTube/VEVO embeds, turning each release into a fan-growth campaign. Listed on the a16z investment list, the early-2010s company is now defunct - tracks.by no longer resolves, tracksby.com is parked for sale, the @TracksBy Twitter account is gone, and its GitHub account has been inactive since 2012. No public API surface was found, so this profile records an inactive portfolio lead with no artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Tractor Supply
providers.description: Tractor Supply Company is the largest rural lifestyle retailer in the United States, providing products to support recreational farming, ranching, and country lifestyles. Tractor Supply integrates with suppliers and vendors via EDI and vendor portal systems, enabling order management, invoice processing, and shipment notifications. The company operates through its vendor transaction portal for supplier collaboration and EDI-based supply chain integrations.

providers.name: Tradesy
providers.description: Tradesy was a Los Angeles-based online marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned luxury and designer fashion, founded in 2009 and backed by 500 Global among others. In March 2022 it was acquired by Paris-based Vestiaire Collective to accelerate that company's expansion into the US resale market, and the standalone Tradesy brand was subsequently wound down. The tradesy.com domain now redirects to vestiairecollective.com, and Tradesy no longer operates an independent website, developer program, or public API. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record.

providers.name: Transport for Berlin, Germany
providers.description: Third-party VBB API

providers.name: Transport for The Netherlands
providers.description: OVAPI, country-wide public transport

providers.name: Treat.co
providers.description: Treat.co was a consumer gifting e-commerce startup surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass the treat.co domain is controlled by Mars, Incorporated: it resolves to an AWS Application Load Balancer presenting a certificate for alb-redirect.mars.com and returns HTTP 403 on every probed path (homepage, /.well-known/security.txt, /api, /developers), with no MX record for email. The company therefore exposes no public website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface today; it appears dormant or absorbed following acquisition. This profile records the domain-security probe and is retained as a network lead pending any revived or successor developer surface.

providers.name: TRED
providers.description: TRED is a Seattle-based peer-to-peer online marketplace for buying and selling used cars, founded in 2011 and backed by Techstars, Maveron, Lowercase Capital, and Founders' Co-op. The platform let private buyers and sellers list vehicles, ask questions, schedule concierge-delivered test drives, and complete financed purchases online, with concierges compensated on customer-service reviews rather than sales commission. The tred.com domain now resolves to Cox Automotive / Autotrader infrastructure, indicating TRED has been absorbed into Cox Automotive; it operates as a consumer web product with no public developer program, API, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: TrendKite
providers.description: TrendKite was an Austin, Texas PR and media intelligence platform founded in 2013 that used AI and big-data analytics to measure the impact of earned media on brand reputation, website traffic, and business goals. It was acquired by Cision in January 2019 for approximately $225 million and folded into the Cision Communications Cloud. TrendKite no longer operates as an independent company. Its former domain (trendkite.com) now redirects to cision.com, and no independent TrendKite developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface exists. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record; there is no standalone API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Trendy Entertainment
providers.description: Trendy Entertainment was a Gainesville, Florida video game studio best known for the Dungeon Defenders tower-defense action-RPG franchise. Insight Venture Partners acquired the studio in 2012 for ~$18.2M and exited in 2019 when founder Augi Lye led an employee buyback and rebranded the company as Chromatic Games (chromatic.games). The only developer-facing surface the studio ever shipped is the Dungeon Defenders Development Kit — an Unreal Engine 3 game-mod SDK distributed as free Steam DLC — not a public web/HTTP API. Enrichment pass found no OpenAPI, REST API, developer portal, or client SDK registries: this is a games company with no programmable API surface, so most scored artifact types are N/A rather than missing.

providers.name: Trinity Industries
providers.description: Trinity Industries, Inc. is a leading manufacturer and lessor of railcars in North America, providing products and services to the industrial, energy, transportation, and construction sectors. The company designs, manufactures, leases, and manages railcars used to transport commodities such as energy products, agricultural goods, construction materials, and consumer staples. Trinity operates a lease fleet of over 140,000 owned and managed railcars through its TrinityRail division.

providers.name: Trion Worlds
providers.description: Trion Worlds was an American video game developer and MMO publisher founded in 2006 in Redwood City, California by Lars Buttler and Jon Van Caneghem, and backed early by Trinity Ventures among others. It developed and operated massively multiplayer titles including Rift, Defiance, Trove and Atlas Reactor, published ArcheAge in Western markets, and ran the Glyph game-distribution client. The company was acquired by German publisher Gamigo in October 2018 and disbanded shortly after; its games, the Glyph platform and the trionworlds.com domain are now operated by Gamigo. Trion Worlds never published a public developer API or developer program, so this network profile carries company identity and domain-security signals only. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: Tripplus
providers.description: TripPlus (點數旅遊) is a Taiwan-based travel-rewards and loyalty-points platform. It provides airline mileage award-ticket search and redemption tools, curated recommendations and comparisons of US travel credit cards, and a marketplace for buying and selling airline miles and reward points. The consumer-facing site (tripplus.cc) is fronted by Cloudflare and, as of this enrichment pass, exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documented well-known endpoints. Backed by 500 Global; tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Trocafone
providers.description: Trocafone is a Brazilian e-commerce company specializing in refurbished and pre-owned smartphones and consumer electronics sold with warranty. Operating primarily in Brazil on the VTEX commerce platform, it runs a consumer marketplace for certified semi-new iPhones, Samsung, Motorola and other devices, a trade-in program ("Venda seu aparelho") that buys used devices from consumers, and a Reparofone device-repair service. Backed by 500 Global, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: TrueLens
providers.description: TrueLens was a marketing-technology startup providing social media analytics and customer intelligence. Its product, Socialgraphics, helped brands target customers using data compiled and analyzed from multiple social networks for marketing campaigns. Google Ventures (GV) led a roughly $1.2M funding round in 2012; the company was small (2-10 employees). TrueLens now appears defunct: its former domain truelens.com 301-redirects to an unrelated retailer (misterspex.de), and no public API, developer portal, or documentation could be found. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Truffle
providers.description: Truffle is an AI-native restaurant operating system building "the autonomous back of house for restaurants" — one platform to manage an entire restaurant operation more profitably. The company, a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) portfolio company operating at usetruffle.ai, positions its product as an autonomous back-of-house layer that unifies the operational and administrative work that normally sprawls across separate tools. As of this profile Truffle is a very early-stage company presenting a single marketing landing page; it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, CLI, or other machine-readable developer surface, so this API Evangelist profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture and will be re-enriched as a developer surface emerges.

providers.name: Trust
providers.description: Trust (Trust Software Inc., trust.co) was a fintech and marketing-technology startup founded in 2019 by James Borow, backed by a 2020 seed investment from Lightspeed Venture Partners. It began as a corporate card and community giving digital businesses higher credit limits and extended payment terms on marketing spend, then pivoted to Market (withmarket.com), an AI marketing assistant that let Shopify merchants chat with their business data. As of July 2026 both trust.co and withmarket.com no longer resolve in DNS and the company appears to have wound down. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface was ever published.

providers.name: TrustWeaver
providers.description: TrustWeaver was a Stockholm-based provider of on-demand e-invoicing and e-signature compliance services, giving multinational enterprises legally compliant electronic invoicing (VAT/tax compliance, authenticity and integrity via digital signatures) across dozens of countries. Backed by Creandum, the company was acquired by Pagero in 2018; Pagero was subsequently absorbed into Sovos (2024). The trustweaver.com domain now issues a 301 redirect to Sovos's e-invoicing compliance solution, so no independent TrustWeaver developer portal, public API, or API documentation remains online. This profile is retained as a historical/acquisition lead in the API Evangelist network; there is no standalone API surface to enrich.

providers.name: TryTry (穿穿)
providers.description: TryTry (穿穿, trytrytw.com) was a Taiwanese women's fashion e-commerce brand ("是妳，決定了這件衣服的表情" — "It's you who decides the expression of this dress"), active around 2015-2016 and surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company. The business appears defunct — as of 2026-07-21 trytrytw.com is domain-squatted (wildcard DNS to a parked Chinese web-design page, serving an expired TLS certificate issued for an unrelated host) and no developer, API, or documentation surface exists.

providers.name: TSM
providers.description: TSM (Team SoloMid) is a North American esports and gaming lifestyle organization, surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners in the consumer sector. Its public web presence at tsm.gg redirects to the official TSM Store (tsmshop.com), a Shopify-hosted storefront selling TSM apparel and accessories. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no first-party developer API surface: no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI, no resolving developer/api/docs subdomains, and no real /.well-known/ discovery documents (every probed path returned the storefront catch-all page). This profile is retained as a consumer-brand lead with only domain-security signals captured.

providers.name: tuhu
providers.description: Tuhu (途虎养车) is a Chinese online-to-offline automotive services platform founded in 2011 and headquartered in Shanghai. Through its app, website, and network of franchised and self-operated workshops it sells tires and provides car maintenance, repair, and related aftermarket services to consumers across China. Tuhu is publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (9690) and counts Qiming Venture Partners among its investors. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; enrichment probes found no public developer API, open platform, or developer portal.

providers.name: Tuhu Car
providers.description: Tuhu Car is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Tujia
providers.description: Tujia (途家) is a Chinese online marketplace for short-term rentals, vacation homes, and homestays, frequently described as "China's Airbnb." Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Beijing, the company connects travelers with apartments, villas, and serviced homes across China and select international destinations through its website, mobile apps, and WeChat mini-program. Tujia runs a consumer-facing booking marketplace and property-management services rather than a public developer platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; the enrichment pipeline probed the domain and found no public API, developer portal, or open platform for the company.

providers.name: Tule Technologies
providers.description: Tule Technologies was an agricultural technology company that measured crop water stress and actual evapotranspiration (ET) directly in the field, giving growers irrigation guidance through its FieldStat monitoring tool for orchards, vineyards, and row crops. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, Tule has been acquired by and integrated into CropX; the tuletechnologies.com domain now 301-redirects to cropx.com, where Tule's ET monitoring is combined with soil sensing, weather data, and irrigation management in one platform. Enrichment found no independent public API, developer portal, SDK, or documented developer program for Tule Technologies.

providers.name: Tumblbug
providers.description: Tumblbug (텀블벅) is a South Korean reward-based crowdfunding platform for creators, where makers launch projects and backers pledge funds to bring creative works — comics, games, publishing, design, music, film and more — to life. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Tumblbug publishes a consumer-facing web platform (help center, creator guides, pricing/advertising, terms and privacy pages) but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or open API surface; this profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Tundra
providers.description: Tundra is a business-to-business wholesale marketplace that connects independent retailers with brands and suppliers, letting shop owners discover, source, and order wholesale products across categories online. Backed by Redpoint Ventures, the company operates in the ecommerce sector. As of this enrichment pass Tundra exposes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface: live probes of tundra.com found no developer/api/docs subdomains and no /.well-known discovery documents, and the public www.tundra.com storefront was reachable but served an expired TLS certificate.

providers.name: Turnstyle
providers.description: Turnstyle (Turnstyle Analytics) was a WiFi-marketing and customer-analytics platform for brick-and-mortar businesses, capturing guest WiFi logins to build customer profiles, segments, and automated re-marketing campaigns. It was a 500 Global portfolio company and was acquired by Yelp, becoming Yelp WiFi. As of this enrichment pass the product no longer operates independently - its domain getturnstyle.com now permanently redirects through app.yelpwifi.com to business.yelp.com (Yelp for Business). No standalone Turnstyle developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs are published; there is no independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Tutornow
providers.description: Tutornow (tutornow.it) is an Italian online tutoring platform ("ripetizioni") that connects students from elementary school through university with qualified tutors across 150+ subjects, including math, physics, chemistry, and languages. It offers individual and group online lessons starting around €15/hour, homework help, exam and university preparation, academic-recovery programs, and specialized support for students with learning differences (DSA/BES), with 250,000+ lesson hours delivered and 20,000+ tutors across major Italian cities. Tutornow is a consumer (B2C) education service and publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal — this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TVTY
providers.description: TVTY is an advertising technology company that bridges television and digital advertising through its Moment Marketing platform. Its TV Ad Alert technology detects when a brand or competitor TV spot airs and synchronizes digital media campaigns — search, social, display and marketplace advertising — to those moments so advertisers reach audiences at the point of highest attention. TVTY was a Partech portfolio company serving global brands and media agencies.

providers.name: Twenty-First Century Fox
providers.description: Twenty-First Century Fox was an American multinational mass media corporation that operated film, television, and cable assets before being largely acquired by The Walt Disney Company in 2019. Its remaining broadcasting and news assets continued under Fox Corporation. The company no longer exists as an independent entity and did not expose public developer APIs.

providers.name: Twice
providers.description: Twice was an online marketplace for buying and selling secondhand clothing that operated at liketwice.com, and it appears on the Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) investment list. eBay acquired the Twice team in 2015 and the marketplace was shut down; liketwice.com now serves an HTTP 301 redirect to ebay.com (verified 2026-07-21) and no longer answers HTTPS. The company is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a defunct a16z portfolio lead with no public API surface.

providers.name: uBEAM
providers.description: uBeam was an ultrasonic wireless power startup founded in 2011 by Meredith Perry and headquartered in Marina del Rey, California. It raised roughly $26 million from Andreessen Horowitz, Upfront Ventures, Founders Fund, Mark Cuban, and Marissa Mayer to charge devices over the air using 45-75 kHz phased-array ultrasound. The company rebranded as SonicEnergy in December 2018 and went defunct on February 5, 2024, without shipping a commercial product. It published no developer APIs, SDKs, or documentation, and both ubeam.com and sonicenergy.com are now parked domains.

providers.name: Ubooly
providers.description: Ubooly was a children's smart-toy company that made "The Learning Toy that Listens" - a plush toy that turned a smartphone, iPod touch, or tablet into an interactive learning companion for kids aged 4-8, with hand-crafted play packs and voice interaction. A 500 Global portfolio company, Ubooly is now defunct; ubooly.com was last archived as a live storefront in late 2015 and today 301-redirects to an unrelated third-party site. No public API, developer portal, packages, or GitHub organization were found.

providers.name: UCode
providers.description: UCode was a STEM coding-education company ("Where Kids Learn to Code and Create") that taught kids and teens ages 6-19 software programming through classes, camps, and online instruction, creating apps, websites, and games. A seed-stage Bloomberg Beta portfolio company founded by Scott Mueller and Michael Yang, it is marked as exited in the Bloomberg Beta Manual. As of 2026-07-21 ucode.com is a parked domain listed for sale, and no API, developer, or platform surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Unifi
providers.description: Unifi Software was a self-service data platform built around an enterprise data catalog, with AI-based recommendations, data discovery, and data preparation tools aimed at business users. A Canaan Partners seed investment (led by Maha Ibrahim), the company was acquired by Dell Boomi, which announced its intent to acquire Unifi Software's data catalog and preparation technology in December 2019; by mid-2020 the Unifi site had been folded into Boomi. Its former domains no longer host the product — unifisoftware.com does not resolve and unifiyourdata.com is parked at Safenames — so no public API surface remains to catalog.

providers.name: United Capital
providers.description: United Capital (United Capital Financial Advisers / United Capital Financial Partners) was a US wealth counseling and financial life management firm founded in 2005, known for its FinLife CX white-label advisor technology platform. Bessemer Venture Partners partnered with the company in 2009. At acquisition it managed roughly $25 billion for 22,000 clients through 220+ advisors in over 90 offices. Goldman Sachs acquired United Capital in May 2019 for $750 million in cash, rebranding it Goldman Sachs Personal Financial Management, which Creative Planning acquired in 2023. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API or developer surface; its historic domain unitedcp.com now returns HTTP 404.

providers.name: Uroam
providers.description: uRoam, Inc. (1999-2003) was a Canaan Partners-backed security company that built FirePass, a clientless SSL-VPN appliance for "radically simplified remote access" to enterprise applications from any browser. After merging with Filanet, uRoam was acquired by F5 Networks in July 2003 for $25 million in cash, and FirePass became F5's SSL VPN product line. The company is defunct; uroam.com now redirects to f5.com, and uRoam publishes no APIs or developer surface of its own.

providers.name: Ursa Space Systems
providers.description: Ursa Space Systems is an Ithaca, New York-based geospatial intelligence company that turns commercial satellite data — primarily Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, combined with electro-optical, RF, AIS, and other ground-truth feeds — into decision-ready insight reports. The company operates a GeoAI platform branded "From pixels to insights" that fuses 90+ geospatial data sources and ingests imagery from a global network of commercial SAR and EO satellite operators, then applies in-house remote-sensing, data science, and GIS expertise to deliver answers about what is happening on the ground at specific places and times. Ursa Space serves U.S. Government customers — including U.S. Space Force Space Systems Command (SSC) under INDOPACOM, AFRICOM, and SOUTHCOM, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) under the Luno A and Luno B delivery orders, the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU), and humanitarian-aid agencies — as well as commercial enterprise customers in energy, commodities, supply chain, maritime, and insurance. Reporting domains span security and defense (border monitoring, military activity, maritime, dark-vessel and ship-to-ship transfer detection, airstrip monitoring), environmental and disaster response (deforestation, earthquakes, flooding, wildfires), and infrastructure and industry monitoring (construction, mining, oil and gas supply chain, power generation, space situational awareness). The platform is currently in beta and Ursa Space does not operate a public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, SDK, or self-service signup; engagement is sales-led through contact@ursaspace.com and tailored to government and enterprise contracts.

providers.name: URX *
providers.description: URX was a San Francisco mobile deep-linking and app-search startup that connected mobile users to relevant in-app commerce experiences. Backed by roughly $15M from investors including GV (Google Ventures) and CyberAgent, it was acquired by Pinterest in May 2016 and its product was wound down. The urx.com domain is now parked and listed for sale on a domain marketplace, and no API, developer portal, or public developer artifacts remain. Profiled in the API Evangelist network as a historical GV portfolio company.

providers.name: VacayHero
providers.description: VacayHero (branded VaycayHero) was a vacation rental marketplace backed by a16z that offered professionally managed vacation rental homes with hotel-style guest service. The brand was absorbed by RedAwning: vacayhero.com now permanently redirects (301) to RedAwning's VaycayHero brand page, which folds the VaycayHero properties into RedAwning's collection of 100,000+ instantly bookable vacation rentals in over 10,000 destinations. VacayHero no longer operates an independent website, developer program, or public API surface.

providers.name: Vamo
providers.description: Vamo was a San Francisco travel startup offering multi-city trip planning that automatically found the best combination of open-jaw flights, low-cost carriers, trains, buses, ferries, and hotels for international itineraries. Backed by DCVC and Slow Ventures, the team joined Airbnb on September 11, 2015 and the product was shut down, so no API surface exists; vamo.com is now parked at MarkMonitor.

providers.name: Vantus
providers.description: Vantus is a stub surfaced from the Mayfield portfolio page whose permalink slug is "vantus" but whose actual company is Vantive Corporation, a historic Mayfield "Milestone" enterprise investment described by Mayfield as call center software leaders. Vantive provided customer relationship management (CRM) software and existed as an independent corporation until its merger with PeopleSoft in 1999; PeopleSoft was later acquired by Oracle and the Vantive brand no longer exists. There is no current company website or API surface to enrich. Unrelated live domains (vantus.com, Vantus Medical Systems; vantus.io, a Spanish AI automation consultancy) are different companies and are intentionally not linked here.

providers.name: Vark (Aardvark)
providers.description: Vark is the Felicis portfolio listing for Aardvark, the social search / knowledge-market startup founded in 2007 by Max Ventilla, Nathan Stoll, Damon Horowitz, and Rob Spiro (The Mechanical Zoo). Users asked questions and were connected live with friends or friends-of-friends who could answer them, over email and IM. Google acquired Aardvark on February 11, 2010 for $50 million and shut the service down in September 2011. The company is defunct and published no public API. Its original domain vark.com no longer resolves, and the vark.io URL listed on the Felicis portfolio page now hosts an unrelated SMS meeting-reminder product operated by Saasology LLC.

providers.name: Vaunte
providers.description: Vaunte was a New York fashion commerce startup, backed by Battery Ventures, that let shoppers buy items directly from the closets of socialites, stylists, editors, and models (the 2013 site billed itself as "Shop fashion closets of socialites, stylists, editors, and models"). The original marketplace is no longer operating, and today vaunte.com hosts an unrelated fashion and lifestyle content site with no API or developer surface. Tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Vayar Vision
providers.description: Vayar Vision Ltd was an Israeli startup (company no. 514054972, incorporated 2007-11-26, Herzliya) that developed a visual search engine enabling search for images based on their visual characteristics rather than textual tagging - positioned as "a Google for pictures" turning images into searchable knowledge. A Battery Ventures portfolio company listed as an exited investment, the company has been wilfully dissolved (last annual report 2021) and its former website vayar.com no longer resolves. No API surface, developer program, or published artifacts exist.

providers.name: VDOnet
providers.description: VDOnet Corp was a mid-1990s streaming-media pioneer whose VDOLive server and player delivered some of the earliest video streamed over the web, alongside the VDOPhone video-telephony product. Backed by Battery Ventures, with Microsoft taking a minority stake in 1996, the company wound down in the late 1990s and its product line was sold off (Citrix negotiated a purchase of the product line for roughly $8 million in 1998). The company is defunct - its former vdo.net domain now resolves to a parked page listed for sale - and no API, developer portal, or other machine-readable surface exists to harvest.

providers.name: Velocity
providers.description: Velocity was an Israeli DevOps / site-reliability-engineering startup that helped engineering teams move faster — originally by letting developers spin up on-demand, fully isolated, production-like development environments, and later by applying AI to automate SRE and major-incident-response workflows so engineers could focus on solving problems instead of chasing alerts. On November 10, 2025 Velocity was acquired by BigPanda (the Insight Partners-backed agentic AIOps / IT operations company) to accelerate its AI Detection and Response product; founder and CEO Tal Kain joined BigPanda as VP of AI Detection and Response. The velocity.tech domain now redirects to bigpanda.io and Velocity no longer operates an independent public developer surface, API, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Velostrata
providers.description: Velostrata was an enterprise cloud-migration technology company founded in 2014 by Issy Ben-Shaul and Ady Degany, headquartered in San Mateo, California with an R&D center in Netanya, Israel. Its patented agentless technology decoupled compute from storage so that workloads could run in the cloud within minutes while the bulk storage migration streamed in the background without performance degradation. Backed by Intel Capital, Norwest Venture Partners and 83North (roughly $31.5M raised across Series A and B rounds), Velostrata was acquired by Google in May 2018 (estimated $100M-$200M). The team joined Google Cloud in Tel Aviv and the product was rebranded Migrate for Compute Engine, later Migrate for Virtual Machines. Velostrata no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no independent API: velostrata.com now redirects to Google Cloud's Migrate for Virtual Machines documentation.

providers.name: VendorHawk
providers.description: VendorHawk was a Seattle-based SaaS subscription and vendor management platform that helped IT and finance teams discover, track, renew, and optimize software spend across the organization. Founded in 2014 and backed by Techstars, VendorHawk was acquired by ServiceNow (NYSE NOW) in an all-cash transaction announced in April 2018 and folded into the ServiceNow platform. The vendorhawk.co domain now 301-redirects to servicenow.com, and the product has no independent public API, developer portal, or artifact surface of its own.

providers.name: Veniam
providers.description: Veniam builds intelligent networking software for the Internet of Moving Things, moving data automatically, securely, and cost-effectively between connected vehicles, mobile IoT devices, and the cloud across all available networks (cellular, Wi-Fi, and DSRC). Its platform serves video telematics, connected fleets, industrial IoT, and auto OEM/Tier 1 use cases, and reports processing 110M+ kilometers of mobile IoT data with 130+ granted patents. Founded by Joao Barros, Susana Sargento, Robin Chase, and Roy Russell, the company was acquired by Nexar in 2022. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. No public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Vera Security
providers.description: Vera Security (Vera, Inc.) was an enterprise data-centric security and information rights management (IRM) company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Its platform applied encryption, access policy, tracking, watermarking, and remote revocation that travel with a file wherever it goes across users, devices, applications, and cloud services, and it exposed an IRM-as-a-service REST API and SDK so developers could embed those data-protection controls into their own applications. Backed by Battery Ventures, Sutter Hill Ventures, Amplify Partners, Hasso Plattner Ventures, and BMW i Ventures (roughly $77M raised), Vera was acquired by HelpSystems (now Fortra) in December 2020; the product now ships as Fortra / Digital Guardian Secure Collaboration. This profile documents the company's residual public surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Verio
providers.description: Verio was a global web hosting provider and internet service provider that pioneered the ISP "rollup" model, acquiring more than 200 smaller ISPs and hosting companies after its 1996 founding in Denver, Colorado. It went public on NASDAQ (ticker VRIO) in 1999 and was acquired by NTT Communications in 2000 for roughly $5 billion. In 2015 its SMB shared-hosting division was sold to Endurance International Group, and the Verio brand is now operated within Newfold Digital, redirecting to Network Solutions / iPage. The company exposes no public developer or API surface; the verio.com apex no longer resolves and www.verio.com redirects to Network Solutions. This profile is retained as a legacy/defunct company record.

providers.name: Veriti.ai
providers.description: Veriti Cybersecurity is a Preemptive Exposure Management (PEM) platform founded in 2021 that continuously discovers, prioritizes, and remediates vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and exploitability risk across an organization's multi-vendor security stack, on-premises and in the cloud. Its AI-driven engine analyzes each environment's exposures, configurations, and existing protections to apply safe controls and automated (including virtual) patching without disrupting business, with integrations spanning 70+ security vendors. Originally an Insight Partners portfolio company, Veriti was acquired by Check Point (agreement announced May 2025); its capabilities are being folded into the Check Point Infinity Platform's Threat Exposure and Risk Management offering, and veriti.ai now redirects to checkpoint.com/exposure-management. Veriti is delivered as an enterprise security platform and does not publish a public self-serve developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: VeriTX
providers.description: VeriTX Corp. is a veteran-owned blockchain and cybersecurity firm based in East Aurora, New York that builds trusted, tamper-evident data and supply-chain infrastructure originally developed for the U.S. Air Force under SBIR, STTR, and Defense Production Act programs. Its flagship product, QuDEFENSE, is a data-security platform that combines post-quantum cryptography with blockchain to protect sensitive files in transit and at rest, providing real-time manipulation detection, automatic quarantine of tampered data, immutable audit trails, and end-to-end data provenance. VeriTX began as a blockchain-powered digital marketplace for aerospace additive manufacturing (3D-printed aircraft parts) built on Algorand, and has since focused on secure data transfer and provenance for defense, aerospace, medical, and industrial customers. QuDEFENSE is offered as an API, an Outlook plugin, and a standalone web interface, though VeriTX does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: Vero Software
providers.description: Vero Software is a developer of CAD/CAM software for manufacturing, headquartered in the United Kingdom and part of Hexagon's Manufacturing Intelligence division (Production Software). Its portfolio spans computer-aided manufacturing across metalworking, sheet metal, stone, and woodworking, with long-established desktop applications such as Alphacam, Cabinet Vision, Edgecam, Radan, SURFCAM, VISI, WorkNC, WorkXplore, Machining STRATEGIST, and PEPS. These are primarily installed engineering and CNC programming products rather than web services; as of this enrichment pass the company does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDK, and the verosoftware.com domain now redirects to Hexagon Manufacturing Intelligence marketing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Verodin
providers.description: Verodin was a cybersecurity company that pioneered security instrumentation and validation — its Security Instrumentation Platform (SIP) continuously measured, tested, and improved the effectiveness of an organization's security controls against real attacker behavior (a category later known as breach and attack simulation). Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and TenEleven Ventures, Verodin was acquired by FireEye in May 2019 for approximately $250 million and rebranded as Mandiant Security Validation. The verodin.com domain still resolves (serving a legacy marketing placeholder) but Verodin no longer operates as an independent company and exposes no public developer or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Verome
providers.description: Music API for searching, streaming, and exploring music data from YouTube Music, YouTube, and Last.fm

providers.name: Versant
providers.description: Versant Corporation was an American software company that built specialized object and NoSQL data-management systems, notably the Versant Object Database (VOD) and the FastObjects embeddable object database. Its persistence technology was accessed through language-native C++, Java (JDO/JPA-style) and .NET APIs rather than a REST web API, and was deployed across telecommunications, energy, financial services, transportation, manufacturing and defense. Backed by Trinity Ventures, Versant IPO'd on NASDAQ (VSNT) in July 1996 and was acquired by Actian Corporation in December 2012; the product line continues today as the Actian NoSQL Object Database.

providers.name: Verse Medical
providers.description: Verse Medical is a software-driven durable medical equipment (DME) supplier delivering hospital-quality healthcare at home across the United States. Founded in 2018 (Y Combinator S18) and based in New York City, the company builds software that replaces fax-based ordering so doctors and clinics can prescribe, order, and manage medical supplies such as catheters, wound dressings, and diabetes supplies for patients at home. Backed by General Catalyst, SignalFire, Sapphire Ventures, Abstract Ventures, and Y Combinator. No public developer API, docs portal, or specification surface was found during enrichment; this profile carries company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Versive
providers.description: Versive was a Seattle-based artificial-intelligence and machine-learning cybersecurity company (originally founded as Context Relevant) whose flagship product, the Versive Security Engine (VSE), applied machine learning to network and security telemetry to automatically surface adversary campaigns and in-progress breaches for security operations teams. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and other investors, Versive was acquired by managed-detection-and-response provider eSentire in October 2018, after which its technology was folded into eSentire's MDR platform and the independent Versive website (versive.com) was retired. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the enrichment pipeline found no live, independent Versive developer or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Vertex Energy
providers.description: Vertex Energy is an energy transition company specializing in producing and marketing high-purity refined products including conventional fuels, renewable diesel, and other specialty products. The company operates refining and processing facilities and is engaged in the recycling and recovery of used motor oil and other petroleum byproducts. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: Vertical Circuits
providers.description: Vertical Circuits, Inc. (VCI) was a semiconductor company based in Scotts Valley, California, supplying high-density semiconductor memories and die-level vertical-interconnect packaging technology. Its patented ViP (vertical interconnect pillar) process stacked die to bridge wire-bond product solutions and through-silicon-via (TSV) technology, serving computer, telecom, consumer-electronics, aerospace, and military customers. The company's die-stacking IP and technology were acquired by Invensas/Tessera around 2013. Vertical Circuits is a hardware and semiconductor-IP company with no public web API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; it was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead and enriched to record that it has no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Vestiaire Collective
providers.description: Vestiaire Collective is a global online marketplace for pre-owned luxury and designer fashion, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Paris, France. The platform connects buyers and sellers of authenticated second-hand clothing, handbags, shoes, watches, and accessories, with in-house physical authentication and quality control for higher-value items. A certified B Corporation, the company promotes circular fashion and sustainable consumption across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific, and is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund among other investors. No public developer API or documentation surface has been found; the api.vestiairecollective.com host is an internal backend serving the vestiairecollective.com web application (CORS-locked, no published OpenAPI or well-known metadata).

providers.name: Vexata
providers.description: Vexata was an all-flash, NVMe-based enterprise storage startup headquartered in Santa Clara, California, known for its Vexata Active Data Fabric software and VX-100 scale-out storage arrays aimed at high-performance database and analytics workloads. The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was acquired by StorCentric in 2019; StorCentric subsequently filed for bankruptcy in 2022. As of this enrichment pass the vexata.com domain no longer belongs to the company and redirects to an unrelated business (farmhousela.com), the api./developer./docs. subdomains do not resolve, and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface could be found. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct company record.

providers.name: Vibely
providers.description: Vibely was a creator-community platform (surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company) that let creators host paid communities, challenges, and group chat. As of this enrichment pass the domain vibely.io no longer serves an independent product; every path — including all /.well-known/ discovery endpoints — 301-redirects to kajabi.com/features/communities, indicating Vibely was folded into Kajabi's Communities product. No standalone Vibely developer portal, API, OpenAPI, SDK, MCP server, or llms.txt could be found; the only artifact captured is a probed TLS/DNS domain-security profile of the surviving redirect domain. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired portfolio lead.

providers.name: Vicarious
providers.description: Vicarious (Vicarious FPC) was an artificial intelligence and industrial robotics company founded in 2010 by D. Scott Phoenix and Dileep George. It pursued brain-inspired machine learning, notably the Recursive Cortical Network that solved text CAPTCHAs with far less training data, then applied that research to general-purpose robotic automation for warehouse and manufacturing tasks. The company was backed by DCVC, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, ABB, Samsung, and Wipro, and was acquired by Intrinsic, Alphabet's robotics moonshot, in 2022. Its vicarious.com domain no longer resolves and it exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: VICI Sports
