providers.description: VICI Sports operates FanFest, a white-labeled fan engagement platform for the sports industry that "turns fan engagement into revenue" by recognizing every fan action across stadiums, homes, and bars and rewarding it automatically. The company reports 150+ activations with sports brands and 30M+ fans commercialized, with partners including AC Milan, the Premier League, Paris Saint-Germain, and Manchester City. Backed by Techstars. No public developer/API surface is currently published; the fanfest.vip site is a single-page marketing app with a contact form only.

providers.name: Vidcaster
providers.description: Vidcaster was a business video experience platform (a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company) that helped organizations use video strategically across marketing, sales, training, and customer support. Its platform let teams host, manage, enrich, distribute, and analyze videos with a customizable player, video galleries, lead-generation gating, video subscriptions, advanced video SEO, and integrations with marketing-automation, CRM, and social channels. The company now appears defunct because the vidcaster.com web application is no longer reachable (HTTPS/HTTP connections time out) and no public API or developer program was ever published. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead profile.

providers.name: View The Space (Fmr Hightower)
providers.description: VTS (View The Space, formed in part from the Hightower merger) is a commercial real estate technology platform for leasing, asset management, tenant experience, and market analytics used by landlords, brokers, and property managers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Probing found the marketing site (www.vts.com) behind a bot challenge and a bare backend host (api.vts.com) with no publicly documented API program, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this remains a company profile rather than a documented API.

providers.name: Vimaan
providers.description: Vimaan is an autonomous inventory intelligence company that combines computer vision, machine learning, and autonomous drones and robotics to verify, count, and audit inventory across warehouses, distribution centers, and supply-chain operations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of wing-venture-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Vimaan publishes no public developer, API, SDK, or documentation surface: the corporate website (vimaan.ai) sits entirely behind an sgcaptcha challenge wall and no developer, docs, or api subdomains resolve. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Vinterior
providers.description: Vinterior is a UK-based curated online marketplace for vintage, antique, and pre-owned furniture and homeware. It connects independent sellers, dealers, and restorers with buyers looking for one-of-a-kind pieces, positioning itself as a more sustainable alternative to mass-produced furniture. The platform handles product discovery, listings, seller storefronts, checkout, and delivery for design-led vintage goods. Vinterior is backed by Seedcamp. As of this profile Vinterior does not publish a public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

providers.name: VIPThink
providers.description: VIPThink (豌豆思维) is a Chinese online education company operated by Guangdong Happy Seeds Technology Co., Ltd. (广东快乐种子科技有限公司), delivering small-class live-streaming courses in mathematical thinking and logic for young children (roughly ages 3-8). It is part of a family of consumer education brands that also includes Hualala drawing classes (画啦啦), Wandou speech training (豌豆口才), Gubi early-learning (咕比启蒙), and Little Lighthouse (小灯塔). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, VIPThink operates only consumer-facing web and mobile learning products and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Virgin Galactic
providers.description: Virgin Galactic is a publicly traded (NYSE: SPCE) commercial spaceflight company founded by Richard Branson that develops and operates suborbital, crewed spaceplanes for space tourism and research payloads. It flies its air-launched SpaceShipTwo-class and next generation Delta-class vehicles from Spaceport America in New Mexico, carrying private astronauts and scientific experiments to the edge of space. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Social Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface: it is a consumer-facing space-tourism business, not an API provider.

providers.name: Virgio
providers.description: Virgio is an India-based direct-to-consumer sustainable fashion brand delivering trend-driven, eco-conscious womens apparel built around circular fashion, recycled and natural fabrics (recycled polyester, organic cotton, viscose, modal, lyocell), ethical production, and zero-waste packaging. It operates as an online-first retail marketplace with a consumer web storefront and mobile app. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Prosus Ventures; an enrichment probe found a consumer e-commerce presence but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: ViridiCO2
providers.description: ViridiCO2 is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of eqt-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: sustainability. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Virsa Systems
providers.description: Virsa Systems was a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) software company founded in 1996 that specialized in helping enterprises meet regulatory requirements such as Sarbanes-Oxley by embedding automated control design, testing, and enforcement directly into their business processes, notably around SAP access controls and segregation-of-duties. Lightspeed Venture Partners invested in the company at an early stage in 2004, and Virsa Systems was acquired by SAP in 2006, becoming the foundation of what is now SAP GRC / SAP Access Control. It no longer operates as an independent company and maintains no separate website, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/portfolio record; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Virtela
providers.description: Virtela was a managed network and cloud-based networking/security services company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of Norwest Venture Partners. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-21 found that virtela.com now redirects to NTT Global (www.nttglobal.net) — the Virtela brand has been absorbed by NTT and operates no independent developer program, public API, or documentation surface. No OpenAPI, well-known metadata, llms.txt, packages, or MCP server were discoverable; the well-known and llms/openapi probe paths all soft-404 to the NTT marketing HTML page.

providers.name: Virtualtech Frontier
providers.description: Virtualtech Frontier (VTF) is a creative technology company that designs immersive experiences by combining human creativity with technology across immersive centres and installations, experiential events and exhibitions, AI-powered audience engagement, metaverse and virtual worlds, and extended reality (XR/AR/VR). It operates the no-code metaverse-building platform Mitoworld and the Lumiworks service, with offices in Kuala Lumpur, Beijing, Dubai, Tokyo, and Singapore, and clients including HP, AIA, Nestle, Laneige, Dynatrace, and Omega. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: VisasQ
providers.description: VisasQ Inc. is a Tokyo-headquartered knowledge-sharing and spot-consulting platform that connects companies seeking specialized insight with a global network of roughly 800,000 experts across 190 countries and diverse industries and job functions. Its flagship "ビザスクdirect" service arranges one-on-one expert consultations, and it has launched "AI Scout" to deliver precision expert matches in under five minutes, 24/7. The company operates six global offices with multilingual support and over 600 employees, serving Japan and the United States as primary markets. VisasQ was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP surface; only domain-security posture could be probed.

providers.name: Vision Space Inc.
providers.description: Vision Space Inc. (VisionSpace) is a South Korean company building Physical AI robot simulation software for automation in the logistics and manufacturing sectors. Its TESSERACT product implements logistics and manufacturing sites as digital twins, visualizing process data and predicting operational efficiency through AI-based simulation, while its TARS product delivers real-time 3D monitoring that integrates and manages data from equipment and robots in a unified 3D control dashboard. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass VisionSpace publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: VisualLogix
providers.description: VisualLogix develops mission-critical CAD, simulation, and analytical software used by engineers who design and validate real-world physical systems. Its tools span computer-aided design, physics and systems simulation, and analytical modeling for engineering teams building and testing products across industrial, mechanical, and infrastructure domains. VisualLogix is backed by Insight Partners. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing website (built with Figma Make) but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: VivaReal
providers.description: VivaReal operates vivareal.com.br, a Brazilian online real estate marketplace and classifieds portal where consumers search, buy, sell, and rent residential and commercial properties across Brazil, connecting property seekers with real estate agents, agencies, and developers. It was originally backed by 500 Global and later became part of Grupo ZAP / OLX Brasil. It was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; an enrichment pass found no public developer API surface, portal, or specification.

providers.name: Vlocity
providers.description: Vlocity was an industry-cloud software company founded in 2014 (by David Schmaier and team) that built vertical CRM applications on the Salesforce Platform for communications, media, energy, insurance, health, and the public sector, along with the OmniStudio low-code toolset (OmniScript, FlexCards, DataRaptor, Integration Procedures). Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Accel, Sutter Hill Ventures, and Salesforce Ventures, Vlocity was acquired by Salesforce in 2020 and folded into Salesforce Industries; the platform now ships as Salesforce OmniStudio. Vlocity no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no independent developer portal or public API — its domain (vlocity.com) is defunct (HTTP 503) and is now operated by Salesforce (confirmed via SPF/DMARC delegation to salesforce.com and a Salesforce, Inc. TLS certificate). Any API surface lives under Salesforce OmniStudio.

providers.name: VNDLY
providers.description: VNDLY is a cloud-based vendor management system (VMS) for managing contingent workforce, external labor, statements of work (SOW), and services procurement. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Mason, Ohio, VNDLY was acquired by Workday in 2021 and is now offered as Workday VNDLY, pairing with Workday Human Capital Management (HCM) for total workforce optimization. The company no longer operates an independent public developer portal or API surface; integration is delivered through the Workday platform. This profile originated as a portfolio-company lead (Battery Ventures, Insight Partners) surfaced into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Votizen
providers.description: Votizen was a Silicon Valley civic-technology startup (founded 2010 by David Binetti, Jason Putorti, and Matt Snider; a 500 Global portfolio company) that built a social network of verified U.S. voters and offered an API for candidates, offices, districts, races, and voter contact tracking. Votizen was acquired by Causes in 2013 and shut down; votizen.com now serves only a bare default web server page, and no live API, developer portal, packages, or security program remains.

providers.name: Voyence
providers.description: Voyence was an enterprise software company that provided network configuration and change management solutions, automating critical change, compliance, and service-activation processes across large IT and network operations environments (the VoyenceControl product line). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment research found that Voyence was acquired by EMC (Dell EMC) on October 30, 2007 and folded into EMC's IT/network management portfolio; it is a long-defunct, exited company with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface. There are no APIs, specifications, or artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: VR Motion
providers.description: VR Motion Corp develops virtual-reality driver-training simulation systems, marketed under its RealDrive product, delivering true-to-life driving simulations that the company says achieve over 70% greater skills retention than traditional training. It serves commercial fleets, last-mile delivery operations, first responders, and driving schools. VR Motion is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass its public web presence is a marketing site with no developer API, docs, SDK, or developer portal, so there is no machine-readable API surface to catalog.

providers.name: VSS Monitoring
providers.description: VSS Monitoring was a network packet broker (NPB) vendor founded in 2003, known for its vBroker appliance range and the vMesh architecture that meshed up to 256 packet brokers into a fault-tolerant network-visibility fabric for monitoring and security tools. It was acquired by Danaher Corporation in 2012 as part of Tektronix Communications, and passed to NETSCOUT Systems when NETSCOUT acquired Danaher's Communications business (Tektronix Communications, Arbor Networks, parts of Fluke Networks) for roughly USD 2.6 billion, closing in July 2015. VSS Monitoring no longer operates as an independent company or brand; its packet-broker technology is now delivered as a NETSCOUT business unit, and it exposes no independent public developer program, API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and is retained for network completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Vue
providers.description: Vue (Vue Technology) was an item-level RFID hardware and software company based in Lake Forest, California, backed by Canaan Partners at Series A. Its product family combined RFID readpoints and networking devices with a software platform for real-time, item-level inventory monitoring and tracking, with notable retail rollouts including American Apparel. Tyco's Sensormatic Electronics acquired Vue Technology in October 2008 for approximately $43M, so the company no longer operates as an independent entity. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead; enrichment finds no active developer portal, public API, or first-party artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: Waffl
providers.description: Waffl is an early-stage website builder — a drag-and-drop platform for creating a website and growing a small business from customizable templates. As of this profile the product is pre-launch ("Coming Soon" at waffl.io) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or other developer surface. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; it carries no API surface to enrich yet.

providers.name: Walkie-Talkie
providers.description: Walkie-Talkie is a Gen Z social audio platform built by Picslo Corp that hosts live audio rooms called "frequencies" — public or private channels where users tune in and talk with friends in high-fidelity audio anytime, anywhere. Thousands of public frequencies run at any given time, connecting people around topics they choose to discuss, alongside private frequencies between close friends. The company raised $3.25M in pre-seed funding from investors including Partech, Breega, Kima Ventures, Heroic Ventures, TI Platform Ventures, LDV Partners, and Diaspora Ventures. It is a consumer mobile application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: WallData
providers.description: WallData (Wall Data Inc.) was a Kirkland, Washington host-connectivity software company, best known for its RUMBA family of PC-to-mainframe and AS/400 terminal-emulation and SNA-to-TCP/IP connectivity products. A Trinity Ventures portfolio company that reached an IPO exit, Wall Data was acquired by NetManage in 1999; the RUMBA product line later passed to Micro Focus and now sits under OpenText. The company is defunct and publishes no current developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio record.

providers.name: Walzay Inc.
providers.description: Walzay Inc. is a global tech-talent recruitment marketplace, founded in 2019 by Humaira Khan and headquartered in New York City. The platform connects companies with vetted remote and in-office software, engineering, and sales professionals — largely sourced from the Middle East and other emerging markets — and offers white-glove recruiting alongside a self-serve candidate marketplace. Walzay is backed by 500 Global and the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Wandbox
providers.description: Code compiler supporting 35+ languages mentioned at wandbox.org

providers.name: Wanderable
providers.description: Wanderable was a honeymoon and experience gift registry startup founded in 2012 by Stanford classmates Jenny Chen and Marcela Miyazawa, backed by the 500 Startups (500 Global) accelerator and its 500 Women Syndicate. Couples could register for honeymoon experiences and travel rather than physical goods, fund trips online and via an iPhone app, and manage registries and thank-you notes on the go. The company ceased operating its registry service in Summer 2022 and now directs former users to Traveler's Joy. It exposes no public developer, API, or discovery surface.

providers.name: Wandoujia
providers.description: Wandoujia (豌豆荚, "pea pod") is a Chinese Android app distribution platform and mobile assistant launched in 2009 by Beijing-based Wandoulabs (Zhuoyi Xunchang Technology). It was known for its PC-based Android management client and its in-app content search that indexed apps, games, video, and other content across the Chinese Android ecosystem. Wandoujia was acquired by Alibaba/UCWeb in 2016 and folded into Alibaba's app-distribution business. Its consumer and developer web properties (www., open., and developer.wandoujia.com) no longer resolve; only residual Alibaba-hosted infrastructure (api. and account.wandoujia.com) remains, and there is no documented public API surface.

providers.name: Wanted
providers.description: Wanted was a talent-sourcing recruitment marketplace, backed by Partech and founded by Jean Meyer, that set out to disrupt traditional headhunting by connecting companies with candidates surfaced and referred through a networked marketplace. It operated out of New York and France under the Applicative SaaS / HR-tech category. The company has since wound down: its team was acqui-hired by Revolut, and the product and website at getwanted.com are no longer live (the domain is now parked and listed for sale on HugeDomains). No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation could be found for this provider. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: wantful
providers.description: Wantful was a personalized online gift-giving service founded in 2011 by John Poisson, based in San Francisco and New York City, that let shoppers assemble curated gift books of design-forward products which recipients could browse and redeem for the item they most wanted. Backed by Slow Ventures and others (roughly $5.5M raised) and partnered with Nordstrom, the company shut down in September 2013 after failing to secure follow-on funding. It is defunct — wantful.com resolves (Route53 NS) but serves no live product, and there is no API, documentation, or developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Wave Capital
providers.description: Wave Capital is an early-stage venture capital seed fund based in San Francisco, founded in 2017 and run as a lean two-partner firm with no additional staff. The fund specializes in marketplace startups and was conceived as the "Airbnb mafia" fund, backing pre-Series-A founders drawn from the Airbnb, Dropbox, and Facebook alumni networks. Wave leads a highly selective portfolio, making no more than four investments per year (typically around $1M) and supporting founders with operating experience beyond capital. It publishes no developer API, documentation, or developer portal — it is a private investment firm, catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a company/VC profile surfaced via foundry-group's portfolio.

providers.name: Waveset
providers.description: Waveset Technologies was a privately held identity-management software vendor based in Austin, Texas, and an early portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its flagship product, Lighthouse, automated user provisioning, password management, and identity brokering to govern access to enterprise systems and data. Sun Microsystems announced its acquisition of Waveset in 2003 and completed it in December 2003; the Lighthouse technology became the basis of Sun Identity Manager and was later carried into Oracle's identity portfolio. Waveset has not existed as an independent company since the acquisition and publishes no active website, developer portal, or API surface today.

providers.name: Wavii
providers.description: Wavii was a Seattle-based startup founded in 2008 by Adrian Aoun that built a news-summarization app using natural-language-processing and machine-learning to convert web content (news articles and blogs) into short structured story summaries. Backed by Battery Ventures, Felicis Ventures and Kapor Capital, Wavii was acquired by Google in April 2013 (reported at over $30M) and immediately shut down its consumer service, with the team moving to Google to work on natural-language products. The company is defunct and operates no public product or API. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the enrichment pass confirmed no live developer surface exists.

providers.name: WaystoCap
providers.description: WaystoCap launched in 2015 in Casablanca, Morocco as a Y Combinator-backed B2B digital marketplace to facilitate cross-border trade across Africa, helping traders source commodities, arrange financing, and secure shipment and payments. The waystocap.com domain now hosts WaysToCap Ventures, a fintech advisory and consulting firm offering strategic and investment advisory, fund raising, innovation consulting, and AI integration. No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface is published; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Wealor
providers.description: Wealor is an AI-native platform for wealth managers, building a centralized, queryable source of truth across wealth management, tax, legal, estate, and insurance. The platform captures data from conversations, financial documents, tax returns, legal documents, and custodial systems into a single knowledge layer, then uses specialized AI agents to automate operational work — account opening, client subscriptions, tax optimization, trade rebalancing, and billable client-plan generation — directly across legacy partner portals and internal systems via APIs and browser automation. Founded in 2026 by Karim Bouri and Pierre Depuydt and backed by Y Combinator (P26 batch), Wealor is based in San Francisco. As of this profile it is an API consumer with no public developer API, documentation, or specification surface.

providers.description: A RESTful free API to check the weather

providers.name: Webhelp
providers.description: Webhelp is a French customer-experience and business-process-outsourcing (BPO) company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Paris, providing outsourced customer support, sales, back-office, content moderation, and payment/collections services to global brands across many languages and geographies. In 2023 Webhelp merged with Concentrix; the combined company operates under the Concentrix brand and the standalone webhelp.com domain no longer resolves to a live website. Webhelp was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It is a services/BPO operator rather than an API producer and publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; the enrichment pipeline found no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: WebMynd
providers.description: WebMynd, later known as Trigger.io, was a 500 Global backed startup that built Forge, a toolkit for building cross-platform mobile applications from HTML, JavaScript, and CSS with native device access. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company now appears inactive, its trigger.io domain no longer serves a live website (only email MX/SPF records remain) and no API, developer documentation, or SDK surface could be located during enrichment.

providers.name: WebsitePros
providers.description: WebsitePros, now operating as Web.com, is an American company that provides website building, web hosting, domain registration, e-commerce, and online marketing services primarily to small and medium-sized businesses. Website Pros, Inc. merged with Web.com in 2007 and adopted the Web.com name. The business offers do-it-yourself and do-it-for-you website builders, managed WordPress hosting, professional email, SEO and digital marketing tools, and is headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida. As surfaced through a VC-portfolio match, it currently exposes no public developer API or documented developer portal.

providers.name: Weddington Way
providers.description: Weddington Way is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Weeby
providers.description: Weeby is a mobile/social game company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. Its listed website, gameclosure.com, now redirects to Playco ("the Game Closure team is now a part of Playco"), and no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or MCP surface could be found for Weeby as of July 2026. The profile is retained as a portfolio-graph node with a probed domain-security artifact rather than an active API producer.

providers.name: Weft
providers.description: Weft was a Burlington, Vermont based supply-chain logistics startup, founded by Marc Held around 2013-2014, that combined hardware sensors and software to track the shipping of physical goods worldwide in real time. It raised a seed round of under $1M led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Data Elite, with plans for a $5M Series A. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct: no live corporate website, no developer portal, and no public API surface could be found. Candidate domains were probed and none host an active product (weft.com refused connection, weft.io does not resolve, weft.ai is a parked domain listed for sale).

providers.name: WeGrow asia CO., LTD.
providers.description: WeGrow asia CO., LTD. (威果) is a Taiwan-based agricultural technology company operating a franchise model for modern, technology-driven farming. It pairs 24-hour AI-assisted remote crop management with a transparent farmer profit-sharing model, specializing in high-value strawberries and cantaloupes while handling production, labor management, marketing, and logistics end to end ("you provide the land, we provide the labor and expertise"). WeGrow surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a bilingual (TW/EN) marketing website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface — every probed developer and well-known path returned HTTP 404.

providers.name: Welcome
providers.description: Welcome (welco.me) was an AI-powered travel planning product (TripNotes) surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, techstars. As of this enrichment pass welco.me 301-redirects to dorsia.com/newsroom/welcome-tripnotes, indicating the standalone product was acquired by / folded into Dorsia; no independent public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known surface remains. Sector: ai. Retained as a network record with a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: WeMash
providers.description: WeMash was a Los Angeles-based, cloud-based video mashup platform founded in 2014 that partnered with movie studios, news organizations, sports entities, and music labels to give creators legal access to premium content for derivative works, with monetization shared across rights holders. Backed by a roughly $420K seed round whose sole institutional investor was Andreessen Horowitz, the company is now defunct - wemash.com no longer resolves and no developer, documentation, or API surface remains to be catalogued.

providers.name: Wetpaint
providers.description: Wetpaint is a media brand operating wetpaint.com, an entertainment and lifestyle publication covering Hollywood gossip, celebrity news, TV series recaps and buzz, and pop-culture storytelling. Originally a Trinity Ventures-backed wiki/collaborative-media startup, the property today runs as an ad- and affiliate-supported editorial content site with no public developer program: as of this enrichment pass it exposes no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a media-sector company record.

providers.name: Wevorce
providers.description: Wevorce is an online divorce and family-law technology company that offered self-guided and professionally supported divorce services, using guided workflows and document preparation to help couples navigate separation more amicably and affordably. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, a16z, and Y Combinator and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. No public API, developer documentation, SDK, or machine-readable interface could be located during enrichment; the primary web property is served behind Cloudflare and blocks automated access.

providers.name: whatiseven
providers.description: whatiseven (Even, formerly Even Responsible Finance) was an earned-wage-access and personal-finance fintech that let workers access a portion of their pay before payday, budget with "okay to spend" guidance, and automatically save. Backed by Slow Ventures, Even was acquired by One (Walmart's fintech venture, now OnePay) and folded into the OnePay @Work earned-wage-access product ("Instapay"). The whatiseven.com domain now redirects through even.com to onepay.com/atwork. Even operates no independent public developer platform, API, or documentation, and the acquirer OnePay publishes no public API surface either. This profile is retained as a network record of the company and its acquisition.

providers.name: When is next MCU film
providers.description: Upcoming MCU film information

providers.name: Wikidocs
providers.description: Wikidocs was a real-time collaboration startup (wikidocs.io) that built a framework for turning any web page into a live, editable, multi-user "docs" service — enabling real-time content creation, editing, and sharing directly in the browser without waiting for updated versions. Backed by Speedinvest, the company was acquired by Atlassian in September 2014 and its collaboration technology was folded into Atlassian's products. Wikidocs no longer operates as an independent product: its former domain, wikidocs.io, is now a parked and email-forwarded registrar domain with no live developer portal, API, documentation, or machine-readable surface to enrich.

providers.name: Wildfire Interactive
providers.description: Wildfire Interactive, Inc. was a social media marketing software company founded in 2008 by Victoria Ransom and Alain Chuard in Redwood City, California. Its platform let brands create, optimize, and measure their presence across social networks — running branded promotions, sweepstakes, contests, and coupons plus page management, advertising, messaging, and analytics across Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, and YouTube. Backed by the Facebook Fund, Summit Partners, Accel Partners, and Founders Fund, Wildfire was acquired by Google in 2012 and folded into Google's advertising products (DoubleClick); the standalone product was wound down by 2014. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of uncork-capital and is retained as a historical record — the company operates no independent public API surface today.

providers.name: Willbros Group
providers.description: Willbros Group was a specialty energy infrastructure contractor that served the oil and gas, power, refining, petrochemical, and other industries before being acquired by Primoris Services Corporation. The company provided engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) services for pipeline, facility, and electrical infrastructure projects. Willbros Group was acquired by Primoris Services in 2018 and no longer operates independently. No public developer APIs are available for this organization.

providers.name: Win-Win
providers.description: Win-Win (trywinwin.com) is a charitable-fundraising platform that gamifies giving. Participants compete in tournaments hosted by celebrities and influencers, predicting head-to-head matchup outcomes and making tax-deductible donations to charitable causes while climbing leaderboards to win prizes and experiences. Win-Win also offers B2B tooling for nonprofits and corporations to launch their own gamified fundraising campaigns, alongside a consumer mobile app. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public API or developer surface is currently published.

providers.name: Windwalk Games
providers.description: Windwalk Games is a gaming-focused company whose mission is "Creating Communities Through Gaming." The company builds and grows player communities and audiences around games and gaming brands. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Windwalk Games operates a single marketing website (windwalk.games) and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable developer surface, so there are no API artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: WISECRICKET HOLDING KY
providers.description: WiseCricket (WISECRICKET HOLDING KY) offers AI-powered fiscal and accounting audit software for businesses ("Software de Auditoria Fiscal y Contable con IA para Empresas"). The Spanish-language platform applies artificial intelligence to tax and accounting compliance, helping companies automate financial and tax audits and surface issues. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found a marketing landing page but no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: WiTag
providers.description: WiTag Inc is an augmented reality mobile gaming company founded in 2016 by Thomas Suarez that built AR laser tag gameplay using only a smartphone's built-in sensors and radios, with no extra hardware. Lightspeed Venture Partners led a seed investment in 2017. As of July 2026 the company appears dormant, its website witag.co no longer resolves in DNS, no app is listed in the Apple App Store, and no public API or developer surface was found.

providers.name: Within
providers.description: Within (Within Unlimited, Inc.) is a Los Angeles virtual-reality studio founded in 2014 by Chris Milk and Aaron Koblin, both alumni of Google's Data Arts team. Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) led the company's 2016 Series A. Within builds Supernatural, a VR fitness service for Meta Quest headsets that pairs live human coaches with rhythm-mapped workouts set in 360-degree virtual locations; its earlier work spans immersive 360 video and AR (Clouds Over Sidra, Wonderscope). Meta Platforms acquired Within in February 2023 after the FTC's challenge to the deal failed, and it now operates as a Meta studio. Within is a consumer VR product company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal; its primary domain within.com is currently parked. This profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Witness Systems
providers.description: Witness Systems, Inc. was a workforce optimization software company founded in 1988 and headquartered in Roswell, Georgia. It built quality monitoring, call and screen recording, and performance management software for contact centers, sold under the Impact 360 and eQuality product lines, and traded publicly on NASDAQ under the ticker WITS. Verint Systems acquired Witness Systems in 2007 for approximately $950 million, folding its products into Verint's Workforce Optimization suite. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API; its former domain (witnesssystems.com) no longer resolves.

providers.name: WizzPass
providers.description: WizzPass is a visitor and workplace access management platform, surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. At the time of this enrichment pass the company's public web presence at wizzpass.com is dormant behind Cloudflare (HTTP 409 / error 1001) and refuses TLS handshakes, so no live developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or API surface could be reached. Email infrastructure is active (AWS SES inbound in eu-west-1, SPF authorizing Amazon SES and TeamSupport), indicating an operating SaaS organization even though the site itself is not currently serving. This profile records the honest probed state and awaits a future pass once the web/API surface is reachable.

providers.name: Wonder
providers.description: Wonder is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, bain-capital-ventures, bloomberg-beta, bullpen-capital, forerunner-ventures, general-catalyst, gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Wonder Brands
providers.description: Wonder Brands is a Latin American digital-first e-commerce company that builds and operates a portfolio of 15+ consumer product brands (including AlebriPets, Tropical Heal, Somos Reyes, Kingsman, KingsHouse, and KingsPort) spanning mattresses and bedroom furniture, sports equipment, home appliances, travel gear, tools, home and garden furniture, pet and baby products, and personal care. Operating an online-first omnichannel model across Uruguay, Mexico, Colombia, and Chile, it fulfills over 2 million annual orders from 25,000+ square meters of warehouse space, backed by proprietary technology for product optimization, marketing, pricing, and demand forecasting. Backed by QED Investors. The company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Wonderbly *
providers.description: Wonderbly is an online publisher that makes personalized books and gifts for kids and adults. Founded in 2013 (originally as Lost My Name), it lets customers design and buy books customized with a recipient's name, themes, and occasion, and has delighted over 10 million readers worldwide. The consumer e-commerce site operates across 40+ language and regional storefronts (US, UK, AU, CA, DE, FR, NL, IT, ES). Backed by GV. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was found during enrichment; this remains a company profile lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: WorkLife
providers.description: Worklife (Heroik Labs, Inc. d/b/a Worklife) was a San Francisco meeting-productivity application that helped teams run highly effective meetings — agenda generation and tracking, meeting organization, calendaring, collaborative real-time notes, and clear action items — with a Slack integration and free and paid tiers. A 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company, it was acquired by Cisco on October 17, 2016 and folded into the Cisco Spark collaboration platform (worklife.com redirected to notes.ciscospark.com by early 2017). The standalone worklife.com domain no longer resolves and no public API surface was ever published; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Woven Software
providers.description: Woven Software, Inc. (Woven, woven.com) was a Mountain View, California startup that built an AI-powered calendar and scheduling application for professionals, raising roughly $4.8M from investors including Battery Ventures, Felicis, Amplify Partners, Salesforce Ventures, and the Slack Fund. Slack acquired the Woven team in an acqui-hire announced in April 2021 and the Woven calendar product was shut down; the company no longer operates and publishes no APIs, developer portal, or other public API artifacts. The woven.com domain no longer serves the product (HTTPS fails; registration is behind a privacy service). This profile records the company as an exited Battery Ventures portfolio investment with no remaining API surface.

providers.name: Wow AI LTD.
providers.description: Wow AI LTD. is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: xchange (Formerly Exchange Applications Inc.)
providers.description: Xchange Inc., formerly Exchange Applications Inc., was a Boston-based (89 South Street, Boston, MA) customer relationship marketing software company that helped enterprises earn a greater share of their customers' business through relevant, personalized customer communications, selling campaign-management and customer-analytics software. A Delaware corporation backed by Insight Partners, it went public in 1998 (S-1 filed 1998-07-22, SEC CIK 0001065857, SIC 7373 Computer Integrated Systems Design). The company went dark after its final 10-Q on 2002-11-19, and the SEC revoked its Exchange Act registration on 2011-01-07. Both historical domains are now parked: xchange.com carries no A record and exchangeapplications.com is a domain-for-sale lander. The company is defunct with no website, developer surface, or APIs; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: XELUS
providers.description: Xelus was a service parts planning and optimization software company founded in 1972 and headquartered in Fairport, New York, providing inventory management and supply chain solutions for the telecommunications, aerospace and defense, and high-tech industries. An Insight Venture Partners portfolio company, Xelus was acquired by Click Commerce on May 27, 2005, and no longer operates independently. Its website (xelus.com) is defunct and the company publishes no public API surface, developer portal, SDKs, or packages.

providers.name: Xurity
providers.description: Xurity, Ltd. is a former Battery Ventures portfolio company, listed as an exited investment on Battery's all-companies roster (Q1 2026). As of July 2026 the company has no discoverable web presence - xurity.com is parked for sale on the Atom.com domain marketplace (Atom nameservers, Afternic verification, no MX records) - and no first-party packages, GitHub organization, or API documentation could be found on npm, PyPI, or GitHub. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-graph record; no API surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Xwork
providers.description: Xwork is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Yards Brewing
providers.description: Yards Brewing Company is an independent craft brewery founded in 1995 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Yards operates a brewery and taproom at 500 Spring Garden Street and distributes its classic and seasonal beers across the Mid-Atlantic. The company emphasizes local craftsmanship, community, and Philadelphia identity, summed up in their tagline that things are not made in Philadelphia but made BY Philadelphia.

providers.name: YesPath
providers.description: YesPath was an account engagement platform based in San Francisco that helped B2B sales and marketing teams reach and win large target accounts, using machine learning to surface real-time recommendations on the right content and next best action for each account. The company was acquired by Medium in April 2017 and no longer operates as an independent product; the yespath.com domain still resolves to AWS IP addresses but serves no live web application. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no live developer, API, or documentation surface to harvest — the entry is retained for portfolio-graph completeness.

providers.name: Yetcargo
providers.description: Yetcargo is a Mexican freight and cargo transportation company that connects businesses needing to move goods with a network of reliable carriers, handling both local and long-distance (foráneo) shipments. Operating a Spanish-language web platform, it positions itself as a trusted cargo-transport provider ("Tu proveedor confiable de transporte de carga") for shippers who need to resolve local and out-of-town delivery problems. Yetcargo was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.description: REST API for Yo Momma Jokes

providers.name: Yodle
providers.description: Yodle was a New York-based local online marketing and lead-generation company for small and medium-sized businesses, offering all-in-one advertising, web presence, and business-automation products such as Marketing Essentials, Yodle Ads, and Lighthouse 360. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, it was acquired by Web.com in February 2016 for roughly $342 million and no longer operates as a standalone brand — its technology was folded into Web.com, now part of Newfold Digital. Yodle exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; api.yodle.com is an internal, auth-gated endpoint (HTTP 401) and the legacy www.yodle.com site is effectively defunct.

providers.name: Yoom (fka Tetavi)
providers.description: Yoom (formerly Tetavi) is an Israeli deep-tech company founded in 2016 that develops volumetric video and markerless performance-capture technology using proprietary AI and neural networks. Its products include YoomTrack, a studio-grade markerless motion-capture system that captures full-body, hand, and facial motion simultaneously, and the YOOM Volumetric plugin for Unreal Engine (distributed via Epic Games' Fab marketplace) that plays back volumetric capture content in real time. Yoom serves gaming, film, TV, VFX, and immersive-media studios and is backed by Insight Partners. The company distributes its technology as game-engine plugins (Unreal Engine, Unity, Autodesk Maya, MotionBuilder) rather than as a public web API; as of this pass it publishes no REST/GraphQL API, developer portal, SDK on a public package registry, or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Your Super
providers.description: Your Super (Your Superfoods, Inc.) is a direct-to-consumer plant-based superfoods brand founded in 2015 in Venice, California by Michael Kuech and Kristel de Groot. It sells functional superfood and protein mixes and bars made from five to six nutrient-dense whole-food ingredients that are certified organic, Non-GMO, glyphosate-free, and gluten-free, sold through Shopify storefronts in the US and Europe and via Amazon. The company raised roughly $22.5M across five rounds from investors including 500 Global and PowerPlant Ventures, and was acquired by The Healing Company in October 2022. It is a consumer e-commerce brand and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: YouStake
providers.description: YouStake is a peer-to-peer sports staking and sponsorship marketplace, founded in 2013, that lets fans invest in skilled poker and esports players in exchange for a share of their tournament winnings. Players list their buy-ins and backers can stake them for as little as $20, structured as a person-to-person sponsorship agreement rather than gambling. The consumer platform has since rebranded and now operates as StakeKings (youstake.com redirects to stakekings.com), which also offers white-label staking-marketplace software to partners. It is a business-to-consumer web application with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or published API documentation.

providers.name: yplanapp
providers.description: YPlan (operated by Leanworks Limited) was a mobile-first event discovery and last-minute booking app founded in London in 2012 by Rytis Vitkauskas and Viktoras Jucikas. It offered a curated feed of things to do and same-day ticket booking across cities including London, Bristol, Dublin and New York, working with thousands of event partners. The company was acquired by Time Out Group plc in October 2016 and the consumer app was discontinued in 2017. The yplanapp.com domain now 301-redirects to checkout.timeout.com. No public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists; enrichment probing found no API artifacts, so this remains an identity-only record for a defunct company.

providers.name: ypxfood
providers.description: ypxfood (YPX Cayman) is a Taiwanese quick-service restaurant company specializing in Taiwanese food and snacks, backed by Qiming Venture Partners, LionRock Capital, and Ignition Capital. It is a consumer restaurant and food business with no public developer or API surface; enrichment probes found the corporate website (Cloudflare-fronted, returning 403 to automated clients) and no documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or well-known discovery endpoints. This profile is retained as a network company record.

providers.name: Yunji
providers.description: Yunji (云集) is a leading membership-based social e-commerce platform in China, founded in Hangzhou in May 2015. Yunji curates a wide range of consumer products across health food, beauty, personal care, digital devices, and apparel, and uses a member-driven model in which members earn rewards by sharing products with their social contacts. The company applies big data and artificial intelligence to optimize the shopping experience and incentivize social promotion. Yunji listed on the Nasdaq Stock Exchange (ticker YJ) in May 2019 as the first membership-based Chinese e-commerce firm to do so. Yunji was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, Yunji operates as a consumer mobile-app commerce platform and publishes no public developer or open API program.

providers.name: Yunyinggu (Viewtrix Technology)
providers.description: Yunyinggu Technology (云英谷科技), which rebranded as Viewtrix Technology, is a Shenzhen-based fabless semiconductor company founded in 2012 that designs AMOLED display driver integrated circuits (DDIC) and color-rendering display solutions for smartphones and other devices. By 2024 sales volume it was the largest AMOLED display driver chip supplier in mainland China and the fifth-largest globally, with R&D and operations across Shenzhen, Shanghai, Beijing, and Hong Kong. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners (Series C and extension), Huawei, and Xiaomi, the company completed a Hong Kong IPO. It is a hardware/semiconductor business and publishes no public developer API surface; this profile is retained as a network identity record. The original yunyinggu.com domain no longer resolves and viewtrix.com is a parked domain-for-sale listing.

providers.name: Zagster
providers.description: Zagster was a venture-funded bike-share startup based in Boston, Massachusetts (a Techstars portfolio company) that designed, built, and operated bike-sharing programs for cities, universities, corporate campuses, hotels, and residential communities across the United States, peaking at more than 200 programs in 2019. The company ceased bike-share operations in June 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic and is now defunct. Its former developer API host (zapi.zagster.com/api/v1/bikeshares) no longer resolves, and zagster.com is now a parked domain, so there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Zappli
providers.description: Zappli was an early mobile-commerce startup, maker of the myShopanion iPhone shopping app, which let consumers browse and shop retail products and share their finds and purchases across social networks such as Facebook and Twitter to get real-time feedback from friends and family. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), Founders' Co-op, Techstars, and the Webb Investment Network, Zappli was acquired by Connexity in July 2013 and is no longer operating. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation, and the zappli.com domain no longer serves a live website.

providers.name: Zebrium
providers.description: Zebrium was an AIOps startup that used unsupervised machine learning to automatically detect anomalies and surface root cause from log data, correlating logs and metrics into plain-language incident summaries without manual rules or training. Backed by Accel, the company was acquired by ScienceLogic in 2022 and its technology folded into the ScienceLogic AIOps / SL1 platform (now surfaced as Skylar). The independent zebrium.com developer/API surface has been retired: the domain 301-redirects to sciencelogic.com and no standalone Zebrium API, documentation, or specification remains publicly discoverable. This profile is retained as a network lead recording the acquisition and the residual domain footprint.

providers.name: Zed.run
providers.description: Zed.run is a digital horse racing platform where players buy, breed, and race NFT racehorses, originally built on the Ethereum and Polygon blockchains and developed by Virtually Human Studio. Players collect uniquely bred digital racehorses as non-fungible tokens, enter them into skill- and bloodline-based races, and trade them on a secondary marketplace. Zed.run was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the public API host (api.zed.run) returns a "zed shutdown" message, indicating the developer/API surface is currently discontinued or paused, so no live API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Zeitgold
providers.description: Zeitgold was a Berlin-based fintech that automated bookkeeping, invoice and receipt processing, payments, and financial administration for small and medium-sized businesses, blending software with human back-office review. It was backed by Battery Ventures and other investors and was acquired by Deel in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no independent public developer surface: zeitgold.com does not respond on HTTP or HTTPS, and zeitgold.de resolves to a parked/reserved domain page. No public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable artifact could be discovered, so this profile remains an identity-only record.

providers.name: Zengaming
providers.description: Zengaming builds gaming marketplaces and community products focused on helping gamers manage and monetize their digital assets. The company is best known for LootBear, a CS:GO / CS2 skin rental and marketplace platform, alongside an eSports social network that connects players and teams to compete and get discovered. Zengaming reports serving over 6 million users across its products and is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a consumer-facing marketing site only (an Unbounce landing page); no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface could be found.

providers.name: Zenprise
providers.description: Zenprise was an enterprise Mobile Device Management (MDM) vendor founded in 2003 by Waheed Qureshi and Jayaram Bhat. It shipped Zenprise MobileManager, an on-premises MDM platform for device lifecycle management and mobile security, and Zencloud, a cloud-based MDM service launched in 2011, together supporting iOS, Android, BlackBerry, Windows Mobile, and Symbian devices across more than 1,000 global enterprise and government customers. In 2010 Zenprise acquired French MDM vendor Sparus Software. Citrix announced its intent to acquire Zenprise in December 2012 and closed the deal in January 2013, folding the product into what became Citrix XenMobile. Zenprise no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live developer, documentation, or API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Zephyr Fusion
providers.description: Zephyr Fusion is a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) company building the first in-orbit fusion power source: a compact, megawatt-class magnetic-confinement fusion reactor designed to enable large-scale industry in space at a fraction of the cost of equivalent solar. Founded by former Lawrence Livermore and Oak Ridge National Laboratory physicists, the company targets microgravity manufacturing, orbital data centers, defense, propulsion, and human habitation in space, exploiting the vacuum of space to accommodate larger plasma regions than Earth-based reactors. As an early-stage deep-tech hardware company, Zephyr Fusion currently publishes no public API, developer platform, SDK, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures its identity in the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 confirmed no API surface exists (no api./docs./developer. hosts resolve; no /developers, /docs, or /.well-known discovery surface is published).

providers.name: ZeroMark
providers.description: ZeroMark is a defense-technology company building an AI-powered targeting system for counter-drone (counter-UAS) defense. Its bolt-on hardware and software components attach to existing weapons, platforms, and sensing systems to detect, track, and neutralize small drone threats in milliseconds while minimizing collateral damage. The product line spans Apex (AI aim-assist for shoulder-mounted rifles), Vanguard (a precision system for turret-mounted and vehicle platforms effective against Group 1-3 drones), and Nexus (a command-and-control software layer that integrates deployments into shared targeting and battlespace-awareness environments). ZeroMark was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or open-source presence; its Nexus C2 integration is delivered through defense procurement rather than a public developer program.

providers.name: Zeus
providers.description: Zeus (Zeus Living) was a furnished and corporate housing rental startup founded by Kulveer Taggar (previously co-founder of Auctomatic with Patrick Collison). The company leased and managed furnished residences that it re-let to business travelers, relocating employees, and companies needing flexible medium-term housing, backed by investors including Bloomberg Beta. Zeus Living has since wound down operations; its zeusliving.com domain no longer resolves and it exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile was surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed no live API or web presence remains.

providers.name: ZipDial
providers.description: ZipDial was a Bangalore, India based mobile marketing and analytics startup founded in 2010 that pioneered "missed call" engagement, letting consumers interact with brands and campaigns by giving a toll-free number a missed call rather than paying for a call or SMS. It was acquired by Twitter in January 2015 and its standalone product was subsequently wound down. The company was backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) among other investors. As of this enrichment pass the original company is defunct and no longer operates a developer program or public API; the zipdial.com domain now resolves to an unrelated general-interest content/news aggregation site with no developer, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: ZipMatch
providers.description: ZipMatch was an online real estate marketplace and property portal based in the Philippines, backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) among other investors, that helped buyers and renters discover homes, condominiums, and other property listings across Metro Manila and the wider Philippine market. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears to be defunct: the zipmatch.com domain is still registered (GoDaddy, registry expiry 2029) but has no DNS delegation — no NS, A, MX, or TXT records resolve — so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; no API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Ziroom
providers.description: Ziroom (自如) is a Beijing-based proptech company operating China's largest centralized long-term apartment rental platform. Spun out of the Lianjia (Homelink) real-estate group in 2011, it leases, renovates, furnishes and manages residential units and re-rents them to urban tenants through its app and website, layering on cleaning, maintenance and smart-home services. It is backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund, Tencent and Sequoia Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment found no publicly discoverable developer or API surface.

providers.name: Zugata
providers.description: Zugata was a San Francisco-based continuous performance-management and peer-feedback SaaS company, backed by Canaan Partners and others. Its platform let employees give and receive real-time, skill-based feedback and driver-of-performance insights for coaching and reviews. Culture Amp acquired Zugata in 2019 and folded its peer-feedback capabilities into the Culture Amp employee-experience platform; the standalone Zugata product and website (zugata.com) have since been retired. The domain still resolves NS and Proofpoint MX records (email routing) but serves no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API. No API surface exists to enrich — this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Zuoyebang
providers.description: Zuoyebang (作业帮) is a Chinese educational technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Beijing, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It operates a "technology + education" online learning platform whose flagship homework-help app lets K-12 students photograph a problem to get step-by-step answers, on-demand tutoring, and self-study tools across all subjects, alongside math tutoring products aimed at elementary-school parents and teachers. It is a consumer mobile/web product with no public developer program, open platform, or documented API surface at the time of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Zwitterco
providers.description: ZwitterCo is an advanced water treatment company that manufactures filtration membranes based on zwitterionic chemistry, a surface science that makes membranes attract water rather than organic compounds and thereby resist the organic fouling that limits conventional membranes. Its product families target food and dairy processing (Evolution membranes for whey and milk concentration), industrial and municipal wastewater (Elevation membranes for landfill leachate, refinery streams, and produced water), and extreme high-fouling waste streams (Expedition superfiltration). ZwitterCo is a DCVC portfolio company. It sells physical membrane hardware and treatment systems through direct sales and does not currently publish any public developer portal, API, SDKs, or machine-readable interface; this profile is a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Zymergen
providers.description: Zymergen was a synthetic-biology and bio-manufacturing company founded in 2013 in Emeryville, California, that used machine learning and automation to engineer microbes and discover novel bio-based materials and molecules. It went public on NASDAQ in 2021 and was acquired by Ginkgo Bioworks in October 2022; the zymergen.com domain now 301-redirects to Ginkgo Bioworks. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, Kindred Ventures, and Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment found no public developer portal, API, documentation, or event surface — the company has no independent API footprint following the acquisition. This profile is retained as a portfolio/history record.

providers.description: Unofficial US Federal Government API Development

providers.name: Advanced Drainage Systems
providers.description: Advanced Drainage Systems (ADS) is a leading manufacturer of stormwater and onsite septic wastewater solutions. The company produces drainage infrastructure including pipes, chambers, basins, and water quality treatment products serving residential, commercial, agricultural, airport, and transportation markets. ADS provides CAD integrations and engineering resources for civil engineering professionals.

providers.name: Arresto Biosciences
providers.description: Arresto Biosciences, Inc. was a privately-held, development-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, focused on medicines to treat fibrotic diseases and cancer by targeting enzymes involved in the synthesis of the extracellular matrix. Its lead product was AB0024, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the human lysyl oxidase-like-2 (LOXL2) protein, then in Phase I studies for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and advanced solid tumors. Founded circa 2007 and backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, HealthCare Ventures, Northgate Capital, DAG Ventures and Abbott Biotech Ventures, Arresto was acquired by Gilead Sciences for $225 million; the deal was announced December 20, 2010 and had closed by February 2011. The company no longer operates as an independent entity, publishes no developer or API surface, and its former domain (arrestobio.com) no longer resolves.

providers.description: Covid 19 spread, infection and recovery

providers.name: First National of Nebraska
providers.description: First National of Nebraska, Inc. is a privately held bank holding company headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. Through its subsidiaries, including First National Bank of Omaha, the company provides a full range of consumer, commercial, and agricultural banking services along with credit card processing and merchant services. It is one of the largest privately owned banking companies in the United States.

providers.name: Frontier Group Holdings
providers.description: Frontier Group Holdings is the parent company of Frontier Airlines, an ultra low-cost carrier headquartered in Denver, Colorado. The airline operates an Airbus A320-family fleet serving destinations across the United States, Mexico, Canada, the Caribbean, and Latin America. No public self-service developer API or developer portal has been identified; airline distribution and partner integrations are typically handled through GDSs, NDC channels, and direct travel-agent agreements.

providers.name: Healthpeak Properties
providers.description: Healthpeak Properties (NYSE: DOC) is an S&P 500 healthcare real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns, operates, and develops real estate for healthcare discovery and outpatient care — concentrated in lab/life-sciences, outpatient medical, and continuing care retirement community (CCRC) senior housing segments. The company tagline is "Where Discovery and Outpatient Care Thrive." Originally founded as HCP Inc. in 1985, the company rebranded to Healthpeak Properties in 2019. On March 1, 2024, Healthpeak completed an all-stock merger of equals with Physicians Realty Trust, combining two of the largest outpatient medical real estate platforms in the United States and adopting the new NYSE ticker DOC (previously PEAK). Healthpeak's portfolio spans roughly 700 properties nationwide, with lab concentrations in the South San Francisco, Boston, and San Diego clusters (including Torrey Pines Science Park and The Cove at Oyster Point) and outpatient medical assets clustered on or near top-ranked hospital campuses such as Medical City Dallas. The company reports that approximately 150,000 scientists, researchers, physicians, and healthcare professionals work in its buildings. As a healthcare REIT, Healthpeak does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or technical integration surface. Its public digital footprint is limited to corporate marketing, an investor relations site, SEC filings, ESG/sustainability reporting, and a press room. Tenant-facing operational systems (work orders, building access, energy reporting) are not exposed externally.

providers.name: Hillenbrand
providers.description: Hillenbrand is a global manufacturer of highly engineered, mission-critical processing equipment and systems serving the plastics, food, and recycling industries. The company operates across more than 60 global locations with a portfolio of leading industrial brands. Hillenbrand reports approximately $2.7 billion in annual revenue and employs over 8,000 associates worldwide.

providers.name: Konfio
providers.description: Konfio is a leading Mexican fintech serving small and medium businesses (SMBs) with an all-in-one platform: working-capital and term loans (Konfio Creditos), a business credit card (Konfio Tarjeta), payment terminals and acceptance (Konfio Pagos / Sirvis), and SMB management tools. Underwriting is powered by a proprietary algorithm that combines alternative data and ML to score creditworthiness in minutes. Konfio's product surface is overwhelmingly direct-to-SMB and the company does not publish a self-service public developer portal. Partner integrations (e.g. PayPal Working Capital, Goldman Sachs / Gramercy capital facilities, marketplace lending) are negotiated bilaterally.

providers.name: ModivCare
providers.description: ModivCare Inc. is a technology-enabled healthcare services company that provides a suite of integrated supportive care solutions for public and private payors and their members. The company offers non-emergency medical transportation (NEMT), personal care services, and remote patient monitoring to address social determinants of health. ModivCare partners with healthcare plans, government agencies, and providers to improve access to care for vulnerable populations.

providers.name: New York Community Bancorp
providers.description: New York Community Bancorp, Inc. (now operating as Flagstar Financial) is a Fortune 500 bank holding company headquartered in Hicksville, New York. Through its banking subsidiary, the company provides commercial banking, multi-family lending, mortgage banking, and consumer banking services across the United States. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with the company. No public developer APIs or documentation portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Pall Corporation
providers.description: Pall Corporation is a filtration, separation, and purification solutions provider serving aerospace and defense, food and beverage, semiconductors, oil and gas, and industrial manufacturing industries. Pall does not currently publish a public developer platform or REST API.

providers.name: People's United Financial
providers.description: Defunct U.S. regional bank holding company, headquartered in Bridgeport, Connecticut. Acquired by M&T Bank Corporation in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $7.6 billion. The acquisition was announced February 22, 2021 and closed April 2, 2022. People's United operated roughly 403 branches at close and was fully integrated into M&T Bank by Q3 2022. The People's United brand has been retired; peoples.com now 301-redirects to mtb.com. No public developer program, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, GitHub organization, or documented APIs existed at any point during its operating history.

providers.name: Rithm Capital
providers.description: Rithm Capital is a global asset manager focused on real estate, credit, and financial services. Through subsidiaries such as Newrez, Genesis Capital, Sculptor Capital Management, and Adoor, Rithm operates across mortgage origination and servicing, single-family rental, business-purpose lending, and alternative investment strategies. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified at the parent company level.

providers.name: Sinclair
providers.description: Sinclair, Inc. is a diversified media company and a leading provider of local news and sports in the United States. The company owns or operates a large portfolio of television stations and is involved in original programming, digital media, technical services, and broadcast technology innovation through subsidiaries such as Dielectric, Bitpath, ONE Media, and CAST.ERA. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: Sylvamo
providers.description: Sylvamo is a global producer of uncoated freesheet paper, pulp, and other forest products, with mills and operations across North America, Latin America, and Europe. The company is recognized for brands such as HP Papers, Hammermill, and Chamex. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified; Sylvamo operates primarily through B2B sales channels and investor and corporate communications channels.

providers.name: Valley National Bancorp
providers.description: Valley National Bancorp is a regional bank holding company with its principal subsidiary, Valley National Bank, providing a full suite of commercial, business, and consumer banking services across the Northeast and Southeast United States. Valley National Bancorp does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: VICI Properties
providers.description: VICI Properties is an experiential real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns one of the largest portfolios of gaming, hospitality, and entertainment destinations in the United States, including Caesars Palace and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas. The company holds long-term triple-net leases with leading gaming operators. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified; VICI engages investors and partners through corporate and investor relations channels.

providers.name: WorldOil.com, Inc./Wellogix
providers.description: Wellogix (originally incorporated as WorldOil.com, Inc.) was a Houston, Texas software company serving the upstream oil and gas industry, backed by Battery Ventures. Its hosted tools - including WorkFlowNavigator, DynaMaps, DrillTeam, and FieldTeam - helped drilling engineers plan wells and let operators and service companies collaborate on and procure complex engineered services, exchanging enterprise data across companies. The company is no longer active as an operating software vendor; wellogix.com still has DNS registered but no responding web server, and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or package registry artifacts were found. Note the worldoil.com domain today belongs to Gulf Publishing's World Oil magazine, a separate, unrelated business.

providers.name: Xtract
providers.description: Xtract was a social-intelligence analytics company (xtract.fi / xtract.com) that refined social interaction, behaviour, and demographic data from telecom operators into detailed subscriber profiles through its Social Links platform, powering churn prevention, product marketing, customer acquisition, and demographics prediction. A Creandum portfolio company now listed as exited; its websites are offline and no public API surface exists.

providers.name: Xylem
providers.description: Xylem is a leading global water technology company committed to developing innovative technology solutions to the world's water challenges across the full water cycle.

providers.name: Accountable
providers.description: Accountable is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Buildscience
providers.description: BuildScience Inc. (Y Combinator Winter 2015) was a PropTech startup based in Mountain View, California that built an operating-system platform for commercial buildings. Its software let building owners and facility operators deploy customized building-management solutions intended to reduce operational costs while improving tenant satisfaction, and the company reported deploying in a one-million-square-foot Class A office building. As of the 2026 enrichment pass the company appears dormant: the buildscience.com domain no longer serves a live product (the host returns a CloudFront default certificate that does not match the domain and a broken origin), no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be located, and the organization's single public GitHub repository was last updated in January 2020. This profile is retained as a verified-identity network record; no API artifacts could be enriched because the provider publishes no live API.

providers.name: Cambridge Cancer Genomics
