Its flagship marketplace, Altrade, provided a real-time, anonymous electronic exchange for trading natural gas, crude oil, natural gas liquids, and power, backed by energy transaction management software spanning deal capture, portfolio monitoring, physical scheduling, and back-office reconciliation and settlement. At its peak the platform served more than 6,000 users worldwide. The company raised roughly $55.5M from investors including Battery Ventures, Austin Ventures, BP, Candescent Partners, and Capital Resource Partners. It ceased to exist as an independent company around 2002: its software operations were acquired by Caminus Corporation and its online marketplace by ChemConnect (recorded elsewhere as Supply Chain Connect). No live developer portal, API, or public developer surface exists for this defunct company.

providers.name: AMEE
providers.description: AMEE (Avoiding Mass Extinctions Engine, also styled Avoidance of Mass Extinctions Engine) was a London-based environmental-intelligence company founded around 2005 by Gavin Starks out of UK firm Dgen. It ran an open web-service API and cloud database that standardized carbon-emissions and energy-consumption data across 150+ countries, letting applications apply government emission factors to tracked activities. AMEE powered carbon calculators and footprinting for clients including Google, Morgan Stanley, Radiohead, Sun Microsystems, and UK and Irish government programs (notably the Act on CO2 campaign). It raised roughly $7.5M from Union Square Ventures, OATV (O'Reilly AlphaTech Ventures), The Accelerator Group, and Amadeus Capital Partners. AMEE was acquired by Pi (PredictX) in late 2015 / early 2016 and no longer operates as an independent company; the amee.com domain currently returns HTTP 502 with no live API or developer surface.

providers.name: AnalytiChem
providers.description: AnalytiChem is a global manufacturer of laboratory supplies, producing certified reference materials, specialized laboratory consumables, and sample-preparation systems for life sciences, environmental, materials, and lab-essentials markets. Its product families span ready-to-use culture media for microbial monitoring in pharmaceutical, food, beverage and environmental testing; laboratory standards for measuring heavy metals, pesticides and other contaminants; reference materials for the petrochemical, mining, metals and EV-battery industries; and reagents and solvents for chemical work and sample analysis. The company operates under ISO 17034, ISO 17025 and ISO 9001 quality accreditations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass AnalytiChem publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Ancora Biotech
providers.description: Ancora Biotech is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing breakthrough biotherapeutics for B cell cancers, metabolic diseases, and chronic hepatitis B infection. Formed by former Teneobio executives and venture investors, it oversees three therapeutic programs across separate spinoffs — TeneoTwo (TNB-486, a T cell engager in Phase I for B-cell malignancies), TeneoFour (TNB-738, an anti-CD38 antibody for inflammatory and metabolic disorders), and TeneoTen (an anti-HBV T cell engager for hepatitis B). It is a drug-development company with no public developer API or platform surface.

providers.name: Anglers
providers.description: Anglers is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Apcera
providers.description: Apcera was an enterprise container and policy management platform founded in 2012 by Derek Collison, offering a "trusted cloud" runtime that layered fine-grained, policy-driven governance over workloads, containers, and services across hybrid infrastructure. Backed by a16z and DCVC, the company took a majority investment from Ericsson in 2015, was fully acquired by Ericsson in 2016, and the platform was subsequently wound down around 2017. The company is defunct - its primary domain (apcera.com) no longer resolves to a company site (it 301-redirects to an unrelated third party), and there is no live developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or reachable API host to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record only.

providers.name: Apieron
providers.description: Apieron Inc. was a private, venture-backed medical device company headquartered in Menlo Park, California, formed in early 2001 to develop a simple-to-use, non-invasive monitor for the measurement of exhaled nitric oxide (eNO) as an aid in the management of asthma. Its patented biosensor platform enabled highly sensitive detection of selected analytes, and its Insight eNO System received U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance and launched in the United States in 2008. Following that launch Aerocrine filed patent-infringement complaints against Apieron and Apieron counterclaimed; citing the legal setbacks and a lack of financing, Apieron filed a Chapter 7 bankruptcy petition in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of California on 30 March 2010. At a court auction on 12 May 2010 Aerocrine acquired all of Apieron's business assets, including its patent and trademark portfolio, ending the litigation; the Insight product was discontinued and not returned to supply. Apieron was a clinical-hardware company and never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface. This profile is retained as a historical record of the Canaan Partners portfolio and is not an active API provider.

providers.name: Applied Biosystems
providers.description: Applied Biosystems is a life-sciences instrumentation brand now part of Thermo Fisher Scientific, known for genetic analysis and applied genomics platforms including real-time and end-point PCR (QuantStudio, StepOne, ViiA 7, ProFlex), Sanger capillary-electrophoresis sequencing (SeqStudio, 3500/3730 Genetic Analyzers), and mass spectrometry. Its software surface is delivered through Thermo Fisher Connect, a cloud platform for storing, analyzing, and sharing instrument data with Applied Biosystems qPCR and Sanger secondary-analysis modules, the Cloud Connect Utility for uploading data from non-cloud-enabled instruments, and the Instrument Connect remote-monitoring app. Applied Biosystems does not publish a standalone public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program; its programmatic footprint is instrument-connectivity and cloud analysis rather than a hosted web API. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with verified company identity only.

providers.name: Argon Networks
providers.description: Argon Networks was a late-1990s networking infrastructure startup that developed a high-speed routing switch for what was then described as the next-generation multi-service Internet, combining IP routing with ATM switching in a single carrier-class platform. The company was venture backed by Canaan Partners (Series B, partner Eric Young), Matrix Partners, New Enterprise Associates and Greylock. Siemens acquired Argon Networks in March 1999 in a deal reported at roughly $240 million and folded the team into Unisphere Solutions / Unisphere Networks, the carrier-infrastructure unit later acquired by Juniper Networks in 2002. Argon Networks predates the public web API era: it shipped carrier networking hardware, never operated a developer program, and has no surviving website, documentation, SDKs or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical venture-portfolio record rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: ARMO BioSciences *
providers.description: ARMO BioSciences was a clinical-stage immuno-oncology biopharmaceutical company based in Redwood City, California, developing biologic therapeutics that activate a patient's own immune system to fight cancer. Its lead candidate was pegilodecakin (AM0010), a PEGylated recombinant human interleukin-10 (IL-10) evaluated across solid tumors. Backed by GV and Kleiner Perkins, the company IPO'd on NASDAQ in 2018 and was acquired by Eli Lilly and Company that same year for approximately $1.6 billion; its former web domain now redirects to lilly.com. As a life-sciences therapeutics developer it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio/acquisition record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Arsanis *
providers.description: Arsanis was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in the life-sciences sector, focused on developing monoclonal antibody immunotherapies to prevent and treat serious infectious diseases. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a company stub. Arsanis operated as a therapeutics developer rather than a software or API provider, and the company no longer exists as an independent entity; its public web presence at arsanis.com is no longer served. This profile is retained as a portfolio-graph lead with no active developer, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Ascend Communications
providers.description: Ascend Communications, Inc. was an Alameda, California manufacturer of wide area networking equipment, founded in 1988 and taken public in 1994. It developed, manufactured and sold WAN access solutions — remote-access concentrators, ISDN and frame relay gear, and the MAX family of access servers — to telecommunications carriers, Internet service providers and corporate customers worldwide, becoming a leading supplier during the dial-up internet build-out of the 1990s. On January 13, 1999 Lucent Technologies announced a definitive agreement to merge with Ascend in a stock deal valued at roughly $20.3 billion, and the merger completed on June 24, 1999, when Ascend became a wholly owned subsidiary of Lucent. The company has not operated independently since. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company; it predates the public web API era and publishes no developer surface today.

providers.name: Atlas Wearables
providers.description: Atlas Wearables was an Austin, Texas fitness-technology startup founded in 2013 by Peter Li, Mike Kasparian, and Alex Hsieh. It raised over $500,000 on Indiegogo in 2014 for the Atlas Wristband, a motion-tracking gym wearable whose "Exercise ID" technology automatically recognized strength exercises and counted reps and sets. The company shipped the Atlas Wristband and Wristband 2 and historically promoted an open developer API and integrations with apps such as MapMyFitness and Fitocracy. Atlas Wearables was acquired by Peloton Interactive in late 2020; the company no longer operates independently and the atlaswearables.com domain no longer resolves (it is now held by Peloton Interactive). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a former Techstars-associated portfolio lead; no live developer surface, API specification, or documentation remains available to enrich.

providers.name: Atomic Alchemy
providers.description: Atomic Alchemy is a deep-tech nuclear company that designs, builds, and operates non-power research reactors to manufacture high-value radioisotopes for medical, research, industrial, defense, and space applications. Its proprietary Versatile Isotope Production Reactor (VIPR) technology and Meitner-1 facility are intended to create a scalable, onshore supply of isotopes such as molybdenum-99 (for cancer diagnostics and treatment), strontium-90, and americium-241, reducing US dependence on foreign isotope production. Founded by CEO Thomas Eiden and headquartered in Idaho Falls, Idaho, the company was backed by DCVC and Y Combinator and was acquired by advanced-fission company Oklo (NYSE: OKLO) in early 2025, operating as a wholly owned subsidiary. In 2026 the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission granted Atomic Alchemy a materials license to handle, process, and distribute isotopes. As a physical radioisotope manufacturer, Atomic Alchemy publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Avanex
providers.description: Avanex Corporation was a fiber-optic components manufacturer founded in 1997 and headquartered in Fremont, California, backed by Mayfield along with Crosspoint Venture Partners, JAFCO America and Sequoia Capital. Avanex designed and built photonic processors, optical components, modules and subsystems used to raise the speed and capacity of fiber-optic communication networks, and went public on NASDAQ in February 2000 raising $216 million. In April 2009 Avanex merged with Bookham Technology to form Oclaro, and Oclaro was in turn acquired by Lumentum in December 2018. Avanex is no longer an operating company: it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API of any kind, and the avanex.com domain is now a parked GoDaddy for-sale listing. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lineage record only.

providers.name: Babylon Bio
providers.description: Babylon Bio (Babylon Biosciences) is a San Francisco-based drug discovery and development company founded in 2023 and backed by Lux Capital. Staffed by experienced medicinal chemists and biologists with a track record of discovering FDA-approved medicines, the company develops therapeutics that rescue essential functions in the brain rather than clearing emergent pathology, leveraging a proprietary high-throughput assay platform with an early focus on neurodegenerative disease including Alzheimer's. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As a private, pre-commercial biotech it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Balanced
providers.description: Balanced was a payments API for online marketplaces and crowdfunding platforms, founded out of Y Combinator (W2011) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), SV Angel, Collaborative Fund, and angels including Brian Chesky and Ashton Kutcher. It offered a developer-first API for processing cards and bank (ACH) payments, paying out to sellers, and handling seller identity/underwriting for marketplaces. Balanced announced on 2015-03-13 that it was shutting down its payments platform and gave customers 90 days notice, striking a transition deal that migrated card, bank account, and seller identity data to Stripe by 2015-06-11. The company and its API are defunct; the balancedpayments.com domain is now a parked/lander page and the api/docs hosts no longer resolve.

providers.name: Beechwood Data Systems
providers.description: Beechwood Data Systems is an IT and software services company historically focused on the telecommunications sector, providing systems that enable telecom companies to exchange and integrate data. It was surfaced as a portfolio company associated with Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. The enrichment pipeline found no live developer portal, documentation host, public API, or machine-readable API specification for this provider, so no API artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived without fabrication. This profile remains an identity-only stub pending a confirmed active developer surface.

providers.name: Beryllium
providers.description: Beryllium was a Singapore- and Delhi-based sports and trading game development platform founded in 2018/2019 by Amay Makhija, best known for its consumer product Sixer — a fantasy cricket game where users bought "Up" or "Down" virtual stocks in professional cricketers, with prices moving on in-game batting, bowling, and fielding metrics. The company raised roughly $3.6M across two rounds, including a $3M pre-Series A in June 2021 led by Bullpen Capital with Genting Ventures and Velo Partners. Beryllium was acquired by Dream Sports (Dream11) in October 2023. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct as an independent operator: sixer.gg no longer resolves in DNS, and beryllium.ai is a parked domain listed for sale on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket. Beryllium never published a public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.

providers.name: Bestcomm
providers.description: Bestcomm (Bestcomm Pharmaceutical) is a China-based pharmaceutical company backed by IDG Capital, surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It operates in the healthcare / life-sciences sector and raised venture funding alongside IDG Capital and regional investors. As a pharmaceutical manufacturer it has no known public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or programmatic API surface; this profile remains a company lead rather than an API provider. It is distinct from the unrelated BestComm Networks wireless-LAN company.

providers.name: Biophero
providers.description: BioPhero is a Danish agricultural biotechnology company that engineers microbes to produce synthetic insect pheromones via microbial fermentation, providing low-cost, bio-based pest control that disrupts insect mating cycles on major row crops without toxic insecticides. Founded as a spin-out from the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), BioPhero raised a DCVC Bio-led Series A (with FMC Ventures, Syngenta Group Ventures, and Novo Holdings) and was subsequently acquired by FMC Corporation. The company is a DCVC portfolio holding surfaced in the API Evangelist network; it operates as a research and product organization in synthetic biology and crop protection and publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or agent-facing surface.

providers.name: bioscience-tj
providers.description: Bioscience (Tianjin) Diagnostic Technology Co., Ltd. (博奥赛斯) is a Chinese in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) company that integrates R&D, manufacturing, marketing, and technical support for diagnostic instruments and reagents. Its product lines span chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) and point-of-care testing (POCT) analyzers together with the supporting reagent kits used in clinical laboratories and hospitals. The company is headquartered in Tianjin, China and is a healthcare portfolio company backed by Qiming Venture Partners. It manufactures medical diagnostic devices and consumables rather than publishing a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead, and no public API, developer portal, documentation, or specification surface has been found at this time.

providers.name: Biotyx Medical
providers.description: Biotyx Medical (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. is a medical device company founded in 2019 as a subsidiary of LifeTech Scientific Corporation (HKEX: 01302), headquartered in Shenzhen, China. It develops iron-based bioresorbable vascular scaffolds (the IBS platform) for coronary, peripheral, and congenital cardiovascular disease, and is the only company in the world commercializing iron-based bioresorbable stents. Its products include the IBS Coronary Scaffold, IBS Titan peripheral scaffold, and IBS Angel pulmonary artery scaffold, with NMPA innovative-device approvals, US and Malaysia sales licenses, and CE certification. This is a medical device manufacturer with no public developer, API, or technology-platform surface; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking.

providers.name: Bipar Sciences
providers.description: BiPar Sciences was a Brisbane, California biopharmaceutical company developing a tumor-selective class of PARP (poly ADP-ribose polymerase) inhibitors for cancer therapy. Its lead candidate, BSI-201 (iniparib), was in mid-stage trials for advanced breast, ovarian, and other tumors. Backed by Canaan Partners, Vulcan Capital, PolyTechnos, Asset Management Company, and Quantum Technology Partners, BiPar was acquired by Sanofi-Aventis for roughly $500 million in April 2009 and no longer operates as an independent company. It was surfaced as a Canaan Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment finds no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: BIZZON
providers.description: BIZZON (formerly AgentCASH) was a London-based hospitality and restaurant technology company founded in 2015, offering an end-to-end point-of-sale (POS) and payments platform for the food-and-beverage and hospitality sector. Its suite spanned sales/ordering tools, business intelligence, and fully certified cloud-hosted omnichannel payment technology, letting operators manage online orders, payments, menus, inventory, staff, and loyalty. Backed by Techstars, Mews, and Ascension, BIZZON was acquired by hospitality cloud platform Mews in March 2022 and its product and infrastructure have since been folded into Mews; the former developer surface (developers.bizzon.com), status page, and the agentcash.com domain are no longer live, and the your.bizzon.com portal now redirects to pos.mews.com. This profile is retained as a historical provider/company record. No independent live API or developer surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Bonnus
providers.description: Bonnus is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Braid Social
providers.description: Braid (Braid Social) was a creator-economy startup building a direct-to-fan engagement platform for the creator economy. Founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro, Braid let creators build customizable landing pages that consolidated their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts, and commerce links), collect fan phone numbers, and reach followers directly through SMS text messages, push notifications, and mailing lists, with link tracking and cross-platform analytics. Positioned as a creator-friendly, direct-to-audience alternative to algorithm-driven social platforms, Braid raised a $6.8M seed round in August 2023 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Initialized Capital. The company appears to be defunct as of this profile — its primary domain (braid.ai) now redirects to a domain-for-sale listing and no developer, documentation, or API surface could be found. Added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead; no public API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Brightmail
providers.description: Brightmail was an email anti-spam software company founded in 1998 by Sunil Paul, best known for its network of "spam probe" honeypot email addresses that fed real-time anti-spam filtering rules to enterprise mail servers. Symantec acquired Brightmail in 2004 for roughly $370 million, and the technology shipped for years as Symantec Brightmail AntiSpam and later Symantec Mail Security; Symantec's enterprise security business was subsequently acquired by Broadcom in 2019. Brightmail today is a defunct brand with no independent developer program or public API surface — www.brightmail.com redirects to broadcom.com and the brightmail.com apex domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained for historical/network completeness rather than active API enrichment.

providers.name: Broadband Access
providers.description: Broadband Access Systems, Inc. was a Westborough, Massachusetts networking company founded in 1998 that built a next-generation Internet Protocol (IP) broadband access platform — a carrier-class cable-modem termination system (CMTS) that let cable operators and communications service providers deliver data, voice and video services over hybrid fiber-coax networks at scale. Matrix Partners was one of eight venture investors in the company alongside North Bridge Venture Partners, Norwest, Blueprint Ventures and Bowman Capital Management. ADC Telecommunications agreed on September 20, 2000 to acquire Broadband Access Systems for approximately $2.25 billion in ADC common stock, and the acquisition closed on October 2, 2000. The company was absorbed into ADC's cable and broadband business, which ADC later divested; ADC itself was acquired by TE Connectivity in 2010. Broadband Access Systems operated no public developer program and shipped hardware platforms rather than APIs; it has had no independent web, documentation, or API surface since 2000. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical venture-portfolio record only.

providers.name: Brooktrout Technology
providers.description: Brooktrout Technology, Inc. was a Needham, Massachusetts telecommunications company founded in 1984 that designed fax and voice-processing hardware and software for computer telephony integration (CTI), including the TR114 and TR1034 fax boards and the SR140 host-based (software) fax product. Its developer kit, the Brooktrout SDK, provided C/C++ APIs for building fax, voice, and unified-messaging applications. Brooktrout was acquired by Excel Switching in 2000 (forming Brooktrout Technology / Excel), and the Brooktrout product line later became part of Dialogic, which continues to ship and document the Dialogic Brooktrout SDK. The brooktrout.com domain now redirects to Dialogic; Brooktrout survives as a legacy product brand rather than an independent company, and it has no standalone modern web-API developer surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead.

providers.name: CakeHealth
providers.description: CakeHealth (Cake Health) was a San Francisco health-insurance management startup founded in 2011 by Rebecca Woodcock, pitched as "Mint for health insurance." Users linked their insurer logins so the service could aggregate health plans, claims, bills, deductibles, and out-of-pocket spending into a single consumer dashboard. It launched as a TechCrunch Disrupt finalist and was backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) and Kima Ventures. Inbox Health acquired the company for its medical-bill tracking technology in April 2016, after which the product was shut down. The company is defunct and no longer operates an API or developer surface; the cakehealth.com domain has since been repurposed and now redirects to an unrelated third-party site.

providers.name: Calibra Medical
providers.description: Calibra Medical, Inc. was a Redwood City, California medical device company founded in 2004 to make mealtime insulin therapy simpler and more discreet. Its product was the Finesse "patch-pen", a fully mechanical, three-day wearable bolus insulin delivery patch (roughly 2 x 1 x 0.25 inches, 200-unit reservoir, no batteries, display, or handheld controller) dosed by pressing two buttons. Backed by Canaan Partners, Frazier Healthcare Partners, Intersouth Partners, Skyline Ventures, and Three Arch Partners, the company raised approximately $61.5M before Johnson & Johnson acquired it in a reported $77M all-cash deal in 2012, folding it into the J&J Diabetes Care Companies. J&J rebranded the device OneTouch Via but never commercially launched it, and on July 17, 2018 sold select Calibra Medical assets and an exclusive worldwide license to Swiss wearable-insulin firm CeQur. Calibra Medical no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no API, and no public source repositories, and the calibramedical.com domain now resolves to a parked "domain may be for sale" page. This profile is retained as a historical medical-device company record with no API surface.

providers.name: Calixa Therapeutics
providers.description: Calixa Therapeutics was a privately held, San Diego-based biopharmaceutical company focused on developing antibiotics to treat serious infections caused by multi-drug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial pathogens. Its lead compound, CXA-201 (later ceftolozane/tazobactam), was an intravenous therapy for serious hospital-acquired Gram-negative infections. Calixa was acquired by Cubist Pharmaceuticals in December 2009 for approximately $92.5 million (plus up to $310 million in milestone payments) and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer or API surface. This profile exists in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub associated with canaan-partners; there are no API artifacts to enrich because it is a defunct pharmaceutical company, not an API provider.

providers.name: Call Levels
providers.description: Call Levels was a Singapore-based financial technology company, founded in 2014 by Cynthia Siantar and Daniel Chia, that built a real-time financial markets monitoring and price-alert service. Its consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) let retail investors set price "call levels" and receive real-time alerts across multiple asset classes including forex, commodities, indices and equities, serving 500,000+ investors globally. On the institutional side it offered an open API and a chatbot/portfolio-management framework marketed to banks and financial institutions for embedding market monitoring into legacy systems. The company was backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) via a pre-Series A round. As of this profile the primary domain (call-levels.com) resolves to a parked registrar lander with no live developer portal, API documentation, or discoverable API surface, so the company appears dormant or defunct and no live API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Camiant
providers.description: Camiant, Inc. was a policy control and application-assurance technology vendor for broadband and mobile service providers, founded in 2003 in Marlborough, Massachusetts (originally Chameleon Solutions). Its Multimedia Policy Engine implemented 3GPP Release 8/9 Policy and Charging Rules Function (PCRF) capabilities and was deployed by operators including Verizon, Vodafone, Sprint, Comcast, and Cox. Tekelec acquired Camiant in 2010 for approximately $130 million, and the business was later folded into Oracle Communications. Camiant no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, API, or documentation; its former domain (camiant.com) is parked. Surfaced as a matrix-partners portfolio lead, this profile records verified public history rather than a live API surface.

providers.name: CapMAC Holdings
providers.description: CapMAC Holdings Inc. (Capital Markets Assurance Corporation) was a New York-based holding company that provided financial guaranty and surety insurance for structured securities worldwide, primarily asset-backed securities, alongside structured financial solutions, advisory and structuring services, and investment management. Founded in 1973 and headquartered at 885 Third Avenue in New York City, it was a Canaan Partners portfolio company. MBIA Inc. acquired CapMAC Holdings in a stock swap valued at more than $500 million, completing the merger on February 17, 1998, after which CapMAC operated as an indirect wholly-owned MBIA subsidiary. Capital Markets Assurance Corporation was merged into MBIA Insurance Corporation during the third quarter of 2010 and ceased to exist as a separately licensed insurer. The company is defunct and operates no website, developer program, or API surface; the capmac.com domain is an unrelated parked domain listed for sale.

providers.name: Caption Health
providers.description: Caption Health was an artificial-intelligence medical-imaging company founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, that built FDA-cleared AI software to guide clinicians through cardiac ultrasound scans in real time. Its flagship products, Caption Guidance and Caption AI, provided real-time image-acquisition guidance, automated image-quality assessment, and automatic ejection-fraction calculation, enabling non-specialist healthcare professionals to capture diagnostic-quality echocardiograms. Backed by DCVC and others (it raised a $53M Series B in 2020), Caption Health was acquired by GE HealthCare in February 2023 for roughly $150M and its technology was absorbed into GE HealthCare's ultrasound portfolio, shipping as Caption AI on the Vscan Air handheld system and within the Verisound AI digital-solutions line. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer API; this profile is retained as a network record of an acquired provider.

providers.name: Cardiovascular Devices
providers.description: Cardiovascular Devices was an early-stage healthcare company backed by Kleiner Perkins, which lists it in its partnerships archive as partnered since 1982, sector healthcare, stage early, and described simply as "cardiovascular monitoring devices". Kleiner Perkins records the company's status as acquired by 3M. It is a historical medical-device portfolio company that predates the public web: enrichment found no live corporate website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no public API surface of any kind, so this profile carries identity and provenance only. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a resolved venture-portfolio lead rather than as an active API provider, and no artifacts were generated because there is nothing real to harvest.

providers.name: CardSpring
providers.description: CardSpring was a card-linked offers and payments platform that provided an API for building card-linked applications, letting developers connect merchant point-of-sale systems and consumer payment cards to deliver digital coupons, loyalty rewards, and receipt-level offers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company was acquired by Twitter in 2014 and subsequently wound down; as of this pass every path on cardspring.com (including the old /help/developer_faq.html) 307-redirects to an Afternic "cardspring.com is for sale" domain-sale lander, developer.cardspring.com fails TLS with no matching certificate, and no first-party CardSpring packages remain on npm or RubyGems. There is no live developer portal, documentation, API, or OpenAPI surface to enrich. Sector: payments.

providers.name: Cayena
providers.description: Cayena is a Brazilian B2B technology company operating an e-procurement marketplace and embedded-fintech platform for the food-service industry. It connects restaurants, bars, hotels, and other food-service buyers with food, beverage, and supply distributors, streamlining ordering, catalog discovery, and fulfillment while layering in payments and short-term credit (buy-now-pay-later) so operators can purchase supplies and defer payment. Headquartered in Sao Paulo, Cayena is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company lead; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal has been confirmed for Cayena at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: cdhot (Hot New Energy Technology)
providers.description: cdhot (Hot New Energy Technology) is a Chinese industrial energy-efficiency company listed in the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio. Qiming describes the company as providing EPC (engineering, procurement and construction) and EMC (energy management contracting) services to industrial customers to achieve waste heat recovery — capturing surplus process heat from industrial operations and converting it into reusable energy. The company is an engineering and energy-services business rather than a software or API provider. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass its published website at cdhot.cc did not resolve over HTTPS, redirected to www.cdhot.cc over HTTP and returned an empty HTTP 404, and no developer portal, documentation, specification, or API surface of any kind could be found.

providers.name: Cell Design Labs
providers.description: Cell Design Labs, Inc. was a biotherapeutics company based at 5858 Horton Street, Emeryville, California, that engineered immune cells into "smart, living therapies" for cancer and other diseases. Its platform was a toolkit of proprietary molecular modules — including synthetic Notch (synNOTCH) receptors and programmable, combinatorial-antigen CAR-T circuits developed out of Wendell Lim's lab at UCSF — deployed inside an immune cell to program its specificity and control its killing force, so a therapy recognizes a disease signature and neutralizes it without harming adjacent tissue. The company ran an exclusive research collaboration with Kite Pharma (announced June 2016) on molecular on/off switches for CAR T-cell immunotherapies, and was acquired by Gilead Sciences, announced 7 December 2017. Cell Design Labs no longer operates as an independent company: celldesignlabs.com is dead (DNS resolves to a parked address, HTTP times out; the archived site shows an expired Squarespace subscription). It published no developer program, API, documentation, SDK, or GitHub organization, and none exists to enrich.

providers.name: Cell Pathways
providers.description: Cell Pathways, Inc. (CPI) was a development-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered at 702 Electronic Drive, Horsham, Pennsylvania, focused on the research and development of products to treat and prevent cancer. Incorporated in Delaware in July 1998 (as Cell Pathways Holdings, Inc., renamed Cell Pathways, Inc. in February 2001), it developed a class of compounds it called selective apoptotic anti-neoplastic drugs (SAANDs), designed to induce selective apoptosis — programmed cell death — in precancerous and cancerous cells without affecting normal cells. Its lead candidate was Aptosyn (exisulind), studied in precancerous lesions such as colonic polyps and cervical dysplasia and later in prostate, lung, and breast cancer; the company also imported, promoted, and sold Gelclair Concentrated Oral Gel into oncology and dental markets, and had previously marketed Nilandron. It traded on the Nasdaq National Market (Commission File No. 000-24889) and employed approximately 34 people full-time as of March 1, 2003. In February 2003 Cell Pathways signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger to be acquired by OSI Pharmaceuticals, Inc. in a stock-for-stock exchange; stockholders approved the merger on June 10, 2003, and the company filed a Form 15-12G on June 12, 2003 terminating its Exchange Act registration with one holder of record. OSI Pharmaceuticals was itself acquired by Astellas Pharma and deregistered on June 18, 2010. Cell Pathways predates the API economy entirely, never operated a developer program or public API surface, and no longer exists as an operating entity. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cellular Research
providers.description: Cellular Research, Inc. was a single-cell genomics company backed by Canaan Partners that developed molecular-indexing (its "Precise" assay) technology for high-throughput single-cell gene expression analysis. The company was acquired by Becton Dickinson (BD) in 2015 and its technology became the foundation of the BD Rhapsody single-cell analysis platform. As a life-sciences instrument and reagent company folded into BD, it exposes no independent public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is retained as a portfolio-lead identity record only.

providers.name: Cerent
providers.description: Cerent Corporation was a Petaluma, California optical-networking startup, founded in the mid-1990s and backed by Kleiner Perkins, that built the Cerent 454 — a compact next-generation SONET multiservice provisioning platform that collapsed traditional add-drop multiplexing into a far smaller, cheaper, data-aware box for carrier metro networks. Cisco Systems acquired Cerent in 1999 for approximately $6.9 billion in stock, at the time the largest acquisition in Cisco's history, and the product line shipped on as the Cisco ONS 15454, one of Cisco's most successful optical transport platforms. Cerent has not operated as an independent company since. Its hardware-era business predated public web APIs entirely, and it maintains no developer platform, documentation, SDKs, or API surface today — the cerent.com domain is now held by Cisco and serves only an acquisition notice. This profile is retained as a venture-portfolio historical record, not an active API provider.

providers.name: CES International
providers.description: CES International was a software company founded in 1989 and based in Alpharetta, Georgia, that built real-time software solutions for distribution utilities — including the Centricity operations resource management (ORM) system with outage-management capabilities and an energy delivery management (EDM) suite for network operations — serving utilities on five continents and more than 35 million metered accounts. It was acquired by SPL WorldGroup in May 2004, and SPL WorldGroup was in turn acquired by Oracle in November 2006, where its utilities software became the foundation of the Oracle Utilities global business unit. CES International no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface, and none of its historical domains resolve to a live company site. This record is retained as a historical / defunct entry in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ChemConnect
providers.description: ChemConnect, Inc. was a Houston, Texas-based electronic exchange (founded 1995) for trading midstream energy, feedstocks, chemicals, and related commodities such as natural gas liquids, refined and intermediate fuels, aromatics, olefins, and commodity polymers, serving thousands of member companies with e-commerce, market information, negotiation, and supply-chain collaboration tooling. It acquired rival CheMatch to form a leading commodity trading platform. The company is a now-exited Battery Ventures portfolio investment; it no longer operates and the chemconnect.com domain is parked and listed for sale (HugeDomains), so there is no live developer, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cinta Networks
providers.description: Cinta Networks, Incorporated was a venture-backed optical networking equipment startup of the dot-com era, funded in part by Battery Ventures and led by CEO John Vaughan. The company built the patented WAVEJunction product family, an architecture that integrated DWDM optical transport with optical switching in a single network element for metro, regional, and long-haul carrier networks, claiming capital-expense savings of more than 50 percent and operational savings of over 70 percent through modular, port-at-a-time growth, universal transponder cards, and dynamic wavelength reconfiguration across ring and mesh topologies. Public activity is visible from roughly 2000 to 2002, including a January 2002 WAVEJunction field-trial agreement with Pacific LightNet and a component supply arrangement with ADC. Cinta Networks appears to have ceased operations in the post-telecom-bust period: archived captures of cintanetworks.com show the site replaced by a parked domain-search page by 2004, and the domain no longer resolves in DNS as of July 2026. Cinta was a hardware manufacturer and never published a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts, so there is no API surface for this profile to describe. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio record.

providers.name: City Reach International
providers.description: City Reach International Limited was a UK-registered telecommunications and internet-infrastructure company, incorporated 14 April 2000 at 8 Salisbury Square, Blackfriars, London EC4Y 8BB (Companies House number 03973748), classified under SIC 6420 (telecommunications) and 7260 (other computer related activities). It was a dot-com era venture backed in part by Battery Ventures, and appears on the Battery Ventures all-companies list, which is how it entered the API Evangelist network. The company was dissolved on 13 May 2014. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found no surviving corporate website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface: the candidate domains cityreach.com, cityreachinternational.com, cityreach.net and cityreachinternational.co.uk do not resolve, and cityreach.co.uk resolves only to a parked domain-for-sale landing page. There is no API, specification, SDK, or event surface to catalog for this company, and none should be fabricated.

providers.name: Civitas Therapeutics
providers.description: Civitas Therapeutics was a privately held biopharmaceutical company founded in 2009 (Chelsea/Cambridge, Massachusetts) that developed inhaled therapeutics using the proprietary ARCUS dry-powder pulmonary delivery platform. Its lead program, CVT-301, was an inhaled levodopa therapy for the rapid relief of OFF episodes in Parkinson's disease patients. The company was acquired by Acorda Therapeutics in 2014 for approximately $525 million and no longer operates as an independent entity. It is a life-sciences / drug-development company with no public developer platform, API, SDK, or technical integration surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and retained in the API Evangelist network for provenance.

providers.name: Clarity Money
providers.description: Clarity Money was a personal-finance and money-management mobile app founded in 2016 by Adam Dell (Oath Holdings / Dell family) that used data-driven analysis to help consumers track spending, cancel unwanted subscriptions, negotiate bills, move savings, and manage budgets. It was acquired by Goldman Sachs in 2018 and folded into the Marcus by Goldman Sachs consumer platform; the standalone Clarity Money app was subsequently discontinued. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. No public developer program, API, documentation, or developer portal was ever published, and the claritymoney.com domain no longer resolves to a live site (held by Goldman Sachs registrar CSC).

providers.name: Clean Urban Energy
providers.description: Clean Urban Energy, Inc. was a Chicago, Illinois cleantech company that turned large commercial office buildings into grid-scale thermal energy storage assets. Its technology harnessed the existing thermal mass of a building — concrete, drywall, furnishings — by pre-cooling during off-peak hours and coasting through peak demand, effectively operating the building as a multi-megawatt battery for demand response and load shifting without installing dedicated storage hardware. The company raised a reported $7 million venture round and appears in the Battery Ventures list of all portfolio companies. As of a July 2026 review the company has no live corporate web presence: the cleanurbanenergy.com domain no longer serves company content, and no developer portal, API, documentation, or GitHub organization could be located. It is catalogued here as an inactive, non-API-provider company record.

providers.name: Clementine
providers.description: Clementine (Clementine Labs) was a New York based enterprise communication startup founded in 2013 and publicly launched in September 2014, offering workplace messaging, chat, and conference calling that let colleagues reach each other without exchanging personal mobile phone numbers. It appears on the Andreessen Horowitz investment list and was acquired by Dropbox in April 2016, after which the Clementine service was shut down and the team folded into Dropbox collaboration efforts. The company operates no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs today: its primary domain, clementine.io, now issues an HTTP 301 redirect to dropbox.com. This profile is retained as a historical, non-operational record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Clinkle
providers.description: Clinkle was a Silicon Valley mobile-payments startup founded in 2012 by Stanford student Lucas Duplan. In 2013 it raised roughly $30 million in what was then reported as the largest seed round in history, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Peter Thiel, Marc Benioff, Accel's Jim Breyer, Richard Branson, and Intel Capital. The company promised a phone-to-phone payments technology but never shipped a viable product, launched a poorly received "Treats" debit-card app, cycled through multiple pivots and leadership turmoil, and lost its window to Venmo and Apple Pay. By 2016 Clinkle had quietly shut down with no official announcement. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a defunct a16z portfolio lead; it publishes no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface today (clinkle.com resolves to a suspended-account page).

providers.name: Cloud Peak Energy
providers.description: Cloud Peak Energy Inc. was an American coal mining company headquartered in Gillette, Wyoming, established in 2009 as a spin-off from Rio Tinto Energy America. The company operated three open-pit mines in the Powder River Basin (Wyoming and Montana) and held a 50% interest in the Decker Coal Company. Cloud Peak Energy filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May 2019 amid declining demand for Powder River coal in East Asian and US markets and is no longer operating. This profile is maintained as a historical record - Cloud Peak Energy did not publish public APIs.

providers.name: Clover Networks
providers.description: Clover Network Inc. was a Silicon Valley mobile-payments startup that launched publicly in March 2012 with a one-click, app-based checkout network aiming to complete a payment in under five seconds using a phone number and PIN, charging merchants a 3% per-transaction fee and seeding adoption with a developer fund and instant-refund incentives. It raised $5.8M from Andreessen Horowitz and Sutter Hill Ventures and was acquired by First Data on December 28, 2012. The Clover name and technology were carried forward by First Data into the Clover point-of-sale platform, which is now owned by Fiserv and covered separately in the API Evangelist network by the `clover` repository. This entity is a historical a16z portfolio lead and no longer operates as an independent company or publishes its own developer surface.

providers.name: Combinatorx
providers.description: CombinatoRx, Inc. was a Cambridge/Boston, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company (SEC CIK 0001135906, SIC 2834 Pharmaceutical Preparations, incorporated in Delaware) that pursued combination drug discovery — screening pairs of approved drugs for synergistic therapeutic effects. It registered with the SEC in 2002 and traded publicly following its 2005 IPO. The company was renamed Zalicus Inc. in September 2010 after its combination with Neuromed Pharmaceuticals, and renamed again to EPIRUS Biopharmaceuticals, Inc. in July 2014 after merging with EPIRUS. EPIRUS was delisted in September 2016 (Form 25-NSE) and its SEC registration was formally revoked on 2024-05-14. The company is defunct: it operated no developer program and published no public API, SDK, or developer documentation, and combinatorx.com is now a parked NameBright listing unrelated to the original company. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Canaan Partners portfolio company and has no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Comprehend
providers.description: Comprehend Systems, Inc. was a clinical-trials software company that built SaaS analytics for the life-sciences industry. Its flagship product, Comprehend Clinical, let clinical data managers and executives monitor studies and make real-time decisions across multiple source systems without moving the underlying data. The company raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series B in 2014 and was acquired by Saama Technologies in 2019, after which the standalone Comprehend product and the comprehend.com domain were retired. This API Evangelist profile is a Lightspeed portfolio lead; the company is defunct as an independent entity and publishes no live developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Concho Resources
providers.description: Concho Resources, Inc. was an independent oil and natural gas company focused on the acquisition, development, exploration, and production of oil and natural gas properties primarily in the Permian Basin of West Texas and southeast New Mexico. On January 15, 2021, ConocoPhillips completed an all-stock acquisition of Concho Resources at a total enterprise value of $13.3 billion, retiring the Concho brand. This profile is preserved as a historical record; Concho no longer operates under this name and never published any public developer APIs.

providers.name: Concord Data Systems
providers.description: Concord Data Systems was a telecommunications equipment manufacturer founded in 1979 by Ken Miller (previously Director of Modem Development at Codex) and based in Marlborough, Massachusetts. The company designed and sold high-speed full-duplex dial-up telephone modems for transmitting digital computer data in analog form over the public switched telephone network. As the modem hardware market commoditized, the business pivoted from industrial data communications to the emerging market for network performance management software and was renamed Concord Communications, best known for its eHealth network management suite. Battery Ventures was one of thirteen investors in that company. Concord Communications was acquired by CA (Computer Associates) on 2005-06-07 for approximately $350 million ($330M cash plus roughly $20M of assumed net debt); CA was itself acquired by Broadcom in 2018. Concord Data Systems is therefore a historical, defunct entity: it operates no website, no developer portal, and no API surface today. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lineage record only.

providers.name: Conexant Systems
providers.description: Conexant Systems, Inc. was an American fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California. Spun off from Rockwell Semiconductor Systems in 1999, it designed mixed-signal and system-on-chip products for audio, voice, imaging, modem, and networking applications, and was best known for its dial-up modem chipsets, audio codecs, and far-field voice-input processors used in smart-home and IoT devices. Conexant's audio and imaging business was acquired by Synaptics in 2017 and the standalone Conexant brand has since been retired. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the company publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface (its former conexant.com domain no longer resolves to an active site), so there are no API artifacts to enrich at this time.

providers.name: Convergent Networks
providers.description: Convergent Networks, Inc. was a carrier-grade broadband voice infrastructure vendor that built next-generation VoIP switching and signaling equipment for telecommunications carriers, including the ICS2000 and Commando media gateways, the PacketMatrix softswitch controller for call screening and number translation, and the ICSG SS7 signaling gateway. Venture-backed by Battery Ventures and Saints Capital (raising roughly $57M across two rounds), the company was acquired by Eastern Photonics, a subsidiary of Global NAPs, in 2003. It is defunct and publishes no active developer portal, API, or specification. This profile was surfaced from the Battery Ventures portfolio as a lead; the enrichment pipeline found no live API surface to harvest.

providers.name: CONXUS Communications
providers.description: CONXUS Communications, Inc. was a United States advanced-messaging and narrowband-PCS carrier, headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina, that operated the Pocketalk voice-messaging and Pocketext text-messaging services built on Motorola's InFLEXion protocol. Formed in the mid-1990s from a group of one-way paging providers and backed by strategic and financial investors, the company offered wireless voice messaging, guaranteed message delivery, automatic acknowledgment of receipt, error correction, longer messages, and subscriber-originated replies across roughly ten U.S. markets. Conxus filed for bankruptcy protection in May 1999 and ceased network operations on August 27, 1999, affecting an estimated 80,000-100,000 subscribers. The company is defunct and publishes no API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio record only.

providers.name: Copper Mountain Network
providers.description: Copper Mountain Networks was a telecommunications equipment maker founded in 1996 by Mark Handzel and Joe Markee that led the 1990s DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) wave in North America, building central-office DSL concentrators (the CopperEdge platform) and customer-premises modems that delivered high-speed broadband over existing copper telephone lines. The company was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and InterWest, held its IPO in 1999, weathered the telecom downturn of 2001, and was acquired by Tut Systems in 2005 (later absorbed into Motorola in 2007). It shipped hardware and network equipment, not a public web/developer API; the company is defunct and operates no live developer platform today.

providers.name: coremed
providers.description: CoreMed (Beijing) Biomedical Research Co., Ltd. is a China-based contract research organization (CRO) founded in 2013 that provides clinical professional services for innovative cardiovascular medical devices and structural-heart products. Its services span animal testing, human clinical trials, data management, statistical analysis, and independent core-laboratory imaging analysis, and it was among the first domestic providers in China to run trials for interventional heart valves, LAA occluders, and bioresorbable scaffolds. Headquartered in Beijing with branches in Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Chengdu, CoreMed is backed by Qiming Venture Partners. This is a services/CRO company with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface; its site (coremed.com.cn) was unreachable at enrichment time (connection refused, expired TLS cert).

providers.name: Cortina Systems
providers.description: Cortina Systems, Inc. was a venture-backed fabless semiconductor company founded in 2001 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, that designed high-speed communications and networking integrated circuits for optical transport, carrier Ethernet, framer/mapper and PHY devices, and broadband access (EPON/GPON and DSL). The company grew through acquisitions and was itself acquired by Inphi Corporation in 2014; Inphi later merged into Marvell Technology in 2021, and the cortina-systems.com domain now redirects to Marvell. Cortina was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a hardware semiconductor business with no public developer platform or API surface, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Corventis
providers.description: Corventis, Inc. was a healthcare technology company that developed wearable cardiac monitoring devices — including the PiiX adhesive sensor and the NUVANT Mobile Cardiac Telemetry (MCT) system — for remote patient monitoring and arrhythmia detection. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, the company was acquired by Medtronic in 2014 and no longer operates as an independent entity. The corventis.com domain now resolves to Medtronic infrastructure (Medtronic nameservers; TLS certificate scoped to Medtronic domains). No public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API surface exists for this provider.

providers.description: Covid 19 cases, deaths and recovery per country

providers.description: Global and countrywise data of Covid 19 daily Summary, confirmed cases, recovered and deaths

providers.name: Crane
providers.description: Crane Co. (NYSE: CR) and its sister company Crane NXT (NYSE: CXT) are industrial manufacturing companies that resulted from the 2023 split of the legacy Crane Holdings, Co. Crane Co. is a diversified manufacturer of highly engineered industrial products serving aerospace and electronics, process flow technologies, and engineered materials markets. Crane NXT is a global leader in trusted technology solutions for payment, security, and authentication including currency, banknote, and authentication products. No public APIs or developer portals are published; integrations with industrial customers are arranged through enterprise channels.

providers.name: Crescendo Bioscience
providers.description: Crescendo Bioscience was a molecular-diagnostics company based in South San Francisco, known for Vectra DA (later Vectra), a multi-biomarker blood test that measures disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis. Backed by Kleiner Perkins and other venture investors, it was acquired by Myriad Genetics in 2014 and its diagnostic product now sits within Myriad. It has no independent public developer surface: no API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs, and its former domains no longer resolve. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Crowdamp
providers.description: Crowdamp is a privately held Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company co-founded by Ruben Mayer-Hirshfeld and Alexandra Botez. The company built SuperFan, a creator-economy messaging product that let fans text their favorite social media stars and receive a personalized reply, using natural language processing to help those creators respond efficiently at scale across their whole audience. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass Crowdamp publishes no developer surface of any kind: there is no developer portal, no documentation, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, no SDK packages in any public registry, and no working product website. The SuperFan domain superfanapp.com no longer resolves to the product and is listed for sale through a domain reseller, indicating the product is no longer operating. This profile is retained as a portfolio-graph record rather than as an API provider.

providers.name: cVidya Networks
providers.description: cVidya Networks was a provider of big-data analytics software for communications and digital service providers, best known for its MoneyMap product suite covering revenue assurance, fraud management, marketing analytics, and data monetization for telecom operators. Founded in 2000 by Alon Aginsky as an Israeli/US company, cVidya grew to roughly 300 employees and about $65M in revenue with deployments across Europe, LATAM, APAC, North America, and Africa. In January 2016 the company was acquired by Amdocs (reported at ~$30M) and absorbed into the Amdocs Revenue Guard and Business Assurance offering; cVidya no longer operates as an independent company and its cvidya.com domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record; there is no live developer portal or public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cyneta Networks
providers.description: Cyneta Networks, Inc. was a wireless data networking equipment company founded around 2000 and headquartered in Plano, Texas, with an additional presence in Cockeysville, Maryland. Backed by Battery Ventures, it developed intelligent hardware and software for wireless data networks — packet control, network element management, and network monitoring / service-quality optimization for mobile operator core networks — and accumulated a patent portfolio in wireless and core network monitoring. The company is a dot-com-era venture that no longer maintains an active public web presence: its former domain, cyneta.com, no longer serves a Cyneta site and its DNS is now operated by an unrelated party. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live developer portal, documentation, GitHub organization, package-registry libraries, or any API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record; there is nothing to catalog on the API supply side.

providers.name: Cyren Call
providers.description: Cyren Call Communications Corp. was a wireless communications company founded in 2005 by Nextel co-founder Morgan O'Brien to advocate for a nationwide public-safety broadband network. Its central proposal asked the FCC to reallocate 30 MHz of 700 MHz-band spectrum (freed by the 2009 analog-TV shutdown) to public-safety users, and it later served as advisor to the Public Safety Spectrum Trust (PSST) after PSST became the nationwide licensee for public safety's 10 MHz of 700 MHz broadband spectrum. The FCC dismissed Cyren Call's original petition as inconsistent with auction requirements, and the PSST advisory relationship ended in early 2009. The company is permanently closed. It never operated a developer program, public API, or SDK surface, so no API artifacts are available for enrichment.

providers.name: Datainsurance
providers.description: Datainsurance is an early-stage US company listed in the Anthemis Group venture portfolio under the Insurance & Risk Management thesis. Anthemis publishes no company website, logo, or description for the listing, and this enrichment pass found no live public web presence: datainsurance.com, .io, .net and .tech all resolve to parked domain-sale landers, and there is no GitHub organization or public repository under the name. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or any other API artifact could be located, so the company is carried in the API Evangelist network as an unresolved venture-portfolio lead rather than an API provider. It appears to be defunct, never publicly launched, or operating under a different brand name.

providers.name: DCP Midstream (Acquired by Phillips 66)
providers.description: DCP Midstream LLC was a Denver, Colorado-based natural gas gathering, processing, and NGL transportation company that operated as one of the largest U.S. producers and marketers of natural gas liquids. In June 2023, Phillips 66 completed the acquisition of all publicly traded common units of DCP Midstream LP for approximately $3.8 billion, taking its ownership stake to 86.8%. DCP Midstream and Phillips 66 Partners were subsequently merged into Phillips 66's NGL and midstream business; the standalone brand, public filings, developer surface, and corporate website have been retired. The dcpmidstream.com domain no longer resolves to a working site, and there is no public DCP-branded developer portal, API reference, status page, or changelog. This repository documents DCP Midstream as a defunct entity absorbed into the Phillips 66 midstream organization.

providers.name: Denbury Resources
providers.description: Denbury Resources (now Denbury Inc.) was an independent oil and natural gas company focused on enhanced oil recovery (EOR) using carbon dioxide injection in mature oil fields. Denbury was acquired by ExxonMobil in November 2023 and operates as a subsidiary inside ExxonMobil's Low Carbon Solutions business. Denbury does not publish public APIs; this profile is preserved as a corporate-history index.

providers.name: Dermira
providers.description: Dermira was a biopharmaceutical company focused on medical dermatology, developing and commercializing treatments for chronic skin conditions such as primary axillary hyperhidrosis (Qbrexza / glycopyrronium) and atopic dermatitis (lebrikizumab). Headquartered in Menlo Park, California and originally backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners, the company went public on NASDAQ (DERM) in 2014 and was acquired by Eli Lilly and Company in 2020. Its assets and operations are now part of Eli Lilly; the dermira.com domain redirects to lilly.com. Dermira did not operate a public developer program, API, or developer portal, so this profile carries company identity only and has no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Destineer
providers.description: Destineer was a networking-solutions provider for telecommunications carriers, and an early-stage Kleiner Perkins portfolio company partnered since 1995. Per Kleiner Perkins' own partnerships archive, the company was acquired by MCI WorldCom and no longer operates as an independent entity. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live web presence: destineer.com, destineer.net, destineer.dev and destineer.us all return NXDOMAIN, there is no developer portal, documentation, or GitHub organization, and the APIs.io catalog lists no APIs for this provider. Because the company predates the public web API era and is defunct, no API, specification, SDK, or agent artifacts exist to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record in the Kleiner Perkins investment graph rather than as an active API provider. Note: the unrelated video-game publisher of the same name (Minnetonka, MN, 2001-2011) and the individual github.com/destineer account are not this company.

providers.name: Dewpoint
providers.description: Dewpoint Therapeutics is a Boston-based biotechnology company, founded in 2018, that pioneers drug discovery based on biomolecular condensates — the membraneless compartments inside cells whose formation and dysregulation underlie many diseases. Its condensate platform combines cell biology, high-throughput screening, and machine learning to identify condensate-modulating drugs (c-mods) against previously undruggable targets across oncology, neurodegeneration, and virology. Dewpoint is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and completed a $150M Series C in 2022. The company operates as a therapeutics developer and, as of this profile, exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this entry captures its identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Diamond Lane
providers.description: Diamond Lane was a hardtech networking-equipment company that built DSL broadband networking equipment, backed by Kleiner Perkins and listed on the firm's partnerships page with a status of acquired. The company predates the modern web API era and no longer operates an independent commercial surface: enrichment probes in July 2026 found no reachable corporate website (diamondlane.com resolves only to a domain-for-sale parking page and diamond-lane.com to a registrar default page), no GitHub organization, no published client libraries on npm or PyPI, and no developer portal, documentation, or API of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Digit
providers.description: Digit was a consumer fintech company that built an automated personal-savings app: it analyzed a user's checking-account activity and quietly moved small, safe amounts into an FDIC-insured savings account, later expanding into automated investing and retirement (Digit Invest, Digit Retirement). Founded in 2013 in San Francisco by Ethan Bloch and backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others, Digit was acquired by Oportun in late 2021 and folded into Oportun's savings product. The standalone Digit brand is now retired: digit.co and hellodigit.com redirect to oportun.com/savings, and there is no public developer portal, documentation, or API. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead with no active developer surface.

providers.name: Diplomat Pharmacy
providers.description: Diplomat Pharmacy was an independent provider of specialty pharmacy services that helped patients with chronic and complex conditions access and manage specialty medications. The company was acquired by UnitedHealth Group's OptumRx, and operations have been integrated under that brand. No publicly documented developer APIs are offered under the Diplomat Pharmacy name.

providers.name: Doelz Networks
providers.description: Doelz Networks Inc. was a data communications networking company headquartered at 9501 Jeronimo Road, Irvine, California. It developed data communication networks designed to be independent of media, speed, attached devices, or protocols, applied across both local area networks (LANs) and wide area networks (WANs), with additional locations in Columbia, Maryland and New Jersey. The company raised roughly $16.9 million from investors including Battery Ventures, Accel, J.H. Whitney, Citi Venture Capital International and Brentwood, and was bought out by its management together with a group of European investors in 1988. The company has since been acquired and is no longer operating: enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live corporate domain, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical record of a venture-backed networking vendor and is not expected to yield API artifacts.

providers.name: Downstream Energy
providers.description: Downstream Energy is a software company that provides business-to-business electronic commerce solutions for the refined petrochemical and downstream petroleum industry, supporting the buying and selling of refined products such as gasoline, distillate, propane, and jet fuel. It is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification has been located for this provider during enrichment, so the profile remains a lightly enriched identity stub pending discovery of a public API surface.

providers.name: Drivetime
providers.description: Drivetime (Drive.fm) was a voice-activated, hands-free in-car entertainment platform founded in 2018 by Niko Vuori, Justin Cooper, and Cory Johnson (veterans of Zynga and Rocket Games). The consumer mobile app delivered interactive trivia games, storytelling, quizzes, news, and audiobooks designed to be safe to play while driving, running on Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, and partnered with the Jeopardy game show for a channel narrated by Alex Trebek. The company raised roughly $15M across seed and later rounds, with backing from Canaan Partners, Makers Fund, the Amazon Alexa Fund, Google Assistant Investments, Sinai Ventures, Fuel Capital, and Access Ventures. Drivetime was a business-to-consumer product and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; as of this profiling the drive.fm / drivetime.fm domain and the associated App Store and Google Play listings no longer resolve, indicating the product has been discontinued.

providers.name: Durata Therapeutics
providers.description: Durata Therapeutics was a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company founded in 2009 around anti-infective assets acquired from Pfizer's Vicuron division, headquartered first in Morristown, New Jersey and from 2012 in Chicago, Illinois. Its lead candidate was dalbavancin, a long-acting semisynthetic lipoglycopeptide antibiotic taken into Phase III trials from 2011 for acute bacterial skin and skin-structure infections and later marketed as Dalvance. The company was backed by Canaan Partners and was acquired by Actavis (now Allergan) on November 17, 2014 for approximately $675 million, at which point it ceased to operate as an independent entity. Durata Therapeutics published no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts; its corporate domain duratatherapeutics.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DWL
providers.description: DWL Inc. was an enterprise software company founded in 1996 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, with significant engineering and operations in Toronto, Ontario. DWL built customer data integration (CDI) middleware — its flagship product, DWL Customer, was a real-time master data hub that consolidated fragmented customer records from across banking, insurance, telecommunications, and retail systems into a single authoritative view, and served that view back to operational applications through a transaction-oriented services layer. Backed by Insight Venture Partners, AGF Investments, Nationwide Mutual Capital, Royal Trust, and Stone Point Capital, DWL was acquired by IBM in August 2005 to fill the CDI gap in IBM's information-management stack. DWL Customer was rebranded IBM WebSphere Customer Center and subsequently folded into IBM InfoSphere Master Data Management. DWL has not operated as an independent company for two decades, never published a public developer program or API, and the dwl.com domain now redirects to ibm.com. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Echelon
providers.description: Echelon Corporation was a pioneer in energy control networking and semiconductors, known for its LonWorks control networking platform and IoT edge computing products. Surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company (listed as an energy-control-networking milestone/exit), the company is no longer an independent entity — its product lines were acquired (Adesto Technologies, 2018) and now live under EnOcean. There is no live Echelon developer portal or public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Echopass
providers.description: Echopass Corporation was a cloud-based (on-demand / hosted) contact center technology company, headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area (San Ramon / Pleasanton, California) and backed by Canaan Partners among other venture investors. Its platform delivered multichannel, carrier-grade contact center and customer-interaction capabilities as a hosted service to enterprises. Echopass was acquired by Genesys in 2013 and folded into the Genesys customer-experience portfolio; it no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live developer, API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for lineage and portfolio-graph purposes rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Edge Medical
providers.description: Edge Medical is one of the fastest growing medical device distributors, operating in the healthcare sector as a portfolio company of Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). It was surfaced from the Hongshan portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The Hongshan portfolio record classifies it as a medical device distribution business rather than an API provider (is_api_provider: false); no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface has been identified for it, and no company website URL is published in the source portfolio listing. This profile remains a lead pending discovery of any first-party developer or API surface.

providers.name: Ekpa
providers.description: Ekpa is an early-stage consumer fintech from Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch, building autonomous research agents for trading. The product connects to a user's brokerage accounts through SnapTrade and consolidates accounts, positions, news, and research into a single dashboard, with AI-generated position analysis grounded in news, analyst ratings, and SEC filings. Ekpa is research-and-education only and makes no buy or sell recommendations, leaving every decision to the user. As of this profile Ekpa publishes a single marketing site at goekpa.com and exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable artifacts.

providers.name: element 5 AG
providers.description: element 5 AG was a German e-commerce and digital-distribution company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Cologne, Germany.
