It operated a platform that let software developers and publishers sell their products and licenses directly to customers online, growing to more than 10,000 clients across 150 countries and becoming one of Europe's leading software e-commerce providers. element 5 was acquired by U.S.-based Digital River (its direct competitor) for roughly $120M and subsequently absorbed and renamed Digital River GmbH, ceasing to operate as an independent company. It was an early Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company; this profile records its identity and exit. No live independent API or developer surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Eliance Corporation
providers.description: Eliance Corporation was a Minneapolis-based provider of bundled payment-processing and back-office e-commerce services that enabled online merchants to accept and process payment transactions over the Internet, lowering the barriers to entry for e-commerce. It was a portfolio company of Insight Partners and has since exited. During enrichment no active company website, developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, or documentation surface could be found, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Encoded Therapeutics
providers.description: Encoded Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing next-generation gene therapies for neurological disorders, translating precision genetic science into transformative genetic medicines. Its Genetic Medicines Product Engine supports a pipeline led by ETX101, an investigational AAV gene therapy for SCN1A-positive Dravet Syndrome, alongside additional research programs. Backed by GV, Menlo Ventures, and SoftBank Vision Fund, the company is added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences profile. As a clinical-stage therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity for the network.

providers.name: Endo Health
providers.description: Endo Health is building Glow, an AI-native clinic for women's weight loss. Describing itself as "the emotional layer of healthcare" and aiming to "make health addictive," the company treats the drivers behind symptoms rather than the symptoms alone, delivering conversational, connection-first care through a mobile health app. Its stated mission is to advance human lifespan by one year. Endo Health is backed by General Catalyst and a16z Speedrun, with teams in San Francisco and Seoul. This is a consumer digital-health product; no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface has been published at this time.

providers.name: Energen
providers.description: Energen Corporation was a U.S. oil and natural gas exploration and production company headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, with operations focused on the Permian Basin in west Texas and southeast New Mexico. In November 2018, Energen was acquired by Diamondback Energy in an all-stock transaction, and the Energen brand was retired as its assets were integrated into Diamondback. No public developer APIs are currently published; this repository preserves the corporate record.

providers.name: Energy Transfer Equity
providers.description: Energy Transfer Equity, L.P. (ETE) was a master limited partnership that owned and operated a diverse portfolio of midstream energy assets. In October 2018, ETE merged with its operating subsidiary Energy Transfer Partners (ETP) to form a single publicly traded partnership, Energy Transfer LP (NYSE: ET). All developer resources, including the Messenger+ API for pipeline messaging and gas scheduling, are now provided under the Energy Transfer LP brand.

providers.name: Envisia
providers.description: Envisia (Envisia Therapeutics, Inc.) was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, spun out of Liquidia Technologies to apply PRINT (Particle Replication In Non-wetting Templates) particle-engineering to sustained-release ophthalmic therapeutics. Its lead candidate, ENV515 (travoprost) extended-release, was an intracameral implant intended to lower intraocular pressure in glaucoma patients for months from a single administration. The company was venture-backed by Canaan Partners, New Enterprise Associates, Morningside, and Batterson Venture Capital, and was acquired by Aerie Pharmaceuticals in October 2016. As a therapeutics company it exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, and its former web domains no longer resolve; this profile is retained as a VC-portfolio lead record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: EnvoyWorldWide
providers.description: EnvoyWorldWide (Envoy WorldWide, Inc.) was a Massachusetts-based automated notification and interactive multi-channel messaging company, backed by Battery Ventures, that sold hosted alerting and customer-communication services. The company rebranded as Varolii Corporation in the mid-2000s, and the envoyworldwide.com property was retired. As of this enrichment pass the domain has no A record and its most recent archived captures show a parked "Under Construction" placeholder rather than a company site. No developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDK, package, or GitHub organization could be located on any public surface. This profile is retained as a historical network entry with no active API surface.

providers.name: Enya
providers.description: Enya is a Singapore-based sustainable period-care consumer brand backed by 500 Global (500 Southeast Asia) and Crusade Partners. Founded by Christian Teo, Enya sells certified organic cotton sanitary pads, liners, tampons, menstrual cups, period underwear and heating patches direct-to-consumer and via subscription (15/30/45/90-day cadence) across Singapore, Asia and the Middle East, through its enya.sg storefront, Shopee and retail partners such as DKSH. It is a consumer packaged-goods / e-commerce business with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: Eon Laboratories
providers.description: Eon Laboratories is a pharmaceutical manufacturer that develops, manufactures, and markets a broad range of generic pharmaceutical products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a generic-drug maker rather than a software or API producer, Eon Laboratories publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts. The record will be revisited if the company later exposes a developer or partner API surface.

providers.name: Equipe Communications
providers.description: Équipe Communications Corporation was an Acton, Massachusetts telecommunications equipment startup established in 1999 by a group of telecom industry veterans. It designed, manufactured, and sold data network switching equipment for large-scale facilities-based carriers and service providers — Incumbent Local Exchange Carriers (ILECs), Inter Exchange Carriers (IXCs), and international carriers. Its product line comprised the Équipe 3200 Multiservice ATM/MPLS Core Data Switch, Évail System Software, ÉvailNet Manager, and Élite LifeCycle service and support. The positioning was to let carriers scale an existing ATM core network while offering a gradual, low-risk transition path to MPLS. The company raised a $40 million third round in March 2002, was awarded the first of 74 patents in February 2002, earned ISO 9001:2000 certification from TÜV Management Service in February 2002, signed a sales agent/reseller agreement with Ciena in June 2002 and a services master agreement with Fujitsu in August 2002, and achieved NEBS certification for the É3200 in January 2003. Équipe was a carrier-hardware vendor of the pre-API era: it never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface. This profile is retained as a historical record of the Battery Ventures portfolio and is not an active API provider. NOTE: unrelated to equipe.com, a Swedish equestrian show-management software company (see x-disambiguation).

providers.name: Estes Energy
providers.description: Estes Energy is a US-based manufacturer of advanced battery packs for heavy-duty transport. Its magnesium-alloy Magnus platform (proprietary MgCarbonit thermo-structural body) delivers roughly 225 Wh/kg for rail, marine, aviation and off-highway applications, with chemistry-agnostic (sodium, LFP, nickel) packs manufactured entirely in the United States. Backed by DCVC, Fortescue Ventures, BMW and New System Ventures. A hardware/manufacturing company with no public API, developer portal, SDK or software product surface at this time.

providers.name: EuSmart
providers.description: EuSmart is a London, UK based company developing a new form of pan-European internet service provider (ISP), backed by Insight Partners and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector portfolio lead. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification has been located to date, so this profile remains a stub awaiting a real API surface before artifact enrichment can proceed.

providers.name: Evalve
providers.description: Evalve, Inc. was a medical-device company that pioneered percutaneous (catheter-based) mitral valve repair with its MitraClip system for treating mitral regurgitation. It was acquired by Abbott Laboratories in 2009 (~$410M) and folded into Abbott Structural Heart / Abbott Vascular; MitraClip is now an Abbott product. Evalve does not exist as an independent operating company and publishes no developer program, public API, SDKs, or developer documentation. The former evalve.com domain is a parked, for-sale page. Surfaced here as a kleiner-perkins portfolio lead, this is a non-API, defunct/acquired entity with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: Evariant
providers.description: Evariant was a healthcare customer relationship management (CRM) software company founded in 2008, offering a Salesforce-aligned platform for health systems covering consumer/patient engagement, physician relationship management, marketing planning, appointment reminders, and service-line growth analytics. Evariant was acquired by Healthgrades in January 2020 and fully absorbed into "Evariant, a Healthgrades company"; the independent product and brand were retired. As of this enrichment pass the former evariant.com domain 301-redirects to a parked GoDaddy marketplace page, and Evariant publishes no independent public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Exonic
providers.description: Exonic is an AI-driven biotechnology company building artificial intelligence for precision gene therapy. The company applies machine learning to the design and development of therapeutic gene treatments, operating in the therapeutics and life-sciences space rather than as a developer-facing API provider. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Exonic publishes a company/marketing website (exonic.ai) but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal were found, so no API artifacts were generated (no fabrication).

providers.name: Fincentric
providers.description: Fincentric Corporation was a Canadian core retail and wealth banking software vendor founded in 1984 and headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia. It provided account processing, core banking, and wealth management technology to credit unions and financial institutions, serving roughly 167 clients worldwide and claiming a large share of Canada's top credit unions. Backed by Battery Ventures alongside BancBoston Ventures, HarbourVest Partners, Shasta Ventures, and Ventures West Capital, the company was acquired by US core-banking vendor Open Solutions in May 2007; Open Solutions was itself acquired by Fiserv in 2013. Fincentric no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct entry — there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: FirstFuel Software
providers.description: FirstFuel Software was a business-focused energy analytics SaaS company that used utility meter and building data to profile commercial and industrial customers, helping utilities target energy-efficiency and customer-engagement programs. The company was acquired by Uplight, and the firstfuel.com domain now redirects to uplight.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. The enrichment pipeline found no active first-party developer surface (no developer, api, or docs subdomains resolve, and no OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP artifacts are published), so this profile remains an identity-only record for a company that no longer operates a standalone API program.

providers.name: Flexus Biosciences
providers.description: Flexus Biosciences was a South San Francisco / San Carlos, California biotechnology company founded in 2013 to develop small-molecule cancer immunotherapies, most notably inhibitors of the IDO/TDO immunosuppressive pathway (lead IDO1 program F001287). Backed by Kleiner Perkins and The Column Group, it was acquired by Bristol-Myers Squibb in February 2015 for up to roughly $1.25 billion (about $800M upfront) to expand BMS's immuno-oncology pipeline. The company no longer operates independently; its domain redirects to the Bristol-Myers Squibb acquisition announcement. It publishes no public developer portal, documentation, or API, so this profile carries company identity only and no technical API artifacts.

providers.name: Focal Communications
providers.description: Focal Communications Corporation was a Chicago-based competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) founded in 1996 that provided switched local phone and data services to large, communications-intensive business customers in Tier I US markets. Backed by Battery Ventures, Madison Dearborn and Frontenac, it went public in 1998, filed Chapter 11 in December 2002, emerged from reorganization in July 2003, and was acquired by Corvis Communications (later Broadwing) in 2004. The company is defunct and operates no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this network profile is a historical stub and no live API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: FORE Systems
providers.description: FORE Systems, Inc. was a computer network switching equipment company based in Warrendale (Pittsburgh), Pennsylvania, founded in 1990 by Carnegie Mellon researchers Francois Bitz, Onat Menzilcioglu, Robert Sansom and Eric Cooper (the "FORE" acronym) to build Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) network interface cards and switches. It was the first company to commercially ship an ATM switch (the ASX-100) in 1992 and grew through acquisitions (ALANTEC, Applied Network Technology, RainbowBridge, CellAccess) before being acquired by Britain's General Electric Company (GEC) in 1999, folded into Marconi, and ultimately absorbed by Ericsson in 2006. The company is defunct and has no active API surface, developer portal, or product endpoints; this profile is a historical/company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Forty Seven 2
providers.description: Forty Seven, Inc. was a clinical-stage immuno-oncology biopharmaceutical company developing therapies that target cancer immune-evasion pathways, based on technology licensed from Stanford University. Its lead program, magrolimab, was a monoclonal antibody against the CD47 "don't eat me" signal, evaluated in myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and solid tumors. Seeded by Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2015, the company completed an IPO in 2018 and was acquired by Gilead Sciences in 2020 for approximately $4.9 billion, becoming a wholly-owned Gilead subsidiary. As a therapeutics developer it exposes no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface; its former site (fortyseveninc.com) now redirects to gilead.com.

providers.name: Function Oncology
providers.description: Function Oncology is a precision oncology company applying single-cell CRISPR functional genomics to map cancer dependencies and identify and validate new therapeutic targets. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Bio + Health, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub for enrichment. As of this pass the company publishes no live public website, developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs — the primary domain resolves to Google Workspace mail records only with no web A record — so no API artifacts could be searched, fetched, or derived. This profile carries identity metadata only until a public developer surface appears.

providers.name: Gainspeed
providers.description: Gainspeed, Inc. was a Sunnyvale, California networking startup that developed a Virtual Converged Cable Access Platform (Virtual CCAP) built on a Distributed Access Architecture (Remote PHY / DAA) for cable multiple-system operators (MSOs). The company was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was acquired by Nokia in 2016, after which its virtual CCAP technology was folded into Nokia's cable access portfolio. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Gainspeed operated no public developer program, API, or live developer portal; its domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: gammastar
providers.description: GammaStar (GammaStar Medical Group) is a Shanghai-based medical-device company backed by Qiming Venture Partners that develops, manufactures, and services precision radiotherapy and oncotherapy equipment, including rotary cobalt-60 gamma-ray radiosurgery systems, and operates a network of oncotherapy and psychosurgery centers. It is a medical-hardware manufacturer rather than an API provider; enrichment found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface, and the gammastar.com domain currently resolves to a parked "for sale" listing on Atom.com rather than a corporate site.

providers.name: gaugene
providers.description: Gaugene (Beijing Zhizhen Biotechnology Co., Ltd. / 知真生物), founded in 2017 and headquartered in Beijing, China, develops and supplies flow cytometry instruments and reagents for the in-vitro diagnostics and life-sciences research market. Its analyzers use high-power lasers and high-sensitivity multi-color fluorescence detection for clinical hematology diagnosis, single-cell analysis, protein screening, and clinical-indicator discovery. Gaugene is a venture-backed diagnostics-hardware and reagents maker rather than an API provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no reachable public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface (its apex domain does not resolve and www.gaugene.com returns a 502). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub via Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Genomic Health
providers.description: Genomic Health, Inc. was a Redwood City, California molecular diagnostics company founded in 2000 and known for its Oncotype DX suite of genomic tests, which analyze tumor gene-expression to guide treatment decisions in breast, colon, and prostate cancer. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, it went public in 2005 and was acquired by Exact Sciences in November 2019. It no longer operates as an independent company: the genomichealth.com domain now 301-redirects to exactsciences.com, and there is no independent Genomic Health developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This record is retained as a VC-portfolio lead; no live API artifacts could be enriched.

providers.name: Getsupp
providers.description: Getsupp was an India-based digital health and wellness platform offering supplement and nutrition product discovery, personalized health recommendations, and online consultations with certified experts (nutritionists, dietitians, and coaches). The company was a General Catalyst portfolio company and was subsequently absorbed into Eka.care. As of this enrichment pass the getsupp.in and getsupp.com domains no longer serve a standalone site: both resolve to Eka.io infrastructure (65.0.57.69, TLS cert altnames *.eka.io) and return HTTP 404 for all paths. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, /.well-known/ discovery, or /llms.txt could be found. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: Giftcard Zen
providers.description: Giftcard Zen was a secondary gift-card marketplace founded in 2012 by Aaron Dragushan in Phoenix, Arizona, that let consumers sell unwanted gift cards for cash and buy discounted gift cards from retailers such as Target, Home Depot, Lowe's, Walmart and Best Buy. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by RetailMeNot in April 2016 for roughly $22 million in cash (plus an earnout) and folded into RetailMeNot's digital savings platform. The giftcardzen.com domain no longer operates as an independent service and redirects to RetailMeNot; the company exposes no public developer or API surface. This profile is retained for network provenance.

providers.name: Gixo
providers.description: Gixo was a consumer live-streaming fitness startup (coached, real-time running and workout classes delivered to a mobile app), surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. The enrichment pipeline probed the company on 2026-07-19 and found no live provider surface: gixo.com and www.gixo.com both HTTP 301-redirect to www.bodi.com (a Beachbody / BODi property), consistent with Gixo having been acquired and wound down into the Openfit / Beachbody / BODi fitness platform. No api.gixo.com or developer.gixo.com host resolves in DNS, and no /.well-known/ discovery surface, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or public API is published. There is no API program to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical consumer-sector lead rather than an active provider.

providers.name: GlobalCare Inc.
providers.description: GlobalCare Inc. was a healthcare technology company founded in 1994 and based in Portland, Oregon, that provided solutions enabling healthcare payers to significantly reduce the cost of out-of-network claims. Backed by an investor group led by Insight Venture Partners (Series A Preferred Stock), GlobalCare merged into Zelis Healthcare in January 2016 and no longer operates as an independent entity. Its out-of-network claims-pricing capabilities are now delivered through Zelis. GlobalCare Inc. itself publishes no independent developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; any current API surface is Zelis's (developer.zelis.com), tracked separately in the network.

providers.name: Govlist
providers.description: Govlist, Inc. (which operated as ProcureNow) was a San Francisco-based govtech startup providing a multi-tenant SaaS platform for government procurement and contract management. Its Government Procurement Automation Cloud helped local and state agencies build, source, and evaluate RFPs and bids, and helped suppliers read, understand, and respond to complex public solicitations. The company, backed by 500 Global and Civstart, was acquired by OpenGov in 2021 (announced June 2021), where the product now lives as OpenGov Procurement. Govlist has no independent developer surface, API, or portal; its original domain (thegovlist.com) no longer resolves. This profile is preserved as a historical lead surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio.

providers.name: GridBank
providers.description: GridBank is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: energy. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Halda Therapeutics
providers.description: Halda Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company and Yale University spinout developing oral, targeted cancer therapies built on its proprietary RIPTAC (Regulated Induced Proximity TArgeting Chimera) platform, a novel "hold and kill" modality for the precision treatment of solid tumors. Its lead program, HLD-0915, is a first-in-class oral RIPTAC therapeutic in development for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), with earlier-stage candidates spanning breast, lung, and other tumor types. Backed by investors including Canaan Partners, Halda was acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2025 for approximately $3.05 billion in cash, with its platform folded into Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine's oncology pipeline. As a therapeutics developer, Halda operated no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity and portfolio-graph record rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Harvest Platform
providers.description: Harvest Platform was a New York City fintech startup founded in 2017 by Gabriel DellAccio and Namrata Baral that built a consumer investing and banking app. Its signature feature used artificial intelligence to identify negotiable bank fees and automatically negotiate refunds with major U.S. banks, later expanding into micro-investing, round-ups, cashback rewards, and savings tooling. The company was backed by Techstars and Financial Venture Studio, raising roughly $3.3M in seed funding. Its domain growmyharvest.com now 302-redirects to Acorns (acorns.com), consistent with reporting that Harvest Platform was acquired by Acorns in 2021. Harvest Platform was a consumer-facing mobile product and never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so it carries no technical API artifacts.

providers.name: Health IQ
providers.description: Health IQ was a venture-backed insurtech founded in 2013 in Mountain View, California that offered lower-cost life insurance to health-conscious individuals, later pivoting in 2019 to selling Medicare Advantage plans to seniors. Backed by a16z and others (~$200M raised), the company laid off staff in December 2022 and filed for Chapter 7 liquidation on August 30, 2023. As of this enrichment pass the healthiq.com domain resolves to a parked "domain may be for sale" page, and the company operates no public website, developer portal, or API. Retained in the network as a defunct a16z portfolio lead with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: Healthmode
providers.description: HealthMode was a machine-learning digital medicine company, founded in 2017 in San Francisco by Bradford Cross and Dan Karlin, that developed AI-enabled digital measurement methods to increase the precision and speed of clinical research. Its techniques improved phenotype understanding, streamlined screening and eligibility, enabled early detection of adverse events, and provided objective, low-burden efficacy endpoints for next-generation clinical trials. HealthMode was acquired by MindMed in 2021 and folded into MindMed's digital-medicine division (Albert); it no longer operates as an independent company, maintains no standalone website or public developer/API surface, and none of its former domains resolve.

providers.name: Healthvision
providers.description: Healthvision was a healthcare-IT software and services company based in Irving, Texas, that provided access to healthcare information to improve clinical and financial outcomes for public and private healthcare organizations. It was formed in 2007 through Battery Ventures' take-private acquisition of Quovadx (NASDAQ QVDX) and its Integration Solutions Division, and was subsequently acquired by Lawson Software (now part of Infor). The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Heartstream
providers.description: Heartstream is an emergency-care and defibrillation brand, now part of Philips, that makes automated external defibrillators (AEDs) and professional monitor/defibrillators for public-access, home, and EMS use. The company originated as a Mayfield-backed medical-device startup that pioneered automatic external defibrillators and was later acquired by Hewlett-Packard; today the Heartstream name lives on across the HeartStart AED and Tempus ALS product lines sold in more than 50 countries and regions. Its public site publishes product support, a document center (instructions for use), and a newsroom, but it exposes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: HilleVax
providers.description: HilleVax was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing novel vaccines, most notably HIL-214, a virus-like-particle based vaccine candidate aimed at preventing moderate-to-severe acute gastroenteritis caused by norovirus infection. The company was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. Enrichment probing found no developer program, no API, no developer portal, and no public API documentation of any kind, which is expected for a clinical-stage vaccine developer rather than a technology/API producer. The company's primary domain (hillevax.com) now redirects to xoma.com (XOMA Royalty), indicating HilleVax has been acquired and wound down as an independent operating company; XOMA Royalty itself was subsequently acquired by Ligand (closed July 2026). This profile is retained as a company/identity record with no API surface.

providers.name: Hinsta
providers.description: Hintsa Performance is a Finnish performance-coaching company founded by Dr. Aki Hintsa, applying methods developed over 30+ years working with Formula 1 drivers and elite athletes to help executives, leaders, and individuals achieve sustainable success. Its "Circle of Better Life" model combines Nordic wellbeing with performance principles proven in Formula 1, delivered as bespoke coaching programs across three segments (sports, businesses, and individuals). The company reports 3,500+ intensive executive coaching programmes delivered for 500+ organisations. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or discovery surface (.well-known, llms.txt) was found during enrichment — this is a non-API wellbeing/coaching business.

providers.name: HNC
providers.description: HNC Software Inc. was a San Diego-based predictive-software company founded in 1986 that built neural-network and decision-management systems for credit-card and workers-compensation fraud detection, customer analytics, and profitability management across financial services, insurance, telecommunications, and retail. Its flagship Falcon product screened a large share of the world's payment-card transactions for fraud. HNC was an early Battery Ventures investment, went public in 1995, and was acquired by Fair Isaac (FICO) in May 2002; it no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no current developer or API surface.

providers.name: Huon Holdings
providers.description: Huon Holdings was a provider of software and implementation administrative solutions for major international insurers, primarily in the property and casualty (P&C) insurance sector. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no live company website, developer portal, API documentation, or any public developer surface for Huon Holdings (Insight Partners lists it with is_api_provider=false and no URL, and its portfolio description is written in the past tense), so no API artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived without fabrication. This record remains an identity-only stub.

providers.name: i-Incubator Healthcare
providers.description: i-Incubator Healthcare is a pharmaceutical innovation incubator established by IDG Capital and officially launched in Shanghai (Xuhui District) in 2024. It operates an "incubation + empowerment" model to develop innovative drug-research programs across oncology, immunology, and metabolic disease areas, pairing global innovation perspectives with China-based execution to advance projects to international quality standards. It is backed by a dedicated, long-horizon (15-year) incubation fund. Surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital; this is a research/biotech venture with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: IDEC Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: IDEC Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: IDI Insurance
providers.description: IDI Insurance is an insurance provider that appears on Battery Ventures' portfolio company list (recorded there as acquired) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal could be located for the company, and the source portfolio data marks it is_api_provider false, so no API artifacts have been captured. This profile remains a lead pending the discovery of a public API surface.

providers.name: iGrow
providers.description: iGrow is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Ikigai
providers.description: Ikigai is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Illuminet
providers.description: Illuminet, located in Seattle, Washington, provides advanced intelligent network, database, and billing services to the telecommunications industry. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass no live public web or API surface could be located (illuminet.com is a parked/for-sale domain, illuminet.io does not resolve, and the Insight Partners portfolio page carries no descriptive content), so this profile remains a company record with no developer or API artifacts.

providers.name: immune-path
providers.description: Immune-Path (Yidao Biotechnology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. / 怡道生物) is a China-based vaccine biotechnology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Suzhou. The company develops human vaccines across recombinant protein antigen, novel viral vector, and messenger RNA (mRNA) platforms, backed by its own vaccine adjuvant technology. Its clinical and preclinical pipeline includes a recombinant zoster (shingles) vaccine produced in CHO cells, a nine-valent recombinant HPV vaccine expressed in Pichia pastoris, a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine, a therapeutic gastric cancer vaccine, and a COVID-19 vaccine. Immune-Path is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It is a life-sciences drug developer with no public developer, API, or software surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Immunicon
providers.description: Immunicon Corporation (NASDAQ IMMC) was a Huntingdon Valley, Pennsylvania biotechnology company that pioneered immunomagnetic cell-selection technology for isolating and characterizing rare circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from blood. It developed the CellSearch and CellTracks diagnostic platforms, licensed to Veridex, LLC (a Johnson & Johnson company) for oncology use. Immunicon filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2008 and was acquired by Veridex/Johnson & Johnson; the CellSearch platform later passed to Menarini Silicon Biosystems. The company was backed by Canaan Partners and publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: In Charge One, Inc.
providers.description: In Charge One, Inc. is a hardware startup behind "Socket to Pocket," a paid charging system for electronic devices in public spaces. The device lets visitors charge smartphones, laptops, drones, e-bikes, and scooters at cafes, shops, clinics, stadiums, airports, and other venues by tapping a card and paying for access, while venue owners monetize the outlet and earn a commission per plugged socket. It ships in wall-mounted, extension-cord, and anti-vandal street versions. Founded in 2023 by Danylo (Daniel) Tonkopii, co-founder of Delfast electric bikes, and Andriy Zinchuk, the company is based in Los Angeles, California and was developed by Ukrainian engineers. It is a consumer/commercial hardware and payments business, not an API provider: no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface has been published, and its incharge.one domain is currently non-resolving and in registrar redemption/pending-delete status. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is retained as an identity record.

providers.name: In-Fusio
providers.description: In-Fusio was a mobile entertainment company founded in 1998 in Bordeaux (Merignac), France, and one of the pioneers of the mobile games industry. In September 2000 it launched ExEn (Execution Engine), the first Java-based game engine dedicated entirely to mobile devices, competing with Sun Microsystems' J2ME, and partnered with Motorola on a client-side mobile gaming API for faster action and richer graphics. The company published games and community services across more than 70 wireless carriers and 140 handsets worldwide, with distribution deals including Verizon, Sprint, AT&T, Vodafone, Orange, Telefonica Moviles and China Mobile. It split its publishing and distribution divisions in January 2006, was acquired by Zenops in May 2007, entered administration in 2008, and went into compulsory liquidation in 2009. In-Fusio is recorded in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio company of Insight Partners; it operates no active developer platform or public API today.

providers.name: inbilin
providers.description: inbilin was a Shanghai-based social networking mobile app founded in 2013 that let users place voice calls to strangers, either dialing a person of interest or being paired at random for a live conversation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Public company databases (Crunchbase, CB Insights, Tracxn) record inbilin as permanently closed / deadpooled; the inbilin.com domain no longer resolves to a live site and no developer program, documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or public API surface could be located during enrichment.

providers.name: Informatics
providers.description: Informatics encompasses the science of information and computation, including bioinformatics, health informatics, clinical informatics, and computational biology. This index is a topic-level placeholder for cataloging APIs and services across informatics tools, data management, and analytical capabilities for research and healthcare applications.

providers.name: Instinct Xyz
providers.description: Instinct (instinct.xyz) is a Y Combinator-backed trading platform operating under the tagline "Trade your instinct." As of this profile the product is pre-launch — the public site shows a "Coming Soon" landing page with no live product, developer program, API, or documentation yet published. Contact is hello@instinct.xyz and the company is active on X as @instinct_xyz. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the Y Combinator portfolio and is a lead awaiting a public API surface before the enrichment pipeline can capture specs and artifacts.

providers.name: Intellicare
providers.description: IntelliCare, Inc. was a specialty healthcare services and application software company founded in 1997 and headquartered in South Portland, Maine. It provided medical contact center outsourcing services and technology products, delivering telephone-based (telephonic) nurse triage and clinical decision-support services to health plans, providers, payors, self-insured employers, hospitals, and health management organizations. IntelliCare was a portfolio company of Canaan Partners (with Liberty Medical and Cutlass Capital) and was acquired by PolyMedica Corporation in 2005. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface; its former intellicare.com domain is parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Intersect ENT
providers.description: Intersect ENT was a medical device company based in Menlo Park, California that developed drug-eluting, bioresorbable sinus implants for patients with chronic rhinosinusitis. Its PROPEL family of steroid-eluting implants maintains sinus patency and delivers localized mometasone furoate to the sinus mucosa following endoscopic sinus surgery, while its SINUVA implant treats recurrent nasal polyps in an in-office setting. Formerly publicly traded on NASDAQ under the ticker XENT, Intersect ENT was acquired by Medtronic in May 2022 and its PROPEL and SINUVA product lines are now sold as part of Medtronic's ear, nose, and throat (ENT) portfolio. The company is a physical medical-device manufacturer and operates no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Intersect ENT
providers.description: Intersect ENT (the "Intersectent" stub) was a Menlo Park, California medical-device company that developed steroid-releasing dissolvable sinus implants — the PROPEL and PROPEL mini families and the SINUVA implant — to improve outcomes for chronic sinusitis and ear, nose and throat surgery. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners (Series D lead), Kleiner Perkins, U.S. Venture Partners and Medtronic, it went public and was acquired by Medtronic on 2022-05-13 for roughly $1.1B, with the FTC-mandated divestiture of its Fiagon products. It is a physical medical-device business with no developer platform, public API, SDK, or developer portal; intersectent.com now redirects to Medtronic's PROPEL product page. This record is retained for lineage from the Norwest portfolio harvest and is not an API provider.

providers.name: Intucell
providers.description: Intucell was an Israeli self-optimizing network (SON) software company headquartered in Ra'anana, Israel, whose platform let mobile carriers automatically plan, configure, manage, optimize and heal cellular radio access networks in real time as network demand changed. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners on roughly $6M raised, Intucell was acquired by Cisco Systems for approximately $475M in a deal completed February 25, 2013, and its SON technology was folded into Cisco's mobility and service-provider portfolio (later divested to HCL). The company operates no standalone public developer program or API today; this profile is retained as an acquired-company / VC-portfolio record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ivella
providers.description: Ivella was a consumer fintech company that built shared money-management and multi-account banking tools aimed at couples and households, backed by the fintech venture firm Anthemis. As of 2026 Ivella's products have been sunset and the team has joined EarnIn to continue building. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an Anthemis portfolio-company lead; the enrichment pipeline found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface, and the company is no longer operating as an independent product.

providers.name: Jambo
providers.description: Jambo is a mobile infrastructure company bringing blockchain and decentralized finance to mainstream users across emerging markets, led by its JamboPhone, a low-cost Web3-enabled Android smartphone with a built-in multi-chain wallet, hardware security, and biometric authentication. The Jambo ecosystem spans JamboWallet (a native multi-chain crypto wallet), JamboEarn (a gamified quest and rewards platform), and JamboPlay (a decentralized app store for games and digital experiences), plus the Jarvis product. The company reports 11M+ active wallets, over 1 million JamboPhones sold across 128+ countries, and 60+ ecosystem partners including Coinbase, Solana, Tether, and OKX. Jambo raised a $30M Series A led by Paradigm with participation from Pantera Capital and others. Sector: crypto. As of this profile Jambo publishes a consumer product and whitepaper surface but no public developer/API, SDK, or documentation program.

providers.name: Jungla
providers.description: Jungla, Inc. was a San Francisco precision-medicine informatics startup founded in 2016 by Alexander Colavin and Carlos Araya. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and IndieBio, it built a cloud-based Functional Modeling Platform (FMP), also described as a Molecular Evidence Platform, that combined functional genomics, computational biophysics, cellular engineering, and machine learning to produce auditable predictive models for clinical genetic and genomic variant interpretation. Jungla emerged from stealth in 2018 and was acquired by Invitae Corporation in July 2019 (approximately $59M), where its technology augmented Invitae's Sherloc variant-classification approach. The company is now defunct; its original developer surface (jungla.io) is offline and no public API, documentation, or SDKs survive. This profile is a historical record surfaced from the a16z portfolio; it carries no live developer artifacts.

providers.name: Justinian
providers.description: Justinian is an applied AI company, backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026), building what it calls the first AI-native government affairs firm. Founded by Parth Badhwar (previously Clipbook, The White House, Deloitte's policy team, and the Harris campaign), Justinian helps early-stage companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts. The firm operates from San Francisco and Washington, DC, pairing staff drawn from the White House and top lobbying firms with engineering, and frames its mission as rebuilding public-private partnerships in America. Justinian currently presents as a services and product company with a demo-request/contact flow; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: justmedical
providers.description: JUST Medical Devices (Tianjin) Co., Ltd. (嘉思特医疗器材（天津）股份有限公司) is a Chinese orthopedic medical device manufacturer based in Tianjin, China, and a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company designs and produces joint replacement implants and orthopedic prosthetics, applying 3D printing and additive manufacturing to hip, knee, and other joint reconstruction systems. Its public presence at justmedical.cn is a corporate marketing website (built on the Faisco/fkw.com site builder); the company publishes no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider entry.

providers.name: Kabbage
providers.description: Kabbage was an Atlanta-based financial technology company (founded 2009) that pioneered fully automated, data-driven cash-flow lending to small businesses, offering flexible lines of credit, online bill payment, cash-flow visualization, and business checking. It exposed a B2B "Kabbage Platform" lending-as-a-service API (formerly documented at kabbageplatform.com) and was backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. American Express announced its acquisition of substantially all of Kabbage in August 2020; the products were folded into American Express Business Blueprint and the standalone Kabbage developer platform was discontinued. As of this enrichment pass no independent Kabbage public API, developer portal, or specification is reachable — kabbage.com redirects to americanexpress.com/business/blueprint and the former developer hosts no longer resolve.

providers.name: Kalto
providers.description: Kalto was a B2B payments and financing platform headquartered in Mexico City, founded in 2021 and seed-backed by QED Investors. It offered an all-in-one B2B checkout for merchants, distributors, wholesalers, and marketplaces, accepting bank transfers, credit and debit cards, and cash, with an integrated financing product that let merchants extend net payment terms (15/30/45 days) to their business buyers. In April 2025 Kalto was acquired by Tiendanube (Nuvemshop) to power "Pago Nube," a native embedded checkout and financial-services experience for Tiendanube merchants in Mexico. As of this profile the standalone kalto.la domain no longer resolves to a company site (it redirects to unrelated parked pages) and Kalto publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI, so there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Kanghui Medical
providers.description: Kanghui Medical (Changzhou Kanghui Medical Innovation Co., Ltd.), founded in 1997 and headquartered in Changzhou, Jiangsu Province, China, is an orthopedic medical device manufacturer focused on the R&D and production of trauma and spine implants and instruments, plus professional surgical education and services across China and emerging markets. Formerly China Kanghui Holdings (NYSE: KH), it was acquired by Medtronic in 2012 and now operates as a Medtronic company. This is a corporate/physical-device provider with a public marketing website but no public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface; the profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Kelun-Biotech
providers.description: Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Kelun Botai, HKEX: 6990), a Chengdu-based subsidiary of Sichuan Kelun Pharmaceutical (SZSE: 002422) established in 2016, is an innovative biopharmaceutical company focused on the research, development, manufacturing, and commercialization of novel drugs. It specializes in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and other conjugated therapies across both large-molecule and small-molecule modalities, targeting oncology and autoimmune diseases. The company operates several core drug-discovery platforms and maintains a pipeline of 30+ candidates with multiple approved and clinical-stage programs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network; as a pharmaceutical manufacturer it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Kerros Health
providers.description: Kerros Health (Kerros) was a digital mental-health and wellness startup building clinically validated, mobile-based programs proven to improve mental health, positioned as an evidence-based consumer brand modernizing established treatments through mobile technology and design. The product began as a teen-created mental-health app (originating out of Scarsdale High School) and grew largely through word of mouth. Co-founded by Justin Ip and backed by Cowboy Ventures at the seed stage, the company has since exited. It was a consumer mobile app with no public developer/API surface; this API Evangelist profile is maintained as a portfolio-lead record and no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation could be found during enrichment.

providers.name: Kespry
providers.description: Kespry was an industrial drone and aerial-intelligence company founded in the San Francisco Bay Area that paired automated fixed-perimeter drones with a cloud analytics platform to turn aerial imagery into measurable data. Its product was used for stockpile and inventory volumetrics in mining and aggregates, construction-site progress monitoring and earthworks, and insurance roof inspection. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Kespry was acquired by Firmatek in 2020 and the brand has since been retired; the former developer and marketing domain kespry.com now issues a 301 redirect to firmatek.com. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for lineage and portfolio mapping, but Kespry publishes no live, standalone developer surface, API, documentation, or client SDKs of its own.

providers.name: Kiira
providers.description: Kiira (Kiira Health) was a student-focused digital health / telehealth platform that partnered with colleges and universities to bridge the gap between students and clinicians, providing online visits with doctors, nurses, and therapists, primary care and gynecological consultations, mental health support, and health literacy workshops and education resources through a patient booking portal. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this pass the company operated a consumer/patient web app only and published no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal, so there is no API surface to enrich. Its recorded domain kiira.io is no longer controlled by the company — it now redirects to an unrelated third-party site — so this profile reflects the company's last-known (archived, Dec 2024) state and is treated as a defunct / lapsed lead.

providers.name: Klir
providers.description: Klir provides an integrated water regulatory solution — software for water and wastewater utilities to manage regulatory compliance, environmental monitoring data, permits, sampling and reporting obligations in one system. Klir was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public developer surface — APIs, documentation, SDKs and specifications — has not yet been verified, so this profile carries identity only and no API or artifact claims until a research pass confirms them.

providers.name: Koffie Financial
providers.description: Koffie Financial (originally Koffie Labs) was a New York based insurtech managing general agency selling commercial trucking insurance to fleets, brokers and agents. Founded by co-founder and CEO Ian White and co-founder and COO Michael Dorfman, it paired telematics driven underwriting with digital policy servicing, partnering with Samsara on fleet safety data, Sutton National and Boost on underwriting capacity, and Snapsheet on claims. It raised a 4.5 million dollar seed in 2021 and an 11 million dollar Series A in 2022 led by Anthemis Group, rebranded from Koffie Labs to Koffie Financial, launched the Koffie Card, and was licensed in states including New York, Georgia, Florida and Tennessee. The company never published a public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs; its only machine surfaces were private broker and fleet portals. As of July 2026 its web presence is retired.

providers.name: Latitude Communications
providers.description: Latitude Communications, Inc. was a Santa Clara, California enterprise conferencing company, incorporated in April 1993 and venture-backed by Mayfield Fund, Menlo Ventures, Asset Management Associates, and Canaan Ventures (Canaan Partners). It developed, sold, and hosted MeetingPlace, an integrated voice and web conferencing system for geographically dispersed enterprises, first shipped commercially in December 1994 and sold to more than 430 enterprise customers by the end of 2002, including Aetna, Cisco, Credit Suisse First Boston, Fidelity Investments, Lockheed Martin, Oracle, and the U.S. Federal Reserve Bank. The company IPO'd on the Nasdaq National Market under the symbol LATD at $12.00 per share in May 1999 and reported revenue of $43.4 million in 2000, $33.9 million in 2001, and $40.5 million in 2002. Cisco Systems acquired Latitude in a cash merger at $3.95 per share, completed in late 2003; Latitude filed a Form 15 terminating its SEC registration on 2004-01-13, and MeetingPlace was absorbed into Cisco's conferencing line as Cisco Unified MeetingPlace. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface — its 10-K describes only internally developed APIs used to integrate MeetingPlace with web, e-mail, and fax servers. This profile is retained as a historical record of the Canaan Partners portfolio and is not an active API provider. NOTE: unrelated to the present-day latitude.sh bare-metal cloud provider and to the parked latitude.com page (see x-disambiguation).

providers.name: Legit Patents
providers.description: Legit (listed by Seedcamp as "Legit Patents", 2016 cohort, legit.ai) was a Cambridge, Massachusetts startup applying natural-language processing to scientific and patent literature, which it developed into an on-demand expert network for the life sciences. Its product let pharmaceutical, biotech and medical-device teams search a corpus the company described as more than two million experts backed by roughly forty million data points, then pay a flat fee per reply to message key opinion leaders directly instead of scheduling calls — marketed for R&D, business development and licensing (BD&L), strategic alliances and integration management. The company is no longer operating: substantive legit.ai content disappears from the web archive after 2021, its LinkedIn company page returns HTTP 404, and the legit.ai domain is now parked on GoDaddy/Afternic and listed for sale (Afternic nameservers, a null MX record and an SPF "-all" policy). No public API, developer portal, documentation or machine-readable specification was ever published; see review.yml for the full probe record.

providers.name: LifeMed Media
providers.description: LifeMed Media was a consumer health media company that operated dLife, a diabetes-focused media brand spanning dLife.com, the dLifeTV television program, the dLife Foundation, a diabetes retail store, and a section for healthcare professionals. Its editorial surface covered type 1, type 2, gestational and pre-diabetes, blood sugar management, insulin, complications, nutrition and recipes, and diabetes lifestyle content, monetized through sponsored sections from device and pharmaceutical advertisers. The company was venture backed by Battery Ventures. As of a 2026-07-19 verification pass the business appears defunct: its corporate domain lifemedmedia.com is parked for sale on HugeDomains and dlife.com no longer resolves. No developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface has ever been identified for this company.

providers.name: Lightera Networks
providers.description: Lightera Networks Inc. was a Cupertino, California optical networking equipment startup backed by Kleiner Perkins. It built optical core switching systems for carrier transport networks during the late-1990s buildout of long-haul optical infrastructure. Ciena Corporation acquired Lightera Networks together with Marlborough, Massachusetts-based Omnia Communications Inc. for $980 million in stock in 1999, and the Lightera technology and team were absorbed into Ciena's optical core switching line. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and never published a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface; this profile is retained as a historical record of the Kleiner Perkins portfolio and is not an active API provider. NOTE: unrelated to the present-day lightera.com, a rebrand of Furukawa Electric / OFS optical fiber manufacturing (see x-disambiguation).

providers.name: LightLogic
providers.description: LightLogic was an optoelectronics company founded in January 1998 and headquartered in Newark, California. It designed and manufactured highly integrated optical modules — transmitters and receivers — for high-speed (10 Gb/s and up) fiber optic telecommunications equipment, specializing in the integration of lasers, micro-optics and high-speed electronics. Its marquee products were 10 Gb/s transponders providing optical-to-electrical conversion for SONET OC-192 and 10 Gigabit Ethernet applications, sold to optical networking OEMs building primarily metro-market systems. The company raised $57.5M and was backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Cisco Systems, Infineon Technologies, Dassault Developpement, Infinity Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners (then Weiss, Peck and Greer), Optical Capital Group, Ridge Ventures, Siemens Mustang Ventures and Viventures. LightLogic was acquired by Intel Corporation; by mid-2002 lightlogic.com redirected to Intel's optical transceiver product pages. This is a hardware component maker with no API, developer or software surface — historically or today — and the lightlogic.com domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: Lightspeed International
providers.description: Lightspeed International Inc. was a software company founded in 1995 that developed voice control software for data communications networks, an early entrant in the mid-1990s effort to carry voice traffic over packet-switched data infrastructure. It was co-founded and led by CEO Lev Volftsun and backed at the early stage by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Cisco Systems, Inc. acquired the company in 1997, absorbing its voice-over-data-networks technology and team. The company has not operated as an independent entity since that acquisition, predates the public web API era entirely, and never published an API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface. Its legacy domain lightspeedinternational.com is now a parked HugeDomains for-sale listing with no live web surface. This profile is retained as a historical record of the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio and is not an active API provider. NOTE: unrelated to Lightspeed Commerce (the retail and restaurant POS company profiled at all/lightspeed and all/lightspeed-pos), to Lightspeed Trading at lightspeed.com, and — despite the shared name — a portfolio company of rather than an affiliate of Lightspeed Venture Partners (see x-disambiguation).

providers.name: Lithia Motors
providers.description: Lithia Motors is one of the largest automotive retailers in the United States, operating new and used vehicle dealerships and providing related vehicle financing, service, and parts.

providers.name: Livongo Health
providers.description: Livongo Health was a digital-health company delivering connected chronic-condition management for diabetes, hypertension, weight management, and diabetes prevention through cellular-connected glucose meters, blood-pressure monitors, and smart scales paired with human health coaching and 24/7 monitoring. Livongo merged with Teladoc Health in 2020 and now operates as "Livongo by Teladoc Health"; the standalone livongo.com domain 301-redirects to teladochealth.com/livongo. The brand exposes no independent public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Long Game
providers.description: Long Game was a San Francisco fintech startup founded in 2015 by Lindsay Holden that used prize-linked savings and casual mobile gaming to help Gen-Z and millennial consumers build healthy financial habits and grow their savings. Backed by Obvious Ventures and others (raising over $20M in venture capital), Long Game was acquired by Truist Financial in May 2022 and folded into Truist Foundry, which relaunched the Long Game app in May 2023. It is a consumer mobile product with no public developer API surface, and the standalone longgame.co domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: LongBio Pharma
providers.description: LongBio Pharma (Suzhou/Shanghai, founded 2020) is a Chinese clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the in-house discovery and development of innovative antibody and fusion-protein therapeutics for allergic, autoimmune, and complement-mediated diseases. Its lead programs include the anti-IgE antibody LP-003 for chronic spontaneous urticaria and asthma. Co-founded by Dr. Bill Nai-chau Sun (co-founder of Tanox and co-inventor of Omalizumab/Xolair), LongBio raised a Series B2 round led by Qiming Venture Partners and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (01779.HK) in June 2026. It is a pharmaceutical drug developer with no public developer or API surface; this profile was surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company and completed an enrichment pass.

providers.name: Looking Glass Networks
providers.description: Looking Glass Networks, Inc. was a facilities-based telecommunications carrier founded in 2000 and headquartered in Oak Brook, Illinois. It built, owned, and operated metropolitan fiber-optic networks (approximately 2,000 route miles across 14 major U.S. metro markets, serving roughly 215 buildings), providing SONET/SDH, wavelength, and Ethernet data-transport services along with dark fiber and carrier-neutral colocation. Backed by Battery Ventures and Madison Dearborn Partners, the company was acquired by Level 3 Communications on August 2, 2006 and no longer operates independently. It exposes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Looly's
providers.description: Looly's PBC (doing business as WeTheTrillions) was a San Francisco public benefit corporation founded in 2013 by Lamiaa Bounahmidi that reengineered preventative healthcare through microbiome science, evidence-based clinical research, telemedicine, and plant-based food. It delivered fresh, ready-to-eat plant-based meal and snack bundles targeted at chronic conditions such as IBS/SIBO, diabetes and PCOS, plus a fertility program. Backed by 500 Global and part of the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead, the company is a consumer food and health business with no public API surface. Its primary domain (wethetrillions.com) no longer resolves and the venture appears to be defunct/deadpooled.

providers.name: Lowy Asia Power Index
providers.description: Get measure resources and influence to rank the relative power of states in Asia

providers.name: Lumius
providers.description: Lumius is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) medical-imaging startup building fast, smart, accessible real-time 3D ultrasound systems — described as "a 3D camera for the body." The technology aims to move ultrasound beyond traditional 2D imaging to intelligent, AI-assisted 3D visualization across larger volumes, with an initial focus on vascular access and central-line placement (where roughly half of first attempts fail among new clinicians) and future targets including blood-clot detection, tumor diagnosis, and biopsy guidance. The company partners with academic institutions such as Duke University and Columbia University. Lumius is a hardware/device company with no public API, SDK, or developer platform; its products are pre-market and not intended for medical use. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC portfolio lead and has been reviewed by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Magellan Midstream Partners
providers.description: Magellan Midstream Partners owned the longest refined petroleum products pipeline system in the United States, along with refined petroleum products and crude oil storage facilities. Magellan Midstream Partners was acquired by ONEOK in September 2023 and its assets and operations have been integrated into ONEOK's Refined Products and Crude segment. This repository tracks any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts made publicly available related to the legacy Magellan operations or successor ONEOK resources.

providers.name: Manas AI
providers.description: Manas AI is an artificial-intelligence drug-discovery company co-founded by Reid Hoffman and physician-scientist Siddhartha Mukherjee, launched in late 2024 and backed by General Catalyst and Greylock. The company applies machine learning and computational biology to accelerate the discovery and design of new medicines, with an initial focus on hard-to-treat cancers such as breast and prostate cancer and lymphoma. Manas AI operates as a private biotech / therapeutics research organization rather than a developer-facing platform: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation. This entry is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio.

providers.name: Marvel Tech (Mufan Power)
providers.description: Marvel Tech (Mufan Power, 慕帆动力) is a Chinese industrial power-equipment manufacturer developing next-generation zero-carbon clean power-generation technology and products. Its portfolio centers on hydrogen-fuelled gas turbine generating sets, high-speed multi-stage cantilever turbines, special-gas and TRT flow-path (通流) turbines, dry low-NOx combustors, and industrial waste-heat and waste-pressure recovery equipment. The company runs a corporate brochure website in Chinese and English (ICP 沪ICP备17001438号) and publishes no public developer, API, or SDK surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Matrix Pharmaceutical
providers.description: Matrix Pharmaceutical is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Maza
providers.description: Maza was an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) backed consumer fintech startup that helped Spanish-speaking and undocumented immigrants in the United States access the financial system - guiding users through applying for an ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number), opening a bank account, and obtaining financial services without a Social Security number. Founded in 2022, Maza raised an $8M seed round led by a16z in June 2023 and grew to more than 50,000 users. In April 2025 Maza was acquired by Flex for a reported $40M. Maza operated a consumer mobile application only and never published a public developer API, SDK, or event surface; following the acquisition its domains (maza.io, joinmaza.com, maza.us) now resolve to parked landing pages.

providers.name: MBX Biosciences
providers.description: MBX Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel precision peptide therapies for endocrine and metabolic disorders, built on its proprietary PEPs platform. Lead programs include canvuparatide (MBX 2109) for hypoparathyroidism, plus MBX 4291, MBX 5765, and MBX 6XXX. Surfaced as a portfolio company of NEA and added to the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found at this time.

providers.name: Medikine
providers.description: Medikine is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in San Diego, California, engineering a new class of medicines called PEPTIKINES — synthetic peptide mimetics of cytokines and growth-factor receptor agonists. PEPTIKINES emulate the beneficial activities of natural cytokines while being much smaller in molecular weight and structurally unrelated in sequence, making them amenable to enhanced pharmacokinetics, cell targeting, and conditional activation without generating neutralizing antibodies to native cytokines. The company's lead candidate, MDK-703, is an Fc-fusion protein containing an IL-7 PEPTIKINE that mimics the T-cell-supporting properties of IL-7, with a pipeline spanning oncology, autoimmune, and infectious-disease therapeutics. Medikine is a private, venture-backed drug-discovery company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or technical developer surface.

providers.name: Medir
providers.description: Medir is a South Korean digital-health company behind Medb (메듭), a non-face-to-face (telemedicine) and prescription-drug delivery platform that connects patients, doctors, hospitals and pharmacies. Through the Medb mobile app, patients receive 100% video consultations with physicians and have their prescribed medications delivered to their door — often within roughly 30 minutes to two hours — with no separate service fee beyond the standard consultation charge. Medir is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global. The business operates as a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network pending any future API surface.

providers.name: Mendra
providers.description: Mendra is an AI-native biopharma company focused on developing breakthrough medicines for rare and ultra-rare pediatric diseases. It partners with R&D-stage biotech companies to accelerate clinical development and commercialization, handling regulatory, clinical, and reimbursement strategy while prioritizing the needs of patients and families. Founded by a team with experience from BioMarin, Palantir, and other pharma and biotech companies, Mendra launched with an $82 million Series A round and is backed by 8VC and Wing Venture Capital. The company operates a corporate marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation.

providers.name: MessageMe *
providers.description: MessageMe was a mobile messaging application built to explore expressive, fun online communication, and a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) in the consumer sector. The MessageMe team was acquired by Yahoo, and the product was shut down: users could access messages until November 7, 2014, after which accounts and personal information were erased. The messageme.com domain now serves only the shutdown announcement. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 confirmed the company is defunct with no live API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or event surface to catalog.

providers.name: Millennial Fox
providers.description: Millennial Fox, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based consumer company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners that set out to bridge the gap between entertainment and fitness. Its flagship product, Tracks Battle Squad, was a socially gamified workout companion for iOS and watchOS that integrated with the Apple Health app to turn physical activity into points, badges, and accessories for a virtual 3D fox character. The app launched in 2017, was featured on Apple Music's Planet of the Apps, and has since been removed from the App Store; the company appears inactive and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known surface.

providers.name: Millennium Pharma
providers.description: Millennium Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company founded in 1993 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, that pioneered a genomics-based, platform approach to drug discovery and development. Backed early on by Mayfield, the company built its reputation on large research and development alliances with major pharmaceutical partners and on discovering and commercializing medicines for cancer and other diseases. Millennium was acquired by Takeda Pharmaceutical Company in 2008 and now operates as the Takeda Oncology unit. It is a therapeutics and drug-discovery organization, not an API or developer-platform provider, and exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Millennium Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Millennium Pharmaceuticals was a biopharmaceutical company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, focused on oncology and inflammation, best known for developing the cancer drug Velcade (bortezomib). Backed early by Kleiner Perkins, it was acquired by Takeda Pharmaceutical Company in 2008 for $8.8B and its brand was retired to "Takeda Oncology" in 2013; it no longer operates as an independent company. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub. This is a research/company profile with no independent developer API surface — the pipeline confirmed the provider publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or event/webhook surface.

providers.name: Minghui Pharmaceutical
providers.description: Minghui Pharmaceutical is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Minova Pharma
providers.description: Nanjing Minova Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd. (南京迈诺威医药科技有限公司) is a drug-discovery and pharmaceutical R&D company founded in February 2021 and headquartered in Nanjing, China. The company focuses on the discovery, development, and industrialization of novel drugs for mental diseases and disfiguring (cosmetic/dermatological) diseases, operating in the consumer-pharmaceutical space as both a drug R&D house and supplier. Its stated capabilities span early drug discovery, compound/drug screening, and druggability (developability) research. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Minova Pharma publishes a corporate marketing website but exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: MLnetworks
providers.description: MLNetworks is an AI-powered telecommunications network optimization company, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The company positions itself around helping telcos "unlock the full potential of your telco network," delivering AI-driven insights, an advertised ~30% reduction in CAPEX/OPEX, and faster network problem resolution. As of this enrichment pass the public surface at mlnetworks.io is a marketing site only (a Next.js/Vercel single-page app) with no published developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery documents — all probed endpoints returned 404 and no docs/api/developer subdomains resolve. Go-to-market is a Calendly discovery-call booking rather than a self-serve developer signup.

providers.name: Mochatrade
providers.description: Mochatrade is a regulated neo-brokerage for Indian traders offering onchain perpetual futures on US stocks and commodities. Traders access 50+ US equities (including TSLA, NVDA, AAPL), pre-IPO names, commodities, and crypto with up to 20x leverage, settled in USDC on Hyperliquid, with INR on- and off-ramps via UPI and self-custody wallets. Founded in 2026 by IIT graduates who previously built a crypto wallet acquired after 2M installs, the company brings professional-grade derivatives execution to India's 140M+ demat account holders. Backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and Pioneer. As of this enrichment pass Mochatrade publishes only a marketing landing page (a client-rendered SPA) and no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Modria.com
providers.description: Modria is an online dispute resolution (ODR) platform originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. Enrichment (2026-07-20) confirmed the company is no longer independent; the modria.com domain 301-redirects in full to www.tylertech.com/solutions/modria, so Modria now operates as a resolution/ODR solution within Tyler Technologies. No independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or .well-known discovery surface exists on modria.com (every path redirects to the Tyler Technologies marketing page). Retained as a network record; there is no standalone API to enrich.

providers.name: Molecular Assemblies
providers.description: Molecular Assemblies is a synthetic biology company that developed a Fully Enzymatic Synthesis (FES) platform for de novo DNA production, using enzymatic chemistry to synthesize longer (up to ~400 base), higher-purity oligonucleotides faster than traditional phosphoramidite methods, targeting next-generation sequencing, gene synthesis, diagnostics, and therapeutics markets.
