Originally a DCVC-backed startup, the company's assets and intellectual property were acquired by Maravai LifeSciences, and its enzymatic DNA synthesis technology is now part of TriLink BioTechnologies. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface; its former molecularassemblies.com domain now redirects to TriLink BioTechnologies.

providers.name: Molecular Stethoscope
providers.description: Molecular Stethoscope (now operating as Superfluid Dx, Inc.) is a South San Francisco clinical-stage diagnostics company developing minimally invasive blood tests for neurodegenerative disease. Its cell-free messenger RNA (cf-mRNA) liquid-biopsy platform aims to detect Alzheimer's disease at early stages from a routine blood draw, as an alternative to spinal taps and brain imaging. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcvc and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical diagnostics R&D company it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or technical platform; this profile is maintained for network completeness rather than API discovery.

providers.name: Monetique
providers.description: Monétique is the French term for the electronic payment industry, encompassing payment cards, card processing, point-of-sale systems, and the financial services infrastructure that supports card-based transactions.

providers.name: More Magic Solutions
providers.description: More Magic Solutions (MoreMagic Solutions) was a mobile commerce and mobile money company that enabled mobile operators, financial institutions, content providers, and distributors to let consumers purchase goods and services on demand via a mobile phone, POS, or the web, with deployments across more than 30 countries. Backed by Battery Ventures, Cipio Partners, DN Capital, Endeavour Vision, and others, the company was acquired by Oberthur Technologies in February 2012 and folded into Oberthur's mobile financial services offering. It no longer operates as an independent entity: the moremagic.com domain is now parked/for-sale and the company publishes no active developer portal, API reference, or API artifacts. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio lead; the enrichment pass found no live API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Movivo
providers.description: Movivo was a London-based mobile rewards startup (500 Startups / Distro Dojo, HQ London) whose consumer app let users cover the cost of their mobile airtime and data by completing surveys, crowdsourced micro-tasks, and app installs, working with mobile operators across emerging markets. The company was surfaced as a portfolio lead of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct — movivo.com resolves to a parked GoDaddy for-sale domain, and no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or GitHub organization could be found. This profile is retained as a network record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: MycoMedica
providers.description: MycoMedica Life Sciences, PBC is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded by mycologist Paul Stamets and backed by Obvious Ventures, True Ventures, and Kittyhawk Ventures. The company develops fungi-derived therapeutic drugs, including its lead psilocybin candidate MLS101 and the "Stamets Stack" (a novel blend of niacin, psilocybin, and lion's mane), for the prevention and treatment of psychiatric and neurological disorders. It raised $60 million in Series A funding in 2022 and is advancing pre-clinical and clinical research toward FDA approval. MycoMedica is a life-sciences drug-development company and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: MycroFriends
providers.description: MycroFriends is a consumer health and wellness company that helps people become healthier through education and coaching centered on the connection between the human microbiome, nutrition, and overall health. Founded by George Cigale (previously founder of the online tutoring company Tutor.com) and headquartered in New York City, the company launched via a 2017 crowdfunding campaign and works with scientists, physicians, dietitians, and technologists to deliver microbiome education, personalized nutritional and lifestyle guidance, and access to expert health coaches. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass MycroFriends publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface, and its former website resolves only to a default (unconfigured) Azure App Service host.

providers.name: Mynvax
providers.description: Mynvax is a clinical-stage vaccine biotechnology company based in Bengaluru, India, developing recombinant, thermostable vaccines for respiratory viral infections. Spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), the company applies protein-stabilization and structure-based antigen design to create thermotolerant COVID-19 and influenza vaccine candidates aimed at affordable distribution in low- and lower-middle-income countries without deep cold-chain requirements. Mynvax is a life-sciences research company and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or technical integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery.

providers.name: Myriad
providers.description: Myriad AG is a Zurich-based financial technology company, founded in 2001 by Jean Andre and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, that provides integrated, secure platforms and open APIs to help partner financial institutions, mobile money operators, and payment solution clients build innovative digital financial services. The company is listed as an Earlybird portfolio exit. As of this enrichment pass no live, publicly reachable developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API artifact could be located for this provider, so it remains a lightly profiled company lead rather than a scored API surface.

providers.name: National Cardiovascular Partners (Fresenius Medical Care)
providers.description: National Cardiovascular Partners (NCP) is a Fresenius Medical Care company that partners with physician entrepreneurs to create, sustain and grow independent, outpatient cardiac catheterization and vascular labs. Headquartered in Edina, Minnesota with operations in Houston, Texas, NCP manages the full development lifecycle of outpatient hybrid cardiovascular facilities in which physicians serve as majority stakeholders. It is a physical healthcare services operator: it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhooks, and its official domain (ncplp.com) is a registrar-parked defensive domain rather than an active site. Parent company Fresenius Medical Care likewise offers no public developer API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nationstar Mortgage Holdings
providers.description: Nationstar Mortgage Holdings was a non-bank residential mortgage loan originator and servicer in the United States that was rebranded as Mr. Cooper Group.

providers.name: NET
providers.description: NET is Network Equipment Technologies, Inc. (formerly NYSE ticker NET), a networking and telecommunications hardware company known for enterprise Session Border Controllers (SBCs) and secure networking equipment, including a large U.S. Federal Government installed base. Surfaced as an exited portfolio company of Battery Ventures, the company was acquired by Sonus Networks in August 2012 (approximately $42M) and later folded into what is now Ribbon Communications. It no longer operates as an independent entity, publishes no public developer program, and has no live domain or API surface.

providers.name: Neumora
providers.description: Neumora Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering a new era of precision medicines to restore brain health and wellbeing. It develops therapeutics for brain diseases and neuropsychiatric conditions, applying a precision-medicine approach to neuroscience drug discovery and development. Neumora was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. As a therapeutics company it maintains a corporate and investor web presence but exposes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or documentation surface: probing its domain for /.well-known/ discovery documents, an OpenAPI/Swagger spec, an llms.txt, and developer/docs paths returned no machine-readable API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Neutun
providers.description: Neutun (Neutun Labs) was a consumer digital-health startup based in Toronto and San Francisco that built a mobile app for people living with epilepsy — helping them track and log seizure activity, manage and fulfill medications, share their journey with a care-circle of loved ones, and surface research-backed health insights to help reduce and prevent seizures. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead. Enrichment probing (2026-07-20) found the company appears defunct: neutun.com is still registered but resolves to no live website (last Wayback Machine snapshot October 2018), and no developer portal, API reference, SDK, OpenAPI, or any public API surface was ever published — only a consumer application with social OAuth sign-in.

providers.name: Newport Communications
providers.description: NewPort Communications was a fabless semiconductor startup that developed mixed-signal integrated circuits for the high-speed optical networking market, including CMOS-based transceivers for 2.5-Gbit/s (OC-48) SONET/SDH applications. Founded in 1999, the company was backed by Mayfield Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Cisco Investments (roughly $28M across Series A and B) before being acquired by Broadcom on October 4, 2000 to strengthen Broadcom's networking semiconductor portfolio. It is a defunct company with no standalone public web presence and no API surface; this record is retained as a historical portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nextcure
providers.description: NextCure, Inc. (NASDAQ NXTC) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing novel immunomedicines to treat cancer and other immune-related diseases. The company uses its FIND-IO platform to identify and characterize immunomodulatory targets and biological pathways, advancing a pipeline of immunotherapy drug candidates. NextCure surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of canaan-partners. Enrichment probe (2026-07-20) found no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; this is a biopharmaceutical R&D organization with no programmatic API surface to catalog.

providers.name: NextG Networks
providers.description: NextG Networks is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Northern Tier Energy
providers.description: Northern Tier Energy was an independent downstream energy company with refining, retail, and pipeline operations. It was acquired by Western Refining in 2016, which itself merged into Marathon Petroleum's brand portfolio. No active public APIs are associated with this entity; the repository is maintained as a historical record within the API Evangelist Network.

providers.name: Nostro
providers.description: Nostro refers to an account that a bank holds in a foreign currency at another bank (correspondent bank). Nostro account management involves reconciliation, liquidity management, and transaction tracking across correspondent banking relationships and multiple currencies.

providers.name: novamab
providers.description: Novamab (洛启生物) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company specializing in VHH (nanobody) antibody drug development for respiratory and inflammatory diseases such as asthma, COPD, and IBD. Its platforms span inhaled antibodies, oral antibodies, and dual/multi-specific antibodies alongside integrated drug formulation and manufacturing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirmed the company publishes a corporate website but no developer API, documentation portal, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Novast Laboratories
providers.description: Novast Laboratories is a pharmaceutical development and manufacturing company (CDMO) headquartered in Nantong, Jiangsu Province, China, founded in 2005 by Dr. Guohua Zhang and a multinational management team. Novast specializes in high-barrier, difficult-to-formulate generic and specialty pharmaceuticals, including ultra-low-dose hormonal and extended- / modified-release oral products built on proprietary drug-delivery technologies. It is noted as one of the first China-based pharmaceutical companies to gain U.S. FDA approval for finished drug products marketed in the United States, and provides contract development and manufacturing services to generic and innovator companies. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Novast is a physical pharmaceutical manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Novaxess
providers.description: Novaxess was a telecommunications / communications company that was venture-backed by Battery Ventures, M/C Partners, and Ramphastos Investments and was acquired in March 2004. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub via the Battery Ventures portfolio graph. Enrichment research (July 2026) found no active company website (the novaxess.com domain is now parked and listed for sale), no developer portal, no public API, and no developer documentation or SDKs. The entity has no current API surface to catalog; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead only.

providers.name: Novome
providers.description: Novome Biotechnologies is a DCVC-backed biotechnology company based in South San Francisco developing genetically engineered microbial medicines (GEMMs) - live bacterial therapeutics designed to colonize the gut and treat chronic conditions such as enteric hyperoxaluria and other GI and metabolic diseases. As a therapeutics developer, Novome is a research-and-drug-development organization rather than a software or API provider; the enrichment pass found no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Omniome
providers.description: Omniome was a San Diego genomics company that developed Sequencing By Binding (SBB) technology, a proprietary chemistry aimed at highly accurate short-read DNA sequencing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcvc, Omniome was acquired by Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) in 2021, and its site now redirects to pacb.com. It builds laboratory sequencing instruments and chemistry rather than a public developer platform, and exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: Oni Systems
providers.description: ONI Systems Inc. was an optical networking equipment company that built optical switching and transport systems for metropolitan-area networks during the fiber-optic boom of the late 1990s and early 2000s. Backed by Canaan Partners and other venture investors, the company went public and was acquired by Ciena Corporation in 2002, after which its product line was absorbed into Ciena's metro optical portfolio. It operated as an equipment maker and has no standalone developer program, public API surface, SDKs, or online documentation of its own. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/defunct portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Onkos Surgical
providers.description: Onkos Surgical is a privately held surgical oncology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Parsippany, New Jersey, focused on innovative solutions for musculoskeletal oncology and complex orthopaedic procedures. Built on a digital platform grounded in patient imaging analysis, personalized surgical planning and advanced 3D printing, Onkos develops limb salvage systems, My3D personalized solutions, uDesign on-demand personalized surgical plans, and antibacterial-coated implants for tumor and revision orthopaedic applications. The company received the first FDA De Novo approval of an antibacterial coating for tumor and revision orthopaedic implants. Onkos does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal; its public surfaces are the corporate website, a product Instructions-for-Use (IFU) documentation library, and a surgeon training portal.

providers.name: Openet
providers.description: Openet was an Irish telecommunications software company (headquartered in Dublin) that built real-time business support systems (BSS) for mobile network operators, including online charging systems, real-time policy and charging control, digital business platforms, and data management for 4G/5G monetization. Openet was acquired by Amdocs in 2020 and its brand and products were absorbed into the Amdocs monetization portfolio; the openet.com domain now redirects to the Amdocs monetization product pages. There is no independent Openet developer portal, public API, or first-party SDK surface remaining. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-graph lead from balderton-capital and processed by the enrichment pipeline, which confirmed the acquisition/redirect and found no live API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Oration *
providers.description: Oration (Oration PBC, product OrationRx) was a Foster City, California prescription-savings SaaS that helped self-insured employers and their employees find the lowest-priced medications, analyzing over $1B in prescription drug purchases. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Andreessen Horowitz, DCVC, Chicago Ventures and others (~$11.2M raised). The company was acquired by PokitDok in June 2017; its own domains (oration.io, orationrx.com) no longer resolve and no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remains. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical life-sciences / pharmacy-benefits portfolio lead.

providers.name: Orative
providers.description: Orative Corporation was an enterprise software company that built conferencing and collaboration software for mobile business users, offering a client-server product to manage conversations, collaborate with colleagues, filter unwanted calls and notifications, and access personal and corporate directories. Founded in the early 2000s, it raised a $12M Series B in July 2004 led by Trinity Ventures (with Mayfield and Diamondhead Ventures) and was acquired by Cisco Systems in October 2006. The company is defunct: there is no live product, developer portal, or API surface today. This profile was surfaced as a Trinity Ventures portfolio company and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline, which confirmed no current API surface exists.

providers.name: Orbital Therapeutics
providers.description: Orbital Therapeutics was a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing next-generation RNA medicines, combining circular and linear RNA, targeted delivery, and AI-guided design across immunomodulation, in vivo CAR-T cell therapy, next-generation vaccines, and protein therapeutics. Its lead program, OTX-201, targeted autoimmune disease through B-cell depletion. Founded out of Beam Therapeutics and backed by ARCH Venture Partners, a16z Bio + Health, and Newpath Partners, the company raised a $270M Series A in 2023. In October 2025 Bristol Myers Squibb agreed to acquire Orbital Therapeutics for $1.5 billion; orbitaltx.com now redirects to bms.com. As a therapeutics developer, Orbital publishes no public developer platform, API, or machine-readable API surface, so this record is an identity-only profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: oricell
providers.description: Oricell Therapeutics (原启生物) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing cell-based immunotherapies for cancer, including GPC3-targeted CAR-T (Ori-C101) for advanced liver cancer and GPRC5D-targeted CAR-T (OriCAR-017) for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. It operates proprietary OriAb antibody-discovery, OriCAR T-cell persistence, and cell-manufacturing (CMC) platforms. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. As a clinical-stage biotech it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or technical developer surface; this profile is retained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Osu
providers.description: Osu is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: fintech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Ott Risk
providers.description: OTT Risk is a UK- and US-based insurtech Managing General Agent (MGA) building parametric, non-damage business interruption (NDBI) insurance for the digital economy. Its revenue-protection cover targets online marketplaces, gig and freelance workers, and enterprises, paying out against economic indices and industry metrics rather than physical-damage claims. OTT Risk is a portfolio company of Anthemis and an alumnus of the Lloyd's Lab Accelerator (Cohort 9, 2022), with underwriting capacity from Apollo ibott Syndicate 1971. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface, and its former ottrisk.com domain now resolves to a domain-sale page, indicating the company may be dormant.

providers.name: OvaScience
providers.description: OvaScience was a Waltham, Massachusetts biotechnology company founded in 2011 (by Michelle Dipp, Richard Aldrich, Christoph Westphal, Jonathan Tilly, and David Sinclair) that developed fertility and assisted-reproduction treatments for female infertility. Its two marquee IVF services were Augment (autologous mitochondrial transfer into a patient's egg) and OvaTure (maturing egg-precursor stem cells into eggs), launched in clinics in the UAE, Canada, and Japan starting in 2014. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. OvaScience is defunct: in August 2018 it merged with Millendo Therapeutics via a reverse merger. It publishes no developer API, no OpenAPI, and no developer/documentation surface; its former domain (ovascience.com) now resolves to a parked lander.

providers.name: Overt
providers.description: OverT Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation, programmed off-the-shelf (allogeneic) cell therapies and biologics for solid tumors. The company pairs AI-powered genome-scale genetic discovery with tumor-targeting receptor engineering and naturally tumor-homing gamma delta T cells, plus scalable manufacturing intended to reduce treatment time and cost. Its pipeline includes OVT-101, a CLDN6-targeted CAR-T for ovarian cancer (first-in-human anticipated H1 2027), and OVT-201, a non-MHC T cell engager for solid tumors. Based in New York City and backed by Wing Venture Capital. As a therapeutics company, OverT Bio publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: P2P, Inc.
providers.description: P2P, Inc. is the Japanese insurtech startup behind justInCase, a smartphone-first micro-insurance (少額短期保険) provider offering short-term, on-demand consumer coverage such as smartphone protection, cancer insurance, and peer-to-peer risk-sharing products. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass its justincase.jp domain returns a 307 redirect to Sony Shoutan Insurance (sony-sasti.jp), a Sony Financial Group micro-insurer, indicating the business has been absorbed. No public developer API, documentation, SDK, developer portal, or technical integration surface was found on either the original or the successor domain.

providers.name: Pallando Therapeutics
providers.description: Pallando Therapeutics is an early-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation targeted protein degraders with an emphasis on precision targeting, under the tagline "Intelligent Degradation, Innovative Therapies." It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile its public website (pallandotx.com) is a coming-soon placeholder and it publishes no developer API, documentation, SDKs, or other technical surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Pardes Bio
providers.description: Pardes Biosciences was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing novel therapeutics to treat and prevent viral diseases. Founded in 2020 and based in Carlsbad, California, it used structure-based drug design and a tunable, reversible covalent chemistry platform. Its lead candidate, PBI-0451, was an oral direct-acting antiviral for SARS-CoV-2. The company was acquired in 2023 and no longer operates independently. It has no public API, developer program, or technical integration surface, and its former domain (pardesbio.com) is now a parked/registrar page.

providers.name: Parla
providers.description: Parla (originally launched as Adia) was a London-based digital reproductive-health startup that gave women access to at-home fertility blood tests, an AI-enabled fertility platform, educational content, and an expert-led peer community around conception, pregnancy, and loss. Backed by Seedcamp, Zinc VC, and other UK investors, Parla was acquired by Holland & Barrett International in April 2022; the myparla.com domain now redirects to hollandandbarrett.com and the company operates no independent public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Pathios Therapeutics
providers.description: Pathios Therapeutics is a clinical-stage oncology and immunology drug discovery and development company based in Oxfordshire, United Kingdom, founded in 2017. The company develops small-molecule inhibitors of the pH-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR65 to counteract the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment; its lead asset PTT-4256 is a first-in-class GPR65 inhibitor now in a Phase 1/2 clinical trial. Backed by Canaan, Brandon Capital, and a strategic investment from Bristol Myers Squibb, Pathios is a research-stage biotech with no public API, developer platform, or technical integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and processed by the enrichment pipeline, which confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Patient IO
providers.description: Patient IO (legal entity Filament Labs, Inc.) was an Austin, Texas care coordination and patient engagement platform founded in 2013 by Jason Bornhorst, Colin Anawaty, and Brian Gambs out of the Techstars Austin accelerator. Its API-first mobile platform connected health systems with patients between visits to support the transition to value-based care. athenahealth acquired Patient IO in August 2016 and its architecture became the foundation of athenahealth's patient-facing athenawell application. The standalone product, developer program, and public API surface have since been retired; patientio.com now serves only a placeholder page and its mail is handled by athenahealth.

providers.name: Paydiant
providers.description: Paydiant was a Boston-based mobile-wallet, point-of-sale and cloud payments platform, backed by General Catalyst, that let banks, merchants and retailers build their own white-label mobile-payment and loyalty apps (notably powering the retailer-led MCX "CurrentC" wallet). PayPal acquired Paydiant in 2015 and folded the technology into its in-store and merchant products; Paydiant no longer operates as an independent company. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio lead; an enrichment probe on 2026-07-20 found no live independent API surface — the paydiant.com domain and its api/developer/docs subdomains wildcard-resolve to a PayPal/MarkMonitor brand-protection parking IP (3.33.139.32) and serve no content.

providers.name: Payworks
providers.description: Payworks was a Munich-based payment-infrastructure company backed by Speedinvest, building a mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) payment-gateway platform that let acquirers, PSPs and ISVs turn commodity smartphones and tablets into card-accepting terminals via a developer SDK and gateway. It was acquired by Visa in 2019 and its technology was folded into Visa's acceptance/CyberSource stack, after which the independent Payworks brand was wound down. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no active independent public developer surface — its primary domains are dormant (payworks.com resolves to a parked AWS S3 redirect bucket with no website configuration; payworks.de is a domain-for-sale parking page) and no docs/developer/api subdomains resolve — so there is no live OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface to harvest into the network. This profile is retained as a historical Speedinvest portfolio record.

providers.name: Peninsula Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Peninsula Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Phoenix Wireless
providers.description: Phoenix Wireless (Phoenix Wireless Group) was a manufacturer of wireless telecommunications accessories and hardware, founded in 1994 and headquartered in West Chester, PA. Its product lines included antennas, Bluetooth headsets, phone clips, mounts and fasteners, induction chargers, travel chargers, and batteries. The company was acquired by Communications Test Design, Inc. (CTDI) on September 26, 2008 and no longer operates as an independent entity. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: Pine Medical
providers.description: Pine Medical was a telehealth provider that offered a medication-supported weight-loss program pairing licensed clinicians with prescription therapies and ongoing patient coaching. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment probe on 2026-07-20 found the public website (pinemedical.com) announcing that Pine Medical wound down its medication-supported weight-loss program effective March 30, 2024, and redirects former patients to alternative providers and insurance-covered options. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found.

providers.name: Ping An Good Doctor
providers.description: Ping An Good Doctor (Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited, since rebranded Ping An Health, HKEX: 1833) is the online-healthcare arm of China's Ping An Insurance Group and one of the country's largest one-stop online healthcare platforms. Through its consumer app it offers online medical consultations delivered by an in-house medical team and AI triage, family-doctor memberships, a health mall for pharmaceutical and wellness e-commerce, and health-management and chronic-disease services. The platform serves individual consumers as well as enterprise and financial channels across China. As surfaced to the API Evangelist network it is a consumer/enterprise app business with no public developer API program: enrichment found no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or open-platform documentation, and the historical corporate domain (pahtg.com) now resolves to a parked landing page.

providers.name: Ping An HealthKonnect
providers.description: Ping An HealthKonnect (Ping An Healthcare Technology), founded in September 2016 and headquartered in Shanghai, is a technology-driven managed care platform in China. As an AI-powered big data platform it brings together patients with providers of health insurance and medical services, offering budget planning, precision healthcare, medical health-care accounts, medical resources management, health records, and fraud/abuse detection to optimize healthcare spending. The platform covers roughly 70% of Chinese cities and a market of some 800 million people, and has raised about USD 1.15 billion backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, IDG Capital, and others. It is a B2B and government-facing enterprise platform with no public developer API surface; this profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Playbrush
providers.description: Playbrush is a consumer oral-care technology brand that makes smart, gamified electric and sonic toothbrushes for children (ages 3+), pairing a Bluetooth-connected brush with a companion mobile app that turns brushing into interactive games and coaching to build good dental-hygiene habits. Founded as a UK/Austria startup and backed by Speedinvest, the Playbrush product line has since been acquired by SUNSTAR and is now sold under the GUM Playbrush brand; the former playbrush.com domain 302-redirects to a Sunstar GUM product page. Playbrush is a hardware/consumer-app company and exposes no public developer portal, API, specification, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile was surfaced as a Speedinvest portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirmed there is no API surface.

providers.name: PlusDental
providers.description: PlusDental was a Berlin-based direct-to-consumer orthodontic company offering clear dental aligners ("Zahnschiene") for teeth straightening, backed by HV Capital. The brand has since been migrated to DR SMILE (operated by Sunshine Smile GmbH); plusdental.com now serves a handover notice redirecting customers to DR SMILE customer service. This is a consumer healthcare service with no public developer program, API, SDKs, or technical integration surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; the enrichment pipeline confirmed no API artifacts exist.

providers.name: Poko
providers.description: Poko was a Singapore-based fintech that built a fiat-to-crypto on-ramp aggregator for Web3 businesses — wallets, wallet-as-a-service providers, marketplaces, dApps, and games. Its product connected 100+ local and international payment methods with local KYC and smart routing so global users could buy crypto or pay for NFTs with familiar local payment rails, exposed to developers via SDKs (including a React Native SDK) and a Dashboard API. Backed by 500 Global, ADB Ventures, Amasia, CE Innovation Capital, and CreditEase, Poko was acquired by Web3Auth (Torus Labs) in October 2023 and its on-ramp aggregator continues under the Web3Auth brand. The original Poko developer surface is no longer operational: the pokoapp.xyz domain is now parked/for sale and the docs.pokoapp.xyz documentation host has been deprovisioned.

providers.name: Poncho
providers.description: Poncho was a consumer weather service founded in 2013 in New York City by Kuan Huang and Paul Murphy that delivered a personalized, personality-driven daily forecast through the messaging layer — Facebook Messenger, SMS, email, and Amazon Alexa — rather than a traditional weather app. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Comcast Ventures, and Lerer Hippeau, the company was acquired by Dirty Lemon and is no longer independently operating. It never published a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile carries identity metadata only.

providers.name: Ponto
providers.description: Ponto is a crypto banking and payments infrastructure company in the fintech sector, surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and Polychain and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface could be located for the company - the previously associated ponto.io domain now redirects to an unrelated party and no other candidate domain resolved to a live crypto-banking product. This profile remains a thin lead pending discovery of a verified developer/API surface, at which point the pipeline can harvest and enrich real artifacts.

providers.name: Pozen
providers.description: POZEN Inc. was a specialty pharmaceutical company headquartered in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, founded in 1996 and focused on developing therapeutics for pain and pain-related conditions, most notably acute migraine. It was best known for the products Treximet (sumatriptan/naproxen) and Vimovo (naproxen/esomeprazole). POZEN traded publicly on NASDAQ under the ticker POZN and in 2016 combined with Tribute Pharmaceuticals to form Aralez Pharmaceuticals. Pozen was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As a pharmaceutical company it operated no public developer program, API, or SDK surface; an enrichment pass confirmed no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: Practice
providers.description: Practice (practice.do) was a Montreal-based all-in-one coaching and consulting business platform that bundled scheduling, client portals, forms, contracts, invoicing, and payments into a single tool for independent coaches. It raised a $10M seed round in 2021 led by a16z (Andrew Chen participating). The company shut down permanently on November 3, 2025 after a failed acquisition process; its domain no longer serves a product and it exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface.

providers.name: Primus Senior Living
providers.description: Primus Senior Living is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of general-catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Proxy
providers.description: This is the index of API proxy, reverse proxy, forward proxy, and proxy middleware service and tooling repos being tracked by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Pub/Sub
providers.description: A messaging pattern where publishers send messages to topics without knowledge of subscribers, and subscribers receive messages from topics they're interested in, enabling asynchronous and decoupled communication between services. Modern distributed architectures rely on it to coordinate workloads across multiple nodes and regions.

providers.name: QEP Resources
providers.description: QEP Resources was an independent natural gas and crude oil exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with operations in the United States. The company was acquired by Diamondback Energy in 2021 and no longer operates as an independent entity.

providers.name: Qlub
providers.description: Qlub is a hospitality payments and digital-menu technology company enabling contactless pay-at-table, order-and-pay, digital menus, secure payment links, a qlub SoftPOS terminal, and the qlub+ rewards program for restaurants, hotels, and hospitality venues. Diners scan a QR code to view the bill, split it, add a tip, and pay from their own phone without downloading an app or creating an account. Qlub operates globally across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, Australia, Brazil, and the United States, and integrates with more than one hundred point-of-sale systems. It is backed by Point Nine. As of this enrichment pass Qlub publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve developer portal; technical integrations are delivered through direct POS partnerships.

providers.name: Renewable Energy Group
providers.description: Renewable Energy Group (REG) is a North American producer of biodiesel and renewable diesel, founded with biodiesel operations dating to 1996 and formally established as a separate company in 2006, with headquarters in Ames, Iowa. REG operated as a publicly traded company on Nasdaq under the ticker REGI until February 28, 2022, when Chevron Corporation announced the acquisition of REG for approximately $3.15 billion; the deal closed on June 13, 2022, and REG now operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Chevron under the Chevron Renewable Energy Group brand at chevron-reg.com. REG operates a fleet of biorefineries across the United States and Europe, producing biodiesel, renewable diesel, and related lower-carbon fuel products from a diversified mix of feedstocks including used cooking oil, inedible animal fats, distillers corn oil, and vegetable oils. As of this profile, neither REG nor the Chevron Renewable Energy Group subsidiary publishes a public consumer-facing developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or GitHub organization; customer, supplier, distributor, and feedstock-partner integrations are handled through Chevron Renewable Energy Group sales, supply, and supplier-relations channels.

providers.name: Rens Energy
providers.description: Rens Energy is a Shanghai-based distributed energy-storage and energy-management company founded in 2017. It builds distributed energy-storage systems and energy-management software that let customers deliver power and energy-balance scheduling, energy-usage analysis, and energy optimization for efficient operation and asset appreciation of their power assets. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment probing found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Revivant
providers.description: Revivant is a medical device company that develops and markets proprietary technology to treat cardiac arrest, backed by Canaan Partners at the Series D stage (Canaan partner Brent Ahrens). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment research found no live company website (the revivant.com domain is parked/for-sale via Sedo and no revivant.io/.ai variants resolve), no developer portal, and no public API, SDK, or documentation surface — as a medical-device manufacturer Revivant exposes no programmable API. This profile is retained as an identity-only lead with no API surface to score.

providers.name: Rf Surgical
providers.description: Rf Surgical (RF Surgical Systems) was a medical-device company in the surgical patient-safety space, known for radio-frequency detection technology used to locate retained surgical items such as sponges and gauze during and after operations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of menlo-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment probing (2026-07-21) found no independent developer surface: the rfsurgical.com domain no longer resolves to a company site and is parked for sale (HugeDomains), consistent with the company having been absorbed into a larger medical-device parent. There is no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, package, MCP server, or documentation to harvest, so no supply-side API artifacts were generated. This profile carries identity metadata only.

providers.name: RhyGaze
providers.description: RhyGaze is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing gene therapy treatments to restore vision for people with retinal degenerative diseases. Its platform combines optogenetic proteins that engineer photosensitivity into mammalian cells with gene therapy delivery tools that install light-sensing machinery into human eye cells, technology originating at the Institute of Molecular and Clinical Ophthalmology Basel (IOB) in Switzerland. The team includes executives who helped develop and commercialize Luxturna, the first FDA-approved gene therapy for a genetic disease. RhyGaze operates from Basel, Switzerland and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and is backed by GV. As a therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Ricerca Biosciences
providers.description: Ricerca Biosciences is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Roclub
providers.description: roclub (roclub GmbH) is a German health-tech company operating a remote-control platform for diagnostic medical imaging. Its software lets healthcare organizations perform MRI and CT examinations remotely ("Remote Scanning") and support on-site technicians from anywhere ("Remote Support"), with real-time screen sharing and device control across multi-vendor scanners (Siemens, Philips, GE, Canon). roclub also runs a marketplace of qualified medical technologists ("rocStars") who can be booked on demand, together with session documentation, scheduling, and built-in liability insurance ("roCover"). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SDLC
providers.description: Software Development Life Cycle - A systematic process for planning, creating, testing, and deploying software systems. Effective use of this practice reduces bugs in production and supports a culture of quality-driven development.

providers.name: Secure Tunneling Protocols
providers.description: Network protocols that create encrypted tunnels for secure data transmission over untrusted networks, including VPN technologies like IPsec, SSL/TLS, WireGuard, and SSH tunneling for protecting communication channels. It is widely adopted across industries to safeguard digital assets and reduce security risks.

providers.name: Security by Design
providers.description: A software development approach that integrates security considerations and practices from the initial design phase through the entire development lifecycle, rather than adding security as an afterthought. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture.

providers.name: Security Protocols
providers.description: A set of rules and standards that define how data is transmitted securely over networks, including protocols like SSL/TLS, HTTPS, SSH, and IPsec that provide encryption, authentication, and data integrity. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture.

providers.name: Security Standards and Procedures
providers.description: Frameworks and documented guidelines that establish security requirements, controls, and best practices for protecting organizational assets and information systems. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture.

providers.name: Semantic Health
providers.description: Semantic Health was a Toronto-based artificial-intelligence company applying natural-language processing and machine learning to autonomous medical coding and clinical-documentation auditing for hospitals and health systems. Backed by DCVC and Y Combinator, it was acquired by AAPC in 2023 and folded into AAPC's coding and auditing product line. The company operates no standalone public developer surface; its primary domain (semantichealth.ai) no longer resolves, and semantichealth.com now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to aapc.com. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documentation were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Semnur Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Semnur Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing non-opioid pain-management therapies. Its lead program, SP-102 (SEMDEXA), is a novel, non-opioid, preservative-free and particulate-free injectable corticosteroid gel formulation intended to treat moderate-to-severe chronic radicular pain (sciatica). Semnur is a subsidiary of Scilex Holding Company and is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, California. As a pharmaceutical R&D company it publishes a corporate website, investor presentation, and scientific publications, but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Serverless Patterns
providers.description: A collection of serverless architectures and patterns for building applications on AWS, featuring ready-to-use templates and best practices for Lambda, API Gateway, EventBridge, and other serverless services. Cloud adoption of this technology supports flexibility, cost optimization, and rapid deployment.

providers.name: Shanghai Desano Pharmaceutical Group
providers.description: Shanghai Desano Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. is a Chinese pharmaceutical company established in 1996 and headquartered in Shanghai's Zhangjiang High-Tech Park. It develops and commercializes medications addressing global public health needs, specializing in anti-AIDS (antiretroviral) and anti-malaria drugs, steroid hormone drugs, and nucleic acid drugs, with operations spanning R&D, manufacturing, regulatory registration, and international distribution across multiple production bases in Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Jiangxi. Note: in this company's domain "API" means Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (drug chemistry), not a web/developer API. Desano publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, developer portal, or other machine-readable API surface, so the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline has no technical artifacts to produce for this provider. It was surfaced as a false-positive lead from the Qiming venture portfolio.

providers.name: Shulan Health
providers.description: Shulan Health (树兰医疗 / Shulan Medical Management Group) is a Hangzhou-based private healthcare group founded in 2014 by academicians Li Lanjuan and Zheng Shusen. It integrates hospital services, life-science research, medical education, and incubation investment, owning and operating comprehensive medical institutions and providing hospital-management services to partner hospitals across China. Services include rehabilitation, nutrition, health examinations, regional medical imaging, and remote consultation. Its information systems are built internally by subsidiary Huazhuo Technology on a self-developed RubikStack hybrid-cloud platform; the group publishes no public developer portal or API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Shurpa
providers.description: Shurpa was a healthcare logistics startup and a Techstars 2019 portfolio company, building a medical transportation management software platform focused on the population health and managed care space (AI-enabled coordination of non-emergency medical transportation and in-home healthcare services). The company raised roughly $220K across two seed rounds and has no visible operations today: the shurpa.com domain now returns HTTP 404 across all paths and is parked on CSC/UltraDNS nameservers, and no developer portal, documentation, API, OpenAPI, or .well-known surface could be found during enrichment. This profile is retained as an identity record for a dormant/defunct provider with no discoverable API surface.

providers.name: Sila
providers.description: Sila Nanotechnologies (silanano.com) is a battery materials company that develops and manufactures Titan Silicon, a next-generation silicon anode that replaces graphite in lithium-ion batteries to increase energy density and enable fast charging. Sila operates silicon anode manufacturing facilities and also offers battery engineering services, targeting electric vehicles, consumer electronics, aerospace, data centers, robotics, and defense. The enrichment pass found no developer API, API documentation, or developer portal: Sila is a B2B advanced-materials hardware company with no public API surface.

providers.name: Silicon Therapeutics
providers.description: Silicon Therapeutics was a Boston-based biotechnology company that built an integrated, physics-based drug-discovery platform combining quantum mechanics, molecular simulation, and machine learning to design small-molecule medicines against historically intractable targets. Founded in 2015, it was acquired by Roivant Sciences in 2021 to form the basis of Roivant's computational discovery engine; its former site (silicontx.com) now redirects to roivant.com. The company is a computational drug-discovery firm with no public API, developer platform, SDK, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Silk Road Medical
providers.description: Silk Road Medical is a medical device company (Plymouth, Minnesota) that pioneered TransCarotid Artery Revascularization (TCAR), a minimally invasive procedure for treating carotid artery disease and reducing stroke risk. Its enRoute Transcarotid Neuroprotection System and enRoute Transcarotid Stent are physician-use devices, not a software or platform product. The company is now part of Boston Scientific. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners; research finds no developer portal, public API, SDK, or machine-readable interface, so this remains a company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Silver Spring Networks *
providers.description: Silver Spring Networks was a smart-grid, smart-city, and IoT networking company that built wireless canopy networks and the SLV/Data Platform for utilities, offering RESTful Data Platform APIs (device registration, device metadata, sensor data, and webhook event notifications) plus an SDK on its developer portal at developer.ssni.com. Itron completed its acquisition of the company in January 2018 for approximately USD 830 million and rebranded it Itron Networked Solutions; the standalone ssni.com and developer.ssni.com properties are now offline. Enrichment pass 2026-07-21 found no live API surface: all legacy domains fail to resolve and the historical developer portal is no longer reachable.

providers.name: Simility
providers.description: Simility was a fraud-detection and risk-decisioning company (a "Digital Trust & Safety" adaptive machine-learning platform) founded in 2014 in Palo Alto, California and backed by Accel and Trinity Ventures. PayPal acquired Simility in 2018 and folded its device fingerprinting, behavioral analytics, and real-time fraud-scoring capabilities into PayPal's risk and fraud-management offerings. The standalone Simility product, developer portal, and any public fraud-scoring API have since been retired: as of this enrichment pass the simility.com domain is registered defensively by PayPal (via MarkMonitor / Google Domains nameservers) but publishes no A record, website, mail, or API host. No live public API surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Sirtris Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Sirtris Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: SLM Software Company
providers.description: SLM Software Company (SLMsoft.com) was a Toronto, Canada based developer of electronic payment systems and real-time transaction processing solutions for the financial services industry, founded in 1986. Its platform bundled a transaction management engine with application modules for Internet banking, IVR, debit and credit card issuing, ATM and point-of-sale network management, retail branch management, and e-CRM, along with brokerage portfolio management, e-health claims settlement, and e-government payment products, serving over 1,500 customers across 52 countries. The company was acquired by The InterCept Group (C$110 million) and is now permanently closed. It was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found no live API, developer portal, documentation, or other public developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: SLP InfoWare
providers.description: SLP InfoWare was a French software company founded in 1989 by graduates of Telecom ParisTech and based in Paris, France, providing customer profiling, churn prediction, fraud detection, and retention analytics to the telecommunications, banking, and insurance industries. Its flagship products included CHURN MINER and a Churn/CPS application that analyzed customer billing data to predict and prevent subscriber attrition. The company raised venture funding and was acquired by Gemplus International SA in October 2000 (Gemplus later became part of Gemalto, now Thales). No independent SLP InfoWare website, developer portal, or public API surface exists today; this record is retained as a historical / portfolio-lineage entry in the API Evangelist network and carries no live API artifacts.

providers.name: Solar City
providers.description: SolarCity was a San Mateo, California based provider of residential and commercial solar energy systems, founded in 2006 by brothers Peter and Lyndon Rive with backing and board chairmanship from their cousin Elon Musk. The company designed, financed, installed, and monitored rooftop solar and energy-storage systems, and became the largest residential solar installer in the United States before its 2012 IPO (NASDAQ: SCTY). In November 2016 SolarCity was acquired by Tesla, Inc. in an all-stock deal valued at roughly 2.6 billion US dollars and was absorbed into Tesla's energy-generation and storage business; the SolarCity brand was subsequently retired and its products relaunched under Tesla (Solar Roof, Solar Panels, Powerwall). SolarCity no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone developer portal, public API, or OpenAPI surface. The solarcity.com domain remains registered under Tesla's DNS infrastructure but no longer serves a live website.

providers.name: Solid (Solid.fi)
providers.description: Solid (formerly Wise) was a venture-backed fintech-as-a-service / embedded finance platform offering banking, card, and payment APIs to fintech builders. Solid raised more than $80M, including a 2022 Series B led by FTV Capital. The company subsequently became the subject of significant legal trouble - including litigation with FTV Capital and reported customer disputes - and substantially wound down operations through 2023-2024. As of this profile, the solidfi.com site is not responding to requests and no active API or onboarding pipeline appears to be operating. This is an honest historical record; treat any API references as unverified / inactive.

providers.name: Standard Signal
providers.description: Standard Signal is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building autonomous AI trading systems for a market-neutral hedge fund, using reasoning models to discover and execute complex trades in real time within predefined risk parameters and with chain-of-thought explainability. Founded by Michael Royzen, the company presents an investor-facing offering (qualified investors, $100k minimum) and a hiring page, but publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or discovery surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Sunshine Lake Pharma
providers.description: Sunshine Lake Pharma (Guangdong East Sunshine Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., also known as HEC Pharm) is a Chinese pharmaceutical company established in 2003 and part of the Dongyangguang (HEC) Group. It engages in drug research, development, production, and commercialization across innovative drugs, improved formulations, generics, and biosimilars, focused on infections, chronic diseases, and oncology. Notable products include oseltamivir phosphate (influenza), sofosbuvir-based hepatitis C therapy, and insulin glargine (diabetes). It is a manufacturer with no public developer or API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Syntax Bio
providers.description: Syntax Bio is a synthetic biology company programming the next generation of cell therapies. Its proprietary Cellgorithm platform uses a CRISPR-based system to program and accelerate stem cell differentiation, replacing slow, labor-intensive processes with a rapid, programmable approach that mimics human development to generate diverse functional cell types at scale. The company is advancing pancreatic beta cell therapy for type 1 diabetes and is backed by DCVC Bio, Astellas Venture Management, Illumina Ventures, and others. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of dcvc; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic developer surface as of this pass.

providers.name: Tact.ai
providers.description: Tact.ai was a Redwood City, California conversational-AI and field-engagement company founded by Chuck Ganapathi that built an AI sales assistant ("Tact Assistant") unifying CRM, email, and calendar data into a voice- and chat-driven interface for enterprise sales teams, later concentrating on the life sciences vertical. It was backed by Accel, Redpoint Ventures, Upfront Ventures, Microsoft's M12, and Salesforce Ventures. In November 2023 its field-engagement and conversational-AI technology was acquired by Aktana and the standalone company wound down. The tact.ai domain no longer hosts a product: it resolves to an Afternic domain-for-sale parking page (nameservers ns1/ns2.afternic.com), and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal to enrich.

providers.name: Talko
providers.description: Talko was a mobile business-communications startup founded by former Microsoft CTO Ray Ozzie and backed by a16z. Launched in September 2014, its app let mobile teams call, text, and exchange voice and video messages, recording live conversations with in-call bookmarks, tagging, and asynchronous voice follow-ups. Microsoft acquired the company in December 2015 to bolster Skype, and the Talko service was fully shut down by March 2016. The company is defunct with no live developer platform, website, or API surface; it remains in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio record.

providers.name: Talkray
providers.description: Talkray (operated by TiKL, Inc., a Y Combinator W12 startup founded in 2012 by Zafer Ahmed in Redwood City, California) was a free cross-platform messaging and calling app spanning the TiKL Touch-To-Talk and Talkray consumer apps, which together saw roughly 28 million downloads. In 2013 the company announced the Talkray Developer API, a white-label cloud platform for embedding one-on-one and group text chat, group voice calls, voicemail, push notifications, and image/video transfer into third-party mobile apps and games. That API never left private beta and no public documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal were ever published. The company is now defunct (deadpooled) - active development ceased around 2018 and the app was removed from Google Play in February 2021. talkray.com currently sits behind Cloudflare and returns HTTP 403 for all paths.

providers.name: TCF Financial Corporation
providers.description: Profile for TCF Financial Corporation, a former Detroit-headquartered regional bank holding company (Twin City Building and Loan Association, founded 1923). TCF was merged into Huntington Bancshares Incorporated on June 9, 2021, and the TCF brand was fully retired. This repository is preserved for historical record only — TCF Financial no longer operates and exposes no APIs. All banking, treasury, deposit, and lending services formerly offered under the TCF brand are now operated by Huntington National Bank under the Huntington brand. See the huntington-bancshares repository for current API surface (which is itself minimal; Huntington exposes no public developer portal).

providers.name: Telcare
providers.description: Telcare was a digital-health company that built the first cellular-enabled blood glucose monitoring (BGM) system: a meter with an embedded cellular module that pushed readings to Telcare's Telserve/Telcloud back end, connected to EMR systems, and paired with companion smartphone apps for people managing diabetes and their caregivers. The brand was acquired into BioTelemetry and is now part of Philips (BioTel Care); the telcare.com domain redirects to Philips ambulatory monitoring, and device-data integration is offered through the third-party Validic health-data platform rather than a first-party public API. Surfaced as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio lead; enrichment found no first-party developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface for the Telcare brand.

providers.name: Teligene
providers.description: Teligene (Suzhou Teligene Biotechnology Co., Ltd.) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2011 in Suzhou, China by Dr. Zhang Dawei, a former chief scientist at Amgen. The company focuses on the design, research and industrialization of innovative small-molecule targeted drugs for oncology, with a pipeline addressing lung cancer, breast cancer, and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Teligene US LLC is a wholly owned US subsidiary advancing these candidates through clinical development. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as a drug-development biotech it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Tellgen
providers.description: Shanghai Tellgen Life Sciences Co., Ltd. (Tellgen Corporation) is a Chinese in vitro diagnostics (IVD) company founded in 2003 and headquartered in Shanghai, focused on the research, development, manufacture, and distribution of high-end diagnostic reagents and instruments. Its portfolio spans tumor markers, HPV detection, autoimmune antibodies, infectious disease, thrombosis and reproductive-health assays across flow-fluorescence, chemiluminescence, real-time PCR / molecular, and clinical-chemistry platforms (TESMI analyzer family). The company was listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange ChiNext board in April 2017 (ticker 300642) and counts Qiming Venture Partners among its early investors. Tellgen is a medical-device and laboratory-reagent manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Telogy Networks
providers.description: Telogy Networks was one of the first companies to deliver software solutions enabling voice over IP (VoIP) networks. Founded in 1989 and headquartered in Germantown, Maryland, the company built the Golden Gateway telephony software and DSP-resident voice/fax media processing stacks that were embedded into carrier and enterprise gateway equipment. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (invested 1997), ABS Ventures, Ameritech Development, Catalyst Venture Partners, and Novak Biddle Venture Partners, Telogy Networks was acquired by Texas Instruments in 1999 for roughly $457 million, where its VoIP media-gateway software became the basis of TI's telephony DSP product line. Telogy no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, public API, or SDK. This record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio company profile.

providers.name: Teneobio
providers.description: Teneobio was a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a new class of biologics, Human Heavy-Chain Antibodies (UniAb), for the treatment of cancer, autoimmunity, and infectious diseases. Its TeneoSeek discovery platform combined genetically engineered animals (UniRat, OmniFlic), next-generation sequencing, bioinformatics, and high-throughput vector assembly. Teneobio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Amgen acquired Teneobio in October 2021 for $900 million upfront plus up to $1.6 billion in contingent milestone payments; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no live developer surface. This is a life-sciences / therapeutics company with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Terra AI
providers.description: Terra AI is a geoscience frontier company building specialized artificial intelligence for the natural resources sector, focused on subsurface characterization and exploration optimization for mining and reservoir operators. Its platform integrates exploration data to generate large populations of geological models, helping teams decide where to drill, characterize deposits, and assess project economics earlier — the company cites 50-60% fewer drilling meters and 2-3x more precise resource estimates versus conventional methods. Terra AI raised a $20M Series A led by Khosla Ventures with BHP Ventures in June 2026 and serves copper, gold, rare-earth (REE), and reservoir projects. The company operates on a B2B model and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Textaurant
providers.description: Textaurant was an early SMS-based restaurant waitlist and table-management startup founded around 2010 by Josh Bob in Waltham, Massachusetts, and later surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Its software let a restaurant manage its waiting list from a laptop and text guests when a table opened up, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative to pager-based systems from JTECH and OpenTable. The original company is defunct: its primary domain, textaurant.com, now resolves to a parked GoDaddy "for sale" landing page with no product, documentation, or API surface. A separate, unaffiliated live app reusing the name exists at app.textaurant.app (a small Twilio-backed Next.js application served through a personal proxy), but it publishes no public API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer documentation. There is no API to onboard against; this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct provider.

providers.name: The Pill Club
providers.description: The Pill Club was a US direct-to-consumer telehealth and pharmacy service for birth control and reproductive health, delivering prescription contraception and sexual-health products by mail. The brand has been consolidated into Nurx (a Thirty Madison company): its domain thepillclub.com now 301-redirects to nurx.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer, API, or documentation surface was found for either the legacy brand or its Nurx successor; this is a consumer healthcare service with no external API program.

providers.name: ThirtyFiveBio
providers.description: ThirtyFiveBio is an Oxford, UK biotechnology company founded in 2021 to develop first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors of G protein-coupled receptor 35 (GPR35) for the treatment of gastrointestinal diseases, including ulcerative colitis, inflammatory bowel disease, and digestive-tract cancers. The company was incubated by the M:M Bio (Molecule to Medicine) drug-discovery ecosystem together with Canaan Partners, and is backed by AbbVie Ventures, Mayewell Capital, and Innovate UK. It is a preclinical drug-discovery company with plans for first-in-human trials, not a software or API provider; this profile carries no developer API surface.

providers.name: Thrive Earlier Detection
providers.description: Thrive Earlier Detection Corp. was a healthcare/biotech company commercializing CancerSEEK, a machine-learning-driven liquid biopsy blood test to detect multiple cancer types from a single blood draw. Spun out of Johns Hopkins technology and backed by Lux Capital, Bain Capital Life Sciences, Casdin, Google Ventures and others, it raised large early rounds before being acquired by Exact Sciences in 2020/2021 for roughly $2.15 billion and folded into Exact Sciences. This profile was surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. It is a clinical-diagnostics company with no public developer API surface; its former web presence (thrivedetect.com) is decommissioned.

providers.name: Tizona Therapeutics
providers.description: Tizona Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing first-in-class cancer immunotherapies by translating novel scientific insights into new medicines. Its lead program, TTX-080, is a first-in-class HLA-G antagonist in clinical trials for advanced solid tumors. Tizona is a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. As a pharmaceutical drug-development company it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface; this profile is retained as a network company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Tobira Therapeutics
providers.description: Tobira Therapeutics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Tola
providers.description: Tola is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: other. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Tome Bioscience
providers.description: Tome Biosciences is a genome-editing therapeutics company founded in 2021 and based in Watertown, Massachusetts. It develops programmable genomic integration (PGI) technology that pairs the site-specificity of CRISPR/Cas with integrase enzymes to insert genetic sequences of virtually any size into the genome without relying on double-strand DNA breaks. The company was cofounded by Omar Abudayyeh and Jonathan Gootenberg, formerly of MIT's McGovern Institute, and raised roughly $213M across Series A and B financing led in part by a16z. Its stated programs target integrative gene therapies for monogenic liver diseases and cell therapies for autoimmune conditions. Tome is a biopharmaceutical R&D company with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; its documented website (tome.bio) does not currently resolve. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company / enrichment lead rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Tomfoolery
providers.description: Tomfoolery, Inc. was a San Francisco mobile-app lab founded in 2012 by Sol Lipman (Chief Product Officer) and Kakul Srivastava (CEO), a team of ex-Yahoo and ex-AOL executives building consumer-grade, mobile-first collaboration apps for the enterprise. Its debut product was Anchor, a real-time conversation platform meant to be a central hub for work discussions, followed by an app called Action. The company raised roughly $1.7M (investors included Andreessen Horowitz) before being acquired by Yahoo in January 2014, after which the Anchor app was shut down. Tomfoolery is now a defunct/deadpooled company with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface. It was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirms there is no API to profile.

providers.name: Topography
providers.description: Topography (Topography Health, Inc.) was a full-stack clinical trials platform that empowered community and private-practice physicians to run clinical drug trials in their local communities across North America, reducing the administrative burden of becoming a clinical trialist. Founded in 2020 by Alexander Saint-Amand, Mac Parish, and Andrew Kirchner and based in New York and Los Angeles, the company launched in January 2022 with $27.5M in funding, including a $21.5M Series A led by Bain Capital Ventures and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). In 2026 Topography Health's Site Business Unit was acquired by FOMAT Medical Research, and the company's public site is now a single-page acquisition announcement. Topography was a B2B clinical-research SaaS, not a developer-facing API company: no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface was ever published, and none exists today.

providers.name: Trading Machines
providers.description: Trading Machines LLC is a proprietary high-frequency options and equities trading firm, founded around 2007 and headquartered in New York City, and registered as a broker-dealer with FINRA (CRD 146274). The firm traded on its own account, at one point reportedly executing a meaningful share of daily US options volume using low-latency, algorithmic and automated trading technology. As a proprietary trading firm it operates for its own book rather than offering a public developer product, and it surfaced in the API Evangelist network only as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead. Research during enrichment found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or other machine-readable developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: Transcend Medical
providers.description: Transcend Medical was a medical device company based in Menlo Park, California, developing minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) devices. Spun out of the ForSight Labs ophthalmic incubator, its lead product was the CyPass Micro-Stent, a suprachoroidal implant designed to lower intraocular pressure in patients with mild-to-moderate glaucoma undergoing cataract surgery. The company raised roughly $89.8M across multiple venture rounds from investors including Canaan Partners, HLM Venture Partners, Finistere Ventures, Kaiser Permanente Ventures, Latterell Venture Partners, Morgenthaler Ventures, Split Rock Partners and Technology Partners, and was acquired by Novartis's Alcon eye-care business in February 2016. It operated no public API, developer platform, or software product; the transcendmedical.com domain no longer resolves following the company's absorption into Alcon.

providers.name: Tremor
providers.description: Tremor Technologies operated a programmatic "smart market" for wholesale risk and reinsurance, applying intelligent market design, auction technology, and optimization to match risk with capital and price and place reinsurance contracts far faster and cheaper than traditional negotiated markets. Founded in 2016 by Sean Bourgeois and later based in Greenwich, Connecticut, the platform ran auction-style placements for insurers, brokers, reinsurers, ILS funds, and Lloyd's syndicates, and added Tremor Wordings to digitize contract negotiation. Backed by Anthemis (lead), W. R. Berkley, Nephila Capital, and Markel, Tremor's assets were sold to W. R. Berkley Corporation in September 2023 and the standalone public marketplace site (tremor.co) is no longer live.

providers.name: Trillium Therapeutics
providers.description: Trillium Therapeutics was a Toronto-based clinical-stage immuno-oncology biopharmaceutical company developing cancer therapeutics (notably CD47-targeting agents). It was acquired by Pfizer in August 2021 for approximately $2.2B and no longer operates as an independent entity. Surfaced as an nea portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences lead.
